Complications of acute tonsillitis : • Chronic tonsillitis - chronic infection may persist in lymphoid follicles of the tonsil in the form of microabscesses • Peritonsillar abscess • Parapharyngeal abscess • Cervical abscess due to suppuration of jugulodigastric lymph nodes • Acute otitis media • Rheumatic fever - often seen in association with tonsillitis due to group A \037-hemolytic streptococci • Acute glomerulonephritis (rare) • Subacute bacterial endocarditis - acute tonsillitis in a patient with valvular heart disease may be complicated by endocarditis . It is usually due to Streptococcus viridans infection

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following nerves is responsible for referred otalgia from tonsillitis ?
mcqs.explanation: The tympanic branch of the glossopharyngeal nerve (cranial nerve IX) is responsible for referred otalgia from tonsillitis .472 The tonsils and tonsillar fossa are supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve. The glossopharyngeal nerve and the styloid process lie in relation to the lower part of the tonsillar fossa. Therefore, any irritation or pain can be referred to the ear along the tympanic branch of the glossopharyngeal (Jacobson's) nerve. Causes of referred otalgia via the glossopharyngeal nerve include acute pharyngitis, tonsillitis, peritonsillar abscess , post -tonsillectomy , foreign bodies embedded in the base of the tongue or tonsillar area and an elongated styloid process (Eagle 's syndrome). The ear receives extensive sensory innervation via four cranial nerves (V , VII , IX, and X) and two spinal segments (C2 and C3). The image below shows the anatomic relations of the tonsil and tonsillar bed :

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 15-year-old girl presented to the ENT surgeon with a history of loud snoring, restless sleep leading to daytime somnolence , and poor academic performance. Her medical history was unremarkable, except for recurrent episodes of acute tonsillitis . Which of the following types of tonsillitis may be implicated in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical presentation is suggestive of obstructive sleep apnea syndrome(OSAS) secondary to chronic parenchymatous tonsillitis . In parenchymatous tonsillitis , the tonsils grow very large following repeated attacks of acute tonsillitis and lead to obstructive symptoms , including OSAS. Types of chronic tonsillitis : • Chronic follicular tonsillitis - tonsillar crypts are full of infected cheesy material, which shows on the surface as yellowish spots . • Chronic parenchymatous tonsillitis - there is hyperplasia of lymphoid tissue . Tonsils are very much enlarged and may interfere with speech , deglutition , and respiration. Attacks of sleep apnoea may occur. Long-standing cases develop features of cor pulmonale . • Chronic fibroid tonsillitis - tonsils are tiny but infected , with a history of repeated sore throats.473

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: You are an intern posted in the ENT department working up a case of chronic follicular tonsillitis. Which of the following clinical signs would you not expect to see in this patient on examining the oral cavity?
mcqs.explanation: M\374ller's sign is the pulsation of uvula during systole seen in aortic regurgitation . It is not seen in patients with chronic tonsillitis . The classical signs of chronic tonsillitis are: • Irwin -Moore sign- tonsils are tiny, but pressure on the anterior pillar expresses frank pus or cheesy material. • Bluish Flushing of anterior pillars compared to the rest of the pharyngeal mucosa is a vital sign of chronic tonsillar infection . • Enlargement of jugulo -digastric lymph nodes even in the absence of acute infection is a reliable sign of chronic tonsillitis . During acute attacks, the nodes enlarge further and become tender .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: An ENT junior resident observed a symptomless yellowish swelling over the tonsil when he was examining a patient for a buccal sore. The swelling was easily drained. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of a tonsillar cyst . It is a condition due to blockage of a tonsillar crypt and appears as a yellowish swelling over the tonsil. Very often , it is symptomless and can be easily drained. Option A: Intratonsillar abscess is an accumulation of pus within the substance of the tonsil. It usually follows a blockage of the opening of the crypt in acute follicular tonsillitis . There is marked local pain and dysphagia . Tonsil appears swollen and red. Option B: Tonsilloliths (calculus of the tonsil) are seen in chronic tonsillitis when its crypt is blocked with retention of debris. Inorganic salts of calcium and magnesium are then deposited leading to the formation of a stone . It may gradually enlarge and then ulcerate through the tonsil. It generally causes local discomfort or foreign body sensation.474 Option D: In follicular tonsillitis , purulent material is present at the opening of the crypts as yellow dots . It presents with fever, dysphagia, and sore throat.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: On examining the oral cavity of a patient who presented with fever and a sore throat, you notice a greyish -white membrane over the tonsils. Which of the following conditions would you not consider as a differential diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Ludwig's angina is not associated with the formation of a grey-white membrane. It is characterized by rapidly spreading infection of the sublingual space initially and later the submaxillary space , often dentogenic in origin. D/D for membrane over tonsil: • Streptococcus & other pyogenic organisms • Diphtheria • Infectious mononucleosis • Vincent's angina • Leukemia • Candida • Agranulocytosis • Malignancy • Apthous ulcer • Traumatic ulcer

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms is implicated in Vincent's angina?
mcqs.explanation: Vincent's angina is caused by fusiform bacilli and spirochaetes , namely Bacillus fusiformis and Borrelia vincenti. The condition presents with low-grade fever and sore throat, and a membrane over the tonsil. The membrane is easily removed to reveal irregular ulcers over the tonsil. Throat swab will show both the organisms typical of the disease , namely fusiform bacilli and spirochaetes .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A worried mother brought her 6-year-old unimmunized child to the ER with complaints of fever, cough , and shortness of breath. On examination, a pseudomembrane was noted in the oral cavity along with the neck finding as shown in the image. Which of the following statements is true regarding the membrane observed?

options.b: Firmly adherent and bleeds on removal

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history and bull-neck appearance (image) point to the diagnosis of diphtheria . The diphtheritic membrane is firmly adherent and bleeds on removal. A greyish -white membrane forms over the tonsils in the oropharynx and spreads to the soft palate and posterior pharyngeal wall. The membrane in diphtheria extends beyond the tonsils onto the soft palate and is dirty grey. It is adherent, and its removal leaves a bleeding surface . In the larynx, the diphtheritic membrane may cause airway obstruction.475 Cervical lymph nodes , particularly the jugulodigastric , become enlarged and tender , sometimes presenting a bull-neck appearance . The patient is ill and toxaemic, but fever seldom rises above 38\260C.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following complications would you not expect to see in a patient diagnosed with diphtheria?
mcqs.explanation: Hard palate paralysis is not seen in diphtheria. The exotoxin produced by C. diphtheriae is toxic to the heart and nerves. It causes : • Myocarditis • Cardiac arrhythmias • Acute circulatory failure Neurological complications include paralysis of the soft -palate , diaphragm, and ocular muscles . In the larynx, the diphtheric membrane may cause airway obstruction.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Following finding was noted in a patient who presented with difficulty breathing and a bull-neck appearance . Which of the following statements is true regarding the treatment of this patient ?

options.a: Treatment is started after the culture comes positive
options.d: Sensitivity to antitoxin should be tested prior to therapy

mcqs.explanation: The pseudomembrane on oral examination and bull neck appearance is characteristic of diphtheria. Sensitivity to diphtheria antitoxin is common and should be tested prior to the initiation of therapy . Treatment is started on clinical suspicion without waiting for the culture report. The aim is to neutralize the free exotoxin still circulating in the blood and to kill the organisms producing this exotoxin. Antitoxins: • Dose - based on the site involved, duration, and severity of the disease • If < 48 hours or just confined to tonsils: ,000 –40,000 units • If > 48 hours or extensive membrane: 80,000 –120 ,000 units • Given by i.v. infusion in saline in about 60 min • Sensitivity tested by a conjunctival or intracutaneous test with diluted antitoxin • If a hypersensitivity reaction occurs, desensitization should be done Antibiotics: • Benzyl penicillin 600 mg 6 hourly for 7 days • Erythromycin is used in penicillin -sensitive individuals (500 mg 6 hourly orally)

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following cases cannot be posted for an elective tonsillectomy ?

options.b: A young adult with chronic tonsillitis refractory to treatment
options.c: A patient with unilateral enlargement of tonsil with suspected malignancy
options.d: A middle -aged man with recurrent quinsy

mcqs.explanation: 476 Acute tonsillitis is a contraindication for tonsillectomy and hence , cannot be posted for elective surgery. Acute tonsillitis or any upper respiratory tract infection is a contraindication for tonsillectomy since there is an increased chance of hemorrhage and sepsis . Indications of tonsillectomy are: • Recurrent episodes of acute tonsillitis – most common indication Seven or more episodes in 1 year, or Five episodes per year for 2 years, or Three episodes per year for 3 years, or Two weeks or more of lost school or work in 1 year • Febrile seizures due to fever in tonsillitis • Peritonsillar abscess (quinsy) - recurrent episodes in adults and a single episode in children • Hypertrophy of tonsils causing airway obstruction, difficulty in deglutition , interference with speech • Unilateral enlargement of tonsil with suspicion of malignancy • Chronic tonsillitis with bad taste or halitosis which is unresponsive to medical treatment (relative indication)

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a contraindication to perform a tonsillectomy ?
mcqs.explanation: Diphtheria and streptococcal carriers are relative indications for tonsillectomy and the surgery can be safely performed in patients presenting with the same. Contraindications for tonsillectomy : • Haemoglobin level less than 10 g%. • Presence of acute infection in upper respiratory tract, even acute tonsillitis . Bleeding is more in the presence of acute infection . • Children under 3 years of age . • Overt or submucous cleft palate . • Bleeding disorders, e.g. leukaemia, purpura, aplastic anaemia or haemophilia . • At the time of epidemic of polio. • Uncontrolled systemic disease , e.g. diabetes , cardiac disease , hypertension or asthma. • Tonsillectomy is avoided during the period of menses .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A patient develops bleeding from the surgical site five hours after an elective tonsillectomy . Which among the following would best describe the condition?
mcqs.explanation: 477 Bleeding from the surgical site within a period of 24 hours is categorised as a reactionary haemorrhage. Primary haemorrhage - occurs at the time of operation. Secondary haemorrhage - usually seen between the fifth to tenth postoperative days.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: While preparing for a procedure , the patient was kept in a specific position as depicted in the image. In which of the following procedures is this position not adopted ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows Rose's position and it is not a suitable position to perform a direct laryngoscopy . The barking -dog position is used for direct laryngoscopy . Rose's position: The patient lies supine with head extended by placing a pillow under the shoulders . It is followed in adenoidectomy, tonsillectomy , and tracheostomy .Barking -dog position: Patient lies supine . The Head is elevated by 10 –15 cm by placing a pillow under the occiput or raising the operation table 's head flap. The neck is flexed on the thorax and the head is extended on the atlanto-occipital joint.478

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following marked structures is the space of Gillette ?
mcqs.explanation: Option 1 is Gillette 's space . Retropharyngeal space is divided into two lateral compartments (spaces of Gillette ) by a median fibrous raphe. Option 2 - Danger space - between alar fascia anteriorly and prevertebral fascia posteriorly . Option 3 - Prevertebral space . Option 4 - Anterior cervical space .487

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: An ENT surgeon is performing an incision and drainage for a retropharyngeal abscess due to suppurative lymphadenitis . Which among the following groups of lymph nodes is most likely to be involved?
mcqs.explanation: Rouvier Nodes or retropharyngeal lymph nodes suppurate to form retropharyngeal abscess . Each lateral compartment of retropharyngeal space contains lymph nodes that usually disappear at 3-4 years of age . Suppuration of these lymph nodes is the most common cause of retropharyngeal space abscess in children. Option B - Delphian nodes are the pre-laryngeal lymph nodes . Option C - Virchow's node is the left supraclavicular lymph node. Option D - Cloquet 's nodes are the deep inguinal lymph nodes .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A concerned mother brought her toddler to the ER with complaints of noisy breathing and the child refusing to feed . On examination, the child has adenoid facies and there is a bulge in the posterior pharyngeal wall lateral to the midline. Which of the following is a false statement regarding the disease described above?

options.a: Suppuration of nodes of Rouvier can cause the above condition
options.b: Caries of the cervical spine is the most common cause
options.c: In adults similar condition may result from penetrating injury of the cervical esophagus
options.d: Torticollis is one of the symptoms .

mcqs.explanation: The above clinical condition is suggestive of acute retropharyngeal abscess whereas caries of the cervical spine results in a chronic retropharyngeal abscess . Acute retropharyngeal abscess is commonly seen in children below 3 years. It is the result of suppuration of retropharyngeal lymph nodes secondary to infection in the adenoids , nasopharynx, posterior nasal sinuses , or nasal cavity. In adults , it may result from penetrating injury of the posterior pharyngeal wall or cervical esophagus . Clinical features of a retropharyngeal abscess include • Dysphagia and difficulty in breathing - as the abscess obstructs the air and food passages . • Stridor and croupy cough • Torticollis - the neck becomes stiff and the head is kept extended . • A bulge in the posterior pharyngeal wall, usually seen on one side of the midline. Chronic retropharyngeal abscess is the result of • Caries of the cervical spine • Tuberculous infection of retropharyngeal lymph nodes secondary to tuberculosis of deep cervical nodes .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 42-year-old HIV positive man presents with an acute onset high-grade fever with chills and shortness of breath. On evaluation, he's diagnosed to have a necrotising mediastinitis secondary to rupture of a retropharyngeal abscess . What is the likely route of spread of infection to the mediastinum?

options.a: Between buccopharyngeal fascia and alar fascia.
options.b: Between alar fascia and prevertebral fascia
options.c: Between the capsule of tonsil and superior constrictor muscle

mcqs.explanation: The likely route of spread of infection is between the alar fascia anteriorly and the prevertebral fascia posteriorly . It is also called the danger space or alar space . It lies just posterior to the retropharyngeal space . It extends from the skull base to the diaphragm. Infections from this space can spread to the mediastinum, and hence it is named the danger space .488

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Given below is an X-ray of a child who presented with stridor. What is your diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given image is suggestive of a retropharyngeal abscess . It can be diagnosed on a lateral x-ray of the soft tissues of the neck. The features include : • Widening of the prevertebral soft tissue shadow • Loss of cervical lordosis • In an acute abscess , air-fluid levels can be seen .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following options is synonymous with quinsy?
mcqs.explanation: Quinsy is synonymous with peritonsillar abscess . It is the collection of pus between the fibrous capsule of the tonsil and the superior constrictor muscles of the pharynx.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A middle -aged diabetic man who had undergone a tooth extraction presents with fever and trismus. On examination, his posterior pillar is pushed medially and there is a swelling in the neck at the upper 1/3rd of the sternocleidomastoid muscle . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario is suggestive of parapharyngeal abscess . Parapharyngeal abscess presents with: • Trismus due to spasm of medial pterygoid • Tonsils pushed medially • Swelling in the upper part of the sternocleidomastoid (space limited to the level of hyoid bone). Option A - Retropharyngeal abscess presents as a bulge in the posterior pharyngeal wall on one side of the midline. Option C - In Ludwig's angina, tonsils are not pushed medially . Option D - Peritonsillar abscess doesn 't produce swelling in the upper 1/3rd of the sternocleidomastoid .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not synonymous with parapharyngeal abscess ?
mcqs.explanation: Parapharyngeal abscess is not synonymous with medial pharyngeal abscess . Parapharyngeal abscess is synonymous with pharyngomaxillary or lateral pharyngeal or pterygomaxillary abscess .489

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is correct regarding a parapharyngeal abscess ?

options.a: Always spreads from the retropharyngeal space
options.c: It has preponderance for male gender

mcqs.explanation: Parapharyngeal abscess has a preponderance for male gender . Parapharyngeal abscess is an emergency condition. Infection can spread to the parapharyngeal space from any of the other deep neck spaces - peritonsillar, retropharyngeal and submandibular spaces . It commonly spreads from a dental infection , tonsillitis or peritonsillar abscesses . The patient is usually systemically unwell , with severe trismus and possibly airway compromise. Initial broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics should include cover against streptococci and anaerobic organisms. Carotid sheath vessel thrombosis, necrotizing fasciitis and mediastinitis are some of the complications. Marked neck swelling , airway compromise, and male gender appear to be predictive of higher-risk cases .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following features will not be manifested in an infection of the post -styloid compartment of the parapharyngeal space ?
mcqs.explanation: Trismus is not a feature of infection of the post -styloid compartment of the parapharyngeal space . Trismus is seen in pre-styloid abscess due to the involvement of medial pterygoid muscle . Parapharyngeal space is divided into two compartments by the styloid process and its attachments. Clinical features depend on the compartment involved. In a post -styloid abscess , there is a bulge of the pharynx behind the posterior pillar, accompanied by paralysis of cranial nerves IX, X (resulting in vocal cord paralysis), XI, XII, and the sympathetic chain, which can manifest as Horner's syndrome. Swelling in the parotid region may also be present . Notably , trismus, the inability to fully open the mouth, is usually absent in this type of abscess . A pre-styloid abscess exhibits distinct features including the prolapse of the tonsil and tonsillar fossa, along with trismus caused by the spasm of the medial pterygoid muscle . Marked odynophagia is common. Additionally , an external swelling can be observed behind the angle of the jaw. Fever, sore throat, torticollis (caused by spasm of the prevertebral muscles ), and signs of systemic toxicity are common features . Diagnosis can be established using a contrast-enhanced CT scan (CECT). If there is suspicion of thrombosis of the internal jugular vein or an aneurysm of the internal carotid artery, magnetic resonance arteriography (MRA) can be useful . Patients require intravenous antibiotic therapy with amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, carbapenem a ntibiotics plus drugs that target anaerobic organisms, such as clindamycin or metronidazole . A parapharyngeal abscess is drained by an external horizontal incision made on the skin a few centimeters below the angle of the mandible. The image attached below shows the components of both spaces :490

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: In which of the following clinical scenarios will you not perform an intraoral incision?

options.a: A 21 -year-old woman with fever, hot potato voice and bulging of soft palate and anterior pillar above the tonsil on the right side .
options.b: A 50-year-old diabetic man with fever, neck swelling over upper \037 rd of the left sternocleidomastoid and the tonsils on the same side pushed medially
options.c: A 3-year-old child with fever and swelling in the posterior pharyngeal wall lateral to the midline
options.d: A 50-year-old man with fever due to penetrating injury of oral mucosa by wood splinters

mcqs.explanation: An intraoral incision is not sufficient in the case of option B - parapharyngeal abscess . An external neck incision must be made always to ensure complete drainage of the abscess . Option A- This is a case of quinsy as the child has odynophagia and a hot potato voice. Option B - This is a case of parapharyngeal abscess as the swelling is in the upper 1/3rd of the neck and the tonsil of the same side is pushed medially Option C- This is a case of retropharyngeal abscess since there is fever and swelling in the posterior pharyngeal wall lateral to the midline. Option D- This is a case of Sublingual abscess involving the sublingual space which is caused by penetrating injuries of oral mucosa due to fishbone or wood splinters . Indications for Incision and Drainage: • Sublingual abscess : Always intraoral incision • Parapharyngeal abscess : Always external neck incision. • Peritonsillar abscess : Always intraoral . • Retropharyngeal abscess : • Intraoral - in rose position • External - Dean approach • Ludwig's angina: • Intraoral —if the infection is still localized to sublingual space . • External—if the infection involves submaxillary space .491

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 9-year-old boy comes with complaints of right ear pain, difficulty in opening the mouth, painful swallowing , and fever. The oral cavity examination reveals the following . The external facial examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is likely?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario describes a child with fever, otalgia, trismus, and odynophagia with a normal external facial examination. The oral cavity shows congested and edematous tonsil and tonsillar pillars with edematous uvula pushed to the opposite side . These findings are highly suggestive of quinsy (peritonsillar abscess ). It is the collection of pus in the peritonsillar space between the fibrous capsule of the tonsil and the superior constrictor muscles of the pharynx. Both aerobic and anaerobic organisms are seen . Patient presents with fever, unilateral throat pain, odynophagia , hot potato voice, torticollis, foul breath, referred otalgia through glossopharyngeal nerve and trismus due to spasm of pterygoid muscles . Oral cavity examination may show congested and edematous tonsils, pillars, and soft palate on the involved side . Edematous uvula pushed to the opposite side . Pus may be seen on the tonsillar region. Jugulodigastric lymph nodes may be enlarged . The management of quinsy is by antibiotics and incision and drainage to drain the abscess followed by interval tonsillectomy 4 to 6 weeks later. Rare complications seen are parapharyngeal abscess , edema of the larynx, septicemia , lung abscess , or jugular vein thrombosis. Other options : Option A: Pharyngitis presents with fever, throat pain, enlarged tonsils, and lymphoid follicles on the posterior pharyngeal wall. Option B: Parotid abscess occurs due to the suppuration of parotid space . It presents with swelling , redness , firmness, and tenderness in the parotid area and at the angle of the mandible. It is usually unilateral, but bilateral abscesses can occur. Due to the thick capsule , fluctuation is often difficult to elicit . Option C: Bezold abscess is a complication of acute otomastoiditis where the infection /pus breaks through the thin medial side of the tip of the mastoid and presents as a swelling in the upper part of the neck.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about quinsy is false ?

options.a: Collection of pus between the capsule of tonsil and superior constrictor
options.b: Presents with odynophagia and drooling of saliva

mcqs.explanation: Peritonsillar abscess or quinsy is usually unilateral. It is a collection of pus in the peritonsillar space which lies between the capsule of the tonsil and the superior constrictor muscle . Usually , it is unilateral though occasionally bilateral abscesses are recorded . It presents with marked odynophagia such that the patient cannot even swallow his saliva which d ribbles from the angle of his mouth. The patient is usually dehydrated . Muffled and thick speech , often called hot potato voice.492

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old girl presented with complaints of fever, right-sided throat pain, and difficulty in swallowing . On examination, she had hot potato speech and halitosis. The right tonsil was not visualised due to oedematous pillars and the uvula was pushed to the left . How will you manage this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario is suggestive of peritonsillar abscess or quinsy and management involves incision and drainage with antibiotics. Management of quinsy • Hospitalization • Intravenous fluids to combat dehydration • Antibiotics - Suitable antibiotics in large IV doses to cover aerobes and anaerobes • Analgesics • Drainage by needle aspiration or incision and drainage • Tonsillectomy when there is airway obstruction or recurrence. Incision and drainage of the abscess : A peritonsillar abscess is opened at the point of the maximum bulge above the upper pole of the tonsil or just lateral to the point of junction of the anterior pillar with a line drawn through the base of the uvula.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: In a patient with recurrent peritonsillar abscess , when is the ideal time to perform a tonsillectomy ?
mcqs.explanation: In a patient with recurrent peritonsillar abscess (quinsy), ideally , an interval tonsillectomy is done 4-6 weeks after the infection settles down. Hot tonsillectomy : Earlier tonsillectomy was done during incision and drainage. But this is not followed now as it is dangerous and can lead to aspiration, bleeding & spread of infection .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A patient presents with complaints of pain while swallowing since 2 days. He also gives a history of toothache since 1 week . On examination, there is a swelling and erythema as in the figure below . What is your diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario is suggestive of Ludwig's angina. Ludwig's angina is an infection of the submandibular space which lies between the mucous membrane of the floor of the mouth and tongue on one side and the superficial layer of deep cervical fascia extending between the hyoid bone and mandible on the other.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a false statement about Ludwig's angina?

options.a: It involves both sublingual and submandibular space
options.c: Dental infections are the most common cause
options.d: H.influenza is the most common organism implicated .

mcqs.explanation: Mixed infection with aerobes and anaerobes is seen in Ludwig's angina. Among these alpha-hemolytic streptococci , staphylococci and Bacteroides groups are common. Ludwig's angina is an infection of the submandibular space . The space is divided into two compartments by the mylohyoid muscle : • Sublingual compartment (above the mylohyoid ). • Submandibular and submental compartment (below the mylohyoid ).493 The two compartments are continuous around the posterior border of the mylohyoid muscle . Both compartments freely communicate in the midline with the opposite side . Therefore infection rapidly becomes bilateral. The most common cause of Ludwig's angina is dental infections (accounts for 80%) of cases .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old man presents to the OPD with odynophagia and swelling . He is diagnosed with Ludwig 's angina. How might you describe the swelling ?

options.a: Tender fluctuant swelling in the floor of mouth
options.b: Tender fluctuant swelling in the parotid region
options.c: Woody hard swelling in the floor of mouth
options.d: Woody hard swelling in the parotid region

mcqs.explanation: Ludwig's angina presents as a tender woody hard swelling on the floor of the mouth. There can be marked difficulty in swallowing (odynophagia ) with varying degrees of trismus. The tongue is progressively pushed upwards and backward, threatening the airway. Laryngeal edema may also be present . Usually , there is cellulitis of the tissues rather than frank abscess . Incision and drainage show salted pork appearance .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with multiple comorbidities , post -op day 5 of major abdominal surgery has developed high-grade fever and swelling over the parotid area. On examination, there is tenderness , induration and pus exuding from the Stenson's duct on applying pressure over the parotids. Which of the following options is not a likely cause for the above condition?
mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario is suggestive of a parotid abscess and excessive gland stimulation is not a cause for its formation. Etiology of Parotid Abscess : • Dehydration, particularly in postsurgical cases (5-7 post -op days) and debilitated patients , with stasis of salivary flow is the predisposing cause . • Infection from the oral cavity travels via the Stenson's duct to invade the parotid gland (retrograde spread of infection ). The most common organism is Staphylococcus aureus but Streptococci , anaerobic organisms, and rarely the gram negative organisms have also been cultured .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A patient with a parotid abscess is planned for incision and drainage (I & D). Which of the following practices will you avoid in this patient ?

options.a: Put an incision that is similar to parotidectomy
options.b: Blunt dissection of the pus pockets
options.c: Dissection parallel to the facial nerve branches
options.d: Wait for the swelling to become fluctuant before performing I & D

mcqs.explanation: In a case of a parotid abscess , one must never wait for fluctuation or pus point to occur. This is because the superficial layer of parotidomasseteric fascia is tense and the fluctuation will be apparent only in later stages . A parotid abscess refers to an infection and pus formation in the parotid space . It is caused most commonly by Staphylococcus aureus. Post-surgical cases and debilitated patients with stasis of salivary flow are at risk of developing parotid abscesses . Patients typically present with unilateral swelling , redness , induration, and tenderness over the parotid gland and angle of the mandible. Dehydration and fever are also present . Diagnosis is by ultrasonography or a CT scan. Multiple small loculi of pus are seen in the parenchyma. Aspiration of abscess can be done to determine the culture and sensitivity of the infective agent .494 Correction of dehydration , improving oral hygiene and promoting salivary flow . Intravenous antibiotics are also used in treatment . Surgical drainage under local or general anesthesia is carried out by a preauricular incision as employed for parotidectomy . A skin flap is raised to expose the surface of the gland, and the abscess or abscesses are bluntly opened working parallel to the branches of the VIIth nerve. The skin incision is loosely approximated over a drain and allowed to heal by secondary intention.495

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: What type of lesion is angiofibroma?
mcqs.explanation: Angiofibroma is a histologically benign tumor but locally aggressive . It is a rare tumor, though it is the commonest of all benign tumors of the nasopharynx. Angiofibroma arises from the sphenopalatine foramen. Recurrent spontaneous epistaxis is the most common presentation of angiofibroma.500 The investigation of choice is a CT scan. There is anterior bowing of the maxillary sinus's posterior wall, which is referred to as the Holman-Miller sign/ antral sign. Surgery is the treatment of choice . Radiotherapy is used for tumors with intracranial extension . Chemotherapy is used in combination with surgery or as monotherapy when surgery is contraindicated .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A patient presented with difficulty in breathing and swallowing . On examination, a painless nasopharyngeal mass was noted . Angiofibroma was suspected . Which of the following statements is false about this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a nasopharyngeal mass suggestive of juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma (JNA), which is causing difficulty in breathing and swallowing . It is more common in males. The tumor is predominantly seen in adolescent males in the second decade of life . It is thought to be testosterone dependent . Patients have a hamartomatous nidus of vascular tissue in the nasopharynx which is activated to form angiofibroma when male sex hormones appear. A biopsy is contraindicated due to the risk of severe bleeding . The vessels lack contractile components and hence bleeding cannot be controlled with adrenaline.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old boy presents to you with complaints of nasal obstruction and frequent nose bleeds . CT scan shows Holman-Miller sign. You suspect a benign tumour of the nasopharynx. What is its most common site of origin?

options.c: Anterior wall of the sphenoid bone

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with a CT scan showing the Holman-Miller sign is suggestive of the diagnosis of juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma (JNA). It most commonly arises from the sphenopalatine foramen. From here the tumour grows into the : • Nasal cavity • Nasopharynx • Pterygopalatine fossa • Pterygomaxillary fossa • Infratemporal fossa Given below is CT showing the anterior bowing of the posterior wall of the maxillary sinus- Holman-Miller sign.501

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following features will not be seen in a patient with nasopharyngeal angiofibroma?
mcqs.explanation: Nasopharyngeal angiofibroma presents with rhinolalia clausa (hyponasal speech ), not rhinolalia aperta (hypernasal speech ). The patients present with progressive nasal obstruction and hyponasal speech due to mass in the postnasal space . Profuse, recurrent, and spontaneous epistaxis is the most common presentation . The patients may be markedly anemic due to repeated blood loss. Conductive hearing loss and otitis media with effusion occur due to obstruction of the eustachian tube . It can spread to the orbit giving rise to proptosis and broadening of the nasal bridge , giving rise to frog face deformity . Other features include swelling of the cheek and cranial nerve palsies (II , III , IV , and VI ).

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A mother brought her 16-year-old boy with a unilateral profuse nosebleed . After successful control of bleeding , a CT scan confirmed the diagnosis of juvenile angiofibroma. What is the reason for it to cause excessive bleeding ?
mcqs.explanation: Angiofibroma is made of vascular and fibrous tissues . Vessels of angiofibroma lack contractile components , they are just endothelium -lined spaces with no elastic or muscle coat. This accounts for severe bleeding as the vessels lose the ability to contract. Hence the bleeding cannot be controlled by the application of adrenaline. Therefore, the biopsy is contraindicated .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following deformity is likely to be seen in a patient with juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma?
mcqs.explanation: Nasopharyngeal angiofibroma when spreads to the orbit, lead to proptosis and broadening of the nasal bridge, giving rise to frog-face deformity .502 Option A: Gorilla-like facies are seen in acromegaly. Option C: Bird-like facies are seen in the Pierre-Robin sequence . Option D: Lion -like facies are seen in Paget 's disease of bone when craniofacial bones are involved.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A teenage boy presents to you with recurrent epistaxis and hearing loss. On examination, he has a frog-face deformity and conductive hearing loss. Which of the following is the investigation of choice to diagnose the condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of nasopharyngeal angiofibroma. Investigation of choice to diagnose this condition is contrast enhancement CT scan (CECT). MRI scan can be used complementary to CT to see soft tissue extensions of the tumor. Carotid angiography shows the extent of the tumor, its vascularity, and feeding vessels which mostly come from the external carotid system . Embolization of vessels can be done at this time to decrease bleeding at operation. A biopsy is contraindicated in this condition as it can lead to massive hemorrhage.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: In a suspected case of nasopharyngeal angiofibroma, CECT is performed . Which of the following signs will help diagnose this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Anterior bowing of the posterior wall of the maxillary sinus in CECT of head and neck is called an antral sign or Holman-Miller sign, which is pathognomonic for angiofibroma.Option A: Tram track sign is used to differentiate optic nerve sheath meningiomas from optic gliomas. Optic nerve sheath meningiomas will show a positive tram-track sign. Option C: Stripe sign/ tigroid pattern represents a specific pattern of demyelination , with sparing of perivascular white matter. It is seen in metachromatic leukodystrophy (MLD).503 Option D: Eye -of-a-tiger sign represents marked low signal intensity of the globi pallidi on T2W MRI images.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Imaging of a patient with recurrent epistaxis shows the following finding. Which of the following statements is false about his condition?

options.b: Tumor does not have a capsule
options.c: Digital palpation should never be done in OPD

mcqs.explanation: The image shows anterior bowing of the posterior wall of the maxillary sinus, which is called an antral sign or Holman-Miller sign. It is pathognomonic for angiofibroma. Recurrence of juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma is common. It is a rare tumor but is the commonest benign tumor of the nasopharynx. It commonly arises from the sphenopalatine foramen. It does not have a capsule . Digital palpation should never be done until at the time of operation, as it can lead to severe hemorrhage.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A teenager has a mass in his nasopharynx that has minimally spread into the sphenoid sinus with no lateral extension . Which stage of nasopharyngeal angiofibroma could this be?
mcqs.explanation: The mass has spread into the sphenoid sinus with no lateral extension , so it's Stage 1B according to the Radkowski classification . Multiple classification systems exist for the staging of juvenile nasal angiofibroma, of which the most commonly used ones are the Fisch and Radkowski classification systems : Staging of juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma (Radkowski, et al): Fisch staging system of juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma (JNA) is a highly vascular and locally aggressive tumor seen almost exclusively in adolescent males, associated with significant morbidity and occasional mortality. Note : The Fisch system is considered to be the more robust and practical of the two .Stag e Spread IA Limited to the nose and/or na sopharyngeal vault IB Extension into \034 1 sinus IIA Minimal extension into the p terygopalatine fossa IIB Full occupation of pterygopal atine fossa with or without er osion of orbital bones IIC Infratemporal fossa with or without cheek or posterior to pterygoid plates504 Stag e Spread IIIA Erosion of skull base-minima l intracranial IIIB Erosion of skull base-extensi ve intracranial with or witho ut cavernous sinusType Details Tumourlimited to the nasoph aryngeal cavity; bonedestruct ion negligibleor limited to th e sphenopalatine foramen Tumourinvading the pterygo palatine fossaor the maxillary, ethmoid , or sphenoidsinus w ith bone destruction A:Tumour invading theinfrat emporal fossaororbital region withoutintracranial involvem ent B:Tumour invading theinfrat emporal fossaororbital region withintracranialextradural(pa rasellar) involvement A:Intracranialintraduraltumo rwithoutinfiltration of the ca vernous sinus, pituitary fossa, or optic chiasm B:Intracranialintraduraltumo rwithinfiltration of the caver nous sinus, pituitary fossa, or optic chiasm

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A young boy with a history of frequent nosebleeds and unilateral nasal blockage . CT scan shows Holman- Miller sign. It also shows the presence of a mass in the nasopharynx that extends into and occupies the pterygopalatine fossa. What is the best treatment for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical picture suggests that of stage IIB nasopharyngeal angiofibroma. Surgery is the mainstay of treatment of angiofibroma for stage I and stage II tumors. Radiotherapy is indicated in stage III where there is an intracranial extension or when the tumor is unresectable. Chemotherapy can be used for very aggressive resurrect tumors and residual lesions . Stages of nasopharyngeal angiofibroma: Hormonal therapy was used in the past, but not anymore.505 Stag e Spread IA Limited to the nose and/or na sopharyngeal vault IB Extension into \034 1 sinus IIA Minimal extension into the p terygopalatine fossa IIB Full occupation of pterygopal atine fossa with or without er osion of orbital bones IIC Infratemporal fossa with or without cheek or posterior to pterygoid plates IIIA Erosion of skull base-minima l intracranial IIIB Erosion of skull base-extensi ve intracranial with or witho ut cavernous sinus

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Radiotherapy is indicated when the spread of angiofibroma extends to which site ?
mcqs.explanation: Radiotherapy is used for intracranial extension of disease when tumour derives its blood supply from the internal carotid system . Recurrent angiofibromas have also been treated by radiotherapy.506

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following viruses is related to etiology of nasopharyngeal carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: Epstein –Barr Virus (EBV) is closely associated with nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC). EBV antigens are currently being used to screen high-risk populations . The antigens being used are • Viral capsid antigen (VCA) - highly sensitive for NPC • Early antigen (EA) - highly specific for NPC.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: What is nasopharyngeal carcinoma also known as?
mcqs.explanation: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is also known as Guangdong tumor. This is because the Southern Chinese province of Guangdong has the highest prevalence of the tumor. Chinese , especially from southeastern China (Canton), have a higher genetic susceptibility to nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC). Chinese emigrants are also genetically more susceptible , however, the susceptibility falls in subsequent generations . Other South-East Asian countries such as Indonesia, Malaysia, and people of Mongoloid origin are also more susceptible .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not associated with a high incidence of nasopharyngeal carcinoma in high-risk populations of China?
mcqs.explanation: Human papillomavirus is not associated with a high incidence of nasopharyngeal carcinoma in high-risk populations of China. EBV (Epstein Barr virus) causes nasopharyngeal carcinoma . HPV (Human papillomavirus) causes inverted papilloma of the nose. High-risk populations such as the Chinese have a very high incidence of nasopharyngeal carcinoma . The following factors have been implicated in the pathogenesis : • Burning of incense or wood (polycyclic hydrocarbons) • Consumption of preserved salted fish (nitrosamines) • Vitamin C deficient diet (vitamin C blocks nitrosification of amines and is thus protective )511

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A patient with a family history of nasopharyngeal carcinoma presents with nasal discharge and a painless lump in the upper neck. On posterior rhinoscopy, where will you most commonly expect to find a mass originating from?
mcqs.explanation: The most common site of origin for nasopharyngeal carcinoma is the fossa of Rosenm\374ller.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: What is the most common presenting feature of nasopharyngeal carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: Painless cervical lymphadenopathy is the most common (60-90%) presenting feature of nasopharyngeal carcinoma followed by- • Hearing loss • Nasal obstruction • Epistaxis • Cranial nerve palsies -Cranial nerves V and VI are the most commonly involved among all the cranial nerves. • Headache • Earache • Neck pain • Weight loss

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A housewife from rural Tripura with a past history of infectious mononucleosis presents with complaints of double vision and a neck swelling that has progressively increased in size. She also gives a history of nasal discharge and is annoyed that her husband is recently complaining of a change in her voice. What is the most likely speech pattern observed here?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario of exposure to EBV, progressive cervical lymphadenopathy , nasal discharge, diplopia (involvement of cranial nerve VI ), and change in voice is suggestive of nasopharyngeal carcinoma . The most likely speech pattern, in this case, is rhinolalia clausa or denasal speech , due to obstruction of the nasopharynx by the tumor.512 Rhinolalia clausa is the lack of nasal resonance for words resonated in the nasal cavity and is usually seen due to blockage of nose or nasopharynx Other nasal symptoms of nasopharyngeal carcinoma are: • Nasal obstruction • Nasal discharge • Epistaxis Option B- Rhinolalia aperta (hypernasal voice) is seen in Velopharyngeal insufficiency . Option C- Puberphonia is the persistence of prepubertal voice into adolescence or adulthood . Option D- Muffled and thick speech , often called "hot potato voice" is seen in peritonsillar abscess or quinsy.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old Chinese woman presents with left -sided cervical lymphadenopathy , nasal obstruction, and left -sided hearing loss. What is the most likely cause for hearing loss in this case?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of nasopharyngeal carcinoma . Hearing loss, in this case, is due to serous otitis media. Serous otitis media is caused due to mechanical obstruction of the Eustachian tube by the tumor. The presence of unilateral serous otitis media in an adult should raise suspicion of nasopharyngeal growth .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: You have sent a patient with nasopharyngeal carcinoma and hearing loss for tympanometry . Which of the following tympanometry curves do you expect to find?
mcqs.explanation: Type B tympanometry curve is expected in nasopharyngeal carcinoma . Due to mechanical obstruction of the Eustachian tube by the tumor, serous otitis media occurs, causing conductive hearing loss.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: You are an ENT resident on a clinical elective in Guangzhou. You receive a patient with painless cervical lymphadenopathy , conductive hearing loss, palatal asymmetry, and facial pain. Which of the following do you see here?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Trotter's triad/Sinus of Morgagni syndrome/Trotter's syndrome seen in nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Trotter's triad consists of: • Conductive hearing loss due to Eustachian tube obstruction. • Ipsilateral temporoparietal neuralgia due to involvement of mandibular branch of the trigeminal nerve (CN V ) which presents as facial pain. • Palatal paralysis due to involvement of vagus nerve(CN X) which presents as palatal asymmetry. Option A - Samter's triad seen in ethmoidal polyps consists of nasal polypi , asthma, and Aspirin intolerance513 Option C - van der Hoeve syndrome is seen in otosclerosis consists of osteogenesis imperfecta , otosclerosis , and blue sclera Option D - Kartagener syndrome consists of bronchiectasis , sinusitis, situs inversus, and ciliary dyskinesia.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following branches of the trigeminal nerve is involved in Trotter's triad?
mcqs.explanation: The mandibular branch of the trigeminal nerve is involved in Trotter's triad. Trotter's triad seen in nasopharyngeal carcinoma . It consists of: • Conductive hearing loss due to Eustachian tube obstruction. • Ipsilateral temporoparietal neuralgia due to involvement of mandibular branch of the trigeminal nerve (CN V ) which presents as facial pain. • Palatal paralysis due to involvement of vagus nerve(CN X) which presents as palatal asymmetry.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A known case of right-sided nasopharyngeal carcinoma now presents with drooping of eyelids , reduced sweating on the right side of the face , and constricted pupil . Involvement of which of the following structures leads to these features ?
mcqs.explanation: Involvement of the sympathetic chain causes these features . The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Horner's syndrome secondary to nasopharyngeal carcinoma involving the cervical sympathetic chain. Horner's syndrome consists of ptosis , miosis, and ipsilateral anhydrosis. Option B - Cranial nerve V (Trigeminal nerve) involvement presents as ipsilateral temporoparietal neuralgia. Option C - Cranial nerve VI (Abducens nerve) involvement causes ophthalmoplegia Option D - Jugular foramen involvement causes paralysis of cranial nerves IX, X, and XI, causing jugular foramen syndrome, also seen in acoustic neuroma and glomus jugulare .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following WHO categories does differentiated non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma of the nasopharynx belong to?
mcqs.explanation: Differentiated non-keratinized squamous cell carcinoma is categorized as Type 2. WHO Classification based on Histopathology : Note - The latest WHO classification has combined types 2 and 3 into one category : Non-keratinizing Squamous cell carcinoma which is further subclassified into differentiated and non-differentiated types .Type Histopathological category Type I Keratinizing Squamous cell c arcinoma (SCC)514 Type Histopathological category Type II Non-keratinizing Squamous c ell carcinomaBasaloid squamous cell carcinoma is a rare subtype of epithelial cancer seen in the nasopharyngeal area. It was included alongside the above classification from 2005 . It is known for its aggressive clinical progression and poor chances of survival .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A patient with persistent cervical lymphadenopathy now came with spontaneous epistaxis . Nasal endoscopy showed a mass arising from the fossa of Rosenmuller. Biopsy from the mass revealed a keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma . What is the treatment of choice in this case?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of nasopharyngeal carcinoma . The treatment of choice is radiotherapy. Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is extremely radiosensitive, hence treatment of local and regional disease is invariably radiotherapy. Stage I and II are treated by radiotherapy alone. Stage III and IV are treated with radiotherapy and chemotherapy . Chemotherapy can be neoadjuvant, concurrent, or adjuvant to radiotherapy.515

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: At what level does the adult larynx end?
mcqs.explanation: In adults , the larynx ends at lower border of C6. It extends from C3 to C6 vertebra.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: What is the average final anteroposterior diameter of glottis in women?
mcqs.explanation: The average anteroposterior diameter of the glottis is 26mm in women and 36 mm in men. Glottis , also known as rima glottidis , is the narrowest part of the laryngeal cavity. It is formed by: • Anterior 2/3rd by membranous cords • Posterior 1/3rd by vocal processes of arytenoids .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: What is the primary function of the larynx?
mcqs.explanation: The primary function of the larynx is to protect the airway from ingested food and aspirated materials. This is done by the sphincteric action of the larynx. Other important functions are: • Respiration • Phonation • Building up of intra-thoracic pressure.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: The presence of which structure is responsible for infants to be able to breathe simultaneously while suckling milk?
mcqs.explanation: The high position of the larynx in infants allows simultaneous breathing while feeding .522 The infant's larynx is positioned high in the neck, level of the glottis being opposite to C3 or C4 at rest and reaches C1 or C2 during swallowing . The high position allows the epiglottis to meet the soft palate and make a nasopharyngeal channel for nasal breathing during suckling. The milk feed passes separately over the dorsum of the tongue and sides of the epiglottis , thus allowing breathing and feeding to go on simultaneously .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which embryological structure develops into the epiglottis ?
mcqs.explanation: The epiglottis develops from the hypobranchial eminence which is a part of the 4th arch.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following comprises the larynx?
mcqs.explanation: The larynx has 3 unpaired and 3 paired cartilages . Unpaired : • Thyroid • Cricoid • Epiglottis Paired: • Arytenoid • Corniculate • Cuneiform.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: The lateral x-ray of an elderly man shows calcification of the laryngeal cartilages . Which of the following is unlikely to be involved?
mcqs.explanation: Epiglottis is unlikely to be calcified as it is made up of elastic cartilage . Only hyaline cartilages can undergo ossification (calcifications on x-ray). It occurs between the ages of 25-65y. These calcifications may be confused with foreign bodies of esophagus or larynx on x-rays. The hyaline laryngeal cartilages are: • Thyroid • Cricoid • Most of arytenoid. The elastic laryngeal cartilages are: • Epiglottis • Corniculate523 • Cuneiform • Tip of arytenoid.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following cartilage has a signet ring shape ?
mcqs.explanation: Cricoid cartilage resembles a signet ring. It has a wide posterior lamina and a thin anterior arch.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: The skeletal remains of a person were found in a nearby forest . The thyroid cartilage was identified and the thyroid angle measures 90 degrees . The deceased person can be deemed as a
mcqs.explanation: The thyroid angle measures 90 degrees (right-angled ) in men. It is the angle between the two thyroid lamina in the midline. It depends on gender : • Men: 90 degrees (forms the prominent adam's apple ) • Women: 120 degrees .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is called cartilage of Santorini ?
mcqs.explanation: Corniculate cartilage is also known as the cartilage of Santorini . Cuneiform cartilage is also known as the cartilage of Wrisberg.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: An ENT surgeon is operating on the larynx of a patient and he approaches the arytenoid cartilage. Which of the following is false regarding the attachments of the arytenoid cartilage ?
mcqs.explanation: The apex of the arytenoid supports the corniculate cartilages .524 The following are the attachments of the arytenoid: • Base - cricoid • Vocal process - vocal ligament • Muscular process - intrinsic muscles of larynx • Apex - corniculate cartilages .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not involved in the closure of glottis ?
mcqs.explanation: The posterior cricoarytenoid opens the glottis as it is the only abductor of the vocal cord. All other muscles close the glottis .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: An opera singer presents with difficulty raising the pitch of her voice while singing. Which of the following muscles is likely to be affected ?
mcqs.explanation: Cricothyroid is likely to be affected . Cricothyroid and vocalis (internal part of thyroarytenoid ) are the tensors of the vocal cord which help in raising the pitch of the voice. The external laryngeal nerve is the smaller, external branch. It descends on the larynx, beneath the sternothyroid muscle , to supply the cricothyroid muscle . The external branch functions to tense the vocal cords by activating the cricothyroid muscle , and increasing pitch .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: You are the ENT resident examining a patient in the wards. On asking him to swallow you notice the larynx moves upwards . Which of the following muscles is not responsible for this movement?
mcqs.explanation: The sternohyoid is not responsible for upward movement (elevation). It is a depressor of the larynx . The extrinsic muscles of the larynx can be elevators or depressors . Elevators: Primary elevators act directly as they are attached to the thyroid cartilage and include • Stylopharyngeus • Salpingopharyngeus • Palatopharyngeus • Thyrohyoid Secondary elevators act indirectly as they are attached to the hyoid bone and include • Mylohyoid (main) • Digastric • Stylohyoid525 • Geniohyoid Depressors : • Sternohyoid • Sternothyroid • Omohyoid Easy to remember: Check the other attachment (non-laryngeal side ). If it's above the level of the hyoid, the muscle is an elevator. If it's below the level of the hyoid, it's a depressor .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an intrinsic membrane of the larynx?
mcqs.explanation: The cricothyroid membrane is an intrinsic membrane of the larynx as it connects laryngeal structures to each other. Extrinsic membranes and ligaments connect laryngeal structures with surrounding structures outside the laryngeal framework like the trachea or hyoid. These are: • Cricotracheal membrane • Thyrohyoid membrane • Hyoepiglottic ligament . Intrinsic membranes and ligaments connect laryngeal structures with each other. These are: • Cricovocal membrane • Quadrangular membrane • Cricothyroid ligament • Thyroepiglottic ligament .[Image unavailable] [Image unavailable] [Image unavailable]

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Following a road traffic accident , a 30-year-old man presents to the emergency department with maxillofacial trauma and inability to open the mouth. To establish an airway, an emergency laryngotomy is performed . Where is the opening made?
mcqs.explanation: In laryngotomy, an opening is made on the cricothyroid membrane. Laryngotomy is also called cricothyrotomy or mini-tracheostomy. It is done as an emergency life -saving procedure to buy some time to allow a patient to be carried to the operation theatre . Once stable , it is replaced by intubation or tracheostomy . Most of the laryngeal foreign bodies are arrested above the vocal cords, i.e. above the middle of the thyroid cartilage . Thus, an effective airway can be provided by piercing the cricothyroid membrane.526

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not seen as part of the larynx?
mcqs.explanation: Labyrinth is seen in inner ear and not in larynx. The 2 mucosal folds within the larynx divide the larynx into 3 cavities: • Vestibule : Above the false /vestibular folds • Ventricle: Between the vestibular and vocal/true folds • Subglottis : Below the true folds Saccule an extension of ventricle is present in the paraglottic space .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A surgeon is worried about the spread of laryngeal carcinoma to the pre-epiglottic space . Which of the following structures do not border this space ?
mcqs.explanation: Suprahyoid epiglottis does not form a boundary of the pre-epiglottic space . The infrahyoid epiglottis forms the posteromedial border. Two potential spaces within the larynx provide an avenue for the spread of tumors: • Pre-epiglottic space • Paraglottic space . The pre-epiglottic space is bounded : • Superiorly by the hyoepiglottic ligament • Anteriorly by the thyroid and thyrohyoid membrane • Posteromedially by the infrahyoid epiglottis and quadrangular membrane. The paraglottic space is bounded : • Laterally by thyroid • Medially by ventricle and quadrangular membrane527 • Inferomedially by conus elasticus • Posteriorly by pyriform sinus.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old smoker presents with hoarseness of voice. On laryngoscopy , there is edema of the Reinke's space . Where is this space located ?
mcqs.explanation: Reinke's space is seen in the glottis . It is a potential space underneath the epithelium of vocal cords. It contains scanty subepithelial connective tissue . Edema of this space is commonly seen in smokers and is called Reinke's edema or smoker's larynx. The laryngoscopy image below shows diffuse bilateral edema of the vocal folds or Reinke's edema .528

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: You are performing a direct laryngoscopy procedure to enter the larynx and visualise the structures it contains. Which of the following structures form the inlet of the larynx?
mcqs.explanation: Aryepiglottic folds form the inlet of the larynx. The laryngeal inlet is an oblique opening with the following boundaries: • Anterior: Free margin of the epiglottis • Posterior: Interarytenoid fold • Sides : Aryepiglottic folds .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following muscle causes opening of laryngeal inlet?
mcqs.explanation: Thyroepiglotticus causes the opening of the laryngeal inlet. The intrinsic muscles of the larynx acting on the laryngeal inlet are: • Openers of laryngeal inlet • Thyroepiglottic • Closers of laryngeal inlet • Interarytenoid (oblique part). • Aryepiglottic (posterior oblique part of interarytenoids ).529

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Stridor and Congenital Conditions of Larynx
mcqs.question: Inspiratory stridor is found in what kind of lesions :
mcqs.explanation: Inspiratory stridor is seen in supraglottic lesions . It is often produced in obstructive lesions of supraglottis or pharynx, e.g. laryngomalacia or retropharyngeal abscess .534 Expiratory stridor is produced in lesions of thoracic trachea, primary and secondary bronchi such as bronchial foreign body, and tracheal stenosis . Biphasic stridor is seen in lesions of glottis , subglottis , and cervical trachea like laryngeal papillomas, vocal cord paralysis, and subglottic stenosis . Stridor is an audible respiratory noise that gets produced by turbulent airflow through an obstructed upper airway. It is an inspiratory sound that may have an expiratory component . It is distinct from stertor which is a snoring-like noise produced from an obstructed nasopharynx or oropharynx. The intensity and pitch of sounds originating from the respiratory system vary based on their site of origin within the respiratory tract and may be heard with or without a stethoscope . Usually, the pitch of the sound increases, and the intensity decreases as one goes lower into the respiratory tract.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Stridor and Congenital Conditions of Larynx
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of congenital stridor?
mcqs.explanation: Laryngomalacia is the most common congenital cause of stridor. It is characterized by excessive flaccidity of the supraglottic larynx which is sucked in during inspiration producing stridor and sometimes cyanosis. It presents just after birth and subsides by 2 years of age . Stridor improves (decreases ) in the prone position, worsens during feeding . The cry is normal . On examination, omega-shaped epiglottis is seen .535

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Stridor and Congenital Conditions of Larynx
mcqs.question: What is congenital laryngeal stridor also known as?
mcqs.explanation: Laryngomalacia is also called congenital laryngeal stridor. It is the most common cause of stridor in newborns.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Stridor and Congenital Conditions of Larynx
mcqs.question: A 1-week old infant has been diagnosed to have laryngomalacia. Which of the following statements is false about this condition?

options.a: Most common cause of stridor in newborn

mcqs.explanation: Laryngomalacia has an excellent prognosis. Laryngomalacia is the most common cause of stridor in newborns. It presents just after birth and subsides by 2 years of age . Stridor improves (decreases ) in the prone position, worsens during feeding . The cry is normal . On examination, omega-shaped epiglottis is seen

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Stridor and Congenital Conditions of Larynx
mcqs.question: A worried mother brings her 2-week old infant to you with complaints of noisy breathing that worsens during feeding . On direct laryngoscopy , the following is seen . What is the preferred treatment for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical picture and omega-shaped epiglottis are suggestive of laryngomalacia. Conservative treatment is preferred for laryngomalacia as this condition self -corrects by two years of age . Tracheostomy may be required for some cases of severe respiratory obstruction. Supraglottoplasty is required in severe laryngomalacia. Signs of severe laryngomalacia include : • Difficulty feeding • Increased effort in breathing • Poor weight gain • Pauses in the breathing536 • Frequent spitting up

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Stridor and Congenital Conditions of Larynx
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old child is brought to you with complaints of noisy breathing. On performing direct laryngoscopy , subglottic stenosis is noted . Which grading system will you use to report the extent of the stenosis ?
mcqs.explanation: Myer Cotton's grading is used for subglottic stenosis . It is the abnormal thickening of cricoid/fibrous tissue proliferation below cords. It causes the airway to narrow and presents with dyspnea , biphasic stridor and a normal cry. Diagnosis: • In full -term infants, subglottic diameter <4mm. • In premature infants, subglottic diameter <3mm. The Myer Cotton's grading system allows to stratify the stenosis and plan for treatment : • Grade 1: <50% stenosis • Grade 2: 51-70% stenosis • Grade 3: 71-99% stenosis • Grade 4: No lumen detected Other options • Option A - Hyams grading is a predictive tool used in olfactory neuroblastoma. • Option B - House Brackmann grading is used as a facial nerve grading system . • Option D - Modified mallampati classification is used to assess difficult airway

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Stridor and Congenital Conditions of Larynx
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man presents to the ENT OPD with a swelling on the right side of his neck. The swelling moves with deglutition . On examination, the swelling is compressible and there is a gurgling sound heard on compression. What is his diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: On compressing the swelling , there is a gurgling /hissing sound known as Bryce's sign. The given clinical picture with a positive Bryce sign is suggestive of laryngocele . Laryngocele is an air-filled cavity within the larynx developing from the saccule . The patient presents with a neck swelling that is soft and compressible . Options A: Branchial cleft cysts does not move with deglutition . Option C: Cystic hygroma does not move with deglutition and usually presents before 2 years. Option D: Thyroglossal cyst presents as a midline swelling .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Stridor and Congenital Conditions of Larynx
mcqs.question: You are the ENT resident performing a direct laryngoscopy procedure on a patient and report the presence of a laryngocele . The given condition is due to an enlarged diverticulum from which part of the larynx?
mcqs.explanation: Laryngocele arises from the saccule of the ventricle. It is an abnormal dilation of the laryngeal saccule and extends beyond the thyroid cartilage and the ventricle.537 It is seen in trumpet players , glass -blowers , or weight lifters due to raised transglottic air pressure . It can be internal, external, or combined. External laryngocele presents as a reducible swelling in the neck which increases in size on coughing or performing Valsalva maneuver. Internal laryngocele is managed by marsupialization. External laryngocele is managed by excision (external/LASER).

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Stridor and Congenital Conditions of Larynx
mcqs.question: A mother brings her 4-month-old infant to the ENT department with complaints of difficulty in breathing. On examination, you notice biphasic stridor. Rigid bronchoscopy shows subglottic hemangioma. Which of the following is not included in the treatment of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture is of congenital subglottic hemangioma. Embolization is not preferred in congenital laryngeal conditions. All congenital laryngeal conditions tend to regress with growth . The principal management is conservative as many hemangiomas involute spontaneously . Depending on the status of the airway, treatment can involve: • To wait and watch • Steroid therapy • Tracheostomy and observation If the condition does not regress with time, the modalities of treatment include : • LASER excision • Laryngofissure and excision • -pexy and -plasty procedures (epiglottopexy , supraglottoplasty , etc )

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Stridor and Congenital Conditions of Larynx
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old singer complains of a change in her voice. Direct laryngoscopy procedure shows the presence of laryngeal cysts . Which part of the larynx does the cyst arise from?
mcqs.explanation: Laryngeal cysts arise in the aryepiglottic folds .538 These are benign conditions that need no intervention unless they are large. Large cysts can cause airway obstruction/change in voice. These require immediate aspiration followed by deroofing .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Stridor and Congenital Conditions of Larynx
mcqs.question: Identify the lesion of vocal cord in the image given below :
mcqs.explanation: The image showing grape-like projections, involving the anterior part of the vocal cords depicts a laryngeal papilloma . Laryngeal papilloma is a benign tumor of the larynx caused by the human papillomavirus (HPV type 6 and 11 ). They can occur in children, most commonly around 3 -5 years of age (juvenile papillomatosis ), as well as in adults . They involve the supraglottic and glottic regions of the larynx. Seeding of the lesions can occur during invasive laryngeal procedures , such as intubation. They have a high recurrence rate and very low potential for malignancy. Adult -onset laryngeal papillomatosis is less common and usually seen in males aged 30-50 years. It is less aggressive and involves the anterior part of the vocal cords. The treatment is the same as juvenile papillomatosis . Patients present with hoarseness , aphonia, dyspnea , or stridor. Laryngoscopy shows pinkish to white grape-like projections that can be sessile or pedunculate with a visible central vascular core. The diagnosis is confirmed by direct laryngoscopy and biopsy . Treatment consists of micro-laryngoscopy and CO2 laser excision. The image below depicts laryngeal papillomatosis on laryngoscopy :Reinke's edema (Option A) is a collection of fluid in the subepithelial space of Reinke. It generally occurs in patients with vocal abuse or smoking. The vocal cords will show diffuse , symmetrical swelling . The laryngoscopic image below shows Reinke's edema :539

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Stridor and Congenital Conditions of Larynx
mcqs.question: A 5 year old with gradually progressive hoarseness of voice over three months and respiratory distress for 2 weeks . Diagnosis is
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of a child presenting with chronic hoarseness (3 months) of voice and respiratory distress for 2 weeks suggests the diagnosis of respiratory papillomatosis (juvenile papillomatosis ). Croup (Option A) and acute epiglottitis (Option D), which cause acute upper respiratory tract obstruction, are ruled out due to the chronic nature of the symptoms . In croup, the upper airway obstruction becomes apparent after 1 to 3 days of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea , and pharyngitis. On the other hand, in epiglottitis , a child experiences respiratory distress within hours of developing a fever. Vocal nodules (Option C) are not typically associated with respiratory distress . Respiratory papillomatosis is the most common respiratory tract neoplasm in children. They are simple warts (benign tumors) caused by human papillomavirus types 6 and 11 commonly seen in children aged 3 to 5 years. The course involves remissions and exacerbations of recurrent papillomas , mostly affecting the glottic area (vocal cords), and supraglottis . The patient presents with progressively worsening hoarseness , sleep -disordered breathing, dyspnea , stridor, and severe airway obstruction if left untreated . Diagnosis confirmed by direct laryngoscopy , which shows grape-like projections (shown below ), and biopsy . Treatment consists of micro laryngoscopy and CO2 laser excision. Antivirals like interferon alpha2a, ribavirin , cidofovir, and acyclovir are used as adjunct therapies .540 Other options : Option A: Croup (laryngotracheobronchitis) is caused by the parainfluenza virus. The patient initially presents with an upper respiratory tract infection (rhinorrhea , pharyngitis, cough , low-grade fever) followed by a characteristic barking cough , hoarseness , and inspiratory stridor. Option C: Vocal nodule (singer's or screamer's nodule ) occurs as a result of chronic vocal abuse . They appear symmetrically at the junction of the anterior one-third and posterior two third of the vocal cord. The patient presents with chronic hoarseness and voice fatigue . The image below shows symmetric vocal nodules :Option D: Acute epiglottitis is caused by streptococcus pyogenes , pneumococci , Hemophilus influenzae , and staphylococcus aureus. It is characterized by an acute rapidly progressive course of high-grade fever, dyspnea , and stridor.541

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following voice changes is seen in dysphonia plica ventricularis?

options.a: High pitched voice in adolescent boys
options.b: Hoarseness due to plication of epiglottis
options.c: Low pitched voice due to use of vestibular folds
options.d: Weak fatiguable voice in TB larynx

mcqs.explanation: Dysphonia plica ventricularis is a low-pitched voice produced by the vestibular folds . It can either be due to functional voice misuse or due to organic lesions like fixation of the true vocal cord. It is characterized by a low-pitched , rough and strained voice. Treatment includes voice therapy and psychological counseling .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about spasmodic dysphonia ?

options.b: May be associated with other dystonias
options.c: Abductor type produces breathy voice and adductor type produces strangulated voice
options.d: Botulinum toxin is used in treatment

mcqs.explanation: Spasmodic dysphonia is not only a local laryngeal disorder. It is associated with many neurological conditions too. There are 2 types of spasmodic dysphonia : Adductor dysphonia • The adductor muscles of the larynx go into spasm causing vocal cords to go into adduction . The voice becomes strained/strangled . • Treatment consists of botulinum toxin injections in the thyroarytenoid muscles on one or both sides to relieve the spasm. Abductor dysphonia • It is due to the spasm of the posterior cricoarytenoid muscle and thus the glottis is kept open . • The patient gets a breathy voice or breathy breaks in voice. Treatment consists of botulinum toxin injections in posterior cricoarytenoid muscles . Patients who do not respond to toxin injection can be treated by type 1 thyroplasty or fat injection.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 17-year-old girl is brought to the ENT OPD by her father who says his daughter has lost her ability to speak following the death of her mother. Her comprehension is normal but she is mute . Which of the following statements is false about her condition?

options.b: Vocal cords fail to adduct on phonation but adduct during coughing
options.c: Aphonia is sudden and unaccompanied by laryngeal symptoms
options.d: Treatment includes reassurance of this patient

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture represents that of functional aphonia. In this condition, vocal cords are normal. Functional aphonia or hysterical aphonia is mostly seen in emotionally labile females in the age group of 15-30 years. Aphonia is usually sudden and unaccompanied by other laryngeal symptoms . Treatment is to reassure the patient of normal laryngeal function and psychotherapy .549

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old boy complains of being bullied in school for his high-pitched voice. A Gutzmann's pressure test is done which helps you to diagnose his condition. What condition does he have?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with a positive Gutzmann's pressure test is suggestive of puberphonia . It is a condition seen in emotionally labile adolescent males. They continue to speak in the prepubertal high pitched voice. Gutzmann's pressure test is positive when pressing the thyroid prominence in a backward and downward direction relaxes the overstretched cords and produces a low tone voice. The treatment is speech therapy .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old teacher comes to you with complaints of dryness , tightness , and soreness in the throat. He says these symptoms appear after long hours of talking in class. He is also unable to hold long conversations. On direct laryngoscopy , the following is seen . What is his possible diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Phonasthenia is the condition seen in this patient . The clinical scenario of voice overuse and keyhole appearance of glottis point to this diagnosis. Here, both thyroarytenoid and inter arytenoid muscles are involved. Phonasthenia is the weakness of voice due to fatigue of laryngeal muscles . This leads to a phonatory gap. The shape of the gap depends on the muscle involved: • Thyroarytenoid alone: elliptical space • Interarytenoid alone: triangular space • Both thyroarytenoid and interarytenoid: keyhole appearance

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: You perform a direct laryngoscopy procedure on a patient and notice a pseudosulcus in the larynx . What is this condition due to?
