Option B: Hemolytic uremic syndrome is characterized by a triad of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia , and acute kidney injury. Option C: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA ) is characterized by fever of at least 2 weeks duration associated with arthritis, evanescent erythematous rash, hepatosplenomegaly , generalized lymphadenopathy , and serositis . Option D: Patients with IgA nephropathy or Berger's disease present with gross hematuria, often associated with a preceding or ongoing viral infection of the upper respiratory tract (synpharyngitic presentation ).

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Cryoglobulinemia is associated with _______.
mcqs.explanation: Cryoglobulinemia is associated with hepatitis C infection .471 Following Hepatitis C infection , there is an aberrant immune response leading to an immune complex formation containing hepatitis C antigens, polyclonal IgG specific to Hepatitis C, and monoclonal IgM rheumatoid factor, which triggers an inflammatory cascade results in Cryoglobulinemic vasculitis. Cryoglobulins are the immunoglobulins that precipitate at temperatures less than 37\260C, the presence of these cryoglobulins in serum leads to Cryoglobulinemia , which is characterized by cutaneous vasculitis, palpable purpura, arthritis, peripheral neuropathy , and glomerulonephritis . Important conditions associated with cryoglobulinemia are: • Hepatitis C • Multiple myeloma • Connective tissue disorders • Lymphoproliferative disorders472

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient receiving anti-tubercular therapy has been recently diagnosed with gout . Which of the following statements is incorrect about this condition?

options.d: Most commonly involves the first MTP joint

mcqs.explanation: In gout , the crystals are negatively birefringent on polarized light microscopy of the joint aspirate. Gout is a metabolic disease that is characterized by the deposition of monosodium urate crystals in joints and connective tissue . It is more common in males. It usually presents as monoarthritis that may be acute and episodic or chronic. Acute gout presents with a joint that is red, hot, swollen , and extremely tender on examination. The metatarsophalangeal joint of the great toe is the most frequently involved joint. Synovial fluid analysis of joint aspirate is diagnostic and shows the following features : • Increased leukocyte count with a neutrophilic predominance • Negatively birefringent crystals on polarized light microscopy of the synovial fluid Antitubercular drugs like pyrazinamide and ethambutol cause hyperuricemia by inhibiting uric acid excretion in the kidney. Monosodium urate crystals as seen on polarized light microscopy:477

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: An elderly man presented to the OPD with painful swelling of his left big toe . Synovial fluid examination showed negatively birefringent needle -shaped crystals. What are these crystals made of?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical presentation and polarised microscopy showing negatively birefringent needle -shaped crystals point towards a diagnosis of gout . In gout , the negatively birefringent needle -shaped crystals are due to the deposition of monosodium urate crystals. Monosodium urate crystals in gout :Option A: Calcium apatite crystals can accumulate in areas of tissue damage , hypercalcemia, or hyperparathyroid states . Option C: Calcium pyrophosphate crystals are positively birefringent rhomboid-shaped crystals that are seen in pseudogout . Calcium pyrophosphate crystals seen in pseudogout :478 Option D: Ammonium urate crystals can cause urinary bladder stones which are radiolucent but may develop a calcific coating making it visible on X-rays.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following synovial fluid crystals cannot be identified using polarized light microscopy ?
mcqs.explanation: Calcium apatite crystals cannot be identified using polarized light microscopy. Polarized light microscopy can identify crystals such as: • Monosodium urate • Calcium pyrophosphate • Calcium oxalate

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient has a history of multiple episodes of painful swelling of ankles and big toes which is relieved with NSAIDs. You would avoid all of the following drugs in her except :
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of multiple painful swelling of ankles and toes that responded to NSAIDs is suggestive of gout . High-dose salicylates (>3g/day) do not precipitate gout . Although high-dose salicylates inhibit both the secretion and reabsorption of urate, the inhibition of reabsorption is more than the inhibition of secretion , and therefore the net effect is uricosuric. On the other hand, low-dose salicylates (<2 to 3g/day) are associated with uric acid retention . They inhibit renal tubular secretion of uric acid resulting in hyperuricemia and may precipitate gout . Aspirin is not used to treat acute attacks of gout due to its uric acid retention property . However, low-dose aspirin used for cardiovascular prophylaxis need not be discontinued during the treatment of a gout flare.479

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient with chronic gout now presented to the emergency room after sustaining trauma to his left foot. Identify the abnormality in his X-ray given below .
mcqs.explanation: The given X-ray of a patient with chronic gout shows Martel 's sign. Martel 's sign also known as the G sign, or rat-bite erosion, refers to the punched -out lytic lesion and overhanging margin of the new bone along the edge of erosion seen in chronic tophaceous gout . Option A: Podagra is the inflammation of the base of the great toe (metatarsophalangeal joint) during flares of gout . It is not a radiological sign. Option C: Chopart's fracture is a fracture between talonavicular and calcaneocuboid joints. Option D: March fracture is fracture neck of 2nd or 3rd metatarsal. X-ray showing Martel 's sign:

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 52-year-old man presented to the OPD with complaints of severe joint pain in his big toe with history of multiple similar episodes in the past. An ultrasound of the first metatarsophalangeal joint was performed . What is the characteristic finding depicted in the image given below ?
mcqs.explanation: The characteristic finding depicted in the given ultrasound image of a patient with chronic gout is the double contour sign. Double contour sign is characterized by an echogenic line on the outer surface of the joint cartilage, due to the deposition of monosodium urate crystals on the surface of articular cartilage . It is seen in chronic gout . Option A: Double wall sign also known as Rigler's sign is an abdominal radiograph finding seen in pneumoperitoneum . Here both the inner and outer walls of the bowel are visible.480 Option B: Double density sign on chest X-ray PA view is seen due to left atrial enlargement . Here, the right border of the left atrium becomes laterally displaced and convex producing this appearance .Option D: Double barrel sign is a USG finding seen in common bile duct (CBD) obstruction causing dilatation of CBD and its lumen size becomes comparable to portal vein giving the appearance of a double -barrel.481

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man presented to the ER with severe pain and swelling as shown in the image below . He told that he had consumed 2 bottles of beer a few hours before . Which of the following drugs is not used in the management of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of an acute attack of gout . Allopurinol is used in the management of chronic gout . Urate-lowering drugs such as allopurinol, probenecid , and lesinurad are not initiated during acute attacks. The treatment options for an acute attack of gout include : • NSAIDs: Indomethacin, naproxen, ibuprofen , and diclofenac are highly effective • Colchicine : It acts by inhibiting neutrophil migration and reduces inflammation. It is used orally and is most effective if given early in an attack. • Glucocorticoids : Systemic glucocorticoids may be used in polyarticular involvement. If the disease is limited to one joint, intraarticular triamcinolone may be given.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is the best agent for the long-term treatment of chronic gout in a 50-year-old patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Allopurinol is the best agent for the long-term treatment of chronic or recurrent gout . Hypouricemic drugs that can be used for definitive treatment of chronic gout include : • Xanthine oxidase inhibitors- allopurinol, febuxostat • Uricosuric agents - probenecid , lesinurad • Recombinant uricases- rasburicase and pegloticase

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 58-year-old man with history of gout is now diagnosed with hypertension . Which of the following is the drug of choice for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: 482 Losartan is the drug of choice for the management of hypertension in a patient with gout because of its uricosuric action. Thiazides (hydrochlorothiazide , metolazone ) and loop diuretics (furosemide ) cause reduced excretion of uric acid from the renal tubules and result in hyperuricemia . Therefore they are not preferred for management of hypertension in patients with gout .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which joint is most commonly affected in calcium pyrophosphate disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The knee joint is most commonly affected in calcium pyrophosphate (CPPD) disease or pseudogout. Other sites include the wrist, shoulder , ankle, elbow , and hands. Acute CPPD arthropathy is commonly seen in the elderly and may be associated with conditions such as primary hyperparathyroidism , hypothyroidism , and hemochromatosis. X-ray of the affected joint may reveal chondrocalcinosis, which represents calcium deposition in articular cartilage . Polarised light microscopy of the joint aspirate demonstrates positively birefringent rhomboid crystals, as shown below :483

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of secondary Sjogren's syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of secondary Sj\366gren's syndrome is rheumatoid arthritis. Sj\366gren's syndrome is a chronic autoimmune disorder that affects the lacrimal and salivary glands. It also affects other organ systems , such as lungs , kidneys, and nervous system . It is seen in association with: • Rheumatoid arthritis • Systemic lupus erythematosus • Scleroderma • Mixed connective tissue disease • Primary biliary cirrhosis • Vasculitis • Chronic active hepatitis C

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which is the most common extraglandular manifestation seen in patients diagnosed with Sjogren's syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: The most common extraglandular manifestation seen in patients with Sj\366gren's syndrome is arthritis or arthralgia. The extraglandular manifestations in Sj\366gren's syndrome are: • Arthralgia or arthritis - most common manifestation. It is usually non-erosive and leads to Jaccoud 's arthropathy. Jaccoud's arthropathy is a deforming non-erosive arthropathy characterized by the ulnar deviation of the second to 5th fingers with metacarpophalangeal joint subluxation . • Raynaud's phenomenon • Interstitial lung disease - most common type is non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) • Renal tubular acidosis - Type 1 (distal) RTA • Primary biliary cirrhosis • Lymphoma - MALToma The give X-ray shows Jaccoud's arthropathy:490 The given image shows a patient with Jaccoud's arthropathy of the hands:

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A middle -aged woman presented with complaints of persistent dry eyes and dry mouth since past few months. On examination, dry mucous membranes, bilateral parotid region swelling , and conjunctivitis were noted . This condition is associated with which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Dry eyes and dry mouth along with parotid swelling and conjunctivitis are suggestive of Sj\366gren's syndrome. It is associated with HLA -DR3 allele .HLA allele Disease HLA DR2 , HL A-DR3 SLE HLA -DR3 Sjogren's syndrome HLA -DR4 Rheumatoid arthritis491 HLA allele Disease HLA -B27 Seronegative arthritis

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A software engineer presented with complaints of dryness and itching of eyes on staring at his laptop screen. On examination, parotid swelling was noted and the test shown below was positive . The serology of this patient is likely to be positive for which of the following antibodies ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of dry eyes , parotid swelling , and a positive Schirmer test is suggestive of Sj\366gren's syndrome. It is associated with anti-Ro/SS-A and anti-La /SS-B autoantibodies . The presence of anti-Ro/SS-A and anti-La /SS-B indicate extra glandular involvement and poor prognosis. Note : Anti-Ro and anti-La in SLE indicate a good prognosis, due to decreased risk of nephritis and vasculitis .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old woman presents with dry mouth, and difficulty swallowing solid food. Physical examination finds enlargement of her parotid glands along with marked dryness of her buccal mucosa. Laboratory examination finds the presence of both SS-A and SS-B antibodies . Which of the following statements is not true about this condition?

options.a: About 75 % of patients have rheumatoid factor
options.b: Patients are at high risk for development of B-cell lymphomas
options.d: Lacrimal gland is a major target for this disease

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Sjogren's syndrome. In this condition, glomerular lesions are extremely rare. Defects of tubular function, including renal tubular acidosis, uricosuria, and phosphaturia , are often seen and are associated histologically with tubulointerstitial nephritis. Lacrimal and salivary glands are the major targets of this disease , while the respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts and the vagina may also be involved. The characteristic decrease in tears and saliva (sicca syndrome) is the result of lymphocytic infiltration and fibrosis of the lacrimal and salivary glands. The infiltrate contains predominantly activated CD4+ helper T cells and some B cells , including plasma cells . Antibodies detected are: • Rheumatoid factor - seen in 75 % of patients , whether or not coexisting rheumatoid arthritis is present • Anti-nuclear antibodies (ANAs) • SS-A (Ro) - associated with early disease onset , longer disease duration, and extra-glandular manifestations, such as cutaneous vasculitis and nephritis • SS-B (La ) These patients are at high risk for the development of B-cell lymphomas. About 60% of patients have another accompanying autoimmune disorder, such as rheumatoid arthritis, and these patients also have the symptoms and signs of that disorder. Biopsy of the lip (to examine minor salivary glands) is essential for the diagnosis of Sj\366gren's syndrome. The image shows an enlargement of the salivary gland with intense lymphocytic and plasma cell infiltration with ductal epithelial hyperplasia in the salivary gland.492 Note : Mikulicz syndrome is characterized by lacrimal and salivary gland enlargement from any cause , including sarcoidosis, lymphomas, and other tumors.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old woman presented with complaints of thickening of her skin and the finding shown below . On workup, ANA was positive and immunofluorescence showed nucleolar pattern. What is the most common extracutaneous manifestation associated with her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given image is suggestive of microstomia. The findings of skin thickening, microstomia, positive ANA, and immunofluorescence showing nucleolar pattern point towards a diagnosis of systemic sclerosis . The most common extracutaneous manifestation of systemic sclerosis (scleroderma) is Raynaud's phenomenon . Raynaud's phenomenon is characterized by episodes of reversible vasoconstriction in the fingers and toes on exposure to cold. Rarely, it affects the lips, tip of the nose, and earlobes . These episodes classically occur in the following sequence : • Affected part turning pale due to vasoconstriction. • Blue due to ischemia, often associated with numbness or pain. • As blood flow returns, the area turns red with a burning sensation.493

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 14-year-old girl has the pallor of extremities followed by pain and cyanosis on exposure to cold. Which of the following diseases is she likely to develop in the later stages of life ?
mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario suggests that the patient has Raynaud phenomenon , which is associated with the risk of developing scleroderma in later stages of life . Raynaud phenomenon is manifested as episodic vasoconstriction of the arteries and arterioles of the extremities , causing pallor of extremities followed by pain and cyanosis. It is seen in virtually all patients with systemic sclerosis or scleroderma and precedes other symptoms in 70% of cases . The image shows features of Raynaud's phenomenon .Systemic sclerosis is characterized by progressive fibrosis involving the skin, gastrointestinal tract, and other tissues . Fibrosis may be the result of the activation of fibroblasts by cytokines produced by T cells .494 Focal, and sometimes diffuse , subcutaneous calcifications may develop , especially in patients with CREST syndrome. The most ominous manifestation is malignant hypertension .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about Raynaud's phenomenon ?

options.a: Secondary Raynaud's is associated with more severe symptoms
options.b: Secondary Raynaud's develops predominantly after the age of 30 years
options.c: Primary Raynaud's is usually ANA negative
options.d: Primary Raynaud's is associated with digital tissue necrosis and ulcers

mcqs.explanation: Primary Raynaud's phenomenon is not associated with tissue necrosis and ulcers .Features Primary Raynaud's phenome non Secondary Raynaud's pheno menon Age & gender Young women (<30y) Older women (>30y) Associations No underlying cause Scleroderma, Sj\366gren's syndr ome and SLE Family history Yes No ANA test Negative Positive Severity - duration, frequenc y & pain Less severe More severe Digital tissue necrosis, ulcera tion & gangrene No Yes Nailfold capillaroscopy (Imag e below ) Normal capillaries in evenly s paced parallel loops Distorted capillaries with wid ened & irregular loops

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common histological pattern of interstitial lung disease seen in patients with systemic sclerosis ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common histological pattern of interstitial lung disease in systemic sclerosis (scleroderma) is non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP). It commonly affects the lower lobes and is characterised by ground-glass opacities .495 Note : Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) is the most common type of ILD in rheumatoid arthritis.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs are implicated in systemic sclerosis -like illness ?
mcqs.explanation: Drugs implicated in systemic sclerosis -like illness are: • Bleomycin • Pentazocine • Cocaine • L-tryptophan -containing dietary supplements Chemicals implicated in systemic sclerosis -like illness are: • Heavy metals • Polyvinyl chloride (PVC ) • Toluene • Trichloroethylene Cyclophosphamide and bosentan are used in the treatment of systemic sclerosis (SSc). Cyclophosphamide reduces the progression of ILD associated with SSc. Bosentan reduces the risk of new ulcers in Raynaud's phenomenon associated with SSc.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 38-year-old woman presents with ulceration over her fingers. She has history of Raynaud's phenomenon and GERD since 3 years. Which of the following can be used as a screening test for her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of digital ulcers , Raynaud's phenomenon , and GERD are suggestive of systemic sclerosis (scleroderma). Antinuclear antibody (ANA) is the preferred screening test as it is the most sensitive test for both limited and diffuse variants of systemic sclerosis . Option B: Anti centromere antibody is the most specific test for CREST syndrome. Option C: Anti topoisomerase I (Scl-70) is the most specific test for diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis . Option D: Anti-cardiolipin antibody is seen in SLE and APLA syndrome.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 47-year-old woman presents with complaints of swollen fingers, heartburn, and occasional joint pains. She gives a history suggestive of Raynaud's phenomenon . Physical examination reveals taut, thickened skin over her hands and fingers with limited mobility. The presence of which of the following antibodies will confirm her diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of skin thickening in the hands and fingers (sclerodactyly ), Raynaud's phenomenon, heartburn (GERD), and occasional arthralgia is suggestive of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc). The presence of anticentromere antibody (ACA) will confirm the diagnosis of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis . Antinuclear antibody (ANA) is positive in most cases of systemic sclerosis . The absence of this antibody suggests considering an alternate diagnosis.496

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 53-year-old woman presented with thickening of skin over the trunk and proximal parts of the limbs. On workup, her serology was found to be positive for anti-topoisomerase I. Which of the following features is not likely to be associated with her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of skin thickening over the trunk and proximal parts of the limbs along with positive anti-topoisomerase I antibodies is suggestive of diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc). Critical limb ischemia is commonly associated with limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc).

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which among the following is more common in limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis when compared to diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis ?
mcqs.explanation: Esophageal dysmotility is more commonly seen in limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc) compared to diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis . Systemic sclerosis is divided into two based on the patterns of involvement - diffuse and limited . Limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis is characteristically associated with CREST syndrome, which includes calcinosis cutis , Raynaud's phenomenon , esophageal dysmotility , sclerodactyly and telangiectasia . Skin involvement, interstitial lung disease (Option C), myopathy (Option B), and scleroderma renal crisis (Option D) are more common in diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc) than limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis . The incidence of ischemic digital ulcers, CREST features , and primary biliary cirrhosis is more in limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis . The frequency of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is equal in both types .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a component of CREST syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Renal failure is not a component of CREST syndrome. CREST syndrome is seen in limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc) and consists of the following : • Calcinosis cutis • Raynaud's phenomenon • Esophageal dysmotility • Sclerodactyly • Telangiectasia497

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following antibodies is likely to be positive in patients who develop scleroderma renal crisis?
mcqs.explanation: Anti-RNA polymerase III antibody is associated with scleroderma renal crisis. Scleroderma renal crisis is scleroderma with accelerated hypertension , acute kidney injury and renal failure. The antibodies associated with it are: • Anti-RNA polymerase III • Topoisomerase I • U3-RNPTarget Antigen Characteristic Clinical Associ ation Topoisomerase I Early ILD , cardiac involveme nt, scleroderma renal crisis RNA Polymerase III Scleroderma renal crisis, incr eased cancer risk , GAVE (gas tric antral vascular ectasia ) U3-RNP PAH, ILD , scleroderma renal crisis, and myositis Th/To Interstitial lung disease (ILD ) and Pulmonary artery hypert ension (PAH) Ku Overlap syndrome

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: An elderly man presents to the ER with severe headache , blurring of vision, and oliguria. Examination reveals BP of 200 /100mmHg and papilledema . Skin thickening is noted over his hands, with contractures in the wrist and fingers. Investigations reveal serum creatinine of 3mg/dL and peripheral smear shows schistocytes . What is the drug of choice ?
mcqs.explanation: 498 The given clinical scenario is suggestive of scleroderma renal crisis. The drug of choice is ACE inhibitors. Scleroderma renal crisis is a medical emergency characterized by acute onset malignant hypertension and kidney failure, usually in the absence of previous evidence of significant kidney disease . The use of steroids is associated with an increased risk of scleroderma renal crisis. Clinical features of scleroderma renal crisis are: • Accelerated hypertension - headache , vomiting, blurring of vision, hypertensive retinopathy , and hypertensive encephalopathy . • Acute kidney injury - oliguria, mild proteinuria, microscopic hematuria, renal failure. • Pulmonary edema , congestive heart failure. • Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (schistocytes ), thrombocytopenia . In patients with persistent hypertension , the addition of angiotensin II receptor blockers, calcium channel blockers, and direct renin inhibitors should be considered .499

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: In patients with sarcoidosis, which of the following is the most commonly affected organ?
mcqs.explanation: Sarcoidosis most commonly affects the lungs . Sarcoidosis is a multisystem inflammatory disease characterized by non-caseating granulomas. It commonly involves the lungs , skin, liver, and eyes .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old woman with history of sarcoidosis presents with skin lesions shown in the image below . Identify the condition.
mcqs.explanation: The given condition is lupus pernio which is a cutaneous manifestation of sarcoidosis. Lupus pernio is a chronic inflammatory skin lesion, which is diagnostic for a chronic form of sarcoidosis. It involves the bridge of the nose, the area beneath the eyes , and the cheeks and often is purple in color. Other options :505 Option A: Acne rosacea is a skin disorder with onset in middle \037aged adults (30–50 years old) and involves the convexities of the face . Option C: Heliotrope rash presents as violaceous lesions around eyelids . It is seen in dermatomyositis. Option D: Malar rash or butterfly rash is classically seen in SLE.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old man presented with fever, productive cough , and weight loss. On examination, the following skin lesions were seen . His chest X-ray showed hilar lymphadenopathy . Which is the next best investigation for the management of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical features along with examination findings of lupus vulgaris is suggestive of tuberculosis . The next best investigation is AFB smear microscopy of the sputum sample . Lupus vulgaris is a manifestation of cutaneous tuberculosis . It has a characteristic slow enlarging plaque with an elevated border and central atrophy.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A man came to the clinic with fatigue , cough , and breathing difficulty . His chest X-ray showed bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and lung biopsy revealed non-caseating granuloma. What is the most common ocular manifestation associated with this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical features along with bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and non-caseating granuloma are suggestive of sarcoidosis. The most common ocular manifestation in sarcoidosis is anterior uveitis. Anterior uveitis presents with photophobia , blurry vision, and lacrimation. Other ocular manifestations include retinitis, pars planitis, and dry eyes .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which is the most common cranial nerve to be involved in sarcoidosis?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cranial nerve to be involved in sarcoidosis is the facial nerve leading to facial palsy. Neurosarcoidosis frequently manifests as follows : • Cranial nerve involvement- optic neuritis (CN II ), extraocular muscles involvement (CN III , IV , VI) and facial palsy (CN VII ) • Space occupying lesions • Diabetes insipidus - due to anterior hypothalamus involvement • Basilar meningitis

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following features would you not expect in a patient diagnosed with Lofgren's syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Parotid enlargement is not a feature of Lofgren's syndrome. Lofgren's syndrome is an acute form of sarcoidosis that has a good prognosis, with most of the patients experiencing disease resolution within 2 years.506 It is characterized by: • Arthritis • Erythema nodosum • Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy Heerfordt –Waldenstr\366m syndrome also known as uveoparotid fever is a variant of sarcoidosis characterized by: • Fever • Parotid enlargement • Facial palsy • Anterior uveitis

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 44-year-old construction worker, who is a known case of sarcoidosis, has now presented with polyuria, constipation , and myalgia for the past 5 days. An ECG was taken which showed a short QT interval. Which of the following is responsible for this condition?\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\ \037\037\037 \037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\ \037\037\037\037 \037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\037\

options.d: Increased production of PTH related peptide

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical features along with a short QT interval points towards hypercalcemia . Hypercalcemia in a patient with sarcoidosis is due to the increased production of vitamin D by the non-caseating granulomas. Hypercalcemia and hypercalciuria are seen in some patients with sarcoidosis. The increased production of vitamin D (1,25-dihydoxyvitamin D) results in increased intestinal absorption of calcium, leading to hypercalcemia . Vitamin D supplementation and increased sun exposure in patients with sarcoidosis can precipitate hypercalcemia .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient was evaluated for unexplained cough and shortness of breath. Investigations revealed elevated serum calcium and a chest X-ray showed hilar lymphadenopathy . A lymph node biopsy was taken to confirm the diagnosis. Which of the following is least likely to be seen in the histopathological examination?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of sarcoidosis, in which the histopathological examination of lesions does not show Masson bodies. Masson bodies are polypoid plugs of loose organizing connective tissue seen in cryptogenic organizing pneumonia. The cardinal histopathologic feature of sarcoidosis, irrespective of the organ involved, is the non-caseating granuloma. Two other microscopic features are sometimes seen in the granulomas: • Schaumann bodies - inclusion bodies with concentric rings of calcification • Asteroid bodies - stellate inclusions in the giant cells

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common abnormality of liver function in sarcoidosis?
mcqs.explanation: The most common abnormality of liver function in sarcoidosis is the elevation of alkaline phosphatase (ALP ) levels .507 Sarcoidosis of the liver presents as a granulomatous disease that causes intrahepatic cholestasis . As the disease advances it leads to elevated liver enzymes followed by elevated bilirubin levels .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A middle -aged woman presented to you with shortness of breath and dry cough for the past 3 months. On examination, the following skin lesions were seen . You will order all of the following investigations except :
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and examination findings of erythema nodosum are suggestive of sarcoidosis. CD4/CD8 ratio in bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL ) fluid , not blood, is used for diagnosis of sarcoidosis. Erythema nodosum is inflammation of the subcutaneous fat (panniculitis) seen in sarcoidosis. The investigations used in the diagnosis of sarcoidosis include : • Serum ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) levels - elevated • BAL - lymphocytosis and increased CD4/CD8 ratio. A ratio of >3.5 in BAL is strongly supportive of sarcoidosis. • PET-CT scan - to identify areas of granulomatous disease • Gallium scan shows the following signs: • Panda sign- due to bilateral involvement of parotid and lacrimal glands in sarcoidosis • Lambda sign- due to bilateral hilar and right paratracheal lymph nodes which resembles lambda (\022) • Biopsy showing non-caseating granulomas in a patient with features of sarcoidosis confirms the diagnosis. The image given below shows the Panda sign:

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: The chest radiograph of a young man with sarcoidosis shows pulmonary infiltrates in the upper lobes of his lungs without hilar lymphadenopathy . What is the grade of lung involvement according to Scadding scoring system ?
mcqs.explanation: 508 According to the Scadding scoring system , the presence of pulmonary infiltrates alone represents grade III . The Scadding scoring system is used to grade lung involvement in sarcoidosis. It is based on the chest radiograph findings: • Grade I: Hilar lymphadenopathy , often with right paratracheal involvement. No pulmonary infiltrates . • Grade II : Hilar lymphadenopathy + pulmonary infiltrates • Grade III : Pulmonary infiltrates only • Grade IV : Fibrosis Sarcoidosis predominantly involves the upper lobes of the lungs .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following lymph nodes is not involved in the Garland triad?
mcqs.explanation: Garland triad does not involve left paratracheal lymph nodes . Garland triad also known as the 1-2-3 sign or Pawnbrokers sign is a lymph node enlargement pattern in sarcoidosis that involves: • Right paratracheal nodes (1) • Right hilar nodes (2) • Left hilar nodes (3)

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the first-line drug for a patient diagnosed with sarcoidosis with multiple organ involvement?
mcqs.explanation: The first-line drug for sarcoidosis with multiple organ involvement is prednisolone . Management of sarcoidosis:509 • Asymptomatic patients - monitored for disease progression • Localized/ limited cutaneous and ocular lesions - treated using topical steroids • Multisystem involvement: • Systemic steroids • Other drugs like hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate , and infliximab are considered when the steroids are ineffective or not tolerated

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions is not associated with a significant elevation of angiotensin-converting enzyme levels ?
mcqs.explanation: Diabetes is associated with a mild elevation of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) levels . Significant elevation of ACE levels is seen in: • Sarcoidosis • Silicosis • Leprosy • Gaucher's disease • Hyperthyroidism • Disseminated granulomatous infections such as miliary tuberculosis510

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common inflammatory myopathy seen in the elderly ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common inflammatory myopathy seen in elderly patients (>50 years) is inclusion body myositis. Inclusion body myositis is a type of inflammatory myopathy . It is characterized by progressive , asymmetric muscle weakness most commonly involving the wrist, finger flexors, and quadriceps. Muscles of the face and neck may also be involved, presenting as dysphagia . Inclusion body myositis is named so because of the presence of inclusion bodies containing amyloid-like protein seen on microscopy.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: An IT professional complained of weakness of fingers while using the keyboard. It has been progressing over the past 2 months. It is more severe on his right hand than his left hand. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given history of progressive and predominantly asymmetric muscle weakness is most likely suggestive of inclusion body myositis. Inclusion body myositis is a type of inflammatory myopathy . It is seen in people older than 50 years of age . It is characterized by progressive , asymmetric muscle weakness most commonly involving the wrist, finger flexors, and quadriceps. Muscles of the face and neck might also be involved, leading to dysphagia . Polymyositis , dermatomyositis , and necrotizing myopathy have predominantly symmetric muscle involvement.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Patients with which of the following myopathies are generally resistant to immunosuppressive therapies ?
mcqs.explanation: Patients with inclusion body myositis are generally resistant to immunosuppressive therapies .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following group of muscles are unlikely to be involved in a patient diagnosed with an inflammatory myopathy ?
mcqs.explanation: Ocular muscles are unlikely to be involved as they are spared in inflammatory myopathy . They are not involved even in advanced, untreated cases . The pattern of muscle involvement in various inflammatory myopathies is: • Proximal muscles are most commonly involved in dermatomyositis and polymyositis , causing difficulty in getting up from a chair, brushing hair, etc . • Proximal and distal muscles are involved in inclusion body myositis, such as wrist, finger flexors, and quadriceps.517 • Pharyngeal and neck-flexor muscles are often involved in all forms of inflammatory myopathy , causing dysphagia or difficulty in holding up the head . Respiratory muscles may also be affected in advanced cases .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which inflammatory myopathy is most frequently associated with other autoimmune diseases ?
mcqs.explanation: Inflammatory myopathy most frequently associated with other autoimmune diseases is polymyositis.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A physician is suspecting dermatomyositis in a 27-year-old woman with complaints of proximal myalgia and dysphagia . The presence of which of the following signs would be pathognomonic of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of Gottron's papules is pathognomonic of dermatomyositis . They are erythematous to violaceous papules that occur symmetrically over the extensor aspects of metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints. Gottron's sign, on the other hand, is erythematous rash over the extensor surfaces of joints such as the knuckles, elbows , knees, and ankles. V sign is confluent macular erythema over the lower anterior neck and upper anterior chest . Shawl sign is the confluent macular erythema over the upper back and lateral aspect of arms. All these signs are present in dermatomyositis , but Gottron's papules and heliotrope rash are pathognomonic.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old woman presented with difficulty in activities like climbing stairs, getting up from a chair, and combing hair. She is a known case of ovarian cancer. The following finding was noted on examination. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows upper eyelid lilac erythema or heliotrope rash. The given clinical presentation of proximal myopathy with the characteristic heliotrope rash and history of an internal malignancy point towards a diagnosis of dermatomyositis . Classic cutaneous signs in dermatomyositis : • Heliotrope rash/ eyelid erythema - violaceous erythema of the upper eyelids . Pathognomonic of dermatomyositis. • V sign- confluent macular erythema over the lower anterior neck and upper anterior chest • Shawl sign- confluent macular erythema over the upper back and lateral aspect of arms • Gottron's papules - erythematous papules and plaques over the extensor surface of the metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints. Pathognomonic of dermatomyositis . • Gottron's sign- erythematous rash over the extensor surfaces of joints such as the knuckles, elbows , knees, and ankles • Mechanic 's hands- rough, hyperkeratotic lines on the lateral and palmer areas of the fingers • Scalp erythema and hair loss518 • Facial rash- confluent erythema in the malar distribution involving the cheeks , nasal bridge , and nasolabial folds • Nail fold changes • Flagellate erythema - linear erythema on the upper back with pruritus • Poikiloderma- mottled pattern of hyperpigmented and hypopigmented macules with telangiectasias • Cutaneous calcinosis- accumulation of calcium deposits in the skin Facial rash in dermatomyositis -Eyelid erythema / heliotrope rash in dermatomyositis -V - sign in dermatomyositis -519 Shawl sign in dermatomyositis -Flagellate erythema in dermatomyositis-520 Gottron papules in dermatomyositis -Poikilodermatous changes in dermatomyositis -521

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following would help you to differentiate between dermatomyositis and polymyositis in a patient presenting with muscle weakness ?
mcqs.explanation: An erythematous rash helps in differentiating between the two conditions as it is seen only in dermatomyositis. Option A: Elevated levels of creatine kinase are seen in all the inflammatory myopathies . Options B and D: The involvement of proximal muscles more than the distal muscles and interstitial lung disease is seen in both polymyositis and dermatomyositis .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with dermatomyositis . She should be screened for which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: This patient should be screened for malignancy as dermatomyositis is often associated with underlying malignancies. The most common cancer associated with dermatomyositis is ovarian cancer. Other malignancies that are commonly associated with dermatomyositis are: • Breast cancer • Melanoma • Colon cancer • Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman complained of difficulty reaching high cabinets and carrying grocery bags. It has been progressing over the past 3 months. Which is the initial investigation of choice in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of an inflammatory myositis for which the initial investigation of choice is creatine kinase (CK).522 Creatine kinase is a marker of muscle breakdown. It is increased in dermatomyositis and polymyositis. However, it may be normal in inclusion body myositis. The most specific investigation for inflammatory myositis is a muscle biopsy .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A middle -aged woman presented with muscle weakness and pain over her shoulders . On examination , the following rash and mechanic's hands were noted . Positive titers of which of the following antibodies are associated with her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and findings of Gottron papules (image) are suggestive of dermatomyositis. Positive titers of Anti-Jo-1 (antisynthetase ) antibodies are associated with interstitial lung disease , arthritis, and mechanic's hands in patients with dermatomyositis . Other autoantibodies seen in dermatomyositis are: • Anti-Mi-2 - highly specific to dermatomyositis • Anti-SRP (anti-signal recognition protein) - associated with severe myositis • Anti–PM-Scl - associated with overlapping myositis and scleroderma • Anti-p155 /140 or anti-transcription intermediary factor (TIF)-1\025 - seen in cancer-associated myositis • Anti-MDA5 (anti-CADM 140 ) - associated with rapidly progressive lung disease and cutaneous ulcer

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient with dermatomyositis presented with cough , hemoptysis , and weight loss. After a detailed evaluation, she was diagnosed with lung cancer. Which of the following autoantibodies is strongly associated with this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Anti-155/140 antibody is strongly associated with dermatomyositis with malignancy. Adenocarcinomas of the cervix, lung, ovaries, and pancreas account for the majority of cancers associated with inflammatory myopathies .Antibody Clinical association Anti-Jo-1 and other antisynth etase antibodies PolymyositisDermatomyositi s with interstitial lung diseas e, arthritis, and mechanic's h ands Anti-Mi-2 Dermatomyositis with rash more than myositis Anti-MDA5(anti-CADM 140 ) Dermatomyositis with rapidl y progressive lung disease an d cutaneous ulcers Anti- 155/140 orAnti-transcri ption intermediary factor (TI F)-1\025 Cancer-associated myositis Anti-SAE Cancer-associated dermatom yositis , dermatomyositis with rapidly progressive lung dise ase523

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A bodybuilder complains that he is facing difficulty in doing squats and is too weak to climb stairs. He denies any headaches or changes in vision. A quadriceps muscle biopsy reveals perimysial inflammation and perifascicular atrophy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical presentation and muscle biopsy finding of perimysial inflammation and perifascicular atrophy makes dermatomyositis the most likely diagnosis. Muscle biopsy findings in various inflammatory myositis are as follows :Dermatomyositis Polymyositis Inclusion body myositis Perimysialinfiltrates Endomysialinfiltrates Endomysialinfiltrates Perivascular infiltrates andpe rifascicularatrophy Perivascular infiltrates Perivascular infiltrates with a myloid inclusion bodies and r immed vacuoles CD4+cellular infiltrates CD8+cellular infiltrates CD8+cellular infiltrates

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A housemaid presents to you with generalized skin thickening and numbness of fingers on exposure to cold. She also complains of muscle pain, and difficulty while walking and climbing stairs. Investigations reveal the following . The presence of which of the following antibodies is diagnostic of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario having features of both systemic sclerosis and dermatomyositis points towards a diagnosis of overlap syndrome. The presence of anti-PM/Scl antibodies is diagnostic of overlap syndrome. Anti-PM/Scl is a specific antinuclear antibody directed against a nucleolar-protein complex . Overlap syndrome also known as mixed connective tissue disease usually involves a combination of three connective tissue diseases : • Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) • Progressive systemic sclerosis (PSS) • Polymyositis (PM) or dermatomyositis (DM)

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old woman presents with severe generalized body ache, fatigue , sleep disturbances , and low mood for the past 4 months. On examination, increased pain sensitivity and tender bony prominences are noted . Laboratory and radiological investigations are normal . What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The most probable diagnosis for the given clinical scenario is fibromyalgia. Fibromyalgia is characterized by chronic widespread musculoskeletal pain and tenderness accompanied by other non-specific somatic symptoms like fatigue and sleep disturbance , for >three months. It is more common in females . On examination, they have tenderness in multiple soft tissue anatomical locations. Laboratory findings are normal . Patients with fibromyalgia may have an increased prevalence of other syndromes associated with pain and fatigue , like chronic headaches , chronic fatigue syndrome, irritable bowel syndrome, interstitial cystitis / painful bladder syndrome, and pelvic pain syndromes.524 Options A and B: Polymyositis and dermatomyositis have positive laboratory findings such as specific antibodies and radiological findings of multiorgan involvement (ex: interstitial lung disease in polymyositis ). Option C: Although the given clinical scenario closely resembles clinical depression , the examination findings showing tenderness and pain sensitivity favor the diagnosis of fibromyalgia.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about fibromyalgia?

options.c: SPECT studies show hyperperfusion of the thalamus
options.d: Opioid analgesics are ineffective in pain management

mcqs.explanation: Single -photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) studies done on fibromyalgia patients show hypoperfusion of the thalamus. Fibromyalgia is characterized by chronic widespread musculoskeletal pain and tenderness . It is more common in females . Patients with fibromyalgia have an increased prevalence of other syndromes associated with pain and fatigue , including chronic fatigue syndrome, chronic headaches , irritable bowel syndrome, interstitial cystitis / painful bladder syndrome, and pelvic pain syndromes. Non-pharmacological treatment strategies for fibromyalgia include physical conditioning and aerobic exercise. Opioid analgesics should be avoided in fibromyalgia as they are not effective and are associated with opioid -induced hyperalgesia that can worsen both the symptoms and function.525

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Seronegative spondyloarthritides are associated with which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Seronegative spondyloarthritides are associated with HLA -B27.532 The spondyloarthritides are a group of overlapping disorders that share certain clinical features and genetic associations (HLA-B27). These disorders include : • Psoriatic arthritis • Ankylosing spondylitis • Reactive arthritis • Enteropathic arthritis • Juvenile onset spondyloarthritis • Undifferentiated spondyloarthritis Usually , rheumatoid factor (RF) assay is negative in spondyloarthritides . Hence , they are also referred to as seronegative arthritis.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old man presented with pain and stiffness in his lower back. His X-ray spine is given below . Which of the following is true about his condition?

options.c: It is associated with HLA B
options.d: Associated with low serum IgA levels

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical features along with the classical bamboo-spine appearance on X-ray point towards a diagnosis of ankylosing spondylitis (AS). In ankylosing spondylitis , the symptoms improve with activity. Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is an inflammatory disorder that affects the axial skeleton primarily, and may also involve peripheral joints. It is strongly associated with HLA -B27. It usually presents in the mid-twenties . It presents with lower back pain that improves with activity and worsens with rest or inactivity. Early morning stiffness is a characteristic feature . It is associated with elevated serum IgA levels . NSAIDs are the first line of pharmacological therapy . It is also associated with extra-articular manifestations like uveitis, interstitial lung disease , aortic regurgitation, etc . NSAIDs are the first-line treatment for ankylosing spondylitis .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What are the key cytokines involved in the pathogenesis of ankylosing spondylitis ?
mcqs.explanation: The key cytokines involved in the pathogenesis of ankylosing spondylitis are TNF-\030 and IL -17. IL-23 also plays a role in pathogenesis .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient with Crohn's disease presents with back pain and stiffness . The physician suspects ankylosing spondylitis and orders an MRI for evaluation. Which of the following joints will be the earliest to be involved?
mcqs.explanation: The earliest joint to be involved in ankylosing spondylitis is the sacroiliac joint. Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is an inflammatory disorder that primarily affects the axial skeleton . It is more common in males, usually presenting between 20 -30 years of age .533 Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) and peripheral arthritis can occur as extra-intestinal manifestations of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD ). They are more common in Crohn's disease than in ulcerative colitis .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old male patient with low backache and early morning stiffness for the past 1 year is diagnosed with ankylosing spondylitis . Which of the following is not associated with the haplotype related to this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Ankylosing spondylitis is related to the HLA -B27 haplotype . This haplotype is not associated with Behcet 's disease . It is associated with HLA B51. Ankylosing spondylitis is a chronic inflammatory disease that mainly affects the spine and sacroiliac joint. Individuals who inherit this class I HLA allele (HLA -B27) have a 100 –200 fold greater chance (odds ratio or relative risk ) of developing the disease compared with those who do not carry HLA -B27. Many autoimmune diseases are associated with different class II HLA alleles .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: The following test is performed in a patient to evaluate back pain associated with stiffness . Identify the test.
mcqs.explanation: The test performed is modified Schober's test . This test is done in patients with suspected ankylosing spondylitis . It is used to detect reduced flexion of the spine . The test involves marking two points- at the lumbosacral junction and 10 cm above it. The patient is then asked to bend forward with knees fully extended and the distance between the two points is measured . This distance normally increases by \0372 cm. An increase of <2 cm indicates reduced flexion. In the image given below the distance increases by 5cm which is normal .Option A: Gaenslen 's test is used to detect primary chronic inflammation of the sacroiliac joint. Option B: Thomas test is used to detect fixed flexion deformity of the hip.534 Option C: Adam's forward bending test is performed on a patient to differentiate structural from non-structural scoliosis .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which is the most common extra-articular manifestation seen in patients diagnosed with ankylosing spondylitis ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common extraarticular manifestation of ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is anterior uveitis. It usually presents with unilateral pain, photophobia and increased lacrimation. It is also associated with other spondyloarthritides like reactive arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and enteropathic arthritis. Other extra-articular manifestations of AS include : • GIT : ileitis , colitis , inflammatory bowel disease • Cardiovascular: increased risk of IHD, aortic insufficiency , heart block • Respiratory: upper lobe fibrosis • Neurological : cauda equina syndrome • Skin : acne fulminans, hidradenitis suppurativa

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions predominantly involve the upper lobe of the lung?
mcqs.explanation: Ankylosing spondylitis predominantly involves the upper lobe of the lung leading to pulmonary fibrosis. Rheumatoid arthritis, scleroderma, and asbestosis predominantly involve the lower lobes of the lungs.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient who presented with chronic lower back pain has been diagnosed with ankylosing spondylitis . What is the first line of pharmacological therapy ?
mcqs.explanation: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are the first line of pharmacological therapy for ankylosing spondylitis (AS). Management of ankylosing spondylitis includes : • First-line management: • Physiotherapy to maintain posture and range of motion. • NSAIDs- reduce pain and tenderness, increase mobility, and slow down the disease progression. • TNF \030 inhibitors- in patients who do not respond to NSAID therapy . It is not used in all patients because of side effects like reactivation of TB , hypersensitivity reactions, pancytopenia , drug-induced psoriasis, etc . • Anti-IL -17 antibodies - in patients with failed anti-TNF therapy . • Surgery- improves mobility in patients with severe arthritis and joint stiffness .535

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 27-year-old man with ankylosing spondylitis is not responding to standard therapy . His physician decides to prescribe him an anti-IL -17 monoclonal antibody. Which of the following drugs would he prescribe ?
mcqs.explanation: Secukinumab is an anti-IL -17 monoclonal antibody used in patients with ankylosing spondylitis who are not responding to NSAIDs and anti-TNF therapy . Management of ankylosing spondylitis includes : • First-line management: • Physiotherapy to maintain posture and range of motion. • NSAIDs- reduce pain and tenderness, increase mobility, and slow down the disease progression. • TNF \030 inhibitors- in patients who do not respond to NSAID therapy . It is not used in all patients because of side effects like reactivation of TB , hypersensitivity reactions, pancytopenia , drug-induced psoriasis, etc . • Anti-IL -17 antibodies - in patients with failed anti-TNF therapy . • Surgery- improves mobility in patients with severe arthritis and joint stiffness . Option A: Ustekinumab is an anti-IL -12 /23 monoclonal antibody used in the treatment of psoriasis. Options C and D: Infliximab and adalimumab are anti-TNF-\030 monoclonal antibodies used in the treatment of ankylosing spondylitis .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 15-year-old boy presents with generalized malaise and painful swelling of his right knee joint since 10 days. He also complains of pain and discomfort during urination. He was treated for diarrhea last month. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario describes an acute arthritis following an infection which is also associated with urethritis and generalized malaise. These features are suggestive of reactive arthritis. Reactive arthritis also known as Reiter's syndrome is a seronegative spondyloarthritis that occurs as a consequence of a recent enteric or urogenital infection . It is associated with HLA B27. It is also associated with extra-articular manifestations such as: • Urogenital - urethritis, prostatitis , cervicitis • Ocular- conjuctivitis, anterior uveitis • Mucocutaneous - oral ulcers , keratoderma blennorrhagica, circinate balanitis In some patients it presents as a triad of: • Arthritis • Urethritis • Conjunctivitis

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient presents with painful knee swelling , dysuria, and conjunctivitis. Which of the following infectious agents is least likely to cause this?
mcqs.explanation: 536 The given scenario of arthritis, urethritis, and conjunctivitis is suggestive of reactive arthritis. It is not caused by Neisseria gonorrhea. Disseminated gonococcal infection causes gonococcal arthritis. It comprises localized septic arthritis and arthritis-dermatitis syndrome. Reactive arthritis is usually caused due to LPS (lipopolysaccharide ) component of the gram -negative organisms or cross-reactivity with synovial antigens. The common causative organisms include : • Chlamydia trachomatis (most common) • Salmonella • Shigella • Yersinia • Campylobacter

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man presented with pain and swelling of his right knee for one week . It started progressing to the ankle joints and feet for the past 2 days. He gives a history of diarrhea and burning micturition 4 weeks ago. On examination, his soles showed the following lesions . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of acute arthritis following a recent infection and additive pattern (involvement of new joints within few days) and examination finding of keratoderma blennorrhagica (image) are suggestive of reactive arthritis. Keratoderma blennorrhagica is a mucocutaneous manifestation of reactive arthritis. It presents as vesicles and pustules that lead to hyperkeratotic lesions or crusting on the palms and soles . Other mucocutaneous manifestations of reactive arthritis include : • Oral ulcers - superficial , transient, and often asymptomatic • Circinate balanitis - consists of vesicles that rupture to form painless superficial erosions on the glans penis

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: An elderly man presents with pain and deformity of his toes . The clinical findings are shown in the image below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical image showing dactylitis , nail changes and telescoping of toes is suggestive of psoriatic arthritis. Clinical features of psoriatic arthritis include : • Psoriatic nail changes - yellowing and hypertrophy • Dactylitis - inflammation of the toes • Telescoping (shortening) of toes due to osteolysis • Severe deformity - suggestive of arthritis mutilans • Enthesitis - heel pain at the sites of ligament or tendon attachment Psoriatic arthritis of the hands commonly involves proximal and distal interphalangeal joints (PIP , DIP) and metacarpophalangeal joints (MCP). The image below shows psoriatic arthritis of537 the hands:

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old girl is being evaluated for arthritis and uveitis. Which of the following would you not consider as a differential diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Juvenile onset spondyloarthritis (JSpA) would not be considered as a differential diagnosis as it has no associated extra-articular manifestations like uveitis, lung involvement, etc . It is a seronegative spondyloarthritis with onset between 7-16 years of age . It usually presents as asymmetric arthritis predominantly involving the lower extremities .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a part of the SAPHO syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Psoriasis is not a part of SAPHO syndrome. The SAPHO syndrome is characterized by: • Synovitis- arthritis • Acne- acne conglobata • Pustulosis - palmoplantar pustulosis , hidradenitis suppurativa • Hyperostosis - sternoclavicular and spinal hyperostosis • Osteitis - sterile osteomyelitis

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Uveitis is an uncommon manifestation in patients with which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Uveitis is a rare manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis (RA ). Ocular manifestation in RA includes scleritis , episcleritis , and keratoconjunctivitis.538 Uveitis is a common ocular manifestation of seronegative arthritis e.g. Reiter's syndrome, ankylosing spondylitis , psoriatic arthritis, and juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (JRA ).539

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What type of hypersensitivity reaction is seen in systemic lupus erythematosus ?
mcqs.explanation: Type III hypersensitivity reaction (immune complex deposition ) is seen in systemic lupus erythematosus . Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune condition in which autoantibodies are directed against a part of the nucleus such as double -stranded DNA, histone , ribonuclear proteins , etc . The presence of these autoantibodies leads to the deposition of immune complexes and activation of the complement system .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Patients with which of the following complement deficiencies are at an increased risk of developing systemic lupus erythematosus ?
mcqs.explanation: C1q complement deficiency is a risk factor for the development of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Risk factors for SLE are: • Genetic • Genetic defects resulting in C1q , C2, C4 complement deficiencies • Presence of HLA DR3 • Mutation in the TREX1 gene • Environmental • Epstein -Barr virus (EBV) infection • Oral contraceptive pills / hormone replacement therapy • Smoking • Prolonged exposure to silica547

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Anti-nuclear antibodies are required for the diagnosis of which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Antinuclear antibodies (ANAs) are required for the diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus . ANAs are autoantibodies that bind to the contents of the cell nucleus . They are present in > 95% of patients with SLE. A positive antinuclear antibody ( ANA ) test with a titer of at least 1:80 is the obligatory entry criterion along with the additive criteria in 7 clinical and 3 immunologic domains. If a total of >10 points achieved , it is indicative of SLE according to 2019 EULAR/ACR Classification Criteria for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) Most sensitive antibody for SLE: ANA Most specific antibody for SLE: Anti smith > Anti dsDNA ANA may also be positive in the other options but it is not a criterion for diagnosis of these conditions. The following antibodies are specific for their respective autoimmune conditions. • Scleroderma (option A): Anti-topoisomerase I(Scl-70) and anti-centromere antibodies highly specific for Systemic sclerosis . • Rheumatoid arthritis (option C): RF and anti-CCP antibodies • Sjogren syndrome (option D): Anti-Ro, Anti-La

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old marathon runner presents with complaints of joint pain and rashes over the face. She says the rashes appear on exposure to the sun. On physical examination, a butterfly rash is seen over her face sparing the nasolabial folds . Which of the following antibodies will you evaluate to screen this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The best screening test in this condition is to evaluate for the presence of antinuclear antibodies (ANAs).

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A school teacher presented with painful oral ulcers , photosensitive rashes, and arthralgia. Presence of which of the following antibodies would be diagnostic of her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of oral ulcers , photosensitive rash, and arthralgia is suggestive of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Anti-Sm antibodies are most specific for SLE and hence their presence is diagnostic of this condition.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: An SLE patient is found to have a butterfly rash. Which of the following is an incorrect statement regarding this finding?

options.a: Most common acute rash in SLE
options.c: Increased risk of squamous cell carcinoma

mcqs.explanation: Butterfly rash or malar rash in a patient with SLE is not associated with an increased risk of squamous cell carcinoma . It is the most common type of acute skin rash seen in SLE. It is a photosensitive , erythematous, and scaly rash that is prominent over the cheeks and the nose. It spares the nasolabial folds . Common causes of malar rash are as follows : • Erysipelas • Cellulitis548 • Systemic lupus erythematosus • Rosacea • Pellagra • Dermatomyositis

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common pulmonary manifestation of SLE?
mcqs.explanation: The most common pulmonary manifestation of SLE is pleuritis , with or without pleural effusion . The most common manifestations of different systems involved in SLE are: • Musculoskeletal - arthritis and arthralgia • Skin - photosensitivity • Kidneys - proteinuria • Neurologic - cognitive impairment • Cardiac- pericarditis • Pulmonary- pleuritis • Hematologic - anemia

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man with history of SLE presented to your OPD with shortness of breath. It is associated with chest pain that worsens on inspiration. On auscultation , you notice a pleural friction rub. Investigations reveal the following . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with elevated hemidiaphragm and no evidence of ILD on chest CT is suggestive of shrinking lung syndrome (SLS), which is a rare complication of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). It is characterized by dyspnea and episodes of pleuritic chest pain. These symptoms occur in the absence of pleural or parenchymal involvement. PFT shows decreased lung volume with a restrictive pattern, and DLCO is often reduced . Radiological investigations show an elevated hemidiaphragm with no evidence of ILD . The following X-ray shows shrinking lung syndrome.549 Pulmonary manifestations seen in SLE are: • Pleuritis with or without pleural effusion- most common pulmonary manifestation. • Lupus pneumonitis - It is the inflammation of the lung tissue (pneumonitis ) due to SLE (lupus ). • Interstitial lung fibrosis • Shrinking lung syndrome • Intra -alveolar hemorrhage

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common neurological manifestation seen in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common neurological manifestation seen in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is cognitive impairment. It can manifest as impaired memory and reasoning. Other common neurological manifestations in SLE are psychosis , depression , and seizures . The most common manifestations of different systems involved in SLE are: • Musculoskeletal - arthritis and arthralgia • Skin - photosensitivity • Kidneys - proteinuria • Neurologic - cognitive impairment • Cardiac- pericarditis • Pulmonary- pleuritis • Hematologic - anemia550

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A young girl is being evaluated for low mood, anhedonia, weight loss, and insomnia since past 1 month. On examination, multiple hesitation marks were seen on her left forearm. She was diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) one year back. Which of the following autoantibodies is associated with this presentation ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of depression in a patient with SLE. It is associated with anti-ribosomal P antibodies . Antiribosomal P antibody is associated with psychosis or depression in SLE.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common cardiac manifestation seen in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus ?
mcqs.explanation: Pericarditis is the most common cardiac manifestation seen in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus . Other cardiac manifestations include : • Myocarditis • Libman -Sacks endocarditis . Patients with SLE are at an increased risk for myocardial infarction, usually due to accelerated atherosclerosis. The most common manifestations of different systems involved in SLE are: • Musculoskeletal - arthritis and arthralgia • Skin - photosensitivity • Kidneys - proteinuria • Neurologic - cognitive impairment • Cardiac- pericarditis • Pulmonary- pleuritis • Hematologic - anemia

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a feature of arthritis in SLE?
mcqs.explanation: Non-erosive arthritis is a common feature of arthritis in SLE. Features of arthritis in SLE are: • Symmetrical and polyarticular arthritis • A predilection for the small joints of the hand (the proximal interphalangeal and carpal joints) • Non-erosive and deforming arthritis (reducible ) In contrast to rheumatoid arthritis which is characterized by erosive, deforming joint involvement, SLE has non-erosive and deforming arthritis (reduciable ).

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A young woman who is a known case of SLE develops proteinuria. The doctor suspects lupus nephritis and performs a renal biopsy . It shows the presence of wire loop appearance without glomerular proliferation. In which class of lupus nephritis will you categorize this patient 's biopsy findings?
mcqs.explanation: 551 Wire loop appearance without glomerular proliferation is seen in diffuse lupus nephritis (Class IV ). The capillaries are thickened due to the subendothelial deposits and appear as wire loops . It is the most common and most severe form of lupus nephritis.Renal involvement is common in patients with SLE. The majority of the patients will present with • Proteinuria, nephrotic syndrome • Microscopic hematuria, hypertension • Urinary casts • Abnormal renal function tests - elevated serum creatinine • Low C3 and C4 levels

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 40 year old female presented to the OPD for her annual routine check-up. she is a patient of SLE diagnosed a decade ago, among the given options what is the most common cause of death in such patients ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of death in patients with SLE after 10 years of disease is accelerated atherosclerosis. The leading causes of death in the first 10 years of the disease are infections and renal failure; subsequently , Cardiovascular events become increasingly frequent causes of mortality.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is recommended for all patients with SLE?
mcqs.explanation: Hydroxychloroquine is recommended for all patients with SLE. It decreases the symptoms , reduces flares and organ damage . Important drugs used in the management of SLE are:552 • NSAIDs- used for a shorter period to reduce pain and fever. They are not used in all patients because of the increased risk of atherosclerosis and renal injury. • Hydroxychloroquine or chloroquine- should be used in all patients with SLE • Glucocorticoids • topical glucocorticoids - in mild skin lesions • systemic steroids - in severe skin lesions and organ involvements. • Immunosuppressive agents - used in combination with glucocorticoids in severe skin lesions and organ involvement. They help to reduce the dose and toxicity of glucocorticoids . Important agents are: • Methotrexate • Azathioprine • Mycophenolate mofetil and cyclophosphamide - immunosuppressive agents of choice in renal involvement. • Biologic drugs- like belimumab and rituximab are used when there is no response to conventional drugs.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient with a history of SLE presented with hematuria and proteinuria. Investigations revealed elevated creatinine and low C3, C4 levels . He was unresponsive to steroid therapy and his physician prescribed him belimumab for further management. What is the mechanism of action of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of lupus nephritis. Belimumab is a BAFF inhibitor used in patients with lupus nephritis who do not show response to initial therapy with steroids . Belimumab is a human monoclonal antibody that inhibits the soluble form of a B cell survival factor (known as BLyS or BAFF) which promotes the formation of memory B cells and autoantibodies . Belimumab inhibits this factor and therefore is used in the management of SLE. It is used in combination with either cyclophosphamide or MMF in patients with lupus nephritis who do not show response to initial therapy with steroids . CD20 is an antigen present on the B cells . Rituximab is an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody that is used in patients who are resistant to the standard therapies .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man presented with fever, malaise, skin rashes, and arthralgia. On further evaluation, his serology was positive for ANA and anti-histone antibodies . Use of which of the following drugs could have led to this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with positive ANA and anti-histone antibodies point towards a diagnosis of drug-induced lupus erythematosus . Hydralazine which is a vasodilator is associated with the development of drug-induced lupus erythematosus . Drug-induced lupus erythematosus is an autoimmune condition caused due to exposure to certain medications. It completely resolves after the causative drug is discontinued . Important drugs associated with this condition are: • Sulfonamides • Hydralazine553 • Isoniazid • Infliximab • Procainamide • Propylthiouracil • ACE inhibitors • Thiazides • TNF-alpha antagonists

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the ratio of occurrence of drug-induced lupus erythematosus in females and males?
mcqs.explanation: The female to male ratio in drug-induced lupus erythematosus (DILE) is 1:1. The female to male ratio in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is 9:1.Systemic lupus erythematosu s (SLE) Drug-induced lupus erythem atosus (DILE) Age Common in young individual s Common in elderly (50-70 ye ars) Female : male rati o 9:1 1:1 Organs involved Can affect many organs Skinis mainly involved.Renal and brain involvement arerar e Complement leve ls Reduced C3, C4 levels Normal C3, C4 levels Antibodies -Antinuclear Common Common -Antihistone Rare Common -Anti ds-DNA Common Rare

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding drug-induced lupus erythematosus ?
mcqs.explanation: Renal involvement is rare in drug-induced lupus erythematosus .Systemic lupus erythematosu s (SLE) Drug-induced lupus erythem atosus (DILE) Age Common in young individual s Common in elderly (50-70 ye ars)554 Systemic lupus erythematosu s (SLE) Drug-induced lupus erythem atosus (DILE) Female : male rati o 9:1 1:1 Organs involved Can affect many organs Skinis mainly involved.Renal and brain involvement arerar e Complement leve ls Reduced C3, C4 levels Normal C3, C4 levels Antibodies -Antinuclear Common Common -Antihistone Rare Common -Anti ds-DNA Common Rare

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Antiphospholipid syndrome is associated with all of the following except :
mcqs.explanation: Thrombocytosis is not associated with antiphospholipid syndrome (APS). On the contrary, thrombocytopenia is seen . APS is an autoantibody -mediated condition that is characterized by arterial thrombosis, venous thrombosis, and recurrent fetal loss. These autoantibodies bind to the phospholipids present on the endothelial cells and activate coagulation and thrombus formation. Important manifestations of venous thrombosis are: • Deep vein thrombosis of legs • Pulmonary embolism • Livedo reticularis • Cerebral venous thrombosis Important manifestations of arterial thrombosis are: • Stroke, transient ischemic attacks • Retinal artery thrombosis • Myocardial ischemia • Libman -Sacks endocarditis - due to the vegetations formed by platelet fibrin microthrombi • Leg ulcers , gangrene of the digits Important obstetric manifestations are: • Preeclampsia • Recurrent fetal loss • Premature birth Important hematological abnormalities are:555 • Thrombocytopenia- occurs due to increased platelet aggregation and thrombus formation • Coombs positive hemolytic anemia- seen when autoantibodies attack red blood cells • Thrombotic microangiopathic syndromes- thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP ) and hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS)

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old woman comes for evaluation of recurrent fetal losses . She has had 4 spontaneous abortions, all of them at <10 weeks of gestational age , and has a history of deep vein thrombosis. Which of the following antibodies is not useful in making a diagnosis in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history of >3 spontaneous abortions at <10 weeks of gestational age along with a history of deep vein thrombosis suggests a diagnosis of antiphospholipid syndrome (APS). Anti beta -2 microglobulin is not useful in diagnosing this condition. For the diagnosis of antiphospholipid syndrome, high titers of one or more of the following three antibodies should be demonstrated along with at least one clinical symptom of thrombosis or pregnancy complications : • Lupus anticoagulant (LA) - most specific • Anticardiolipin (aCL) antibodies - most sensitive • Anti-beta-2 glycoprotein antibodies

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man presented with painful swelling of his right calf muscle . The clinical test shown below was positive . Investigations revealed elevated D-dimer, high titres of lupus anticoagulant and anti-cardiolipin antibodies . You would use all of the following drugs for his management except :
mcqs.explanation: The given findings of positive Moses ' sign with elevated D-dimer, lupus anticoagulant, and anti-cardiolipin antibodies are suggestive of antiphospholipid syndrome (APS). Glucocorticoids are not useful in the general management of APS, they are used only in the treatment of catastrophic APS.
