Squeezing of the relaxed calf muscles from side to side is painful as the thrombosed deep veins in the calf are always tender . This test is known as Moses ' sign. The clinical manifestations in APS occur due to the activation of coagulation and thrombus formation. Therefore, anticoagulants and antiplatelet agents are the mainstays in the treatment . Important drugs used are: • Warfarin - is an anticoagulant that inhibits vitamin K dependant epoxidase . • Low molecular weight heparins (LMWH )- warfarin cannot be used in pregnancy due to its teratogenicity . In these situations , LMWH is used for anticoagulation . • Aspirin- is an antiplatelet agent . • Hydroxychloroquine- is an immunomodulatory agent that can be used to prevent recurrent thrombosis. • Statins Note : The only condition where corticosteroids are beneficial is catastrophic APS. It is a life -threatening rapidly progressive thromboembolic disease involving simultaneously three or more organs. It is seen in very few patients .556

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is associated with rheumatoid arthritis?
mcqs.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis is associated with HLA DR4.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which part of the spine is most commonly affected in patients with rheumatoid arthritis?
mcqs.explanation: The atlantoaxial joint (C1 & C2) is the most commonly affected part of the spine in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. The joints in rheumatoid arthritis are bilaterally and symmetrically involved. The commonly affected joints are: • Metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints • Wrists • Proximal interphalangeal (PIP ) joints • Metatarsophalangeal joints (MTP) joints • Atlantoaxial joint There is relative sparing of the DIP joint in rheumatoid arthritis. The involvement of DIP joints should direct suspicion towards osteoarthritis.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Identify the following deformity seen in a patient complaining of pain and swelling of her hands.
mcqs.explanation: The image is showing flexion of the PIP joint with hyperextension of the DIP joint is suggestive of Boutonni\350re deformity seen in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. Heberden 's and Bouchard's nodes are nodules in osteoarthritis that are palpable in the distal interphalangeal joint and proximal interphalangeal joints respectively .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient presents to your clinic with the following deformity . In which of the following conditions is this deformity seen ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a swan-neck deformity seen in a patient with established rheumatoid arthritis(RA ). Swan-neck deformity is hyperextension at the proximal interphalangeal (PIP ) joint and flexion at the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint. Some of the other small joint deformities of the hand in a patient with RA include :565 Boutonnie\037re deformity with flexion at the PIP joint and hyperextension at the DIP joint. Z-line deformity with hyperextension at the DIP joint and subluxation of the 1st metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: An elderly woman presents with a chronic history of pain in the small joints of hands with stiffness of joints in the early hours of the day. The image of the patient 's hands is given below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The above image shows flexion at the PIP joint and extension in the DIP joints which is known as boutonniere deformity which is seen in rheumatoid arthritis(RA ). If the patient gives a history of pain/stiffness in the joints in the early hours of the day which usually decreases as the day progresses suggesting inflammatory arthritis and if it presents with predominant involvement of smaller joints, it is most likely a case of RA(option A). It occurs due to the accumulation of inflammatory mediators which on increased joint mobility are flushed out due to increased blood supply . Pain and stiffness in osteoarthritis (Option B) usually increase as the day progresses due to an increase in the activity of the joint. They typically present with nodules around the distal interphalangeal joint (Heberden nodes ) and proximal interphalangeal joint (Bouchard nodes ).

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common extra-articular manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis?
mcqs.explanation: The most common extra-articular manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis(RA ) is subcutaneous nodules . The nodules are generally benign, non-tender, and firm, and occur in areas subjected to repeated trauma such as the forearm, sacral prominences, and Achilles tendon. They can also occur in the lungs , pleura , pericardium, and peritoneum. Patients who have a history of cigarette smoking had early onset arthritic manifestations and tested positive for RA factor or ACPA are more likely to develop extra-articular manifestations . Other common extra-articular manifestations include secondary Sjogren's syndrome, interstitial lung disease , pulmonary nodules , and anemia. FELTY'S syndrome is a triad of neutropenia , splenomegaly , and nodular RA.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which is the most common cardiac valvular lesion seen in patients with rheumatoid arthritis?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cardiac valvular lesion seen in patients with rheumatoid arthritis is mitral regurgitation.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following would you not expect to see in a patient diagnosed with Felty syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Hepatomegaly is not seen in Felty syndrome.566 Felty syndrome is defined by the clinical triad of: • Neutropenia • Splenomegaly • Rheumatoid arthritis It occurs in the late stages of rheumatoid arthritis (RA ). Other syndromes associated with rheumatoid arthritis are: • Caplan's syndrome- characterized by both rheumatoid arthritis and pneumoconiosis . It is associated with development of multiple peripheral basilar nodules in the lungs . • Secondary Sjogren's syndrome- development of keratoconjunctivitis sicca or xerostomia in association with connective tissue disorder.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which is the most common type of lymphoma seen in patients with rheumatoid arthritis?
mcqs.explanation: The most common histopathologic type of lymphoma seen in patients with rheumatoid arthritis is diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL ). The risk of developing lymphoma increases if the patient has Felty 's syndrome or high levels of disease activity.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient complains about difficulty doing chores due to morning stiffness of the joints. Investigations show elevated ESR, CRP, and positive Rheumatoid factor. Which of the following is not likely to be seen in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of rheumatoid arthritis, which is associated with hypoandrogenism. It is characterized by low levels of serum testosterone , LH , and DHEA. The conditions associated with rheumatoid arthritis are: • Cardiovascular disease , congestive heart failure • Osteoporosis - hip fractures are more likely to occur • Ocular - keratoconjunctivitis sicca, episcleritis , scleritis , keratitis • Secondary Sjogren's syndrome • Hypoandrogenism in men and postmenopausal women

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: All of the following characteristics are found in the pleural effusion fluid of a rheumatoid arthritis patient except :
mcqs.explanation: Low glucose (<60 mg/dL) is seen in the pleural effusion fluid of a patient with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). RA causes exudative pleural effusion and fulfills the Light's criteria. High LDH and RA factor are found in the pleural fluid of RA patients . Less commonly, patients with RA may have a cholesterol567 effusion . It is sterile and has a milky or opaque appearance . The milky appearance is due to the presence of cholesterol crystals and an elevated cholesterol level . Light's criteria is used to distinguish between exudative and transudative pleural effusions . An exudative pleural effusion satisfies at least one of the following criteria: • Pleural fluid protein/serum protein > 0.5 • Pleural fluid LDH / serum LDH > 0.6 • Pleural fluid LDH more than 2/3rds upper limit of normal for serum

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following radiological features would help to differentiate between rheumatoid arthritis and SLE?
mcqs.explanation: Articular erosions on X-ray is seen in rheumatoid arthritis (RA ), but not in SLE. Juxta-articular osteoporosis , swelling of PIP joint, and ulnar deviation can be seen in both SLE and RA. Jaccoud arthropathy is a deforming non-erosive arthropathy characterized by the ulnar deviation of the second to 5th fingers with metacarpophalangeal joint subluxation seen in SLE. The give X-ray shows Jaccoud's arthropathy:568 The given image shows a patient with Jaccoud's arthropathy of the hands:

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of death in patients with rheumatoid arthritis?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of death in patients with rheumatoid arthritis is cardiovascular disease .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: In a suspected case of rheumatoid arthritis, which of the following markers should be used to diagnose this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The most appropriate marker to diagnose rheumatoid arthritis (RA ) is the anti-CCP (cyclic citrullinated peptide ) antibody as it is the most specific marker for RA. Anti-CCP, ESR, and CRP values correlate with the disease activity.569 Rheumatoid factor can occur in other autoimmune diseases as well as in chronic infections . Therefore it is not considered specific .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the drug of choice for the treatment of a patient with rheumatoid arthritis?
mcqs.explanation: Methotrexate which is a DMARD is the drug of choice for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). A combination regimen is used when there is a failure to achieve adequate improvement with methotrexate only. Methotrexate in low doses causes adenosine release and suppresses joint inflammation. However, in high doses, it causes inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR).

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient with rheumatoid arthritis is being treated with methotrexate and low-dose corticosteroids for the past 4 months. However, the disease is still progressing . What would be your recommendation for the further management of this patient ?

options.a: Stop oral methotrexate and start parenteral methotrexate

mcqs.explanation: For further management of a patient with rheumatoid arthritis (RA ) with worsening disease activity, the preferred therapy is a step-up to oral triple therapy with methotrexate , sulfasalazine, and hydroxychloroquine. The addition of leflunomide or a biological (anti - TNF) to methotrexate is another alternative. Ideally , the approach to a patient with early RA is aggressive . Methotrexate is always the first DMARD that the patient is started on, and if an adequate response is not observed within 3-6 months, a step up in therapy is made by adding on drugs. For assessment of progression, composite indices like Disease Activity Score - 28 (DAS-28) can used . Other options : Option A: Changing the route of administration of methotrexate from oral to parenteral is not a part of step up Option C: Priority is given to minimising the duration the patient is on steroids . Option D: Anti -TNF agents (adalimumab, etanercept ) are not recommended as a monotherapy, and are reserved for treatment in combination with DMARDs. This is due to the fact that the efficacy of monotherapy is lesser than that of DMARDs, and the adverse effects include increased risk of serious infections , re-activation of latent TB and opportunistic fungal infections . They are reserved for cases where there is a lack of response with the first line agents .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a Janus kinase inhibitor used in patients with rheumatoid arthritis?
mcqs.explanation: The Janus kinase inhibitor used in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis is tofacitinib. Tofacitinib, baricitinib, and upadacitinib are Janus kinase inhibitors used as monotherapy or combination therapy in rheumatoid arthritis.570 Option A: Anakinra is an IL -1 antagonist. Option B: Tocilizumab is an IL -6 antagonist. Option C: Abatacept acts by inhibiting co-stimulation of T cells .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old pregnant lady visits your OPD with complaints of painful swelling of her hands since past 2 months. Investigations reveal positive rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies . Which of the following DMARDs should not be prescribed to her?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of rheumatoid arthritis (RA ). Leflunomide should not be prescribed in pregnancy as it is a category X drug. DMARDs classified as Category X in pregnancy (contraindicated in pregnancy) are: • Methotrexate • Leflunomide

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the isotype of the rheumatoid factor most commonly measured in the laboratory?
mcqs.explanation: IgM isotype is the rheumatoid factor (RF) most commonly measured in laboratories. IgM RF has been found in 75 –80% of patients with rheumatoid arthritis. IgG and IgA isotypes of RF have also been identified . However, RF is not specific for rheumatoid arthritis and can also be found in the following conditions: • Primary Sj\366gren's syndrome • Systemic lupus erythematosus • Subacute bacterial endocarditis • Hepatitis B and C

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Iritis is seen in all except :
mcqs.explanation: Iritis is seen in all the above conditions except rheumatoid arthritis. Iritis or iridocyclitis is also known as anterior uveitis. Anterior uveitis is seen in: • Ankylosing spondylitis • Juvenile rheumatoid arthritis • Psoriasis • Reactive arthritis • Systemic lupus erythematosus • Leprosy571 Posterior uveitis is seen in: • Vogt-Koyanagi Harada syndrome • Diseases like toxoplasmosis , cysticercosis , coccidioidomycosis , toxocariasis, histoplasmosis • Infections- Candida, Pneumocystis carinii , Cryptococcus , Aspergillus , and Cytomegalovirus • Cat-scratch disease , Whipple 's disease, and brucellosis Both anterior and posterior uveitis is seen in: • Sarcoidosis • Behcet 's disease • Inflammatory bowel disease • Herpes infections , Syphilis , Lyme disease , TB , onchocerciasis Intermediate uveitis/pars planitis is seen in multiple sclerosis .572

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which among the following about idiosyncratic asthma is false ?

options.d: Negative skin test for common inhalant allergens

mcqs.explanation: Idiosyncratic or intrinsic asthma does not present in childhood . It typically shows a later onset of disease (adult -onset asthma).

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 36-year-old woman presented with wheezing after taking aspirin for a headache . Which of the following is true regarding this condition?

options.b: Positive skin test for inhaled allergens

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of aspirin-sensitivity asthma. It is closely associated with nasal polyps. Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD), also known as Samter's triad or aspirin-sensitive asthma. It is a chronic medical condition that consists of: • Intrinsic asthma • Recurrent sinus disease with nasal polyps • Sensitivity to aspirin and other NSAIDs581 It has normal serum IgE levels and a negative skin test for inhaled allergens .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the best way to diagnose patients with suspected bronchial asthma?
mcqs.explanation: The best way to diagnose bronchial asthma is by the demonstration of reversible obstruction of the airways. Following the administration of an inhaled beta 2 agonist, a 12 % and 200 ml increase in the FEV1 demonstrates the reversibility of airway obstruction. Options A and B: Chest X-ray and skin test for inhaled allergens are not diagnostic of bronchial asthma. Option C: FEV1 values are measured to calculate FEV1/FVC ratio to diagnose any obstructive pathology and not specifically for asthma alone.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A young woman is rushed to ED due to wheezing and gasping for breath. She is unable to speak in full sentences . Her husband reports that she has had a cough with fever for 3 days. On examination, PR- 121 /min, RR - 32 /min, and has cyanosis. Her ABG analysis and chest X-ray are given below . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of dyspnea , tachycardia along with the ABG analysis suggestive of respiratory alkalosis and chest -Xray showing hyperinflated lungs is pointing to a diagnosis of acute severe asthma. A history of cough with fever is indicating a probable respiratory infection to have triggered the asthma exacerbation. Features of acute severe asthma vs asthma with impending respiratory failure: Note : The X-ray is not showing the features of ARDS and pneumothorax, hence they are ruled out as the right options .Acute severe asthma Asthma with impending respi ratory failure Dyspneic , speaks in words Mute patient Agitated patient Silent / confused patient Heart rate > 120 /min, tachyc ardia Relative bradycardia Pulsus paradoxus present Pulsus paradoxus absent (du e to respiratory muscle fatigu e) Accessory muscles of respirat ion used Paradoxical breathing is seen Loud wheeze throughout the respiration Silent chest Peak expiratory flow rate < 4 0 ml/min Peak expiratory flow rate < 2 5 ml/min Respiratory alkalosis Respiratory acidosis Hyperventilation leading to l ow or normal PaCO2 Normal or rising PaCO2582

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is not recommended in the treatment of patients with bronchial asthma?
mcqs.explanation: Roflumilast is a phosphodiesterase -4 inhibitor used in the treatment of COPD, not asthma. Drugs used in the treatment of bronchial asthma Bronchodilators • Beta-2 sympathomimetics : Salmeterol , formoterol • Methylxanthines : Theophylline , aminophylline • Anticholinergics : Ipratropium bromide, tiotropium bromide Anti-inflammatory • Corticosteroids (inhalational): Beclomethasone , budesonide , fluticasone • Corticosteroids (systemic ): Prednisolone, hydrocortisone • Mast cell stabilizers: Sodium cromoglycate , ketotifen • Leukotriene antagonists: Montelukast, zafirlukast • Anti-IgE: Omalizumab • Anti-IL5 : Mepolizumab , reslizumab • Anti-IL4 receptor : Dupilumab

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding leukotriene modifiers in the management of bronchial asthma?
mcqs.explanation: Ketotifen is an example of a mast cell stabilizer, not leukotriene modifiers. Leukotriene modifiers are a group of agents used for mild persistent asthma. They block LT1 -receptors thus causing reduced eosinophilic inflammation and causing bronchodilator. They include montelukast , zafirlukast, and zileuton . Leukotriene modifiers are less effective than inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in controlling asthma. They are used as add-on therapy in some patients whose asthma is not controlled with low doses of ICS. Churg–Strauss syndrome (CSS) is a rare granulomatous small vessel vasculitis, that affects the heart, kidneys, peripheral nerves, etc . It occurs against a background of long-standing asthma and marked peripheral eosinophilia . Several cases of CSS are associated with the use of montelukast and zafirlukast.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Treatment of choice for patients with type 2 brittle asthma is:
mcqs.explanation: The treatment of choice for type II brittle asthma is subcutaneous adrenaline.583 Brittle asthma is a type of severe asthma where patients have very serious and often , life -threatening attacks despite appropriate therapy . It is of two types :Type 1 Type 2 A persistent pattern of variab ility in PEFR (peak expirator y flow rate) readings Generally normal or near-nor mal PEFR readings but few u npredictable exacerbations o ccur without an obvious trigg er Oral steroids , infusion of bro nchodilators, and dietary excl usion of allergens may be hel pful Respond only to subcutaneou s epinephrine

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following class of drugs cannot be used in the treatment of patients with bronchial asthma?
mcqs.explanation: The treatment options for asthma do not include IL -1 antagonists (anakinra ). Anakinra is used in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis. Cytokines mediating airway inflammation in asthma: IL -4, IL -5, IL -13 , TGF-\031, and chemokines. Omalizumab is a monoclonal antibody against IgE. It is available for the treatment of children \0376 years of age with documented allergen -induced asthma that is inadequately controlled by inhaled corticosteroids . The new treatment options for asthma under clinical trial are: • Mepolizumab : anti–IL -5 antibody • Benralizumab: anti–IL -5 receptor antibody • Dupilumab : anti–IL -4 receptor antibody

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 6-year-old asthmatic boy is rushed to the casualty . He is not responding to the commands and is having fast shallow breathing. On auscultation , the chest is silent and paradoxical breathing is present . ABG analysis shows respiratory acidosis. What is the best step in management for him?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of severe asthma with impending respiratory failure. The best step in the management is immediate endotracheal intubation. Features of asthma with impending respiratory failure are: • Mute or confused patient • Paradoxical breathing • Silent chest on auscultation • Relative bradycardia • Peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) <25ml/min • Arterial blood gas analysis shows respiratory acidosis.584 Option A: Hyperbaric oxygen is given in CO poisoning and high altitude pulmonary edema . Option B: MDI with salbutamol and corticosteroids is only useful for acute severe asthma. Option D: Intravenous magnesium sulfate is not routinely used .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding COPD?

options.a: Increased resistance is seen in airways \0262 mm diameter
options.b: Changes in large airways cause cough and sputum

mcqs.explanation: The rise in post -bronchodilator FEV1>12 % is a feature of asthma, not COPD. It suggests reversible airflow obstruction. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a chronic respiratory disease characterized by the presence of airflow obstruction that is partially reversible. Cigarette smoking is the most common cause of COPD. Cigarette smoke exposure affects large airways, small airways, and alveoli: • Changes in large airways cause cough and sputum • Changes in small airways (\0262mm ) and alveoli are responsible for physiologic alterations The major site of increased resistance in most individuals with COPD is in airways \0262 mm diameter. Characteristic cellular changes include goblet cell metaplasia . Goblet cells are mucus-secreting cells that replace surfactant-secreting Club cells . Nonuniform ventilation and ventilation-perfusion mismatching are characteristic of COPD.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What happens to Reid index in patients with chronic bronchitis?
mcqs.explanation: Reid index is increased in chronic bronchitis. Reid index is the ratio of the thickness of the mucous gland layer to the thickness of the bronchial wall.585

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following findings is least likely to be seen in patients with COPD?
mcqs.explanation: Clubbing is not a sign of COPD. Its presence should trigger the investigation of the causes of clubbing, particularly lung cancer. Signs of COPD: • Signs of respiratory distress • Tripod posture - facilitates the use of accessory muscles of respiration • Pursed lip breathing - seen in emphysema • Central cyanosis • Signs of cachexia • Severe weight loss • Bitemporal wasting • Signs of hypercapnia (type 2 respiratory failure) - more common in chronic bronchitis • Barrel-shaped chest - increase in the anteroposterior diameter • Enlarged lung volumes • Positive Hoover's sign - paradoxical inward movement of the chest during inspiration • Early inspiratory coarse crackles • Normal vesicular breath sounds of reduced -intensity with bilaterally prolonged expiration • Blue bloaters - cyanotic (blue ) and edematous (bloaters ), chronic bronchitis predominant features • Pink puffers - thin, non-cyanotic (pink) at rest, and severely dyspneic (puffers ), emphysema predominant features586 Causes of clubbing : • Pulmonary • Bronchogenic carcinoma • Lung abscess , empyema , bronchiectasis • Chronic interstitial pneumonitis • Cystic fibrosis • Sarcoidosis • Gastrointestinal • Inflammatory bowel disease • Sprue • Neoplasms - esophagus , liver, bowel • Cardiovascular • Cyanotic congenital heart disease • Subacute bacterial endocarditis • Aortic aneurysm • Arteriovenous fistula • Endocrine • Hyperthyroidism (Grave's disease ) The image below shows the characteristic tripod posture in a patient with COPD.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old coal miner presented with breathing difficulties . He reported that his symptoms get aggravated at work. His chest X-ray showed features of emphysema . On evaluation, he was found to have an \0301-antitrypsin deficiency . Which pathological type of emphysema is most likely present in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: 587 The pathological type most likely to be present in this patient is pan-acinar emphysema . This type is commonly seen in patients with \0301-antitrypsin deficiency .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: An elderly man is being evaluated for exertional dyspnea , cough , and weight loss. His chest CT is given below . What is it suggestive of?
mcqs.explanation: The CT scan shows emphysematous lungs, with reduced parenchymal markings and focal areas of low attenuation . This represents the emphysematous destruction of the lung, indicative of hyperinflation . Radiographic studies in COPD show: • Emphysematous bullae • A paucity of parenchymal markings • Hyperlucency suggests the presence of emphysema • Increased lung volumes and flattening of the diaphragm suggest hyperinflation Option B: Atypical pneumonia shows patchy bilateral ground-glass opacities . Option C: Calcified granulomas are seen as dense , bright nodules . Option D: Interstitial fibrosis shows a honeycomb pattern of the lung parenchyma as shown below .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 55 -years old chronic smoker presented with chronic cough with expectoration . He has been having similar episodes for the past 2 years. He also reported that he had to rest every few minutes while walking due to breathlessness . Pulmonary function tests showed FEV1/FVC of 0.5 and FEV1 of 50%. Which of the following is not a feature of the given condition?

options.d: Associated with ineffective repair of elastin

mcqs.explanation: The clinical picture is highly suggestive of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). An increase in the residual volume is a feature of COPD. COPD is defined as a chronic respiratory disease characterized by the presence of airflow obstruction that is partially reversible.588 COPD is the clinical expression of abnormalities of airways and/or alveoli and includes : • Emphysema is defined pathologically as the abnormal and permanent dilation of airways distal to the terminal bronchiole, along with the destruction of their walls . • Chronic bronchitis is defined clinically as the presence of persistent cough with sputum production on most of the days for \0373 months in 2 consecutive years. • Small airways diseases are conditions affecting airways of \0262 mm, resulting in inflammation and narrowing of the same.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Chest X-ray of an emphysematous patient is as shown. What is the best investigation to measure his lung volume?
mcqs.explanation: Body plethysmography is the best investigation to measure lung volume in an emphysematous patient with bullous lesions as seen on the X-ray. To measure absolute lung volumes, two techniques are used : • Body plethysmography : It is used to measure the volume of any gas containing space in the thorax including bullae . It is accurate in both obstructive and restrictive diseases . • Inert gas dilution technique : It is used to measure the volume of regions that are well ventilated which excludes trapped gas or bullae . It is accurate in restrictive diseases only. The amount of gas trapped in bullae can be measured by subtracting lung volumes measured by inert gas dilution technique from lung volume measured by body plethysmography . Fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FENO ) is a non-invasive test used in the diagnosis and monitoring of bronchial asthma. NO levels are increased in asthmatics and related to the eosinophilic inflammation in the airways.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 66-year-old chronic smoker presents with progressive shortness of breath and chronic cough . On examination, he has a barrel chest and has pursed -lip breathing. Hyperresonance and inspiratory wheezes are heard. Pulmonary functions are likely to reveal all of the following , except :

options.b: Increased diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical diagnosis is suggestive of COPD and the underlying pathological change is likely to be emphysema . It is associated with a decreased diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO). Emphysema is defined pathologically as the abnormal and permanent dilation of airways distal to the terminal bronchiole, along with the destruction of their walls . This leads to hyperinflation due to air trapping and impaired diffusion of gases . Pulmonary function tests in COPD: • TLC : Normal or increased • FEV1: Decreased (<80% predicted ) • FVC: Decreased • FEV1/FVC: Decreased • DLCO: Decreased Diseases associated with lowered DLCO:589 • Emphysema • Interstitial Lung disease • Primary pulmonary hypertension Note - Bronchial asthma is associated with an increased DLCO.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: The Gold's criteria for severe COPD are:
mcqs.explanation: Gold's criteria for severe COPD (stage III ) are FEV1/FVC <0.7 and FEV1 \037 30% but <50% The severity of COPD is assessed by Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) classification: Note : FEV1/FVC and FEV1 predicted are measured after the administration of a bronchodilator.GOLD S tage Severity Spirometry I Mild FEV1/FVC <0.7 and FEV1 \0378 0% predicted II Moderate FEV1/FVC <0.7 and FEV1 \0375 0% but <80% predicted III Severe FEV1/FVC <0.7 and FEV1 \0373 0% but <50% predicted IV Very seve re FEV1/FVC <0.7 and FEV1 <3 0% predictedRecent update : PRISm refers to a group of COPD patients with apparent normal spirometry, but with emphysema (as seen on radiographic evaluation) and a wide range of lung function impairment. These patients have a higher mortality risk as compared to other COPD patients . The possible risk factors are exposure to smoking, high BMI, and reduced total lung capacity . Spirometry findings are low to normal FEV1, and normal FEV1/FVC ratio.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient presents to the OPD with shortness of breath. He reports walking slower than his peers due to breathlessness . He has had two hospitalizations for similar complaints this year. His post -bronchodilator PFTs are FEV1/FVC < 0.55 and FEV1 55 %. Under what category would he be classified based on GOLD criteria?
mcqs.explanation: This patient belongs to moderate COPD, group E category . The severity of COPD assessed by the Global Initiative for Lung Disease (GOLD) is classified as: According to GOLD 2023 guidelines , COPD patients are classified into Group A, B, or E based on the severity of dyspnoea , frequency of exacerbations and hospitilization . Dyspnoea may be assessed using the modified MRC Dyspnoea scale or COPD Assessment Test (CAT score) * single inhaler therapy maybe more convenient and effective than multiple inhalers ICS - inhaled corticosteroids LAMA - Long-acting Muscarinic Antagonists590 LABA - Long-acting Beta Agonists Modified MRC (mMRC) dyspnoea scale : • 0- Breathless only with strenuous exercise • 1- Breathless when hurrying on a level or walking up a hill • 2- Walks slower than peers or has to stop for breath when walking on level • 3- Stops for breath after walking about 100m or for a few minutes • 4- Breathless at restGOLD S tage Severity Spirometry I Mild FEV1/FVC <0.7 and FEV1 \0378 0% predicted II Moderate FEV1/FVC <0.7 and FEV1 \0375 0% but <80% predicted III Severe FEV1/FVC <0.7 and FEV1 \0373 0% but <50% predicted IV Very seve re FEV1/FVC <0.7 and FEV1 <3 0% predicted>=2 moderate exacerbations or >=1 leading to hospitalisat ion Group E:LABA +LAMAconsid er LABA +LAMA+ICS* if bloo d eosinophil count >=3000 or 1 moderate exacerbation (not leading to hospital admi ssions) Group A: mMRC 0-1, CAT<1 0Bronchodilator Group B: mMRC >=2, CAT >=10LABA + LAMA*

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding acute exacerbations in COPD patients ?

options.a: May not be accompanied with fever
options.b: Viral infection is a common precipitating factor
options.d: May present with congestive heart failure

mcqs.explanation: Glucocorticoids are used during an exacerbation of COPD. They hasten recovery and reduce the chances of future exacerbations. Exacerbations are episodes of increased dyspnoea and cough , with a change in the amount and character of sputum . They are often triggered by an infection with one-third of cases having a viral etiology . They may or may not have other signs of illness such as fever, myalgias, and sore throat. In severe cases , they may present with pneumonia and congestive heart failure. Note : While oral glucocorticoids are contraindicated in long-term treatment due to side effects , they are used for acute exacerbation of COPD.591

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old male patient who is a known case of COPD presented with acute exacerbation and is admitted to the ICU. Which of the following statements is correct with regards to the initial management of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Non-invasive positive pressure ventilation (NIPPV ) should be the first mode of ventilation used in COPD patients with acute respiratory failure provided there are no absolute contraindications. This approach improves gas exchange , reduces work of breathing and the need for intubation, decreases hospitalization duration and enhances overall survival outcomes . Invasive positive pressure ventilation is only considered after failure of NIPPV , resulting in severe respiratory distress , life threatening hypoxemia , severe hypercarbia and/or acidosis, markedly impaired mental status , respiratory arrest or hemodynamic instability (Option B). Apart from NIPPV , short-acting inhaled beta 2 agonists (albuterol , salbutamol ) with or without short-acting anticholinergics (ipratropium) and Long-acting anticholinergics (tiotropium) are recommended as the initial bronchodilators. Maintenance therapy with long-acting beta 2 agonists (formoterol) must be started as soon as possible . Systemic corticosteroids are useful in the treatment of acute exacerbations of COPD as they reduce airway inflammation and improve lung function over time. However, the effects are not immediate . NIPPV on the other hand provides immediate relief to the patient and reduces the work of breathing. Therefore, it would not be the best choice in this case. (Option C) Antibiotics can also be considered , as they reduce duration of hospitalisation . Treatment is given for 5 days. Permissive hypercapnia refers to a ventilation strategy where tidal volume is reduced in order to avoid hyperinflation-associated lung trauma. It is not preferred at the initial presentation . It is only permitted once invasive PPV is started following NIPPV failure (Option D) An exacerbation of COPD is defined as an event characterized by dyspnea and/or cough and sputum that worsen over < 14 days. Exacerbations of COPD are often associated with increased local and systemic inflammation caused by airway infection , pollution , or other insults to the lungs .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old obese chronic smoker is rushed to the ER with difficulty in breathing and a productive cough . He has a past history of two similar episodes this year. On examination, RR - 34/min, with use of accessory muscles and central cyanosis is present . ABG is as shown. Chest X-ray shows increased vascular markings . What is the best initial step of management?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with the ABG and X-ray findings is suggestive of acute exacerbation of COPD with respiratory failure. The best initial step of management is low-flow humidified oxygen . Oxygen supplementation is a crucial component of acute therapy . Administering O2 should target a SpO2 - -92% or PaO2- 60-70 mmHg. This helps to minimize the risk of worsening hypercapnia with excess supplemental oxygen . The given ABG shows respiratory acidosis as PaCO2 >45 mmHg, and pH<7.35. In respiratory acidosis , a trial of non-invasive ventilation is given. Hence , low-flow humidified oxygen is the first step in management. Option B: High flow oxygen causes dryness , crusting epistaxis , and damages the lung hence not used . Option C: Salbutamol and budesonide nebulization are not effective as initial management in exacerbation of COPD with respiratory failure.592 Option D: Methylxanthines are not recommended in the management of acute exacerbations due to their side effect profiles .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: In patients with which of the following conditions is NIPPV contraindicated ?
mcqs.explanation: Noninvasive positive -pressure ventilation (NIPPV ) is contraindicated in cardiovascular instability . NIPPV can impede venous filling of the heart, decrease cardiac output , and worsen/precipitate hypotension . Moreover, in unstable states with impending cardiovascular collapse , invasive ventilation is preferred . Indications of NIPPV : • Apnea - central and obstructive • Central hypoventilation syndrome • Neuromuscular and chest wall disorders • Respiratory failure - PaCO2 >45 mmHg Contraindications of NIPPV : • Cardiovascular instability • Impaired mental status or inability to cooperate • Copious secretions or the inability to clear secretions • Craniofacial abnormalities • Trauma precluding effective fitting of the mask

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not used in the long-term treatment of COPD patients ?
mcqs.explanation: Oral glucocorticoids are not used in the long-term treatment of COPD because of an unfavorable benefit /risk ratio. Chronic use of glucocorticoids is associated with significant side effects , including osteoporosis , weight gain, cataracts, glucose intolerance, and increased risk of infection . Treatment of COPD: • Smoking cessation • Anticholinergic agents - Ipratropium bromide • Beta Agonists- Long-acting inhaled \031 agonists, such as salmeterol or formoterol are commonly used . • Methylxanthines - theophylline produces improvements in expiratory flow rates and vital capacity . • Phosphodiesterase inhibitors - roflumilast is used when FEV1<50%. • Antibiotics- macrolides like azithromycin reduce exacerbations when used over one year593 • N-acetylcysteine has been used in patients with COPD for both its mucolytic and antioxidant properties • Oxygen therapy Non-pharmacologic therapies : • Lung volume reduction surgery • Lung transplantation594

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms can cause both typical and atypical pneumonia?
mcqs.explanation: Legionella pneumonia presents as both typical and atypical pneumonia. Pneumonia is an infection of the lung parenchyma. Pneumonia that develops outside the hospital setting is commonly referred to as community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). There are two types of community-acquired pneumonia. • Typical Pneumonia • Atypical Pneumonia

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: There is an outbreak of legionella pneumonia in the hospital . Which of the following is least likely to have played a role in the transmission of the organism?
mcqs.explanation: Home split air-conditioning units do not use water to cool the air, so they are not a risk factor for legionella transmission. The following are the risk factors for transmission of legionella : • Contamination of water supplies in large facilities such as hospitals , hotels , apartment buildings • Contaminated water sources such as hot tubs , birthing pools , fountains, whirlpools • Water using machinery- cooling towers, evaporative condensers , humidifiers

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old smoker presents with high-grade fever, shortness of breath, diarrhea, and confusion. Gram-staining of the sputum revealed neutrophilia with no organisms. Chest x-ray showed bilateral multilobar infiltrates . Lab values are given below . Which pathogenic agent is suspected ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is highly suggestive of atypical pneumonia caused by legionella . Clinical features of Legionnaire's disease: • High-grade-fever( >104 F) • Cough with scanty sputum • Extrapulmonary manifestations involve • gastrointestinal - diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting • neurological - most common-confusion, headache , encephalopathy603 • Relative bradycardia • Occurrence of illness in an environment in which water supply is at risk of contamination • Failure to respond to beta -lactams and aminoglycoside antibiotics Investigations: • On gram-staining of the sputum , numerous neutrophils with no organisms • Hyponatremia • Elevated liver enzymes

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Urinary antigen detection test is recommended for diagnosing patients with?
mcqs.explanation: A urinary antigen detection test is recommended for the diagnosis of Legionella pneumonia. The sensitivity (70%) and specificity (99%) of the test are high. The test can detect antigen even after the initiation of appropriate antibiotic therapy . Urinary antigen detection test can also be used for Streptococcus pneumonia but is not used due to the availability of better alternatives. Other investigations for Legionella : • DFA (direct fluorescent antibody)- is highly specific but not sensitive • Culture - Gold standard, BCYE media is used • DNA detection with PCR Treatment: Drugs of choice are azithromycin and respiratory fluoroquinolones (levofloxacin, moxifloxacin).

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man presents with fever, cough with scanty sputum , and fatigue . He had a throat infection a week ago. His blood investigations and chest X-ray are given below . Which is the most likely causative agent for his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with chest X-ray and lab values is suggestive of atypical pneumonia caused by Mycoplasma pneumoniae . The blood investigations show decreased hemoglobin , elevated LDH , and elevated unconjugated bilirubin suggestive of hemolytic anemia. Mycoplasma is the most common bacteria causing atypical pneumonia and the second most common cause of pneumonia. Clinical Presentation: • Pulmonary manifestations : • URTI - tracheobronchitis/ pharyngitis • Pneumonia( seen in only 10 % patients) • Extrapulmonary manifestations : • Cold agglutinin disease ( IgM mediated autoimmune hemolytic anemia) • Erythema multiforme or Steven Johnson syndrome604 • Arthralgia with adenopathy • Guillain Barre Syndrome • Myocarditis • Pericarditis • Encephalitis • Bullous myringitis Chest X-ray shows patchy consolidation at the hilum and fanning to the periphery . Azithromycin is the drug of choice . Doxycycline is the second -best drug for the management of atypical pneumonia.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true for patients with Mycoplasma pneumonia?

options.a: Causative organism cannot be cultured routinely
options.b: Diffuse infiltrates in the lung are seen
options.c: Cefotaxime is the drug of choice

mcqs.explanation: Cefotaxime is not the drug of choice for the treatment of Mycoplasma pneumonia. Cefotaxime is a cell -wall synthesis inhibitor, hence it is not effective on M.pnemoniae as they lack a cell wall. Investigations: • PCR of respiratory secretions • Chest X-ray shows - • Patchy consolidation at the hilum and fanning to the periphery • Diffuse peribronchial and perivascular interstitial infiltrates • Airspace consolidation • Reticulonodular opacification • HRCT shows - areas of ground-glass attenuation • On PPLO agar (Dienes method ) shows- fried-egg appearance . The diagnosis is made by serology /PCR. Azithromycin is the drug of choice for management. Doxycycline is the second -best drug for the management of atypical pneumonia.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A chronic alcoholic presents to the OPD with fever, shortness of breath, chest pain, and productive cough . On examination, there is bronchial breathing on the right side and a dull note on percussion . A chest x-ray is done. What is the most likely causative agent ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and chest X-ray are suggestive of lobar pneumonia caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae. Klebsiella pneumonia is associated mostly with alcoholics and shows upper lobe involvement. The patients present with red-currant jelly sputum . Chest X-ray shows : • Cavitation • Pneumatocele (also seen in S. aureus)605 • Bulging fissure sign: Classically seen in Klebsiella pneumonia. It represents expansive lobar consolidation causing fissural bulging ; or displacement of copious amounts of inflammatory exudates within the affected parenchyma. It is seen in any space -occupying process in the lung such as pulmonary hemorrhage, lung abscess , and lung tumors.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 3-month-old male child was brought with a history of fever and respiratory distress . Suspecting pneumonia, a chest X-ray was ordered . Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The most likely causative agent of pneumonia in an infant with X-ray showing pneumatoceles (air-filled cysts within lung parenchyma) is Staphylococcus aureus. In newborns and infants, S. aureus is a significant cause of severe respiratory tract infections , presenting with dyspnea , fever, and respiratory failure. Community-acquired infections are often preceded by viral infections , most commonly influenza. Among adults , nosocomial S. aureus pulmonary infections are frequently observed in intubated patients within intensive care units. S. aureus often causes necrotizing pneumonitis that may be associated with complications such as pneumothorax and empyema . Pneumatocoele can also be caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae , Haemophilus influenzae , E. coli, group A streptococci , Klebsiella pneumoniae , etc . However, Staphylococcus aureus is most commonly implicated . Other options : Option A: Klebsiella pneumoniae causes lobar pneumonia in alcoholics and diabetics . Patients present with fever, dyspnea , and a productive cough with red currant jelly sputum . Classic chest X-ray findings include upper lobe consolidation, classically on the right side , cavitation, and bulging fissure sign. The following image shows bulging fissure sign:606 Option B: Streptococcus pneumoniae causes lobar pneumonia. Patients with pneumococcal pneumonia present with fever, dyspnea, and productive cough . On examination, the involved lobes are dull to percussion , bronchial breath sounds , and crackles are heard on auscultation . The following image shows right lower lobe consolidation:Option C: Mycoplasma pneumoniae causes atypical pneumonia. Patients present with dry cough , fever, chills, malaise, and upper respiratory tract symptoms . On auscultation , wheezes or rales are heard. Chest X-ray shows peribronchial pneumonia with prominent bronchial markings , interstitial infiltration, and atelectasis . The below chest X-ray shows patchy consolidation at the hilum and fanning to the periphery :607

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the best biomarker for lobar pneumonia?
mcqs.explanation: The best biomarker for lobar pneumonia is procalcitonin. The most commonly used biomarkers of severe inflammation are C-reactive protein (CRP) and procalcitonin (PCT). Levels of these acute phase reactants increase in the presence of bacterial pathogens . PCT testing distinguishes between bacterial (mostly lobar pneumonia) and viral infection to decide the need for antibacterial therapy or discontinuation of treatment . CRP, fibrinogen, and serum amyloid A are other acute phase reactants.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: All are components of CURB65 except

options.c: Blood urea nitrogen value greater than 7 mmol/L
options.d: Systolic blood pressure less than 100 mm Hg

mcqs.explanation: Among the options , systolic blood pressure less than 100 mm Hg (Option D) is not a component of CURB-65. CURB65 includes blood pressure , systolic \02690 mmHg or diastolic \02660 mmHg. CURB-65 criteria is used to assess the severity of illness in a case community-acquired pneumonia. It includes confusion (C), urea >7 mmol/L (U), respiratory rate \03730/min (R), blood pressure systolic \02690 mmHg or diastolic \02660 mmHg (B) and an age of \03765 years. Pneumonia severity index (PSI) is another index to assess the severity of illness and the risk of mortality in the case of pneumonia. It includes 20 variables and depending on the score, patients are assigned into one of the 5 classes . Class, I, II , III - at low risk of death and can be treated on an outpatient basis Class IV & V require hospitalization

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 71-year-old man presents to the OPD with high-grade fever, productive cough . On examination , the respiratory rate was found to be 32 / min, heart rate of 102 / min, and blood pressure of 90/60 mmHg. How will you manage this patient ?

options.a: Admit to ICU and treat with azithromycin and ceftriaxone
options.b: Admit to the ward and treat with levofloxacin and doxycycline
options.c: Treat him on OP basis with azithromycin and ceftriaxone
options.d: Admit to the ward and treat with azithromycin and levofloxacin

mcqs.explanation: 608 The given clinical scenario is highly suggestive of lobar pneumonia and the patient belongs to a CURB-65 score of 3. The patient can be best managed by a combination of azithromycin and ceftriaxone in an ICU setting . After culture sensitivity , specific management is done.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient in the ICU is diagnosed with community acquired-MRSA. What is the best line of management ?
mcqs.explanation: The Empiric treatment of choice for ICU in patients with suspected CA-MRSA is: • \031-lactam (e.g., ceftriaxone ) + Fluoroquinolone/Azithromycin PLUS • Linezolid / Vancomycin with or without Clindamycin to cover CA-MRSA

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: An epileptic patient presented with fever, breathlessness , and productive cough for 2 days. The last episode of seizures occurred a week ago. On examination, PR-102 /min, RR -30/min, and oral cavity revealed a gingival infection . Bronchial breath sounds were heard on auscultation on the right side . What is the drug of choice for his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is highly suggestive of lobar pneumonia due to aspiration. The drug of choice is clindamycin as anaerobes are implicated . Anaerobes play a significant role only when an episode of aspiration has occurred days to weeks before presentation for pneumonia. The combination of an unprotected airway (e.g., in patients with alcohol or drug overdose or a seizure disorder) and significant gingivitis constitutes the major risk factor. Anaerobic pneumonia is often complicated by abscess formation and significant empyemas or parapneumonic effusions .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old HIV -positive man presents with fever for 3 weeks , dry cough , and significant weight loss. He complains of retrosternal chest pain that is worse on inspiration. His chest X-ray is given below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The most likely diagnosis in a case of pneumonia in a HIV positive patient , along with the presence of fever, and non-productive cough with radiographic findings of diffuse interstitial infiltrates and symmetric perihilar involvement is Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP). A characteristic feature of PCP is retrosternal chest pain, which worsens on inspiration and is described as sharp or burning. It is important to note that even though the incidence of PCP is the highest at CD4+ counts of <200 /�ML (80%), it can be seen in patients with higher counts. Other options : Option D: Tuberculosis (TB ) should be considered as a possibility in cases of pneumonia in people living with HIV . However, the absence of hilar lymph node involvement, non-productive cough , and no extrapulmonary (pleural , pericardial, lymphatic ) features are not consistent with tuberculosis . TB can occur at any stage of HIV infection . In the early stages , pulmonary TB appears typically with upper -lobe infiltrates and cavitation. In advanced HIV infection , with CD4+ T- cell count below 200 / �M L, TB presents with diffuse interstitial infiltrates , minimal cavitation, pleural effusion ,609 and lymphadenopathy . Extrapulmonary TB is fairly common in HIV , with it being documented in 40-60% of cases .Option A: Staphylococcal pneumonia most commonly presents with a productive cough , and radiologically presents with pneumatoceles (cavitations)Option B: Patients with pneumococcal pneumonia also present with fever, dyspnea , and productive cough . Imaging usually shows lobar involvement.610

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: In an immunocompromised patient , which of the following is the drug of choice for prophylaxis of pneumocystis jirovecii?
mcqs.explanation: Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole combination (commonly known as cotrimoxazole) is the first-line drug for both prophylaxis and treatment of Pneumocystis jirovecii infections in immunocompromised patients . Cotrimoxazole acts by causing a sequential block of folate metabolism . CD4+ T cell counts below 200 cells /�ML are an indication to start prophylaxis.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding patients with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia?

options.a: Glucocorticoids are indicated if Pao2 <70 mmHg
options.b: Recent oropharyngeal candidiasis is an indication for prophylaxis
options.c: Elevation of LDH is a common finding
options.d: Aerosolized pentamidine is used in the treatment

mcqs.explanation: Aerosolised pentamidine is not used in the treatment of PCP. It is used in PCP prophylaxis . Diagnosis of PCP: • Histopathological staining of induced sputum examination • Bronchoscopy with BAL (most sensitive) • Elevated LDH Treatment and Prophylaxis: • Drug of choice - trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) • IV pentamidine - treatment of choice for severe disease in the patient unable to tolerate TMP-SMX • Glucocorticoids - indicated if PaO2 <70 mmHg or with an A–a gradient >35 mmHg • Other drugs used - dapsone /pyrimethamine + leucovorin, clindamycin/primaquine, and atovaquone • Aerosolised pentamidine is an alternative used in PCP prophylaxis.611 Prophylaxis is indicated when CD4+ T cell count <200/uL ( CD4 cell %<15), recent oropharyngeal candidiasis, and prior PCP infection .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 36-year-old male HIV patient presents to the ED with a cough with bloody sputum . He also has night sweats, chills, and difficulty in breathing. A chest X-ray and examination of the sputum show the following findings. Which of the following is the drug of choice for his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with the chest X-ray and gram-staining is suggestive of Nocardiosis. The drug of choice is cotrimoxazole. Nocardia is a gram-positive and acid-fast bacteria. Nocardia pneumonia has a sub-acute presentation with mostly cough with thick sputum and fever. Generally , hemoptysis is uncommon. Chest radiography shows nodular infiltrations involving bilateral lung fields . Extrapulmonary manifestations are common, the brain is the most commonly involved organ. It is associated with dense bilateral infiltrates with cavitating nodules and subacute brain abscesses . The drug of choice is cotrimoxazole. Severe disease is treated with a combination of cotrimoxazole, amikacin , and ceftriaxone , or imipenem . Note : Mnemonic SNAP: Sulfamethoxazole -trimethoprim (Cotrimoxazole) is the drug of choice for Nocardia. For Actinomyces , Penicillins are the drugs of choice .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is commonly used for treating community-acquired pneumonia in OPD?
mcqs.explanation: Azithromycin is the drug of choice for treatment of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in an OPD setup . Outpatient management of CAP: 1. For previously healthy patients who have not taken antibiotics within the past 3 months: • A macrolide – Azithromycin, 500 mg orally as a first dose and then 250 mg orally daily for 4 days, or 500 mg orally daily for 3 days, or • Clarithromycin, 500 mg orally twice a day; or • Doxycycline 100 mg orally twice a day 2. For patients with such comorbid medical conditions as chronic heart, lung, liver, or kidney disease , diabetes mellitus , alcoholism, malignancy, asplenia , immunosuppressant conditions or use of immunosuppressive drugs or use of antibiotics within the previous 3 months: • A respiratory fluoroquinolone (moxifloxacin, 400 mg orally daily; gemifloxacin , 320 mg orally daily; levofloxacin, 750 mg orally daily) or • A macrolide (as above) plus a beta -lactam (amoxicillin, 1 g orally three times a day; amoxicillin-clavulanate, 2 g orally twice a day ; cefuroxime , mg orally twice a day). 3. In regions with a high rate (> 25%) of infection with high level (MIC \037 16 mcg/mL) macrolide-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae , consider the use of alternative agents listed in (2) for patients with comorbidities .612 Other options : Vancomycin , Ceftriaxone, and Streptomycin are administered parenterally , and hence , not appropriate for outpatient management.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most likely causative organism of ventilator-associated pneumonia among the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , Acinetobacter species is the most commonly isolated organism in cases of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP). VAP develops in a mechanically ventilated patient >48 hours after endotracheal intubation. The organisms causing ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) significantly vary from one hospital to another. However, the organisms that frequently cause VAP in hospital settings are Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter sp., Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, and gram-negative rods (Enterobacter species , K. pneumoniae , and Escherichia coli). Three factors distinguish nosocomial pneumonia from community-acquired pneumonia: • Different infectious agent • Different antibiotic susceptibility patterns, specifically , a higher incidence of drug resistance • Poorer underlying health status of patients putting them at risk for more severe infections Within 48 hours of admission, % of seriously ill hospitalized patients have their upper airway colonized with organisms from the hospital environment. Impaired cellular and mechanical defense mechanisms in the lungs of hospitalized patients raise the risk of infection after aspiration has occurred. VAP patients may be infected with Acinetobacter species and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia. Anaerobic organisms (Bacteroides , anaerobic streptococci , Fusobacterium ) may also cause pneumonia in the hospitalized patient .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding patients with parapneumonic effusion ?

options.b: pH <7.2 may be a finding in pleural fluid analysis
options.c: Pleural fluid protein >4 gm/dL is an indication of tube thoracostomy
options.d: USG is helpful in characterizing the effusion

mcqs.explanation: Pleural Fluid Protein >4 gm/dL is not an indication of tube thoracostomy. Parapneumonic effusion is pleural effusion associated with bacterial pneumonia, lung abscess , or bronchiectasis. When it worsens, it can result in the collection of frank pus in the pleural space . This is known as empyema . Risk factors include diabetes , immunosuppression , alcoholism, cancer, and poor dental hygiene . Investigations: • Chest X-ray: • Loculations or encystments (complicated parapneumonic effusion ) • Intrapleural air-fluid level (bronchopulmonary fistula ) • Parenchymal infiltrations (underlying pneumonia) • Ultrasound : Shows echogenic pleural fluid with septations and helps in characterizing the effusion613 • Pleural fluid analysis: • Exudative neutrophilic effusion • Low pH <7.2, low glucose <60 mg/dL, high LDH >1000 IU/L in complicated parapneumonic effusion • CECT: Split pleura sign seen in empyema Treatment: • Antibiotics: Tailored according to the microorganism • Therapeutic thoracocentesis • Tube thoracostomy is indicated if: • Pleural fluid pH <7.2 • Frank pus • Microorganism isolated in Gram stain or culture of pleural fluid614

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common interstitial lung disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common interstitial lung disease (ILD ) is idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). ILD refers to the remodeling of interstitial space , the region between the epithelium and endothelium . The main pathology is fibrosis, mediated by TGF-\337 and platelet -derived growth factor.Classification of Interstitial L ung Disease (ILD ) ILDs of known etiologyOccup ational: Coal worker's pneum oconiosis, silicosisTreatment - related : Radiation, drug-indu cedConnective tissue disease - related : Rheumatoid arthritis, Sjogren's syndrome, sclerode rma ILDs of unknown etiologyIdi opathic pulmonary fibrosis (I PF):Most commontypeNon -s pecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP)Cryptogenic organizin g pneumonia (COP)Acute int erstitial pneumonia (AIP)/Ha mman-Rich syndromeRespir atory bronchiolitis associated ILD (RBILD )Desquamative i nterstitial pneumonia (DIP)L ymphocytic interstitial pneu monia (LIP )Pleuroparenchy mal fibroelastosis GranulomatousSarcoidosisH ypersensitivity pneumonitis623 Classification of Interstitial L ung Disease (ILD ) Other formsLymphangioleio myomatosis (LAM)Pulmonar y Langerhans ' cell histiocytos is (PLCH )Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP)

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: An 80-year-old woman was found to have a restrictive disease with reduced lung volumes on a pulmonary function test . A high-resolution CT of the thorax was done and is shown below . Which of the following is not a feature of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The above HRCT shows a honeycomb appearance of lung parenchyma due to interstitial fibrosis in a restrictive lung disorder that is suggestive of interstitial lung disease (ILD ). Inspiratory coarse crackles are not a feature of interstitial lung disease . Auscultating a patient with ILD will reveal bilateral basal end-inspiratory fine crackles also called velcro crackles or rales. Patients with interstitial lung disease usually present with a non-productive cough and breathlessness on exertion. Clubbing may be seen on examination, especially in advanced cases .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old woman presents with breathlessness on exertion and dry cough for 4 weeks . She has swollen joints and early morning stiffness for which she is on treatment for a few years. On auscultation , inspiratory fine crackles were heard. An HRCT was ordered and it showed bilateral, subpleural and basilar honeycombing pattern. PFT of the patient is likely to show which of the following patterns ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with the HRCT findings are suggestive of interstitial lung disease (ILD ). FEV1/FVC ratio >0.7 and decreased DLCO are likely to be seen in the PFT. A history of swollen joints and early morning stiffness hints at rheumatoid arthritis. It is associated with the usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern of ILD . In ILD , restrictive pattern is seen on pulmonary function test , which is characterized by: • Decreased total lung capacity (TLC ) • Decreased forced vital capacity (FVC) • Decreased residual volumes (RV) • Decreased DLCO (diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide) • FEV1/FVC ratio - normal or increased, >0.7

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a characteristic HRCT finding of usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP)?

options.a: Honeycombing and loss of lung architecture

mcqs.explanation: Ground-glass opacities on HRCT are not a characteristic finding in UIP. Honeycombing , loss of lung architecture, traction bronchiectasis , and basilar subpleural reticular opacities are seen in UIP pattern of ILD on HRCT .624

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions is also known as Hamman -Rich syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Acute interstitial pneumonia (AIP) is also known as Hamman –Rich syndrome. AIP is a rare, idiopathic , fulminant interstitial lung disease (ILD ) that is similar in presentation to ARDS. It is often preceded by a viral upper respiratory tract infection . Histologically , it shows diffuse alveolar damage . HRCT shows bilateral patchy , ground-glass opacities . Lung biopsy shows diffuse alveolar damage with hyaline formation.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 52-year-old woman presented with dyspnoea . General physical examination revealed deformity of the hand as shown below . There is restricted mobility in the small joints and loss of wrinkle lines on the facial skin. An HRCT of the thorax showed diffuse subpleural , symmetric, ground-glass opacities of the lungs . Which of the following histopathological finding is likely to be seen in the lung biopsy of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the image showing sclerodactyly suggestive of scleroderma along with the HRCT findings point to a diagnosis of non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP). It is characterized by homogeneous interstitial involvement. NSIP is often associated with connective tissue disease but can also be drug-induced . The common drugs implicated in NSIP are: • Bleomycin • Busulfan • Methotrexate • Amiodarone It usually affects middle -aged woman who have never smoked. There is uniformity of interstitial involvement across the biopsy section , and this may be predominantly cellular or fibrosing. HRCT shows homogenous involvement with symmetrical ground-glass opacities . Non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) responds to steroids . Other treatment modalities include cytotoxic drugs like azathioprine or cyclophosphamide and also biologics like rituximab.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a smoking-related interstitial lung disease (ILD )?
mcqs.explanation: Pulmonary lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM) is not related to smoking. It is usually seen in young females with tuberous sclerosis . LAM can lead to pneumothorax or chylous effusions . Pulmonary function testing usually reveals an obstructive or mixed obstructive -restrictive pattern. HRCT shows thin-walled cysts surrounded by normal lung parenchyma. The smoking-related ILDs are: • DIP - Desquamating interstitial pneumonia. • RB -ILD - Respiratory bronchiolitis associated ILD . • LCH - Langerhans cell histiocytosis .625

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A man presented with progressively worsening cough with sputum , breathlessness , easy fatiguability , and loss of appetite for 6 months. PFT was suggestive of a restrictive disorder. Trans -bronchial biopsy showed cells positive for CD1a and langerin (CD207). Which of the following is not a feature of this condition?

options.a: They may present with spontaneous pneumothorax
options.b: Cysts and nodules are seen on HRCT
options.c: It is a smoking related interstitial lung disease

mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH). It is a smoking-related ILD that typically affects young adults . Smoking cessation leads to improvement in the condition. The specific immunohistochemical markers for LCH are CD1a and langerin (CD207). On electron microscopy , the presence of Birbeck granules in the cytoplasm is characteristic (as shown below ).HRCT shows bilateral irregularly shaped cysts with nodules , predominantly in the upper lobe . There is a risk of spontaneous pneumothorax in this condition due to cyst rupture .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding pulmonary alveolar proteinosis ?

options.a: Acquired due to antibodies formed against GM-CSF

mcqs.explanation: Chunky, gelatinous , PAS-positive sputum is a feature of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP). PAP is a condition characterized by the accumulation of surfactants in alveoli and terminal airways. It can be due to impaired clearance or abnormal production of surfactants. PAP can be of three forms: • Primary (most common): There is impaired GM-CSF-dependent surfactant clearance by the alveolar macrophages . It can be due to: • Autoantibodies against GM-CSF (acquired/idiopathic /autoimmune PAP) • Mutation in GM-CSF receptors (hereditary PAP) • Secondary: There is a reduction in the number or ability of alveolar macrophages that causes impaired surfactant clearance. It can be due to: • Silicosis • Immunodeficiency disorders • Hematopoietic disorders and malignancies626 • Congenital : It affects neonates and children. There is abnormal surfactant production due to mutation in the genes coding for: • Surfactant protein B • Surfactant protein C • ATP binding cassette protein member 3 About 30% of patients are asymptomatic . Symptomatic patients can have persistent dry cough , progressive dyspnea , and pleuritic chest pain X-ray shows bilateral, diffuse opacities and HRCT shows a crazy-paving pattern (as shown below ). The treatment is whole lung lavage.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Farmer's lung is associated with which of the following organisms?
mcqs.explanation: Farmer's lung is a hypersensitivity pneumonitis caused due to exposure to mouldy hay, which contains thermophilic actinomycetes , principally Thermopolyspora polyspora .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A daily-wage worker from the cement industry got a chest X-ray as a part of his routine health check-up. What could be the cause of the findings shown below ?
mcqs.explanation: The given X-ray shows irregular opacities , which appear to be pleural thickenings i.e., pleural plaques. The sign along with a history of working in the cement industry suggests a diagnosis of asbestosis . Workers of the cement , shipping , and textile industries are at a higher risk of developing asbestosis . Asbestos tends to involve the pleura first. The earliest manifestation is benign asbestosis -related pleural effusion . With time, the plaques calcify resulting in the formation of thick pleural plaques . The pleural thickenings can be seen on the X-ray. This is the "holly leaf sign".627 Lung parenchymal involvement occurs after years of exposure (at least 10 years). They present with cough and exertional dyspnoea . It predominantly affects the lower lobes of the lung, in contrast to other forms of pneumoconiosis, which affect the upper lobes . Pulmonary function testing in asbestosis typically shows a restrictive pattern with a decrease in both lung volumes and diffusing capacity. The image below shows thick plueral plaques .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A woman has been working for a company that manufactures roofing sheets for 12 years, but the company does not provide her with personal protective equipment . Which of the following cancers is commonly seen in such individuals?
mcqs.explanation: Workers in the roofing industry are exposed to asbestos . Lung cancer (of all histologic types ) is the most common cancer associated with asbestos exposure . Smoking along with asbestos exposure multiplies the risk to a great extent . Cough and hemoptysis are common presentations . Pleural mesothelioma is the most specific cancer associated with asbestos exposure , but not the most common. Smoking does not seem to be associated with mesothelioma . Pleuritic chest pain or a mass on the radiographic image are common presentations .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which among the following is a common concern for a patient presenting with chronic dry cough , working in the granite mining industry?
mcqs.explanation: Silicosis is a common concern for people working in granite mining industries . Silica is found in rock , granite, slate , and sandstone . People working in mining, stone cutting , sandblasting, glass and cement manufacturing, and quarrying are exposed to silica. The active molecule that causes silicosis is free silica or crystalline silica (quartz). Silicosis can present as: • Acute silicosis - due to heavy exposure in closed spaces and they manifest within 2 years.628 • Chronic silicosis (simple silicosis ) - due to long-term (10 to 30 years), less intense exposure . • Complicated silicosis - simple silicosis may progress to complicated silicosis that presents with chronic cough and progressive dyspnoea on exertion. Note : Silicosis is the most common pnemoconiosis in the world.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man comes to the emergency room with an acute onset of dyspnoea . He tells you that he has been working in the sandblasting industry for about a year and the company does not provide personal protective equipment . He also gives a history of on and off dry cough . CT scan shows the following . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: A history of working in the sandblasting industry for about a year without PPE suggests a heavy exposure to silica. This along with the CT finding of bilateral nodules , interstitial fibrosis, and crazy pavement pattern suggests a diagnosis of acute silicosis . Acute silicosis is seen rarely. It manifests within 2 years of heavy exposure . Common presentations are dyspnoea and hypoxemia . The X-ray may show diffuse miliary infiltrates or consolidation. HRCT may also show bilateral centrilobular nodules and ground-glass opacification . Bronchoalveolar lavage yields a PAS-positive milky white fluid .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man has recently started work in the stone cutting industry. The company provides him with a respirator mask but they do not use dust control measures . If he works in similar conditions for 20 more years, which of the following will you most likely see in his HRCT scan image?

options.b: Small round opacities in upper lobes
options.c: Thin -walled cysts surrounded by normal lung parenchyma

mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, the man works in the stone cutting industry, indicating exposure to silica. He is expected to have less intense , long term exposure owing to a few but substandard measures to control exposure to silica. Such individuals are more likely to develop simple silicosis . These patients are asymptomatic , and HRCT shows small round opacities in the upper lobes . This can progress to complicated silicosis. Here, the nodules coalesce and form masses leading to impairment of lung function. They present with chronic cough and progressive dyspnoea on exertion. This may progress further to cause progressive massive fibrosis. PFT shows a mixed obstructive and restrictive pattern. Calcification of hilar lymph nodes is seen in a few cases , called eggshell calcification. This is depicted in the image below .629 Option A: A crazy pavement pattern is seen with acute silicosis . Option C: Thin -walled cysts surrounded by normal lung parenchyma are seen in pulmonary lymphangiomyomatosis (LAM). Option D: Pleural plaques are seen in patients suffering from asbestosis .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following pneumoconiosis is associated with an increased incidence of tuberculosis ?
mcqs.explanation: Silicosis is associated with an increased incidence of tuberculosis . Silica causes pulmonary alveolar macrophage dysfunction and hence , patients with silicosis have a higher risk of developing lung infections from organisms like M. Tuberculosis , atypical mycobacteria and fungi. Radiographic imaging of silicotuberculosis shows cavitation.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Choose the correct option with respect to Caplan's syndrome.
mcqs.explanation: Caplan's syndrome also called rheumatoid pneumoconiosis , is a combination of rheumatoid arthritis and pneumoconiosis . It manifests as pneumoconiotic nodules along with features of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis. Caplan syndrome was first described in coal miners and later in patients with silicosis too. Option C: Hilar adenopathy , polyarthritis, and erythema nodosum are characteristic of Lofgren syndrome. Option D: Arthritis, urethritis, and conjunctivitis are characteristic of Reiter syndrome.630

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A factory worker presents to the clinic with fever, tiredness , and a chronic dry cough . He says his symptoms are worst on the first day of the week , improve by the end of the week , and are almost non-existent over the weekends . What could be the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The above characteristic pattern of symptoms is called Monday fever or Monday chest tightness and is due to byssinosis . Byssinosis is seen commonly in cotton factory workers due to cotton dust exposure . It is also caused due to flax, hemp , and jute dust . It is due to occupational hypersensitivity reaction with symptoms occurring (or recurring) on the first day of the workweek and diminishing by the weekend due to development of tolerance .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which interstitial lung disease is likely to be seen in a patient suffering from systemic sclerosis ?
mcqs.explanation: Non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) pattern of ILD is the most common pulmonary manifestation in systemic sclerosis . The CT scan of NSIP shows ground-glass opacities . It responds to steroids given along with azathioprine or cyclophosphamide . Other connective tissue diseases associated with ILD : • Rheumatoid arthritis • Sj\366gren syndrome • Dermatopolymyositis • Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man who has worked as a miner for the past 25 years, comes to the OPD with complaints of dyspnoea and cough . Pulmonary function tests and a lung biopsy are done. The histopathology of the sample is shown below . Which type of emphysema can this condition give rise to?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the microscopic image showing abundant black-colored pigment within the macrophages of lung parenchyma is characteristic of pulmonary anthracosis/coal worker's pneumoconiosis . It may give rise to centrilobular emphysema . The inhaled carbon particles are engulfed by the lung macrophages . They accumulate in the connective tissue along lymphatics or in lymphoid tissue along the bronchi or the hilum, which causes the blackening of the tissues . Aggregates of carbon dust are present as coal macules or nodules which consist of carbon-laden macrophages .
