mcqs.question: A 65-year-old hypertensive patient has recently been diagnosed with stage 3 chronic kidney disease . According to the ESC 2018 guidelines , what target blood pressure would you choose for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: 711 According to the ESC 2018 guidelines , the target blood pressure in hypertensive patients with CKD is < / 80 mm Hg regardless of age .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man who has been on dialysis for 2 years presents with bone pain and bowing of legs . Further evaluation reveals hyperparathyroidism and hyperphosphatemia . What is the initial treatment of choice in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario is suggestive of secondary hyperparathyroidism (HPT ) and hyperphosphatemia in a patient with CKD. Sevelamer is the best initial treatment for this patient . It is a phosphate binder that reduces the absorption of phosphate from the gastrointestinal tract. Other phosphate binders that can be used include : • Calcium containing • Calcium acetate • Calcium carbonate • Non-calcium containing • Sevelamer • Lanthanum Calcitriol and cinacalcet are used to decrease PTH levels in secondary hyperparathyroidism . However, they also cause increased serum phosphate levels . Hence , they should not be given as initial treatment in patients with hyperphosphatemia . Bisphosphonates like pamidronate are used in the treatment of primary hyperparathyroidism .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate definitive treatment for anemia in patients with chronic kidney disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Anemia in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) is primarily due to decreased erythropoietin production . Hence , human recombinant erythropoietin (EPO) such as darbepoetin is the most appropriate treatment and is considered the mainstay. However, an optimal response to treatment with EPO occurs only when iron stores are adequate . Hence , iron supplements (oral or IV ) must be given first to ensure the effectiveness of EPO therapy . Other treatment options for anemia in CKD are: • Vitamin B12 and folate supplementation • Blood transfusion - in severe anemia and failure to EPO therapy

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following should not be used in a patient with CKD?
mcqs.explanation: Diclofenac should not be used in a patient with CKD as it is nephrotoxic.712 Renal blood flow is regulated by prostaglandin E2. Aspirin, diclofenac and other NSAIDs inhibit cyclooxygenase . This decreases prostaglandin E2 concentration, thereby causing a reduction in blood flow and GFR. Nephrotoxic drugs include the following : • NSAIDs • Antifungals (amphotericin B) • Antibiotics • Aminoglycosides • Vancomycin • Cephalosporins • Sulfonamides • Streptomycin • Antivirals • Acyclovir • Foscarnet • Chemotherapy drugs • Methotrexate • Platins • Immunosuppressants (cyclosporine )

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with type 2 diabetes has developed stage 4 CKD secondary to diabetic nephropathy . He currently takes insulin for his diabetes . What changes need to be made to his regimen?
mcqs.explanation: In CKD patients with diabetes , the dose of insulin must be reduced . In CKD patients , the plasma levels of insulin are elevated due to diminished renal degradation of insulin by the impaired kidney. This impaired renal clearance of insulin can lead to hypoglycemia . Hence , the dose of insulin must be reduced to prevent this.713

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following criteria is diagnostic of acute kidney injury in a patient ?

options.a: Rise in creatinine 1.5 times the baseline value within 7 days
options.b: Rise in creatinine \037 0.3mg/dl from baseline within 7 days
options.c: Rise in creatinine \037 0.5 mg/dl from baseline within 48 hours

mcqs.explanation: 719 A rise in creatinine 1.5 times the baseline value within 7 days is diagnostic of acute kidney injury (AKI). AKI is an abrupt decrease in kidney function within hours to days. According to the KDIGO definition, it is defined as any of the following : • Increase in serum creatinine by \0370.3 mg/dL within 48 hours OR • Increase in serum creatinine to \0371.5 times the baseline within 7 days OR • Urine volume <0.5 mL /kg/h for 6 hours.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: AKIN and RIFLE criteria are used to classify
mcqs.explanation: AKIN and RIFLE criteria are used to classify acute kidney injury (AKI). The various classifications used in AKI are: • RIFLE criteria (Risk , Injury, Failure, Loss, End-stage ) • AKIN (AKI Network) Classification • KDIGO (Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes ) Classification RIFLE , AKIN, KDIGO definitions of AKI: RIFLE , AKIN, KDIGO staging of AKI:RIFLE AKIN KDIGO S. creatinin e >50% increase that develops in <7 days >0.3 mg/dl increase or >50% increase that develops in <48 hr >0.3 mg/dl increase or >50% increase that develops in <7 days Urine outp ut <0.5ml/kg/hr for >6 hr <0.5ml/kg/hr for >6 hr <0.5ml/kg/hr for >6 hrRIFL E Increase in S.creatinine AKIN Increase in S.creati nine KDIG O Increase in S.creati nine Urine output Risk \03750% Stage \0370.3mg/dl or \03750% Stage \0370.3mg/dl or \03750% <0.5mL/kg/hr for >6h Injur y \037100 % Stage \037100 % Stage \037100 % <0.5mL/kg/hr for >12 hr Failu re \037200 % Stage \037200 % Stage \037200 % <0.3mL /kg/hr for >24hr or anuria >12hr Loss Need for renal replacem ent therapy (RRT )>4 we eks End-s tage Need RRT for >3 month s720

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Patients with urine output below what level are said to have anuria ?
mcqs.explanation: Anuria is defined as urine output less than 100 mL /day. Oliguria is defined as urine output less than 400 mL /day. Acute kidney injury (AKI) can have varied clinical features depending on the etiology . The history and physical examination in AKI aims mainly at: • Finding the etiology • Identifying the occurrence of any complications The following clinical features may be seen : • Oliguria or anuria • Gross hematuria • Renal colic pain (in renal stones ) • Loss of skin turgor, dry mouth, hypotension , tachycardia (in hypovolemia) • Prostatomegaly and/or a pelvic mass (in post -renal obstruction) • Dysuria, fever with chills and rigors, increased frequency of micturition, renal angle tenderness (in pyelonephritis) • Edema , hypertension (volume overload) • Encephalopathy , seizures , platelet dysfunction (uremia)

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following causes prerenal AKI?
mcqs.explanation: NSAIDs, Rhabdomyolysis and ACE inhibitors cause prerenal acute kidney injury (AKI). The use of NSAIDs causes reduced production of vasodilatory prostaglandins. This leads to decreased renal perfusion and glomerular capillary pressure . NSAIDs can also lead to acute interstitial nephritis, a cause of renal AKI. However, this is relatively uncommon. ACE inhibitors cause inhibition of efferent arteriole vasoconstriction, leading to reduced renal perfusion. Rhabdomyolysis causes AKI by both prerenal mechanisms (due to volume sequestration ) and ATN (due to precipitation of myoglobin in the renal tubules ). Nephrotoxins like myeloma light chains, snake venom, myoglobin (due to rhabdomyolysis ) cause acute tubular necrosis (ATN). This leads to renal or intrinsic AKI.721

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 48-year-old woman presented with severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and dark -coloured urine for the past 3 days. She has been on a combination painkiller for rheumatoid arthritis for 10 years. On examination, severe pallor was noted and BP was 180/120 mmHg. CT abdomen is shown below . What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario and CT scan showing papillary calcifications are highly suggestive of chronic kidney disease caused by analgesic nephropathy . This condition is more common in females secondary to excessive prolonged use of a combination of analgesics . The mechanism of injury is medullary hypoxia leading to papillary necrosis and finally causes chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis. Patients can remain asymptomatic for a long time. Sloughing or obstruction of papillae can cause abdominal pain and hematuria. It increases the risk of urothelial malignancies. The following CT findings can be seen : • Papillary calcifications • Small kidneys • Irregular contour Note : NSAID-induced nephropathy causes acute interstitial nephritis. It is a type IV hypersensitivity reaction. The features include non-oliguric AKI, fractional excretion of sodium (FeNa) < 1, and hyperkalemia. It is seen within a few days of use and is reversible. The image below shows papillary calcifications:722 The given image shows papillary calcification on ultrasonography :

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 38-year-old woman presents with nausea, vomiting, fatigue , and oliguria for the past three days. On further investigation, urine osmolality was 800 mOsm/kg, urinary sodium 10 meq/L , and BUN: creatinine ratio was 20 :1. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is highly suggestive of prerenal AKI based on the following : • Urine osmolality >500 mOsm/kg • Urinary sodium < 20 meq/l • BUN: Creatinine ratio of 20 :1 Differences between prerenal, and renal AKI:723 Indices Prerenal Renal Spot urine sodium (mEq/L\ <20 >40 Fractional excretion of sodiu m (FENa) <1% >2% Fractional excretion of urea ( FEUrea ) <35% >35% Urine osmolality (mOsm/kg\ >500 <350 BUN to serum creatinine rati o >20 :1 <10 :1 Urine creatinine/plasma creat inine >40:1 <20 :1 Urinary sediment Nil or hyaline casts only Renal tubular epithelial casts, muddy brown granular casts

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man was admitted following a crush injury to his left leg . Two days later, his urine/plasma creatinine levels are < 20 . What is the likely cause ?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario and urine/ plasma creatinine ratio of <20 is suggestive of renal AKI due to rhabdomyolysis-induced acute tubular necrosis. Rhabdomyolysis is a serious complication of crush injuries. It leads to muscle breakdown, releasing a high amount of myoglobin in the blood. Myoglobinuria can lead to acute kidney injury by the following mechanisms: • Direct toxic effect of myoglobin and heme on the PCT • Tubular obstruction by precipitation of pigmented casts • Renal vasoconstriction can cause FeNa < 1 (unlike other renal causes of AKI)Indices Prerenal Renal Spot urine sodium (mEq/L\ <20 >40 Fractional excretion of sodiu m (FENa) <1% >2% Fractional excretion of urea ( FEUrea ) <35% >35% Urine osmolality (mOsm/kg\ >500 <350 BUN to serum creatinine rati o >20 :1 <10 :1 Urine creatinine/plasma creat inine >40:1 <20 :1 Urinary sediment Nil or hyaline casts only Renal tubular epithelial casts, muddy brown granular casts724

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 38-year old woman presents with severe muscle pain and high-coloured urine for the past 3 days. She joined a gym 2 weeks ago and has been strenuously working out. She was diagnosed with hypothyroidism 8 years back. Work -up reveals high serum creatine kinase, uric acid, and creatinine. Which of the following is likely to be present in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of rhabdomyolysis . Hypocalcemia is seen in this condition. The causes of rhabdomyolysis include : • Hypothyroidism (precipitated by exertion, alcohol, infection ) • Crush injury • Electric shock • Prolonged seizures • Malignant hyperthermia • Exertion • Drugs like fibrates, statins • Polymyositis / Dermatomyositis • McArdle 's disease (GSD-5) causes recurrent rhabdomyolysis . Patients often present with muscle pain and high-colored urine. The following features are seen : • High serum CK (> 5 times normal ) • High serum myoglobin • High serum LDH • Hyperkalemia • Hypermagnesemia • Hyperphosphatemia • Hypocalcemia725 • Hyperuricemia • Once AKI develops , high serum creatinine and urea The treatment includes administration of large amounts of IV fluids (5-6 liters), alkalization of urine, and hemodialysis .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 54-year-old man presented with reduced urine output , swelling of his feet , and eyelid puffiness for 1 week . He also complains of back pain for the past 3 months, unresponsive to painkillers. Investigations reveal the following . What is the possible cause of renal failure in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Bence-Jones proteins on urine analysis are suggestive of multiple myeloma. It causes acute kidney injury (AKI) by the following mechanisms: • Hypercalcemia - leads to intense renal vasoconstriction and reduced perfusion • Myeloma light chains - cause direct tubular toxicity .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Non-oliguric renal failure may be seen in patients with which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Non-oliguric renal failure may be seen in the following conditions: • Acute interstitial nephritis • Acute tubular necrosis (aminoglycoside toxicity , contrast-induced nephropathy ) All the causes of acute tubular necrosis (ATN) cause non-oliguric AKI except acyclovir (oliguric AKI). The difference in urine output between oliguric and non-oliguric AKI may be due to variations in GFR or in the rate of tubular reabsorption. Non-oliguric forms may be associated with less severe injury. Other options : Prerenal causes such as congestive heart failure cause oliguric AKI. In post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, oliguria occurs as a result of decreased GFR.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 47-year-old electrician was rushed to the hospital following an electrical shock. Examination reveals electrical burns. During the course of treatment , he developed an arrhythmia and was managed appropriately . What arterial blood gas finding would you expect in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Electrical burns result in rhabdomyolysis . It presents with hyperkalemic metabolic acidosis. Muscle breakdown in rhabdomyolysis leads to hyperkalemia which causes arrhythmias. It also causes high anion gap metabolic acidosis due to the increase in H+ ions and liberation of organic anions.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient with acute renal failure was found to have metabolic acidosis on evaluation. What is the likely cause ?
mcqs.explanation: In acute renal failure, metabolic acidosis occurs due to decreased excretion of ammonium. This impairs the excretion of H+ ions as NH4 ions.726 Normally, H+ are excreted via the kidney in combination with ammonia which acts as a urinary buffer . In AKI, there is a decreased capacity of tubules to secrete ammonia . Due to reduced amounts of ammonia , the production of NH4 is impaired. Hence , H+ ions cannot be excreted , which leads to metabolic acidosis.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 75 -year-old obese woman, who is a known diabetic presented with chest pain. Coronary angiography was done. Her S.creatinine levels before and after the procedure are given below . Which of the following is not a risk factor for the complication she developed ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario shows >0.5 mg/dL increase in S.creatinine levels , which is indicative of contrast-induced nephropathy for which obesity is not a risk factor. Contrast-induced nephropathy is defined as a 25% or 0.5 mg/dL increase from the baseline value of serum creatinine within 48-72 hours of intravenous contrast administration. It occurs due to tubular damage and as a result , the patient develops non-oliguric transient nephropathy . Risk factors for contrast medium-induced nephropathy : Patient-related : • eGFR < 60 mL /min/1.73 m2 before intra-arterial administration • eGFR < 45 mL /min/1.73 m2 before intravenous administration • Patient conditions that increase the risk : • Diabetic nephropathy • Dehydration • Congestive heart failure (NYHA grade 3–4) and low LVEF • Recent myocardial infarction (<24 h) • Intra -aortic balloon pump • Peri-procedural hypotension • Low hematocrit level • Age over 70 • Concurrent administration of nephrotoxic drugs • Known or suspected acute renal failure Procedure -related : • Intra -arterial administration of contrast medium • High-osmolality agents • Large doses of contrast medium • Multiple contrast medium administrations within a few days Side effects of iodinated contrast material include : • Idiosyncratic anaphylactoid reaction - patient develops bronchospasm and hypotension727 • Dose -dependent side effect – contrast-induced nephropathy seen especially with the use of high osmolar agents Prevention of contrast-induced nephropathy : • IV fluids (isotonic saline or sodium bicarbonate) started 1 hour before and continued for at least 3-6 hours after the procedure • Low volume low osmolar contrast should be used • N-acetyl cysteine may be given prior to contrast exposure

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding contrast-induced nephropathy ?

options.d: Hypoxia due to nephrotoxic agents is the cause

mcqs.explanation: Dialysis-requiring AKI is uncommon in contrast-induced nephropathy . Contrast-induced AKI is generally associated with the use of high osmolar contrasts such as: • Iodinated contrast agents • High-dose gadolinium Mechanism of contrast-induced injury includes : • Medullary ischemia and hypoxia: By inducing intense vasoconstriction • Toxic tubular damage : By direct injury It usually develops within 24-48 hrs. Serum creatinine peaks by 3-5 days and normalizes by 7-10 days. It manifests mainly as a non-oliguric renal failure and has an excellent prognosis. Contrast-induced AKI can be prevented by: • Use of iso-osmolar or non-ionic contrast agents (least toxic) • Administering minimum required quantity of contrast • Pre- and post -hydration (IV normal saline 1 mL /kg/h x 12 h prior and post -exposure ) • N-acetyl cysteine may be given prior to contrast exposure .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a marker of kidney injury?
mcqs.explanation: Acid phosphatase is not a marker of kidney injury. The various markers of kidney injury are as follows : • IL -18 • Cystatin C • NGAL (neutrophil gelatinase -associated lipocalin) • KIM-1 (kidney injury molecule -1) • LFABP (liver fatty acid-binding protein) • 728 • NHE3 (sodium hydrogen exchanger 3) • NAG (N-acetyl glucosaminidase ) • Alanine aminopeptidase • Osteopontin • ALP

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which intravenous fluid is preferred for the hydration of patients with pre-renal acute kidney injury?
mcqs.explanation: Isotonic crystalloids like 0.9% NaCl are preferred for the correction of hypovolemia in pre-renal AKI. Management of AKI: 1. AKI care bundle : • Nephrotoxic drugs should be avoided and the dosage of other drugs must be adjusted according to kidney function • Creatinine levels and urine output must be closely monitored 2. Hemodynamic management: • If hypovolemic - fluid replenishment using isotonic crystalloids (normal saline) • If euvolemic - fluid intake = urine output + additional ~500 mL • If hypervolemic - diuretics are administered . If the response is unsatisfactory , dialysis is required. 3. Management of complications : • Pulmonary edema - Treated with diuretics , non-invasive ventilation, and dialysis if refractory • Metabolic acidosis - Treated when pH <7.2 with oral or IV sodium bicarbonate • Hyperkalemia - Treated by restriction of dietary potassium , administration of sodium polystyrene sulfonate , insulin, glucose, inhaled \031-agonist, and calcium gluconate Options A and B: Hydroxyethyl starch solutions and dextrans increase the risk of severe AKI and are contraindicated . Option D: Ringer's lactate is preferred only when a large volume of fluids is required.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Continuous renal replacement therapy is preferred in patients with which of the following features ?
mcqs.explanation: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is a modality of dialysis that involves hemodialysis and hemofiltration. It is the preferred option in AKI patients with severe hypotension . It is preferred in the following cases : • Acute renal failure complicated by hemodynamic instability or heart failure • Severe volume overload unresponsive to diuretic therapy729 • Brain edema • Hypercatabolism state • Acute or chronic liver failure as a renal support measure It is an extracorporeal blood purification therapy intended to substitute for impaired renal function over an extended period of time, aimed at being applied for 24 hours a day. There is no rapid shift of volume and osmolarity with this process as in intermittent hemodialysis . The other types of dialysis are: • Intermittent hemodialysis - may be done in hemodynamically stable patients with AKI • Peritoneal dialysis - used when hemodialysis is not available.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not seen in tumor lysis syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Hypocalcemia , not hypercalcemia , is seen in tumor lysis syndrome (TLS). TLS is a potentially life -threatening condition characterized by the rapid destruction of a large number of tumor cells . The release of calcium phosphate from lysed cells contributes to hyperphosphatemia and subsequent reciprocal depression in serum calcium levels . The consumption of ionized calcium during the formation of calcium phosphate crystals leads to hypocalcemia . TLS is commonly observed after initiation of chemotherapy in hematologic malignancies characterized by high cell turnover rates, such as Burkitt's lymphoma and acute lymphoblastic leukemia. The destruction of neoplastic cells results in the release of nucleic acids, which are broken down into uric acid, leading to hyperuricemia . The acidic environment in the renal tubules can cause uric acid to precipitate , leading to acute renal failure. Potassium is released in large quantities during tumor cell lysis leading to hyperkalemia. TLS is diagnosed using the Cairo-Bishop criteria which includes both laboratory and clinical criteria. Prevention is the mainstay of the management of TLS , which involves includes allopurinol, which inhibits the production of uric acid, and aggressive hydration to promote urine flow . Urinary alkalization is not recommended . Febuxostat , a selective xanthine oxidase inhibitor, can be used as an alternative. In severe cases or when renal failure is present , rasburicase, a recombinant urate oxidase , is used for treatment . Rasburicase rapidly lowers uric acid levels by converting it into a highly soluble compound called allantoin. Renal replacement therapy is often required and should be considered in case of acute renal failure.730

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Dialysis is not an absolute indication for patients who present with which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Dialysis is not indicated in patients who initially present with hyperkalemia. It is indicated in the case of refractory hyperkalemia that has failed to respond to other modalities of treatment . Indications for dialysis can be remembered using the mnemonic AEIOU: • Acidosis - metabolic acidosis that is refractory to medical treatment . • Electrolyte abnormality - refractory hyperkalemia and hypercalcemia . • Intoxication - barbiturates, alcohol, and lithium. • Overload - hypervolemia and pulmonary edema . • Uncontrolled hypertension (and) • Uremia - encephalopathy , pericarditis, asterixis, seizures , intractable nausea and vomiting, and bleeding diathesis .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most commonly used therapeutic modality for patients with end-stage renal disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common therapeutic modality for patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) is hemodialysis. The various modalities of renal replacement therapy include the following : • Dialysis: • Acute intermittent hemodialysis • Continuous renal replacement therapy - includes hemodialysis and ultrafiltration techniques • Peritoneal dialysis • CAPD - Continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis • CCPD - Continuous cycling peritoneal dialysis • NIPD - Nocturnal intermittent peritoneal dialysis • Renal transplant738

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about hemodialysis ?\

options.a: Dialyzers are made up of cellulose membranes
options.b: Bicarbonate is commonly used as a buffer
options.c: Glutaraldehyde is used as a reprocessing agent
options.d: Urea is cleared more efficiently than creatinine

mcqs.explanation: In hemodialysis , the dialyzer is made up of biocompatible membranes derived from polysulfone . Cellulose is bio-incompatible and is no longer used . Hemodialysis is based on the principle of solute diffusion using an artificial semi-permeable membrane. Smaller molecules (urea) diffuse faster and are cleared more efficiently than larger molecules (creatinine). There are three components to this system : • Dialyzer - a chamber that contains compartments for blood and dialysate solution , separated by a semipermeable membrane. • Dialysate - a solution that helps in the removal of metabolic waste products . Bicarbonate is used as a buffer to correct acidosis in CKD patients . • Blood delivery system - consists of the vascular access and extracorporeal circuit. The dialyzers used during a session of dialysis are reprocessed and reused for the next dialysis sessions . The reprocessors used for dialyzers are: • Glutaraldehyde • Formaldehyde • Peracetic acid-hydrogen peroxide The following image depicts hemodialysis .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with stage 5 chronic kidney disease is planned for hemodialysis . Which of the following is incorrect regarding the vascular access for this procedure ?

options.a: Tunneled catheters are associated with lower infection rates
options.b: Access of choice is radiocephalic arteriovenous fistula
options.c: Most common complication of arteriovenous grafts is infection
options.d: Fistulas have higher long term patency rates

mcqs.explanation: The most common complication of arteriovenous (AV ) grafts is stenosis , not infections .739 In order to perform hemodialysis , vascular or hemodialysis access must first be established . The preferred site is the forearm. The following types of vascular access may be used for hemodialysis : • AV fistulas : • Fistula refers to the anastomosis of an artery and an adequately large vein (either side -to-side or end-to-side ). • This causes arterialization of the vein, thereby causing venous wall thickening and increasing venous diameter. • Fistulas need 4-6 weeks to mature before they can be used . • The access of choice is radiocephalic AV fistula (Brescia-Cimino fistula ). • Fistulas have higher long-term patency rates than grafts. • Thrombosis is a common complication. The following image depicts a radiocephalic fistula .• AV grafts: • The artery and vein are connected by a prosthetic graft such as PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene ). • The advantage is that it can be performed with smaller veins. • Complications include stenosis (most common), due to intimal hyperplasia at anastomosis between graft and vein, and infections . • Central venous catheter : • Tunneled catheters are used for long-term IV access . As they tunnel through the skin before entering the vein, they have a lower risk of infection .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the rate of blood flow in the hemodialysis machine?
mcqs.explanation: 740 During hemodialysis , heparinized blood flows through the dialyzer at a rate of 250–450 mL /min. On the other hand, the dialysate flows in the opposite counter-current direction at 500–800 mL /min.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: In a patient undergoing hemodialysis , which of the following can be used to monitor the adequacy of dialysis ?
mcqs.explanation: The adequacy of dialysis is determined by the urea reduction ratio. It is defined as the fractional reduction in blood urea nitrogen per hemodialysis session . It is calculated as (Co - C) / Co, where : Co - predialysis serum urea C - postdialysis serum urea The target urea reduction ratio is 65–70%.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following has been most commonly implicated as a cause of dialysis -induced hypotension in patients ?
mcqs.explanation: Acetate is used as a buffer in the dialysate solution . It is the most common cause of dialysis-induced hypotension because of its vasodilatory and cardio-depressive effects . For this reason, acetate is less commonly used these days and has been largely replaced by bicarbonate.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common acute complication in patients who undergo hemodialysis ?
mcqs.explanation: Hypotension is the most common acute complication of hemodialysis , particularly among patients with diabetes mellitus .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 61-year-old man is brought to the casualty following a seizure episode . His wife says that he has been very drowsy and has not passed urine for the past 2 days. Investigations reveal serum urea of 71 mg/dl and creatinine of 5.6 mg/dl. He is referred for urgent hemodialysis . You would take all of the following precautions except :

options.b: Removing more fluid during the beginning than the end of the procedure
options.c: Maintaining fluid removal rate below 13 mL /kg/hour

mcqs.explanation: Cooling, not warming, the dialysate before dialysis must be done to prevent hypotension during dialysis. Hypotension is the most common acute complication of hemodialysis . The mechanism is not fully understood and occurs due to multiple factors. However, the following precautions have been shown to frequently prevent this complication: • Careful calculation of the dry weight and adjustment of the filtration rate accordingly. • Ultrafiltration modeling such that more fluid is removed during the beginning than the end of the procedure . • Avoiding rapid fluid removal and maintaining the rate < 13 mL /kg/hour. • Avoiding heavy meals during dialysis . • Cooling of the dialysate during the dialysis .741

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 67-year-old woman with CKD underwent her first session of hemodialysis . Towards the end of the session , she became drowsy and had a sudden seizure episode . What is the likely cause for this presentation ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of the dialysis disequilibrium syndrome or the reverse urea effect . It is an acute complication that occurs especially in patients undergoing dialysis for the first time. During dialysis , urea in blood vessels is rapidly removed as compared to that in the interstitium . This decreases the osmolality of blood. This results in a fluid shift from the blood vessels into the interstitium and brain parenchyma, causing cerebral edema . In order to prevent this, the rate of flow of dialysate must be adjusted to avoid the rapid removal of solutes .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about anaphylaxis associated with hemodialysis ?

options.a: Occur due to lack of cellulose in the membranes
options.b: Ethylene oxide is the cause of Type B reaction
options.c: Dialysis is discontinued in Type A reaction
options.d: Type A reaction associated with complement activation

mcqs.explanation: Dialysis must be discontinued immediately in case of a type A reaction. It is an IgE -mediated immediate hypersensitivity reaction that can lead to shock and death . Bio-incompatible cellulose -containing membranes are commonly associated with hemodialysis-associated anaphylaxis. The reactions can be of two types :Type A reaction Type B reaction IgE-mediated immediate hyp ersensitivity reaction in respo nse toethylene oxide. (used t o sterilize dialyzers). Delayed reaction due tocomp lementactivationand cytokine release . Occur within minutes . Occur after hours. Stop dialysisand give subcuta neous adrenaline or steroids . It isself -limitingand dialysis c an be continued .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient on hemodialysis may develop all of the following chronic complications except :
mcqs.explanation: Hypovolemia is an acute complication of hemodialysis . The chronic complications of hemodialysis are: • Amyloidosis • Adynamic bone disease • Dementia (aluminum toxicity )

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A physician is evaluating a patient with carpal tunnel syndrome. He has been undergoing dialysis for the past 7 years. Deposition of which of the following is responsible for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: 742 Carpal tunnel syndrome in the setting of chronic dialysis is suggestive of dialysis -associated amyloidosis. It occurs due to the deposition of amyloid \337-2 in tissues . This condition is seen in patients undergoing long-term hemodialysis or continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (CAPD). Amyloid deposition can lead to the following complications : • Destructive osteoarthropathies - carpal tunnel syndrome, flexor tenosynovitis • Subchondral bone cysts and pathologic fractures • Paraplegia - due to deposits along paravertebral ligaments and intervertebral discs • Visceral involvement - GI tract, heart, tongue Management involves providing symptomatic relief by means of analgesics , anti-inflammatory drugs, physical and occupational therapy, and surgical procedures . Renal transplantation is the treatment of choice .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 57 -year-old man is referred urgently for management of pulmonary edema . He was diagnosed with stage -5 CKD 3 weeks ago but was reluctant to start dialysis . On examination, he is confused and has a flapping tremor. Investigations are as follows . Which of his clinical features will not improve with dialysis ?
mcqs.explanation: Renal osteodystrophy does not show improvement with dialysis . Failure of renal function leads to decreased renal vitamin D production . The resulting hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia , in turn, lead to secondary hyperparathyroidism . This can be corrected only by vitamin D and calcium supplementation . Other manifestations of renal dysfunction and uremia show improvement with regular dialysis sessions .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of death in patients undergoing chronic dialysis ?
mcqs.explanation: Cardiovascular disease due to accelerated atherosclerosis is the major cause of death in patients with ESRD on chronic dialysis . Cardiovascular mortality is higher in dialysis patients compared to patients after transplantation.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: You are educating a patient about performing peritoneal dialysis at home. During this process, how much fluid is infused into the peritoneum ?
mcqs.explanation: In peritoneal dialysis , 1.5–3 L of dialysis fluid is infused into the peritoneal cavity. In this process , the peritoneum itself acts as a semipermeable membrane. A peritoneal catheter is used to infuse the fluid into the cavity. It is allowed to dwell for a set period of time usually 2–4 hours to allow for the removal of metabolic waste products . The dialysis fluid contains osmotically active agents such as glucose or icodextrin. The following image shows the process of peritoneal dialysis .743

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 56-year-old man presents with fever and severe abdominal pain for 2 days. He has been on peritoneal dialysis for the past 1 year. On examination, there is abdominal distension , guarding, and rebound tenderness . Which of the following is the most common cause of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario in a patient undergoing peritoneal dialysis is suggestive of peritonitis . It is most commonly caused by gram-positive cocci such as Staphylococcus , which spread from the skin.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A woman is started on continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis . Which of the following complications is she unlikely to develop ?
mcqs.explanation: Weight gain is a complication of peritoneal dialysis , not weight loss. The complications of peritoneal dialysis include : • Peritonitis • Catheter -associated non-peritonitis infections • Weight gain • Metabolic disturbances - hypoproteinemia and hyperglycemia • Residual uremia - especially among patients with no residual kidney function • Insulin resistance • Hypertriglyceridemia

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about renal transplants?

options.a: ABO and HLA mismatch are relative contraindications
options.b: Contraindicated in overt AIDS and active hepatitis
options.c: Complications in donor include hypertension and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
options.d: The most common cause of death after renal transplant is infections

mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of death in renal transplant recipients is cardiovascular causes . It occurs in > 50% of patients .744 Other complications in recipients include : • Infections • Most common - CMV. • Most specific - BK (polyoma) virus • Most common fungal - pneumocystis. • Malignancy - most commonly of skin and lip Donors can develop long-term complications related to premature failure of the single remaining kidney including: • Hypertension • Proteinuria • Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) ABO and HLA mismatch are relative, not absolute contraindications due to the availability of desensitization procedures . The absolute contraindications for transplantation are as follows :Recipient Donor Any active infections / malign ancy Any active infections (includi ng HIV )/ malignancy Shortened life expectancy du e to other causes Uncontrolled diabetes / hyper tension Active substance abuse / unco ntrolled psychiatric condition Uncontrolled psychiatric con dition or suicidality Treatment nonadherence Age < 18 or lack of mental ca pacity Reversible renal failure

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about rejection reactions following a kidney transplant?

options.a: Acute rejection can occur due to both type 4 and type 2 hypersensitivity reactions
options.b: Hyperacute rejection is a type 2 hypersensitivity reaction
options.c: Induction therapy for prophylaxis of rejection is cyclosporine , azathioprine, prednisolone .
options.d: Alemtuzumab is monoclonal antibody against CD52 used for immunosuppression

mcqs.explanation: Cyclosporine , azathioprine, prednisolone constitute the prophylactic maintenance therapy used after renal transplant. Immunosuppressive therapy is given to reduce the risk of transplant rejection reactions. The following regimen is commonly followed : • Induction therapy : • Given at the time of transplant to reduce the risk of early acute rejection . • The preferred treatment is anti-lymphocyte serum and alemtuzumab . • Maintenance therapy : • Given to all kidney transplant patients except when the donor and recipient are identical twins. • The most common combination used is :745 cyclosporine , azathioprine, and prednisolone (also known as triple therapy ). • Belatacept is a co-stimulatory blocking antibody approved by the FDA for maintenance therapy . Rejection reactions can be hyperacute , acute , or chronic. Treatment of rejection is as follows : • First episode - IV prednisolone for 3 days • Failure to respond to prednisone or second episode - anti-thymocyte globulin

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man with polycystic kidney disease underwent renal transplantation 3 months ago. Which of the following infections is he at the highest risk of?
mcqs.explanation: The most common opportunistic infection occurring 1-6 months after renal transplant is Cytomegalovirus (CMV). Pneumocystis carinii is rare these days due to universal prophylaxis for 6-12 months following transplantation.Opportunistic infections after renal transplant < 1 month 1-6 months > 6 months Wound infectionsHerpesviru sOral candidiasisUrinary trac t infection Pneumocystis cariniiCytomeg alovirusLegionellaListeriaHe patitis B, C AspergillusNocardiaBK virus Herpes zosterHepatitis B, C

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following lesions does not recur in the transplanted kidney?
mcqs.explanation: Alport syndrome does not recur in the transplanted kidney. This is because it occurs due to an inherited defect in type 4 collagen in the glomerular basement membrane. This defect is absent in the transplanted kidney. Diabetic nephropathy , membranous glomerulonephritis , and lupus nephritis can recur in the transplanted kidney.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Patients with which of the following conditions have the highest risk of disease recurrence after renal transplant?
mcqs.explanation: Patients with diabetic nephropathy have the highest risk of disease recurrence after renal transplant. Nearly 52% of transplant recipients have histological evidence of diabetic kidney disease /mesangial sclerosis at 10 years after transplantation. The recurrence rates of the other conditions are as follows : • Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis: -48% • Membranous glomerulonephritis : -45% • Lupus nephritis: 2-11 %746

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the average life expectancy in patients following a living-donor kidney transplant?
mcqs.explanation: The average life expectancy of a living-donor graft is around 14 years and that of a deceased -donor graft is around 10 years.747

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Cystic and Inherited Disorders of the Kidney
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease ?

options.a: ADPKD progresses to end-stage renal disease in early adulthood
options.b: Calcium oxalate stones are the most common kidney stones
options.c: Renal cyst infections are rarely seen
options.d: Cardiovascular complications are a major cause of mortality

mcqs.explanation: Cardiovascular complications are the most common cause of mortality in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). Infections are the second most common cause . ADPKD is usually clinically silent . Many cases remain asymptomatic until the fifth decade of life and are diagnosed incidentally . PKD-1 mutations cause more severe disease than PKD-2 mutations. The following clinical features may be seen in symptomatic patients : • Abdominal mass • Back or flank pain • Recurrent UTIs - Renal cyst infections by Gram-negative bacteria are common • Nephrolithiasis - most commonly uric acid stones • Hematuria • Cardiac: • Hypertension - early feature • Left ventricular hypertrophy • Mitral valve prolapse , valvular insufficiency753 • Extra-renal: • Intracranial aneurysms • Hepatic cysts As the cysts grow they compress on the surrounding normal tissue which leads to a progressive reduction in the GFR. Eventually , it leads to end-stage renal disease (ESRD) by the fifth decade of life .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Cystic and Inherited Disorders of the Kidney
mcqs.question: A 48-year-old woman developed a sudden severe headache and vomiting. Her neighbor rushed her to the hospital where she was declared dead on arrival . She lived alone and her family history is unknown. An autopsy revealed a subarachnoid hemorrhage and the following findings in her kidneys. Which of the following is incorrect about this condition?

options.a: Mutation of PKD-1 is responsible for 85% of cases
options.b: PKD-2 mutation has higher risk of end-stage renal disease than PKD-
options.c: The PKD genes code for the polycystin protein
options.d: Cysts are formed only in 5% of the tubules of the kidney

mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario with a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and multiple renal cysts is suggestive of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). The PKD-1 mutation has a higher risk of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) than PKD-2. ADPKD is a disorder which is characterized by progressive bilateral formation of renal cysts . It is caused by the following mutations: • PKD1 gene on chromosome 16 (85%) - codes for polycystin -1 • PKD2 gene on chromosome 4 (15%) - codes for polycystin -2 Polycystins are transmembrane proteins that are present on the primary cilia of the tubular cells . The mutated proteins in ADPKD alter the normal functioning and triggers cell growth and cyst formation. Though cysts are formed only in 5% of the tubules of the kidney, they compress surrounding renal tissue due to their enormous growth . This results in loss of renal function.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Cystic and Inherited Disorders of the Kidney
mcqs.question: In patients with ADPKD, cysts are least likely to be present in which of the following sites ?
mcqs.explanation: In patients with ADPKD, cysts in the lungs are very rare. There are very few case reports with lung cysts in ADPKD patients , but the association between ADPKD and lung cysts has not been proved. However, there is a three -fold increase in the incidence of bronchiectasis in ADPKD patients . The common extrarenal manifestations of ADPKD include : • Hepatic cysts (50-70%) - most common • Seminal vesicle cysts (40%) - can result in infertility • Arachnoid membrane cysts (8%) - usually asymptomatic , may increase the risk of subdural hematoma • Pancreatic cysts (7-36%) • Splenic cysts754

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Cystic and Inherited Disorders of the Kidney
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man presents with loss of weight and appetite over the last 3 months. He was diagnosed with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease 15 years ago. A CT abdomen reveals bilateral, multicentric renal masses along with enlarged retroperitoneal lymph nodes . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario is suggestive of renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with lymph node metastases . The sarcomatoid type of RCC is commonly associated with ADPKD. Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is a relatively rare complication of ADPKD. There does not seem to be an increased frequency of RCC in these patients compared to the general population . However, when it occurs, it tends to be bilateral, multicentric and of sarcomatoid type .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Cystic and Inherited Disorders of the Kidney
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old woman presented with persistent headaches over the last 1 month. Her father and paternal uncle suffered from kidney disease and both died in their 50's of a 'brain bleed '. Her blood pressure is 160 /110 mm Hg and had also been elevated during a previous visit. Which of the following investigations should be avoided in this patient ?

options.b: Contrast enhanced CT of the abdomen
options.c: Non-contrast CT scan of the abdomen
options.d: MR angiography of the cerebral vasculature

mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario is suggestive of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). These patients usually have impaired renal function. Hence , contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) would usually be avoided due to the risk of contrast nephrotoxicity . The following investigations are done in patients with ADPKD: • USG abdomen - for screening and diagnosis • Non-contrast CT abdomen - more sensitive and picks up cysts of smaller size • MR-angiography of brain - pre-symptomatic screening for intracerebral aneurysms

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Cystic and Inherited Disorders of the Kidney
mcqs.question: How many renal cysts on USG are required to diagnose a 45-year-old patient with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease ?

options.a: At least 2 cysts in each kidney
options.b: At least 3 cysts in each kidney
options.c: At least 4 cysts in each kidney
options.d: Even a single cyst in each kidney

mcqs.explanation: Between 40-59 years of age , the presence of \0372 cysts in each kidney is needed to diagnose ADPKD. This condition is diagnosed based on the USG findings using the Ravine 's criteria:Age (in years) Imaging findings 15-39 Total of \0373 cysts , unilateral o r bilateral 40-59 \0372 cysts in each kidney \037 \037 4 cysts in each kidney

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Cystic and Inherited Disorders of the Kidney
mcqs.question: A 56-year-old woman on dialysis is being planned for a renal transplant with her son as an organ donor. He undergoes a USG scan as part of routine donor evaluation. The following findings are seen . Which of the following will you not recommend for the son?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario and USG showing a cystic appearance of the kidney is suggestive of asymptomatic autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). Surgical decompression is not a routine procedure performed in these patients . It may be required only in cases of very large cysts causing persistent pain and infected cysts . The management includes the following : • Analgesics755 • Increased fluid intake • Prevents renal stone formation • Reduces growth of cysts by suppressing ADH release • ACE inhibitors and ARBs • Blood pressure control • Slowing of cyst growth • Tolvaptan (V2 receptor antagonist) • Reduce pain and slow the decline in renal function • Renal transplant • Definitive management • Pre-transplant nephrectomy may be required in patients with very large polycystic kidneys

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Cystic and Inherited Disorders of the Kidney
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old G2P1L0 female patient came for an antenatal check-up at 26 weeks gestation . On examination, her abdominal girth was less for gestational age and the fetal parts were easily palpable . Medical records from her previous pregnancy showed that the deceased infant had been positive for a PKHD1 mutation. Which of the following statements is correct regarding the most likely diagnosis of the fetus ?

options.a: It is commonly an asymptomatic and mild disease
options.b: In severe cases , it can be diagnosed antenatally on USG
options.c: Respiratory insufficiency is uncommon in newborns
options.d: It is commonly diagnosed at 5-10 years of age

mcqs.explanation: A PKHD1 mutation in the deceased infant is suggestive of autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD). As the woman has signs of oligohydramnios, it is likely that this fetus also has ARPKD. Severe cases of ARPKD can be diagnosed in-utero with a USG. Prenatal testing can also be done. ARPKD is a hereditary renal disease of childhood caused by a mutation in the PKHD1 gene on chromosome 6. It codes for fibrocystin/ polyductin (FPC), a membrane protein present in the cells of the cortical and medullary collecting ducts . Affected fetuses show greatly enlarged kidneys and reduced fetal urine production . This leads to oligohydramnios and pulmonary hypoplasia . About 30% of neonates die soon after birth due to respiratory insufficiency . Most deaths occur < 1 month of life . Others develop chronic kidney disease and hypertension in early childhood .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Cystic and Inherited Disorders of the Kidney
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a typical feature seen in patients with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Hepatic cysts are not a typical feature of autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD). They occur only in rare cases . ARPKD is usually diagnosed in the neonatal period . These patients commonly have the following findings: • Hypertension • Chronic renal insufficiency • Congenital hepatic fibrosis • Biliary dysgenesis with periportal fibrosis is seen • Can lead to portal hypertension756 • Caroli's disease - dilatation of intrahepatic bile ducts Note : Caroli's disease is also associated with medullary sponge kidney.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Cystic and Inherited Disorders of the Kidney
mcqs.question: Match the following :
mcqs.explanation: The gene mutations causing the following cystic disorders are: • Medullary cystic kidney disease -1 (MCKD-1) - MUC1 • Medullary cystic kidney disease -2 (MCKD-2) - UMOD • Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD) - PKHD1 • Adolescent nephronophthisis - NPHP 1-20 Medullary cystic kidney disease (MCKD) is an autosomal dominant disorder. It presents with a late-onset , slowly progressive renal failure. Renal cysts are not common but can be seen occasionally. Medullary cystic kidney diseases are of two types , MCKD1 and MCKD2. MCKD1 is due to a defect in the mucin 1 (MUC1) gene . The mutated gene codes for a large protein fragment that has a toxic effect on the tubules . It is not associated with elevated uric acid levels and gout . MCKD2 is due to a defect in the UMOD gene , which codes for the protein uromodulin. It is associated with hyperuricemia and gout.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Cystic and Inherited Disorders of the Kidney
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an autosomal recessive renal cystic disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Nephronophthisis is an autosomal recessive renal cystic disease . It belongs to a category of conditions called ciliopathies . It occurs due to an underlying defect in the primary cilia of the tubular epithelial cells . The cilia play an important role in cell signaling and maintenance of cell growth , proliferation, and secretion . Other ciliopathies include autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease , autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease , and medullary cystic kidney disease .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Cystic and Inherited Disorders of the Kidney
mcqs.question: What is the most common inherited cause of kidney failure in children?
mcqs.explanation: The most common inherited cause of kidney failure in childhood is nephronophthisis . Nephronophthisis (NPHP) refers to a group of related , but genetically distinct , autosomal recessive disorders. Mutations are seen in the NPHP genes 1-20 . These genes code for nephrocystins which are expressed on the kidney tubules . NPHP is classified into infantile, juvenile, and adolescent forms. The juvenile form is the most common form. Common features include tubulointerstitial fibrosis, renal cysts , and chronic kidney disease .757

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Cystic and Inherited Disorders of the Kidney
mcqs.question: A child with Joubert syndrome will have which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Joubert's syndrome is defined by the presence of juvenile nephronophthisis (NPHP) and multiple neurologic findings. A few examples of multiorgan syndromes associated with nephronophthisis are: • Senior-Loken syndrome: NPHP with retinitis pigmentosa • Joubert syndrome: NPHP with multiple neurologic findings • Bardet-Biedl syndrome: NPHP with truncal obesity , cognitive impairment, retinal dystrophy , and polydactyly

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Cystic and Inherited Disorders of the Kidney
mcqs.question: The following finding on intravenous pyelography is seen in which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a paintbrush or bouquet of flowers appearance on intravenous pyelography (IVP ). It occurs in medullary sponge kidney (MSK ). MSK is a sporadic benign condition that is often diagnosed incidentally . It is a developmental defect affecting the formation of collecting tubules and results in cystic dilatation of the medullary and papillary portions of collecting ducts . It is characterized by medullary cysts that are of variable size. It is associated with distal RTA which leads to hypercalciuria. The hypercalciuria leads to a tendency to form calcium oxalate and calcium phosphate stones . The patients can also have recurrent UTIs and hematuria. CT urography has largely replaced intravenous pyelography as the investigation of choice .758

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What acid-base disturbance is seen in patients with renal tubular acidosis?

options.a: Normal anion gap hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis.
options.b: High anion gap hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis
options.c: Normal anion gap hypochloremic metabolic acidosis
options.d: High anion gap hypochloremic metabolic acidosis.

mcqs.explanation: In renal tubular acidosis (RTA), there is normal anion gap hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis. RTA refers to a group of disorders in which there is impaired tubular transport of H+ and/or HCO3- despite relatively well -preserved renal function. There are 4 types : • Type I - impaired H+ secretion (distal), leading to decreased HCO3- production • Type II - impaired HCO3- reabsorption (proximal) • Type III - carbonic anhydrase deficiency causing defects in the transport of both H+ and HCO3- (mixed) • Type IV - hypoaldosteronism (hyperkalemic ) The overall deficiency of HCO3- in all the types is compensated by Cl- secretion . Hence , the serum anion gap remains normal .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common type of renal tubular acidosis?
mcqs.explanation: The most common type of renal tubular acidosis (RTA) is the type 4 or hyperkalemic type .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about type 4 renal tubular acidosis?

options.a: The most common cause is diabetes mellitus
options.b: It can occurs in patients with interstitial renal diseases
options.d: It is caused by hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism

mcqs.explanation: Type 4 renal tubular acidosis can be a congenital or acquired disorder.763 It is caused by conditions that result in hypoaldosteronism or hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism including: • Diabetic nephropathy - most common • Tubulointerstitial disease • Addison's disease • Obstructive uropathy • Drugs like NSAIDs, ACEI, ARBs can increase the risk • Psuedohypoaldosteronism type 1 (due to aldosterone resistance ) • Psuedohypoaldosteronism type 2/ gordons syndrome (due to defects in Na-Cl cotransporter) • Congenital isolated hypoaldosteronism (due to enzyme deficiency )

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 52-year-old man presented with dizziness and infrequent urination. He was diagnosed with stage 4 chronic kidney disease last month. Investigations reveal metabolic acidosis and hyperkalemia. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Hyperkalemia is a characteristic feature of type 4 RTA or generalized distal RTA . It commonly occurs in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). In CKD patients , renal dysfunction results in hyperkalemia only when the GFR is severely impaired (stage 5). Hyperkalemia in the earlier stages of CKD is suggestive of type 4 RTA . In CKD, volume overload leads to low levels of renin and, hence , aldosterone . This leads to Na+ loss and K+ retention in the distal tubule . The resultant hyperkalemia causes impaired NH3 synthesis in the proximal tubule . Hence , H+ cannot be excreted as NH4+ ions. Retained H+ ions lead to reduced HCO3- production and acidosis.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following would not be seen in patients with type 1 renal tubular acidosis?

options.c: Urinary pH is < 5.5 after acid loading

mcqs.explanation: Urinary pH will be > 5.5 after acid loading in RTA type 1. In this condition, there is a defect in H+ secretion by the distal tubules . Hence , there is a failure of urine acidification. H+ combines with NH3 to form NH\037\037 and thus in RTA type 1, NH4+ excretion is reduced . In the acid loading test , acidosis is induced by the administration of NH4Cl (releases H+). In normal individuals, this results in increased excretion of H+, leading to acidic urine (pH < 5.5). However, this fails to occur in RTA type 1. Impaired secretion of H+ leads to potassium wasting and hypokalemia (via the H+/K+ATPase antiporter). The resulting metabolic acidosis causes bone demineralization and resorption.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 6-month-old infant is being evaluated for failure to thrive. Lab investigations are as follows . Hypokalemia is found to improve following alkalinization therapy . What type of renal stones is this infant at a higher risk of developing ?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario is suggestive of type 1 RTA . In this condition, calcium phosphate and oxalate stones are formed in the distal convoluting tubules (DCT ).764 In this condition, there is a defect in H+ secretion by the distal tubules . This leads to: • Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis • Urinary pH > 5.5 • Hypokalemia • Impaired H+ secretion causes K+ wasting • It improves following alkalinization therapy with NaHCO3 Acidemia leads to hypercalcemia and then hypercalciuria. There is also hypocitraturia as acidemia induces increased cell citrate utilization. Normally, citrate in the urine binds to calcium and increases its solubility . In the absence of citrate in the urine, calcium begins to precipitate . This leads to nephrocalcinosis and calcium phosphate and oxalate stones .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following would you not expect in a patient with Lowe's syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Hypertonia is not a feature of Lowe's syndrome or oculo -cerebro-renal syndrome. The following clinical features are seen in this condition: • Hypotonia • Cataract • Glaucoma • Intellectual disability • Renal tubular acidosis (RTA) type 2

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is unlikely to be seen in patients with Dent's disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Dent's disease is an inherited cause of type 2 RTA . A proximal renal tubular defect is seen in this condition, not a distal tubular defect . It is an X-linked recessive condition. It is caused by inactivating mutations in CLCN5, a chloride transporter expressed in endosomes of the proximal tubule . The resulting dysfunction of the proximal convoluted tubule and failure of reabsorption of substances leads to: • Hypercalciuria • Hypophosphatemia • Recurrent kidney stones

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Patients with which of the following are not at risk of developing type 2 renal tubular acidosis?
mcqs.explanation: Medullary sponge kidney is a cause of RTA type 1, not type 2. The causes of RTA type 2 include :765 • Amyloidosis • Wilson's disease • Galactosemia • Hereditary fructose intolerance • Cystinosis • Lowe syndrome • Drugs - tenofovir, acetazolamide , topiramate The causes of RTA type 1 include : • Familial defects • Autoimmune conditions - SLE, Sjogren syndrome • Drugs - amphotericin, lithium, aminoglycosides , ifosfamide • Medullary sponge kidney

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about renal tubular acidosis type 2?

options.b: It can be caused by Lowe's syndrome
options.c: Renal stones may occur in patients

mcqs.explanation: Renal stones are not a feature of type 2 or proximal RTA . This is because high levels of citrate in the urine bind with calcium and prevent stone formation. In this condition, the cells of the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) fail to reabsorb HCO3-. In the initial stages, this HCO3- loss leads to a urine pH > 5.5. However, as the body's HCO3- stores are depleted , the urinary pH falls to < 5.5 as the secretion of H+ in the DCT remains intact. Hence , the minimum urinary pH is < 5.5. It can be caused by Lowe's syndrome but a majority of type 2 RTA cases are associated with Fanconi's syndrome. This syndrome is characterized by a generalized defect of reabsorption of various substances at the PCT. This leads to loss of HCO3-, glucose , amino acids, phosphate, citrate, and calcium in the urine. Loss of phosphate leads to vitamin -D resistant hypophosphatemic rickets /osteomalacia. Note : An exception is Dent's disease , a genetic cause of RTA type 2 in which renal stones are present .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 14-month-old baby was brought with complaints of refusal to walk after a minor fall while playing. Imaging revealed a left tibial fracture along with generalized sclerosis and a bone-in-bone appearance . Additionally , his developmental milestones were found to be delayed . Investigations are as follows . What is the likely renal tubular defect present in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Pathological fractures and a bone-in-bone appearance point towards a diagnosis of osteopetrosis . The lab values are significant for hypokalemia with normal anion gap metabolic acidosis. These findings are suggestive of renal tubular acidosis (RTA) type 3. Type 3 or mixed RTA is a rare condition that usually occurs in neonates and infants. It is due to an autosomal recessive , inherited carbonic anhydrase-2 (CA-2) deficiency . This results in features of both distal and proximal RTA with: • Failure to reabsorb HCO3 at PCT766 • Failure to excrete H+ at DCT This results in the following findings: • Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis • Hypokalemia • Urinary pH > 5.5 • Positive urine anion gap As CA-2 is widely expressed , mutations of this gene result in a condition called marble brain disease or Guibaud-Vainsel syndrome. It presents with multiple clinical findings including: • Cerebral calcifications • Mental retardation • Mixed RTA (Type 3 RTA ) • Osteopetrosis

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man is being evaluated for high blood pressure noted on multiple occasions. Investigations reveal metabolic alkalosis, suppressed renin levels , and high urine chloride levels . What is the likely cause ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario with hypertension and metabolic alkalosis is suggestive of Liddle's syndrome. It is an autosomal dominant condition due to a gain of function mutation in the ENaC gene . This gene codes for the epithelial sodium channels present in the kidney. This leads to increased sodium retention and results in a state of pseudo -hyperaldosteronism . The following findings are seen : • Hypertension • Hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis • Normal-low aldosterone • Low renin Treatment is with diuretics that directly block the ENaC channels, like amiloride and triamterene. Spironolactone is not effective as it is an aldosterone -receptor antagonist.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A young patient presented with polyuria and polydipsia . His BP is 130 /80 mm Hg. Laboratory parameters revealed serum K+ of 3.2 mmol/L , blood pH of 7.46, and hypomagnesemia . Urinary calcium was elevated . He is not on any medications . This condition is likely due to a defect in which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario is suggestive of Bartter syndrome. It occurs due to a defect in the Na+/K+/Cl- channel in the thick ascending loop of Henle . A defect in the Na+/K+/Cl- channel impairs the transport functions of the thick ascending loop of Henle . It results in the following features: • Polyuria and polydipsia • Natriuresis with high aldosterone (due to RAAS activation)767 • Hypokalemia • Metabolic alkalosis • Hypomagnesemia • Hypocalcemia and hypercalciuria The clinical features of this condition are similar to the effects of loop diuretics . These drugs also act on the Na+/K+/Cl- channel. Hence , response to loop diuretics may be blunted . Treatment is with potassium -sparing diuretics like spironolactone and amiloride. NSAID's like indomethacin are second line drugs however they can reduce renal function. Option A: Defect in the proximal tubule results in Fanconi's syndrome. These patients have acidosis , with glycosuria , generalized aminoaciduria, and phosphaturia . Option B: Defect in the Na+/Cl- cotransporter in distal convoluted tubule (DCT) results in Gitelman syndrome. These patients also present with hypokalemic alkalosis and hypomagnesemia . However, they also develop , hypocalciuria, and chondrocalcinosis. Option D: Increased activation of the epithelial sodium channels (ENaC) channels results in Liddle syndrome. This causes increased reabsorption of Na+ exchanged for K+ causing hypokalemia. Increased Na absorption leads to hypertension .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 17-year-old boy is being evaluated for fatigue and muscle weakness for 3 months. On examination , Chvostek's sign is positive and BP is 90/60 mm Hg. Investigations show hypokalemia and hypercalcemia with metabolic alkalosis. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Chvostek's sign (spasm of facial muscles on tapping the facial nerve) indicates tetany . In this patient with hypercalcemia , it is likely due to hypomagnesemia . These clinical features are suggestive of Gitelman syndrome. This condition occurs due to a mutation of Na+/Cl- cotransporter in the distal collecting tubule (DCT). The resulting impairment of the tubular transport leads to the following features : • Mild natriuresis with normal -low BP • Increased renin and aldosterone • Hypokalemia • Metabolic alkalosis • Hypercalcemia and hypocalciuria • Hypomagnesemia The clinical features of this condition are similar to the effects of thiazide diuretics . These drugs also act on the Na+/Cl- cotransporter. Hence , response to thiazide diuretics may be blunted . Treatment is with potassium -sparing diuretics like spironolactone and amiloride. Option A: Bartter syndrome affects the Na+/K+/Cl- channels. It causes hypocalcemia and hypercalciuria. Option C: Liddle syndrome causes increased activation of ENaC channels. It results in hypokalemia and hypertension . Option D: Fanconi's syndrome occurs due to a defect in proximal tubular function . It results in metabolic acidosis.768

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true regarding renal vein thrombosis?

options.a: Right renal vein is more commonly involved
options.b: Most common cause in children is nephrotic syndrome
options.c: Investigation of choice is doppler ultrasound of renal vein
options.d: Most common cause in elderly is renal cell carcinoma

mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of renal vein thrombosis in the elderly is renal cell carcinoma (RCC). The most common causes of renal vein thrombosis in different age groups are as follows : • Children - Dehydration, followed by sepsis • Adults - Nephrotic syndrome (most commonly membranous glomerulonephritis ) • Elderly - Renal cell carcinoma The left renal vein is more commonly involved and 2/3rd of cases are bilateral. Doppler USG is used for screening but the investigation of choice is CT angiography.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 10 -year-old child develops hematuria after 4 days of severe diarrhea. Peripheral smear shows fragmented RBCs and thrombocytopenia . Ultrasound reveals the enlargement of both kidneys. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario is suggestive of renal vein thrombosis secondary to dehydration . Hematuria in children following diarrhea can be due to the following : Henoch-Schonlein purpura would present 1-3 weeks after an upper respiratory infection . It causes hematuria, non-blanching rash over the buttocks , and abdominal pain.773 Hemolytic uremic syndro me Renal vein thrombosis Onset 5-10 days after diarrhea Depends on severity of dehyd ration Renal failure Present Present Hematuria + + Peripheral smear fragmente d RBCs + + Platelets Decreased Decreased USG kidney Normal Enlarged due to congestion b y renal vein thrombosis (bilat eral in 67% cases )

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of hemolytic uremic syndrome globally ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) globally is Escherichia coli O157:H7. The causes of HUS are as follows : • Infections: Usually occur 5-10 days after diarrheal diseases due to bacterial exotoxins. • E.coli O157 :H7 - Shiga-like toxin (verotoxin) • Shigella dysenteriae type I - Shiga toxin • Streptococcus pneumoniae • Autoimmunity • Complement activation (in atypical HUS)

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about hemolytic uremic syndrome?

options.a: Symptoms and signs of HUS develops as diarrhea begins to improve
options.b: Only supportive managment of acute renal failure is done in typical HUS
options.c: Eculizumab improves microangiopathic hemolytic anemia in atypical HUS
options.d: Coomb's positive hemolytic anemia is seen in HUS

mcqs.explanation: The hemolytic anemia in hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) occurs as a result of mechanical RBC destruction caused by microthrombi. Hence , Coomb's test is negative . There are two types of HUS, namely typical and atypical .Typical HUS Atypical HUS 5-10 daysafter diarrheal illne ssE .coliO157 :H7orShigella dy senteriaetype I Mutation in genes encoding c omplement regulatory protei n774 Typical HUS Atypical HUS Shiga-liketoxinsproduced cau seendothelialdamage .This lea ds to platelet activation and t hrombi.
