mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 56-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with sudden onset headache and photophobia . On examination, she is disoriented and febrile . The investigations and peripheral smear are given below . Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding this disease ?

options.a: It is caused by ADAMTS13 deficiency
options.b: 20 % patients will have falsely positive RA factor
options.c: Arrhythmias are a frequent cause of death
options.d: Mainstay of treatment is blood transfusion

mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario and image showing schistocytes (fragmented RBCs) in a woman are suggestive of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP ). Blood transfusion is not preferred in TTP as it can aggravate the condition. TTP is a type of thrombotic microangiopathy that occurs due to deficiency or autoantibodies against the ADAMTS13 metalloprotease , which is responsible for cleaving von Willebrand factor multimers. In the absence of this protein, vWF multimers aggregate and form thrombi. It presents with a classical pentad of clinical features : • Fever • Thrombocytopenia • Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia • Renal failure • Neurological manifestations It is treated with plasmapheresis and rituximab.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most\037 common cause of clinically significant renal artery stenosis ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of clinically significant renal artery stenosis is atherosclerosis . Renal artery stenosis is a relatively common finding in older patients with chronic essential hypertension. However, it is considered clinically significant only when renovascular hypertension develops . It occurs in the case of: • > 70% stenosis in both renal arteries • > 50% stenosis with post stenotic dilatation The causes of renal artery stenosis are: • Atherosclerosis (most common) - common in older patients with cardiovascular risk factors • Fibromuscular dysplasia – more common in young, white females and is usually bilateral • Less common causes include : • Thromboemboli775 • External compression by tumors • Systemic vasculitis • Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome • Transplant renal artery stenosis • Infrarenal aortic aneurysms and dissections The investigation of choice for renal artery stenosis is renal angiography.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect about fibromuscular dysplasia ?

options.a: String of beads appearance on angiography
options.c: Most commonly affected peripheral artery is subclavian artery

mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario and the string of beads appearance on CT angiography is characteristic of fibromuscular dysplasia . The most common peripheral (limb) arteries affected are the iliac arteries. Fibromuscular dysplasia is a segmental , non-atheromatous, dysplastic type of angiopathy that predominantly affects females . The most common subtype is medial fibroplasia. It is one of the major causes of renovascular hypertension . The most common sites of involvement in decreasing order of frequency are as follows : • Renal arteries • Carotid arteries • Peripheral (limb) arteries - most commonly iliac arteries On angiography, a string of beads appearance is seen as shown below .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is unlikely in patients with atheroembolic kidney disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Atheroembolic kidney disease is associated with decreased complement levels .776 Atheroembolic kidney disease is more frequent in males with a history of diabetes , hypertension, and ischemic heart disease . Most clinical atheroembolic events follow angiographic procedures , often of the coronary vessels . It is associated with aortic aneurysms and renal artery stenosis . Systemic embolic manifestations such as fever, abdominal pain, and weight loss are also present , although cutaneous manifestations are more common like livedo reticularis and localized toe gangrene . The lab findings include : • Rising serum creatinine • Transient eosinophilia • Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate • Hypocomplementemia Definitive diagnosis depends on kidney biopsy which demonstrates microvessel occlusion with cholesterol crystals that leave a cleft in the vessel as shown below .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old patient is being evaluated for uncontrolled hypertension despite being on 3 antihypertensive drugs. He has a history of myocardial infarction which was managed with percutaneous intervention last month. On examination, an abdominal bruit is noted . Lab values indicate elevated serum urea and creatinine. Which of the following investigations is the gold standard test to diagnose this condition?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario is suggestive of renal artery stenosis . Renal intra-arterial angiography is the gold standard for diagnosis.In a patient with hypertension and increased creatinine, an ultrasound of the abdomen must be performed first to visualize the renal size and morphology to look for a unilateral shrunken kidney and thereby renal artery stenosis . Option A: MR angiography is less preferred as gadolinium contrast can lead to nephrogenic fibrosis, particularly in patients with reduced kidney function. Option C: CT scan with image reconstruction provides an excellent image but also carries a risk of contrast nephropathy . Option D: Renal arterial doppler ultrasound measures renal artery velocities and can predict hemodynamically important lesions . However, it is not the gold standard test . Duplex777 ultrasonography is used as a screening investigation.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs must be avoided in patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis ?
mcqs.explanation: ACE inhibitors must be avoided in patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis (RAS). In renal artery stenosis , blood flow to the kidney is reduced , thereby reducing blood flow to the afferent arterioles . Hence , constriction of efferent arterioles is needed to maintain hydrostatic pressure within the glomerulus in order to maintain GFR. ACEIs and ARBs inhibit efferent renal arteriolar vasoconstriction. In bilateral RAS, this causes a decline in the GFR within a few days of starting the drug. Note : Bilateral renal artery stenosis has been classically considered as an absolute contraindication to the use of ACE inhibitors. However, new studies show that they may be used in some cases with careful monitoring.778

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: 'a' wave in JVP corresponds to?
mcqs.explanation: The "a" wave in jugular venous pressure (JVP ) is a positive wave, which corresponds to right atrial contraction. The waveforms seen in a normal JVP are: • a wave corresponds to atrial contraction and occurs just after the P wave (on ECG) and just before the first heart sound. • c wave represents the bulging of the tricuspid valve into the right atrium during ventricular systole . • x descent corresponds to the atrial relaxation during atrial diastole . • v wave represents atrial filling during ventricular systole and peaks at the second heart sound. • y descent represents passive emptying of the right atrium into the right ventricle after tricuspid valve opening.789

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: The c wave seen in a normal JVP waveform represents ?

options.a: Bulging of tricuspid valve into the right atrium
options.c: Venous filling of the right atrium
options.d: Emptying of the right atrium into the right ventricle

mcqs.explanation: The c-wave in a JVP waveform represents the bulging of the tricuspid valve into the right atrium during ventricular systole . JVP measured in the internal jugular vein is a reflection of the right atrial pressure . The waveforms seen in a normal JVP are: • a wave corresponds to atrial contraction and occurs just after the P wave (on ECG) and just before the first heart sound. • c wave represents the bulging of the tricuspid valve into the right atrium during ventricular systole . • x descent corresponds to the atrial relaxation during atrial diastole . • v wave represents atrial filling during ventricular systole and peaks at the second heart sound. • y descent represents passive emptying of the right atrium into the right ventricle after tricuspid valve opening.790

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: The following abnormality on a JVP waveform can be seen in which of the given conditions?
mcqs.explanation: The given waveform shows a cannon 'a' wave seen in ventricular tachycardia. It occurs since atria contract against a closed tricuspid valve in ventricular tachycardia. JVP measured in the internal jugular vein is a reflection of the right atrial pressure . Note : Giant/prominent a-waves occur during every beat while cannon a-waves result from arrhythmias, therefore , are usually intermittent . The ECG is helpful to look for rhythm disturbances that are associated with cannon a-waves whereas echocardiography can be used to assess structural defects (of right atrium) that are associated with giant a-waves.791

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 37-year-old male patient comes to the clinic with complaints of weakness , restlessness , and chest pain. On examination, his blood pressure is found to be 90/60 mmHg, his heart sounds are muffled , and his neck veins are distended . What is the typical JVP finding in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Hypotension , soft or absent heart sounds , and jugular venous distention (Beck's triad) are the three principal features of cardiac tamponade . The typical JVP finding here is absent y-descent . JVP shows a prominent x (early systolic) descent and an absent y (early diastolic ) descent because of the ventricle's limited or absent early diastolic filling. JVP is almost always elevated in cardiac tamponade and may be associated with venous distention in the forehead and scalp . There may be reductions in the amplitude of the QRS complexes , and electrical alternans of the P, QRS, or T waves in cardiac tamponade. Note : Alternation of QRS complexes , usually in a 2:1 ratio, on ECG is called electrical alternans. It is caused by the movement of the heart in the pericardial space . Electrical alternans is also seen in patients with myocardial ischemia, acute pulmonary embolism, and tachyarrhythmias.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Deep y descent in JVP is seen in all except :
mcqs.explanation: The y-descent in jugular venous pulse (JVP ) corresponds to the fall in right atrial pressure after the tricuspid valve opening in the early diastolic phase of the right ventricle. Y-descent is attenuated or absent in cardiac tamponade because of resistance to ventricular filling in the early diastole . Other options : Options B and C: Restrictive cardiomyopathy and constrictive pericarditis can have deep y descent due to rapid filling of the right ventricle during early diastole . Option D: In patients with tricuspid regurgitation , increased blood flow to the right atria through the incompetent tricuspid valve during ventricular systole results in a prominent v wave. When the tricuspid valve opens during ventricular diastole , this increased blood in the right atria enters rapidly into the right ventricle during early diastole resulting in deep y-descent .792

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: The following four patients were examined on a tilt table for postural hypotension . The blood pressures before and immediately after performing head -up tilt are given below . Choose the correct option regarding the patients who suffer from orthostatic hypotension .
mcqs.explanation: Orthostatic hypotension is defined as a reduction in systolic blood pressure of at least 20 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure of at least 10 mmHg within 3 min of standing or head -up tilt on a tilt table . On standing, blood is displaced to the lower extremities , causing a drop in the venous return to the heart. This drop leads to a decrease in cardiac output and stimulation of compensatory mechanisms which trigger a reflex increase in sympathetic (vasoconstrictor) outflow . Orthostatic hypotension is a manifestation of sympathetic (autonomic) failure. Symptoms include light -headedness , dizziness, and presyncope (near-faintness) in response to sudden postural change.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Pulsus paradoxus is seen in all of the following except :
mcqs.explanation: Pulsus bisferiens is seen in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy , not pulsus paradoxus. Pulsus paradoxus refers to the fall in systolic pressure by > 10 mmHg with inspiration. It is an exaggeration of the normal response . It is seen in the following conditions: • Cardiac tamponade • Massive pulmonary embolism • Hemorrhagic shock • Obstructive lung disease • Tension pneumothorax

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Pulsus bisferiens is seen in all of the following conditions except :
mcqs.explanation: Pulsus alternans (characterized by alternating strong and weak beats ) is seen in left ventricular dysfunction . Pulsus bisferiens is a bifid pulse with two systolic peaks. It is seen in the following conditions: • Advanced aortic regurgitation (AR) • Aortic stenosis (AS) with AR • Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy793

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Water hammer pulse is seen in which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Water hammer pulse , also known as Corrigan 's pulse , is characterized by a sharp rise and a rapid fall-off and is seen in aortic regurgitation (AR) due to the fact that arterial pressure falls rapidly in late systole and early diastole . In AR, the pulse pressure is widened due to systolic hypertension and decreased diastolic pressure . The diastolic pressure is measured at Korotkoff phase IV . In certain patients with AR or a combination of aortic stenosis (AS) and AR, the carotid arterial pulse may exhibit a bisferiens pattern, characterized by two systolic waves separated by a trough. The apical impulse is heaving and displaced inferiorly. A diastolic thrill may be palpable along the left sternal border. A2 is usually absent in AR. An early diastolic murmur can be auscultated in chronic AR. It is best heard in the third intercostal space along the left sternal edge .794 Severe AS (Option A) would show pulsus parvus et tardus, characterized by the carotid pulse rising slowly to a delayed peak. Chronic mitral regurgitation (Option D) shows a sharp, low volume upstroke due to reduced cardiac output and acute mitral regurgitation demonstrates narrow pulse pressure .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A loud S1 is associated with?
mcqs.explanation: Rheumatic mitral stenosis is associated with loud S1. The greater the distance the valve travels to close , the louder is the sound. Increased left atrial pressures in rheumatic mitral stenosis force the mobile portion of the mitral valve leaflets far apart such that they are forced closed from a relatively far distance , resulting in a loud S1. In calcific mitral stenosis , leaflet mobility is poor, and they are not separated by a large distance , resulting in a soft S1. Loud S1 is heard in the following : • Short PR intervals • Early stages of mitral stenosis as long as the valves are pliable • Atrial myxoma • High output states • Tachycardia Soft S1 is heard in the following : • Mitral regurgitation • Aortic regurgitation • Long PR intervals • Calcified Mitral stenosis795 • Left ventricular contractile dysfunction • Beta-receptor blockers • Pericardial effusion , obesity , COPD- due to decreased conduction through the chest wall

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A hypertensive patient presented with chest pain and was found to have dilated cardiomyopathy on an echocardiogram. On auscultation , a reversed splitting of second heart sound was heard. Which of the following could most likely be responsible for the same?
mcqs.explanation: Reversed (or paradoxical) splitting refers to the situation when P2 is heard before A2 . This is seen in the following: • LBBB • HOCM • Right ventricular pacing • Severe AS • Acute myocardial ischemia

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Disappearance of loud S1 in mitral stenosis occurs in all except :
mcqs.explanation: Loud S1 is heard in mild mitral stenosis (MS). The intensity of S1 depends on the distance over which the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve moves, leaflet mobility, LV contractility , and PR interval. It is independent of the severity of MS. Loud S1 is seen in early rheumatic MS, short PR interval, and hyperdynamic circulatory states . S1 becomes soft in case of calcified leaflets , long PR interval, associated aortic regurgitation and LV dysfunction .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: While examining a patient , you hear a widely split S2 on auscultation . Which of the following is not a possible diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: A wide split of S2 is not seen in the left bundle branch block (LBBB ), however paradoxical splitting is seen . S2 is normally heard as A2 -P2 . This split is exaggerated in conditions that cause early aortic valve closure or delayed pulmonary valve closure . Option A: In atrial septal defect (ASD), left ventricle (LV ) ejection time decreases due to the shunting of the blood from the left atrium (LA ) to the right atrium leading to early aortic valve closure . Option B: In mitral regurgitation (MR), due to the regurgitation of blood from the LV to the LA , the LV ejection time decreases leading to early aortic valve closure . Option C: In pulmonary stenosis (PS), the delayed closure of pulmonary valves leads to the splitting of S2.796 Wide splitting of S2 is also heard in RBBB and LV pacing.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions is associated with a fixed wide splitting of S2?
mcqs.explanation: Fixed wide splitting of S2 is seen in atrial septal defect (ASD). The ASD creates a left to right shunt that increases the blood flow to the right side of the heart. This causes the pulmonary valve to close later than the aortic valve independent of inspiration/expiration.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.a: S3 and S4 are high pitched systolic sounds
options.c: S4 is heard during the ventricular-filling phase
options.d: S3 occurs due to rapid filling of the ventricles during atrial systole

mcqs.explanation: S4 is heard during the ventricular-filling phase . S3 and S4 are diastolic sounds that are low pitched , and best heard with the bell of the stethoscope at the cardiac apex in the left lateral decubitus position. The presence of an S3 and S4 heart sound is called a summation gallop and sounds like a galloping horse.S3 - Ventricular gallop S4 - Atrial gallop Occurs during early ventricul ar diastole Occurs near the end of ventri cular diastole During the first rapid ventric ular filling During active ventricular filli ng (filling by atrial contra ction) Due to a sudden rush of bloo d entering a volume-depleted ventricle (normal ventricular compliance ) Due tovibration of the ventric ular wall during atrial contra ction because of increased sti ffness of ventricular walls (de creased ventricular complian ce) Itcan be physiologicalin child ren and young adults . Always pathological In older patients , it indicates systolic heart failure Indicates diastolic heart failu re

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: An ECG of a patient who underwent pulmonary artery catheterization showed a right bundle branch block. On auscultation , a widely split S1 was observed. Which of the following is true regarding this auscultatory finding?

options.c: The split remains constant with inspiration and expiration
options.d: The change in split depends on the degree of bundle branch block

mcqs.explanation: In a patient with a right bundle branch block (RBBB ), there 's a widely split S1 which increases with inspiration. S1 is normally heard as a single sound. Any delay in the closure of the tricuspid valve or early closure of the mitral valve produces a split in S1. During inspiration, venous return to the right797 atrium increases. Therefore, the atria take a longer time to empty into the ventricles delaying the closure of the tricuspid valve. This increases the split in S1 during inspiration. In a patient with an RBBB , the tricuspid valve closure is further delayed leading to a wide split in S1.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old woman presents with a history of occasional palpitations . She has no history of chest pain or dyspnea . On examination, blood pressure is 110 /70 mmHg, the pulse is 82/min and regular. Joint hypermobility and thoracolumbar scoliosis are present . Gorlin's sign is positive . On auscultation , a click is heard after S1, followed by a late systolic murmur . What is the probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The probable diagnosis of the above scenario is Ehlers -Danlos syndrome (EDS). EDS is a group of clinically and genetically heterogeneous connective tissue disorders. Typical presenting features include joint hypermobility, skin hyperextensibility , and tissue fragility. EDS type 6 is also characterized by scoliosis . Gorlin's sign refers to the ability of patients of Ehlers -Danlos syndrome to touch the tip of the nose with the tip of their tongue . Mitral valve prolapse (MVP) is a frequent finding in patients with EDS. An early systolic click which may be followed by a late systolic murmur is the auscultatory finding heard in MVP.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a diastolic sound?
mcqs.explanation: The ejection click is a systolic sound. Ejection clicks are high-pitched sounds that occur at the moment of the maximal opening of the aortic or pulmonary valves. They are heard just after the first heart sound. Ejection clicks occur in: • Non-calcific aortic or pulmonary stenosis • Aortic or pulmonary root dilatation • Congenital bicuspid aortic or pulmonary valves Nonejection clicks, which occur after the onset of the carotid upstroke , are related to the mitral valve prolapse .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: On auscultation of a patient , you hear a murmur between S1 and S2. Which of the following conditions is not likely to be associated with this finding?
mcqs.explanation: A murmur occurring between S1 and S2 is a systolic murmur . Pulmonary regurgitation produces a diastolic murmur. The causes of systolic murmurs are as follows : • Mid-systolic - aortic stenosis , pulmonic stenosis , ASD, HOCM. • Holosystolic /pansystolic - mitral regurgitation , tricuspid regurgitation , VSD. • Late systolic - mitral valve prolapse . The causes of diastolic murmurs are as follows : • Early diastolic - aortic regurgitation , pulmonic regurgitation .798 • Mid/late diastolic - mitral stenosis , tricuspid stenosis , Austin-Flint. The causes of continuous murmurs are as follows : • Patent ductus arteriosus (machinery or Gibson's murmur ). • Venous hum • AV fistula • Ruptured sinus of Valsalva aneurysm

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: While examining a patient , you hear a mid-diastolic murmur with presystolic accentuation on auscultation of the precordium. Which of the following condition is associated with this finding?
mcqs.explanation: A mid-diastolic murmur with presystolic accentuation and an opening snap is typically seen in mitral stenosis. The presystolic accentuation is due to the atrial contraction forcing blood through the stenosed mitral valve. The presystolic accentuation disappears in atrial fibrillation. Option A: Mitral regurgitation presents with a holosystolic murmur , best heard at the apex with radiation to the left axilla. Option B: Mitral valve prolapse presents with an early systolic click followed by a late systolic murmur is heard. Option C: Aortic stenosis presents with a harsh crescendo -decrescendo ejection systolic murmur heard best at the right upper sternal border, with radiation of the murmur to the carotid arteries.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: You are a part of a health camp conducting check-ups for cardiovascular ailments. On auscultation of a patient 's precordial area, you hear a systolic murmur . On asking the patient to perform the following maneuver, the intensity of the murmur increased . Which of the following conditions is associated with this finding?
mcqs.explanation: The above image shows the Valsalva maneuver. The murmur of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) increases in intensity while performing the Valsalva maneuver. The murmurs produced by TR (tricuspid regurgitation ), AS (aortic stenosis ), and MR (mitral regurgitation) decrease in intensity while performing the Valsalva maneuver. Note : Valsalva maneuver decreases the intensity of all murmurs except MVP (mitral valve prolapse ) and HCM.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: While auscultating a patient 's precordium, a murmur was heard that decreased in intensity on performing the following sustained maneuver. Which of the given condition is associated with this finding?
mcqs.explanation: The above image shows a sustained handgrip maneuver. The murmur of aortic stenosis decreases in intensity during sustained handgrip. Maneuvers like sustained handgrip, simultaneous inflation of blood pressure cuffs above the systolic in both upper limbs, and infusion of vasopressors increase the systemic vascular resistance (afterload ). Since increasing afterload will prevent blood from flowing in a normal forward path, it will increase any murmurs that are due to backward flowing blood and decresase the ones due to forward blood flow .799 Murmurs that increase in intensity on sustained handgrip: • Mitral regurgitation • Ventricular septal defect • Aortic regurgitation Murmurs that decrease in intensity on sustained handgrip: • Aortic stenosis • Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following murmur increases on standing?
mcqs.explanation: The murmur of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HOCM) increases with standing, as there is a reduction in preload . In conditions of reduced preload , there is lesser end diastolic volume in the left ventricle, leading to a narrower outflow tract, and a louder murmur is heard. The murmur heard in HOCM is a mid-systolic murmur , which is loudest along the left sternal border. It increases in conditions of decreased preload and afterload (standing, valsalva , vagal maneuvers) or conditions of increased contractility (inotropic stimulation) and decreases when preload and afterload are increased (squatting, vasopressors). Most murmurs decrease in intensity with reduced preload and afterload except HOCM and mitral valve prolapse (MVP).

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A child was being evaluated for an underlying cardiac defect . On auscultation , a murmur was heard which began in systole , enveloped the second heart sound, and continued through some portion of the diastole . Which of the following condition is not associated with this finding?

options.a: Ventricular septal defect with aortic regurgitation

mcqs.explanation: The murmur described above is a continuous murmur . A continuous murmur is produced when there is a pressure gradient between the cardiac chambers or the blood vessels throughout the systole and diastole . Continous murmurs are characterised by the flow of blood in the same direction and through the same channel during systole and diastole . These murmurs begin in systole , envelope the second heart sound (S2), and continue through some portion of diastole . Conditions producing a continuous murmur : • Patent ductus arteriosus • Venous hum • AV fistula • Ruptured sinus of Valsalva aneurysm Ventricular septal defect with aortic regurgitation does not produce a continuous murmur . It produces a systolic -diastolic murmur as the blood flows through different channels during systole and diastole . These murmurs do not envelope S2.800

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about Gallavardin effect ?

options.a: It is associated with a diastolic murmur
options.b: It is seen in aortic stenosis
options.c: It refers to the radiation of murmur to the carotids
options.d: The transmission makes the murmur low pitched

mcqs.explanation: The Gallavardin effect refers to the phenomenon of the transmission of the mid-systolic murmur of aortic stenosis to the apex where it becomes higher pitched .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient presents with easy fatiguability and shortness of breath on moderate physical activity. On auscultation , a holosystolic murmur is heard over the lower left sternal border and radiating to the epigastrium . Which of the following condition is most likely to be associated with this finding?
mcqs.explanation: A holosystolic murmur that is best heard over the lower left sternal border and radiating to the epigastrium most likely arises from tricuspid regurgitation .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about Still's murmur ?

options.a: It is heard in mitral regurgitation
options.b: It is best heard in left lateral decubitus position

mcqs.explanation: Still's murmur refers to the benign grade 2 mid-systolic murmur heard at mid or lower left sternal border in normal children and adolescents . Louder in hyperdynamic states (fever, anxiety). The anatomic basis for the murmur has not been definitively determined . It is best heard in a supine position.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Graham Steell murmur is heard in?
mcqs.explanation: Graham Steell murmur is the early to mid-diastolic murmur heard in pulmonary regurgitation . It is best heard in 2nd left intercostal space and radiates along left sternal border. It can increase with inspiration.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Carey Coombs murmur is heard in?
mcqs.explanation: Carey Coombs murmur is heard in mitral valvulitis. It is a mid-diastolic murmur heard during an episode of acute rheumatic fever causing mitral valvulitis. It is produced due to the flow of blood through an edematous mitral valve and dissipates with the resolution of the acute attack.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Austin-Flint murmur is associated with which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Austin-Flint murmur is a low-pitched mid to late diastolic murmur of chronic severe AR. It results from the turbulence at the mitral inflow area from the mixture of regurgitant and forward blood flow . It is best heard at the apex.801 Austin-Flint murmur is often confused with the murmur of mitral stenosis . This can be differentiated based on the following :Features Chronic AR MS Opening snap Absent Present Effect of vasodilator administ ration Murmur becomes shorter an d softer.Mechanism- Fall in t he diastolic pressure gradient between the aorta and left ve ntricle. Murmur remains constant or increases in intensity .Mecha nism- Reflex increase in cardi ac output and mitral valve flo w.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man presented with an episode of acute onset dizziness and loss of consciousness which lasted for a few seconds followed by a regain of full consciousness . There were no similar episodes in the past. Which of the following is a true statement regarding this scenario?

options.a: ECG to rule out atrial fibrillation
options.b: If ECG is normal , CT scan should be done
options.d: Vestibular neuritis is a possible condition that can cause these symptoms

mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario of transient loss of consciousness in this patient is suggestive of syncope . Hence , an ECG must be done to rule out cardiac causes for syncope like - arrhythmias (atrial fibrillation, sinus node dysfunction , supra ventricular tachycardias) or a structural cardiac abnormality. A CT would only be required if a seizure or transient ischemic attack (TIA ) is suspected . However, in this case - the episode only lasted for a few seconds , the patient has no history of similar episodes in the past and there are no lasting neurological deficits after the episode . Therefore, option B is incorrect. Syncope is a transient loss of consciousness caused by global cerebral hypoperfusion . It can be due to multiple causes , but is broadly divided into - neurally mediated syncope , orthostatic hypotension and cardiac syncope . The initial workup for a case of syncope includes : • Detailed history of the episode and past history of similar episodes • Physical examination mainly to check BP in standing and supine positions to • rule out orthostatic hypotension . • A resting ECG to look for cardiac arrhythmia • Option B: If the ECG is normal , no further tests are needed . If the ECG is suggestive of cardiac arrhythmia, then further tests including continuous ECG monitoring and electrophysiological studies may be done. Option C: Tilt-table testing is done in patients with recurrent syncopal attacks who are suspected to have vasovagal syncope . Psychiatric evaluation is done in patients with recurrent unexplained syncopal attacks. Option D: Vestibular neuritis is associated with vertigo, where the patients typically complain of dizziness and a sense of spinning of the head .802

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which electrophysiological activity is responsible for the T wave in ECG?
mcqs.explanation: The T wave in ECG is due to ventricular repolarisation.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: The PR intervals obtained from the ECG recording of 4 patients are given below . Which of the following patients has a normal PR interval?
mcqs.explanation: The normal duration of the PR interval is 0.12 -0.2 seconds (3 to 5 small boxes). PR interval is said to be prolonged if it is > 0.2 seconds and short if it is < 0.12 seconds . It is measured from the beginning of the P wave to the beginning of the QRS complex . It represents the time from the start of atrial depolarization to the start of ventricular depolarization .813

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the normal QRS interval?
mcqs.explanation: The normal duration of the QRS interval is normally 0.1-0.11 seconds (less than 3 small boxes). QRS interval represents the duration of ventricular depolarization. When the QRS complex is > 0.11 seconds , it is called a wide QRS complex . It can occur in: • Bundle branch blocks (RBBB or LBBB ) • Depolarizations originating in the ventricles • Wolff-Parkinson -White syndrome • Hyperkalaemia

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which lead does the given ECG tracing represent in a normal ECG?
mcqs.explanation: As all the waves (P, QRS, T) are negative in the given ECG, it should be lead aVR . All the depolarisations waves (P, QRS, T) move away from lead aVR in the normal sinus. Depolarisation wave moving towards the positive pole of the lead (or active electrode ) produces a positive deflection in the ECG and depolarization moving away from the positive pole of the lead produces a negative deflection in the ECG. The lead aVR provides information from the right upper side of the heart.814 The given image shows a normal 12 lead ECG:

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: In a normal ECG obtained from a patient , a biphasic P wave may be seen in which of the following lead (s)?
mcqs.explanation: In a normal ECG, a biphasic P wave is seen in lead V1 only. Lead V1 is a chest lead . So, it records potentials in the horizontal plane . The P wave in lead V1 consists of: • Positive component reflecting right atrial depolarization (due to anteriorly oriented vector) • Negative component reflecting left atrial depolarization (due to posteriorly oriented vector)815

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following leads would show maximum R wave with the cardiac axis as +90 degrees ?
mcqs.explanation: With the cardiac axis at +90 degrees , lead aVF would show the maximum R wave. The cardiac axis represents the mean QRS axis (direction of mean depolarization vector). The normal adult QRS axis is directed downward and to the left , which is between -30 degrees and +100 degrees . The position of lead aVF is at +90 degrees . If the cardiac axis is also at +90 degrees , it would be in the same direction as lead aVF and hence aVF would show maximum R wave amplitude . If the mean axis is: • More negative than –30 degrees : left axis deviation • More positive than +90 to +100 degrees : right axis deviation • Lies between -90 to +180 degrees : extreme axis deviation816

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Pseudo P pulmonale is seen in which electrolyte abnormality?
mcqs.explanation: Pseudo P pulmonale refers to tall peaked P waves seen in hypokalemia. P-pulmonale refers to P waves taller than >2.5mm in an ECG lead .Hypocalcemia (Option C) prolongs the QT interval. Hypercalcemia (Option D) shortens the QT interval.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following ECG findings are seen in a patient with hypokalemia?

options.a: Prolonged PR interval with ST elevation
options.b: Decreased PR interval with ST depression
options.c: Decreased QT interval with tall T waves
options.d: Prolonged QT interval with flat T waves

mcqs.explanation: Prolonged QT interval with flat T waves is seen in hypokalemia.817 Hypokalemia prolongs ventricular repolarization. The ECG changes seen are as follows : • Flattening of T wave • ST-segment depression • Prolongation of QT interval • The appearance of U wave

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old male patient with a long-standing history of rheumatic heart disease comes to the clinic with complaints of dyspnea . Interpret the ECG finding.
mcqs.explanation: The P waves in the given ECG are broad and notched . This is the P mitrale pattern which is seen in left atrial enlargement . This patient has likely developed mitral stenosis (heard as a mid-diastolic murmur ) secondary to his rheumatic heart disease . Mitral valve stenosis and atrial inflammation in rheumatic carditis lead to left atrial dilation. The features of P mitrale are: • lead II : broad (>2.5mm) notched P waves • Lead V1 : Biphasic wave with a prominent negative terminal component (representing delayed depolarization of the LA ) P pulmonale is seen in right atrial enlargement .818 Option A: The rabbit ear pattern is seen in the right bundle branch block. The ECG of RBBB below shows the rSR ' pattern of the QRS complex (rabbit ear) in leads V1 -V2 and slurred S wave in lead V6 .Option D: Sawtooth pattern in ECG is seen in atrial flutter (shown below ).819

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 67-year-old man with a history of COPD presented with worsening dyspnea for 2 weeks . On examination , pedal edema was present. An ECG was done and lead II showed the following pattern. Which of the following is responsible for this ECG finding?
mcqs.explanation: In the given ECG, a peaked P wave can be seen . This is called P pulmonale and it is seen in cases of right atrial enlargement . The patient is showing features of heart failure possibly as a consequence of dysfunction caused by the overload. Signs of heart failure in this patient : • Bilateral pitting edema in lower extremities (systemic congestion ) • Worsening dyspnea due to increased PCWP causing pulmonary hypertension and pulmonary edema (pulmonary congestion ) The features of P pulmonale include : • The amplitude of the P wave is >2.5mm on Lead II • Prominent positive wave in the biphasic P wave of lead V1820

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the likely diagnosis of this patient based on the given ECG?
mcqs.explanation: The given ECG shows deep S-waves in V6 and large R-waves in V1 . This is suggestive of right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH ). Diagnostic criteria for RVH : • Dominant R wave in V1 (R/S ratio > 1). • Dominant S wave in V5 or V6 (R/S ratio < 1). • Right ventricular strain pattern - ST depression /T wave inversion in the right precordial (V1-4) and inferior leads (II , III , aVF) • Right axis deviation of +110 \260 or more. For left ventricular hypertrophy , Sokolow Lyon criteria are commonly used . It is based on the presence of tall left precordial R waves and deep right precordial S waves (S wave in V1 + [R wave in V5 or V6 ] >35 mm).821

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man comes to the emergency room with complaints of sudden onset chest pain that radiates to the left arm and jaw. He is profusely sweating . An ECG was taken immediately . Interpret his ECG.
mcqs.explanation: The patient has a myocardial infarction (MI) with ECG changes of a left bundle -branch block (LBBB ), which can be identified by the following classical features : • Wide QRS complex - QRS \037120 ms • Predominantly negative (QS) complexes in lead V1 and entirely positive (R) complexes in lead V6. • M pattern seen in left chest leads (V5, V6 ) MI can have the following ECG changes : • ST-segment elevation- zone of injury • T wave depression • Deep Q waves- late sign to develop • New left bundle branch block (LBBB )822 The ECG findings below are characteristic of LBBB : Mnemonic WILLIAM (W pattern in V1-V2 ; L-LBBB ; M pattern in V3 -V6 )The ECG findings below are characteristic of RBBB : Mnemonic MARROW (M pattern in V1 -V2 ; R-RBBB ; W pattern in V3 -V6 )823

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old patient comes to the emergency room with a history of severe retrosternal pain radiating to the jaw. The patient initially felt some uneasiness while eating lunch after which he experienced pain. His ECG is as shown. Interpret his ECG.
mcqs.explanation: The given ECG shows ST-segment elevation in the anterior chest leads suggestive of myocardial infarction. Features of MI on ECG: • ST-segment elevation: Zone of injury • T wave inversions • Deep Q waves: late sign to develop • New left bundle branch block (LBBB ) Option A: Atrial flutter shows a sawtooth wave pattern. Option B: WPW syndrome shows delta waves. Option D: Ventricular tachycardia has wide QRS complex and increased heart rate.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 72-year-old man comes to the emergency room complaining his heart is pounding and that he is going to die . The emergency physician orders an ECG. What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given ECG shows ST elevation in leads V1 -V4 which is suggestive of acute anteroseptal myocardial infarction (MI). ST depression in the leads III and aVF signifies an old inferior wall infarction.824

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 52-year-old diabetic man presents with retrosternal chest pain and profuse sweating and lightheadedness. Based on the ECG findings, what is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The ECG shows ST elevations in leads I, aVL , and V1 -V6 . This is suggestive of extensive anterior wall MI.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the diagnosis based on the given ECG?
mcqs.explanation: The ECG is suggestive of lateral wall MI and possible posterior wall MI. ST-elevation is present in the high lateral leads (I and aVL ) and in V5 and V6 . Reciprocal ST depression is seen in the inferior leads (III and aVF) with associated ST depression in V1 , V2 , and V3 (which could represent posterior wall MI). This pattern is consistent with an acute infarction localized to the superior portion of the lateral wall of the left ventricle (high lateral STEMI).

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old patient presents with chest pain on the left side radiating to the arm and jaw on the same side . Cardiac troponins are found to be raised. What is the diagnosis based on this ECG?
mcqs.explanation: The given ECG is of posterior wall MI. The ECG findings in posterior wall MI include , • Reciprocal ST depressions in leads V1 to V3 . Posterior wall ischemia is indirectly recognized in this way • Tall and broad R waves (>30ms) in V2 and V3 • Dominant R waves (R/S ratio > 1) in V2 • Upright terminal portions of the T waves in V2 and V3

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following ECG findings are unlikely to be present in a patient with hyperkalemia?
mcqs.explanation: Prolonged QT interval is not a feature of hyperkalemia, it is a feature of hypokalemia.825

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient was brought to the ER with complaints of multiple episodes of vomiting, increased frequency of urination, and constipation for the past 5 days. He also complained of lethargy and muscle pain. He is a known case of SCC of the lung. What is likely to be seen in the ECG of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The above scenario is suggestive of hypercalcemia due to ectopic production of PTH -related peptides . It is mostly associated with squamous-cell lung cancer (SCC). ECG is likely to show a decreased QT interval. Hypocalcemia shows increased QT interval.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: ECG of a patient revealed a QT interval of 0.55s . Which of the following will not be a differential diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: QT interval of 0.55s suggests QT prolongation. It is not seen in digitalis toxicity . Rather, a QT shortening with characteristic "scooping" of the ST–T-wave complex , called a digitalis effect , is seen . The ECG changes seen in digitalis toxicity are as follows : • Prolonged PR interval • ST-segment depression • Short QT interval QT interval represents the time taken for the ventricles to depolarize and repolarize. It is prolonged in the following : • Hypocalcemia • Hypokalemia • Congenital long QT syndromes such as Romano -Ward syndrome • Hypothermia • Drugs: Class IA and Class III antiarrhythmics826 • Intracranial bleeds : particularly SAH

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Osborn waves in ECG are seen in:
mcqs.explanation: Osborn waves are seen in hypothermia. Osborn waves can also be seen in severe hypothyroidism (Option A), but even in those cases , hypothermia is the reason for the appearance of Osborn waves. Therefore, hypothermia is the better answer here. It consists of an abrupt ascent right at the J point (the junctional point between the QRS complex and the ST segment ) and then an equally sudden plunge back to the baseline . It is also called the J wave. This is because systemic hypothermia prolongs repolarisation.Osborn wave can also be seen in: • Hypercalcemia • Brain injury • Subarachnoid hemorrhage • Vasospastic angina • Cardiopulmonary arrest from oversedation • Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: In a patient with a left -sided massive pneumothorax, all of the following ECG changes are seen except :
mcqs.explanation: Right axis deviation is seen in left -sided pneumothorax. The ECG changes seen in left -sided pneumothorax are as follows :827 • Reduced R wave amplitude • Inversion of T wave in precordial leads • Amplitude changes in QRS complex • Right axis deviation828

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 52-year-old man has come to the emergency complaining of a burning type of chest pain. Comment on his ECG recording shown below .
mcqs.explanation: The above ECG strip shows normal sinus rhythm. The features in this ECG that suggest this diagnosis are as follows : • The QRS complexes are narrow (<120 ms or 3 small squares) which implies that the impulse is supraventricular and is conducted via the normal conduction pathway .• Each QRS complex is preceded by a P wave. This means that all the atrial depolarizations that arise in the sinus node are conducted to the ventricles.840 • The PR interval is constant for all the impulses and is normal (<200 ms) in duration.• The RR interval is constant which implies a regular rhythm.841

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: All of the following are supraventricular tachycardias except :
mcqs.explanation: Premature ventricular beats are a type of ventricular tachycardias, not supraventricular tachycardias. Tachycardia is defined as a heart rate of >100 beats /min. It can be classified based on the site of origin of the cardiac impulse as follows: • Supraventricular tachycardias (SVTs) originate above the ventricles, that is, in the sinoatrial node , atria, or the atrioventricular node. Supraventricular tachycardias include : • Tachycardias originating from the atrium: • Sinus tachycardia- from the SA node • Focal atrial tachycardia • Multifocal atrial tachycardia • Atrial flutter • Atrial fibrillation • Tachycardias originating from the AV node: • Junctional tachycardia- automaticity within AV Node • AV nodal reentry tachycardia (AVNRT) • Tachycardia associated with accessory atrioventricular pathways : atrioventricular reentry tachycardia (AVRT ) • Ventricular tachycardias originate from the ectopic foci or the reentry pathways in the ventricles . Ventricular tachycardias include : • Premature ventricular beats • Ventricular tachycardia (VT )842 • Monomorphic VT - Very rapid monomorphic VT is also known as ventricular flutter • Polymorphic VT - associated with Torsades de pointes • Ventricular fibrillation

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: ECG of a patient who presented with palpitations to the ER is shown below . Which of the following is a likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The above ECG shows increased heart rate with wide QRS complexes (> 0.12s ). This is suggestive of ventricular tachycardia (VT ). Types of ventricular tachycardia based on QRS morphology : • Monomorphic- a stable QRS morphology from beat to beat • Polymorphic- changing or multiform QRS variance from beat to beat . Torsades de pointes is an example of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. • Bidirectional- has a beat -to-beat alternation in the QRS frontal plane axis. It is associated with digitalis toxicity or catecholaminergic polymorphic VT . The most common cause of VT is ischemic heart disease . Ventricular tachyarrhythmias occur due to impulses that originate within the ventricles. These impulses are conducted through the normal ventricular myocardial cells instead of the fast conducting Purkinje system . Hence , they present with wide QRS complexes ( >0.12 sec ) on the ECG. Supraventricular tachyarrhythmias occur due to impulses originating above the ventricles. These impulses reach the ventricles through the proper fast conduction pathway resulting in a narrow QRS complex . SVTs are associated with wide QRS in few exceptional conditions like: • Conduction block in the left or right bundle branch • Activation of ventricles from an accessory pathway - antidromic AVRT The given ECG shows wide stable QRS complexes in monomorphic ventricular tachycardia:843

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which is the most common supraventricular tachyarrhythmia?
mcqs.explanation: The most common supraventricular arrhythmia is sinus tachycardia. It can either be physiological or pathological . Physiological sinus tachycardia is seen in exercise , fever, anemia, hyperthyroidism , etc . Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardias are those supraventricular tachycardias that occur with sudden onset and termination, they are non-sustained arrhythmias (lasts < 30 seconds ). They include AVNRT , AVRT , and atrial tachycardias. The most common sustained (lasts > 30 seconds ) arrhythmia is atrial fibrillation. Junctional tachycardia originates from ectopic foci in the AV node. It is an uncommon tachycardia.844

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 49-year-old woman was brought to the emergency with complaints of dizziness, shortness of breath, and palpitations . ECG showed tachyarrhythmia with narrow QRS complex and irregular RR intervals. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: ECG showing tachyarrhythmia with a narrow QRS complex suggests a supraventricular tachycardia. An irregular RR interval is seen with the following supraventricular tachycardias: • Atrial fibrillation • Multifocal atrial tachycardia • Atrial flutter / atrial tachycardia with variable block The ECG below shows atrial fibrillation. Note the narrow QRS complexes and irregular RR intervals. Disappearacne of P-wave is another feature .845

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old hypertensive patient presents with chest pain and dyspnea following an alcohol binge. His ECG is shown below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The ECG shows narrow QRS complexes with irregular RR intervals and no distinct P waves. This is suggestive of atrial fibrillation. Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a supraventricular tachycardia caused by ectopic foci or small reentry circuits within the atria. It has an atrial rate of 400 -600 /min and a ventricular rate of -160 /min. Risk factors for developing AF include: • Age - usually above 60 years of age • Underlying heart disease • Hypertension • Diabetes mellitus • Obesity • Sleep apnea • Post-cardiac surgery • Inflammatory pericarditis Acute precipitating factors for AF include : • Hyperthyroidism • Acute alcohol intoxication • Acute illness like myocardial infarction and pulmonary embolism

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man was diagnosed with STEMI. He was admitted and given thrombolytic therapy. The next day he complained of palpitations and an ECG was taken. Which of the following drugs can be used to treat his condition?
mcqs.explanation: 846 The above ECG shows narrow QRS complex , irregular RR intervals, and absent P waves which are suggestive of atrial fibrillation. Among the given options, amiodarone can be administered in patients having atrial fibrillation with coronary or structural heart disease . Drugs for rhythm control in atrial fibrillation: In patients without structural heart disease , class I agents are used . Class I agents act by blocking the Na+ channels leading to slower depolarization: • Flecainide • Propafenone • Disopyramide In patients with coronary or structural heart disease , class III agents are used . Class III agents act by blocking the K+ channels leading to slower repolarization causing increased refractory period : • Amiodarone • Dofetilide • Sotalol • Ibutilide

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man who is on treatment for chronic AF presents with nausea, dizziness, and anorexia. He has a regular heart rate of 50/min. The most likely cause is:
mcqs.explanation: A patient of atrial fibrillation usually has an irregular heart rate of >100/ min but this patient presents with a regular slow heart rate. The most likely cause of slow regular heart rate in chronic AF is digitalis toxicity . Symptoms such as nausea, anorexia are also suggestive of digitalis toxicity . Digitalis lowers the AV nodal conduction by stimulating the vagal nerve endings leading to increased vagal tone. Hence digitalis toxicity can cause AV nodal block. This leads to a junctional escape rhythm taking over the ventricles causing slow and regular heart rate.847 Digitalis toxicity can also lead to a variety of arrhythmias as it increases the intracellular calcium levels increasing the risk of tachyarrhythmias.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: ECG of a patient who was brought to the casualty due to severe chest pain followed by syncope is given below . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given ECG is suggestive of atrial flutter . The given ECG shows narrow QRS complexes , hence it is supraventricular tachycardia. The RR intervals are regular and the normal P waves are replaced by sawtooth -shaped waves, known as flutter waves. In atrial flutter , the ventricular rate is determined by the AV conduction ratio. The commonest AV ratio is 2:1. In the above ECG, the rhythm is atrial flutter 4:1 block with an atrial rate of about 270 and a ventricular rate of 68/min. The image below shows sawtooth shaped waves in atrial flutter .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man was brought to the emergency in an unconscious state . He had a fever for the past two days and is a known case of severe COPD. His ECG is given below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of chronic pulmonary disease and the ECG showing different p wave morphologies are suggestive of multifocal atrial tachycardia. Multifocal atrial tachycardia (MAT) occurs due to impulses arising from multiple abnormal foci in the atria. This leads to supraventricular tachycardia with p waves and QRS complexes of different morphologies . It is usually encountered in patients with chronic pulmonary disease and acute illness . Therapy for MAT is directed at treating the underlying disease and correcting any metabolic abnormalities. Calcium-channel blockers and radiofrequency ablation of the AV node are the other treatment modalities .848 The given ECG shows narrow QRS complexes with irregular RR intervals, hence it can be atrial fibrillation or multifocal atrial tachycardia. The next step is to look at the p waves. Multifocal atrial tachycardia (MAT) is characterized by at least 3 distinct P-wave morphologies (shown by arrows in the image). Whereas, in atrial fibrillation, there would be no distinct p waves seen .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardias do not include :
mcqs.explanation: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardias do not include atrial fibrillation. Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardias are tachycardias that occur with sudden onset and termination, they are not sustained arrhythmias. They include • AVNRT • AVRT • Atrial tachycardia Whereas, atrial fibrillation is the most common sustained arrhythmia among supraventricular tachycardias. Features suggestive of PSVT : • Narrow complex tachycardia at 150 bpm • No visible P waves • Pseudo R' waves due to retrograde atrial activation The given ECG shows pseudo R' waves:849

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old man is brought to the casualty after he developed sudden onset dyspnea , chest pain, and palpitations at a party. His blood pressure is 100 /62 mmHg. His ECG is shown below . What is the drug of choice to treat his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The ECG is suggestive of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT ) as it shows : • Narrow QRS complexes • No visible p waves • Pseudo R' waves in V1 lead Adenosine is the preferred drug in stable paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT ). Treatment of PSVT : In hemodynamically unstable patients, QRS-synchronous DC cardioversion should be done. In hemodynamically stable patients , 1. Mechanical measures : These maneuvers result in an acute increase in the vagal tone which decreases AV conduction and terminates the arrhythmia . They include the following : • Valsalva maneuver • Lowering the head between the knees • Coughing • Splashing cold water on the face • Breath-holding • Carotid sinus massage 2. Pharmacologic therapy : • Adenosine - it is the first-line agent . It blocks conduction across the AV node and terminates the SVT . It is given as a 6-18 mg bolus • Calcium channel blockers- verapamil and diltiazem850 • Beta-blockers- esmolol , propranolol, and metoprolol • IV Procainamide- it is administered if the tachycardia is being mediated through an accessory pathway . It facilitates the AV conduction and therefore causes an initial increase in rate. Therefore, it is given after administering calcium channel blockers or beta -blockers. The given ECG shows pseudo R' waves:

mcqs.question: The ECG of a patient who presented to the ER is as given below . The patient was already given a carotid massage and IV Adenosine but the BP is currently 60/30 mm Hg. What is the next best step of management?
mcqs.explanation: The given ECG showing narrow QRS complex (<0.12 s) tachycardia with absent P wave is suggestive of paroxysmal ventricular tachycardia (PSVT ). The next best step in the management of a patient with unstable vitals (systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg) is synchronized cardioversion.851 Synchronized cardioversion is the treatment of choice in unstable PSVT patients , in which shocks are delivered with the defibrillator /monitor in synchronized mode with an initial energy level of 100J . Synchronization times the delivery so that it is given at the peak of the QRS complex . If the shock occurs in the ST segment or the T wave (unsynchronized), it can precipitate a more serious arrhythmia such as ventricular fibrillation.Synchronized cardioversion Defibrillation Used inunstable PSVT , atrial flutter , atrial fibrillation, and ventricular tachycardiawith a pulse Used in ventricular tachycard iawithout pulseand ventricul ar fibrillation. Shock is delivered in sync wit h the R wave (in absolute refr actory period ) Shock is delivered at any tim e during the cardiac cycle . Monophasic : -200 JBipha sic: 50-100 J Monophasic : 360 JBiphasic:1 -200 JOther options : Option A: In the absence of hemodynamic instability , a repeat dose of injection adenosine (maximum of 12mg ) could be attempted . Option B: IV Amiodarone is rarely used in the acute management of PSVT . Instead, it is used as an alternative to calcium channel blockers in chronic suppressive therapy . Option D: Defibrillation is only done for ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient came with sudden onset palpitations . ECG showed a narrow complex , regular tachycardia without P waves, and a rate of 160 BPM. His blood pressure is 96/68 mmHg. What is the next step in management?
mcqs.explanation: 852 The given clinical scenario and the electrocardiogram (ECG) showing narrow QRS complex regular tachycardia without P waves are suggestive of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT ). The next step in the management of PSVT in a hemodynamically stable (systolic blood pressure >90 mm Hg) patient is vagotonic maneuvres such as carotid sinus massage or Valsalva maneuver. Carotid sinus massage can be considered in the absence of carotid bruits and no history of stroke. If vagal maneuvers fail or cannot be performed, intravenous adenosine can be used . Non-DHP calcium channel blockers and beta blockers are second -line pharmacological agents in the management of PSVT . They can cause hypotension before and after terminating the arrhythmia . If the patient is hemodynamically unstable (systolic blood pressure <90 mmHg or mean arterial pressure <65 mm Hg), immediate QRS-synchronous direct current cardioversion is necessary . mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario describes an unconscious patient , who is hemodynamically unstable (systolic BP <90 mmHg or mean arterial pressure <65 mmHg).
