mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about accessory pathways ?

options.a: Bundle of Kent has antegrade conduction

mcqs.explanation: Retrograde conduction via accessory pathways does not cause preexcitation . Accessory pathways (APs) are abnormal conduction pathways connecting the atrium and ventricle . They can conduct impulses in the following ways: Antegrade conduction : • Occurs from the atria to the ventricle854 • The impulses from atria reach the ventricles faster via the accessory pathway as compared to the normal AV nodal pathway as they bypass the AV nodal delay . • This leads to an earlier excitation of the ventricles known as the preexcitation of the ventricles and thus a wide QRS complex . • Examples - WPW syndrome and antidromic AVRT Retrograde conduction : • Occurs from the ventricle to the atria. • The impulses reach the ventricles via the normal AV nodal pathway but re-enter the atria through the accessory pathway . • Ventricular depolarization is normal, there is no preexcitation and thus a narrow QRS complex . It causes supraventricular tachycardia as the impulses re-enter the atria via the accessory pathway . • Examples - concealed accessory pathways (can cause SVTs ) and orthodromic AVRT .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common reentrant tachycardia caused by an accessory pathway ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common reentrant tachycardia caused by an accessory pathway is orthodromic AV reentry . Accessory pathways (APs) are abnormal conduction pathways connecting the atrium and ventricle . They can conduct impulses in the following ways: Antegrade conduction : • Occurs from the atria to the ventricle • The impulses from atria reach the ventricles faster via the accessory pathway as compared to the normal AV nodal pathway as they bypass the AV nodal delay . • This leads to an earlier excitation of the ventricles known as the preexcitation of the ventricles and thus a wide QRS complex . • Examples - WPW syndrome and antidromic AVRT Retrograde conduction : • Occurs from the ventricle to the atria. • The impulses reach the ventricles via the normal AV nodal pathway but re-enter the atria through the accessory pathway . • Ventricular depolarization is normal, there is no preexcitation and thus a narrow QRS complex. It causes supraventricular tachycardia as the impulses re-enter the atria via the accessory pathway . • Examples - concealed accessory pathways (can cause SVTs ) and orthodromic AVRT . AV nodal reentry tachycardia (AVNRT) is not caused by an accessory pathway . It involves tissues with different conduction speeds within the AV node or just adjacent to the AV node, known as the fast pathway and the slow pathway . This is known as dual AV nodal physiology .855

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient 's ECG shows a short PR interval and delta wave. Additional findings include atrial fibrillation and rapid ventricular rate. He is hemodynamically stable . All of the following drugs can be used in the management except :
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario describes a patient with WPW syndrome with atrial fibrillation. Rate-slowing drugs such as non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (eg , verapamil, diltiazem), beta -blockers, and digoxin are contraindicated in these patients . They increase the refractoriness of the AV node with minimal or no effect on the accessory pathway . This can lead to faster ventricular rates, increasing the risk of ventricular fibrillation. The ECG below shows a short PR interval (<120 ms) and delta waves in WPW syndrome.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: The most common location of the accessory pathway in WPW syndrome is:
mcqs.explanation: The most common location of an accessory pathway in WPW syndrome is on the left free wall. It is present between left atrium and free wall of left ventricle.856

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: All are true about the condition that is diagnosed by the given ECG except :

options.b: Can be seen in asymptomatic individuals
options.d: Caused by an abnormal accessory pathway

mcqs.explanation: The given ECG is suggestive of Wolff-Parkinson -White syndrome (WPW ). Its prevalence decreases with age . The classic ECG features in WPW are as follows : • A shortened PR interval (typically <120 ms) • A slurring and the slow rise of the initial upstroke of the QRS complex (delta wave) • A widened QRS complex (total duration >0.12 seconds ) • ST-segment –T wave (repolarization) changes , generally directed opposite the major delta wave and QRS complex, reflecting altered depolarization857

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman comes to the clinic with complaints of recurrent palpitation and lightheadedness. An ECG was taken and is as shown below . What is the best step in management?
mcqs.explanation: The ECG shows the presence of delta waves (preexcitation wave), wide QRS, and short PR interval which are classically seen in Wolff Parkinson White (WPW ) syndrome. In this patient , catheter ablation is the best for long-term management. Patients with preexcitation who have symptoms of arrhythmia are at risk for developing AF and sudden death if they have an accessory pathway that allows rapid antegrade conduction (preexcitation & tachyarrhythmias are features of WPW syndrome due to the abnormal accessory pathway ). Complications of catheter ablation are rare but include AV block, cardiac tamponade , thromboembolic events , and hematoma at the access site .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true regarding sick sinus syndrome?

options.a: Most patients are symptomatic in the early stages
options.c: Frequently seen in patients with atrial fibrillation

mcqs.explanation: Sick sinus syndrome is frequently seen in patients with concomitant atrial fibrillation. Sick sinus syndrome (or sinus node dysfunction ) is a group of abnormal heart rhythms. It is a disorder of the sinoatrial node caused by impaired pacemaker function and impulse transmission. This leads to a combination of abnormal rhythms, including atrial bradyarrhythmias, atrial tachyarrhythmias, and sometimes a pattern of alternating bradycardia and tachycardia, known as tachy-brady syndrome. These irregular rhythms can cause symptoms such as palpitations , decreased tissue perfusion , subsequent fatigue , lightheadedness , pre-syncope , and syncope . The management of sick sinus syndrome includes identifying and correcting reversible factors, as an initial step . Some examples of reversible causes of Sinus Node Dysfunction include , • Hypothyroidism858 • Sleep apnea • Anti-hypertensive medications eg . Beta-blockers • Anti-arrhythmic medications eg . Amiodarone, Procainamide Ambulatory ECG monitoring is required to diagnose as the symptoms are nonspecific . Treatment involves permanent pacing. Other options : Option A: The course of sinus node dysfunction is usually a slow progression over decades . In the early stages , most patients are asymptomatic. Option B: It occurs most commonly in elderly patients due to the gradual loss of SA node function. Option D: Beta-blockers are contraindicated in this condition.859

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A hypertensive patient was brought to the emergency due to complaints of palpitations and breathing difficulty . Comment on his ECG.
mcqs.explanation: The above ECG shows a pattern of premature ventricular contractions, one premature beat after one normal beat . This is seen in ventricular bigeminy. Premature ventricular contractions/beats (PVC ) are single ventricular beats that occur earlier than the next normal supraventricular beat. They originate from abnormal foci in the ventricular tissue : • Unifocal PVCs arise from a single focus and hence have the same QRS morphology871 • Multifocal PVCs arise from multiple foci and therefore have different QRS morphologies They are not preceded by a P wave as they do not originate in the atria. They show wide QRS complexes (>0.12 ms) on the ECG because they are conducted via normal myocardial tissue instead of the Purkinje system . Ventricular bigeminy refers to a pair of normal and premature ventricular contractions, whereas ventricular trigeminy refers to a premature beat that occurs after two normal beats . Quadrigeminy is when a premature beat follows three normal beats . Few other terms associated with premature ventricular contractions: • Two successive PVCs are known as a couplet • Three successive PVCs are known as a triplet . The given ECG shows ventricular bigeminy with premature beats circled in red and normal ventricular contractions circled in green .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Identify the marked ECG feature in a patient diagnosed with ventricular tachycardia.
mcqs.explanation: The ECG feature of ventricular tachycardia seen in the given image is a fusion beat . It occurs when a sinus and ventricular beat coincide to produce a hybrid complex . Ventricular tachycardia (VT ) is defined as \037 3 consecutive premature ventricular contractions at a rate of >100/min. It is characterized by: • Wide QRS complex • AV dissociation - Atrial activity independent of ventricular activity, seen on the ECG as every p wave not followed by QRS complex • Fusion beats - occur when a sinus and ventricular beat coincide to produce a hybrid complex • Capture beats occur when the SA node transiently 'captures ' the ventricles, that is, ventricles are depolarized by the impulses from the SA node producing a QRS complex of normal duration.872 The given ECG shows a fusion beat (red arrow), and a capture beat (green arrow) can also be seen :The given image shows capture beats in VT :Option C: Polymorphic QRS, that is, continuously changing QRS morphology is seen in polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. Option D: Triphasic QRS (eg . RSR \021 pattern on V1 ) is seen in supraventricular tachycardias with the wide QRS complex .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the diagnosis of this patient from the ECG shown below ?
mcqs.explanation: The rate of the given ECG is around 188 BPM ( >100 BPM) and it shows wide QRS complexes ( \037 0.12 s) with abnormal morphology (red arrows) and absence of P waves which suggests a diagnosis of ventricular tachycardia.873 Ventricular fibrillation (Option B) would not show discreet QRS complexes , and hence is not the answer in this case.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man is brought to the emergency following an episode of syncope during his morning walk. His blood pressure is 80/60 mm Hg. He has a history of myocardial infarction 5 yrs back. His present ECG is given below . Which is the most appropriate treatment for the patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario describes a man with history of coronary artery disease developing syncope . The ECG shows wide QRS complex (> 0.12 s) tachycardia with a single QRS morphology suggestive of monomorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT ). The most appropriate treatment of VT in a hemodynamically unstable (systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg) patient is DC cardioversion. VT can be casued by structural heart disease , scar-related reentry, cardiomyopathies , or abnormalities in the conduction pathways . VT is said to be sustained if it lasts for at least 30 seconds or requires intervention for termination.874 Rapid VT can lead to hypotension and syncope , especially in patients with ventricular dysfunction . Patients with normal cardiac function may tolerate sustained VT , presenting with palpitations . Monomorphic VT associated with structural heart disease can progress to ventricular fibrillation (VF) and sudden cardiac arrest. QRS synchronous electrical cardioversion is performed for unstable patients . Intravenous amiodarone is the preferred drug for stable VT associated with heart disease . After restoring sinus rhythm, further evaluation is necessary to determine the underlying heart disease . Treatment options include antiarrhythmic medications , catheter ablation, or implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) for recurrent or high-risk VT . ICDs are commonly used for secondary prevention of sudden death in patients with sustained VT and structural heart disease .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: All of the following are effective in the management of patients with ventricular tachycardia except :
mcqs.explanation: Carotid sinus massage will be effective only in supraventricular tachycardias but not in ventricular tachycardias. This is because it acts by increasing the AV node block which does not play any role in the pathogenesis of ventricular tachycardia. Hence , AV node blocking maneuvers (carotid sinus massage , valsalva ) and drugs (adenosine) are not used in the management of VT .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Accelerated idioventricular rhythm is the most common arrhythmia associated with:
mcqs.explanation: Accelerated idioventricular rhythm is the most common arrhythmia associated with myocardial reperfusion , most commonly in the first 2 days after presentation . Idioventricular rhythm is defined as \037 3 consecutive premature ventricular contractions with a heart rate of <50 bpm. If the heart rate is 60-100 bpm, it is known as accelerated idioventricular rhythm, and if it is more than 100 bpm it is known as ventricular tachycardia. It may be the result of an abnormal focus in the ventricle that generates an impulse faster than the sinus node and therefore assumes control. Other causes of AIVR include : • Buerger disease • Congenital heart disease • Dilated cardiomyopathy • Myocarditis • Drugs: Digoxin toxicity , cocaine toxicity , and various anesthesia agents • Electrolyte abnormality • Postresuscitation Episodes of AIVR have not been found to affect prognosis in acute MI and usually do not require intervention. If AIVR is accompanied by hemodynamic compromise, treatment with atropine or atrial pacing will often suppress the rhythm.875

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Automatic implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (AICD) implantation is done for all of the following conditions except :

options.c: Acute coronary syndrome with low ejection fraction

mcqs.explanation: An automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (AICD) is a device placed in the chest or abdomen to detect arrhythmias and perform cardioversion, defibrillation , and pace the heart. It is contraindicated in patients experiencing tachyarrhythmias with reversible or transient causes such as acute MI. It is used in: • Brugada syndrome- refers to a sodium channelopathy with a high risk of arrhythmias that can lead to sudden cardiac death . • Ventricular fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia. • Cardiac resynchronization therapy for prevention of sudden cardiac death in heart failure. • High-risk situations of sudden cardiac death in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Sudden cardiac death is defined as unexpected nontraumatic death in stable patients within:
mcqs.explanation: Sudden cardiac death is defined as unexpected non-traumatic death in clinically well or stable patients who die within 1 hour after onset of symptoms . The causative rhythm in most cases is ventricular fibrillation, which is usually preceded by ventricular tachycardia except in the setting of acute ischemia or infarction.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man with a history of ischemic heart disease is brought to the emergency in an unconscious state . He has been neglecting symptoms of dizziness and palpitations for the past few days. His ECG is given below . The most possible diagnosis is:
mcqs.explanation: The given ECG is suggestive of ventricular fibrillation. The features in the above ECG that support the diagnosis are: • Disordered electrical ventricular activation with no identifiable QRS complexes • No identifiable P-waves, no PR interval Possible mechanisms of ventricular fibrillation include spiral wave reentry and multiple circulating reentry wavefronts. The ECG features suggestive of ventricular tachycardia are as follows : • Wide QRS complex with abnormal morphology (marked with red arrows in image below ) • Absence of the P waves • Rate >100/min- in the ECG below , it is ~180 beats /min (1500/no. of small boxes between two R waves)876

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient who is a known case of Crohn's disease was brought to the emergency . He complained of sudden onset cold sweats and palpitations . Which among the following is the likely cause of his ECG finding shown in the given image?
mcqs.explanation: The given ECG finding shows torsades de pointes , which can occur due to hypomagnesemia (Crohn's disease causes chronic diarrhea which can cause excess GI loss of magnesium). Torsades de pointes means twisting of points, it implies twisting of the QRS complexes around the isoelectric line of the ECG. It is a form of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia that is seen in patients with a prolonged QT interval. A prolonged QT interval usually results from prolonged ventricular repolarization (lengthening of T wave). A premature ventricular contraction falling in the elongated T wave can initiate torsades de pointes . The features of torsades de pointes are: • Polymorphic QRS complexes that change in amplitude • Cycle length giving an appearance of oscillations around the baseline • QT prolongation877

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: The ECG of a pregnant lady having pre-eclampsia is shown below . Her vitals are stable . What is the best step in the management of the condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given ECG showing a wide QRS complex tachycardia with waxing and waning QRS amplitude points to the diagnosis of torsades des pointes . As the patient is hemodynamically stable , intravenous MgSO4 is the treatment of choice . Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT ) has a continually changing QRS morphology . Polymorphic VT that occurs in individuals with congenital or acquired prolongation of QT interval is referred to as torsades des pointes . Patients present with near-syncope , syncope , or cardiac arrest. IV MgSO4 is highly effective for both treatment and the prevention of recurrence of long QT-related ventricular ectopic beats that trigger torsades des pointes . If magnesium alone is ineffective , isoproterenol infusion or pacing, to a rate of 100 -120 depolarization/minute usually suppresses VT recurrences. If the patient is hemodynamically unstable , then immediate defibrillation should be done.Synchronized cardioversion Defibrillation Used inunstable PSVT , atrial flutter , atrial fibrillation, and ventricular tachycardiawith a pulse Used in ventricular tachycard iawithout a pulse , and ventric ular fibrillation. Shock is delivered in sync wit h the R wave (in absolute refr actory period ) Shock is delivered at any tim e during the cardiac cycle . Monophasic - 100 to 200J Monophasic - 360J Biphasic - 50 to 100J Biphasic - 120 to 200J878

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Identify the false statement about the bundle of Kent .

options.a: It is faster than AV nodal pathway
options.b: It is slower than AV nodal pathway

mcqs.explanation: The bundle of Kent is the accessory pathway of conduction between the atria and ventricle in Wolff -Parkinson-White syndrome. It conducts impulses faster than the AV nodal pathway and avoids AV nodal delay , leading to shortened PR interval. QRS is prolonged because of the AV nodal impulse reaching the ventricles after the aberrant impulse .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is seen in patients with Brugada syndrome?

options.c: ST segment elevation in 1, V5, AvL
options.d: ST segment elevation in II , III AvF

mcqs.explanation: The major feature of Brugada syndrome is transient or concealed ST-segment elevation in V1 to V3. Brugada syndrome is a rare syndrome characterized by ST-segment elevation and negative T waves in more than 1 anterior precordial leads ( V1 - V3 ). It is associated with mutations involving cardiac sodium channels. The patients have episodes of polymorphic VT which may lead to syncope or cardiac arrest. It shows an autosomal dominant inheritance pattern and affects males more than females . The episodes of VT may occur either in sleep or maybe provoked by febrile illness or sodium channel-blocking drugs (Class I antiarrhythmics) like ajmaline, flecainide , and procainamide. The episodes of VT can be suppressed using quinidine or catheter ablation. ICD can be used in individuals who have been resuscitated from cardiac arrest.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Brugada syndrome is associated with:
mcqs.explanation: Brugada syndrome is associated with right bundle branch block. It is an inherited disease that predisposes patients to potentially life threatening arrythmias. The ECG below is depictive of Brugada syndrome with concave ST segments and negative T waves (to be seen in more than one anterior precordial leads , i.e., V1 -V3 )879

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Romano -Ward syndrome is:

options.a: Congenital short PR associated with deafness
options.c: Congenital long QT associated with cataract

mcqs.explanation: Romano -Ward syndrome is a congenital long QT syndrome without deafness . Romano -Ward syndrome is associated with specific genetic mutations affecting membrane potassium and sodium channels. The inheritance pattern may be autosomal recessive or autosomal dominant. The preferred drugs for managing this condition are the beta -blockers. Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) implantation can also be done. Jervell-Lange-Nielsen syndrome is congenital long QT with deafness . mcqs.question: The ECG of a patient as given below is suggestive of:
mcqs.explanation: The above ECG rhythm strip shows 1st degree AV Block. The following features of this ECG support the diagnosis: • The P wave precedes each and every QRS complex • PR interval is prolonged• The PR interval is constant in every beat881

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions is associated with AV block?
mcqs.explanation: Hypothyroidism is associated with AV block. In hypothyroidism , there is reduced myocardial contractility and reduced pulse rate leading to a reduced stroke volume and bradycardia, AV block. Causes of AV block: Autonomic: • Carotid sinus hypersensitivity Metabolic : • Hyperkalemia • Hypermagnesemia • Hypothyroidism • Adrenal insufficiency Drug related : • Beta blockers • Calcium channel blockers • Adenosine • Digitalis • Lithium • Class 1 and class 3 anti arrhythmics Infections: • Endocarditis882 • Lyme disease • Chaga's disease • Syphilis • Tuberculosis • Diphtheria • Toxoplasmosis Inflammatory : • SLE • RA • Scleroderma Infiltrative: • Amyloidosis • Sarcoidosis • Hemachromatosis

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A concerned wife brought her 43-year-old husband to the clinic after an episode of light-headedness and palpitations . An ECG was taken. What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: This patient has symptoms and ECG findings suggestive of Mobitz type I or Wenckebach block. In the given ECG PR segment progressively increases in each successive cycle , until a P wave of the series fails to produce a QRS complex (dropped QRS). In this example , for every 5 'P' waves, there are only 4 'QRS' complexes ; hence, this is a 5:4 Wenckebach block.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: All of the following may be seen in Mobitz type II heart block except :

options.b: Atrial rate more than the ventricular rate

mcqs.explanation: The absence of a constant relationship between the P wave and the QRS complex (P-QRS dissociation) is a feature of complete heart block. It is not seen in Mobitz type II second -degree heart block. The PR interval remains constant in Mobitz type II second -degree heart block but few p waves are not followed by QRS complex . It occurs due to a block in the bundle of His. The atrial rate is more than the ventricular rate.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 56-year-old woman was brought to the emergency room after she lost consciousness briefly during a speech . An ECG was taken immediately . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given ECG shows a constant PR interval in each successive cycle followed by a dropped QRS (P wave fails to produce a QRS complex ). This pattern is suggestive of Mobitz type II block.883 Mobitz type II block is characterized by an intermittent failure of conduction of the p wave without any change in the preceding impulses . The dropped QRS is marked in the image below :Note : Bradyarrhythmias that cause syncope include those due to severe sinus node dysfunction and AV block( Mobitz type II block, complete AV block). Syncope due to bradycardia or asystole is referred to as Stokes-Adams attack.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Interpret the given ECG:
mcqs.explanation: The above ECG shows a complete heart block. Features in the ECG supporting the diagnosis of complete heart block: • PP interval is constant • RR interval is constant • P waves more in number than QRS complexes • There is no relation between P waves and the QRS complexes . For a second -degree heart block, the QRS complex should be preceded by the P wave, whereas in a third-degree heart block, the QRS complex is independent of the P wave. The ECG features are marked in the image below :884

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: You observe that an ECG recording revealed a QRS complex > 0.12 seconds . Which of the following would you not include in the differential diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: QRS > 0.12s points towards a wide QRS complex . The left anterior fascicular block does not cause a wide QRS complex . Fascicular blocks do not prolong the QRS interval. They only lead to axis deviation. • Left anterior fascicular block: left axis deviation • Left posterior fascicular block: right axis deviation Wide QRS complexes (\037 0.12 seconds ) are seen in the following : • Ventricular tachycardias • Ventricular premature contractions • Wolff-Parkinson -White syndrome • Bundle branch blocks (complete blocks- QRS interval \037 0.12 seconds , incomplete blocks- QRS interval between 0.10 –0.12 seconds ) • Hyperkalemia

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old male patient came to ED with complaints of weakness , paresthesia , and breathing difficulty . Relevant investigations were done. The ECG obtained is suggestive of :
mcqs.explanation: The symptoms of weakness , paresthesia, and dyspnea along with the given ECG showing depression of the ST segment , a decrease in the amplitude of the T wave (flattening or inversion ), and an increase in the amplitude of U waves (at the end of the T wave) are characteristic of hypokalemia. In the given ECG, leads V1 -V6 exhibit T wave inversion . U waves are well appreciated in leads V2-V5.885 Hypokalemia leads to dynamic ECG changes . The image given shows the sequence of changes observed:Hypokalemia is defined as plasma K+ concentration of <3.5meq/L. It can also cause premature atrial and ventricular beats , sinus bradycardia, paroxysmal atrial or junctional tachycardia, atrioventricular block, and ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation. Other options : Option B: Hyperkalemia causes tall peaked T waves with a shortened QT interval. There is a progressive lengthening of the PR interval and QRS duration with an increase in potassium levels , eventually leading to the disappearance of the P wave; and widening of the QRS complex to a sine wave pattern.886 Option C: Hypocalcemia causes prolongation of the QT interval. There is a lengthening of the ST segment , while the T wave (which correlates with the time for repolarization) remains unaltered . Option D: Hypercalcemia causes shortening of the QT interval and a decrease in the ST segment duration.887

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of valvular heart disease in developing countries ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of valvular heart disease in developing countries is rheumatic fever. This is mainly due to the repeated infections with rheumatogenic streptococci and inadequate coverage of antibiotics. It mainly affects the mitral valve. In developed countries , degenerative or inflammatory processes are the most common cause of valvular heart diseases .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the normal range for the mitral valve area in an adult ?
mcqs.explanation: The size of the mitral orifice in a normal adult is 4-6 sq cm. Depending on the area of mitral valve opening (MVA), mitral stenosis can be classified as: • Progressive MS - MVA > 1.5 sq cm • Severe MS - MVA \026 1.5 sq cm • Very severe MS - \026 1 sq cm

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman is diagnosed with mitral stenosis . Which of the following features is least likely to be seen in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Left ventricular hypertrophy is not seen in mitral stenosis . On the contrary, right ventricle hypertrophy is seen .896 Mechanism of mitral stenosis (MS): In a normal mitral valve, there is no obstruction to the flow of blood from the left atrium(LA ) to the left ventricle. Therefore a small LA pressure is sufficient to empty the blood into the ventricle. When the MVA is <~2 sq cm, blood flows from the left atrium to the left ventricle, propelled by a mildly elevated atrial pressure . Hence , patients are usually asymptomatic and may develop dyspnea only when the heart rate increases, as seen in exertion, excitement , fever, etc . All these conditions: • Increase the rate of blood flow across the mitral orifice, resulting in further elevation of the LA pressure • Decrease the diastolic filling time, resulting in a reduction in cardiac output The image below explains the mechanism of mitral stenosis .
