mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: A patient presented with angina and ECG showed ST-segment elevation. The pulse rate was found to be 54 beats /min and blood pressure was 98/56 mm Hg. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The above scenario is suggestive of STEMI with bradycardia which is a feature of inferior wall myocardial infarction. Up to one-half with inferior infarction show evidence of parasympathetic hyperactivity (bradycardia and/or hypotension).950 Many patients have a normal pulse rate and blood pressure within the first hour of STEMI. About one-fourth of patients with anterior infarction have manifestations of sympathetic nervous system hyperactivity (tachycardia and/or hypertension ).

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: A patient was admitted with acute MI. During a daily examination, a transient murmur was heard. What is the most likely cause for this finding?
mcqs.explanation: A transient midsystolic or late systolic apical murmur due to mitral regurgitation secondary to dysfunction of the mitral valve apparatus (papillary muscle dysfunction , LV dilation) may be present in STEMI.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: Which of the following cardiac biomarkers is the earliest to rise after acute myocardial infarction?
mcqs.explanation: Myoglobin is the earliest to rise in acute MI followed by troponin, CK-MB and then LDH . Serum myoglobin and heart-type fatty acid-binding protein are smaller molecules that diffuse through interstitial \037uids more rapidly after cell death than the larger CK and troponin molecules . They become abnormal as early as 30 minutes after myocardial injury. Neither molecule is specific to myocardial tissue . Myoglobin levels are not tested in routine practice .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: A patient is under evaluation for acute MI. Which of the following biomarkers would you prefer to test for?
mcqs.explanation: The most preferred cardiac biomarker for myocardial injury/acute MI amongst the given options is cardiac troponin-I. Cardiac troponin-I, CK-MB, and myoglobin are significantly more specific for acute -MI than cardiac troponin-T. The cardiac troponins are particularly valuable when there is clinical suspicion of a small MI that may be below the detection limit for CK-MB measurement . They have replaced CK-MB as the biomarker of choice for diagnosing myocardial infarction. Cardiac troponins: • Most specific cardiac biomarker for myocardial injury/acute MI • Elevations are useful for short & long-term prognoses in MI • Elevations correlate with the estimation of infarct size and risk of death • Newer highly sensitive assays for troponins become positive within the first 3 hours after onset of chest pain in MI

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: Elevated cardiac troponins may not be seen in which of the following patients ?

options.b: A 65-year-old woman suffering from Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
options.c: A patient who underwent cardioversion for VT in the emergency room

mcqs.explanation: 951 Troponins are not elevated in patients suffering from angina. Troponins are elevated in the case of myocardial necrosis (seen in MI) whereas angina is associated with myocardial insufficiency /ischemia. Conditions associated with an elevation in cardiac troponins: • MI • Myocarditis • Takotsubo cardiomyopathy • Myocardial contusion • Cardioversion/defibrillation • LV strain from CHF • Hypertensive crisis • RV strain from PE • Renal disease • Sepsis

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: Which of the following biomarkers is preferred for diagnosing reinfarction in a patient post-NSTEMI?
mcqs.explanation: Troponin (serial) is the preferred biomarker for diagnosing reinfarction. Serial troponin levels are used to detect reinfarction, an acute MI that occurs within 28 days of an incident or recurrent MI. In case of suspected reinfarction, an immediate measurement of cardiac troponin followed by a second sample after 3-6 hours. \03720 percent rise in the second sample suggests reinfarction.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is likely to be seen in a patient diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction?

options.a: Ratio of LDH 1 / LDH 2 < 1 in plasma
options.b: Ratio of LDH 1 / LDH 2 > 1 in plasma
options.c: Ratio of LDH 1 / LDH 4 < 1 in plasma
options.d: Ratio of LDH 2 / LDH 1 > 1 in plasma

mcqs.explanation: In myocardial injury, the LDH -1 fraction increases, and the ratio of LDH -1 to LDH -2 becomes >1 in the plasma. This is called flipped LDH pattern. Normally, the LDH -2 fraction is greater than the LDH -1 fraction in the plasma, and therefore , the ratio of LDH-1 to LDH -2 is normally <1.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: What is the maximum predicted heart rate in a 50-year-old gentleman on exercise tolerance test ?
mcqs.explanation: Maximum predicted heart rate on an exercise tolerance test (treadmill test ) is given by: HRmax = – Age So in a 50-year-old male, the maximum predicted heart rate is 220 - 50 = 170 bpm.952

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a contraindication for performing an exercise tolerance test ?

options.d: AAA with transverse diameter of 5.5 cm

mcqs.explanation: Treadmill exercise testing (treadmill test ) may be safely performed in patients with an abdominal aortic aneurysm. Absolute contraindications to exercise testing : • Acute myocardial infarction (within 2 days) • High-risk unstable angina • Uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia with hemodynamic compromise • Active endocarditis • Symptomatic severe aortic stenosis • Decompensated heart failure • Acute pulmonary embolism or pulmonary infarction • Acute myocarditis or pericarditis • Severe pulmonary hypertension • Aortic dissection Relative Contraindications to exercise testing : • Known left main coronary artery stenosis • Moderate aortic stenosis with uncertain relation to symptoms • Tachyarrhythmias with uncontrolled ventricular rates • Acquired complete heart block • Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with severe resting gradient • Mental impairment with limited ability to cooperate

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs cannot be used for a patient undergoing stress echocardiography?
mcqs.explanation: Phenylephrine , an alpha-receptor agonist, cannot be used for a patient undergoing stress echocardiography as it causes vasoconstriction. Dobutamine (preferred agent ) and vasodilators (dipyridamole , adenosine , regadenoson ) are used for pharmacological stress echocardiography . Pharmacologic stress testing is used in those who cannot exercise because of pulmonary veno-occlusive disease , musculoskeletal disease , or exertional dyspnea . Stress echocardiography can be done using either exercise (e.g.: treadmill test or bicycle test ) or pharmacologic agents .953

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: Which of the following findings during an exercise tolerance test is not associated with multivessel coronary artery disease ?

options.b: Persistence of ST segment changes late into recovery phase
options.c: Failure to increase systolic BP by at least 20mmHg

mcqs.explanation: A failure to increase systolic blood pressure by 10 mm Hg, or a sustained decrease in systolic blood pressure of 10 mm Hg or more, is suggestive of multivessel (or left main) CAD. Other abnormalities on exercise testing that are suggestive of multivessel CAD include : • Early-onset of ischemic ST-segment depression • ST-segment depression of \0372 mm (0.2mV ) involving 5 or more leads , or persisting \0375 minutes into recovery • Exercise -induced ST-segment elevation is also consistent with multivessel CAD • Recent evidence suggests that ST-segment elevation of \0371 mm in lead aVR may be a significant predictor of left main coronary artery disease , proximal left anterior descending (LAD ) artery disease , or at least multivessel CAD An exercise tolerance /treadmill test involves walking in place on a treadmill while monitoring the electrical activity of your heart. Throughout the test , the speed and incline of the treadmill increase. The results show how well your heart responds to the stress of different levels of exercise .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: Which of the following compounds is used for myocardial perfusion imaging?
mcqs.explanation: Myocardial perfusion imaging is done with either thallium-201 or technetium -99m labeled compounds (e.g., technetium -99m sestamibi).

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: A patient is being considered for CABG in order to achieve coronary revascularization . Which of the following test will not be useful to assess myocardial viability for predicting the risk of perioperative morbidity?
mcqs.explanation: Modalities for the determination of myocardial viability include : • Thallium-201 imaging • MRI • Dobutamine echocardiography • PET scan (investigation of choice ) The investigation of choice for assessing the ventricular function is cardiac MRI.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: Which questionnaire is used for the assessment of a patient who presented with symptoms of angina?
mcqs.explanation: WHO Rose questionnaire is used for the assessment of angina. Option B: International prostate symptom score (IPSS) questionnaire is used for BPH. Option C: The CAGE questionnaire is used to check for signs of possible alcohol dependency .954 Option D: The youth tobacco survey (YTS) questionnaire is used to study the prevalence of use of tobacco products amongst youth .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: Which of the following ECG findings is first to appear in a patient suspected of acute myocardial infarction?
mcqs.explanation: During acute myocardial infarction, the ECG evolves through 3 stages : • T-wave peaking and T-wave inversion : • Peaked T-wave aka hyperacute T-wave- first ECG change (occurs within minutes ) • If the blood flow is restored or the oxygen demands of the heart are met, the T waves will revert to normal • If myocardial cell death has occurred, T wave inversions appear (over days) and persist for months to years. • A nonspecific finding and is indicative only of ischemia and not diagnostic of infarction • ST-segment elevation occurs over minutes to hours (after T-wave peaking) • The appearance of new pathologic Q-waves: • Occurs over hours to days (after ST-segment elevation) and is indicative of an evolving MI • The persistence of pathological Q-waves indicates irreversible myocardial cell death

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: A patient presented with the complaints of chest pain. Which among the following is the best investigation to diagnose MI within 2-4 hours?
mcqs.explanation: Measurement of troponin is the best investigation to diagnose MI within 2-4 hours.955 Troponin T/I: • Highly specific for MI • Troponin I is more important than troponin T. • Troponins will remain elevated longer than creatine kinase (CK), for up to 14 days. • This makes troponins a superior marker for diagnosing MI in the recent past (late diagnosis). • Reinfarction: It is now clear that cardiac troponin (cTn) increases rapidly, even if it is from an abnormal baseline in patients with reinfarction. • Sometimes cTn concentration is elevated , but stable or decreasing at the time of suspected reinfarction. In this case, the diagnosis of reinfarction requires a 20 % or greater increase in the cTn measurement Creatine kinase (CK): • Less sensitive and specific than troponins • When cTn is available, CK-MB should not be used for the initial diagnosis of acute MI Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH ): • Normally, LDH2 >LDH1; but, in MI, LDH1 >LDH2. This is called flipping of the LDH ratio. • Current recommendations suggest that LDH no longer has a role in the diagnosis of MI. Myoglobin : • Earliest enzyme to increase after MI. • Not specific to cardiac muscle and can be elevated to any form of injury to skeletal muscle . Heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP), which mainly exists in cardiomyocytes , has recently emerged as a potential biomarker , which was found to be sensitive for the early diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction. H-FABP as an early marker and cTnI as a late marker would be the ideal combination to cover the complete diagnostic window for AMI956

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Presentation and Diagn...
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions is not associated with an ST-segment elevation?
mcqs.explanation: There is no ST-segment elevation in unstable angina. Differential diagnosis of ST-segment elevation (Mnemonic-ELEVATION): • Electrolytes (Hypercalcemia , Hyperkalemia) • Left bundle branch block • Early(Benign) repolarization, Embolism(Acute pulmonary) • Ventricular hypertrophy • Arrhythmia (Brugada syndrome), Aneurysm of LV , Aortic dissection , Antiarrhythmic drugs(Class 1c) • Tako -tsubo syndrome, Tumor invading left ventricle, Trauma to ventricles • Infarction (MI), Inflammation (Myocarditis, Pericarditis) • Osborn J waves (Hypothermia or hypercalcemia ) • Non-atherosclerotic vasospasm(Prinzmetal's angina)957

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: A 38-year-old woman presented with chest pain that was unrelated to physical exertion. ECG showed ST-segment elevation. Intracoronary acetylcholine provocation testing revealed a transient spasm of the right coronary artery. What is the drug of choice in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The above scenario in which rest pain is associated with ST-segment elevation and transient coronary vasospasm is suggestive of Prinzmetal's angina. The drug of choice is a calcium channel blocker. Prinzmetal variant angina (PVA ) is a clinical syndrome in which chest pain occurs without the usual precipitating factors. It usually results from coronary vasoconstriction (vasospasm) and tends to involve the right coronary artery. It is a supply ischemia and usually causes transmural ischemia (subendocardial in classic angina pectoris). It often affects women under 50 years of age . It characteristically occurs in the early morning , awakening patients from sleep , and may be associated with arrhythmias or conduction defects . The clinical diagnosis of PVA is made by the detection of transient ST-segment elevation with rest pain. Coronary angiography demonstrates transient coronary spasm which is the diagnostic hallmark of PVA . Nitrates and calcium channel blockers both can be used in alleviating symptoms in Prinzmetal's angina. However due to the development of nitrate tolerance in some individuals, they are less preferred and calcium channel blockers such as verapamil, diltiazem are used as first-line agents .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: A patient who presents to the ER with chest pain and dyspnea is diagnosed with STEMI. Swift revascularization by thrombolysis is planned for her. What is the dose of streptokinase to be used ?
mcqs.explanation: Streptokinase is given in a dose of 1.5 million units IV given over 1 hour for treatment of MI. Fibrinolytic therapy should ideally be initiated within 30 min of presentation . The fibrinolytic agents that have been approved for IV use in patients with STEMI are: • Tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) • Streptokinase • Tenecteplase (TNK)966 • Reteplase (rPA ) Adverse effects of streptokinase : • Transient hypotension • Allergic reactions • Hemorrhage

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: Which of the given fibrinolytic agents is least preferred for thrombolysis in a patient with MI?
mcqs.explanation: Streptokinase has the lowest clot selectivity among the fibrinolytic agents . Fibrinolytic agent with: • Least fibrin specificity – streptokinase • Most fibrin specificity – tenecteplase

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: While planning thrombolysis for a patient with MI, use of which of the following agents will reduce the chances of a dosing error ?
mcqs.explanation: Tenecteplase is given as a single bolus dose (based on body weight ) which reduces the rate of medication errors (common with IV infusions). Tenecteplase and reteplase are referred to as bolus fibrinolytics as their administration does not require prolonged intravenous infusion.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an absolute contraindication for the use of a fibrinolytic agent in patients with an acute MI?
mcqs.explanation: Prolonged cardiopulmonary resuscitation is a relative contraindication for fibrinolytic therapy .Contraindications for the use of fibrinolytic agents Absolute contraindications Relative contraindications History of hemorrhagic strok e at any time Current use of anticoagulants (INR \0372) Non-hemorrhagic stroke or o ther cerebrovascular events within the past year Recent (<2 weeks ) invasive or surgical procedure Marked hypertension (SBP>1 80mmHg and/or a DBP>110 mmHg) at any time during th e acute presentation Prolonged (>10 min) cardiop ulmonary resuscitation Suspicion of aortic dissection Known bleeding diathesis967 Contraindications for the use of fibrinolytic agents Active internal bleeding (excl uding menses ) Pregnancy Hemorrhagic ophthalmic con dition (e.g., hemorrhagic dia betic retinopathy ) Active peptic ulcer disease History of severe hypertensio n that is currently adequately controlled

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: All of the following drugs should be avoided in a patient with angina except :
mcqs.explanation: Trimetazidine is an antianginal drug. It is a PFox (partial fatty acid oxidation) inhibitor. It inhibits the beta -oxidation of fatty acids and thus enhances glucose oxidation. This results in decreased oxygen consumption in ATP synthesis as beta -oxidation consumes more oxygen. Option A: Thyroxine increases the heart rate, which can increase the myocardial oxygen demand and can precipitate angina. Option B: Sumatriptan and other triptans cause coronary vasospasm. They are therefore contraindicated in patients with CAD. Option C: Dipyridamole can produce coronary steal phenomenon and can worsen angina.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: Which of the following combinations should be avoided while treating a patient with angina?
mcqs.explanation: Verapamil and \031-blockers have additive effects on inhibiting SA node and AV conduction , the combination should be avoided to prevent severe bradycardia and conduction block. These agents can also have additive effects on decreasing left ventricular function which could seriously impair cardiac output in a patient with heart failure. Diltiazem can be combined with beta -blockers in patients with normal ventricular function and no conduction disturbances . Amlodipine and \031-blockers have complementary actions on coronary blood supply and myocardial oxygen demands . Whereas the former decreases blood pressure and dilates coronary arteries, the latter slows the heart rate and decreases contractility .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: What is the mechanism of action of ranolazine?
mcqs.explanation: 968 The predominant mechanism of action of ranolazine is inhibition of the late sodium current in myocardial cells . Ranolazine is useful for patients with chronic angina despite standard medical therapy . It is administered at a dose of 500-1000 mg twice daily. Contraindications: • Hepatic impairment • QT prolongation • Drugs inhibiting CYP3A metabolic system - ketoconazole , diltiazem, verapamil, macrolide antibiotics, HIV protease inhibitors, and large quantities of grapefruit juice

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: A patient on clopidogrel is scheduled to undergo an elective operation. What is your advice regarding the drug?
mcqs.explanation: Clopidogrel should be stopped 5-7 days prior to surgery to avoid the risk of increased surgical bleeding .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs would you prescribe to prolong life in a post -MI patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Beta-blockers are the only antianginal agents that have been demonstrated to prolong life in patients with coronary disease (post -myocardial infarction). Note : B-blockers and spironolactone have been demonstrated to improve survival in individuals with heart failure.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man post -MI had the following lab values. Which of the following must be his treatment plan?
mcqs.explanation: In this 60 yr old patient with post -myocardial infarction (Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease patient), high-intensity statins should be given irrespective of cholesterol levels . So atorvastatin 80mg is the treatment plan in the given case scenario. Examples of high-intensity statins include high-dose atorvastatin 40–80 mg/day and rosuvastatin 20–40 mg/day. Note : Fenofibrate is not advocated unless TG is more than 500 mg/dl. It can be administered along with a moderate -intensity statin.969

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: A patient presents with an intense exertional chest pain radiating to the neck along with shortness of breath for 30mins . ECG reveals ST-segment depression . Cardiac troponins are elevated . Which of the following is incorrect regarding the management of this condition?

options.a: Aspirin loading dose should be commenced immediately
options.b: ACC/ AHA guidelines call a P2Y12 inhibitors as a class I recommendation
options.c: Glycoprotein IIB /IIIA inhibitors are useful adjuncts
options.d: Fibrinolytic therapy is useful in this condition

mcqs.explanation: The above scenario is suggestive of NSTEMI. Antiplatelet and anticoagulation therapies and coronary intervention are mainstays of treatment . A distinction in acute coronary syndrome between patients with and without ST-segment elevation at presentation is essential to determine the need for reperfusion therapy . Fibrinolytic therapy is harmful in acute coronary syndrome without ST-segment elevation, unlike with ST-segment elevation, where acute reperfusion saves lives.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: A patient is diagnosed with STEMI on presentation . Coronary angiography showed complete occlusion of the infarct-related artery. Immediate primary PCI with a drug-eluting stent is planned . Which of the following drug-eluting stents will have a relatively higher risk of restenosis and late stent thrombosis?
mcqs.explanation: Sirolimus and paclitaxel are a part of first-generation drug-eluting stents that carry a relatively higher risk of restenosis and late stent thrombosis than second -generation drug-eluting stents . Second -generation drug-eluting stents use newer agents such as everolimus, biolimus, and zotarolimus. These second -generation drug-eluting stents are more effective with fewer complications like stent thrombosis than first-generation stents . An antiproliferative agent is attached to the stent by the use of a thin polymer coating. This antiproliferative drug elutes from the stent over a 1 to 3 month period after implantation.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old male patient presents to the emergency department with chest pain for 2 hours. The ECG shows ST-segment depression and cardiac troponins are elevated . The patient has a history of PCI 3 months back. He is given aspirin, clopidogrel , nitrates, and unfractionated heparin and shifted to the coronary care unit. What is the next best course of action?

options.a: Continue conservative management and monitoring of cardiac enzymes and ECG
options.b: Continue conservative management and plan for delayed revascularization procedure after the patient is discharged

mcqs.explanation: The patient described above is categorized as a high-risk patient due to his history of PCI 3 months ago. The next best course of action for this patient is immediate revascularization with PCI.970 Revascularization with PCI (percutaneous coronary intervention) is indicated in high-risk patients who have one or more of the following: • New ST-segment depression • Diabetes mellitus • Renal dysfunction - eGFR <60mL/min per 1.73m2 • Ejection fraction <40% • Early postinfarction angina • PCI within the past 6 months • Prior CABG • Refractory angina • Symptoms of congestive heart failure • Hemodynamic instability • Recurrent angina at rest/low-level activity despite treatment • Elevated troponin T or troponin I • Sustained VT or VF

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: For an acute STEMI patient with cardiogenic shock, what would be the treatment of choice ?
mcqs.explanation: The treatment of choice in patients with acute STEMI with cardiogenic shock is revascularization with PCI. The 2013 ACCF/AHA guidelines for the treatment of cardiogenic shock in patients with acute MI are: • Emergency revascularization with PCI or CABG is recommended in suitable patients irrespective of the time delay from MI onset . • In the absence of contraindications, fibrinolytic therapy should be administered to patients with STEMI and cardiogenic shock who are unsuitable candidates for either PCI or CABG. Routine use of Intra -Aortic Balloon Pump counterpulsation (IABP ) is not recommended for cardiogenic shock (based on IABP -SHOCK II trial). IABP can be useful for those patients with cardiogenic shock after STEMI who do not quickly stabilize with pharmacological therapy or have mechanical complications (eg , acute mitral regurgitation or rupture of the ventricular septum ). Alternative left ventricular assist devices for circulatory support may be considered in patients with refractory cardiogenic shock.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old chronic smoker comes with acute epigastric discomfort for the past one hour. ECG shows ST-segment depression . What is the immediate intervention?
mcqs.explanation: The above scenario is suggestive of a non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS). Immediate intervention is the administration of aspirin.971 Aspirin is the first drug given in acute coronary syndromes. An initial dose of 325 mg to be chewed and swallowed is given. If oral administration is not feasible , it should be given as a rectal suppository . The following protocol must be followed in the management of patients with acute coronary syndrome: • Stabilization of airway, breathing, and circulation • Administration of O2 • Treatment of sustained ventricular arrhythmia rapidly according to ACLS protocols • Give aspirin 325 mg • History and examination, assess cardiac biomarkers • Give three sublingual nitroglycerin tablets each 5 min apart. Add IV nitroglycerin for the persistence of symptoms . • Treat left heart failure if present with an after-load reducing agent or loop diuretic • Give beta -blockers • Give morphine for the persistence of anxiety and discomfort related to MI • In patients with STEMI - Reperfusion with PCI or fibrinolysis (if PCI is unavailable within 120 min) followed by antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy . In patients with NSTEMI - antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy are indicated .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: A previously healthy 58-year-old man is admitted to the hospital because of an acute MI. ECG is shown below. Within several hours, he becomes oliguric and hypotensive . On auscultation , no added sounds were present . What is the most likely reason for this patient being in shock?

options.d: Decreased ejection fraction from the left ventricle

mcqs.explanation: The above ECG shows ST-segment elevation in leads II , III , and aVF suggestive of an inferior-wall MI. In the given scenario, the most likely reason for the patient to have shock is right ventricular infarction. The diagnosis of right ventricular MI is suspected in patients with inferior-wall MI, clear lung fields (no added sounds on auscultation), and shock. It can also be confirmed by the use of right-sided electrocardiogram (ECG) leads . In patients with presumed right ventricular shock, intravenous (IV ) fluid replacement is indicated if jugular (central) venous pressure is not elevated . Options A, B, and D: No added sounds on auscultation clearly rule out mitral regurgitation , septal defect (pansystolic murmur is heard), and decreased ejection fraction from the left ventricle (leads to pulmonary congestion and added sounds), as the cause of shock in this patient .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: A patient presented with sudden circulatory collapse and engorged neck veins 3 days post -MI. A bedside transthoracic echocardiogram revealed the following . Which of the following is false regarding the cause of this patient 's findings?

options.a: It usually results in immediate death

mcqs.explanation: The echocardiogram shows pericardial effusion with cardiac tamponade (swinging heart sign). The likely diagnosis in the above scenario is myocardial rupture post -MI. It usually occurs 3 - days postinfarction and commonly involves the anterior wall.972 This condition usually results in immediate death . It is common in older women. Incomplete or gradual rupture may be sealed off by the pericardium creating a pseudoaneurysm . Immediate pericardiocentesis should be done to relieve the symptoms of shock due to tamponade . Early surgical repair is the definitive treatment .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about Dressler syndrome is false ?

options.c: First line therapy consists of aspirin

mcqs.explanation: Dressler syndrome commonly occurs 1-12 weeks after MI, not 2-7 days. However, it can recur over months. Dressler syndrome is a post -myocardial infarction syndrome that presents as pleuritic chest pain, fever, and sometimes a pleuritic rub and effusion . The ECG findings include PR segment depression or ST-segment elevation. It is an autoimmune phenomenon occurring due to immune-complex deposition in the pericardium and lung pleura . The first-line therapy consists of aspirin. Note : NSAIDs and corticosteroids impair the infarct healing and predispose the patients to myocardial rupture . Therefore these drugs must be avoided in the early postinfarction period .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: Left ventriculography with contrast was performed in a post -MI patient and is shown below . Infarct involving which portion of the myocardium is most likely to cause this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The above image showing left ventriculography with contrast is suggestive of a left ventricular aneurysm. Anterior transmural infarcts are involved in causing aneurysms as a post -MI complication. Patients with anterior transmural infarcts are at the greatest risk for: • Free -wall rupture • Expansion • Mural thrombi • Aneurysm Posterior transmural infarcts are more likely to be complicated by: • Conduction blocks • Right ventricular involvement, or both

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man started experiencing chest pain and was rushed to a primary care facility at 10 AM. A diagnosis of acute severe MI was made. Due to the unavailability of PCI, he was taken to a tertiary center by 10 :30 AM. By what time should PCI be performed in this patient at the latest ?
mcqs.explanation: The door-to-balloon time for a patient arriving in a hospital that is not equipped to perform a PCI and is then transported to a hospital where PCI can be performed is 120 min. The door-to-balloon time is the time interval between the first medical contact and PCI.973 It is 90 min or less for a patient arriving in a hospital equipped with PCI (ACC/AHA guidelines and MoHFW, India guidelines ). In patients who cannot receive PCI within 120 min of first medical contact, fibrinolysis is given. Fibrinolysis is only considered if the patient presents within 12 hours of symptom onset . Note : The European society of cardiology (ESC) recommends 60 min target time for patients presenting in a PCI-centre and 90 min maximum target time for PCI-mediated reperfusion .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: Which of the following defines PCI related MI ?

options.a: Elevation of cTn > 5 times normal in the absence of any other features
options.b: Elevation of cTn > 5 times normal in the presence of symptoms of MI, ECG changes , angiographic findings or imaging abnormality
options.c: Elevation of cTn > 3 times normal in the absence of any other features
options.d: Elevation of cTn > 3 times normal in the presence of symptoms of MI, ECG changes , angiographic findings or imaging abnormality

mcqs.explanation: PCI related MI is defined as elevation of cTn > 5 times normal in the presence of symptoms of MI, ECG changes , angiographic findings or imaging abnormality. The imaging abnormality could be a new loss of viable myocardium or new regional wall motion abnormality. If the baseline cTn values are elevated but stable or falling, a rise in cTn >20 % defined PCI related MI. CABG related MI is defined as elevation of cTn > 10 times the normal baseline values in the presence of new pathologic Q waves, angiographic findings or imaging abnormality.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: A patient comes to the hospital with chest pain for the last 3 hours. Vitals are stable . ECG revealed ST depression and T wave inversion in anterior chest leads . Which of the following would be the most appropriate line of management in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Based on the given clinical scenario of a patient presenting with sudden onset of chest pain, with ECG findings of ST depression in the anterior chest leads and T wave inversion , the most likely diagnosis is a non-ST-segment elevation-acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS). The most appropriate line of management in this patient would be to administer aspirin with heparin. Percutaneous coronary intervention is indicated after coronary angiography in high-risk patients . Fibrinolytic therapy is not indicated in patients with NSTE-ACS. Arrhythmia prophylaxis is generally not routinely recommended in all patients with NSTE-ACS. Acute coronary syndrome is classified into 2 groups : • ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) • NSTE-ACS NSTE-ACS further includes : • NSTEMI (myocyte necrosis present and cardiac troponins elevated ) • Unstable Angina (myocyte necrosis absent and cardiac troponins not elevated ) The diagnosis of NSTE-ACS is based on the following : Severe chest discomfort with at least one of 3 features : • Occurring at rest or minimal exertio n and lasting for more than 10 minutes • Recent onset • Crescendo pattern974 ECG showing : • ST segment depression • T wave inversion Elevated cardiac troponins in case of NSTEMI. Management of NSTE-ACS: To provide relief of pain and discomfort, initial treatment includes bed rest, nitrates, beta blockers, and inhaled oxygen (only if arterial O2 saturation <90%). Antithrombotic therapy consisting of antiplatelet and anticoagulant drugs: • Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT ): Aspirin (162 -325 mg) AND one ADP receptor inhibitor (Ticagrelor, clopidogrel or prasugrel ) • Anticoagulation : Enoxaparin, unfractionated heparin, fondaparinux or bivalirudin • An early invasive strategy including diagnostic coronary angiography (within 2–72 hours of presentation) followed by revascularization (percutaneous coronary intervention/ coronary artery bypass grafting) is indicated for stabilized patients who are at high risk of coronary events (Based on TIMI , GRACE or HEART score).975

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common protein mutation seen in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common mutations in HCM are those affecting the myosin heavy chain. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is an autosomal dominant disease . In the majority of cases it is due to missense mutations in the following two sarcolemmal protein genes : • Myosin binding protein C (MYBC) • Beta myosin heavy chain (MYH7 ) Option B: Alpha-tropomyosin mutation is seen in HCM but is not common. Options C and D: Mutations in cardiac troponin C and titin are associated with dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM).

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 19-year-old basketball player collapses during a match and regains consciousness several minutes later. He reveals that he has had similar episodes before . His older brother, a soccer player , had died suddenly at the age of 22 years during a soccer game due to a heart ailment. Which of the following is least likely to be found on echocardiography in this patient ?

options.a: Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
options.b: Systolic anterior motion of mitral valve
options.c: Mitral regurgitation with anteriorly directed regurgitant jet

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of exercise intolerance (syncope ) in the patient and family history of sudden cardiac death in his elder brother at a young age is suggestive of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Mitral regurgitation with posteriorly directed regurgitant jet is usually seen on echocardiogram in HCM. ECG and echocardiogram are used to confirm the diagnosis of HCM. HCM is characterized by myofiber disarray in the heart, resulting in a hypertrophic myocardium. The hypertrophy leads to the following pathophysiological changes in HCM: • Diastolic dysfunction - presenting as exercise intolerance • Systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve • The hypertrophied muscles result in a narrow outflow tract • This leads to the production of a high-velocity jet pulling the mitral leaflets towards the septum posteriorly • SAM leads to mitral regurgitation • Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT ) obstruction Echocardiography features of HCM are as follows :981 • Left ventricular wall thickness >15 mm • Hypertrophied heart more confined to the interventricular septum resulting in banana -shaped ventricular cavity

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: While evaluating a young man for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy you hear a harsh and late peaking systolic ejection murmur at the lower left sternal border. On performing which of the following maneuvers, the intensity of this murmur is expected to decrease ?
mcqs.explanation: Squatting increases the preload and afterload thereby decreasing the outflow obstruction and intensity of murmur in HCM. In HCM left ventricular size is small, thus the approximation of the interventricular septum with the mitral valve increases. The following mechanisms further increase this approximation and increase blood outflow obstruction and intensity of murmur : • A decrease in left ventricular cavity volume or pressure (decreased preload ) • A decrease in systemic vascular resistance and/or arterial pressure (decreased afterload ) • Increase in left ventricular contractility The image below shows a cross-section of a heart with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy .Note : All murmurs increase in intensity on squatting except that of HOCM and MVP.Parameters Murmur intensity increased Murmur intensity decreased Preload ValsalvaStanding (\023preload = \027obstruction) SquattingPassive leg raising (\027preload = \023obstruction) Force of contractio n Exercise (\027force = \027obstructio n) Afterload Vasodilators(\023afterload = \027o bstruction) Isotonic handgripSquatting(\027 afterload = \023obstruction)982

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 20 -year-old patient has been diagnosed with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy . Which of the following is not a major risk factor for sudden death in this condition?

options.c: Family history of sudden cardiac death

mcqs.explanation: Atrial fibrillation in HCM is not associated with increased HCM-related mortality. It frequently accounts for unexpected hospital admissions, lost productivity , and impaired quality of life . Among HCM patients , the greatest risk for sudden cardiac death is seen in patients who have sustained ventricular tachycardia (VT ). These patients must undergo placement of an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) for secondary prevention.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 17-year-old boy presents with complaints of syncope . ECG is suggestive of LV hypertrophy . A doppler echocardiography revealed abnormal systolic anterior leaflet motion of the mitral valve. Which of the following drugs should be avoided in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy . Digoxin should be avoided as it may increase contractility and worsen obstruction. Drugs that can lead to possible aggravation of outflow tract obstruction and thus contraindicated in HCM are: • Digoxin • Inotropes • Nitrates • ACE inhibitors • Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (eg - nifedipine , amlodipine ) Beta-blockers and verapamil are first-line agents in the treatment of HCM. Disopyramide and amiodarone are the preferred antiarrhythmic agents .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which is the most common sustained arrhythmia in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy ?
mcqs.explanation: Symptomatic atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained arrhythmia in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). It frequently accounts for unexpected hospital admissions, lost productivity , and impaired quality of life . Treatment of atrial fibrillation in HCM: • Amiodarone - drug of choice • Disopyramide • Radiofrequency ablation for medically refractory cases • Anticoagulation to prevent embolic events Note : A sustained arrhythmia is one that lasts for >30 seconds .983

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: You are counseling the parents of a 15-year-old boy who was recently diagnosed with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy . What is the recommendation regarding his participation in sports?

options.a: Participation in competitive sports is not recommended
options.b: Only non-contact competitive sports are allowed
options.c: Non-contact competitive sports with beta -blocker therapy is allowed
options.d: High-intensity exercise is acceptable with verapamil therapy

mcqs.explanation: Participation in competitive sports is not recommended for patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy . The following general measures are advised for patients with HCM: • Patients are advised against engaging in competitive athletics or vigorous physical activities • Maintaining low to moderate levels of exercise as a part of a healthy lifestyle has been proven to be beneficial • Adequate hydration at all times Note : Non-contact sports are those sports wherein the participants are physically separated with almost no physical contact (ex: tennis, badminton) between them. Contact sports involve some form of physical contact between the participants (ex: wrestling , boxing)

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old Japanese woman was brought to the emergency department with worsening angina and palpitations . Her physical examination was normal . ECG showed giant T wave inversions and coronary angiography was normal . Left ventriculography showed spade -like deformity . What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of giant T wave inversions and spade -like deformity on left ventriculography points to a diagnosis of apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy . Apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is also called Yamaguchi syndrome. It is characterized by hypertrophy of the myocardium, predominantly in the left ventricular apex. It was first described in the Japanese population and is uncommon in other populations . The symptoms are milder and the risk of sudden cardiac death is lower than in the traditional septal form of HCM. The image below shows the ace of spades appearance on left ventriculography:The image below shows the ace of spades appearance on echocardiography with massive hypertrophy of the apex and relative sparing of the base:984

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Two brothers were arguing over a property dispute when the elder of the two complained of chest pain and collapsed and was later declared brought dead by the hospital . His family says he was previously healthy and there was no similar disease in the family members. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of sudden heart failure in a previously healthy person under a stressful situation is suggestive of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy . Takotsubo cardiomyopathy is also called broken heart syndrome, apical ballooning syndrome, or stress-induced cardiomyopathy . It is a transient myocardial stunning from microcirculation spams due to a catecholamine surge during stress . It is usually seen in middle -aged women. The patients can present with pulmonary edema , hypotension , and chest pain. ECHO reveals apical dilatation with basal hypercontraction of the heart, resembling a Takotsubo (pot for catching octopus ). The ECG changes can mimic myocardial infarction but changes extend beyond a particular coronary arterial territory. Coronary angiography, therefore , may be needed to rule out coronary occlusion . (Option B) It is a self -limiting disorder resolving within days to weeks . The prognosis is generally good . The image below shows left ventriculography during systole showing apical ballooning resembling a Takotsubo pot .985 Other options : Option A: Infective cardiomyopathy : The most common causes of infective myocarditis are viral infections and the protozoan Trypanosoma cruzi, which is associated with Chagas' disease . Acute viral myocarditis often presents with symptoms and signs of heart failure, although it can also manifest as chest pain and show electrocardiogram (ECG) changes resembling pericarditis or acute myocardial infarction. In Chagas' disease , specific features include abnormalities in the conduction system , particularly dysfunction of the sinus node and AV node, as well as the right bundle branch block. Option C: Dilated cardiomyopathy : It is the most common cardiomyopathy and is predominantly characterised by systolic dysfunction . Though it may present acutely , it progresses chronically. The familial form is due to mutations in TTN gene which encode the sarcomeric protein titin. Other etiologocal agents include alcohol, infective myocarditis, doxorubicin, hemochromatosis and sarcoidosis. Option D: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy : Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is the most common genetic cardiovascular disorder and is a prominent cause of sudden death before the age of 35 years. Family history is commonly present , a sarcomere mutation is present in ~50% of patients . Sudden death can be due to polymorphic ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation. Risk factors for sudden death in this disease include young age , nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, failure of blood pressure to increase during exercise , recent (within 6 months) syncope , ventricular wall thickness >3 cm, and possibly the severity of LV outflow obstruction.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: The observed myocardial stunning pattern does not match the ECG findings of a patient . What is the probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy is the probable diagnosis when the observed myocardial stunning pattern does not match ECG changes . Myocardial stunning is a state where certain segments of the myocardium (usually corresponding to an area of major coronary occlusion) show forms of contractile abnormality (dysfunction) on echocardiography .986 In Takotsubo cardiomyopathy , while the ECG changes mimic a myocardial infarction(MI), the left ventricular dysfunction extends well beyond the distribution of a specific coronary artery. Thus, the myocardial stunning pattern might not fully match the ECG. Ventriculography shows apical dilation with basal contraction. Takotsubo cardiomyopathy occurs typically in older women and is associated with a sudden increase in emotional or physical stress , presenting with hypotension , chest pain with ECG changes of acute MI, and pulmonary edema . Its also known as apical ballooning syndrome or acute stress -induced cardiomyopathy . Option B: Restrictive cardiomyopathy is characterized by diastolic dysfunction with reduced contractility and ejection fraction, most commonly seen in amyloidosis , and enlarged ventricles on imaging with low-voltage ECG complexes . Option C: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC ) is a type of familial dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), having defects in desmosomal proteins , affecting the ventricles showing thin ventricular walls on Echo, epsilon waves, and low voltage ECG complexes . Option D: Pericardial tamponade is characterized by hypotension , muffled heart sounds and increased jugular venous pressure with muffled heart sounds with total electrical alternans and sinus tachycardia in ECG.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 17-year-old Chinese boy presented with prolonged fatigue , shortness of breath, and swelling in the legs . His echocardiography was suggestive of dilated cardiomyopathy . Which of the following nutritional deficiencies can explain his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The patient is probably suffering from Keshan 's disease , which is due to selenium deficiency . It is endemic dilated cardiomyopathy that affects children and women of childbearing age in some areas in China. The nutritional deficiencies that can lead to cardiomyopathy are: • Thiamine • Selenium • Carnitine • Calcium • Phosphate • Magnesium

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Endomyocardial biopsy of a patient shows vacuolar degeneration and myofibrillar loss. Which of the following drugs may be responsible for this finding?
mcqs.explanation: Endomyocardial biopsy showing vacuolar degeneration and myofibrillar loss is seen in cardiotoxicity due to anthracyclines (doxorubicin). mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: In which of the following patients , the risk of developing peripartum cardiomyopathy is less ?

options.a: A 26-year-old pregnant woman with an obstetric score of G2P

mcqs.explanation: Low parity is not a risk factor for peripartum cardiomyopathy . Increased parity is a risk factor. Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a type of dilated cardiomyopathy . It develops during the last month of pregnancy or within the first 5 months following delivery . The risk factors are: • Increased maternal age • Increased parity • Twin pregnancy • Malnutrition • Use of tocolytic therapy for premature labor • Preeclampsia or toxemia of pregnancy

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A young male patient presents with progressive dyspnea and weakness . He gives a history of fever, myalgia, and sore throat one week ago. To further evaluate him as per Dallas criteria, which of the following tests need to be performed ?
mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario is suggestive of infective myocarditis. The Dallas criteria used for the diagnosis of myocarditis is based on endomyocardial biopsy . It is used to define the disease . Active myocarditis is defined as an inflammatory infiltrate of the myocardium with necrosis and/or degeneration of adjacent myocytes not typical of the ischemic damage associated with coronary artery disease . Borderline myocarditis is the term used when the inflammatory infiltrate is too sparse or myocyte injury is not demonstrated .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which is the most common infective cause of myocarditis?
mcqs.explanation: The most common infective cause of myocarditis is Trypanosoma cruzi causing Chagas disease . Infective myocarditis is most commonly associated with viruses (adenovirus, coxsackie B virus, HHV -6) and the protozoan Trypanosoma cruzi. The most common noninfective cause of myocarditis is sarcoidosis.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 13 -year-old boy collapsed while playing football . ECG showed V5, V6 inversion and prominent inverted T-waves. 2D echocardiography showed systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve leaflet . Which of the following features will be seen on clinical examination and which of the following are true regarding the management?
mcqs.explanation: 988 The given clinical scenario of a young patient with a history of sudden collapse following physical activity along with ECG findings of V5, V6 inversion , and prominent inverted T-waves, and 2D echocardiography showing the systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve leaflet point toward a diagnosis of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HCM). In HCM, clinical examination may reveal pulsus bisferiens and an ejection systolic murmur that increases on standing. Beta-blockers and implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICD) are used in the management. HCM is a leading cause of sudden death in young. It is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern with variable penetrance . HCM is characterized by the thickening of the septal myocardium below the aortic valve leading to obstruction of the left ventricular outflow tract. Symptoms : • Exertional dyspnea • Syncope • Angina, palpitations , cardiac arrhythmias • Sudden cardiac death (particularly during or after intense physical activity) Examination: • Systolic ejection murmur best heard at the apex or lower left sternal border • Holosystolic murmur from mitral regurgitation • Sustained apex beat • S4 gallop • Paradoxical split of S2 • Pulsus bisferiens : LV outflow obstruction causes a sudden quick rise of the pulse followed by a slower longer rise. ECG findings: • Left axis deviation • P wave abnormalities • Prominent abnormal Q waves • Deeply inverted T waves Echocardiography findings: • LV wall thickness \03715 mm • Systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve leaflet • Mitral regurgitation Treatment: • Beta-blockers and calcium channel blockers are the first-line treatment • Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) - indicated when the history of cardiac arrest or sustained ventricular tachycardia is present989 Parameters Murmur intensity increased Murmur intensity decreased Preload ValsalvaStanding (\023preload = \027obstruction) SquattingPassive leg raising (\027preload = \023obstruction) Force of contractio n Exercise (\027force = \027obstructio n) Afterload Vasodilators(\023afterload = \027o bstruction) Isotonic handgripSquatting(\027 afterload = \023obstruction)990

On examination, the pulse is irregular at 118 beats /min. Bilateral pitting pedal edema is present . ECG is suggestive of right axis deviation. Which of the following feature is unlikely to be present in this patient ?

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient who is being evaluated for heart failure undergoes echocardiography for assessment of ejection fraction (EF). When will you categorize his condition as heart failure with reduced ejection fraction based on the results ?
mcqs.explanation: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction is ejection fraction <40%. According to the European society of cardiology (ESC) heart failure guidelines 2016 - • Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)- ejection fraction <40% • Heart failure with mid-range ejection Fraction (HFmrEF)- ejection fraction 40-50% • Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF )- ejection fraction >50%

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old male patient came with complaints of episodes of shortness of breath and coughing at night which awakens him from sleep . On examination, distended neck veins were observed and S3 was heard on auscultation . Which of the following biomarkers can be used for the diagnosis in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: 997 The given clinical scenario suggests a diagnosis of heart failure. The brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) can be used to confirm this. Natriuretic peptides are protein molecules that are secreted by the ventricular myocytes in response to volume or pressure overload. Ventricular musculature releases pre-proBNP which is cleaved into active BNP and inert NT-proBNP. BNP causes natriuresis, vasodilatation, and diuresis that leads to improved myocardial relaxation. These peptides also counteract the actions of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system . Measurement of both BNP and inert NT-proBNP levels can be used in the diagnosis of heart failure and to determine the prognosis.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Falsely low values of BNP can be seen in which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Falsely low values of BNP can be seen in obese patients . It is also falsely low in: • Flash pulmonary edema • Heart failure due to- mitral regurgitation , mitral stenosis , constrictive pericarditis, restrictive cardiomyopathy It falsely increases in: • Advanced age • Renal impairment • Female patients

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a newer biomarker to assess the prognosis in a patient with heart failure?
mcqs.explanation: Soluble ST-2 is a newer biomarker that can be used for determining the prognosis of patients with heart failure. Other newer biomarkers used are galectin -3, GDF 15. Options B and D: Lipocalin, also known as neutrophil gelatinase -associated lipocalin (NGAL) or siderocalin, cystatin C, and IL -18 are biomarkers of acute kidney injury (AKI). Option C: Endothelin -1 is a useful biomarker for early detection of bronchiolitis obliterans in lung transplant recipients .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient is diagnosed with heart failure with an ejection fraction < 40%. What is the treatment of choice in this patient after the euvolemic status has been achieved ?
mcqs.explanation: ACE inhibitors + beta-blockers are the treatment of choice in patients with heart failure with an ejection fraction of <40% after euvolemic status is achieved using diuretics . The first-line drugs used in congestive heart failure with reduced ejection fraction are ACE inhibitors + diuretics . Once the euvolemic status is achieved , ACE inhibitors + beta-blockers are the drugs of choice .998 Beta-blockers that improve survival in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction are carvedilol, metoprolol , and bisoprolol .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: The preferred drug for a patient with chronic symptomatic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction is:
mcqs.explanation: Sacubitril/Valsartan , an angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI ), is used in patients with chronic symptomatic HFrEF to reduce morbidity and mortality (class I recommendation). Sacubitril (neprilysin inhibitor) is approved in combination with valsartan (ARB ), in a ratio of 1:1. The combination is approved for use in chronic heart failure. Sacubitril is a prodrug that is activated to sacubitrilat. It inhibits the enzyme neprilysin (neutral endopeptidase ), which is responsible for the degradation of atrial and brain natriuretic peptides (reduction of blood volume). Thus, it increases the levels of atrial and brain natriuretic peptides and lowers blood pressure .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is a selective myosin activator?
mcqs.explanation: Omecamtiv mecarbil is the selective myosin activator. It activates cardiac myosin and prolongs systole without increasing oxygen consumption of the heart.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs used in heart failure is an inhibitor of I(f) current in the sinoatrial node ?
mcqs.explanation: Ivabradine is an inhibitor of If current in the sinoatrial node. It reduces the heart rate without decreasing the force of contraction. It is used in patients with chronic HFrEF with a sinus rhythm and a resting heart rate \03770 bpm who are either on a maximum tolerated beta -blocker dose or have a contraindication for beta -blockers. The concurrent treatment should include ACE inhibitor ( or ARB ) and aldosterone receptor antagonist. Option A: Omapatrilat is a dual neprilysin inhibitor+ ACE inhibitor. Option C: Nesiritide belongs to the intravenous vasodilators class and is a recombinant human brain natriuretic peptide (BNP). Option D: Levosimendan belongs to the positive inotropes class and is a combined calcium sensitizer and PDE3 inhibitor.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: In a patient with heart failure, which of the following is not used as an inotropic agent ?
mcqs.explanation: Nesiritide is not used as an inotropic agent . It belongs to the intravenous vasodilator class and is a recombinant brain natriuretic peptide (BNP)999 Option A: Levosimendan belongs to the positive inotropes class and is a combined calcium sensitizer and PDE3 inhibitor. Option B: Milrinone belongs to the positive inotrope class and is a PDE-3/4 inhibitor. Option C: Omecamtiv mecarbil is a selective myosin activator that increases myocardial contractility without increasing the myocardial oxygen demand.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following beta -blockers would you prefer to use in a patient with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction?
mcqs.explanation: Bisoprolol is preferred for use in patients having heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). The only beta -blockers that have been proved to improve the survival of patients with HFrEF or chronic HF are - • Bisoprolol • Metoprolol • Carvedilol Note : Nebivolol is not approved by FDA for the treatment of heart failure.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs does not reduce mortality in a patient with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction?
mcqs.explanation: Digoxin does not reduce mortality in patients with HFrEF. The drugs which reduce mortality in patients with HFrEF are : • ACE inhibitors • Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) • Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI ) • Beta-blockers • Aldosterone antagonists • Spironolactone • Eplerenone • Hydralazine+Nitrates

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old female patient has NYHA class III heart failure with dyspnea , pedal edema and K+ levels of 5.5 mg% and creatinine 1.1 mg%. Which of the following drugs can be used in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario describes a patient with symptomatic heart failure and K+ levels of 5.5 mg%. She requires a diuretic for symptom control. Furosemide can be given safely as it causes hypokalemia.1000 Other options : Option A: Digoxin is not used as a first-line drug in the management of symptomatic heart failure. Options B and C: Spironolactone (K+ sparing diuretic ) and enalapril (ACE inhibitor) can cause hyperkalemia. The first step in managing acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) is addressing the factors that caused the decompensation . They include nonadherence to medications , dietary indiscretion, medication use that exacerbates heart failure, coronary ischemia, arrhythmias, valvular heart disease , infection , and pulmonary thromboembolism. Volume management is crucial in ADHF. Intravenous loop diuretics are used to relieve congestion . The effectiveness of diuretic therapy can be assessed by changes in weight , improvement in symptoms , and clinical examination findings. Natriuretic peptide levels can also help assess the adequacy of therapy and predict risk . Cardiorenal syndrome, characterized by the interplay between heart and kidney dysfunction , is a common complication of ADHF. Diuretic therapy should be carefully managed to avoid worsening renal function in patients with elevated right-sided filling pressures . In cases of severe low cardiac output , inotropic therapy or mechanical circulatory support may be necessary to preserve or improve renal function temporarily. Vasodilators like nitroglycerin, sodium nitroprusside , and nesiritide (recombinant BNP) are used to reduce filling pressures and systemic vascular resistance . Inotropic therapy with drugs like dopamine and milrinone is used to increase myocardial contractility and improve cardiac output in patients with low-output ADHF. Dopamine has dose -dependent effects on different receptors , while milrinone is a phosphodiesterase -3 inhibitor.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient was brought to the emergency with dyspnea , cough , and chest pain. His blood pressure was 180/100 mmHg and SpO2 was 90%. Chest X-ray is shown below . Echocardiography revealed reduced LV ejection fraction (LVEF ). Which of the following will you not use in the management of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The above X-ray showing batwing appearance along with the given symptoms and reduced LVEF is suggestive of acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema . Digoxin has no role in the management of this condition. The management of acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema consists of: • Oxygen therapy and positive pressure ventilation • Reduction of preload : • Diuretics : Furosemide is the diuretic of choice • Nitrates : sublingual nitroglycerin is the first-line therapy . If pulmonary edema persists , IV nitroglycerin is administered . • Morphine: It is a transient venodilator that reduces preload , thereby reducing dyspnea and a nxiety . • ACE inhibitors: They reduce both preload and afterload and are recommended for hypertensive patients . • Nesiritide : It is an IV recombinant BNP which is a potent vasodilator with diuretic properties .1001 • Inotropic and inodilators: • Dopamine, dobutamine -inotropic agents . • Milrinone- stimulates myocardial contractility and promotes peripheral vasodilatation. • Intra -aortic balloon counterpulsation- or LV assist devices are used in cardiogenic shock and end-organ failure.

mcqs.question: A patient presents with abrupt worsening of renal function leading to acute cardiac disorder. Which type of cardiorenal syndrome would this be?
mcqs.explanation: Type III cardiorenal syndrome is an abrupt worsening of renal function leading to acute cardiac disorder. mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Who comes under category III non-heart-beating donor?

options.a: A patient who died during transportation to the hospital
options.b: A patient who died after failed resuscitation after reaching the hospital
options.c: A patient who was brought dead to the hospital
options.d: A patient who is awaiting death in the hospital

mcqs.explanation: Category III donors are patients with non-survivable injuries who have their treatment withdrawn and if such patients wished in life to be organ donors, the transplant team can attend at the time of treatment withdrawal and retrieve organs after cardiac arrest has occurred. Modified Maastricht classification - Categories of non-heart-beating donors:1002 Category Description Circumstances Category I Includesvictims of accident a nd suicidewho arefound dead at the sceneand resuscitation is deemed pointless (e.g. fata l cervical spine fracture). mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man with a known history of DM and HTN on regular medications presents with a history of progressively worsening dyspnoea on exertion. On examination, there is elevated JVP , positive hepatojugular reflux, crackles at the lung bases , hepatomegaly , ascites , and pedal oedema \037. What is your provisional diagnosis?

Portal hypertension (Option D) can be a result of right-sided heart failure, however, the presence of worsening dyspnea along with the other symptoms implies a primary cardiac condition. Heart failure is a common endpoint for most chronic cardiac conditions such as hypertension , valvular heart disease , and coronary heart disease . mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a radiological finding in a patient with left heart failure?
mcqs.explanation: Focal oligemia is not a radiological feature of left heart failure. It is seen in pulmonary embolism and is also called Westermark 's sign.It is defined by a hyperlucent area with decreased vascularity due to oligemia of the involved part of the lung. It is caused by a cutoff of circulation due to an embolus , leading to the loss of visibility of a patch of pulmonary vasculature on an X- ray. Radiological signs of left heart failure include :1004 • Cardiomegaly - enlargement of the cardiac silhouette (increased cardiothoracic ratio) • Upper lobe pulmonary venous congestion (cephalisation of vessels ) • Interstitial edema . • Kerley B lines - horizontal lines in the periphery of the lower posterior lung fields as shown below .Other radiological signs of Pulmonary embolism : • Hampton's hump - a peripheral wedged -shaped density usually located at the pleural base • Palla's sign - an enlarged right descending pulmonary artery1005

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the defined duration for the diagnosis of acute pericarditis?
mcqs.explanation: Clinically, acute pericarditis is of <6 weeks duration. Pericarditis is the inflammation of the pericardial sac. This inflammation can lead to excessive secretion of the pericardial fluid leading to pericardial effusion . When the accumulation of fluid causes obstruction to the inflow of blood into the ventricles, it is called cardiac tamponade . Clinically, pericarditis is classified as: • Acute - < 6 weeks • Subacute - 6 weeks to 6 months • Chronic - > 6 months

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man presented with low-grade fever and severe retrosternal chest pain for 1 week. The pain got exaggerated on lying down and relieved on sitting up. On auscultation of the precordium, a grating sound was audible . Which of the given statements is false regarding this auscultatory finding?

options.c: Best heard with the patient in left lateral position
options.d: Loudest at the lower left sternal border

mcqs.explanation: 1010 In this patient , Low-grade fever, chest pain that got relieved on leaning forward, and characteristic auscultatory findings are suggestive of acute pericarditis. The grating sound heard on auscultation is a pericardial friction rub. Features of the pericardial rub: • Superficial scratchy/leathery /grating sound caused due to friction between the visceral and parietal pericardium • Best heard at end-expiration with the patient sitting and leaning forward • Very high-pitched sound best heard with the diaphragm of the stethoscope , at the lower left sternal border • Consists of three components corresponding to atrial systole , ventricular systole , and early ventricular diastole • Pathognomonic of acute pericarditis

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A young man presents to the medicine OPD with dyspnea , cough , and severe chest pain for 1 week. Chest pain is pleuritic in nature. On examination, the apical impulse is not palpable and breath sounds are normal . Which of the following is likely to be seen in the ECG of this patient ?

options.a: ST-segment elevations with a convex upward configuration
options.b: PR-segment depressions early in the disease progression
options.c: Reciprocal ST-segment depressions in all corresponding leads
options.d: T-wave inversions developing concurrently with ST-segment elevations

mcqs.explanation: The above scenario is suggestive of acute pericarditis. PR-segment depressions are seen early in acute pericarditis. The ECG changes in acute pericarditis evolve through 4 stages - • Stage 1 - Generalized ST-segment elevation with upward concavity with reciprocal depressions only in aVR and V1 and PR segment depression . • Stage 2 - The ST segments return to normal • Stage 3 - Diffuse T-wave inversion • Stage 4 - ECG returns to normal in weeks or months ECG in acute pericarditis vs acute MI: Cardiac biomarkers are grossly elevated in acute -MI, whereas in acute pericarditis the elevation if present is only mild and indicative of epi -myocarditis causing myocyte necrosis. The ECG below shows acute pericarditis causing diffuse ST-segment elevations in leads I, II , aVF, and V2 to V6, with reciprocal ST depressions in lead aVR .Acute pericarditis Acute MI Distribution of ST-segment el evations More generalized Limited to anterior or inferio r leads because of the localize d area of infarct Morphology of ST-segment e levations Concave upwards Convex upwards Reciprocal ST-segment depre ssions in the opposite leads Not present Typically present1011 Acute pericarditis Acute MI T-wave inversions Only after ST-segment return s to baseline T wave inversions can be see n even before the ST-segmen t returns to baseline PR-segment Depressed (or elevated in lea d aVR) in 75 % to 80% of pati ents Usually not depressed (can b e depressed only if concomita nt atrial infarction is present ) .
