Superantigens are protein toxins that stimulate large numbers of T cells , irrespective of antigen specificity . They bind to the class II MHC molecule outside the peptide -binding groove and V\037 region of the TCR . Some examples of superantigens are staphylococcal enterotoxins , toxic shock syndrome toxin, and group A streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxin. The below image shows the binding of superantigen to T-cell receptor .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following types of streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxins is bacteriophage mediated ?
mcqs.explanation: Streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxins type A and type C are bacteriophage -mediated toxins. The streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxin(SPE) is so named because the primary effect of the toxin is the induction of fever. It is also known as erythrogenic toxin because its intra-dermal injection into susceptible individuals produced an erythematous reaction (Dick Test). There are 3 types of streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxins namely: • type A - phage mediated . • type B - chromosome mediated . • type C - phage mediated .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a streptococcal toxin responsible for connective tissue breakdown?
mcqs.explanation: 106 Hyaluronidase is the streptococcal toxin responsible for connective tissue breakdown. Hyaluronidase or spreading factor is expressed by non-capsulated strains of Streptococcus pyogenes , such as M type 4 and 22 . It acts by cleaving hyaluronic acid, which is present in the connective tissue , epithelial , and neural tissues . This results in the spread of infection along the intercellular space .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which streptococcal antigen cross reacts with myocardium?
mcqs.explanation: Antibodies to the cell wall M antigen present on the Streptococcus cross-reacts with a similar myocardial antigen. This cross-reaction with myocardium is the cause of acute rheumatic fever.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 12 -year-old child presented with a sore throat for 3 days. Which of the following medium is used to culture the throat swab?
mcqs.explanation: Blood agar is the preferred culture media as it is used for the culture and isolation of Streptococcus pyogenes which is the most common cause of sore throat. The selective medium for Streptococcus pyogenes is Crystal violet blood agar and the transport media for this organism is Pikes medium.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms show beta -hemolysis on blood agar, resistance to bacitracin, and a positive CAMP test ?
mcqs.explanation: Streptococcus agalactiae is a group B streptococci that shows \037-hemolysis on blood agar, is resistant to bacitracin, and gives a positive CAMP test . The CAMP test is used to identify group B \037-hemolyitic -streptococci based on their ability to form CAMP factor. This factor causes synergistic hemolysis with \037-hemolysin formed by Staphylococcus aureus, when Streptococcus agalactiae is inoculated perpendicular to a streak of Staphylococcus aureus on blood agar. This produces the characteristic arrow-head zone of hemolysis . The below image shows a positive CAMP test .107 The following table provides important laboratory characteristics which differentiate Streptococcus pyogenes from Streptococcus agalactiae .Species Lancefield Gro up Typical Hemoly sis Important Lab Characteristic s S.pyogene s A \037 Bacitracin sensitive , PYR test positive S.agalactia e B \037 Bacitracin resistant, PYR test negative , Hippurate hydrolys is positive , CAMP test positiv e

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A child presents to the OPD with an infective skin lesion over his leg . On microscopic examination of the pus from the lesion, gram-positive cocci in chains are visualized and pus culture shows \037-haemolytic colonies on blood agar. Which of the following tests can be performed to identify the causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: \037 hemolytic colonies on blood agar with gram-positive cocci in chains seen on microscopy suggest the organism is a \037-hemolytic streptococcus . Bacitracin sensitivity is used to differentiate between group A and group B \037-hemolytic streptococci . Group A: Bacitracin -sensitive (S. pyogenes ) Group B: Bacitracin -resistant (S. agalactiae ) Options A & B: Bile solubility and optochin sensitivity are used to differentiate Streptococcus pneumoniae and viridans streptococci. They are both �o hemolytic on blood agar but some species of viridans streptocci are non hemolytic. Option D: Catalase test is used to differentiate streptococcus and staphylococcus . Staphylococcus appear as clusters of gram positive cocci on microscopy and not chains.108

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following bacteria is associated with the causation of colorectal carcinoma , rectal polyp , endocarditis and septicaemia and is pyrrolidinyl arylamidase test negative?
mcqs.explanation: Streptococcus gallolyticus is associated with the causation of colorectal CA, rectal polyp , endocarditis, and septicemia and is pyrrolidinyl arylamidase test (PYR test ) negative . Streptococcus gallolyticus , formerly called Streptococcus bovis, is a non-enterococcal Group D streptococci . It is bile insoluble , esculin hydrolysis positive , PYR negative and shows no growth in 6.5% NaCl.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms can survive up to 60\260C, is PYR positive , and can grow on media with 6.5% NaCl?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , Enterococcus feacalis can survive up to 60\260C, is PYR test positive , and can grow in the presence of 6.5% NaCl. Enterococci have the following features : • Formation of tiny deep pink colonies on MacConkey's medium • Survives at 600C for 30 minutes . • Growth in the presence of 40 % bile, 6.5% sodium chloride at pH 9.6. • PYR (Pyrrolidonyl Arylamidase) positive • Esculin hydrolysis is positive . • Usually nonhemolytic , but may show �o or \037 hemolysis . Option A: Streptococcus pyogenes is a delicate organism, easily destroyed by heat (54\260C for 30 min), PYR positive . Option B: Streptococcus agalactiae is PYR test negative . Option D: Streptococcus pneumoniae are readily destroyed by heat (52\260C for 15 min).

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient admitted to an ICU spiked a fever and his blood culture was positive for gram -positive cocci in chains, which are catalase -negative . He was being given ceftazidime and amikacin via a central venous line for the past week . Following this, you started him on vancomycin but his blood culture remained positive for the same organism even after 2 weeks of therapy . Which of the following is the most likely organism causing the infection ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of vancomycin -resistant enterococci (VRE ) infection . Gram-positive cocci in chains that are catalase -negative suggest that the organism belongs to Streptococcaceae family. Positive culture after 2 weeks of vancomycin therapy suggests resistance to vancomycin . Option A: Streptococcus pyogenes are sensitive to vancomycin and are not commonly implicated in central venous line infections . Option B: Viridans streptococci are usually mouth commensals and are sensitive to vancomycin . Option D: Coagulase -negative staphylococci are gram-positive cocci in clusters which are catalase -positive . Hence , they can be ruled out.109

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Oral examination of a young patient shows the following finding. Which bacteria belonging to viridans group is most commonly implicated in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The above image shows dental caries which are commonly caused by Streptococcus mutans. It belongs to the viridans group/�o -hemolytic streptococci . Streptococcus mutans breaks down the dietary sucrose producing acid and a tough adhesive dextran. The acid damages dentine while the dextrans bind together with food debris, epithelial cells , mucus, and bacteria to form dental plaques , leading to formation of dental caries.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 49-year-old man presented with high-grade fever, cough and shortness of breath. On examination , he was febrile , tachypneic and tachycardic. A chest X-ray was performed which is shown in the image. What is the single most likely causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history and the X-ray showing right lower lobe consolidation is strongly suggestive of lobar pneumonia, most commonly caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae (>95 % of cases ). Lobar pneumonia is an acute exudative inflammation of an entire pulmonary lobe . The below image shows the histopathological picture of lobar pneumonia.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old male presented with fever, chills and cough associated with chest pain. His sputum sample was sent for culture on blood agar which showed the presence of �o -hemolytic colonies the following day. Which of the following best describes the organism likely implicated here?

options.a: Gram-positive cocci in short chains, catalase negative and bile resistant
options.b: Gram-positive cocci in pairs, catalase negative and bile soluble
options.c: Gram-positive cocci in clusters , catalase positive and coagulase positive
options.d: Gram-positive cocci in clusters , catalase positive and coagulase negative

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the growth of alpha-hemolytic colonies from the sputum of the patient are strongly suggestive of pneumococcal pneumonia. Pneumococci are gram-positive cocci in pairs, catalase negative , and bile soluble . The image below shows Gram positive cocci in pairs. bile solubility , and catalase reaction.110 The image below shows positive bile solubility test shown by Streptococcus pneumoniae .The below image shows catalse test .111

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Quellung reaction is used to demonstrate _______.
mcqs.explanation: Quellung reaction is used to demonstrate the capsule of streptococci . Quellung reaction (Quellung = swelling ): • A suspension of pneumococci is mixed on a slide with a drop of type -specific antiserum and a loop full of methylene blue solution . • In the presence of homologous antiserum, the capsule becomes apparently swollen , sharply delineated and refractile . • The Quellung test can be done directly with sputum from acute pneumonia cases . The below image shows the swollen capsule of pneumococci following the addition of homologous antiserum.112

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following factors is responsible for the draughtsman appearance of pneumococcal colonies ?
mcqs.explanation: The factor responsible for the draughtsman appearance of pneumococcal colonies is autolysin . When pneumococci are incubated on blood agar for a prolonged duration, the resultant colonies are surrounded with concentric rings and have a central umbonation. This appearance of pneumococcal colonies is known as carrom coin appearance or draughtsman appearance . Autolysin is an amidase enzyme produced by pneumococci that cleaves peptidoglycan , leading to the autolysis of cells . It is also responsible for the bile solubility of pneumococci . The below image shows the characteristic draughtsman appearance of pneumococcal colonies .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: In a splenectomized patient , there is an increased risk of infection by all capsulated organisms. Which of the following is least likely to cause an infection in such patients ?
mcqs.explanation: In splenectomized patients , there is an increased risk of infection by capsulated organisms such as Streptococcus pneumoniae , Haemophilus influenzae , and Klebsiella pneumoniae . Staphylococcus aureus does not have a capsule and so poses no increased risk to these individuals. The phagocytosis of capsulated organisms is prevented by their capsule . Thus, the body's main defence against these organisms is the spleen . Certain components called opsonins attach to these capsulated organisms, and then they are delivered to the spleen , where their uptake is facilitated by receptors present on the surface of splenic phagocytes . After splenectomy , this defence mechanism is lost leaving patients susceptible to infection from these bacteria.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true about the pneumococcal vaccine?

options.a: Pneumococcal polyvalent vaccine PPSV23 is indicated in splenectomized patients .
options.b: Pneumococcal polyvalent vaccine PCV13 is contraindicated in children less than 2 years.
options.c: Pneumococcal polyvalent vaccine PPV 23 gives protection for 10 years.
options.d: Pneumococcal polyvalent vaccine is contraindicated if age > 65 years.

mcqs.explanation: 113 Pneumococcal polyvalent vaccine PPSV23 is indicated in splenectomised patients . There are two kinds of polyvalent pneumococcal vaccines: • Pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine - PPSV23 • It is indicated in splenectomized patients , sickle cell disease , immunocompromised patients , and patients above 65 years of age . • CDC currently recommends the administration of one additional dose of PPSV23 at least 5 years after the last dose . • Children younger than 2 years old should not get this vaccine since they fail to mount an adequate response . • Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine- • It includes PCV10 and PCV13 . • It is indicated in children less than 2 years.114

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A child injures his knee while playing . A few days later, the wound on his knee shows signs of inflammation. The wound is cultured and its Gram-stained smear is given below . Further testing shows that the cultured organism is coagulase -positive . Identify the organism.
mcqs.explanation: An infected wound culture showing Gram-positive cocci arranged in clusters which are coagulase -positive suggest that the cultured organism is Staphylococcus aureus.120 Staphylococci are Gram-positive cocci that are catalase -positive . They grow in clusters because the cells divide successively in three perpendicular planes , with the daughter cells remaining attached to one another following each successive division. Among the 45 different species of Staphylococcus , Staphylococcus aureus is the only one which is coagulase positive . Other options : Option A: Streptococci are catalase negative . They are Gram-positive cocci arranged in chains. Options C & D: S. epidermidis and S. saprophyticus are both coagulase negative .Different bacteria with their typical arrangements are given below : • Staphylococcus : Clusters • Streptococcus : Chains • Pneumococcus : Pairs/lanceolate shaped • Micrococcus : Tetrads

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The specimen obtained by performing incision and drainage of a breast abscess was sent for culture on nutrient agar. An image of the culture plate is given below . Microscopy of the isolated organism revealed gram-positive cocci arranged in clusters . Which of the following is a false statement regarding this organism?

options.b: Golden yellow pigmentation is due to \037-carotene
options.c: Pigment production is enhanced by adding milk to culture media
options.d: Confluent growth presents a characteristic 'oil-paint appearance '

mcqs.explanation: Gram-positive cocci arranged in clusters that produce golden -yellow pigment on nutrient agar is suggestive of Staphylococcus aureus. The pigment production occurs optimally at 22 \260C. Staphylococcus aureus is a Gram-positive coccus . On nutrient agar, its colonies are large (2-4 mm in diameter ), convex, smooth, shiny, opaque and easily emulsifiable . The colonies appear golden yellow due to the presence of staphyloxanthin (carotenoid). Pigment production occurs optimally at 22 \260C and in aerobic conditions. It is enhanced when 1% glycerol or milk is incorporated in the medium. On a nutrient agar slope , there is confluent growth of Staphylococcus , which appears as a characteristic oil-paint appearance .121

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which factor forms the basis of co-agglutination reaction shown by Staphylococcus aureus?
mcqs.explanation: Protein A forms the basis of the co-agglutination reaction shown by Staphylococcus aureus. Protein A bearing staphylococci are coated with IgG antiserum. Protein A binds to the Fc terminal of IgG, leaving the Fab terminal free to combine with its specific antigen. The corresponding antigen is then added to this mixture which causes agglutination of the bacteria. This is known as the co-agglutination reaction. It is used for streptococcal , gonococcal or hemophilus typing .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following toxins exhibits hot-cold phenomenon ?
mcqs.explanation: \037-hemolysin exhibits a hot-cold phenomenon. \037-hemolysin is a sphingomyelinase that is hemolytic only for sheep cells but not human cells . It initiates hemolysis at 370C but the hemolysis is evident only after chilling. This is called the hot-cold phenomenon .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of toxins produced by Staphylococcus aureus are called synergohymenotropic toxins?
mcqs.explanation: \035-toxin and Panton-Valentine-toxin (leucocidin ) of Staphylococcus aureus are called synergohymenotropic toxins. Synergohymenotropic (synergo - working together , hymenotropic - form pores ) toxins are a family of bicomponent toxins that act through the synergistic activity of 2 non-associated secretory proteins - class F and class S proteins . Gamma hemolysin has two components necessary for its hemolytic action. It is encoded by three genes HlgA and HlgC (belonging to class S) and HlgB (belonging to class F), resulting in 2 pairs of class S and F components - HlgA and HlgB, or HlgC and HlgB.122 Panton-Valentine Leucocidin is composed of two components - S and F - encoded by two contiguous and cotranscribed genes , lukS-PV and lukF-PV . It is associated with the majority of community-associated methicillin -resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA).

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following staphylococcal infections is not toxin mediated ?
mcqs.explanation: Staphylococcal septicemia is not toxin mediated . Septicemia occurs due to the invasion of bacterial organisms into the bloodstream . This causes an inflammatory response to bacterial products , leading to various manifestations seen in sepsis - fever, hypotension, alkalosis. Toxin mediated staphylococcal infections include food poisoning caused by enterotoxin, toxic shock syndrome caused by toxic shock syndrome toxin and staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome caused by exfoliative /epidermolytic toxin.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A college student with a history of intravenous drug abuse presents with a fever for the last 3 weeks . Echocardiography is performed which reveals large friable vegetations on the cusps of the tricuspid valve. Which of the following organisms is the most common cause for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Fever with vegetations on the tricuspid valve points to a diagnosis of right-sided infective endocarditis. Staphylococcus aureus is the most common cause of right-sided infective endocarditis among intravenous drug abusers. Infective endocarditis is the microbial infection of heart valves or endocardium, leading to the formation of vegetations (thrombotic debris and microbial organisms).The following image shows a graphical illustration of vegetations seen in infective endocarditis .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: By which of the following mechanisms is penicillin resistance commonly transferred to Staphylococcus aureus?
mcqs.explanation: 123 Penicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus is determined by plasmids that are most commonly transferred by transduction. Penicillin resistance in Staphylococci most commonly occurs due to bacterial production of beta -lactamase, which inactivates penicillins by splitting their beta -lactam ring. These enzymes are inducible and are plasmid-mediated . They confer resistance to penicillin G, ampicillin, piperacillin etc . The genetic transfer of antibiotic resistance can occur in the following ways: • Transformation : After death or cell lysis , some bacteria release their DNA into the environment. Other bacteria , generally of the same species , can come into contact with these free DNA fragments, take them up and incorporate them into their DNA by recombination. • Transduction: This method involves the transfer of DNA, episome or plasmid from one bacterium to another with the use of a bacteriophage . • Conjugation: This mechanism requires the presence of a special plasmid called the F plasmid that codes for the sex pilus . It is the most common method of transfer of antibiotic resistance in most other bacteria. Note : Change in penicillin binding proteins (PBPs) and production of \037-lactamases are modes of penicillin resistance seen in S. aureus but the question asks for methods of transfer of drug resistance .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Contact based isolation is employed for which of the following diseases ?
mcqs.explanation: Contact based isolation is employed for patients who are infected with MRSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus). The three categories of transmission-based precautions include : • Contact-based isolation is used for infections , diseases , or germs that are spread by touching the patient or items in the room. Examples include MRSA, vancomycin -resistant enterococci (VRE ), diarrheal illnesses , open wounds , and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV ). • Droplet -based isolation is employed for diphtheria and mumps. • Airborne precautions are required to protect against conditions like measles , severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), varicella (chickenpox), and Mycobacterium tuberculosis .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An outbreak of methicillin -resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection was reported in the surgical ward of a hospital . Which of the following precautionary measures would you recommend to best curb its spread ?

options.a: Administration of vancomycin empirically to all the patients
options.c: Wearing masks before performing invasive procedures
options.d: Washing of hands before & after treating the patients

mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , washing hands before and after treating the patients is the most effective way to curb the spread of methicillin -resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infections . In addition to this, personnel with active S. aureus lesions and carriers should be excluded from areas havin g patients at highest risk for severe staphylococcal infections like newborn nurseries, intensive care units, operating rooms, and cancer chemotherapy wards. In such individuals, the application of topical antiseptics such as mupirocin to nasal or perineal carriage sites may diminish the shedding of MRSA.124

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old man presented with multiple tender , erythematous fluctuant skin lesions as shown in the image. You suspect it to be a case of botryomycosis . Which of the following is the most likely organism implicated in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of botryomycosis is Staphylococcus aureus. Botryomycosis is a rare chronic bacterial granulomatous disease that usually involves the skin and rarely viscera. It is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus but can also be caused by Pseudomonas , Escherichia coli, Proteus, and Streptococci . Patients present with chronic, suppurative , granulomatous skin lesions like nodules , abscesses and sinuses . Actinomycetoma , eumycetoma and botryomycosis are difficult to distinguish clinically but are readily distinguished with microbiologic testing or biopsy . Granules of botryomycosis consist of loose masses of cocci. Organisms can also be seen in wound discharge or histologic specimens .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 14-year-old boy presents with a history of vomiting within 3 hours of consumption of food at a party. Which of the following organism is most likely to cause these symptoms ?
mcqs.explanation: Vomiting 2 hours after the consumption of food is likely food poisoning by Staphylococcus aureus . Staphylococcus aureus can grow in carbohydrate and protein food sources , producing enterotoxins. There are 15 types , all of which are superantigens . They are preformed toxins that are relatively heat stable . They stimulate the vagus nerve, vomiting centre of the brain and intestinal peristaltic activity. Type A enterotoxin is responsible for most cases of food poisoning. The common sources of infection are the foods that are not cooked after handling. These include sliced meats, puddings , pastries , and sandwiches . Ingestion of such contaminated food causes food poisoning within 30 minutes to 6 hours after consumption. Patients present with nausea, vomiting, stomach cramps, and diarrhoea.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An 18-year-old girl presented with burning micturition and fever with chills for three days. Urine culture grew bacteria which were coagulase -negative and novobiocin -resistant. Which of the following is the most likely organism implicated here?
mcqs.explanation: Burning micturition and fever with chills in a young woman points to a diagnosis of urinary tract infection (UTI). The most likely organism implicated here is Staphylococcus saprophyticus as it is coagulase -negative and novobiocin-resistant. Staphylococcus saprophyticus is a part of the normal flora of human skin and periurethral area and thus is a common cause of urinary tract infection (UTI) in young women.125 Option A: Staphylococcus aureus is a coagulase -positive bacterium. It is an uncommon cause of UTI . Options B and C: Staphylococcus hominis and Staphylococcus epidermidis are coagulase -negative and novobiocin-sensitive. They are usually considered contaminants if found on urine culture but they may also cause UTIs in children with underlying urinary tract abnormalities.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Choose the incorrect statement regarding Micrococci.

options.c: It is rarely associated with disease .

mcqs.explanation: Micrococci are arranged in pairs, tetrads or clusters of eight . Micrococci are Gram-positive cocci that are often mistaken for S. aureus. However, they are larger in size and mostly occur in pairs, tetrads or clusters of eight . They form smaller colonies in culture in comparison to S. aureus. Hugh-Leifson oxidation-fermentation test can be used to differentiate between micrococci (oxidative pattern) and staphylococci (fermentative pattern). Micrococci are catalase -positive and modified oxidase -positive . They are ordinarily non-pathogenic but can rarely cause infections in an immunocompromised host. They are part of normal bacterial flora in the body. The following image shows the tetrad arrangement of micrococci:126 Different bacteria with their typical arrangements are given below : 1. Staphylococcus : Clusters 2. Streptococcus : Chains 3. Pneumococcus : Pairs/lanceolate shaped 4. Micrococcus : Tetrads127

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A father brought his 9-year-old unimmunized child to the pediatric OPD with complaints of fever , sore throat and difficulty in swallowing . The findings of oropharyngeal examination are shown in the image below . Which of the following is the most likely causative organism of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Fever, sore throat and difficulty in swallowing with the presence of a dirty white pseudomembrane on the posterior pharynx is strongly suggestive of diphtheria caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae . They are described as club-shaped gram positive bacilli. Corynebacterium diphtheriae are gram-positive, non-sporing, non-capsulated and non-motile bacilli. They possess polymetaphosphate granules that serve as storage granules and are called metachromatic granules. These give the bacilli a beaded or club-shaped appearance on microscopic examination.136 Other options : Option A: Gram-negative diplococci describes Neisseria menigitidis and N. gonorrhoeae. Option C: Spiral gram-negative bacteria describes Campylobacter spp . and Helicobacter spp .. Option D: Gram-positive cocci in chains describes Streptococci . They typically cause acute exudative pharyngitis characterised by purulent exudate over the tonsils.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient has complains of fever with chills. A throat examination reveals swollen glands and a thick, whitish membrane over his tonsils. Albert staining is to be done. What are the constituents of Albert's stain?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of diphtheria caused by Corynebacterium diphtheria . This organism is stained using Albert's stain which contains toluidine blue 'O' and malachite green . Both these dyes have an affinity for acidic cytoplasm as they are basic dyes . Albert's, Neisser 's, and Ponder's stain are used to demonstrate the metachromatic granules(Volutin / Babes Ernst granules) of Corynebacterium diphtheria . Corynebacterium diphtheria appears as green -coloured bacilli with purple -blue -coloured metachromatic granules in cuneiform arrangement.137

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a selective medium for Corynebacterium diptheriae ?
mcqs.explanation: Loeffler 's serum slope is an enriched medium for the growth of Corynebacterium diphtheriae . It is not a selective medium as other organisms can also grow on this medium. The selective media for Corynebacterium diphtheria are potassium tellurite agar, Tinsdale medium and McLeod's medium (tellurite blood agar). Tellurite inhibits the growth of other bacteria. C. diphtheria reduces the tellurite to metallic tellurium , giving its colonies a grey black colour. On On Loeffler 's serum slope , colonies appear as small white opaque discs that may acquire a yellow ting. The advantages for growing C. diphtheriae on Loeffler 's serum slope are rapid growth in 6-8 hrs and that its the best medium for metachromatic granules production . The disadvantage of using this medium is that on incubation beyond 6-8 hrs, it supports the growth of commensals as well .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A throat swab taken from a patient who presented with fever, dysphagia and cervical lymphadenopathy was sent for culture on potassium tellurite agar. The resultant colonies had a poached egg appearance . Which among the following is the most likely organism implicated here?
mcqs.explanation: Poached egg colonies on potassium tellurite agar indicate Corynebacterium diphtheriae mitis. Macleod classified diphtheria bacilli based on colony morphology on tellurite blood agar into the following three types : • Gravis : They form daisy head colonies and are variably hemolytic . They ferment glycogen and starch. • Intermedius: They form frog's egg colonies and are non-hemolytic . They do not ferment glycogen and starch. • Mitis: They form poached egg colonies and are hemolytic . They do not ferment glycogen and starch.138 The following image shows the various colony morphologies of C. diphtheriae .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The toxin produced by the organisms shown below acts via ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows gram-positive rods with club-shaped ends , beaded appearance , and a Chinese -letter pattern of arrangement indicative of Corynebacterium diphtheriae . The toxin produced by the bacteria - diphtheria toxin - inhibits polypeptide chain elongation and protein synthesis by inactivating the elongation factor-2 (EF-2) by ADP ribosylation. It has two fragments - fragment B helps in binding of the toxin to host cells and fragment A inactivates EF-2.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following bacteria gain toxigenicity by lysogenic conversion?
mcqs.explanation: 139 Lysogenic or phage conversion is seen in Corynebacterium diphtheriae . The toxigenicity of diphtheria bacillus depends on the presence of the corynephages (tox+). When the bacillus is cured of the phage , its toxigenic capacity is lost. A bacteriophage is a virus that parasitises bacteria. It can carry host DNA and transfer it to another bacterium. In lysogenic conversion, the viral DNA is integrated with the bacterial DNA and thus can code for new characteristics, like toxin production . The conversion of non-toxigenic bacterial strains to toxigenic by infecting them with bacteriophages is known as lysogenic conversion.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following factors does not affect the toxin production of Corynebacterium diphtheria?

options.a: Concentration of iron in the medium
options.d: Concentration of zinc in the medium

mcqs.explanation: Toxin production of Corynebacterium diphtheriae depends on the concentration of iron in the medium , presence of tox phage , and its biotype . Concentration of zinc in the medium has no effect on this process . An increase in iron concentration (option A) upregulates the DT (diphtheria toxin) repressor gene , thereby decreasing the toxin production. The optimum level of iron in the medium for toxin production is 0.14 �Mg/millilitre, while a concentration of 0.5 �Mg/millilitre inhibits the formation of toxins. The gene for diphtheria toxin is coded by bacteriophage (corynebacteriophage tox+) and thus the presence of phages (option B) is integral to toxin production . Toxin production also depends on the biotype (option C) - gravis, intermedius , mitis and belfanti - of the bacilli. All four biotypes are toxigenic . Diphtheria toxin is also produced by Corynebacterium ulcerans and Corynebacterium pseudotuberculosis .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: What is Elek's gel precipitation test used to test ?
mcqs.explanation: 140 Elek's test is used to test the toxigenicity of Corynebacterium diphtheriae . Elek's gel precipitation test is an in vitro immunoprecipitation (immunodiffusion) test used to determine whether or not a strain of Corynebacterium diphtheriae is toxigenic . In this test , a rectangular strip of filter paper impregnated with diphtheria antitoxin is placed on the surface of a % normal horse serum agar. Narrow streaks of the C. diphtheriae strains are made at right angles to the filter paper strip with positive and negative controls. If the strain produces toxins, the toxin will diffuse in the agar and produce a line of precipitation (arrowhead) where it meets the antitoxin at optimum concentration. The test is shown in the image below .Option A: For checking susceptibility to diphtheria , Schick test is used . Option B: The biotype of diphtheria can be determined based on colony morphology and biochemical reactions. Option D: The antibody titer against diphtheria can be measured by various serological methods like passive haemagglutination , latex agglutination test , toxoid enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (Toxoid-ELISA), and toxin-binding inhibition ELISA (ToBI -ELISA ).

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: What diphtheria antibody titer is considered optimally protective ?
mcqs.explanation: Diphtheria antibody titer is considered optimally protective if the titre is >0.1 IU/mL . Diphtheria is primarily the result of the action of diphtheria toxin, not bacterial invasion . Hence , antibodies to the diphtheria toxin is a good measure of protection against diphtheria . These antibodies can be induced by immunisation with diphtheria toxoid vaccine. The titers of IgG antibody against diphtheria toxoid vaccine reflect various levels of protection against the disease as follows : • <0.01 IU/mL : No protection • 0.01 -0.1 IU/mL : Minimal protection141 • >0.1 IU/mL : Optimal protection Note : The question asks optimally protective titer and not minimum effective titer which is >0.01 IU/mL .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old boy presented with fever, sore throat, dysphagia , and a tonsillar pseudomembrane . Which of the following complications will you not anticipate in him?
mcqs.explanation: A child with fever, sore throat, dysphagia , and a tonsillar pseudomembrane likely has diphthteria . Pupillary reactions remain normal and pupillary paralysis is not a complication seen with diphtheria . The complications of diphtheria include asphyxia due to the mechanical airway obstruction by the pseudomembrane . Myocarditis and polyneuropathy are toxic complications of diphtheria . Patients may develop post diphtheritic paralysis involving palatine and ciliary nerves. Paralysis of the diaphragm and neurogenic bladder dysfunction may also occur. Acute circulatory failure, septic complications , such as pneumonia and otitis media and renal failure may also occur.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following features is not typically seen in diphtheroids ?

options.a: They possess few or no metachromatic granules
options.b: They are usually arranged in parallel rows
options.c: Most of them do not produce toxins

mcqs.explanation: Diphtheroids ferment both sucrose and glucose , whereas Corynebacterium diphtheriae ferments only glucose. Sucrose fermentation is done to differentiate between C. diphtheriae and diphtheroids . Diphtheroids : • They are corynebacteria resembling C. diphtheriae which occur as normal commensals in the throat, skin, conjunctiva and other areas. • In general , diphtheroids stain more uniformly than diphtheria bacilli and possess few or no metachromatic granules. • Most of them do not produce toxins. • They tend to be arranged in parallel rows (palisades ) rather than the cuneiform pattern. • The common diphtheroids include Corynebacterium xerosis.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old fisherman presents with pain and a lesion in his hand similar to what is shown in the image. What is the causative organism for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The above image shows a raised, well -circumscribed, violaceous lesion with the absence of pus . Thus, it is erysipeloid which is a skin infection caused by Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae . Erysipeloid usually occurs on the fingers by direct inoculation at the site of a cut or abrasion, in people who handle animals, fish or animal products . Pain, swelling and erythema develop and the condition has been called seal finger and whale finger. Pus is usually absent at the infection site , which helps differentiate it from staphylococcal and streptococcal skin infections . It resolves without treatment in 3-4 weeks .142 Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae is a slender , non-motile, non-sporing Gram positive bacillus . It is catalase , oxidase , and indole negative . It causes disease in multiple land animals like swine , turkeys and sheep . Note : Erysipelas is caused by Streptococcus pyogenes . It presents as erythematous raised lesions with sharply demarcated edges .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 1-day-old newborn developed severe sepsis and died after 1 day despite aggressive treatment. On examination, multiple granulomas are present over the skin. The organism isolated from the blood sample shows the motility depicted below . What is the most likely causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: Early onset sepsis with skin granulomas and organisms showing tumbling motility points to a diagnosis of granulomatosis infantiseptica caused by Listeria monocytogenes . Listeria monocytogenes shows slow tumbling motility when grown at 25 \260C. But at 37\260C, it is non-motile because the peritrichous flagella are produced by the bacillus optimally between \260C and 30\260C. This is known as differential motility as motility pattern changes with a change in temperature . Listeria moves from cell-to-cell using host cell actin framework. Listeria infection can manifest as febrile gastroenteritis , bacteremia, neurolisteriosis and granulomatosis infantiseptica .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man presents to the OPD with complaints of fever with chills, headache , abdominal pain, and diarrhoea. He gives a history of consuming raw refrigerated cucumbers the previous day. What is the most likely etiologic organism?
mcqs.explanation: Fever, headache, abdominal pain, diarrhoea following consumption of refridgerated food is suggestive of food poisoning caused by Listeria monocytogenes . Listeria monocytogenes can survive at refrigerator temperatures (4\260C), under conditions of low pH and high salt. So it is able to overcome food preservation and safety barriers , making it an important foodborne pathogen . Healthy persons exposed to L. monocytogenes in food may develop a mild, self -limiting febrile gastroenteritis lasting 1–3 days. This develops after an incubation period of 6–48 hours. Symptoms include fever, chills, headache , myalgias, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. Immunocompromised individuals can develop meningoencephalitis , bacteremia, or focal infections . The drug of choice is high dose intravenous ampicillin.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Multiple abscesses with discharging sinuses , demonstrating sulphur granules in pus , are caused by
mcqs.explanation: Multiple abscesses with discharging sinuses , demonstrating sulfur granules in pus , are characteristic of actinomycosis caused by Actinomyces . Actinomycosis is a chronic granulomatous infection characterized by indurated swellings in the connective tissue with suppuration and discharge of sulfur granules. The most common causative agent is Actinomyces israelli.143 Various clinical forms of actinomycosis include cervicofacial, thoracic, abdominal, and pelvic actinomycosis . Among them, oral-cervicofacial actinomycosis is most common, presenting as a soft tissue swelling , abscess , or mass lesion involving the angle of the jaw.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a false statement regarding Nocardia?
mcqs.explanation: Nocardia are free -living organisms and not commensals. Nocardia are aerobic Gram-positive filamentous bacilli. They are non-sporing. They are considered weakly acid-fast, determined by Kinyoun's acid-fast staining technique . They produce urease and are catalase positive . They are found in the soil. Nocardia asteroides is the Nocardia species which is most commonly involved in human disease (cutaneous and systemic ). The paraffin bait technique is used for the isolation of Nocardia.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Identify the organism from the given image.
mcqs.explanation: The organism shown in the image is Nocardia asteroides . Nocardia species are weakly acid-fast filamentous organisms with hyphae -like branching on microscopy . They are aerobic, gram-positive, catalase -positive , and urease -positive . They are weakly acid-fast because they stain with carbolfuchsin and retain when decolourized with 1–4% sulfuric acid instead of the stronger acid-alcohol decolorant . Infection follows traumatic inoculation of the organism into the subcutaneous tissue from soil or vegetable sources . They can present with a characteristic powdery substance that appears as gritty or necrotic material on the skin or within soft tissues . Accompanying this are multiple discharging sinuses , which are abnormal openings that form as the body attempts to expel infected material. These sinuses can drain purulent , often foul -smelling discharge typically associated with localised abscesses , and the discharge may be viscous, sometimes containing necrotic tissue . Other options : Options A and B: Mycobacteria species are acid-fast but not have branching filaments . Option C: Actinomyces species are not acid-fast. They are Gram-positive arranged in a sun-ray appearance .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient presents with a mobile, warm to touch nodule in the neck. On the anaerobic culture of the biopsy material from this swelling, it showed colonies as shown in the image which had gram-positive branching rods on staining. Which of the following is the drug of choice in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows molar tooth colonies that are characteristic of Actinomyces species . The given clinical scenario of a mobile, warm to touch nodule in the neck describes cervicofacial actinomycosis also known as 'lumpy jaw syndrome'. Penicillin is the drug of choice for actinomyces infection . Actinomyces are Gram- positive anaerobic bacilli that produce molar tooth colonies on incubation for 72 hours on brain -heart infusion agar. They cause a chronic suppurative and granulomatous infection called actinomycosis. It can present as one of the following clinical types :144 • Cervicofacial type - Fluctuant mass in the jaw area producing draining fistulas . • Thoracic type - Pulmonary infection with fever, cough , and purulent sputum . • Abdominal type - Occurs following ruptured appendix or ulcer. It may spread throughout the peritoneum and involve multiple organs. Actinomycosis can spread to bones and surrounding tissue and produce multiple discharging sinuses . Treatment requires prolonged administration of penicillin for 6–12 months. In penicillin -allergic patients , clindamycin or erythromycin is effective . Surgical excision and drainage may be required in some cases . The given image shows cervicofacial actinomycosis .The given image shows a patient with multiple cutaneous lesions caused by Actinomyces :145

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following toxins act by inhibiting elongation factor -2?
mcqs.explanation: Both diphtheria toxin and pseudomonas exotoxin act by inhibiting elongation factor-2(EF-2).

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The most common clinical form of actinomycosis is
mcqs.explanation: The most common clinical form of actinomycosis is cervicofacial. Actinomycosis is a chronic granulomatous infection characterized by indurated swellings , mainly in the connective tissue , suppuration , and discharge of sulphur granules. The most common causative agent is Actinomycetes israelli. Various clinical forms of actinomycosis involves cervicofacial, thoracic, abdominal, and pelvic actinomycosis . Among them, actinomycosis most frequently occurs as oral-cervicofacial form presenting as a soft tissue swelling , abscess , or mass lesion involving the angle of jaw.146

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms is capsulated ?
mcqs.explanation: Clostridium perfringens is the capsulated organism among the given options. Most of the clostridial species are non-capsulated except C.perfringens and C.butyricum. All clostridia are motile , with a peritrichate flagella , with the exception of: • C. perfringens • C. tetani type VI .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A young man presented with complaints of severe abdominal pain and watery diarrhoea eight hours after consuming meat at a restaurant. A stool sample was sent for culture and the isolated organism showed this appearance on litmus milk fermentation. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: 154 The given clinical history and the image showing stormy fermentation of lactose in litmus milk is suggestive of gastroenteritis caused by Clostridium perfingens type A. The fermentation of lactose by this organism leads to the formation of acid which coagulates the casein in litmus milk. The clotted milk is disrupted due to vigorous gas production and this characteristic finding is obtained that is called stormy fermentation.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions are positive for Clostridium perfringens ?
mcqs.explanation: Target hemolysis and reverse CAMP test are positive for Clostridium perfringens . A narrow zone of complete hemolysis due to \027-toxin and a wider zone of incomplete hemolysis due to �o -toxin results in development of target hemolysis on blood agar by C. perfringens . In the reverse CAMP test , C.perfringens is streaked over the centre of the plate and Streptococcus agalactiae is streaked at right angles to it. A positive reverse CAMP test shows the presence of an arrow-shaped zone of enhanced hemolysis pointing towards C.perfringens . �o -toxin produced by C.perfringens interacts with the CAMP factor and produce synergistic hemolysis . M'fadyean reaction is positive Bacillus anthracis. The CAMP test is positive for Streptococcus agalactiae where it is inoculated on a plate streaked with Staphylococcus aureus. Elek's test is positive for Corynebacterium diptheriae .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged diabetic man presented to the ER with severe abdominal pain, diarrhea and vomiting following consumption of pork and sweet potato curry. Following admission, the patient developed intra-abdominal sepsis and was taken into emergency surgery. Histopathology of the resected intestine showed mucosal necrosis. Which of the following toxins is likely implicated in his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The condition described here is necrotising enteritis (pigbel ) that is caused by \037-toxin of Clostridium perfringens type -C. This is a severe and often fatal enteritis caused by C.perfringens type C strains with heat -resistant spores that germinate in the intestine producing beta toxin, causing mucosal necrosis. The evocative name 'pigbel ' is New Guinea pidgin for abdominal pain and diarrhea following unaccustomed feasting on pig meat along with trypsin inhibitors like sweet potatoes . Immunisation with the type C toxoid has been shown to protect against this condition.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the toxins produced by clostridium species is the basis of Nagler's reaction?
mcqs.explanation: �o -toxin produced by Clostridium perfringens forms the basis of Nagler's reaction. The �o -toxin of C.perfringens has lecithinase activity. When C.perfringens is grown on a media containing egg yolk with the �o -antitoxin spread on one half of the plate , colonies on the other half without the antitoxin will be surrounded by a zone of opacity . There will be no opacity around the colonies on the half of the plate with the antitoxin due to the specific neutralization of �o - toxin. This is known as Nagler's reaction.155

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient presents with a laceration over his leg following trauma with an unclean sharp metal rod 3 days ago. He also complains of difficulty in opening his mouth and abdominal cramps. Microscopy of the wound discharge revealed rod-shaped bacilli with terminal spherical spores . Which of the following is the organism most likely implicated here?
mcqs.explanation: The above clinical vignette is strongly suggestive of tetanus caused by Clostridium tetani. It is a gram -positive, slender bacillus that has a spherical and terminal spore, giving it a characteristic drumstick appearance . The genus clostridium consists of gram-positive, anaerobic, spore-forming bacilli. Classification of Clostridium based on shape and position of spores : • Central or equatorial: Clostridium bifermentans • Subterminal: Clostridium perfringens, Clostridium novyi, and Clostridium botulinum • Oval and terminal (tennis racket shaped ): Clostridium tertium and Clostridium difficile • Spherical and terminal (drumstick appearance ): Clostridium tetani The below image shows the characteristic drumstick appearance of C. tetani.156

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the first sign of generalized tetanus ?
mcqs.explanation: The first sign of generalized tetanus is increased tone of the masseter muscle , which results in trismus or lock-jaw. Tetanus: • Route of entry of organism- injury, unhygienic surgery, abortion/delivery, otitis media • The incubation period is 6-10 days. • First clinical sign- increased masseter tone (trismus/lock-jaw) followed by descending tetanus • Deep tendon reflex is exaggerated . • In neonates , difficulty in feeding is the usual presentation . • Diagnosis is always clinical, microscopy is unreliable . • Treatment includes cleaning the entry wound first in order to remove anaerobic foci of infection and prevent further toxin production . Metronidazole is preferred for antibiotic therapy . Antitoxin should be given early in an attempt to deactivate any circulating tetanus toxin. Spasms are controlled by heavy sedation with benzodiazepines . Symptomatic treatment is given for respiratory and cardiovascular derangements .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Strychnine toxin acts by blocking the action of glycine at the post -synaptic receptors in the motor neurons of the anterior horn of the spinal cord. Which of the following has a similar mechanism of action but acts presynaptically ?
mcqs.explanation: Tetanus toxin has similar mechanisms of action as strychnine but acts pre-synaptically . Strychnine prevents the uptake of glycine at inhibitory synapses post -synaptically , while tetanospasmin blocks release of inhibitory neurotransmitters like glycine and gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) pre-synaptically . This leads to increased release of acetylcholine , thereby leading to the development of spastic paralysis.157 The image below depicts the mechanism of action of tetanus toxin.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An 18-year-old girl presents with a contaminated wound sustained 4 hours ago. She had received complete immunization against tetanus 7 years ago. Which of the following injections should be given to her?

options.d: Human tetanus immunoglobulin and single dose of toxoid

mcqs.explanation: As she has received complete immunization against tetanus 7 years back, she should be given a single dose of tetanus toxoid for her contaminated wound .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An elderly diabetic man presented to the ER with a contaminated wound with necrotic material. As a first-year surgical resident, which of the following would be your first step in treating the conditon?
mcqs.explanation: Initial treatment for contaminated wounds with necrotic material is debridement . A contaminated wound with necrotic material is suggestive of a higher risk of clostridial infection that may lead to gas gangrene . Emergent surgical exploration and thorough debridement are extremely important in the management of gas gangrene . Antibiotics (penicillin G plus clindamycin) and anti-gas gangrene serum have to be initiated after debridement . Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may also be considered .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An 18-year-old man presented with sudden onset descending paralysis and blurred vision 3 days after the intake of canned food. On examination, the patient has quadriparesis with areflexia. Both the pupils are nonreactive. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette of acute onset descending flaccid paralysis with a history of consumption of canned food is suggestive of botulism . The incubation period from ingestion of contaminated food to the onset of symptoms in food-borne botulism is usually 8–36 h but can be as long as 10 days and is dose -dependent . The clinical syndrome of botulism consists of bilateral cranial-nerve palsies that may progress to respiratory compromise, a bilateral descending flaccid paralysis of voluntary muscles , and even death .158 Cranial nerve deficits may manifest as some of the following : • diplopia • dysarthria • dysphonia • ptosis • ophthalmoplegia • facial paralysis and impaired gag reflex The absence of cranial nerve palsies makes botulism highly unlikely, as does a lack of cranial nerve deficits at the onset of illness . Pupillary reflexes may be depressed and fixed or dilated pupils are sometimes noted . The cornerstones of treatment for botulism are meticulous intensive care and administration of botulinum antitoxin. Option A: In poliomyelitis , weakness is generally asymmetric, more proximal than distal , and may involve the legs (most commonly), the arms, or the abdominal, thoracic, or bulbar muscles . Option C: Guillain–Barre syndrome is usually associated with ascending flaccid paralysis. Option D: Tetanus causes spastic paralysis.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms is predominantly proteolytic in Robertson cooked meat medium ?
mcqs.explanation: Clostridium botulinum A is predominantly proteolytic in Robertson cooked meat medium. In Robertson cooked meat media, the saccharolytic species like C.perfringens , C.difficile , and C.septicum turn the meat pink, while the proteolytic species such as C.botulinum A turn the meat black. Examples of predominantly proteolytic clostridia: • C.bifermentans • C.botulinum A, B, F • C.histolyticum C. tetani is slightly proteolytic but not saccharolytic. Examples of predominantly saccharolytic clostridia: • C.perfringens • C.septicum • C.novyi • C.difficile C.botulinum C, D and E are saccharolytic but not proteolytic .159

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms form the citron bodies ?
mcqs.explanation: Citron bodies are boat or leaf -shaped pleomorphic bacteria, usually associated with Clostridium septicum . It is a gram-positive, spore -forming, obligate anaerobic bacterium. Gram stain morphology of Clostridium septicum from CSF (a) and blood culture (b) in 1000 \327 magnification with spore formation(arrow) is shown below .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An elderly diabetic lady was brought to the hospital with complaints of diarrhoea and abdominal pain. She had recently been treated with intravenous clindamycin for cellulitis . She was febrile at the time of examination and the blood reports revealed a Hb level of 12g/dl; WBC count of 18000 /mm3 ; and C-reactive protein 160mg/l. What is the most sensitive test to detect the causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette of a patient having diarrhea following antibiotic administration is suggestive of pseudomembranous colitis due to Clostridium difficile . Toxigenic culture is the most sensitive method for the detection of Clostridium difficle infection . The methods for diagnosis of Clostridium difficle infection are: • Toxigenic culture - Anaerobic incubation of the sample in cycloserine -cefoxitin -fructose agar (CCFA) or its variant for several days. This is followed by identification of the organism in the growth and tests to confirm toxin production . This method has a sensitivity of 100 %. • Cell cytotoxicity neutralization assay (CCNA)- A stool filtrate is prepared and applied onto a monolayer of an appropriate cell line. The cells are observed for toxin-induced cytopathic effect (CPE). This is followed by a neutralization assay to confirm that the CPE is attributable to C.difficile toxins. Sensitivity is around 75 -85% when compared to toxigenic culture (reference standard) • Nucleic acid amplification tests (e.g.PCR)- More sensitive (93.3%) for C.difficile detection than toxin immunoassays but less sensitive than toxigenic culture . • Toxin immunoassays- Enzyme immunoassays using monoclonal or polyclonal antibodies against C.difficile toxins. Sensitivity is lower than other tests .160 • Glutamate dehydrogenase immunoassays- Detects glutamate dehydrogenase , a metabolic enzyme produced by all isolates of C.difficile (toxigenic and nontoxigenic). The test is highly sensitive but has low specificity .Test Substance detected Sensitivit y Specificity Toxigenic culture C.difficilevegetative cells or s pores High Low* Nucleic acid amplification tes ts C.difficilenucleic acid for toxi n genes High Low/mode rate Glutamate dehydrogenase C.difficilecommon antigen High Low* CCNA Free toxins High High Toxin A and B immunoassay s Free toxins Low Moderate *Must be combined with a to xin test to increase specificity

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A veterinarian developed an ulcer with central black eschar over the forearm as shown in the image. Which of the following is the most probable causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of cutaneous anthrax which is caused by Bacillus anthracis. Human anthrax presents in one of three ways: • Cutaneous Anthrax (hide porter's disease )- Black eschar at the base, with a very prominent inflammatory ring around the eschar, is referred to as a malignant pustule . • Pulmonary Anthrax (Wool sorter's disease )- Hemorrhagic pneumonia. • Intestinal Anthrax - Hemorrhagic diarrhoea. It occurs mainly in primitive communities that eat the carcasses of animals dying of anthrax . Robert Koch validated the germ theory of disease after discovering the anthrax bacillus as the cause of anthrax . He also discovered the causative agents of tuberculosis and cholera. Hence , he is known as the Father of Bacteriology . Koch's postulates , which link specific microorganisms to specific diseases , state that the microorganism must be: • Found in abundance in diseased organisms, but not in healthy organisms. • Isolated from a diseased organism and grown in pure culture • Able to cause disease when inoculated into a healthy organism • Re-isolated from the diseased experimental host and identical to the original specific causative agent161

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following bacilli characteristically shows the M'Fadyean 's reaction?
mcqs.explanation: M'Fadyean 's reaction is shown by Bacillus anthracis. When a blood film containing anthrax bacilli is stained with polychrome methylene blue for a few seconds and examined under the microscope , amorphous purplish material is noticed around the bacilli. This represents the capsular material and is called M'Fadyean 's reaction. The following micrograph shows M'Fadyean's reaction:

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A dairy farmer presented to the dermatology OPD with an ulcer with central black eschar over the forearm. Which of the following media can be used as a selective medium for the growth of the likely etiological agent ?
mcqs.explanation: Based on his profession and clinical description of the lesion, the diagnosis is most likely to be cutaneous anthrax (most common form of anthrax ) caused by Bacillus anthracis. The selective medium for this organism is PLET (polymyxin-lysozyme -EDTA-thallous acetate ) medium. Other options : Option B: Buffered charcoal yeast extract medium is used for Legionella . Option C: Cetrimide agar is a selective medium for Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Option D: Mannitol, Egg Yolk, Phenol red, Polymyxin Agar (MYPA) medium is a selective medium for Bacillus cereus .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A swab was taken from an ulcer and sent to the laboratory for culture . The following image depicts a blood agar culture plate on which gamma phage suspension has been applied . Which of the following is the most likely organism implicated ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image with a circular spot of diminished growth in the culture plate from a swab from an ulcer depicts the gamma phage lysis assay. The most likely organism implicated is Bacillus Anthracis.162 This test is performed by inoculating Bacillus Anthracis in sheep blood agar followed by the application of gamma phage suspension over one area of the culture plate . The gamma phage suspension inhibits the growth of Bacillus anthracis colonies resulting in an an area of diminished growth called a plaque.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following tests is used for the diagnosis of anthrax ?
mcqs.explanation: Ascoli's thermoprecipitation test is used for the diagnosis of anthrax caused by Bacillus anthracis. It is an example of a ring precipitation test . Option A: Paul-Bunnell test is used to diagnose infectious mononucleosis . Option B: Kahn test is used to diagnose syphilis . Option D: Rose-Waaler test is used to diagnose rheumatoid arthritis.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A young patient presented to the medicine OPD with complaints of nausea and vomiting. He gave a history of having fried rice from a local Chinese restaurant a few hours ago. What is the most likely causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: Based on the symptoms and a history of consuming fried rice 6 hours ago, we can diagnose this to be a case of food poisoning due to Bacillus cereus . Food poisoning cause by B. cereus is of two types :Bacillus cereus Diarrheal type Emetic type Incubation peri od 8-16 hours 1-5 hours Toxin Secreted in intestine Preformed Heat Heat labile Heat stable Food items Meat Rice Clinical feature Diarrhea, abdominal cram ps Vomiting, abdominal cra mps

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following can grow in an acidic pH?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , lactobacilli is the one that can grow in an acidic pH. It is a gram-positive, facultatively anaerobic, non-motile, non–spore-forming bacterium. Lactobacillus derives lactic acid from glucose , creating an acidic environment, and can grow in an acidic medium. It is found in the vagina as part of its normal microbiota.163

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The following slide is given as a spotter in your microbiology practical examination. Identify the following organism.
mcqs.explanation: 168 The image shows pink non-branching acid-fast bacilli on a blue background. These findings are consistent with the staining characteristics of mycobacteria. The stain used is the Ziehl-Neelsen stain. Other options : Option B: The image below shows Nocardia stained using an acid-fast staining technique . Nocardia is partially acid-fast and appears as branching filaments .Option C: The image given below is of a gram-stained specimen of Actinomyces israelii. A. israelii is non acid-fastOption D: The images below show the staining characteristics of Corynebacterium diphtheriae . It is stained with Albert's stain which shows the needle appearance .169

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the component of mycobacteria which makes it acid fast?
mcqs.explanation: Mycobacteria are acid-fast due to the presence of mycolic acid in their cell walls . On being stained with carbol fuchsin or fluorescent dyes such as auramine-O or rhodamine, they resist decolourization by 20 % sulphuric acid and absolute alcohol for 10 minutes . This property is referred to as acid and alcohol fastness and is routinely used to identify mycobacteria.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient presents early in the morning to the DOTS center to provide sputum samples . Which of the following reagents are used in the digestion and decontamination of his samples before smear preparation?
mcqs.explanation: NaOH and N-acetylcysteine are used for the digestion and decontamination of sputum used in smear preparation for Mycobacterium tuberculosis .170 Sputum and specimens from non-sterile sites need prior treatment for digestion (to liquefy the thick pus ), decontamination (to inhibit the normal flora), and concentration (to increase the yield ) before they can be used for testing . Methods used for digestion and decontamination of sputum : • Petroff 's method - Uses 4% NaOH and HCl. • N-acetyl cysteine (NALC) + 2% NaOH - NALC liquefies the sputum and NaOH kills the normal flora. This method is better suited for automated culture systems and is superior to Petroff 's method . Note : Formalin or hypochlorite can be used only if smear microscopy is being done. They are not useful for culture or animal pathogenicity testing .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient with suspected tuberculosis gives a sputum sample for microscopic examination. What is the minimum number of acid-fast bacilli that should be present in 1 mL of sputum for them to be detected by this method ?
mcqs.explanation: At least 10 ,000 acid-fast bacilli should be present per milliliter of sputum for them to be readily demonstrable in direct smears. Slide reporting as per NTEP guidelines :No. of A FB No. of oil immersionfields ex amined Repo rt 0 100 1-9 100 Scan ty -99 100 1+ 1-10 1 2+ >10 1 3+

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient has chronic cough with occasional blood in the sputum . He has a history of significant weight loss and night sweats . Which of the following media cannot be used to culture the organism causing his symptoms ?
mcqs.explanation: This patient with chronic cough and hemoptysis with a concurrent history of significant weight loss and night sweats most likely has tuberculosis , caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis . McLeod's medium is not used to culture M. tuberculosis . It is a selective medium for Corynebacterium diphtheriae . Culture media used to cultivate Mycobacterium tuberculosis include : • Solid- Loeffler 's medium is a serum-containing solid medium used for the culture of M. tuberculosis . Other solid media used include Lowenstein - Jensen medium, Dorset medium, Tarshis medium, and Pawlowsky's medium.171 • Liquid - Middlebrook 's media are used for the preparation of antigens and vaccines and in sensitivity testing . Other examples of liquid mycobacterial culture media include Dubos' medium, Sula's medium and Sauton's medium.• Automated culture methods : • • BACTEC 460- uses radioisotopes for detection • BacT alert- colorimetric method of detection • BACTEC MGIT- fluorometric detection method .172

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A microbiology resident is performing liquid automated culture on the sputum sample of a TB suspect patient . Which of the following culture media would he not use for the same?
mcqs.explanation: Tarshis medium is a solid growth medium used for culturing mycobacterium species . Versatrek, BactiAlert , and BACTEC MGIT 960 are liquid automated cultures used for tuberculosis . The diagnostic tools for TB are as follows: 1. Sputum microscopy for AFB • Ziehl Neelson staining • Fluorescence staining 2. Culture • Solid media– Lowenstein -Jensen (most common), Petragnini and Dorset, Tarshis , Loeffler , Pawlowsky. • Liquid automated culture – Versatrek, BactiAlert, BACTEC MGIT 960 (MGIT stands for Mycobacteria Growth Indicator Tube) • Drug Sensitivity Testing / Proportionate Sensitivity Testing: • Using MGIT, LJ medium 3. Rapid molecular diagnostic testing • Line probe assay • CB-NAAT - Nucleic acid amplification test using GeneXpert system 4. Other diagnostic tools are as follows : • Chest X-ray • Tuberculin sensitivity testing173

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following tests can simultaneously detect TB and rifampicin resistance in <2 hours?
mcqs.explanation: Xpert MTB/RIF detects tuberculosis (TB ) and rifampicin resistance simultaneously within 2 hours. It is a fully automated , real-time nucleic acid amplification technology , with high specificity and sensitivity . The WHO recommends its use worldwide as the initial diagnostic test in adults and children who are presumed to have multi-drug resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB ) or HIV -associated TB . Xpert MTB/RIF should also be the first test applied to the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of patients in whom tubercular meningitis is suspected as well as a replacement test (over conventional microscopy, culture , and histopathology ) for gastric lavage, pleural and other biopsies , and fine-needle aspiration specimens . The image below shows the Xpert MTB/RIF system .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a method of testing drug susceptibility in Mycobacterium tuberculosis ?
mcqs.explanation: Disc diffusion method is used for drug susceptibility testing for most bacteria; however, it is not used for Mycobacterium tuberculosis . The disc diffusion technique is not suitable for testing Mycobacterium tuberculosis because the organism grows so slowly that the drug has time to diffuse throughout the medium, and sharp zones of inhibition are not seen .174 Methods used in the drug susceptibility testing of M.tb include : For agar-based methods , 7H10 or 7H11 Middlebrook media are used and only the proportion method can be applied . Radiometric techniques measure the metabolic activity of the bacteria. Based on changes in these values , drug susceptibility can be estimated.Conventional drug-sensitivity testing Radiometric Techniques Molecular methods Proportion methodAbsolute c oncentration methodResistan ce ratio method BACTEC 460MB/BacTMycob acteria growth indicator tube (MGIT)VersaTREK PCR-based assaysDNA probe -basedDNA microarrayGene Xpert

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: TB test done only on whole blood sample is ___________.
mcqs.explanation: TB test done on a whole blood sample is the interferon-gamma release assay. It has been used for the diagnosis of latent tuberculosis in patients with HIV (who frequently have a negative Mantoux test ). Interferon-gamma release assays include : • QuantiFERON -TB Gold • T-SPOT.TB QuantiFERON -TB Gold quantitates the amount of IFN-\035 produced by CD4+ T cells in response to the antigens from Mycobacterium tuberculosis . QuantiFERON -TB Gold Plus (QFT- Plus) is an improved version of the QuantiFERON -TB Gold test . QuantiFERON -TB Gold detects only TB -specific CD4+ responses . However, QuantiFeron-TB Gold Plus detects both CD8+ and CD4+ T-cell responses to TB -specific antigens. T-SPOT.TB determines the total number of individual effector T cells expressing IFN-\035.175 The TrueNat TB test is a new molecular test that can diagnose TB in one hour as well as test for rifampicin resistance . This test uses a sputum sample taken from the patient . Only about 0.5 ml of the sample is required. Gene Xpert is also a molecular method of testing that cannot use blood as a sample . (Option A and B)

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A urine LAM (Lipoarabinomannan ) assay was performed in an HIV +ve patient with a CD4+ count of 40/�ML . Infection with which of the following organisms can be diagnosed using this test?
mcqs.explanation: Urine lipoarabinomannan (LAM) assay is used for the diagnosis of tuberculosis . Lipoarabinomannan (LAM) antigen is a lipopolysaccharide present in the mycobacterial cell wall, released from metabolically active cells or degenerating cells of patients having tuberculosis . Urine LAM is a useful tool in diagnosing tuberculosis , especially in patients with HIV and low CD4+ T cell count. Most diagnostic tests for tuberculosis rely on sputum samples , which are difficult to obtain and have low sensitivity in immunocompromised patients , patients with disseminated TB , and children, delaying treatment initiation. Lipoarabinomannan (LAM) is the only WHO-endorsed TB biomarker that can be detected in urine, an easily collected sample .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man came with a history of fever and night sweats for the past 2 weeks . He has had noticeable weight loss. Bronchoalveolar lavage was done, but Mycobacterium tuberculosis was not detected . Extra-pulmonary TB is suspected . Which site is most likely affected ?
mcqs.explanation: Lymph nodes are the most common site of extrapulmonary TB . The diagnosis is established by fine needle aspiration biopsy . In descending order of frequency, the extrapulmonary sites most commonly involved in TB are: • lymph nodes • pleura • genitourinary tract176 • bones and joints • meninges , peritoneum and pericardium. In less than 50% of these cases , there is associated pulmonary disease .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Your neighbour is worried about a scar on her 5-month-old daughter 's arm that is shown below . She tells you the child has received all vaccines on time. Which of the following statements is true about the vaccine that caused this finding?

options.a: Distilled water is used as diluent for this vaccine
options.c: The route of administration is subcutaneous
options.d: WHO recommends Danish 1331 strain for vaccine

mcqs.explanation: The scar shown in the image results from the BCG (Bacillus Calmette -Gu\351rin) vaccine. The WHO recommends Danish 1331 strain for BCG vaccine production . Normal saline is recommended as the diluent for the BCG vaccine as distilled water is an irritant . The dose administered is 0.1ml containing 0.1mg. It is administered intradermally by using 26 gauge tuberculin syringe on the left deltoid .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: You are performing the pre-employment check up of a young man. You need to perform a tuberculin skin test as a part of this process . Which of the following tests would you not use for this purpose ?
mcqs.explanation: QuantiFERON -TB gold is not a type of tuberculin skin test . It is a type of interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs), a whole -blood test that can aid in diagnosing Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection . There are 3 described methods for tuberculin skin testing (TST ): • Mantoux test , also known as the Pirquet test (preferred method ) • Heaf test • Tine test In contrast, IGRAs that have been approved by the FDA are: • QuantiFERON -TB Gold In -Tube test (QFT-GIT ) • T-SPOT.TB test (T-Spot) • QuantiFERON -TB Gold Plus (QFT- Plus) IGRA is not used in India due to a higher probability of a false positive due to universal BCG vaccination. It can also lead to a diagnosis of active TB in a patient with latent TB and may lead to overtreatment. This test is banned in India after the WHO advised against it in low and middle -income countries .177

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a pigment -producing species of mycobacteria?
mcqs.explanation: 182 Mycobacterium scrofulaceum is a pigment -producing species of mycobacteria. M. scrofulaceum is a scotochromogen which produces yellow or orange colored pigments , even in the dark . It belongs to group II of Runyon's classification . It can cause scrofula or cervical adenitis in children. M.ulcerans, M.avium intracellulare complex (MAC), and M. xenopi belong to group III -non photochromogens as they do not form pigment even on exposure to light .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A microbiologist working with mycobacteria notes moist, smooth, flat, white colonies growing on Lowenstein -Jensen media. Which species of mycobacteria is she likely studying ?
mcqs.explanation: The species of mycobacteria being studied here is Mycobacterium bovis. It forms moist, smooth, flat, white colonies on Lowenstein -Jensen (LJ ) media that break-up easily when touched . Mycobacterium bovis belongs to the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex . It causes tuberculosis -like disease in humans. Lowenstein –Jensen medium is a commonly used , egg -based , selective media for mycobacteria. It contains: • Egg - Provides fatty acids and protein required for metabolism • Malachite green - Prevents the growth of contaminants. Makes it a selective medium. • Mineral salt solution - Buffer • Glycerol - Source of carbon, favors growth of M. tuberculosis , but not M. bovis. LJ medium without glycerol , which contains pyruvate, is used for culture of M. bovis. • L-asparagine- Nitrogen source The image below shows M.bovis colonies on LJ media.Mycobacterium tuberculosis colonies on LJ medium are dry, rough, raised and irregular with a wrinkled surface . They are creamy white or buff -colored , tenacious and difficult to emulsify (rough, tough , buff ).183

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The following findings are obtained during biochemical testing of a mycobacterial species . Identify the organism.
mcqs.explanation: The given biochemical findings are characteristic of Mycobacterium simiae. Eventhough atypical mycobacteria or non-tuberculous mycobacteria(NTM) are usually niacin test negative , some NTM like M. simiae and M. chelonae give a positive niacin test positive .
