Option D: Cefotaxime or ceftazidime are the drugs of choice for the treatment of hemophilus meningitis .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not caused by non-typable H. influenzae ?
mcqs.explanation: Meningitis is caused by typable H. influenzae . Non-typable H. influenzae cause : • Otitis media • Sinusitis • Puerperal sepsis • Exacerbations of COPD.255 H. influenzae is typed into 6 serotypes (a to f) based on the capsular polysaccharide . Serotype b (Hib) is the most virulent and accounts for most of the invasive infections . The differences between type b strains and non-typable strains of H. influenzae are given in the table below :Feature Type B strains Nontypable strains Capsule Made of Ribosyl-ribitol phos phate Unencapsulated Pathogenesis Invasive infections due to he matogenous spread Mucosal infections due to co ntagious spread Clinical manifestations Meningitis and invasive infec tions incompletely immunize d infants and childrenEpiglot titisCellulitisPneumonia Otitis media in childrenExace rbation of COPD,Puerperal s epsisSinusitis Vaccine Highly effective conjugate va ccines Not available

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: All of the following Hemophilus species require both Factors X and V except _______.
mcqs.explanation: Hemophilus parahemolyticus requires only factor V for its growth . It does not require factors X. Hemophilus species requiring both factors X and V : (Mnemonic to remember: HAI ) • H. hemolyticus • H. aegypticus • H. influenzae Factor V- It refers to the co-enzyme, NAD. It is heat -labile (destroyed at 120 \260C in a few minutes ) and present inside RBC. Factor X- It refers to Hemin. It is heat stable and is present in the blood.Species X factor requireme nt V factor requireme nt H. influenzae + + H. aegypticus + + H. ducreyi + - H. parainfluenza � + H. haemolyticus + + H. parahaemolytic us � +256

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 7-year-old girl presents to the emergency with acute stridor. The mother gives a history of fever, drooling, and breathing difficulty since that morning . An X-ray of her neck appears as given below . What is the most likely causative agent ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette and 'thumb sign' on the X-ray are suggestive of acute epiglottitis caused by Hemophilus influenzae . It is an acute inflammation of the epiglottis causing obstructive laryngitis and presents with high fever, severe sore throat, tachycardia, systemic toxicity , and drooling as patients are unable to swallow . The patient characteristically leans forward while sitting for ease of breathing. The diagnosis often is made on clinical grounds. On direct fiberoptic laryngoscopy , the typical edematous cherry-red epiglottis is visualized. Neck radiographs reveal an enlarged edematous epiglottis (Thumb sign). The below image shows the Thumb sign. In some countries , widespread vaccination against Hib has drastically decreased acute epiglottitis cases in children by over 90%. However, the incidence in adults has remained largely unchanged since the Hib vaccine was introduced . Despite vaccination efforts , many pediatric cases of epiglottitis today are still caused by Hib due to either lack of vaccination or vaccine ineffectiveness . In adults and increasingly in children, other bacterial pathogens , particularly group A Streptococcus , have been linked to cases of epiglottitis . Treatment includes airway management followed by administration of antibiotics like ampicillin/sulbactam, cefotaxime , or ceftriaxone .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Pneumonia due to a gram-negative pleomorphic bacillus growing on chocolate agar which is catalase and oxidase-positive is:
mcqs.explanation: Pneumonia due to a gram-negative pleomorphic bacillus growing on chocolate agar which is catalase and oxidase -positive is most likely Haemophilus influenza. Haemophilus pneumonia typically occurs in infants and is accompanied by empyema and sometimes meningitis as well . In older children and adults , the picture is of lobar pneumonia. Sputum is collected for the detection and isolation of Hemophilus . As the bacillus is very sensitive to low temperatures , specimens should never be refrigerated before inoculation. H.infiuenzae is a Gram-negative, non-motile, non-sporing bacillus , exhibiting considerable257 pleomorphism . In sputum , it usually occurs as clusters of coccobacillary forms. The bacillus has fastidious growth requirements. The accessory growth factors, named X and V, present in the blood are essential for growth . Catalase and oxidase reactions are positive . Nitrates are reduced to nitrites. Biotyping has been done on the basis of indole production . Cultures may be preserved for about a month on chocolate agar slopes . Chocolate agar is made by heating blood agar to 80-90\260C for 15-20 minutes . This causes the release of V factor from within the erythrocytes . Treatment- Amoxycillin-clavulanate or clarithromycin is more effective in treating respiratory infections by Haemophilus influenzae .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man who is a known case of diabetes and chronic bronchitis presents to the OPD with low-grade fever and productive cough for 5 days. Which of the following is not a virulence factor of the likely causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario describes an acute exacerbation of COPD characterized by low-grade fever, increased cough , sputum production , and shortness of breath. The most common cause of these are non-typable H. influenzae which lack a capsule and so capsular antigen cannot be a virulence factor. All H. influenzae have the following virulence factors: • Outer membrane proteins (OMP) • Lipooligosaccharide (LOS) • Pili In addition to the above factors, H. influenzae type b also has its capsular polysaccharide as a virulence factor. The differences between Hib and non-typable strains are given below :Feature Type b strains Nontypable strains Capsule Made of Ribosyl-ribitol phos phate Unencapsulated Pathogenesis Invasive infections due to he matogenous spread Mucosal infections due to co ntagious spread Clinical manifestations Meningitis and invasive infec tions incompletely immunize d infants and childrenEpiglot titisCellulitisPneumonia Otitis media in childrenExace rbation of COPD,Puerperal s epsisSinusitis Vaccine Highly effective conjugate va ccines Not available

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following bacteria does not belong to the HACEK group?
mcqs.explanation: 258 Escherichia coli does not belong to the HACEK group. The acronym HACEK refers to a group of fastidious slow -growing bacteria, normally residing in the mouth. These can sometimes cause severe infections , particularly culture -negative subacute bacterial endocarditis . The group includes : • Haemophilus species (H. parainfluenzae, H. aphrophilus , H. paraphrophilus ) • Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans (previously called as Actinobacillus ) • Cardiobacterium hominis • Eikenella corrodens • Kingella kingae

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old man presented with painful, bleeding genital ulcers . On examination, tender inguinal lymphadenopathy is present . Scraping from the ulcer base was taken and the microscopic appearance of the Gram-stained smear is shown below . What is the causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows the ' school of fish' or 'railroad track' appearance of Haemophilus ducreyi . This appearance is seen when the bacilli are arranged in small groups , whorls or in chains. The given case scenario is suggestive of chancroid. Chancroid is characterized by non-indurated, tender , irregular ulcers that may bleed on touch . The neighbouring lymph nodes are enlarged , painful, and tender . Other options : Option B - Treponema pallidum causes syphilis , characterised by chancre - a single painless ulcer with a clean base and a firm raised border, with painless lymphadenopathy . Persistent or multiple chancres may be seen in HIV -infected or other immunodeficient patients . Options C and D - Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1 , L2 and L3 cause lymphogranuloma venereum , characterised by shallow , painless ulcers that progress to painful lymphadenopathy .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The following are true about chancroid:
mcqs.explanation: Chancroid is a painful genital ulcer caused by Haemophilus ducreyi , which is a gram-negative coccobacillus . Microscopic appearance of H. ducreyi is called the school of fish appearance or railroad appearance. Chancroid ulcers have a soft base that bleeds easily to touch . They also cause painful lymphadenopathy . The image below shows the 'school-of-fish' appearance characteristic of H. ducreyi .259 Note : Groove sign is a characteristic sign seen in lymphogranuloma venereum. It refers to the depression created by the inguinal ligament as it passes between the groups of inflamed inguinal lymph nodes .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not involved in urethritis?
mcqs.explanation: Haemophilus ducreyi does not cause urethritis. It causes chancroid (soft chancre), which presents as a genital ulcer. Urethritis is classified into two types : • Gonococcal urethritis - caused by Neisseria gonorrhoea. • Non-gonococcal urethritis - caused by: • Chlamydia trachomatis (most common) • Ureaplasma urealyticum • Adenovirus • Haemophilus vaginalis • Mycoplasma genitalium • Tricomonas vaginalis (rare) • Herpes simplex virus (rare)

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old girl presents with conjunctivitis, fever, and hemorrhagic skin lesions . There's a history of travel to Brazil . Which of the following etiological agents would you suspect in this case?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of Brazilian purpuric fever (BPF) caused by Haemophilus aegypticus (Koch-Weeks bacillus ).260 Recent DNA studies have shown that the bacillus is identical to non-capsulated H.influenzae and it is now named H.influenzae biotype aegypticus . It is worldwide in distribution and causes : • A highly contagious form of conjunctivitis ('pink eye ') which is especially common in the tropics and subtropics and may lead to epidemics. It responds to local sulphonamide or gentamicin administration. • Brazilian purpuric fever characterized by fever, purpura, and conjunctivitis which proceeds to fulminant septicemia in infants and children. It has a high fatality rate.261

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The milk ring test is found to be positive for a sample of milk. Which organism has it most likely been contaminated with?
mcqs.explanation: Milk ring test (MRT) is positive for Brucella. It is used for the detection of infected animals in dairy farms. A sample of whole milk is mixed with a drop of Brucella antigen and incubated at 70 \260C for 40–50 min. If antibodies are present in the milk, the bacilli are agglutinated and rise with the cream to form a blue ring at the top , leaving the rest of the milk unstained (MRT positive ). If antibodies are absent, the solution remains uniformly blue (MRT negative ).

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an intracellular pathogen ?
mcqs.explanation: Brucella suis is primarily an intracellular pathogen affecting reticuloendothelial system . This accounts for its refractoriness to chemotherapy .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A farmer was diagnosed with brucellosis . Which of the following patterns of fever will be seen in this disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Brucellosis is a bacterial zoonosis caused by Brucella sp which presents with undulant fever. It is referred to as undulant fever because of the rising and falling of fever like a wave (remittent fever). Patients may also have arthralgia, muscular pain, sweating , loss of weight , and appetite . CNS symptoms such as fatigue , irritability, and depression might also occur. Other options Option A: Pel-Ebstein fever is seen in Hodgkin's lymphoma. It is characterized by fever lasting 3–10 days followed by afebrile periods of 3–10 days.271 Option C: Relapsing fever is seen in infection with Borrelia recurrentis in which days of fever are followed by a several-day afebrile period and then relapse into additional days of fever. A similar picture is also seen in malaria . Option D: Saddleback fever is seen in dengue . Saddleback fever is defined as temperature >37.5\260C with defervescence of at least one day, followed by a second peak lasting at least one day.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 56-year-old dairy farmer presented with remittent fever and night sweats for 1 month. On examination , he was hypotensive and pallor was present . Rose Bengal card tests done on milk samples from his farm were found to be positive . Which blood culture method with a biphasic medium will be used to isolate the organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario of remittent fever with anemia with a positive Rose Bengal card test is suggestive of brucellosis . Castaneda method for blood culture is used to isolate Brucella sp. In the Castaneda method , blood is inoculated into a bottle of trypticase soy broth or brucella broth in a biphasic blood culture bottle (with liquid and solid media in the same bottle ). This method minimizes materials and manipulation, thus reducing the chances of contamination and risk of infection to laboratory workers. Blood cultures are positive in only 30–50% of cases even when repeated samples are tested . B.melitensis and B.suis are isolated more readily than B.abortus. The below image shows Castaneda 's bottle .Lab diagnosis of brucellosis is done using the following methods : • Blood culture with • Castaneda 's method - recommended • BACTEC - an automated method . It is faster than Castaneda 's method . • Serological tests : • Standard agglutination test (SAT) • ELISA for specific IgG/IgM272 • Dipstick assays • Detection in milk and infected cattle is carried out by: • Microscopic demonstration by staining or immunofluorescence • Milk ring test • Rose Bengal card test

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old farmer presents with fever, weight loss, and lower backache for three weeks . Blood reports show predominant lymphocytosis . What are the drugs of choice for treating this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of a farmer with fever, weightloss and back pain with a predominant lymphocytosis points towards a diagnosis of acute brucellosis . The drugs of choice for this condition in adults are intramuscular streptomycin with doxycycline . The usual alternative regimen (and the current World Health Organization recommendation) is rifampin plus doxycycline . However, this is associated with a higher relapse rate, possibly because rifampicin increases clearance of doxycycline and reduces serum doxycycline levels . In children, cotrimoxazole along with rifampicin or gentamycin may be used for the treatment of brucellosis . Note : B. melitensis is endemic to the Middle East .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old man presents to the hospital with fever, joint pain and a rash on his hands. He gives a history of a rat bite 1 week back. Which of the following can cause this disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of rat-bite fever. This can be caused by Streptobacillus moniliformis and Spirillum minus. Rat-bite fever (RBF) is characterized by fever, rash, and arthralgia which usually occurs days or weeks after a bite . The two types of rat-bite fever are: • Streptobacillary RBF develops 2–10 days after a rat bite , associated with sudden onset of fever, headache , and myalgia followed by petechial rash and arthritis. It is also called Haverhill fever or Erythema arthrititicum epidemicum . • Spirillary RBF is similar to streptobacillary type but it is also associated with regional lymphadenopathy . It is also called Sodoku. Diagnosis is based on demonstration of causative organisms in peripheral blood films. Serology can also be used for diagnosis. RBF is treated with intravenous Penicillin G. Alternative drugs include ampicillin, cefuroxime, and cefotaxime. Note : Pasteurella multocida causes cellulitis and lymphangitis following bites by cats and dogs . Bartonella henselae causes cat sratch disease and bacillary angiomatosis. Borellia burgdorferi causes Lyme disease .273

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: While evaluating the Pap smear of a patient , you come across the following finding. What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows clue cells which are seen in bacterial vaginosis. They are epithelial cells with their surface covered by adherent bacilli seen in stained or unstained films. Bacterial vaginosis is a polymicrobial infection characterized by a malodorous (fishy smell ) vaginal discharge. Causative organisms include : • Gardnerella vaginalis • Mycoplasma hominis • Prevotella • Ureaplasma • Peptostreptococcus . Bacterial vaginosis is diagnosed using Amsel's criteria and Nugent 's score: 1. Amsel's Criteria: (any 3 should be present ) • Thin , white /yellow homogenous vaginal discharge • pH of Vaginal fluid >4.5 • Fishy odour of discharge accentuated on adding 10 % KOH (Whiff test ) • Clue cells seen on microscopy 2. Nugent 's score is obtained by counting the number of Gardnerella vaginalis, Mobilincus and lactobacillus in the gram-stained smear of vaginal discharge . A score of \0247 is diagnostic Treatment is oral metronidazole 500 mg BD for 7 days. The images below show clue cells from microscopy.274

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient from Kolar, Karnataka presented with fever and hemoptysis . The findings of his peripheral smear examination are given below . Which of the following is the causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario and the image showing the characteristic "safety -pin appearance " in peripheral smear is suggestive of plague caused by Yersinia pestis . On staining with Giemsa stain or methylene blue (Wayson's stain), the bacteria has bipolar staining with two ends densely stained and the central area clear. This is the characteristic 'safety -pin appearance ' seen in Y. pestis. Bipolar staining is also shown by the following organisms: • Haemophilus ducreyi • Vibrio parahemolyticus • Calymmatobacterium granulomatis • Burkholderia mallei • Burkholderia pseudomallei . Note : In India, 4 foci of plague are known: • Kolar at the trijunction of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka . • Beed -Latur belt in Maharashtra • Rhoru, Himachal Pradesh • Uttarakhand The image given below shows the safety -pin appearance of Yersinia pestis on Wayson's stain275

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A child from Uttarakhand suddenly developed fever with chills and malaise. He also developed a tender swelling which is shown in the image. There's a history of similar complaints in the community. What is false about the disease he's likely suffering from?

options.a: Wild rodents and their infected fleas are the primary reservoir.
options.b: The septicemic form cannot be acquired directly .
options.c: The pneumonic form is far more contagious than the bubonic form.
options.d: The bubonic form may progress to the pneumonic form.

mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario of sudden -onset fever with painful lymphadenopathy and a history of similar complaints in the community is suggestive of a diagnosis of plague caused by Yersinia pestis . The septicemic form of the disease may be acquired directly if the bacteria enter the bloodstream via infected blood transfusions. Wild rodents and their infected fleas are the primary reservoirs of Yersinia pestis . Infection is transmitted to humans by the bite of infected fleas . Human plague occurs in 3 clinical forms (in increasing order of severity ): bubonic plague < pneumonic plague < septicemic plague Bubonic plague - It is the most common variety of the disease . It is named after the buboes meaning swollen lymph nodes , which typically develop within a week after an infected flea bite . Other clinical features include sudden onset of fever and chills, headache , and fatigue . Pneumonic plague - Bubonic plague can advance and spread to the lungs . It is the most virulent form of plague . Any person with pneumonic plague may transmit the disease via droplets to other humans. The symptoms include dyspnoea, chest pain, cough , fever, and hemoptysis . Septicemic plague - When the bacteria enter the bloodstream directly and multiply there , it is known as septicemic plague . When left untreated , both bubonic and pneumonic plague can lead to septicemic plague .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A sudden epidemic of pneumonic plague has occurred in the Beed -Latur belt of Maharashtra. The primary contact of a suspected case came to you for preventive treatment . What will you prescribe for chemoprophylaxis in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The drug of choice for chemoprophylaxis of plague is doxycycline . It is given for 7 days to all close contacts of a patient having pneumonic plague .276 Ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, and moxifloxacin are the other first-line drugs used for antimicrobial prophylaxis. The drug of choice for the treatment of plague is streptomycin . Streptomycin is nephrotoxic and ototoxic and should , therefore be cautiously used . Doxycycline or ciprofloxacin (and other fluoroquinolones) are considered as alternative drugs for the treatment of plague .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms do not cause yersiniosis?
mcqs.explanation: The term yersiniosis denotes infections with yersiniae other than Y.pestis . Yersiniosis includes zoonotic infections by Y.pseudotuberculosis and Y.enterocolitica .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old patient presents to the OPD with high fever, chest pain, dyspnoea , and hemoptysis . The patient also complains of watery diarrhea. The direct fluorescent antibody stained film of his pleural fluid is given below . Identify the most likely etiologic agent .
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette and the image showing fluorescent organisms in the direct fluorescent antibody (DFA) stained film of pleural fluid suggest the diagnosis of Legionnaire's disease , caused by Legionella pneumophila . Two distinct clinical patterns of legionellosis have been identified : • Legionnaires' disease presents with fever, non-productive cough , and dyspnea rapidly progressing to pneumonia if left untreated . Patients can also develop a hyponatremia. Diarrhea and encephalopathy are also common. It is often included in the differential diagnosis of atypical pneumonia. Atypical pneumonia is also caused by: • Chlamydia pneumonia • Chlamydia psittaci • Mycoplasma pneumonia • Coxiella burnetii • Viruses such as influenza virus, adenovirus and respiratory syncytial virus • Pontiac fever is a milder, non-fatal, influenza-like illness with fever, chills, myalgia, and headache . Other options : Option A: Chlamydia pneumonia causes pharyngitis, sinusitis, bronchitis, and pneumonia. It has also been associated with adult onset asthma. Outbreaks have been reported in closed communities . Real-time PCR is used for its diagnosis. Option C: Haemophilus influenzae typically causes pneumonia in infants. While the primary infections occur due to capsulated strains, bronchopneumonia may occur as a secondary infection due to non-capsulated strains. Gram stain and culture are used for diagnosis. Option D: Klebsiella pneumonia causes fatal pneumonia, which occurs in middle -aged or older persons with risk factors such as alcoholism, chronic bronchopulmonary disease or diabetes mellitus . Gram stain and culture are used for diagnosis.277

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: BCYE medium is used to culture :
mcqs.explanation: BCYE medium (buffered charcoal yeast extract agar) is used to culture Legionella pneumophila . Legionella pneumophila has fastidious growth requirements and grows on complex media such as BCYE medium with L-cysteine and antibiotic supplements (e.g., polymyxin B, cefazolin, vancomycin ). The charcoal acts as a detoxifying agent . It grows slowly , and the colonies may take 3–6 days to appear. Other options : Option A: Leptospira is cultured on EMJH (Ellinghausen , McCullough , Johnson and Harris ) medium Option B: Bacillus cereus is cultured on PEMBA (Polymyxin pyruvate egg -yolk mannitol–bromothymol blue ) agar Option C: Campylobacter is cultured on Skirrow 's, Campy BAP or Butzler's agar.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man is diagnosed with Legionnaires' disease . He had recently attended a conference . What is the most likely way he acquired the infection ?

options.a: From the air-conditioned rooms at the conference
options.b: From a chronic carrier of the disease
options.c: From sharing a towel with a fellow colleague in the conference
options.d: From drinking the water provided at the conference

mcqs.explanation: This patient most likely acquired infection with Legionella pneumophila from inhalation of aerosol in the air-conditioned rooms at the conference . Legionella pneumophila can be found in natural, freshwater environments, but generally is not present in sufficient numbers to cause disease . Infection is typically by inhalation of aerosols produced by cooling towers , air conditioners, and showerheads which act as disseminators No animal reservoirs exist . No evidence of human-to-human transmission has been found and no carrier state is established .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient presented with fever and regional lymphadenopathy , following a scratch from his pet kitten. His lymph node biopsy specimen was examined with Warthin -Starry staining; the findings are shown in the given image. What is the causative organism of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: This patient presents with fever and lymphadenopathy after a cat scratch and the above image shows the black short rod-shaped bacilli arranged in chains or clumps , suggestive of cat scratch disease , This condition is caused by Bartonella henselae . Cat scratch disease presents as a febrile illness with lymphadenopathy following a cat scratch. Patients present with a painless papule or pustule at the site of the scratch and lymph node enlargement and can be suppurative . The disease is usually self resolving. However, it can be treated with azithromycin only in patients who have severe complications .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Choose the correct statement regarding 5-day fever.

options.d: Treatment is necessary only in the severe cases

mcqs.explanation: 5-day fever is an exclusively human disease and no animal reservoir is known.278 5-day fever is also known as trench fever/quintan fever. It is caused by Bartonella quintana . It is characterized by sudden onset of fever accompanied by headache , malaise, restlessness , and shin pain. Trench fever is transmitted by the body louse . (Option A). It has an incubation period ranging from 14-30 days. Symptoms coincide with the release of B. quintana in blood every 3-5 days with each episode lasting 5 days. Recrudescence and relapses are common. (Option B) All cases are treated using doxycycline. Macrolides and fluoroquinolones can also be used in its treatment. (Option D)

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A young man presented to the ER with fever and suppurative lymphadenopathy of his left axilla a few days after he sustained a scratch from his pet cat. Which of the following will most likely be seen on biopsy of the lymph node?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario points to a diagnosis of cat-scratch disease caused by B. henselae . Stellate granulomas are characteristically present in this condition. They are granulomas containing central granular debris and neutrophils ; giant cells are uncommon. The image below shows a stellate granulomaOther options : Option A: Foreign body granulomas are incited by relatively inert foreign bodies , such as talc, sutures . Epithelioid cells and giant cells are apposed to the surface of the foreign body. The foreign material can usually be identified in the center of the granuloma. The given image shows suture granuloma. The suture material is surrounded by lymphocytic infiltration279 Option B: Naked granulomas are seen in sarcoidosis. They are non-caseating granulomas minimally surrounded by lymphocytes. The image below shows a naked granulomaOption C: Durck granulomas are seen in cerebral malaria . The image below shows a Durck granuloma280

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient who is a known case of AIDS presents to the OPD with fever, chills, weight loss and the cutaneous lesions shown below . The microscopic examination of the lesions revealed predominant neutrophilic infiltration. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical vignette of a patient with HIV infections and the violaceous lesions with a neutrophilic infiltrate is suggestive of bacillary angiomatosis. Bacillary angiomatosis is seen in severely immunocompromised patients and is caused by B. henselae or B. quintana . It is characterized by neovascular proliferative lesions involving the skin. It consists of lobular proliferation of small blood vessels lined by enlarged endothelial cells interspersed with mixed infiltrates of neutrophils and lymphocytes , with a predominance of the former. Both bacillary angiomatosis and Kaposi 's sarcoma can have the clinical presentation mentioned in the question. However, the major differentiating factor is the microscopic examination: • Bacillary angiomatosis predominantly has mixed infiltrate accompanied by neutrophils with clumps of bacilli. • Kaposi 's sarcoma predominantly has plasma cells and lymphocytic infiltrates .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient has presented with lesions on the dorsum of the hand followed by axillary lymphadenopathy . What significant history will you ask for in this case?

options.c: History of similar complaint in family members

mcqs.explanation: This scenario of lesions on the hand followed by axillary lymphadenopathy is suggestive of cat scratch disease , hence we should ask about the history of exposure to cats. It is caused by Bartonella henselae . Bartonella henselae is an intracellular, pleomorphic , gram-negative bacillus . They can be identified in lymph node biopsy with Warthin -Starry Silver stain. In addition to cat scratch disease , in immunocompromised individuals, it can also cause bacillary angiomatosis and peliosis hepatis .281 In immunocompetent hosts , cat scratch disease is a self limiting illness . However in patients with severe disease , azithromycin can be used to treat the infection .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrectly matched ?
mcqs.explanation: Parinaud's oculoglandular syndrome is an atypical form of cat scratch disease and is caused by Bartonella henselae . Bartonella henselae also causes bacillary angiomatosis in HIV -infected and other immunodeficient patients . . It presents as vascular nodules or tumours on the skin, mucosa, and other locations. Bartonella bacilliformis causes Oroya fever also known as Carrion 's disease . Note : Ehrlichia phagocytophila has been renamed as Anaplasma phagocytophilum .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient with fever and hemolytic anemia developed characteristic Peruvian warts 1 month later. What is the causative organism for this disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario of fever, hemolytic anemia followed by verruga peruana lesions (Peruvian warts) is suggestive of Oroya fever. It is caused by Bartonella bacilliformis. The vector for Oroya fever is sandfly . Oroya fever or Carrion 's disease is associated with verruga peruana which are cutaneous vascular lesions carrying the bacteria. It presents as fever with progressive anemia due to bacterial invasion of erythrocytes . A late sequela in survivors of Oroya fever or in those with asymptomatic infection is verruga peruana, which is characterized by vascular nodular skin lesions carrying the bacteria that occur in successive crops. An image of verruga peruana is given below . Image shows verruga peruana lesions .282 Bartonella quintana causes trench fever or 5 day fever. Bartonella henselae causes cat scratch disease . It also causes bacillary angiomatosis and bacillary peliosis in HIV infected people .283

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a risk factor for Neisseria meningitidis infection ?
mcqs.explanation: Hypogammaglobulinemia is a risk factor for Neisseria meningitidis infection , not hypergammaglobulinemia. Risk factors for meningococcal infection include : • Overcrowding • Cigarette smoking • Mycoplasma infection • Hyposplenism • Hypogammaglobulinemia • History of travel like pilgrimage • Recent viral infection • Terminal complement pathway deficiency (C5-C9 Deficiency ) - increases the risk of disseminated gonococcemia

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 22 -year-old student presented with high-grade fever, and purpuric rash as shown in the image below . CSF sample showed gram-negative diplococci . Which of the following is the most likely aetiology ?
mcqs.explanation: This patient has a high-grade fever and is a student , so he presumably spends a lot of time in crowded areas. The above image shows a purpuric rash. This patient 's features are seen in meningococcemia caused by Neisseria meningitidis , which are gram-negative diplococci . The organism enters the body through the nasopharynx by attaching to the epithelial cells with the help of pili. From the nasopharynx, they enter the bloodstream producing bacteremia, and the symptoms may resemble upper respiratory tract infection . Fulminant meningococcemia is the severe form, where the patient presents with high-grade fever and hemorrhagic rash. There is thrombosis of several small blood vessels in various organs with perivascular infiltration and petechial hemorrhages. Some patients with fulminant meningococcemia may also develop disseminated intravascular coagulation , and circulatory collapse , a condition known as Waterhouse –Friderichsen syndrome.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: What is the most common manifestation of Neisseria meningitidis infection ?
mcqs.explanation: Infection with Neisseria meningitidis is most commonly asymptomatic colonization in the nasopharynx of healthy individuals. Hence , a nasopharyngeal swab is used in the detection of carriers. In some patients , local inflammation ensues with rhinitis and pharyngitis. Ceftriaxone as a single -dose IV /IM injection is highly (97%) effective in the eradication of carrier state and can be used at all ages and also in pregnancy. Ciprofloxacin is also highly effective and can be given orally, but it is not recommended in pregnancy and below 18 years of age .291

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old girl with thalassemia major was prophylactically immunized with a polysaccharide meningococcal vaccine before being taken up for elective splenectomy . Which group of Neisseria meningitidis would she be susceptible to even after immunization ?
mcqs.explanation: Polysaccharide vaccines of Neisseria meningitidis do not offer protection against group B meningococci . This is because the group B capsule is made up of sialic acid residue which is also expressed on the surface of neural cells in the fetus . So, the B polysaccharide is perceived as 'self ' and is poorly immunogenic. To overcome this issue and provide protection against group B meningococci, a new vaccine was developed based on the surface protein i.e., non-capsular antigen of serogroup B meningococci. This is the multicomponent meningococcal vaccine - 4CMenB. Meningococcal polysaccharide vaccines developed based on capsular antigen can be classified as: • Plain polysaccharide vaccines: • Bivalent (A and C), • Trivalent (A, C and W-135) • Tetravalent (A, C, Y, and W-135) • Conjugated polysaccharide vaccines: • Monovalent (A or C) • Quadrivalent (A, C, Y, and W-135) MenQuadfi vaccine

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A young man is brought to the ER with complaints of headache and fever. On examination, a maculopapular rash is seen over his trunk & extremities , and the following sign is elicited . Which of the following antibiotics should he be started on empirically ?
mcqs.explanation: The clip given shows a positive Kernig's sign. This in combination with the other clinical features indicates a diagnosis of meningococcal meningitis. Third-generation cephalosporins such as ceftriaxone , cefotaxime , and ceftazidime are used empirically for the initiation of treatment for suspected meningococcal meningitis. These drugs are administered as they also cover the various other potentially penicillin -resistant bacteria that may produce clinical features similar to that of meningococcal meningitis like penicillin -resistant pneumococcus . Also, some instances of reduced meningococcal sensitivity to penicillin have also been reported . Both meningococcal meningitis and meningococcal septicemia are conventionally treated for 7 days, although courses of 3–5 days may be equally effective . Rifampicin can be used for prophylaxis for close contacts . Ceftriaxone can also be used for chemoprophylaxis , especially in pregnant individuals. The image below shows petechial rashes in meningococcal infection292

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: You have to administer chemoprophylaxis to the contacts of a patient diagnosed with meningococcal meningitis. Which of the following combinations is correct?
mcqs.explanation: Ciprofloxacin, ceftriaxone , and rifampicin can be used for chemoprophylaxis of meningococcal meningitis . Ciprofloxacin should not be given in pregnancy and to those below 18 years of age . Ceftriaxone is preferred in these cases as a single IM or IV dose . However, reduced susceptibility of isolates to ceftriaxone has occasionally been reported . Recommended chemoprophylaxis for high-risk close contacts of meningococcal meningitis:Age Drug Dose Route and duration Remarks <1 mo nth Rifampicin 5 mg/ kg Oral every 12 hrs for 2 days - >1 mo nth Rifampicin 10 mg /kg Oral every 12 hrs for 2 days Not recommended in pregna ncy <15 yea rs Ceftriaxone 125m g IM single dose Can be given to children and is recommended in pregnanc y >15 yea rs Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose Can be given to children and is recommended in pregnanc y >18 ye ars Ciprofloxac in mg Oral single dose Not recommended in pregna ncyPreferred for mass proph ylaxis

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following differentiates meningococcus from gonococcus ?
mcqs.explanation: 293 Only meningococcus can ferment maltose , whereas both gonococcus and meningococcus can ferment glucose . Both species are catalase and oxidase positive and neither of them can reduce nitrate. The only Neisseria species that can reduce nitrate is N. mucosa.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man has treatment -resistant gonorrhea. You plan to send a sample of his urethral discharge to the lab for culture and sensitivity testing . What transport media would you use for this purpose ?
mcqs.explanation: Stuart's medium is the transport media used for Neisseria gonorrheae and Neisseria meningitidis . Stuart's medium is a semisolid , non-nutrient medium, which prevents microbial proliferation. It ensures that microorganisms present are able to survive for a sufficiently long period of time.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 25-year old man presents with a history of urethral discharge for the last three days. A gram stain smear of the discharge is shown below . All of the following are true regarding the likely etiology except ?
mcqs.explanation: The given slide shows gram-negative diplococci within the polymorphs , characteristic of Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection . Neisseria is not an obligate intracellular organism, it can also occur extracellularly i.e, it is a facultative intracellular organism. The other neisseria that are found as normal inhabitants of the human respiratory tract occur extracellularly . Neisseria gonorrhoeae is a gram-negative, non-sporulating, non-motile diplococcus that is aerobic but may grow anaerobically also. It is oxidase and catalase -positive . Although Neisseria are non-motile organisms, they show twitching motility . This is a flagella -independent form of bacterial translocation over moist surfaces that occurs by the extension and retraction of polar type IV pili. These pili act as virulence factors by promoting attachment to host cells and inhibiting phagocytosis . Virulence factors for gonococci : • Outer Membrane Proteins (OMPs) • IgA proteases • Pili • Lipo-oligosaccharide (LOS) • Transferrin • Lactoferrin-binding protein

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common manifestation of gonorrhoea in males?
mcqs.explanation: Gonorrhea in males most commonly manifests as acute urethritis. In males, the disease starts as acute urethritis. This infection may extend along the urethra to involve the prostate , seminal vesicles , and epididymis . Chronic urethritis may lead to stricture formation. The infection may also spread to the periurethral tissues causing abscesses and multiple discharging sinuses (watercan perineum ).294 In females , the initial infection involves the cervix, uteri and urethra which may extend to Bartholin glands, endometrium , and fallopian tubes . The vaginal mucosa is not usually affected in adults because the stratified squamous epithelium is resistant to infection by the cocci, and also because of the acidic pH of vaginal secretions. Pelvic inflammatory disease and salpingitis may lead to sterility . Rarely peritonitis may develop with perihepatic inflammation (Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome) which may also occur following Chlamydia trachomatis infection.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient with a history of sexual intercourse with a commercial sex worker 3 days back has developed genital discharge resembling 'flow of seed ' as shown below . What medium should be used for the culture of the discharge ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario is suggestive of gonococcal urethritis caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Thayer-Martin and modified Thayer-Martin media are used for the culture of this organism. Gonorrhoea may manifest as mucopurulent genital discharge which can be described as resembling 'flow of seed ' (semen ). Thayer-Martin medium contains vancomycin , colistin and nystatin. Gonorrhea is a sexually transmitted disease caused by N. gonorrhea. The major symptoms include urethritis, vaginal discharge , dyspareunia, and dysuria. In the laboratory diagnosis of N. gonorrhea, the discharge on Gram's stain reveals gram\037negative intracellular diplococci within phagocytes . It acidifies glucose but not maltose in serum sugars. Stuart's medium is used for transport while Thayer-Martin agar is used as a selective medium used to isolate N. gonorrhoeae. Cultures can be obtained from chocolate agar or Mueller -Hinton agar. Stuart's medium is the transport media used for Neisseria gonorrhea and Neisseria meningitides . It is a semisolid, non-nutrient medium. Charcoal present in the medium neutralizes certain bacterial inhibitors while a reducing agent prevents oxidation.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a content of modified Thayer-Martin medium?
mcqs.explanation: Modified Thayer-Martin medium does not include polymyxin B. It includes polymyxin E, which is also known as colistin. Modified Thayer–Martin medium is a selective media for Neisseria species . It includes : • Vancomycin - to inhibit most gram-positive bacteria. • Colistin (Polymyxin E) - to inhibit most gram-negative bacteria other than Neisseria . • Nystatin or anisomycin - to inhibit yeast . • Trimethoprim - to inhibit proteus . The contents of the Thayer-Martin medium are the same as that of the modified Thayer -Martin medium except for the presence of trimethoprim in the modified version . The image below depicts Thayer-Martin medium.295

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An unresponsive middle -aged man with fever and petechial rashes was rushed into the ER. You successfully resuscitate him. Abdominal ultrasound shows bilateral adrenal hemorrhage. Which of the following statements is false regarding his condition?

options.a: Patients who recover may suffer from sloughing of the skin
options.b: The implicated organism can be isolated from the petechial rashes
options.c: The causative organism is Neisseria gonorrheae
options.d: Hypoplastic spleen is a risk factor for this condition

mcqs.explanation: The above scenario depicts Waterhouse -Friderichsen syndrome which is a complication seen in infection with meningococci. Waterhouse -Friderichsen syndrome is also known as hemorrhagic adrenalitis or fulminant meningococcemia and is characterized by bilateral adrenal gland hemorrhage. Though Waterhouse -Freiderichsen syndrome is most often associated with meningococcal septicemia , it may complicate sepsis caused by other organisms like certain streptococcal species also. Hypoplastic spleen may also be associated with this condition and the implicated organism can be isolated from the petechial rashes. Complications : • Shock, extensive hemorrhage within the skin • May fall into a coma • Death , usually after a few hours, due to adrenal insufficiency • Patients who recover may suffer from extensive sloughing of the skin and loss of digits due to gangrene. Fulminant meningococcemia is a medical emergency and needs to be treated with adequate antibiotics as fast as possible . Ceftriaxone is an antibiotic commonly used nowadays.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman with a history of recurrent pelvic inflammatory disease presents to the OPD with fever and right upper abdominal pain. A diagnostic laparoscopy was done and the findings are as given below . Which of the following organisms could be the causative agent ?
mcqs.explanation: The scenario depicted is Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome which is a rare complication of pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) following infection with Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae.296 It causes liver capsule inflammation leading to the creation of violin-string adhesions which can be seen on laparoscopy . On CT imaging it appears as perihepatic inflammatory stranding and hepatic capsular enhancement . The major symptom and signs include right upper quadrant pain. It is also associated with minimal pelvic pain, vaginal discharge , or cervical motion tenderness .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which is the true statement regarding gonococcal urethritis?

options.a: Symptoms are more severe in females than in males
options.b: Infection does not involve rectum and prostate
options.c: Dysuria is the most common presentation
options.d: Single dose of cefixime is the first line of treatment

mcqs.explanation: Acute urethritis is the most common clinical manifestation of gonorrhea in males and major symptoms include urethral discharge and dysuria, usually without urinary frequency or urgency . Other options : Option A: The stratified squamous epithelium of the vagina is resistant to gonococcus , so infection is less severe in females . Option B: In males, it can involve rectum, prostate , and epididymitis , but it never involves testes . Option D: Rising minimum inhibitory concentration of cefixime worldwide has led the CDC to discontinue its recommendation of this agent as first-line treatment for uncomplicated gonorrhea. Third-generation cephalosporins have remained highly effective as single -dose therapy for gonorrhoea. Ceftriaxone (250mg, IM) single dose + azithromycin 1 g PO, single dose or doxycycline 100 mg PO BD for 7 days is given. This also covers treatment for chlamydia (if chlamydial infection is not ruled out).

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about Neisseria gonorrhoeae?

options.a: It is exclusively a human pathogen
options.b: Some strains may cause disseminated disease
options.c: Vaccination has no role in prevention
options.d: Drug resistance is only due to acquisition of plasmids

mcqs.explanation: Neisseria gonorrheae acquires resistance to antibiotics either by chromosomal mutations or by the acquisition of plasmids (R factors). These resistant strains are also known as: • PPNG - penicillinase -producing N. gonorrhoeae (plasmid-borne resistance ) • TRNG - tetracycline-resistant N. gonorrhoeae (plasmid-borne resistance ) • CMRNG - chromosomally mediated resistance in N. gonorrhoeae (resistance to both penicillin and tetracycline) • QRNG - quinolone resistant N. gonorrhoeae (due to alterations in DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV ) Other options : Option A: N. gonorrhea is a fastidious organism and is exclusively a human pathogen . Option B: Some strains of N. gonorrhea can ascend up the genital tract and can lead to many disseminated diseases such as septic arthritis and pelvic inflammatory disease . Option C: Vaccines are not effective against N. gonorrhea due to its antigenic variation and ability to invade neurophils .297

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about Moraxella catarrhalis?

options.b: An uncommon cause of COPD exacerbation

mcqs.explanation: Moraxella catarrhalis is a DNAse positive gram-negative diplococcus . It is the second most common bacterial cause of COPD exacerbations (after H. influenzae ). It can also cause otitis media, sinusitis, tracheobronchitis, and pneumonia. It differs from pathogenic Neisseria as: • It does not ferment any carbohydrates - Asaccharolytic • Gives a positive tributyrin hydrolysis test . • Shows positive DNAse test . Angular conjunctivitis is caused by Moraxella lacunata, which is a gram-negative rod-shaped bacteria. Treatment is with oral amoxicillin and clauvulanic acid.298

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Transovarial transmission is a feature of which of the following diseases ?
mcqs.explanation: Transovarial transmission is a feature of Orientia tsutsugamushi which causes scrub typhus . Transovarial transmission refers to passing on the disease -causing bacteria from parent arthropod to offspring arthropod. Orientia tsutsugamushi is maintained by transovarial transmission in trombiculid mites . It is also seen in Rickettsia rickettsii, Rickettsia conorii, and Rickettsia akari . The image below shows a trombiculid mite.Trench fever (option D) is caused by Bartonella quintana .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 36-year-old trekker presented with fever, headache , and rashes following a tick bite . He was later diagnosed to have Rocky Mountain spotted fever. Which of the following statements is false about the microbe implicated ?
mcqs.explanation: Rocky Mountain spotted fever is caused by Rickettsia rickettsii. A cell wall is present in rickettsial organisms. Rickettsiae are obligate intracellular, gram-negative pleomorphic coccobacilli . They are unable to grow in cell -free media and are thus cultured in yolk sacs of embryonated eggs . They are non-motile, non-capsulated organisms that contain both DNA and RNA. They reproduce by binary fission and are transmitted by arthropods like ticks and lice (except Coxiella burnetii and Bartonella henselae ). The rickettsiae are localized in endothelial cells of small blood vessels (except Ehrlichia and Anaplasma) in humans. They cause endothelial cell enlargement and degeneration , predisposing307 to thrombus formation. Tetracyclines , macrolides, and fluoroquinolones are effective against this group but, beta -lactams are ineffective.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding endemic murine typhus ?
mcqs.explanation: The vector for endemic murine typhus is the rat flea , Xenopsylla cheopis . Endemic murine typhus is cuased by Rickettsia typhi (option B) while epidemic typhus is caused by Rickettsia prowazekii. The zoonotic reservoir for R. typhi is the rat. Humans are infected when flea feces contaminate pruritic bite lesions . Transmission can also occur via inhalation of aerosols of dried feces of rickettsemic rat flea . No man-to-man transmission occurs. Patients present with fever, chills, vomiting and a maculopapular rash that is more prominent on the trunk. Diagnosis is by serology and treatment is with doxycycline . When male guinea pigs are inoculated intraperitoneally with blood from a case of endemic typhus , they develop fever and a characteristic scrotal inflammation. The scrotum becomes enlarged and the testes cannot be pushed into the abdomen. This is known as the Neil -Mooser reaction. It is positive with Rickettsia typhi (option D) and negative with Rickettsia prowazekii. The image below shows the rat flea , Xenopsylla cheopis .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Multiple inmates at a prison are suspected to have epidemic typhus following an arthropod infestation . Which of the following vectors is implicated in the spread of this disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Louse (image B), Pediculus humanus corporis, transmits epidemic typhus . Gaol fever/ Jail fever/ epidemic typhus is caused by Rickettsia prowazekii.308

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man from Kashmir presents with fever, chills and rash for 1 week . The rash appeared on the 5th day of the fever starting from the trunk and progressing to the limbs. Epidemic typhus is suspected . Which of the following statements is incorrect about the disease ?

options.b: Brill-Zinsser disease is a recrudescent form
options.c: Rash is present on palms and soles

mcqs.explanation: Epidemic typhus rash spares the palms and soles . Epidemic typhus , caused by Rickettsia prowazekii, is transmitted by the louse Pediculus humanus corporis. There is no transovarial transmission of R. prowazekii. The disease spreads through infected louse feces deposited when the louse feeds on the human host. It is commonly seen in poor unhygienic or cold conditions. Epidemic typhus starts with fever and chills. A characteristic rash appears on the fourth or fifth day, starting on the trunk and spreading over the limbs but sparing the face , palms, and soles . In some patients who recover from epidemic typhus , the rickettsiae may remain latent in the lymphoid tissues or organs for years. Such latent infection may, at times , be reactivated leading to recrudescent typhus (Brill-Zinsser disease ). Transovarial transmission refers to passing on the disease -causing bacteria from parent arthropod to offspring arthropod. It occurs with Orientia tsutsugamushi , Rickettsia rickettsii, R. conorii and R. akari . Note : Rash on palms and soles is typically described in Rocky Mountain spotted fever, secondary syphilis and hand, foot, and mouth disease The image below shows the rash of epidemic typhus .309

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: What is the drug of choice for scrub typhus ?
mcqs.explanation: The drug of choice for scrub typhus is doxycycline . To treat scrub typhus , oral doxycycline 100 mg is given twice daily for 7–15 days. In the case of pregnant women, oral azithromycin 500 mg for 3 days may be used as doxycycline is contraindicated in pregnancy. Scrub typhus is a rickettsial infection caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi . The vector is a trombiculid mite. Humans are infected when they are bitten by the mite larvae known as chiggers . The incubation period is 1- 3 weeks . Patients develop a characteristic eschar at the site of the mite bite , along with regional lymphadenopathy and maculopapular rash. It can be associated with fever, headache , myalgia, meningoencephalitis , myocarditis, and pneumonia. Serologic assays are used for diagnosis. Weil-Felix reaction is a heterophile agglutination reaction used for diagnosis, wherein the sera are tested for agglutinins to the O antigens of Proteus strains OX19, OX2, and OXK . OXK alone is agglutinated in scrub typhus .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old man came with complaints of fever and a skin lesion as shown below . He gives a history of hiking in scrub forests a week prior, where he suffered an insect bite . On examination, there is regional lymphadenopathy and a maculopapular rash. Which of the following arthropods is involved in the spread of this disease ?
mcqs.explanation: A history of contact with scrub vegetation with fever, regional lymphadenopathy , maculopapular rash, and eschar at the bite site is suggestive of scrub typhus . Scrub typhus is caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi and transmitted by trombiculid mite. Doxycycline 100mg BD for 7-14 days is the drug of choice for treatment of scrub typhus in adults . In case of pregnant women and children, azithromycin or chloramphenicol may be preferred where doxycycline is relatively contraindicated .310

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A wildlife photographer presents with a blackish lesion at the site of an insect bite from a few days back. He also gives a history of fever. A positive Weil-Felix test with OX K agglutinins was observed. What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: In the above clinical scenario, a history of insect bite followed by the development of a characteristic eschar at the site of the bite and a positive Weil-Felix test with OX K agglutinins suggests a diagnosis of scrub typhus . Weil-Felix reaction is a heterophile agglutination reaction, wherein the sera are tested for agglutinins to the O antigens of certain Proteus strains OX 19, OX 2, and OX K. The basis of the test is sharing an alkali stable carbohydrate antigen by some Rickettsiae and by some strains of Proteus.DISEASE OX 1 OX 2 OX K Epidemic typhus +++ + - Endemic typhus +++ +/- - Rocky Mountain spotted fev er ++ ++ - Scrub typhus - - +++ Rickettsial pox --- Trench fever --- Q fever ---

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A veterinarian presents with new-onset mitral regurgitation and fever. An echo reveals valve vegetations and blood cultures show no growth . Q fever is suspected . Which of the following statements is false regarding the organism implicated ?
mcqs.explanation: Coxiella burnetii is the causative organism of Q fever. It is transmitted by ixodid ticks in animals; however, it is not transmitted to humans via ticks. Coxiella burnetii is a filterable , obligate intracellular pathogen . They are gram-negative but are better stained with Gimenez, Giemsa stains. They are heat resistant and hence survive Holder's method of pasteurization . Q fever is a zoonosis and the primary source of human infection are infected cattle , sheep , and goats. It spreads through the inhalational route. Veterinarians are at higher risk due to increased exposure . Acute disease resembles influenza, nonbacterial (atypical ) pneumonia, and hepatitis . Chronic disease presents as culture -negative bacterial endocarditis in patients with valvular heart disease .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient presents with redness of the eye and foreign body sensation. On examination, there is follicular hypertrophy in the lower lids and moderately abundant exudates . Chlamydial infection is suspected . Which strains could have caused this condition?

options.b: Serotypes A, B, Ba and C

mcqs.explanation: Redness , foreign body sensation with follicular hypertrophy in the lower lids and moderately abundant exudates suggests inclusion conjunctivitis which is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serotypes D to K.311 Inclusion conjunctivitis is a type of acute follicular conjunctivitis caused by C. trachomatis serotypes D to K. The infection is transmitted to the eye from genitals , or contaminated swimming pools . Patients present with foreign body sensation, redness and mucopurulent discharge . On examination, there is acute follicular hypertrophy of the lower palpebral conjunctiva and fornix, non-tender pre-auricularlymphadenopathy and superficial keratitis in upper half of cornea. C. trachomatis is a Gram-negative , obligate intracellular bacteria. It cannot produce ATP . It causes a variety of human diseases (ocular and genitourinary) and has two main biological variants : • TRIC biovar which causes trachoma inclusion conjunctivitis (TRIC biovar ). This is further divided into 12 serological variants : • A, B, Ba, C serovars which cause blinding or endemic trachoma • D to K servovars which cause inclusion conjunctivitis • LGV biovar (L1 , L2 , L3 serotypes ) which causes lymphogranuloma venereum

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A thick, yellowish discharge is noted from the eyes of a five-day-old neonate in the step -down ward during rounds. An iodine-stained smear of the exudates is positive for large cytoplasmic inclusions as shown in the image. Which of the following is false about the organism responsible for the above condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of a thick yellowish discharge from the eye showing iodine-stained inclusion bodies is suggestive of inclusion conjunctivitis caused by Chlamydia trachomatis. As chlamydia is a bacteria, it possesses both DNA and RNA. Chlamydiae are obligate intracellular organisms that produce basophilic inclusion bodies . They are filterable like viruses. They are called energy parasites as they lack enzymes for ATP synthesis . They cannot grow on artificial media but can grow on cell lines like McCoy , HeLa, or the yolk sac of the chick embryo. Chlamydiae occur in two forms, the elementary body and the reticulate body. The extracellular , infective form is called the elementary body. The intracellular, non-infective, growing, and replicative form is called the reticulate body. These are found inside a membrane-bound compartment called the inclusion body which can be visualized within infected epithelial cells by iodine or Giemsa stain. The cell wall of the reticulate body is fragile and pliable , leading to pleomorphism .312

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A poultry worker was admitted to ICU with severe pneumonia. Bronchoalveolar lavage was done; it showed Levinthal Cole Lillie bodies . Which of the following is the causative organism for the above condition?
mcqs.explanation: Pneumonia in a poultry worker with Levinthal-Cole-Lillie bodies on bronchoalveolar lavage specimens is suggestive of psittacosis . Levinthal-Cole-Lillie bodies are inclusion bodies of Chlamydia psittaci seen in infected cells including alveolar macrophages from patients suffering from psittacosis . C. psittaci can be transmitted to humans by direct contact with infected birds or by inhalation of aerosols from avian feather dust . Psittacosis presents with fever, chills, muscular aches and pains, severe headache , hepatosplenomegaly and gastrointestinal symptoms . Severe pneumonia may develop . It is treated with tetracycline .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient presented with painful swellings on both sides of the groin as shown in the image. The clinician suspects lymphogranuloma venereum. Which is the most common serovar causing the above condition?
mcqs.explanation: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV ) is caused most commonly by Chlamydia trachomatis LGV serovar L2 . LGV is a sexually transmitted disease , characterized by suppurative inguinal adenitis .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: What is the incubation period of lymphogranuloma venereum?
mcqs.explanation: The incubation period of Lymphogranuloma venereum ranges from 10 -30 days. Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1 , L2, and L3 cause lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV ). The most common presentation is the inguinal syndrome, which is characterized by painful inguinal lymphadenopathy .313

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Lesion scrapings from a genital ulcer show numerous polymorphs , but no bacteria. Which of the following is the most appropriate culture medium for organisms responsible for the above condition?
mcqs.explanation: Clinical scrapings from a genital ulcer showing polymorphs in the absence of bacteria is suggestive of chlamydial infection and the most appropriate culture medium is McCoy cells (human synovial carcinoma cell line). C. trachomatis is a small gram-negative bacterium and an obligate intracellular parasite that appears as an intracytoplasmic inclusion body. The gram stain of the cervical smear would show leucocytes but no organisms. Hence , selective culture media like the McCoy cells culture is used to isolate the organism. Option B: Thayer–Martin agar is used for isolation of Neisseria spp . Option C: Robertson's cooked meat is used for the culture of anaerobes, especially Clostridia Option D: Pleuropneumonia -like organisms (PPLO ) broth is used to culture Mycoplasma spp . and Ureaplasma spp . Note : Abnormal urethral gram stain showing >10 PMNs/1000 \305~ field in women with dysuria but without coliform bacteriuria supports the diagnosis of chlamydial urethritis.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old woman presented with a 3-day history of mucopurulent cervical discharge . Gram staining of the discharge revealed numerous pus cells , but no organisms. What is the investigation of choice for the diagnosis of this infection ?
mcqs.explanation: Mucopurulent cervical discharge for 3 days is suggestive of acute cervicitis. As gram stain does not show any organism, gonococcal infection is less likely. In this case, Chlamydia trachomatis is the most likely organism. For C. trachomatis, the investigation of choice is the nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT). NAATs are the most sensitive tests to detect chlamydia. These tests also have a high specificity comparable to culture , and in contrast to culture , do not depend on viable pathogens . Therefore, NAATs are generally considered the test of choice for chlamydia and have replaced culture as the diagnostic gold standard. Mucopurulent cervicitis is the inflammation of the columnar epithelium and subepithelium of the endocervix in women. Its commonly caused by Neiserria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following microbes is also referred to as Eaton's agent ?
mcqs.explanation: Eaton's agent refers to Mycoplasma pneumoniae . Eaton was the first to isolate Mycoplasma pneumoniae . Because it was filterable , it was considered to be a virus previously . It was formerly known as PPLO – Pleuro pneumonia-like organism.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 20 -year-old military recruit presented with fever, sore throat, and non-productive cough which showed no improvement with beta -lactam antibiotics. X-ray showed peribronchial pneumonia with thickened bronchial markings . Primary atypical pneumonia is suspected . Which of the following statements is false regarding the organism responsible for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: 314 The above clinical scenario of fever, non-productive cough , no improvement with beta -lactam antibiotics along with X-ray features showing peribronchial pneumonia with thickened bronchial markings is suggestive of Mycoplasma pneumonia, also known as primary atypical pneumonia or walking pneumonia. Mycoplasmas are not obligate intracellular parasites . They are free -living bacteria devoid of cell walls. They are highly pleomorphic , with no fixed shape or size. Because of their plasticity , they can pass through bacterial filters and have often been mistaken for viruses. Mycoplasmas do not possess spores , flagella , or fimbria. Some species exhibit gliding motility . Mycoplasmas are gram-negative, but are better stained by Giemsa stain.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Diene 's method of staining is used for which of the following organisms?
mcqs.explanation: Diene 's method is used for mycoplasma. Mycoplasma shows a 'fried-egg ' colony on Diene 's method of staining. The central dark bluish area represents the area of mycoplasmal down growth whereas the pale blue periphery indicates superficial growth of mycoplasma on the agar.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Mycoplasma is inherently resistant to which of the following antibiotics?
mcqs.explanation: Mycoplasma is inherently resistant to beta -lactam antibiotics. Mycoplasma lack cell wall, and therefore , are inherently resistant to beta -lactam antibiotics as these drugs act on the cell wall.315

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Identify the organism.
mcqs.explanation: .The given image shows Treponema pallidum demonstrated by dark ground microscopy. Treponemes are short, slender with regular and sharp spirals. Option A: Leptospira have a large number of closely wound spirals and characteristic hooked ends as shown in the image below324 Option C: Borrelia are large with irregular and wide open coils. Option D: Helicobacter pylori is a spiral rod (bacilli) that is not classified as a spirochete .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old truck driver presented with a painless ulcer in the genital area. On examination , a single ulcer with an indurated base was found. An image of the tissue section is shown below . Identify the staining method .
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows Treponema pallidum demonstrated by Levaditi's method . Single painless ulcer with indurated base points towards the diagnosis of syphilis . Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum, a spirochete bacillus . It is a sexually transmitted infection . Intrauterine transmission can lead to congenital syphilis . It shows corkscrew motility which can be demonstrated by darkfield microscopy. Treponema can be stained by silver impregnation methods . • Fontana's method is used on smear • Levaditi's method is used for tissue sections The clinical manifestations of syphilis include : Primary syphilis : The typical primary chancre usually begins as a single painless papule that rapidly becomes eroded and usually becomes indurated , with a characteristic cartilaginous consistency on palpation of the edge and base of the ulcer. Inguinal lymphadenopathy is bilateral and may occur with anal as well as with genital chancres. The chancre generally heals within 4–6 weeks (range, 2–12 weeks ), but lymphadenopathy may persist for months. Secondary syphilis : The various features include mucocutaneous or cutaneous lesions and generalized nontender lymphadenopathy. macular, papular, papulosquamous , and occasionally pustular syphilides . Other features of secondary syphilis include sore throat, fever, weight loss, malaise, anorexia, headache , and meningismus. Ocular findings associated with secondary (or later/ unknown-stage ) syphilis include pupillary abnormalities and optic neuritis as well as the325 classic iritis or uveitis. Latent syphilis : Early latent syphilis is limited to the first year after infection , whereas late latent syphilis is defined as that of 1 year's duration (or of unknown duration). T. pallidum may still seed the bloodstream intermittently during the latent stage , and latent syphilis in a pregnant woman may infect the fetus in utero. Neurosyphilis : The major clinical categories of symptomatic neurosyphilis include meningeal , meningovascular, and parenchymatous syphilis . Cardiovascular syphilis : Cardiovascular involvement results in uncomplicated aortitis, aortic regurgitation , saccular aneurysm (usually of the ascending aorta), or coronary ostial stenosis . Congenital syphilis : The earliest manifestations of congenital syphilis include rhinitis, or "snuffles "; mucocutaneous lesions , bone changes , including periostitis detectable by x-ray examination of long bones; hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy , anemia, jaundice , thrombocytopenia , and leukocytosis . Serologic tests for syphilis recommended by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC): • Screening or diagnosis (RPR or VDRL ), • Quantitative measurement of antibody to assess clinical syphilis activity or to monitor response to therapy (RPR or VDRL ) • Confirmation of a syphilis diagnosis in a patient with a reactive RPR or VDRL test (FTA-ABS, TPHA, EIA/CIA) Treatment of syphilis is with 2.4 million units of intramuscular benzathine penicillin .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: What type of motility is shown by Treponema pallidum ?
mcqs.explanation: Treponema pallidum show corkscrew motility , i.e movement by rotation around the long axis. The characteristic feature of spirochetes is the presence of endoflagella , situated between the outer membrane and cell wall, that facilitates this movement.326

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old pregnant lady tests VDRL positive at her 1st-trimester antenatal check-up. An FTA-ABS confirms the diagnosis. Which of the following is a false statement about the organism causing this disease ?

options.a: It cannot be cultured in vitro
options.b: Endoflagella is in the periplasmic space .
options.c: Humans are the only known natural hosts

mcqs.explanation: VDRL positive status is suggestive of syphilis , caused by Treponema pallidum . Fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption (FTA-ABS) is a confirmatory test . Reiter's strain is a cultivable , non-pathogenic treponeme , showing morphological and antigenic similarities with T.pallidum. It is widely used as the antigen in group-specific treponemal tests for the diagnosis of syphilis . Nichol's strain is virulent and non-cultivable in artificial media. However, it can be grown in cell culture through serial passage in live rabbit testes .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient had a solitary, painless penile ulcer 2 months back. Now, he presents with a generalized maculopapular rash over the body. What is the sensitivity of VDRL at this stage of the disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The sensitivity of VDRL is 100 % in secondary syphilis . History of solitary painless ulcer with a generalized maculopapular rash is consistent with secondary syphilis . The VDRL test becomes positive 4–5 weeks after exposure to T. pallidum and 1–2 weeks after the appearance of the chancre. The VDRL test is a highly sensitive test. The sensitivity of the test depends on the stage of the disease : • Primary syphilis - 60–75% • Secondary syphilis - % • High antibody titers may be found in patients developing gummatous lesions and neurovascular or cardiovascular complications . • Tertiary syphilis - usually negative • Negative test :327 • Early primary syphilis • Latent acquired syphilis • Late congenital syphilis Secondary syphilis is the most infective stage in the course of the illness . The patient may present with a roseolar or papular skin rash, condyloma lata, and mucous patches . The image below shows lesions of secondary syphilis .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a false statement regarding the serological tests of syphilis ?

options.a: Rapid plasma reagin test is a group specific treponemal test
options.b: VDRL test is the test of choice for response to therapy
options.c: VDRL is the test of choice for examining CSF
options.d: Treponemal tests are likely to remain reactive even after adequate therapy

mcqs.explanation: RPR is a non-specific test . It uses the VDRL antigen (cardiolipin) containing carbon particles . Hence , results can be seen by the naked eye , whereas VDRL requires a microscope for visualization of flocculation . The test of choice for monitoring response to treatment and for examining CSF is VDRL The test of choice for syphilis screening is RPR . After treatment , in early syphilis , • Non-treponemal tests - titers decline or become non-reactive • Treponemal tests - remain reactive For diagnosis of syphilis , a 2 test approach is used i.e., screening with an NTT (non-treponemal test ) which includes either VDRL or RPR . Confirmation of syphilis is done by a treponemal test , most commonly by TPHA (Treponema pallidum hemagglutination test ). Follow -up is done using NTT (as treponemal tests remains positive for years after treatment ).

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 55 -year old man was brought to the OPD with complaints of rapid decline in cognition, impaired position, and vibratory sense . There is a history of sporadic short-term relationships with many promiscuous sexual partners. Romberg's sign is positive and bilateral Argyll Robertson pupils are seen on checking for pupillary reflex . Which of the following is the investigation of choice ?
mcqs.explanation: 328 The clinical scenario given above with a positive sexual history, Romberg test , and Argyll Robertson pupils is suggestive of neurosyphilis . The investigation of choice for neurosyphilis is VDRL . The CSF VDRL test is highly specific and, when reactive, is considered diagnostic of neurosyphilis . Involvement of the CNS in syphilis is detected by examination of CSF for: • Mononuclear pleocytosis (>5 white blood cells /�ML). • Increased protein concentration (>45 mg/dL). • CSF VDRL reactivity.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: You treated a case of secondary syphilis with a single dose of benzathine penicillin -G 2.4 million IU IM. What follow -up advice would you give for the assessment of the patient 's response to treatment ?

options.a: Follow up with VDRL after 6 months and 12 months
options.b: Follow up with VDRL after 3 months and 6 months
options.c: Follow up with TPHA after 6 months and 12 months
options.d: Follow up with TPHA after 3 months and 6 months

mcqs.explanation: The investigation used to assess response to treatment in syphilis is VDRL . In the case of secondary syphilis , follow -up VDRL should be done at 6 months and 12 months. VDRL and RPR become negative after adequate treatment whereas specific treponemal tests remain positive indefinitely despite treatment . Guidelines for follow up: • Patients with primary or secondary syphilis should be examined 6 and 12 months after treatment. • Patients with latent or late syphilis should be examined at 6, , and 24 months after treatment .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman at 10 weeks of gestational age tested VDRL positive but negative for specific treponemal tests . What is your interpretation ?
mcqs.explanation: Pregnancy can give rise to false -positive VDRL . Biological false -positive (BFP) reactions are defined as positive reactions obtained in non-specific treponemal tests (RPR , VDRL ) with negative results in specific treponemal tests , in the absence of past or present treponemal infections and not caused by technical faults .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 2-month-old infant presented with a runny nose and bullous lesions on the skin and legs . Her X-ray (given below ) showed features suggestive of periostitis . Which of the following is the initial investigation of choice ?
mcqs.explanation: The newborn baby has characteristic signs and symptoms of congenital syphilis . Periostitis is a hallmark of skeletal manifestation. VDRL or RPR is the initial investigation of choice in congenital syphilis . The earliest manifestations of congenital syphilis include rhinitis, or "snuffles "; mucocutaneous lesions , bone changes , including periostitis detectable by x-ray examination of long bones; hepatosplenomegaly , lymphadenopathy, anemia, jaundice , thrombocytopenia , and leukocytosis .
