mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about Japanese encephalitis ?

options.d: Vaccinating pigs is helpful in disease control

mcqs.explanation: Humans are the dead -end hosts for the Japanese encephalitis virus.425 Option A: The disease is transmitted by Culex tritaeniorhynchus and Culex vishnui (common in India) species. Option B: Herons act as reservoir hosts and pigs as amplifier hosts . Option D: The control measures include mosquito control, locating piggeries away from the human dwellings and vaccinating pigs. The image below shows the life cycle of the Japanese B encephalitis virus.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A mother brings her 9-month-old child for vaccination against Japanese encephalitis . Which of the following statements is false regarding this vaccine?

options.a: Two doses are recommended at age 9 months and 18 months
options.b: Inactivated vero cell culture is given 4 weeks apart
options.c: Live vaccine SA 14-14-2 is administered intramuscularly
options.d: The live attenuated vaccine can be given to adolescents

mcqs.explanation: Live SA 14-14-2 strain of Japanese encephalitis (JE) vaccine is administered subcutaneously . Types of JE Vaccines:SA 14-14-2 cell culture derive d vaccine Inactivated vero cell culture derived Kolar (Jenvac 82156 XY ) Live attenuated Inactivated Route of administratio n Subcutaneous Intramuscular Intramuscul ar Dosage 2 doses 2 doses 2 doses Duration between dose s At ages 9months and 16-18 m onths 4 weeks apart 4 weeks apar t Ages 9 months, 16-18 months, ado lescents and non-immune ad ults up to 15 years up to 18 year s426

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient presents with fever, arthralgia, and pain behind the eyes for 3 days. On examination , she has the following rash. Lab reports show thrombocytopenia and leucopenia . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with the symptoms and the rash suggests dengue fever. It presents with sudden -onset fever, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, arthralgia, and a rash. The rash in dengue appears as white islands on a red sea due to erythema with petechiae . The alternative name for dengue , breakbone fever, comes from the associated muscle and joint pains. Suspected cases of dengue are confirmed by the presence of NS1 antigen or IgM antibodies . The treatment of dengue is supportive with hydration taking top priority.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old wildlife photographer presents with sudden onset of fever, headache , and myalgia. On examination, you notice gingival bleeds and conjunctival hemorrhages. He recently visited a forest in Karnataka that has a large population of monkeys. Which of these is the vector for the suspected disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario with exposure to monkeys, fever, myalgia, headache , conjunctival hemorrhage and gingival bleeds is suggestive of Kyasanur forest disease (KFD), which is transmitted by ticks (Haemophysalis spinigera). It is endemic to the forests of Karnataka and Kerala. The clinical features include : • Fever • Headache • Conjunctivitis • Myalgia • Meningoencephalitis • Hemorrhagic symptoms - hemorrhages in skin, mucosa and gastrointestinal bleeds . The case fatality rate is about 5 percent. Monkeys are amplifier hosts , rodents are reservoirs and humans are incidental hosts . A killed KFD virus vaccine was used in a small field trial and appeared to provide some degree of protection .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man presents with delirium, fever, jaundice , and a hemorrhagic diathesis . The patient is agitated and has had no urine output in the last 6 hours. On investigation, there is azotemia and elevated liver enzymes . A viral disease with the vector shown below is suspected . Which of the following inclusion bodies may be seen ?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows the Aedes aegypti mosquito and the clinical scenario with hepatic and renal dysfunction with delirium points towards a diagnosis of yellow fever. Torres bodies are amorphous eosinophilic nuclear inclusions associated with yellow fever, a disease caused by the Flavivirus . Inclusion bodies are structures with distinct sizes and shapes that are seen in virus-infected cells under light microscopy. Note : Dengue hemorrhagic fever can be a differential diagnosis, but there are no inclusion bodies seen in dengue .427

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: What is the duration of validity of 17D vaccination ?
mcqs.explanation: 17D vaccine (yellow fever vaccine) is valid for a lifetime , beginning 10 days after vaccination. According to the amendment in 2016 to International Health Regulations 2005 , the validity of the related international certificate of vaccination against yellow fever has been changed from ten (10) years to the lifespan of the person (traveler) vaccinated. It is a live-attenuated vaccine derived from the 'Asibi strain', administered subcutaneously . Immunity after a single dose is long-lasting and provides lifetime protection . It is thermolabile . Vaccination is compulsory for travel to and from endemic areas. In India, 17D is manufactured at the Central Research Institute , Kasauli .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A pest control technician with a history of fever, vomiting, hematuria, and decreased urine output was diagnosed with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome. Which of the following statements is false about the causative virus?

options.a: Hantaviruses are the natural pathogens of rodents
options.b: Transmission primarily occurs by Culex mosquitoes
options.c: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome presents with pulmonary edema

mcqs.explanation: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is caused by Hantaviruses. They are rodent-borne viruses that are transmitted by inhalation of the virus contained in dried excreta of rodents. They are the natural pathogens of rodents like mice, rats, and voles. HFRS presents with acute kidney injury, hemorrhages, fever, and circulatory collapse . Hantaviruses can also cause Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome. Note : In Aug 2016 , The International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses (ICTV ), has renamed and moved the genus Hantavirus to Orthohantavirus.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An epidemic of paralytic poliomyelitis occurs in a non-immune population . Which among the following strains of poliovirus is the most common cause of this?
mcqs.explanation: Type 1 poliovirus is the most common cause of epidemics in populations . Poliovirus strains have been classified into 3 types : • Type 1- most common and causes most of the epidemics . • Type 2- endemic infections . • Type 3- epidemics but rarer than type 1. Immunity is type -specific . Note :- Type 2 is declared eradicated in September , 2015 and Type 3 is declared eradicated in October , 2019

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old girl is brought to the pediatrics OPD with a history of lower -limb paralysis and the following deformity . Which of the following will be the most common form of presentation of this illness ?
mcqs.explanation: 428 The given case scenario with a history of lower limb paralysis and deformity is suggestive of poliomyelitis . The given image shows deformity of the right lower limb, namely hyperextension at the knee joint and muscle wasting . Inapparent infection is the most common (90-95%) presentation of polio. Only seroconversion occurs without any clinical manifestations . Option B: Abortive poliomyelitis is associated with primary viremia and presents as fever, headache , sore throat, and malaise lasting for 1-5 days. Option C: Paralytic poliomyelitis occurs following minor illness , characterized by biphasic fever with headache, stiff neck, and flaccid paralysis. Option D: In non-paralytic poliomyelitis, the disease does not progress beyond the stage of aseptic meningitis .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 20 -year-old unimmunized patient presents to you with complaints of weakness of lower limbs, inability to pass urine, and fever, for 3 days. His stool samples were sent to the district lab to confirm the diagnosis. Which region of the spinal cord will primarily be affected in these cases ?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario of fever, lower limb paralysis, urinary retention , and stool samples being sent for diagnosis, is suggestive of paralytic polio. The anterior horn cells of the spinal cord are primarily affected , causing acute flaccid paralysis. Posterior horns and intermediate columns/lateral horns may also be involved to some extent . In the central nervous system , the virus multiplies selectively in the neurons and destroys them. The earliest change is the degeneration of Nissl bodies (chromatolysis). Nuclear changes follow . Note : Fecal samples of all cases of acute flaccid paralysis are obtained (2 samples ) and transported to the laboratory within 72 hours of collection at 4–8\260C or frozen at -20 \260C. This is known as the reverse cold chain and is done as a part of gold standard polio surveillance/acute flaccid paralysis surveillance (AFP surveillance).

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding vaccination against polio?

options.a: Sabin type has the live attenuated virus
options.b: OPV should not be administered to immunocompromised persons
options.c: Salk vaccine is associated with mutations that lead to reversal of virulence
options.d: Both OPV and IPV induce humoral IgG

mcqs.explanation: Salk type is the killed vaccine, hence there is no risk of mutation that can lead to a reversal of virulence . There are two types of vaccines for polio - IPV (inactivated poliovirus vaccine) and OPV (oral poliovirus vaccine).

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following strains of poliovirus have been eradicated worldwide ?
mcqs.explanation: Type 2 and 3 have been eradicated worldwide . Type 2: In September 2015 , WHO declared the eradication of the wild type 2 poliovirus strain. In India, the last type 2 infection was detected in 1999 . Type 3: It has not been detected anywhere in the world since November 2012 . On World Polio Day in October 2019 , the type 3 virus was declared to be eradicated worldwide .429 The only circulating strain is type 1.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 68-year-old woman presented with acute chest pain which was stabbing type in nature. The pain is spasmodic and associated with fever spikes . There's an outbreak of coxsackievirus B in her community. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario with stabbing type chest pain which is spasmodic in nature, associated with fever spikes , and history of an outbreak of coxsackievirus B is suggestive of Bornholm disease or epidemic pleurodynia . Symptoms include paroxysms of acute pleuritic chest pain associated with fever spikes . Involved muscles are tender . Chest X-ray is usually normal . Most cases occur during epidemics of coxsackievirus B. The disease is named after the Danish island of Bornholm where early cases occurred. The treatment is non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents or hot fomentation of the involved muscles . Other diseases associated with coxsackievirus B: • Neonatal myocarditis and pericarditis • Juvenile diabetes mellitus • Orchitis • Severe disseminated congenital infection- hepatitis , meningoencephalitis , adrenocortical involvement

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old boy presents with headache , fever, and vomiting. On examination, you observe the following . He is diagnosed with herpangina. Which group of viruses causes the same?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows palatal ulcers in herpangina. It is caused by the coxsackievirus A, a large subgroup of the enteroviruses . Herpangina or vesicular pharyngitis is characterized by grayish- white papulovesicular lesions on an erythematous base that ulcerate . These are present on: • Soft palate • Anterior pillars of tonsils • Uvula • Posterior oropharynx It is a common clinical manifestation of coxsackievirus A infection in children, but it can also be caused by coxsackievirus B, echoviruses , or enterovirus 71. Treatment is usually only supportive , as the disease is self -limiting and usually runs its course in less than a week .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms causes the following disease ?
mcqs.explanation: 430 The image shows vesicles on the palms, soles , and oral mucosa, consistent with hand-foot-and-mouth disease . It is caused by coxsackievirus. Hand-foot-and-mouth disease (HFMD) is an exanthematous fever affecting mainly young children, characterized by oral and pharyngeal ulcerations and a vesicular rash of the palms and soles that may spread to the arms and legs . Vesicles heal without crusting, which clinically differentiates them from the vesicles of herpesviruses and poxviruses. It is usually a benign illness resolving in 1-2 weeks . Coxsackie A16, A9, and B 1-3 are common causative agents . Other diseases caused by Coxsackie A virus: • Aseptic meningitis associated with a maculopapular rash. • Herpangina • Minor respiratory infections

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old presented with eye pain, watering of eyes , and increased sensitivity to light . On examination , you see the following . Which of the following viruses can cause this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis (AHC) caused mainly by Enterovirus 70 and Coxsackievirus A24 variant (CA24v ). It is characterized by sudden swelling , congestion , and watering of the eyes . Subconjunctival hemorrhages are a characteristic feature and corneal involvement may occur transiently. There is no treatment currently available . The disease is self limiting, and resolves within a five to seven-day period. Note : Acute follicular conjunctivitis is caused by Adenovirus serotypes 3, 4, 7 and 11 .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 42-year-old woman presented with fever, joint pains, and headache . Chik sign (image given below ) is present on the patient 's nose. Which of the following vectors transmits the etiological agent ?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario with fever, joint pain, headache , and Chik sign is suggestive of chikungunya which is transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes . Chikungunya presents with sudden onset of fever, crippling joint pain, lymphadenopathy , and conjunctivitis. The fever is typically biphasic with a period of remission after 1–6 days. Nose pigmentation is striking in cases of Chikungunya fever and is termed as Chik sign No animal reservoir has been identified. Note : Although Chikungunya is transmitted by both Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus , A.Aegypti is considered primary vector of transmission for Chikungunya.431

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A newborn baby has a characteristic rash as shown below . On examination, bilateral pearly white nuclear cataracts are noted , and a continuous murmur is auscultated . What family does the virus implicated in this syndrome belong to?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario of bilateral nuclear cataracts, blueberry muffin rash (image), and patent ductus arteriosus(murmur) suggest congenital rubella syndrome. Rubella virus belongs to the family Matonaviridae. Rubella virus previously belonged to family Togaviridae, but has been recently changed to family Matonaviridae by the International Committee on the Taxonomy of viruses (ICTV ), making it the sole genus under the family Matonaviridae. Option A: Rhabdoviridae includes Rabies virus.438 Option B: Filoviridae includes Marburg virus and Ebola virus. Option D: Calciviridae includes Norwalk agent .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A brain biopsy done at the time of autopsy shows spongiform encephalopathy . Which of the following is unlikely to be the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Spongiform encephalopathy is a feature of prion disease . Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is not a prion disease . SSPE is a rare and chronic form of progressive brain inflammation caused by a persistent infection with the measles virus. Slow virus diseases are characterized by a long asymptomatic period , often months or years in duration, between the introduction of the infectious agent and the appearance of clinical illness . Examples : AIDS, Kuru, CJD, SSPE, PML CJD, Kuru, and mad cow disease are classified under slow virus diseases which are caused by prions.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which strain of the Ebola virus has the highest case fatality rate?
mcqs.explanation: The Zaire strain has a case fatality rate of 90% There are five identified Ebola virus strains, four of which are known to cause disease in humans: • Ebola virus (Zaire ebolavirus) • Sudan virus (Sudan ebolavirus) • Ta\357 Forest virus (Ta\357 Forest ebolavirus) • Bundibugyo virus (Bundibugyo ebolavirus).439 The fifth , Reston virus (Reston ebolavirus), has caused disease in nonhuman primates, but not in humans. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus, Zaire ebolavirus, and Sudan ebolavirus have been associated with large outbreaks in Africa. The strain that caused the 2014 –2016 West African outbreak belongs to the Zaire ebolavirus species .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a leading cause of diarrheal death in children?
mcqs.explanation: Rotavirus is a leading cause of diarrheal death among children in the developing world. Rotavirus infections occur in most children below the age of 5 years and are most frequent between 6-24 months of age . Neonatal infections are common but are often asymptomatic or mild. Vaccines for rotavirus : RotaTeq and Rotarix , given orally. Note : Viruses that can cause diarrhoea in children include : • Rotavirus (most common) • Norwalk virus • Adenovirus- types 40 and 41 • Astrovirus • Coronavirus • Sapovirus The image below shows an electron micrograph image of the Rotavirus .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An 18-year-old went on an exchange program to Singapore. An adventurous eater , she tried clams and oysters on a cruise ship. 2 days later, she developed fever, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. What is the causative agent ?
mcqs.explanation: 440 The clinical scenario describes a case of Norwalk infection . It is the most common cause of diarrhea in older children and adults . They occur in group settings such as banquet halls, cruise ships , dormitories, and campgrounds, where outbreak sources are usually contaminated food and/or water. Potential sources of contaminated food include shellfish such as clams and oysters , which are contaminated by water. Clinical features are nausea, vomiting, watery diarrhea, abdominal pain. Symptoms of gastroenteritis develop 12 to 48 hours after being exposed to norovirus . The image below is an electron micrograph of Norovirus (Norwalk virus).

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old lady with recent onset , progressive dementia comes with myoclonus . The brain imaging is shown below . What biochemical component is responsible for this disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical features and imaging suggest a diagnosis of Creutzfeldt -Jakob disease (CJD), caused by prions. Prions are composed of protein. These are infectious protein particles that lack any nucleic acid. They are filterable like viruses but are resistant to agents of sterilization. Prion proteins have two isoforms: • PrPSc is the prion protein that causes disease . • PrPc is the normal prion protein, found in human cells . Prions cause diseases such as CJD, Kuru, Alzheimer's, Parkinson 's. Laboratory diagnosis of prion diseases : • Measurement of PrPSc by immunoassay • Brain MRI • Brain biopsy • Stress protein 14-3-3441 • Sequencing PRNP gene • Abnormal EEG

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old lady is admitted to the ICU with COVID -19. Which of the following statements is false regarding the organism causing it?

options.a: These viruses have club-shaped peplomers on their surface
options.d: It acts by binding to ACE1 and TMPRSS4 receptors

mcqs.explanation: The coronavirus spike protein binds to the ACE2 and TMPRSS2 receptors to enter the human cells . Coronaviruses are a group of spherical or pleomorphic enveloped RNA viruses having club or petal -shaped peplomers . Coronaviruses are named for the crown-like spikes on their surface . It spreads through coughing , sneezing, and close personal contact such as touching the mouth, nose . The virus is highly mutable and so vaccine prophylaxis for all strains is difficult . Coronaviruses cause upper respiratory tract infections , severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), and Middle Eastern respiratory syndrome (MERS). They spread by inhalation of the virus present in droplets or aerosols of respiratory secretions of the patients . Basic protective measures against the new coronavirus : (SARS-CoV-2) • Wash your hands frequently for at least 20 seconds . • Maintain social distancing- Maintain at least 1 meter distance between yourself and anyone who is coughing or sneezing • Avoid touching eyes , nose, and mouth • Practice respiratory hygiene - cover your mouth and nose with your bent elbow or tissue when you cough or sneeze , then dispose of the used tissue immediately . • If you have fever, cough , and difficulty breathing, seek medical care early • Stay informed and follow the advice given by your healthcare provider442

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A person who comes in contact with a case of coronavirus (COVID - 19) needs to be followed up for __________.
mcqs.explanation: A person who comes in contact with a coronavirus (COVID -19) case (confirmed or probable ) needs to be followed up for apperance of symptoms of coronavirus for the maximum incubation period of 14 days. Treatment: There is no specific antiviral treatment recommended for COVID -19. People with COVID -19 should receive supportive care to help relieve symptoms . For severe cases , treatment should include care to support vital organ functions. Basic protective measures against the new coronavirus : (SARS CoV 2) • Wash your hands frequently for atleast 20 seconds . • Maintain social distancing- Maintain at least 1 metre distance between yourself and anyone who is coughing or sneezing • Avoid touching eyes , nose and mouth • Practice respiratory hygiene - cover your mouth and nose with your bent elbow or tissue when you cough or sneeze , then dispose of the used tissue immediately . • If you have fever, cough and difficulty breathing, seek medical care early • Stay informed and follow advice given by your healthcare provider

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: In a patient undergoing testing for SARS-CoV, a FELUDA test is done. Which of the following statements is false about this technology ?

options.a: It is the acronym for FNCAS9 Editor Linked Uniform Detection Assay
options.b: Based on CRISPR gene editing technology
options.c: It is slower than RT PCR in detecting SARS-CoV
options.d: It uses CAS-9 protein to bind to the viral signature

mcqs.explanation: FELUDA is faster than RT -PCR in detecting SARS-CoV2 . FELUDA (FNCAS9 Editor Linked Uniform Detection Assay) is a newly approved method based on CRISPR gene -editing technology to identify and target the genetic material of SARS-CoV2 . The CRISPR technology uses a highly specific CAS9 protein to find and bind to the target Covid signature. This is then coupled with paper -strip chemistry to elicit a visual readout on a paper strip. It is a very affordable , sensitive (96%), and specific (98%) strip test which can detect viral genetic material within 45 minutes .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A confirmed case of which of the following viral haemorrhagic fevers was found in India?
mcqs.explanation: Crimean Congo hemorrhagic fever is a severe form of viral hemorrhagic fever, is caused by Nairovirus species . It is zoonotic in origin with ticks as vectors. The outbreak was caused due to person-to-person transmission in hospitals .443

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A woman presents with a positive urine pregnancy test , 1 month after taking the MMR vaccine. At the time of receiving the vaccine, she had been advised to avoid conception . What advice do you give her now?

options.c: Low risk ; termination of pregnancy may be considered
options.d: High risk of anomalies; serious consideration for termination

mcqs.explanation: In this case scenario, the doctor should advise the patient to wait and watch . The vaccine should not be administered during pregnancy. If pregnancy occurs within 28 days of immunization, the patient should be counseled on the theoretical risks for the fetus . Studies of over 200 women who had been inadvertently immunized with rubella vaccine during pregnancy showed that none of their offspring developed congenital rubella syndrome. Therefore, termination of pregnancy is probably not warranted.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: While working at a WHO outreach post in Africa, you conduct an educational program about the Zika virus. What family does this virus belong to?
mcqs.explanation: Zika virus belongs to the family Flaviviridae . It is classified by the International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses (ICTV ): • Family: Flaviviridae • Genus : Flavivirus • Species : Zika virus Zika virus is an RNA virus that is transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquito bite and by sexual contact. It causes microcephaly and is associated with Guillain-Barr \351 syndrome.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Zika virus is transmitted by:
mcqs.explanation: Zika virus may be transmitted by the bite of infected Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus . The symptoms of Zika virus disease include fever, rash, conjunctivitis, muscle and joint pain, malaise, or headache . These symptoms are mild and usually last for 2-7 days. Zika virus infection during pregnancy may cause lead to microcephaly or congenital Zika syndrome. The complications of Zika virus infection include Guillain-Barr \351 syndrome, neuropathy , and myelitis .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following features do not support a diagnosis of Zika fever?
mcqs.explanation: A petechial rash is not a primary feature of Zika virus infection . Though petechiae may rarely appear in Zika virus disease it is however not included in the CDC case definition of Zika virus disease . Petechial rash points towards a diagnosis of dengue fever while a maculopapular rash suggests a Zika virus disease . Zika virus infection is characterized by influenza-like clinical signs including fever, headache, and malaise. A maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, myalgia, and arthralgia usually accompany or follow those manifestations .444 The complications of Zika virus are: • Guillain-Barre syndrome • Fetal microcephaly in pregnant women.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The transplacental transmission of the organism given in the image which causes microcephaly is-
mcqs.explanation: The transplacental transmission of Zika virus given in the image causes microcephaly . The condition shown in the image is microcephaly . It is caused by Zika virus transmission from an infected pregnant mother to her child. Zika virus is a mosquito-borne Flavivirus mainly transmitted through Aedes aegypti . Symptoms are mild and usually last for 2-7 days. • Fever • Rash • Conjunctivitis • Muscle and joint pain • Malaise • Headache • In pregnancy- congenital Zika syndrome or microcephaly The complications of Zika virus infection include Guillain-Barr \351 syndrome, neuropathy , and myelitis . NCDC Delhi and the National Institute of Virology Pune, are the only institutes that have the capacity to provide the diagnosis in an acute febrile stage . RT -PCR is the standard test available for the diagnosis of Zika virus infection .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Tropical spastic paraparesis is caused by:
mcqs.explanation: is the causative agent of the neurodegenerative disorder HTLV -1-associated myelopathy or tropical spastic paraparesis (HAM/TSP). The condition resembles multiple sclerosis and is associated with progressive weakness of legs and lower body. The patients develop spastic paraparesis or paraplegia , hyperreflexia , ankle clonus, and extensor plantar response. The disease progresses slowly and takes the form of thoracic myelopathy . Other conditions caused by HTLV -1 include : • Adult T-cell leukemias and lymphomas (ATL) • Uveitis • Infective dermatitis445 • Arthritis • Sjo\037gren's syndrome

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: What family does the Nipah virus belong to?
mcqs.explanation: Nipah virus belongs to the family Paramyxoviridae . Togaviridae contains chikungunya virus. Flaviviridae contains yellow fever virus, dengue virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, hepatitis C virus, Zika virus Bunyaviridae contains sandfly fever virus, hantaviruses.446

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a component of the fungal cell wall?
mcqs.explanation: Chitin is a component of the fungal cell wall. General characteristics of Fungi: • They are unicellular /multicellular eukaryotes . • The cell wall contains chitin, glucan, mannan and other polysaccharides . • The cytoplasmic membrane contains ergosterol . • They possess true nuclei with the nuclear membrane and paired chromosomes. • They divide sexually , asexually or by both. Raymond Sabouraud is known as the Father of Mycology .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a yeast ?
mcqs.explanation: Cryptococcus is a yeast .458 Option A: Candida is a yeast -like fungus . Option C: Fusarium is a mold/filamentous fungus . Option D: Talaromyces is a dimorphic fungus .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which among the following is not a sexual spore ?
mcqs.explanation: Sporangiospore is not a sexual spore . It is an asexual spore . Fungi can be classified into 4 classes based on sexual spore formation: Fungi imperfecti (Deuteromycetes ): These are the fungi whose sexual phases are yet to be identified . Most of the fungi of medical importance belong to this group. Note : The earlier classification of Phycomycetes , under which Zygomycetes , Oomycetes , and other sub-phyla were present , is now obsolete . Phylum Glomerulomycota has replaced it.Class Sexual spore Asexual spore Glomerulomycetes Oospores , Zygospo res Sporangiospo res Ascomycetes Ascospores Conidia Basidiomycetes Basidiospores Conidia Fungi imperfecti (Deuteromy cetes ) Yet to be identified Conidia

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following fungal spores are formed by condensation of the hyphal elements ?
mcqs.explanation: Arthrospores are asexual spores that are formed along the mycelium /hyphae by segmentation and condensation of hyphae . Arthrospores are commonly formed by dermatophytes , especially those belonging to the genus Trichophyton. They are also formed by dimorphic fungi like Coccidiodes sp.459

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A young patient presents to the dermatology OPD with a history of itchy hypopigmented patches over her chest for 6 months. A KOH mount is prepared with the skin scraping sample , which on microscopy reveals a characteristic appearance as shown in the image. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture and the KOH mount preparation showing the spaghetti and meatball appearance suggest pityriasis versicolor. Pityriasis versicolor is a chronic superficial infection of the stratum corneum caused by Malassezia globosa and Malassezia furfur. The most common site involves the neck, chest , back, and upper arms. The lesions often appear as hypopigmented areas. The KOH mount reveals fungal hyphae that are short and thick (like spaghetti or banana ) and many variously sized spores (like meatballs or grapes ) referred to as spaghetti and meatballs or bananas and grapes appearance . Treatment includes topical azoles or terbinafine for 2 weeks . The image below shows the hypopigmented lesions of P. versicolour over the chest .460 Electron microscopic image of Malassezia furfur

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about dermatophytes is true?
mcqs.explanation: Microsporum infects only skin and hair, not nails. Dermatophytes include 3 genera: • Microsporum: It infects only hair and skin (not nails). The species included in this genus are- • M. gypseum • M. canis • M. nanum. • Epidermophyton : It infects only skin and nails (not hair). E. floccosum is the only species in this genus . • Trichophyton: It infects skin, hair, and nails. The species falling under this genus are- • T. rubrum • T. mentagrophytes • T. tonsurans • T. schoenleinii • T. violaceum

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old-lady came to the dermatology clinic with complaints of hair loss and the presence of firmly adherent , black, gritty, hard nodules along the hair shaft as shown. There is no associated pruritis of the scalp . Which of the following could be the most probable causative agent ?
mcqs.explanation: 461 The presence firmly adherent , black, gritty, hard nodules along the hair shaft is suggestive of black piedra. The causative agent of this condition is Piedraia hortae. Piedra is a superficial fungal infection of the hair shaft. It is of two types : • Black piedra: It is characterized by firmly adherent , black, gritty, hard nodules along the hair shaft. Scalp hair is most often affected. Hair becomes brittle and breaks easily leading to complains of hair loss. It is caused by Piedraia hortae. • White piedra: It is characterized by soft , white or light brown transparent nodules that are easily detached from the hair. It affects pubic, axillary, facial hair more commonly than scalp hair. It is caused by Trichosporon beigelii . Management involves shaving or cutting off the affected hair along with topical antifungals .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old diabetic patient presented with complaints of discoloration of his toenail for the past 4 months as shown in the image below . Which pathogen most commonly causes this condition?
mcqs.explanation: 462 The given clinical scenario points to a diagnosis of onychomycosis and the pathogen most commonly causing this condition is Trichophyton rubrum. Diabetes increases the risk of onychomycosis . Onychomycosis refers to nail infections caused by fungi. It can be due to dermatophytes , non-dermatophytic moulds , and candida. Tinea unguium refers to nail infections caused by dermatophytes . This condition may affect toenails or fingernails, but toenail infections are particularly common. The following photomicrograph of the nail segment in KOH shows T. rubrum fungal hyphae invading nail cells .The following image is of a lactophenol cotton blue (LPCB ) mount showing pyriform shaped microconidia on the hyphae of T. rubrum.463

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms causes disease following traumatic inoculation into the skin ?
mcqs.explanation: Sporothrix schenckii causes infection followed by traumatic inoculation into the skin. It is a dimorphic fungus that lives on vegetation such as grasses , trees , rose bushes , etc . Following traumatic inoculation into the skin as in thorn prick, S schenckii causes sporotrichosis, a chronic granulomatous infection . This is usually further followed by spread along the draining lymphatics and lymph nodes as shown in the image below .Subcutaneous mycoses are usually caused by traumatic inoculation of the causative fungus . These include :Subcutaneous myc oses Causative agent /s Sporotrichosis Sporothrix schenckii464 Subcutaneous myc oses Causative agent /s Chromoblastomyco sis Phialophora verrucosaFonsec aea pedrosoiFonsecaea comp actaRhinocladiella aquaspers aCladophialophora carrionii Phaeohyphomycosi s Exophiala jeanselmeiPhialop hora richardsiaeBipolaris spi ciferaWangiella dermatitidis Mycetoma Pseudallescheria boydii (Ana morph Scedosporium apiosp ermum).Madurella mycetom atisMadurella griseaE jeansel meiAcremonium falciforme

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about the most commonly used culture media for growing fungi?
mcqs.explanation: Sabouraud dextrose agar (SDA) is the most commonly used culture media for growing fungi. It does not contain taurocholate . It consists of antibiotics like gentamicin or chloramphenicol to inhibit the contaminant bacteria and also cycloheximide to inhibit the growth of saprophytic fungi. It has an acidic pH of 5.4. Media used in mycology can be classified as: • Specific media- • SDA agar • Czapek-Dox medium • Birdseed agar • Cornmeal agar • Non-specific media- • Blood agar • Brain heart infusion agar465

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A gardener from the sub-Himalayan region presented with multiple ulcerative eruptions along the lymphatics of his hand. A tissue biopsy was taken and sent for culture . Microscopic examination of the organism cultured is shown in the image. Identify the organism.
mcqs.explanation: The presence of multiple ulcerative eruptions along the lymphatics in a gardener from the sub-Himalayan region and the microscopic finding of flower -like clusters of conidia are suggestive of sporotrichosis, caused by Sporothrix schenckii. It is a thermally dimorphic fungus that lives on vegetation . The lesions occur following traumatic inoculation of the fungus . A granulomatous nodule is first formed at the site of inoculation that may progress to form a necrotic or ulcerative lesion. The infection can spread via lymphatic channels from the skin and subcutaneous tissue to the lymph nodes resulting in formation of secondary ulcers on the lymph nodes . This condition is known as lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis. This disease is commonly encountered among gardeners, forest workers and manual labourers. Clinical presentation of lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis:466

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A farmer developed multiple ulcerative nodules along the lymphatics following a rose thorn prick a week ago. Microscopic finding of the skin biopsy is given below . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows an asteroid body which is characteristically seen in a case of sporotrichosis. Asteroid bodies are formed due to the deposition of the immune complexes around the yeast cell . It consists of a central rounded or oval basophilic , cigar-shaped yeast cell surrounded peripherally by eosinophilic radiations. Formation of such structures is called the Splendore -Hoeppli phenomenon . Note : Asteroid bodies are also seen in sarcoidosis. Those are irregular, star-shaped inclusions seen in multinucleate giant cells .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A farmer from the sub-Himalayan belt had a thorn prick injury a year back and developed a warty, verrucous growth at the site of prick. A skin biopsy sample was taken and sent for histopathological examination. The characteristic microscopic body as shown in the image was seen . Which of the following could be the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The history of a slowly spreading warty, verrucous lesion following a thorn prick injury and the histopathological image showing medlar bodies is suggestive of chromoblastomycosis . Chromoblastomycosis (chromomycosis) is a subcutaneous mycotic infection that is usually caused by traumatic inoculation. Over months to years, the primary lesion becomes verrucous and wart-like with extension along the draining lymphatics . Histologically , the lesions are granulomatous and the dark sclerotic bodies may be seen within leukocytes or giant cells called medlar/copper penny bodies .Subcutaneous myc oses Causative agent /s Sporotrichosis Sporothrix schenckii Chromoblastomyco sis Phialophora verrucosaFonsec aea pedrosoiFonsecaea comp actaRhinocladiella aquaspers aCladophialophora carrionii Phaeohyphomycosi s Exophiala jeanselmeiPhialop hora richardsiaeBipolaris spi ciferaWangiella dermatitidis Mycetoma Pseudallescheria boydii (Ana morph Scedosporium apiosp ermum).Madurella mycetom atisMadurella griseaE jeansel meiAcremonium falciforme

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man from south India presented to the OPD with a swelling in his left foot that is unresponsive to antibiotics. On examination, multiple discharging sinuses were noted . The discharge contained brown granules that were soft in consistency . Which of the following is likely the causative agent ?
mcqs.explanation: 467 A swelling with multiple discharging sinuses with brown granules that is unresponsive to the antibiotics is suggestive of eumycetoma caused by Madurella mycetomatis . Mycetoma is a chronic, granulomatous infection of the skin, subcutaneous tissues , fascia and bone, which most often affects the foot or the hand. It can be divided into three types - eumycetomas , actinomycetomas and botryomycosis . Infection follows traumatic inoculation of the organism into the subcutaneous tissue from soil or vegetable sources . Within host tissues, the organisms develop to form compacted colonies (grains) 0.5–2 mm in diameter , the color of which depends on the organism responsible . It results in tumefactions , deformities and draining sinuses discharging these grains or granules. Laboratory Diagnosis: • A. Direct Examination: The presence of grains in pus collected from draining sinuses or in biopsy material is diagnostic . • B. Culture Samples should also be cultured , at both 25–30\260C and 37\260C, on brain -heart infusion agar or blood agar for actinomycetes and on Sabouraud agar (without cycloheximide ) for fungi. Treatment: The management of eumycetoma is difficult , involving surgical debridement or excision and chemotherapy . Actinomycetoma on the other hand, responds well to rifampicin in combination with sulfonamides or cotrimoxazole. Option A: Actinomadura madurae causes actinomycetoma which would respond to antibiotics. Option B: Sporothrix schenckii causes sporotrichosis which is characterised by lesions along the route of lymphatics . Option C: Fonsecaea pedrosoi causes chromoblastomycosis which would not have discharging sinuses .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a dimorphic fungus ?
mcqs.explanation: Pneumocystis jirovecii is a yeast -like fungus and not a dimorphic fungus . Dimorphic fungi exist in the yeast form in body tissues and cultures maintained at 37\260C, and in the filamentous form in cultures at room temperature (25\260C). Examples of dimorphic fungi include : • Blastomyces dermatitidis • Coccidioides immitis • Paracoccidioides brasiliensis • Talaromyces marneffei • Sporothrix schenckii • Histoplasma capsulatum • Coccidioides posadasii468

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 54-year-old man had presented to the clinic with a history of chronic cough . His chest X-ray showed a mass in the left lung with hilar lymphadenopathy . Biopsy of the mass was done and findings are shown below . Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history and the presence of tiny yeast forms within macrophages are suggestive of Histoplasmosis which is also called Darling's disease . Other names of this condition include Cave's disease and Ohio disease . The causative agent is a dimorphic fungus called Histoplasma capsulatum . Transmission occurs via inhalation of conidia. After inhalation, the conidia develop into yeast cells and are engulfed by alveolar macrophages . Within macrophages , the yeasts may disseminate to reticuloendothelial tissues , such as the liver, spleen , bone marrow , and lymph nodes. Biopsy reveals tiny (2-4 microns) oval-shaped yeast cells inside macrophages . On culture and microscopy, tuberculate macroconidia and hyaline septate mold with microconidia are seen . It is treated using azole antifungals .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 7-year-old boy with a recent history of travel to South America was brought to the hospital with fever, enlarged lymph nodes and multiple skin lesions on his face . Tissue sample from the lesion shows the following findings under microscopy. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history and the characteristic pilot 's wheel appearance on culture (image) is suggestive of paracoccidioidomycosis caused by Paracoccidioides brasiliensis. It is also called Lutz mycosis/ South American blastomycosis . Paracoccidioides brasiliensis is a thermally dimorphic fungus that causes a chronic granulomatous disease affecting the lungs , skin, mucosa, lymph nodes . On culture , yeast form is seen at 37\260 C and the mycelial form at 25\260 C. Microscopy of tissue sample reveals thick walled , round, yeast cells with numerous buds attached to each other circumferentially giving the classic mickey mouse or pilot wheel appearance . Most infections are asymptomatic and few individuals with acute disease present with hepatosplenomegaly , lymphadenopathy and skin lesions . The below image shows skin lesions in a child with paracoccidioidomycosis .469 Treatment: • Mild /moderate disease : Itraconazole • Severe disease : Amphotericin B for 2-3weeks followed by Itraconazole.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old male presents with low-grade fever and a skin lesion as shown below . He had a history of recent travel to North America. Chest X-Ray reveals consolidation in the right lung with hilar lymphadenopathy . Culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar at 37\260C shows thick-walled , large (7-20 \265\round yeast cells with a single broad-based bud. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with pulmonary and cutaneous involvement along with a history of travel to North America and the characteristic culture findings suggests the diagnosis of Blastomycosis caused by Blastomyces dermitidis . Blastomycosis is a chronic infection , characterized by the formation of suppurative and granulomatous lesions , especially , in the lungs and skin. It is most common in North America and so is also called North Amerian Blastomycosis . The causative organism is a thermally dimorphic fungus called Blastomyces dermatitidis . Humans are infected by the inhalation of spores in the soil. Blastomycosis can present in three forms: • Pulmonary disease : • Presents with cough , sputum production, chest pain, and fever • Hilar lymphadenopathy may be present • Focal or diffuse consolidation, miliary lesions , or abscess formation may occur. • Resembles TB and Histoplasmosis • Cutaneous disease : • Involvement of face and exposed parts of the skin • Skin lesion: ulcerated verrucous granulomas with an advancing border and central scarring. The border is filled with microabscesses and has a sharp, sloping edge . (image in stem )470 • Disseminated disease : • Multiple skin lesions are the most common presentation • Highly fatal • Genitourinary tract (especially prostate ) is frequently involved • Bone involvement resembles chronic osteomyelitis . It can be diagnosed based on culture findings. Characterictic findings include the presence of thick-walled round yeast cell with a single broad-based bud when cultured at 37\260C. (figure of 8 appearance ) Treatment: • Localised mild/moderate disease - Itraconazole (6 months) • Disseminated / severe disease - Amphotericin B

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man residing in a rural area presents with psychosis , ataxia and convulsions. On further inquiry , you find out there is history of similar complaints in the family members who recently consumed food prepared with grains as shown in the image. What is the poisoning is most likely due to?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette and the presence of dark coloured ergot growing on the wheat as shown in the image are suggestive of ergotism due to Claviceps purpurea Mycotic poisoning is of two types : Mycetism and Mycotoxicosis Mycetism : The fungus itself causes toxic effects . Examples : • Claviceps \022 Ergot poisoning • Coprine \022 coprine poisoning • Inocybe \022 muscarine poisoning Mycotoxicosis : Fungal toxins contaminate food and cause toxic effects . Examples : • Aflatoxins: These are a type of mycotoxins produced by Aspergillus species of fungi, such as Aspergillus flavus and Aspergillus parasiticus. • Fusarium toxins • Citrinin toxin was first isolated from Penicillium citrinum.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The below given image shows result of hair perforation test . The organism likely to show below given appearance is
mcqs.explanation: Image shows surface erosion of shaft caused by Trichophyton mentagrophytes . Hair perforation test :471 • Done to differentiate Trichophyton rubrum from mentagrophytes . • Few strands of human hair are placed in a petridish with 20 ml of distilled water and autoclaved . • Few drops of sterile 10 % yeast extract and a few fragments of the test fungus are added to the hair strands. • Incubated at 250C for 2-3 weeks . • Hair is removed and examined microscopically in a lactophenol cotton blue stained wet preparation. • T.mentagrophytes causes surface erosion of the shaft resulting in wedge shaped appearance of the shaft.472

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: What is the stain used for identifying cryptococcus ?
mcqs.explanation: Mucicarmine stain is used in the identification of cryptococcus . Mucicarmine stained specimen of lung tissue containing cryptococci :

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a false statement regarding Cryptococcus neoformans?

options.b: It most commonly causes meningitis in AIDS patients
options.c: There are 3 serological types based on capsular polysaccharide
options.d: Niger seed agar is used to demonstrate melanin production

mcqs.explanation: Pathogenic varieties of cryptococcus including C. neoformans and C. gattii are laccase positive . They also have ability to grow at 37\260 C and these factors are used to differentiate them from non-pathogenic cryptococci . Cryptococci have been classified into 5 serotypes (A, B, C, D, and AD) based on their capsular polysaccharide : • Three serotypes fall under Cryptococcus neoformans - A(var . grubii), D(var . neoformans), and AD(a hybrid of serotypes A and D). Although serotype AD is very similar to serotypes A and D, the isolates still comprise a discrete group that can be distinguished . • The serotypes B and C are now considered a different species - Cryptococcus gattii . Niger seed agar is a solid medium used for selective and differential isolation of Cryptococcus neoformans from clinical specimens . C. neoformans and C. gattii produces brown480 colonies on this medium due to the formation of melanin. Melanin is produced by laccase using caffeic acid as the substrate . The following image shows pigmented colonies of C. gattii growing on niger seed agar.Cryptococcal meningitis caused by Cryptococcus neoformans, is an opportunistic infection seen in individuals with AIDS. Flucytosine and amphotericin B are used in the treatment of this condition.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms cannot be grown on any culture media?
mcqs.explanation: Rhinosporidium seeberi and Pneumocystis jirovecii are non-cultivable organisms and cannot be grown on any culture media. Another example of a non-cultivable fungus is Lacazia loboi. It causes Jorge Lobo's disease which is a chronic subcutaneous mycosis. Rhizopus oryzae is a mold which is easily cultivable on SDA. Dimorphic fungi like Histoplasma capsulatum and Paracoccidiodes brasiliensis are identified based on their colony morphology on SDA. Note : Recently , molecular biological techniques have demonstrated that Rhinosporidium is an aquatic protistan parasite. Infections due to Rhinosporidium have been classified under infections due to Protozoa under the ICD 11 .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient with HIV presented complaining of cough and progressively worsening breathing difficulty . Chest X-ray showed bilateral interstitial infiltrates . The findings of microscopic examination of his bronchoalveolar lavage is given below . Which is the most probable causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture and the GMS stained smear showing the black-colored cysts resembling crushed ping pong balls are suggestive of pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) caused by Pneumocystis jirovecii.481 Patients with PCP generally present with fever and cough that is usually non-productive. Chest X-ray is either a normal film if the disease is suspected early, or with diffuse bilateral interstitial infiltrates . The classic finding of dense perihilar infiltrate is unusual in patients with AIDS. Treatment of choice is trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (cotrimoxazole) and pentamidine isethionate . Cotrimoxazole can also be used for prophylaxis in patients having AIDS. The following X-ray image shows a cyst (arrow) and bilateral lung infiltrates in a patient with PCP:

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged immunocompromised patient presents with complaints of pain during swallowing . She describes it as a burning sensation that radiates to her back every time she swallows . Oral examination reveals creamy white patches on the oral mucosa. The wet mount microscopy of the scraping obtained from the patches is given below . Identify the organism.
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of odynophagia, creamy white patches on the oral mucosa and the wet mount microscopy showing budding yeasts with pseudohyphae are suggestive of oral candidiasis caused by Candida albicans.482 It is an opportunistic infection commonly seen in immunocompromised states like AIDS, diabetes etc. Treatment includes topical azoles or nystatin.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The following test is positive for identification of ________
mcqs.explanation: The image shows the germ tube test used for identifying Candida albicans. Unlike other species of candida, yeast cells of Candida albicans will begin to form germ tubes after incubation in serum maintained at 37\260C for about 90 minutes . This is known as the Reynolds -Braude phenomenon . This test is positive for Candia dubliniensis as well .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old HIV positive \037 patient presents with mucosal lesions in the mouth as shown in the image below . On microscopy, budding yeasts and pseudohyphae are seen . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The most likely diagnosis of the given clinical scenario is oral candidiasis. Oral candidiasis or thrush is a patchy , pseudomembranous lesion that develops over the tongue , lips, gum or palate . It is composed of epithelial cells , yeasts , and pseudohyphae . The causative agent is usually Candida albicans. It occurs in almost all individuals with AIDS. Other risk factors include hyperglycemia , cellular immunodeficiency , corticosteroids or antibiotics. It is treated with topical nystatin or oral ketoconazole or fluconazole . Option B: Hairy leukoplakia is a wart-like growth on the tongue , caused by Epstein Barr virus. It is commonly seen as a white lesion on the lateral side of the tongue . Option C: Lichen planus is a pruritic disease characterized by papules commonly seen over the flexor surfaces and trunk. Oral and vulvovaginal lesions may also occur. Oral lesions appear as lacy, white , and raised lesions . Option D: Diphtheria is characterized by the presence of a grey pseudomembrane covering the tonsils and pharynx. It is caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Galactomannan in serum is seen in:
mcqs.explanation: The galactomannan assay is used for the diagnosis of invasive (deep -seated ) mycoses caused by Aspergillus species . Galactomannan is a component of the cell wall of Aspergillus . It can be detected in serum or bronchoalveolar lavage by ELISA for the diagnosis of invasive aspergillosis in adults and children. This test is especially useful in hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients or patients with hematologic malignancies. Other diagnostic features of invasive aspergillosis are: • A positive culture from the affected organ483 • Aspergillus antigen detection of galactomannan • Narrow, septate hyphae with branching at 45o and conidiophores • Halo sign on CT scan

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Identify the organism in the given slide stained with Gomori methenamine silver stain.
mcqs.explanation: The given slide stained with GMS shows acute -angled (45o) uniform, branching septate hyphae which is suggestive of Aspergillus species. Aspergillus species grow rapidly, producing aerial hyphae that bear characteristic conidial structures . Long aseptate conidiophores are seen with terminal vesicles on which phialides are arranged in basipetal chains. The following image shows the lactophenol cotton blue solution (LPCB ) mount of Aspergillus fumigatus showing the long conidiophores with terminal vesicles .Option A: Mucor produces nonseptate, broad hyphae with aerial sporangiophores which end in a sporangium. Option B: Penicillium produces septate hyphae with branched, septate and brush-like conidiophores . Option D: Rhizopus appears similar to Mucor but it has rhizoids with sporangiophores arising in groups directly above the rhizoids.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A young lady complains of recurrent rhinitis, nasal discharge and bilateral nasal blockage for two years. She has a history of allergic rhinitis. On rhinoscopy, multiple ethmoidal polyps with mucosal thickening and impacted secretions are seen in both the nasal cavities. A tissue biopsy is taken and sent for culture , which on microscopic examination shows the following appearance. What is the most probable organism implicated here?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture and the microscopic appearance is suggestive of fungal rhinosinusitis. The most probable causative organism is Aspergillus fumigatus . It is commonly involved in paranasal sinus mycoses (fungal sinusitis).484 The disease has been described to have four types : • allergic • non-invasive • invasive • fulminant A possible fifth type called non-invasive destructive type may also exist . Zygomycetes like mucor and rhizopus are the common agents in fulminant type of fungal sinusitis. The characteristic microscopic appearance of Aspergillus fumigatus : • The vesicle is conical. • Phialides are arranged in a single row. • Conidia arise from the upper third of the vesicle and are hyaline. Option B: Aspergillus flavus appears as follows :• The vesicle is globular. • Phialides are arranged in one or two rows. • Conidia arise from the entire vesicle and are hyaline. Option C: Aspergillus niger appear as follows :485 • The vesicle is globular shaped . • Phialides are in two rows. • Conidia arise from the entire vesicle and are black. Option D: Penicillium chrysogenum appear as follows :• Septate hyphae with branched conidiophores bearing chains of spores (brush or broom appearance ).

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: What is the drug of choice for invasive pulmonary aspergillosis ?
mcqs.explanation: Voriconazole is the drug of choice in the treatment of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis . It can also be used against candida species (including glabrata and krusei), scedosporium and fusarium.486 The other options can be used as alternatives for the treatment of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis if voriconazole is unavailable.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: \037 1-3 glucan assay is used to diagnose all except ?
mcqs.explanation: The \037 1-3 glucan assay cannot be used to diagnose mucormycosis. This condition is usually diagnosed based on clinical features and culture . The test detects the presence of (1-3)-\037-d-glucan (BDG) which is an abundant cell wall polysaccharide found in most fungi. It is a chromogenic, quantitative enzyme immunoassay (EIA) designed to detect beta D Glucan by using purified , lysed horseshoe crab (Limulus polyphemus ) amebocytes . 1,3 Beta D Glucan level of \02480 pg /mL is considered a positive result . Fungi that do not contain BDG in their cell walls include • Cryptococcus neoformans • Zygomycetes like rhizopus and mucor • Blastomyces dermatitidis Mucormycosis is an opportunistic mycosis caused by zygomycetes , which do not contain (1-3)-\037-d-glucan, and hence , the \037 1-3 glucan assay cannot be used for its diagnosis.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which fungus is most commonly associated with orbital cellulitis in patients with diabetic ketoacidosis ?
mcqs.explanation: Rhizopus is the most common fungus associated with orbital cellulitis in patients with diabetic ketoacidosis . Diabetic patients are immunocompromised and so prone to develop opportunistic infections . Orbital cellulitis with Rhizopus may turn fatal in these patients as it is an angioinvasive fungus and could lead to septicemia and thromboses .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 68-year-old post -COVID -19 patient presented with a black, foul -smelling nasal discharge and blurred vision. On examination, a blackish necrotic mass eroding the septum and hard palate was visualised . Lactophenol cotton blue mount from the culture is given below . Which of the following statements is false regarding the condition?

options.b: Iron administration to patients with active infection should be avoided
options.c: Posaconazole can be used to treat it
options.d: Pulmonary form is the most common

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the LPCB mount showing aseptate hyphae branching at right-angles is strongly suggestive of mucormycosis. Rhino-orbito-cerebral mucormycosis is the most common form of mucormycosis. Pulmonary mucormycosis is the second most common form. Mucormycosis is an invasive disease caused principally by species of Rhizopus, Mucor, and Lichtheimia. The disease is often characterized by hyphae growing in and around the blood vessels . It can turn fatal on cerebral involvement and development of speticemia . Risk factors for the infection include : • Diabetes (Diabetic ketoacidosis ).487 • Elevated levels of free iron. • Defects in phagocytic function. • Organ or hematopoietic stem transplantation. Treatment of choice is Amphotericin-B. Posaconazole can be used as an alternative drug.488

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 9-year-old child infected with Toxocara canis is diagnosed to have visceral larva migrans. It is an example of________.
mcqs.explanation: 494 Toxocara canis (dog roundworm) infecting a human is an example of an aberrant parasite. It is defined as a parasite that infects a host where they cannot develop further. Parasites can be classified as: • Ectoparasites - inhabit only the body surface of the host without penetrating the tissue . The term infestation is often used for parasitization. e.g., lice , ticks, and mites . • Endoparasite - lives within the body of the host and causes infection . Endoparasites are further classified as follows : • Obligate parasites - cannot exist without a host. e.g., Toxoplasma gondii and Plasmodium. • Facultative parasites - exist as either parasitic or free -living forms. e.g., Naegleria fowleri . • Accidental parasites - infects an unusual host. e.g., Echinococcus granulosus infects man • Aberrant/Wandering parasites - infects a host where they cannot develop further. e.g., Toxocara canis (dog roundworm) infecting humans.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following refers to a host in which the larval stage of the parasite remains viable without further development ?
mcqs.explanation: A host in which the larval stage of the parasite remains viable without further development is referred to as the paratenic host. For example , in the lifecycle of Diphyllobothrium latum (fish tapeworm ), humans are the definitive host. The first intermediate host is cyclops and the second is small freshwater fish. If the small freshwater fish with the plerocercoid larva get eaten by a larger fish, the larva survives in the larger fish. This makes the larger fish a paratenic host. Host is an organism that harbors the parasite and provides nourishment and shelter to it. It is relatively larger than the parasite. Types of hosts : • Definitive host - harbors stages of sexual reproduction of the parasite. • Intermediate host - harbors stages of asexual multiplication of the parasite. • Paratenic host - harbors only the larval stage of the parasite which remains viable without further development . • Reservoir host - harbors the parasite and acts as an important source of infection to other susceptible hosts , especially in endemic areas. • Accidental host - harbors a parasite that is not usually found in the host.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 46-year-old farmer came to the clinic with cough and chest pain for one week and fatigue for a month. He was diagnosed to have a hydatid cyst in his right lung. Which of the following classes does the causative organism of this disease belong to?
mcqs.explanation: The causative organism of hydatid disease is Echinococcus granulosus and it belongs to the class cestodes . It is a tape -like , segmented worm. It infects man accidentally , giving rise to hydatid cysts .495 The image below shows the classification of parasites .Note : Zoonoses refers to diseases caused by zoonotic organisms. It is not a class of organisms.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the smallest cestode infecting humans?
mcqs.explanation: The smallest cestode infecting humans is Hymenolepis nana . Option A: Diphyllobothrium latum is the longest cestode infecting man. Option C: Heterophyes heterophyes is the smallest trematode infecting man. Option D: Strongyloides stercoralis is the smallest nematode infecting man. Also, Fasciolopsis buski is the largest trematode infecting humans.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following parasites has a direct life cycle ?
mcqs.explanation: Enterobius vermicularis has a direct life cycle . Parasite requiring a single host to complete its development is said to have a direct life cycle . Parasites having a direct life cycle are: Parasite requiring two or more hosts to complete its development is said to have indirect life cycle , e.g. Plasmodium spp .496 Protozoa Helminths Entamoeba histolyticaGiardi a lambliaTrichomonas vagina lisBalantidium coliCryptospo ridium parvumCyclospora ca yetanensisIsospora belliMicr osporidia. Ascaris lumbricoidesEnterobi us vermicularisTrichuris tric huraAncylostoma duodenale Necator americanusHymenol epsis nana .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Match the following :
mcqs.explanation: The correct answer is option B. A boy from Kolkata with fever and massive splenomegaly is likely suffering from Kala-azar caused by Leishmania donovani . Its intermediate host is sandfly .A lady from Kerala with bilateral non-pitting pedal edema is likely suffering from lymphatic filariasis caused by Wuchereria bancrofti. Its intermediate host is the culex mosquito.497 A man presenting with new-onset seizures and MRI brain showing cyst with a dot sign is likely suffering from neurocysticercosis caused by ingestion of Taenia solium eggs (Cysticercus cellulose ). The intermediate host of Taenia Solium is the pig.A woman having fever with her peripheral smear showing Maltese cross appearance is likely suffering from babesiosis caused by Babesia microti. Its intermediate host is human.498

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An entomologist who had recently visited Mexico presented to the OPD with fever, fatigue , and an alleged history of contact with the insect given in the image. Which of the following diseases is it a biological vector for?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows reduviid bug which is the biological vector for the transmission of Chagas disease . Acute Chagas disease can present as fever with fatigue and a subcutaneous swelling known as a chagoma. It may lead to fatal myocarditis. Biological vectors not only help in the transfer of parasites but the parasites undergo development or multiplication in their body as well. They are also called true vectors. Examples of biological vectors are: • Mosquito - Malaria, filariasis • Sandfly - Kala-azar • Tsetse fly - Sleeping sickness • Reduviid bugs - Chagas disease • Ticks - Babesiosis

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Autoinfection is not seen with which of the following parasites ?
mcqs.explanation: Autoinfection is not seen in infection with Ascaris lumbricoides . Autoinfection refers to either of the following : • Reinfection by microbes or parasitic organisms that are present on or within the body. It is also known as internal reinfection . e.g., Strongyloides . • Self -infection by direct contact with a contagious agent , as with parasite eggs in the infectious state transmitted by fingernails. e.g., Pinworm. The following are the parasites causing autoinfection (mnemonic: CHEST.C)499 • Cryptosporidium parvum • Hymenolepis nana • Enterobius vermicularis • Strongyloides stercoralis • Taenia solium • Capillaria philippinensis .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A microbiologist is doing research about antigenic variations in parasites . Which of the following parasites will exhibit this phenomenon ?
mcqs.explanation: Trypanosoma brucei exhibits antigenic variation within the host. This genetic switch protects them from antibodies . These trypanosomes exhibit unique antigenic variations of their glycoproteins . There is a cyclical fluctuation in the trypanosomes occurring in the blood of infected vertebrates after every 7–10 days. Parasites exhibiting antigenic variation include : • Trypanosoma brucei gambiense • Trypanosome brucei rhodesiense • Plasmodium spp . • Giardia lamblia The following image shows Trypanosoma brucei.The following image shows Plasmodium spp .500 The following image shows the trophozoite of Giardia lamblia.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: You order a peripheral blood film examination while evaluating a patient with pyrexia of unknown origin. Which of the following organisms cannot be detected by this investigation?
mcqs.explanation: Stool examination is useful for the detection of Giardia lamblia, not peripheral blood film examination . Examination of blood is of vital importance for demonstrating parasites that circulate in blood vessels . Examples of parasites found in the peripheral blood film:501 Protozoa Nematodes Plasmodium spp .Babesia spp . Trypanosoma spp .Leishmani a spp . WuchereriabancroftiBrugia malayiLoa loaMansonella sp p.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A Giemsa stain of a thin peripheral smear is prepared . Which of the following cannot be diagnosed ?
mcqs.explanation: The diagnosis of Coxiella burnetii cannot be done using a Giemsa stain of a thin peripheral smear. It is done mainly by serology , which shows a rise in the titer of specific antibodies to C. burnetii. Microorganisms such as Histoplasma, Leishmania , Toxoplasma, and Pneumocystis can also be detected with Giemsa, and in gastric tissues , Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) appear thin and distinctly blue . Giemsa's stain is frequently used for diagnostic purposes in haematology to differentiate the nuclear and cytoplasmic morphology of platelets , RBCs, WBCs, and parasites .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient has presented to the PHC with fever and chills. You order a rapid diagnostic test to detect HRP -2 antigen. Which of the following diseases is it used to diagnose ?
mcqs.explanation: HRP -2 antigen detection is used in the diagnosis of malaria . Malaria antigens detected by the rapid immunochromatographic test are: • pLDH - positivity is seen in all Plasmodium species • HRP -2 - positivity is specific for P. falciparum The below image shows rapid diagnostic test (RDT ) kit for malaria .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: In a patient with a positive Casoni's skin test , which of the following infections will you suspect ?
mcqs.explanation: 502 Casoni's skin test is done in patients with hydatid disease . It is an immediate hypersensitivity reaction (type I). This test is abandoned now due to non-specificity and has been supplemented by serological tests .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient presented to the OPD with cough , chest pain, and expectoration of rusty colored sputum . He is diagnosed to have an oriental lung fluke infection . Which of the following parasites is implicated here?
mcqs.explanation: Paragonimus westermani is commonly known as oriental lung fluke or Japanese lung fluke . It causes a pulmonary syndrome characterised by cough , chest pain and hemoptysis . Paragonimus westermani is a trematode . The transmission to humans occurs by eating raw or undercooked crab or crayfish containing metacercariae. The metacercariae excyst in the human gut and young worms migrate to the lungs , where they become encapsulated in lung tissue . The patient complains of cough , chest pain, and hemoptysis . The viscous sputum is speckled with golden -brown eggs . Treatment: Praziquantel (25 mg/ kg TDS for 1-2 days) is the drug of choice . The following image shows the life cycle of Paragonimus westermani , the oriental lung fluke .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A college student from Mangalore comes to the OPD with intermittent fever, headache , and chills for 1 week . She gives a history of malaria 1 year back for which she had received treatment . Which of the following species you would expect to see in the peripheral smear of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of malaria relapse and it is caused by Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium ovale species . In case of P.vivax and P.ovale, two kinds of sporozoites are seen . Some multiply inside hepatic cells to form schizonts while others persist and remain dormant as hypnozoites (resting forms). These dormant forms may get activated and release merozoites , which go on infecting RBCs producing true clinical relapse . It usually occurs after 6 to 12 months of complete cure from the disease .503 In case of P.falciparum and P.malariae, the initial tissue phase disappears completely and no hypnozoites are found, hence relapse is not seen . In Plasmodium falciparum, recrudescence can be seen which is defined as the recurrence of asexual parasitemia. It usually occurs within 8 weeks of treatment and is due to incomplete treatment or drug resistance .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged woman comes to the clinic with abdominal pain, diarrhea, fatigue , and weight loss. Stool examination revealed bile -stained eggs . Which of the following organisms may not be implicated in this case?
mcqs.explanation: Enterobius vermicularis eggs are non-bile stained and the others are bile stained . Enterobiasis commonly occurs in young children and is characterised by anal pruritus. The worm may migrate up to the uterus , fallopian tubes and into the peritoneum in adult women. This can lead to: • Chronic salpingitis • Cervicitis • Peritonitis • Recurrent urinary tract infections .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: You are examining a wet mount stool sample of a patient with diarrhea. As the eggs are not visible , you concentrate the sample using the saturated salt solution technique . Which of the following eggs will not float in this technique ?
mcqs.explanation: The eggs of Strongyloides stercoralis will not float in a saturated salt solution . Concentration methods are used when the parasites in stool are scanty and difficult to identify in routine stool examination. It is of 2 types : • Floatation methods - the feces are suspended in a solution of high specific gravity and eggs will float up. e.g. saturated salt solution technique , zinc sulfate centrifugal floatation technique . • Sedimentation Methods - the feces are suspended in a solution with low specific gravity and eggs will sediment at the bottom. e.g. formol-ether sedimentation technique .504

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The life cycle given below is of which of the following :
mcqs.explanation: The given life cycle is of Entamoeba histolytica . Its life cycle includes 2 stages - the motile trophozoite and the non-motile cyst , both of which are seen in the image shown above. The transmission is primarily by the fecal -oral route. There is no animal reservoir. The ingested cysts differentiate into trophozoites in the ileum which invade the colonic epithelium . The trophozoites penetrate to the submucosal layer and form abscesses which break down to form flask-shaped ulcer. The trophozoites multiply by binary fission and produce cysts , and both stages are passed in the feces . Trophozoites are rapidly destroyed outside the body. Cysts survive in the external environment and are responsible for transmission. The most frequent site of systemic disease is the liver. Note : The genus Entamoeba has four morphologically identical species - E. histolytica , E. dispar, E. bangladeshi , and E. moshkovskii . E. moshkovskii which was initially thought to be non-pathogenic has recently been shown to be a causative agent of non-invasive diarrhea.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man is diagnosed to have amoebic dysentery . Which of the following is the infective form of the protozoan causing this disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The mature quadrinucleate cyst is the infective form of Entamoeba histolytica causing amoebic dysentery . It is passed in feces and can remain viable under moist conditions for about 10 days. The following are the characteristic features of various life stages of Entamoeba histolytica : The trophozoite is found only in tissues . Its cytoplasm has a ground-glass appearance . The nucleus has a central karyosome with radiating fibrils called linin network giving a cartwheel appearance . Pseudopodia are present which exhibit gliding motility . The below image shows trophozoite form.518 The precystic stage has a large glycogen vacuole and 2 chromatid bars. It secretes a refractile cyst wall to become a cyst . The cystic stage has a mature cyst with 4 nuclei and no glycogen mass. Chromatid bars disappear . The below image shows cystic form.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old woman presented with complaints of abdominal pain and 6 episodes of passing foul-smelling dark stool mixed with mucus and blood streaks. There is no history of fever and tenesmus. On examination, vitals are stable and localized tenderness is present in the right iliac fossa. Which of the following is most likely to cause this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of amoebic dysentery and the causative agent is Entamoeba histolytica . Clinical features of intestinal amebiasis: • Acute intestinal amebiasis- dysentery , lower abdominal discomfort, and flatulence .519 • Chronic amebiasis- low-grade symptoms such as occasional diarrhea, weight loss, and fatigue . • The amoebic ulcer which is flask-shaped is the typical lesion seen in intestinal amoebiasis. The ulcers are multiple and are confined to the colon. Sometimes , in secondary intestinal lesions , the ulcers are numerous in the cecum , followed by the sigmoido -rectal region.
