A granulomatous lesion called an ameboma may form in the cecal or rectosigmoid areas of the colon which can resemble an adenocarcinoma of the colon. The most appropriate treatment is intravenous metronidazole . Option A - Giardia is often asymptomatic, but in some cases can lead to fat malabsorption, dull epigastric pain, and flatulence . Option C - Campylobacter presents with fever, pain, and watery diarrhea. The stool contains leucocytes and blood. Option D - Shigella causes bacillary dysentery which is characterised by fever and generalised abdominal tenderness .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: You received a stool sample of a patient suspected to have dysentery in the microbiology lab. On microscopy, you observe the structures shown in the image. What other findings you will expect to see in this stool sample ?

options.a: RBCs as discrete or in rouleaux

mcqs.explanation: The given image is showing erythrophagocytosis (trophozoite with ingested RBCs) and this in the stool sample of a patient with features of dysentery is indicative of amoebic dysentery . The other stool microscopic finding seen in amoebic dysentery is Charcot-Leyden crystals. The ingested erythrocytes appear as dark inclusions. Erythrophagocytosis is the only characteristic that can be used to morphologically differentiate E. histolytica from the nonpathogenic entamoeba . Amoebic dysentery : Clinically, it is insidious in onset with localized abdominal tenderness . Tenesmus , toxicity , and fever are absent. Under microscopy, RBCs are clumped , yellowish -brown in color. Charcot-Leyden crystals and eosinophils are present . Charcot-Leyden crystals are diamond-shaped , clear, and refractile structures that may be seen in stool specimens under microscopy and represent breakdown products of eosinophils . The below image shows Charcot-Leyden crystals:520

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient with abdominal pain and mucus in stool is diagnosed to have intestinal amoebiasis. Which of the following is the most common extraintestinal complication of this disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common extraintestinal complication of amoebiasis is hepatic amoebiasis. In intestinal amoebiasis, most of the trophozoites reach the liver. However, only a small portion of them actually lodge and multiply in the liver cells . Patients usually present with an enlarged , tender liver without detectable impairment of liver function called amoebic hepatitis . Few patients go on to develop amoebic liver abscess . The center of the abscess contains thick chocolate brown pus (anchovy sauce pus ), which is made up of liquefied necrotic liver tissue . It is bacteriologically sterile and free of amoeba. The periphery is made up of nearly normal liver tissue containing invading amoeba. Complications and sequelae of intestinal amoebiasis: • Fulminant amoebic colitis • Toxic megacolon • Perianal ulceration • Amoeboma • Extraintestinal amoebiasis • Hepatic amoebiasis (most common)- Amoebic hepatitis and Amoebic liver abscess • Amoebic appendicitis and peritonitis • Pulmonary amoebiasis • Cerebral amoebiasis • Splenic abscess • Cutaneous amoebiasis • Genitourinary amoebiasis521

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man was brought to the casualty with complaints of nausea, vomiting and disorientation. His brother tells you they had recently gone on a camping trip where they had swum in a freshwater lake. On examination, Kernig's sign is positive . A spinal tap is performed and the findings of CSF wet mount microscopy are shown below . Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and microscopy showing amoeboid trophozoite form with pseudopodia is suggestive of primary amoebic meningoencephalitis . It is caused by Naegleria fowleri . It is also known as brain -eating amoeba. It occurs in 3 forms: cyst , amoeboid trophozoite and flagellate trophozoite forms. The infection usually follows swimming in freshwater rivers or ponds. The amoebae invade the nasal mucosa and pass through the olfactory nerve branches in the cribriform plate into the meninges . Incubation period is 2 days to 2 weeks . Treatment is with intravenous amphotericin B. Options B & D: Both Acanthamoeba and B.mandrillaris cause granulomatous amoebic meningoencephalitis which is a subacute condition. Option C: A. cantonensis is the most common cause of eosinophilic meningitis in Southeast Asia. It is a nematode (roundworm).

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A college student presents with ocular redness , foreign body sensation, and corneal ulcers following the use of contact lens. The saline mount preparation of the corneal scraping shows polygonal cysts . What would be the most probable cause ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history and the demonstration of polygonal cysts are suggestive of amoebic keratitis caused by acanthamoeba. Acanthamoeba culbertsoni is a free -living amoeba. It exists as trophozoite form and resistant cystic form. Both these forms are infective. The trophozoite is large and characterized by spine -like pseudopodia (acanthopodia). Human beings acquire the infection by inhalation of cysts or trophozoites , ingestion of cysts , or directly through traumatized skin or eyes .522 It presents as two chronic conditions- acanthamoeba keratitis and granulomatous amoebic encephalitis . Diagnosis of amoebic keratitis is made by the demonstration of the cyst in corneal scrapings by wet mount, histology , and culture . The below image shows the ring lesion seen in acanthamoeba keratitis.The below image shows cysts of acanthamoeba in lactophenol cotton blue staining.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following protozoan parasites is found in the lumen of the human small intestine ?
mcqs.explanation: Image 2 shows the trophozoite of Giardia lamblia, which is the only protozoan parasite found in the lumen of the human small intestine . It lives in the duodenum and upper jejunum.523 Other protozoan parasites found in the human small intestine do not occur in the lumen but are present in the epithelial cells lining the small intestine . These include : • Isospora belli • Cyclospora cayetanensis • Cryptosporidium parvum • Sarcocystis hominis Options A and C: Entamoeba histolytica and Balantidium coli are found in the human large intestine . Option D: Trichomonas vaginalis is found in the genital tract. The image given below shows the trophozoite of Giardia lamblia.The image given below shows the trophozoite of Entamoeba histolytica .524 The image given below shows the trophozoite of Balantidium coli.The image given below shows the trophozoite of Trichomonas vaginalis.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old HIV -positive patient presented with a chronic history of watery diarrhea. The histopathology of the \037duodenum is shown in the image below . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with the histopathology showing trophozoites of Giardia lamblia in the duodenal wall is suggestive of giardiasis. Giardia lamblia, also called Giardia duodenalis , is the causative agent of giardiasis. It is the only common pathogenic protozoan found in the duodenum and jejunum of humans. Infection occurs by the ingestion of mature cysts in contaminated water and food and is transmitted by the faeco -oral route.525 It is weakly pathogenic in humans. Secretory IgA and IL -6 are responsible for clearing the infection . Hence , giardiasis usually occurs in immunosuppressed , agammaglobulinemic , or malnourished individuals. Clinical features : • Diarrhea • Fat malabsorption • Dull epigastric pain • Belching and flatulence • Iron deficiency and growth stunting . • Stool will have excess mucus and fat but no blood. Detection of antigen by ELISA is more sensitive and specific than microscopy. Entero test is also used in the diagnosis. Histopathology of the duodenum reveals several heart-shaped or pear-shaped trophozoites with two equally sized nuclei . The small intestinal morphology is usually normal . However, in heavy infections , there may be villous blunting and intraepithelial infiltrates . Metronidazole /tinidazole/nitazoxanide are the first-line agents in the treatment . The image given below shows a magnified view of the pear-shaped trophozoites of Giardia lamblia.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient is undergoing the test depicted in the image given below . Which of the following diseases does it help to diagnose ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image depicts a string test or entero test and is used in the diagnosis of giardiasis. It is a useful method for obtaining the duodenal specimen in giardiasis.526 In this test , a coiled thread inside a small weighted gelatin capsule is swallowed by the patient , after attaching the free end of the thread in the cheek . The capsule passes through the stomach to the duodenum . After 2 hours, the thread is withdrawn, placed in saline, and is shaken. The centrifuged deposit of the saline is then examined for giardia.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The findings of the microscopic examination of the wet mount preparation of stool of a patient with diarrhoea is shown below . Which of the following organisms will exhibit this type of motility ?
mcqs.explanation: The given wet mount preparation of stool shows organisms having falling leaf motility . It is exhibited by Giardia lamblia. The trophozoite is motile with a slow oscillation along its long axis resembling a falling leaf .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient came to the gynecology OPD with complaints of foul -smelling frothy vaginal discharge and intense itching. The per speculum finding is given below . Which of the following statements is false regarding the causative organism of this disease ?

options.a: It exists in cyst and trophozoite form
options.c: The gold standard for diagnosis is culture on CPLM or PEM

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with the image showing strawberry cervix is suggestive of Trichomonas vaginalis infection . It exists only in trophozoite form. Trichomonas vaginalis is the only protozoan with one stage in its life cycle ie., trophozoite form (no cyst stage is seen ). It is an obligate parasite and cannot live without close association with vaginal, urethral or prostatic tissues . The common presentation of trichomoniasis is foul -smelling frothy vaginal discharge , itching, and dysuria. The gold standard for diagnosis is culture on CPLM (cysteine -peptone -liver-maltose) or PEM (plastic envelope medium). The treatment of choice is metronidazole . T. vaginalis infection in women may lead to infertility , preterm birth and low-birth-weight infants. In men, trichomoniasis has been also associated with infertility through inflammatory damage to the genitourinary tract or interference with sperm function. The below image shows the trophozoite form of Trichomonas vaginalis.527

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 12 -year-old child presented to you with fever, malaise, and weight loss. On examination, you notice the finding shown in the image. In which of the following conditions is this seen ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows posterior cervical lymphadenopathy which is called Winterbottom's sign. It is seen in West African sleeping sickness. It is seen in stage I of West African sleeping sickness caused by Trypanosoma brucei gambiense . The table below shows diseases caused by various Trypanosoma species .Protozoa Disease Trypanosoma brucei gambie nse West African sleeping sicknes s Trypanosoma brucei rhodesi ense East African sleeping sicknes s Trypanosoma cruzi Chagas' disease /South Ameri can trypanosomiasis

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding Trypanosoma?

options.a: Tsetse fly is the vector for both T. rhodesiense and T. gambiense
options.d: Humans are the reservoir for T. rhodesiense

mcqs.explanation: Humans are the reservoir for T. gambiense , not for T. rhodesiense . The table below shows characteristic differences between West African and East African trypanosomiasis. Parasites causing myocarditis include : • Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense • Trypanosoma cruzi • Toxoplasma gondii • Echinococcus granulosus • Trichinella spiralisCharacteristics West African trypanosomias is East African trypanosomiasi s Organism T. brucei gambiense T. brucei rhodesiense Vector Tsetse fly Tsetse fly Reservoir Humans Wild and domestic animals Course of diseas e Chronic Acute Parasitemia Low High Virulence Less More528 Characteristics West African trypanosomias is East African trypanosomiasi s Mortality Low High

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged woman presents to the OPD with fever and malaise for the past 4 months. On examination , the following ocular finding is noted along with hepatosplenomegaly and lymphadenopathy . What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with the image showing Romana 's sign is suggestive of Chagas disease . It is caused by T. cruzi. Reduviid bugs are vectors for Chagas disease . Inoculation of T. cruzi in conjunctiva causes unilateral, painless edema of periocular tissues in the eye is called Romana 's sign. This is classically seen in acute Chagas disease that lasts for 1 to 4 months. The following image shows a patient with Romana 's sign.Acute Chagas disease is also characterised by the presence of chagomas which are subcutaneous lesions occurring at the site of inoculation. Chronic Chagas disease is characterized by megaesophagus , megacolon , and myopathy . Shown below is an image of the Reduviid bug.529

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is used for the culture of Trypanosoma?
mcqs.explanation: NNN (Novy, McNeal , and Nicolle ) medium is used for the culture of Trypanosoma brucie and cruzie. It is also used for the culture of Leishmania . The other media used in the culture of Trypanosoma are Weinman 's medium and Tobie's medium . Options B, C & D: Boeck and Drbohlav medium, Craig's medium and NIH polygenic medium are used for the culture of E.histolytica.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The given life cycle belongs to which of the following organisms?
mcqs.explanation: The given life cycle belongs to Trypanosoma cruzi. T. cruzi is the causative organism of Chagas disease or South American trypanosomiasis. They are intracellular parasites . It passes its life cycle in two hosts - the definitive host is the man and the intermediate host (vector) is reduviid bug or triatomine bugs . Metacyclic trypomastigotes are the infective forms to the man that are found in feces of reduviid bugs . Transmission occurs when mucus membranes, conjunctiva, or wound on the surface of the skin are contaminated by feces of the bug. Inside the definitive host, the trypomastigotes differentiate into intracellular amastigotes . The amastigotes multiply by binary fission and differentiate into trypomastigotes , which are then released into the bloodstream . These are the infective stage for triatomine bug. No multiplication occurs in this stage . Inside the triatomine bug, the trypomastigotes are transformed into epimastigotes and then into metacyclic trypomastigotes in the hindgut which are excreted in feces .530 Note : Amastigote forms resemble the Leishmania spp . and hence they are frequently known as Leishmanial forms. They are found in muscular tissue , nervous tissue , and reticuloendothelial system .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The given life cycle belongs to which of the following organisms?
mcqs.explanation: The given life cycle belongs to Leishmania donovani . The definitive hosts are man, dog , and other mammals and the vector/intermediate host is female sandfly. Promastigotes are infective forms to man. L. donovani exists in 2 forms: • Amastigote form- in humans and other mammals • Promastigote form- in the sandfly and artificial culture When the infected sandfly bites a person, infectious promastigotes are released into the host dermis along with the sandfly saliva, which potentiates parasite infectivity . Amastigote form (as shown in the image below ) is also known as Leishman-Donovan (LD) body. It is an intracellular form found inside macrophages , monocytes and reticuloendothelial cells . It contains a kinetoplast which consists of a parabasal body and a blepharoplast . Flagellum is absent.Promastigote form (as shown in the below image) is present in the midgut of the female sandfly . The kinetoplast lies transversely near the anterior end. A single flagellum is seen . It is the infective form of Leishmania donovani for humans.531

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: You are performing the following diagnostic procedure in a patient having fever for the past 2 weeks to find the causative organism. Which disease are you most likely testing for?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows bone marrow aspiration and it is most commonly done to diagnose Kala-azar . The microscopic demonstration of amastigotes from bone marrow is the gold standard for the diagnosis of Kala-azar Generally , the sternal marrow is aspirated by puncturing the sternum at the level of the 2nd or 3rd intercostal space , using a sternal puncture needle . Other samples collected are peripheral blood, splenic aspirate, and enlarged lymph node. In kala-azar : • Most common specimen collected for microscopy- bone marrow aspirate. • Most sensitive method - splenic aspirate. Option B: Schistosomiasis is typically diagnosed by stool examination for parasite eggs . Option C: Toxoplasmosis is usually diagnosed based on serologic testing . Option D: Chagas disease is diagnosed by peripheral blood smear examination, culture and examination of aspirates from lymph nodes and chagoma.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: What is the vector for the condition diagnosed by the image shown below ?
mcqs.explanation: The image shown is of the Leishman-Donovan bodies whose presence are diagnostic of Kala Azar . The vector of Kala Azar is a sandfly . Leishman-Donovan bodies are amastigotes with a double dot appearance containing a nucleus and small rod-like kinetoplast . They are present inside the macrophage.532

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 15-year-old boy from Delhi presented to the OPD with the finding seen in the image. It is diagnosed to be an oriental sore. Which of the following causes this?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows cutaneous leishmaniasis and is caused by Leishmania tropica complex . It is also called oriental sore/Delhi boil/Bagdad boil/Aleppo button . It is seen mainly among children in endemic areas. Old world Leishmania tropica complex includes 3 species : • L. tropica • L. major • L. aethiopica New world Leishmania tropica complex includes 3 species : • L. mexicana complex • L. braziliensis complex It begins as a raised papule that grows into a nodule which then ulcerates over some weeks . The margins of the ulcer are raised and indurated . The ulcer is usually painless unless secondary bacterial infection occurs.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A medicine resident is evaluating a patient with abdominal pain and diarrhoea. The stool wet mount finding is given below . What is the most likely causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows the trophozoite form of the Balantidium coli. Living trophozoites /cysts are yellowish or greenish in color on wet mount. Balantidium coli occurs in two stages : • Trophozoites are oval in shape and contain two nuclei . There is the presence of cilia over the entire surface and are larger around the mouth. Its anterior end is narrow and the posterior end is broad. At the anterior end, there is a groove leading to the mouth (cytostome ). Posteriorly, there is a small anal pore (cytopyge ). • Cysts are smaller, round with a micronucleus , a macronucleus and many contractile vacuoles.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: What is the investigation of choice for the diagnosis of kala-azar ?
mcqs.explanation: The rapid dipstick test is the method of choice for the diagnosis of kala-azar . The following tests are used for the laboratory diagnosis of kala-azar : • Rapid diagnostic tests - rK39 and dipstick test strip. • Parasitological diagnosis - demonstration of LD bodies on microscopy is confirmatory • Surveillance purposes - Aldehyde test of Napier533 • Serological diagnosis - Rapid dipstick test , direct agglutination test , ELISA , indirect fluorescent antibody test • Assessing immune status - Leishmanin (Montenegro) test • Induration of \024 5 mm is considered positive • Usually becomes positive 4-6 weeks after onset of cutaneous leishmaniasis534

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old man comes with complaints of fever and increasing fatigue for the past week . On examination, he is febrile , hypotensive and tachycardic. The findings of microscopic examination of his peripheral blood smear is given below . What is the causative agent ?
mcqs.explanation: 541 The given clinical history and the blood smear showing multiple ring forms in RBCs are suggestive of malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum. Falciparum malaria infects both young and mature erythrocytes . Binucleate rings (double chromatin) seen in RBCs are common and they resemble stereo headphones in appearance . The rings are often attached to the margins of the red cells and are described as form applique or accole . There may be several rings present within a single erythrocyte . Hypnozoites are not present in P. falciparum infection . The peripheral smear finding of P. falciparum malaria are: • Multiple ring form • Accole form • Absent schizont • Banana shaped gametocytes • Maurer's dots The below image shows banana shaped gametocyte :

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: During your rural posting , a patient presents with a high fever and chills. Malaria is endemic in the area so you order a peripheral smear. While examining the peripheral blood smear, you note that the schizont stage is not seen . Which of the following organisms is implicated here?
mcqs.explanation: The schizont stage is usually not seen in the peripheral smear of individuals having Plasmodium falciparum malaria . A mature schizont contains merozoites and hemozoin. This will burst to release merozoites into circulation. The merozoites invade fresh erythrocytes , in which they go through the same process of development called erythrocytic schizogony or merogony. After the ring form is formed in peripheral blood, the remaining RBC cycle of falciparum occurs in the capillaries of the brain and other internal organs. Hence only the ring form is seen in the peripheral smear.542 However, for other Plasmodium species, all erythrocytic stages occur in peripheral blood vessels . The below image shows the life cycle of Plasmodium spp .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following Plasmodium spp . has the longest incubation period ?
mcqs.explanation: Plasmodium malariae has the longest incubation period of 28 days. The incubation period is the interval between the infective mosquito bite and the first appearance of clinical symptoms . The average incubation periods for Plasmodium species are: • P. vivax : 8-31 days (14 days) • P. falciparum: 8-14 days (12 days) • P. ovale: 8-31days (14 days) • P. malariae: 18-40 days (28 days) Note : The pre-patent period is the interval between the entry of the parasites into the host and the time when they first become detectable in blood.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following Plasmodium spp . mainly affects the old RBCs?
mcqs.explanation: Plasmodium malaria mainly affects the old RBCs. Options A and D- P. vivax and P. ovale infect young RBCs and reticulocytes . Option B- P. falciparum infects RBCs of all ages . The degree of parasitization is not heavy for P. vivax and P. malariae while very high intensity of parasitization is seen in infection with P. falciparum.543

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A microbiologist is examining the slide shown in the following image under the microscope . Which of the following is false regarding this?

options.a: 'B' is used for determining the species
options.c: 'A' is air dried rapidly and stained with one of the Romanowsky stains
options.d: For 'B' to be considered negative , at least 200 oil immersion fields should be examined

mcqs.explanation: In the given image 'A' is a thin smear and 'B' is a thick smear. The thin smear is used for determining the species , not the thick smear. The two types of smears are prepared from the peripheral blood are: • Thin smear– It is used for detecting the parasites and determining the species . They are air-dried rapidly and stained with Romanowsky stains. • Thick smear– It is more sensitive and examined under oil immersion microscope . It is more suitable for the rapid detection of malarial parasites . Species identification is difficult . It is recommended that 200 oil immersion fields should be examined before a thick film is declared negative . The image below shows the thin and thick smears.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 15-year-old boy presents to the OPD with high-grade fever, chills, and rigors for the past 3 days. A peripheral blood smear revealed the following . Which of the following is false regarding the diagnostic methods used to detect the condition he is likely suffering from?

options.a: Jaswant Singh Bhattacharya stain is used for peripheral smear examination
options.b: HRP -2 antigen test is done for detection of P.vivax
options.c: Acridine orange dye is used in quantitative buffy coat method
options.d: Rapid diagnostic tests have lesser sensitivity than microscopy

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the peripheral smear showing ring forms are suggestive of P. falciparum malaria . HRP -2 antigen detection used in rapid diagnostic tests for malaria is specific for P. falciparum. Jaswant Singh Bhattacharya (JSB ) stain is routinely used in India to stain peripheral blood smears for the diagnosis of malaria . Acridine orange dye is used in the quantitative buffy coat (QBC) method of diagnosis which provides better yield compared to peripheral smears. Rapid diagnostic tests are based on the detection of antigens using immunochromatographic methods . They are less sensitive than microscopy and also cannot differentiate between species except P. falciparum. The 2 antigens detected are: • pLDH (parasite lactate dehydrogenase )- pan malarial antigen544 • HRP -2 (histidine-rich protein 2)- specific for P.falciparum.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with a 5-day history of fever is brought to the casualty by his son after an episode of seizures. He is diagnosed with malignant tertian malaria . Which of the following complications will you not expect to see in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Metabolic acidosis (and not alkalosis) is a complication of malignant tertain malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum. Complications of falciparum malaria include : • Metabolic acidosis • Cerebral malaria • Algid malaria • Septicemic malaria • Blackwater fever • Pulmonary edema • Acute renal failure • Hypoglycemia • Hyperpyrexia • Severe anemia • Shock

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old patient presents with a high-grade fever, headache , and weakness for 5 days. He gives a history of blood transfusion 4 months back. The microscopic examination of the thin blood smear is given below . What is the most probable causative agent ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history and the microscopy showing Maltese crosses or tetrads are suggestive of babesiosis caused by Babesia microti. The definitive host for babesia are ixodid ticks. Man is an incidental , dead -end host. On microscopic examination, babesia trophozoites appear as intraerythrocytic round or pyriform or ring form. The ring form is the most common and it lacks the central hemozoin deposit which differentiates it from P. falciparum. Other distinguishing features are the absence of schizonts and gametocytes and the presence of tetrads /Maltese crosses , which are pathognomic of B. microti or B. duncani. The below image shows Maltese cross appearance of Babesia microti.545

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Sabin-Feldman dye test is used for diagnosis of which of the following condition?
mcqs.explanation: Sabin-Feldman dye test is used for the diagnosis of toxoplasmosis . It is based on the principle that the presence of anti-toxoplasma antibodies in the patient 's serum inhibits the staining of trophozoites by alkaline methylene blue dye . Toxoplasma trophozoites and complement are added to the patient 's serum which is then incubated for an hour at 37\260C. After incubation, methylene blue dye is added . If anti-toxoplasma antibodies are present in the serum, these are activated by complement and the parasite membrane is lysed . Thus, the trophozoites are not stained (positive result ). If there are no antibodies , trophozoites will take up the stain and appear blue under the microscope . This is considered to be a negative result . The dilution of the test serum at which 50% of the tachyzoites are not stained is reported as the antibody titer of the test serum. The test is highly sensitive and specific . It cannot differentiate between recent or past infections as it detects only IgG antibodies .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding Toxoplasma gondii?

options.b: Oocysts are formed within the intermediate host
options.c: The tachyzoites inside the tissue cyst can be reactivated on immunosuppression

mcqs.explanation: Human toxoplasmosis is a zoonosis. It is transmitted by cats. Toxoplasma gondii has two types of life cycles : • Enteric cycle • Exoenteric cycle The enteric cycle occurs in definitive hosts such as cats. Exoenteric cycle occurs in intermediate hosts such as humans, mice, rats, etc .546 Both asexual reproduction (schizogony) and sexual reproduction (gametogony ) occur within the mucosal epithelial cells of the small intestine of the cat. The tachyzoites and tissue cyst represent stages in asexual multiplication , while the oocyst is formed by sexual reproduction . All three forms, tachyzoites , tissue cyst, and oocyst occur in the definitive host. Only the asexual forms, tachyzoites , and tissue cysts are present in the intermediate host. Tachyzoites continue to multiply and spread locally by the lymphatic system and blood, while the bradyzoites multiply slowly inside the tissue cyst . The dormant bradyzoites inside the cyst may be reactivated on immune suppression causing renewed infection in the host. The below image shows the life cycle of Toxoplasma gondii.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An HIV positive pregnant woman was brought to the ER after an episode of generalized tonic-clonic seizures . CECT was done which showed multiple enhancing lesions . A stereotactic biopsy of the cerebral lesions was done and the image is given below . Which of the following is the most appropriate drug for her treatment ?
mcqs.explanation: 547 The given clinical scenario and the image showing lymphocytes , macrophages , and eosinophils surrounding the toxoplasma bradyzoites which are encased in cysts are suggestive of cerebral toxoplasmosis . Spiramycin is the drug of choice during pregnancy. Cerebral toxoplasmosis is an opportunistic infection commonly found in HIV +ve patients and usually occurs when CD4+ T cell counts <100/�ML. It appears as ring enhancing lesions on contrast enhanced CT. Calcification may also be seen in old lesions . Sabin-Feldman dye test is a serological test done for the detection of antibodies against toxoplasma. IIF (indirect immunofluorescence ), IHA (indirect heamagglutination ), and CFT (complement fixation test ) are also used for the diagnosis of toxoplasmosis . Dye test remains positive throughout life , while CFT becomes negative soon after acute infection . ELISA is most commonly used and IgM and IgG antibodies are estimated separately . Standard treatment is sulfadiazine /pyrimethamine and leucovorin for a minimum of 4–6 weeks . The drug of choice for toxoplasmosis in pregnancy is spiramycin.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A Kinyoun-positive oocyst (25 �Mm) isolated from an HIV patient with diarrhea is shown in the image. What is the likely organism implicated here?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with diarrhea in an HIV patient is suggestive of a coccidian parasitic infestation . Kinyoun-positive oocysts with the size of 25 �Mm in the image are formed by Cystoisospora . Comparison of coccidian parasites causing diarrhea in an immunocompromised host: The below image shows oocysts of Cyclospora cayetanensis in the modified acid-fast stain.Property Cryptosporidium Cyclospora Cystoisospora Sporulated oocyst 4-6 �Mm, round, contains f our sporozoites 8-12 �Mm, round, contains 2 sporocysts , each having two sporozoites -36 �Mm, oval, contain t wo sporocysts , each havin g four sporozoites Acid-fast detection Uniformly acid fast Variable acid fast Uniformly acid fast Sporulation of the ooc yst Occurs inside the host cell Occurs in soil Occurs in soil Diagnostic form Sporulated cyst Unsporulated cyst Unsporulated oocyst548 The below image shows oocysts of Cryptosporidium parvum in the modified acid-fast stain.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient who underwent a renal transplant 3 months ago came with complaints of diarrhea for the last 9 days. The stool sample subjected to Kinyoun staining revealed 4-6 \265 m structures as shown below . Which of the following is true about the causative organism?

options.b: It is an obligate intracellular organism
options.c: Oocysts are immediately infective after being excreted in stool
options.d: Metronidazole is the drug of choice

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with Kinyoun stain positive oocysts of size 4-6 \265 m is suggestive of cryptosporidiosis . The oocysts are immediately infective after being excreted in the stool . Cryptosporidium is a coccidian parasite and implicated in causing traveler's diarrhea in immunocompromised patients . The two cryptosporidium species responsible are C. hominis and C. parvum. The infective form is the oocyst excreted in the patient 's feces , which can be acquired through drinking or during recreational water activities. The oocysts are immediately infectious (unlike isospora oocysts , which require maturation), and may cause autoinfection or be implicated in549 person-to-person transmission. Because of their small size (4-5micron), they is difficult to see using routine staining. Hence acid-fast/Kinyoun's stain is used . Once ingested , the 4 sporozoites are released from the cyst and attach to the small intestinal mucosa. It causes crampy abdominal pain and non-inflammatory watery diarrhea. Treatment is mainly supportive , though nitazoxanide has been FDA approved for use in cryptosporidium infection . Comparative features of coccidian parasites :Property Cryptosporidium Cyclospora Cystoisospora Sporulated oocyst 4-6 �Mm, round, contains f our sporozoites 8-12 �Mm, round, contains 2 sporocysts each having t wo sporozoites -36 �Mm, oval, contain t wo sporocysts , each havin g four sporozoites . Acid-fast detection Uniformly acid-fast Variable acid-fast Uniformly acid-fast Sporulation of the ooc yst Occurs inside the host cell Occurs in soil Occurs in soil Diagnostic form Sporulated cyst Unsporulated cyst Unsporulated oocyst

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Match the following :
mcqs.explanation: The below image shows trophozoites of Trichomonas vaginalis with flagella .Parasite Organ of locomoti on Balamuthia mandrillar is Pseudopod Balantidium coli Cilia Trichomonas vaginalis Flagella Toxoplasma gondi No Particular orga n550 The below image shows the trophozoite of Balantidium coli with cilia.The below image shows the trophozoite of Balamuthia mandrillaris with pseudopodia .551 The below image shows tachyzoites of Toxoplasma gondi. They have no specialised structure for locomotion.552

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following cestodes requires only one host?
mcqs.explanation: Hymenolepis nana requires only one host for its development . Man serves as the host for H. nana . Usually , cestodes complete their life cycle in 2 different hosts except : • Hymenolepis requires only 1 host, man. • Diphyllobothrium requires 3 hosts Parasite requiring a single host to complete its development is said to have a direct life cycle . Parasites having a direct life cycle are:Protozoa Helminths Entamoeba histolyticaGiardi a lambliaTrichomonas vagina lisBalantidium coliCryptospo ridium parvumCyclospora ca yetanensisIsospora belliMicr osporidia. Ascaris lumbricoidesEnterobi us vermicularisTrichuris tric huraAncylostoma duodenale Necator americanusHymenol epsis nana .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 10 -year-old child is brought to your clinic with complaints of diarrhea and abdominal pain for the last 4 days. Stool microscopy is shown below . The eggs present in the stool float in a saturated solution of salt. Which of the following can you use to treat her?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history and the egg seen on stool microscopy are suggestive of infection with Hymenolepis nana . A single dose of praziquantel (25 mg/kg) is the drug of choice .563 The Hymenolepis nana eggs have a thin colorless outer membrane and inner embryophore enclosing the hexacanth oncosphere . The space between two membranes contains yolk granules and 4-8 thread-like polar filaments arising from two knobs on the embryophore . The eggs float in saturated salt solution and are non-bile stained . Hymenolepiasis occurs more commonly in children and is usually asymptomatic . In heavy infections , they present with nausea, anorexia, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and irritability. Sometimes pruritus may occur due to an allergic response . The image given below shows the egg of Hymenolepis nana .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient is brought to the hospital , with complaints of seizures and the MRI image of the brain is given below . The disease is most probably caused by?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and MRI brain showing scolex within multiple cystic lesions are suggestive of neurocysticercosis caused by the larval form of T. solium called Cysticercosis cellulosae . Neurocysticercosis is the most common central nervous system parasitic infection . The clinical features of neurocysticercosis include : • Epilepsy • Increased intracranial tension • Hydrocephalus • Psychiatric disturbances • Meningoencephalitis • Transient paresis • Behavioral disorders • Aphasia564 • Visual disturbances . The CT and MRI findings seen in neurocysticercosis are: • Scolex within a cyst • Cystic lesions with or without ring enhancement • Nodular calcifications • Focal enhancing lesions • Multilobulated cystic lesions in the subarachnoid space . Note : About 70% of adult -onset epilepsy is due to neurocysticercosis . Albendazole is the drug of choice for neurocysticercosis . Glucocorticoid therapy is usually begun before initiating albendazole (antiparasitic drug). This is continued for several days after the institution of therapy to reduce the incidence of side effects from inflammatory reactions to dead and dying cysticerci of Taenia solium.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 42-year-old man presented to the ER with complains of abdominal discomfort, indigestion , nausea and diarrhea after consuming measly pork. Stool examination reveals round eggs as shown in the image below . Which of the following statements is true regarding the causative organism?

options.a: Eggs are not infective to man
options.c: The eggs do not float in saturated salt solution

mcqs.explanation: Development of the given symptoms following the consumption of measly pork is suggestive of intestinal taeniasis caused by Taenia solium (pork tapeworm ). The eggs of Taenia solium do not float in the saturated salt solution . The eggs of T. solium are infective to man and pigs . The eggs of T. saginata are infective only to cattle and not to man. The adult worm of Taenia solium is usually 2-3 meters long and the scolex has dagger -shaped hooks. Man is the definitive host. The intermediate host is usually pig, but occasionally it can be man. The below image shows the life cycle of T. solium.565

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The adult form of echinococcus is seen in which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: The adult form of echinococcus is seen in dogs and other canids which are its definitive hosts . The larval stage is passed in intermediate hosts such as sheep , cattle , goat, swine , horse, camel, and man. Man acts as an accidental intermediate host (dead end). Human infection follows the ingestion of eggs due to the intimate handling of dogs or by eating raw vegetables or other food contaminated with dog feces . Note : Humans can become accidental definitive hosts , second intermediate hosts , or paratenic hosts for spirometra. These are cestodes belonging to the Diphyllobothriidae family. They cause a condition called sparagnosis. The image below shows the life cycle of Echinococcus granulosus.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms cause multiple alveolar-like lesions in the liver?
mcqs.explanation: Echinococcus multilocularis causes multiple alveolar-like lesions in the liver. E. multilocularis leads to formation of a multilocular hydatid cyst , most commonly affecting the liver. It presents as multiple small cysts in the liver. Note : Echinococcus granulosus causes a hollow fluid -filled unilocular cyst in the liver. The CT below shows water lily sign, which is seen in the hydatid disease of the lung. It is caused by Echinococcus granulosus.566 The water-lily sign occurs due to detachment of the endocyst membrane from the cyst wall giving the apparance of floating membranes within the pericyst . This mimics the appearance of a water lily. It is classically visualised on plain radiographs (mainly chest X-ray) when the collapsed membranes are calcified but may be seen on ultrasound, CT, or MRI.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: While examining a patient with right upper quadrant pain, you note the abdomen is soft with localised tenderness present . CT abdomen findings are given below . Based on these findings, you post the patient for a PAIR procedure . Which of the following is not used in this procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and CT findings are suggestive of hydatid disease of the liver. Hypotonic saline is not used as a scolicidal agent for the PAIR procedure (Puncture, Aspiration, Injection, and Re-aspiration) which is the treatment of choice in the early stages of this condition. Computed tomography (CT) scan is the best imaging modality for hydatid cyst . It shows the presence of a space -occupying lesion with a smooth outline with septa . In PAIR the steps involved are: • USG or CT guided puncture of the cyst • Aspiration of the cyst fluid • Injection of scolicidal agent • Re-aspiration of fluid after 5 minutes The following agents can be used as scolicidal agents : The below image depicts the PAIR procedure .Scolicidal agent Complications associated wit h it Cetrimide Acidosis 95% Alcohol Cholangitis567 Scolicidal agent Complications associated wit h it Hypertonic saline Hypernatremia Sodium hypochlor ite Hypernatremia Hydrogen peroxid e

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old woman presented to the OPD with a history of progressive breathlessness and cough for 3 months. A chest X-ray was done which showed a cavitary lesion in the lower lobe of the right lung. Wedge resection of the lesion was done and the histopathology image is given below . What is the most probable causative agent ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the histological slide showing the hydatid cyst are suggestive of infection with Echinococcus granulosus. The hydatid cyst wall consists of 3 layers: • Pericyst- the outer dense fibrous capsule that is formed as a result of host inflammatory response . • Ectocyst - the intermediate layer consisting of acellular , chitinous, laminated hyaline material. • Endocyst - the inner germinal layer that is cellular and consists of a number of nuclei embedded in protoplasmic mass and is extremely thin. It is the vital layer of the cyst and it is the site of asexual reproduction giving rise to brood capsules with scolices . The clinical features of hydatid disease of lung are breathlessness , cough , hemoptysis and chest pain. Treatment includes wedge resection or lobectomy and administration of albendazole . The below image shows the histology of hydatid cyst .568

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms does the given life cycle belong to?
mcqs.explanation: This is the life cycle of Diphyllobothrium latum. It is also known as fish tapeworm or broad tapeworm. The 3 hosts of Diphyllobothrium latum are: • Definitive host- man, dog, and cat. • First intermediate host- freshwater crustacean • Second intermediate host- freshwater fish. The infective form to humans is the third stage plerocercoid larvae. It possesses a rudimentary scolex . The adult worm lives inside the small intestine and lays operculated eggs . These freshly passed eggs contain an immature embryo surrounded by yolk granules. This hexacanth embryo with 6 hooklets inside the egg is called oncosphere .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old woman presented to you with complaints of tingling and numbness in her legs . On examination, her hands appear as shown in the image, ankle reflex was absent and Romberg's test was positive . Which of the following is most likely implicated in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with cutaneous hyperpigmentation and features of subacute combined degeneration are suggestive of vitamin B12 deficiency . This can be caused by Diphyllobothrium latum. The anemia develops because the tapeworm absorbs a large quantity of vitamin B12 and interferes with its ileal absorption leading to vitamin B12 deficiency . This can also lead to megaloblastic anemia (Bothriocephalus anemia). In severe cases , patients may exhibit neurological features of vitamin B12 deficiency like: • Tingling and numbness569 • Bilateral lower limb weakness • Bilateral hypertonia • Sensory ataxia (Romberg's positive ) • Absent deep tendon reflexes . It is treated with parenteral vitamin B12 supplementation .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms most commonly causes Katayama fever?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , Katayama fever is most commonly caused by Schistosoma mansoni. It is an immune complex mediated disease caused by antibodies to the schistosomulae , adult worms, and eggs . This acute illness consists of fever, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and allergic manifestations . The diagnosis is by the demonstration of the eggs in feces . Praziquantel is effective in the treatment. Glucocorticoids are given to suppress hypersensitivity reactions . Instances of Katayama fever are rarer in infections with Schistosoma haematobium compared to S. mansoni. *Note : Katayama fever is most commonly caused by S. japonicum and S. mansoni. But, among the given options , S. mansoni is the most common cause of Katayama fever.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 20 -year-old male patient presents to the OPD with complaints of fever, intermittent abdominal pain, and burning micturition. He gives a history of swimming in a freshwater lake 10 days back. Urine microscopy shows the following . Which of the following is the causative agent?

options.d: Schistosoma species cannot be determined based on egg

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture and image showing an egg that is non-operculated with the terminal spine at one pole are suggestive of infection with Schistosoma hematobium . Species differentiation of schistosoma can be done based on the location of the spine as follows : • Terminal spine - Schistosoma hematobium • Lateral spine - Schistosoma mansoni • Rudimentary lateral spine - Schistosoma japonicum The image below shows egg of Schistosoma mansoni. Adult worms of S. mansoni live in the inferior mesenteric vein.570 Adult worms of S. japonicum live in the superior mesenteric vein draining the ileocecal region. They are also seen in the intrahepatic portal venules and hemorrhoidal plexus of veins. The image below shows an egg of Schistosoma japonicum.Adult worms of S. hematobium live in the vesical and pelvic plexus of veins. The below image shows the life cycle of S.hematobium :571

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old fisherman presented with complaints of blood in the urine. A diagnostic cystoscopy was done and the microscopic view of the biopsied specimen is given below . Which of the following is most likely to be associated with this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the image showing keratin pearls are suggestive of squamous cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder . It is associated with Schistosoma hematobium infection . Chronic schistosomiasis presents as painless hematuria, dysuria, and proteinuria. Fibrosis may cause obstructive uropathies like hydronephrosis and hydroureter . It has been associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder. Such malignancy is detected in a younger age group as compared to transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder . The following parasites cause malignancies: • Schistosoma hematobium - bladder carcinoma • Clonorchis sinensis and Opisthorchis viverrini - bile duct carcinoma

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Identify the parasite from the given life cycle .
mcqs.explanation: The given life cycle belongs to Fasciola hepatica . Fasciola hepatica (sheep liver fluke ) causes disease primarily in sheep and other domestic animals. Humans are infected by eating watercress (or other aquatic plants) contaminated by larvae (metacercariae) that excyst in the duodenum , penetrate the gut wall, and reach the liver, where they mature into adults . The adult flukes in the bile ducts produce eggs , which are excreted in the feces . The eggs hatch in freshwater and miracidia enter the snails. Miracidia develop into cercariae, which then encyst on aquatic vegetation . Sheep and humans eat the plants, thus completing the life cycle .572 Most infections are asymptomatic . Halzoun is a painful pharyngitis caused by the presence of adult flukes on the posterior pharyngeal wall after eating raw sheep liver. Obstructive jaundice can occur months or years later. Diagnosis is made by identification of the eggs in the feces .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms does the given life cycle belong to?
mcqs.explanation: The given life cycle belongs to Clonorchis sinensis. It causes clonorchiasis (Asian liver fluke infection ). The hosts for Clonorchis sinensis are: • Definitive host- humans • First intermediate host- snail • Second intermediate host- fish Humans are infected by eating raw or undercooked fish containing the encysted larvae (metacercariae). In the duodenum , metacercaria will undergo excystation and migrate to bile ducts to develop into adult worms. The eggs containing miracidia are excreted in human feces which are then ingested by snails. Miracidium hatches out in the midgut of the snail. Inside the snail, sporocyst develops into 1st and 2nd generation redia and then to cercariae. The cercariae now penetrate the fish and develop into metacercaria (infective form). Chronic clonorchiasis is strongly associated with cholangiocarcinoma.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A wet mount examination of the stool sample of a patient with abdominal pain and diarrhea is given below . Which of the following parasites is he likely infected with?
mcqs.explanation: The given image showing an operculated egg (egg having a lid-like structure on its end) in the stool sample is suggestive of Fasciola hepatica infection . The eggs of Fasciola hepatica are large, ovoid, operculated , and bile stained . They contain an immature larva (miracidium) and do not float in the saturated salt solution . The following are the parasites with operculated eggs : • Fasciola hepatica • Fasciolopsis buski • Fasciola gigantica • Paragonimus westermani • Opisthorchis felineus • Clonorchis sinensis • Gastrodiscoides hominis • Diphyllobothrium latum573 Eggs of Schistosoma japonicum, Enterobius vermicularis, and Ancylostoma duodenale are non-operculated .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old patient has a history of travel to China and the consumption of pickled crab. He now complains of rusty sputum and cough . What is the most likely causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of infection with Paragonimus westermani . Paragonimus westermani is a trematode . The transmission to humans occurs by eating raw or undercooked crab or crayfish containing metacercariae. The metacercariae excyst in the human gut and young worms migrate to the lungs , where they become encapsulated in lung tissue . The patient complains of cough , chest pain, and hemoptysis . The viscous sputum is speckled with golden -brown eggs . Praziquantel (25 mg/ kg TDS for 1-2 days) is the drug of choice .574

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following parasites is ovoviviparous ?
mcqs.explanation: Strongyloides stercoralis is an ovoviviparous parasite. Nematodes are classified as follows : • Oviparous - lay eggs : • Unsegmented eggs : Ascaris lumbricoides , Trichuris trichuria • Segmented eggs : Ancylostoma duodenale, Necator americanus • Eggs containing larva : Enterobius vermicularis • Viviparous - produce larvae. e.g., Trichinella spiralis, Wuchereria bancrofti, Brugia malayi • Ovoviviparous – lay eggs containing fully formed larvae that hatch immediately . e.g., Strongyloides stercoralis587

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Identify the helminth from the life cycle given below .
mcqs.explanation: The image shows the life cycle of Strongyloides stercoralis. The infective form of strongyloides is the filariform larva . Infection occurs through penetration of the skin by larvae in the soil. Then, they migrate to the small intestine . The larvae molt twice and become adult female worms in the small intestine . The eggs laid in the mucosa of the intestine hatch immediately releasing the rhabditiform larva (L1 stage ). These rhabditiform larvae in the bowel can develop directly into filariform larvae that penetrate the colonic wall or perianal skin and enter the circulation to repeat the migration. This establishes ongoing internal reinfection . The rhabditiform larva can be seen on microscopic examination of stool .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old patient presented with complaints of diarrhea, vomiting, and abdominal pain for 1 week . The stool microscopy revealed the following . What is the appropriate treatment for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the stool microscopy showing the rhabditiform larva of S. stercoralis are suggestive of strongyloidiasis. The most appropriate treatment for this condition would be ivermectin. Strongyloidiasis is caused by Strongyloides stercoralis. It is generally a benign and asymptomatic condition. In some cases , there may be cutaneous , pulmonary, and intestinal manifestations .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An 8-year-old child was brought with complaints of perianal itching which is worse in the night. The scotch tape method demonstrates eggs as shown in the image given below . What is the most likely causative agent ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of perianal itching and the scotch tape microscopy showing the eggs are suggestive of infestation with pinworm (Enterobius vermicularis). The eggs of pinworm are plano-convex in shape , colorless , non-bile stained , and float in the saturated salt solution . Eggshell is double layered and relatively thick, though transparent. Since pinworms are not released in feces , the diagnosis cannot be made by conventional fecal ova and parasite tests . NIH swab method and the scotch tape method are used for the collection of specimens . The NIH swab (National Institutes of Health , USA) consists of a glass rod, at one end of which a piece of transparent cellophane is attached with a rubber band. The cellophane part is used for swabbing by rolling over the perianal area. It is returned to the test tube and sent to the laboratory. The cellophane piece is detached , spread over a glass side , and examined microscopically . The image given below shows the NIH swab.588 In scotch tape method , the tape is firmly pressed against the anal margin, covering all sides . The tape is transferred to a glass slide with sticky side down. Then a drop of toluene is added for clearing and examined under the microscope .The below image shows the life cycle of Enterobius vermicularis.589

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following helminthic infections that is commonly transmitted by soil, is characterized by\037 the egg in stool as shown in the image below ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows the egg of Trichuris trichiura (whipworm). The characteristic features of whipworm eggs are: • Eggs are barrel-shaped in the middle with a projecting mucus plug at each pole containing an unsegmented ovum. The plugs are colorless . • They float in the saturated salt solution. • It has a triple shell , the outermost layer of which is stained brown. They are commonly transmitted by soil. The eggs passed in the stool are unembryonated . Microscopic identification of the eggs in a stool specimen is diagnostic of whipworm infection . In moderate infections of 20 adult worms or less , the worms are confined to the caecum and ascending colon. The symptoms include epigastric and lower abdominal pain, diarrhoea (rarely bloody ), vomiting, flatulence and distention, weight loss, and increased blood and iron loss. In heavy infections of 200 adult worms or more (trichuriasis dysentery syndrome), the worms are in the distal colon and rectum. The symptoms include bloody diarrhoea with profuse mucus, abdominal pain, tenesmus , weight loss leading to cachexia, severe anemia, and rectal prolapse . On examination, clubbing may be present. Blood investigations may show moderate eosinophilia . Chronic infection leads to growth retardation and nutritional deficiencies . Around 0.005 ml of blood is lost per day per worm. In heavy infections , as much as 4 to 5 ml can be lost per day per worm. Treatment is mebendazole or albendazole .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A college student came to the OPD with fever and muscle aches . He tells you he had consumed smoked pork at a party 2 weeks back. Following this, he had developed abdominal cramps and diarrhea which had resolved on their own. CBC revealed eosinophilia and the muscle biopsy showed the following finding. What is the causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: 590 The given clinical scenario and muscle biopsy showing larvae are suggestive of trichinellosis . It is caused by Trichinella spiralis. Trichinella spiralis is known as the pork worm since the infection is acquired by consuming raw or undercooked pork. The initial infection presents with diarrhea and abdominal pain. In the later phase of the infection , the larvae move from the intestines into the circulation and migrate into muscles where they are encysted . This causes symptoms like fever and myalgia. These larvae are calcified in about 5-6 months. Eosinophilia caused by parasitic infection also comes down after 6 months. Detection of spiral larva in muscle tissue is done by performing a muscle biopsy . Deltoid , biceps , gastrocnemius, or pectoralis muscles are usually selected for biopsy . Other parasites that can be demonstrated in a muscle biopsy are: • T. solium • T. cruzi (amastigote ) The image below shows Trichinella spiralis larvae within the muscle .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: In a patient with a positive Bachman intradermal test , which of the following infections will you suspect ?
mcqs.explanation: Bachman intradermal test is used for the diagnosis of trichinellosis . In this test , 1:5,000 or 1:10 ,000 dilution of the trichinella larval antigen is injected intradermally. An erythematous wheal appears in positive cases within 15-20 minutes . The test remains positive for years after infection .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Identify the organism shown in this image.
mcqs.explanation: 591 The given image shows the Ascaris lumbricoides (roundworm). It is the most common of human helminths and is distributed worldwide. Adult worms live in the small intestine (85% in the jejunum and 15% in the ileum ). The roundworm, Ascaris lumbricoides is the largest nematode parasite in the human intestine . The adult worms are large cylindrical worms, with tapering ends , the anterior end being more pointed than the posterior. Man is the natural host. There is no intermediate host. Infection occurs through food or water contaminated with nightsoil or human feces containing eggs of ascaris. The eggs contain the infective rhabditiform larva .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 9- year-old boy was brought to the casualty with fever and colicky abdominal pain. An erect X-ray abdomen showed multiple air-fluid levels . Stool examination revealed the following egg . Which of the following is false about the organism causing this condition?

options.d: Egg containing L1 larva is infective

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the image are suggestive of ascariasis caused by Ascaris lumbricoides . Embryonated egg containing the L3 larva is the infective form. Man is the only natural host. There is no intermediate host. The infection is acquired via the consumption of food or water contaminated with eggs . The eggs hatch after reaching the duodenum to release the larvae. These penetrate the intestinal mucosa and enter the portal vessels . From the liver, larvae reach the systemic circulation, lungs and then reach the small intestine to produce symptoms . Clinical features : Due to the migrating larvae: • Fever • Dry cough • Asthmatic wheezing • Loeffler 's syndrome Due to the adult worm: • Asymptomatic • Nutritional effects - protein-energy malnutrition, Vitamin A deficiency • Toxic effects - urticaria, angioedema due to hypersensitivity • Mechanical effects - colicky abdominal pain, volvulus, and intestinal obstruction • Ectopic ascariasis - acute biliary obstruction, pancreatitis , and obstructive appendicitis . The life cycle of Ascaris lumbricoides is given below .592

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause for visceral larva migrans?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause for visceral larva migrans is Toxocara canis. It occurs most commonly in children and presents as fever, hepatosplenomegaly , and pneumonitis . Larva migrans is generally seen when human infection occurs with nonhuman species of nematodes . It can be classified into cutaneous or visceral types , depending on whether the larval migration takes place in the skin or in deeper tissues . Visceral larva migrans is caused by the migration of nematode larvae that are acquired via the oral route . Cutaneous larva migrans is caused by the migration of nematode larvae (most commonly Ancylostoma braziliense) that are acquired via skin penetration . Patients having visceral larva migrans may develop neurological disturbances (neural larva migrans) and endophthalmitis (ophthalmic larva migrans). Differences between cutaneous larva migrans and visceral larva migrans:Cutaneous larva migrans Visceral larva migrans Tissue involved Skin Various organs of the body li ke the liver, lungs , and eyes Infecting Organis m Mostly by non-human nemat odes Mostly by non-human nemat odes (mainly by dog and cat) Portal of Entry Penetration of skin Ingestion of infected eggs Eosinophilia Mild Persistent high Serodiagnosis Not developed Well developed Treatment Thiabendazole Diethylcarbamazine and pred nisolone593

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged woman comes to the OPD with complaints of weakness for the past 3 months. She is diagnosed to have microcytic hypochromic anemia. The stool microscopy reveals the following . What is the most probable causative agent ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of iron deficiency anemia and the stool microscopy showing the egg is suggestive of infection by Ancylostoma duodenale . Eggs of both Ancylostoma duodenale (old world hookworm) and Necator americanus (new world hookworm) are identical . The hookworm eggs are oval or elliptical in shape , colorless , and non-bile stained . It has a thin transparent hyaline shell membrane. The ovum is segmented with 4 to 8 blastomeres . There is a clear space between the segmented ovum and eggshell . Eggs float in the saturated salt solution . Humans are infected when filariform larvae in moist soil penetrate the skin or subcutaneous tissue . The larvae are then carried in the venous circulation to the heart and lungs , where they may cause mild transient pneumonitis or bronchitis. They migrate up the respiratory tract to the pharynx, are swallowed , and reach the small intestine producing epigastric pain, dyspepsia, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. A. duodenale or N. americanus ingest blood, secrete anticoagulants , and interfere with the absorption of iron, B12 , and folic acid. This leads to iron deficiency anemia and protein-energy malnutrition resulting from blood loss. The average blood loss of the host per worm per day is 0.2 mL with Ancylostoma duodenale and 0.03 mL with Necator americanus.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient presented to the OPD with dry cough , low-grade fever and wheezing . He is diagnosed with Loeffler 's syndrome. Which of the following parasites does not cause this?
mcqs.explanation: Loeffler 's syndrome is an eosinophilic inflammation of the lung caused by Ascaris lumbricoides , Strongyloides stercoralis and Necator americanus. Enterobius vermicularis does not cause Loeffler 's syndrome. It is associated with pneumonia characterized by dry cough , low-grade fever, wheezing , urticaria, and eosinophilia. Parasites causing Loeffler 's syndrome are: • Migrating larva of: • Ascaris lumbricoides • Strongyloides stercoralis • Ancylostoma duodenale • Necator americanus • Echinococcus granulosus • Cryptosporidium parvum • Eggs of Paragonimus westermani • Entamoeba histolytica • Trichomonas tenax594

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 27-year-old woman had gone on a trek in the Amazon rainforest. A month later she presented to the OPD with the following lesion which was painful and pruritic. Her systemic examination was normal . Which of the following organisms is most likely to cause this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the image showing serpiginous skin lesions are suggestive of cutaneous larva migrans or creeping eruption or ground itch. This is most commonly caused by Ancylostoma braziliense. Cutaneous larva migrans is caused by non-human hookworms like Ancylostoma braziliense and Ancylostoma caninum. It is acquired via direct skin contact with soil contaminated by dog or cat feces . The larvae remain confined to the outer layers of skin, as they are unable to penetrate the basement membrane of the human skin. It presents as erythematous , pruritic papules at the site of entry and serpiginous tracks in the epidermis . The symptoms begin to appear within the first two weeks of the patient 's return from a tropical or endemic country. The larval track progresses at approximately 1 cm/h with cutaneous lesions only progressing a few millimeters to a few centimeters daily. Diagnosis is based mainly on clinical features . The treatment includes : • Thiabendazole topical application • Albendazole 400mg/day X 3 days or • Ivermectin 200mcg /kg single dose stat The differences between cutaneous larva migrans and visceral larva migrans are: Note : A rapidly moving lesion (10cm/hr) produced by Strongyloides stercoralis is known as larva currens (running larva ). It occurs as an otherwise asymptomatic lesion in immunocompetent individuals. In immunocompromised, hyper -infestation syndrome occurs with paralytic ileus and secondary Gram-negative sepsis .Cutaneous larva migrans Visceral larva migrans Tissue involved Skin Various organs of the body li ke the liver, lungs , and eyes Infecting Organis m Mostly by non-human nemat odes Mostly by non-human nemat odes (mainly by dog and cat) Portal of Entry Penetration of skin Ingestion of infected eggs Eosinophilia Mild Persistent high Serodiagnosis Not developed Well developed Treatment Thiabendazole Diethylcarbamazine and pred nisolone

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which the following filarial worms are non-pathogenic to humans?
mcqs.explanation: Mansonella ozzardi is generally non-pathogenic to humans.595 Option A: Onchocerca volvulus infection may manifest as skin nodules or onchocercoma which are formed as a result of fibroblastic reaction around adult worms deep in the subcutaneous tissues . Microfilariae cause lesions in the skin and eyes . Options B and C: In lymphatic filariasis (Wuchereria and Brugia), the typical manifestations are caused by the adult worms blocking lymph nodes and vessels . Microfilaria (larval form) are responsible for allergic manifestations seen in occult filariasis.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old man came to the hospital with complaints of progressive swelling of his legs . On examination, you note bilateral non-pitting edema of the lower limbs with thickening of the overlying skin. What is the best next step in the management of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture is suggestive of lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis ). The best next step would be to test the night blood for worms since the filarial species is nocturnally periodic (between 10 pm and 4 am) in India. Lymphatic filariasis is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti and Brugia malayi. Elephantiasis is a delayed sequel to repeated lymphangitis , obstruction, and lymphedema . Repeated leakage of lymph into tissues first results in lymphedema , then to elephantiasis . Diethylcarbamazine is the drug of choice. Option A: PCR is negative in chronic filariasis. Options B & D: Lymphangiography and lymphoscintigraphy may be used to demonstrate abnormal lymphatic urinary fistula leading to chyluria in chronic filariasis.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A child from Bihar is brought to the AIIMS ER with a high-grade fever. On examination, bilaterally enlarged, tender inguinal lymph nodes are present . The peripheral smear examination finding is shown in the image. What is the most likely causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the peripheral smear showing sheathed microfilaria with two nuclei at the tail tip is suggestive of infection with Brugia malayi. Acute infection may manifest as acute adenolymphangitis which is characterized by high fever, lymphatic inflammation (lymphangitis and lymphadenitis ) and transient local edema . The most commonly affected lymph nodes are inguinal nodes followed by axillary nodes which become enlarged , painful and tender . The following are the characteristic features of microfilaria of Brugia malayi: • Smaller in size compared to microfilaria of W. bancrofti. • Shows kinks and secondary curves. • Cephalic space is longer. • Carries double stylets at the anterior end. • Nuclear column appears blurred in Giemsa-stained films. • Tail tip carries 2 distinct nuclei , one terminal and the other subterminal. The below image shows the microfilaria of Brugia malayi.596

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient from Kerala has presented to your OPD with fever. A magnified view of peripheral blood smear is shown below . Which of the following is false regarding the organism seen ?

options.a: DEC provocation test is used to demonstrate microfilaria during the day
options.b: Second stage filariform larva is the infective form
options.c: Microfilaria is the major diagnostic form
options.d: Filarial stage of adult worms are responsible for disease

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with a peripheral smear showing sheathed microfilaria with a pointed tail free of nuclei is suggestive of Wuchereria bancrofti. The third stage filariform larva is the infective form. Wuchereria bancrofti infection is usually asymptomatic . The symptoms are due to obstruction of lymphatics by the filarial stage of adult worms. The lymphatic vessels of the male genitalia are most commonly affected in bancroftian filariasis, producing episodic funiculitis , epididymitis , and orchitis. Adenolymphangitis of the extremities is less common. Hydrocele is the most common sign of chronic bancroftian filariasis, followed by lymphedema , elephantiasis , and chyluria. The swelling involves the whole leg , the whole arm , the scrotum, the vulva , or the breast. DEC provocation test is used to demonstrate microfilaria during the day. The image below shows the life cycle of Wuchereria bancrofti.597 The image below shows the difference between microfilaria of various filarial nematodes .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 54-year-old farmer from Assam presented with the finding shown in the image. He had also developed a painless swelling in his elbow 2 years back which has gradually been increasing in size. Which of the following is the drug of choice to treat this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario and image showing sclerosing keratitis are suggestive of onchocerchiasis (river blindness ). The drug of choice is ivermectin. It is caused by Onchocerca volvulus. It is also known as convoluted filaria or blinding filaria. The vector is blackfly (Simulium species ) which breed in fast-flowing rivers , and therefore the disease is most common along the course of rivers . Hence , it is also called river blindness . The usual presentation is formation of a subcutaneous nodule or onchocercoma. It is a firm non-tender nodule arising from bony sites like scalp , elbow , ribs, and iliac crest. It is associated with pruritus and rashes.598 The microfilaria in the eyes cause photophobia and gradual loss of vision. The most severe manifestation is sclerosing keratitis and chorioretinitis which causes blindness . It is the 2nd major infective cause of blindness in the world after trachoma. Suramin and diethylcarbamazine (DEC) were used earlier but are not used nowadays. DEC destroys microfilariae but usually causes Mazzotti reaction consisting of pruritus, rash, lymphadenopathy , fever, hypotension , and occasionally, eye damage . Note : Onchocerciasis is not endemic in India but sporadic cases have been reported from North-Eastern India.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged woman presents to your clinic with photosensitivity , redness , and watering of the eyes for the last 2 days. She shows you this photo of a swelling in her hand that had arisen 2 weeks back but disappeared in just 3 days. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the image showing Calabar swelling is suggestive of loiasis caused by Loa loa. Calabar swellings are temporary foci of inflammation that appear as Loa loa wanders through the subcutaneous tissues . They are up to 3 cm in size and are also called fugitive swellings because they disappear in a few days only to reappear elsewhere . Loa loa is transmitted by the bite of Chrysops species (deerflies ). The infective form is the third stage microfilaria. After entry into human skin, it grows into an adult worm. The ocular manifestations occur when the worm reaches the subconjunctival tissue during its wanderings. They include : • Granuloma in bulbar conjunctiva • Painless edema of the eyelids • Proptosis. The image below shows Calabar swelling.The image below shows a live, adult Loa loa in the anterior chamber of the eye .599

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is also known as Weingarten syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Tropical pulmonary eosinophilia is also known as Weingarten syndrome. Tropical eosinophilia occurs as a result of hypersensitivity reaction to microfilarial antigens and not directly due to lymphatic involvement. It is a manifestation of occult filariasis (Meyer 's-Kouwenaar syndrome). Clinical features of occult filariasis include massive eosinophilia and hepatosplenomegaly . Synonyms of tropical pulmonary eosinophilia include - • Weingarten syndrome • Pseudo -tuberculosis of the lung • Eosinophilic pseudo -leukemia • Tropical eosinophilic asthma • Frimodt-Moller and Barton 's syndrome

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is known as serpent worm?
mcqs.explanation: Dracunculus medinensis is known as serpent worm. It is a viviparous nematode . This has been eradicated from India and all of the southeast Asian region in the year 2000 .
