mcqs.question: Match the following parasites with their respective hosts :
mcqs.explanation: 600 Parasite Definitive host First intermediate host Second intermediate ho st Diphyllobothri um Humans Cyclops Cyclops and fish Paragonimus Humans Snail Crayfish and crab Fasciola Sheep and hu mans Snail Aquatic vegetations Brugia Humans Mansonia mosquito -601

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: While assessing the quality of drinking water in a village, you detect the presence of coliform bacilli by the multiple tube technique . Following this, you decide to perform the Eijkman test . What is this test also known as?
mcqs.explanation: Eijkman test is also known as differential coliform test . Drinking water should be free of any pathogenic microorganisms . The presence of coliform bacteria in the water may indicate faecal pollution , while the detection of E.coli confirms it. The presumptive coliform test is done by the multiple tube technique . Following this, the Eijkman test is done to confirm the presence of E. coli. They can grow at 44\260C (faecal thermotolerant bacilli), ferment lactose and cause indole and gas production . Option A: Presumptive coliform count detects the probable number of coliform bacilli in water. It can be positive due to the presence of organisms other than E.coli also. Option C: Colony counts provide an estimate of the general bacterial purity of water. Option D: Methylene blue reduction test is used to assess the bacterial contamination of milk.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Faecal contamination of a water source is suspected by the mayor of a municipal corporation. He asks you to test the water for evidence of recent contamination. The presence of which of the following organisms would suggest this?
mcqs.explanation: Recent fecal contamination of water is suggested by the presence of enterococcus (fecal streptococci ). Clostridium perfringens may be present for a long duration. If it is present in water, it suggests that contamination is not recent . If Escherichia coli is detected , it is definitive proof of fecal contamination. However, it is non-specific for suggesting the duration of the contamination.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following tests is not used for bacteriological examination of milk?
mcqs.explanation: Pasteurization is not used for the bacteriological examination of milk. Pasteurization is the process of applying heat , to milk, for a specified period for the purpose of killing pathogenic bacteria. There are two methods : holder method and flash method . Option A: Methylene blue reduction test depends on the reduction of methylene blue by bacteria in milk when incubated at 37 \260C in complete darkness. Option B: Resazurin test is similar to methylene blue reduction test , but the dye resazurin on reduction passes through a series of colour changes from blue to pink to colourless . The shade of colour after incubation with milk for a particular period of time depends on the degree of contamination.608 Option C: Phosphatase test is used to check whether milk has been pasteurised . Positive test after pasteurisation of milk shows contamination after pasteurisation .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The following image depicts :
mcqs.explanation: The image depicts the production of monoclonal antibodies by hybridoma technology . The following are the steps involved in hybridoma technology : • Mice are immunized with an antigen. After several weeks of immunization , blood samples are obtained from mice for measurement of serum antibodies . • When the antibody titer is high enough , mice are commonly boosted by injecting antigen without adjuvant intraperitoneally or intravenously. Then the mice are euthanized and their spleens removed for in vitro hybridoma cell production . • Fusing antibody-producing spleen cells , which have a limited life span with myeloma cells (derived from an immortal tumor of lymphocytes ) results in a hybridoma that is capable of unlimited growth . • The cells are cultured in a medium containing hypoxanthine , aminopterin, and thymidine (HAT medium ) which allows only the fused cells to survive in culture . • Monoclonal antibodies are then harvested .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about hybridoma is false ?

options.a: Specific antibody-producing cells are integrated with myeloma cells .
options.b: Myeloma cells using salvage pathway grow well in HAT medium.
options.c: Aminopterin, a folate antagonist, inhibits de novo pathway .
options.d: HGPRTase and thymidylate synthetase are required for salvage pathway .

mcqs.explanation: Aminopterin is a folate antagonist present in the HAT medium that inhibits the de novo pathway of nucleotide synthesis . Since myeloma cells cannot use the salvage pathway for nucleotide synthesis due to the lack of HGPRTase enzyme, they cannot survive in the HAT medium.609 Hybridoma technology is a method for producing large numbers of identical antibodies (monoclonal antibodies ). Hybridomas are somatic cell hybrids produced by fusing the antibody-forming spleen cells with myeloma cells . The resultant hybrid thus has both the antibody-producing ability of the B-cell and the ability to multiply indefinitely of the myeloma. The following are the steps involved in hybridoma technology : • Mice are immunized with an antigen. After several weeks of immunization , blood samples are obtained from mice for measurement of serum antibodies . • When the antibody titer is high enough , mice are commonly boosted by injecting antigen without adjuvant intraperitoneally or intravenously. Then the mice are euthanized and their spleens removed for in vitro hybridoma cell production . • Fusing antibody-producing spleen cells , which have a limited life span with myeloma cells (derived from an immortal tumor of lymphocytes ) results in a hybridoma that is capable of unlimited growth . • The cells are cultured in a medium containing hypoxanthine , aminopterin, and thymidine (HAT medium ) which allows only the fused cells to survive in culture . • Monoclonal antibodies are then harvested .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is both a diffusion and a dilution method of testing antibiotic sensitivity?
mcqs.explanation: Epsilometer (E-test ) is both a diffusion and a dilution method of testing antibiotic sensitivity . It is a quantitative technique for determining the antimicrobial susceptibility (AST) and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) in \265 g/mL of gram-negative and gram-positive aerobic bacteria.610 The antibiotic sensitivity tests are classified as follows : • Diffusion methods : Kirby–Bauer method , Stokes method • Dilution methods : Tube dilution method , Agar dilution method • Diffusion and dilution method : E–test (Epsilometer )

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: In which of the following is the disc diffusion method for antibiotic susceptibility testing applied ?
mcqs.explanation: The disc diffusion method for antibiotic susceptibility testing is applied in the Kirby-Bauer method . To perform Kirby-Bauer's disc diffusion method , a suitable standard dilution of a broth culture of the test bacterium is inoculated on the surface of a solid medium (Cation-adjusted Mueller -Hinton agar) as a lawn culture . After drying, various antibiotic discs are placed on its surface . Zones of inhibition around the disc are recorded and interpreted according to the zone diameters available in the tables of the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI ) guidelines . The results obtained are qualitative (resistant, sensitive , or partially sensitive ). Laboratory testing for antibiotic sensitivity can be done by: • Diffusion method - Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method , Stokes disc diffusion method • Dilution method - broth dilution method, agar dilution method • Combination of diffusion and dilution method - E–test (Epsilometer ) The image below shows Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method .611

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following methods of antibiotic susceptibility testing cannot be used to calculate the minimum inhibitory concentration of an antimicrobial drug?
mcqs.explanation: Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) cannot be calculated using Kirby-Bauer's disk diffusion method and Stokes disk diffusion method as they are semi-quantitative methods . MIC is the lowest concentration of an antimicrobial agent that will inhibit the visible growth of a microorganism . Methods to determine MIC include : • Tube dilution method • Agar dilution method • E-test method

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A microbiologist is about to run a polymerase chain reaction assay on the serum of a patient suspected to have Q fever. He wishes to quantify the PCR by monitoring the amplification process while the PCR is ongoing. Which of the following types of PCR should he perform?
mcqs.explanation: Real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) can be used to quantify the PCR by monitoring the amplification process while the PCR is ongoing. Types of PCR: • Reverse transcriptase PCR- The enzyme reverse transcriptase (RT) is used to synthesize a complementary copy of DNA (cDNA) from RNA and this cDNA is then used as a template for PCR. • Real-time PCR- This helps quantify the PCR and gives an estimate of the pathogen DNA load in the specimen. It uses fluorescent dyes or specific DNA probes . It is also known as qPCR (Quantitative PCR) • Multiplex PCR- Primers to more than one pathogen are used simultaneously and hence multiple products are obtained .612 • Nested PCR- It involves the sequential use of two primer sets . The first primer set is used for amplification and the amplicon obtained is then used as a target sequence for second amplification. This ensures specificity .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following investigations does not use antibody marking ?
mcqs.explanation: The hemagglutination test is not based on the principle of antibody marking . When antibodies bind to antigens on the surface of red blood cells , the resultant clumping reaction is referred to as hemagglutination. It is routinely performed to type red blood cells in ABO blood-typing . The image below shows hemagglutination.In ELISA , radioimmunoassay and immunofluorescence , the antigens or antibodies are labeled or marked with enzymes , fluorescent dyes, etc . Note : If no hemagglutination occurs it means the patient 's serum has anti-haemagglutinin antibodies that bind to hemagglutinin and prevent the clumping reaction. This hemagglutination inhibition reaction is a method of detection of viruses and antiviral -antibodies and is used to make a diagnosis of influenza.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not used as an immediate test in the screening of urinary tract infections ?
mcqs.explanation: Pour plate culture (quantitative test ) is not used as an immediate test for screening of UTI . However, it is considered the best diagnostic test for confirmation of UTI due it's high sensitivity and specificity . The screening tests for UTI are as follows : • Wet mount examination- It is done to demonstrate pus cells in urine.613 • Leukocyte esterase test - It is a rapid and cheaper method and detects leukocyte esterases secreted by pus cells present in urine. • Nitrate reduction test (Griess test )- Nitrate reducing bacteria like E. coli gives a positive result . • Catalase test - E. coli and other bacteria that produce the enzyme catalase give a positive result . Quantitative Culture : • Standardized loop technique • Pour plate method

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The CLED medium is preferred over MacConkey agar for the culture of organisms in case of UTI because :

options.b: It promotes the growth of candida, streptococcus and staphylococcus
options.c: It differentiates between lactose -fermenting and non-lactose fermenting bacteria
options.d: It promotes the growth of pseudomonas

mcqs.explanation: CLED (Cysteine lactose electrolyte -deficient) medium is preferred over MacConkey agar for the culture of organisms involved in urinary tract infections because it is less inhibitory and promotes the growth of gram-positive bacteria (except \037 hemolytic streptococcus ) and candida. It is used as an alternative to the combination of blood agar and MacConkey agar, for the processing of urine specimens . CLED medium is not similar to blood agar in the fact that it can prevent swarming of proteus . It is similar to MacConkey agar in that it differentiates between lactose fermenters and non-fermenters.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient who had been receiving ceftazidime and amikacin via central venous line for a week suddenly spiked a fever. Blood culture is positive for a vancomycin -resistant, catalase -negative organism whose Gram-stained image is given below . Identify the organism.
mcqs.explanation: From the given case scenario and image we can deduce that the most likely organism involved is Enterococcus faecalis . The image shows gram-positive cocci in chains, that are described as catalase negative . This helps rule out Staphylocococcus aureus and coagulase -negative staphylococcus .614 Streptococcus viridans is usually sensitive to penicillin and vancomycin hence it is ruled out. The mechanism of vancomycin resistance seen in E. faecalis is the alteration of the D-alanyl–D-alanine chain in the cell wall.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a bioterrorism category A agent ?
mcqs.explanation: Bacillus anthracis which causes anthrax is categorized under category A bioterrorism agent .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The test kit shown in the image below works on the principle of:
mcqs.explanation: The above image shows a HbsAg card test kit which works on the principle of immunochromatography. The immunochromatographic membrane is used for antigen detection , while a nitrocellulose membrane is used to absorb the antigen from a specimen . A coloured reaction appears directly on the membrane with the sequential addition of conjugate followed by the substrate . In some cases , the antigen is captured by a bound antibody directed against the antigen. These assays have the advantage of being rapid and also frequently include a built -in internal control.615

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a part of the vulva ?
mcqs.explanation: Cervix is not a part of the vulva . The vulva includes : • Mons veneris • Labia majora • Labia minora • Clitoris • Vestibule • Vestibular bulb • Greater vestibular glands. The vulva is posteriorly related to the perineum . The triangular space bounded by clitoris, labia minora and fourchette is the vestibule . It is present between the labia minora anteriorly and the introitus posteriorly . The posterior part of the vestibule between the fourchette and the vaginal introitus is called fossa navicularis . The vestibule has 4 openings :13 • Urethral opening • Vaginal orifice opening • Bartholin's duct on either side • Ducts of paraurethral glands

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding labia majora ?

options.a: They join posteriorly to form the posterior commissure
options.b: It is homologous to scrotum in male
options.c: The round ligament terminates at its posterior end
options.d: It contains sebaceous glands and apocrine glands

mcqs.explanation: The round ligament terminates at the anterior end of the labia majora . The labia majora lie on either side of the vulva and join posteriorly to form the posterior commissure. The inner side is hairless. Labia majora are homologous to the scrotum in males. The labia majora and the mons veneris contain: • Hair follicles • Sebaceous glands • Modified sweat glands, known as apocrine glands The labia minora are two cutaneous folds between the labia major . Anteriorly they enclose the clitoris and unite with each other in front and behind the clitoris to form prepuce and frenulum respectively . The labia minora are homologous to the ventral aspect of the penis . The clitoris is a small erectile body lying in the anterior-most part of the vulva . The clitoris is homologous to glans penis .14

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient presented to the gynecology OPD with the following finding. Which structure in men is homologous to the affected structure ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a Bartholin's cyst , which involves the Bartholin's glands. These glands are homologous to the male bulbourethral or Cowper glands. The ducts of Bartholin's glands open in the groove between the hymen and the labia minora at approximately 5 and 7 o'clock positions. They are stimulated by sexual arousal. The glands contain columnar cells that secrete mucus with lubricant properties . Contraction of the bulbospongiosus muscle expresses gland secretions . Bartholin's cyst occurs due to obstruction of the ducts of the Bartholin's glands by proteinaceous material, or due to infection . Symptomatic or recurrent cysts may require marsupialization or gland excision. An infected Bartholin's cyst can lead to an Bartholin's abscess . This requires surgical drainage.15

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the pH of the vagina before puberty ?
mcqs.explanation: The pH of the vagina before puberty is 7. In adult females , the pH is acidic. Doderlein 's bacilli (Lactobacillus sp.) are part of the normal vaginal flora. They produce lactic acid from glycogen in the vaginal epithelium and make the vaginal pH acidic. They are present in newborns and disappear in 10 -14 days. They reappear at puberty and disappear after menopause . Vaginal flora also includes microbes such as Clostridium welchii . Vaginal defence mechanisms are influenced by estrogen . In newborns, maternal estrogens maintain the defence mechanisms for 10 -14 days. After that, the levels wane. During puberty , the circulating estrogen maintains the defence mechanism. mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about relations of the vagina ?
mcqs.explanation: Bartholin's gland is present lateral to the vagina . The vagina is related to the following structures : • Anteriorly: • Bladder (upper 1/3rd) • Urethra (lower 2/3rd) • Posteriorly • Pouch of Douglas • Ampulla of the rectum • Perineal body • Laterally16 • Mackenrodt's ligament • Levator ani • Bartholin's glands

mcqs.question: Identify the type of hymen.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with uterine prolapse and urethrocele has weakness in the superficial and deep perineal muscles . What level of support is lost here?
mcqs.explanation: 18 In the given case scenario, level 3 supports including the superficial and deep perineal muscles are lost. This causes urethrocele . DeLancey's levels of support are used to describe the supports of the genital organs.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Anteflexion of the uterus is at the level of ___.
mcqs.explanation: Anteflexion of the uterus is seen at the level of the internal os. (Mnemonic - V for version, V for vagina ) The uterus normally lies in a position of anteversion and anteflexion . In the anteverted position, the external os is directed downward and backwards. On vaginal examination , the fingers come in contact with the anterior lip of the cervix as it is the lowest part. When the uterus is retroverted, the cervix is directed downward and forwards. The lowest part of the cervix becomes either the external os or its posterior lip.Angle of Anteversion Angle of Anteflexion The angle between thecervix and vagina The angle betweencervix and uterus 90o 120o19

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G3P2L2 woman presents in her third trimester with vaginal leaking. On PV examination, the anterior lip of the cervix can be palpated . What is the position of her uterus and the ligament that maintains this position?
mcqs.explanation: In the given clinical scenario, the uterus is anteverted as the anterior lip of the cervix was palpable . The round ligament helps maintain the anteversion of the uterus during pregnancy. However, the anteversion in the non-pregnant uterus is maintained by both the uterosacral ligament and round ligament . (Mnemonic - V for version, V for vagina ) The uterus normally lies in a position of anteversion and anteflexion . In the anteverted position, the external os is directed downward and backwards. On vaginal examination , the fingers come in contact with the anterior lip of the cervix as it is the lowest part. When the uterus is retroverted, the cervix is directed downward and forwards. The lowest part of the cervix becomes either the external os or its posterior lip. mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A multiparous woman presented with a urethrocele , due to weakness of the urogenital diaphragm. What is this structure also known as?
mcqs.explanation: The urogenital diaphragm is also known as the triangular ligament . The urogenital diaphragm extends from the pubic arch anteriorly to the central point of the perineum posteriorly and consists of two layers of fascia through which pass the vagina and the urethra. The central point of the female perineum lies between the vagina and the rectum. Urogenital triangle: • Present between 2 ischiopubic rami • Stretching transversely across the rami there are 3 membranes. • From above downwards the membranes are as follows : • Superior fascia of urogenital diaphragm • Inferior fascia of urogenital diaphragm • Membranous layer of superficial perineal fascia21

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the cavity of the uterus lined by?

options.a: Single layer of ciliated columnar epithelium
options.b: Double layer of ciliated columnar epithelium
options.c: Single layer of ciliated cuboidal epithelium
options.d: Double layer of ciliated cuboidal epithelium

mcqs.explanation: The uterine cavity is lined by a single layer of ciliated columnar epithelium . The wall of the uterus consists of 3 layers: • Perimetrium is the serous coat adherent to the underlying muscle . • Myometrium - it consists of thick bundles of muscles that form 3 distinct layers during pregnancy: • Outer longitudinal • Inner circular • Middle interlacing called living ligature • Endometrium - It is the mucous lining of the cavity. It consists of lamina propria and surface epithelium which is a single layer of ciliated columnar epithelium .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding uterine anatomy?

options.a: Round ligaments receive their blood supply from Sampson's artery
options.b: Transverse cervical ligaments are also called cardinal ligaments
options.c: Uterine innervation is by the pudendal nerve plexus
options.d: Lymphatic drainage is primarily to the obturator, internal and external iliac nodes .

mcqs.explanation: The uterus is innervated by the fibers of the uterovaginal plexus , also known as the Frankenhauser ganglion. Option A: Round ligaments receive their blood supply from Sampson's artery which represents the anastomosis of the uterine artery and ovarian artery. Option B: The cardinal ligaments are also called transverse cervical ligaments or Mackenrodt ligaments . They consist primarily of perivascular connective tissue . They attach to the posterolateral pelvic walls near the origin of the internal iliac artery and surround the vessels supplying the uterus and vagina . Option D: Lymphatic drainage of the uterus is primarily to the obturator and internal and external iliac nodes . One theory of endometriosis, states lymphatic spread as cause for seeding in the pelvis.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A gynecologist is performing a hysterectomy . She accidentally nicks the ureter in the ureteric canal as it pierces the Mackenrodt's ligaments . Which vessels are likely to be damaged here?

options.a: Uterine artery above and the uterine plexus of veins below
options.b: Uterine plexus of veins above and the uterine artery below
options.c: Ovarian artery above and the uterine artery below
options.d: Uterine artery above and the ovarian artery below

mcqs.explanation: The uterine artery above and uterine venous plexus below are likely to be damaged here, as the ureter is present between these vessels . The ureter pierces the Mackenrodt's ligament , forming the ureteric canal. In this canal, the ureter is crossed by the uterine artery above and the uterine plexus of veins below , thus being present in between the uterine vessels . The ureteric canal provides the necessary room for normal peristalsis , without pressure from the surrounding structures . After leaving the ureteric canal, the ureter passes forwards and medially to reach the bladder . It is 1-2 cm away from the cervix.23

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You take a culture swab from the portio vaginalis of a woman having foul smelling vaginal discharge. What is this region also known as?
mcqs.explanation: Portio vaginalis or exocervix is the other name for the vaginal part of the cervix. Cervix is the lowermost part of the uterus extending from the histological internal os to the external os. It is cylindrical in shape measuring 2.5 cm in length and diameter . Cervix is made up of 10 % muscle and the rest is collagen , elastin , and proteoglycan . The lining of the cervix has the following parts: • Exocervix - also known as portio vaginalis. It is lined by non keratinized stratified squamous epithelium . • Endocervix - it is lined by high columnar, ciliated epithelium . • Endocervical glands - secrete alkaline mucus. When enlarged , they form swellings called Nabothian follicles /cysts . • Transformation zone - the epithelium gradually changes from columnar to squamous in this region.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the cervix: corpus ratio before puberty ?
mcqs.explanation: The cervix:corpus ratio before puberty is 2:1. The relationship between the length of the cervix and that of the body of the uterus varies with age .Age Cervix/Corpus ratio Before puberty 2:1 At puberty 1:224 Age Cervix/Corpus ratio Reproductive a ge 1:3 or 1:4 After menopau se 2:1 - however, the uterus and cervix are both atrophied

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The remnants of Wolffian ducts in females are located in________.
mcqs.explanation: The Gartner's duct is a remnant of the Wolffian ducts in women. These are located in the broad ligament and the vagina . The Gartner's duct is an embryological remnant of the mesonephric duct /Wolffian duct formed during the development of the urinary and reproductive organs. It runs parallel to, but below , the fallopian tube in the mesosalpinx . The duct passes downwards by the side of the uterus to the level of the internal os where it passes into the tissues of the cervix. It then runs forwards to reach the anterolateral aspect of the vaginal wall and may reach as far down as the hymen. The duct can sometimes form a cyst in the broad ligament or in the vagina . It is called Gartner's cyst. It is a benign condition and can be treated with marsupialization.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about the contents of the broad ligament ?

options.a: Ovarian vessels in its infundibulopelvic part
options.c: Ureter is present the lower portion
options.d: Ovarian ligament in its anterior fold

mcqs.explanation: The ovarian ligaments are contained in the posterior fold of the broad ligament . The broad ligament contains the following parts: • Mesosalpinx - it lies between the fallopian tube and ovarian ligament . It contains the pelvic vessels - anastomoses between uterine and ovarian arteries. The ovary is attached via ovarian ligament through the posterior folds to the mesovarium.25 • Mesometrium - it contains the ovarian vessels within the infundibulopelvic ligament . The ureter is present in the inferomedial part of the broad ligament . It is related to the uterine artery here and may be damaged during hysterectomy . Note : Broad ligament is not a support of the uterus .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Where are Peg cells seen ?
mcqs.explanation: Peg cells are seen in the fallopian tubes. A peg cell is a non-ciliated epithelial cell within the fallopian tube . These cells are also known as intercalated or intercalary cells whose function is not yet known. The image below shows pale ciliated cells (arrows) and narrow , dark , non-ciliated peg cells (arrowheads).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the longest part of the fallopian tube ?
mcqs.explanation: The longest and widest part of the fallopian tube is the ampulla (5 cm).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Where is the tunica albuginea of the adult ovary derived from?

options.b: The sub epithelial connective tissue layer

mcqs.explanation: Tunica albuginea of the adult ovary is derived from the sub-epithelial connective tissue layer. Structure of the ovary : • Surface epithelium - a single layer of cuboidal cells is present , which later gives rise to the surface epithelium of the adult ovary . It is morphologically continuous with the mesothelium of the peritoneum .26 • The subepithelial connective tissue layer - gives rise to the tunica albuginea of the adult ovary and the basement membrane beneath the surface epithelium . • The parenchymatous zone - becomes the cortex and contains the egg nests and ovarian follicles . • Zona vasculosa - becomes the medulla and contains the blood vessels . Hilar cells present here are homologous to interstitial cells of testes . They can rarely produce hilar cell tumors of the ovary .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: During the histopathological examination of an ovarian mass, Call-Exner bodies are seen . In which of the following layers are these structures seen ?
mcqs.explanation: Call-Exner bodies are formed by granulosa cells present within the granulosa cell layer of the ovary . They are small, distinctive , glandlike structures filled with acidophilic material, resembling immature follicles . They are characteristically seen in granulosa cell tumors of the ovary . The image below shows Call-Exner bodies (circled in black).27 Graafian follicle : The mature Graafian follicle is spheroidal or ovoid in shape . It contains pent -up secretion known as the liquor folliculi . The lining consists of: • Theca externa • Theca interna - contain the theca cells • Granulosa cell layer • Cumulus oophorus - projection of granulosa cells into the cavity of the Graafian follicle . It is also called the discus proligerus .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Where is the sympathetic nerve supply of ovary derived from?
mcqs.explanation: 28 The efferent preganglionic sympathetic fibres to the ovary are derived from the T10 -T11 spinal levels . These fibres travel to the prevertebral ganglia, where they synapse . The postganglionic sympathetic fibres arising from these ganglia contribute to the ovarian plexus , which innervates the ovary . The ovarian plexus is a network of nerves comprising: • Postganglionic sympathetic fibres • Preganglionic parasympathetic fibres from the sacral outflow (S2-S4) • Visceral afferent fibres (responsible for transmitting sensory signals) The ovarian plexus has two parts based on its connections: • Upper part: Derived from branches of the renal plexus and aortic plexus • Lower part: Derived from the superior and inferior hypogastric plexuses .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Bleeding during normal menstruation occurs due to rupture of ____
mcqs.explanation: Rupture of the spiral arteries causes bleeding during normal menstruation. This is a branch of the uterine artery. The blood supply of the uterus is as follows : Uterine artery\037Arcuate artery\037Radial artery\037Basal artery\037Spiral artery

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A uterine artery embolization is being planned for a patient with uterine fibroids. Blood flow in which of the following arteries will not be affected by this procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: In the given case scenario, blood flow in the vaginal artery will not be affected , as it is not a branch of the uterine artery. The vaginal artery is a branch of the anterior division of the internal29 iliac artery. It is homologous to the inferior vesical artery in males. It supplies the vagina and the base of the bladder in women. It should not be confused with vaginal branches of the uterine artery. Branches of the uterine artery: • Ureteric branch • Vaginal branches (descending ) - these unite to form the anterior and posterior azygos arteries of the vagina • Circular cervical branch • Sampson's artery - it runs in under the round ligament . It represents the anastomosis of the uterine artery and ovarian artery. • Arcuate--> Radial--> Basal--> Spiral and straight arterioles of the functional layer of the endometrium30

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with stress incontinence required surgical management. While performing a Burch colposuspension , the surgeon approached the space of Retzius. What is this space also known as?
mcqs.explanation: The space of Retzius is the other name for prevesical or retropubic space . Burch colposuspension is a procedure done to relieve stress urinary incontinence. If an extraperitoneal approach is selected , the retropubic space is entered by perforating the transversalis fascia layer of the anterior abdominal wall. Once the retropubic space is dissected, the bladder neck and the vaginal fascia underneath are identified . The bladder is mobilized to the opposite side . At each side of the bladder neck, two to four, preferably non\037absorbable sutures are placed in the space of Retzius. Note :The presacral space is a retroperitoneal space that lies between the peritoneum of the posterior abdominal wall and the sacrum. It contains the superior and inferior hypogastric plexuses . The sacral sympathetic trunk lies against the sacrum's ventral surface .31

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: When do germ cells appear in the yolk sac?
mcqs.explanation: Germ cells appear in the yolk sac in the 3rd week . The sequence of events in primordial germ cell formation and migration are: • 2nd week - Germ cells are formed in the epiblast . • 3rd week - Germ cells move through the primitive streak and migrate to the wall of the yolk sac. • 4th week - Germ cells begin to migrate from the yolk sac to gonads. • 5th week - Germ cell migration is complete . Gametes are derived from these primordial germ cells .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: When does the ovary contain the maximum number of oogonia?
mcqs.explanation: The ovary contains the maximum number of oogonia at the 5th month of intrauterine life . The number of oogonia is estimated to be 7 million. Oogenesis is the process wherein oogonia differentiate into mature oocytes . It begins before birth. At birth, there are approximately 2 million primordial follicles . At the initiation of puberty , the follicle count is less than 400 ,000 , of which less than 500 are destined to ovulate. Every month, 15–20 follicles are released , out of which one matures to form the ovum.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A man with oligospermia has completed his course of hormonal treatment . After how many days will you test his sperm count?
mcqs.explanation: The sperm count is tested 80-90 days after hormonal treatment , as the average time is taken for spermatogenesis is 74 days, and approximately 14 days to reach the ejaculatory ducts . The effect of hormonal therapy on the early phase of spermatogenesis is reflected in the ejaculated sperm concentration after three months. Spermatogenesis is the process of the formation of sperms from spermatogonia . Approximately 100 million sperms are produced daily. In patients diagnosed with oligospermia , hormonal treatment is carried out using FSH, hCG, or testosterone . Improvements in sperm count can take a few months, hence the course is usually for 3-6 months. Normal spermatogenesis occurs after this time period . Spermiogenesis refers to the series of changes that occur in the formation of spermatozoa from spermatids . These are: • Acrosome formation38 • Condensation of the nucleus • Formation of the neck, middle piece , and tail • Shedding of cytoplasm as residual bodies Complete motility is obtained in the epididymis .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the time taken for capacitation of the sperm?
mcqs.explanation: The time taken for the capacitation of sperms is 6-8 hours (approximately 7 hours). Sperms have to undergo two changes in the female reproductive tract to be able to fertilise the ovum: 1) Capacitation • It is the functional maturation of the spermatozoa. • It occurs in the fallopian tube and involves epithelial interactions between the sperm and the mucosal surface of the tube . • The glycoprotein coat and seminal plasma proteins are removed. • Only capacitated sperms can pass through the corona cells and undergo the acrosomal reaction. 2) Acrosomal reaction • It occurs after binding to zona pellucida , induced by zona proteins . • Enzymes such as acrosin and trypsin-like protein are released to penetrate the zona pellucida • Ca2+ plays an important role.39

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true about the resumption of meiosis-I?
mcqs.explanation: Meiosis -I in the primary oocyte is resumed after LH surge .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In which of the following steps does reductional division occur?
mcqs.explanation: Meiosis I or reductional division occurs in the transition from primary spermatocyte to secondary spermatocyte . Meiosis takes place in germ cells to generate male and female gametes . Meiosis involves two stages of cell division, namely, meiosis I and II .40 Meiosis I produces two haploid cells . Because the ploidy is reduced from diploid to haploid , meiosis I is referred to as a reductional division. Meiosis II is an equational division analogous to mitosis, resulting in the creation of four haploid daughter cells .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about the primary oocyte ?

options.a: It is formed after meiosis I

mcqs.explanation: The secondary oocyte is formed after meiosis I. Primordial germ cells divide by mitosis to form oogonia. The majority of the oogonia divide by mitosis, however, some enter meiosis I and are arrested in the diplotene stage of prophase and are now called primary oocytes . Primary oocytes have not yet completed meiosis, hence they are diploid . The primary oocyte along with surrounding epithelial cells forms the primordial follicle . Meiosis I is completed after LH surge during puberty . Hence at the completetion of meiosis I, secondary oocyte is produced .41

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An embryologist is preparing embryos for implantation. When is zona hatching expected to occur?
mcqs.explanation: Zona hatching occurs at around 5 days after fertilization. Fertilization is divided into the following phases : • Penetration of the corona radiata • Penetration of the zona pellucida • Fusion of the oocyte and sperm cell membranes After fertilisation , the zygote differentiates to form the morula and then the blastocyst . The zona pellucida disappears at this stage , which is called zona hatching. The trophoblasts (outer cell mass) are now able to associate with the endometrium during implantation.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You are performing intrauterine insemination during the ovulatory period in a patient with infertility . When will you expect implantation to occur?
mcqs.explanation: The fertilized ovum implants by 6–10 days in the uterine cavity. Implantation involves: • Apposition : Initial contact of the blastocyst to the uterine wall • Adhesion: Increased physical contact between the blastocyst and uterine epithelium • Invasion : Penetration and invasion of syncytiotrophoblast and cytotrophoblasts into the endometrium A successful implantation requires receptive endometrium primed with estrogen and progesterone released by the corpus luteum .42

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The following figure shows the transverse section of the uterus with an implanted zygote . Identify structure A.
mcqs.explanation: In the given image, the decidua basalis is marked as A. This part of the decidua forms the placenta.Implantation occurs 6 to 7 days after fertilization. After implantation, the endometrium is called the decidua . It is of the following types: • Decidua basalis - present over chorion frondosum. Decidua basalis and chorion frondosum form the placenta . • Decidua capsularis - present over abembryonic pole . • Decidua parietalis - present on the opposite side of the uterus . The villi cover the entire surface of the chorion during the early weeks . As the fetus grows, the villi on the embryonic pole continue to grow, giving rise to the chorion frondosum. At the abembryonic pole , the villi degenerate . By the third month, this side of the chorion becomes smooth, and is called the chorion laeve.43 As the fetus grows, the chorion laeve comes into contact with the decidua parietalis on the opposite side of the uterus , and fusion occurs. Thus, the uterine lumen is obliterated . The amnion and chorion fuse , to form the amniochorionic membrane. Rupture of the amniochorionic membrane during labor is called 'breaking of waters '. Note : Superfetation can theoretically occur till the time the uterine lumen is not obliterated .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What do the Langhans cells form?
mcqs.explanation: Langhans cells form the cytotrophoblast . The cells of the blastocyst differentiate into an outer trophectoderm and an inner cell mass. The trophectoderm is further differentiated into: • An inner mononuclear cellular layer called cytotrophoblast or Langhans layer made of Langhans cells . • An outer layer of multinucleated syncytium called syncytiotrophoblast . The blastomere further divides to form the morula.44

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the structure marked A.
mcqs.explanation: The structure marked A is primary oocyte . Primary oocytes are the germ cells seen in the medullary region of the ovary . These enlarge at the beginning of the growth phase . During this cell growth period , many oocytes undergo degeneration , both before and after birth. A single layer of flattened follicular cells that were derived originally from the germinal epithelium soon surrounds the primary oocytes . The structure that is formed is now called a primordial follicle . These are seen first in the medulla and later in the cortex.45

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In which part of the fallopian tube does fertilization occur?
mcqs.explanation: Fertilization usually occurs in the ampulla of the fallopian tube . During ovulation, the ovum is released and it enters the fallopian tube . It is propelled towards the uterine cavity by the peristaltic action of the fallopian tubes , prostaglandins in the male seminal fluid and oxytocin. It can only be fertilized within 24 hours of ovulation. If coitus takes place during this period , the spermatozoa swimming up into the tubes meet the ovum in the ampulla.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A newborn is admitted to the NICU with the following teratoma. Which embryonic layers is this derived from?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows an oropharygeal teratoma, which contains derivatives from all three germ layers. The tumor may include gut , bone, skin, and teeth . These tumors arise from pluripotent stem cells that differentiate into any of three germ layers forming tissues of all three germ layers.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the structure marked as A.
mcqs.explanation: The structure marked A is the allantois. The posterior wall of the yolk sac forms the allantois on the 16th day of development . Its distal portion forms the urachus which forms the median umbilical ligament . The given image shows an embryo at the end of the third week .46

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The anatomical classification of the pelvis based on shape was given by ______.
mcqs.explanation: The anatomical classification of the pelvis based on shape was given by Caldwell and Moloy .52 The greatest transverse diameter of the pelvic inlet divides the pelvis into anterior and posterior segments . The shapes of these segments help classify the pelvis as follows : • Gynecoid • Anthropoid • Android • Platypelloid The various differences between these types is summarised below :Gynecoid Anthropoid Android Platypelloid Shape Round Anteroposteriorly ova l Triangular / Heart-sha ped Transversely oval / Fl at bowl shaped Sacral angl e >90\260 >90\260 <90\260 >90\260 Side walls Straight or slightly di vergent Straight or divergent Convergent Divergent Ischial spin es Not prominent Not prominent Prominent Not prominent Subpubican gle Wide (85\260) Slightly narrow Narrow Very wide (>90\260) Fetal Positi on OccipitolateralObliqu e occipitoanterior Direct occipitoanterio rOccipitoposterior OccipitolateralObliqu e occipitoposterior Occipitolateral Engaging d iameter Transverse / oblique Anteroposterior Transverse / oblique Transverse Delivery No difficulty Face-to-pubis - most common. Deep transverse arres t is common.Difficult delivery with an incre ased chance of perine al injuries No difficulty53 Option B: McAfee and Johnson's regimen is for the conservative management of placenta previa. Option C: Page's and Sher's classification system is used to grade abruptio placentae . Option D: Burns and Marshall maneuver is used in breech delivery .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An obese woman with dysmenorrhea and irregular periods is diagnosed with dystocia dystrophia syndrome. What type of pelvis is seen here?
mcqs.explanation: In dystocia dystrophia syndrome, an android pelvis is seen . Dystocia dystrophia syndrome: • The patient is stockily built with a bull neck, broad shoulders , and short thighs . She is obese with a male distribution of hair. • Subfertile , with dysmenorrhea, oligomenorrhea, or irregular periods . • There is an increased incidence of pre-eclampsia and a tendency for postmaturity . • The pelvis is of the android type . The occipito -posterior position is common. • During labor, there is a tendency for deep transverse arrest or outlet dystocia , leading to difficult instrumental delivery or cesarean section . • There is a chance of lactation failure.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about anthropoid pelvis?
mcqs.explanation: The anthropoid pelvis has straight side walls , not convergent side walls . Given below are the differences between various types of pelvis as per Caldwell -Moloy classification.Gynecoid Anthropoid Android Platypelloid Shape Round Anteroposteriorly ova l Triangular / Heart-sha ped Transversely oval / Fl at bowl shaped Sacral angl e >90\260 >90\260 <90\260 >90\260 Side walls Straight or slightly di vergent Straight or divergent Convergent Divergent Ischial spin es Not prominent Not prominent Prominent Not prominent Subpubican gle Wide (85\260) Slightly narrow Narrow Very wide (>90\260) Fetal Positi on OccipitolateralObliqu e occipitoanterior Direct occipitoanterio rOccipitoposterior OccipitolateralObliqu e occipitoposterior Occipitolateral Engaging d iameter Transverse / oblique Anteroposterior Transverse / oblique Transverse54 Gynecoid Anthropoid Android Platypelloid Delivery No difficulty Face-to-pubis - most common. Deep transverse arres t is common.Difficult delivery with an incre ased chance of perine al injuries No difficulty

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old term primigravida gave birth to a male baby by face to pubis delivery . Which type of pelvis is this mode of delivery commonly seen with?
mcqs.explanation: Face to pubis delivery is most commonly associated with anthropoid pelvis. As the anthropoid pelvis is wider posteriorly , the fetal occiput occupies the posterior segment of the pelvis. Thus, the fetus is present in the occipitoposterior position which leads to a high chance of face -to-pubis delivery .55

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An obstetrician performing clinical pelvimetry finds that the smallest transverse diameter is 8 cm. Which of the following parameters has she assessed ?
mcqs.explanation: The interspinous diameter is the smallest transverse pelvic diameter . The interspinous diameter or bispinous diameter is measured in the mid pelvis. It is the distance between the tips of two ischial spines . Normally, it is 10 -10 .5 cm. It is useful in predicting obstructed labor. If the interspinous diameter is too small, the baby's head may get stuck at a higher station. Note : The obstetric conjugate is the smallest anteroposterior pelvic diameter measuring 10 cm.56

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: During clinical pelvimetry , the obstetrician determines the diagonal conjugate to be X cm. What is the obstetric conjugate ?
mcqs.explanation: The obstetric conjugate is X-2cm where X is the diagonal conjugate . Anteroposterior diameters of the pelvis: • True conjugate or the anteroposterior diameter , extends from the upper most margin of the symphysis pubis to the sacral promontory. It is normally 11 cm. • Obstetrical conjugate is the shortest distance between the sacral promontory and the symphysis pubis. It is normally 10 cm. It is estimated indirectly by subtracting 1.5–2 cm from the diagonal conjugate . • Diagonal conjugate is determined by measuring the distance from the lowest margin of the symphysis to the sacral promontory. It is normally 12cm . It is measured clinically.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A diabetic primigravida is suspected to have cephalopelvic disproportion. What should her obstetric conjugate be for a trial of labor to be conducted ?
mcqs.explanation: In the given case scenario, a trial of labor or vaginal delivery can be allowed if the obstetric conjugate is 10cm or more. The obstetric conjugate is the shortest distance between the sacral promontory and the symphysis pubis. Normally, it is 10 cm or more. The diagonal conjugate measures 12cm and the true conjugate measures 11cm . Clinically, only the diagonal conjugate is assessed by measuring the distance between the base of the examiner's fingers and the fingertip touching the sacral promontory. This determines the lowest margin of the symphysis to the sacral promontory. The obstetric conjugate is estimated indirectly by subtracting 1.5–2 cm from the diagonal conjugate . Note : Overt diabetes can cause fetal macrosomia during pregnancy. Thus, it may lead to cephalopelvic disproportion.57 Given below is an image of the lateral plane in CT pelvimetry , showing the anteroposterior diameters of the pelvis. Line no. 4 is the obstetric conjugate and line no. 5 is the pelvic outlet .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following parameters cannot be viewed in lateral plate X-ray pelvimetry ?
mcqs.explanation: The bispinous diameter can be viewed in the anteroposterior view and not the lateral plate pelvimetry. X-ray pelvimetry is done using 3 views: • Anteroposterior - Transverse diameter and bispinous diameter is determined . • Lateral - Obstetric conjugate , sacral curve and pelvic inclination are seen . • Outlet - Outlet diameters are determined .58 Note : CT pelvimetry is preferred over X-ray pelvimetry due to the lower dose of radiation delivered . Given below are images of CT pelvimetry , anteroposterior and lateral views respectively . The marked diameters are as follows : 2 - Interspinous diameter 3 - Intertuberous diameter 4 - Obstetric conjugate 5 - Pelvic outlet

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A P1A1 woman with a history of obstructed labor is being evaluated for a contracted pelvis. CT pelvis shows both sacral alae are absent . What is the type of pelvis seen here?
mcqs.explanation: 59 The type of pelvis seen here is Robert's pelvis. In it, the pelvis is transversely contracted and the ala on both sides are absent and the sacrum is fused with the innominate bones. Option A: In Naegele 's pelvis, there is arrested development of one ala of the sacrum. Option C: Kyphotic pelvis occurs secondary to the kyphotic changes of the vertebral column either following tuberculosis or rickets. Option D: In rachitic pelvis, due to softening of bones, flattening of the pelvis occurs.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with prolonged second stage of labor is referred to the district hospital . You suspect her to have a contracted pelvis. Which of the following is true about this condition?

options.a: Transverse diameter of inlet is 10 cm
options.b: Anteroposterior diameter of inlet is 12 cm
options.c: Transverse diameter of inlet is 12 cm
options.d: Anteroposterior diameter of inlet is 14 cm

mcqs.explanation: To make a diagnosis of contracted pelvis, the transverse diameter of the pelvic inlet should be 10cm. The pelvic inlet is considered to be contracted if: • the greatest transverse diameter is < 12 cm or • the shortest anteroposterior diameter is < 10 cm. The anteroposterior diameters of the pelvic inlet are the true conjugate , diagonal conjugate and obstetric conjugate . These extend between the sacral promontory and symphysis pubis . The obstetric conjugate is the shortest diameter, normally measuring 10 cm. The transverse diameter of the pelvic inlet is at a right angle to the obstetric conjugate . It extends between the linea terminalis on either side . Normally, the transverse diameter is about 13 cm.60

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the smallest diameter of the fetal head ?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , the bitemporal diameter is the smallest . It is the distance between the anteroinferior ends of the coronal suture and usually measures 8 cm. This is the smallest engaging diameter . Option A: The biparietal diameter is a transverse diameter between two parietal eminences , measuring 9.5cm. Option B: The suboccipitofrontal diameter is an anteroposterior diameter , measuring 10 cm. Option C: The suboccipitobregmatic diameter is an anteroposterior diameter , measuring 9.5 cm. Note : The bimastoid diameter is a transverse diameter . It is the smallest diameter in the fetal skull at about 7.5 cm. However it is not clinically relevant as it does not engage .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old woman in labor is referred to a tertiary care center . On PV examination, the resident notes that the fetus is in brow presentation , and the largest diameter of the fetal skull is engaged . Identify this diameter .
mcqs.explanation: In brow presentation , the mentovertical diameter is engaged which is the longest diameter of the fetal skull. Normally, it measures 14 cm. The mentovertical diameter extends from the midpoint of the chin to the highest point on the sagittal suture . Engaging diameters of the fetal skull vary with the attitude of the fetal head as given below :Diameters Attitude of the hea d Suboccipitobregma tic Complete flexion61 Diameters Attitude of the hea d Suboccipito -frontal Incomplete flexion Occipitofrontal Marked deflexion Mento -vertical Partial extension Submentovertical Incomplete extensi on Submentobregmati c Complete extension

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G6P5L5 woman presented to the casualty with abdominal pain. The PV examination findings are given below . What is the engaging diameter ?
mcqs.explanation: In the given clinical scenario, the engaging diameter is the suboccipito -bregmatic diameter . It is engaged when the fetus is in vertex presentation with an attitude of complete flexion of the head . The table given below shows the engaging diameter with each attitude of the fetal head .Diameters Attitude of the hea d Suboccipitobregma tic Complete flexion Suboccipito -frontal Incomplete flexion Occipitofrontal Marked deflexion Mento -vertical Partial extension Submentovertical Incomplete extensi on Submentobregmati c Complete extension

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: How many fontanelles are present in a newborn?
mcqs.explanation: Newborns have a total of 6 fontanelles . These are fibrous, membrane-covered gaps between cranial bones. The fontanelles seen in newborns are: • Anterior fontanelle : • It is also called bregma. • Diameter ranges from 0.6-3.6 cm, with a mean of 2.1 cm. • It completely closes by 24 months of age . • Posterior fontanelle :62 • It is also called lambda. • Diameter ranges from 0.5-0.7 cm. • It completely closes by 2 months of age . • 2 sphenoid fontanelles • 2 mastoid fontanelles Note : A third fontanelle between the anterior and posterior fontanels is associated with hypothyroidism and Down's syndrome.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old primigravida delivered a full -term male baby by assisted forceps delivery . The next day, you note a swelling over the infant's head that is limited by suture lines. Which of the following is true regarding the swelling ?

options.a: Tension in the swelling varies on crying

mcqs.explanation: In the given clinical picture , the swelling over the infant's head is likely to be a cephalhematoma . Infants with cephalohematomas are at a heightened risk of developing jaundice because as the blood breaks down, the levels of bilirubin increase. Cephalohematoma is a collection of blood in between the pericranium and the flat bone (subperiosteal) of the skull, usually unilateral and over a parietal bone.It is never present at birth but gradually develops after 12 –24 h. The swelling is limited by the suture lines of the skull as the pericranium is fixed to the margins of the bone Option A: Tension in the swelling varies with crying in meningocele . Option C: Edematous fluid collects in caput succedaneum . Option D: Caput succedaneum may be present at birth.63

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The pediatrician notices a diffuse , reddish scalp swelling in a newborn born by vacuum extraction. Which of the following is not a characteristic of this condition?

options.c: It does not disappear within 2-3 days.
options.d: It is a diffuse edematous swelling of the soft tissues of the scalp .

mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of caput succedaneum which disappears within 2-3 days. In vertex presentation , labor forces alter the shape of the fetal head . In prolonged labor, before complete cervical dilatation, the portion of the fetal scalp immediately over the cervical os becomes edematous. A swelling is formed is due to the stagnation of fluid in the layers of the scalp beneath the girdle of contact. This is known as caput succedaneum . The swelling is diffuse , boggy , and not limited by the suture lines. It resolves spontaneously within 2-3 days after birth. It is a result of the static position of the head for a long period of time. Chignon is a type of artificial caput succedaneum , which is a swelling produced on the fetal head because of the scalp getting sucked into the cup during vacuum extraction.64

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: How is the normal placenta described ?
mcqs.explanation: 74 The normal human placenta is discoid, deciduate , and hemochorial. The term deciduate means that the placenta is shed at the time of parturition. Hemochorial means that the maternal blood directly comes in contact with the fetal trophoblasts . The image given below shows a normal human placenta .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What does a placental cotyledon comprise of?

options.a: Portions of the basal plate divided by clefts
options.b: Portions of the chorionic plate divided by cleft
options.c: Area supplied by multiple truncal chorionic villi
options.d: Area supplied by one spiral artery

mcqs.explanation: A placental cotyledon is comprised of portions of the basal plate divided by clefts . It is the functional unit of the placenta . A placental cotyledon or placental lobule constitutes one truncal or main stem villi and its ramifications (rami). Each lobule is supplied by a single truncal branch of the chorionic artery. Each lobule also has a single vein. The lobules constitute functional units of placental architecture . The fetal surface is the chorionic plate . The umbilical cord inserts in the center of the chorionic plate . Note : The entire placenta is supplied by chorionic villi while each cotyledon is only supplied by a single main stem villus with its branches.75

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not contribute to the prevention of rejection of fetus ?
mcqs.explanation: Maternal leucopenia is not seen in pregnancy, instead leucocytosis is seen . This plays no part in the prevention of rejection of fetus . The fetus is a semiallogenic graft inside the maternal body as half of its genes are from the father. Uterine transplantation immunity contributes to the survival of the fetus in spite of it being semiallogenic . This occurs due to the following factors: • Decidual natural killer cells are inefficient , and therefore are unable to attack the 'foreign' fetal cells . • Decidual stromal cells work with natural killer cells to allow trophoblastic invasion . • Villous trophoblastic cells don't express HLA antigens and therefore , they are non-immunogenic.76

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: At what period of gestation are the weights of the fetus and placenta equal?
mcqs.explanation: At 17 weeks , the weights of the fetus and placenta are equal. In the first trimester, the placental growth is more rapid than that of the fetus . By approximately 17 weeks , the placental weight and fetal weight are almost equal. And by term, placental weight is approximately 1/6th of the fetal weight .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the uteroplacental blood flow at term?
mcqs.explanation: The uteroplacental blood flow at term is 500-750 ml/min.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about human chorionic gonadotropin?

options.a: Alpha subunit is identical to LH , FSH, TSH
options.b: It causes involution of corpus luteum
options.c: Maximum level is seen at 60-70 days of gestation
options.d: Detected in serum 8-9 days after fertilisation

mcqs.explanation: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) does not cause involution of the corpus luteum , but it maintains corpus luteum function. hCG is produced by the syncitiotrophoblasts of the placenta . It is a glycoprotein hormone with two subunits . The alpha-subunit is similar to LH , FSH and TSH. The beta -subunit is specific and is measured by pregnancy tests . hCG can be detected in maternal blood 8 days after fertilisation . Thus, it can help in diagnosis of pregnancy even before the period is missed . Its levels nearly doubles every 48 hours in early pregnancy reaching a maximum of 50000 - 100000 IU/L by 60-70 days of gestation . Then the level starts falling reaching a minimum at 16 weeks , which continues throughout pregnancy. The various placental hormones and their functions are given below . Other placental hormones include : • GnRH, TRH , GHRH, Growth hormone variant (hGH-V) • Parathyroid hormone-releasing protein (PTH-rP) • Inhibin • Activin • RelaxinPlacental hormones Functions Human chorionic gonadotrop in (hCG)Structurally similar t o - LH, FSH, TSH Maintains corpus luteum fun ctionRegulates testosterone s ecretion from fetal testesStim ulates maternal thyroid77 Placental hormones Functions Placental lactogen (PL )Struct urally similar to - GH, Prolac tin Helps the mother adapt to fet al energy requirements Corticotropin-releasing horm one (CRH) Vascular and myometrial sm ooth muscle relaxationInitiati on of parturitionStimulates p lacental ACTH production Placental adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) Stimulates fetal and maternal adrenal glucocorticoid produ ction

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following cannot cross the placenta ?
mcqs.explanation: Albumin and IgM cannot cross the placenta . High molecular weight substances such as proteins (e.g., albumin, IgM, IgA) cannot cross the placenta, except IgG. Substances which can cross the placenta are as follows : Note : Maternal hormones like insulin, steroid hormones, and thyroid hormones cross the placenta very slowly , and only in amounts enough to support fetal development . However, calcitonin and parathormone do not cross the placenta.Substances Mechanism O2CO2WaterElectrolytesAne sthetic agents Simple diffusion Immunoglobulin G(molecula r weight 160 ,000 Da) Endocytosis via Fc receptors in the trophoblast Glucose Facilitated diffusion via gluco se transport proteins (GLUTs) Amino acids Transport -protein-mediated active transport Lipids:GlycerolEssential fatty acidsLDL Endocytosis via specific recep tors Minerals:IodineIron (unidire ctional from mother to fetus ) CalciumPhosphorus Carrier -mediated active trans port Vitamins :Vit AVit CVit D Carrier -mediated active trans port

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A primigravida delivered a baby at term with a birth weight of 1.9 kg via normal vaginal delivery. The placenta delivered appears as shown in the image below . What is this condition known as?
mcqs.explanation: 78 The given image shows a circumvallate placenta . The membranes at the periphery are thickened and consist of a double fold of chorion and amnion . Normally, the chorionic plate and basal plates are of the same size. In conditions of extrachorial placentation, the chorionic plate is smaller than the basal plate . There are two types of extrachorial placentation : • Circummarginate placenta - In this type , the space between the fetal membranes and the basal plate is filled up by fibrin and old hemorrhage. • Circumvallate placenta - In this type , the peripheral chorion is thickened into a ridge composed of a double fold of chorion and amnion . Complications associated with circumvallate placenta are: • Preterm delivery • Abortions • IUGR • Antepartum hemorrhage • Retained placenta and membranes79 Option A: Placenta succenturiata has one or more small lobes of the placenta placed at varying distances from the main placental margins. Options B & D: Placenta marginata or circummarginate placenta - a thin margin is present between the chorionic and basal plates.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Following a normal vaginal delivery , the placenta delivered by controlled cord traction appeared as shown below . What is this condition known as?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a placenta with a small, accessory lobe . This condition is known as placenta succenturiata . A succenturiate placenta contains single or multiple accessory lobes . Accessory lobes are attached to the main lobe by a membrane that has a leash of blood vessels . Option A: Bilobate placenta - it consists of two placental lobes . The cord inserts between the two lobes . Option C: Placenta membranacea - entire surface of the fetal membranes are covered by functioning villi and the placenta develops as a thin membranous structure occupying the entire periphery of the chorion. Option D: Placenta marginata - chorionic plate is smaller than the basal plate , and a thin margin is present between the chorionic and basal plates .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The USG scan of a multiparous woman at 30 weeks of gestation showed the presence of an accessory placental lobe . Which complication will you not anticipate in her?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of the presence of an accessory placental lobe is suggestive of placenta succenturiata . Preterm delivery is not a complication seen in this condition. Complications of placenta succenturiata include : • Retained placenta80 • Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) • Subinvolution of uterus • Sepsis • Placental polyp formation • Vasa previa - vessels overlying the accessory lobes can cross the cervix. Their rupture can lead to hemorrhage from the fetus Note : Preterm delivery is a complication associated with circumvallate placenta .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following types of morbidly adherent placenta is shown in the given image?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows placenta increta. Morbidly adherent placenta occurs due to the partial or total absence of the decidua basalis and imperfect development of the fibrinoid or Nitabuch layer. It is of three types : • Placenta accreta - villi are attached to the myometrium. • Placenta increta - villi invade deep into the myometrium. • Placenta percreta - villi penetrate through the entire myometrium and to or through the serosa. Based on the adherence of placental lobules , all three types of morbidly adherent placenta can be: • Total - involving all lobules of the placenta • Focal - involving a single lobule or part of a lobule of the placenta Morbidly adherent placenta can lead to torrential post -partum hemorrhage. It is managed via C-section and peripartum hysterectomy.81

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What contributes to the formation of amniotic fluid during early pregnancy?
mcqs.explanation: Ultrafiltrate of maternal plasma contributes to the formation of amniotic fluid during early pregnancy. Amniotic fluid is formed by: • Early pregnancy - ultrafiltrate of maternal plasma. • Second trimester - the extracellular fluid that diffuses through the fetal skin and thus reflects the composition of fetal plasma. • After 20 weeks - keratinization of fetal skin prevents diffusion across the skin. Hence , fetal urine forms amniotic fluid . Note : Fetal kidneys start producing urine at 12 weeks (8–11 weeks ), and by 18 weeks , they produce 7 to 14 mL per day.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: While performing the USG assessment of a woman at 28 weeks of gestation , you note her amniotic fluid index to be 12 .8. When does this parameter reach its maximum value in a normal pregnancy?
mcqs.explanation: The amniotic fluid index (AFI) is a measure of the amniotic volume which is maximum at 34 weeks of gestation. The volume of amniotic fluid at each week is variable. The volume gradually increases till 32 -34 weeks of gestation. At 34 weeks , it is maximum and thereafter there is a gradual reduction till term. Amniotic fluid volume is a passive reflector of the fetal condition. Its volume is determined by the following : Any alteration in fetal homeostasis , caused by fetal and maternal conditions, affects the amniotic fluid volume. Thus, AFI is measured as a part of the biophysical score.Pathway Volume in ml Fetal urination +1000 Fetal swallowing -750 Fetal lung fluid secretion +350 Intramembranous flow acros s fetal vessels on the placenta l surface -350

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a function of amniotic fluid ?

options.c: Provide nutrition in the form of fat and protein
options.d: Prevent ascending infection to uterine cavity during labor

mcqs.explanation: The nutritive value of amniotic fluid is negligible because amniotic fluid is predominantly water. It contains the following : • Water - 98–99%82 • Solids 1–2% - Organic, inorganic, suspended particles Functions of amniotic fluid during pregnancy: • It acts as a shock absorber and prevents trauma to the fetus • Temperature regulation of the uterine environment • It distends the amniotic sac and thereby allows for growth and free movement of the fetus . • It has no nutritive function, as it is mostly formed by water. • Bacteriostatic property Functions of amniotic fluid during labor: • The amnion and chorion are combined to form a hydrostatic wedge which helps in dilatation of the cervix. • During uterine contraction, it prevents any interference in placental circulation so long as the membranes remain intact. • It protects the umbilical cord by providing a cushion between the fetus and the umbilical cord during contraction • It flushes the birth canal at the end of the first stage of labor and by its aseptic action protects the fetus and prevents ascending infection to the uterine cavity.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: When does keratinization of fetal skin occur?
mcqs.explanation: Keratinization of fetal skin occurs at 22 –25 weeks . Therefore, diffusion across fetal skin does not occur after this period . So fetal plasma does not contribute to amniotic fluid formation after this time period .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about amniotic fluid ?

options.b: Major source is fetal urine after 20 weeks
options.c: It is primarily reabsorbed by fetal swallowing

mcqs.explanation: The composition of amniotic fluid is not the same throughout pregnancy but changes later in pregnancy due to contamination by fetal urinary metabolites . In early pregnancy, it is identical to plasma in composition as it is mainly composed of a transudate of plasma. In late pregnancy, as amniotic fluid is primarily formed by fetal urination, the composition is altered . Disorders of the fetal kidney can lead to oligohydramnios. Fetal swallowing is the primary method of resorption of amniotic fluid . Disorders of swallowing in the fetus can cause polyhydramnios. Amniotic fluid is alkaline in nature and this helps in differentiating it from vaginal secretions which are acidic. This forms the basis of the nitrazine paper test used for the diagnosis of premature rupture of membranes.83

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A multigravida presents at 34 weeks of gestation with preterm premature rupture of membranes. On examination, the amniotic fluid is golden -colored . Which condition will you suspect here?
mcqs.explanation: Golden -colored amniotic fluid is seen in Rh incompatibility . This appearance is due to presence of excess bilirubin in the amniotic fluid due to hemolysis of fetal RBCs.Color of amniotic fluid Conditions Pale straw Near-term due to exfoliated l anugo hairs, exfoliated cells f rom fetal skin Green MeconiumListeria infection Golden -yellow Rh-incompatibility Saffron Post-maturity Blood-stained Low lying placentaVasa previ a Dark maroon Altered blood in accidental h emorrhage Brown (Tobacco juice ) Intrauterine fetal demise

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Ultrasound findings of a few patients are given below . Which of the following patients have oligohydramnios?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , an AFI of 4.5cm (<5cm) or an SDP of 1.8cm (<2cm) indicate oligohydramnios. Oligohydramnios means an abnormally decreased amount of amniotic fluid (liquor volume is <200ml ). It is diagnosed using ultrasound parameters such as: • Single deepest pocket (SDP) - The largest vertical pocket of amniotic fluid identified in the sagittal plane on ultrasound is the SDP. The normal range of SDP is between 2 to 8cm. Oligohydramnios is diagnosed if SDP < 2cm. • Amniotic fluid index (AFI) - It is the sum of the deepest pocket of amniotic fluid from each quadrant of the abdomen. The normal range of AFI is between 5 to 25 cm. Oligohydramnios is diagnosed if AFI < 5cm.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old primigravida at 30 weeks of gestation came for a regular antenatal checkup . On examination , size of the uterus corresponds to 26 weeks of gestation and the fetal heart rate is 130 beats /min. On ultrasound, AFI is 4. Which fetal anomaly would you suspect ?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of oligohydramnios. It is associated with renal agenesis . Oligohydramnios has the following features : • Fundal height less than period of gestation • Fetal parts easily palpable • AFI <5cm • SDP <2cm84

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old G3P2L2 woman with multifetal pregnancy is diagnosed with polyhydramnios. What is the amniotic fluid volume required to diagnose it as this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Polyhydramnios is an abnormal increase in amniotic fluid . It is defined as the presence of amniotic fluid volume >2000ml. Ultrasound parameters used to diagnose polyhydramnios are: • AFI > 25 cm • SDP > 8 cm

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A lady at 30 weeks of gestation came for an antenatal check-up. On examination, the uterus corresponds to 34 weeks of gestation and FHR is normal . Ultrasound revealed an AFI of 26 cm. Which fetal anomaly is most likely to be seen with this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture is suggestive of polyhydramnios. It can be seen with a fetus having a cleft palate as fetal swallowing is impaired by this anomaly. Polyhydramnios has the following features : • Fundal height greater than period of gestation • Fetal parts are not well palpable • AFI >25cm • SDP >8cm

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A routine ultrasound of a multigravida at 28 weeks of gestation revealed an AFI of 27cm. Which of the following cannot cause the given condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of polyhydramnios. Preeclampsia is a cause for oligohydramnios, and not polyhydramnios.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old G2P1L1 at 35 weeks of gestation is complaining of difficulty in breathing. On examination , flanks are full , and abdominal girth is 160cm . Ultrasound determined that the SDP is 10cm . What is the next step in management?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of polyhydramnios associated with respiratory distress . In such cases , therapeutic amniocentesis termed amnioreduction is done. Amnioreduction helps in polyhydramnios by: • Relieving respiratory distress by reducing mechanical pressure on the diaphragm • May improve obstructive uropathy • May lower the preterm delivery risk if the patient has preterm labor or premature rupture of membranes Option A: Diuretics have no role in this condition. Option B: Indomethacin therapy used to be given earlier as it reduced amnionic fluid volume. However, it is not given anymore due to the risk of premature closure of ductus arteriosus.85 Option D: Artificial rupture of membranes (ARM) is avoided as: • It cannot be employed in a patient with an unfavourable cervix. • Once ARM is done, delivery needs to be performed . In this case, preterm delivery would occur, hence ARM is avoided. • ARM should be used with caution in patients with chronic polyhydramnios. It can lead to sudden decompression of the uterus causing placental abruption. Thus, controlled ARM is done in these patients .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A female presents with 35 weeks and 3 days of gestation , AFI = 5 and there is no end-diastolic blood flow . What is the management?

options.b: Give surfactant and wait till 36 weeks
options.c: Do Doppler everyday to check for reversion

mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of fetal compromise. The management in this patient is immediate termination of pregnancy. Since this pregnancy has crossed 34 weeks , it can be terminated by cesarean section . Abnormal flow patterns in the umbilical artery: • Reduced end-diastolic flow indicates uteroplacental insufficiency (S/D ratio increases) • Absent end-diastolic flow suggests fetal compromise, hence the pregnancy is terminated by C-section if >34 weeks . • Reverse end-diastolic flow suggests impending doom of death , hence the pregnancy is terminated by C-section if >32 weeks .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about the umbilical cord?

options.a: It has one artery and two veins
options.b: It contains a gelatinous substance called Wharton 's jelly
options.c: Presence of a single umbilical artery is associated with congenital anomalies
options.d: Normal average umbilical cord length is 50-60 cms

mcqs.explanation: The umbilical cord normally has two arteries and one vein. The presence of a single umbilical artery is the most common vascular anomaly of the cord.
