mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old woman presents with 6 weeks of amenorrhea and a positive urine pregnancy test . She states her brother had cystic fibrosis and asks if her child might have the same. Which of the following methods would not be useful for prenatal diagnosis of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Fetal skin biopsy is not a recommended method of prenatal diagnosis of cystic fibrosis. It is done to detect inherited skin conditions such as: • Ichthyosis155 • Epidermolysis bullosa • Oculocutaneous albinism Invasive procedures for prenatal diagnosis of CFTR gene mutations in cystic fibrosis include : • Chorionic villus sampling (CVS) • Amniocentesis • Cordocentesis or percutaneous umbilical blood sampling (PUBS)

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G2P1 woman at 35 weeks of pregnancy presents with complaints of decreased fetal movement. What is the next step in management?
mcqs.explanation: In case of reduced fetal movements, the first step of management is to do a non-stress test (NST). Interpretation of NST: • Reactive • \0312 accelerations of >15 beats /minute above the baseline and longer than 15 seconds in duration are present in a 20 -minute observation • Reassure the patient and send back home • Non-reactive - biophysical profile (BPP) has to be assessed .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The CTG shown in the image below may be seen in which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: The given CTG shows early deceleration which is seen in cases of head compression.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old G2P1 at 38 weeks of gestation came to the labor room with complaints of decreased fetal movements. Non-stress test was done and late decelerations were noted. What does this indicate ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of fetal hypoxia. Late decelerations are seen on an NST in this condition. Deceleration is a decrease in fetal heart rate below the baseline by 15 bpm for more than 15 seconds . Absent variability of FHR with late decelerations is an indication for immediate Cesarean section .156

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman brings her son to the hospital for routine immunization . While awaiting his turn, she realizes that her seat is stained with blood. She is rushed to the nearby antenatal clinic. Pulse - 96/min, BP - 110 /80 mmHg. Vaginal bleeding is noted and her NST is shown below . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with the NST showing a sinusoidal pattern point towards a diagnosis of vasa previa. Vasa previa is a condition where fetal vessels travel within the membranes and overlie the cervical os. Hence , there can be bleeding during cervical dilatation or membrane rupture . Fetal mortality is high due to fetal exsanguination. When bleeding is present in vasa previa, an emergency cesarean section is indicated . Causes of sinusoidal pattern on NST include : • Severe fetal anemia - Rh isoimmunisation, vasa previa, fetomaternal hemorrhage, or twin to twin transfusion • Opioids - meperidine , morphine, alphaprodine, butorphanol • Amnionitis • Fetal distress • Umbilical cord occlusion .157

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old woman presents with 2 months of amenorrhea and a positive UPT. On ultrasound examination, all of the following are assessed except ______.
mcqs.explanation: Amniotic fluid volume is assessed on ultrasound in the second and third trimesters . Ultrasonographic evaluation during the first trimester includes : • Gestational sac size, location, and number • Embryo and/or yolk sac identification • Crown-rump length165 • Fetal number, including amnionicity and chorionicity of multifetal gestations • Embryonic/fetal cardiac activity • Maternal uterus , adnexa, and cul-de -sac • Fetal nuchal translucency .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A primigravida presents to the antenatal clinic for the first time at 18 weeks of amenorrhea. She does not remember her LMP and no ultrasound scans were done in the first trimester. In this situation, gestational age can be most accurately estimated by which of the following parameters?
mcqs.explanation: In the second trimester, the parameter to assess gestational age most accurately is the biparietal diameter (BPD). Accuracy varies from 7 to 10 days. BPD is measured in the transthalamic view, at the level of the thalamus and cavum septum pellucidum (CSP). It is measured from the outer edge of the skull in the near field to the inner edge of the skull in the far field .Trimes ter Parameter First Crown rump length (CRL ) Second Biparietal diameter (BPD) Third Femur length (FL)

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old woman presented with complaints of 7 weeks of amenorrhea and a positive UPT. Her ultrasound scan is shown below . What does the red arrowhead represent ?
mcqs.explanation: The red arrowhead represents the yolk sac. The yellow arrowhead shows the double ring - outer decidua parietalis and inner decidua capsularis. It is referred to as the double decidua sign and is seen in the first trimester transvaginal sonogram. It is useful to confirm an early intrauterine location for the pregnancy.166

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Head circumference is measured from which of the following ultrasonographic views?
mcqs.explanation: Head circumference (HC) is measured from the transthalamic view by placing an ellipse around the outer edge of the skull HC can also be calculated from the biparietal diameter (BPD) and occipital -frontal diameter (OFD).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the normal range of femur length to abdominal circumference ratio?
mcqs.explanation: The normal range for the femoral length (FL) to abdominal circumference (AC) ratio is 20 -24 percent . Low FL/AC (< 16) ratio suggests a lethal skeletal dysplasia , particularly if other skeletal abnormalities are present .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman presents at 33-weeks of gestation and the umbilical artery Doppler imaging shows the following finding. What is the next step of management?

options.c: Terminate the pregnancy at 34 weeks of gestation

mcqs.explanation: The umbilical artery Doppler depicts reversal of end-diastolic flow or REDF (waves appearing below the baseline ) which is seen in intrauterine growth restriction. As the period of gestation has exceeded 32 weeks , the pregnancy can be terminated . In case of absent end-diastolic flow (AEDF), the waves just touch the baseline , but don't appear below it. This suggests a fetal compromise, hence the pregnancy is terminated by C-section if >34 weeks .167 Reversed end-diastolic flow (REDF) suggests impending fetal death , hence the pregnancy is terminated by C-section if >32 weeks .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the first-trimester ultrasound?

options.a: A gestational sac can first be seen 4 weeks after LMP
options.b: Accuracy of USG dating decreases after the 1st trimester
options.c: Yolk sac is the first sign of pregnancy on USG
options.d: A normal gestational sac implants in the midline of the endometrial cavity

mcqs.explanation: The accuracy of determining gestational age using ultrasound is the highest in the first trimester and decreases afterwards . Option A: Gestational sac is reliably seen at 5 weeks of gestation on transvaginal sonography(TVS ). Option C: The first sign of pregnancy seen on sonography is the gestational sac. Visualisation of the yolk sac within the gestational sac confirms an intrauterine location for pregnancy. Option D: A normal gestational sac implants eccentrically in the endometrium , whereas a pseudosac is seen in the midline of the endometrial cavity.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the ideal time for nuchal translucency evaluation?
mcqs.explanation: Nuchal translucency evaluation, a component of first-trimester aneuploidy screening , is done between 11 -14 weeks . It represents the maximum thickness of the subcutaneous translucent area between the skin and soft tissue , overlying the fetal spine , at the back of the neck. When the nuchal translucency is increased , the risk of fetal aneuploidy and structural anomalies such as heart defects is significantly elevated . First trimester aneuploidy screening combines two maternal serum analytes and a sonographic measurement: • Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)168 • Pregnancy-associated plasma protein A (PAPP -A) • Nuchal translucency (NT) It is performed between 11 and 14 weeks of gestation . In cases of fetal Down syndrome, the first-trimester serum-free \032-hCG level is higher and the PAPP -A level is lower . With trisomy 18 and trisomy 13 , levels of both analytes are lower . Note : Nuchal fold is a normal fold of skin seen at the back of the fetal neck during the second trimester of pregnancy. Increased nuchal fold thickness is associated with fetal aneuploidy .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following are sonographic markers for Down's syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Ultrasound markers for Down's syndrome: • First trimester • Nuchal translucency >3 mm • Second trimester • Echogenic intracardiac focus • Ventriculomegaly • Nuchal thickness >6 mm • Echogenic bowel • Hypoplastic /absent nasal bone • Shortened humerus, femur • Mild pylectasis • Aberrant subclavian artery.169

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The anomaly scan of a G3A2 woman is given below . Identify the sign.
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows banana sign. An abnormal anterior curvature of cerebellum along with effacement of cisterna magna produces this appearance . It is seen in spina bifida associated with Arnold-Chiari malformation.Lemon sign: Axial USG image of the fetal head at the level of the biparietal diameter shows inward concavity of both frontal bones instead of the normally seen convexity. This gives the head the appearance of a lemon. It has a strong association with spina bifida and is very useful for detecting this condition.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A doctor tells a 31 -year-old woman, who is 20 weeks pregnant, that her baby has a developmental defect . She has come to you for a second opinion. The following USG finding is seen . Identify the defect .
mcqs.explanation: 170 The given ultrasound image shows an open defect in the calvaria and skin leading to the exposure of the cranial neural tube . This is consistent with the diagnosis of anencephaly . Anencephaly results from incomplete closure of the neural tube . It is one of the earliest detectable congenital defects that can be detected as early as 10 to 11 weeks of gestation . Screening can also be done by serum estimation of maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein (MSAFP). The following are the radiological signs seen in anencephaly . • Frog eye sign - Absence of cranial calvaria , prominent orbits thereby resembling the face of a frog. • Shower cap sign - The absence of the cranium could lead to the protrusion of a disorganized mass of brain tissue . This resembles a shower cap giving rise to a characteristic triangular facial appearance . Neural-tube defects can be prevented with pre-conceptional supplementation of folic acid. A dose of 4 mg daily is recommended in subsequent pregnancies . The frog eye and showercap signs are shown below :171 Option B: Omphalocele is a midline anterior abdominal wall defect through which the solid abdominal viscera and/or bowel may herniate. The extruded abdominal contents are covered in a sac. Given below is an ultrasound image of the fetus suggestive of an omphalocele (asterix).Cystic hygroma is a congenital multiloculated lymphatic lesion that is classically found in the left posterior triangle of the neck. It occurs as a result of sequestration or obstruction of developing lymph vessels . This defect can be picked up in a first-trimester ultrasound. The images below show the MRI and USG appearance of cystic hygroma, respectively :172 Encephalocele is caused due to defects in the skull through which the meninges and/or neural tissue herniate. The squamous part of the occipital bone is the most frequently affected bone. The image shows a newborn with encephalocele .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is Robert's sign?
mcqs.explanation: Robert's sign is a gas shadow in the fetal heart. It is seen in fetal demise in utero and may appear as early as 12 hours. Other sonographic signs seen in fetal demise in utero are: • Absent fetal heartbeat • Absent fetal movements173 • Occasional findings • Overlapping of skull bones - Spalding 's sign • Gross distortion of fetal anatomy (maceration) • Soft tissue edema - skin >5 mm • Echogenic amniotic fluid (fetal demise fragments) • Uncommon findings • Thrombus in fetal heart • Gas shadow in the fetal heart - Robert's sign.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the frequency of a transabdominal transducer?
mcqs.explanation: The frequency of trans abdominal transducer is 4-6 megahertz (MHz) since a lower frequency penetrates better . On the other hand, a vaginal transducer has a frequency of 5-10 megahertz since a higher frequency yields a better image with minimal penetration .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: When is fetal cardiac activity first detected on transabdominal USG?
mcqs.explanation: The cardiac activity of the fetus is first detected on transabdominal USG (TAS) at the 6th week of intrauterine life .Fetal structure TVS (we eks) TAS(we eks) Gestational sac 4.5 5.5 Yolk sac 5 6 Cardiac activit y 6 - 6.5 6 - 7

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman has her first antenatal visit in the 8th month of gestation . On examination , the uterus corresponds to 30 weeks and the fetal heart rate is 136 /min. What is the best parameter for the estimation of fetal age by USG in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Femur length is the best parameter for the estimation of fetal age by USG in the 3rd trimester. Best USG parameters for estimation of fetal age :Trimes ter Parameter First Crown-rump length (CR L)174 Trimes ter Parameter Second Biparietal diameter (BPD) Third Femur length (FL)

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding sonography in pregnancy?

options.b: All machines must display thermal index
options.c: Tissue heating is higher with shorter examination time
options.d: Risks are greater during organogenesis than later in pregnancy

mcqs.explanation: Tissue heating is higher with longer examination time. Sonography should be performed in compliance with the ALARA principle which is As Low As Reasonably Achievable. The theoretical risks are greater during organogenesis (8-15 weeks ) than later in pregnancy. All sonography machines must display 2 indices - the thermal index and the mechanical index.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant diabetic woman presents for a routine antenatal visit during the third trimester. During the evaluation, you perform obstetrical Doppler imaging. Which among the following would indicate fetal compromise?

options.a: Increased pulsatalilty index in umbilical artery

mcqs.explanation: Absent end diastolic flow indicates fetal compromise in Doppler . Umbilical artery vessels : • They are characterized by forward low-resistance flow . • As gestation increases, there is a gradual fall in all the resistance indices so the amount of forward diastolic flow increases. • S/D ratio decreases as the period of gestation increases. Abnormal flow patterns in umbilical artery: • Reduced end-diastolic flow - Uteroplacental insufficiency (systolic /diastolic ratio increases) • Absent end-diastolic flow - Fetal compromise (hence pregnancy is terminated by cesarean section if >34 weeks ) • Reverse end-diastolic flow - Impending death (pregnancy is terminated irrespective of gestational age ) Doppler of the middle cerebral artery helps in detecting fetal anemia. Increased fetal diastolic flow in the middle cerebral artery with absent diastolic flow in the aorta implies fetal acidemia.175

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following acts as the primary trigger for onset of labour in pregnant women?
mcqs.explanation: The fetal ACTH causes an increase in estrogen acting as the onset of labour in pregnant women. It results in the growth of the fetal adrenal gland which has the capacity for steroid biosynthesis i.e. estrogen . Daily steroid production of fetal adrenal glands near term is more than in adults .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: All of the following changes are seen during cervical ripening in a patient except _____.
mcqs.explanation: Collagen fibrils are loosely packed during cervical ripening. Changes in cervical ripening: • Collagen fibril diameter is increased , and there is increased spacing between fibrils leading to increased tissue compliance • Increase in the amount of proteoglycan and glycosaminoglycan within the matrix • Stromal invasion with inflammatory cells

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An obstetrician performs the following procedure for labor induction in a patient . What is the reflex elicited in the process ?
mcqs.explanation: Stripping of membranes is depicted in the image, which elicits the Ferguson reflex . Fetal ejection reflex or Ferguson reflex is a phenomenon in which mechanical stretching of the internal cervix enhances uterine activity. Release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary has been suggested but not proven. It is seen in stripping /sweeping and artificial rupture of membranes. Both of these are methods of induction of labor. It is associated with an increase in blood levels of prostaglandin F2�o metabolite , also known as dinoprost/carboprost.188

mcqs.question: Which of the following image shows the Duncan method ?
mcqs.explanation: Image B shows the Duncan method of placental separation.Comparison between two types of placental separation methods : Brandt Andrew's method or controlled cord traction is a manoeuvre of expressing the placenta from the uterus in the third stage of labour. One hand grasps the umbilical cord while the other is placed on the mother's abdomen with the fi ngers over the anterior surface of the uterus . While the hand on the abdomen is pressed backwar ds and slightly upward , the other applies gentle traction on the cord. Type III placenta previa is a type of incomplete or partial central placenta previa. Here, the placenta covers the internal os partially i.e. it covers the internal os when closed but does not entirely do so when fully dilated .Schultze method Duncan method Separation begins from the c enter of the placenta to the p eriphery . Separation begins from the p eriphery to the center . Blood does not escape extern ally, as the blood pours into t he membrane sac. Blood escapes from the vagin a as the blood collects betwee n the membranes and the ute rine wall.

mcqs.question: In which stage of labour, is the following expelled ?
mcqs.explanation: The placenta and membranes are expelled in the third stage of labour.189 The clinical stages of labour may be summarized as follows :Stages of labou r Definition First True labour pain tofull dilata tion of cervix Second Full dilatation of cervix toexp ulsion of fetus Third Expulsion of fetus toexpulsio n of placenta Fourth One hour observationafter th e expulsion of placenta

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What does fetal position refer to?

options.a: Part of presentation which lies over the internal os
options.b: Relation of different parts of fetus to one another
options.c: Relation of the denominator to different quadrants of the pelvis
options.d: Part of fetus lying in the lower segment of uterus

mcqs.explanation: Fetal position refers to the bony fixed point of reference on presenting part with respect to different quadrants of the pelvis. Definition of various terminologies used for fetus in-utero:Term: Definition: Lie Relationship of the long axis of fetus to the long axis of th e maternal spine190 Term: Definition: Presentation Part of the fetus occupying th e lower pole of the pelvis Presenting pa rt Part of the presentation whic h overlies the internal os Attitude The relation of the different parts of the fetus to one anot her Denominator An arbitrary bony fixed point on the presenting part which comes in relation with the va rious quadrants of the mater nal pelvis Position Relation of the denominator to the different quadrants of the pelvis Engagement When the biparietal diameter has passed the plane of the p elvic brim, the head is said to be engaged .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A senior resident examines a primigravida in labour and informs that the fetus is cephalic in attitude of flexion. What is the most common presenting part of this fetus ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common presenting part when the fetus is in attitude of flexion is vertex.Attitude Presenting part Complete flexion Vertex (occipitoanterior) Incomplete flexio n Vertex (sinciput ) Deflexion Vertex (occipitoposterior ) Partial extension Brow Complete extensi on Face191

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The ultrasonogram shows the diameter of the fetal head which is taken as a reference for engagement . Which diameter does this refer to?
mcqs.explanation: The fetal head is said to be engaged when the biparietal diameter (shown in the image) passes through the pelvic brim. Engagement of fetal head is with reference to this biparietal diameter . It is the greatest transverse diameter in an occiput presentation . It also reflects the gestational age in the second trimester, with a variation of 7-10 days. BPD is measured in the transthalamic view, at the level of the thalamus and cavum septum pellucidum (CSP). It is measured from the outer edge of the skull in the near field to the inner edge of the skull in the far field .192

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a part of a partograph?
mcqs.explanation: Fetal temperature is not a part of a partograph. Assessment of progress of labor is best done by partograph. Components of partograph: • Patient identification • Fetal heart rate recorded every 30 min • Pulse recorded every 30 min • Blood pressure and temperature recorded every 4 h • Uterine contractions recorded every 30 min • Oxytocin-dose and concentration • Urine analysis • Vaginal examination done every 4 hours • State of membranes and colour of liquor

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What are the cardinal movements of labour?
mcqs.explanation: The cardinal movements of labour are engagement , descent , flexion, internal rotation, extension, external rotation, expulsion . (Mnemonic: Every Day FIRE Raises Extremely ) • Every: Engagement • Day: Descent • F: Flexion • IR : Internal rotation • E: Extension • Raises: external Rotation • Extremely : Expulsion The most common presentation is cephalic and presenting part is vertex. Head enters the pelvis through transverse diameter majorly and left occipito transverse is the commonest fetal position. Internal rotation of fetal head occurs at the level of ischial spine . In a vertex delivery , the baby's head is delivered by extension and in a breech delivery , the baby's head is delivered by flexion. The best time to give episotomy is after crowning has occured .193

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A multigravida with gestational diabetes mellitus was admitted in labour at term and progressed to full dilatation. The fetal vertex failed to descend beyond -3 station. The descent of the fetus is facilitated by all except :

options.a: Extension and straightening of the fetal body

mcqs.explanation: A well -flexed head facilitates internal rotation, not the descent of the presenting part. The descent of the fetus is brought about by: • Pressure of amniotic fluid • Direct pressure of the fundus upon the breech with contractions • Bearing-down efforts of maternal abdominal muscles • Extension and straightening of the fetal body

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a prerequisite for internal rotation of the fetal head for a woman in labor?
mcqs.explanation: The tone of levator ani muscles is a prerequisite for internal rotation of the head . Prerequisites of internal rotation of the head are as follows : • Well-flexed head • Efficient uterine contraction • Favorable shape at mid-pelvic plane • Tone of the levator ani muscles

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the internal rotation of the fetal head ?

options.a: Occiput turns towards the transverse axis
options.b: Rotation is not essential when the fetus is unusually small
options.c: Internal rotation is followed by external rotation
options.d: Rotation is earlier in primigravida than in multigravida

mcqs.explanation: Internal rotation is not essential in the completion of labor when the fetus is unusually small.194 Internal rotation begins with the occiput turning away from the transverse axis. In majority, internal rotation is completed by the time the head reaches the pelvic floor. Internal rotation is followed by extension of the head , which is then followed by external rotation. Rotation occurs earlier in multigravida than primigravida whereas engagement occurs earlier in primigravida than multigravida.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the minimum rate of cervical dilatation in primigravida during active labour?
mcqs.explanation: During active labor, the minimal rate of cervical dilatation in primigravida is 1.2 cm/hr. First stage of labour is divided into 2 phases : The cervical dilatation ranges from a minimal rate of 1.2 cm - 6.8 cm/hr in nullipara. Also, the multiparas progress faster in the active phase of labor with a minimal dilatation rate of 1.5 cm/hr. Friedman curve is the sigmoid curve plotting the pattern of cervical dilatation during the latent and active phase of normal labour.Latent phase Active phase The onset of true labor pain up to 6 cm cervical dilatation Starts from \031 6 cm cervical di latation with regular uterine contractions Duration:12 h (nullipara)8 h ( multipara) The minimum rate of cervical dilatation:1.2 cm/h (nullipar a)1.5 cm/h (multipara) Concerned with cervicaleffac ement Concerned with cervicaldilata tion195

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is part of the WHO guidelines for the management of second stage of labor?

options.b: Manual support to perineum to maintain flexion of head
options.c: Never give warm compress to the perineum

mcqs.explanation: The practice of guarding the perineum during delivery of the fetal head is part of the WHO management guidelines for the second stage of labor. The fingers of one hand support the perineum, while the second hand applies pressure to the fetal head to control the speed of crowning. The advantage of this is to prevent perineal tears. The second stage of labor begins with full dilatation of the cervix and ends with the delivery of the fetus . The main events include the descent of the fetus (bearing down by the mother, uterine contractions), cardinal movements of labor, and delivery of the fetus . Management of the second stage of labor: • The most common position used is the dorsal position with the hips flexed , knees flexed and abduction of the thighs . WHO recommends any position of choice including the upright position. • WHO recommendations for the prevention of perineal tears include warm compresses to the perineum, perineal massage , guarding the perineum , and modified Ritgen's maneuver. • Modified Ritgen's maneuver: A sterile towel or pad is held in one hand and placed over the perineum; the other hand applies gentle downward pressure on the occiput to promote flexion and controlled delivery of the head (ensuring the smallest diameter of the head passes through the outlet ). Once the occiput is born–with gentle pressure , the head is extended –forehead , nose, and mouth are then delivered . • WHO doesn 't recommend fundal pressure and routine episiotomy . Other options : Option A: A liberal or routine episiotomy is discouraged . Episiotomy is indicated in cases of: • Shoulder dystocia • Breech delivery • Fetal macrosomia • Operative vaginal deliveries • Persistent occiput posterior positions Option C: Manual techniques , such as massage or application of warm compresses , are recommended for healthy pregnant women requesting pain relief during labor. Option D: The position that is most comfortable to the mother i.e. upright /squatting position is encouraged . This position gives: • less discomfort and difficulty in bearing down • less labor pain • less perineal /vaginal trauma and wound infectionsSecond stage Nulliparous Multiparous Mean/average duration 50 minutes 30 minutes Maximum duration 2 hours (+1 with epidural ) 1 hour (+1 with epidural )196 Second stage Nulliparous Multiparous WHO maximum duration of 2nd stage /diagnosis of arrest 3 hours 2 hours

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Modified Robson's classification class 1 includes :

options.c: Multiparous without previous CS, spontaneous labour
options.d: Multiparous without previous CS, induced /CS before labour

mcqs.explanation: Class 1 of modified Robson's classification includes nullipara, equal to or >37 weeks , single , cephalic , spontaneous labor. It is the most widely accepted classification system available for analyzing characteristics of delivering women worldwide . It consists of 10 patient population categories . The basis for these categories include : • Parity • Onset of labor and mode of delivery • Gestational age • Fetal presentation • No. of fetuses The modified Robson system classification is as follows :Class Nullipara, equal to or >37 we eks, single , cephalic , spontan eous labor Class Nullipara, equal to or >37 we eks, single , cephalic2a:induce d labor2b :CS before labor Class Multipara, equal to or >37 we eks, single , cephalic , spontan eous labor (excludes previous CS) Class Multipara, equal to or >37 we eks, single , cephalic4a :induce d labor4b:CS before labor Class Multipara, previous CS, equa l to or >37 weeks , single , cep halic Class Nullipara, single , breech Class Multipara, single , breech (inc luding previous CS) Class Multiple pregnancies (with or without previous CS)197 Class Nullipara, equal to or >37 we eks, single , cephalic , spontan eous labor Class Singleton pregnancy, oblique /transverse lie (with or witho ut previous CS) Class Single , cephalic <37 weeks (i ncluding previous CS)

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the fetal position in the given image.
mcqs.explanation: In the given vertex presentation , the fetal position is right occipitoanterior. Fetal position refers to the relation of the denominator (arbitrary bony fixed point on the presenting part), with respect to different quadrants of the maternal pelvis. In vertex presentation, the denominator is taken as the occiput (which is close to the triangular posterior fontanelle ). To determine the fetal position the following two steps are followed : • Determine the direction in which the occiput is facing: • Towards the pubic symphysis - occipito -anterior • Towards the sacral promontory - occipito -posterior • Midway between pubic symphysis and sacral promontory - occipito -transverse • Determine if the occiput is facing the left or the right in relation to the materal pelvis

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Uterine contractions are palpable when its intensity is more than _____.
mcqs.explanation: Uterine contractions are palpable when the intensity is >10 mmHg.198 Uterine contractions cause cervical dilatation at 15 mmHg and are painful beyond 15 mmHg. Units for measuring the intensity of uterine contractions are mmHg and Montevideo units (MV). 1 MV = intensity of uterine contractions x number of contractions in 10 min. During labour, normal uterine contractions are between 190 and 300 MV and at the time of delivery, it is 300 MV.Stage of labou r Pressure 1st 40–50 m mHg 2nd –120 mmHg 3rd –120 mmHg

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A primigravida presents to the labor room at 39 weeks of gestation . On examination, you notice the fetal head has appeared at the vulva . Which of the following maneuvers can be used to assist the delivery of the head ?
mcqs.explanation: Ritgen's maneuver is done for delivery of head in normal labor. This maneuver is done when the head distends the vulva and perineum enough to open the vaginal introitus to a diameter of >5 cm. A towel is draped and a gloved hand may be used to exert forward pressure on the chin of the fetus through the perineum . The other hand exerts pressure superiorly against the occiput . This maneuver allows controlled delivery of the head .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which dermatome is pain in the early stage of labor limited to?
mcqs.explanation: 199 Pain in the early stage of labor is limited to dermatomes T10 -L1 . This is of uterine origin. Pain in the late stage of labour is due to dilatation of cervix and perineal stretching . The nerves carrying the pain include S2,3,4.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young primigravida at 39 weeks of gestation presented to the casualty crying of intense abdominal pain. She was diagnosed to be in labour. Which of the following is not a characteristic of this pain?
mcqs.explanation: True labor pain is not relieved by enema and sedatives . It is characterized by the following : • Painful uterine contractions at regular intervals • The frequency of contractions increases gradually • The intensity and duration of contractions increase progressively • Associated with 'show'- extrusion of the mucus plug that had previously filled the cervical canal during pregnancy • Progressive effacement and dilatation of the cervix • Progressive descent of the presenting part • Formation of the 'bag of forewaters ' i.e., bulging fluid -filled amniotic membrane presenting in front of the fetal head • Not relieved by enema or sedatives False labour pain is seen more in primigravidae than in parous women. It usually appears prior to the onset of true labor pain by 1 or 2 weeks in primigravidae and by a few days in multiparae. Such pains are probably due to stretching of the cervix and lower uterine segment with consequent irritation of the neighboring ganglia.Features True labour pains False labour pain s Cervical dilatation and efface ment Present Absent Pain Lower abdomen and back, ra diating to thighs Lower abdomen only Show Present Absent Bag of water Formed Absent Relief with enema No Yes

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You notice the gynecology resident administer the nerve block seen in the image before performing an episiotomy . Which nerve roots are blocked ?
mcqs.explanation: The nerve roots blocked in pudendal nerve block are S2,3,4. It is blocked just above the tip of the ischial spine by piercing the sacrospinous ligament .200 Pudendal nerve block can be used for: • Analgesia in the second stage of labor • Episiotomy repair • Pelvic floor relaxation for outlet instrument delivery • Minor procedures of the lower vagina and perineum • Perineal analgesia prior to application of vacuum/forceps Pudendal block does not impact the cervix or upper vagina . It is ineffective for pain relief associated with uterine manipulation such as manual extraction of the placenta .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Paracervical block relieves pain from all except :
mcqs.explanation: Pain from the lower third of the vagina is relieved by pudendal block, not paracervical block. Paracervical block relieves the pain of uterine contractions and cervical dilatation. It also relieves pain from upper third of the vagina . It is not useful at the time of episiotomy as the lower part of the vagina is not anesthetized . Note : Paracervical block is no longer considered safe as it causes fetal bradycardia. Epidural analgesia is preferred when complete relief of pain is needed throughout labour.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: All of the following are indications for early clamping of cord in a new born baby except :
mcqs.explanation: Postdated pregnancy is not an indication for early cord clamping. Early cord clamping is indicated in: • Birth asphyxia • Rh isoimmunization • Diabetic mother The benefits of delayed cord clamping for up to 60 seconds is an increase in total body iron stores , expand blood volume and a decrease in anemia incidence in the neonate . On the other hand, delayed cord clamping can lead to a higher hemoglobin concentration, which increases risks for hyperbilirubinemia and extended hospitalization for neonatal phototherapy . Delayed cord clamping can also hinder timely neonatal resuscitation . According to AIIMS Protocols in Neonatology, in uncomplicated preterm birth, delayed cord clamping should be attempted . This is done for a minimum time of 60 seconds after delivery for preterm infants not requiring immediate resuscitation after birth. It states that DCC must be done even if the mother has an HIV infection. But as per the NACO guidelines , early cord clamping is advised.201

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a sign of placental separation in stage 3 of parturition of a pregnant woman?
mcqs.explanation: Lengthening of the umbilical cord is seen in placental separation. Signs of placental separation: • The uterus becomes globular, firm, and ballottable (earliest sign to appear) • Schroeder 's sign - Slight rise of fundal height as the separated placenta comes down in the lower segment and uterus rests over it • Slight suprapubic bulging due to separated placenta distending the lower segment . • Kustner 's sign - On pushing , the uterus cephalad with a hand on the abdomen, the cord no longer recedes • A sudden gush of blood • Permanent lengthening of cord Note : Schroeder 's ring is a constriction ring/contraction ring formed due to incoordinate uterine action.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding the modified WHO partogram?

options.a: Right side of alert line indicates immediate referral to First Referral Unit (FRU)
options.b: Alert and action line are separated by a difference of 4 hours
options.c: Each small square in partogram is equal to 1 hour
options.d: Partograph recording should be started once the cervical dilatation reaches 4 cm

mcqs.explanation: Each small square in a modified WHO partogram is equal to 30 minutes . Each small square in a composite WHO partogram is equal to 1 hour.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the following instrument commonly used in obstetrics .
mcqs.explanation: The instrument given in the picture is episiotomy scissors. The angulation in the scissor is to prevent the extension of pelvic tears into the anal margins and obstetric anal sphincter injuries / complete perineal tears. Complications of episiotomy : They can be immediate or remote . Immediate complications include an extension of the incision into the rectum, vulval hematoma, wound dehiscence and injury to anal sphincter . Remote complications include dyspareunia, chances of perineal lacerations in subsequent labor and scar endometriosis (rare). Mayo scissors are long and stout scissors. They can be blunt-tipped /pointed tip/straight or curved. Straight mayo scissors are designed for cutting body tissues near the surface of a wound . They are also used to cut sutures and are also known as suture -cutting scissors. Curved mayo scissors allow much deeper penetration into the wound and are used to cut thick tissues such as those found in the uterus , muscles , breast, and foot. Mayo scissors used for dissection are placed in tissue with the tips closed . The scissors are then opened so that the tips open and spread out the tissue during the dissection process .202

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A nursing assistant posted in the obstetric care unit was asked to monitor the progress of labour. After how much dilatation of the cervix, should she start the documentation ?
mcqs.explanation: The WHO Labour Care Guide begins the documentation of labour progression at 5 cm of cervical dilatation. The WHO Labour Care Guide is a tool designed to help health personnel involved in labour care. It aims to • Guide the monitoring and help in the documentation of the progress of labour. • Guide the health professionals to offer supportive care throughout labour. • Assist doctors in promptly identifying and addressing emerging labour complications . • Prevent the use of unnecessary interventions in labour. • Support audits and quality improvement.203 The differences between the WHO-modified partograph and the latest WHO Labour Care Guide are tabulated below : Note : Previously the answer to the question was 4 cm (according to the modified WHO patograph). However, this information is outdated , therefore the answer to this question has been revised per the latest WHO guidelines.WHO modified partograph WHO Labour Care Guide Documentation of labour pro gression begins at4 cmof cerv ical dilatation. Documentation of labour pro gression begins at5 cmof cerv ical dilatation. Fixed1 cm/hour 'alert' and 'ac tion'lines Time-based cut-offsforeach c entimetreof cervical dilatatio n to guide the obstetrician to take action. For example , at 5 cm of cervical dilatation, if t here is no progress >6 hours, action needs to be taken. Monitoring of labour is restri cted to thefirst stageonly . Monitoring ofthe second stag e of labouris included No section on supportive car e interventions Addition of a section onsupp ortive careof the mother- lab our companionship, pain reli ef , oral fluid intake and postu re Documentation ofstrength , d uration, and frequencyof uter ine contractions Documentation ofonlythedur ation and frequency of uterin e contractions204

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young woman delivered her baby on the way to the hospital . While examining her, you notice a perineal tear. This injury could have been prevented by all except :

options.c: Slow delivery of the head in between contractions

mcqs.explanation: Perineal injury cannot be prevented in normal labor by routine timely episiotomy . Routine episiotomy is associated with an increased incidence of disruption of anal sphincters and rectal tears. Indications of episiotomy : • Shoulder dystocia • Breech delivery • Fetal macrosomia • Operative vaginal deliveries • Persistent occiput posterior positions Methods of prevention of perineal laceration: • Avoid delivery by early extension • Deliver head in between contractions • Perform timely episiotomy when indicated (not routine).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of true cephalopelvic disproportion in India?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of true cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD) in India is rickets. The most common cause of true CPD in developing countries is vitamin D deficiency and rickets. In developed countries , it is trauma to the pelvis. It occurs due to pelvic dystocia (larger fetus and smaller pelvis). Relative CPD is the most common type of CPD. It is caused due to fetal malposition (occipitoposterior position/brow presentation).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You are monitoring uterine contractions in a term primigravida in labor. You find that the contractions are uncoordinated and the frequency is about 8 contractions every 10 minutes . Which of the following is incorrect regarding your finding?

options.b: It is common in nulliparous labour
options.d: Management includes wait and watch policy

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical finding is suggestive of uterine tachysystole . Oxytocin administration is not beneficial here as it leads to hyperstimulation of the uterus . Tachysystole (hypertonic uterine dysfunction ):212 • The uterine contractions are uncoordinated and increased in frequency (>5 contractions in 10 minutes ) • Contractions occur with an increase in the baseline tone without rest in between them • It is associated with late active phase dysfunction i.e., when the cervix is almost 7 cm dilated • The most common cause is occipito -posterior position. Hence , a wait and watch policy is adopted • It is more common in nulliparous females • Oxytocin administration leads to hyperstimulation of the uterus and is not recommended . Hypotonic uterine dysfunction : • Uterine contractions are inadequate • It is associated with early active phase • It is more common in nulliparous females .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 37-week primigravida has mild labor pains for 20 hours and the cervix is persistently 1 cm dilated but non-effaced . What would be the appropriate management?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of either false labor pain or prolonged latent phase . The appropriate management is to sedate the patient and wait. False labor can be differentiated from the latent phase of labor by therapeutic rest i.e., the patient is sedated with morphine. Augmentation with oxytocin is done only in those patients who even after therapeutic rest continue to be in prolonged latent phase. There is no indication of cesarean section unless cephalopelvic disproportion is present . Amniotomy is not useful and should be avoided in patients with prolonged latent phase .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old G3P2L2 woman presents to the ER with hypotension and severe abdominal pain. On examination, fetal parts are palpable over the abdomen. USG abdomen revealed a large uterine wall defect . Which of the following is not a feature of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of uterine rupture . Maternal tachycardia is seen in this condition. Clinical features of uterine rupture : • Maternal tachycardia • Fetal bradycardia/absent fetal heart sounds • Hypotension • Abdominal tenderness • Palpable fetal parts on per abdomen examination • Bandl's ring • Bleeding per vagina213 • Hematuria Common causes of uterine rupture are previous caesarean delivery , myomectomy , silent rupture (in previous pregnancy), excess use of oxytocin, grand multipara, uterine overdistension, obstructed labour, difficult forceps delivery, placenta percreta

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young primigravida at 36 weeks of gestation came with complaints of decreased perception of fetal movements for the past 2 days. NST is non-reactive and on ultrasound fetal cardiac activity is absent. What will be the best management in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture is suggestive of intrauterine fetal death (IUFD). The best management for such cases at 36 weeks is waiting for spontaneous expulsion . Forceps extraction is only necessary if spontaneous expulsion doesn 't take place . Artificial rupture of membranes (ARM) is not done due to the risk of infections . Cesarean section is avoided as far as possible in case of fetal death . Waiting till term is not recommended in cases of uterine infections , disseminated intravascular coagulation, and psychological upset .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G2P1L0 woman presents to OPD at 36 weeks of gestation for a routine visit. She mentions that she has a history of prior stillbirth at 37 weeks . What is the best time for delivery in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The best time for elective delivery in patients with a history of previous stillbirth is 39 weeks , either by induction or cesarean section . The recommendations for the management of subsequent pregnancy after stillbirth is as follows : • Ultrasonographic screening for fetal growth restriction after 28 weeks • Kick counts starting from 28 weeks of gestation • Antepartum fetal surveillance starting at 32 weeks or 1-2 weeks earlier than prior stillbirth • Support and reassurance Labor induction is suitable in such cases . Cesarean delivery is done for those with a contraindication to induction.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman presents with obstructed labor and is grossly dehydrated . Investigations reveal fetal demise . What will be the management?
mcqs.explanation: The best management in the given clinical scenario is cesarean section . Obstructive labor management involves administering intravenous fluids to correct dehydration , providing antibiotics to prevent infection, and promptly performing a cesarean section to relieve the obstruction. If the fetus is alive, an immediate cesarean section is typically performed . Management of obstructed labor never involves a wait-and-watch approach or augmenting with oxytocin. Clinical features of obstructed labor include maternal exhaustion , dehydration , tachycardia, tachypnea , genital sepsis , postpartum hemorrhage, and shock.214 On P/A examination the upper uterine segment is tender and tonically contracted . The lower uterine segment is thin and stretched . A groove/depression is felt between the upper uterine segment and the lower uterine segment. This is called a Bandls ring. Complications of obstructed labor include rupture of the uterus and vesicovaginal fistula .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The partogram of a 28 year old G2P1 is shown below . What is the next step in management?
mcqs.explanation: The above partogram shows a case of obstructed labour and management is caesarean section . There is a secondary arrest of dilatation for >2 hours and arrest of descent for >1 hour. The patient has adequate uterine contractions as shown. The amniotic fluid is stained with meconium and there is fall in fetal heart rate which indicates that the baby is in distress . There is no place for wait and watch and use of oxytocin to stimulate uterine contractions in obstructed labor. Forceps can be applied only when the cervix is fully dilated and the head is low down.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: After successful delivery of the baby, the obstetrician witnesses that the episiotomy performed has extended backwards beyond the perineal body. Which among the following structures is likely to be injured in this case?
mcqs.explanation: External anal sphincter is the structure injured in an episiotomy extended posteriorly beyond the perineal body. Perineal tear have been divided into four degrees : • First degree - laceration is restricted to the skin of the fourchette • Second degree - muscles of the perineal body are torn through • Third degree - the tear extends partially backward through the external sphincter of the anus • Fourth degree - the external anal sphincter is torn and anal mucosa is also involved A central tear of the perineum is when the head penetrates first through the posterior vaginal wall, then through the perineal body and appears through the skin of the perineum . It usually occurs in patients with a contracted outlet .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A midwife is examining a pregnant woman in labour when she noticed that the cord is prolapsed . What should be the next immediate step of management?

options.a: Gently replace the cord inside the vagina
options.b: Inform the doctor and shift to OT
options.d: Do vaginal examination and find the fetal presentation

mcqs.explanation: In this scenario the midwife should put the pregnant women in a Trendelenburg position or in an exaggerated and elevated Sims' position with a pillow or wedge under the hip or thigh. Caesarean section is the recommended treatment of choice for cord prolapse . Prior to performing the procedure , several measures can be taken to alleviate cord compression. These measures involve: • Manually elevating the fetal presenting part using two fingers or the entire hand through the vagina215 • Positioning the patient in steep Trendelenburg , exaggerated Sim's position, or knee-chest position • Filling the bladder with 500–700 cc or more of saline (known as the Vagos method ) After the diagnosis of cord prolapse is made, it is crucial not to attempt cord replacement . Such attempts are not only ineffective but also result in the inevitable rupture of the membranes, leading to cord prolapse .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Abdominal examination of a 28-year-old primigravida , who is in the second stage of labour, reveals retraction ring between the active upper segment and the distended lower segment . Which would best describe this ring?
mcqs.explanation: Bandl's ring refers to pathological retraction ring. It is formed in cases of obstructed labour. The upper segment of the uterus contracts and retracts vigourously in an attempt to overcome the obstruction while the lower segment dilates . With each contraction there is myometrial shortening so that the actively contracting upper segment becomes progressively thicker and shorter. The passive lower segment is progressively stretched and becomes thinner. The junction between the two segments stands out prominently as a pathological retraction ring.216 Schroeder 's constriction ring is formed due to incordinate uterine action when there is localized spastic contraction of a ring of circular muscle fibres of the uterus . It is formed due to injudicious use of oxytocin and premature rupture of membranes (PROM).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old term primigravida presents to the clinic for a regular check-up. On examination , uterus corresponds to term and head of the fetus is non-engaged . What is the most common cause for this finding?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of non-engagement at term in a primigravida is deflexed head followed by cephalopelvic disproportion. Non-engagement at the onset of active phase of labour is a risk factor for caesarean section . The problems of prolonged labour are that the woman is exposed to high risk of infection , ketosis and obstructed labour while the fetus faces the danger of asphyxia and infection .217

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a cardinal movement occurring during labor?
mcqs.explanation: Asynclitism is not a cardinal movement during labor. Asynclitism refers to the position of a baby in the uterus such that the head of the baby is presenting first and is tilted to the shoulder . This causes the fetal head to no longer be in line with the birth canal. Moderate degrees of asynclitism are the rule in normal labor. However, if severe , this condition is a common reason for cephalopelvic disproportion even with an otherwise normal sized pelvis. Asynclitism can be of 2 types : • When the sagittal suture lies anteriorly, the posterior parietal bone becomes the leading presenting part and is called posterior asynclitism. • When the sagittal suture lies posteriorly, the anterior parietal bone becomes the leading presenting part and is called anterior asynclitism.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old primigravida is brought to the labour room in the latent phase of labor. How long will you wait till you declare her latent phase to be prolonged ?
mcqs.explanation: Latent phase is said to be prolonged in a primigravida if it lasts for more than 20 hours. Friedman defined prolonged latent phase as: • A nullipara who has not entered the active phase by 20 hours after the onset of the latent phase • A multipara who has not entered the active phase by 14 hours after the onset of the latent phase

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: All of the following findings are seen in the partogram of a patient except :
mcqs.explanation: The above partogram shows secondary arrest of dilatation for >2 hour, arrest of descent for >1 hour and a fall in fetal heart rate suggestive of fetal distress .218 These are characteristic findings of obstructed labour and management is caesarean section .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old primigravida presents with labour pains. At 39 weeks of gestation , she was diagnosed with prolonged phase of labour. Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.c: Excessive sedation can prolong this phase

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical features suggest that the patient is in latent phase of labor. Latent phase is said to be prolonged if it is: • >20 h in nullipara • >14 h in multipara Causes of prolonged latent phase : • Excessive sedation /epidural analgesia • Poor cervical conditions (thick, uneffaced ) • False labour (most common cause in multipara) Friedman's curve is used in the diagnosis of prolonged labour. It is the sigmoid curve plotting the pattern of cervical dilatation during the latent and active phase of normal labour.Management includes morphine administration, rest and oxytocin stimulation.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Protracted active phase dilatation in a multiparous woman is when cervical dilatation is _____.
mcqs.explanation: Protracted active phase dilatation in a multiparous woman is when cervical dilatation is less than 1.5 cm/hour.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which among the following is false with respect to active phase of labor?

options.a: The minimum rate of cervical dilatation is 1.2cm /hr in nullipara
options.b: Arrest of dilatation is cessation of dilatation for >2 hours
options.c: Arrest of descent is cessation of descent for >1 hour
options.d: Poor cervical dilatation causes prolonged active phase

mcqs.explanation: 219 Poor cervical dilatation causes a prolonged latent phase . Arrest of cervical dilatation is defined as the lack of cervical dilatation for \031 2 hours during the active phase of labour. According to the Obstetric Care Consensus Committee , when cervical dilatation has reached \031 cm with ruptured membranes, and there is no cervical change despite 4 hours of adequate uterine contractions or 6 hours of inadequate contractions, a cesarean delivery is warranted.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Protracted descent in labor in a nullipara is ______
mcqs.explanation: The protracted descent in labor in a nullipara is less than 1 cm/hour.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A multigravida is posted for C-section due to arrest of descent in labor. It is defined as no descent for ______
mcqs.explanation: Arrest of descent in labor in a multigravida is no descent for more than 1 hour.220

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the technique of stimulating uterine contractions in a pregnant patient prior to the onset of spontaneous labour known as?
mcqs.explanation: The technique of stimulating uterine contractions prior to the onset of spontaneous labor is known as induction of labor. It can be done irrespective of the rupture of membranes. Augmentation is the enhancement of spontaneous contractions that are considered inadequate because of failed cervical dilation and fetal descent .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a contraindication for the induction of labor?

options.d: History of lower transverse cesarean section in last three pregnancies

mcqs.explanation: 227 Heart disease is currently not considered a contraindication for the induction of labor. Vaginal delivery is preferred in such patients .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old G3P2 woman was admitted to the ward at 40 weeks of gestation for induction of labor. You were asked to calculate her Bishop's score. What should be the minimum score before performing this procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: The minimum Bishop Score required before proceeding with induction of labour is 6. A Bishop score >8 conveys a high likelihood of a successful induction. The latest guidelines state that a cut-off score of 6 can be used to choose between pharmacological and mechanical methods of induction. This score is calculated based on the : • station of the fetal head • dilation of cervix • cervical length • position of cervix • consistency of the cervix. This score is an important determinant of a successful induction.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: During rounds in the postnatal ward, you notice a patient 's case sheet mentioning she had uterine tachysystole following labor induction. What is the criteria for this diagnosis?

options.a: More than 5 contractions in a 5-min period
options.b: More than 5 contractions in a 10 -min period
options.c: More than 10 contractions in a 5-min period
options.d: More than 10 contractions in a 10 -min period

mcqs.explanation: Uterine tachysystole is defined as >5 contractions in a 10 min period and may occur in spontaneous or stimulated labor. It should always be qualified by the presence or absence of fetal heart rate abnormalities. Tachysystole interrupts maternal blood flow to the placenta during contractions and may lead to a reduction in fetal oxygenation . It is also associated with placental abruption. It is caused by pharmacological agents used for cervical ripening and induction such as misoprostol (both oral and vaginal) and dinoprostone . Management includes stopping oxytocin infusion and terbutaline 0.25 mg SC.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A primigravida was admitted to the labor room at 41 weeks of gestation for the induction of labor. What is the dose of misoprostol used for this procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: Misoprostol (PGE1) is given as 25mcg 3-6 hourly vaginally or 25mcg 2 hourly orally for the induction of labor. It is associated with the following side effects : • Uterine tachysystole • Meconium stained amniotic fluid • Uterine rupture228

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Oxytocin is being given for augmentation of labour in a multigravida admitted to the labour room. Which of the following is not a mechanism of action of this drug?

options.a: Receptor mediation through G-protein coupled receptors
options.b: Activation of voltage mediated Ca channel

mcqs.explanation: Competitive blocking of acetylcholine is not a mechanism of action of oxytocin. Mechanism of action of oxytocin is as follows : • Receptor mediation through G protein-coupled receptors • Activation of voltage -gated Ca channel leading to calcium entry • Prostaglandin production by a positive feedback mechanism. This induces production of more prostaglandins and stronger contractions.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In which of the following patients would you perform a controlled artificial rupture of membranes?

options.a: G3P2 lady with absent fetal cardiac activity at 34 weeks of gestation
options.b: Multigravida with HIV at 36 weeks of gestation
options.c: G2P1 lady with AFI of 28 cm at 38 weeks of gestation
options.d: Term primigravida with red, tender, vesicular lesions on her vulva

mcqs.explanation: Controlled artificial rupture of membranes (ARM) is performed in a patient with amniotic fluid index (AFI) \031 25 cm. This points towards a diagnosis of polyhydramnios. This is because if ARM is not done under controlled conditions in these patients , it can cause sudden decompression of the fetus . This can lead to abruption of placenta . Contraindications to ARM: • Intrauterine fetal death • Active genital herpes infection • Maternal HIV -AIDS

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An obstetrician performs the following procedure for labor induction in a patient . Which of the following is false about the reflex elicited here?

options.a: Occurs due to pressure at the external os of cervix
options.b: It is associated with increased level of PGF2�o
options.c: Artificial rupture of membranes initiates this reflex
options.d: It is an example of positive feedback mechanism

mcqs.explanation: Stripping of membranes is being depicted in the image, which elicits the Ferguson reflex . It is also known as the fetal ejection reflex and is seen due to the pressure at the internal os of the cervix. It is associated with an increase in blood levels of a prostaglandin F2�o metabolite , also known as dinoprost. This is released due to mechanical stretching of the internal os. This enhances the uterine activity and causes release of more prostaglandins. It is an example of a positive feedback mechanism.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: All of the following are true about laminaria tents except :

options.b: Leads to the release of endogenous prostaglandins

mcqs.explanation: The Bishop's score is rapidly improved by the use of laminaria tents . It is a mechanical cervical dilator and acts by hygroscopic osmotic action, leading to slow dilatation of the cervix. The gentle dilatation by laminaria tents induces an endogenous synthesis of prostaglandins causing a softening of the cervix. This is useful in cervical ripening before induction of labour.229

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A nursing assistant posted in the obstetric care unit was asked to plot a partograph to monitor the progress of labour. Where should she start marking the cervical dilatation?
mcqs.explanation: In a partograph, the first marking of cervical dilatation should be made on the left of the alert line. In a normal partograph, the plotting remains on the left of the alert line.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You are monitoring the number, duration, and intensity of uterine contractions in a 34-year-old G2P1 woman with a term pregnancy. How long should they last for you to classify them as moderate ?
mcqs.explanation: Moderate uterine contractions last for 20 –40 s. Weak contractions last for <20 s and strong contractions are >40 s. During active labour, uterine contractions are 5 min apart for 1 hour, i.e., \031 12 contractions in 1 hour. This is accompanied by cervical dilatation of \0313–5 cm.230

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G2P1 woman with polyhydramnios, presents to the clinic with respiratory distress at 38 weeks of gestation. The obstetrician plans for induction of labor. What is a safe method of induction in this patient ?

options.c: Abdominal amniocentesis followed by oxytocin drip

mcqs.explanation: Abdominal amniocentesis followed by oxytocin drip is a safe method for induction of labor in polyhydramnios. Abdominal amniocentesis drains a good amount of liquor (amnioreduction), after which the oxytocin infusion can be started . This will minimize the sudden decompression and reduce the risk of placental separation, cord prolapse and change in lie of the fetus . Although polyhydramnios does not constitute an absolute contraindication for the application of prostaglandins, these substances should be administered with caution. There is a marked increase in the incidence of postpartum hemorrhage and amniotic fluid embolism with their use . Hence , amnioreduction is a preferred mode of treatment in polyhydramnios.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Given below is the partograph of a primigravida in labor. What should be the next step in managing her condition?

options.d: Induction of labor by mechanical methods

mcqs.explanation: As the plotting on the above partograph has crossed the action line, the next step of management is Caesarean section .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the half-life of oxytocin?
mcqs.explanation: The half-life of oxytocin is approximately 3–5 min. Therefore, once oxytocin infusion is stopped , its concentration in plasma rapidly falls.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: During your OBG rotations, one of the senior residents asks you to induce labor in a primigravida admitted at 40 weeks of gestation . Identify the following device that you will use for the same.
mcqs.explanation: This is an image of a cervidil vaginal insert. It is used for cervical ripening and improves the Bishop's score. It contains 10 mg of dinoprostone designed to release at a rate of approximately 0.3 mg/hr over 10-hours.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: According to the WHO Labour Care Guidelines , documentation of labour progress begins at a cervical dilatation of -
mcqs.explanation: According to the WHO Labour Care Guidelines , documentation of labour progress begins at a cervical dilatation of 5cm. WHO Labour Care Guidelines : • Time axis - examination findings are plotted every one hour231 • Alert column- has values which if reached indicates the need for urgent medical intervention • Active first stage - findings are plotted every hour upto 12 hours. If the first stage continues , a new sheet is used . • Second stage - plotted every hour upto 3 hours 1) Section 1: Preliminary information Name, parity, labour onset , active labour diagnosis (date ), ruptured membranes (date &time), risk factors 2) Section 2: Supportive care • Companionship • Pain relief • Oral fluid • Posture 3) Section 3: Baby • Baseline FHR • FHR deceleration • Amniotic fluid • Fetal position • Caput • Moulding 4) Section 4: Vitals Pulse , SBP, DBP, temperature , and urine for proteins are recorded every 4 hours 5) Section 5: Labour progress • Count the number of uterine contractions over a 10 -minute period . • Assess the duration of contractions • Cervical dilatation: starts at 5 cm and is plotted as X; it is assessed every hour. For example - if the cervical dilatation remains at 5cm for \031 6hrs, it indicates the need for urgent intervention. Similarly, the cut-offs for - 6cm is \031 5hrs; 7cm is \031 3hrs; 8cm is \031 2.5hrs; 9cm is \031 2 hrs • Descent - plotted as O 6) Section 6: Medication • Oxytocin • Medicine • IV fluids 7) Section 7: Shared decision making • Assessment • Plan232 *Fetal position, vitals of the mother and cervical dilatation can be assessed at 4 hourly if the labour is progressing adequately *If birth is not completed by 3 hours from the start of the active second stage in nulliparous and 2 hours in multiparous women, intervention is needed

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following modifications have been made in the WHO Labour care guidelines as compared to the modified partograph
mcqs.explanation: WHO modified partograph WHO Labour Care Guide Documentation of labour pro gression begins at4 cmof cerv ical dilatation. Documentation of labour pro gression begins at5 cmof cerv ical dilatation. Fixed1 cm/hour 'alert' and 'ac tion'lines Time-based cut-offsforeach c entimeterof cervical dilatatio n to guide the obstetrician to take action. For example , at 5 cm of cervical dilatation, if t here is no progress >6 hours, action needs to be taken. Monitoring of labour is restri cted to thefirst stageonly . Monitoring ofsecond stage of labouris included No section on supportive car e interventions Addition of a section onsupp ortive careof the mother- lab our companionship, pain reli ef , oral fluid intake and postu re Documentation ofstrength , d uration, and frequencyof uter ine contractions Documentation ofonlythedur ation and frequency of uterin e contractions233

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman with gestational diabetes mellitus is admitted to the labour room. The delivery of the baby's shoulder is delayed after the delivery of the head . When is shoulder dystocia considered ?

options.a: Head to shoulder delivery time >30 sec
options.b: Head to shoulder delivery time >45 sec
options.c: Head to shoulder delivery time >60 sec
options.d: Head to shoulder delivery time >120 sec

mcqs.explanation: Shoulder dystocia is defined as head to shoulder delivery time of more than 60 seconds . It occurs when either the anterior or the posterior fetal shoulder gets impacted on the maternal symphysis or on the sacral promontory respectively. Prelabour risk factors: • Diabetes Mellitus • Obesity • Postdatism and prior history • Excessive weight gain during pregnancy Intrapartum risk factors:243 • Prolonged 1st and 2nd stage of labour • Instrumental delivery • Augmentation of labour with oxytocin

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old primigravida with a history of gestational diabetes mellitus is in active labour. After delivery of the head , turtle sign was noticed . Which of the following can be used for the management of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: A patient with gestational diabetes and the presence of turtle sign is suggestive of shoulder dystocia . Mc Robert's manoeuvre, Wood's corkscrew manoeuvre, Gaskin's manoeuvre, and Rubin's manoeuvre are all used in its management. Shoulder dystocia occurs when either the anterior or the posterior fetal shoulder gets impacted on the maternal pelvis. Turtle sign may be seen which refers to the recoil of the fetal head against the perineum . Management of labour in case of shoulder dystocia : • 1st line of management - Mc Roberts manoeuvre (flexion and abduction of thigh) • 2nd line of management - Rubin's (rotation of the easily accessible shoulder by 30-45\260), Woods corkscrew manoeuvre (rotate the posterior shoulder to 180o in a cork screw fashion) ; OR Gaskin (all four's position) • Last line of management - Zavanelli manoeuvre (head is rotated to its pre-restitution position and caesarian section is performed ); OR procedures such as cleidotomy (fracture of the clavicle of the baby); symphysiotomy (divide pubic symphysis of mother) In a case of bilateral shoulder dystocia , directly proceed to perform cesarean section after doing Zavanelli manoeuvre.244

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The first manoeuvre for shoulder dystocia consists of:

options.a: Forceful adduction by extension of legs on abdomen
options.b: Forceful adduction by flexion of legs on abdomen
options.c: Forceful abduction of legs by extending them on abdomen
options.d: Forceful abduction of legs by flexing them on abdomen

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of shoulder dystocia . Mc Roberts manoeuvre is the first manoeuvre to be performed in shoulder dystocia . It involves flexion and abduction of the maternal hips, positioning the maternal thighs on her abdomen.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G2P1 obese woman was diagnosed with arrest of descent during labour. Identify the following manoeuvre performed for this patient .
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of shoulder dystocia and the manoeuvre shown above is the McRoberts manoeuvre. This is the most effective intervention and should be the first manoeuvre to be performed in shoulder dystocia .245 McRoberts manoeuvre: • Flexion and abduction of the maternal hips (positioning the maternal thighs on her abdomen). • The pelvic rotation which occurs due to the straightening of the sacrum tends to free the impacted anterior shoulder of the baby. • Suprapubic pressure may be used simultaneously . • The lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh is the most common nerve to get injured during this manoeuvre. If the first line of management fails, proceed with internal rotational manoeuvres such as Rubin's and Wood corkscrew in McRoberts position. Rubin's manoeuvre: • Internal rotational manoeuver used to deliver the baby in case of shoulder dystocia . • It involves dislodging the easily accessible shoulder towards the anterior aspect of the chest from under the pubic symphysis by 30-45\260 while staying in the McRoberts' position. • Pressure is applied on the scapular aspect (posteriorly ) of the shoulder .Wood corkscrew manoeuvre: • Internal rotational manoeuver used to deliver the baby in case of shoulder dystocia . • It involves dislodging the posterior shoulder by 180\260 in a corkscrew fashion to lie beneath the pubic symphysis while staying in McRobert's position. • Pressure is applied on the clavicular aspect (anteriorly) of the shoulder .246

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of these steps would you undertake for the management of a patient with shoulder dystocia along with performing the McRoberts manoeuvre?

options.c: Flex the legs over the abdomen

mcqs.explanation: Applying a gentle suprapubic pressure is the first step in the management of shoulder dystocia along with McRoberts manoeuvre. Fundal pressure is not a method of delivery in such cases . Hernandez and Wendel suggested the use of a shoulder dystocia drill to better organize emergency management: • Call for help and mobilize labour assistants , anaesthesia and pediatric doctors. • An attempt at traction is tried followed by episiotomy to afford room posteriorly . • Apply pressure suprapubically , not fundally , with the palm or fist, directing the pressure on the anterior shoulder . • This should be both downward (below the pubic bone) and laterally (toward the baby's face or sternum) in conjunction with the McRoberts manoeuvre. These manoeuvres will resolve most cases of shoulder dystocia . If the above-listed steps fail, the following steps may be attempted , and any of the manoeuvres may be repeated : • Rubin's manoeuvre • Woods corkscrew manoeuvre • Gaskin (all four's position) • Zavanelli manoeuvre • Cleidotomy (fracture of the clavicle of baby) • Symphysiotomy (divide pubic symphysis of mother).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common fetal malpresentation ?
mcqs.explanation: 247 The most common fetal malpresentation is the breech presentation . The most common breech presentation in primigravida is frank breech and in multigravida, it is flexed /complete breech . It is most commonly seen with prematurity . In breech presentation : • The most common position is left sacroanterior • The engaging diameter is bitrochanteric. • Cord prolapse is common in footling presentation and rare in frank breech . However, among all malpresentations , cord prolapse is most common in transverse lie.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In which of the following conditions is Vagos method used ?
mcqs.explanation: Vagos method is used in cord prolapse . Vagos method is also known as the bladder filling method . Here, the bladder is distended with saline to push the presenting part higher up, thereby preventing compression in case of cord prolapse . The bladder is filled with 400–750 mL of normal saline with a Foley 's catheter . Then, the balloon is inflated and the catheter is clamped .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman presented to the clinic with the following fetal presentation . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of frank breech . Breech presentation can be divided into the following : • Incomplete : Breech with extended legs , footling , knee presentation • Complete : Breech with flexed legsBreech type Description Presenting part Frank breech (with extended l egs ) Thighs flexed on the trunk, le gs extended at the knee joint. Buttocks and genitalia Footling Both thighs and legs are parti ally extended Foot Knee Thighs extended , Knee flexed Knee Complete /flexed Both thighs and legs are flexe d. Buttocks, genitalia , foot248

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A multigravida presented to the clinic at 36 weeks of gestation . She was found to have a breech presentation clinically and on sonography. Which of the following is not an indication for cesarean section in this type of presentation ?
mcqs.explanation: Flexed breech is not an indication for cesarean section in breech presentation . This baby can be delivered vaginally. Factors favouring cesarean delivery of the breech fetus : • Large fetus (> 3800 to 4000 g) • Severe IUGR • Footling presentation (due to risk of cord prolapse ) • Hyperextended head • Contracted pelvis • Previous cesarean section • Preterm breech • Primi with breech • Twins, with the first baby in the breech • Lack of surgeon experience • Patient requests for cesarean delivery .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A footling breech comes under ______ type of breech presentation .
mcqs.explanation: A footling breech is a type of incomplete breech presentation with one or more feet below the breech . Breech presentation can be divided into the following :249 • Incomplete : Breech with extended legs , footling or knee presentation • Complete : Breech with flexed legsBreech type Description Presenting part Frank breech (with extended l egs ) Thighs flexed on trunk, legs e xtended at knee joint. Buttocks and genitalia Footling Both thighs and legs are parti ally extended Foot Knee Thighs extended , knee flexed Knee Complete /flexed Both thighs and legs are flexe d. Buttocks, genitalia , foot

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
