mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An anxious mother pregnant with twins was recently diagnosed with twin-twin transfusion syndrome. She wants to know the possible fetal outcome of the pregnancy. Which of the following investigations can be used to predict this?
mcqs.explanation: In twin-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS ), the fetal outcome depends on the cardiac function of the recipient twin. Tei index or myocardial performance index (MPI) is used to assess the325 ventricular function using doppler . Option A: Deepest vertical pocket on USG is used to diagnose polyhydramnios-oligohydramnios in TTTS . Options B and D: Fetal haemoglobin and MCA peak systolic velocity are used to diagnose TAPS (Twin anaemia polycythemia syndrome).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is/are the placental vascular abnormality that can be seen in the condition depicted in the image given below ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows an acardius acephalus fetus . This refers to the acardiac twin seen in twin reversed arterial perfusion (TRAP ). Both artery-artery and vein-vein anastomosis can be seen in TRAP . TRAP is a placental vascular anastomotic complication seen in monochorionic twins. In this disorder, deoxygenated blood from the donor twin enters the recipient twin through the anastomosis and supplies the lower half of the recipient 's body. Hence , the heart and upper body of the recipient is poorly developed . The below image depicts the circulation pattern seen in TRAP .Based on the supply of deoxygenated blood, the recipient twin might have the following fates : The donor twin develops high output cardiac failure. The treatment for this condition is radiofrequency ablation of the acardiac or recipient twin.Fate Type Lower body is perfused with f ailed head growth Acardius acephalus Partially developed head with identifiable limbs Acardius myelecephal us326 Fate Type No recognizable structure Acardius amorphous

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old woman, pregnant with twins, goes into labour. Following the vaginal delivery of the first twin, she was taken to the OT for internal version. What could have been the possible indication for this procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: The second twin being in transverse lie is the only indication for internal version in modern obstetrics . In a twin pregnancy, if the first twin has vertex presentation , vaginal delivery can be performed . Following the vaginal delivery of the first twin, if the second twin is in transverse lie, it is corrected by external version (preferably cephalic ) into a longitudinal lie. If external version fails and the membranes are intact, internal version is done under general anaesthesia , followed by breech extraction. If the membranes are ruptured , caesarean section is done immediately . Mode of delivery depends on the presentation of the 1st twin:Presentation of the 1st twin Mode of deliver y Vertex Vaginal Breech Caesarean secti on Transverse Caesarean secti on

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify this condition.
mcqs.explanation: The given specimen depicts a monochorionic monoamniotic pregnancy as: • 2 umbilical cords are arising from 1 placenta (monochorionic) • No intervening amniotic membrane is attached to the placenta . This means that both fetuses must have been inside a single amniotic cavity (monoamniotic). Option B: In Monochorionic diamniotic pregnancy, on gross examination, there will be 1 placenta and intervening 2 layers of amnion attached to the placenta . In this type of pregnancy, each fetus will have its own amniotic cavity (diamniotic) with a shared placenta (monochorionic). This is seen if the fertilized zygote divides into 2 between 4-8 days. The below given gross image of monochorionic diamniotic pregnancy shows two umbilical cords arising separately from the placenta with the intervening amniotic membrane held by the forceps .327 Option D: In dichorionic diamniotic pregnancy each fetus has it's own amnion & chorion. The placentas here may be fused or separate . This is seen in dizygotic twins as well as monozygotic twins that divide within 0-4 days. Option A: Twin to twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS ) most commonly complicates monochorionic (single placenta ) twin pregnancy. In TTTS blood is transfused from the donor twin to the recipient twin through the abnormal vascular connections within the placenta leaving the donor anemic while the recipient becomes polycythemic . mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman was diagnosed with triplets on ultrasound. The obstetrician has planned to do a selective fetal reduction of one of the fetuses to improve the outcome of the pregnancy. What is the ideal timing and the method for the procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: Selective fetal reduction is done between 10 -13 weeks via intracardiac injection of KCl. In multi-chorionic multifetal gestations , selective reduction of the smallest or anomalous fetus /fetuses is done to increase the chance of survival of the other fetuses . Laser ablation or bipolar coagulation of the umbilical cord of the targeted fetus is done. This protects the surviving fetuses from the adverse effects of the drug.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old primigravida who conceived after in-vitro fertilization therapy came for an antenatal checkup at 38 weeks of gestation . Her obstetric history revealed that she was pregnant with DCDA twins. On examination, the first twin was found to be in a breech position and the maternal blood pressure was found to be greater than 140 /90 mm Hg on two occasions with grade 1+ proteinuria. What should be done next?

options.a: Monitor BP and terminate pregnancy if BP rises
options.c: Terminate pregnancy at 40 weeks of gestation

mcqs.explanation: Immediate cesarean section is done as the first twin is in breech presentation . Uncomplicated dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancies are terminated at 38 weeks of gestation . Timing of delivery depends on the type of twin pregnancy: The mode of delivery depends on the 1st twin: After delivery of 1st twin, if the 2nd twin is in breech , assisted breech delivery is done. If the 2nd twin is in a transverse lie, the internal podalic version is done under GA in the OT followed by breech extraction. Complications in attempting vaginal delivery in non-vertex presentation (i.e) transverse and breech : • Interlocking of twins • Fetal head trapping above the cervix • Umbilical cord prolapse329 According to ACOG criteria (2019 ), preeclampsia requires proteinuria of grade 2+ or more. In the case of pre-eclampsia , termination of pregnancy must be done at 37 weeks . According to the updated criteria, this patient does not have pre-eclampsia . Hence , a Caesarean section can be done at 38 weeks as for any uncomplicated DCDA twin pregnancy.Type of twin pregnancy Timing of delivery Dichorionic diamniotic 38 weeks Monochorionic diamniotic 34 - 37 weeks + 6 days Monochorionic monoamn iotic - 34 weeks by Caesarean s ection1st twin presentatio n Mode of delive ry Vertex Vaginal Breech Cesarean secti on Transverse Cesarean secti on

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old primigravida with dichorionic diamniotic twins presents to the clinic in active labor. The first twin is delivered vaginally but the second has a transverse lie. A trial of ECV was unsuccessful . What is not a complication of the procedure performed next for the delivery of the second twin?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical procedure is suggestive of internal podalic version for the second twin. Shoulder presentation, and not face presentation, is a complication of this procedure . The complications seen with internal podalic version are as follows : • Maternal- • Failure of the procedure • Uterine rupture • Vaginal and perineal trauma • Placental abruption • Postpartum haemorrhage • Ascending infection • Anaesthetic risks • Fetal - • Cord prolapse • Shoulder presentation with prolapsed arm • Skeletal injury (femur, hips, humerus, skull) • Visceral injury (kidney, liver, spleen )330 • Neural injury (facial nerve) • Hypoxic brain injury • Death331

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Arrange the following sites of ectopic pregnancy from the most common to the least common.
mcqs.explanation: 337 The order of the most common site to the least common site in the fallopian tube for ectopic pregnancy is ampulla>isthmus>fimbriae>interstitium . An ectopic pregnancy is any pregnancy implanted outside of the endometrial cavity. Extrauterine sites : The most common site of ectopic pregnancy is the extrauterine fallopian tube . • Tubal - 97% (most common) • Ampulla - 55 % • Isthmus • Infundibulum • Interstitium • Ovarian • Abdominal Intrauterine ectopic sites : • Cervical • Caesarean scar • Rudimentary horn of a bicornuate uterus • Heterotopic pregnancy

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following factors maximally increases the risk of tubal pregnancy?
mcqs.explanation: Prior tubal surgery for ectopic pregnancy has the highest risk of tubal pregnancy among the given options. Risk factors for ectopic pregnancy: • Prior ectopic pregnancy • Prior tubal surgery for ectopic , recanalization of tube post -sterilization • Pelvic inflammatory disease - most common cause for ectopic pregnancy • Infertility • Artificial reproductive therapy • Endometriosis • Smoking • Maternal age >40 years • Contraceptive methods - intrauterine device , progesterone -only pills

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The fall in which of the following hormone/s leads to endometrial sloughing in ectopic gestation ?
mcqs.explanation: 338 Endometrial sloughing in ectopic gestation is due to the fall in the levels of progesterone and hCG. During normal pregnancy, endometrium is maintained by the high levels of hCG and progesterone. In ectopic pregnancy, a fall in the levels of these hormones will cause endometrial sloughing and uterine bleeding . If the decidua is expelled as a single piece through the cervix, it is called a decidual cast.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which type of tubal pregnancy ruptures at a later stage ?
mcqs.explanation: Interstitial tubal pregnancy ruptures at a later stage i.e. at 12 -16 weeks . This is because pregnancy at this site is closer to the uterine myometrium which provides support as pregnancy progresses . Isthmic and ampullary pregnancies terminate by tubal rupture . However, isthmic pregnancy ruptures earlier. Ampullary and infundibular pregnancy can terminate by tubal abortion as well .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following clinical features is not seen in a patient with ruptured ectopic pregnancy?
mcqs.explanation: A shock index of >0.85 is seen in a case of ruptured ectopic pregnancy. There is massive blood loss (SBP<110 mmHg) sometimes leading to shock. The shock index is calculated as HR/systolic BP. Option A: Sub-diaphragmatic blood irritates the phrenic nerve. This causes a referred pain at the shoulder tip. This is called as Danforth sign. Option B: The expulsion of decidua in a single piece through the cervix is called a decidual cast. This is due to the fall in the levels of \032 hCG and progesterone . Option C: Vertigo and syncope are due to reflex vasomotor disturbances due to peritoneal irritation from hemoperitoneum .Condition Range of shock ind ex Normal value of shock index (non-pregnant) 0.5 - 0.7 Normal value of shock index in pregnancy (i.e) obstetrical shock index 0.7 - 0.8 Significant or massive blood l oss 0.9 - 1.1

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman presented with complaints of amenorrhoea for 6 weeks and a history of prior ectopic pregnancy. Serial serum beta hCG levels were estimated in her. Which of the following findings will increase the suspicion of ectopic gestation in her?

options.a: Low levels with prolonged doubling time
options.b: High levels with decreased doubling time

mcqs.explanation: Low levels of \032 hCG and prolonged doubling time increase the suspicion of ectopic pregnancy.339 Urine pregnancy test is very sensitive and found positive in most ectopic pregnancies . Hence, serial serum \032 hCG levels are estimated to detect ectopic pregnancy. In early normal pregnancy, the doubling time of \032 hCG concentrations in plasma is 1.4 to 2 days.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient presented with 6 weeks of amenorrhoea and a positive UPT. TVS revealed a tubal ectopic pregnancy. Which of the following findings can be usually picked up on colour Doppler ?

options.a: Enhanced blood flow pattern in the uterine artery

mcqs.explanation: Ring of fire pattern is seen on color doppler in a tubal ectopic pregnancy. This is due to placental blood flow in the tubal pregnancy. This finding may also be seen in corpus luteum cysts but the wall is less echogenic compared to tubal ectopic . Option A: There is an enhanced blood flow pattern outside the uterine cavity in case of ectopic pregnancy.Option B: Arias-Stella reaction/phenomenon is a histological finding. It is an atypical endometrial change due to the action of progesterone on the endometrial tissue seen in normal , ectopic, and molar pregnancies . On histology , there are: • large cells with abundant eosinophilic or vacuolated cytoplasm • nuclear enlargement • hyperchromasia340 Option D: Whirlpool sign refers to the twisted ovarian pedicle seen on USG of ovarian torsion.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman came for routine antenatal USG. Which of the following features is suggestive of a pseudogestational sac?
mcqs.explanation: Central location is a feature of the pseudogestational sac seen in ectopic pregnancies . Pseudogestational sac is a collection of fluid between the endometrial layers, surrounded by a thick decidua . Its presence increases the suspicion of ectopic pregnancy. Differences between pseudogestational sac and true gestational sac:Feature Pseudogestational sa c True gestational sa c Location within the endomet rial cavity Central Eccentric Shape Usually ovoid Usually round Fetal and yolk sac poles Absent Present Double ring sign Absent Seen Intradecidual sign Absent Seen

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with suspected tubal pregnancy underwent transvaginal ultrasound which was inconclusive. What is the next step of management?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, the next step would be to confirm the tubal ectopic by measuring serum \032 hCG. This can be used to differentiate tubal ectopic pregnancy from missed abortion and early intrauterine pregnancy.341 If the level is \0312000 IU/L, ectopic pregnancy is suspected . If the level is <1500 IU/L, a repeat serum \032 hCG is taken after 48 hours. If the levels are: • Doubled - early intrauterine pregnancy • Decreased - abortion • Increased but less than doubled value - ectopic pregnancy Investigations for ectopic pregnancy: • Serum \032 hCG - lower levels compared to normal pregnancy, prolonged doubling time • Transvaginal ultrasound - empty uterine cavity, fluid in pouch of Douglas , adnexal mass • Colour Doppler - ring of fire pattern • Laparoscopy • Dilatation and curettage - decidua identified without villi • Serum progesterone • Culdocentesis Diagnostic laparoscopy may be done when the diagnosis is still uncertain after serial \032-hCG monitoring and repeat ultrasonography. In high-risk situations , such as a history of previous ectopic pregnancy, earlier diagnostic laparoscopy is considered .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman is diagnosed with unruptured ectopic gestation . Which of the following is not an indication for expectant management in this patient ?

options.a: Initial serum beta hCG level of 200 mIU/mL

mcqs.explanation: A gestational sac size of <4 cm is an indication of expectant management. Expectant management is done only in the case of unruptured tubal pregnancy. In this, observation is done till there is spontaneous resolution . It can be done but is not preferred due to prolonged follow -up and uncertainty in resolution . The indications are:342 • Initial serum \032 hCG <1500 IU/L • Falling serum \032 hCG levels • Gestational sac size <4 cm • No fetal cardiac activity on TVS • No evidence of rupture or bleeding on TVS

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A primigravida in her first trimester came for a routine ANC. USG findings revealed an empty uterine cavity. Serum beta hCG was measured and was found to be 1700 IU/mL . All of the following drugs can be used in managing this patient except :
mcqs.explanation: Oxytocin is not used in the management of unruptured ectopic pregnancy. Indications for medical management of unruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy: • Hemodynamically stable patient • Serum \032 hCG <5000 IU/L • Tubal diameter <4 cm • No fetal cardiac activity • No intra-abdominal haemorrhage Medical management of unruptured tubal ectopic : • Direct local therapy (laparoscopy or USG guidance ) - • Methotrexate • Potassium chloride • Actinomycin • Hyperosmolar glucose • PGF2�o • Systemic therapy - single dose of methotrexate 50 mg/m2 IM Follow -up after medical management is done by measuring the decline in serial serum \032 hCG.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with unruptured ectopic pregnancy is planned for medical management with methotrexate . What is the multi-dose protocol for this drug?
mcqs.explanation: In the multi-dose protocol , methotrexate is given at a dose of 1 mg/kg as an IM injection on alternate days 1, 3, 5, and 7. This regimen is continued on alternating days until the hCG level drops by 15% over two days. Up to 4 doses may be given. Along with this, leucovorin rescue (folinic acid) is given at 0.1 mg/kg after 24 hrs (on days 2, 4, 6, and 8) to buffer the side effects of methotrexate . Note : If the decline is \03115%, the patient is followed up weekly till the levels fall to <10 IU/L.343 MTX Protocol Multi -dose regimen Single -dose regimen Dose 1 mg/kg(+ 0.1 mg/kg LEU) 50 mg/m2(Body surface area) Regimen Alternate daily doses Day 0 hCG measurement Days 0, 1, 3, 5, Days 0, 4, Treatment success hCG declines >15%from thep revious value hCG declines >15%betweenD ay 4 and 7 When to administer addition al dose 2nd, 3rdor 4thdose to be give n if hCG does not decline 15 % from the previous value. M aximum 4 doses Second dose onDay 7if hCG d oes not decline 15%

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following must be avoided by a patient with tubal pregnancy on methotrexate ?
mcqs.explanation: Sunlight exposure , sexual intercourse and NSAIDs must be avoided when patients are on methotrexate therapy . The following should be avoided when methotrexate therapy has been initiated for the treatment of ectopic gestation : • Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs - can cause reduced renal blood flow and delay drug excretion • Alcohol - can predispose to concurrent hepatic enzyme elevation • Sunlight - may provoke methotrexate-related dermatitis • Sexual intercourse - can rupture the ectopic pregnancy • Phenytoin, tetracyclines , salicylates , and sulfonamides - can increase serum methotrexate levels

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman was brought to the casualty in a drowsy state with complaints of bleeding PV associated with abdominal pain and a history of amenorrhoea for 8 weeks. On examination, BP was 90/60 mmHg, PR was 140 bpm, and UPT was positive . What is the next step of management?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of ruptured ectopic pregnancy which must be immediately managed with simultaneous resuscitation and laparotomy. On laparotomy, salpingectomy is the definitive surgery. Diagnosis of ruptured ectopic pregnancy is made based on clinical features : • Amenorrhoea for 6-8 weeks followed by bleeding PV • Abdominal pain • Hemodynamically unstable • Urine pregnancy test - positive Surgical treatment of ectopic pregnancy includes salpingectomy or salpingostomy , performed either through laparoscopy or laparotomy.344 Management of suspected ruptured ectopic pregnancy consists of initial resuscitation and stabilization, followed by point-of-care ultrasound (FAST) to identify intraperitoneal free fluid and surgical exploration. Laparotomy is done for hemodynamically unstable patients with ruptured ectopic pregnancies . Salpingectomy is the treatment of choice and is done with preservation of the ipsilateral ovary and its vascular supply . For patients wishing to preserve future fertility , if the contralateral fallopian tube is damaged , salpingostomy is preferred . However, salpingostomy may result in inadequate evacuation of the products of conception and a recurrence of symptoms . Therefore, after a patient undergoes salpingostomy , it is important check the \032-hCG level on a weekly basis to ensure that it reaches zero. The image given below shows a laparoscopic visualization of a tubal pregnancy.345

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Match the following criteria used for the diagnosis of ectopic pregnancy:
mcqs.explanation: Spiegelberg 's criteria used for the diagnosis of ovarian pregnancy include intact ipsilateral tube , pregnancy occupying ovary connected by the utero-ovarian ligament . Studdiford 's criteria used for the diagnosis of primary abdominal pregnancy include the presence of normal bilateral tubes and pregnancy related to the peritoneal surface . Rubin's criteria used for the diagnosis of cervical pregnancy includes presence of soft , enlarged cervix and closed internal os and partially opened external os.Ectopic pregnan cy Criteria Abdominal Studdifor d Cervical Rubin Ovarian Spiegelbe rg

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An O-ve primigravida underwent surgery for ectopic pregnancy at 13 weeks of gestation . What will be the dose of anti-D immunoglobulin to be given to her?
mcqs.explanation: Anti-D is given at a dose of 300 �Mg intramuscularly for alloimmunization after surgical management of ectopic pregnancy. The dose of anti-D in a surgically treated case of ectopic is 50 �Mg if gestation <12 weeks . If the gestation is >12 weeks , �Mg of anti-D is given intramuscularly. Anti-D is not given when the ectopic is treated with medical methods .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old female patient (G2P0A1 ) with a history of FSH therapy and in vitro fertilization presented with lower abdominal pain, vomiting, and vaginal discharge . On examination, she was hemodynamically stable . Transvaginal ultrasound showed a viable intrauterine pregnancy of 8 weeks associated with a heterogeneous right adnexal mass showing a positive bagel sign. What is the most appropriate management?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of heterotopic pregnancy. Surgery is the ideal treatment in heterotopic pregnancy. A normal uterine pregnancy co-existing with an extrauterine (ectopic ) pregnancy is termed a heterotopic pregnancy. Although heterotopic pregnancy can occur spontaneously , it is more likely after ART and ovulation induction. Tubal ring sign also referred to as bagel sign is one of the ultrasound signs of a tubal ectopic . It comprises an echogenic ring that surrounds an unruptured ectopic pregnancy. USG image showing bagel sign or tubal ring sign:346 Methotrexate is not to be given as it harms even the normal intrauterine fetus . Although potassium chloride may be injected into the sac of the ectopic , the safer method would be surgery to remove the ectopic .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Methotrexate was administered to a patient with unruptured ectopic pregnancy. At what serum beta hCG levels will this drug be most effective ?
mcqs.explanation: Methotrexate is most effective when given at \032 hCG levels are <5000 IU/L. Methotrexate is given at a dose of 50 mg/m2 of body surface area. Monitoring is done by measuring \032 hCG levels on days 4 and 7. If the decline is \03115% of the initial value, the patient is followed up weekly till the levels fall to <10 IU/L. If the decline is <15%, a 2nd dose of methotrexate is given on day 7.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Studdiford 's criteria is used for the diagnosis of _____________
mcqs.explanation: Studdiford 's criteria is used for the diagnosis of primary abdominal pregnancy. Primary abdominal pregnancy is the rarest type of ectopic gestation . The conceptus implants on the peritoneal surface of the abdomen. Studdiford 's criteria: • The presence of normal bilateral tubes and ovaries with no evidence of recent or past pregnancy. • No evidence of a uteroperitoneal fistula. • The presence of pregnancy, related exclusively to the peritoneal surface , early enough to eliminate the possibility of secondary implantation Criteria used in the diagnosis of ectopic pregnancy are: • Cervical pregnancy: Paalman and McElin (clinical criteria); Rubin's criteria (histological criteria)347 • Ovarian pregnancy: Spiegelberg 's criteria348

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: Abortion is the expulsion of fetus weighing _____.
mcqs.explanation: According to WHO, abortion is defined as pregnancy termination or loss before 20 weeks of gestation or with a fetus weighing <500 g. Some common causes of spontaneous abortion are: • Chromosomal abnormalities • Luteal phase defects • Diabetes mellitus and thyroid disorders • Cervical incompetence • Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome357 • Maternal infections • Alcohol and cigarette smoking

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A patient presented with vaginal bleeding following 6 weeks of amenorrhoea. Her UPT was positive. What is the most common cause of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of first-trimester abortion which is most commonly caused by chromosomal abnormalities. Autosomal trisomies are the most common (50%) genetic abnormality overall. Of these , the most common trisomy involved in abortions is trisomy 16. Turner syndrome (monosomy X) is the single most common chromosomal abnormality in miscarriages. Causes of spontaneous abortion are: • Genetic - • Numerical chromosomal abnormalities • Chromosomal rearrangements • Mendelian etiology • Endocrine - • Luteal phase defects • Thyroid abnormalities • Diabetes mellitus • Anatomical - • Cervical incompetence • Congenital uterine malformations • Uterine fibroid • Uterine synechiae • Infectious (TORCH infections ) • Immunological - • Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome • Autoimmunity • Maternal illness - • Cyanotic heart diseases • Hemoglobinopathies • Environmental - • Radiation exposure • Alcohol • Cigarette smoking358

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A patient presented with a spontaneous abortion at 7 weeks of gestation . Which of the following is the least likely chromosomal abnormality that can lead to this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The least likely chromosomal abnormality involved in first-trimester abortions is trisomy 1. The most common chromosomal abnormality in first trimester abortions is trisomy. The common trisomies are: • Edwards syndrome (Trisomy 18) • Down syndrome (Trisomy 21 ) • Patau syndrome (Trisomy 13 ) • Trisomies 16 and 22 Turner syndrome (Monosomy X) is the single most frequent chromosomal abnormality. It usually results in abortion.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A woman with 6 weeks of amenorrhea had a positive urine pregnancy test . The following finding was seen on transabdominal USG. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given USG image shows an empty gestational sac which is seen in missed abortion before 12 weeks . At this gestational age , the entire ovum is covered by the chorionic villi giving rise to the empty gestational sac. If this condition occurs beyond 12 weeks of gestation , a dead fetus is seen on USG. This is not preceded by any warning signs and the fetus is not expelled outside spontaneously .359

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: You are examining a primigravida with complete abortion. Which of the following findings would you not expect ?

options.a: Uterus smaller than period of amenorrhea

mcqs.explanation: The cervical os is closed in complete abortion.360

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: Recurrent miscarriage is the loss of:
mcqs.explanation: Recurrent miscarriage is defined as \0313 consecutive pregnancy losses at \035 20 weeks or with a fetal weight <500 g. It can be of 2 types : • Primary recurrent miscarriage where there are multiple losses in a woman who has never delivered a liveborn • Secondary recurrent miscarriage where multiple pregnancy losses occur in a patient who has had a prior live birth

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions does not usually cause recurrent miscarriages?
mcqs.explanation: Infections do not usually cause recurrent miscarriages. Common causes of recurrent miscarriage: • Parental chromosomal abnormalities • Anatomical factors - • Uterine synechiae or Asherman syndrome • Uterine leiomyomas • Congenital genital tract anomalies • Immunological factors - • Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome • Endocrine factors - 361 • Luteal phase defect • Polycystic ovarian syndrome

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A primigravida had a spontaneous abortion at 18 weeks . On examination, the fetus was morphologically normal . Further investigations were performed upon the patient 's insistence and the results are given below . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given lab findings are suggestive of anti-phospholipid antibody syndrome(APLS). Criteria for diagnosis of antiphospholipid antibody syndrome: Clinical criteria - • Obstetric • Three or more unexplained consecutive spontaneous abortions before 10 weeks • One or more deaths of a morphologically normal fetus at or beyond 10 weeks • Severe pre-eclampsia necessitating delivery before 34 weeks • Vascular • One or more episodes of arterial, venous, or small vessel thrombosis in any tissue or organ Laboratory criteria - • Presence of lupus anticoagulant • Presence of IgG or IgM anti-cardiolipin antibodies • Presence of IgG or IgM anti-beta-2 glycoprotein I antibodies At least one clinical and one laboratory criteria is needed for the diagnosis. Non-specific tests for lupus anticoagulant are increased aPTT , Kaolin clotting time, and dilute Russell viper venom time.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A woman comes to the casualty at 18 weeks of gestation with complaints of vaginal bleeding . She has a history of two early pregnancy losses . USG reveals the absence of fetal cardiac activity. Which of the following investigations need not be done in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of recurrent abortions, and extensive infection workup is not done. Even though recurrent abortions are defined as \0313 pregnancy losses , investigations must be done after 2 consecutive losses . Diagnostic evaluation of recurrent pregnancy loss based on etiology is given as follows :Etiology Diagnostic evaluation Genetic Parental karyotyping Anatom ic HysterosalpingographyUltras oundSaline -infusion sonogra phy362 Etiology Diagnostic evaluation Endocri ne TSHTesting for insulin resist anceSerum prolactin levelOv arian reserve testingAntithyr oid antibodies Infectio us No evaluation is recommend ed unless the patient has evid ence of chronic endometritis / cervicitis on examination, or is immunocompromised Autoim mune Anticardiolipin antibody level s (IgG and IgM)Lupus antico agulantHomocysteineFactor V LeidenProthrombin promo ter mutationActivated protei n C resistance

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A pregnant lady with a \037history of recurrent abortions is now diagnosed to have antiphospholipid syndrome. What would be the best mode of treatment for her?
mcqs.explanation: The best mode of treatment for a pregnant woman with antiphospholipid syndrome(APS) is aspirin and heparin. APS is a prothrombotic disorder (autoantibody -mediated thrombophilia) affecting both arterial and venous systems . Patients present with recurrent pregnancy loss due to thrombosis of uteroplacental vessels , poor placental perfusion, and prevention of normal decidual changes after zygote implantation. They may also present with preterm delivery, pre-eclampsia , intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), and fetal death . Criteria for APS include : • at least one otherwise unexplained fetal death at or beyond 10 weeks ; • at least one preterm birth before 34 weeks gestation because of eclampsia , severe preeclampsia , placental insufficiency ; or • at least three unexplained consecutive spontaneous abortions before 10 weeks . Aspirin (60-80mg daily) with heparin (5000-10 ,000 U subcutaneously every 12h ) is the most effective therapy for APS. Treating APS with only aspirin (option A) is not recommended as heparin is crucial in preventing thrombus formation at the decidual -thrombotic interface , Corticosteroids (option C, D) should not be used in primary APS (without an associated connective tissue disorder) but are indicated in patients with pre-existing systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and APS (secondary APS).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A G3A3 patient was admitted to the hospital with catastrophic APLS following a spontaneous abortion. Which of the following is false about this condition?

options.a: It is a rapidly progressive thromboembolic disorder
options.b: At least 2 organ systems should be involved to make a diagnosis
options.c: Infections can act as a trigger
options.d: IVIG can be used for treatment

mcqs.explanation: 363 Catastrophic antiphospholipid antibody syndrome (CAPS) is a complication of APLA syndrome, in which \0313 organ systems are involved. It is also known as Asherson syndrome. It is seen in both primary and secondary APLA syndrome. Triggering factors include infections , trauma, and obstetric causes . IVIG can be used in CAPS when the first-line therapies with aspirin and heparin have failed . Note : Asherman syndrome is an acquired condition characterised by formation of intrauterine adhesions or synechiae .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: Which of the following features can be seen in a patient with cervical incompetence ?

options.c: Repeated third trimester painless cervical dilatation
options.d: Bleeding per vaginum in the first trimester

mcqs.explanation: Cervical incompetence or insufficiency is characterized by repeated mid-trimester painless cervical dilatation. Escape of amniotic fluid followed by painless expulsion of products of conception can also be seen . Risk factors for cervical incompetence : • Congenital uterine anomalies • Acquired - • Dilatation and currettage • Dilatation and evacuation • Vaginal operative delivery through an undilated cervix • Amputation of cervix • Multiple gestations • Prior preterm birth

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: Which of the following increase the risk of developing cervical incompetence ?
mcqs.explanation: In -utero exposure to DES, twin pregnancy, and bicornuate uterus increase the risk of cervical incompetence. Offsprings born to pregnant mothers who were treated with diethylstilbestrol may develop cervical hypoplasia and malformation. They may also present with cervical incompetence during their 2nd trimester. Cervical incompetence can be seen following MTP with surgical methods and not with medical methods . The retentive power of the internal os may be compromised by anatomical abnormalities like bicornuate uterus and overdistended uterus due to twin gestations . Risk factors for cervical incompetence : • Congenital uterine anomalies • Acquired -364 • Dilatation and currettage • Induced abortion by dilatation and evacuation • Vaginal operative delivery through an undilated cervix • Amputation of cervix • Multiple gestations • Prior preterm birth

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: The transvaginal ultrasound of a pregnant woman is given below . What are the cutoff values of the parameters marked A and B for a diagnosis of cervical incompetence ?
mcqs.explanation: In the given image, the parameter marked A is funnelling of the internal os and the parameter marked B is cervical length . Funnelling of internal os and cervical length <25 mm are diagnostic of cervical incompetence on transvaginal ultrasound.365

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old woman presents with 6 weeks of amenorrhea and a positive UPT. Her past obstetric history was significant for 2 mid-trimester abortions. On USG, cervical length was 20 mm and no bulging membranes were seen . What is the next step in her management?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of cervical incompetence . It can be managed with prophylactic cervical cerclage done between 12 and 14 weeks of gestation . Rescue or emergency cerclage is done anytime within 24 weeks of gestation . It should only be done when there is bulging of membranes through the dilated cervix. Investigations for cervical incompetence: • In interconceptional period - • Passage of number 6 - 8 Hegar's dilator beyond the internal os without resistance or pain • Funnel-shaped shadow in premenstrual hysterocervicography • During pregnancy - • Per speculum examination showing cervical dilatation with herniation of membranes • USG revealing cervical length <2.5 cm and funnelling of internal os >1 cm

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A patient with cervical insufficiency is posted for McDonald's procedure . Which of the following is not a contraindication for this surgery?
mcqs.explanation: McDonald's procedure is a type of cervical cerclage . It can be done up to 24 weeks of gestation . Contraindications to cervical cerclage are: • Absolute • >24 weeks of gestation • Active labour • Active vaginal bleeding • Abruptio placenta • Premature rupture of membranes • Chorioamnionitis • Severe uterine irritability • Fetal death or defect • Relative366 • Prolapsed membranes • Vaginal spotting

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A woman with cervical incompetence is posted for prophylactic McDonald's cerclage . Which of the following statements is false about this procedure ?

options.a: Removal of stitch must be done by 37th week
options.b: A mersilene tape is tied around the cervix
options.c: Done at the level of internal os

mcqs.explanation: In McDonald's cerclage , a nonabsorbable suture , such as Mersilene , is placed as a purse -string suture as high as possible at the level of the internal os, positioned at the junction where the rugose vaginal epithelium transitions to the smooth vaginal portion of the cervix, below the bladder . Another cerclage procedure is Modified Shirodker's technique . In this, a non-absorbable (mersilene ) tape is passed subcutaneously through a transverse anterior incision and is tied posteriorly . Removal of cerclage should be done by 37 weeks of gestation . It can be removed earlier in case of preterm labour. Complications of cervical cerclage : • Slipping of suture • Chorioamnionitis • Rupture of membranes • Abortion or preterm labour • Cervical laceration or scarring

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A 20 -year-old female patient came for medical termination of pregnancy. From whom will you obtain consent for the procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: 367 Only the patient 's consent is required for medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) and her male partner's consent is not required. Consent of parent/guardian is needed if the age of the patient is <18 yrs or if the patient is mentally ill.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A patient with contraceptive failure requires MTP at 5 weeks of gestation . You plan to use a medical method of abortion in her case. Which of the following is not a contraindication for this?
mcqs.explanation: Chronic diabetes mellitus is not a contraindication to medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) with medical methods . Contraindications to medical methods of abortion are: • Women with in situ intrauterine device • Severe anemia, coagulopathy , or anticoagulant use • Long term corticosteroid therapy • Severe liver, renal, pulmonary, or cardiovascular disease • Inherited porphyria • Uncontrolled hypertension Contraindications to surgical methods of abortion are: • Suction and evacuation - uterine size >10 weeks • Intrauterine instillation of hypertonic solution - cardiovascular or renal lesion and severe anaemia

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old pregnant rape victim was posted for a suction and evacuation procedure . This procedure can be done up to _____ of gestation .
mcqs.explanation: Suction and evacuation can be done up to 12 weeks of gestation . It is a method of termination of pregnancy in the first-trimester. The various methods of termination of pregnancy are:Timing Medical methods Surgical methods 1st trimester(up to 12 weeks ) MifepristoneMifepristone an d MisoprostolMethotrexate a nd MisoprostolTamoxifen an d Misoprostol Menstrual regulationVacuum aspiration (MVA/EVA)Suctio n evacuation and/or curettag eDilatation and evacuation - Rapid methodSlow method 2nd trimester(13 - 20 weeks ) MisoprostolDinoprostoneCar boprost Dilatation and evacuationIntr auterine instillation of hyper osmotic solutionsOxytocin in fusionHysterotomy368

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: You have performed MTP on a multigravida at 10 weeks of gestation . As a part of post -op advice, you must prescribe her a prophylactic antibiotic. Which of the following drugs would you prefer ?
mcqs.explanation: Doxycycline is the preferred drug for post -abortal antibiotic prophylaxis in this case. Oral doxycycline 100 mg is given 1 hour before surgical evacuation. 200 mg is given after the procedure is complete . The best method of MTP at 7-12 weeks is by suction and evacuation. Following this procedure , antibiotic prophylaxis is given with doxycycline .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: You are about to administer misoprostol to a woman who requires MTP in the 8th week of her pregnancy. What is the dose of this drug when given by the mucosal route, according to WHO guidelines ?
mcqs.explanation: Misoprostol is given at a dose of 800 mcg by mucosal route for MTP. Mucosal misoprostol administration has increased efficacy and minimizes gastrointestinal side effects . Hence , it is preferred over oral administration. WHO guidelines for medical management in induced abortion for <12 weeks of gestation : • Combined regimen (recommended ): 200 mg of oral Mifepristone followed 1-2 days later by 800 mcg of buccal, vaginal, or sublingual misoprostol • Misoprostol only regimen (alternative): �Mg misoprostol administered vaginally, sublingually , or buccally

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the methods of MTP?

options.a: Pain is more in medical methods of abortion
options.b: Incomplete abortion is more common in medical methods
options.c: Bleeding is prolonged in surgical methods
options.d: Failure rate is low in surgical methods of abortion

mcqs.explanation: Bleeding is prolonged and unpredictable in medical methods of abortion. Comparison of drawbacks of medical and surgical methods of MTP:Factor Medical methods Surgical methods Invasiveness Usually not invasive Invasive Pain More Less Vaginal bleeding Prolonged, unpredictable Light, predictable Incomplete aborti on More common Uncommon Failure rate 2-5% 1% Severe bleeding 0.1% 0.1% Infection rate Low Low Anesthesia Usually not given Always given Time involved Multiple visits for follow -up Usually one visitNo follow -up s required369

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A 21 -year-old woman is brought in a drowsy state from a PHC with complaints of fever, severe lower abdominal pain, and purulent vaginal discharge . Her mother revealed that she had had an unsafe abortion a week ago. On examination, her abdomen was distended , BP was 80/60 mmHg, PR was 140 bpm, and RR was 36 breaths/ minute. Which of the following is not a causative agent of her present condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of toxic shock syndrome (TSS) following septic abortion. Escherichia coli can be detected in septic abortion, but it is not a causative agent for TSS. Organisms causing toxic shock syndrome in septic abortion: • Streptococcus pyogenes • Clostridium perfringens • Clostridium sordellii Clinical features of septic abortion: • Fever with chills and rigors • Abdominal or chest pain • Diarrhoea and vomiting • Renal angle tenderness • Offensive purulent vaginal discharge. Clinical grading of septic abortion: • Grade I - infection localized in the uterus • Grade II - infection spreads to parametrium, tubes , ovaries, or pelvic peritoneum • Grade III - generalized peritonitis , endotoxic shock, jaundice , or acute renal failure Empirical antibiotic therapy in septic abortion is started for the broadest microbial coverage. Piperacillin-tazobactam or carbapenem and clindamycin are given intravenously. Antibiotics can be changed once culture sensitivity reports are available.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a risk factor for stillbirth?

options.b: Illicit drug abuse by the mother

mcqs.explanation: An untreated seizure disorder in pregnancy is not a risk factor for stillbirth. However, the use of certain anti-epileptic drugs like valproate could lead to the development of neural tube defects in the baby. Recent studies haven't consistently shown that untreated women with epilepsy face a higher risk , though it's hard to rule out entirely because those who manage without medication usually have milder symptoms . Recent research found that birth defects were more common in children of women who used anticonvulsants. Risk factors for stillbirth are: • Advanced maternal age • African-American race • Smoking • Illicit drug use370 • Maternal medical diseases - overt diabetes or chronic hypertension • Assisted reproductive technology • Nulliparity • Obesity • Previous adverse pregnancy outcomes - prior preterm birth or IUGR Note : Stillbirth rates appear to be slightly increased in pregnancies conceived via assisted reproductive technology .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A young female has history of a spontaneous abortion. She has had amenorrhea since then. Her FSH now is 6 mIU/ml. Which of the following can be a cause for her amenorrhea?
mcqs.explanation: The development of uterine synechiae is the most likely cause of amenorrhoea in the given clinical scenario. Certain types of spontaneous abortions such as inevitable, incomplete and missed abortions might require medical assistance for complete removal of products of conception including procedures such as dilatation and curettage . Vigorous uterine curettage in early pregnancy damages the basal layer of endometrium leading to scarring and adhesions in the uterus that interferes with normal endometrial growth and shedding .This causes the clinical feature of secondary amenorrhea as seen in this patient . This intrauterine adhesions are known as uterine synechiae or Asherman syndrome. As there is no defect in the hypothalamo-pituitary-ovarian axis in the asherman syndrome, the levels of FSH remain within the normal range of 4 - 25 IU/L as seen in this patient . In the case of Pituitary dysfunction (option A) the FSH levels are usually decreased . In ovarian dysfunction (option B) the negative feedback of ovarian hormones (estrogen ) on pitutary and hypothalamus is lost. Hence, the levels of FSH is increased (\031 25 IU). Asherman syndrome is characterised by a spectrum of intra uterine scarring including thin adhesions , dense bands, or complete obliteration of the uterine cavity. It occurs due to endometrial damage following vigorous curettage , usually in miscarriage, or elective abortion. Damage may also occur from other uterine surgeries such as myomectomy or cesarean delivery or from an infection related to an intrauterine device . Depending on the degree of scarring, patients may present with amenorrhea, hypomenorrhea or recurrent pregnancy loss due to inadequate placentation . Asherman syndrome shows multiple filling defects on hysterosalpingography (HSG) or saline-infusion sonography. Definitive diagnosis requires hysteroscopy . Hysteroscopic lysis of adhesions is the preferred surgical treatment for the syndrome.371

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Antepartum hemorrhage is defined as bleeding from the genital tract after ____.
mcqs.explanation: Antepartum haemorrhage (APH) is defined as bleeding from or into the genital tract after 28 weeks of gestation up to the delivery of the baby. The lower limit is the period of viability and the upper limit includes the 1st and 2nd stages of labour. Causes of APH: • Placental causes : • Abruptio placenta (most common) • Placenta previa (2nd most common) • Circumvallate placenta • Circummarginate placenta • Fetal causes : • Vasa previa • Extraplacental causes (local cervicovaginal lesions ): • Local trauma • Varicose veins • Cervical polyp379 • Carcinoma cervix. Note : According to RCOG criteria, the lower limit for APH is 24 weeks . However, in India, the period of viability is 28 weeks , so it is taken as the lower limit for APH.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of antepartum haemorrhage?
mcqs.explanation: Abruptio placenta is the most common cause of antepartum haemorrhage (APH). Placental abruption or abruptio placenta is the premature separation of a normally situated placenta. The bleeding can be revealed , concealed or mixed type . Causes of APH: • Placental causes : • Abruptio placenta (most common) • Placenta previa (2nd most common) • Circumvallate placenta • Circummarginate placenta • Fetal causes : • Vasa previa • Extraplacental causes (local cervicovaginal lesions ): • Local trauma • Varicose veins • Cervical polyp • Carcinoma cervix.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Transvaginal ultrasound findings in a multiparous woman revealed a low lying placenta . What does this mean?

options.a: Placental edge within 2 cm from the internal os
options.b: Placental edge within 3 cm from the internal os
options.c: Placental edge within 4 cm from the internal os

mcqs.explanation: In low lying placenta , the edge of the placenta lies within 2 cm from the internal os but does not cover the internal os. Placenta previa is a condition where the placenta is implanted over the lower uterine segment (partially or completely ). ACOG classification of placenta previa: • True placenta previa - placenta covers the internal os partially or completely • Low lying placenta - placenta does not cover the internal os but the edge is within 2 cm of the internal os380

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following types are included in the major degrees of placenta previa?
mcqs.explanation: Major degree of placenta previa includes posterior marginal, partial and complete central. Clinical classification of placenta previa: • Mild degree • Type I or lateral or low lying • Type II anterior or anterior marginal • Major degree • Type II posterior or posterior marginal or dangerous placenta previa • Type III or partial central • Type IV or complete Older (Browne's) classification of placenta previa:Type Position Definition Type I Lateral The placenta dips into the lo wer segment but does not rea ch up to the os Type II Marginal The placental edge reaches th e os Type III Incomplete or partial central The placenta partially covers the internal os Type IV Complete or central The placenta completely cove rs the internal os

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old multiparous woman presented at 32 weeks of gestation with complaints of recurrent painless vaginal bleeding . On examination, fundal height corresponded to gestational age and fetal heart rate was 140 bpm. Which of the following is not a risk factor for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: 381 The given clinical scenario is suggestive of placenta previa. Pre-eclampsia is a risk factor for abruptio placenta, not placenta previa. Painless bleeding PV , fundal height proportional to gestational age and presence of FHS are the differentiating features of placenta previa from abruptio placenta . Risk factors for placenta previa are: • Demographic factors • Maternal age >35 years • Multiparity • Cigarette smoking • Clinical factors • Prior caesarean section • Past history of placenta previa • Artificial reproductive technology • Multifetal pregnancy • Succenturiate lobe .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Per speculum examination findings in a pregnant woman with vaginal bleeding showed placenta protruding through the cervical os. What is the type of placenta previa in this case?
mcqs.explanation: Placenta protruding through the internal os on per speculum examination indicates complete placenta previa or type IV placenta previa. Older (Browne's) classification of placenta previa: Cervical digital examination must only be done in suspected cases of placenta previa in an operation theater with provisions for cesarean section kept ready.Type Position Definition Type I Lateral The placenta dips into the lo wer segment but does not rea ch up to the os Type II Marginal The placental edge reaches th e os Type III Incomplete or partial central The placenta partially covers the internal os Type IV Complete or central The placenta completely cove rs the internal os382

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient at 34 weeks of gestation presented with placenta previa. Which of the following is false about this condition?

options.a: Painful recurrent vaginal bleeding is seen
options.b: The size of the uterus corresponds to gestational age

mcqs.explanation: Painless recurrent vaginal bleeding is seen in placenta previa. Clinical features of placenta previa: • Bleeding per vaginum - sudden onset , painless , recurrent, bright red in colour, sometimes a history of warning haemorrhage is present • Uterus - relaxed , soft , no tenderness , size proportional to the period of gestation • Floating head i.e., persistent displacement of fetal head as it cannot be pushed down into the pelvis • Fetal heart sound - present • Stallworthy sign - seen in low lying placenta , especially the posterior type . Slowing of fetal heart rate (FHR) on pressing the head down into the pelvis, which recovers promptly as pressure is relieved , is called Stallworthy sign.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Abdominal examination during a routine antenatal checkup gave a positive Stallworthy sign. What could be the most probable cause ?
mcqs.explanation: Stallworthy sign is observed in posterior placenta previa. The slowing of fetal heart rate on pressing the head down into the pelvis, which recovers promptly when the pressure is relieved , is called Stallworthy sign. Note : This sign is not always significant as this could also occur in normal pregnancies due to fetal head compression.383

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G2P1 woman presents to the casualty at 30 weeks with a history of self -limiting painless bleeding PV 3 hours ago. On examination, BP - 110 /70 mmHg and PR - 80 bpm. What is the next best step in management?

options.a: Transvaginal ultrasound to confirm the diagnosis
options.b: Start injection corticosteroids for fetal lung maturity

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of antepartum haemorrhage (APH) due to placenta previa (painless bleeding PV ). The next step in the management is to confirm the diagnosis with transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) as the patient is stable . Transabdominal ultrasound (TAS) is used to detect the cause of APH. If the placenta is in the lower uterine segment on TAS, confirmation of placenta previa is done by TVS. TVS provides a clearer image of the relationship between the edge of the placenta and the internal cervical os than TAS. Approach to placenta previa after confirmation with TVS : • Minor placenta previa - repeat USG at 36 weeks • Major placenta previa or accreta - USG at 32 weeks followed by elective caesarean delivery • Bleeding present - individual management On TAS, if the placenta is in the upper uterine segment with evidence of retroplacental blood clot, abruptio placenta is suspected . Per vaginal examination in placenta previa must not be done as it may further separate the placenta and cause excessive bleeding . However, transvaginal ultrasound is safe as long as the probe is 2-3 cm away from the cervix.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G2P1L1 woman at 30 weeks of gestation was rushed to the casualty with complaints of painless vaginal bleeding . She had woken up to find herself in a pool of blood. On examination, her vitals were unstable . Active bleeding per vaginum was present . Which of the following complications would not be anticipated in her?
mcqs.explanation: Then given clinical scenario is suggestive of placenta previa and precipitate labour is not a complication. Precipitate labour is seen in abruptio placenta and uterine tachysystole . Vaginal bleeding in placenta previa is sudden in onset , recurrent, painless , unrelated to activity, and often occurs during sleep . Complications of placenta previa: Maternal complications : Fetal complications : • Low birth weight • Asphyxia • Intrauterine death • Birth injuries • Congenital malformations.Period Complication Antepart um Antepartum haemorrhageMa lpresentationPreterm labour384 Period Complication Intrapart um Early rupture of membranesS low dilatation of cervix Postpart um Postpartum haemorrhage Puerperi um SepsisSubinvolution

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Transvaginal ultrasound in a multiparous woman at 32 weeks confirmed placenta previa. Her vitals are stable and there is no active bleeding PV . What is the next step in management?

options.c: Manage as per McAfee and Johnson method
options.d: Manage as per Sher and Page grading

mcqs.explanation: In the given clinical scenario, the next best step of management is conservative management till 37 weeks i.e., McAfee and Johnson's regimen. The aim of conservative management is to continue the pregnancy for fetal maturity without compromising maternal health . Prerequisites : • Blood for transfusion • Facilities for cesarean section Selection of cases for expectant management for placenta previa: • Mother is hemodynamically stable (Hb >10 g% and/or hematocrit > 30%) • Duration of pregnancy <37 weeks • No active vaginal bleeding • Fetus reactive on cardiotocography and no congenital anomalies on USG Conduct of expectant treatment : • Corticosteroids for fetal lung maturity • Bed rest or pelvic rest • Periodic monitoring of mother for bleeding PV • Fetal surveillance with USG • Tocolytics if contractions are present • Anti-D to all Rh-negative unsensitized women Option A: Immediate caesarean section after resuscitation is done if the patient is unstable . Option B: Vaginal delivery is considered when the edge of the placenta is >2 cm away from the internal os. Option D: Sher and Page grading is for abruptio placenta .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Suitable cases for expectant management in case of placenta previa include all except :
mcqs.explanation: 385 The duration of pregnancy must be less than 37 weeks for expectant management which was advocated by McAfee and Johnson. The aim of conservative management is to continue the pregnancy for fetal maturity without compromising maternal health . Prerequisites : • Availability of blood for transfusion • Facilities for cesarean section available Selection of cases for expectant management for placenta previa: • Mother is hemodynamically stable (Hb >10 g% and/or hematocrit > 30%) • Duration of pregnancy <37 weeks • No active vaginal bleeding • Fetus normal on USG and reactive on CTG Conduct of expectant treatment : • Corticosteroids for fetal lung maturity • Bed rest or pelvic rest • Periodic monitoring of mother for bleeding pv • Fetal surveillance with USG • Tocolytics if contractions are present • Anti-D to all Rh-negative (unsensitized) women.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of consumptive coagulopathy in obstetrics ?
mcqs.explanation: Placental abruption is the most common cause of severe consumptive coagulopathy in obstetrics . Consumptive coagulopathy , also known as disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), is a pathologic disruption of hemostasis . It is characterized by systemic activation of blood coagulation , which results in thrombosis and fibrin deposition in the small blood vessels throughout the body. Other causes of DIC in pregnancy: • Amniotic fluid embolism • Sepsis • Preeclampsia and HELLP syndrome • Acute fatty liver of pregnancy • Postpartum haemorrhage.386

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not increase the risk of placental abruption?
mcqs.explanation: Post term pregnancy does not increase the risk of abruptio placenta . Risk factors for placental abruption: • Prior abruption • Increased age and parity • Pre-eclampsia and chronic hypertension • Chorioamnionitis • Preterm ruptured membranes • Multifetal gestation • Cocaine use • Cigarette smoking • Uterine leiomyomas • Single umbilical artery.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following clinical features can be seen in a patient presenting with accidental haemorrhage?
mcqs.explanation: Abruptio placenta is also known as accidental haemorrhage or premature separation of placenta . Tender uterus is seen in abruptio placenta. Abruptio placenta is defined as premature separation of a normally situated placenta . It is of the following types : • Concealed • Revealed • Mixed Clinical features of abruptio placenta : In mixed type , features of concealed variety will be predominant.Features Revealed Concealed General conditi on Proportionate to visible bloo d loss Shock may be pronounced w hich may be out of proportio n to visible bleeding . Symptoms Abdominal discomfort or pai n followed by bleeding Abdominal acute intense pai nNo or minimal bleeding Uterine height Proportionate to the period o f gestation Maybe disproportionately enl arged FHS Usually present Usually absent387

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A multiparous woman at 34 weeks of gestation presented with bleeding per vaginum and was diagnosed to have grade 2 abruptio placenta . Which of the following features may be seen in her?
mcqs.explanation: Grade 2 abruptio placenta is characterized by fetal distress . Sher and Page clinical classification of placental abruption: Grade 0 of abruptio placenta is seen in an asymptomatic patient , where a retroplacental clot is observed only after delivery of placenta .Feature Grade 1 Grade 2 Grade 3 Vaginal bleeding Slight Mild to moderate Moderate to severe or concea led type Uterine tenderness Minimal Present Marked Maternal BP and pulse rat e Unaffect ed BP maintainedPulse rate incr eased Hypovolemic shockAnuria Fetal condition FHS go od Fetal distress Fetal death Maternal fibrinogen Unaffect ed Decreased Coagulation defect

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old primigravida at 32 weeks of gestation presents to the labour room with lower abdominal pain. Her vitals are BP - 90/60 mmHg and PR - 120 bpm. Fetal distress was noted and she was taken up for a caesarean section . The uterus appears as shown below . Which of the following is true regarding this condition?

options.a: It is seen in revealed abruptio placenta
options.b: It is an indication for hysterectomy
options.c: It is a case of uteroplacental apoplexy

mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a couvelaire uterus or uteroplacental apoplexy which is seen in severe forms of concealed abruptio placenta . There is massive extravasation of blood into the uterine musculature up to the serosa. Thus, the uterus has a port wine colour, which can be patchy or diffuse . They can also extend to the broad ligament , ovaries and peritoneal cavity. It is usually observed during caesarean section . It is not an indication of hysterectomy .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Colour doppler studies in a patient with velamentous cord insertion revealed fetal vessels which were overlying the cervical os. Which of the following is false regarding her condition?

options.b: Bleeding is triggered by membrane rupture
options.c: Bleeding is managed by category I caesarian section

mcqs.explanation: The doppler findings are suggestive of vasa previa. Maternal mortality is not seen in vasa previa, but fetal mortality is seen . Vasa previa is a condition where fetal vessels travel within the membranes and overlie the cervical os. Hence , there can be bleeding during cervical dilatation or membrane rupture . Fetal mortality is high and is due to fetal exsanguination.388 Investigations of vasa previa: • Colour flow Doppler (TVS ) • Singer's alkali denaturation test - to detect nucleated red blood cells • Apt test (alkali denaturation test ) - to detect fetal haemoglobin Management of vasa previa: • No bleeding • 28-32 weeks - antenatal corticosteroids • 30-34 weeks - admission for surveillance • \03137 weeks - elective caesarean section • Bleeding present • Category I emergency caesarean section is done (immediate threat to the life of mother or fetus and decision delivery interval <30 mins)

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Sample from a patient with bleeding PV at 30 weeks showed a positive Apt test . What is the most probable cause ?
mcqs.explanation: Apt test is an alkali denaturation test to detect fetal haemoglobin (HbF). It is positive in vasa previa and Rh incompatibility . Apt test is based on the principle that HbF is resistant to alkali denaturation, while HbA is not. It is done by taking the blood sample in a test tube containing water and adding 10 % NaOH. Maternal blood turns yellow -brown, while fetal blood remains pink in the test tube . Bleeding due to vasa previa must be managed immediately with an emergency caesarean section . Hence , Apt test is not practically done in all cases . Other options : Bleeding due to cervical polyp , placenta previa, and abruptio placenta is of maternal origin. So, Apt test will be negative in these cases .389

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following investigations can be used in the antenatal diagnosis of vasa previa in a patient with no history of bleeding PV ?
mcqs.explanation: The antenatal diagnosis of vasa previa can be done by colour doppler . Vasa previa is a condition where fetal vessels travel within the membranes and overlie the cervical os. Hence , there can be bleeding during cervical dilatation or membrane rupture . Fetal mortality is high due to fetal exsanguination. Investigations of vasa previa: • Colour flow Doppler (TVS ) • Singer's alkali denaturation test - to detect nucleated red blood cells • Apt test - to detect fetal haemoglobin Management of vasa previa: • No bleeding • 28-32 weeks - antenatal corticosteroids • 30-34 weeks - admission for surveillance • \03137 weeks - elective caesarean section • Bleeding present • Emergency caesarean section done by category I Options A and B: Colour Doppler is superior to MRI and TAS in the antenatal diagnosis of vasa previa. Option D: Singer's alkali denaturation test to detect fetal RBCs can be used in intrapartum diagnosis of vasa previa (as there might be bleeding ).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A multiparous woman at term presents to the labour room with bleeding per vaginum and ruptured membranes. NST shows fetal distress and sinusoidal heart rate pattern. How will you manage this patient ?

options.a: Rapid induction and delivery by vacuum
options.b: Rapid induction and delivery by forceps
options.d: Adopt Vagos method and rapid vaginal delivery

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of vasa previa since bleeding is associated with fetal distress and sinusoidal pattern in NST. Actively bleeding vasa previa in a term gestation is managed by immediate LSCS. Sinusoidal pattern in CTG is a regular, smooth, undulating signal resembling a sine wave. It can be seen in conditions associated with severe fetal anemia like: • Anti-D allo-immunisation • Fetal -maternal haemorrhage • Twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome • Ruptured vasa previa • Acute fetal hypoxia • Infection390 • Cardiac malformations • Hydrocephalus • Gastroschisis Sinusoidal pattern on CTG:Management of vasa previa: • No bleeding • 28-32 weeks - antenatal corticosteroids • 30-34 weeks - admission for surveillance • \03137 weeks - elective caesarean section • Bleeding present • Emergency caesarean section Note : Vagos method is used in the management of umbilical cord prolapse .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The classical triad of amniotic fluid embolism includes all except _____.
mcqs.explanation: The classical triad of amniotic fluid embolism does not include metabolic acidosis. Classical triad of amniotic fluid embolism: • Hypotension • Hypoxia • DIC Conditions predisposing to the development of amniotic fluid embolism: • Rapid labour391 • Meconium -stained amniotic fluid • Tears in uterine and other large pelvic veins • Older maternal age • Post-term pregnancy • Labour induction or augmentation • Eclampsia • Cesarean/forceps /vacuum delivery • Placental abruption/placenta previa • Polyhydramnios.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G2P1L1 woman presented with placental abruption and was delivered by normal vaginal delivery. The next day, she develops petechiae , cold extremities , and her BP drops to 90/60 mmHg. Her blood reports show increased FDP, D-dimer, and decreased platelets . Which of the following is not used in the management of her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). Epsilon-aminocaproic acid and tranexamic acid are not used in the treatment of DIC. Evaluation and management of DIC: • Vigorous restoration and maintenance of circulation to treat hypotension • Crystalloids and colloids to treat hypotension • Whole blood and packed cells • Fresh frozen plasma - contains fibrinogen, antithrombin III , factors V, XI, XII • Cryoprecipitate - contains fibrinogen, factor VIII , von Willebrand's factor, factor XIII • Platelet replacement if low • Identification of the cause : • Abruptio placenta • PPH • HELLP syndrome • Amniotic fluid embolism • Sepsis • Acute fatty liver • Assess the fetal condition and plan for termination of pregnancy.392

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In a patient who has completed the 3rd stage of labor following vaginal delivery , what is the minimum amount of blood loss required for her to be diagnosed with postpartum hemorrhage?
mcqs.explanation: Postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) in vaginal delivery is defined as a blood loss of more than 500 ml after completion of the third stage of labour. In Caesarean section , blood loss of more than 1000 mL from the genital tract is called PPH. Depending upon the amount of blood loss, PPH can be: • Minor (<1L ) • Major (>1L) • Severe (>2L) In most cases , the magnitude of haemorrhage cannot be assessed accurately as visual estimates are unreliable . Note : as per the latest ACOG guidelines, PPH is defined as cumulative blood loss \0311000 mL or bleeding associated with hypovolaemia in the first 24 hours after birth, irrespective of the route of delivery . It is added that despite the new definition , blood loss >500 mL in a vaginal delivery should raise suspicion and mandates further evaluation.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A grand multipara had continuous , moderate vaginal bleeding immediately after delivery . What could be the most probable cause of bleeding in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Uterine atony is the most common cause of postpartum haemorrhage in a grand multipara.400 Uterine atony is the failure of the uterus to contract sufficiently after delivery . Contraction helps to arrest bleeding from vessels at the placental implantation site . Types of PPH: • Primary /early: Haemorrhage occurring within 24 hours of childbirth. Uterine atony is the most common cause of primary PPH. • Secondary/late : Hemorrhage occurring after 24 hours and up to 12 weeks postpartum . Retained placenta is the most common cause . The risk factors for atonic uterus include : • Primiparity or grand multiparity • Previous PPH • Overdistended uterus as in multiple pregnancies , hydramnios, macrosomia • Precipitate labour • Prolonged labour • Uterine malformations • Uterine fibroid • Induction of labour with prostaglandins or oxytocin • Placental abnormalities like placenta previa, accreta, increta, percreta , or abruptio placenta • Obesity • Age >40 years Note : Uterine inversion occurs rarely and causes secondary PPH.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most probable cause of bleeding per vaginum occurring 24 hours after delivery?
mcqs.explanation: Retained cotyledon is the most probable cause of late or secondary PPH i.e., bleeding that occurs after 24 hours of delivery . Other options are causes of early PPH. Types of PPH include : Primary /early: Haemorrhage occurring within 24 hours of childbirth. The causes are: (mnemonic 4T) • Tone: Atonic PPH (80%) • Trauma : Traumatic PPH • Thrombin : Coagulopathy • Tissue: retained products of conception Risk Factors for primary PPH: Atonic PPH:401 • Primiparity or grand multiparity • Previous PPH • Overdistended uterus as in multiple pregnancy, hydramnios, macrosomia • Precipitate labour • Prolonged labour • Uterine malformations • Uterine fibroid • Induction of labour with prostaglandins or oxytocin • Placental abnormalities like placenta previa/accreta/increta/percreta /abruptio placenta • Obesity • Age >40 years Traumatic PPH: • Instrumental delivery • Episiotomy • Precipitate labour • Macrosomia Coagulopathy : • Sepsis • IUD • HELLP syndrome Secondary/ late PPH: Hemorrhage occurring after 24 hours and up to 12 weeks postpartum . Causes include : • Retained parts of cotyledon or membranes • Endometritis • Abnormal involution of placental site • Secondary haemorrhage from caesarean section wound • Placental polyp • Infected fibroid • Uterine AV fistula • Puerperal uterine inversion • Carcinoma cervix.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a cause of secondary PPH?
mcqs.explanation: 402 Placenta previa does not cause secondary postpartum hemorrhage. It causes primary postpartum hemorrhage. Types of PPH: Primary /early: Hemorrhage occurring within 24 hours of childbirth. Secondary/ late : Hemorrhage occurring after 24 hours and up to 12 weeks postpartum . Causes and risk factors for PPH: The image below shows the prevention and management of PPH:Primary PPH Secondary PPH Atonic PPH Traumatic PPH Coagulopath y Primiparity or grand multipa rity Instrumental deliver y Sepsis Retained bits of cotyledon or membranes Placental abnormalities like p lacenta previa/accreta/increta /percreta /abruptio placenta Precipitate labour HELLP synd rome Secondary haemorrhage fro m Caesarean section wound Overdistended uterus as in m ulti -gestational pregnancy, hy dramnios, macrosomia Macrosomia IUD Puerperal uterine inversion Induction of labour with pros taglandins or oxytocin Episiotomy Abnormal involution of place ntal site Prolonged labour Infected fibroid Precipitate labour Endometritis Previous h/o PPH Placental polyp Obesity Carcinoma of cervix Age >40 years Uterine av fistula403

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following complications during pregnancy does not increase the risk of PPH?
mcqs.explanation: Oligohydramnios does not increase the risk of PPH. However, polyhydramnios can increase the risk by causing uterine atony, due to an overdistended uterus . Risk factors for primary PPH: Atonic PPH: • Primiparity or grand multiparity • Previous PPH • Overdistended uterus as in multi-gestational pregnancy, hydramnios, macrosomia • Precipitate labour • Prolonged labour • Uterine malformations • Uterine fibroid • Induction of labour with prostaglandins or oxytocin • Placental abnormalities like placenta previa/accreta/increta/percreta / abruptio placenta • Obesity • Age >40 years Traumatic PPH: • Instrumental delivery • Episiotomy • Precipitate labour • Macrosomia Coagulopathy : • Sepsis • IUD • HELLP syndrome Causes of secondary PPH: • Retained bits of cotyledon or membranes • Endometritis • Abnormal involution of placental site • Secondary haemorrhage from Caesarean section wound • Placental polyp • Infected fibroid404 • Uterine av fistula • Puerperal uterine inversion • Carcinoma cervix.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In a patient with GDM complicating pregnancy, there was severe bleeding following the delivery of the placenta . On abdominal palpation , the fundus felt soft and later became hard on massaging. Which of the following is not a risk factor for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: In the above scenario, a soft uterus that becomes hard on massaging indicates an atonic uterus . Uterine rupture is a risk factor of traumatic PPH, not atonic PPH. Uterine atony is the failure of the uterus to contract sufficiently after delivery . Thus, bleeding from the placental implantation site is not arrested . GDM complicating pregnancy can cause macrosomia, which is a risk factor of this condition. Risk factors for atonic PPH: • Primiparity or grand multiparity • Previous PPH • Overdistended uterus as in multi-gestational pregnancy, hydramnios, macrosomia • Precipitate labour • Prolonged labour • Uterine malformations • Uterine fibroid • Induction of labour with prostaglandins or oxytocin • Placental abnormalities like placenta previa/accreta/increta/percreta / abruptio placenta • Obesity • Age >40 years

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not included in the active management of the third stage of labor to prevent postpartum hemorrhage?

options.b: Delayed clamping, cutting and ligation of cord

mcqs.explanation: As per the latest guidelines , uterine massage is no longer a core component of Active Management of the Third Stage of Labor (AMTSL ) that is performed for the prevention of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH). Uterine massage or fundal massage is not recommended as an intervention to prevent PPH in women who have already received prophylactic uterotonics such as oxytocin (core component of AMTSL ). Hence , it is now an optional component of AMTSL that is done in patients with uterine atony as a part of the management of PPH.
