AMTSL is recommended by the WHO to prevent postpartum hemorrhage (PPH). Uterotonics are the most important components in AMTSL to do so. The currently recommended components of AMTSL are as follows :405 Note : In the event that uterine atony is diagnosed during the assessment of uterine tone, uterine massage can be performed to control PPH.1. Injectinguterotonicswithin1 minuteof delivery of the baby or immediately after delivery of theanterior shoulder Most importantstepOxytocin 10 IU im/iv infusion is thepre ferred uterotonic .(Not recom mendedby WHO-carboprost) 2 Delayed cord clamping Done within1-3 minsof delive ry80 mlof additional blood g oes to the fetusPreventsfetal anemia 3 Delivery of placenta by contr olled cord traction: Modified Brandt Andrews technique The uterus is pushed upward s and backwardThe traction o f cord is downwards and forw ards 4 Intermittent assessment of ut erine tone Done every 15 mins for 2 hou rs

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with pre-eclampsia presents with profuse bleeding after delivery . Which of the following drugs can be used in the medical management of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: PPH in a patient with pre-eclampsia can be treated with misoprostol . It is a PGE1 analogue used as a second line uterotonic in the treatment of PPH. The drug of choice for PPH in normal patients is oxytocin. Option A: Methergine and other ergot derivatives cause dangerous hypertension in pre-eclampsia . Options B and D: Carboprost and Dinoprost cause severe hypertension in pre-eclampsia . Medical Management of PPH:Drug Dose Side effects Contraindications Oxytocin 10 -40 U in 1L crystalloid (nev er given as iv bolus ) Water intoxication - Methergi ne 0.2 mg Hypertension Pre-eclampsia Carbopro st 0.25 mg (8 doses max) DiarrhoeaHypertensionVomi ting Bronchial asthmaCardiac, re nal or hepatic diseases Misopros tol -1000 mcg FeverTachycardia -

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In a case of atonic PPH, a methyl PGF2 alpha derivative was given every 15 mins as a uterotonic. What is the maximum number of times the drug can be administered ?
mcqs.explanation: Carboprost is a methyl PGF2 alpha derivative. The normal dosage is 0.25mg. The maximum dose is 2mg.406 So, 2/0.25 = 8 times . Carboprost is a 15-methyl PGF2 alpha derivative used as a 2nd line drug in the treatment of PPH that is unresponsive to oxytocin. Side effects : • Diarrhoea • Hypertension • Nausea • Vomiting Contraindications: • Bronchial asthma • Suspected amniotic fluid embolism • Active cardiac, renal or hepatic diseases .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: As per 2017 WHO guidelines for the treatment of PPH, which of the following statements is true?

options.a: Uterine massage is not recommended in PPH when oxytocin is administered
options.b: Intravenous colloids are the recommended fluids for initial resuscitation
options.c: If the PPH is not responsive to uterotonics, uterine artery embolisation is the next step
options.d: Tranexamic acid is administered early in all cases of PPH

mcqs.explanation: Early administration of tranexamic acid is done in all cases of PPH. Tranexamic acid for the treatment of PPH is used as follows : • Tranexamic acid should be given in all cases of PPH, regardless of the cause . • Early use of iv tranexamic acid (i.e) within 3 hours of birth • Fixed -dose of 1 g in 10 mL (100 mg/mL) iv at 1 mL per minute • If bleeding continues after 30 minutes , the second dose of 1 g iv is given Option A: Uterine massage must be done in addition to oxytocin in all cases of PPH. This will help in the contraction of an atonic uterus . In normal patients , uterine massage is not compulsory as per AMTSL . Option B: IV crystalloids are the recommended fluids for resuscitation . Option C: Balloon tamponade is the next step after uterotonics .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Following normal vaginal delivery , a patient developed PPH and lost about 700mL of blood. Her PR was 100 bpm and her BP was 100 /60mmHg. What is the value and corresponding interpretation of her shock index?
mcqs.explanation: Shock index = 1 and it indicates significant blood loss. The shock index is calculated as HR/systolic BP. Here, PR=100 and systolic BP=100 . Shock Index = 100 /100 = 1 If the shock index is 0.9 – 1.1, it indicates massive blood loss and the need for intensive resuscitation.407 Description Range of shock ind ex Normal value of shock index (non-pregnant) 0.5 - 0.7 Normal value of shock index in pregnant (i.e) Obstetrical s hock index 0.7 - 0.8 Significant or massive blood l oss 0.9 - 1.1

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient was referred to the casualty from a district hospital with atonic PPH. Which of the following measures is least likely to be done?

options.b: Use non-pneumatic anti-shock garment to stabilize the patient

mcqs.explanation: Using a non-pneumatic anti-shock garment (NASG) is not one of the first measures for the management of atonic PPH. NASG is used to reduce bleeding and stabilize the patient for shifting to tertiary centers . The below image shows a non-pneumatic anti-shock garment.Non-pneumatic anti-shock garment (NASG) works by applying circumferential counterpressure. It decreases blood flow to the abdomen, pelvis, and lower extremities . It increases the blood flow to the heart, lungs , and brain . First step measures in the management of PPH must be done immediately and simultaneously . This includes : • Continuous iv oxytocin infusion • Fundal massage and bimanual uterine compression • Volume resuscitation with crystalloids • Insertion of Foley 's catheter to monitor urine output408 • Alert the anesthesia team to begin a manual exploration of the uterus under GA to check for: • Retained placental fragments • Uterine abnormalities • Lacerations • Rupture • Blood transfusion should be done if vitals are still unstable If bleeding still continues , further steps are taken depending on the patient profile : • Balloon tamponade • Surgical methods : • B lynch compression sutures • Uterine artery ligation • Internal iliac artery ligation • Angiographic embolization • Hysterectomy .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old multipara with atonic PPH continues to bleed profusely despite medical management and tamponade . Which of the following methods cannot be used to reduce bleeding in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Thermal endometrial ablation is a treatment modality for Abnormal Uterine Bleeding (AUB). It is not used in the treatment of PPH. In patients who are unresponsive to initial resuscitation and medical management, the following methods can be used : • Balloon tamponade • Surgical methods : • B lynch compression sutures • Uterine artery ligation • Internal iliac artery ligation • Angiographic embolization • Hysterectomy .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the instrument in the image given below .
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a Bakri balloon. It is used in uterine tamponade in patients with atonic PPH who are unresponsive to medical management. The Bakri balloon has a three -way valve and a separate tubing to drain the blood from the uterine cavity.409 It acts by stimulating uterine contraction and direct hemostatic pressure to the open uterine sinuses (tamponade effect ). The maximum capacity of the balloon is 500mL . It is inflated with normal saline (200 -500mL ) and can be retained for up to 12 hours. Success rates are high and it can be used to avoid hysterectomy . Other options : Sengstaken Blakemore tube , condom catheter , and 34F Foley with 60mL balloon are other instruments that can be used for uterine tamponade . The image below depicts Sengstaken Blakemore tube .The image below depicts Foley 's catheter .410

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the capacity of balloon tamponade to arrest PPH?
mcqs.explanation: The capacity of balloon tamponade to arrest PPH is 300 to 500 mL . Bakri balloon is used in uterine tamponade in cases of atonic PPH unresponsive to medical management. Insertion of Bakri balloon requires three team members. • One to perform abdominal sonography during the procedure . • Another member places the deflated balloon into the uterus and stabilizes it. • The third member instills fluid to inflate the balloon. Initially, rapid infusion of at least 150 mL of normal saline is done. It is followed by further infusion over a few minutes up to 300 to 500 mL .411

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A P3 woman bleeds profusely after delivery of the placenta . You initiate oxytocin infusion. The patient continues to bleed and the uterus fails to contract despite bimanual compression. She becomes tachycardic and hypotensive . What is the next best step in her management?
mcqs.explanation: Balloon tamponade is the next step in the management of atonic PPH unresponsive to medical management and bimanual uterine massage .Option A: Tight intrauterine packing has become unpopular due to the dangers of concealed bleeding and infections . It can be used in low-resource settings while shifting the patient to tertiary care centers . Option C: Uterine artery ligation is done when tamponade fails (Bakri balloon and compression sutures ). Option D: Hysterectomy is the last option when all the other treatment modalities fail. Usually, the uterus contracts and bleeding stops with ligation or embolization. However, hysterectomy is done sooner rather than later in cases of placenta accreta and uterine rupture .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant lady delivered her baby unattended while she was on the way to the hospital . While examining her, you note a perineal tear in which the anal sphincter is disrupted . This tear is classified as___.
mcqs.explanation: The perineal tears in which anal sphincter is disrupted are classified as third-degree perineal tear.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify B lynch suture from the image given below .
mcqs.explanation: Image 1 depicts B lynch suture .412 All these stitches are types of uterine compression sutures . They used to surgically oppose the walls of the uterus to arrest bleeding in case of atonic PPH.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with severe PPH is shifted to the emergency OT for B lynch compression sutures . Which of the following statements is false about this procedure ?

options.a: The suture loops over the fundus
options.d: Uterine ischaemic necrosis is a complication

mcqs.explanation: The procedure is B-lynch compression sutures and it is used in atonic PPH. B lynch suture is a technique to arrest hemorrhage in severe postpartum atony.The suture bites are taken over the lower uterine segment anteriorly. Then it is looped over the fundus to go posterior. Another bite is taken posteriorly . Then it is looped back over the fundus and taken anteriorly. The final bite is taken over the lower uterine segment and the free ends are tied in a surgical knot. The uterus is compressed antero-posteriorly.413 The success rate is high. Ischaemic uterine necrosis is a complication of this procedure .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements are true?
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are true. Statement 4: Hematomas <5 cm can be managed conservatively with cold compress . Larger hematomas need to be explored surgically. Statement 5: Lower uterine segment rupture causes supra-levator hematoma. Types of pelvic hematomas:Feature Infralevator hematoma Supralevator hematoma Incidence Common Rare Location Below the levator ani Above the levator ani Causes Improper hemostasis during repair of vaginal/ perineal tea rs or episiotomy wound Extension of cervical lacerati on, lower uterine segment ru pture Presentati on Severe pain with rectal tenes mus Unexplained shock with feat ures of internal haemorrhage Treatment Small hematomas can be con servatively managed with col d compress Laparotomy

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In a patient with hydramnios complicating pregnancy, the third stage of labour was managed by applying fundal pressure and controlled traction of the cord. On palpation , the uterus was still soft and boggy . Within a few minutes , there was moderate bleeding per vaginum following which a reddish -purple mass was expelled . The patient then developed hypotension , bradycardia and went into shock. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The most probable diagnosis is uterine inversion . Hydramnios is a risk factor for uterine inversion due to uterine over-distension. Fundal pressure while the uterus is atonic (soft , relaxed , and boggy ) causes uterine inversion . It results in haemorrhage followed by complete uterine inversion protruding out of the vulva . Neurogenic type of shock develops due to stretching of the infundibulopelvic ligament and the ovaries. Option A: Amniotic fluid embolism causes cardiac arrest, acute hypoxia and severe haemorrhage. Option B: There was only moderate bleeding per vaginum and soft uterus . But since there is protrusion of the uterus per vaginum, the most probable diagnosis is uterine inversion . Option D: Placenta accreta rarely causes uterine inversion . Uterine inversion is an extremely rare but life -threatening complication in the 3rd stage of labor, in which the uterus is turned inside out partially or completely . Causes : • Most common cause is mismanagement of 3rd stage of labour414 • Spontaneous • Placenta accreta (rarely) Features : • Shock immediately after delivery • The degree of shock is out of proportion to the amount of bleeding • Shock is either neurogenic or hemorrhagic • Per abdomen examination - fundus of the uterus is not palpable . Management of uterine inversion :Vaginal operatio ns Abdominal operati ons Hydrostatic meth od Kustner Huntingtons O Sullivan Spinelli Haultain Oguch

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which among the following is the most potent drug to control PPH?
mcqs.explanation: Carboprost is the most potent drug to control PPH. Though oxytocin is the most commonly used drug for the prevention and treatment of PPH, Carboprost is highly efficacious than oxytocin in treating PPH. If the question would have been "Drug of choice to treat PPH" then the answer will be Oxytocin. Initially for PPH, oxytocin or methergin (ergometrine ) is given. If it fails to control the bleeding then Misoprostol is given.Drug Use in PPH Oxytocin DOC to prevent and treat PP H Methergin Drug to prevent and treat PP H Carboprost(PGF 2) Best drug to control PPH Misoprostol (PG E1) 2nd line drug to treat PPH415

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Preterm labour is defined as when the labour starts before _____
mcqs.explanation: Preterm labour is defined as when labour starts before 37 completed weeks (<259 days) counting from the first day of the last menstrual period .Timing of deliver y Terminolog y <33 weeks Early prete rm 34 to 36 weeks Late preter m 37to 38 weeks Early term 39 to 40 weeks Full term

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a risk factor for preterm labour?
mcqs.explanation: Progesterone intake is not a risk factor for preterm labour. Progesterone is used for prophylaxis of preterm labour. Risk factors for preterm labour: • Maternal history - • Previous history of spontaneous abortion or preterm delivery423 • Artificial reproductive technique • Asymptomatic bacteriuria or recurrent UTI • Smoking • Maternal stress • Pregnancy complications - • Pre-eclampsia • Antepartum haemorrhage • PROM • Overdistended uterus - polyhydramnios, multiple pregnancy • Cervical incompetence • Uterine malformations • Intrauterine death • Maternal chronic diseases - • Hypertension • Nephritis • Diabetes • Severe anaemia • Periodontal diseases Option A: Multifetal pregnancies are common following artificial reproductive techniques and can be associated with preterm labour. Option B: Asymptomatic bacteriuria or bacterial vaginosis can cause spontaneous preterm labour. Option C: Chronic diseases like periodontal disease increase the risk of preterm labour.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Late preterm births include births between _____.
mcqs.explanation: Late preterm births include births between 34 to 36 weeks of gestational age .Timing of deliver y Terminolog y <33 weeks Early prete rm 34 to 36 weeks Late preter m 37 to 38 weeks Early term 39 to 40 weeks Full term424

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 31 -year-old G3P2 woman presents at 29 weeks of gestation with a blood-tinged vaginal discharge. She is suspected to have preterm labour. Which of the following findings will not help confirm her diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: A cervical length of 32 mm (3 cm) does not help in confirming preterm labour as it is highly unlikely when the cervical length is >3 cm. The length of the cervix in preterm labour, as measured in transvaginal ultrasound is \0352.5 cm. Preterm labor is the onset of labor before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy (less than 259 days of gestation ). Features of preterm labor: • Uterus - regular contractions at least one in every 10 minutes , with/without pain • Cervix - dilatation >2 cm and effacement >80% • TVS - length of cervix <2.5 cm and funneling of the internal os >1 cm • Pelvic pressure , backache, vaginal discharge or bleeding PV Predictors of preterm labor: • Clinical predictors : • History of prior preterm birth • Multiple pregnancies • Presence of genital tract infection • Symptoms of preterm labour • Biophysical predictors : • Uterine contractions \0314/hour • Bishop score \0314 • Cervical length (TVS ) \03525 mm • Biochemical predictors : • Fetal fibronectin (fFN) in cervical/vaginal discharge >50 ng/mL • Increased levels of IL -6, IL -8, TNF-alpha The best predictors of preterm labor in a woman with a previous history of preterm birth are fetal fibronectin >50ng/ml and cervical length <2.5cm on TVS .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following cannot be used to predict preterm labour in a patient having irregular uterine contractions at 30 weeks of gestation ?
mcqs.explanation: IL -2 is not a biochemical predictor of preterm labour. Biochemical predictors of preterm labor: • Fetal fibronectin • IL 6425 • IL 8 • TNF�o Investigations of preterm labour: • Fetal fibronectin >50 ng/ml • TVS - length of cervix \0352.5 cm • Urine culture • High vaginal swab • Maternal salivary estriol • Uterine activity monitoring

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old G2P1L0 woman came for a routine antenatal checkup at 20 weeks of gestation . She is worried about preterm labour as her previous baby was born preterm. What will be the timing and cut-off limit for fetal fibronectin (fFN) assay to predict this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Fetal fibronectin value of >50 ng/mL in the cervicovaginal discharge between 24 and 34 weeks is predictive of preterm labor. Fibronectin is a glycoprotein that binds the fetal membranes to the decidua . It is normally found in the cervicovaginal discharge before 22 weeks and after 37 weeks of gestation . It is measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. When the test is negative , it reassures that the delivery will not occur within the next 7 days.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman presented with blood-tinged vaginal discharge at 35 weeks of gestation . A nitrazine paper test was performed on her. What is this test used to detect ?

options.b: Fetal blood cells in Rh isoimmunisation

mcqs.explanation: The nitrazine paper test is used to detect premature rupture of membranes. The nitrazine paper test detects the pH of the secretions from the vaginal pool . It turns blue at pH >6. Amniotic fluid is slightly alkaline with a pH of 7.1 - 7.3 and vaginal secretions have a pH of 4.5 - 6.0. False -positive nitrazine test can be seen in contamination of the discharge with blood, semen, and bacterial infections . The below image shows the nitrazine paper .426 Option A: Fetal hemoglobin in vasa previa is detected by Apt test . Option B: Estimation of the volume of fetal blood entering the maternal circulation in Rh isoimmunisation is done by Kleihauer -Betke test . Option D: In abruptio placenta , the diagnosis is mainly based on clinical features .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A sample of the vaginal fluid from the posterior fornix of a patient gave a positive nitrazine paper test . Which of the following conditions does not give a false positive result ?
mcqs.explanation: Oligohydramnios shows a false negative nitrazine paper test . Nitrazine paper test detects the pH of the secretions from the vaginal pool . It turns blue at pH >6. Amniotic fluid is slightly alkaline with a pH of 7.1 - 7.3 and vaginal secretions have a pH of 4.5 - 6.0. False -positive nitrazine test can be seen in contamination of the discharge with blood, semen, and bacterial infections . False -negative nitrazine test can be seen in the case of scanty amniotic fluid .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Transvaginal sonography in a case of clinically suspected preterm labour revealed a short cervix and funnelling of the internal os. What is the shape of the cervix that is likely to be seen here?
mcqs.explanation: U-shaped cervix is seen on tranvaginal sonography (TVS) in preterm labour. On TVS , the cervix should be assessed to determine whether funnelling (internal os width >5 mm) is present. mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A multigravida presents with preterm premature rupture of membranes. According to RCOG guidelines , which of the following antibiotics is preferred for her?
mcqs.explanation: According to RCOG guidelines , erythromycin is the preferred antibiotic in the case of PPROM (preterm premature rupture of membranes). Spontaneous rupture of membranes before the onset of labour between 28 to 37 weeks is called preterm premature rupture of membranes. If PPROM occurs between 28 to 34 weeks , prophylactic antibiotics and corticosteroids are given to the patient .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A primigravida at 30 weeks of gestation presents with labour pains but her membranes were intact. You decide to start her on corticosteroids and a tocolytic . Which of the following drugs will not be useful in this case?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of preterm labour with intact membranes and progesterone is not used as a tocolytic in these cases . Progesterone can be used for the prophylaxis of preterm labour in women with a previous history of spontaneous preterm labour. Glucocorticoid therapy is given in preterm labour when the period of gestation is <34 weeks to hasten fetal lung maturity. Short term therapy with tocolytics is given in conjunction with steroids for 1-3 days to delay labour for at least 48 hours or to transfer the patient to a tertiary centre (with428 NICU). Tocolytics that can be given as short term therapy include : • Terbutaline • Magnesium sulphate • Indomethacin • Nifedipine • Atosiban

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A primigravida at 32 weeks of gestation was admitted for management of preterm labour. Which of the following tocolytics would be preferred for this?
mcqs.explanation: Nifedipine is the preferred tocolytic as it has minimum maternal side effects . According to ACOG guidelines , the use of tocolytics in preterm labour does not prolong gestation but may delay delivery upto 48 hours. Hence , short-term therapy with tocolytics is given for 1-3 days to delay labour for the action of corticosteroid therapy or to transfer the patient to a tertiary centre (with NICU). mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a contraindication for tocolysis in a patient with preterm labour?
mcqs.explanation: Placenta previa is not a contraindication for tocolysis . In placenta previa, nifedipine and magnesium sulphate are used as tocolytics . Contraindications to tocolysis :429 • Chorioamnionitis • Preeclampsia /Eclampsia • Advanced labour • Fetal distress • Intra -uterine death • Congenital anomalies not compatible with life • Pregnancy >34 weeks • Abruptio placenta

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G3P1A1 woman presents with preterm labour at 27 weeks of gestation . She tells you that her previous child who was born preterm developed cerebral palsy . Which of the following drugs can you use to reduce the incidence of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Magnesium sulphate has a neuroprotective effect and hence decreases the risk of developing cerebral palsy . Magnesium sulphate can be used for neuroprotection in preterm labour when the pregnancy is <32 weeks. The dose is 4 g IV over 20 mins followed by an infusion of 1 g/hr.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A primigravida was administered tocolytics and corticosteroids for preterm labour. The following day, she suddenly started coughing and gasping for air. On examination, her BP was 160 /100 mmHg and SpO2 was 80% in room air. Which of the following drugs could have caused this?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of acute pulmonary edema which is a side effect of the tocolytic ritodrine. Acute pulmonary edema in pregnancy can be due to: • Non-cardiogenic causes - • Pre-eclampsia • Acute haemorrhage • Sepsis • Tocolysis with ritodrine and magnesium sulphate • Vigorous IV fluid therapy • Cardiogenic causes Tocolytics used in preterm labour and their side effects :Tocolytics Maternal side effects Fetal / neonatal side effects Beta-adrenergic agonists:Rito drineTerbutalineIsoxsuprine Headache , palpitations , tachy cardia, hypotension , pulmon ary edema , cardiac failure, A RDS Fetal heart failure, intrauteri ne deathNeonatal hypoglyce mia, intraventricular haemor rhage Calcium channel blockers:Nif edipineNicardipineVerapamil Hypotension , headache , flush ing, nausea -430 Tocolytics Maternal side effects Fetal / neonatal side effects Oxytocin antagonists:Atosiba n(not approved for use in Ind ia) Nausea , vomiting, chest pain - Magnesium sulphate Flushing , perspiration, heada che , muscle weakness , respir atory paralysis Neonatal cardiac arrest, letha rgy, hypotonia, respiratory d epression COX inhibitors:Indomethaci nSulindac Heartburn, asthma, GI bleedi ng, thrombocytopenia , renal i njury, platelet dysfunction , ol igohydramnios Constriction of ductus arterio sus, pulmonary hypertension , intrauterine growth retardati on

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following tocolytics can cause multiple fractures in the fetus if given for a prolonged duration?
mcqs.explanation: Magnesium sulphate can cause multiple fractures and hypocalcemia in a preterm baby. The FDA warned against prolonged use of magnesium sulphate to arrest preterm labour. The antagonistic effect of magnesium lowers the calcium levels in the fetus . This causes bone thinning and fractures in fetuses exposed to the drug for more than 5 to 7 days.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Post-term pregnancy refers to pregnancy continuing beyond ______.
mcqs.explanation: ACOG defines post -term pregnancy as a pregnancy continuing beyond 42 completed weeks of gestation . For clinical purposes , a pregnancy continuing beyond 2 weeks of the expected date of delivery (> 294 days) is called a post -term pregnancy. Inaccurate LMP is the most common cause of misdiagnosis of post -term pregnancy. Hence, early ultrasound dating is important to determine fetal gestational age .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman presented for an antenatal checkup 2 weeks past her EDD. Which of the following is not an etiological factor for her condition?
mcqs.explanation: Maternal stress is associated with preterm labour, not post -term pregnancy. Etiological factors of post -term pregnancy are: • Inaccurate LMP • Heredity • Primiparity • Previous prolonged pregnancy • Sedentary habits • Elderly multipara431 • Anencephaly • Placental sulphatase deficiency

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You have performed an artificial rupture of membranes in a primigravida for augmentation of labour. You note the amniotic fluid to be saffron-coloured . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Saffron-coloured amniotic fluid is seen in postmaturity .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A newborn baby was found to have wrinkled, patchy skin, a long thin body and long nails. Which of the following could be a cause for his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of postmaturity syndrome which can occur due to placental sulphatase deficiency . Etiology of post -term pregnancy: • Wrong dates - inaccurate LMP (most common) • Heredity • Previous prolonged pregnancy • Anencephaly • Placental sulphatase deficiency (leads to decreased estrogen synthesis ) • Primipara / elderly multipara Features of postmaturity syndrome in a newborn: • Wrinkled , patchy , peeling skin, particularly prominent on the palms and soles • Long, thin body suggesting wasting • Long nails • Eyes open and unusually alert • Looks old and worried Note : Placental aromatase deficiency causes disorder of sexual development of fetus .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G2P1L1 woman came for a routine ANC at 41 weeks of gestation . On examination, her Bishop score was 2. She was admitted for fetal monitoring and induction. Which of the following complications would you not anticipate in the fetus even if her pregnancy continues further?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, the pregnancy continuing further would cross 42 weeks of gestation and thus turn into a post -term pregnancy. Hypoglycemia is seen in a post -term neonate . Complications of post -term pregnancy: • During labour: • Fetal hypoxia • Labour dysfunction432 • Macrosomia • Shoulder dystocia • Oligohydramnios • Cord compression • Birth trauma • Meconium aspiration • Intracranial haemorrhage • Following birth: • Meconium aspiration syndrome • Hypoxia • Hypoglycemia • Polycythemia • Neonatal convulsions

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A primigravida was admitted at 42 weeks for induction of labour. Which of the following conditions is she not at an increased risk for?
mcqs.explanation: The risk of post -partum haemorrhage does not increase in post -term pregnancy. Complications of post -term pregnancy are due to placental insufficiency and placental ageing . It manifests as placental infarcts and calcifications . During post -term pregnancy, diminished placental function can cause oligohydramnios. Complications of post -term pregnancy are: • During labour: • Fetal hypoxia • Labour dysfunction • Macrosomia • Shoulder dystocia • Oligohydramnios • Cord compression • Birth trauma • Meconium aspiration • Following birth: • Chemical pneumonitis , atelectasis , pulmonary hypertension (due to meconium aspiration) • Hypoxia • Hypoglycemia433 • Polycythemia • Neonatal convulsions

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The term small for gestational age implies birth weight ______
mcqs.explanation: Small for gestational age implies birthweight is <10th percentile for gestational age . With respect to the size, a newborn can be appropriate , small or large for gestational age .Birth weight Terminology <10th percentile Small for gestational age >90th percentile Large for gestational age Between 10th and 90th perce ntile Appropriate for gestational a ge

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the normal pH of amniotic fluid ?
mcqs.explanation: The normal pH of the amniotic fluid is 7.1 - 7.3 The normal pH of the vaginal secretions is 4.5 - 5.5. In premature rupture of membranes (PROM), the pH of the vaginal secretions becomes 6 - 6.2 as the amniotic fluid mixes with it. This forms the basis for nitrazine paper test .434

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the chromosome number of a partial hydatidiform mole?
mcqs.explanation: Partial hydatidiform mole has a 69XXY or 69XYY karyotype .442 Hydatiform mole belongs to the benign group of gestational trophoblastic diseases (GTD). It is an abnormality in chorionic villi making them partly proliferative and degenerative , thereby resulting in the formation of multiple small cysts . Based on the portion of the chorionic villi involved, they could be complete (diffused ) or partial (focal)

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding hydatidiform moles ?

options.a: Complete moles show diffuse trophoblastic hyperplasia
options.b: Fetal tissue is seen in partial mole
options.c: Early USG is sensitive for partial moles
options.d: Complete moles have higher malignant potential

mcqs.explanation: Early ultrasonography is not highly sensitive in a patient with partial molar pregnancy. However, USG features like thickened , multicystic placenta along with fetal tissue or even a fetus may be seen . Hydatidiform mole or molar pregnancy is an abnormal condition of the placenta . It is characterized by trophoblastic proliferation and stromal edema . They are classified into complete and partial moles based on the absence or presence of embryonic elements . Pathogenesis of complete and partial moles are as follows :443

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not associated with the development of a hydatidiform mole?
mcqs.explanation: Vitamin A deficiency , not Vitamin C deficiency is a risk factor for hydatidiform mole. Risk factors for hydatidiform mole are: • Maternal age - pregnancy in teenage and women >35 years • Previous history of gestational trophoblastic disease • Dietary deficiency - vitamin A deficiency , inadequate protein and animal fat intake • AB blood group.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 20 -year-old primigravida with bleeding PV was diagnosed to have a complete hydatidiform mole . Which of the following is not true in this condition?

options.d: Serum free T4 levels normalise after uterine evacuation

mcqs.explanation: Theca lutein cysts are rare in partial molar pregnancy, but may be seen in 25-30 % of patients with complete molar pregnancy. Serum \032-hCG levels are elevated more than expected for gestational age in a complete mole. The sensitivity of most hCG tests is set to the pregnancy hCG range. An excessive \032-hCG hormone causes an oversaturation of the test assay giving a false negative UPT. This is called the hook effect . The thyrotropin-like effects of hCG frequently cause serum free -T4 levels to be elevated which normalize after uterine evacuation.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman at 12 weeks of gestation presents with spotting PV , hyperemesis , and lower abdominal pain for the past 2 days. USG done is shown below . What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: 444 The given clinical scenario and USG showing snowstorm appearance is suggestive of a complete mole . The snowstorm appearance is due to an echogenic uterine mass that has numerous anechoic cystic spaces . Fetus and amniotic sac are absent. Investigations for molar pregnancy are: • USG - shows snowstorm appearance • Serum \032 hCG - elevated to >2 MoM (multiples of median) for corresponding gestational age • Histological examination of products of conception Snowstorms in radiology: • Complete hydatiform mole (ultrasound ) • Extracapsular breast implant rupture (ultrasound ) • Carcinoma thyroid - pulmonary metastases (chest X-ray).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A primigravida at 12 weeks of gestation presented with complaints of the expulsion of grape-like vesicles PV for the past day. A diagnosis of molar pregnancy was made on USG examination. Incidentally , the following adnexal lesion was also noted . What is the lesion?
mcqs.explanation: The given USG image shows theca lutein cysts in the ovary . These cysts are usually seen in patients with complete molar pregnancies. They are usually bilateral and are also seen in multiple pregnancies . Theca lutein cysts result from the overstimulation of lutein elements by massive amounts of \032 hCG. The cystic fluid is rich in chorionic gonadotropin, estrogen , and progesterone .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient who was treated for molar pregnancy came for follow -up after 4 months. Her USG revealed a large, twisted theca lutein cyst. How will you manage this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Untwisting of the cyst is the only management in an asymptomatic patient with a twisted theca lutein cyst . Laparoscopic oophorectomy is done only when there is associated extensive necrosis or hemorrhage. Theca-lutein cysts regress within 2 months after pregnancy evacuation, and hence expectant management is preferred in uncomplicated cases . If the cysts are symptomatic , they can be aspirated trans-abdominally under ultrasound guidance .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman at 14 weeks of gestation complains of excessive vomiting and mild vaginal bleeding for 2 weeks . On examination, fundal height corresponds to 16 weeks and fetal heart sounds are absent. USG shows a snowstorm appearance and no fetus . What is the best step of management?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of molar pregnancy which is managed by suction and evacuation, regardless of uterine size. If the cervix is unfavorable, slow dilatation is done with vaginal PGE1. Volume resuscitation with IV fluids and parenteral antibiotics can be given as supportive therapy . Blood transfusion is done445 if the patient is anaemic. Intraoperative sonography is recommended to help ensure that the uterine cavity has been emptied . Indication for hysterectomy in molar pregnancy: • Women who have completed their family • Age >40 years • Uncontrolled hemorrhage • Perforation during surgical evacuation.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 36-year-old woman underwent suction evacuation for a hydatidiform mole. Which of the following statements is true regarding her follow -up with \032-hCG estimation?

options.b: Twice weekly estimation for a month following evacuation
options.c: Monthly follow -up for 6 months after three consecutive normal values
options.d: After 6 months of follow -up, regular yearly estimation should be done

mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, the patient is followed up with serum \032 hCG every month for 6 months. Follow -up after the termination of molar pregnancy is done with serum \032 hCG levels . During the follow -up period , pregnancy must be avoided as it might interfere with the \032 hCG levels . The initial \032-hCG level is obtained within 48 hours after evacuation and used as a baseline . It is measured weekly till it becomes negative , and three consecutive normal values are obtained . This normally happens in 4-8 weeks . After this, \032 hCG levels are measured monthly for 6 months. Women who undergo chemotherapy must be followed up for 1 year.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following are complications that can be seen in a patient with molar pregnancy?
mcqs.explanation: Thyrotoxicosis is seen as a complication of molar pregnancy, not hypothyroidism . Complications in molar pregnancy include : • Immediate: • Early-onset pre-eclampsia - molar placentas produce more antiangiogenic proteins than normal placentas . • Thyrotoxicosis - as �o component of hCG mimics TSH and causes thyroid storm • Acute pulmonary insufficiency - due to embolization of trophoblastic cells • Electrolyte imbalance i.e., hypokalemia, hyponatremia - due to hyperemesis caused by \032 hCG • Shock - hemorrhage due to the separation of vesicles and intra-peritoneal haemorrhage • Disseminated intravascular coagulation • Late: Choriocarcinoma .446

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasm does not include
mcqs.explanation: A partial mole is not a gestational trophoblastic neoplasm (GTN). Gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD) is the term used to describe a group of tumors due to abnormal trophoblast proliferation. Malignant forms of GTD are termed gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN). Modified WHO Classification of GTDMolar Pregnancies Trophoblastic tumors Hydatidiform mole (benign) - PartialandCompleteInvasive mole (malignant) Choriocarcinoma (malignant) Placental site trophoblastic t umor (malignant)Epithelioid trophoblastic tumor (maligna nt)

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: All of the following are non-molar trophoblastic neoplasms except _____.
mcqs.explanation: Invasive mole is a molar trophoblastic neoplasm .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common non-metastatic gestational trophoblastic neoplasia that develops following hydatidiform mole?
mcqs.explanation: Chorioadenoma destruens or invasive mole is the most common non-metastatic GTN that follows hydatidiform moles . Almost all invasive moles arise from partial or complete moles . Invasive mole is characterized by extensive tissue invasion by trophoblast and whole villi. They can penetrate deep into the myometrium, peritoneum , parametrium, or vaginal vault. They are locally aggressive and do not usually metastasize .447 The most common GTN following term pregnancy or miscarriage is choriocarcinoma .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following are risk factors for malignant change in a patient with molar pregnancy?
mcqs.explanation: Maternal age >40 years, \032-hCG levels >100,000 mIU/mL and grand multiparity are risk factors for malignant change in a patient with molar pregnancy. Risk factors for malignant change are: • Patient's age \031 40 years or <20 years • Parity \0313 • Uterine size >20 weeks • Previous history of molar pregnancy • Complete moles have 15-20 % risk of malignant transformation , partial moles have 1-5% risk • Serum \032 hCG >1,00,000 mIU/mL • Large theca lutein cysts >6 cm in diameter Post-evacuation uterine sonographic surveillance can be used as a predictor of subsequent neoplasia . Findings indicative of malignant transformation are: • Suburethral nodules • Myometrial nodules • Hypervascularity.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: All of the following can be indicators of choriocarcinoma except :

options.a: Increased number of theca lutein cysts

mcqs.explanation: 448 Increased number of theca lutein cysts is not an indicator of choriocarcinoma . Increased size or persistence of theca lutein cysts indicates choriocarcinoma . Plateau of high serum \032-hCG level for four measurements for \0313 weeks is an indicator of choriocarcinoma . Risk factors for malignant change are: • Molar pregnancy - complete moles have 15-20 % risk , partial moles have 1-5% risk • Patient's age \031 40 years or <20 years • Parity \0313 • Serum \032 hCG >1,00,000 IU/mL • Uterine size >20 weeks • Previous history of molar pregnancy • Large theca lutein cysts >6 cm in diameter Post-evacuation uterine sonographic surveillance can be used as a predictor of subsequent neoplasia . Findings indicative of malignant transformation are: • Suburethral nodules • Myometrial nodules • Hypervascularity.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with a history of molar pregnancy was treated with suction and evacuation. Which method of contraception would you not recommend for her?
mcqs.explanation: IUCD (intrauterine contraceptive device ) is contraindicated in this patient as the uterus is friable and can cause further bleeding . Accepted methods of contraception after suction evacuation in molar pregnancy include : • Oral contraceptive pills • Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate • Barrier methods .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What will be the WHO score in a patient with low-risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia ?
mcqs.explanation: Low-risk GTN has a WHO score of 0 to 6. High-risk GTN has a WHO score of \031 7.Features Low risk High risk Total score 0-6 \0317 Age \03539 years \03140 years hCG \035105IU/L \031105IU/L449 Features Low risk High risk Type of antecedent pregnanc y Molar pregnancy Full term pregnancy Duration of antecedent pregn ancy <4 months >12 months Metastasis site Lungs, vagina Brain , liver Number of metastases <4 >8 Size of the tumor <3 cm >5 cm Antecedent chemotherapy Single -agent chemothera py Multiple -agent chemothera py

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient was diagnosed to have choriocarcinoma two years post -evacuation of molar pregnancy. Which of the following is the most common site of metastasis in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The common sites of metastases of choriocarcinoma are in the following order: • Lungs - most common • Vagina - second most common • Vulva • Kidneys • Liver • Ovaries • Brain • Bowel Lung metastases present as cannon-ball or snowstorm appearance on chest X-ray. Vaginal metastases present as purplish sub-urethral nodules .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A case of gestational trophoblastic neoplasm is detected to have metastasis in the lungs . It is considered as stage _____.
mcqs.explanation: Metastases in the lungs are considered stage III GTN (gestational trophoblastic neoplasia ) in FIGO classification. International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) staging for GTN is as follows : The chest X-ray below shows lung metastasis - stage III GTN.Stag e Description I GTN confined to theuterus450 Stag e Description II GTN extends outside of the u terus but is limited to thegeni talstructures (adnexa, vagina , broad ligament ) III GTN extends to thelungs , wit h or without known genital tr act involvement IV Allothermetastatic sites i.e. ki dney , liver, brain , bowel , etc .Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) refers to the aggressive invasion of the endometrium and myometrium by trophoblast cells . It includes invasive mole, gestational choriocarcinoma , placental site trophoblastic tumors, and epithelioid trophoblastic tumors. GTN is diagnosed based on elevated \032-hCG levels . FIGO criteria for diagnosis of GTN: • Persistence of \032-hCG level plateau in 4 measurements for 3 weeks or longer • Rise in \032-hCG levels in 3 or more consecutive measurements done weekly , over a period of 2 weeks or longer • Elevated \032-hCG level for 6 months or more • Histologic diagnosis of choriocarcinoma Treatment for low-risk disease is chemotherapy with methotrexate , while those with high-risk disease are treated with etoposide , methotrexate , and dactinomycin alternating with cyclophosphamide and vincristine (EMA/CO) chemotherapy .451

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 43-year-old woman presents with complaints of hemoptysis , vaginal bleeding , and abdominal pain for 7 days. Chest X-ray is shown below . Transabdominal USG revealed a solid mass occupying the uterus which was found to be choriocarcinoma with a WHO score of 8. How would you manage this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of high-risk (WHO) stage III choriocarcinoma which is treated with EMA-CO regimen. The given X-ray shows numerous, dense , bilateral metastatic nodules , of varying sizes indicative of lung metastases . The components of EMA-CO are: • Etoposide • Methotrexate • Actinomycin D • Cyclophosphamide • Oncovin i.e. vincristine Option A: PSTT (placental -site trophoblastic tumor) and ETT (epithelioid trophoblastic tumors) are treated by hysterectomy only, as they are resistant to chemotherapy . Option B: R-CHOP regimen is used for B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. Option D: MVAC regimen is used for advanced bladder carcinoma .Risk Criteria Treatment Low FIGO stage I GTNFIGO Stag e II or III GTN with a WHO r isk score<6 Single agent chemotherapy w ith Methotrextate or Actinom ycin D. High Stages II and III with WHO r isk score>7Stage IV disease EMA-CO regimen452

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Placental-site trophoblastic tumor arises from _____.
mcqs.explanation: Placental-site trophoblastic tumor arises from implantation site intermediate trophoblast . As syncytiotrophoblastic cells are generally absent in this site , it is composed mainly of cytotrophoblastic cells . Patients with placental site trophoblastic tumors present with vaginal bleeding and modestly elevated serum \032-hCG levels . Local invasion into the myometrium and lymphatics occurs. Hysterectomy is the preferred treatment .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old woman with a history of early miscarriage presented with amenorrhoea. Her serum beta hCG levels were persistently low and USG revealed a single solid mass in the uterine fundus . Histopathological examination of the biopsy showed abundant intermediate trophoblastic cells . What is the next step of management?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of placental -site trophoblastic tumor (PSTT ). Hysterectomy is the treatment of choice because they are locally invasive tumors and resistant to chemotherapy . PSTT is a rare tumor arising from intermediate trophoblastic of the placental bed . Patients with placental site trophoblastic tumors present with vaginal bleeding and modestly elevated serum \032-hCG levels . They produce variant forms of hCG.453

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman presented to the clinic with complaints of dizziness. On examination, pallor was present . She will be considered severely anemic if her hemoglobin is less than _____.
mcqs.explanation: Severe anemia is defined as Hb < 7 g/dL. Anemia in pregnancy is said to occur when Hb level is <11 g/dL. It is classified as shown below :Hemoglobin values (g/d L) WHO classification of anemi a in pregnancy ICMR classification of anemi a in pregnancy \03111 NormalIn thesecond trimeste r, Hb\03110 .5g /dL is considered normal Normal -10 .9 Mild Mild 7-9.9 Moderate Moderate <7 Severe Severe459 Hemoglobin values (g/d L) WHO classification of anemi a in pregnancy ICMR classification of anemi a in pregnancy <4 - Very severe

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the second most common pathological cause of anemia in pregnancy?
mcqs.explanation: The second most common pathological cause of anemia during pregnancy is anemia associated with chronic disease . The most common pathological cause of anemia during pregnancy is iron deficiency anemia. Women with chronic disorders may develop anemia for the first time during pregnancy. Causes include : • Chronic renal insufficiency - the most common cause . Recombinant erythropoietin is used for treating anemia due to chronic renal failure. • Inflammatory bowel disease • Connective tissue disorders • Granulomatous infections • Malignant neoplasms • Rheumatoid arthritis • Chronic suppurative conditions. Note : The most common cause of anemia in pregnancy is physiological . It is normally seen during pregnancy. This occurs due to the expansion of plasma volume by 30–40%. This increase is much more than the increase in red cell mass (20 -30%) during pregnancy. This leads to hemodilution and an apparent decrease in hemoglobin levels .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the average maternal requirement of iron during a singleton pregnancy?
mcqs.explanation: Maternal requirement of iron during a singleton gestation averages close to 1000 mg. The average iron stores in a non-pregnant female is around 300 mg. This falls short of the requirement of iron during pregnancy which is 1000 mg. Hence iron supplementation is necessary to prevent iron deficiency anemia during pregnancy. This also forms the basis for prophylactic iron supplementation during pregnancy. Note : The Federation of Obstetrics and Gynaecology (FOGSI) states that the iron requirement in pregnancy is 840 mg, as about 160 mg of iron is saved due to amenorrhea during pregnancy.Iron requirement during pre gnancy Fetus and placenta mg460 Iron requirement during pre gnancy Expansion of maternal hemo globin mass mg Losses through normal excret ion routes mg Total mg

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You initiate iron and folic acid supplements for a woman at 13 weeks of gestation . According to the ministry of health & family welfare (MoHFW), what is the minimum duration for which she should take these supplements ?
mcqs.explanation: The guideline recommends 60 mg of elemental iron and 500 �Mg of folic acid daily for at least 180 days, starting from the 4th month of pregnancy, and to be continued throughout pregnancy. Ideally , this must be continued until 180 days postpartum .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the correctly matched dose for folic acid supplementation that should be given in pregnant women with the following conditions?

options.b: Previous child with neural tube defect - 1 mg

mcqs.explanation: The amount of folic acid to be given to pregnant women suffering from sickle cell anemia is 5 mg. This is to reduce the risk of neural tube defects and to compensate for the increased demand for folate during pregnancy. Normally in all sickle cell patients (irrespective of age or sex), 1mg of folic acid is given to prevent folate deficiency . Note : William's Obstetrics 26th Edition mentions folic acid 4 mg daily for pregnant women with sickle cell disease . However various other sources and RCOG guidelines mention it as 5 mg daily. Hence this is the best answer.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman at 10 weeks of gestation presented with insomnia due to a compulsive urge to keep moving her legs . Blood tests revealed a Hb value of 10 .1 g/dl. Which of the following is the most sensitive indicator for her underlying condition?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, history suggestive of restless leg syndrome and Hb of 10 .1g/dL points to a diagnosis of iron deficiency anemia. Serum ferritin is the most sensitive indicator of iron deficiency anemia in pregnant women. This is because its concentrations are not affected by the recent intake of iron-rich foods . Serum ferritin concentration <15 �Mg/L indicates iron deficiency anemia. However, treatment needs to be initiated when the concentration falls <30 �Mg/L, as this indicates early iron depletion . Restless leg syndrome also called Willis-Ekbom Disease , causes unpleasant or uncomfortable sensations in the legs along with an irresistible urge to move them. It may be associated with iron deficiency anemia.461

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant teacher presented with complaints of difficulty concentrating at work. Investigations revealed normal MCV with blood picture as shown below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: In the given clinical scenario presence of microcytic hypochromic RBCs indicates iron deficiency anemia, and hyper segmented neutrophils indicate anemia due to folic acid or vitamin B12 deficiency . This is also known as dimorphic anemia. Blood picture in iron deficiency anemia: • Microcytic hypochromic RBCs • Typical photo pencil cells • Presence of poikilocytes (pre-erythrocytes ) Blood picture in folic acid/vitamin B12 deficiency anemia: • Hyper segmented neutrophils - earliest change • Macrocytic RBCs

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman at 36 weeks of gestation was brought to the clinic by her concerned husband. He mentioned that over the last few weeks he noticed her chewing on cardboard pieces and ice cream sticks on multiple occasions. On examination, pallor was present and Hb was 8.6 g/dl. What is the most appropriate treatment regimen?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of pica associated with moderate iron-deficiency anemia. Since the anemia was diagnosed late in pregnancy, the most appropriate treatment is parenteral iron therapy . Ferrous sucrose is a form of parenteral iron given as an IV infusion. If anemia is diagnosed : • In the first trimester - Oral iron therapy is preferred • In the second trimester - Oral iron therapy should be switched over to parenteral iron if Hb falls <8g/dl or if serum ferritin is <15ng/ml • In the third trimester - Parenteral iron therapy is preferred462 Ferrous sucrose is the most commonly used preparation for IV infusion. It is safe and does not require a test dose . Other iron preparations include : • Oral preparations- Ferrous sulfate , ferrous gluconate , ferrous ascorbate • IM preparations- Iron sorbitol, Iron polymaltose • IV preparations- Ferric carboxymaltose • Both IM and IV - Iron dextran.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most effective parenteral iron preparation prescribed for postpartum women with iron deficiency anemia?
mcqs.explanation: Ferric carboxymaltose is considered superior to all other parenteral iron supplementation especially for iron deficiency anemia in postpartum women. Ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) is a dextran-free IV iron preparation. It allows rapid administration of high doses of iron (up to 1000 mg iron in 15 min). It is safe and effective in improving the mean Hb level . It avoids the need for blood transfusions.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You have been asked to start parenteral iron infusion for a woman at 38 weeks of gestation . What formula would you use to calculate the required dosage ?
mcqs.explanation: The formula for calculating dose of parenteral iron is: Total dose in mg = 2.4 X (Target Hb - Actual Hb) X Body Wt. + 500 mg • 2.4 - conversion factor • Target Hb - Hb you want to achieve • Actual Hb- level of current Hb • 500 mg - additional amount to replenish the iron stores Iron sucrose must be diluted only using normal saline at a concentration of 1-2 mg of iron/mL of saline. It is given over 20 -30 minutes intravenously.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true regarding parenteral iron therapy for iron deficiency anemia in pregnant women?

options.a: Can be given in first trimester
options.c: Sensitivity test is mandatory before administration
options.d: Can be given alongside oral iron therapy

mcqs.explanation: Parenteral iron therapy for iron deficiency anemia in pregnancy is avoided if the patient has a history of chronic liver disease . It is used as an alternative therapy in people who cannot tolerate oral iron. Contraindications include : • A history of prior anaphylactic reaction to parenteral iron therapy463 • First trimester of pregnancy - there is no evidence on the use of IV iron in the first trimester of pregnancy • Chronic liver disease • Active infection (acute or chronic) A sensitivity test prior to the infusion is not mandatory. IV iron should be given with caution even if previous administrations have been well tolerated . Oral iron should be stopped at least 24 hours prior to therapy to avoid iron toxicity .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G3P2 female patient who is an agricultural laborer presents with complaints of fatigue at 36 weeks of gestation. On examination, pallor and mild pedal edema are present . Her hemoglobin is 6.7 g/dl. How will you manage this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The treatment of choice for severe anemia (< 7g /dL) in the third trimester is packed cell transfusion. It is preferred over whole blood as it avoids volume overload. Indications of blood transfusion in pregnancy include : • Pregnancy <34 weeks • Hb <5 g/dL with or without signs of cardiac failure or hypoxia • Hb 5-7 g/dL – in presence of impending heart failure • Pregnancy >34 weeks - Hb <7 g/dL.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman was brought by her husband after fainting at home. He gave a history of her being clumsy and forgetful over the last few weeks . Investigations revealed high MCV with hypersegmented neutrophils . How will you manage this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario points to vitamin B12 deficiency . It is treated by vitamin B12 injections with folic acid supplementation . �Mg of IM cyanocobalamin should be given initially every week for 6 weeks , following which it should be given once every month. Megaloblastic anemia caused by Vit B12 deficiency should be identified and treated accordingly because folic acid supplementation alone will not help . Causes of Vit B12 deficiency leading to anemia in pregnancy: • Gastric resection • Addisonian pernicious anemia • Crohn's disease • Ileal resection • Bacterial overgrowth in the small bowel .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An anxious primigravida with sickle cell trait comes to you for her first antenatal checkup . Which of the following is she at a higher risk of developing during the course of this pregnancy?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , patients with sickle cell trait are at a higher risk of developing urinary tract infections .464 Sickle cell disease , on the other hand, is associated with increased risk of : • Miscarriages • Fetal growth restriction • Preterm labor • Venous thromboembolism • Pre-eclampsia • Placental abruption • Fetal distress in labor Note : Sickle cell trait is a benign condition in which the affected person has only one abnormal hemoglobin beta gene allele whereas , in sickle cell disease , the affected person has two abnormal hemoglobin beta gene alleles and is hence severely symptomatic . Unlike individuals with sickle cell disease , those with sickle cell trait do not have symptoms related to sickling and mostly lead a normal life .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A sexually active woman with sickle cell anemia comes to the clinic for advice regarding contraception. Which of the following is the ideal contraceptive for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Low-dose oral progestins or progesterone injections or implants are ideal contraceptives in a patient with sickle cell anemia. Progesterone has been known to prevent painful sickle cell crises. It is considered very safe in pregnancy. It is rated level 1 indicating that there is no restriction in their use . Contraceptive methods and their safety profile in sickle cell anemia: Level 1 contraceptives (no restriction): • Progestogen -only injection (DMPA) • Levonorgestrel intrauterine system (Mirena) • Emergency contraception containing progestins Level 2 contraceptives (advantages outweigh disadvantages ): • Combined oral contraceptive • Copper intrauterine device .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman with thalassemia major presents to the clinic at 24 weeks of gestation with fatigue and shortness of breath. Which of the following is not true regarding the management of this condition?

options.a: Parenteral iron therapy is the treatment of choice
options.c: Breast feeding is safe after delivery
options.d: Repeated transfusions are necessary to maintain Hb levels above 10 g/dl

mcqs.explanation: In thalassemia major , both oral and parenteral iron preparations are avoided. This is because these patients are already in a state of iron overload due to multiple blood transfusions. Pregnancy in patients with thalassemia major is very rare. In case pregnancy occurs the following strategies are adopted : • Iron chelating agents should be stopped465 • 5mg folic acid supplementation should be given daily • Pneumococcal vaccination and boosters are advised prior to pregnancy • Repeated blood transfusions are given to maintain Hb levels above 10 g/dL • Breastfeeding is safe and iron chelation therapy can be resumed post -delivery .466

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Gestational hypertension is defined as:
mcqs.explanation: Gestational hypertension is defined as BP >140/90 after 20 weeks of gestation . Hypertension in pregnancy is defined as BP of >140/90 mmHg measured 2 times with at least a 4-hour interval. Proteinuria is not an essential criterion to define pre-eclampsia . Pre-eclampsia is hypertension with any of the following features : • Proteinuria • Thrombocytopenia476 • Renal insufficiency • Liver involvement • Cerebral symptoms • Pulmonary edema . Note : A normotensive pregnant woman may have an acute increase in BP from baseline levels and develop eclamptic seizures /HELLP syndrome, despite being normotensive. This condition is known as delta hypertension .Gestational hypertensio n Pre-eclampsia Chronic hypertension in p regnancy Rise in BP After 20 weeks of pregn ancy After 20 weeks of pregnan cy Before 20 weeks of gestati on Proteinuria Absent May be present :>300 mg i n 24 hrs urine>30 mg/dl i n a random urine sample Urine dipstick 2+ Absent Fall in BP to normal lev els Within 12 weeks of deliv ery Within 12 weeks of deliver y Does not return to normal

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the minimum cut-off for defining proteinuria in a random urine sample ?
mcqs.explanation: The cut-off for defining proteinuria is \03130 mg/dl (0.3 g/L) in a random urine sample . Proteinuria in preeclampsia is also defined by: • \0310.3 g protein in a 24-hour urine specimen . • Random urine protein: creatinine ratio (PCR) \0310.3 mg protein/mg creatinine • Protein \0311+ on urine dipstick A urine dipstick is used only if the above quantitative methods are not available. Note : Proteinuria is not an essential criterion to define pre-eclampsia .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In a normal pregnancy, when does the remodeling of spiral arteries begin?
mcqs.explanation: In a normal pregnancy, the remodeling of spiral arteries begins at 12 weeks . Remodeling of arteries includes invasion of arteries by trophoblasts that convert them from low-flow , high-resistance to high-flow , low-resistance vessels . These modified vessels are more capable of meeting the demands of the developing fetus . Uteroplacental vessel development takes place in two stages : The first stage occurs before 12 weeks post -fertilization. During this stage , invasion of spiral arteries up to myometrium occurs.477 The second stage occurs between 12 -16 weeks . It involves invasion of the endovascular trophoblasts into the intra-myometrial segments of spiral arteries. Interstitial trophoblasts surround the arteries. Incomplete trophoblastic invasion leads to pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH ) where the vessels remain in a state of high resistance leading to placental ischemia and release of inflammatory mediators and vasoactive substances leading to endothelial injury. As the second stage of invasion occurs by 18 weeks , PIH develops after 20 weeks of pregnancy.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old G2P1 patient at 17 weeks of gestation comes for a routine antenatal visit. Her blood pressure is 142 /94 mm of Hg. A repeat blood pressure after 4 hours is measured to be 148/92 mm Hg. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: In the above scenario of hypertension in a patient with gestational age <20 weeks , the diagnosis is chronic hypertension . Chronic hypertension is diagnosed when the patient is a known hypertensive (or) BP > /90 mmHg before 20 weeks of gestation . Gestational hypertension and preeclampsia are only diagnosed after 20 weeks of gestation .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not put a patient at an increased risk for preeclampsia ?
mcqs.explanation: Smoking is not a risk factor for pre-eclampsia rather it is protective . Although smoking during pregnancy causes various adverse pregnancy outcomes , it is associated with a reduced risk for hypertension in pregnancy. Risk factors for pre-eclampsia are: • Previous history of pre-eclampsia • Primigravida : young or elderly • Family history: Hypertension , pre-eclampsia . • Placental abnormalities: • Hyperplacentosis : excessive exposure to chorionic villi (molar pregnancy, twins, diabetes ) • Placental ischemia • Thrombophilias: APLA , Protein C, Protein S deficiency , Factor V laden mutation, homocysteinemia • Twin pregnancy • Molar pregnancy • Rh-negative pregnancy • New paternity - A new partner for subsequent pregnancies478

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not occur in patients developing pre-eclampsia ?

options.a: Abnormal trophoblastic invasion of uterine vessels
options.b: Maladaptive immunological tolerance to fetal antigens
options.c: Maladaptation to cardiovascular changes of normal pregnancy
options.d: Increased placental perfusion due to inflammation

mcqs.explanation: Placental perfusion is reduced in patients developing pre-eclampsia . The development of pre-eclampsia may be explained by: • Abnormal trophoblastic invasion of uterine vessels , leading to decreased placental perfusion . • Maternal inflammatory response directed against foreign fetal antigens leading to immunological maladaptation. • Maternal maladaptation to cardiovascular and inflammatory changes of normal pregnancy. • Genetic factors and epigenetic influences .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the management of patients with an increased risk of pre-eclampsia ?

options.a: Low dose aspirin may reduce severity of disease
options.b: Calcium supplementation above RDA reduces the incidence
options.c: Treatment with magnesium lowers endothelin -1 concentrates
options.d: Megadoses of vitamin C has no proven benefit

mcqs.explanation: Calcium supplementation above the RDA does not reduce the incidence of pre-eclampsia . However, women who have a calcium-deficient state may benefit from calcium supplementation to reduce their risk of preeclampsia . Prophylactic measures for the prevention of pre-eclampsia include low-dose aspirin administration (50–150 mg/day). It is started after the 1st trimester, continued throughout pregnancy, and is to be stopped 7 days before labor. Magnesium administration may be beneficial as it lowers endothelin -1 concentrates . There is no role of a low salt diet , anti-oxidants, or vitamin C.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the pathogenesis of pre-eclampsia ?

options.a: Vascular sensitivity to angiotensin 2 is increased
options.c: There is an increase in sFlt -1 levels
options.d: A decrease in the level of soluble endoglin is seen

mcqs.explanation: In pre-eclampsia , there is an increase in the level of soluble endoglin . Excessive amounts of antiangiogenic factors, increased sensitivity to angiotensin, and lowered angiotensinase levels worsen hypoxia at the uteroplacental interface . Trophoblast of women who develop preeclampsia overproduces at least two antiangiogenic peptides that enter the maternal circulation. They increase months before clinical preeclampsia develops . • Soluble endoglin (sEng) is derived from the placenta and blocks endothelial nitric oxide-dependent vasodilatation. It also inhibits various TGF\032 isoforms from binding to endothelial receptors . • Soluble Fms-like tyrosine kinase 1 (sFlt-1) is a variant of the Flt-1 receptor for placental growth factor (PlGF) and for VEGF. Increased maternal sFlt -1 levels inactivate and decrease circulating free PlGF and VEGF concentrations, leading to endothelial dysfunction .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old primigravida at 22 weeks of gestation came for a regular antenatal checkup . Her BP is 152/96mmHg. Urine analysis shows proteinuria of 3+. All of the following would be consistent with her probable diagnosis, except :
mcqs.explanation: 479 The given clinical picture is suggestive of pre-eclampsia and low fibronectin is not a feature of pre-eclampsia. Features associated with pre-eclampsia : • Fibronectin is a glycoprotein associated with vascular endothelial cell basement membrane and is elevated in women with preeclampsia. • Thrombocytopenia (HELLP syndrome) • Hemolysis (HELLP syndrome) • Increased hemoglobin , caused by a decrease in plasma volume. Hemoconcentration is a hallmark of eclampsia. In preeclampsia , hemoconcentration is present but usually not marked.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which finding is most likely to be seen in a patient with pre-eclampsia ?
mcqs.explanation: Decreased GFR is seen in pre-eclampsia . During normal pregnancy, renal blood flow and GFR are increased . However, in pre-eclampsia , renal blood flow and GFR decrease due to increased renal afferent arteriolar resistance . The hallmark renal lesion is glomerular endotheliosis . Diminished filtration causes serum creatinine levels and plasma uric acid concentration levels to rise. The elevation is also due to enhanced tubular reabsorption. The most common system involved in pre-eclampsia is the renal system . Several studies have demonstrated that pre-eclampsia is associated with low urinary calcium. This is often used as a predictive test .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Ophthalmic manifestations in patients with preeclampsia syndrome include all, except :

options.b: Central vision loss due to temporary scotoma
options.c: Permanent visual loss due to retinal artery occlusion
options.d: Permanent blindness due to serous retinal detachment

mcqs.explanation: Serous retinal detachment does not cause permanent visual loss. The most common visual symptom of preeclampsia is scotoma. Blindness can be due to occipital cortex edema , Purtscher's retinopathy (retinal ischemia), or retinal detachment. The blindness is mostly reversible and corrects automatically after delivery . Retinal artery occlusion sometimes causes permanent vision loss.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient , diagnosed with preeclampsia was brought to the emergency room with three episodes of generalized tonic-clonic seizures, urinary incontinence, and altered sensorium for 3 hours. After stabilization, an MRI revealed the following findings. Which of the following is true regarding this condition?

options.a: Anterior circulation is most commonly involved
options.b: This lesions may be seen in most pre-eclampsia patients

mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario and radiological image are suggestive of posterior reversible leukoencephalopathy syndrome (PRES). This condition is usually reversible. Endothelial dysfunction and cerebral autoregulation failure are implicated as etiologies of PRES. PRES lesions are almost universal in women with eclampsia but less frequent in480 pre-eclampsia . PRES is characterized by the following: • Severe headaches • Altered sensorium • Seizures • Visual disturbances . Radiological findings in PRES: • Hyperintense T2 lesions in the subcortical and cortical regions of the parietal and occipital lobes . • The basal ganglia, brainstem, and cerebellum are commonly involved. • Posterior circulation is commonly involved, and anterior circulation involvement is seen in severe cases . Neurological manifestations of preeclampsia include : • Headaches • Convulsions • Cerebral edema • Blindness • Cerebral hemorrhage.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following are indicators of severe disease in a patient with preeclampsia ?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given statements , the presence of pulmonary edema , scotoma, or epigastric pain is indicative of severe pre-eclampsia . Criteria for diagnosing severe preeclampsia include : Signs and symptoms of significant end-organ dysfunction are: • New -onset cerebral or visual disturbance i.e., photopsia , scotoma, altered mental status , and severe headache • Severe, persistent right upper quadrant or epigastric pain, unresponsive to medication and not accounted for by an alternative diagnosis (OR) Serum transaminase concentration \0312 times upper limit of normal . • Thrombocytopenia with platelets <100,000 /microL . • Progressive renal insufficiency (serum creatinine >1.1 mg/dL) • Pulmonary edema .481 Systolic BP Diastolic BP Proteinur ia Signs of end-organ dama ge \031160 mm Hg \031110 mm Hg + +/- \031140 mm Hg \03190 mmH g +/- +

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient at 32 weeks of gestation with pre-eclampsia is admitted to your ward. All of the following symptoms would warn you of impending eclampsia , except :
mcqs.explanation: Decreased deep tendon reflex is not a symptom of impending eclampsia . There will be increased deep tendon reflex i.e., hyperreflexia . Symptoms and signs of impending eclampsia include : • Severe occipital or frontal headache • Oliguria - diminished urine output <400 ml/day • Epigastric pain • Visual symptoms - blurring, scotomas, blindness • Disturbed sleep • Ankle clonus • Severe elevation in blood pressure • Pulmonary edema .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G2P1 woman with a history of pre-eclampsia presents at 24 weeks of gestation for an antenatal check-up. You decide to evaluate her risk of developing pre-eclampsia in the present pregnancy. Which of the following results is not an indicator?

options.a: Absence of diastolic notch on Doppler
options.b: High resistance index in uterine artery Doppler in the second trimester
options.d: Presence of free fetal DNA in maternal serum

mcqs.explanation: In this above scenario, the absence of a diastolic notch at 24 weeks on Doppler is not a predictor of pre-eclampsia . In normal pregnant women, a diastolic notch in the uterine artery disappears by 24 weeks . Thus, a persistent diastolic notch present in uterine artery flow between 22 -24 weeks is predictive of preeclampsia . Predictors of preeclampsia : • Free fetal DNA in maternal plasma • Diastolic notch present in uterine artery flow between 22 -24 weeks (high resistance index in the second trimester) • Average MAP >90 mmHg Predictors no longer used include : • Hemoconcentration • Elevated fibronectin482 • Increase in uric acid levels • Hypocalciuria - calcium in urine <12mg/dl in 24 h • Increased homocysteine levels • Roll-over test - screening test is done between 28-32 weeks .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old G3P2 at 34 weeks of gestation was admitted as her BP was 150/90mmHg and urine dipstick was 2+ on antenatal checkup . Which of the following drugs is not suitable to control BP in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Captopril is an ACE inhibitor and it is contraindicated in pregnancy. High BP and proteinuria are diagnostic of preeclampsia . The following drugs are used for the management of pre-eclampsia . ACE inhibitors inhibit the conversion of angiotensin I to the potent vasoconstrictor angiotensin-II. When given in the second and third trimesters , they can cause severe fetal malformations such as: • Bony malformations • Persistent PDA • Respiratory distress syndrome • Limb contracture • Pulmonary hypoplasia . Anti-hypertensives to be avoided in pregnancy include : • ACE inhibitors • Angiotensin receptor blockers • Diuretics (contraindicated as anti-hypertensive but can be given in CCF) • Reserpine • Sodium nitroprusside (used only as a drug of last resort in refractory severe hypertension ) • Diazoxide.Drug Dose Labetalol 100 mg TID or QID Methyl -d opa 250–500 mg TID or QID Nifedipin e –20 mg BD Hydralaz ine –25 mg BD

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which is the drug of choice for controlling BP in a patient with severe pre-eclampsia ?
mcqs.explanation: 483 Intravenous labetalol is the drug of choice for controlling BP in severe pre-eclampsia . It is the first-line agent for urgent control of BP in pregnancy. It is effective , has a rapid onset of action, and has a good safety profile . Labetalol is a nonselective \032 blocker and vascular �o blocker. It should be avoided in patients with asthma and congestive heart failure due to bronchoconstriction. Option B: Hydralazine causes maternal hypotension and fetal distress . Option C: Nifedipine causes reflex tachycardia and headache in the mother. Option D: In methyldopa , a change in BP is an indirect action. So it is less effective in controlling BP. Note : Experimental antihypertensive drugs for pre-eclampsia treatment are calcitonin gene -related peptide (CGRP) and anti-digoxin antibody Fab (DIF). DIF is directed against endogenous digitalis -like factors, also called cardiotonic steroids .Choice of anti-hypertensives i n pregnancy PIH /pre-eclampsia / severe p re-eclampsia Labetalol Acute hypertension / Hyperte nsive crisis IV labetalol , nifedipine , hydr alazine Chronic hypertension in preg nancy Labetalol > methyl dopa.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G3P1A1 , preeclamptic patient at 33 weeks of gestation came for a regular antenatal check-up. At present , her BP is 130 /90 and an NST is reactive. What is the plan of management for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The scenario is suggestive of mild pre-eclampsia as the patient has a BP of 130 /90 mmHg and no fetal compromise.
