mcqs.explanation: Enlarged and pale placenta is due to infection by syphilis . Other clinical manifestations and complications include : • Spontaneous abortion • Stillbirth • Non-immune hydrops • Intrauterine growth restriction • Perinatal death .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Hepatic Disorders and Infections in Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A sexually active woman presents with amenorrhea for the past 3 months and a history of a painless genital ulcer. UPT is positive and routine antenatal tests revealed a reactive VDRL report. What is the dose of benzathine penicillin that should be given for this patient ?

options.b: 2.4 million units intramuscularly as a single injection
options.c: 2.4 million units intramuscularly daily, plus probenecid 500 mg orally for 14 days
options.d: 2.4 million units intramuscularly weekly for three doses

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of early syphilis in a pregnant woman. 2.4 million units of benzathine penicillin should be given intramuscularly as a single injection. Treatment of syphilis includes : • Early syphilis - Benzathine penicillin G, 2.4 million units intramuscularly as a single injection • Late syphilis (>1 year duration) - Benzathine penicillin G, 2.4 million units intramuscularly weekly for three doses Treatment of neurosyphilis : • Aqueous crystalline penicillin G, 3–4 million units intravenously every 4 hours for 10 –14 days551 • Procaine penicillin , 2.4 million units intramuscularly daily, plus probenecid 500 mg orally four times daily, both for 10 –14 days.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Hepatic Disorders and Infections in Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A woman at 24 weeks of gestation presented with complaints of fatigue , joint pain, and the following rash for 3 weeks . Urinalysis showed proteinuria and anti-Smith antibodies were positive . Which of the following complications is least likely in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The above scenario points to a diagnosis of SLE. Preterm labor is a complication in pregnant women with SLE, not post -term delivery . Complications in a pregnant patient with SLE include : • Thrombophilia • Preterm labor • Hypertension , eclampsia , and preeclampsia • Anemia • Thrombocytopenia • Stroke • Renal failure Features of neonatal lupus include : • Cardiac abnormalities - Complete heart blocks • Cutaneous lupus • Hepatobiliary diseases - liver failure, transient conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, transient transaminase elevations • Hematologic abnormalities - thrombocytopenia , neutropenia , or anemia

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Hepatic Disorders and Infections in Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A woman with HIV presents for a routine antenatal checkup at 35 weeks of gestation . Investigations revealed a viral load of >1000 copies /ml. What will be the best mode of delivery in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Cesarean delivery is the preferred mode of delivery in a woman with HIV viral load above 1000 copies /ml at 34-36 weeks of gestation . Cesarean delivery is usually scheduled at 38 weeks of gestation , or two weeks before the due date . Pregnant women with HIV on ART throughout pregnancy, with a viral load <1000 copies /mL evaluated within 4-6 weeks of delivery , may choose to have a vaginal delivery .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Hepatic Disorders and Infections in Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A woman is diagnosed to be positive for HIV in her first trimester. What is the appropriate management ?

options.a: Start ART immediately and continue till 6 weeks after delivery
options.b: Start ART after 1st trimester and continue life -long
options.c: Start ART immediately and continue life -long
options.d: Start ART after 1st trimester and continue till 6 weeks after delivery

mcqs.explanation: ART should be initiated immediately and continued lifelong in all pregnant and breastfeeding women with HIV . This is regardless of their WHO clinical stage and CD4 cell count. *Note : Pearl attached below has been updated according to the NACO ART guidelines 2021 . Efavirenz has been replaced by Dolutegravir as per the new guidelines .552

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Hepatic Disorders and Infections in Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A woman with HIV on antiretroviral therapy is in labor. Which of the following will be given to her newborn baby prophylactically ?

options.c: 12 weeks of zidovudine, nevirapine and lamivudine

mcqs.explanation: In India, according to the NACO guidelines , nevirapine is given in the syrup form for 6 weeks to an infant of a mother who is on long-term ART . In infants born to mothers with HIV who are not on ART , syrup nevirapine should be continued for 12 weeks . According to the NIH guidelines , zidovudine should be given to the neonate for 4 weeks .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Hepatic Disorders and Infections in Pregnancy
mcqs.question: The risk of developing a stroke is highest during what period of gestation in a pregnant woman?
mcqs.explanation: The highest incidence of stroke in pregnancy is 5 days to 2 weeks postpartum . This is followed by the intrapartum period . There is an increased risk of cerebrovascular thrombosis post -delivery due to a sudden reduction in the blood volume, a fall in the level of circulating antithrombotic factors, and venous stasis. Risk factors of stroke in pregnancy include : • Hypertensive disorders • Gestational diabetes • Antepartum hemorrhage • Cesarean delivery .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Hepatic Disorders and Infections in Pregnancy
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding epilepsy in pregnancy?

options.a: It increases risk of fetal malformations by 5%
options.b: Seizure risk is more at the time of delivery
options.c: Seizure frequency increases in 30% of women
options.d: Ideal contraceptive in breast feeding mother with seizure disorder is DMPA

mcqs.explanation: Untreated epilepsy has no association with fetal malformations. Anti-epileptic medications such as valproate, phenytoin , etc ., are responsible for fetal malformations. Seizure frequency is unchanged in 50%, increased in 30%, and decreased in 20 % women. Seizure risk increases during labor as pain and hyperventilation decrease the seizure threshold . The ideal contraceptive in a breastfeeding mother with a seizure disorder is depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA), as progestins increase the seizure threshold .553

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding amenorrhoea?

options.a: MRKH syndrome is associated with secondary amenorrhoea
options.b: Primary amenorrhoea is seen in Turner syndrome
options.c: Primary amenorrhea is absence of menarche by 13 years
options.d: Secondary amenorrhea is absence of menses for 6 months

mcqs.explanation: Primary amenorrhoea is seen in Turner syndrome Amenorrhoea is a symptom and not a disease entity . It refers to the absence of menstruation that can be physiological or pathological . Primary amenorrhea is defined as an absence of menstruation by the age of 15 years. At age 13 years, if no menses have occurred and there is a complete absence of secondary sexual characteristics such as breast development , evaluation for primary amenorrhea should begin. Mullerian agenesis (MRKH syndrome), androgen insensitivity syndrome, and Turner syndrome present with primary amenorrhea. In Turner 's syndrome, gonadal dysgenesis causes primary ovarian failure, resulting in hypogonadism and amenorrhea. Secondary amenorrhea is defined as the absence of menses for 3 or more months or fewer than 9 cycles per year after the establishment of regular menstrual cycles . Polycystic ovarian syndrome and hypothyroidism are associated with secondary amenorrhea. Pregnancy is the most common physiological cause of secondary amenorrhea.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: While evaluating a patient with secondary amenorrhoea, you administer her estrogen and progesterone . However, withdrawal bleeding is not seen . What is the likely site of lesion here?
mcqs.explanation: The absence of withdrawal bleeding after the estrogen -progesterone challenge test points towards a local endometrial lesion. Estrogen –progesterone challenge test is indicated as an investigation in case of secondary amenorrhea. It depends on estrogen -primed endometrium being present in the uterus . Procedure : • Ethinyl estradiol 0.02 mg or conjugated equine estrogen 1.25 mg is to be taken daily for 25 days. • Medroxyprogesterone acetate 10 mg daily is added from day 15–25. • Alternately , one course of oral contraceptive pill is given and to observe whether withdrawal bleeding occurs or not. Results : • If there is no bleeding , a local endometrial lesion is present such as uterine synechiae . This is to be confirmed by HSG or hysteroscopy. • If withdrawal bleeding occurs, the endometrium is responsive but the endogenous estrogen production is inadequate . Hence , the defect lies in the ovary , hypothalamus , or pituitary .560

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The risk of Asherman syndrome is highest if D&C is done for ____.
mcqs.explanation: The risk of developing Asherman syndrome is the highest if D&C is done for postpartum hemorrhage. This is because the postpartum uterus is larger and bulkier. Hence , a greater area of the uterine wall is curetted . This increases the risk of developing Asherman syndrome. Asherman syndrome is the presence of uterine synechiae , due to the destruction of large areas of the endometrium . The treatment of Asherman syndrome is by hysteroscopic adhesiolysis .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding oligomenorrhea?

options.c: Menstruation occurring at an interval of more than 30 days

mcqs.explanation: Oligomenorrhoea can progress to develop into amenorrhoea. Oligomenorrhoea means infrequent, irregularly timed episodes of bleeding usually occurring at intervals of more than 38 days.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with uterine fibroids complains of frequent menstruation with an average cycle duration of 19-21 days. What is this menstrual irregularity called ?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of polymenorrhoea, also known as epimenorrhea. It refers to frequent episodes of menstruation, usually occurring at intervals of 21 days or less . The definitions of various menstrual cycle irregularities are: Amenorrhoea refers to the absence of menstruation. Intermenstrual bleeding refers to occasional episodes of bleeding (usually not excessive ) that occur between otherwise normal menstrual cycles . Hypomenorrhea refers to regularly timed cycles , but having scanty episodes of bleeding . Menorrhagia refers to regularly timed menstrual cycles with excessive bleeding (>80 mL in amount) and/or increased duration of flow (>8 days). Metrorrhagia refers to normal cyclical bleeding with superimposed irregularly timed episodes of bleeding . Menometrorrhagia refers to excessive , prolonged bleeding that occurs at irregularly timed and frequent intervals. Oligomenorrhea refers to infrequent, irregularly timed cycles with intervals of more than 38 days. Precocious menstruation refers to the occurrence of menstruation before the age of 10 years.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding menorrhagia?

options.a: Heavy and regularly timed episodes of bleeding
options.c: Amount of bleeding greater than 50 ml
options.d: Duration of bleeding greater than 5 days

mcqs.explanation: 561 Menorrhagia is defined as heavy but regular menstrual bleeding . Menorrhagia denotes regularly timed episodes of bleeding that are excessive in amount (>80 mL) and/or duration of flow (>8 days). Nowadays , menorrhagia has been replaced by the term heavy menstrual bleeding . This is defined as greater than 80 mL per cycle , which will result in anemia if recurrent Investigations done in case of menorrhagia: • Complete blood count (CBC) - to rule out anemia and thrombocytopenia . • Coagulation studies are ordered only in case of clinical suspicion and correlation with CBC • Sonohysterography /Hysteroscopy - to diagnose endometrial polyps and fibroids • Endometrial biopsy - in case of suspected endometrial hyperplasia • Transvaginal ultrasound - supplements biopsy

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 33-year-old female patient comes with complaints of menorrhagia for the past 3 months. The duration and regularity of her menstrual cycles are normal . Non-hormonal management has been tried without success . What is the most appropriate next step ?
mcqs.explanation: Hormonal therapy is the next best step in the given scenario of menorrhagia that is unresponsive to non-hormonal therapy . Menorrhagia/heavy menstrual bleeding is defined as heavy but regular menstrual bleeding , >80mL of blood loss, or >8 days of bleeding per menstrual period . It can be acute (<6 months) or chronic (>6 months). It is managed as follows : • Medical - first line of treatment . • NSAIDs • Tranexamic acid • OCPs/progestogens - if non-hormonal management fails • Mirena IUCD • GnRH agonists • Blood transfusion, if required • Surgical - if medical management fails, depending on the diagnosis: • Endometrial ablation - hysteroscopic , TCRE, RITEA , microwave, NovaSure, etc (option B) • Uterine artery embolization (option A) • Uterine tamponade • Hysterectomy - if all minimally invasive methods fail (option D)

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a feature of menometrorrhagia?
mcqs.explanation: Menometrorrhagia refers to menstrual bleeding at frequent intervals.562 Menometrorrhagia means excessive , prolonged bleeding that occurs at irregularly timed and frequent intervals. It can be caused by cervical cancer and granulosa cell tumors.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient who had undergone a dilatation and curettage procedure comes to the clinic 6 months later for a follow -up visit. She informs you that since the procedure , she has had scanty blood loss during menses which only lasts for 1-2 days. What is this pattern of bleeding called ?
mcqs.explanation: In the given clinical scenario, the pattern of bleeding is called hypomenorrhea. Hypomenorrhea along with a prior history of dilatation and curettage are suggestive of partial Asherman's syndrome. Hypomenorrhoea refers to regularly timed but scanty episodes of bleeding . It can be seen in: • Partial Asherman's syndrome - uterine synechiae , causing scarring • Oral contraceptive use • Perimenopausal age group

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 36-year-old woman presents to the gynecology OPD with complaints of occasional bleeding PV between her usual menstrual cycles . Which of the following is true about her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of intermenstrual bleeding , also known as metrorrhagia. Usually , this is scanty, and not excessive . Intermenstrual bleeding or metrorrhagia refers to irregularly timed episodes of bleeding superimposed on normal cyclical bleeding. It can be caused by: • Ovulation (physiological ) • Polyps • Cervical cancer • Lower genital tract infections etc .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young girl with McCune -Albright syndrome is noted to have precocious menstruation. This condition is defined as the occurrence of menstruation at____.
mcqs.explanation: Precocious menstruation refers to the occurrence of menstruation before the age of 10 years. Precocious puberty in a girl is the appearance of any of the secondary sexual characteristics before the age of 8 years or the occurrence of menarche before the age of 10 years. McCune Albright syndrome is associated with cafe -au-lait spots , precocious puberty (and precocious menstruation), and polyostotic fibrous dysplasia leading to recurrent fractures. The image given below shows cafe -au-lait spots .563

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman presents with profuse , painless vaginal bleeding . She has a history of 6-8 weeks of amenorrhea and her UPT is negative . On ultrasound, endometrial thickness is 21mm . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of metropathia hemorrhagica. Metropathia hemorrhagica is a form of anovulatory abnormal uterine bleeding . It is characterized by continuous painless vaginal bleeding at the onset of menses or preceded by a 6-8 week period of amenorrhea. It is usually seen in the age group of 40-45 years. A history of menorrhagia may be present . On examination, the uterus is bulky and uniformly enlarged . Histopathological findings are: • Myohyperplasia of the uterine wall - up to 2.5cm • Thick endometrium with cystic glandular hyperplasia appearing as swiss cheese pattern • Absence of secretory endometrium i.e absence of corkscrew glands • Thin , slender endometrial polyps project into the uterine cavity • Corpus luteum is absent • One or both ovaries may contain a cyst Option A: Senile endometritis occurs after menopause when the endometrium is thin and atrophic. It may be associated with accumulation of pus in the uterine cavity. Option B: Halban's disease is irregular shedding and is due to persistent corpus luteum . Regular cycles with prolonged bleeding and normal flow is present . Option D: Endometriosis usually presents in the reproductive age group, with symptoms of menorrhagia, dysmenorrhea and chronic pelvic pain.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which does 'I' stand for in the PALM-COEIN classification for abnormal uterine bleeding ?
mcqs.explanation: 564 The 'I' in the FIGO PALM-COEIN classification for abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) stands for iatrogenic causes . AUB in the reproductive age group was previously known as dysfunctional uterine bleeding , however, that term is now obsolete . AUB can be acute or chronic: • Acute AUB - it can start sporadically or be superimposed on chronic AUB. • Chronic AUB - it lasts for 3-6 months minimum. PALM-COEIN classification of AUB: • Polyp (AUB-P): • Endometrial polyps • Endocervical polyps • Adenomyosis (AUB-A) • Leiomyoma (AUB-L ). Fibroids are further classified as: • Submucosal (SM) • Other (O) • Malignancy and hyperplasia (AUB-M) • Endometrial hyperplasia • Endometrial carcinoma • Coagulopathy (AUB-C) • von Willebrand's disease • Hemophilias • Ovarian causes (AUB-O) • PCOD • Hypothyroidism • Hyperprolactinemia . • Endometrial causes (AUB-E) • Tubercular or chlamydial endometritis • Iatrogenic causes (AUB-I) • Intrauterine contraceptive devices • Anticoagulants • Tricyclic antidepressants • Not yet classified (AUB-N) includes rare causes such as • Arteriovenous malformations • Myometrial hypertrophy565

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old P1L1 woman presented with heavy menstrual bleeding and occasional spotting between cycles . What is the first investigation to be done for her?
mcqs.explanation: The first investigation to be done in a case of abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) in the reproductive age group is urine \032-hCG estimation. This is done to rule out pregnancy. In the reproductive age group, anovulatory uterine bleeding is encountered less often . Therefore, pregnancy must be excluded . Pregnancy complications such as miscarriage, ectopic pregnancies , and molar pregnancies may present with AUB, hence these need to be ruled out by urine \032-hCG levels . This is done for all women in the reproductive age group. Other investigations to be done for AUB are: • Pap smear - to rule out cervical cancer and preinvasive lesions (CIN). • Transabdominal ultrasound - to visualize the pelvic organs and lesions such as endometrial hyperplasia , polyps , fibroids, etc . • Transvaginal ultrasound - to visualize the pelvic organs. It is done after evaluating \032-hCG. This is more comfortable for a patient compared to a transabdominal ultrasound as it doesn 't require a full bladder .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman with AUB-E, who was unresponsive to medical management, underwent a hysteroscopic ablation. Which of the following is false about this procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: Fertility is not preserved with ablative procedures , because the endometrium and superficial myometrium are destroyed . In ablative procedures , the uterus is preserved, and hysterectomy is avoided. The endometrium along with 2-3mm of superficial myometrium is destroyed . Various methods of endometrial ablation include : • Hysteroscopic endometrial ablation • Transcervical endometrial resection (TCRE) - now replaced by bipolar electrode called Versapoint • Radiofrequency induced thermal ablation (RITEA ) • Microwave ablation • NovaSure - impedance -controlled endometrial ablation • Bilateral uterine artery embolization • Uterine tamponade

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: When is dilatation and curettage contraindicated ?
mcqs.explanation: Dilatation and curettage (D&C) is contraindicated in pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) as it increases the risk of ascending genital infection . D&C is a minor gynecological procedure of dilating the cervix and curetting the endometrial tissue from the uterine cavity. Diagnostic indications of D&C include AUB, secondary566 amenorrhea to detect tubercular endometritis , postmenopausal bleeding to rule out endometrial cancer or hyperplasia , and infertility due to genital TB . Therapeutic indications of D&C include missed abortion, incomplete abortion, retained products of conception , and endometrial polypectomy . Absolute contraindication of D&C includes Suspected / desired pregnancy and lower genital tract infection . However, D&C is performed in some cases with genital infections like septic abortion (where retained pieces of placenta act as a nidus and need to be removed) and pyometra (as there is cervical obstruction with superinfection of menstrual blood and cellular debris, D&C is appropriate to remove the obstruction as well as the source of infection ) Complications of D&C include ascending infection , cervical tear with bleeding , incompetent os, uterine perforation, and ashermann syndrome.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 31 -year-old woman presented with acute abdominal pain and spotting . UPT was negative . On examination, she was tachycardic and afebrile . Guarding and abdominal tenderness was present . CT abdomen showed air in the uterine wall and pneumoperitoneum . Which of the following is her condition most likely to be a complication of?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of uterine perforation. In a non-pregnant uterus , uterine perforation is most likely to occur due to dilatation and curettage . In pregnancy and uterine malignancies, the uterus is soft . Hence , uterine perforation is common during surgeries . The etiology of uterine perforation is as follows : • Insertion of intrauterine contraceptive devices (IUCD)- due to the lack of provider experience . • Spontaneous migration of IUCD within the myometrium • Dilatation and curettage (D&C) • Hysteroscopy - diagnostic (e.g, hysteroscopic biopsy ) or therapeutic (adhesiolysis ) • Laparoscopy567 It can present with fever, acute abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, and bleeding pv. Imaging reveals air within the uterine wall or pneumoperitoneum . The management is as follows : • Conservative management - Fundal injuries are managed conservatively, as the myometrium contracts around the defect . • Surgical management: • Small defects can be repaired laparoscopically or hysteroscopically . • Emergency laparotomy - as abdominal viscera may prolapse through the defect . • Hysterectomy - if the defect is large, and the patient has completed her family, hysterectomy is done as last resort.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An 18-year-old girl presents to you with cramping abdominal pain. It starts at the onset of menses and is more pronounced in the first two days. Which condition is she likely suffering from?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of spasmodic dysmenorrhea. It presents with cramping pain at the onset of menses which is more pronounced in the first two days of menstruation. Dysmenorrhoea is defined as cramping pain accompanying menstruation. It can be classified as follows : A. Etiological classification : • Primary dysmenorrhoea - no identifiable pelvic pathology . Commonly occurs in the age group of 18 to 25 years, with ovulatory cycles . • Secondary (acquired) dysmenorrhoea - is associated with pelvic pathologies such as fibroids, adenomyosis, PID, and endometriosis. Unilateral dysmenorrhoea can occur in a rudimentary horn of a bicornuate uterus , IUCD users, and cervical stenosis . B. Clinical classification : • Spasmodic dysmenorrhoea: • Most prevalent • Cramping pain at the onset of menses , more pronounced on the first 2 days. • Occurs due to myometrial contractions due to increased PGF2�o • Common in adolescents and young women • Congestive dysmenorrhoea: • Pelvic pain and pelvic discomfort occurs, a few days before menses begin • Occurs due to pelvic venous congestion • Seen in pelvic endometriosis , PID, fibroids, and IUCD users • Membranous dysmenorrhoea: • Least prevalent568 • The endometrium is shed as a cast at the time of menstruation • The passage of the cast is associated with painful uterine cramps

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An increase in which of the following is spasmodic pain during dysmenorrhoea attributed to?
mcqs.explanation: Spasmodic pain is attributed to myometrial contractions occuring due to increased PGF2�o . This is secreted under the effect of progesterone . Progesterone is secreted after ovulation by the corpus luteum . Hence , in anovulatory cycles , menstruation is not accompanied by spasmodic pain.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old woman presents to the psychiatry OPD with complaints of mood swings and depression 10 days prior to her menses . This is associated with fatigue , breast tenderness , and bloating. Her symptoms resolve once menses begin. What is the treatment of choice in this case?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD). Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs ) such as fluoxetine , sertraline, and paroxetine are the treatment of choice for PMDD. DSM-5 defines premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) as the presence of at least five of the associated symptoms most of the time during the premenstrual week . Symptoms improve within a few days after menses and are minimal in the postmenstrual period . These symptoms include : • Marked emotional lability • Marked irritability or anger • Marked depressive mood, self -deprecating thoughts • Marked anxiety • Decreased interest in activities • Difficulty in concentration • Lethargy • Appetite changes • Bloating • Breast tenderness • Weight gain Treatment of PMDD is as follows : • Lifestyle changes such as - stress reduction, adequate sleep , and exercise , reduction in caffeine intake, smoking cessation • Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs ) - fluoxetine , paroxetine , sertraline • Evening primrose oil - to treat breast tenderness • Ovulation suppression - danazol, leuprolide , drospirenone • Other less proven methods - cognitive behavioral therapy , calcium supplements , etc .569 Note : Premenstrual syndrome has no scientific definition . The constellation of symptoms is now defined under PMDD.570

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman with urinary incontinence was diagnosed to have a vesicovaginal fistula . What is the most common cause of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Vesicovaginal fistulas are mostly acquired. In developing countries , the most common cause is obstetric trauma. In developed countries, iatrogenic injury during pelvic surgery is responsible for 90% of the vesicovaginal fistulas . Congenital genitourinary fistulas and fistulas resulting from infectious conditions are rare.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following types of genitourinary fistulas has not been reported ?
mcqs.explanation: Uterourethral type of fistula has not been reported . A genitourinary fistula is defined as an abnormal communication between the urinary system (ureter, bladder, urethra) and the genital systems (vagina , cervix, uterus ). Most genitourinary fistulas are acquired. In developing countries , the most common cause is obstetric trauma. In developed countries, iatrogenic injury during pelvic surgery is responsible578 for 90% of the vesicovaginal fistulas . Congenital genitourinary fistulas are rare. If present , they are commonly associated with other renal or urogenital abnormalities.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not cause genitourinary fistulas ?
mcqs.explanation: Hysteroscopy is not an etiology for genitourinary fistulae . It can occur following hysterectomy . Most genitourinary fistulas are acquired. Its causes are enumerated below : • Prolonged obstructed labor - major cause in developing countries • Difficult instrumental or manipulative deliveries • Injury to bladder or ureter during hysterectomy - major cause in developed contries • Congenital (rare) • Other causes include : • Radiation • Malignancy • Trauma • Infections - PID, tuberculosis etc .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A P1L1 woman presents with constant dribbling of urine. She gives a history of unattended vaginal delivery following a difficult and prolonged labor 3 months back. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of a vesicovaginal fistula . Vesicovaginal fistulas usually present with: • Constant dribbling of urine from the vagina • Excoriation in the groin region due to constant leakage of urine • History of pelvic surgery, vaginal delivery or prolonged labor • Amenorrhea may be present On examination, the fistula may be visualized by observing urine collection in the vagina . Bimanual examination reveals its fixity and extent . Note : Ureterovaginal fistulas usually occur following accidental ureteric injury during C-sections in developing countries .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most useful test in vesicovaginal fistula ?
mcqs.explanation: Cystoscopy is the most useful test and also the investigation of choice for vesicovaginal fistula (VVF ).579 Cystoscopy or cystourethroscopy helps to visualize the size of the fistulas , the exact location of multiple fistulas and their proximity to the ureteral orifice. It can also assess the bladder mucosa for any injuries. The 3-swab test (Option B) is done to identify the types of genitourinary fistula . In this test , three sterile pieces of cotton swabs are serially placed in the vaginal cavity, while 50-100ml of methylene blue solution is instilled in the bladder using a catheter . The cotton swabs are placed one at the vault, one at the middle , and one just above the introitus. Interpretation: • Uppermost swab gets wet and not stained - the leak is from the ureter, as seen in ureterovaginal fistula • Middle swab gets stained - the leak is from the bladder , as seen in vesicovaginal fistula • Lowermost swab gets stained - the leak is from the urethra,as seen in urethrovaginal fistula The below image shows the 3-swab test.Option C: MRI is usually not needed for the diagnosis of VVF . They can be used to study vesicouterine fistulas . Option D: Cystometry is done to measure the capacity of the bladder . It is used to investigate urge incontinence.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient comes with a complaint of dribbling of urine from the vagina during micturition. She has a history of obstructed labor. Methylene blue 3 swab test is done, and the lowest swab gets stained . What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of a urethrovaginal fistula . Urethrovaginal fistulas have the following clinical features : • Continent and dry at rest • Urinary dribbling during micturition580 • Fistulous opening is seen on per speculum examination In the methylene blue 3-swab test , a catheter is introduced into the bladder through the urethra. The vaginal cavity is packed with three sterile cotton swabs. One at the vault, one at the middle , and one just above the introitus. 50–100 mL of dilute methylene blue dye is injected into the bladder using a catheter . Interpretation: • The uppermost swab gets wet and not stained - the leak is from the ureter , seen in ureterovaginal fistula • Middle swab gets stained - the leak is from the bladder , seen in vesicovaginal fistula • The lowermost swab gets stained - the leak is from the urethra, seen in urethrovaginal fistula The given image shows the 3-swab test.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old woman with a history of colporrhaphy is diagnosed with a vesicovaginal fistula . Which of the following investigations is not preferred in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: MRI is not preferred for a case of vesicovaginal fistula as other investigations are more specific and useful . Investigations in VVF include : • Urine culture - to treat concurrent UTI. • Ultrasound abdomen - kidney, bladder and ureter should be observed for the presence of a urinoma or hydronephrosis . • Intravenous pyelography - to look for hydronephrosis • Cystoscopy - used to visualise the number of fistulae and their location. Methylene blue 3-swab test in urinary fistulae - A catheter is introduced into the bladder through the urethra and 50-100ml methylene blue is injected . The vaginal cavity is packed with three sterile cotton swabs. It is interpreted as follows :581 • The uppermost swab gets wet and not stained - the leak is from the ureter , seen in ureterovaginal fistula . • Middle swab gets stained - the leak is from the bladder , seen in vesicovaginal fistula . • The lowermost swab gets stained - the leak is from the urethra, seen in urethrovaginal fistula . The given image shows the methylene blue 3-swab test .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old woman came for a follow -up visit one week following a vaginal hysterectomy . You note she has developed a large vesicovaginal fistula . What is the best time for fistula repair in this case?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, the best time to perform fistula repair is 6 weeks after the inciting surgery. In uncomplicated fistulas , early surgical intervention is preferred within the first 24 to 48 hours following the inciting surgery. This avoids the brisk postoperative inflammatory response . However, if extensive and severe inflammation is present , repair of fistula can be delayed to 6 weeks after the surgery. This is usually done in a patient who has undergone major surgery, During this delay it is ensured that all the tissue inflammation has subsided , tissue vascularisation has improved and local infection has cleared . Estrogen therapy should be instituted in postmenopausal women in this time period . In case the fistula repair fails, a second attempt is made only after 3 months.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old woman presents to the OPD with complaints of blood in her urine. She informs you that this happens every month for 1 week and stops on its own. She underwent a C-section 1 year ago and has no history of incontinence. During clinical examination, a catheter is inserted into the bladder , and the following finding is seen . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows the catheter emerging from the cervical os. This, along with the history of cyclical hematuria, is suggestive of Youssef syndrome seen in a case of vesicouterine fistula . Vesicouterine fistulas can develop after cesarean section , uterine rupture , and placenta accreta. Most cases present weeks to years later.582 Vesicouterine fistulas can present with cyclical hematuria, urinary incontinence or complete continence , menstrual abnormalities, and urinary tract infections . Youssef syndrome is seen in cases of vesicouterine fistulas , and it is associated with a classic triad: • Amenorrhea • Cyclical hematuria - also called menouria: Menstrual blood trickles into the bladder through the fistula , causing hematuria • Urinary continence (there is no vaginal leakage of urine) Hysteroscopy and cystoscopy are gold -standard investigations. Vesicouterine fistulas are treated as follows : • Prolonged bladder catheterization - leads to spontaneous closure • Surgical repair via abdominal route

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Intravenous pyelography in a patient suspected to have a genitourinary fistula revealed a ureteric fistula . Which of the following is false about this condition?

options.a: It is mostly caused by gynecological surgeries
options.b: Continuous dribbling of urine occurs, but the patient can also micturate
options.c: In 3-swab test , the swab is stained blue
options.d: Hydronephrosis is present on the affected side

mcqs.explanation: Swabs stained with methylene blue are obtained in a bladder fistula and not in a ureteric fistula . Ureteric fistulas can present with the following features : • Constant urinary dribbling • Flank pain or loin tenderness • Renal angle tenderness • Fever • Hematuria • Oliguria Ureteric fistulas are most commonly caused by iatrogenic trauma during pelvic surgeries , especially gynecological surgeries . An excretory urogram (intravenous pyelography ) or a CT urogram are the investigations of choice. Hydronephrosis may be present on the affected side . It is managed by performing a ureteroneocystostomy and percutaneous nephrostomy .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You need to locate the ureter while performing an abdominal hysterectomy . Which of the following features will help you identify it?
mcqs.explanation: The ureter is identified intraoperatively by the following features : • Ovarian artery crosses anterior to it • It is cord-like on palpation • Peristalsis occurs on palpation • It has a pale , glistening appearance • Uterine artery crosses it, from lateral to medial, 2 cm lateral to the cervix583

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: During post -op rounds, you note one of the patients has developed fever and flank pain. The nurses inform you that her abdominal drain outputs have been consistently high. Which of the following procedures has the highest incidence of the complication suspected here?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of ureteric injury. The highest incidence of this complication is seen with Wertheim's hysterectomy . Urinary tract injury occurs almost exclusively in major gynecologic surgery that involves surgical dissection in proximity to the ureters or bladder . Vaginal hysterectomy tends to have lower rates of ureteric injuries than open (abdominal, Wertheim) or laparoscopic routes . The highest risk for ureteric injury is associated with the following procedures : • Surgical debulking of gynecological cancers • Advanced pelvic reconstructive surgery • Laparoscopic hysterectomy Patients with ureteric injuries have a complicated post -operative period . They can present with the following features : • Fever • Flank pain • Abdominal distension • Prolonged paralytic ileus - bowel sounds are absent • High drain outputs , in case abdominal drains are placed . CT urogram and retrograde pyelography are the investigations of choice . They reveal urinary extravasation from the ureter. Ureteric injuries are prevented by careful division of tissue planes during pelvic or genitourinary surgeries . The condition is managed by prompt surgical repair by ureteroureterostomy or percutaneous ureterostomy .584

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with uterine fibroids is set to undergo a hysterectomy . While obtaining informed consent for the procedure , you counsel her about the potential risk of ureteric injury. Which of the following sites is the injury least likely to occur at?
mcqs.explanation: Iatrogenic injury to the ureter is unlikely to occur at the ureteropelvic junction during gynaecological surgeries like a hysterectomy . Ureteric injury is most commonly caused by gynecological surgeries such as laparoscopic hysterectomy, abdominal hysterectomy, etc . It can occur at: • The infundibulopelvic ligament on the lateral pelvic wall • In the ureteric canal when the uterine vessels are ligated • Near the internal cervical os • Near the uterosacral ligament

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of rectovaginal fistula ?
mcqs.explanation: Improper suturing of complete perineal tears is the most common cause of rectovaginal fistula . Rectovaginal fistulas occur most commonly due to obstetric causes such as perineal tears, obstructed labor, and instrumental deliveries . Other causes include : • Tuberculosis • Lymphogranuloma venerum • Bartholinitis - rupture of an abscess into the rectum can cause a fistula • Diverticulitis • Carcinoma cervix • Radiotherapy - can cause ulceration which can develop into a fistula

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a prerequisite for maintaining female urinary continence ?

options.a: Normal urethral closure pressure more than 20 cm of water
options.c: Internal urinary sphincter must lie above levator ani
options.d: Innervation of internal sphincter by Onuf's nucleus

mcqs.explanation: The external urinary sphincter is innervated by the Onuf's nucleus , but not the internal one. The following factors are prerequisites for continence in women: • Position of internal urinary sphincter lies above levator ani muscles • Normal urethral closure pressure is >20 cm of water • Urethrovesical angle >100 • The tone of pelvic floor muscles

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An elderly woman presented with a mass per vaginum and incontinence. She complains that she has to push the mass inwards to be able to urinate normally. What is the type of incontinence seen here?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of a cystocele in a case of genital prolapse . Stress incontinence is seen in these cases .585 In stress incontinence, involuntary leakage of urine occurs when there is increased intraabdominal pressure , such as during laughing , sneezing , or coughing . There is no normal urge to pass urine. Option A: Urge incontinence is the involuntary voiding of urine when there is an imminent urge to urinate. Option C: Overflow incontinence is an old term that refers to the inability to empty the bladder , with involuntary, continuous urinary dribbling. Currently, it refers to another presentation of urge incontinence. Option D: Neurogenic bladder occurs due to defects anywhere in the pathway of the micturition reflex , e.g., spinal cord trauma, diabetes etc . It presents with with urgency or urge incontinence.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A gynecologist performs a Marshall and Bonney test in the OPD on an elderly woman. Which of the following conditions is this used to diagnose ?
mcqs.explanation: Marshall and Bonney's test is used to diagnose genuine stress incontinence. It also helps in assessing how successful a surgical repair will be. It is performed as follows :Test Marshall test Bonney's test Procedure The vagina in the region of th e bladder neck is infiltrated with local anesthetic and it is elevated . Two fingers are placed in the vagina at the urethrovesical j unction and the bladder neck is elevated . Positive tes t Absence of leakage of urine o n straining or coughing Absence of leakage of urine o n straining or coughing

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A wrestler in the post -partum period complains of spurting of urine during weight -lifting practice. Which of the following investigations will help aid your diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of stress incontinence. It can be diagnosed with the help of the Q-tip test . This test is performed by placing a xylocaine-covered Q-tip cotton swab stick in the patient 's urethra. Initially, the stick will be parallel to the floor. Then the patient is asked to strain or cough . Normally the stick will reach an angle of around 10 -15\260. In genuine stress incontinence (GSI), this angle increases by 20 \260 or more. A positive test indicates a sufficient degree of bladder neck descent. Unfortunately , all patients with GSI may not have a positive test , and it is not specific . Tests done for GSI(Genuine stress incontinence) include : • Stress test • Cotton swab stick test • Marshall and Bonney test586 • Urethroscopy • Urodynamic evaluation- cystometry , urethrocystometry , uroflowmetry etc

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young mother presented with dribbling of urine on coughing or sneezing . Marshall and Bonney's test was positive . What is the next step in management?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of stress incontinence. In this case, the first line of treatment is conservative management. Stress incontinence is managed as follows : Conservative management: • It is the first line of treatment . • It includes : • Kegel pelvic floor exercises for 4–6 months • Electric /magnetic stimulation for nerve damage , magnetic stimulation • Artificial urinary sphincter in neurological condition • Vaginal cones • It is also done in case surgery fails. Medical management: • Estrogen cream in menopausal woman • Venlafaxine 75 mg daily • Imipramine 10 –20 mg BD Surgical management: • Kelly 's repair - vaginal approach • Marshall–Marchetti –Krantz operation - abdominal approach. It not done anymore as it causes osteitis of the pubis . • Burch colposuspension • Combined vaginal and abdominal suspension - Pereyra operation • Slings • Tension-free vaginal taping • Transobturator taping • Laparoscopic suspension of the bladder neck • Periurethral collagen injection Vaginal sling operations have the highest long term cure rate in cases of GSI (genuine stress incontinence). Their long term cure rate is more than 90%.587

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old primiparous woman with Grade 2 genuine stress incontinence did not respond to conservative management. Which of the following surgeries will not be beneficial for her condition?
mcqs.explanation: Latzko procedure is not beneficial for a patient with genuine stress incontinence as it is done for vesicovaginal fistula . The various surgeries done for genuine stress incontinence (GSI) are as follows : • Vaginal approach • Kelly repair • Pacey repair • Marshall-Marchetti -Krantz operation - abdominal approach. It is not done anymore as it causes osteitis of the pubis . • Burch colposuspension • Combined vaginal and abdominal suspension - Pereyra operation • Slings • Tension-free vaginal taping • Transobturator taping • Laparoscopic suspension of the bladder neck • Periurethral collagen injection

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 62-year-old woman presented with complaints of urinary urgency followed by involuntary escape of urine. What is the etiology of the condition she 's likely suffering from?

options.a: Pelvic mass in pouch of Douglas

mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of urge incontinence. It occurs due to detrusor instability . During normal micturition, the detrusor muscle contracts after being stimulated by the parasympathetic nerves. In detrusor instability , detrusor muscle contracts spontaneously or on provocation during filling of the bladder. It is often caused by overactivity of parasympathetic nerves. It is usually seen in older women and is caused by: • Decreased bladder capacity - due to fibrosis • Decreased sensation • Central nervous system (CNS) inhibition - due to stroke, multiple sclerosis , spinal cord involvement etc . It is associated with the following symptoms : • Incontinence • Urge to urinate • Increased frequency • Nocturia • Urination during sexual intercourse and with the sound of water, hand-washing.588

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following patients with urinary incontinence will not have detrusor instability ?
mcqs.explanation: In patient 3, detrusor instability is not seen , as this is a case of functional incontinence. During normal micturition, the detrusor muscle contracts after being stimulated by the parasympathetic nerves. In detrusor instability , detrusor muscle contracts spontaneously or on provocation during filling of the bladder. It is often caused by the overactivity of parasympathetic nerves. It is seen usually in older women and is caused by: • Decreased bladder capacity - due to fibrosis • Decreased sensation • Central nervous system (CNS) inhibition - due to stroke, multiple sclerosis , spinal cord involvement etc . It is associated with the following symptoms : • Incontinence • Urge to urinate • Increased frequency • Nocturia • Urination during sexual intercourse and with the sound of water, hand-washing. Treatment is initially conservative and include decreasing caffeine intake, smoking cessation , fluid restriction and weight reduction . Anticholinergic drugs and bladder training may also be tried. Note : Functional incontinence occurs in patients with disabilities , whose bladder movements are normal. However, due to environmental or physical barriers , involuntary leakage of urine occurs.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old G3P2L2 woman presents to the ER with hypotension , tachycardia, and severe abdominal pain. On examination, fetal parts are palpable in the abdomen. USG abdomen revealed a large uterine wall defect . What's the most common cause of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of uterine rupture . The most common cause is scar dehiscence due to a previous cesarean section . This can occur due to trial of labour after C-section , or due to spontaneous labor in a patient with previous C-section . Other causes of uterine rupture are: • Prolonged induction or augmentation of labor • Obstructed labor • Blunt abdominal trauma during pregnancy • Rupture of hematometra • Rupture of pyometra Uterine rupture is managed as follows : • Immediate cesarean section • Depending upon the extent of rupture: • Subtotal hysterectomy589 • Hysterectomy590

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an uncommon etiology for prolapse ?
mcqs.explanation: Congenital prolapse is an uncommon cause of prolapse . The most important etiological factors that lead to prolapse are the atonicity of the uterus and asthenia, which occurs due to aging and follows menopause . The other factors which lead to prolapse are as follows : • Pregnancy • Vaginal childbirth • Menopause • Aging • Hypoestrogenism • Peripheral nerve injury to the pudendal nerve • Premature bearing down before full dilatation of the cervix • Chronically increased intra-abdominal pressure • Chronic bronchitis • Constipation • Obesity • Spina bifida occulta • Congenital weakness of pelvic floor muscles • Abdominoperineal excision of rectum • Surgeries such as Stamey and Pereyra operation for stress incontinence

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most important support of the pelvic viscera?
mcqs.explanation: The most important support of the pelvic viscera is the levator ani muscle . The levator ani forms a large portion of the pelvic floor. It is composed of three separate paired muscles : • Pubococcygeus • Puborectalis • Iliococcygeus Supports of the genital organs are given by DeLancey's levels of support . However, the broad ligament is a fold of the peritoneum , which doesn 't provide support to pelvic organs.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman presented to you with the following finding. Which of the following is not a risk factor for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: 599 The given image shows uterine prolapse, for which an episiotomy is not a risk factor. Episiotomy shortens the second stage of labor and prevents the atonicity of the uterus , thus reducing the risk of prolapse . The risk factors for uterine prolapse are: • Pregnancy • Vaginal delivery • Menopause • Aging • Hypoestrogenism • Peripheral nerve injury to the pudendal nerve • Premature bearing down before full dilatation of the cervix • Chronically increased intra-abdominal pressure • Chronic bronchitis • Constipation • Obesity • Spina bifida occulta • Congenital weakness of pelvic floor muscles • Abdominoperineal excision of rectum • Surgeries such as Stamey and Pereyra operation for stress incontinence

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 64-year-old woman presents to the gynecology clinic with complaints of a mass descending PV . On examination, you note that the external os lies at the level of the introitus. What is the degree of uterine prolapse ?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of 2nd degree prolapse .600

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is correctly matched between classification systems of prolapse and their reference point?
mcqs.explanation: In Baden-Walker halfway system of classification of prolapse , the reference point is the hymen.Prolapse classification syste m Reference poi nt Shaws Introitus Baden Walker halfway Hymen POP-Q Hymen

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is seen in congenital elongation of the cervix?

options.a: The vaginal portion of the cervix gets elongated
options.b: The supravaginal portion of the cervix gets elongated
options.c: Both the vaginal and supravaginal portions of the cervix get elongated
options.d: There is no true elongation and it is a misnomer

mcqs.explanation: In congenital elongation of the cervix, the vaginal portion of the cervix is elongated . The fornices are hence deep , and there is no accompanying vaginal prolapse . In 2nd and 3rd degree uterine prolapse , the supravaginal portion of the cervix gets stretched and elongated as it is well supported by the Mackenrodt's ligaments , while the vaginal portion of the cervix prolapses with the vagina . In prolapse , the cervix can elongate to as much as 10cm in length . However, in procidentia , the entire uterus slides with the vagina , and hence the cervix retains its normal length .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following differential diagnosis will you not consider in a case of prolapse ?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of uterine prolapse . A retroverted uterus is not a differential diagnosis for uterine prolapse . However, retroversion of the uterus does occur with uterine prolapse . Differential diagnoses of genital prolapse include : • Congenital elongation of the cervix - vaginal part of the cervix is elongated . In genital prolapse , supravaginal part is elongated and vaginal part is prolapsed . • Vulval cyst and Gartner cyst - large cysts may mimic prolapse • Cyst of the anterior vaginal wall - tense with well -defined margins and cannot be reduced on pressure . • Urethral diverticula - rare, small, and situated low in the anterior vaginal wall. Urethroscopy helps in the diagnosis. • Cervical fibroid polyp - cervix remains high up in its anatomical position.601 • Chronic inversion of the uterus - Uterine sound is used to confirm the diagnosis. USG and laparoscopy will show fundal depression and the absence of uterine fundus in the pelvis. • Rectal prolapse

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 57 -year-old woman presents to you with complaints of mass descending per vaginum for the past 6 months. On examination, grade 3 uterovaginal prolapse and a decubitus ulcer are observed. What causes this ulcer?
mcqs.explanation: Decubitus ulcer seen in uterine prolapse is due to venous congestion and local circulatory changes . Decubitus ulcer refers to the ulceration of prolapsed tissue which occurs due to the chronic dependent position causing venous congestion and stasis. It has a clean edge and usually heals well with prolapse reduction and daily packing with glycerine (hygroscopic agent ) and acriflavine (antiseptic ). It is a benign and non-infectious disease and does not require further investigation such as biopsy or culture .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A post -menopausal woman presents with a mass protruding from the vagina that increases in size on coughing and sneezing . Which of the following is not a complication of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of pelvic organ prolapse . Urge incontinence is not a complication of this condition. Complications of prolapse are: • Damage to the ureter - can occur during • Surgical repair • Kinking due to procidentia • Urinary tract infection - due to retention of urine in a cystocele • Hydronephrosis and hydroureter • Incarceration of the prolapse - the prolapsed organ becomes irreducible • Decubitus ulcer • Stress incontinence • Squamous cell carcinoma over the decubitus ulcer (rare)

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A multiparous woman notices a bulge at the vulva that diminishes in size on lying down. She also finds it difficult to initiate micturition. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of a cystocoele . A cystocele is the herniation of the urinary bladder into the vagina . It is usually associated with uterine prolapse , and presents with the following features : • Mass descending in the vagina - • Increases in size on straining and coughing602 • Reduces on lying down, or manual reduction • Difficulty in micturition - difficulty initiating, straining required • Mass needs to be pushed inwards to urinate - repositioning of cystocele required • Increased frequency of micturition • Backache - due to stretching of uterosacral ligaments

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is correct about the POP-Q staging system ?

options.a: Stage 4 involves complete eversion of the vagina .
options.b: In stage 3, the leading point is 1 cm above hymen.
options.c: Five reference points are present in the vagina .
options.d: The points above the hymen are described as plus .

mcqs.explanation: The Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification (POP-Q) system was described by the International Continence Society and has the following features : • The hymen is taken as a fixed point. • Six reference points are measured , using a scaled spatula : • Two on the anterior vaginal wall • Two on the apical vagina • Two on the posterior vaginal wall • Three measurements : The genital hiatus, perineal body, and total vaginal length . • The points above the hymen are described as minus and points below as plus . Staging of pelvic organ prolapse according to the POP-Q system :Stag e Description Stag e 0 No descent of pelvic organs Stag e 1 The leading edge of the prola pse is>1 cm abovethe level of thehymen . Stag e 2 The leading edge of the prola pse is<1 cmproximal or distal to the hymen. Stag e 3 The leading point of prolapse is>1 cm belowthehymenbut protrudes no further than 2 c m less than the total length o f the vagina . Stag e 4 Completeeversionof the vagin a603

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old woman presents with pelvic pain, and a mass descending PV with increases in size on coughing. She is posted for a Fothergill repair. Which of the following is false about this procedure ?

options.a: It is also known as Manchester operation
options.b: It does not preserve the reproductive functions
options.c: Recurrent abortions are a sequelae of this operation

mcqs.explanation: Fothergill 's operation preserves menstrual and reproductive functions. Fothergill 's repair is also known as Manchester 's operation. It is suitable for women under 40 years who are desirous of retaining their menstrual and reproductive functions. The steps are: • Preliminary D and C • Anterior colporrhaphy with amputation of the cervix. • Raw area covered with the vaginal mucosa. • Mackenrodt ligaments sutured in the front of the cervix • Colpoperineorrhaphy Since the uterus is preserved in this procedure , the patient is able to menstruate and can conceive and carry the pregnancy. However, fertility decreases due to the loss of cervical mucus. Moreover, cervical incompetence occurs, leading to recurrent abortions and preterm deliveries .604 Shirodkar 's modification of Fothergill 's repair avoids cervical amputation, hence subsequent pregnancy complications are avoided.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old lady presents with third degree uterine prolapse . Which of the following is the best management for her?

options.c: Vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair

mcqs.explanation: In the clinal scenario of a 55 -year-old woman with third-degree uterine prolapse , the ideal management is vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair. Uterine prolapse is the descent of the uterus from its normal position which usually occurs due to laxity of ligaments that offer support , seen often due to childbirth, aging, or trauma. The uterine descent is clinically categorized into: • First degree : the external os remains above the vaginal introitus605 • Second degree : The external os protrudes below the vaginal introitus but the uterine body remains inside the vagina • Third degree (Syn: Complete prolapse ): The uterine , cervix, body, and fundus descend to lie outside the introitus • Procidentia involves prolapse of the uterus with the entire vagina everted . The patient usually presents with a sense of heaviness in the pelvic region with lower back discomfort. Based on the structures involved the patient can additionally have urinary symptoms (like incontinence and urgency ), bowel disturbances (constipation and tenesmus ), or sexual discomfort during intercourse . Symptomatic uterine prolapse is managed surgically with different procedures based on the profile of the patient . Conservative management is done for old asymptomatic women with mild degree prolapse . A vaginal hysterectomy is recommended for patients who satisfy the following criteria: • >40 years of age • Have completed their families • Do not wish to preserve menstrual and child-bearing function Other options : Option A: Fothergill repair or Manchester operation is a procedure done to preserve the reproductive function and vaginal prolapse with supravaginal cervix elongation . It initially involves preliminary curettage with low amputation of the cervix. After Mackenrodt's ligament is plicated , anterior colporrhaphy and colpoperineorrhaphy are performed . Option B: Sling operation (Purandare's operation) is indicated in congenital or nulliparous prolapse without cystocele . The procedure involves the extraperitoneal passage of rectus sheath strips joined to the anterior surface of the cervix by silk sutures . Option D: Shirodkar procedure is a type of abdominal sling surgery done in young women to retain menstrual and reproductive function. It involves using a sling to fix the cervix to the lumbosacral fascia.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 75 -year-old woman diagnosed with procidentia is posted for operative repair. During a pre-anesthetic check-up, she was determined to be medically unfit for major surgery. Which of the following procedures is recommended in her?
mcqs.explanation: Le Fort's repair is recommended in this case. This repair is done in patients who satisfy the following criteria: • Elderly (>60 years) • Do not wish to retain sexual function • Medically unfit for major surgeries

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old nulliparous woman presents to you with primary infertility . On examination, stage 2 uterine prolapse is present . What is the next step in management?
mcqs.explanation: 606 Sling operations are recommended in cases of nulliparous prolapse , who wish to retain menstrual and child-bearing function Mackenrodt's and uterosacral ligaments of the uterus are strengthened , by using nylon or Dacron tapes as slings. Abdominal sling operations include : • Abdominal wall cervicopexy - cervical supports are fixed to the abdominal wall • Shirodkar 's sling operation - cervix is fixed to the lumbosacral fascia using Mersilene tape • Khanna's abdominal sling operation - isthmus of the cervix is fixed to the anterior superior iliac spines . It is not done anymore due to the risk of periosteitis . • Virkud 's sling operation - the tape is fixed from the isthmus and attached to the rectus compartment • Joshi's sling operation - the uterus is suspended from the pectineal ligaments .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 67-year-old woman diagnosed with uterine prolapse , now presented with dyspareunia and fecal incontinence. After manually reducing the prolapse , a peristaltic bulge is seen in the posterior vaginal wall. What is the preferred method of management in this case?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of an enterocele associated with fecal incontinence. It is preferably repaired using an abdominal approach like Moschcowitz repair. An enterocele is herniation of the pouch of Douglas and small bowel loops into the rectovaginal septum . Enteroceles are most commonly associated with uterine prolapse . Patients present with the following clinical features : • Fecal incontinence • Sexual dysfunction • Constipation /diarrhea • Mass descending PV • Pelvic pain or pelvic discomfort • A bulge in the posterior vaginal wall: • Upper 1/3rd - enterocele • Lower 2/3rd - rectocele • Peristalsis may be observed in the bulge Enterocele repair is done via the following methods : • Vaginal approach - it is usually preferred over an abdominal approach. In McCall 's culdoplasty , the uterosacral ligaments are used to suspend the vaginal vault. The posterior peritoneum and uterosacral ligaments are approximated . • Abdominal approach - it is preferred in cases where there is associated fecal incontinence. It includes : • Moschcowitz repair - the pouch of Douglas is obliterated by several purse -string sutures . • Halban's procedure - the peritoneal sac is obliterated using vertical sutures . This can also be done transvaginally.607 Option B: Purandare's sling operation is abdominal wall cervicopexy for uterine prolapse . It is done for young nulliparous women. Option D: Le Fort's repair is done in elderly patients with uterine prolapse , who are unfit for surgery. Note : Enteroceles may be present along with uterine prolapse . Failure to identify and repair it during vaginal hysterectomy can lead to vault prolapse .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: How many degrees of vault prolapse are there ?
mcqs.explanation: There are 3 degrees of vault prolapse . Vault prolapse is a delayed complication of both abdominal and vaginal hysterectomy . It can also occur due to failure to identify and repair an enterocele during a hysterectomy . In vault prolapse , level 1 supports become weak and deficient . Risk factors apart from past history of surgery are: • Advanced age • Menopause - due to estrogen deficiency • Parity • Obesity • Chronic cough

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old woman presented with a mass bulging into the vagina , difficult intercourse , and back pain. She has a history of hysterectomy 2 years back. On examination, you observe that the vaginal vault is protruding outside the introitus. What is the best management in this case?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of vault prolapse . Sacrospinous colpopexy is the gold standard management for vault prolapse . Vault prolapse presents with pelvic or back pain, the descent of the vault through the vagina , difficulties in intercourse , and difficulty in walking due to the mass. It is commonly associated with a cystocele or a rectocele . It can be prevented by identifying and repairing an enterocele and by attaching the uterosacral and cardinal ligaments to the vault during a hysterectomy . Vault prolapse is managed as follows : • If the patient is fit for abdominal surgery: Transabdominal sacral colpopexy , i.e., uterosacral suspension • If the patient is not fit for abdominal surgery: Transvaginal sacrospinous ligament fixation/colpopexy - the gold standard • Laparoscopic colpopexy • If the patient does not want to retain sexual function: • Colpocleisis608 • Le Fort's repair • Anterior colporrhaphy in case of cystocele • Posterior colporrhaphy in case of rectocele • If the patient is unfit for surgery, ring pessaries can be tried • Posterior intravaginal slingplasty Note : Kelly 's repair and Burch colposuspension are done to manage stress incontinence.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young woman with uterine prolapse following pelvic trauma underwent a hysterectomy . A year later, she presents with vault prolapse . What would you not recommend for her?
mcqs.explanation: In a young patient with vault prolapse , ring pessary is not recommended . Vault prolapse is managed as follows : • If the patient is fit for abdominal surgery: Transabdominal sacral colpopexy , i.e., uterosacral suspension - The best method for vault prolapse . • If the patient is not fit for abdominal surgery: Transvaginal sacrospinous ligament fixation. • Laparoscopic colpopexy • If the patient does not want to retain sexual function: • Colpocleisis • Le Fort's repair • Anterior colporrhaphy in case of cystocele • Posterior colporrhaphy in case of rectocele • If the patient is unfit for surgery, ring pessaries can be tried • Posterior intravaginal slingplasty

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The given instrument was used to treat a patient with uterine prolapse . Which of the following statements is false about this instrument?

options.a: It should be changed every 3 months.
options.b: It can be used in pregnant patients .
options.d: It may rarely cause carcinoma of vagina .

mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a ring pessary , which is only a palliative treatment for genital prolapse . A ring pessary is used for patients who cannot be surgically managed, such as pregnant patients and very elderly women. In these patients, it is used as an adjunct to pelvic floor physiotherapy . Pessaries provide mechanical support to the pelvic organs. After being placed , they should be changed every 3 months. They may cause vaginitis; dyspareunia ; and, rarely, carcinoma if retained for a long time. The image below shows the types of pessaries :609

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the first step after fitting the pessary to check if the pessary is adequately retained ?

options.a: Asking the patient to void and see if the pessary is in place
options.b: Seeing if the patient feels any discomfort, which means that the pessary is retained
options.c: Asking the patient to perform the Valsalva manouvre and see if the pessary is in place
options.d: Being able to admit two fingers between the ring and the pessary .

mcqs.explanation: The first step after fitting the pessary to check if the pessary is adequately retained is to ask the patient to perform Valsalva 's maneuver or cough and see if the pessary is in place . There is some level of descent of the pessary with these maneuvers is to be expected , but the pessary should return to its normal position when these efforts are stopped . If the pessary descends to the introitus with these maneuvers, then a larger size pessary should be tried. The pessary is well -fitted if you are able to slide the ring of the pessary up and down along the vaginal sidewall . It is well -fitted if you are able to insert one finger between the vaginal sidewall and the edge of the pessary . When the labia are separated , a well -supported pessary is not usually visible.610 The patient should be comfortable , and able to void urine with the pessary in place before leaving the clinic.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The deepest part of perineal body injury, which causes cystocoele , enterocoele and urethral descent is ____
mcqs.explanation: Pubococcygeus is the deepest part of the levator ani muscle . Injury to it can cause enterocele , cystocele , and urethral descent . Levator ani muscles are the most important muscles in the pelvic floor and maintain a constant state of contraction. They provide a stable floor and support the weight of the abdominopelvic contents against intra-abdominal forces . Weakening of levator ani and pelvic fascia from stretching or tearing during childbirth, may decrease support for the vagina , bladder , uterus , or rectum or alter the position of the neck of the bladder and urethra. The levator ani muscle is a complex unit, which consists of 3 muscle components namely • Pubococcygeus (anterior fibers) • Pubovaginalis - elevates the urethra and hence contributes to urinary continence • Puboperinealis - draws the perineal body towards the pubic symphysis • Puboanalis - elevates the anus and keeps the urogenital hiatus narrowed • Puborectalis (intermediate fibers) • Iliococcygeus (posterior fibers) Origin: The levator ani muscle has a linear origin from the pelvic surface of the body of the pubis , a tendinous arch of obturator fascia, and the pelvic surface of the ischial spine . Insertion: • The anterior fibres form a sling around the prostate (levator prostatae ) or vagina (sphincter vaginae) and are inserted into the perineal body (a mass of fibrous tissue ) in front of the anal canal.611 • The intermediate fibres (puborectalis ) form a sling around the anorectal junction to be inserted into the anococcygeal raphe (a fibrous raphe which extends from the anorectal junction to the tip of the coccyx). • The posterior fibres (iliococcygeus ) are inserted into the anococcygeal raphe and the coccyx. Nerve supply : • perineal branch of 4th sacral nerve (S4) from its pelvic surface . • perineal branch of the pudendal nerve (S2, S3) from its perineal surface . Actions: • The levator ani muscles of two sides together support the pelvic viscera and resist the intra-abdominal pressure during straining and expulsive efforts of the anterior abdominal wall muscles . • They also subserve a sphincteric action on the anorectal junction to maintain the continence of faeces in both sexes and vagina in females .The given image below shows the pelvic floor:612

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: All of the following are correctly matched regarding the management of prolapse except _______

options.b: Vaginal pessary is contraindicated in pregnancy
options.c: Postnatal - Ring pessary and pelvic floor exercises for 3–6 months
options.d: Woman beyond 40 years and multipara - Vaginal hysterectomy and pelvic floor repair

mcqs.explanation: The vaginal pessary is not contraindicated in pregnancy. During pregnancy, depending on the severity and patient preference , prolapse is managed conservatively as follows : • Intravaginal pessaries - simple , effective , potentially effective in preventing preterm birth • Pelvic floor exercises • Pelvic physiotherapy • Electrical therapy

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: All of the following surgeries are done in vault prolapse except ______
mcqs.explanation: Colposuspension is done in stress urinary incontinence and not for vault prolapse . Management of Vault prolapse : • If the patient is fit for abdominal surgery: Transabdominal sacral colpopexy , i.e., uterosacral suspension • The best method for vault prolapse . • If the patient is not fit for abdominal surgery: Transvaginal sacrospinous ligament fixation.613

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about fibroids?

options.a: More common in Asians than African-Americans
options.d: Does not usually increase in size during pregnancy

mcqs.explanation: Fibroids are more common in African-American women. Uterine fibroids are benign, smooth muscle tumors present in the uterine musculature . They are most commonly seen during reproductive years. Estrogen and progesterone promote the development of fibroids. Option B: Hypoestrogenism occurs in smokers, therefore smoking is protective for fibroids. Option C: Estrogen exposure is increased in nulliparous women, therefore fibroids are more common. Increased parity is protective for fibroids. Option D: Most fibroids do not increase in size during pregnancy. Pregnancy can have an unpredictable effect on fibroids based on individual genetic and environmental factors.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following genes is not associated with leiomyomas ?
mcqs.explanation: MLH1 gene is not associated with leiomyomas . Its mutation leads to endometrial carcinoma . MED12 and HMGA2 are the most common genes associated with leiomyomas . Other genes involved are COL4A5-A6 and the gene for fumarate hydratase (FH). FH gene mutation leads to hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer (HLRCC ) syndrome.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Leiomyomas create a hyperestrogenic state by all of these mechanisms except :

options.a: Cells contain a greater density of estrogen receptors
options.c: Have higher levels of cytochrome P450 aromatase

mcqs.explanation: Leiomyomas convert less estradiol to the weaker estrone .624 Leiomyomas create a hyperestrogenic environment, which is a requisite for their growth and maintenance. The hyperestrogenic environment is created by the following mechanisms: • Compared to normal myometrium, leiomyoma cells contain a greater density of estrogen receptors , which results in greater estradiol binding. • These tumors convert less estradiol to the weaker estrone . • There are higher levels of cytochrome P450 aromatase in leiomyomas compared with normal myocytes . This specific enzyme catalyzes the conversion of androgens to estrogen .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Initially, all fibroids are ____.
mcqs.explanation: Initially, all fibroids are intramural . Fibroids develop in the myometrium, as intramural /interstitial and then branch out to form the other types . Classification of fibroids based on anatomical location: • Body (corporeal) fibroids- • Interstitial/intramural fibroids: They are the most common (75 %). • Subserosal fibroids: They are the least common (10 %). Interstitial fibroids grow outwards to form subserous fibroids and are covered by the peritoneum . These include wandering or parasitic fibroids and broad ligament fibroids. • Submucous fibroids: Interstitial fibroid grows inwards towards the uterine cavity. It is the most symptomatic type . • Cervical fibroids

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old lady comes with abnormal uterine bleeding . A hysterectomy was performed and the following specimen was retrieved. What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: 625 The given cut section image showing multiple nodules , well -circumscribed, firm, and white -greyish with a whorled appearance is Leiomyoma (Fibroid). Leiomyoma is the most common benign and the most common pelvic tumor in females and is more common in obese females (hyper -estrogenism ). They are mostly asymptomatic and the most common symptom is menorrhagia. Leiomyomas can also present with bleeding areas, cystic degeneration , and calcifications . The uterine cavity is compressed . The image below different types of uterine fibroids classified according to their locations:Sub-mucous fibroids are the most symptomatic type and intra-mural fibroids are the most common type of uterine fibroids. Other options : Option B: Endometrial cancer presents as a polypoid mass protruding into the uterine cavity or as a diffuse thickening of the endometrium. The cut surface may appear white to yellow and may show areas of necrosis or hemorrhage. Option C: Endometrial polyps are usually small and may be single or multiple . Grossly, they appear as soft, red to pink, often pedunculated (attached by a stalk) masses protruding into the uterine cavity. It presents with heavy cyclic or intermenstrual bleeding , or without complaints as an incidental finding on imaging. Estrogen and progesterone have been implicated in the growth of endometrial polyps , and higher receptor levels are seen compared with the normal endometrium .
