Option D: In Adenomyosis (Endometriosis interna), the uterus may appear bulky and symmetrically enlarged . On the cut section , the myometrium may appear thickened and may show tiny cystic spaces filled with old blood (chocolate cysts ). The preferred treatment is hysterectomy . Localised excision or levonorgestrel IUCD is tried in younger women. The image below shows both the gross and histologic appearances of adenomyosis :626

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following symptoms would you not expect in a patient diagnosed with uterine fibroids?
mcqs.explanation: Menouria and hypomenorrhea are not seen in patients with uterine fibroids. Menouria occurs due to vesicouterine fistulas . Hypomenorrhea is seen in Asherman's syndrome and due to OCP use . Fibroids present with the following clinical features : • Menstrual symptoms such as: • Menstrual irregularities - heavy menstrual bleeding /menorrhagia which is the most common symptom, polymenorrhoea , and intermenstrual bleeding (metrorrhagia) • Dysmenorrhea • Postmenopausal bleeding • Abdominal pain • Abdominal distension , mass abdomen • Vaginal discharge • Infertility • Recurrent abortions • Pressure symptoms such as: • Urinary retention • Increased frequency of urination • Constipation • Broad ligament fibroids can cause compression of the ureter leading to hydronephrosis or hydroureter.627

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient presented with intermenstrual bleeding for the past 6 months. Which of the following types of fibroid is usually associated with this symptom ?
mcqs.explanation: Intermenstrual bleeding is common with submucous fibroids. Metrorrhagia or intermenstrual bleeding refers to bleeding that occurs during the middle of the menstrual cycle . Metrorrhagia in a woman over 40 years warrants a dilatation and curettage procedure to rule out endometrial cancer. This is associated with fibroids in 3% of cases . Polymenorrhoea in a patient with fibroids occurs when she has polycystic ovaries or pelvic inflammatory disease (PID). Progressive menorrhagia is seen in intramural and submucous myoma due to increased vascularity, endometrial hyperplasia , and an enlarged uterine cavity. Note : Further the distance of the fibroid from the cavity, lesser is the possibility of menorrhagia. For this reason, subserous and pedunculated fibroids do not cause menorrhagia.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 46-year-old woman presented with heavy menstrual bleeding and dysmenorrhea. You suspect a diagnosis of submucous uterine fibroids. Which of the following investigations will help you confirm this?
mcqs.explanation: Investigations required to identify submucous fibroids include : • USG - most commonly done. Transvaginal USG is useful to assess the location, dimension, and associated adnexal pathology . • MRI gives better soft tissue details but is not routinely done • Saline infusion sonography and hysteroscopy - help to visualise submucous fibroid more clearly • Laparoscopy - If uterus <12 weeks size and associated pelvic pain and infertility and to detect pelvic endometriosis and tubal pathology . • Uterine curettage – A bump is felt in submucous fibroid during endometrial curettage . Dilatation and curettage is done in patients presenting with postmenopausal bleeding . • Hysterosalpingography – A filling defect is seen . CT abdomen is not very useful for the identification of submucous fibroids. These cannot be visualised on colposcopy either . The image below shows the ultrasonographic appearance of a submucous fibroid (asterisk):628 The image given below shows hysteroscopic view of a submucous fibroid:

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An adnexal mass seen on ultrasound in a 38-year-old woman was diagnosed to be a secondary broad ligament fibroid. Which of the following is true about the same?

options.a: It arises from the broad ligament
options.b: The uterine vessels always lie medial to it
options.c: The ureter always lies lateral to it
options.d: It is also known as true broad ligament fibroid

mcqs.explanation: The ureter and uterine vessels lie lateral to a secondary broad ligament fibroid. There are 2 types of broad ligament fibroids: Primary broad ligament fibroid: • It is also known as true broad ligament fibroid. • The arise from: • Uterosacral ligament • Round ligament629 • Tissues in the broad ligament • Relations: • The uterine vessels lie medial to it. • The ureter is usually beneath the fibroid. However, it can be present anywhere in relation to it. Secondary broad ligament fibroid: • It is also known as false broad ligament fibroid. • They arise from the lateral wall of the uterus or cervix, but grow laterally , between the two layers of the broad ligament . • Relations - the uterine vessels and ureter lie lateral to it.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about fibroids?

options.b: Hyaline degeneration begins at the centre

mcqs.explanation: Fibroid calcification begins at the periphery and spreads inwards along the vessels . A typical myoma is a well -circumscribed tumor with a pseudo -capsule and firm in consistency . Its cut surface has a whorled appearance . The vessels that supply blood to the tumor lie in the capsule and send radial branches into the tumor. Therefore, the central portion of the tumour receives the least blood supply , and degeneration is noticeable early in this part of the tumour. However, fibroid calcification begins at the periphery . The image given below show the gross appearance of fibroids.The below image shows the histological appearance of fibroids.630

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with a history of miscarriage underwent a myomectomy . The specimen is shown below . Where does the degenerative change shown here begin from?
mcqs.explanation: The given specimen shows red degeneration of fibroid. Degeneration is most likely to start from the centre of the fibroid. In a fibroid, centre of the tumor is the least vascular part and hence degeneration is more common here. The only exception is calcareous degeneration where phosphates and carbonates of lime are deposited in the periphery along the course of the vessels .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 44-year-old woman presenting with acute abdominal pain had previously been diagnosed with uterine fibroids. Which of the following complications is most unlikely to have occurred here?
mcqs.explanation: Hyaline degeneration of fibroids is unlikely here as it is usually painless and presents as an abdominal mass causing distension and heaviness. Acute pain in fibroids is seen in the case of: • Fibroid torsion • Hemorrhage into the fibroid • Red degeneration • Sarcomatous change - seen in postmenopausal women.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A primigravida presented with severe abdominal pain and fever at 28 weeks of gestation . Ultrasound reveals a healthy fetus in utero and a large submucosal fibroid with multiple, hyperechoic areas within. Blood investigations reveal leukocytosis and a raised ESR. What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of red degeneration of fibroid. It is most common during the second trimester of pregnancy. The gross appearance is described as follows :631 • Fishy odor • Thrombosis of subcapsular vessels and vessels within the fibroid • Purplish-red color due to diffusion of blood pigments from the thrombosed vessels . Red degeneration presents with acute abdominal pain, fever and, vomiting. Investigations reveal leukocytosis and a raised ESR. On radiology, the hemorrhagic areas appear hyperechoic within the fibroid. The image given below shows the MRI appearance of red degeneration of fibroidsOption B: Torsion of subserous pedunculated fibroid presents with severe pain abdomen, but fever and leukocytosis are absent. Option C: Infection is more common in puerperium and presents with blood-stained vaginal discharge. Option D: Sarcomatous changes occur very rarely, and are unlikely in patients <40 years of age . They are more commonly seen in post -menopausal women.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 34-year old woman with a history of fibroids presented with 1.5 months of amenorrhea. UPT is positive. Which of the following complications will you not expect in this patient?
mcqs.explanation: Fetal malformations have not been recorded to occur due to fibroids. Pregnancy complications due to fibroids are: • Increased risk of abortion or miscarriage • Preterm labor • Abnormal presentation • Fibroid degeneration (Red degenaration ) • Accidental hemorrhage • Dystocic labor632 • Postpartum hemorrhage • Puerperal sepsis • Uterine inversion

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following changes are not seen in fibroids?
mcqs.explanation: Squamous metaplasia is not seen in fibroid.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: CT pelvis of a woman with fibroids is shown below . Which type of degeneration is seen here?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows womb-stone appearance on CT, suggestive of calcific degeneration of fibroid. These are also called calcareous myomas and are seen in old patients with long-standing myomas. This occurs due to the deposition calcium phosphates and calcium carbonates in the periphery of the fibroid, along the course of the vessels . It is easily visualized on radiography.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the least common secondary change seen in fibroids?
mcqs.explanation: Sarcomatous change is the least common secondary change in fibroids. Its incidence is <0.5%. Sarcomatous change leads to the development of malignant leiomyosarcomas. This is seen in postmenopausal women and is rare in women <40 years of age . Intramural and submucous tumors have a higher potential for sarcomatous change than subserous tumors. Its gross appearance is described as follows : • Soft consistency • Yellowish -grey • Hemorrhagic spots seen Radiology shows dark , irregular areas and air levels within the fibroid. These are indicative of sarcomatous change. The image given below shows the CT appearance of a large fibroid that has undergone sarcomatous change. The image on the right shows a fluid level within the tumor.633

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 46-year-old woman presents with a lower abdominal mass for the past 2 years. She had undergone uterine artery embolisation for fibroids 5 years ago. Ultrasound showed a homogeneous mass near the uterine fundus . On exploratory laparotomy, the mass was observed to be attached to the greater omentum and it was excised . Histopathology of the mass is shown below . What is your diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of a parasitic fibroid. The given histopathological image shows interlacing bundles of uniform spindle -shaped smooth muscle cells with blunted nuclei that are characteristic of a fibroid. A parasitic fibroid or a wandering fibroid gets cut off from its uterine origin and derives its blood supply from the vessels of the organ it is attached to. Thus, it can continue to grow in spite of uterine artery embolisation . It is managed by complete resection . Option A: Pedunculated fibroids have a pedicle with which they 're attached to the myometrium. Option C: Leiomyosarcoma commonly presents in postmenopausal women with sudden increase in size and postmenopausal bleeding . It would show nuclear atypia on histology . Option D: Disseminated intraperitoneal leiomyomatosis involves large areas of sub peritoneal surfaces . It is seen during pregnancy and while on oral contraceptives .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman with a fibroid uterus develops severe acute pain abdomen at 28 weeks of gestation . There is no history of fever and the WBC count is 8000 cells /mL . The most likely diagnosis is:
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of severe acute abdominal pain without fever/leucocytosis in a pregnant woman with a fibroid is suggestive of fibroid torsion. The incidence of fibroid in pregnancy is about 1 in 1,000 . Due to increased vascularity in pregnancy, the fibroid increases in size and becomes softer . The torsion is seen in the subserous pedunculated fibroid where the venous return is blocked at its site of attachment in the uterus . This leads to severe acute abdominal pain. Due to the complication being more local than systemic , fever or leucocytosis are generally not seen . A transvaginal ultrasonogram is immediately done to detect the position and size of the fibroid, which is followed by laparotomic myomectomy as a part of emergency surgical management.634 Other options : Option A: Red degeneration of fibroid is seen commonly in the second half of pregnancy or puerperium . It is due to a hemorrhagic infarction of the tissue and typically presents as acute focal abdominal pain with fever and leucocytosis . Treatment is usually conservative with bed rest, analgesics , and sedatives . Option B: Preterm labor is where the labor starts before 37 completed weeks . It is characterized by true labor pain. The abdominal pain is slowly increasing in intensity and duration and is also accompanied by show (expulsion of the cervical mucus plug ). There are intervals between episodes of contractions where the patient doesn 't complain of abdominal pain.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A primigravida at 24 weeks presents to you for a routine antenatal checkup . On ultrasound, you incidentally note the presence of two 3x3cm submucosal fibroids. How will you manage this case?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of an uncomplicated fibroid during pregnancy. These are managed conservatively. Surgery is only indicated in the case of a pedunculated fibroid undergoes torsion.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old woman presented with menorrhagia and increased frequency of micturition. Ultrasound abdomen shows the following picture . Which of the following drugs is not used in the management of her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario and ultrasound image showing a well -defined , heterogeneous hypoechoic mass are suggestive of a uterine fibroid. Misoprostol does not help to reduce the size of the fibroid and so is not recommended for its management. Medical management of fibroids helps to reduce their size. The drugs used in therapy are as follows : • Antiprogesterone – Mifepristone / RU-486 • GnRH analogs • Agonists – goserelin , leuprorelin , nafarelin, buserelin • Antagonists – cetrorelix, ganirelix • Levonorgestrel releasing intrauterine system • Selective progesterone receptor modulator (SPRM) – Asoprisnil • Danazol - usually not used due to androgenic side effects .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient diagnosed with leiomyoma was prescribed an intranasal spray to manage her disease . Which of the following drugs is it unlikely to contain?
mcqs.explanation: The nasal spray is unlikely to contain histrelin, as it is only available as a subcutaneous implant. GnRH analogues are used to treat leiomyomas . Intranasal preparations are available for leuprolide , nafarelin, and buserelin . However, leuprolide has maximal action as an intramuscular injection.635 GnRH analogue therapy in fibroids is given as follows : • Leuprolide acetate (Lupron) - given intramuscularly. It is also available as an intranasal spray, but isn't commonly used . • Goserelin (Zoladex) - subcutaneous depot implant • Triptorelin (Trelstar) IM injection • Nafarelin and buserelin - given as intranasal sprays bd • Histrelin - available as subcutaneous implants.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman was diagnosed with red degeneration of fibroid at 26 weeks of gestation . What is the next step in her management?
mcqs.explanation: Red degeneration of fibroid is managed conservatively with bed rest and analgesics . It is most common during the second trimester of pregnancy. Red degeneration presents with acute abdominal pain, fever and, vomiting. Investigations reveal leukocytosis and a raised ESR. On radiology, the hemorrhagic areas appear hyperechoic within the fibroid.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old woman presented with anemia due to heavy menstrual bleeding in spite of medical management of fibroids. She was posted for a myomectomy as she wanted to have children in the future . Which of the following is not an indication for this procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: Red degeneration is not an indication of myomectomy . It is conservatively managed. Myomectomy is indicated in the following: • Symptoms compromising the quality of life such as: • Heavy menstrual bleeding , causing anemia • Pelvic pain • Urinary symptoms and ureteric obstruction. • The patient is unwilling for hysterectomy • The patient wishes to preserve childbearing function • Fibroids causing infertility

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following modalities is not used for the treatment of leiomyomas ?
mcqs.explanation: Ultrasound -guided transcervical metroplasty is not used in the treatment of leiomyomas . It is used for the resection of the uterine septum . Uterine artery embolization/Uterine fibroid embolization (UAE /UFE ) is an angiographic interventional procedure that delivers polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) microspheres or other synthetic particulate emboli into both uterine arteries thus producing ischemia and necrosis. The vessels serving leiomyomas have a larger caliber, hence these microspheres are preferentially directed to the tumors, thus sparing the surrounding myometrium.636 Nd:YAG myolysis is laparoscopic myolysis performed with an Nd:YAG laser. It causes coagulation of a subserous fibroid. The below image shows uterine artery embolization.Magnetic Resonance guided Focused Ultrasound (MRgFUS ) is also called MR-guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (MR-HIFU). Ultrasound energy is focused to heat and incite coagulative necrosis in selected myomas. Concurrent MR imaging enables precise targeting and provides real-time tissue temperature feedback to limit surrounding thermal injury. The given image shows MRgFUS .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The following procedure was planned for a patient with uterine fibroids. Which of the following statements is false about this procedure ?

options.a: Can be done in nulliparous women
options.b: Ovarian failure is one of the complications

mcqs.explanation: 637 The given image shows uterine artery embolization (UAE ). UAE cannot be done in nulliparous women as embolization of ovarian vessels can cause ovarian failure and premature menopause . Under local sedation , bilateral UAE is approached through percutaneous femoral catheterization . Embolization is done by releasing polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), gel foam particles or metal coils into the uterine artery.638

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following accurately describes Sampson's theory for endometriosis ?
mcqs.explanation: Sampson's theory describes the implantation of endometrial tissue due to retrograde menstruation. The various theories for the etiology of endometriosis include : Given below is an illustration showing retrograde menstrual flow that is leading to the development of patches of endometriosis .645 Theory Mechanism Sampson's implantation theo ry Reflux of menstrual endomet rium and subsequent implant ation in the surrounding stru ctures Theory of coelomic metaplasi a by Meyer and Ivanoff Metaplastic changes in embr yonic mesothelium which res pond to hormone stimulation Metastatic theory by Halban Embolization of menstrual fr agments through vascular an d lymphatic channels Theory of histogenesis by ind uction Induction of undifferentiated peritoneal cells to endometri al tissue by an endogenous fa ctor

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about endometriosis ?

options.c: In utero exposure to DES increases risk
options.d: Most common site is the cervix

mcqs.explanation: The most common site of occurrence of endometriosis is the ovary . Endometriosis of the ovary is known as endometrioma. By definition , endometriosis is the occurrence of benign endometrial tissue (glands and stroma) outside the cavity of the uterus . Endometriosis can occur anywhere in the body (except spleen ) including the abdominal wall, lung, pleura , brain , etc . It is a proliferative, hormone-dependent disease of the childbearing period . Women between the age groups of 30-40 years are most commonly affected . Risk factors for endometriosis are as follows : • Family history (7-10x risk with a 1st-degree relative) • Nulliparity646 • In utero exposure to Diethylstilbestrol (DES) • Estrogen dependent conditions/Estrogen therapy • Immunological factor - Impaired T cell and NK cell activity and altered immunology in a woman may increase the susceptibility to proliferation and growth .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common symptom associated with endometriosis ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common symptom of endometriosis is dysmenorrhea. Pain begins before the onset of menstruation and builds up continuously until the flow starts. Thereafter , the pain gradually declines. This pattern of pain is called triple dysmenorrhea.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In a patient diagnosed with endometriosis , which of the following symptoms would you not expect ?
mcqs.explanation: Patients diagnosed with endometriosis are not likely to present with vaginal discharge . Clinical features of endometriosis include : • About 30% of the patients are asymptomatic . • The classic symptom complex includes : • Dysmenorrhoea • Dyspareunia • Menorrhagia • Infertility (30-40%) • Dysmenorrhoea - most common symptom • Dyspareunia - occurs when the pouch of Douglas and rectovaginal septum are involved. • Deep -seated pelvic pain • Premenstrual and postmenstrual spotting

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old lady presented with complaints of severe pain on menstruation and heavy flow . She is subsequently diagnosed with endometriosis . The pain in this condition mainly correlates with_____
mcqs.explanation: Pain in endometriosis mainly correlates with the depth of penetration . Lesions penetrating more than 5mm are responsible for pain, dysmenorrhea and dyspareunia . The dysmenorrhea associated with endometriosis precedes menses by 24 to 48 hours and is less responsive to NSAIDs and combined OCPs.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Arrange the following sites of endometriosis in the order of frequency of occurrence.
mcqs.explanation: 647 The sites of endometriosis arranged in the order of frequency of occurrence are: Ovary > Pouch of Douglas > Broad ligament > Uterosacral ligament > Fallopian tube . Endometriotic lesions have been identified on all organs except the spleen .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A middle -aged woman presented with dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia , and infertility . On examination , you note tender nodularity of the uterosacral ligaments . Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with the tender nodularity of the uterosacral ligament points towards a diagnosis of endometriosis . The nodularity of the uterosacral ligament in endometriosis gives rise to the cobblestone appearance seen on laparoscopy . This is referred to as 'sine qua non of endometriosis '. The below image shows the cobblestone appearance of the uterosacral ligament .Note : Endometrioma or chocolate cyst is endometriosis of the ovary . It presents as an adnexal mass.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young woman presented to your clinic with complaints of painful menstruation and postmenstrual spotting . On examination, you note tender nodules in the posterior fornix and a fixed retroverted uterus . Which of the following is the gold standard investigation to confirm the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of dysmenorrhea with tender nodules in the posterior fornix and a retroverted uterus is suggestive of endometriosis . The gold standard investigation for the diagnosis of this condition is a visual inspection by laparoscopy , preferably with histological confirmation. It is also the investigation of choice for the condition. Role of laparoscopy in endometriosis : • Detect and diagnose pelvic endometriosis • Locate the site of endometriosis and staging • To take biopsy648 • To surgically treat endometriosis by ablation Other investigations for endometriosis include : • Estimation of CA-125 levels - raised in endometriosis . • Estimation of MCP-1 (Monocyte chemotactic protein) levels - raised in the peritoneal fluid of women with endometriosis .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A diagnostic laparoscopy was performed on a 27-year-old woman with severe dysmenorrhoea and dyspareunia . The following finding was seen on the pelvic peritoneum . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history and the image showing characteristic powder burn spots seen over the pelvic peritoneum on laparoscopy point toward a diagnosis of pelvic endometriosis . On laparoscopy , the typical endometriotic lesions appear like small black, dark brown or bluish dots. These are called powder burns or gunshot appearance of the serosal surfaces of the peritoneum . They are nodules or small cysts containing old haemorrhages surrounded by a variable degree of fibrosis. Subtle appearances of endometriosis seen on laparoscopy are: • Red flame-shaped areas • Red polypoid areas • Yellow -brown patches • White peritoneal plaques or scarring • Peritoneal defects - known as Allen Masters Syndrome • Subovarian adhesions . The lesions mentioned above are thought to be more active than the powder burn areas. Endometriotic lesions in the peritoneal cavity contain yellowish -brown fluid . This fluid contains prostaglandins that are responsible for the pain associated with this condition. Endometriosis of the ovary leads to formation of the chocolate cyst which is a true cyst with columnar epithelium lining. The image below shows the laparoscopic appearance of endometriotic lesions in the pouch of Douglas and on the right, the sacrouterine ligament . Dyspareunia occurs when the pouch of Douglas and rectovaginal septum are involved.649

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In endometriotic lesion, histology represents its:
mcqs.explanation: In endometriotic lesions , histology represents its high estrogen activity. Endometriosis is defined by the presence of "ectopic " endometrial tissue at a site outside of the uterus . Endometriosis is a proliferative hormone-dependent disease of the childbearing period . It is extremely rare before menarche and disappears after menopause . The endometriotic implants show certain differences when compared to normal endometrium . There is increased production of estrogen by endometriotic stromal cells due to high levels of the enzyme aromatase. This is absent in normal endometrial stroma. Management of endometriosis :650

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following operative procedures are least likely to be followed by scar endometriosis?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given operative procedures , hysterectomy is least likely to be followed by scar endometriosis. Operations most likely to be followed by scar endometriosis are: • Hysterotomy • Classical Cesarean section • Myomectomy • Ventrofixation (fixing uterus to the abdominal wall) • Episiotomy

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 39-year-old nulliparous woman presented with dysmenorrhea and a progressively growing, painless abdominal mass. USG scan revealed a cystic lesion of the left ovary which was excised . The below image shows the excised specimen . Which of the following statements is false about this condition?

options.a: It is seen in endometriosis of ovary
options.b: It is lined by columnar epithelium
options.c: It is usually a bilateral condition
options.d: It is a malignant cystic lesion

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history and the image is suggestive of a chocolate cyst of the ovary which is a benign cystic lesion. Chocolate cysts of the ovary are a manifestation of endometriosis . Both the ovaries are usually affected . On histology , the cyst is lined by columnar epithelium . Pseudoxanthoma cells are present which are large macrophages or scavenger cells that appear brown in colour due to ingested blood pigments such as haemosiderin. They are polyhedral in shape and resemble lutein cells . Given below is a gross image of the chocolate cyst of the ovary .Given below is a histopathological section of an endometriotic lesion showing the pseudoxanthoma cells .651

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient is being evaluated for chronic abdominal pain. Her lab reports revealed elevated CA-125 levels . Which of the following conditions is the least likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: CA-125 levels are not expected to be elevated in malignant pancreatic tumours. CA-125 is a glycoprotein and cell surface antigen. Its levels are raised in the following conditions: • Abdominal or pelvic tuberculosis • Pelvic inflammatory disease • Endometriosis • Malignant epithelial ovarian tumour • Chronic liver disease • 2% of normal women, especially during menstruation. Endometrioma refers to ovarian endometriosis . CA-125 levels are raised to more than 35 U/mL in 80% of cases of endometriosis . The level is directly proportional to the extent of the disease .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman with dyspareunia is diagnosed to have endometriosis . Which of the following drugs is not useful for her treatment ?
mcqs.explanation: Estrogen is not used in the treatment of endometriosis as the condition is estrogen -dependent . For minimal disease , the drug of choice is NSAIDs. Oral contraceptive pills are given if associated menstrual complaints are present . OCPs inhibit gonadotropin release and decrease the menstrual flow . For moderate to severe disease , oral progestogens are the first drugs to be started . They are known to antagonize estrogenic effects on the endometrium causing endometrial atrophy. The drug of choice is GnRH agonists.652 Note : The best time to conceive in a patient with endometriosis is immediately after surgery.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with endometriosis requires treatment with GnRH analogues . She is scared of injections so you plan to prescribe a nasal preparation for her. Which of the following GnRH agonists could you prescribe ?
mcqs.explanation: The GnRH agonist available as a nasal preparation for the treatment of endometriosis is nafarelin. GnRH analogues are used in the management of endometriosis and are given by continuous administration. This suppresses the secretion of pituitary gonadotropins and leads to atrophy of the endometrial tissue in 90% of cases. Leuprolide and triptorelin are GnRH agonists which are given IM. Goserelin is available as a depot preparation.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding adenomyosis ?
mcqs.explanation: Patients with adenomyosis commonly present with symptoms of menorrhagia and dysmenorrhea. Adenomyosis (endometriosis interna) is the ingrowth of stromal and glandular components of the endometrium directly into the myometrium. It usually occurs following vigorous curettage , repeated childbirth or in conditions with an excess of estrogen . Adenomyosis is more common in multiparous women aged 40 years and above. They commonly present with menorrhagia and dysmenorrhea. Other symptoms include pelvic discomfort, backache and dyspareunia . On per-vaginal examination, there is a gross symmetrical enlargement of the uterus corresponding to 12 -14 weeks size. The uterus is soft and tender on bimanual examination. This is known as Halban's sign. Diagnosis is mainly based on clinical assessment . A diagnostic hysteroscopy combined with curettage is the initial step in the management because of menorrhagia. Total hysterectomy is the treatment of choice . Localised excision and levonorgestrel containing IUCD can be tried in younger patients .653 The image below is an illustration of adenomyosis .The image below shows adenomyosis as seen during laparoscopy . The uterus is soft and enlarged ; the blue spots represent subserous endometriosis .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with menorrhagia and backache is diagnosed with adenomyosis . Which of the following is not associated with this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Adenomyosis is not associated with sub involution of the uterus . Uterine subinvolution is impaired or retarded involution of the uterus . It is associated with uterine fibroid, cesarean section and conditions causing overdistension of the uterus like twin pregnancies or polyhydramnios. Adenomyosis often coexists with the following conditions: • Uterine fibromyomas654 • Pelvic endometriosis (15%) • Endometrial carcinoma

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 43-year-old multiparous woman presented with menorrhagia and secondary dysmenorrhea. On examination, Halban's sign was positive . The transvaginal USG findings are given below . Which of the following is the definitive treatment for her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette and the transvaginal ultrasound(TVS) showing the Venetian blind appearance is suggestive of adenomyosis . The definitive treatment for adenomyosis is hysterectomy . Adenomyosis (endometriosis interna) is the ingrowth of stromal and glandular components of the endometrium directly into the myometrium. Diagnosis is mainly based on clinical assessment . Painful, symmetrical enlargement of the uterus is suggestive of adenomyosis . On bimanual examination, the uterus is softened and tender . This is known as Halban's sign. TVS findings include salt and pepper appearance of the myometrium and the presence of subendometrial striations producing the Venetian blind appearance . MRI can also be done for diagnosis. However, the only definitive mode of diagnosis is histopathological examination. Since most women affected by the condition are past the childbearing age , total hysterectomy is the treatment of choice . Localized excision/Levonorgestrel containing IUCD can be tried in younger women.The image below is of a sagittal MRI showing a uterus with adenomyosis in the posterior wall. Gross enlargement of the posterior wall is noted , with many foci of hyperintensity .655

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young lady who presented with oligomenorrhea and infertility is diagnosed with PCOS. Mutation of which of the following genes can cause this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Mutation of the CYP21 gene can cause polycystic ovarian syndrome.662 The gene for 21 -hydroxylase (CYP21 ) is located in the short arm of chromosome 6. Heterozygosity of the gene has been linked to the development of PCOS. Defects in this gene also lead to congenital adrenal hyperplasia .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A teenage girl presented with complaints of excessive growth of coarse hair on her jawline and upper lip. Which of the following is the most common cause for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history of excessive growth of coarse hair is suggestive of hirsutism. The most common cause for hirsutism in female patients is polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS). Hirsutism is defined as excessive growth of androgen-dependent sexual hair or male distribution of hair in female patients . PCOS accounts for 70-80% of the cases of hirsutism, which typically begins in late adolescence or the early 20s . Idiopathic hirsutism is the second most frequent cause . The most common rapid onset of hirsutism in young females is a testosterone -producing tumour like granulosa cell or Sertoli-Leydig cell tumours. Other less common causes of hirsutism include : • Late-onset congenital adrenal hyperplasia • Tumours of the ovary and adrenal gland • Cushing's syndrome • Drug-induced Virilisation : Characterized by more extensive androgen-induced changes than hirsutism alone. It has the following features : • Acne • Increased oily skin • Temporal balding • Clitoromegaly • Deepening of the voice • Development of male muscular pattern and body habitus • Atrophy of breasts Hypertrichosis : Excessive growth of non-sexual hair.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A mother brought her 15-year-old daughter to the OPD with concerns of excessive growth of coarse hair over her face and chest . Which scoring system is used to clinically grade this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of hirsutism. The Ferriman -Gallwey score is used to clinically assess and quantify the degree of hirsutism. Within this system , abnormal hair distribution is assessed at nine body areas and each of them scored from 0-4. Increasing numeric scores correspond to greater hair density within a given area. The maximum score is 36. The degree of hirsutism is mild if the score is \0318. Moderate to663 severe hirsutism is present if the score is \03115. Note : Ferriman Gallwey score originally had 11 sites which were modified later to exclude 2 sites , viz., forearm, and legs .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions is the Rotterdam criteria used to diagnose ?
mcqs.explanation: The Rotterdam criteria is used to diagnose Stein-Levinthal syndrome or PCOS. ESHRE/ASRM or Rotterdam criteria (2003 ): Any two out of these three must be present - • Clinical/ Biochemical hyperandrogenism • Oligo /anovulation • Polycystic ovaries Other criteria used for diagnosing PCOS: • National Institute of Health (NIH) criteria (1990 ) • To include both • Clinical/Biochemicalhyperandrogenism • Oligo /anovulation • Androgen excess and PCOS society (AE-PCOS) criteria: • To include both: • Clinical/Biochemicalhyperandrogenism • Oligo /anovulation/polycystic ovaries Option A: Meig 's syndrome refers to ascites and pleural effusions that accompany a benign ovarian tumor. Option B: Asherman's syndrome refers to the formation of intrauterine synechiae , usually following endometrial destructive procedures like curettage or ablation. Option C: Mayer-Rokitansky-K\374ster-Hauser syndrome is characterised by congenital absence of vagina, primary amenorrhoea, rudimentary cornua uteri and morphologically normal ovaries and Fallopian tubes situated on the pelvic sidewall .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An adolescent girl was brought by her mother to the clinic with complaints of irregular periods and acne. A USG scan was performed which showed the following finding. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history and the necklace appearance on ultrasound are suggestive of polycystic ovarian disease . The original Rotterdam consensus defined polycystic ovaries when \03112 follicles were seen per ovary on USG. Each follicle should measure between 2 and 9 mm, and/or an ovarian volume should be >10 ml. Due to improvement in imaging modalities since that time, the threshold for664 follicle number has now been raised to 20 per ovary .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old woman who presented with complaints of irregular cycles and weight gain was diagnosed with PCOS. This condition is characterised by multiple ovarian cysts that are less than _____ in size.
mcqs.explanation: PCOS is characterised by multiple small ovarian cysts , each less than 1 cm in size. Sonographic findings seen in PCOS are: • \031 12 small cysts of 2 to 9 mm in diameter. • Increased ovarian volume (> 10 mL ) or both. A single ovary with these findings is sufficient to define PCOS. However, this criteria does not apply to women taking combined oral contraceptive pills . Note : In settings with improved sonographic imaging resolution , a follicle number \031 20 cysts per ovary can be considered significant for PCOS.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 29-year-old lady presented to your clinics with lesions as shown in the below images. Which of the following is a false statement regarding her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The hyperpigmented areas in the given image are acanthosis nigricans and this is associated with hyperinsulinemia. This skin condition is thought to be a cutaneous marker of insulin resistance . Acanthosis nigricans is a velvety, darkening of the skin that usually occurs in the intertriginous areas. It has poorly defined borders, usually occurs in skin fold areas, such as the back of the neck, axilla, and groin, and may include thickening of the skin. The pathogenesis of acanthosis nigricans is linked to growth factor levels and insulin-mediated activation of insulin-like growth factor (IGF) on keratinocytes and increased growth factor levels . Acanthosis nigricans is usually seen in people younger than 40 years of age and is associated with the following disorders: • Obesity • Hypothyroidism • Acromegaly • Polycystic ovary disease • Insulin-resistant diabetes • Cushing's disease • Addison's disease • Gastrointestinal malignancies such as adenocarcinoma of the stomach or pancreas. The treatment for acanthosis nigricans is directed towards the management of the underlying cause .665

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old female patient presented with hirsutism. After further evaluation, a diagnosis of HAIR -AN syndrome was made. Which of the following statements is false regarding this condition?
mcqs.explanation: HAIR -AN syndrome is not characterized by mild hyperandrogenism but marked hyperandrogenism (HA). It also includes insulin resistance (IR ) and acanthosis nigricans (AN). HAIR -AN syndrome and ovarian hyperthecosis are exaggerated phenotypes of polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS). Women affected by HAIR -AN syndrome often present with symptoms of severe hyperandrogenism (hirsutism, acne) and may occasionally display signs of virilization like clitoromegaly , temporal balding and voice deepening . Ovarian hyperthecosis is a rare condition characterized by nests of luteinized theca cells distributed throughout the ovarian stroma.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young lady being evaluated for infertility is diagnosed to have PCOS. Which of the following lab findings would you not expect to see in her?
mcqs.explanation: A depressed HDL level and elevated total cholesterol :HDL ratios are seen in patients with PCOS. The following are associated with PCOS: • Insulin resistance • Impaired glucose tolerance and type 2 diabetes mellitus • Dyslipidemia: Increased LDL and triglyceride levels , elevated total cholesterol levels :HDL ratios. • Infertility/subfertility • A three -fold increased risk of endometrial cancer • Mild elevations in testosterone levels <200 ng/dL Normal range of testosterone in women is 20 -70 ng/dL. A mild elevation in testosterone is consistent with the diagnosis of PCOS. However, values > 200 ng/dL may suggest an ovarian tumour and warrant pelvic sonography.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A teenage girl who recently got diagnosed with PCOS presented with skin lesions on her forehead as shown in the image below . On examination, hirsutism was also noted . Which of the following drugs would you prescribe to this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The lesions shown in the image are acne. The drugs used to treat acne and hirsutism in a patient with PCOS are OCPs with cyproterone acetate . The first step in the management of PCOS is weight reduction . OCPs are the drugs of choice for regularisation of cycles . They are also the drugs of choice for hirsutism and acne. OCPs used for PCOS should contain a 3rd/4th generation progestagen like cyproterone acetate . OCPs induce regular menstrual cycles , lower androgen levels and causes thinning of the endometrium . Insulin sensitizers like metformin have been found to improve metabolic and gynecologic issues . It acts by reducing the insulin level and reducing hepatic production of glucose (liver neoglycolysis ). Other benefits of metformin include improvement in fertility rate and reduction of the total and free testosterone levels . It also increases levels of sex hormone-binding globulin . Metformin is contraindicated in hepatic and renal disease .666 Treatment of infertility associated with PCOS is done using ovulation-inducing drugs like letrozole and clomiphene citrate. If medical management fails, surgical options like laparoscopic ovarian drilling can be considered . Note : FOGSI, in 2024 , has replaced Letrozole as the first-line drug for induction of ovulation in patients with PCOS. However, the FDA approval for the same is still pending .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 31 -year-old lady has been unable to conceive for the past 2 years in spite of regular intercourse . She has recently been diagnosed with PCOS. Which of the following is the FDA approved medication that you could recommend to her?
mcqs.explanation: Clomiphene is an FDA approved drug used for the treatment of infertility associated with PCOS. Clomiphene induces ovulation in 80% of the cases and 40–50% patients conceive. However, abortions are common due to luteal phase defects . Ovarian hyperstimulation occurs in <1% cases . Co-administration with dexamethasone leads to better outcomes . In resistant case, tamoxifen 20 –40 mg daily for 5 days should be tried. Currently, letrozole has proven to be more effective in ovarian infertility in obese women but its use in such cases is pending FDA approval.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In a patient diagnosed with PCOS, which of the following is not an indication for surgical management ?
mcqs.explanation: Surgical management is indicated in all the above conditions except for morbid obesity . Indications of surgery in PCOS include: • Failed medical therapy • Ovarian hyperstimulation • Infertility • Previous pregnancy losses Surgery comprises of laparoscopic drilling or puncture of not more than four cysts in each ovary . It is done using a laser or by unipolar electrocautery . It restores the endocrine milieu and improves fertility for a year or so. Thereafter, pelvic adhesions caused by surgery may again reduce the fertility rate. The formation of adhesions can be reduced by hydrofloatation . The advantages of surgery are as follows : • Tubal testing with chromotubation can be performed simultaneously • Other causes of infertility like endometriosis can be looked for • One-time treatment • Intense and prolonged monitoring for side effects is not required • Cost-effective compared to IVF • Reduces androgen and LH production667 • Following surgery, single ovulation occurs with drugs, and hyperstimulation and multiple pregnancies are avoided • Ovulation occurs in 80–90% and pregnancy in 60–70% The disadvantages of surgery are as follows : • It involves giving anaesthesia and performing an invasive procedure like laparoscopy • Adhesions may form postoperatively • If cautery is used , premature ovarian failure due to destruction of ovarian tissue may be seen

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman with a history of infertility is on treatment with human menopausal gonadotropin. She presented with the following finding in the USG. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The image showing enlarged ovaries with multiple large cysts along with the history of treatment for infertility with human menopausal gonadotropin suggests the diagnosis of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS). Human menopausal gonadotropin (HMG) is a medication that is composed of FSH and LH . It is used to stimulate the release of ova in women who do not ovulate spontaneously . It can lead to ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. Ovarian Hyperstimulation Syndrome (OHSS) is a condition associated with ovarian enlargement due to exogenous gonadotropin therapy . Symptoms include abdominal pain, distention , ascites , gastrointestinal problems , respiratory compromise, oliguria, and thromboembolism. It can occur during ovulation induction or in early pregnancies conceived through exogenous ovarian stimulation. Predisposing factors for OHSS include multi-follicular ovaries (such as in PCOS), young age , high estradiol levels during ovulation induction, and pregnancy. Vasoactive substances produced by the corpus luteum , such as vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and angiotensin II , are believed to contribute to enhanced capillary permeability , resulting in the loss of fluid, protein, and electrolytes into the peritoneal cavity and hemoconcentration. Sonographic examination reveals enlarged ovaries with numerous follicular cysts and ascites . Maintaining fluid balance with isotonic fluids like normal saline is crucial. Strategies to prevent OHSS during exogenous ovulation include reducing follicular stimulation (low FSH dose ), coasting (withholding FSH administration one or more days prior to the hCG trigger), prophylactic volume expanders , and substituting hCG for FSH towards the end of ovarian stimulation. Other options : Option B: Theca lutein cysts are a rare form of follicular cysts characterized by luteinization and hypertrophy of the theca interna layer. Both ovaries are enlarged and cystic . This condition is commonly associated with gestational trophoblastic disease , multifetal gestation , and placentomegaly . Option C : Polycystic ovarian syndrome shows 12 or more small follicles each 2-9 mm in size placed peripherally (necklace pattern) (shown below ). The patient presents with menstrual668 irregularities , hirsutism, acne, etc .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 21 -year-old nulliparous woman presented with galactorrhoea and breast engorgement . Which of the following is a false statement regarding this condition?

options.a: Prolactin is the most important hormone involved in its pathophysiology
options.b: Prolactin levels more than 25 ng/ml cause this condition
options.c: All patients with hyperprolactinemia present with galactorrhoea
options.d: The drug of choice is Cabergoline

mcqs.explanation: All patients with hyperprolactinaemia do not present with galactorrhoea. Galactorrhoea is the secretion of milky fluid from the nipple which is unrelated to childbirth. Prolactin is the most important hormone involved in the pathophysiology of amenorrhoea and galactorrhoea. Majority of women (80%) with high prolactin levels present with galactorrhoea. However, some hyperprolactinemic women may not have this symptom . Normal prolactin level is 25 ng/mL and levels more than this can cause galactorrhoea. Levels up to 100 ng/mL occur in hyperprolactinaemia but prolactin level over 100 ng/mL is seen in pituitary tumours. Galactorrhoea is caused by pituitary adenoma and hyperprolactinemia . The condition is associated with amenorrhoea, oligomenorrhoea and infertility . The drug of choice for this condition is cabergoline .669

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about the rhythm method ?

options.a: Anencephaly is seen on accidental conception
options.b: It is a cost effective method
options.c: Safe period is determined using temperature or mucous method
options.d: Abstinence is required for 7-10 days in a month

mcqs.explanation: Anencephaly is not seen in the case of accidental conception in a woman using the rhythm method . It occurs due to deficiency of folic acid in the mother. The calendar method or the rhythm method is one of the natural methods of contraception by fertility awareness . The couple is advised avoidance of sexual intercourse around ovulation. Thus, it is very cost-effective but it can only be used by educated couples . According to this method , safe period in a normal 28-day cycle is from the 1st day of menstrual period to the 10th day and from the 18th to the 28th day. An alternate method is by calculating the risk period i.e., 3 days before and 3 days after ovulation. Ovulation can also be estimated by changes in cervical mucus and basal body temperature . Another method of calculating the safe period is the Knaus–Ogino method . The fertile period is determined by subtracting 18 days from the shortest cycle and 10 days from the longest cycle . This gives the first and the last day of the fertile period , respectively .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What does Billing's method of contraception refer to?
mcqs.explanation: Billing's method of contraception refers to the cervical mucus method . It is also called ovulation method . The properties of the cervical mucus change during the menstrual cycle . The female partner can predict the fertile period by examining her cervical mucus. Under the influence of estrogen , the mucus increases in quantity and becomes more slippery and elastic i.e. wet days. This continues till it reaches a peak. After this, under the influence of progesterone , it becomes thicker, scanty i.e. dry days. Abstinence is advised during the wet days till 4 days after the peak day. The safe period includes the dry days after menses till the appearance of mucus and from the 4th day after the peak day. The pattern of cervical mucus secretion during a menstrual cycle is given below .679

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the contraceptive shown in the given image.
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a female condom. It consists of a pouch made of polyurethane which is 17 cm in length with a flexible ring at each end. The inner ring at the closed end is smaller than the outer ring. The inner ring is inserted at the apex of the vagina and the outer ring remains outside . It covers the cervix, the entire vagina , and external genitalia . Hence , it provides protection against HIV and STDs. It has a failure rate of 5–15 per 100 woman-years, which is higher than that of a male condom. It can be fitted by the patient hours before intercourse , and easily removed soon after. It covers the cervix, vagina , and external genitalia and is protective against sexually transmitted diseases . It can also be worn in the puerperal period, unlike the cervical diaphragm. The female condom should not be used along with a male condom because if worn together they may slip, tear, or become displaced . The given image below shows the insertion of a female condom:

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A nulliparous woman has been using Today sponge as a contraceptive . What does this contain?
mcqs.explanation: Today sponge contains 1 g of nonoxynol 9. It is a mushroom-shaped polyurethane disposable sponge that is 2 inches wide and 1.25 inches thick. It is provided with a loop for easy removal. It should be placed high up in the vagina with the concave side covering the cervix. It can remain effective for 24 h. It can be used only once. It acts as a mechanical barrier preventing the entry of sperms into the cervical canal, absorbs semen, and contains a spermicidal agent. The failure rate is 9-16 per 100 woman-years.680

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a contraindication for the use of the contraceptive shown below ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a cervical diaphragm or Dutch cap. It can be used by women having multiple sex partners. Contraindications of cervical diaphragm usage : • Prolapse, cystocele , rectocele - accurate fitting is not possible • Recurrent urinary tract infection • Allergy to rubber or spermicidal agent It must be removed following intercourse as it can lead to toxic shock syndrome (TSS) if left in the vagina for a long period . TSS is caused by Streptococcus pyogenes or Staphylococcus aureus infection .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You are prescribing nonoxynol-9 jelly to a woman using a cervical diaphragm for contraception. What is its mechanism of action?
mcqs.explanation: Nonoxynol-9 is one of the spermicidal agents which act by disruption of the sperm cell membrane. Spermicidal agents are chemical contraceptives as they contain surfactants, such as nonoxynol-9, octoxynol, menfegol and enzyme-inhibiting agents . These are available as: • Foam tablets • Soluble pessaries • Creams • Jellies • Films681 The spermicidal agent remains effective for 1–2 hours after the application . They are always used along with other contraceptives such as the diaphragm, cervical cap, and condom. When they are used alone, the failure rate is high i.e., 30 per 100 woman-years. Chronic use of spermicides can cause vaginal irritation , abrasion, and ulceration. This increases the risk of HIV spread . Hence , spermicidal agents should not be recommended to HIV -positive couples .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young woman who is using a cervical diaphragm asks for an alternative contraceptive . You suggest a recently launched contraceptive Phexxi. What is its composition?

options.a: Lactic acid, Citric Acid, Potassium bitartrate
options.b: Ascorbic acid, Citric acid, Calcium bitartrate
options.c: Lactic acid, Ascorbic acid, Potassium bitartrate
options.d: Ascorbic acid, Lactic acid, Calcium bitartrate.

mcqs.explanation: Phexxi is a vaginal gel that contains lactic acid, citric acid, and potassium bitartrate. Phexxi is a vaginal pH regulator which is a non-hormonal contraceptive . It works by maintaining vaginal pH within the range of 3.5 to 4.5. This acidic environment is inhospitable for sperms. Phexxi comes in pre-filled vaginal applicators . A single dose must be applied before vaginal intercourse . If more than one act of vaginal intercourse occurs within one hour, an additional dose must be applied .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A newly married woman was prescribed Mala-N at a PHC. What is its composition?
mcqs.explanation: Mala-N is a combined oral contraceptive containing 0.15 mg levonorgestrel (LNG) and 0.03 mg ethinyl estradiol . It is supplied free of cost through all PHC's, urban family welfare centers , etc . All combined oral pills contain a mixture of ethinyl estradiol in a dose of 20 -30 mcg and an orally active progestogen . Mala-D has the same composition as Mala-N but is available at a price of Rs 3/- per packet . Combined oral pill works by suppressing pituitary hormones, FSH, and LH peak which prevents ovulation. At the same time, progestogen causes atrophic changes in the endometrium and682 prevents implantation. Progestogen also acts on the cervical mucus making it thick and tenacious and impenetrable by sperms. It also interferes with tubal motility and alters tubal transport. , so the fertilized egg reaches the uterine cavity before the endometrium is receptive for implantation. These tablets are taken starting on the first day of the cycle for 21 days. A new course of tablets should be commenced 7 days after the cessation of the previous course . They should be taken at bedtime , preferably after a meal.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an advantage of norgestimate OCPs?
mcqs.explanation: Norgestimate is one of the 3rd generation progesterone agents . All OCPs have the disadvantage of increasing the risk of venous thrombosis. Third-generation progesterone agents are less androgenic and so reduce the occurrence of acne and hirsutism. They also have a lower risk of metabolic and cardiovascular disorders compared to the previous generation progesterone agents . Benefits of combined pills : • Effective contraceptive • Useful in menorrhagia and polymenorrhoea • Relieves dysmenorrhoea and premenstrual tension • Prevents anaemia by reducing the menstrual loss • Lower incidence of benign breast neoplasia (fibrocystic disease ), functional ovarian cyst , ovarian and uterine malignancy • Reduced risk of PID - due to thick cervical mucus caused by progestogen , preventing the organisms from entering into the uterine cavity • Reduced incidence of ectopic pregnancy - due to suppression of ovulation and decreased risk of PID • Protects against rheumatoid arthritis • Reduces the risk of anorectal cancer • Useful in acne, PCOD, and endometriosis

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a contraindication to the use of OCPs?
mcqs.explanation: Thyroid disorders like hypothyroidism are not a contraindication for OCP usage . Contraindications of OCPs: • Absolute contraindications - • Breast and genital cancers683 • Liver disease • History of thromboembolism • Cardiac abnormalities • Congenital hyperlipidemia • Undiagnosed abnormal uterine bleeding • Relative contraindications - • Age over 40 years, if smoker >35 years • Mild hypertension • Chronic renal disease • Epilepsy • Migraine • First 6 months of breastfeeding • Diabetes mellitus • Gallbladder disease • History of infrequent bleeding or amenorrhea

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs do not lead to failure of OCPs?
mcqs.explanation: Sodium valproate is an inhibitor of CYP enzymes that are responsible for OCP metabolism . Thus, it does not lead to OCP failure. Drugs leading to OCP failure are : • Rifampicin • Tetracyclines - interferes with enterohepatic circulation of estrogen • Phenytoin • Phenobarbitone • Antifungals • Cephalosporin • Ritonavir for HIV - interferes with absorption of OCP Most of the anti-convulsants are enzyme inducers and hence increase the clearance of OCPs. This leads to OCP failure.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not the mechanism of action of progesterone only pills ?

options.c: Kills the sperms in the cervical canal

mcqs.explanation: Minipills or progesterone -only pills (POP) do not kill sperm in the cervical canal. Progesterone-only pills act by thickening the cervical mucus (the main mechanism of all POPs684 except cerazette ) that inhibits penetration of sperms, inhibiting tubal motility , and suppressing ovulation. Other advantages of POPs include a reduction in the incidence of pelvic inflammatory diseases and sexually transmitted diseases (due to thickened cervical mucus). Due to the inhibition of tubal motility , the absolute risk of all pregnancies including ectopic pregnancy decreases , while the relative risk of ectopic pregnancy increases. But a previous history of ectopic pregnancy is not a contraindication for POP. POPs do not affect clotting , lipid metabolism, and carbohydrate metabolism . So they can safely be used by women who are obese , breastfeeding , hypertensive , have SLE or a history of thromboembolism, diabetic with vascular disease . Significant adverse effects of POPs are irregular bleeding (mostly scanty), and secondary amenorrhea after longtime usage as it causes endometrial atrophy. Contraindications for POPs include undiagnosed vaginal bleeding , pregnancy, known or suspected breast cancer, and benign or malignant liver tumors.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient has come to your clinic for contraceptive advice. As she has a family history of breast cancer, you suggest a non-hormonal oral contraceptive to her. What is the initial dose of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Centchroman is a non-hormonal oral contraceptive that is started at a dose of 30 mg on the first day of the menstrual cycle . It can be given to women with a family history of breast cancer where hormonal contraceptives are contraindicated . Centchroman or ormeloxifene is a synthetic nonsteroidal contraceptive . Following the initial dose of 30 mg on the first day of menses , it is taken twice weekly for 12 weeks and weekly thereafter . It prevents implantation through endometrial changes . The return of fertility occurs within 6 months of stopping the drug. It can also be used as a postcoital pill, given in 60 mg dose within 24 hours of coitus . It has a failure rate of 1.83 per 100 woman years. It does not provide protection against HIV and other STDs. Side effects of centchroman: • Headache , nausea, vomiting • Weight gain • Delay in return of fertility (up to 6 months) • Atypical endometrial hyperplasia - prolonged use Contraindications of centchroman: • PCOD • Hepatic dysfunction • Cervical dysplasia • Allergy to the drug This drug has been developed by Central Drug Research Institute , Lucknow. It has been released in India under the name of Chhaya ( previously called Saheli) under the National Family Planning685 Programme.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most effective reversible method of contraception ?
mcqs.explanation: The most effective reversible method of contraception among the given options is Norplant, which is a subdermal hormonal implant. The most effective method of contraception overall is sterilization, which is one of the permament methods . Both methods belong to the first-tier category of contraceptives . There are 2 types of subdermal implants: • Implanon (which has replaced Norplant I) • Norplant II The implants work by inhibition of ovulation, endometrial atrophy, and thickening of cervical mucus . Implanon contains desogestrel and also reduces acne and osteoporosis . The implants are inserted on the first day of the menstrual cycle , within 5 days of abortion, and 3 weeks after the delivery . The woman needs to use barrier contraception or abstain in the first 7 days of insertion. The image below shows an implanon:686 The image given below shows the insertion of a subdermal implant:Advantages of implants: • Long-acting with sustained effect • Good compliance • Coital-independent with no nuisance of daily oral or frequent injections • Failure rate - 0.2 and 1.3 per 100 woman-years • Implanon reduces acne and osteoporosis . Disadvantages of implants: • Breakthrough bleeding • Irregular cycles687 • Amenorrhoea • Ectopic pregnancy • Local infection • Requires insertion and removal with nonbiodegradable capsules • Expensive .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a mechanism of action of the device given in the image below ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows Multiload Cu250, which is one of the copper containing IUCDs. Formation of cervical mucus plug is not one of its mechanisms of action. However, progesterone -containing IUCDs can alter the cervical mucus along with the local effects . The various mechanisms of action of a copper -containing IUCD are: • Interference with the migration of spermatozoa • Foreign body reaction releasing prostaglandins - provokes uterine contractility and increases the tubal peristalsis which interferes with implantation • Leucocytic infiltration in the endometrium - macrophages engulf the fertilized egg if it enters the endometrial tissue • Enzymatic and metabolic changes in the endometrial tissue which interferes with implantation of the fertilized ovum Some IUCDs like CuT-380A are effective for up to 10 years. They are a good choice of method of contraception for the following groups of women: • Having low risk of STD • Multiparous woman • Having a monogamous relationship • Wanting long-term reversible method of contraception • Unreliable users of oral contraception or barrier contraception IUCDs are avoided in unmarried and nulliparous patients because of the risk of PID and subsequent tubal infertility . Copper IUCDs can also be used as emergency contraception following intercourse .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: IUCD insertion is being considered in a multiparous woman who wants long-term contraception. This method of contraception is absolutely contraindicated in all of the following except _______.
mcqs.explanation: IUCDs can be used in HIV -affected women. Intrauterine contraceptive devices (IUCDs) provide long-term contraception by preventing fertilization. Contraindications for IUCD insertion:688 • Suspected pregnancy • Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) • Lower genital tract infection • Presence of fibroids • Severe anaemia • Uncontrolled diabetes - due to increased pelvic infection • Scarred uterus eg , post caesarean section • Septate uterus • Menorrhagia and dysmenorrhoea - if Copper T is used • Breast cancer - if LNG IUCD is used Complications of IUCD usage : • Immediate - • Vasovagal attack • Uterine cramps • Early - • Expulsion of IUCD • Perforation of uterus • Spotting , menorrhagia • Dysmenorrhoea • Vaginal infection • Actinomycosis • Late - • PID • Ectopic pregnancy • Perforation of uterus • Menorrhagia • Dysmenorrhoea The failure rate of IUCD is 1–3 per 100 woman-years. Levonorgestrel IUCD also causes hormonal adverse effects such as headache , acne, breast tenderness , and functional ovarian cysts . Amenorrhoea occurs in 35% of women after 2 years of use .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You are inserting Nova-T in a patient for spacing of births. This device contains______.
mcqs.explanation: 689 Nova-T contains both copper and silver. The addition of the silver increases its effective lifespan .In copper -carrying devices , copper wire is wrapped around the vertical stem of a polypropylene frame. Some of them have copper wire wrapped around the arms too. Based on the surface area, they are of various types : • Copper T 380 A • Multiload copper 250 • Copper T 200 • Copper 7 • Copper T 220 • Nova-T They are effective for 3–5 years. It is estimated that about 50 mcg of copper is eluted daily in the uterus . Copper T 380A, known as Paraguard, has a lifespan of 10 years. Nova T has a lifespan of 5 years.690

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A nursing mother was prescribed progestasert for contraception . How much progesterone is released by this device ?
mcqs.explanation: Progestasert releases 65 �Mg of progesterone/day. Progestasert is a T-shaped device carrying 38 mg of progesterone in a silicon oil reservoir in the vertical stem. The progesterone released causes the formation of a thick plug of mucus at the cervical os. This prevents entry of the sperms in addition to the local contraceptive effect of IUCDs. There is lesser incidence of menstrual problems like menorrhagia and dysmenorrhoea compared to copper -containing intrauterine devices . However, it is expensive and requires yearly replacement .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following increases the risk of pelvic inflammatory disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Copper IUCDs increase the risk of PID. OCPs, Mirena and DMPA injectables contain progesterone which causes thickening of the cervical mucus and decreases the motility of the female genital tract. Thus, they reduce the risk of PID by preventing the ascent of bacteria from the vagina .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most effective mode of contraception for a woman with heart disease ?
mcqs.explanation: IUCDs are the most effective mode of contraception for women with heart diseases . IUCDs are safe in these patients and come under the first-tier contraceptive methods . Condoms are not contraindicated in heart disease patients but they are third-tier contraceptives . Hence , they are not as effective as IUCDs.691 OCPs and hormonal implants are contraindicated in patients with heart diseases as the constituent hormones can cause thromboembolic disorders.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following techniques of permanent contraception does not require an abdominal incision?
mcqs.explanation: Essure permanent device is a method of hysteroscopic sterilization. Pomeroy, Parkland , and Irving procedures are methods for tubal ligation via an abdominal approach. Essure device consists of a micro-inserter with a flexible inner coil made of stainless steel and a dynamic outer coil made of nickel titanium alloy (nitinol). This device is inserted into the fallopian tube by hysteroscopy . It acts by benign local fibrous tissue growth leading to occlusion of the tube . The failure rate is 3.5%. Its advantages are that there is no abdominal scar and the procedure can be done under local anaesthesia . Disadvantages of Essure : • Hysteroscopy required for the procedure and to confirm the blockage • Expensive procedure • Expertise required • Irreversible - tuboplasty for reversal not possible • 3 months waiting time to ensure sterility - HSG must be done after 3 months to confirm tubal blockage • Bilateral insertion difficult due to spasm • Can cause perforation of the tube692

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman has come to your clinic for a checkup following tubal ligation by Pomeroy technique. Which portion of the tube is ligated in this technique ?
mcqs.explanation: Isthmus of the fallopian tube is ligated in Pomeroy technique . It is the most popular technique of tubal ligation. Midline , paramedian or transverse abdominal incision is made 2 inches above the pubic symphysis (1 inch in puerperal sterilisation). The fallopian tube is identified , made into a loop and tied at the base. The loop is then excised . The operation is simple and requires a short period of hospitalization. The failure rate is only 0.4% and it is mainly due to spontaneous canalization. It is surgically reversible. The below image shows Pomeroy's method of tubal ligation.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Fimbriectomy is also known as:
mcqs.explanation: Fimbriectomy is also known as Kroener's procedure . This procedure involves ligation of the distal ampulla of the tube with two permanent sutures . Then, resection of the infundibulum of the tube is done.693 Some more techniques of permanent sterilization include : Pomeroy method - The fallopian tube is identified on each side , brought out through the incision. The middle portion is formed into a loop which is tied at the base with catgut and excised . This is the most commonly used technique .Uchida 's method - The tubal serosa is stripped off the muscular layer in the midsegment of the tube . The muscle layer is excised . The proximal end is ligated and buried in the broad ligament . This minimal excision of the tube preserves the potential for tuboplasty .694 Irving 's procedure - The mid-portion of the tube is ligated and the intervening portion is excised . The proximal end is buried in the myometrium and the distal end is buried in the broad ligament . It is a reliable method but irreversible and may require a laparotomy incision.Madlener 's procedure - A loop of the fallopian tube is crushed and then ligated with a nonabsorbable suture .695

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old male patient underwent a vasectomy. What is the failure rate of this procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: The failure rate of vasectomy is 0.15% This procedure is done under local anaesthesia . A small incision is made in the scrotum. The vas deferens are divided on both sides which disrupts the passage of sperms. The no-scalpel technique has been now adopted . One single incision is made with special forceps and skin stitch is not required. Clips and plugs can be applied over the vas instead of cutting . The sperms can remain in the reproductive tract for up to 3 months. Hence , sterility is not immediate . The couple must abstain from intercourse during this period or use other methods of contraception . Approximately , 20 ejaculates clear the semen of all sperms. Two semen analysis reports must confirm the absence of sperms before the man can be declared sterile .696

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A couple with a history of unprotected sexual intercourse requires emergency contraception . Which of the following is not a mechanism by which these drugs act?

options.c: Preventing the implantation of the fertilized egg

mcqs.explanation: Emergency contraceptives do not interrupt early pregnancy, once conception has occured . They are used to prevent pregnancy after unprotected intercourse . Hence , they are also called interceptives . The main action of emergency contraceptives is to make the endometrium unsuitable for implantation. They can also delay or inhibit ovulation, and prevent fertilization of the egg by sperms. Methods of emergency contraception :Drug Dose Levonorgestrel 0.75mg stat and repeat dose after 12 hours or1 .5mg as a si ngle dose Ethinyl estradiol 50 �Mg + Nor gestrel 0.25 mg 2 tabs stat and 2 tabs after 12 hours RU486 (Mifepristone ) Single dose of 25-50mg Ethinyl Estradiol 2.5 mg BD X 5 days Copper IUDs Insertion within 5 days of int ercourse Centchroman 2 tabs(60 mg) to be taken twi ce at an interval of 12 hoursS hould be taken within 24 hou rs of intercourse . Ulipristal 30 mg within 5 days of interc ourse

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old woman comes to the clinic with a history of unprotected intercourse 2 days ago. Which of the following will you prescribe as a single dose contraceptive ?
mcqs.explanation: Levonorgestrel (LNG) 1.5 mg i.e. 2 tablets of LNG 0.75 mg can be used as a single dose emergency contraceptive . This should be taken within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse . Alternatively, one tablet of LNG 0.75mg can be followed by another tablet 12 hours later. The tablets can be offered up to 120 hours but the efficacy decreases with the increase in interval between coitus and drug intake. LNG prevents ovulation and makes endometrium unsuitable for implantation. The failure rate is 1.1%. If pregnancy occurs as a result of contraceptive failure, the risk of ectopic pregnancy increases but it is not teratogenic . Advantages of LNG: • No oestrogen and its associated side effects697 • Can be used in hypertensive , cardiac and diabetic patients • Suitable for lactating woman • Can be given up to 120 hours after the unprotected intercourse • Single -dose therapy Contraindications of LNG: • Liver disease • Thrombophlebitis • Migraine • Galactose allergy - as the tablet contains lactose

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the dose of ulipristal for emergency contraception ?
mcqs.explanation: The dose of ulipristal is 30 mg tablet and it should be taken within 5 days of intercourse . Ulipristal is a synthetic progesterone receptor modulator. It attaches to the progesterone receptor and acts by: • Preventing/delaying ovulation • Suppressing endometrial and follicular growth • Inhibiting implantation Side effects are headaches and mood changes . It is contraindicated in women with severe hepatic dysfunction and severe asthma. Note : The use of ulipristal for the treatment of fibroids has been discontinued due to the increased incidence of severe liver injury.698

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a risk factor for bacterial vaginosis?
mcqs.explanation: Caucasian race is not a risk factor for bacterial vaginosis. The risk factors for bacterial vaginosis are:706 • Oral sex • Vaginal douching • African race • Cigarette smoking • Sex during menses • Intrauterine device • Early age of sexual intercourse • New or multiple sexual partners • Sexual activity with other women Note : Bacterial vaginosis is not an infection . It most commonly affects young women. Although it is not a sexually transmitted disease , the chances of developing bacterial vaginosis seem to increase with the number of sexual partners that a woman has had.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young woman was suspected to have bacterial vaginosis. Which of the following statements is false about this condition?

options.a: Gardnerella vaginalis is a causative agent
options.b: Amsel's criteria is used for diagnosis
options.d: Oral metronidazole is given for treatment

mcqs.explanation: Vaginal itching is not seen in bacterial vaginosis. It is a symptom of Trichomonas vaginitis. About half of the women having bacterial vaginosis are asymptomatic . Symptomatic women mostly present with a profuse , fishy vaginal discharge . It does not cause pruritus, dysuria, and dyspareunia . Option A: Bacterial vaginosis occurs due to the absence of lactobacilli . This causes an increase in the growth of other anaerobic bacteria namely Gardnerella vaginalis, Mobiluncus , and Myco - plasma? hominis. Option B: Amsel's criteria is used for diagnosing bacterial vaginosis. 3 out of 4 criteria are needed to make a positive diagnosis.
