Option D: Oral metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days or oral clindamycin 300 mg twice daily for 7 days is given for the treatment of bacterial vaginosis. Treatment remains the same in pregnancy.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 30-year old woman presents to your OPD with complaints of foul -smelling vaginal discharge for the past 2 weeks . On examination, the discharge is adherent to the vaginal mucosa and has a fishy odour. What is the most likely cause ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of bacterial vaginosis (BV ) caused by Gardnerella. Patients with BV have profuse and yellowish vaginal discharge with a fishy odour. It is adherent to the vaginal mucosa. Dysuria, dyspareunia , and vaginal itching are absent. On microscopy, clue cells are visible. Option A: In trichomonas vaginitis, the vaginal discharge is frothy, greenish -yellow and has an offensive smell . Dysuria, dyspareunia , and vaginal itching are generally present . Option B: In candidal vaginitis, the discharge is thick and curdy white .707 Option D: In chlamydial infection , the vaginal discharge is generally scanty.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In a patient with bacterial vaginosis, which of the following microscopic features would not be seen ?
mcqs.explanation: An abundance of polymorphs is not a microscopic finding of bacterial vaginosis because it is not an inflammatory condition. It occurs due to an alteration in the normal vaginal flora. A swab of the discharge is taken from the vaginal wall and a smear is prepared . The microscopic evaluation is done using a gram stained smear. In bacterial vaginosis, this would reveal a clean background with an abundance of gram variable coccobacilli adhering to the epithelial cells . These are called clue cells . A few inflammatory cells , other pathogenic organisms, and a reduced number of Lactobacilli would also be seen . Shown below is the Gram-stained smear of vaginal discharge of a patient diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis. It reveals vaginal epithelial cells that have a fuzzy border due to the adherence of bacteria. These are called clue cells .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Given below is the image of a smear prepared from the vaginal discharge of a patient . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of clue cells on microscopy is suggestive of bacterial vaginosis. A swab of the vaginal discharge is taken from the vaginal wall and a smear is prepared . The microscopic evaluation of the smear is done on a gram stained smear. It would reveal a clean background with an abundance of gram variable coccobacilli adhering to the epithelial cells . These are called clue cells . A few inflammatory cells , other pathogenic organisms, and a reduced number of Lactobacilli would also be seen . Shown below is the Gram-stained smear of vaginal discharge of a patient diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis. It reveals vaginal epithelial cells that have a fuzzy border due to the adherence of bacteria. These are called clue cells .708

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman comes to the clinic with complaints of foul -smelling vaginal discharge . On examination , the discharge was profuse and had a fishy odour. Which of the following is the best criteria to confirm the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of bacterial vaginosis which is confirmed by using Amsel's criteria. 3 out of 4 of the following criteria are needed , to make a positive diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis: • A homogeneous , thin, greyish -white discharge that smoothly coats the vaginal walls . • A vaginal pH > 4.5. • A positive whiff test - an amine like fishy odour is produced when a drop of 10 % KOH is added to the sample of vaginal discharge . • The presence of >20% clue cells on saline wet mount. These are vaginal epithelial cells studded with adherent coccobacilli at the edge of the cell . Option A: Boer-Miesel 's criteria is used for the prognostic evaluation of pelvic inflammatory disease . Option B: Light's criteria is used for determining the nature of the pleural fluid i.e., transudate or exudate , in the diagnosis of pleural effusion . Option D: Nugent 's criteria can also be used for diagnosing bacterial vaginosis. However, it is not the best confirmatory method .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In a patient with suspected bacterial vaginosis, Nugent 's criteria is used to quantify the following bacteria except ....
mcqs.explanation: Nugent 's criteria is used to evaluate three types of bacteria in a case of suspected bacterial vaginosis: Mobiluncus , Lactobacillus, and Gardnerella/Bacteroides . Bacteria are graded through gram stain of vaginal samples . They are each graded on a scale of 1+ to 4+ where :709 • 1+ is < 1 cell per field • 2+ is 1-5 cells per field • 3+ is 6-30 cells per field • 4+ is >30 cells per field Lactobacillus and Bacteroides /Gardnerella are given scores between 0-4, but Mobiluncus is graded only from 0-2 . The total scores are then calculated and interpreted as follows : • 0-3 - Normal • 4-6 - Intermediate bacterial count • 7-10 - Bacterial vaginosis

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A gynaecology resident noted a frothy, greenish , offensive -smelling vaginal discharge in a young lady. Whiff test was positive . Which organism is most likely implicated ?
mcqs.explanation: Trichomonas vaginalis is the likely organism implicated in this patient , causing trichomonas vaginitis. The whiff test can be positive in both Trichomonas and Gardnerella infections . However, greenish frothy discharge is seen in trichomonas vaginitis.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient came to the gynaecology OPD with complaints of foul -smelling frothy vaginal discharge and intense itching. On examination, the cervix was spotted and had the appearance of a strawberry. Identify the causative organism.
mcqs.explanation: In the given clinical scenario, Trichomonas vaginalis is the likely causative agent . Vaginal itching and foul -smelling frothy vaginal discharge are seen in trichomonas vaginitis. The given image shows colpitis macularis or strawberry cervix, which is a characteristic finding of trichomoniasis. This is due to microscopic, punctate haemorrhages of the cervix.710

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms can be detected on a hanging drop preparation?
mcqs.explanation: Trichomonas vaginalis can be detected on a hanging drop preparation. Trichomonas vaginalis is a protozoan with four anterior flagellae , and a fifth posterior flagellum responsible for motility . The image given below shows trophozoites of Trichomonas vaginalis with flagella .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old woman came with complaints of greenish vaginal discharge . On saline microscopy , motile flagellated organisms were seen . What is the best treatment option for her?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of trichomonas vaginitis and the best treatment option for her is oral metronidazole 2 g stat. The treatment regimen for trichomonas vaginitis is: • An oral dose of metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days or • A single oral dose of metronidazole 2 g The male partner should be treated with a single dose of oral metronidazole in case of recurrent infection . Treatment in pregnancy remains the same.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman in her 7th week of gestation was diagnosed with trichomoniasis. Which of the following can be used to treat her condition?
mcqs.explanation: Trichomonas vaginitis is treated with oral metronidazole in pregnant women. According to the current guidelines , metronidazole is now considered safe for treating trichomonas vaginitis in pregnancy as it has no teratogenic effect . The treatment regimen for trichomonas vaginitis in pregnant women include :711 • An oral dose of metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days or a single oral dose of metronidazole 2 g • Usage of trichofuran suppositories • Vinegar douche to lower the vaginal pH • Betadine gel The male partner should be treated with a single dose of oral metronidazole in case of recurrent infection .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old diabetic woman presents to your OPD with complaints of curdy white vaginal discharge and intense itching. What is the likely causative agent for her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of moniliasis and Candida albicans is the likely causative agent . The risk factors for moniliasis are: • Diabetes mellitus • Obesity • Multiple sexual partners • Immunosuppression • HIV • Pregnancy • Steroid therapy • Following long-term broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy • Oral contraceptive pills • Poor personal hygiene .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In an obese lady with complaints of vaginal discharge , a vaginal pH of 4.2 was detected . Which organism is implicated in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The likely causative agent in the given clinical scenario is Candida which is known to flourish in an acidic environment. The pH of the vaginal discharge in candidal vaginitis is in the range of 4-4.5.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a risk factor for developing a candidal infection ?
mcqs.explanation: Hypertension does not increase the risk of developing a candidal infection . The risk factors for developing candidal vaginitis (moniliasis) are: • Diabetes mellitus712 • Obesity • Multiple sexual partners • Immunosuppression • HIV • Pregnancy • Steroid therapy • Following long-term broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy • Oral contraceptive pills • Poor personal hygiene .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 32 -year old woman presents to you with complaints of vaginal discharge and itching. On examination , you note a curdy white discharge and an inflamed vagina . What is the best treatment for her?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of candidal vaginitis. A single dose of fluconazole 150 mg is the best treatment for treating candidal vaginitis. Intravaginal antifungal (imidazole/miconazole/clotrimazole) vaginal pessaries or creams can also be used for 3–6 days.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a primary site for gonococcal infection ?
mcqs.explanation: Ectocervix and vagina are lined by squamous epithelium which is resistant to gonococcal infection . The principal sites of invasion for gonococcal infection are the columnar and transitional epithelium . Hence , gonococcus usually affects the following structures : • Endocervix • Urethra713 • Skene's glands • Bartholin's glands.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following presentations is unlikely to be seen in a patient with gonorrhoea?
mcqs.explanation: Haematuria is unlikely to be seen in a patient with gonorrhoea. Gynaecological presentation of gonorrhoea is: • Excessive vaginal discharge associated with pruritus and inflammation • Acute unilateral pain and swelling over labia due to the involvement of Bartholin's gland • Intermenstrual bleeding Non-gynaecological presentation of gonorrhoea is: • Pharyngeal infection • Dysuria • Rectal discomfort due to associated proctitis .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of non-gonococcal urethritis?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of non-gonococcal urethritis is Chlamydia trachomatis. The causes of non-gonococcal urethritis are: • Chlamydia trachomatis (most common) • Ureaplasma urealyticum • Adenovirus • Haemophillus vaginalis • Mycoplasma genitalium • Tricomonas vaginalis (rare) • Herpes simplex virus (rare)

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old sex worker was suspected to have chlamydial cervicitis. What is the most sensitive method for confirming the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The most sensitive method for confirming the diagnosis of chlamydial cervicitis is the polymerase chain reaction (PCR). It is fast, highly sensitive and specific (96%).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old woman had complaints of lower abdominal pain and vaginal discharge . On microscopy , the following finding was present . What is the selective culture media used to isolate the causative organism?

options.c: Culture on bilayer human blood agar

mcqs.explanation: 714 Chlamydia trachomatis is the most likely causative organism. This is suggested by the presence of characteristic iodine-stained inclusion bodies in the McCoy cell culture of the patient 's endocervical sample . Chlamydia is a gram-negative coccobacillus . The gram stain of the cervical smear would show abundant leucocytes but no organisms. The nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) is currently done for the diagnosis of lymphogranuloma venereum.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with complaints of vaginal discharge was evaluated . On an endocervical biopsy , chlamydia was detected . How will you treat this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: A single dose of 1 g of azithromycin is given and contact tracing is done to treat a patient diagnosed with a chlamydial infection . Treatment of chlamydial infection : • Azithromycin 1 g single dose (or) • Doxycycline 100 mg orally BID \327 7 days (or) • Ofloxacin 200 mg orally BID \327 7 days (or) • Erythromycin 500 mg orally BID \327 7 days Contact tracing should always be done. The sexual partner should also be treated with the same regimen .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old lady complains of thick curdy white vaginal discharge with itching and burning. What is the route of administration of the first non-azole drug approved to treat this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical history of thick curdy white vaginal discharge with itching and burning are suggestive of vulvovaginal candidiasis. The first and the only non-azole antifungal approved for the treatment of vulvovaginal candidiasis is Ibrexafungerp. The route of administration of this drug is oral. Ibrexafungerp is a triterpenoid antifungal agent that acts by inhibiting glucan synthase . Glucan synthase is an enzyme involved in the formation of 1,3-beta-D-glucan which is an essential component of the fungal cell wall. The recommended dosage is 600 mg orally as 2 divided doses 12 hrs apart. Contraindications include pregnancy and hypersensitivity to ibrexafungerp . The most frequent adverse reactions are diarrhea, nausea, abdominal pain, dizziness, and vomiting.715

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the causative organism of vulval warts?
mcqs.explanation: The causative agent of vulval warts is the human papillomavirus (HPV ). Genital warts/venereal warts/condyloma acuminata are verrucous growths that affect the skin of the labia majora , perineum , perianal region and vulva . The lesions may be discrete or coalesce to form cauliflower -like growth . The disease is sexually transmitted . The growth of the warts is favoured by vaginal discharge , the use of oral contraceptives , and pregnancy. HPV causes structural changes in the epithelial cells of the skin called koilocytes , and their presence is characteristic of HPV infection . The koilocytes have large hyperchromatic nuclei and a perinuclear halo, as shown below .The diagnosis is made by colposcopic studies . The lesions on the vulva are stained by toluidine blue . The abnormal areas of the skin retain the blue dye . These areas are then biopsied for histopathological examination. The given image below shows condyloma acuminata:721

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young woman presented with the following lesion on her vulva . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given image is suggestive of condyloma acuminata that shows cauliflower -like masses of tissue on and around the female anogenital region. Condyloma acuminatum is an epidermal manifestation of the human papillomavirus (HPV ). HPV is transmitted through contact with infected skin or mucosa. The virus invades the cells of the epidermal basal layer through microabrasions . However, anogenital HPV infection is almost always acquired through sexual contact. Warts are not required for transmission but are highly infectious because of their high viral load. Option B: The image given below shows shiny, pearly white , umbilicated papules with a characteristic dimple at the centre . These are seen in molluscum contagiosum caused by the pox virus.722 Option C: The image given below shows firm papules with a rough horny surface . These are seen in verruca vulgaris caused by the human papillomavirus type 2.Option D: The image given below shows condyloma lata which is the characteristic feature of secondary syphilis . It is caused by Treponema pallidum .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A sexually active woman presents with cauliflower -like lesions on the vulva . The biopsy of the lesion is taken and histopathology reveals the following picture . What is the most likely causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows koilocytes , a characteristic feature of infection with human papillomavirus (HPV ). Other features that can also be seen on histology are: • Perinuclear halo723 • Multinucleation • Orangeophilic cytoplasm • Acanthosis • Chronic inflammatory infiltrate Option A: Henderson-Paterson bodies are seen in molluscum contagiosum , caused by poxvirus. Option C and D: Cowdry bodies are seen in herpes infection .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following serotypes are present in the bivalent vaccine against the human papillomavirus?
mcqs.explanation: Serotypes 16 and 18 are present in the bivalent vaccine against the human papillomavirus (HPV ). It is called Cervarix . Cervarix is given at 0, 1 and 6 months. Gardasil/Silgard is the quadrivalent vaccine against HPV . It has serotypes 6, , 16 and 18 and is given at 0, 2 and 6 months. Gardasil 9 is the nonavalent vaccine against HPV . It has serotypes 6, , 16, 18, , 33, 45, 52 and 58. In 2020 it has received an expanded indication which now includes the prevention of oropharyngeal and head and neck cancers.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a treatment option for a patient with genital warts?
mcqs.explanation: Genital warts are treated by a local application of 25% trichloracetic acid + 5% fluorouracil. Treatment of genital warts includes the local application of: • Podophyllin 25% in alcohol/podophyllin 20 % in tincture benzoin daily for 4 days (or) • 25% trichloracetic acid +5% fluorouracil daily for 4 days If this fails, the following treatment is given: • Interferon ointment/cream or intralesional interferon injection • Imiquimod cream thrice a week for 4 months If medical treatment fails then cryosurgery, diathermy or laser removal is done.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A sexually active woman who presented with an ulcer over the vulva was diagnosed with primary syphilis . What is the characteristic feature associated with this condition?

options.a: Non suppurative , tender , and enlarged nodes
options.b: Firm, shotty , and painless nodes that do not suppurate
options.c: Painful, tender , and matted nodes forming an abscess
options.d: Painful, inflamed, necrotic nodes developing a chronic sinus

mcqs.explanation: The characteristic feature associated with primary syphilis is firm, shotty , painless nodes that do not suppurate. Syphilis is a sexually transmitted infection caused by the motile spirochete , Treponema pallidum . In primary syphilis , the classical lesion i.e., chancre appears within 9–90 days from the first exposure .724 The macular lesion becomes papular and then ulcerates . The ulcer(s) is painless and firm, with a punched out base and rolled edges . If left unattended , these heal within 3–9 weeks . It is accompanied by painless inguinal discrete lymphadenopathy .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old woman known to have syphilis presented with the following lesions over the vulva. What is the stage of the disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows condyloma lata, a classic finding of secondary syphilis . Multiple moist well -demarcated papules and plaques are seen in condyloma lata. They are highly contagious , exophytic broad excrescences that ulcerate and are commonly seen on the vulva , perianal area and upper thighs .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A sexually active patient was diagnosed with lymphogranuloma venereum. What is the causative organism for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The causative agent for lymphogranuloma venereum is Chlamydia trachomatis (serotypes L1/L2 /L3 ). Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV ) is a sexually transmitted disease that causes genital ulcers . It has the following three stages of infection : Chlamydia trachomatis is a small gram-negative bacterium and an obligate intracellular parasite that appears as an intracytoplasmic inclusion body. The gram stain of the cervical smear would show leucocytes but no organisms. Hence , selective culture media like the McCoy cells culture is used to isolate the organism. The slide given below is an iodine-stained smear prepared from the patient 's endocervical sample . It shows inclusion bodies characteristic of Chlamydia trachomatis.Stage of LGV Characteristic features Primary stage Painless genital ulcerPapules Lymphangitis Secondary sta ge Painful unilateral/bilateral ly mphadenopathyBuboesGroov e sign Late stage Stricture formationFibrosis a nd fistulae of the anogenital r egion725

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old sexually active man comes to the STD clinic with a painful genital ulcer. On examination , the ulcer and the right inguinal lymph nodes were tender . What is the causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of chancroid caused by Haemophilus ducreyi which is a gram -negative anaerobe. Chancroid is symptomatic in men. Both ulcer and lymphadenopathy are painful. Lymphadenopathy in chancroid is either unilateral or bilateral. Chancroid is generally asymptomatic in women but sometimes presents as painful lymphadenopathy . The image below shows a chancroid ulcer with purulent and haemorrhagic discharge . It has a non-indurated, erythematous base.726

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A sexually active man presents with complaints of painful swelling over the inguinal region. He also gives a history of a painless genital ulcer that resolved spontaneously . On examination, groove sign is seen . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The pathognomic groove sign of Greenblatt is suggestive of lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV ) caused by Chlamydia trachomatis (serovars L1 , L2 , L3 ). This image shows groove sign which is seen in \037 of the cases in the secondary stage of LGV . It refers to the depression between the enlarged femoral and inguinal lymph nodes on either side of the inguinal ligament .Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV ) is a sexually transmitted disease that causes genital ulcers . It has the following three stages of infection :727 Stage of LGV Characteristic features Primary stage Painless genital ulcerPapules Lymphangitis Secondary sta ge Painful unilateral/bilateral ly mphadenopathyBuboesGroov e sign Late stage Stricture formationFibrosis a nd fistulae of the anogenital r egion

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 20 -year-old female sex worker presents with complaints of constipation and blood in stools for 3 months. On DRE, a circumferential constriction is felt beyond which the finger cannot be advanced. Which of the following is a probable cause for this complication?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of rectal stricture which is a complication of lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV ). LGV is a sexually transmitted disease caused by Chlamydia trachomatis (serotypes L1 /L2 /L3 ). Rectal involvement is commonly seen in women as the primary disease often goes unnoticed and untreated . Anorectal involvement causes proctocolitis and causes rectal strictures . This occurs due to the contiguous spread of the primary infection from the perirectal nodes leading to scar tissue formation. The complications of lymphogranuloma venereum include : • Rectal stricture formation may lead to: • Intestinal obstruction • Rectovaginal fistulae • Proctitis • Vulvar cancer.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the causative agent for granuloma inguinale?
mcqs.explanation: The causative agent for granuloma inguinale (donovanosis) is Calymmatobacterium granulomatis. It is now called Klebsiella granulomatis and is a gram-negative bacillus causing chronic ulcerative infection of the vulva . It is highly contagious and transmitted through repeated sexual or non-sexual contact. The incubation period is 1-12 weeks . Clinical features : It begins as a painless nodule which later ulcerates to form multiple beefy red painless ulcers that tend to coalesce ; the vulva is progressively destroyed , and minimal adenopathy may occur. Diagnosis: Microscopic examination of smears from the lesion/ biopsy specimens reveals pathognomonic intracytoplasmic Donovan bodies and clusters of bacteria with a bipolar (safety pin) appearance.728 Blue-black stained organisms are seen in the cytoplasm of mononuclear cells . Management : Azithromycin 1 g orally once per week or 500 mg daily for at least 3 weeks and until all lesions have completely healed . The given image below shows the donovanosis in a female patient with a beefy red ulcer:

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 19-year-old girl presented with multiple beefy -red ulcers over the labia. Microscopic examination of smear from the lesion showed intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies and gram-negative bacteria having a safety pin appearance . What is your likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of granuloma inguinale which is caused by a gram -negative bacteria, Klebsiella granulomatis. Granuloma inguinale begins as a painless nodule that later ulcerates to form multiple beefy red painless ulcers. These ulcers tend to coalesce and bleed easily on contact. If secondarily infected , they may become painful. The ulcers heal by fibrosis, which can result in scarring resembling keloids . The lymph nodes are usually uninvolved but can become enlarged . New lesions can appear along the lymphatic drainage channels. The gross image below shows granuloma inguinale of the cervix with a beefy red appearance of the hypervascular intravaginal tissues .729 The microscopic image below shows the pathognomonic intracytoplasmic Donovan bodies . It also shows clusters of gram-negative bacteria with a bipolar/safety -pin appearance .730

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The Pap smear of a healthy 30-year-old lady is given below . Identify the microorganism seen .
mcqs.explanation: The organism seen in the given image of a Pap smear is the Doderlien 's bacillus , also known as Lactobacillus . This is a gram-positive, rod-shaped bacillus that grows in anaerobic conditions. It is a part of the normal vaginal flora that is responsible for the vaginal defence mechanism. It is an estrogen -dependent bacillus and appears at puberty and disappears after menopause . It converts glycogen into lactic acid and maintains the acidic ph in the vagina . This prevents the growth of pathogenic bacteria in the vagina . Its absence causes a condition called bacterial vaginosis where pathogenic organisms replaces the normal flora of the vagina . In this condition, clue cells are visible. Option B: Gardnerella vaginalis is the most common organism involved in bacterial vaginosis. As the patient in the given question is healthy , this is not the correct option. Option C: Trichomonas vaginalis is flagellated protozoa that causes trichomonas vaginitis. The organism and the nucleus of epithelial cells appear equal in size on the pap smear. This criterion is used for the identification of trichomonas as flagella are not visible on a pap smear. Option D: Frisch bacillus is another name for Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis. It is not seen on Pap smears.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: All of the following are risk factors for PID except ______.
mcqs.explanation: Pregnancy is not a risk factor for PID. Instead, it plays a protective role in this condition.739 The risk factors for developing PID are: • Unprotected sexual intercourse • Having multiple sex partners • Previous history of PID • IUD insertion • Early age of sexual intercourse (<18years) The protective factors for PID are: • Pregnancy • Using barrier contraception like condoms, diaphragms • Oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) • Menopause

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old woman is diagnosed with pelvic inflammatory disease . Which of the following is not included in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Cervicitis is not included in pelvic inflammatory disease (PID). Pelvic inflammatory disease is a spectrum of infection and inflammation of the upper genital tract, typically causing: • Endometritis • Salpingitis • Oophoritis • Peritonitis The minimum criteria for diagnosis of PID are: Pain in the lower abdomen + any one of the following : • Uterine tenderness • Cervical motion tenderness • Adnexal tenderness Cervicitis and vaginitis are lower genital tract infections .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common symptom seen in acute PID?

options.d: Pain in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen

mcqs.explanation: The most common symptom of acute PID is bilateral lower abdominal pain. The pain is severe in acute stages and it may or may not be accompanied by a high temperature ( >38.3 degrees C). It may be followed by vomiting. Some patients with PID can present with pain in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. This is seen in Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome which is a form of perihepatitis .740 If PID occurs due to sexually transmitted organisms, dysuria and vaginal discharge may be seen .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young woman with fever and lower abdominal pain is diagnosed to have PID. Which is the most common cause for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Chlamydia trachomatis is the most common cause of PID. PID is an infection of the upper genital tract. It is generally transmitted sexually as an ascending infection along with sperms. It is usually a polymicrobial infection , Organisms causing PID include : Sexually transmitted : • Chlamydia (most common) • Gonococcus • Mycoplasma • Trichomonas Pyogenic Aerobes : • Staphylococci • Streptococci • E Coli Anaerobes: • Bacteroides fragilis • Peptostreptococcus • Clostridium • Actinomyces (most common in IUD users) Other: • Mycobacterium tuberculosis Note : Genital tuberculosis is the only PID that does not spread sexually . It has a hematogenous spread. Thus, it is the most common PID in virgin girls.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 42-year-old woman presented to the emergency room with abdominal pain and fever for the last 48 hours. She has been using a Cu T 380A for contraception for the past 8 years. On examination, cervical motion tenderness was present . What is the most likely organism to have caused her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario points towards a diagnosis of PID in an IUCD user. The most common organism causing this condition is Actinomyces . It has been reported in 7% of IUCD users if the device is worn for more than 2 years. This emphasizes the need for strict asepsis during insertion of the device and the need for strict follow up of women wearing these devices. Organisms causing PID are:741 Sexually transmitted : • Chlamydia (most common) • Gonococcus • Mycoplasma • Trichomonas Pyogenic Aerobes : • Staphylococci • Streptococci • E Coli Anaerobes: • Bacteroides fragilis • Peptostreptococcus • Clostridium • Actinomyces (most common in IUD users) Other: • Mycobacterium tuberculosis

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the mechanism of the spread of gonococci to the tubes in pelvic inflammatory disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The mechanism of the spread of gonococci to the tubes in pelvic inflammatory disease is mucosal. Gonococci ascend to the tubes mainly through mucosal continuity . This is facilitated by sexually transmitted vectors such as sperms and Trichomonas . The mucous membranes of the fallopian tubes are affected first. They become edematous and are infiltrated with leukocytes and plasma cells . Another route of spread is through the reflux of mucosal blood. Option A: Hematogenous spread is seen in genital tuberculosis . Option B: Lymphatics are involved in the spread of secondary organisms and in PID following post-abortal and puerperal infection . Option C: Parametrium facilitates the spread of Mycoplasma . The gut flora can directly spread to tubes .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which infection causes more damage to the mucosa and the wall of the tube leading to fibrosis and tubal blockage ?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , chlamydial infection causes the most amount of damage to the mucosa and the wall of the fallopian tubes leading to fibrosis and tubal blockage .742 Chlamydial infection can remain asymptomatic in the endo-cervix. Hence , the infection goes unnoticed and untreated . Thus, it can lead to more damage and complications . Gonococcal infection is more symptomatic than chlamydial infection . Hence , it is diagnosed early and causes less damage to the tubes than chlamydial infection . Mycoplasma and Mobiluncus generally cause lower genital tract infections like cervicitis and vaginitis.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a differential diagnosis of acute PID?
mcqs.explanation: Pelvic endometriosis is not a differential diagnosis of acute PID. It is a differential diagnosis of chronic PID. Differential diagnosis of acute PID: • Acute appendicitis • Septic abortion • Cholecystitis • Twisted ovarian cyst • Ectopic pregnancy • Diverticulitis • Ruptured endometriotic cyst Differential diagnosis of chronic PID: • Uterine fibroids • Pelvic endometriosis • Ovarian tumour • Tubercular tubo-ovarian mass

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old female with endometritis did not complete the course of antibiotics she was prescribed . Following this, her infection failed to resolve and she developed a tubo-ovarian mass. How can this mass manifest?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of development of a chronic tubo-ovarian mass following acute PID points towards a diagnosis of chronic PID. A chronic tubo-ovarian mass can manifest as a tubo-ovarian cyst , hydrosalpinx or even a chronic pyosalpinx. Failure to complete treatment of acute PID or drug resistance can lead to the development of chronic PID. This can lead to the development of chronic tubo-ovarian masses which may manifest as: • Hydrosalpinx • Chronic pyosalpinx • Chronic interstitial salpingitis743 • Tubo-ovarian cyst • Tuberculous form A twisted ovarian cyst and a ruptured endometriotic cyst are differential diagnoses of acute PID.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the condition seen in the image given below ?

options.c: Flattening of tubal plicae is seen on histology
options.d: Its ampullary region is filled with clear fluid

mcqs.explanation: The above image depicts a hydrosalpinx. Its wall is not opaque but translucent . If a pyosalpinx responds to antibiotics, the pus present inside becomes sterile within 6 weeks of the initial attack. However, the damage to the tube remains as chronic pyosalpinx or hydrosalpinx. A hydrosalpinx represents the end result of previous acute salpingitis and is often bilateral. The tube becomes retort shaped due to the enormous dilatation of the ampullary region that is filled with clear fluid . Histological examination shows a flattening of the tubal plicae and exfoliation of the lining epithelium .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with fever and abdominal pain presented to the emergency . On examination, you note mucopurulent vaginal discharge and cervical motion tenderness . You suspect she has PID. Which of these is not included in the criteria to diagnose this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Bilateral abdominal pain is not included in the criteria to diagnose PID. Bilateral abdominal pain is a clinical symptom of PID. Lower abdominal tenderness is included in the criteria to diagnose PID. CDC criteria for the diagnosis of PID: Definitive criteria: • Histopathologic evidence of endometritis on biopsy • Imaging study (TVS /MRI) evidence of thickened fluid -filled tubes (tubo-ovarian abscess ) • Laparoscopic evidence of PID Minimum criteria: • Cervical motion tenderness • Uterine tenderness • Adnexal tenderness Additional criteria: • Oral temperature >38.3 oC • Mucopurulent cervical or vaginal discharge , cervical friability • Raised ESR or CRP • Laboratory documentation of positive cervical infection with Gonorrhea or Chlamydia744

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a definitive criterion used to diagnose PID?
mcqs.explanation: A temperature of more than 38.3\260C is an additional criterion and not a definitive criterion for the diagnosis of PID. CDC 2006 criteria for the diagnosis of PID: Definitive criteria: • Histopathologic evidence of endometritis on biopsy • Imaging studies (TVS /MRI) evidence of thickened fluid -filled tubes (Tubo-ovarian abscess ) • Laparoscopic evidence of PID Minimum criteria: • Lower abdominal tenderness • Adnexal tenderness • Cervical motion tenderness Additional criteria: • Oral temperature >38.3C • Mucopurulent cervical or vaginal discharge and cervical friability • Raised ESR or CRP • Laboratory documentation of positive cervical infection with Gonorrhea or Chlamydia

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old woman presented with bilateral abdominal pain for 3 days and a temperature of 102 \260F. She also had a mucopurulent vaginal discharge , cervical motion tenderness , and a negative urine pregnancy test . Which is the gold standard investigation to confirm her likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is likely to be acute PID. Laparoscopy is the gold standard to confirm acute PID. Laparoscopy is not done routinely as it is an invasive procedure . It is reserved for only cases where the differential diagnosis is salpingitis , appendicitis , ectopic pregnancy or a case of a non-responding pelvic mass. The diagnosis of PID is mostly clinical. If diagnosis is unclear, the investigation of choice for PID is USG and culdocentesis . CDC 2006 criteria for the diagnosis of PID: Definitive criteria: • Histopathologic evidence of endometritis on biopsy • Imaging studies (TVS /MRI) evidence of thickened fluid -filled tubes (tubo-ovarian abscess ) • Laparoscopic evidence of PID Minimum criteria:745 • Lower abdominal tenderness • Adnexal tenderness • Cervical motion tenderness Additional criteria: • Oral temperature >38.3C • Mucopurulent cervical or vaginal discharge and cervical friability • Raised ESR or CRP • Laboratory documentation of positive cervical infection with Gonorrhea or Chlamydia

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The laparoscopy report of a woman with pelvic inflammatory disease states she has Gainesville stage III PID. Which of the following presentations could have been seen in her?
mcqs.explanation: Gainesville stage III includes two forms of PID - acute salpingitis with superimposed tubal occlusion or tubo-ovarian complex . Gainesville has described the stages of PID depending upon the severity of tubal damage as follows :Stage Condition Stage I Acute salpingitis without peri tonitis - no adhesions Stage I I Acute salpingitis with periton itis - purulent discharge Stage I II Acute salpingitis with superi mposed tubal occlusion or tu bo-ovarian complex Stage I V Ruptured tubo-ovarian absce ss Stage V Tubercular salpingitis

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In a patient with PID, laparoscopy shows the following appearance . What is true about the syndrome this patient likely has?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows the laparoscopic finding of violin string adhesions that are characteristic of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome. It is a form of perihepatitis that occurs in the setting of PID. It is characterized by right upper quadrant pain with a pleuritic component , sometimes referred to the right shoulder . It rarely occurs in women with acute PID. The pathological mechanism is as follows : Gonococcal / Chlamydial infection \037 transperitoneal /vascular spread \037 inflammation of the liver capsule and peritoneal surfaces \037 adhesions and fibrosis in the perihepatic region \037 Fitz-Hugh-Curtis Syndrome746 Cholecystitis and ruptured tubo-ovarian abscess are the differential diagnoses of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome. Violin string adhesions would not be seen in these conditions.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the wrong statement with respect to silent PID.

options.d: Mycobacterium can be grown from menstrual blood

mcqs.explanation: Dysmenorrhea rarely occurs in PID. Pain is uncommon and is a result of subacute PID. Silent PID is thought to follow multiple or continuous low-grade infections in asymptomatic women. It is not a clinical diagnosis. Rather, it is an ultimate diagnosis given to women with tubal-factor infertility who lack a history of upper genital tract infection . On laparoscopy or laparotomy, these women may have evidence of prior tubal infection such as adhesions , but for the most part, the fallopian tubes are grossly normal . They can have ectopic pregnancies due to tubal dysmotility . Silent PID can occur following infection with M. tuberculosis .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient is admitted to the gynaecology ward for pelvic inflammatory disease . Which of the following is a part of this patient 's treatment regimen?

options.a: Administration of cefotetan 2 g IV 12 hourly + doxycycline 100 mg IV BD
options.b: Removal of IUD irrespective of antibiotic response
options.c: Administration of a single dose of ceftriaxone 250 mg IM
options.d: Administration of 10 doses of Placentrex 2ml IM daily or on alternate days

mcqs.explanation: Administration of cefotetan 2 g IV 12hourly + doxycycline 100 mg BD orally/ IV for 48 hours forms the crux of the treatment regimen for PID. This is followed by oral doxycycline 100 mg +/-metronidazole 400 mg for 14 days in all hospitalized patients having PID. Treatment of PID in hospitalized patients: • Cefotetan 2 g IV 12hourly + doxycycline 100 mg BD orally/ IV for 48 hours is given followed by oral doxycycline 100 mg +/- metronidazole 400 mg for 14 days • Cefoxitin 2 g IV 6hourly + doxycycline 100 mg IV followed by oral route. • Azithromycin 500 mg IV 6 hourly for 2 days, then orally for Chlamydia. Outpatient treatment of PID (according to the current RCOG guidelines ): • A single dose of IM ceftriaxone 250 mg followed by oral doxycycline 100 mg BD +/- metronidazole 400 mg BD x 14 days • A single dose of IM ceftriaxone 250 mg followed by azithromycin 1 gm per week x 2 weeks . IUD is not removed in a woman who responds to antibiotics. It is removed only in case of a failed antibiotic response . Barrier contraceptives and OCPs are recommended only in women unresponsive to antibiotics. The use of Placentrex (aqueous extract of the placenta ) is outdated and is not recommended currently.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old female presents to the OPD with fever, lower abdominal pain and purulent vaginal discharge . On examination, her vitals are stable and per vaginal examination reveals lower abdominal and cervical motion tenderness . What is the best treatment option for her?

options.a: Single IM injection of ceftriaxone 250 mg with oral doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days
options.b: Single IM injection of ceftriaxone 250 mg with oral metronidazole 400 mg for 7 days
options.c: Oral doxycycline 100 mg BD with oral metronidazole 400 mg for 7 days
options.d: Oral ofloxacin 200 mg BD with oral metronidazole 400 mg for 14 days

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of fever and lower abdominal pain associated with lower abdominal and cervical motion tenderness is suggestive of PID. The best treatment option for this patient is747 outpatient treatment with a single dose of IM ceftriaxone 250 mg + oral doxycycline 100 mg BD +/- metronidazole 400 mg BD x 14 days. Outpatient treatment of PID (according to the current RCOG guidelines ): • A single dose of IM ceftriaxone 250 mg + oral doxycycline 100 mg BD +/- metronidazole 400 mg BD x 14 days • A single dose of IM ceftriaxone 250 mg followed by azithromycin 1 gm per week x 2 weeks . Treatment of PID in hospitalized patients: • Cefotetan 2 g IV 12hourly + doxycycline 100 mg BD orally/ IV for 48 hours is given followed by oral doxycycline 100 mg +/- metronidazole 400 mg for 14 days • Cefoxitin 2 g IV 6hourly + doxycycline 100 mg IV followed by oral route. • Azithromycin 500 mg IV 6 hourly for 2 days, then orally for Chlamydia.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following would be an indication for surgery in a 30-year-old woman diagnosed with PID?
mcqs.explanation: Intestinal obstruction would be an indication for surgery in a patient diagnosed with PID. Criteria for surgery in PID include : • Drainage of pelvic abscess by colpotomy. • Dilatation and evacuation of septic products of conception or for haemorrhage in the postabortal period. • Acute spreading peritonitis resistant to a full course of chemotherapy . Presence of pyoperitoneum mandates laparotomy. • Intestinal obstruction • Suspected intestinal injury as diagnosed in criminal abortion. • Ruptured tubo-ovarian abscess A tubo-ovarian abscess of 2 cm is not an indication for surgery. Minimally invasive surgery is done in a tubo-ovarian abscess measuring more than 10 cm, that fails to respond to antibiotics in 48-72 hours. Peritonitis and sepsis are not an indication for surgery. They should be managed medically first. If they do not respond to antibiotic treatment then surgical management should be done.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which among the following is an indication for minimally invasive surgery for tubo-ovarian abscess ?

options.a: The size of the abscess is more than 5 cm
options.b: The size of the abscess is more than 2cm
options.c: The abscess fails to respond to antibiotics in 48 - 72 h
options.d: The abscess fails to respond to antibiotics in 24 - 36 h

mcqs.explanation: If the abscess fails to respond to antibiotics in 48–72 h, minimally invasive surgery is indicated . Criteria for minimally invasive surgery in PID: • The size of the abscess is more than 10 cm • The abscess fails to respond to antibiotics in 48-72 hours748 • The abscess ruptures • Pyoperitoneum Minimal invasive surgery includes laparoscopic drainage of the tubo ovarian abscess or posterior colpotomy .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old multiparous woman who presented with chronic lower abdominal pain has been diagnosed with chronic PID. What is the treatment of choice for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The treatment of choice for an old multiparous woman with chronic PID is abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo -oophorectomy . A radical hysterectomy involves the removal of the whole uterus , tissue from the sides of the uterus , the cervix, and the upper part of the vagina . It is generally done only in cancer patients . A supracervical hysterectomy involves the removal of only the body of the uterus and is not done in chronic PID. It is done for the treatment of endometriosis , uterine fibroids, and uterine prolapse .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Who has described the prognostic evaluation for PID?
mcqs.explanation: Boer-Meisel has described the prognostic evaluation for PID. It depends upon the following : • Extent of adhesions • Nature of adhesions such as flimsy or dense . • Size of hydrosalpinx • Macroscopic condition of hydrosalpinx. • The thickness of the tubal wall. Boer-Meisel system is specifically used for predicting pregnancy outcomes in patients treated for PID. Gainesville has described the stages of PID depending upon the severity of tubal damage . Westrom has reported that women with one previous attack of PID have a predisposition to another attack.Stages of PID Stage I Acute salpingitis without peri tonitis - no adhesions Stage I I Acute salpingitis with periton itis- purulent discharge Stage I II Acute salpingitis with superi mposed tubal occlusion or tu bo-ovarian complex749 Stages of PID Stage I V Ruptured tubo-ovarian absce ss Stage V Tuberculous salpingitis

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Long-standing pelvic inflammation may lead to which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Long-standing pelvic inflammation may lead to pyometra . This refers to the collection of pus in the uterine cavity. The initial infection involves the cervix uteri and urethra which may extend to Bartholin glands, skene glands, endometrium , and fallopian tubes . Unilateral pain and swelling over the labia may be caused by the inflammation of the Bartholin glands. Depending on the extent of tissue involved, PID can be classified into five stages • Stage I - Acute salpingitis without peritonitis - No adhesions • Stage II - Acute salpingitis with peritonitis - purulent discharge • Stage III - Acute salpingitis with superimposed tubal occlusion or tubo ovarian complex • Stage IV - Ruptured tubo-ovarian abscess • Stage V - Tubercular salpingitis Long-standing pelvic inflammation may also lead to: • Dyspareunia • Infertility • Ectopic pregnancy • Formation of adhesions like hydrosalpinx, pyosalpinx , tubo-ovarian abscess • Chronic pelvic pain Note : Chronic pelvic inflammation leads to dense adhesions between the uterus and the appendages. Thus, it becomes difficult to define the uterus from the pelvic masses . They form a hard mass which is called the frozen pelvis. The most common cause of the spread of PID: Ascending infection along with sperms The only PID that does not spread with the sexual route is genital TB . It has a hematogenous spread. The most common PID in virgin females is genital TB . Investigation of choice in PID: Abdominal USG The surest sign of salpingitis is pus extruding from the fimbrial end of the tube .750

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common site for genital tuberculosis ?
mcqs.explanation: The ampulla of the fallopian tubes is the most common site for genital tuberculosis . The distribution of genital tuberculosis is given below :Site Percent age Fallopian tubesAmpulla is th e most common site .Intramu ral part is the least common site .Fimbriae are not involve d even in advanced genital T B. 90-100 % Endometrium 50-60% Ovaries -30% Cervix 5-15% Vulva and vagina <1%

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common mode of transmission of tuberculosis to the endometrium ?
mcqs.explanation: Endometrial tuberculosis is most commonly acquired by direct spread from the fallopian tubes . Hematogenous spread is thought to be the process by which the tubercle bacilli implant into the mucosa of the fallopian tubes and subsequently affect the endometrium by direct extension . Female genital tuberculosis is an important cause of significant morbidity, short and long-term sequelae especially infertility . Genital tuberculosis usually occurs secondary to pulmonary (commonest) or extrapulmonary TB like gastrointestinal , renal, skeletal , and miliary TB . However, primary genital TB can rarely occur in women whose male partners have active genitourinary TB754 (e.g., tuberculosis epididymitis ) by transmission through infected semen Most common site involved in secondary genital TB is fallopian tube (90-100 %) >endometrium (50-80%) >ovaries (20-30%) >cervix 5-15%) >vulva. The most common symptom of genital TB is infertility . Causes of infertility in genital TB : • Tubal blockage • If tubes are patent , then also infertility occurs due to loss of tubal function. • Tubercular endometritis causes uterine scarring resulting in the destruction of the endometrium . • Ovarian damage with poor ovarian reserve and volume A laparoscopy and dye hydrotubation (lap and dye test ) is the most reliable tool to diagnose genital TB , especially for tubal, ovarian and peritoneal disease . The test can be combined with hysteroscopy . Multiple drug therapy ( ATT regimen provided by DOTS) in adequate doses and for sufficient duration is the mainstay in the treatment of TB including genital tuberculosis .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young woman with fertility issues is diagnosed to have genital tuberculosis . Which of the following statements is false about this condition?

options.a: The causative agent is Mycobacterium bovis
options.b: It generally occurs secondary to a primary focus
options.d: It commonly presents as a unilateral condition

mcqs.explanation: Genital tuberculosis is a bilateral condition. It can be caused by both Mycobacterium tuberculosis (95% cases ) and Mycobacterium bovis (5% cases ). It almost always occurs secondary to a primary focus elsewhere in the body. The most common primary focus is lungs > lymph nodes > abdomen > generalised miliary infection . It mostly spreads hematogenously . Lymphatic spread is also seen sometimes . It can rarely spread by direct contact with the affected intraabdominal organs or peritoneum . The fallopian tubes are the first to be affected . The disease subsequently spreads to other genital organs and the peritoneum . This is followed by the involvement of bilateral pelvic lymph nodes . Vulvovaginal involvement is usually secondary to uterine involvement. The most common presentation of genital tuberculosis in the reproductive age group is infertility .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common presenting symptom of genital tuberculosis in the reproductive age group?
mcqs.explanation: The most common presentation of genital tuberculosis in the reproductive age group is infertility . Genital tuberculosis mostly presents in young women in the reproductive age group. It can present as: • Infertility is the only complaint in 35-60 % of cases . Of these , % of women present with primary infertility . • Menstrual abnormalities are seen in 10 - % of cases . • Asymptomatic in 10 % of cases .755 • Other symptoms like fever and malaise can be seen . The treatment of infertility in women with genital TB depends on the condition of the endometrium. If the endometrium is receptive and the uterus is normal , then assisted reproductive techniques such as in-vitro fertilisation can be tried. If the endometrium is unfavourable then surrogacy may be considered .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In a patient with tubercular salpingitis , which of the following statements is false ?

options.a: The tubes are enlarged , roughened , and may show presence of greyish tubercles
options.b: The ampulla of the tube appears dilated with the fimbrial end open and pouting
options.c: The granulomas and hyperplasia seen can be mistaken for carcinoma
options.d: The fimbriae are commonly involved in advanced tuberculous salpingitis

mcqs.explanation: The fimbriae are often spared even in advanced forms of tubercular salpingitis . The involvement of fallopian tubes is 100 % and bilateral, secondary to hematogenous spread . The ampullary part of the tube appears dilated with the fimbrial end open and pouting . This gives the characteristic tobacco-pouch appearance as seen in the image below .The external surface of the tubes are enlarged , roughened , and may show the presence of greyish tubercles . The cut section shows yellowish-grey caseous matter in the lumen. Sometimes , serosanguinous fluid can also be seen in the lumen of the fallopian tube . This is called tuberculous hematosalpinx . On histopathological examination of the tubes , granulomas and chronic inflammatory infiltrate with hyperplasia is seen . This could be mistaken for malignancy as it also produces a similar histological image.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An 18-year-old girl presents with a history of low-grade fever, weight loss, abdominal pain and amenorrhoea for six months. On examination, a pelvic mass is felt on the left side and signs of ascites are positive . What is your diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with abdominal pain, amenorrhoea, pelvic mass and ascites is suggestive of genital tuberculosis . Genital tuberculosis :756 It is caused by M. tuberculosis and almost always occurs secondary to primary infection elsewhere in the extragenital states . The sites and frequency of involvement are as follows : • Fallopian tubes (90-100 %) • Endometrium (50-60%) • Ovaries (20 -30%) • Cervix (5-15%) • Vulva and vagina (< 1%) Presentation is variable and it can be asymptomatic in 10 -20 % of cases , infertility , menstrual irregularities, abdominal pain and mass, vaginal discharge , fistula formation, ectopic pregnancy and ascites . The mass is made up of rolled -up omentum that is adherent to the uterus and adnexa. Constitutional symptoms such as fever, weakness , anorexia or night sweats may be present . Investigations: • CBC, ESR and Mantoux test • Hysterosalpingography shows a lead -pipe appearance of the fallopian tube , calcification of the tube , beading and variation in the filling, cornual block, jagged fluffiness of tubal outline and tobacco pouch appearance of hydrosalpinx and pyosalpinx . • Laparoscopy establishes the diagnosis of genital TB . It shows tuberculous lesions and perihepatic adhesions (if present ). Differential diagnosis: • Ovarian cyst , broad ligament cyst or encysted fluid • Pelvic inflammatory disease • Ectopic pregnancy • Carcinoma cervix • Elephantiasis of the vulva • Pregnancy • Puberty menorrhagia and postmenopausal bleeding • Fungal infection and sarcoidosis Management : It is treated with anti-tubercular therapy for 6 months (DOT strategy ): Indications and contraindications for surgery: Types of surgery include vulvectomy (if vulval hypertrophy is present ), removal of the adnexal mass, drainage of pyometra and fistula repair. TAH +BSO is rarely required nowadays. Tuboplasty is contraindicated . Option B: Ovarian tumors usually don't affect menstrual cycles . Though virilizing tumors can cause amenorrhoea, other features of virilization such as hirsutism, flattening of breasts, and enlargement of the clitoris are generally present .757 Option C: Though ectopic pregnancy may be suspected here, the tube is likely to rupture with exacerbation of pain, bleeding , and peritonitis before six months of gestation . Additionally, the absence of vaginal bleeding /spotting , and the presence of weight loss makes the diagnosis unlikely. Option D: Submucous fibroid is associated with menorrhagia.First 2 months Next 4 months Isoniazid 15 mg/ kg body wei ghtRifampicin 450-600 mgP yrazinamide 30 mg/body wei ghtEthambutol 30 mg/ kg bo dy weight3 times a week . Isoniazid 15 mg/kg body weig htRifampicin 450-600 mg3 ti mes a weekIndications Contraindications Unresponsiveness of the dise ase in spite of adequate antit ubercular chemotherapy .Tub ercular pyosalpinx , ovarian a bscess or pyometra .Persisten t menorrhagia and/or chronic pelvic pain causing deteriora ting health status Presence of active tuberculosi s in extragenital siteFavorabl e response to antimicrobial t herapy with the diminishing size of the pelvic massThe ac cidental discovery of tubercul ar tubo-ovarian mass on lapa rotomy in a young patient .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A gynaecologist suspects tuberculous salpingitis in a young woman and suggests some investigations to confirm the diagnosis. Which of the following statements is true about these investigations?

options.a: A differential WBC count shows lymphocytosis in advanced disease .
options.b: The ESR is frequently raised and is non-specific in early disease .
options.c: The Mantoux test is positive and indicative of current exposure to tubercle bacilli.
options.d: The Quantiferon test is positive and indicates latent tuberculosis .

mcqs.explanation: The Quantiferon test will be positive in patients having genital TB . It is an indicator of latent tuberculosis . The Quantiferon test measures the release of interferon-gamma by T cells following stimulation by antigens unique to Mycobacterium tuberculosis . A differential WBC count shows lymphocytosis at all stages of genital tuberculosis . The ESR is frequently raised and is a non-specific investigation at any stage of the disease . None of these tests can be used for confirmation as these markers are raised in many infections . The Mantoux test is positive in 90% of cases of genital TB . It is indicative of past exposure to the tubercle bacilli. It is not a confirmatory investigation but a negative result indicates tuberculosis to be unlikely.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Hysterosalpingography was done in a young woman with infertility and menstrual abnormalities. Which of the following findings would not point towards a diagnosis of tubercular salpingitis ?

options.a: A wedge shaped defect at the uterine isthmus
options.b: Beading and variations in filling defect
options.d: Jagged fluffiness of the tubal outline

mcqs.explanation: A wedge -shaped defect is not suggestive of tubercular salpingitis . It is seen at the uterine isthmus in patients with a history of Cesarean section with a uterine scar. Hysterosalpingography (HSG) features of genital tuberculosis are: • Lead pipe appearance due to rigid nonperistaltic pipe -like tube758 • Beading and variation in filling defect • Calcification of the tube • Jagged fluffiness of the tubal outline • Tobacco-pouch appearance of hydrosalpinx and pyosalpinx • Golf club appearance with slight or moderate dilatation of the ampullary portion of the fallopian tube . • Rosette type appearance secondary to multiple small diverticular like outpouching surrounding the ampulla produced by caseous ulceration. HSG is contraindicated in genital tuberculosis as it causes dissemination of the infection . This further increases the damage to the fallopian tubes . The investigation of choice in genital tuberculosis is an endometrial biopsy . The tubercle bacilli are present in the deeper layers of the endometrium . They come to the surface just before menstruation. Hence , an endometrial biopsy is done 1 or 2 days before menstruation. Menstrual blood can also be used for detecting mycobacteria. An HSG showing the features of tuberculous salpingitis is given below .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The image below shows the hysterosalpingogram of a 37-year-old nulliparous woman. Identify the false statement about this finding.

options.a: It is a thick walled structure on sonography
options.c: Tubal plicae are flattened on histology

mcqs.explanation: The given image shows bilateral hydrosalpinx. It appears as a thin-walled structure . A hydrosalpinx is a chronic cystic swelling of the fallopian tube that forms after a distal tubal obstruction. The tubes are enormously distended due to filling with clear serous fluid and become retort-shaped . On histology , the tubal plicae appear flattened . The interstitial end of the tube is open whereas the fimbrial end is indrawn and closed . This permits the dye to enter but not exit the tube during HSG. It is caused due to:759 • Pelvic inflammatory disease • Endometriosis • Tuberculosis - tubercular salpingitis may also cause tobacco-pouch appearance , lead pipe appearance and pyosalpinx • Fallopian tube neoplasms (rare) It can be an incidental finding during a pelvic exam or ultrasound. The patient may be asymptomatic , or present with infertility or chronic pelvic pain. On HSG, it appears as terminal sacculation and occlusion of both fallopian tubes with a normal uterine cavity. Usually , a thin-walled , hypoechoic , cystic structure is seen . However, it may appear as multiple hyperechoic mural nodules around the inner circumference of the tube creating a 'beads on a string' appearance . Treatment: • Treat the underlying cause • Laparoscopic salpingostomy - in mild disease • IVF recommended for women with infertility and severe hydrosalpinx760

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the accepted minimum period of sexual cohabitation required to establish the diagnosis of infertility in a couple ?
mcqs.explanation: The accepted minimum period of sexual cohabitation to establish the diagnosis of infertility in a couple is one year of regular, unprotected sexual intercourse . Infertility is an apparent failure of a couple to conceive while sterility is an absolute inability to conceive. Infertility is of two types : • Primary infertility - when there have been no previous pregnancies . • Secondary infertility - when there has been a prior pregnancy (although not necessarily a live birth).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of male infertility ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of male infertility is disorders of spermatogenesis . Male factor is the cause of infertility in about 20 % of infertile couples . However, it is a contributing factor for infertility in 50% of cases .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The secretion of FSH in men is inhibited by the negative feedback effect of _______.
mcqs.explanation: The secretion of FSH in men is inhibited by the negative feedback effect of inhibin secreted by Sertoli cells . GnRH stimulates the anterior pituitary gland to secrete FSH (follicle -stimulating hormone) and LH (luteinizing hormone). FSH acts on Sertoli cells while LH triggers testosterone secretion by the Leydig cells . Sertoli cells secrete inhibin B which in turn inhibits FSH but stimulate LH secretion .770

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old man underwent semen analysis as a part of an infertility workup. The results are given below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: In the given clinical scenario, the most likely diagnosis is normospermia. Different types of disorders of sperms are as follows : • Aspermia is defined as the absence of semen . • Oligospermia is defined as a sperm concentration <15 million/mL . • Severe oligospermia is defined as a sperm concentration of <5 million/mL . • Teratospermia is defined as the presence of abnormal sperm morphology . • Asthenospermia is defined as the absence of motile sperms or diminished sperm motility . • Necrospermia is defined as the presence of dead sperms. Note : Morphology > motility is the most important marker in sperm analysis.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: While going through a patient 's file at an infertility clinic, you note his semen analysis is reported to be normal . What had his semen leukocyte level likely been ?
mcqs.explanation: The normal leucocyte level in human semen is approximately 1 million/ml. The semen sample should be collected after 2-7 days of ejaculatory abstinence . The patient should collect the sample by masturbation at the doctor's office . If not possible , then the sample may be collected at home and delivered to the laboratory within an hour of collection .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What does azoospermia refer to?
mcqs.explanation: 771 Azoospermia is defined as the complete absence of sperm in semen . Other types of sperm disorders are as follows : • Aspermia is defined as the absence of semen . • Oligospermia is defined as a sperm concentration <15 million/mL . • Severe oligospermia is defined as a sperm concentration of <5 million/mL . • Teratospermia is defined as the presence of abnormal sperm morphology . • Asthenospermia is defined as the absence of motile sperms or diminished sperm motility . • Necrospermia is defined as the presence of dead sperms.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young couple being treated for infertility require donor semen for artificial insemination. Which of the following is the likely cause of infertility here?

options.d: Presence of antisperm antibodies in the cervical mucucs

mcqs.explanation: Artificial insemination with donor semen is done in cases of infertility where the husband has azoospermia. Azoospermia is defined as a complete absence of sperms. Hence artificial insemination with the husband's/partner's semen cannot be performed . Indications for artificial insemination with husband's/partner's semen are: • Chronic medical disorder • Oligospermia after sperm washout • Impotence • Premature and retrograde ejaculation • Hypospadias • Antisperm antibodies in cervical mucus • Unexplained infertility - direct intraperitoneal insemination (DIPI ) is done • HIV -positive male or female • X-Y fractionation of sperms for sex selection in cases of genetic and chromosomal abnormalities Indications for artificial insemination with donor semen are: • Azoospermia • Uncorrectable immunological factors • Genetic disease in husband/partner • Chronic ill health Sperms can be frozen and used later for artificial insemination e.g. if the husband requires to undergo radiotherapy or chemotherapy , or if the husband is a frequent traveler and is not available at the time of ovulation. Artificial insemination techniques include : • Intrauterine Insemination (IUI)772 • Intrafallopian-tube Insemination • Intracervical Insemination • Direct Intraperitoneal Insemination (DIPI ) Steps required to do artificial insemination are: • The semen is washed to remove abnormal sperms, debris, and seminal plasma containing antibodies . It is concentrated , and its quality is improved by the 'swim up technique ' or by the use of the Percoll gradient. • Semen with normal sperms and good motility is obtained . • Around the time of ovulation, semen obtained is inseminated into the female genital tract. About 0.5 ml of semen is injected 36 hours after hCG injection when the ovarian follicle reaches 20 mm.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Indications for artificial insemination with donor's semen are all except ______.
mcqs.explanation: Artificial insemination with donor's semen is not indicated in idiopathic male infertility . The preferred treatment in such cases is in vitro fertilization (IVF).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with erectile dysfunction requires treatment with sildenafil . Which of the following is not a contraindication for the use of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Pulmonary hypertension is an indication for the use of sildenafil . The contraindications for the use of sildenafil are: • Retinitis pigmentosa • Diabetic retinopathy • Patient on antihypertensive drugs, nitrates • Cardiac disease , previous myocardial infarct, stroke In the treatment of erectile dysfunction, sildenafil in the dose of 25–100 mg is given 1 hour before intercourse . However, it does not improve libido.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of infertility in women?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause for infertility in women is due to ovarian causes . According to WHO, female factor infertility was reported in 37% of infertile couples in developed countries. Male factor infertility was reported in 8% of infertile couples while 35% of couples had both male and female factor infertility. The major ovarian causes of infertility are: • Anovulation (PCOS) • Decreased ovarian reserve, e.g., premature menopause773 In women with ovulatory disorders, clomifene and metformin increase ovulation and pregnancy rates . Less common factors responsible for female infertility are: • Endometriosis • Pelvic adhesions • Tubal blockage • Other tubal abnormalities • Hyperprolactinemia

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old woman presented with secondary infertility following radiation therapy for Hodgkin's lymphoma. You plan to test her ovarian reserve. Which of the following is the best indicator of this parameter?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , the level of follicular stimulating hormone (FSH) is the best indicator of ovarian reserve. Ovarian reserve is the capacity of the ovary to produce eggs . FSH levels are measured in the early follicular phase on day 2 or 3 of the menstrual cycle . A high FSH level indicates that the ovarian reserve is getting depleted and fewer oocytes are present in the ovary . FSH is high in ovarian hypofunction and postmenopausal women. Anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH) is a better marker than FSH for ovarian reserve. Unlike FSH, its levels can be estimated at any time of the cycle . AMH is produced by the granulosa cells in ovarian follicles . Note : Studies show that AMH levels decrease under the current use of oral contraceptive pills and tobacco smoking.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What will be the level of the anti-Mullerian hormone in low ovarian reserve?
mcqs.explanation: In low ovarian reserve, the level of anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH) will be <1 ng/ml. AMH is a glycoprotein secreted by the granulosa cells of the primordial follicle of the ovary . It helps in oocyte maturation and mono-follicular development . AMH is also used in assessing ovarian reserve. In women, AMH is always absent during embryogenesis and is secreted by the granulosa cells after puberty. It helps in follicular development and oocyte maturation. Estimation of serum AMH is used in the study of ovarian reserve in female infertility and secondary amenorrhoea. In men, AMH starts to be secreted by the Sertoli cells in the testes by the 7th week of intrauterine life . It continues until puberty . It inhibits the development of the M\374llerian system . The absence of AMH results in the development of hermaphroditism.774 AMH levels in ng/ ml Interpretation 2–6.8 Normal <1 Poor ovarian reserve >10 PCODHyperstimulation synd rome

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In a woman diagnosed with infertility , which of the following antihormonal substance can be used to induce ovulation?
mcqs.explanation: Clomiphene citrate is an antihormonal substance used to induce ovulation in a patient diagnosed with infertility. Ovulation can be induced by giving clomiphene citrate 50 mg daily, starting from day 2 to day 6 of the menstrual cycle for 5 days.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman with irregular periods was evaluated for infertility , and underwent an endometrial biopsy . The histology image is given below . Which phase is seen here?
mcqs.explanation: The image depicts the proliferative phase of the endometrium . During menstruation, the endometrium goes through three phases , namely; proliferative, secretory , and menstrual phases . Their histological features are given below : Proliferative phase • The glands of the functional layer are simple tubules with regular epithelium . • Arteries become more coiled and spiralled. • The endometrium is thick, the stoma is compact and short straight glands are present . The image below shows proliferative endometriumSecretory phase775 • The secretory phase of the endometrium begins on the 15th day and persists until the onset of menstruation. • Subnuclear vacuolation (presumptive evidence of progesterone activity) • Corkscrew-shaped glands The image below shows secretory endometriumMenstrual phase : Glands shrink with prominent vessels and haemorrhagic spots .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The microscopic appearance of the cervical mucus of a woman having irregular periods and infertility is shown in the image below . In which phase of the menstrual cycle was this sample likely taken?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows the characteristic ferning pattern of cervical mucus which is seen in the estrogenic phase of the menstrual cycle . A specimen of cervical mucus is obtained using a platinum loop or pipette . This is spread on a clean glass slide and allowed to dry. When viewed under the low-power microscope , a palm leaf or fern type pattern is seen in the follicular phase . The ferning is due to the presence of sodium chloride in the mucus secreted under the effect of estrogen . This pattern disappears after ovulation. If it was previously present , its disappearance is presumptive evidence of corpus luteum activity. Under the influence of progesterone , the cervical mucus becomes thick and tenacious and impenetrable to sperms and bacteria. The below image shows the microscopic appearance of dried cervical mucus showing the fern appearance .776

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about the Miller -Kurzrok test ?

options.a: Penetration of > 3 cm at 30 minutes is considered normal
options.b: Cervical mucus is placed alongside husband's semen on a glass slide
options.c: It is done at the time of ovulation
options.d: Jerky motility of sperm is considered normal

mcqs.explanation: In the Miller –Kurzrok test , sperm acquiring jerky motility after penetrating cervical mucus is considered abnormal . The Miller-Kurzrok test is a special test done in semen analysis to diagnose the cause of infertility . It is an in vitro test of sperm–mucus interaction. It is based on the basic principle that a normal cervical mucus permits invasion by motile sperms. It is done at the time of ovulation. The test consists of placing cervical mucus on a glass slide alongside the specimen of the husband's semen and studying the penetration of sperms under the microscope . The penetration of sperm > 3 cm into the mucus at 30 minutes is considered normal . Other special tests in semen analysis include : • Sperm penetration test • Semen–cervical mucus contact test • Postcoital test (Sims' or Huhner's test )

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A post -coital test was done in a couple who presented with an inability to conceive despite staying together for 4 years and having unprotected intercourse . Which of the following conditions cannot be detected by this test ?
mcqs.explanation: The post -coital test can not detect a fallopian tube block. It can evaluate the following conditions: • Sperm count • Sperm morphology • Ferning during the estrogenic effect • Ovulation777 • The ability of the cervical mucous to allow sperm penetration • Detection of anti-sperm antibodies in the cervical mucous In the post -coital test , the couple is advised to have intercourse early in the morning close to the ovulation phase . The woman is asked to visit the clinic within 2 hours of having intercourse . The mucus is aspirated from the cervical canal and spread over a glass slide . Another smear made from the posterior fornix serves as a control. On microscopy, –50 motile sperms are normally seen per high-power field . The cervical mucus is also examined for its quantity and viscosity. The post -coital test is useless in the presence of cervical infection . An immunological factor causing infertility is encountered in around 5% of infertile couples .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: During your posting in the infertility clinic, you notice the following instrument. Identify it.
mcqs.explanation: The instrument in the given image is Rubin's cannula. It is used while performing a hysterosalpingogram (HSG). The cone prevents the retrograde spillage of the dye into the vagina , while the dye is instilled into the uterine cavity. This investigation is performed to study tubal patency in women. Another cannula that can be used to perform HSG is Spackman cannula. It allows for the intra-operative manipulation of both anteverted and retroverted uterus .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with secondary amenorrhea and infertility is diagnosed to have Asherman syndrome. Hysteroscopic evaluation revealed 30% adhesions of the endometrial surfaces , but no agglutination of the uterine wall. How would you classify this patient ?

options.d: Cannot be classified with the given information
