mcqs.explanation: This patient would be classified as a case of moderate Asherman syndrome as 30% adhesions of the endometrial surfaces are present . Asherman syndrome (uterine synechiae ) is classified as follows : • Minimal: <25% adhesion involves the uterine cavity, flimsy adhesions involving the fundus and tubal ostia. • Moderate : 25–70% adhesion of the endometrial surfaces , but no agglutination of the uterine wall. • Severe: % adhesions with agglutination and thick adhesions . Asherman syndrome can present in the following ways: • Secondary amenorrhea • Oligomenorrhoea • Dysmenorrhoea • Habitual abortions • Infertility The causes of Asherman syndrome are:778 • Dilatation and curettage (D&C) • Medical termination of pregnancy (MTP), spontaneous abortions, recurrent abortions • Uterine packing in postpartum haemorrhage • Uterine infection • Tubercular endometritis

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old patient with complaints of inability to conceive underwent the following investigation. Which of the following is false about the same?

options.a: The best time to perform it is before ovulation
options.b: It is perfomed to detect uterine anomalies
options.c: It is the first-line investigation in genital tuberculosis
options.d: Premedication can be done with atropine

mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a hysterosalpingogram (HSG). HSG is contraindicated in genital tuberculosis . Procedure of HSG: • It is best performed in the period between the last day of menses to ovulation, usually on the 9th/10th day of the cycle . • -15ml radioopaque dye is injected into the uterine cavity via Leech-Wilkinson cannula, Rubin's cannula, or Foley 's catheter . • Fluoroscopy is performed as the dye passes through the uterine cavity and fallopian tubes . • If the tubes are patent , the dye will spill out of the tubal ostia into the peritoneum , and smear the adjacent bowel . It is used for the detection of: • Tubal block - It can be due to: • Strictures - fibrotic block • Inspissated amorphous material • Tubal spasm - This can occur in apprehensive patients . It is prevented by premedication with atropine and analgesia. • Uterine anomalies • Uterine polyps • Uterine synechiae • The feasibility of tuboplasty , by studying the location and extent of tubal pathology . Contraindications: • Genital tract infections , such as genital tuberculosis . This is due to the risk of spreading infection . • Bleeding • Suspected pregnancy • Allergy to the dye • Premenstrual phase : • If by chance pregnancy has occurred, it may be dislodged .779 • Thick endometrium might prevent the smooth flow of the dye , at the cornual end. • There is a risk of embolism and endometriosis if HSG is done during this phase .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient who has been trying to conceive for the past 6 months underwent hysterosalpingography (HSG). The findings are given below . What is your interpretation ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a normal hysterosalpingogram (HSG). Both fallopian tubes are patent with a spill into the peritoneal cavity. The following images show the findings of an abnormal hysterosalpingogram : The hysterosalpingogram given below shows bilateral dilated fallopian tubes with no free spill suggestive of bilateral hydrosalpinx:The hysterosalpingogram given below shows a unicornuate uterus :780 The hysterosalpingogram given below shows a bicornuate uterus /septate uterus : There is an overlap in the appearance of the bicornuate uterus and septate /sub-septate uterus on HSG. The distinction lies in the shape of the uterine fundus , which is usually not visible on HSG. An ultrasound or MRI should be done to differentiate between these conditions if intervention is planned .The hysterosalpingogram given below shows filling defects :

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which the following are not the advantages of fertiloscopy over laparoscopy ?

options.b: Trauma is avoided as no trocar is needed
options.d: Good view of the anterior surface of the ovary and genital organs

mcqs.explanation: Fertiloscopy helps in obtaining a good view of the posterior surface (and not the anterior surface ) of the ovary and genital organs. This is an advantage of fertiloscopy over laparoscopy . The other advantages of fertiloscopy over laparoscopy are:781 • The Trendelenburg position is not needed . The procedure can be done in a lithotomy position • Trauma can be avoided as no trocar is needed • No CO2: Hydroperitoneum with saline • Peritoneal spill can be seen Fertiloscopy is a new mini-invasive diagnostic technique that allows the visualization of the posterior pelvis. In this technique , an optical device is introduced into the pouch of Douglas , through the posterior vaginal fornix, under general /local anaesthesia . It can also be used for small interventions, such as adhesiolysis , ovarian drilling, coagulation of endometriosis spots and to perform chromosalpingoscopy and salpingoscopy . With fertiloscopy , surgical intervention can be avoided and it is a good alternative to diagnostic laparoscopy . The image given below is of a fertiloscope .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old woman underwent a workup for primary infertility . On hysterosalpingography , there was a bilateral cornual block. What is the next step in management?
mcqs.explanation: In the given clinical scenario, the next step in management will be hysteroscopy and laparoscopy -guided surgery. Tubal contractions, particularly cornual spasms, can give an incorrect impression of proximal fallopian tube obstruction (a false -positive result ) on hysterosalpingography . Laparoscopy with chromotubation is therefore considered to confirm the diagnosis of cornual spasm. Laparoscopy is both diagnostic and therapeutic in this condition. Hysteroscopy is an operative procedure that provides an endoscopic view of the endometrial cavity and tubal ostia via the cervix, performed in the preovulatory phase . It can be diagnostic or therapeutic . It is the gold standard investigation for visualizing the uterine cavity and tubal ostia. Contraindications to hysteroscopy are as follows : • Acute genital tract infection (Eg : genital herpes infection )782 • Viable intrauterine pregnancy • During menstruation, the view is obscured , and the infection rate is high. • Scarred uterus and enlarged uterus of size \031 12 weeks are relative contraindications. • Cervical stenosis can cause cervical tears and uterine perforation. • Cardiopulmonary disorder due to increased risk of fluid overload and pulmonary edema . • Known cases of cervical cancer Laparoscopy is the gold standard for the evaluation of tubal factors in infertility , commonly done in the proliferative phase . It can be diagnostic or therapeutic . Benefits of laparoscopic evaluation: • Tubes: For detection of tubal patency , block (site and side ), motility , hydrosalpinx change, peritubal adhesions , fimbrial agglutination • Ovaries: PCOS changes , endometriosis, PID, adhesions • Uterus : Anomalies, fibroids • Peritoneal factors: Adhesions , PID, endometriosis , tuberculosis • Therapy at the same sitting (as appropriate)Therapeuticindications of hys teroscopy Diagnosticindications of hyst eroscopy Uterine septumAsherman sy ndromeRetained IUCDPolyp ectomySubmucous fibroidAb normal uterine bleedingTuba l sterilization using sclerosin g agents To study the endocervical mu cosal liningCongenital malfor mations of the uterusEndom etrial tuberculosisMisplaced I UCDEndometrial lesionsEnd ometrial polypAsherman syn dromeCornual tubal blockageDiagnostic Therapeutic (Operative ) Age >35 yearsHistory of pelvi c pain, dyspareunia , pelvic su rgery, adhesionsAbnormal H SGFailure to conceive after a reasonable period (6 months) with normal HSGWomen wi th comorbid pelvic pathology (PID, endometriosis ) Unexplained infertilityRecon structive tubal surgeryAdhesi olysisFulguration of endomet riotic implantsOvarian drillin g in PCOSGIFT and ZIFT pro cedures

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman came to the clinic complaining of amenorrhoea and inability to conceive. She had undergone hypophysectomy for a tumour a year ago. What would be the best line of management for her?

options.d: Human menopausal gonadotrophin, followed by hCG

mcqs.explanation: The best line of management for the given patient is human menopausal gonadotropin (hMG) followed by hCG.783 The patients who have undergone hypophysectomy i.e. removal of the pituitary gland, can not produce endogenous gonadotropins. Exogenous gonadotropins such as hMG are given to such patients . Timed administration of hCG is needed to induce ovulation after the follicle has matured. The human menopausal gonadotropin is an extract of urine from postmenopausal women. It contains FSH and LH in the required ratio for follicular growth . Clomiphene , letrozole , and GnRH analogs stimulate the release of gonadotropins from the pituitary gland. These are not helpful in a patient whose pituitary gland has been removed.784

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Menopause is defined as cessation of menses for a period of _____.
mcqs.explanation: Menopause is defined as cessation of ovarian function for 12 months resulting in permanent amenorrhoea. It is a retrospective diagnosis.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman with menorrhagia is diagnosed with uterine fibroids. Prior to starting treatment , you want to check if she is premenopausal . On which day of the menstrual cycle will you estimate her FSH levels ?

options.a: On day 2-5 after last menstrual period
options.b: On day 11 -14 after last menstrual period

mcqs.explanation: The follicular stimulating hormone (FSH) level is studied on day 2–5 after the last menstrual period to detect the premenopausal stage . It is a period of 3–4 years before menopause and is associated with mild ovarian hormonal deficiency leading to menstrual disorders, especially menorrhagia. The climacteric phase is the phase of waning of ovarian activity. It begins 2 to 3 years before menopause and may continue 2-5 years after menopause . It marks the transition from active to inactive ovarian function and involves physical , sexual , and psychological adjustments .790 The predictors of approaching menopause include : • A fall in the level of inhibin B and a corresponding rise in FSH level • A fall in the level of anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH) - This is a better marker of ovarian reserve and can be tested on any day of the cycle .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the diagnostic value of FSH in menopause ?
mcqs.explanation: The diagnostic value of FSH in menopause is >40 mIU/mL . Hormone levels in menopausal women:Hormone Level Estradiol 5 to 25 pg /m l FSH >40 mIU/m L LH 50-100 mIU L/ml Growth hormone, inhibin B, AMH Decreases

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the average age of menopause ?
mcqs.explanation: The average age of menopause in India is 47 years, and ranges from 45 to 50 years. Menopause sets in when the follicle number falls below 1000 . If this happens before 40 years, it is termed premature menopause while attaining it after 55 years is delayed menopause . The age at which menopause is attained is not related to age at menarche, race, number of pregnancies, socio-economic status , or oral contraceptive pills usage . However, it is directly influenced by smoking and genetic disposition .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A menopausal woman presents with complaints of hot flushes . Which of the following neurotransmitters are responsible for these symptoms ?
mcqs.explanation: Norepinephrine and serotonin are responsible for hot flushes in menopausal women. A fall in the level of estrogen causes a reduction in hypothalamic endorphins. This causes a release of more norepinephrine and serotonin, which lower the set point in the thermoregulatory nucleus . As a result , the heat -loss mechanism is triggered by even subtle changes in core body temperature . Risk factors for hot flushes : • Low estradiol levels791 • High BMI • Sedentary lifestyle • Surgical menopause has increased risk • Low socioeconomic status • History of premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) • Depression .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 53-year-old woman presents with episodes of sensation of intense heat involving the face and upper chest which rapidly spreads across the entire body. The episodes last about 2-4 minutes and are associated with profuse sweating . What is the most effective treatment for her?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical features are suggestive of vasomotor symptoms (hot flushes ) in a menopausal woman for which the most effective treatment is estrogen therapy . Treatment options include : • Hormonal • Estrogen therapy - most effective • Combined OC pills - given when estrogen is contraindicated • Tibolone • Non-hormonal • Clonidine • SSRIs (eg : fluoxetine ) • Dopamine antagonist • Non-prescriptive • Vitamin E • Soya • Isoflavones Hormone therapy is only indicated for the treatment of vasomotor symptoms , osteoporosis (prevention and treatment ), and vaginal atrophy. Endometrial hyperplasia can occur after 6 months of estrogen therapy . Hence , for patients with a uterus , it is recommended to add micronized progesterone . This is not necessary for women who have undergone hysterectomy . Note : Even though OCPs contain both estrogen and progesterone , a lesser dosage of each component is given for the treatment of hot flushes .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 53-year-old postmenopausal lady presented with complaints of dyspareunia and vaginal spotting . On examination, the vagina appeared pale with small petechiae . Transvaginal ultrasound revealed a 3mm thick endometrium with no abnormality. Which among the following would be the next step in management?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario is suggestive of atrophic vaginitis. The next step in management should be topical estrogen therapy such as the estradiol -releasing vaginal ring.792 Atrophic vaginitis is a common cause of post -menopausal bleeding due to low estradiol levels . Patients may present with dry vagina , dyspareunia and a purulent or blood-tinged discharge . The vagina appears pale , dry, and may show petechiae . Treatment of atrophic vaginitis involves topical estrogens in the form of creams, tablets , or rings. Estrogen replacement restores vaginal mucosal elasticity , vaginal fluid secretion levels , blood flow , and sensorimotor responses . Systemic therapy may help prevent recurrence. Vaginal lubricants and moisturizers can be given for symptomatic relief . FOGSI guidelines for evaluation of postmenopausal bleeding :

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Reduction in breast size in post -menopausal women is due to the withdrawal of ______.
mcqs.explanation: The reduction in breast size in postmenopausal women is due to the withdrawal of estrogen and progesterone. Estrogen exerts proliferative effects on the ductal component , while progesterone exerts a proliferative effect on the glandular component.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 67-year-old woman is being screened for osteoporosis with a DEXA scan. Which of the following sites are useful for the detection of early rapid bone loss?
mcqs.explanation: Early rapid bone loss can be determined from a dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DEXA ) scan of the hip and lumbar vertebra. The risk for most fractures is inversely proportional to bone density . The reference standard for the diagnostic purpose is DEXA at the hip (femoral neck or total hip). These sites are superior to the spine in predicting hip as well as an overall osteoporotic fracture. DEXA is used to assess bone mineral density (BMD). It is interpreted as follows :793 Condition T Score range Normal +2.5 and -1.0 Osteopenia -1.0 and -2.5 Osteoporosis -2.5 and below Severe or established osteopo rosis -2.5 and below with one or m ore fracturesOR-3.5 or below even in the absence of fractur es

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Hormone replacement therapy is not indicated in which of the following patients ?
mcqs.explanation: HRT is no longer recommended for the management of menopausal women with ischemic heart disease . Indications for HRT is as follows : • Severe hot flushes • Premature menopause • Surgical oophorectomy • Turner syndrome (gonadal dysgenesis ).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a contraindication for estrogen therapy ?
mcqs.explanation: Hypertension is not a contraindication for hormone replacement therapy (HRT ). HRT can be initiated in patients with a history of hypertension , diabetes , or smoking; provided they are regularly monitored. Contraindications of estrogen therapy : • Breast cancer, uterine cancer, or family history of cancer • Previous history of thromboembolic episode • Liver and gall bladder diseases • Uterine fibroids - as the fibroids may enlarge in size.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about hormone replacement therapy and breast cancer?

options.a: Cancer risk is not increased up to 3 years of combined HRT
options.b: Cancer risk is not increased up to 5 years of estrogen -only replacement therapy
options.c: HRT impedes screening for breast cancer with mammography
options.d: HRT may cause high grade breast cancer with poor prognosis

mcqs.explanation: Breast cancer developing subsequent to HRT is of low grade and has a good prognosis. The risk of breast cancer is not increased up to 3 years of HRT and 5 years of estrogen -only replacement therapy . Lower risk is seen with the use of dydrogesterone in HRT .794 HRT can cause recurrence of breast cancer and is, therefore , contraindicated in a woman who has been treated for breast cancer. HRT increases the density of breast tissue and subsequently impedes the screening for breast cancer with mammography.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You are prescribing estrogen therapy for a woman with hot flushes . What is the minimum number of days in a month during which you should combine it with progesterone ?
mcqs.explanation: A minimum of 12 days (in a month) of progesterone must be added to estrogen therapy . This reduces the risk of endometrial cancer to 2%. The risk of cancer with estrogen therapy is dose and duration-dependent . Combined estrogen and progesterone provides better protection against endometrial cancer. Tibolone is a safe drug and does not cause endometrial hyperplasia .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old woman presents with complaints of vaginal bleeding and mentions that her last menstrual period was 10 months ago. What is the minimum duration of amenorrhoea following which she should be evaluated for possible causes ?
mcqs.explanation: Vaginal bleeding occurring after 6 months of amenorrhoea in women of menopausal age group should be considered as postmenopausal bleeding and investigated . This must be done irrespective of a previous diagnosis of menopause . All postmenopausal women with unexpected uterine bleeding should be evaluated for endometrial carcinoma . Even in those women who are perimenopausal , endometrial carcinoma must be suspected if they fall under the above-mentioned clinical category .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the investigation of choice in a 55 -year-old woman who presents with post-menopausal bleed ?
mcqs.explanation: Endometrial biopsy is the investigation of choice in a case of post -menopausal bleed , as the chances of endometrial cancer are quite high. For those who undergo TVUS and have an EEC (endometrial echo complex ) >4 mm, localized thickening, or an indistinct or nonvisible EEC , endometrial sampling is a reasonable next step . Investigations for endometrial carcinoma include : • Endometrial aspiration biopsy is the first investigation in abnormal uterine bleeding , especially in females >35 years. • Dilatation and fractional curettage was the best method to diagnose but now it is not used . • Hysteroscopy and biopsy is the investigation of choice for endometrial cancer. • Transvaginal USG is used as an adjunct to endometrial biopsy . • Pap smear is not reliable to diagnose endometrial carcinoma . It is more useful as a screening tool rather than a diagnostic tool. If symptoms of postmenopausal bleeding persist , imaging of the endometrial cavity should be performed with one or a combination of the following : TVUS, contrast sonography, or795 hysteroscopy . Note : Surgical staging is the gold standard investigation for staging endometrial carcinoma .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old woman presented with post -menopausal bleeding . Ultrasonography revealed a mass with feeding vessel as shown in the image below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Visualization of a mass with a single feeding vessel on a color Doppler is characteristic of an endometrial polyp . In contrast, submucous leiomyomas often receive blood flow from multiple vessels (option A). Endometrial polyps are soft , fleshy growths within the uterus that consist of endometrial glands, fibrous stroma, and surface epithelium . Risk factors for endometrial polyps include increasing age , obesity , and tamoxifen use . They are usually asymptomatic . When symptomatic , they present with heavy menstrual bleeding , prolonged bleeding , intermenstrual bleeding , or infertility . The main diagnostic tools for endometrial polyps include transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) with applied color Doppler , saline infusion sonography, and hysteroscopy . The risk factors for the malignant transformation include postmenopausal status , age older than 60, and abnormal bleeding . Other factors such as larger polyp size (>1.5 cm), tamoxifen use , diabetes , and obesity may also contribute to a higher risk . Hysteroscopic polypectomy may be considered most effective for symptomatic women or those with risk factors for malignant transformation.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient is planned to undergo hysteroscopic polypectomy using bipolar electrocautery . What is the ideal agent for distention ?
mcqs.explanation: Normal saline is the ideal fluid media used for bipolar electrocautery as it can function regardless of the fluid electrolyte content . Normal saline and lactated Ringer solutions are commonly used isotonic, electrolyte -containing fluids in operating rooms for diagnostic hysteroscopy procedures . These solutions can cause volume overload and, if rapidly absorbed in large volumes, may lead to pulmonary edema . Isotonic, electrolyte -containing fluids are contraindicated for use with monopolar electrosurgical devices because they conduct electrical current, dissipate instrument energy and render the instrument ineffective . Low-viscosity, electrolyte -poor fluids such as 1.5-percent glycine , 3-percent sorbitol, and 5-percent mannitol are preferred as they are non-conductive and can be safely used with monopolar electrosurgical energy devices . The primary risk of using hypotonic , hypoosmolar solutions is the intravascular absorption of these fluids , which can lead to acute hyponatremia and hypo osmolality . The criteria for terminating the procedure for electrolyte -deficient fluid is a deficit of 1 L and e lectrolyte - rich fluid is a deficit of 2.5 L.796

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which is the most common type of ovarian tumor?
mcqs.explanation: Epithelial tumors are the most common type of ovarian tumors.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most carcinogenic gene in ovarian cancer?
mcqs.explanation: BRCA 1 is the most carcinogenic gene in ovarian cancer.805 5–10% of malignant ovarian tumors are genetic . BRCA 1 is associated with hereditary breast-ovarian cancer syndrome. BRCA 1 is on chromosome 17q and BRCA 2 is on chromosome 13q . MSH2 and MLH1 gene mutation is seen in hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC). It is associated with malignancy of the colon, ovary , and endometrium .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which among the following reduces the risk of developing ovarian cancers?
mcqs.explanation: Bilateral tubectomy and hysterectomy reduce the risk of ovarian cancer. Some ovarian malignancies originate in the fallopian tubes as dysplastic lesions which later spread to the ovary (dropping down theory ). Thus, bilateral tubectomy reduces the risk of ovarian malignancy. Risk factors for ovarian cancer: • Advancing age • Early menarche and late menopause • Talc exposure to the perineum • Family history of breast / ovarian cancer • Ovulation induction therapy by clomiphene citrate Protective factors against ovarian cancer: • Use of oral contraceptive pills • Multiparity • Breastfeeding • Anovulation.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which among the following is the largest benign ovarian tumor?
mcqs.explanation: Mucinous cystadenoma is the largest benign ovarian tumor. Mucinous cystadenoma is a mucoid-containing, thick-walled cyst . It is usually multilocular and lined by single columnar epithelium . It is the third most common epithelial tumor of the ovary . It has a 10 % chance of becoming malignant. About 40% of dermoid cysts are found in conjunction with mucinous cystadenomas .806

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding borderline ovarian tumors?

options.a: Mitotic figures are < 4/10 high power field
options.d: Serous type is more common than mucinous type

mcqs.explanation: Stromal invasion is not seen in borderline ovarian tumors. Borderline tumors of the ovary (also called tumors of low malignant potential ) are a heterogeneous group of lesions defined histologically by atypical epithelial proliferation without stromal invasion . The clinical progression of these tumors is distinct from ovarian carcinoma , so they are considered a distinct clinical entity . Features of borderline ovarian tumors: • No stromal invasion • Mitotic figures <4/10 high power field • Survival rate is 90% • Usually occurs between 35-55 years of age • Serous type is the most common, followed by mucinous type .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding ovarian cysts ?

options.a: Cobweb appearance is seen on USG in haemorrhagic cyst
options.b: Theca lutein cyst regresses with a fall in hCG levels
options.c: Leutoma of pregnancy is associated with multiple pregnancy
options.d: Follicular cyst is a benign epithelial tumor

mcqs.explanation: Follicular cyst is a physiological /functional cyst of the ovary . Physiological /functional cysts of the ovary : • Follicular cyst - Failure of rupture of the follicle during ovulation. • Theca lutein cyst - Stimulation of atretic follicles by abnormal HCG levels . It regresses when hCG levels fall. • Luteoma of pregnancy - Due to prolonged elevation of hCG, like in multiple pregnancies .807 Hemorrhagic ovarian cysts usually occur due to bleeding into the corpus luteum or other functional cysts at the time of ovulation. Hemorrhagic cysts are normal findings in ovulatory women, generally resolving within 8 weeks . Cobweb appearance on USG in a hemorrhagic cyst is shown below .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Meigs ' syndrome was suspected in a woman with right-sided pleural effusion , ascites , and an ovarian tumor. Which of the following statements is false regarding this condition?

options.a: Can be caused by ovarian fibroma
options.b: The tumor would be immobile with an irregular surface
options.c: Ascites and hydrothorax resolve after resection of the tumor
options.d: Pleural effusion is more common on the right side

mcqs.explanation: In Meig 's syndrome, a benign ovarian mass is likely to be seen . Irregular surface and immobility are features of malignant tumors. Meig 's syndrome is characterized by a triad of: • Benign ovarian tumors • Ascites • Right-sided pleural effusion . The pleural effusions are usually right-sided , even though the left -sided and bilateral effusions are possible . Tumors causing Meigs ' syndrome include ovarian fibroma, granulosa cell tumor, Brenner tumor, or thecoma . However, when the causative factor is ovarian secondaries , leiomyoma, and benign ovarian cysts (such as teratoma and mucinous cystadenoma), the condition is called Pseudo Meigs ' syndrome. Resolution of ascites and pleural effusion is seen after the removal of the tumor. Management : • Repeated paracentesis for ascites . • Unilateral salpingo -oophorectomy in young patients for preserving fertility808 • Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo -oophorectomy (TAH -BSO) in postmenopausal women. Note : Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients may also have a combination of ascites , pleural effusion, and elevated serum levels of CA-125. This is known as Tjalma syndrome or pseudo -pseudo Meigs ' syndrome.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An elderly woman who was found to have an ovarian mass underwent staging laparotomy. Histopathological examination revealed the presence of Psammoma bodies . What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Psammoma bodies are a histopathological finding of serous cystadenocarcinoma of the ovary . They are calcified structures seen in areas of cellular degeneration . Their presence does not denote malignancy. Psammoma bodies are seen in the following conditions: • Papillary carcinoma of the thyroid • Papillary serous carcinoma of the endometrium • Serous cystadenocarcinoma of the ovary • Meningioma The image below shows Psammoma body.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 49-year-old woman presented with complaints of dull pain over the right lower abdomen for the past 2 months. CT scan revealed a left -sided multiloculated adnexal mass and exploratory laparotomy showed small mucoid implants scattered in the peritoneal cavity. Which of the following is associated with this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario and findings point to a diagnosis of pseudomyxoma peritonei . It is associated with mucinous cystadenoma . Pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP) is a rare clinical entity characterized by diffuse intra-abdominal gelatinous and mucoid material on peritoneal surfaces . Spontaneous perforation of a mucinous809 cystadenoma leads to implantation of low-grade malignant tumor cells in the peritoneum . However, the most common cause of pseudomyxoma peritonei is carcinoma of the appendix . Diagnosis is by CT, MRI, and laparoscopy . Even after the removal of the ovarian tumor, these cells continue to secrete mucin. Recurrence rates are high.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 22 -year-old woman at 14 weeks of gestation was rushed to the ER with complaints of severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. USG showed an edematous right ovary with a large cyst and disruption in adnexal flow on Doppler . Which of the following most commonly leads to this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The above scenario is suggestive of ovarian torsion. Mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst ) is the commonest tumor to undergo torsion, especially at the end of the 1st trimester or during puerperium . Management includes derotation and cystectomy in pregnancy irrespective of gestational age . This is also done in non-pregnant women of reproductive age to preserve ovarian function. Resection is reserved for patients in whom malignancy is suspected . Dermoid cyst is the most common germ cell tumor. It is also the most common benign tumor of the ovary in the reproductive age group and in pregnancy. It is bilateral in 10 -15% of cases . Dermoid cyst is derived from all three germ cell layers, but ectodermal derivatives are most common. Rokitansky 's protuberance is the most common site for the development of malignancy. It is seen as a projection covered by skin, sebaceous glands, sweat glands, teeth , and bones. Sometimes thyroid tissue can be seen on histopathological examination, known as struma ovarii . The image below shows a dermoid cyst with Rokitansky protuberance .810

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Staging laparotomy was performed in a teenage girl who presented with an adnexal mass. Histopathological examination showed the following . What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given histopathological image shows Schiller-Duval bodies . It is suggestive of a yolk sac tumor (endodermal sinus tumor). It is an aggressive malignant germ cell tumor of the ovaries. It occurs in ovaries or testes and sacrococcygeal areas in young children. It is usually unilateral. These tumors are usually associated with raised AFP and alpha 1 antitrypsin. The image below depicts Schiller-Duval bodies . It consists of a central capillary surrounded by tumor cells , present within a cystic space that may be lined by flat to cuboidal tumor cells . 50% of yolk sac tumors have Schiller-Duval bodies and they are pathognomonic when present .811

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the counterpart of seminoma in females ?
mcqs.explanation: The counterpart of seminoma in females is dysgerminoma. It is a germ cell tumor. It usually arises in young women or in children. It is the most common malignant germ cell tumor diagnosed during pregnancy. They account for approximately 1/3rd of all malignant ovarian germ cell tumors. Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH ) and the isoenzymes LDH -1 and LDH -2 may be used in monitoring individuals or disease recurrence. Treatment involves unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy . It is highly radiosensitive and has a good prognosis. Dysgerminoma was considered to be the most common malignant germ cell tumor of the ovary . Recent data indicates that in the past few decades , their incidence has reduced considerably . Immature teratomas are now the most common type of malignant germ cell tumor of the ovary . The image below shows the histopathology of a dygerminoma, characterized by uniform cells resembling primordial germ cells separated by fibrous septa with lymphocytes .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The most common ovarian tumor in women less than 20 years of age is _____.
mcqs.explanation: Germ cell tumors are the most common ovarian tumor in women aged less than 20 years. Epithelial tumours are the commonest tumours. It accounts for 80% of all ovarian malignant tumours.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following tumors show raised CA-125 levels ?
mcqs.explanation: Non-mucinous cystadenocarcinoma is an epithelial tumor of the ovary . It has elevated CA- levels .812 CA-125 value > 35 U/ml is suggestive of epithelial ovarian cancer. Malignant conditions with raised CA 125 levels : • Ovarian epithelial carcinoma (most common cause ) • Endometrial cancer • Pancreatic cancer • Colon cancer • Breast cancer • Lung cancer • Lymphoma Benign conditions with raised CA 125 levels : • Pregnancy • Pelvic inflammatory disease • Endometriosis • Uterine fibroid • Normally elevated in 1% females • Acute peritonitis

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young woman with an adnexal mass is diagnosed with dysgerminoma. Which of the following tumor markers are likely to be elevated in her?
mcqs.explanation: Lactate dehydrogenase is the tumor marker in dysgerminoma. Dysgerminomas are primitive neoplasms. They are the only germ cell malignancy with a significant rate of bilateral ovarian involvement (15-20 %). It is seen in young women with an average incidence of 20 years of age . It is the most common malignant germ cell tumor diagnosed during pregnancy. They account for approximately 1/3rd of all malignant ovarian germ cell tumors. It secretes placental alkaline phosphatase (PALP ), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH ), and \032-hCG. Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH ) and the isoenzymes LDH -1 and LDH -2 may be used in monitoring individuals or disease recurrence. Treatment involves unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy . It is highly radiosensitive and has a good prognosis.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A post -menopausal woman is found to have an adnexal mass on evaluation. Above what risk of malignancy index (RMI) score is there a high risk of ovarian malignancy?
mcqs.explanation: Risk of malignancy index (RMI) score of 200 or more indicates a high risk for ovarian cancer in a patient with an adnexal mass. Risk of malignancy index (RMI) = U x M x CA125813 • U = Ultrasound score • The ultrasound result is scored 1 point for each of the following characteristics: multilocular cysts , solid areas, metastases , ascites , and bilateral lesions . • U = 0 (for an ultrasound score of 0) • U = 1 (for an ultrasound score of 1) • U = 3 (for an ultrasound score of 2–5). • M = Menopausal status • M= 1 (for pre-menopausal ) • M= 3 (for post -menopausal ) • CA-125 = Serum CA-125 level (in IU/ml) For any post -menopausal woman with an ovarian cyst of size >1cm, RMI should be calculated .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding Brenner tumor?

options.b: It is associated with Meig 's syndrome
options.c: Walthard cell rests and coffee bean nuclei are seen
options.d: It is not a malignant tumor

mcqs.explanation: Brenner tumors are usually benign but rarely they can turn malignant. Brenner tumor (transitional cell tumor) is a benign, epithelial , unilateral tumor, resembling a fibroma. Histologically , Walthard cell rests and coffee bean nuclei are seen . Brenner tumor represent only 2-3% of all ovarian neoplasms , and <2% of these tumors are malignant. It is called Meigs ' syndrome if the clinical picture is caused by an ovarian fibroma, granulosa cell tumor, Brenner tumor, or thecoma . Meig 's syndrome is characterized by a triad of: • Benign ovarian tumor • Ascites • Right-sided pleural effusion . Pseudo Meigs ' syndrome is when the causative factor is ovarian secondaries , leiomyoma, and benign ovarian cysts such as teratoma and mucinous cystadenoma . The image given below shows Walthard cell rest.814 The image given below shows coffee bean nuclei .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 31 -year-old woman presenting with 12 weeks of amenorrhea and passage of vesicles per vagina is suspected to have a molar pregnancy. On transvaginal ultrasonography , the left ovary appears as shown below . Which of the statements is not true regarding this condition?

options.a: Regresses spontaneously after removal of molar pregnancy
options.b: It is seen with clomiphene administration
options.d: Oral contraceptive use is a risk factor

mcqs.explanation: The above scenario points to a diagnosis of theca lutein cysts in association with molar pregnancy. Theca lutein cysts are not associated with the use of oral contraceptives . Lutein cysts types : • Granulosa lutein cysts - They occur due to failure of regression of corpus luteum after 14 days of ovulation. • Theca lutein cysts - They are found in association with hydatidiform moles , choriocarcinoma, and gonadotropin (hCG), or clomiphene therapy .815 Theca lutein cysts occur due to the hyperstimulation of ovaries as a result of high hCG levels in molar pregnancies and other conditions. They are usually bilateral. These cysts usually regress spontaneously in a period of 2-4 months following the evacuation of a molar pregnancy. Sometimes they can undergo torsion and cause marked pelvic pain. In such instances, laparoscopic untwisting of the cyst has to be done.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman noticed premature breast development in her 7-year-old daughter and brought her to the gynecology OPD. USG revealed a right-sided adnexal mass. The patient underwent laparotomy and the biopsy revealed Call-Exner bodies . Which of the following is true regarding this condition?

options.a: Most common malignant tumor of ovary
options.d: Inhibin A is elevated more than inhibin B

mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario points to a diagnosis of granulosa cell tumor. It is associated with carcinoma endometrium . Granulosa cell tumors cells are estrogen-secreting ovarian tumors. It is seen in 80% of women over 40 years and 5% of pre-pubertal girls. Precocious puberty is seen due to excess secretion of estrogen . It is a low-grade malignancy. It is almost always unilateral. Tumor marker inhibin B is frequently elevated more than inhibin A. Surgical resection is the treatment of choice . On histopathology , it has characteristic Call-Exner bodies . It appears as a rosette arrangement of cells around an eosinophilic fluid space , as shown below .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which among the following high-risk patients are suitable for prophylactic oophorectomy ?

options.b: History of ovarian cancer in a 2nd-degree relative
options.c: Abnormal ovary in reproductive age group woman
options.d: One ovary removed for benign neoplasm

mcqs.explanation: Prophylactic oophorectomy is indicated if one ovary has already been removed for benign neoplasm . Candidates suitable for prophylactic oophorectomy : • Nulliparous aged > 45 years816 • Any age with a history of ovarian , endometrial , or colon cancer in a 1st-degree relative • Grossly abnormal ovary in the premenopausal age group • One ovary removed for benign neoplasm • Previous history of breast carcinoma • Radiation-induced menopause

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 63-year-old woman presented with complaints of pelvic and abdominal pain, and significant weight loss. On CT scan, a bilateral ovarian tumor with pelvic lymph node and liver capsule involvement was seen . What stage does this belong to?
mcqs.explanation: Stage 3 ovarian cancer is a unilateral or bilateral ovarian tumor with pelvic lymph node and/or regional lymph node involvement and liver capsule involvement. Grading of ovarian cancer: • Grade 1 - well -differentiated cancers have cells that closely resemble normal cells and are less likely to spread or recur. • Grade 2 - moderately differentiated cancer cells . • Grade 3 - poorly differentiated cancers show increasing abnormality of appearance compared to normal cells. They are also more likely to spread and recur.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old nulliparous woman is diagnosed with early-stage ovarian cancer. Which surgery should be done in her case?
mcqs.explanation: Unilateral oophorectomy is preferred in a young woman who has not completed her family in case of early-stage disease .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following ovarian tumors is the most radiosensitive?
mcqs.explanation: Dysgerminoma is the most radiosensitive ovarian tumor. They are highly susceptible to radiotherapy.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 62-year-old post -menopausal woman on HRT presented with abdominal pain for the past 6 months. On examination, a non-tender, right adnexal mass was palpable . USG showed a 3 x 3 cm smooth ovarian cyst . What is the next best step in her case?

options.a: Reassure and advise regular follow up once in 6 months
options.b: Confirmation of USG findings by CT scan
options.c: Exploratory laparotomy for evaluation of cyst
options.d: CA- 125 level estimation; if normal , advise regular follow -up

mcqs.explanation: CA-125 level measurement is the next best step according to the latest RCOG guidelines for post-menopausal ovarian cysts . Management includes the following : • Calculation of Risk of Malignancy Index (RMI) = U x M x Ca-125, where • U = ultrasound score • M = menopausal status817 • Ca 125 = serum levels • Laparotomy/laparoscopy only indicated if size >5 cm or RMI >200 . Option B - CT scan is not recommended for initial evaluation. It is done only for further evaluation and when RMI > .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Examination of a resected specimen of an ovarian mass reveals signet ring cells are seen as shown below . Which of the following conditions is this associated with?
mcqs.explanation: Signet ring cells are seen in Krukenberg tumor. A Krukenberg tumor is an ovarian malignancy that metastasized from a primary site , most commonly from the stomach (70%). Carcinomas of the colon, appendix , and breast (mainly invasive lobular carcinoma ) are the next most common primary sites . The route of spread may be: • Lymphatic • Hematogenous • Transcoelomic They are usually bilateral and have a smooth surface with a waxy consistency . They retain the shape of a normal ovary . Given below are the images of the Krukenberg tumor's gross appearance and histological appearance with signet ring cells :818

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which among the following is not a premalignant lesion of vulva ?
mcqs.explanation: Condyloma lata is not a premalignant lesion of vulva . Premalignant lesions of the vulva include : • Vulval intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN ) - most common • Paget 's disease • Lichen sclerosus • Squamous cell hyperplasia • Condyloma acuminata • Bowen's disease (erythroplasia of Querat)

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a common differential diagnosis of verrucuos carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: Condyloma acuminata is the common differential diagnosis of verrucous carcinoma . It refers to anogenital warts and has a verrucous appearance . Verrucous carcinoma is a variant of squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix. It is locally invasive and rarely metastasizes . Condyloma lata is a benign and painless cutaneous manifestation of secondary syphilis . It is characterized by gray to white lesions , typically located in the oro-genital region. Chancre is a painless genital ulcer most commonly formed during the primary stage of syphilis .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A sexually active woman presents with multiple lesions over her genital region as shown below . Which of the following organisms are implicated in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and image are suggestive of genital warts. Human papillomavirus (HPV ) 6 and 11 cause nearly all genital warts. It is usually clinically diagnosed but if co-existing neoplasia is suspected then a biopsy is required. HPV serotyping is not required for routine diagnosis.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the earliest symptom in patients with vulval intraepithelial neoplasia ?
mcqs.explanation: Pruritus is the earliest symptom of VIN as well as vulvar cancer. Clinical features of VIN include :825 • Pruritus • White discharge per vagina • Dyspareunia • Vaginal bleeding

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman with vaginal itching is suspected to have vulval intraepithelial neoplasia . Which of the following is the most common cause of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: HPV 16 is the most common cause of vulval intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN ). Causes of VIN include : • HPV 16, 18, , • HSV 2 • Syphilis • Gonorrhea • Gardnerella vaginalis

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An elderly woman is diagnosed with vulval intraepithelial neoplasia 3. Which of the following is false regarding this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Elderly women with vulval intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN ) - 3 are HPV negative . VIN 3 is of two types : • Young women – HPV +ve, multiple lesion, 90% regress • Elderly women – HPV –ve, single lesion, associated with lichen sclerosis , often progress to invasive cancer

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Sentinel lymph node biopsy is most useful in which of the following gynecological malignancies?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given gynecological malignancies, sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB ) is most useful in vulval carcinomas. This is because women with earlier stages of vulval cancer can have diseased lymph nodes even without palpable enlargement of nodes. Hence , sentinel lymph node biopsy helps in early diagnosis lymph node spread which can be managed by lymph node dissection . A sentinel lymph node is a physiologically , the first lymph node to receive tumor lymphatic drainage. Malignancies where sentinel lymph node biopsy is commonly done are : • Vulval carcinoma • Breast carcinoma826 • Penile carcinoma • Malignant melanoma Lymphatic mapping is similar technique to SLNB that can also be used in vulval cancers.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which is most common type of vulval cancer?
mcqs.explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common type of vulval cancer. Other types of vulval cancer include : • Adenocarcinoma • Melanoma • Basal cell carcinoma • Sarcoma

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common type of vaginal cancer likely to be seen in a woman with a history of intrauterine di-ethyl stilbesterol exposure?
mcqs.explanation: Clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina is commonly seen in adoloscent girls with a history of intrauterine DES exposure . It involves the upper third of the anterior vaginal wall. Radical hysterectomy , vaginectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy is the treatment of choice . The most common lesion due to DES exposure is vaginal adenosis and not clear cell adenocarcinoma. It is a benign condition.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common site of vulval cancers?
mcqs.explanation: The most common site of vulval cancer is labia majora > clitoris > labia minora .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Vulvar carcinoma was diagnosed in a 68-year-old woman who presented with itching and mass over the vulva for 6 months. Sentinel lymph node biopsy revealed positive inguinal nodes . What is the stage of the tumor?
mcqs.explanation: According to FIGO staging , tumor with positive inguinal lymph node is classified as stage III .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In patients with vulval cancer, what is the least common route through which the malignancy spreads ?
mcqs.explanation: Vascular route of spread is rare in vulval cancer. Lymphatic is the most common route of spread in vulval cancer.827 Lymph node status is the most important prognostic factor. The sentinel lymph node biopsy is helpful for evaluating the spread of vulval cancer. Lymph nodes involved are, superficial inguinal nodes (sentinel node) > deep inguinal nodes > femoral group of nodes .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An elderly woman is found to have abnormal cells on a pap smear. Further investigations reveal vaginal squamous cell carcinoma extending up to the pelvic wall. There is no evidence of distant metastasis . What is the stage of the tumor in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Vaginal cancer extending up to the pelvic wall is stage III . Vaginal cancer commonly affects females >70 years of age . Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common histologic type . It commonly involves the upper third of the posterior wall of the vagina . Patients are mostly asymptomatic . They may present with painless abnormal vaginal bleeding , post-coital bleed , and foul -smelling discharge per vagina . Vaginal cancer staging : • Stage 0 - Vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia • Stage I - Carcinoma limited to the vaginal wall • Stage II - Carcinoma extending beyond the vagina , but not extending to the pelvic walls • Stage III - Carcinoma extends up to the pelvic walls • Stage IVA - Carcinoma extending beyond the true pelvis/or involving the bladder and/or rectum, or evidence of distant metastasis • Stage IVB - Spread to the distant metastasis

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old presented with a lesion over the vulva as shown below . Bilateral inguinal lymph nodes were palpable . Biopsy of the lesion revealed cells containing large, pleomorphic nuclei . Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.a: It is the 2nd most common vulval cancer
options.b: The most common site is clitoris
options.c: It may arise from a junctional naevus
options.d: Radical vulvectomy with bilateral regional lymphadenectomy is the preferred treatment

mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of vulval melanoma. The most commonly involved site is labia majora followed by labia minora and clitoris. Vulval melanoma is the second most common vulval cancer. It may arise from junctional naevus. It has a high propensity for local and distant recurrence and has a poor prognosis. Radical vulvectomy and bilateral regional lymphadenectomy is the preferred treatment .828

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which serotype of HPV is responsible for carcinoma cervix?
mcqs.explanation: HPV serotypes 16, 18, , 33, 35, 39, 45, 52, 56, 58, 59, 68 are associated with carcinoma cervix. Risk factors for carcinoma cervix include : • Human Papilloma virus (most important) • Sexual intercourse before 18 years • Multiple sexual partners • Multiparity • Poor personal hygiene • Smoking and drug abuse • Women with STD, HIV , HSV • Immune suppression837 Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) or southern blot or Hybrid capture technique is used for HPV DNA detection .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true regarding HPV ?

options.a: E1 and E2 are viral proteins needed for replication
options.b: E6 and E7 are viral proteins needed for malignant transformation
options.c: E6 acts via the retinoblastoma gene
options.d: HPV 16 is the most common serotype causing carcinoma cervix

mcqs.explanation: E6 acts via the tumor suppression gene p53. It increases proteasome -dependent p53 degradation. E7 binds and acts via the retinoblastoma (Rb) gene . The viral E6 and E7 oncoproteins encoded by the high-risk type HPVs (such as HPV 16 and HPV 18) are necessary for malignant transformation. E1 and E2 oncoproteins are responsible for viral replication.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which is the HPV serotype most commonly associated with carcinoma cervix?
mcqs.explanation: HPV 16 is the most common type associated with carcinoma cervix. Associations between human papilloma virus (HPV ) serotypes and carcinoma cervix: • Most common serotype - HPV 16 • Most malignant serotype - HPV 18 • Most specific serotype - HPV 18 • Most common serotype associated with • Squamous cell carcinoma - HPV 16 • Adenocarcinoma - HPV 18 Cancers caused by HPV : • Male - penile , oral, anal • Female - cervix, vagina , vulva

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about the Cervarix vaccine?
mcqs.explanation: The Cervarix vaccine is not protective against genital warts. It is mainly protective against CIN and cervical cancer.Vaccine Type Cervarix Gardasil Gardasil 9 Bivalent vaccine Quadrivalent vaccine Nonavalent vaccine HPV types HPV 16,18 HPV 6, , 16, HPV 6, , 16, 18, , 33, 45, 52, and 58 Dosage 0.5 mL 0.5 mL 0.5 mL Schedule 0, 1, 6 months 0, 2, 6 months 0, 2, 6months838 Vaccine Type Cervarix Gardasil Gardasil 9 Diseases prevent ed CINCarcinoma cer vix CINCarcinoma cervixGenital warts CINCarcinomacervixGenital wartsVulvalcancerVaginalepit helial cancerOropharyngealca ncer Adjuvant AS04 Alum Alum

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: HPV nonavalent vaccine is active against which of the following serotypes ?
mcqs.explanation: HPV nonavalent vaccine (Gardasil 9 or HPV9 ) is active against HPV 6,11 ,16,18,31 ,33,45,52,58. Currently, HPV nonnavalent vaccine has replaced Gardasil which is a quadrivalent vaccine acting against 6,11,16,18. Vaccines available for HPV :Brand name Cervarix Gardasil Gardasil-9 Cervavac Characteristic and HPV subtypes Bivalent:16,18 Quadrivalent:6,11 ,1 6,18 Nonavalent:6,11 ,16, 18,31 ,33,45,52,58 Quadrivalent:6,11 ,1 6,18 Protects against: CINCA cervix Anogenital wartsCI NCA cervix Anogenital wartsCI NCA cervixVulvalin traepithelialneoplas iaVaginalintraepith elialneoplasiaAnal c ancerOropharyngea l cancerHead and n eck cancers Anogenital wartsCI NCA cervix Dose 0.5 ml,IM. 0.5 ml,IM. 0.5 ml,IM. 0.5 ml,IM. Ideal Age range: Ideally at 11 -12 year s or9-26 years Ideally at 11 -12 year s or9-26 years Ideally at 11 -12 year s or9-26 years The targeted age gr oup is 9-26 years

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old patient comes with repeated infections of trichomonas vaginitis, her physician advises for a Pap smear. She asks you regarding the purpose of this test . What would be your appropriate response ?

options.a: It is a screening test for cervical cancer
options.b: It is a diagnostic test for trichomonas infection
options.c: It helps to diagnose cancer in her genital tract
options.d: It helps to diagnose other associated genital infections in her

mcqs.explanation: A pap smear is a screening test for cervical cancer. It is not a diagnostic test (option C). The presence of abnormal cells / a positive test requires further evaluation by colposcopy , cervical biopsy , or fractional curettage . If trichomonas is reported from Pap testing , it should be confirmed by saline microscopic preparation (option B). Cervical cancer screening should start at age 21 . Women aged 21 -29 should have a Pap smear every 3 years, while women aged 30-65 should have both HPV and Pap co-test every 5 years. Women should stop having cervical cancer screening after the age of 65 years. If suspicious PAP, screening till 75 years. HIV + women should have annual checkups until three consecutive negative tests followed by testing every 3 years for life .839 Pap testing should be done prior to vaginal examination. Lubricants should not be used and the patient should not be menstruating during the pap test . The patient should not have intercourse 24hrs prior to the test . The ideal time is around ovulation. Procedure : • The patient is put in a dorsal position, and the labia are parted • Cusco 's self -retaining speculum is introduced • The squamocolumnar junction is scraped with Ayer's spatula : • Bifid end - ectocervical sample • Blunt end - vaginal cytology • Endocervix is scraped with a cytobrush • The sample is spread on a glass slide • The slide is immediately fixed using 95% ethyl alcohol • Stained with Papanicolau stain or short-duration Papanicolau stain (SPS).840

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old woman comes to the gynecology OPD for a routine Pap smear. The histopathology slide is shown below . Identify the cell marked as "A".
mcqs.explanation: The cell marked A is the superficial cell . ACOG guidelines recommend cervical exfoliative cytology every 3 years starting 21 years as screening for cervical cancer. The image below shows a superficial cell (a) and an intermediate cell (b):The image below shows parabasal cells (marked by black arrows):841 Koilocytes are epithelial cells that contain eccentric , hyperchromatic, moderately enlarged nucleus that is displaced by large perinuclear vacuole. It is a feature of HPV infection .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Match the following :
mcqs.explanation: Various systems of classification are used to describe cervical cytology after Pap smear such as: • Papanicolaou classification - describes the exfoliative cytology of the cervix in a Pap smear. • Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) - histopathological description of how much of the thickness of the cervical epithelium is replaced by dysplastic cells • Bethesda classification - it is another method to describe cervical dysplasia The various systems and their corresponding classes are given below :842 where , CIS: Carcinoma in situ, CIN: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia , SCC: Squamous cell carcinoma , SIL : Squamous intraepithelial lesion, ASCUS: Atypical squamous cell of undetermined significance , HPV : Human papillomavirus.Pap classification (1943 ) Cervical intraepithelial neopl asia / CIN (WHO 1975) Bethesda system Grade I Normal Normal Grade II Inflammatory InflammatoryHPV ASCUS Grade III CIN I Low SIL Grade IV CIN II , CIN III , CIS High SIL Grade V SCC SCC

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old lady complains of post -coital bleeding . She has a positive pap smear. What is the next line of management?
mcqs.explanation: The appropriate management of a 45-year-old with a positive pap smear and post -coital bleeding is a colposcopy-directed biopsy . A per speculum examination must be done whenever a female comes with post -coital bleeding in order to evaluate for carcinoma of the cervix. If growth is visible, a punch biopsy should be done, and else if no growth is visible, then a pap smear is done. A pap smear is a screening test for cervical cancer. The presence of abnormal cells / a positive test requires further evaluation by colposcopy , cervical biopsy , or fractional curettage . Cervical cancer screening should start at age 21 . Women aged 21 -29 should have a pap smear every 3 years, while women aged 30-65 should have both HPV and pap co-test every 5 years. Women should stop having cervical cancer screening after the age of 65 years. If a pap smear is suspicious , then screening is continued till 75 years. HIV +ve women should have annual checkups until three consecutive negative tests followed by testing every 3 years for life . Pap testing should be done prior to vaginal examination. Lubricants should not be used and the patient should not be menstruating during the pap test . The patient should not have intercourse 24hrs prior to the test . The ideal time is around ovulation.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old sex worker presented with irregular menses , post -coital bleeding , and occasional foul -smelling vaginal discharge. She was advised to undergo a Pap smear. What is the best time for this investigation?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of cervical carcinoma . The best time to do a Pap smear is around ovulation, but it can be performed at any other time as well . Prerequisites of doing a Pap smear: • It should be done prior to vaginal examination • Lubricants should not be used • The patient should not be menstruating during the pap test843 • The ideal time is around ovulation • The patient should not have intercourse 24hrs prior to the test . Based on Pap smear findings, dysplasia of cervical cells is graded using various classification systems such as WHO grading, CIN grading, and the Bethesda system .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about Schiller's test ?

options.a: Lugol's iodine is used to paint the cervix
options.b: The epithelium is stained mahogany brown
options.d: It detects the presence of glycogen in the epithelium

mcqs.explanation: The abnormal cells remain unstained on performing Schiller's test . Schiller's test , also known as VILI (visual inspection with Lugol's iodine), involves painting the cervix with Lugol's iodine. It is used to detect any abnormal cytology in the cervix and vagina , such as in cases of carcinoma cervix. The normal vaginal and cervical epithelium contains glycogen , therefore stains mahogany brown on being painted with Lugol's iodine. The abnormal cells remain unstained . These areas need to be biopsied and sent for histopathological examination.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following would you not expect to see in the colposcopic biopsy of a patient with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia ?
mcqs.explanation: The basement membrane is intact in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). Features of CIN: • Varying degree of dysplasia • Altered nuclear-cytoplasmic (N:C) ratio • Hyperchromatic nuclei • Mitotic figures • Intact basement membrane.844

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following methods is most commonly used for the treatment of CIN?

options.b: Large loop excision of transformation zone

mcqs.explanation: Large loop excision of the transformation zone (LLETZ ) is the most commonly used treatment option for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). It is also known as loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP). It is applicable for the treatment of CIN anywhere in the lower genital tract. This uses electric current through a monopolar wire electrode to either cut or coagulate cervical lesions . Like other excisional procedures , it is done in the immediate post menstrual phase . The procedure involves minimal patient discomfort, cost, and complications . Since it can be performed using local anesthesia , it has become the primary outpatient treatment modality for high-grade cervical lesions .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which among the following is the treatment of choice when microinvasion of cervix neoplasia is suspected ?
mcqs.explanation: Conization is the treatment of choice when microinvasion is suspected . • Indications of conization • Endocervical dysplasia • Transformation zone is not completely visualized • When there is discrepancy of findings between cytolology , colposcopy & biopsy • Microinvasion is suspected • Indications of hysterectomy • Older & parous women • Uterus is associated with fibroid, DUB, prolapsed • Recurrence or persistent lesion • In -situ adenocarcinoma cervix

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old woman has cervical intraepithelial neoplasia III . What would be the management ?
mcqs.explanation: Colposcopy with LEEP would be appropriate management for CIN III . Loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) is an opd procedure done under colposcopic view and local anesthesia .Here, a low voltage current is passed through the loop and a cone of tissue is removed from the cervix. This procedure causes minimal bleeding and the tissue removed is sent for histopathological examination (HPE). This is the treatment of choice for CIN 2&3 of any age and parity.845

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which is the most common malignancy in women in India?
mcqs.explanation: Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women in India as well as globally . Cervical cancer is the most common genital cancer in India. Lip and oral cavity cancer is the most common malignancy in men. Risk factors for carcinoma cervix include : • Human Papilloma virus (most important) • Sexual intercourse before 18 years • Multiple sexual partners • Multiparity • Poor personal hygiene • Smoking and drug abuse • Women with STD, HIV , HSV • Immune suppression

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding the transitional zone?

options.c: Nabothian cysts mark the original site
options.d: It is limited to external os

mcqs.explanation: The transitional zone or squamocolumnar junction is well outside the external os during the reproductive period . It is the site where the squamous epithelium lining the vagina merges with the columnar epithelium of the endocervix. The original squamocolumnar junction is marked by the presence of Nabothian cysts and glandular openings . It is a dynamic part and moves with age and hormonal influence : • During pregnancy and with oral contraceptives , it pouts out of os. • Following menopause , it gets indrawn inside the os. The cells here are highly sensitive to irritants, mutagens and viral agents such as HPV . Cancer screening using Pap smear involves scraping this area and studying the cells for nuclear changes .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the false statement regarding adenocarcinoma of the cervix.

options.a: Most common site is transformation zone
options.b: Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among women in India

mcqs.explanation: The most common site of adenocarcinoma is endocervix. It commonly occurs in young females and OCP users, and is associated with HPV 18.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You would suspect and evaluate for carcinoma cervix in patients presenting with which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: 846 Patients with carcinoma cervix most commonly present with metrorrhagia, now known as intermenstrual bleeding . Post-coital bleeding is the most specific symptom of carcinoma cervix.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common site of hematogenous metastasis of cervical cancer?
mcqs.explanation: The most common site of hematogenous metastasis of cervical cancer is the lung. About 1-2% of patients with cervical carcinomas present with lung metastases , and 5-35% eventually develop lung metastases . Other common sites of blood-borne metastases include bone, liver and bowel .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old woman comes for follow -up a few months after surgery for carcinoma cervix. On evaluation, she is found to have a recurrence of the malignancy. Which of the following is true about her condition?

options.a: Most common site of recurrence is pelvic lymph node
options.b: Mortality in patients with recurrence is due to pulmonary embolism
options.c: Treatment involves surgery with lymph node dissection
options.d: Recurrent tumor with largest diameter <3cm has good prognosis

mcqs.explanation: A recurrent tumor with the largest diameter of <3cm is associated with a good prognosis. The extent of recurrent disease and involvement of pelvic lymph nodes are prognostic factors for survival . An isolated central pelvic tumour with no involvement of the pelvic sidewall also has a good prognosis. Most recurrences are seen within 3 years and the prognosis is poor with uremia being the most common terminal event. Recurrences most commonly involve the pelvis than the para-aortic or pelvic lymph node. All patients with a suspected recurrence should undergo PET/CT for evaluation and biopsy for confirmation. Treatment involves either radical chemoradiation or pelvic exenteration . Concurrent chemotherapy with cisplatin and/or 5-fluorouracil may improve the outcome .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the true statement about the staging of cancer cervix.

options.a: Clinical examination is the first step in staging
options.b: Tumor markers are important for diagnosis of metastasis
options.c: CT scan is the best method to assess principal tumors
options.d: MRI is the best method to assess nodal metastasis

mcqs.explanation: Clinical examination is the first step in staging carcinoma cervix. Clinical examination was the principal method in staging until the 2018 FIGO guidelines which recommended the use of imaging and histological investigations when available. USG, CT, MRI, and PET-CT can be used to assess the extent of the tumor, nodal status , and local or systemic spread . MRI is the best method to assess the principal tumor while PET-CT is the best method to assess nodal metastasis. FIGO no longer mandates biochemical investigations, such as tumor markers , for diagnosis of metastasis .847

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The CT of a patient with cervical carcinoma revealed a lesion of 6 cm, extending to the upper part of the vagina and parametrium. What is the stage of the disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The stage of cervical carcinoma is II B as it involves the upper part of the vagina and parametrium.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old woman presented to her gynecologist with postcoital bleeding . She was diagnosed with carcinoma cervix stage IB after evaluation. What is the treatment of choice for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Type III hysterectomy is the treatment of choice in carcinoma cervix - stage IB . It involves radical hysterectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy and para-aortic lymph node evaluation. Stage IB is defined as a macroscopic lesion still confined to the cervix, with the depth of invasion \0315mm. It is the first stage in which lesions become clinically visible. Hysterectomy types include : • Type I - Simple / extrafascial • Type II - Modified radical / Wertheim • Type III - Radical / Meigs -Wertheim • Type IV - Extended radical Hysterectomy • Type V - Exenteration .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman is found to have a lesion in the cervix which is 7mm wide and has a depth of 4mm. She has one child and wishes to preserve fertility . What is the most appropriate management?
mcqs.explanation: The woman has stage I A2 cervical cancer and the most appropriate management is radical trachelectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy . Radical trachelectomy is a fertility -preserving surgical procedure . This involves the removal of the entire cervix and parametrium. Cervical conization with laparoscopic or extraperitoneal pelvic lymphadenectomy is an alternative that also preserves fertility .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which among the following are contraindications for radiotherapy in carcinoma cervix?
mcqs.explanation: Post-menopausal status is not a contraindication for radiotherapy in carcinoma cervix. Contraindications for radiotherapy in carcinoma cervix include : • Pelvic inflammatory disease • Young patient (to preserve ovarian function) • Associated myoma, prolapse , ovarian tumor, genital fistula • Vaginal stenosis • Adenocarcinoma or adenosquamous carcinoma – surgery preferred .848

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You are planning to administer radiotherapy to a 58-year-old woman diagnosed with carcinoma cervix. What is the dose to be administered at point B?
mcqs.explanation: In the treatment of carcinoma cervix, the dose to be administered at point B is 6000 cGy. Radiotherapy in carcinoma cervix:Point A Point B Locatio n 2cm above and 2cm lateral to external os 2cm above and 5cm lateral to external os Structu re Paracervical /Parametrial lym ph node Obturator lymph node Dose 7000-8000 cGy 6000 cGy849

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of postmenopausal bleeding ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of postmenopausal bleeding all over the world is senile endometrial atrophy. In a menopausal woman, hypoestrogenism causes atrophy of the endometrium and vagina .The atrophic endometrial surfaces contain little or no fluid to prevent intracavitary friction. This855 results in micro-erosions of the surface epithelium and a subsequent chronic inflammatory reaction, making the endometrium prone to light bleeding or spotting . Hormone replacement therapy is the second most common cause of post -menopausal bleeding all over the world. Cervical cancer is the most common cause of postmenopausal bleeding in India, while endometrial cancer is the most common cause of postmenopausal bleeding in developed countries . Note : Endometrial cancer accounts for only 10 % of cases of post -menopausal bleeding . Still, all postmenopausal women with unexpected uterine bleeding should be evaluated for endometrial carcinoma , since this is a potentially lethal disease .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 58-year-old, postmenopausal woman presented with bleeding PV . Hysteroscopic biopsy revealed complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia. What is the risk of progression of this condition to cancer?
mcqs.explanation: Complex hyperplasia with atypia has a 29% increased risk of progression to endometrial cancer. It has the highest risk of progressing to carcinoma compared to other varieties of endometrial hyperplasia . The risk of endometrial hyperplasia progressing to cancer is tabulated below .Type of hyperplasia Progression to cance r Simple without atypia 1% Complex without atyp ia 3% Simple with atypia 8% Complex with atypia 29%

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which is the most common benign cause of pyometra ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of pyometra is senile endometritis . Pyometra refers the collection of pus in the uterus . The most common cancer that causes pyometra is carcinoma cervix followed by carcinoma endometrium .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which among the following is an ideal treatment for a 55 -year-old female with simple hyperplasia of the endometrium with atypia?
mcqs.explanation: Simple hysterectomy is the best treatment in a case of atypical endometrial hyperplasia in a peri-menopausal and post -menopausal female . Endometrial hyperplasia with atypia carries 29% risk of developing into endometrial carcinoma and hence , must be treated with total abdominal hysterectomy (simple hysterectomy ).856 The presence of any concomitant endometrial cancer must be ruled out by doing fractional curettage (or dilatation and curettage ) before doing a hysterectomy . If a premenopausal woman does not desire to undergo hysterectomy , progesterone can be given and the patient is followed up every 3-6 months. If the atypia persists during the follow -up hysterectomy should be performed . The table below summarizes the management of patients with endometrial hyperplasiaManagement of Endometrial hyperplasia Hyperplasia without atypia Pre-menopausal women Progesterone therapy Postmenopausal women:Sim ple hyperplasia without atypi aComplex hyperplasia withou t atypia Follow up without therapyPr ogesterone therapy Hyperplasia with atypia Pre-menopausal women If patient wishes to preserve uterus ,give High-dose proges terone therapyIf atypia persis ts, then perform Total abdom inal hysterectomy Peri-menopausal women Total abdominal hysterectom y Post-menopausal women Total abdominal hysterectom y +BSO (bilateral salphingo -o phorectomy )

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the minimum endometrial thickness on transvaginal ultrasonography , above which you perform a biopsy in a case of postmenopausal bleeding ?
mcqs.explanation: A finding of endometrial thickness \031 4 mm (according to ACOG) in a postmenopausal women requires further evaluation, such as endometrial biopsy . If the endometrial thickness is \0354 mm in a post menopausal female , malignancy is rare and hence , can be managed by tranexamic acid. If the bleeding still persists , the patient needs to undergo fractional curettage and hysteroscopy . The algorithm for next step for abnormal uterine bleeding in different age groups is as follows :Age group Endometrial thickness on T VS Action Age <40years >12mm Endometrial sampling/Endo metrial biopsy Age >40 years or Age >45 yea rs - Endometrial sampling/Endo metrial biopsy is done irrespe ctive of usg findings857 Age group Endometrial thickness on T VS Action Post menopausal women \0314mm Endometrial sampling/Endo metrial biopsy Post menopausal women <4mm Reassurance+tranexamic aci dIf, bleeding still persists the n do endometrial biopsy

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the most common histopathological variety of endometrial cancer?
mcqs.explanation: The most common variety of endometrial cancer is adenocarcinoma. The other varieties of endometrial cancer are squamous cell , clear cell , and serous . The most malignant varieties are clear cell carcinoma and papillary serous tumor.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following predisposes a patient to develop type 2 carcinoma endometrium ?
mcqs.explanation: Type 2 carcinoma endometrium is commonly seen in menopausal women with atrophic endometrium. Histological classification of endometrial cancer: Note : Type 1 (estrogen -dependent ) endometrial CA is the more common type .Type 1 (Endometrioid) Type 2 (Nonendometriod) Estrogen dependent Estrogen independent Occurs in Pre- and Peri-meno pausal women Occurs in post -menopausal w omen858 Type 1 (Endometrioid) Type 2 (Nonendometriod) Hyperplasia present Hyperplasia absent Good prognosis Poor prognosis Associated with PTEN/KRAS mutation Associated with p53 mutatio n

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following constitute corpus cancer syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Corpus cancer syndrome constitutes of: • Diabetes mellitus • Obesity • Hypertension • Cancer of the body of the uterus . Etiology of endometrial carcinoma : (Mnemonic: Family Has OLD AUNTI) • Family history • Hypertension • Obesity • Late menopause /Early menarche • Diabetes • Atypical endometrial hyperplasia • Unopposed estrogen /increased estrogen \037 Hormone replacement therapy , fibroid, PCOD • Nulliparous • Tamoxifen therapy (Raloxifene has no genito -urinary action) • Infertility/irregular menses . Protective factors against endometrial carcinoma include the use of OCPs, smoking, and multiparity .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A gynecologist is performing the following procedure in a woman with postmenopausal bleeding . Identify it.
mcqs.explanation: The image depicts saline infusion sonography (SIS), also known as sonohysterography . It is usually done after a transvaginal ultrasound, to assess the detailed anatomy of the uterine cavity.
