In this procedure , a balloon catheter is inserted through the cervix and the endometrial cavity is distended with 20 -40ml of sterile saline. The balloon is inflated to block the backflow of the infused sterile saline and transvaginal ultrasound is performed to visualize the cavity. It is used :859 • To determine the endometrial thickness • To determine the cause in cases of infertility • To identify Mullerian anomalies • To visualize endometrial polyps and pedunculated fibroids The image given below shows the appearance of the uterus on SIS.Option A: Transvaginal ultrasound is the initial evaluation for postmenopausal bleeding . Option B: In balloon endometrial ablation, a balloon is inserted into the uterus and inflated with glycine or 5% glucose . It is then heated up, and the endometrium is ablated by the tamponade effect . Option D: In hysterosalpingography , contrast dye is inserted into the uterus via a catheter , and the uterine and fallopian tube anatomy is visualized.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A menopausal patient suspected to have endometrial carcinoma is undergoing a transvaginal ultrasound. Which of the following findings would be inconsistent with her diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Decreased vascular resistance with increased tumor vascularity is seen in carcinoma endometrium. USG findings in carcinoma endometrium include : • Endometrial thickness >4 mm in postmenopausal women and >10 mm in perimenopausal women • Hyperechoic endometrium with irregular outlines • Increased tumor vascularity with low vascular resistance • Fluid in uterine cavity860

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 52-year-old\037 woman with postmenopausal bleeding has an endometrial thickness of 7 mm on ultrasound. What is the next step in her management?
mcqs.explanation: The next line of management in a patient with increased endometrial thickness is an endometrial biopsy . In a postmenopausal woman, the normal endometrium should not exceed 4 mm in thickness. If it exceeds 4 mm, then histopathological examination (HPE) of the endometrium is mandatory, irrespective of the presence or absence of symptoms . In a perimenopausal woman, the cutoff for normal endometrial thickness is 10mm . Hysteroscopy and biopsy is preferred over other blind curettage methods for HPE. A biopsy is made from suspicious areas after visualization so chances of missing the lesion are reduced .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 54-year-old woman with postmenopausal bleeding is suspected to have an endometrial lesion. What is the gold standard investigation to confirm her diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Hysteroscopic inspection and selective biopsy is now considered the gold standard in the diagnosis of an endometrial lesion. It is preferred for the initial evaluation of women with bleeding suspicious for malignancy. Endometrial sampling can be done by hysteroscopic biopsy . It is more sensitive for focal endometrial lesions . Dilatation and curettage may also aid the sampling of endometrial lesions . Ultrasound , CT, and MRI are adjuvant to other investigations. Diagnostic laparoscopy will be required to study the nature of the tumor and its spread if ultrasound picks up a pelvic tumor. The image given below shows the procedure of hysteroscopy .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 62-year-old woman presents with vaginal bleeding 11 years after she had attained menopause . An endometrial biopsy reveals adenocarcinoma. What is the gold standard method for staging her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario depicts endometrial carcinoma and the gold standard method for staging this condition is surgery.861 According to FIGO/TNM classification system , a total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and pelvic and para-aortic lymph node dissection is the standard staging procedure for endometrial cancer. Option A: Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) appears to be the best radiographic modality for detecting myometrial invasion or cervical involvement. Option C: Hysteroscopy visualizes the entire uterine lining and a biopsy is taken from suspicious areas. This is not 100 % predictive , as an early lesion can be missed . Recently , the concern has been raised regarding the spilling of cancer cells into the peritoneal cavity during hysteroscopy . Option D: PET–CT reveals metabolic activity in the tissue and is highly sensitive and specific for detecting positive pelvic and/or para-aortic lymphadenopathy as well as distant metastases in selected high-risk patients with endometrial cancer.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which lymph nodes are most commonly involved in patients with endometrial carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: Pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes are commonly involved in endometrial cancer. The spread is through the infundibulopelvic ligament . Rarely, inguinal & femoral lymph nodes are involved.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient presented with carcinoma endometrium involving >50% myometrium, extending to the vagina but with no involvement of para-aortic and pre aortic nodes . What is the stage of her disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Carcinoma endometrium involving the vagina but having no lymph node involvement is classified as stage IIIB.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is indicated for the treatment of a patient with early endometrial cancer?

options.a: Hysterectomy , B/L salpingo -oophorectomy, lymph node sampling

mcqs.explanation: Early endometrial cancer (stages I & II ) is primarily managed surgically . The surgery performed here is abdominal hysterectomy, B/L salpingo -oophorectomy , omentectomy and pelvic & para-aortic lymph node sampling. Postoperative management of endometrial cancer: In low-risk endometrial cancer, no further treatment is required. In intermediate -risk , radiotherapy is done. In high risk , chemotherapy + radiotherapy is done.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman with endometrial carcinoma is undergoing radiotherapy. Which of the following is true?

options.a: Intensity is inversely proportional to squared distance
options.b: Small blood vessels are most radioresistant
options.c: Rapidly proliferating cells are most radioresistant

mcqs.explanation: The intensity of radiation is inversely proportional to the squared distance . This is known as the inverse square law in radiotherapy.862 Chemoradiation is the mainstay of treatment of stage III and IV endometrial cancers. They are treated with brachytherapy followed by external radiation. Brachytherapy is a form of radiation therapy in which the radiation source is placed close to the tumor. Other options : Option B: Larger blood vessels are more radioresistant than microvasculature. Option C: Permanent non-dividing cells are more radioresistant than rapidly proliferating cells . Option D: Small intestinal epithelial cells (intestinal crypts ), which divide rapidly with no differentiation are the most radiosensitive.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which among the following is the mainstay of treatment in a patient diagnosed with Stage III endometrial cancer?
mcqs.explanation: Chemotherapy is the mainstay of treatment in Stage III endometrial cancer. In order to stage carcinoma endometrium, total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and lymphadenectomy is done (surgical staging ). Thus the management, once staging is done, is mainly postoperative . Up to stage II , radiotherapy can be given. Stages III & IV are managed by chemotherapy such as doxorubicin, cisplatin, and paclitaxel . Note : Stage III is said to be inoperable but debulking surgery is sometimes attempted . However, the mainstay of treatment for stage III disease remains chemotherapy .863

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You notice the following instrument being used to monitor a primigravida in the first stage of labor. What is the investigation being performed here?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a cardiotocograph (electronic fetal monitor) that is used to perform cardiotocography in labor. It can be used in both antenatal and intranatal mothers. It measures fetal heart rate and uterine contractions. It is used to perform the non-stress test (NST) in the antenatal period and cardiotocography during labor.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: During your OBG posting , one of the senior residents asks you to induce labor in a primigravida admitted at 40 weeks of gestation . Identify the following device that you can use for this purpose .
mcqs.explanation: This is an image of cervidil vaginal insert. It is used for cervical ripening and improves the Bishop's score. It contains 10 mg of dinoprostone designed to release at a rate of approximately 0.3 mg/hr over 10-hours.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The following instrument is used to augment labour in a 28-year-old primigravida via low rupture of membranes. Identify this instrument.
mcqs.explanation: 879 The given instrument is Kocher 's artery forceps and is identified by the presence of a single tooth at the tip. Kocher 's artery forceps are used to achieve hemostasis by holding bleeding vessels . They are also used in low rupture of membranes to augment labour or for the surgical induction of labour. The difference between artery forceps and needle holders is in the edge and smoothness of corrugations. Artery forceps have smooth edges and single lined corrugations whereas , needle holders have rough edges and crossed lines forming square to diamond shaped corrugations.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A primigravida was diagnosed with a prolonged second stage of labor due to the fetus being in occipitoposterior position. The obstetrician decided to give a posterior mediolateral cut at the introitus to facilitate delivery . Which of the following instruments would she use for the same?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of prolonged second stage of labor can be managed by performing an episiotomy . In the given figure , the instrument marked as "D" corresponds to episiotomy scissors. An episiotomy is done to prevent posterior extention leading to obstetric anal sphincteric injuries.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The following instrument is used on an exhausted primigravida during crowning of the fetal head. Which of the following is false about this instrument?

options.a: It can be used in caesarean sections .
options.b: It can be used to deliver aftercoming head in breech .
options.c: It is a type of outlet forceps .

mcqs.explanation: The given image shows Wrigley's forceps . These are used as outlet forceps for the extraction of the fetal head . It is used to provide traction force. It can also be used in C-section for delivery of the baby. The instrument is light and short due to a reduction in the length of the shanks and handles . It has a marked cephalic curve with a slight pelvic curve. Conditions that require to be fulfilled for the use of outlet forceps are: • The fetal scalp is visible without separating the labia (crowning) • The fetal skull has reached the pelvic floor, or is on the perineum880 • The sagittal suture is in the anteroposterior diameter or right or left occiput anterior or posterior position (rotation does not exceed 45\260) Note : Delivery of aftercoming head in breech is done with Pipers forceps .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: While assisting in the caesarean section of a multigravida, you see the senior obstetrician using the following instrument. Identify it.
mcqs.explanation: The given instrument is Green-Armytage forceps . Its tips are broad and hence can compress a wide area. During lower segment caesarean section (LSCS), these forceps are applied at the bleeding cut uterine edges for hemostasis .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: An obstetrician performs an aspiration of the endometrial cavity in a woman with complaints of a missed period 2 weeks back. Identify the following instrument. What is the procedure it is used for?
mcqs.explanation: The instrument is Karman 's cannula and syringe, which is also used for menstrual regulation . Menstrual regulation is the aspiration of the endometrial cavity within 14 days of a missed period in a woman with a previous normal cycle . Under aseptic precautions , the cervix may be gently dilated using 4-5 mm size dilators. Then 5-6mm Karman's cannula is inserted and attached to a 50ml syringe for suction. The cannula is rotated , and pushed in and out with gentle strokes. This procedure is contraindicated in advanced pregnancy and in the presence of local pelvic inflammation. The drawbacks of the procedure include a missed implanted zygote or an unrecognized ectopic pregnancy. This procedure is not commonly done anymore.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 20 -year-old woman at 9 weeks of gestation comes to the clinic for check-up following an MTP. On ultrasound, retained tissue was found and the following instrument was used for its removal. What is this instrument?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) syringe. Manual vacuum aspiration can be safely done upto 12 weeks of gestation . However, WHO recommends it as the procedure of choice for MTP only upto 10 weeks of gestation . The indications of this procedure are given as follows : • Medical termination of pregnancy • Incomplete abortion or missed abortion • Molar pregnancy • Endometrial aspiration881

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the following instrument that is commonly used in a dilatation and curettage procedure .
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows Hegar's double -ended dilator which is used to dilate the cervix in dilation and curettage procedure . Pratt dilator is also a double -ended dilator but has a more linear shape as compared to the curved Hegar's dilators. The image given below shows a Pratt dilator.Option A: Hawkin dilator is a single -ended dilator. The image given below shows a Hawkin dilator.882 Option C: Bakes rosebud dilator is a single -ended dilator used to dilate the urethra. It is called so since its tip is similar to a rosebud . The image given below shows a Bakes dilator.Option D: Fenton dilator is also double -ended but it has a notch in the middle . The image given below shows a Fenton dilator.883

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old woman presents with dyspareunia due to scarring secondary to perineal tears from previous vaginal delivery . The gynaecologist advises the use of the following dilator to widen the introitus. Identify this instrument.
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a Fenton dilator. These can be identified by the neck/notch at the centre . Fenton's or modified Fenton's procedure is performed to widen the introitus in women with superficial dyspareunia secondary to scarring. The narrowing of introitus could be due to scarring secondary to perineal tears during childbirth or from conditions such as lichen sclerosus or vestibulitis . Fenton dilators come in sizes numbered from 3-10 and the sizes of the dilators range from 3mm to 26mm . Option B: Hawkins dilator is single -ended . Options A and C: Hegar and Pratt dilators are also double -ended dilators but they do not have a notch at the centre . Pratt dilator is more linear in appearance compared to Hegar dilator.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You have posted a 43-year-old woman with abnormal uterine bleeding for dilatation and curettage in the minor OT. Identify the following instrument used in this procedure .
mcqs.explanation: The instrument shown in the image is Sim's curette . It is a single -ended uterine curette used for dilatation and curettage . It is designed to remove tough tissue from the lining of the uterus for biopsy or excision. The curette features a sharp loop tip to aid in the removal of the uterine tissue .884

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The following instrument is used for all except :
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a double -ended uterine curette with a sharp and a blunt end. It is not used in uterine length measurement . Uterine length measurement is done with a uterine sound which is given below .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a false statement about the instrument given below ?

options.a: It measures the uterine cavity and the cervical length
options.b: It differentiates between chronic inversion and fibroid polyp
options.c: It retracts the posterior vaginal wall to expose the cervix
options.d: It is used to diagnose cervical stenosis

mcqs.explanation: The given instrument is Simpson's uterine sound. It is not used to retract the vagina for cervical examination . This is done using Sim's speculum .885 The instrument is held like a pencil with the thumb and the first 2 fingers and introduced into the uterine cavity by keeping it in the midline and ensuring it is not forced . The uses are given as follows : • To measure uterine cavity and cervical length • To diagnose cervical stenosis • To sound a polyp , IUCD or uterine septum • To break adhesions • To differentiate between chronic inversion and fibroid polyp

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You see a resident use the following instrument to grasp the anterior lip of the cervix in a patient posted for a vaginal hysterectomy. What is this instrument known as?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows vulsellum forceps . It is used to grasp the cervical lip and steady the cervix during vaginal surgery. It is a long instrument with a gentle curve so that the line of vision is not obstructed . Option A: Allis forceps can be identified by continuous teeth , equal on both ends . It is used to hold structures with a firm grip.Option C: Kocher 's artery forceps are non-traumatic with a single tooth at the tip. They help in achieving hemostasis by firm pressure. Option D: Lahey's tissue grasping forceps has teeth similar to dinner forks. They are used to hold fibrous tissue and they give a firm grip without slippage .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the following instrument.
mcqs.explanation: 886 The given instrument is a towel -holding clip. It is used to secure drapings and towels during surgery.Sponge -holding forceps are non-traumatic forceps . They are used for painting and preparation of parts preoperatively. Filshie clips are used for laparoscopic tubal sterilisation . They are made of titanium on the outer side and sialistic material on the inner side .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You are assisting a case of vaginal hysterectomy where your assistant professor asks you to hold the retractor shown in the image. What is this retractor known as?

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: The newborn eye is usually ______.
mcqs.explanation: A newborn is usually hypermetropic by +2D to +3D. The anteroposterior (AP) diameter of the eyeball at birth is about 16.5 mm, which is about 70% of the adult size. This reduced axial length causes light to converge behind the retina, leading to12 hypermetropia . Additionally , the corneal diameter at birth is 10 mm. The adult size (11.7 mm) is attained by 2 years of age . The orbit is more divergent (50\260) as compared to adult (45\260). Note : The lacrimal glands are underdeveloped in a newborn and, hence , do not secrete tears.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: At what age would a child attain full visual acuity ?
mcqs.explanation: Full visual acuity is attained by the age of 6 years. Important milestones in visual development are: • At birth, there is no central fixation, and the eyes move randomly. • By the first month of life , the fixation reflex starts developing and becomes established by 6 months. • By 3 months, binocular vision is established . • By 6 months, macular stereopsis and accommodation reflex are fully developed . • By 6 years of age , full visual acuity (6/6) is attained .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old lady presents with the abnormality as shown below . She is diagnosed with uveal melanoma. What is the embryological origin of the cells involved?
mcqs.explanation: Uveal melanomas arise from uveal melanocytes . Uveal and conjunctival melanocytes are derived from the neural crest cells .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the development of the eye ?

options.a: The macula is fully developed at birth.
options.c: The cornea attains normal diameter by 2 years.
options.d: Full visual acuity is attained by 6 years of age .

mcqs.explanation: The macula is fully developed by 4–6 months of age . Apart from the macula, the rest of the retina is fully developed at birth. Postnatal Development of Eye : • 3 Months - Binocular single vision develops . • 4-6 Months - Macula fully develops . Fusional reflexes , stereopsis , and accommodation become well developed • 6 Months - Fixation, which had started developing in the first month is now complete • 2 Years - Cornea develops to the normal adult diameter • 6 Years - Visual acuity fully develops and reaches 6/6 • The lens, however, continues to grow throughout the life13

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: By how many weeks of embryonic development does the optic groove appear?
mcqs.explanation: The optic groove appears by 3 weeks . By approximately day 22 , 2 small grooves appear on either side of the developing forebrain in the neural folds , these are called optic grooves. As the neural tube closes , these grooves develop outpouchings called optic vesicles . These optic vesicles extend from the forebrain to the surface ectoderm .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Embryonic development of ciliary muscles is from _______.
mcqs.explanation: Embryonic development of ciliary muscles is from the neural crest.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: After conception , the canal of Schlemm appears by __________________ .
mcqs.explanation: 14 The canal of Schlemm appears by the 4th month after conception .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: What is the anteroposterior diameter of the adult eyeball ?
mcqs.explanation: The anteroposterior (AP) diameter of the adult eye is 24 mm/2.4 cm. At birth, the average axial length of the eyeball is 16.5 mm. By 3 years, it grows rapidly to approximately 23 mm. From 3 to 14 years of age , the axial length gradually increases by a further 1 mm, bringing it to the adult size of 24 mm. This overall adjustment in the eye size, including the refractive power , is called emmetropization.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old lady comes to the clinic complaining of problems in her vision. On perimetry , a visual field defect as shown below is obtained . Which of the following vessels does not supply the anatomical location of the lesion?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows bitemporal hemianopia, a defect caused by optic chiasmal lesions . The middle cerebral artery does not supply the optic chiasma. Blood supply of optic chiasma: • Anterior cerebral artery - dorsal chiasma • Anterior communicating artery - ventral chiasma • Internal carotid artery - ventral chiasma • Superior hypophyseal artery - ventral (branch of internal carotid artery).

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A college student comes to the OPD for refractive error testing . Her eyes are dilated using tropicamide. Which of the following statements is false about the structure this drug acts on?

options.a: It is triangular in cross section .
options.b: There are around 30-40 processes in pars plana and pars plicata
options.c: Its epithelium is derived from the anterior edge of the optic cup .
options.d: The pars plana is approximately 4.5 mm from the limbus.

mcqs.explanation: Tropicamide is a cycloplegic drug that acts on the ciliary body to cause mydriasis for refractory error testing . The ciliary body is a triangular structure that contains 60-70 ciliary processes in15 each eye , present on the pars plicata. The pars plana is 4.5mm from the limbus while the distance between the equator and the limbus is 14mm . The ciliary epithelium is derived from the optic cup (neuroectoderm ) by the continued growth of the outer lip's anterior edge .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 12 -year-old girl you examined in an outreach camp is found to have this abnormality. What is the most common site where the condition is seen ?
mcqs.explanation: The condition depicted in the image is a coloboma of the iris, and the most common site of coloboma is the inferonasal quadrant. A coloboma is a congenital malformation in one of the structures in the eye , such as the iris, retina, choroid, or optic disc, due to the failure of embryonic fissure closure . Coloboma of the uveal tract may be typical (seen in the inferonasal quadrant ) or atypical (occasionally found in other positions ). Typical coloboma is of two types : • Complete : Extends from pupil to optic nerve, causing a corresponding lens indentation. • Incomplete : May involve iris alone, or iris and ciliary body (more common), or iris, ciliary body and a part of choroid. Other embryonic remnants in the eye : • Mittendorf 's dot - Remnant of the anterior end of the hyaloid artery • Bergmeister papilla - Remnant of the posterior end of the hyaloid artery • Persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous (PHPV ) - Failure of fetal vasculature to regress The image below shows a fundoscopy view of persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous.16

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A child was brought with complaints of decreased vision. Fundus examination shows a developmental anomaly as shown below . What is the cause of this anomaly?

options.a: Incomplete closure of the embryonic fissure
options.b: Faulty migration of neural crest cells

mcqs.explanation: The image shows a coloboma of the optic disc, accompanied by a large chorioretinal coloboma located below the optic disc, which is caused by incomplete closure of the embryonic fissure . This developmental anomaly may involve the optic nerve, choroid, retina, and iris. Coloboma of the optic disc can present in two forms: a minor effect often associated with refractive errors like hypermetropia and astigmatism and a fully developed coloboma that appears as a large inferonasal whitish excavation resembling the optic disc. Defective vision and superior visual field defects are typically associated with fully developed coloboma. Additionally , this condition may be associated with chorioretinal coloboma, a congenital anomaly where the developing optic cup fails to fuse completely , leading to abnormal choroidal and retinal development . Note : Faulty migration of neural crest cells results in anterior segment dysgenesis .

mcqs.question: What is the embryological origin of the structure marked in the image?
mcqs.explanation: The lacrimal gland arises from the surface ectoderm .17

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: The optic foramen is situated between the :

options.a: Lesser and greater wings of the sphenoid
options.b: Lesser wing and body of the sphenoid
options.c: Greater wing and body of the sphenoid
options.d: Two roots of the lesser wing of the sphenoid

mcqs.explanation: The optic foramen is situated between the two roots of the lesser wing of the sphenoid . The optic foramen leads into the optic canal, which is formed medially by the body and laterally by the lesser wing of the sphenoid bone, connecting the orbit's apex to the middle cranial fossa. The optic canal transmits the optic nerve with its meningeal coverings; the ophthalmic artery, which is below the nerve, is embedded in its dural sheath , and a few twigs from the sympathetic plexus accompanying the artery.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: During a game, a 26-year-old baseball player is hit in the head by a baseball , which fractures the optic canal. Which of the following pairs of structures is most likely to be damaged ?
mcqs.explanation: 18 In the given clinical scenario, a fracture of the optic canal is most likely to damage the ophthalmic artery and optic nerve, as these are the primary structures passing through it. The optic foramen leads into the optic canal, which is a short cylindrical structure bounded medially by the body and laterally by the lesser wing of the sphenoid bone, connecting the orbit's apex to the middle cranial fossa, serving as a pathway for the aforementioned structures along with its sympathetic plexus . Optic canal fractures, often associated with basilar skull fractures, can lead to optic neuropathy . The intracanalicular and intracranial portion of the optic nerve is most commonly affected in head trauma. Note : The greater and lesser wings of the sphenoid bound the superior orbital fissure .

mcqs.explanation: The anterior segment of the eye does not include vitreous humor as it is a constituent of the posterior segment of the eye .Anterior Segment Posterior Segme nt Cornea Vitreous humor Iris Retina Lens Choroid Anterior and Posterior cham bers with aqueous humor Optic Disc

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: The posterior chamber in the eyeball is filled with _______.
mcqs.explanation: 19 The posterior chamber of the eyeball is filled with aqueous humor. The eyeball is divided into anterior and posterior segments . The anterior segment includes the lens and the structures anterior to it, such as the cornea, iris and two aqueous humor-filled spaces : • Anterior chamber: Located between cornea and iris, contains aqueous humor and communicates with the posterior chamber through the pupil . • Posterior chamber: Triangular -shaped space , also contains aqueous humor, bounded anteriorly by the posterior surface of the iris, laterally by the ciliary body, and posteriorly by the lens. The posterior segment includes all structures located posterior to the lens, comprising of the vitreous humor, retina, choroid and optic disc.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following structures is attached to Whitnall's tubercle ?

options.a: Check ligament of the medial rectus
options.c: Check ligament of the lateral rectus

mcqs.explanation: Check ligament of the lateral rectus is attached to Whitnall's tubercle . Lateral orbital tubercle or Whitnall's tubercle is a small elevation on the orbital surface of the zygomatic bone, just within the lateral orbital margin. It is about 11 mm below the fronto-zygomatic suture . Four structures are attached to it: • Check ligament of the lateral rectus • Lockwood's ligament (Suspensory ligament of the eyeball ) • Lateral palpebral ligament • Lateral horn of the levator aponeurosis The Whitnall's ligament or the superior transverse ligament of the eye , is attached to the superior tarsal plate and the orbital bone.20

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the tarsal plates ?

options.b: They give structural support to the eyelid .
options.c: LPS aponeurosis is attached to the superior border of the upper tarsal plate .
options.d: Their medial and lateral ends form the medial and lateral palpebral ligaments , respectively.

mcqs.explanation: The tarsal plates are not cartilaginous structures but firm, dense connective tissue (fibrous tissue ) plates . The tarsal plates serve as the structural support of the eyelids . The height of the upper tarsal plate is about 10 mm, and that of the lower tarsal plate is 4 mm. Both plates have a thickness of about 1 mm. The ends form the medial and lateral palpebral ligaments (medial and lateral canthal tendons ). The levator palpebrae superioris (LPS) aponeurosis is attached to the superior border of the upper tarsal plate . The meibomian glands are located within the tarsus. These are holocrine-secreting sebaceous glands that are not associated with lash follicles .21

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old man is being evaluated for herpes zoster ophthalmicus . On eliciting corneal reflex , there is no response . Which of the following nerves forms the afferent limb of this reflex ?
mcqs.explanation: The sensory supply of the cornea comes from the long ciliary nerve (branch of the nasociliary nerve). It forms the afferent limb of the corneal reflex . The sensory nerve supply of the eye is by the ophthalmic nerve. • Lacrimal nerve- lacrimal gland, conjunctiva, lateral eyelid • Frontal nerve- conjunctiva, eyelid , part of the forehead • Nasociliary nerve • Long ciliary nerve- cornea, ciliary body, iris • Infra -trochlear nerve- conjunctiva, lacrimal sac, caruncle, medial part of the eyelids Corneal sensation is reduced in leprosy and diabetes mellitus (neuropathy ).

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: A 6-year-old child complains that she cannot see anything on the whiteboard clearly. On ophthalmological examination, she is found to have a 2 mm shortening of the axial length of the eyeball . How much eye power will this lead to?
mcqs.explanation: Shortening of 2mm of the axial length of the eyeball will lead to 6D of hypermetropia . In axial hypermetropia , 1mm shortening of the anteroposterior diameter of the eye results in 3 dioptres of hypermetropia . Therefore, 2-mm shortening will lead to 6D of hypermetropia . In curvature hypermetropia , a 1mm increase in radius of curvature results in 6 dioptres of hypermetropia.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: You are studying the optics of a patient with regular astigmatism. Identify the point at which the clearest image is formed?
mcqs.explanation: The given figure is a Sturm's conoid. It represents a bundle of light rays formed by a regularly astigmatic surface . The image is clearest or least confusing as point D, the circle of least confusion. When light passes through a regularly astigmatic surface (surface with toric curvature), vertical and horizontal rays converge at different points. The distance between the points of convergence (focus ) of the vertical and horizontal rays is called the focal interval of strum. (distance between points B and F). The circle of least confusion/ circle of diffusion lies at the mid-point of this interval. For the given Sturm's conoid, • At point A, a horizontal oval is formed because vertical rays converge more rapidly than horizontal rays. • At point B, vertical rays come to a focus, while horizontal rays are still converging; so, it will be a horizontal straight line. • At points C, D, and E, the vertical rays are diverging and horizontal rays are still converging.37 • At point D, the vertical rays have diverged as much as the horizontal rays have converged; so, we get a perfect circle called the circle of least confusion. • At point E, a vertical oval is formed. • At point F, a vertical straight line is formed • At point G and beyond , both rays are diverging, and we always get a vertical oval/prolate ellipse .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: What is the Stiles -Crawford effect ?

options.a: Cutting off of the peripheral rays by the iris
options.b: High refractive index of the core of nucleus of the lens than that of the peripheral cortex
options.c: Low sensitivity of the peripheral retina
options.d: More sensitivity of the retina to perpendicular rays than the oblique rays

mcqs.explanation: The Stiles –Crawford effect refers to the greater sensitivity of the retina to perpendicular rays than the oblique rays. It is one of the natural mechanisms that decrease aberration in the eye . The rays of light that enter through the center of the pupil have higher sensitivity as compared to those entering from the periphery of the pupil . Natural mechanisms that decrease aberrations in the human eye : • Cutting -off of the peripheral rays by the iris • The high refractive index of the core of the nucleus of the lens than that of the peripheral cortex • Low sensitivity of the peripheral retina • Stiles –Crawford effect

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false ?

options.a: Rods and cones release Ach at their synapses .
options.d: Bipolar cells show either depolarization or hyperpolarization.

mcqs.explanation: Rods and cones release glutamate (not acetylcholine ) at their synapses . Photoreceptors get hyperpolarized in response to stimulus , and hence , phototransduction is associated with hyperpolarization. Amacrine cells secrete at least eight types of neurotransmitters, including GABA, glycine , dopamine, acetylcholine , and indolamine, all of which function as inhibitory neurotransmitters. mcqs.question: Which of the following is responsible for inducing phototransduction ?
mcqs.explanation: Metarhodopsin II is responsible for phototransduction . It activates transducin member of G proteins . This leads to the closure of Na+ channels and hyperpolarization, thereby inducing phototransduction (signal transduction in the retina).40

mcqs.question: During the dark phase of the visual cycle , which form of vitamin A combines with opsin to form rhodopsin?
