mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the physiology of photoreceptors ?

options.a: Phototransduction results in closure of c-GMP-gated cation channels.
options.b: Chromophore regeneration occurs in the outer segment of photoreceptors .
options.c: Photon absorption induces photo -isomerisation of 11 -cis-retinal to all-trans-retinal.
options.d: 11 -cis-Retinal is bound to opsins by covalent bonds.

mcqs.explanation: Chromophore regeneration occurs in the retinal pigment epithelial cells . Phototransduction: • Rhodopsin is a G-protein-coupled receptor found in the outer segments of rod photoreceptors . • -cis-retinal (a chromophore) is covalently bound to opsins via a lysine residue on one of the transmembrane domains. • The receptor is activated by photo -isomerization of prebound 11 -cis-retinal to ALL -TRANS -retinal. • Activation of the receptor causes binding and activation of the G protein, transducin, with signal transduction via cGMP phosphodiesterase , resulting in a decrease in the intracellular cGMP levels and closure of the cGMP-gated Na channels. • This causes hyperpolarization of the photoreceptor cell , which modulates neurotransmitter release at the synapse with bipolar cells . • This entire process triggered by the activation of rhodopsin is phototransduction , which occurs in the outer segment of photoreceptors and converts light energy into an electrical signal. Chromophore regeneration : • All-trans retinAL is converted to all-trans-retinOL.41 • All-trans-retinOL gets transported by interphotoreceptor retinoid-binding protein (IRBP ) to the retinal pigment epithelial cells , where it is reconstituted into the 11 -cis retinal isoform.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: What signals are carried by the parvocellular pathway from the lateral geniculate body to the visual cortex?

options.b: Colour vision, shape , and fine details

mcqs.explanation: The parvocellular pathway gives signals for color vision, texture , shape , and fine details . LGB : lateral geniculate body The interlaminar pathway gives signals for color vision to layers 2 and 3 of the visual cortex having clusters of cells called blobs.Feature Parvocellular Pathway Magnocellular Pathway Arises layers 3, 4, 5, and 6 of LGB Layers 1 and 2 of LGB Termina tes Layer 4 of visual cortex Layer 4 of visual cortex Use Color vision, texture , shape , and fine details Movement , depth , flicker, an d spatial organization42

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding "blobs" in the primary visual cortex?

options.b: Are rich in the enzyme citrate synthase
options.c: Are present in layers 2 and 3 of the visual cortex
options.d: Receive input from the interlaminar pathway

mcqs.explanation: Blobs in the primary visual cortex are rich in the enzyme cytochrome oxidase . Blobs are sections of the visual cortex where groups of neurons that are sensitive to color assemble in cylindrical shapes . They are present in layers 2 and 3 of the visual cortex.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: What are Konio cells involved in transmitting?
mcqs.explanation: Konio cells are involved in the transmission of color. The koniocellular pathway is ventral to each parvocellular and magnocellular layer of the lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN). K cells are neurochemically and anatomically distinct from M and P cells . They contain calbindin protein, whereas M cells and P cells contain parvalbumin . K1, K4, and K6 receive ipsilateral retinal inputs , and K3 and K5 receive contralateral retinal inputs . K2 receives both.Lateral geniculat e Striate corte x Extra-striate cortex Higher centers for bod y Magno cells \033 \033 Motion and stereo Parvo cells \033 \033 Form Konio cells \033 \033 Color43

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: What is the visible range of the electromagnetic spectrum of the human eye ?
mcqs.explanation: The visible range of the electromagnetic spectrum for the human eye is 400 –700 nm. Theories of color vision: • Trichromatic theory (Young –Helmholtz theory ) assumes that there are three types of color receptors . Each receptor is assumed to respond to all wavelengths , however, each has different spectral sensitivities . • Opponent process theory , also known as the Hering theory , assumes three sets of receptor systems —red-green, blue -yellow , and black-white . Each one of these functions as an antagonistic pair (e.g., red light stimulates the red receptors and, at the same time, inhibits the green ). • Edwin Land 's theory has three separate color systems (retinexes ). Each is an analog to a black-and-white picture .44

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: What is the characteristic visual defect in deuteranomaly ?
mcqs.explanation: In deuteranomaly , the perception of green color is defective . It is the most common disorder of color vision. Monochromacy: Only one of the three primary colors (red, blue , or green ) can be appreciated . Dichromacy: Two primary colors are appreciated . (anopia = absent). • Protanopia: Red color is not perceived . • Deuteranopia : Green color is not perceived . • Tritanopia : Blue color is not perceived . Trichromacy : All the three primary colors are appreciated , but one of them can be defective (anomaly = defective ). • Protanomaly: Red color perception is defective . • Deuteranomaly : Green color perception is defective . • Tritanomaly : Blue color perception is defective . Achromatopsia: No color perception due to the absence of cones. It may also occur in the lesion of area V4 or V8 of the visual cortex.45

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: Majority of the energy requirement in the lens is met by the ______________.
mcqs.explanation: Majority of the energy requirement of the lens is met by glycolysis . 90–95 % of the glucose that enters the lens is converted to glucose 6 phosphate by hexokinase. The remaining 5% is converted to sorbitol and gluconic acid. The glucose -6-phosphate formed is metabolized in 3 ways: • Glycolysis : 80 % • Pentose phosphate pathway : % • TCA cycle : 3% Energy in the lens is stored in the form of ATP .46

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: What is the angle subtended by the optotype on the second line of Snellen 's chart when viewed from a distance of 6 meters ?
mcqs.explanation: The angle subtended by the optotype (individual letters on the chart) on the second line of Snellen 's chart in the above case would be 30 minutes of arc. The second line on Snellen 's chart corresponds to a distance of 36 meters . When viewed from a 6m distance , it is denoted as visual acuity 6/36. Where, • The numerator (6) denotes the distance from which the patient is actually viewing it • The denominator (36) denotes the distance at which it should be ideally viewed . It denotes the distance at which each stroke of the letter would subtend the minimum angle of resolution (MAR) of one minute of arc. MAR = 1/Visual acuity Each letter is shaped such that it can be placed in a square, the sides of which are five times the breadth of individual limbs of the letters . Hence , the angle subtended by the optotype = MAR x 5 For eg : At exactly 6 meters distance from the patient , the letters on the 6/6 line shall subtend 5 minutes of arc (such that the individual limbs of the letters subtend 1 minute of arc). The equation to calculate the minimum angle of resolution (MAR) is given as follows : For the given question, MAR = 1/ 6/36 MAR = 36/6 MAR = 6 minutes of arc Hence , the angle subtended by the entire letter is 6 \327 5 = 30 minutes of arc.47

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: A 42-year-old man with monocular aphakia wears contact lenses . What is the approximate percentage of aniseikonia in his eyes ?
mcqs.explanation: The approximate percentage of aniseikonia in a person with monocular aphakia wearing a contact lens would be 8%. Aniseikonia is defined as the difference in image size between the two eyes and can lead to disturbances in stereopsis . The tolerable limit of aniseikonia is 5–8%. It is reduced with contact lens (8%) compared to glasses (25–30 %) in aphakia. However, the percentage of aniseikonia is least with an intraocular lens (IOL) (1–3%), thus secondary IOL implantation is the most preferred management of unilateral aphakia.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: Which cerebellar nucleus controls the ocular saccade ?
mcqs.explanation: The Floccular nucleus of the cerebellum controls ocular saccades . A saccade is a rapid ballistic movement to change the point of fixation. It is the fastest of all eye movements and is initiated by the contralateral frontal lobe . Smooth pursuit is a slow tracking movement to keep the target on the fovea. It is controlled by the ipsilateral parieto-occipital lobe . Following an object from the right to left is left pursuit and is controlled by ipsilateral (left) parieto-occipital lobe , and the corrective movement is a saccade (in this case, left to right) termed right saccade and is controlled by the contralateral (left ) frontal lobe . The floccular nucleus is found in the lobule HX of the cerebellar vermis. Its functions include matching pulse -step , gaze holding, and sustained smooth pursuit . Bilateral lesions of the flocculus result in the following : • Post-saccadic drift- saccadic movements do not stop , but there is a brief, several hundred milliseconds drift of the eyes after each saccade . • Saccadic pursuit - smooth tracking is replaced by simultaneous rapid jerking motions of the eye to follow an object toward the ipsilateral visual field . • Gaze-evoked nystagmus - impaired ability to hold the eyes in the eccentric position, resulting in gaze-evoked nystagmus towards the affected side of the cerebellum . Emboliform and globose nuclei : Generation of vertical saccades Fastigial nuclei : Pursuit initiation

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: Purely depolarizing cells in the optic pathway are ________.
mcqs.explanation: Amacrine cells are the cells that produce purely depolarizing potential and spikes .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: Most afferent fibers from the lateral geniculate body terminate in the primary visual cortex in ______.
mcqs.explanation: Most afferent fibers from the lateral geniculate body ( LGB ) terminate in the primary visual cortex in layer 4.48 Both the magnocellular and parvocellular pathways from the LGB terminate in layer 4 of the visual cortex. Only the interlaminar pathway terminates in layers 2 and 3.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: What is the mean value for outflow facility of the aqueous in the normal eye ?
mcqs.explanation: The aqueous outflow facility is about 0.28 \265 L/min/mmHg. Aqueous humor is produced at an average rate of 2.0–2.5 \265 L/min. The ease with which the aqueous humor leaves the eye is called an aqueous outflow facility . • The outflow facility is measured using tonography. • The normal range is between 0.22 –0.28 \265 L/min/mmHg. • A juxtacanalicular portion of the trabecular meshwork is the primary limiting factor for the outflow facility . • Uveoscleral outflow accounts for 10 % of the total aqueous outflow facility . • Aqueous outflow facility decreases with aging. • Trabecular outflow facility is reduced in glaucoma. • Laser trabeculoplasty reduces intraocular pressure (IOP) in open -angle glaucoma by increasing the trabecular outflow facility .49

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: The term ametropia refers to all except _____.
mcqs.explanation: The term ametropia refers to conditions of refractive error . Emmetropia refers to an optically normal eye . The term ametropia includes conditions such as • Myopia (shortsightedness ) • Hypermetropia (longsightedness ) • Astigmatism57

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A small kid is brought for examination due to difficulty reading from the board at school. Visual acuity was 20 /60 in both eyes . His vision got corrected with concave lens spectacles . Which of the following is the most common cause of this refractive error ?

options.a: Increased anteroposterior diameter of the eye ball
options.d: Increase in the refractive index of lens

mcqs.explanation: Poor vision for distance (difficulty reading from board) that is corrected with concave lens spectacles suggest that the child has myopia. The most common cause of myopia (shortsightedness ) is increased anteroposterior length of the eyeball . Myopia is a type of refractive error seen when the parallel rays of light from infinity are focused in front of the retina when accomodation is at rest.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following range defines moderate myopia?
mcqs.explanation: Moderate myopia is defined when the refractive error is between -3D and -6D. Note : Myopia according to age of onset : • Congenital : Present at birth • Youth onset : 2–20 years of age • Early adult onset : –40 years of age • Late adult onset : >40 years of age

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following myopias is not associated with high degree of refractive error ?
mcqs.explanation: School myopia or simple myopia is associated with a low to moderate degree of refractive error . Simple myopia is the most common type of myopia. It results from a normal biological variation in the development of the eye i.e. increased anteroposterior diameter of eyeball or increased curvature of the cornea.58 Other options : Options A and D: Pathological /Degenerative /Progressive myopia occurs due to degenerative changes in the retina, leading to a high degree of refractive error . Option B: Congenital myopia is associated with congenital anomalies of the eye , and a high degree of refractive error . Note : Other types of myopia include : 1. Nocturnal myopia: Accommodation is induced by low contrast in dim illumination 2. Induced myopia: Temporary and reversible myopia due to external agents (e.g., pilocarpine-induced accommodation spasm)/variations in blood sugar levels 3. Pseudomyopia : Inappropriately excessive accommodation due to overstimulation/ciliary spasm.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A woman comes to the ophthalmology OPD because of having vision difficulties for the last 3 months. On fundoscopic examination, the following findings are seen . Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a fundus typical of pathological myopia due to the stretching of the retina. The tigroid appearance or tessellated appearance of the fundus can be appreciated . As the eye enlarges, the retinal pigment epithelium becomes thinner, resulting in: • A tessellated (checkered ) appearance of the fundus • Increased visibility of the choroidal vasculature Other features of the myopic fundus are as follows : • Lacquer cracks are spontaneous ruptures of the elastic lamina of Bruch's membrane. It appears yellowish -white . it is usually located in the posterior pole . • Annular gray shadow around the optic disc • Lattice degeneration • Foster Fuchs spots • Cystoid degeneration • Total retinal atrophy59

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A woman with pathological myopia visits the ophthalmology OPD for an annual eye check-up. What is the least likely finding to be seen on her ophthalmologic examination?
mcqs.explanation: The shallow anterior chamber is not a feature of pathological myopia. Signs of pathological myopia include the following : • Prominent eyeballs • Large cornea • Deep anterior chamber (AC) • Fundus picture • Large, pale optic disc with the temporal myopic crescent • Degenerative changes in retina and choroid • Foster Fuchs spots (blackish spots due to retinal pigment epithelial hyperplasia ) • Lattice degeneration • Cystoid degeneration • Total retinal atrophy • Posterior staphyloma • Degenerative changes in the vitreous—posterior vitreous detachment60

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about degenerative myopia?

options.a: It is seen in less than 6 dioptres of myopia.
options.b: It is more common in males than in females .
options.c: Myopic degeneration can lead to retinal detachment .
options.d: The condition has no racial prediliction.

mcqs.explanation: The statement that is true for degenerative myopia is that myopic degeneration can lead to retinal detachment. Degenerative myopia is seen in more than 6 dioptres of myopia. It is more common in females as compared to males. The condition has a racial predilection ; it is more common in Jews and Japanese people , and most cases are of genetic origin. Changes seen in degenerative myopia are myopic crescent , rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (due to degenerative changes in the periphery of the retina with subsequent tear) and floaters (due to degenerative changes in the vitreous).

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common complication of pathological myopia?
mcqs.explanation: Macular degeneration is the most common complication of myopia, followed by rhegmatogenous retinal detachment. Complications of pathological myopia include the following : • Macular degeneration • Retinal detachment • Complicated cataract • Vitreous hemorrhage • Choroidal hemorrhage • Strabismus fixus convergence61 • Primary open -angle glaucoma, which is not a complication, but reported to occur in association with pathological myopia.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: While performing the following procedure on a 35-year-old male at a distance of 1 meter, you found out that the red reflex was not moving with the movement of the instrument. How will you interpret your findings?
mcqs.explanation: The above image shows the procedure of retinoscopy (skiascopy) being performed . As the red reflex is not moving with the movement of the retinoscope , the patient is interpreted as having myopia of 1D. Retinoscopy is an objective method of determining the error of refraction. It is based on the principle that when light is reflected from a mirror into the eye , the direction in which tlhe light will travel across the pupil depends upon the refractive stale of the eye . Interpretation of retinoscopy done at 1m is: • No movement of red reflex : Myopia of 1D • Movement of red reflex with retinoscope : Emmetropia , hypermetropia , myopia less than 1D • Movement of red reflex against the retinoscope : Myopia more than 1D

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A worried mother brought her son for vision examination when she noticed him reading a book too closely . She says he also narrows his eyes while watching television . Examination revealed myopia. Which of the following lens should be prescribed to correct this child's vision?
mcqs.explanation: Concave lenses are used for correcting myopic errors.62 Other options : Option A: Convex lenses are used in the correction of hypermetropic eye and presbyopic eye . Option C: Cylindrical lenses are used in the correction of astigmatism.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statement about the management of myopia is false ?

options.a: In high myopia, it is better to slightly under-correct for distance .
options.b: Concave lens is used to correct myopia.
options.c: Contact lens provides a wider field and larger image size as compared to glasses .
options.d: Myopia must never be under-corrected with spectacles .

mcqs.explanation: The false statment is that myopia must never be under-corrected with spectacles . In fact, it is better to slightly under-correct cases of high myopia. Concave lens are used to correct myopia. In high myopia, it is better to slightly under-correct to avoid the problem of near vision and that of minification of images. Contact lens are preferred in high myopia as they provide a wider field and larger image size as compared to glasses .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A college student is fed up with wearing spectacles for her myopia. During her annual eye checkup , she asks the ophthalmologist for eye surgery to get rid of the glasses . Which of the following is not a surgical option to correct her refractive error ?
mcqs.explanation: Conductive keratoplasty is a cornea-based surgical procedure used in the correction of hypermetropia. Surgical procedures are undertaken after the stabilization of myopia which usually occurs after 18 years of age .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following laser is used in the treatment of myopia?
mcqs.explanation: Excimer laser is used in the treament of myopia. Laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK ) is the most popular treatment modality for myopia. It is performed using an excimer laser. Surgical correction is only done in individuals who have a63 stable refractive error for at least 1 year. Corneal thinning disorders must be ruled out prior to this procedure .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A mother asks for LASIK surgery for the correction of her 15-year-old daughter 's myopia. Which of the following is not an eligibility criterion for this procedure ?

options.a: Stable refraction for the past 1 year

mcqs.explanation: Age of 15 years is not a criterion for LASIK surgery. LASIK surgery is performed after 18 years of age . Laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK ) is performed using excimer laser in individuals aged > 18 years who have a stable refractive error for 1 year. It is done in individuals who have had unsatisfactory results with non-surgical treatment . Corneal-thinning disorders such as keratoconus must be ruled out before this procedure .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about the refractive error in which the image is formed behind the retina?
mcqs.explanation: Hypermetropia is the refractive error where the image is formed behind the retina. In hypermetropia, near point becomes distant. The near point or punctum proximum is the nearest point at which small objects can be seen clearly. It recedes with age . Hypermetropia is also called long-sightedness since patients are able to focus distant objects more easily than near objects . Accommodative convergent squint in children is a complication of uncorrected long-standing hypermetropia. The fundus may show pseudopapillitis . Hypermetropia is classified into the following types : • Latent hypermetropia : Masked by the tone of the ciliary body • Facultative hypermetropia : Masked by the voluntary accommodative effort of the person • Absolute hypermetropia : Apparent/manifest64

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: You have been asked to perform fundoscopy by your senior resident in one of his patients diagnosed with hypermetropia . Which of the following options represent the findings that could be seen in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Shot silk appearance with pseudopapillitis can be seen on fundal examination of the hypermetropic eye . Hypermetropia is a refractive error of the eye in which parallel rays of light from infinity focus behind the retina when accommodation is at rest. Fundoscopy findings in hypermetropia include shot silk appearance (retina may shine due to the greater brilliance of light reflections ) and pseudopapillitis (optic disc is small, hypervascular, with ill-defined margins without disc edema ).Other signs of hypermetropia include small eyeball , small cornea and short anteroposterior length of the eyeball . Convex lens (plus lens) is used for the correction of hypermetropia .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following grades of error defines high hypermetropia ?
mcqs.explanation: High hypermetropia is defined as an error of >5D.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man wants to undergo surgery for hypermetropia . All of the following are options to treat his refractive error except ?
mcqs.explanation: Photorefractive keratectomy is not the surgical modality of the treatment of hypermetropia . Photorefractive keratectomy is a laser ablation technique for the correction of myopia. An excimer laser is used to cause flattening of the central cornea.65

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A physician observed the following finding in a small child who came for an eye exam. This finding is associated with which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows convergent squint or esotropia , which is commonly seen in children with hyperopia , also known as hypermetropia. Esotropia results due to increased accommodative effort in cases where there is under correction of hypermetropia . The condition may be prevented by full hypermetropic correction. If the child is unable to wear the glasses due to flat nasal bridge or if the child is less than 2 years old, the accommodation may be treated with drugs. Miotic drugs with anticholinesterase activity such as di-isopropyl fluorophosphate (DFP) or echothiophate can be used in these children. Further treatment may include orthotropic training or surgical correction of the squint.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A boy was brought by his parents for an eye exam. He has been having headaches , nausea, and visual discomfort since he started school. His ophthalmological examination revealed a refractive error of + 2D in the right eye and -1 D in the left eye . His fundus appears to be normal . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: A child with refractive error of + 2D in the right eye and -1 D in the left eye has anisometropia. Anisometropia is the condition wherein the total refractive power of the two eyes is unequal. A difference of up to 2.5 D between two eyes is well tolerated . If the anisometropia exceeds 2.5D, ambylopia may develop . Contact lenses are preferred for treatment due to less optical defects as compared to glasses .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: What is aniseikonia?

options.a: Difference in the axial length of the two eyes
options.b: Difference in the size of the image formed by the two eyes
options.c: Difference in the size of the pupil in the two eyes
options.d: Difference in the curvature of the cornea in the two eyes

mcqs.explanation: Aniseikonia is a condition in which there is a difference in the size of the image formed by the two eyes . Up to 5–8% aniseikonia is well tolerated . Treatment includes contact lens in patients with phakia and intraocular lens implantation in patients with aphakia.66

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 20 -year-old girl started having frequent headaches and blurring of vision while studying for college exams. She says she feels better when she closes her eyes . On examination, she is found to have astigmatism. Which of the following is the most common cause responsible for this condition?

options.a: Irregularity of the curvature of the cornea
options.b: Irregularity of the curvature of the lens

mcqs.explanation: Abnormalities of the curvature of the cornea is the most common cause of astigmatism. Astigmatism is a refractive error in which the rays of light entering the eye are refracted differently in different meridia of the eye . Meridia of the eye correspond to the lines of longitude on a globe . There are two types of astigmatism. In regular astigmatism, refractive power changes uniformly from one meridian to another. In irregular astigmatism, there is irregular change of the refractive power in different meridia. It can be caused by corneal scars. Etiology of regular astigmatism: • Corneal: Most common cause . Occurs due to abnormalities of curvature of the cornea • Lenticular: Occurs due to abnormalities of lens curvature and position • Curvatural: Seen in lenticonus • Positional: Due to tilting or oblique placement of the lens or subluxation of lens • Retinal: Due to oblique placement of the macula74 Note : Spherical aberration is a high-order refractive error of the eye . It is seen when light rays passing through the periphery of the cornea and lens focus at a slightly different location than light rays passing through the center of the cornea and lens. It improves on using a pinhole .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which among the following is normal astigmatism seen in eyes due to the pressure of the eyelids ?
mcqs.explanation: With-the-rule astigmatism is normally seen in the eyes due to the pressure of the eyelids . In with-the -rule astigmatism, the vertical meridian is more curved. This is more common and often occurs due to the pressure of eyelids on the eye . In against-the -rule astigmatism (ATR) (option B), the horizontal meridian is more curved than the vertical meridian. In both these types , the principal meridia are vertical and horizontal (90 and 180 degrees ) and are at right angles to each other. The other types of astigmatism include oblique and bi-oblique astigmatism. In oblique astigmatism (option C), the two principal meridians are not the horizontal and vertical meridians, although they are at right angles to each other. In bi-oblique astigmatism (option D), the two principal meridians are not at right angles to each other; for example , one may be at 40 degrees and the other, at 100 degrees .75

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding with-the -rule astigmatism?

options.a: The horizontal meridian is more myopic.
options.b: The vertical meridian is more myopic.
options.c: The vertical meridian is more hyperopic.
options.d: The horizontal meridian is more hyperopic .

mcqs.explanation: In with-the -rule astigmatism, the curvature of the vertical meridian is more than the horizontal meridian. Greater the curvature of the meridian, more the myopia of that meridian. Hence, the vertical meridian is more myopic in with-the -rule astigmatism. With-the-rule astigmatism is the type of astigmatism wherein the vertical curvature is always more than the horizontal curvature. Thus, irrespective of the type or cause of with-the -rule astigmatism, the vertical meridian is always more myopic (curved) than the horizontal meridian.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Match the images shown with the refractive errors they represent .
mcqs.explanation: 76 The correct answer is 1 - d, 2 - b, 3 - c, 4 - a. Astigmatism is a refractive error in which the rays of light entering the eye are refracted differently in different meridia of the eye . Meridia of the eye correspond to the lines of longitude on a globe . There are two types of astigmatism - regular and irregular. In regular astigmatism, refractive power changes uniformly from one meridian to another. Thus, two principal meridia are present . The rays of light from infinity form two focal points due to the difference in curvature of the two principal meridia. Based on the relation of the two focal points to the retina, regular astigmatism has the following types : • Simple astigmatism: One focal point lies on the retina. In simple myopic type , the second focal point lies in front of the retina while in simple hypermetropic type , the second focal point lies behind the retina. • Compound astigmatism: In compound hypermetropic type , both focal points lie behind the retina. In compound myopic type , both focal points lie in front of the retina. • Mixed astigmatism: One focal point lies in front of while the second focal point lies behind the retina.Imag e Refractive error 1 d. Simple hypermetropic asti gmatism 2 b. Simple myopic astigmatis m 3 c. Compound myopic astigma tism 4 a. Mixed astigmatism77

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: In compound myopic astigmatism, with parallel rays of light entering the eye in relaxed accommodation, the image(s) formed is/are __________.

options.a: One focal point in front of the retina
options.b: Two focal lines in front of the retina
options.c: Two focal lines behind the retina
options.d: Two focal lines, one behind and the other in front of retina

mcqs.explanation: In compound myopic astigmatism, parallel rays of light entering the eye in relaxed accommodation form two focal lines in front of the retina. Option A: One focal point in front of retina describes myopia. Option C: Two focal lines behind the retina describes compound hypermetropic astigmatism. Option D: Two focal lines, one behind and one in front of the retina describes mixed astigmatism.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following would be prescribed for simple myopic astigmatism?
mcqs.explanation: Among the above options , -1.00 DC \327 180 degrees is the correct prescription for simple myopic astigmatism (SMA). There are 3 components for prescription of glasses . 1. The first number is the refractive power of the spherical component . It is represented as convex (+) or concave (-) dioptre sphere (DS). 2. The second number denotes the power of the cylinder, represented as convex (+) or concave (-) dioptre cylinder (DC). 3. The above two components are followed by an x representing the axis (orientation) of the cylinder.78 In the most common type of SMA - with-the -rule astigmatism - meridian A (represented by 90 degrees ) is more curved than meridian B (represented by 180 degrees ). The light rays refracting from B focus on the retina, whereas those refracting from A focus in front of the retina. To correct this error , a negative cylindrical lens (DC) is used to focus the myopic rays of meridian A on the retina. This correction needs to occur at 90 degrees (meridian A). The axis of a cylindrical lens is perpendicular to the required correction and thus , the spectacles will have an axis of 180 degrees . There is no spherical refractive error since the light rays from meridian B lies on the retina. Thus DS is 0.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: The PARK procedure is used in the correction of which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: 79 PARK is a technique used for correcting astigmatism. Photo-astigmatic refractive keratotomy (PARK) is performed using excimer laser for the correction of astigmatism. The other surgical procedures used for correction of astigmatism are astigmatic keratotomy, LASIK and SMILE.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: An 80-year-old man is reading a newspaper in his backyard. His accommodation while reading a newspaper is due to______.
mcqs.explanation: Near vision accommodation is due to the contraction of the ciliary muscle . Accommodation is the phenomenon of increasing the convergence power . This occurs by increasing the refractive power of the lens and increasing its curvature. The capsule of the lens is more elastic than the lens itself and plays a role in increasing the curvature of the lens. When the circular fibres of the ciliary muscles contract, the ciliary body approaches the lens. This slackens the zonules so that the capsule , relieved of its tension, is able to mould the lens to its accommodative form.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: During a routine school eye examination camp, a 5-year-old boy is able to read everything written on the board. Which of the following mechanisms aids in establishing normal distant vision in this child?

options.c: Shortening of the focal length of the lens

mcqs.explanation: Relaxation of the ciliary muscles would aid in establishing a normal distant vision. Relaxation of the ciliary muscles keeps the zonules in a taut state and maintains the radius of curvature of the anterior lens surface at 10 mm. Thus, the focal length is maximum and distant objects are most clearly visualized. Option B: The pupils constrict during accommodation to increase the depth of focus . Option C: During accommodation, ciliary muscles contract causing relaxation of zonular fibers, rounding of the lens, and shortening of the focal length . Option D: The radius of curvature of the anterior lens surface becomes 6 mm i.e rounder during accommodation.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: The condition of the accommodative power being significantly less than the normal physiological limits for the patient 's age is called _________.
mcqs.explanation: The condition in which accommodative power is significantly less than normal physiological limits for the patient 's age is called insufficiency of accommodation Anomalies of accommodation:Presbyopia Insufficiency of accommo dation Paralysis of accommodati on(cycloplegia ) Spasm of accommodatio n Failing near vision due to age -relateddecrease in th e amplitude of accommo dation orincreaseinnear point Inadequacy of the accom modative power . It issign ificantly lessthannormal physiological limitsfor th e patient 's age Complete absenceofacco mmodation Exertion orabnormally ex cessive accommodation80 Presbyopia Insufficiency of accommo dation Paralysis of accommodati on(cycloplegia ) Spasm of accommodatio n Causes :Age -related chang e in the lens- decreased e lasticity and sclerosis .Age -related decline in ciliary muscle power Causes :Premature scleros is of the lensWeakness of the ciliary muscles due t o systemic causes like an emia and malnutrition.W eakness of the ciliary mu scles associated with pri mary open -angle glauco ma Causes :Drug-inducedInte rnal ophthalmoplegia du e to diphtheria , diabetes mellitus , etc .As a compo nent of 3rdnerve palsy Causes :Drug-induced spa sm, e.g., ecothiophate , pi locarpineSpontaneous sp asm: Found in children w ho use eyes for excessive near work in conditions o f bad illumination.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: What is the accommodative amplitude of a patient with a near point at 20 cm and a far point at infinity?
mcqs.explanation: The amplitude of accommodation for the above patient would be 5. Near point of accommodation (NPA) is the closest distance at which the near object is clearly focussed without blur. Amplitude of accommodation is the maximum power of the lens that permits clear near vision without blur. Its unit is dioptre (D). The amplitude of accommodation is the reciprocal of NPA in meters . 20 cm is 1/5th of a meter. Therefore, accommodative amplitude is its inverse, that is, 5D. The NPA is measured clinically using a scale device such as the Prince, Berens, or Royal Air Force (RAF) ruler.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 45 year old woman complains of an inability to read books and stitch garments for the past few months. Which of the following is false regarding her condition?

options.b: Decrease in elasticity and plasticity of the crystalline lens
options.c: Age -related decrease in the power of ciliary muscles
options.d: It is corrected with a concave lens

mcqs.explanation: A 45 year old woman presenting with an inability to do near vision work (reading, stitching ) likely has presbyopia. Presbyopia is corrected by the use of a convex lens (weakest convex lens).81 Presbyopia can be caused by an age -related decline in the ciliary muscle power or age -related change in the lens including: • • Hardness (sclerosis ) of the lens substance, which is less easily molded • Decrease in the elasticity of lens capsule

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 51-year-old woman comes for an ophthalmological examination. She says she is unable to thread a needle and is facing difficulty making a sweater for her grandson. She never had vision problems in her youth . What power of glasses would roughly correct her vision difficulties ?
mcqs.explanation: The power of prescription glasses for a 51-year-old woman should be +1.5D. Presbyopia is the condition of decreased near vision. It is due to an age -related decrease in the amplitude of accommodation or an increase in punctum proximum (near point). For correction of presbyopia , convex lenses are used . Roughly , the power of prescription glasses age -wise is as follows :Age Power 45 ye ars +1 to +1.25 D 50 ye ars +1.5 to 1.75 D 55 ye ars +2 to +2.25 D 60 ye ars +2.5 to +3D

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: During your morning jogging routine, you found a pair of spectacles lying on the sidewalk . The spectacles are shown below . What type of presbyopic lens is present in these spectacles ?
mcqs.explanation: The given lens in the image is a typical example of progressive lenses . Progressive lenses are identified as such due to the absence of the line of demarcation on the lens. They are gradually optimized for reading vision, distant vision, and for intermediate vision, such as computer work.82

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old male with limbal scar presents to the ophthalmology clinic with marked defects in both near and far vision. Clinical examination reveals a wide and deep anterior chamber, iridodonesis , and a dark pupillary reflex . A vision of 6/6 is achieved with correcting lens of +11D . Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: A limbal scar with defective near and distant vision, a wide and deep anterior chamber, iridodonesis, and dark pupillary reflex suggests aphakia. Aphakia is the condition in which the lens is absent from the pupillary area. Signs of surgical aphakia include limbal scar, deeper anterior chamber than normal , iridodonesis (tremulousness of the iris), jet black color of the pupil . On Purkinje's test , only the first and second images are seen . A small disc is seen on fundus examination and high hypermetropia is seen on retinoscopy . The best treatment option is secondary intraocular lens (IOL) implantation.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is used to differentiate pseudophakia from aphakia?
mcqs.explanation: Pseudophakia shows 4 images in the Purkinje image test , whereas aphakia shows only 2 images. Other features can be seen in both. When aphakia is corrected with an intraocular lens implant (IOL ), the condition is referred to as pseudophakia. Signs of pseudophakia with posterior chamber IOL include : • Surgical scar • Anterior chamber slightly deeper than normal • Mild iridodonesis (tremulousness ) of the iris • Purkinje image test shows 4 images • Pupil blackish in color but when the light is thrown in the pupillary area, shining reflex is observed Purkinje images are reflections of objects from the structure of the eye . They are also known as Purkinje reflexes or Purkinje–Sanson images. Normally, 4 images are formed from four different83 reflecting surfaces i.e.Imag e Location Directi on Imag e 1 Anterior surface of the corne a Erect Imag e 2 Posterior surface of the corne a Erect Imag e 3 Anterior surface of the lens Erect Imag e 4 Posterior surface of the lens Inverte dIn aphakia, as the lens is absent, image 3 and image 4 are absent.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Roving –ring scotoma is seen after the correction of aphakia by which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Roving -ring scotoma is seen in the correction of aphakia with spectacles due to prismatic effects at the edge of the lens. The difficulties in the correction of aphakia by spectacles include the following : • Image magnification by 25–30 % • Spherical aberrations producing a "pin cushion effect " • Jack -in-the-box phenomenon from the prismatic effects at the edge of the lens • Reduced visual fields • Physical inconvenience For aphakia, the best correction is obtained by an intraocular lens (IOL).84 Roving -ring scotoma:The edge of a convex lens acts as a prism. The greater the angle of the prism, the more will be the bending. In aphakic spectacles , the angle of the lens is large. Thus, the light falling at the edge of the lens bends towards the center of the lens and does not reach the pupil . This results in a ring-shaped scotoma as this prismatic effect is present all around the edges of the lens. The position of this scotoma is not fixed in the visual field because the eye keeps moving (or roving ) in relation to the aphakic spectacle . Hence , the result is a roving ring scotoma.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Soft contact lenses are made of _____.
mcqs.explanation: Soft lenses are made up of hydroxyethyl methyl acrylate (HEMA).

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which among the following is not an advantage of contact lens?

options.a: It helps in eliminating peripheral aberrations.
options.c: It is helpful in dry eye .

mcqs.explanation: Contact lenses decrease corneal oxygen supply . The cornea obtains its O2 supply from the atmosphere . The use of contact lenses decreases the O2 supply from the atmosphere . Contact lens eliminate peripheral aberrations and can correct irregular astigmatism. Although dry eye is caused by wearing contact lenses , lenses made of hydrogel which are high in water content are beneficial in dry eye . Rigid gas-permeable /semi-soft contact lens are used for keratoconus. Toric contact lens are used for astigmatism.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: The spectacles shown in the image are not used for the management of which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: 85 The given image shows spectacles made of lenses with two different optical power . Thus, it is a pair of bifocal spectacles which is not used in hypermetropia or myopia. Bifocal glasses have different corrective powers in the upper segment for distant vision and lower segment for near vision. Thus, they are useful in conditions where both distance and near vision are affected , like the following : 1. Presbyopia (option A): It is a definitive indication. It is used to correct age -related near and far vision defects. 2. Aphakia (option B): It provides both near and far vision correction when intra-ocular lens insertion is contraindicated . 3. Paediatric pseudophakia (option C): It is used to correct refractive errors or accommodative fluctuations post intra-ocular lens (IOL) insertion. 4. Non refractive accomodative esotropia In hypermetropia there is defect in near vision only and hence a single vision glasses having uniform corrective power throught the entire surface is used instead of bifocal glasses .86

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following characteristic features would you expect to see in a histopathology slide of conjunctiva?

options.a: Amacrine cells within non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium
options.b: Goblet cells within non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium
options.c: Goblet cells within keratinized stratified squamous epithelium
options.d: Amacrine cells within keratinized stratified squamous epithelium

mcqs.explanation: The presence of goblet cells within the non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium would help identify the conjunctiva. Goblet cells are involved in the secretion of mucin. Amacrine cells are a type of retinal interneuron, and hence would be found in the retina, not the conjunctiva.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: What is the causative organism of angular conjunctivitis?
mcqs.explanation: Moraxella species , a type of gram-negative diplobacilli , are involved in causing angular conjunctivitis which is a type of chronic conjunctivitis. Angular conjunctivitis is a chronic type of conjunctivitis where there is inflammation of the conjunctiva at the lid margins and the inner and outer canthi of the eyes with red, scaly, excoriated , macerated and fissured skin at the canthi. This is because of the proteolytic enzymes secreted by the Moraxella species . Patients with angular conjunctivitis usually experience eye irritation , a burning sensation and collection of dirty-white , foamy discharge at the angles . These patients can also have associated blepharitis and papillary and follicular conjunctivitis. Causative organisms are Moraxella lacunata, Moraxella axenfeld and Staphylococcus aureus (Rare cause ). The source of infection is typically the nasal tract or the nasal discharge of patients with angular conjunctivitis. The infection spreads from the nasal cavity to the eyes through contaminated hands or handkerchiefs. Treatment includes oxytetracycline 1% ointment for 10 to 14 days, and zinc oxide as it inhibits proteolytic enzymes . The image given below shows the eye of a patient infected with angular conjunctivitis.99 Other options : Option B: Haemophilus influenzae causes acute conjunctivitis. Option C: Adenovirus is the most common cause of viral conjunctivitis and it most commonly causes follicular conjunctivitis, pharyngoconjunctival fever, and epidemic keratoconjunctivitis. Option D: Coxsackie B virus is known to cause aseptic meningitis, encephalitis , pericarditis, and myocarditis. There are no known mentions of ocular disease caused by the virus. mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A child presents with irritation and redness of the left eye at a primary health center . There are no previous immunization records. Examination showed a greyish -white membrane over the bulbar and palpebral conjunctiva which bled on peeling . What is the likely etiology ?
mcqs.explanation: The of a child with irritation and redness of the eye with no previous vaccination records is suggestive of a case of membranous conjunctivitis and among the given options , Corynebacterium diphtheriae is the most likely etiological agent . Membranous conjunctivitis presents with irritation and redness of the eye and is characterized by the formation of a greyish -white membrane that bleeds on peeling . Vaccines are routinely used to prevent diphtheria infection and hence , unvaccinated status increases his susceptibility to the bacteria. Moreover, the bacteria thrive in crowded populations and poor hygienic surroundings, hence a background of low socioeconomic context , such as an orphanage, acts as a risk factor in this case. This condition is associated with the formation of fibrinous exudates on the surface and into the substance of the conjunctival epithelium. The causes include beta -hemolytic streptococci , Streptococcus pneumonia, Haemophilus aegyptius , Corynebacterium diphtheria , and Neisseria gonorrhea The image given below shows the eye of a patient with pseudomembranous conjunctivitis. It differs from membranous conjunctivitis in that the membrane can be easily peeled off in this condition leaving an intact underlying epithelium .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A child with pharyngitis, and fever subsequently develops conjunctivitis. Initially, the left eye was affected , followed by the right eye 's involvement in 2 days. Epiphora, conjunctival hyperemia , and chemosis are noted . What is its most likely etiological agent ?
mcqs.explanation: This child with pharyngitis and subsequent involvement of the eyes most likely has pharyngoconjunctival fever. This condition is commonly caused by adenovirus serotypes 3, 4, and 7. Pharyngoconjunctival fever is an acute and highly infectious illness characterized by fever, pharyngitis, acute follicular conjunctivitis, and regional lymphoid hyperplasia with tender , enlarged preauricular adenopathy . Within the classical triad, symptoms may vary in severity . It is usually bilateral, with one eye typically having onset 1-3 days prior to the second eye . It is a101 self -limiting disease and treatment is mainly symptomatic , as follows : • Cold compresses several times per day for 1-2 weeks . • Artificial tears 4-8 times per day for 1-3 weeks . Newcastle conjunctivitis is usually clinically indistinguishable from this condition and is derived from contact with diseased fowls . Another conjunctivitis caused by adenovirus serotypes 8, and 37 is known as epidemic keratoconjunctivitis. The image given below shows the eye of a patient with pharyngoconjunctival fever. Significant conjunctival hyperemia , petechial subconjunctival hemorrhages, and conjunctival follicles are noted .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding this condition?

options.a: The condition is commonly associated with a benign course .
options.b: It can occur spontaneously in elders with systolic hypertension .
options.c: The blood gets absorbed gradually in 6-8 weeks time without treatment .
options.d: Use of NSAIDs and aspirin to treat the condition should be avoided.

mcqs.explanation: The image given above shows a subconjunctival haemorrhage in the eye . In this condition, the blood gets absorbed gradually in 1-3 weeks time without treatment . A subconjunctival hemorrhage is also called subconjunctival ecchymosis . It is due to the rupture of small blood vessels and can occur spontaneously in elders with systolic hypertension or after local trauma. The condition is commonly associated with a benign course but, if the posterior limit of the hemorrhage is not seen , one should check for the base of the skull fracture. Recurrent episodes warrant investigations for a bleeding diathesis or leukaemia. The use of NSAIDs and aspirin to treat the condition should be avoided.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A UNICEF volunteer presented with a bilateral red eye of 2 days duration beginning on a return flight from Ghana. The infection spread among all her family members within a day of her return. Initial examination revealed lid edema , serous discharge , and severe sub-conjunctival hemorrhage. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of a patient with bilateral red-eye and a rapid spread of infection to family members points towards a likely diagnosis of hemorrhagic conjunctivitis. Examination findings of lid edema , serous discharge , and subconjunctival hemorrhage further consolidate this102 diagnosis. Causes : • Enterovirus 70 (most important) • Coxsackievirus 24 • Echovirus 34 • Adenovirus • Pneumococcus • Haemophilus There is no treatment currently available . The infection generally resolves itself within a five to seven-day period . The use of steroids can actually cause a corneal microbial superinfection which then requires antimicrobial therapy to eliminate . The image given below shows the eyes of a patient with acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: What is the cause of acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis?
mcqs.explanation: Acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis is caused by picornoviruses namely enterovirus 70. Acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis also known as "Apollo conjunctivitis" is caused by picornoviruses such as enterovirus 70 and coxsackievirus A24 . Rarely it is also caused by adenovirus type 11 . It manifests with severe conjunctival congestion , chemosis , subconjunctival hemorrhages, painful follicular conjunctivitis, tearing, lid edema and pre-auricular lymphadenopathy . The cornea may demonstrate a fine punctate keratopathy. The disease is usually self -limiting, running a course of 3-7 days. The image given below shows the eyes of a patient with acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis.103 Enterovirus 71 (Option D) is associated with fatal meningitis, encephalitis , and paralysis. It is also implicated in Hand-Foot-Mouth disease (HFMD) and Herpangia which is papulo -vesiculo -ulcerative rash in oral cavity.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A tribal farmer, presented with a three -day history of right eye redness with pain. He had spent the prior week trekking up a mountain in order to travel to the nearby town and takes such trips frequently . The following lesion was observed on examination. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of right eye redness with pain, and findings of a raised whitish-yellowish lesion surrounded by mild erythema , points toward a likely diagnosis of pinguecula . A history of trekking, along with chronic sunlight exposure as a farmer, acts as a risk factor because it increases the exposure to the stronger UV radiation in the mountains. Pinguecula has a fatty appearance and is usually bilateral. They are more often located nasally than temporally . It has horizontally oriented areas of bulbar conjunctival thickening that adjoin the limbus in the palpebral fissure area. They are associated with a 2- to 3-fold increased incidence of age -related macular degeneration. It is seen in most eyes by 70 years of age and in almost all by 80 years of age . Pingueculitis responds to a brief course of NSAIDs or topical corticosteroids . Simple excision may be warranted in rare cases , wherein pingueculae may be chronically inflamed or cosmetically unsatisfactory .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: What is the likely diagnosis from the image given below ?
mcqs.explanation: The likely diagnosis, based on the above image, is pterygium . Pterygium is a subconjunctival fibrovascular tissue encroaching the cornea. It is a degenerative condition of the sub-conjunctival tissue and is never inflammatory. It occurs due to exposure to UV-B radiation and the most common site is the nasal.104 It is made up of three parts, "cap" (an avascular halo-like zone at the advancing edge ), a head , and a body. Clinical features : • Astigmatism with the rule - most common finding • Stocker's line - deposition of iron on the advancing edge • Fuchs islets - small, discrete , whitish flecks consisting of clusters of pterygial epithelial cells , often present at the advancing edge . The differential diagnosis is pseudo pterygium . The treatment for pterygium is usually excision. To prevent a recurrence, mitomycin C or 5 fluorouracil is used . Other methods : • Auto-grafting- Conjunctival limbal autograft (CLAG) from the superior limbal conjunctiva is the best method . • Bare sclera technique - high recurrence rate of 30 to 80%. • PERFECT surgery- zero rates of recurrence. (PERFECT stands for Pterygium Extended Removal Followed by Extended Conjunctival Transplant)Pterygium Pseudo -pterygium Degenerativeprocess Inflammatoryprocess Occurs inelderly Can occur at any age Situated at thepalpebral aper ture Can occur at any site Either progressive , regressive , or stationary Always stationary Aprobe cannotbepassedunde rneath A probe can be passed under the neck

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: The excision of a pinkish, triangular tissue growth at the 1 o'clock position of the eye is being performed. The patient had a history of blurry vision and persistent redness in both eyes for a month. In order to secure the graft in the scleral bed , which of the following will not be used ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette , with symptoms of blurry vision and persistent redness , along with findings of an abnormal triangular mass of thickened conjunctiva, is suggestive of pterygium . Cyanoacrylate is not used for pterygium surgery. The various glues used in ophthalmology are as follows : • Cyanoacrylate glue - Mainly used as a corneal patch to seal acute corneal perforations and improve visual outcomes , with reduced enucleation rates and need for tectonic keratoplasty • Fibrin glue - It is a biological adhesive, which reduces the total surgical time. It is used in corneal and conjunctival surgeries , squint surgeries , cataract (to fix the haptics of intraocular lens [IOL] to the tissue in place of sutures in glued IOL ), refractive surgeries , trabeculectomy , and even retinal surgeries . • Newer tissue adhesives like bio-dendrimers and photo -cross-linkable adhesives -105 • Bovine serum albumin-based bioadhesives : used in squint surgery • Riboflavin -based bioadhesive activated on exposure to ultraviolet A: used in post -LASIK ectasia , infectious keratopathy , pseudophakic bullous keratopathy • Hyaluronic acid-based photocatalytic glue activated with argon LASER : used in the repair of corneal lacerations

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A man presented with red eyes associated with a sandy, gritty sensation. He was diagnosed with conjunctivitis last week , however, his symptoms persisted . He has had multiple sexual partners in the past. Examination revealed palpable preauricular nodes and a follicular reaction involving the bulbar conjunctiva and semilunar folds . Conjunctival scrapings were sent for culture. What is the likely organism involved?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of red eyes , along with the examination findings of palpable preauricular nodes and follicular reaction involving the bulbar conjunctiva and semilunar folds , is suggestive of inclusion conjunctivitis. It is also known as chlamydial conjunctivitis, caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serotypes D–K. It is a sexually transmitted disease occurring commonly in young adults . The modes of transmission include orogenital activities and hand-to-eye spread of infective genital secretions . Hence , it is important to treat all sexual partners simultaneously to prevent re-infection and to rule out other venereal diseases , such as gonorrhoea and syphilis . Treatment includes a single 1g dose of azithromycin or doxycycline 100 mg twice a day for 7 days. The image given below shows the eye of a patient with chlamydial conjunctivitis.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions is closely related to mucus fishing syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Mucus fishing syndrome is closely related to giant papillary conjunctivitis. In Mucus fishing syndrome, patients develop a chronic papillary reaction due to repetitive manual removal of mucus. The severe form of mechanically induced papillary conjunctivitis is known as giant papillary conjunctivitis (GPC). It is most frequently encountered with contact lens (CL) wear; in such cases , it is termed contact lens-associated papillary conjunctivitis (CLPC).106 The increased risk in contact lens users is because of the build -up of proteinaceous deposits and cellular debris on the contact lens surface . It may be also be caused by ocular prostheses , exposed sutures , and scleral buckles , corneal surface irregularity, or filtering blebs .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A young man presented with watering , redness and photophobia . He had similar complaints in the past which improved with self -medicated topical drops. His best -corrected visual acuity is 6/36 improving to 6/24. Slit-lamp examination revealed a 3 mm \327 2 mm epithelial defect in the paracentral part of the cornea that stained positive with fluorescein dyes . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of spring catarrh . Slit-lamp examination finding of shield ulcer is typical of vernal keratoconjunctivitis (VKC) or warm weather conjunctivitis (another name of VKC). Shield ulcers are transverse ulcers seen in the upper cornea due to epithelial macroerosions in VKC. It is a rare complication of VKC and should always be kept in mind for patients suffering from vernal conjunctivitis. Corneal signs in VKC: • Shield ulcers • Vernal plaques • Subepithelial scarring • Pseudo -gerontoxon- resembles arcus senilus ; has a cupid 's bow outline Treatment of VKC is mainly with allergy avoidance and lid hygiene . Cool compresses , topical antihistamines, topical NSAIDs and topical steroids can be used to reduce the intensity of symptoms . The image given below shows a shield ulcer in a patient with VKC.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: While browsing through the news channels, Geeta came across a panel discussion on public health diseases celebrating the elimination of a peculiar condition of the eye . It was known as the most important cause of corneal blindness in India and shows the following finding. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: 107 The given sago-grain appearance of the conjunctiva is seen in trachoma. It was the most important cause of corneal blindness in India affecting young children. Conjunctival appearance : 1. In trachoma • Sago-grain appearance • A follicular reaction 2. In vernal keratoconjunctivitis • Cobblestone appearance • A papillary reaction seen in palpebral conjunctiva 3. Phlyctenular conjunctivitis • White-pinkish nodule in the bulbar conjunctiva 4. Xerophthalmia • Epithelial xerosis • Bitot spot in bulbar conjunctiva

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following will not be seen as a corneal sign in a 6-year-old patient with trachoma?
mcqs.explanation: Arlt's line is a conjunctival sign of trachoma.Cornealsigns Conjunctivalsigns Superficial keratitisFollicles i n the limbal areaPannus-sup erior limbusCorneal ulcerHer berts pits -near Limbal areaC orneal opacity Congestion - On upper tarsal, fornixFollicles (containingLe ber cellson histopathology )- On upper tarsal, fornixPapill ary hyperplasiaArlt 's line-Lin ear scarring in sulcus subtars alisConcretions-Inspissated mucus, dead epithelial cells i n the glands of Henle

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A young girl has been brought in by her grandmother because she has constant pain, photosensitivity and discharge from her eyes . From the notes , you see that the child has had multiple presentations for prior eye infections . You observe severe scarring on the palpebral conjunctiva, as well as trachomatous trichiasis. Which McCallan stage will this be classified under?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical vignette of a young child with pain, photosensitivity and discharge , having repeated infections , along with findings of scarring and trichiasis is suggestive of trachoma. Cicatrising trachoma is stage 3 of trachoma and is characterized by scarring of the palpebral conjunctiva. Cicatricial trachoma is the end result of scarring that occurs in individuals who suffer from severe , persistent infections in childhood . Trachomatous scarring is recognized by the presence of easily visible white bands on the underside of the upper eyelid . Severe scarring can result in contraction of the tarsal conjunctiva which causes the lid margin to roll inwards. This results in buckling of108 the lid so the lashes rub on the eye known as trachomatous trichiasis. These lashes can lead to corneal opacities and scarring and eventually blindness . The four stages of trachoma according to McCallan are as follows : • Stage 1: Incipient - Immature follicles are present , but clinical symptoms are not obvious. • Stage 2: Established - Typical trachomatous lesions without scarring. • Stage 3: Cicatrising - Scarring along with active infection . • Stage 4: Healed - Only scarring, the disease is either cured or quiet. The image below shows trachomatous trichiasis with severe scarring-

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: What is the drug of choice under the SAFE strategy for trachoma management?
mcqs.explanation: Oral azithromycin is the drug of choice in the SAFE strategy of trachoma management. The adult dose is 1 g while 20 mg/kg body weight is given for children. Oral azithromycin is slowly replacing tetracycline eye ointment as the first line drug used in trachoma treatment . The experience of Morocco, the first country that used azithromycin in a large-scale , nationwide elimination programme, has paved the way for the worldwide application of azithromycin as part of the SAFE strategy .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 21 -year-old man presented with the following lesion in his eye . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The image depicts Bitot's spot , a pathognomonic feature of xerophthalmia. Hence , the likely diagnosis in this 21 -year-old man presenting with the above lesion is xerophthalmia. Bitot's spot is a triangular, silvery-white , foamy patch on the bulbar conjunctiva which is usually bilateral. The most common site is temporal.109

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 10 year old malnourished boy is brought with a 2-month history of diminished night vision. His dietary history revealed a restricted diet , consisting of mainly chips and nuggets , and he would refuse to eat green leafy vegetables . What is the conjunctival change seen in this deficiency ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario indicates that this patient has nyctalopia (diminished night vision) most likely due to vitamin A deficiency, suggested by his poor consumption of vegetables . Changes seen in the conjunctiva in vitamin A deficiency is hyperkeratosis of the squamous epithelium . This occurs due to the metaplasia of the non-keratinized epithelium to keratinized epithelium .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Ophthalmia nodosa occurs due to which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Ophthalmia nodosa occurs due to irritation due to caterpillar hair. It is often mistaken for tuberculosis . On examination, small, semitranslucent , reddish and yellowish -grey nodules are formed in the conjunctiva, cornea, and iris. Microscopy contains caterpillar hair surrounded by giant cells and lymphocytes . Treatment includes excision of the nodules in the conjunctiva. The image below shows a patient 's eye infected with ophthalmia nodosa.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old woman with redness and photophobia of the left eye was seen in the OPD. An image of a characteristic lesion of her eye is as shown below . Identify the lesion.
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a white -pinkish nodule surrounded by hyperemia on the bulbar conjunctiva near the limbus with associated symptoms of redness and photophobia most likely has phlyctenular conjunctivitis. The given finding is referred to as a phlycten . Phlyctenular conjunctivitis is a type 4 hypersensitivity reaction due to endogenous allergens like Staphylococcus aureus (most common) and Mycobacterium tuberculosis .110 It is characterized by the following : • Phlycten that may eventually form ring ulcers • Shallow marginal ulcer due to the breakdown of limbal phlycten known as scrofulous ulcer • Fascicular ulcer with a prominent parallel leash of blood vessels that heals leaving a band-shaped opacity Treatment: Topical steroids ; atropine if the cornea is involved. Note : This can be differentiated from pinguecula by the following points: Pinguecula is a yellow triangular patch on the conjunctiva near the limbus. It usually remains free from conjunctival congestion . The following image shows a yellow patch with tortuous blood vessels . There is no congestion as seen with a phlycten .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following should not be considered in the differential of a patient who presents with the following finding?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows symblepharon, which is not seen in phlyctenular conjunctivitis. It is a partial or complete adhesion of the palpebral conjunctiva of the eyelid to the bulbar conjunctiva of the eyeball . Causes of symblepharon: • Chemical injuries (especially alkalis) • Burns • Ocular cicatrical pemphigoid (OCP) • Steven–Johnson syndrome • Erythema multiforme • Pemphigus bullosa • Membranous conjunctivitis111 Management : • Lubrication • Sweeping of fornices • Symblepharon ring • Symblepharon release and amniotic membrane graft

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of ophthalmia neonatorum in developed countries ?
mcqs.explanation: Chlamydia is at present the most common cause of ophthalmia neonatarum in developed countries. Ophthalmia neonatarum also called neonatal conjunctivitis is inflammation of the conjunctiva occurring in an infant <30 days after birth.It should be ruled out in any infant having discharge or watering within the first week of birth. Causes include : • Chlamydia(Option A): neonatal inclusion conjunctivitis caused by serotypes D-K is at present the most common cause in developed countries . • Gonorrhoea(Option B): effective prophylaxis against gonococcal infection and its subsequent decline has almost eliminated it's incidence in developed countries . • Staphylococcus aureus(Option D), Haemophilus species , Streptococcus haemolyticus , and Streptococcus pneumoniae are other less commonly seen causes of ophthalmia neonatarum • Herpes simplex ophthalmia neonatrum rarely occurs and is caused by Herpes simplex type 2 virus from the mother. • Chemical conjunctivitis(Option C) is caused by the application of prophylactic antibiotics or silver nitrate at the time of birth.Time of presentatio n Causative agent Within 48 h Chemical, Gonorrhoea 48–72 h Staphylococcus aureus,Strept ococcus pneumoniae 5–7 days Herpes simplex II >1 week ChlamydiaProphylactic treatment : 1% tetracycline or erythromycin eye ointment is applied to the eyes , if the mother is suspected to have gonococcal or chlamydia infection . Curative treatment : • Chlamydia trachomatis (D– K)- Erythromycin eye ointment • Neisseria gonorrhoeae- Ceftriaxone injection, gentamicin drops, bacitracin eye ointment112 The below image shows an infant presenting with ophthalmia neonatarum.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: An 8-year-old boy had to miss school because the matting of his eyelids made it difficult to open them in the morning and caused severe pain. His agonized mother rushed him to the hospital and reported that he had a fever and red eye for 4 days. Which group of lymph nodes is likely to be enlarged ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario of fever and red eyes , associated with matting of eyelids and pain, is suggestive of conjunctivitis. Lymph from the conjunctiva drains directly into the submandibular and preauricular nodes and hence , these group of lymph nodes are likely to be enlarged . The lymphatic drainage of the conjunctiva is as follows - • From the medial side , one-third of the superior and medial two -thirds of the inferior conjunctiva \033 Submandibular nodes • From the lateral side , two -thirds of the superior conjunctiva and lateral one-third of the inferior conjunctiva \033 Preauricular nodes Specialized collections of T and B lymphocytes underlying a modified epithelium is known as conjunctiva-associated lymphoid tissue (CALT ) present in the stroma (substantia propria). It is critical in the initiation and regulation of ocular-surface immune responses . Note : The stroma also consists of the accessory lacrimal glands of Krause and Wolfring which are exocrine glands responsible for the basal secretion of the middle aqueous layer of the tear film. The image given below shows the lymphatic drainage of the conjunctiva.113

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: The image of the eye of a 32 -year-old woman having superior limbic keratoconjunctivitis is given below . Which of the following is commonly associated with it?
mcqs.explanation: Superior limbic keratoconjunctivitis has a definite association with thyroid dysfunction . It affects one or both eyes of middle -aged women and about 65% of patients have abnormal thyroid function (usually hyperthyroidism ). It is a chronic disease of the superior limbus and the superior bulbar and the tarsal conjunctiva. Clinical features : • Papillary hypertrophy of the superior tarsal plate , often having a diffuse velvety appearance . • Hyperemia of a radial band of the superior bulbar conjunctiva that stains with rose bengal . • • Superior filamentary keratitis that develops in about one-third of cases . Management : • Preservative-free lubricants • Topical acetylcysteine 10 % to 20 %, four times daily to break down filaments • Topical rebamipide

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is not characteristic of pterygium ?

options.a: Abnormal activity of p53 is seen in the pterygium tissue .
options.b: Decreased activity of tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases is seen .
options.c: Destruction of Bowman's layer occurs when the pterygium invades the cornea.
options.d: Elastotic degeneration and hyalinization of the connective tissue of the conjunctiva occur.

mcqs.explanation: Elastotic degeneration and hyalinization of the conjunctival connective tissue occurs in pinguecula (and not pterygium ). In pterygium , there is elastotic degeneration of collagen with fibrovascular proliferation. It is important to distinguish a pterygium from a pinguecula . A pterygium , while histologically similar to a pinguecula , is distinguished by fibrovascular tissue that grows onto the cornea.114 Pingueculae do not have vascularized tissue and do not cross the limbus.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 7-year-old boy complains of intense lacrimation, associated with photophobia . On examination , the following finding is seen in his upper tarsal conjunctiva. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The above image depicts cobblestone appearance , which is a papillary reaction in the palpebral conjunctiva seen in vernal keratoconjunctivitis (VKC). No follicular reaction is seen . Vernal conjunctivitis is also called spring catarrh or warm weather conjunctivitis. It primarily affects boys, and the onset is generally from the age of 5 years. It is primarily a type 1 hypersensitivity reaction that is IgE mediated . It also involves a type 4 hypersensitivity reaction. Classical features of the conjunctiva in VKC: Palpebral VKC - Cobblestone papillae are present in the upper tarsal conjunctiva associated with ropy discharge . Maxwell –Lyon sign is present which is a pseudomembrane formation of the upper lid when everted and exposed to heat Limbal VKC - Horner – Trantas spots are white dots consisting of eosinophils and epithelial debris in the limbal area. The image given below shows Horner-Trantas spots .Treatment of this condition is with topical steroids and mast cell stabilizers such as cromolyn sodium. Topical cyclosporine can be used in patients who do not respond to first line treatment modalities .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Your professor has assigned you to proofread a seminar on the anatomy of the conjunctiva made by a junior. In the explanation of conjunctival follicles , you spot a wrong statement that needs revision. What is that statement ?

options.a: Conjunctiva of new born does not produce follicles before 2-3 months of age .
options.b: Slit lamp may be necessary to differentiate between follicles and papillae .
options.c: Follicles are a hyperplasia of the normal vascular system .
options.d: Follicles are found in the sub-epithelial adenoid layer of the conjunctiva.

mcqs.explanation: Papillae (not follicles ) are hyperplasia of the normal vascular system , with glomerulus -like branches of capillaries growing into the epithelium in inflammatory conditions. On the other hand, follicles are yellowish -white , round elevations of 1-2 mm diameter . Follicles are a localized115 aggregation of lymphocytes present in the sub-epithelial adenoid layer of the conjunctiva. Image: Conjunctival papillae (hyperplastic epithelium and capillaries ) shown in the first image followed by conjunctival giant follicles (round yellowish -white elevations ) shown in the second image.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: In the grading of trachoma, the follicular stage is defined by the presence of which of the following ?

options.a: 5 or more follicles in the lower tarsal conjunctiva
options.b: 3 or more follicles in the upper tarsal conjunctiva
options.c: 5 or more follicles in the upper tarsal conjunctiva
options.d: 3 or more follicles in the lower tarsal conjunctiva

mcqs.explanation: In the grading of trachoma, follicular stage is defined by the presence of 5 or more follicles in the upper tarsal conjunctiva.
