It can help shape community health ser vices w ith regards to resource allocation, manpower policy, choice of technology, and the degree to which these services are made available & accessible to all segments of the society. The percentage of GDP spent on health is an indicator of political commitment. WHO recommends at least 5% of GDP to be spent on health care. India spends about 2.1 % of its GDP on health(budget 2022-23).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a socio-economic indicator of health?
mcqs.explanation: Annual family income is not a socioeconomic indicator of health. Socio-economic indicators o f health (mnemonic: H – FLAGGED): • Housing (number of persons per room) • Family size • Literacy rate (especially female literacy rate) • Availability of per capita calorie • GNP per capita • Growth rate of population • UnEmployment level • Dependency ratio

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding positive health in today's world?

options.a: It is dependent on social, economic, and cultural determinants
options.b: It is a mirage because of changing environment
options.c: It means that the body and mind are at peace
options.d: It includes provision of free heal th c amps by the government

mcqs.explanation: The provision of free health camps by the government is a concept of state medicine. Health does not merely mean the absence of disease or provision of diagnostic, curative, and preventive services. It is a state o f physical, mental , and social well-being. The state of positive health is based on the idea of perfect functioning of the body and mind. According to this concept, health is: • Biologically a state in which every cell and organ in the body is functioning at optimum capacity • Psychologically a state in which the individual feels a sense of perfect well-being and mastery over his environment37 • Socially a state in which the individual's capacities for participation in the social system are optimal This concept is too idealistic and can never become a reality. Humans can never be so perfectly adapted to the environment because everything in our life is subject to change. As the goal of positive health is unattainable, a broader concept of improving the quality of life has emerged. This highlights that positive health depends on medical action and also on economi c, c ultural, and social factors in the community.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: As per the WHO, which of the following is not included in the standard of living?
mcqs.explanation: Social security is a component of the level of living as per the United Nations and not standard of living. According to the WHO, the standard of living includes: • Income and occupation • Standards of housing, sanitation, and nutrition • Level of provision of health, educational, and recreational services It depends on per capita GNP.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following are components of the physical quality of life index (PQLI)?
mcqs.explanation: Infant mortality rate, literacy rate, and life expectancy at 1 year of age are the components of the physical quality of life index (PQLI).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the best measure of the standard of living?
mcqs.explanation: Human development index (HDI) is the best measure of the standard of living of a population. Physical quality of life index (PQLI) measures the quality of life.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a component of the human development index (HDI)?
mcqs.explanation: Infant mortality rate (IMR) is not a component of HDI. It is a component of the physical quality of life index (PQLI). The human development index (HDI) is used to compare living standards in different countries. It includes the following dimensions or components: Each d imension index is calculated using the formula: Dimension Index = (Actual Value - Minimum Value)/(Maximum Value - Minimum Value)38 HDI is the geometric mean of the three indices: ILife1/3 x IEducation1/3 x IIncome1/3. As per the Human Development Report 2023-2024, India's Human Development Index (HDI) value is 0.644. This places India at 134th out of 193 countries.Compo nent Indicator Index Longev ity Life expectancy at birth Life expectancy index Knowl edge Literacy and enrolment Education index Incom e GNI per capita US$ (purchasi ng power parity-PPP) GNI index(income ind ex)

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What are the minimum and maximum values established for the calculation of the life expectancy index in HDI?
mcqs.explanation: The minimum value established for the calculation of the life expectancy index in HDI is 20 years and the maximum is 85 years. These minimum and maximum values are used to calculate the dimension indices in HDI and are called goalposts. Each dimension index is calculated using the formula: Dimension Index = (Actual Value - Minimum Value)/(Maximum Value - Minimum Value).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true regarding the education index used for calculating the HDI?

options.a: It includes expected years of schooling
options.c: Adult literacy rate is not considered
options.d: Minimum and maximum values are based on global data

mcqs.explanation: The gross enrollment ratio is no longer used in obtaining the education index in HDI. It was used as an indicator e arlier. The education index is calculated by taking into account the mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling. Maximum and minimum values are based on global data. Adult literacy rate and gross enrollment ratio were used as indicators before 2009.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following indices measures the deprivation in basic dimensions of the country in human development?
mcqs.explanation: Human poverty index (HPI) measures deprivation in basic dimensions of human development. HPI-1 is used for developing countries and HPI-2 is used for developed countries. It is based upon the following indicators: T he range of HPI is from 0 to 100. The term HPI has now been replaced with multidimensional poverty index (MPI).39 Human Poverty Index(HPI -1) fordeveloping countries Human Poverty Index(HPI -2) forselected OECD countries A long and healthy life Probability at birth of not sur viving to age 40 Probability at birth of not sur viving to age 60 Knowledge Adult illiteracy rate Percentage of adults lacking f unctional literacy skills A decent standard of living Percentage of the population not using an improved water sourcePercentage of children underweight for ageDeprivati on of a decent standard of liv ing Percentage of people living b elow the poverty line Social exclusion Not included as a dimension Long term unemployment rat e

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not included in the Ottawa charter for health promotion?
mcqs.explanation: Building social security is not included in the Ottawa charter for health promotion. The first international conference for health promotion was held in Ottawa on 21st Nov 1986. It produced a charter known as the Ottawa charter. The charter identified five key action areas as given below: • Build healthy public policy • Create supportive environment for health • Strengthen community action for health • Develop personal skills • Reorient health services40

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a component of the epidemiological triad for tuberculosis?
mcqs.explanation: Duration of illness is not a part of the epidemiological triad for tuberculosis. The epidemiological triad includes host, agent and environment: • Host factors: Age, sex, religion, race, genetic profile, immune system • Agent factors: • Biological - bacteria, viruses • Chemical - poisons, alcohol, smoke • Physical - trauma, fire, radiation • Nutrition - lack/excess • Environmental factors: • Temperature, humidity, altitude • Water, milk, food • Radiation, polluti on, noise • Crowding , housing, neighborhood49 Hence, a malnourished child (host), Mycobacterium tuberculosis (agent) and overcrowding (environment) form the epidemiological triad for tuberculosis.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most logical sequence?
mcqs.explanation: Disease \037 Impairment \037 Disability \037 Handicap is the most logical sequence among the given options. Disease is a state of physiological/psychological dysfunction. Impairment is any loss or abnormality in normal structure or function. Disability is the inability to carry out normal actions due to impairment. Handicap is the disadvantage due to disability that limits fulfilment of a role that is normal.50

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A salesman met with an unfortunate accident that led t o him eventually losing his left foot. He has been unable to walk after this incident and so been rendered unemployed. Match the following examples with the corresponding events explaining the concept of disability.
mcqs.explanation: The correctly matched events relating to the given example are as follows: The WHO definition of impairment is "any loss or abnormality of psychological, physiological or anatomical structure or function". E.g., loss of a foot. An initial impairment may cause a secondary impairment as well. The WHO defines disability as ''any restriction or lack of ability to perform an activity in the manner or within the range considered normal for a human being". Because of impairment, t he affected person may be unable to carry out certain activities and hence the person is considered disabled. According to the WHO, a handicap is "a disadvantage for a given individual, resulting from an impairment or a disability, that limits or prevents the fulfilment of a role that is normal (depending on age, sex, and social and cultural factors) for that individual". The disadvantages experienced by a person as a result of disability makes them handicapped.Event Example Disease /Disord er Accident Impairment Loss of fo ot Disability Cannot W alk Handicap Unemploy ed51

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is most appropriate about the web of disease causation?

options.a: It implies that individual factors in the web have equal weightage
options.b: It implies that all the chains of causation m ust be controlled to prevent disease
options.c: It is mostly applicable for acute and rare diseases
options.d: It suggests ways of interrupting the disease occurrence

mcqs.explanation: The web of causation for a disease suggests a number of ways to interrupt the disease occurrence/progression. This model was suggested by MacMahon and Pugh in their book 'Epidemiologic Principles and Methods'. Web of causation considers all the predisposing factors and their complex interrelationship with each other. This model is ideally suited in the study of chronic disease. The web of causation does not imply that the disease is controlled only when all the multip le c hains of causation are removed . Sometimes removal of one significant link is sufficient to control the disease. In a multifactorial event, individual factors are by no means of equal weightage. The importance of each factor is expressed in terms of relative risk.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true regarding the pathogenesis period of a disease?

options.b: Recovery is seen in this period
options.c: Entry of causative agent is seen

mcqs.explanation: Primary prevention is not possible in the pathogenesis period of a disease. It can only be done in the period of pre-pathogenesis. The two phases in the natural history of a disease include: • Period of pre-pathogenesis: I t is before the onset of disease in humans. The disease agent has not entered the host, but the factors favouring the disease already exist. Primary prevention (health promotion and specific protection) is applicable in this period. • Period of pathogenesis: It begins with the entry of the organism till recovery, death or disability. Secondary (halting of the disease process) and tertiary prevention (measures to limit disability) are applicable in this per iod. I t isn't always characterised by the presence of disease symptoms as it also includes subclinical cases.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In the iceberg phenomenon of disease, which of the following does not represent the submerged portion of the iceberg?
mcqs.explanation: Epidemiologically, the iceberg phenomenon of disease, diagnosed cases are represented by the floating tip of the iceberg. The iceberg phenomenon of disease is related to the spectrum of disease. The water surface is the line of demarcation between the apparent and inapparent infections. The submerged portion of the iceberg represents the hidden mass of diseases l ike asymptomatic, latent , and undiagnosed cases. Screening is done to identify these cases. The iceberg phenomenon of disease is depicted in the image below.52

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following diseases shows the iceberg phenomenon?
mcqs.explanation: Rubella shows the iceberg phenomenon of disease. The iceberg phenomenon of diseases is not shown by diseases such as tetanus, rabies, and measles. Iceberg phenomenon is shown by: • Polio • Influenza • Rubella • Mumps • Japanese Encephalitis • Diphtheria • Hepatitis A and B • Tuberculosis • Diabetes • Malnutrition • Hypertension Note: If a disease has more number of subclinical infections, it shows the iceberg phenomenon of disease depicted in the image below.53

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the term used to describe the interruption in the transmission of a disease?
mcqs.explanation: Interruption in the transmission of a disease is called elimination. It is a step towards eradication. Elimination is a reduction in the number of new cases of an infectious disease to zero (or a very low defined target rate) in a defined geographical area as a result of deliberate efforts. Continued measures to prevent re-establishment of transmission are required. Eradication is a complete and permanent worldwide reduction to zero new cases of an infectious disease through d eliberate efforts. No further control measures are required. Surveillance is the continuous scrutiny of factors that determine the occurrence and distribution of disease and ill health. Control aims at decreasing the incidence, duration and transmission of the disease. It also aims at decreasing the physical and psychological complications of a disease.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Among the following options, which aids the most in disease elimination?
mcqs.explanation: Herd immunity aids the most in disease elimination. Herd immunity achieved, especially through immunization, g oes a long way in helping the elimination of diseases. When a high level of herd immunity is maintained, the susceptible population is reduced to a small proportion, thereby eliminating the disease. The purpose of isolation is to protect the community by preventing the transfer of infection from the reservoir to the possible susceptible hosts. Quarantine refers to restrictions on the healthy contacts of an infectious disease.54

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: While collecting surveillance data for disease X, you find that the incidence of the disease is zero in your region. Which of the following statements best describes this scenario?

options.a: Disease is eliminated from the region.
options.b: Disease is well controlled in the region.
options.c: Disease is eradicated from the region.
options.d: Disea se s hows iceberg phenomenon in the region.

mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, as the disease has zero incidence, we can say the disease has been eliminated from the region. Elimination is a reduction in the number of new cases of an infectious disease to zero (or a very low defined target rate) in a defined geographical area as a result of deliberate efforts. Continued measures to prevent re-establishment of transmission are required. Eradication is a complete and permanent worldwide reduction to zero new cases of an infectious d isease through deliberate efforts. No further control measures are required. Control aims at decreasing the incidence, duration and transmission of the disease. It also aims at decreasing the physical and psychological complications of a disease. The iceberg phenomenon of disease is related to the spectrum of disease. The submerged portion of the iceberg represents the hidden mass of diseases like asymptomatic, latent, and undiagnosed cases. The clinical or dia gnosed c ases are represented by the floating tip of the iceberg and not the submerged portion. As disease incidence is zero here, there are no cases to form the iceberg.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a silent epidemic?
mcqs.explanation: Alzheimer's disease is referred to as the silent epidemic of the century. Nearly 50 million people globally are living with this disease. Since it strikes so often, so arbitrarily, and with such little warning, many have dubbed it the silent epidemic.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the analysis of routine measurements aimed at detecting changes in the health status of a population called?
mcqs.explanation: The analysis of routine measurements aimed at detecting changes in the health status or environment of a population is called monitoring. Surveillance is the continuous scrutiny of factors that determine the occurrence and distribution of disease and ill health. Sentinel surveillance is a method of identifying the missing cases and thereby supplementing the notified cases. Systematic reviews involve a detailed plan with the goal of reducing bias by identifying, appraising, and synthesizing all relevant studies on a par ticular t opic.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In which of the following does surveillance of disease not have a direct role?

options.c: Data on new and changing trends

mcqs.explanation: Surveillance of a disease does not have a direct role in breaking the chain of transmission. Surveillance is the continuous scrutiny of factors that determine the occurrence and distribution of disease and ill health.55 It helps in health planning and provides information about public health disasters including data on new and changing trends of disease. Surveillance requires professional analysis and sophisticated judgment of data, leading to recommendations for control activities.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Measures in sentinel surveillance do not aim at identifying:
mcqs.explanation: Sentinel surveillance does not include identifying cases free of disability. Sentinel surveillance helps in identifying the missing cases, in addition to the already existing and new cases. It is u sed for supplementing routine notifications.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is public health surveillance preferentially a imed at?
mcqs.explanation: Public health surveillance is preferentially aimed at health planning. Public health surveillance provides important feedback on the health status of the population, about planning control and prevention activities, and also for public health disasters.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is included under primordial prevention of coronary artery disease?
mcqs.explanation: Adoption of a healthy lifestyle from childhood would fall under the category of primordial prevention of coronary artery disease. Primordial prevention is preventing t he emergence of risk factors among population groups in which these risk factors have not yet appeared. Most adult health problems (obesity, hypertension) have their early origins in childhood. It is in childhood that lifestyles are formed i.e. eating patterns, physical exercise, smoking, etc. In primordial prevention, efforts are made to discourage children from adopting harmful lifestyles. These lifestyle changes when made by adults are known as primary preve ntion.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What type of prevention is the prescriptive screening of a disease?
mcqs.explanation: Prescriptive screening of a disease is an example of secondary prevention. Prescriptive screening of disease can lead to early diagnosis of disease. By early diagnosis, intervention can be made to prevent disability. Hence, it comes under secondary prevention.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What form of prevention is prospective screening?
mcqs.explanation: 56 Prospective screening is a type of primary prevention. Prospective screening is done on healthy individuals to screen for disease. It is done prior to the onset of the disease. E.g., screening donated blood for HIV before it is transfused. This type of prevention reduces the incidence of disease. Note: Prescriptive screening is done for case detection. People are screened for their own benefits. It is an early diagnosis of diseases existing in them. This is a form of secondary p revention. E .g., neonatal screening for hypothyroidism, pap smear for detection of cervical cancer.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You advise a reproductive age woman to vaccinate against HPV . What is this type of prevention called?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of immunisation is an example of primary prevention. Primary prevention is an action taken before the onset of disease. This reduces the possibility of disease occurrence. Hence, immunization is a form of primary prevention, through specific protection. Examples of primary prevention include immunization, sanitation, solid and liquid waste m anagement etc.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Who among the f ollowing is not a target for primary prevention?
mcqs.explanation: Asymptomatic patients are the target population for secondary prevention but not for primary prevention. Primary prevention is implemented before the onset of the disease. Hence, all patients including asymptomatic ones are not included in the target group.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: As a part of the iodine deficiency control programme, you advocate the usage of iodized salt in hilly areas. What is this type of prevention an example of?
mcqs.explanation: The usage of iodized salt in iodine-deficient areas like in hilly regions is an example of primary prevention as it provides specific protection.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are performing a routine pap smear on a 30-year-old woman in the gynecology OPD. What level of prevention does this fall under?
mcqs.explanation: Pap smear is a screening test for carcinoma cervix and is an example of secondary prevention. Early diagnosis (including screening) and treatment are the components of secondary prevention. Some of the examples of secondary prevention are as follows: • Papanicolaou (Pap) smear for early detection of cervical cancer • Mammography for early detection of breast cancer • Colonoscopies for early detection of colon cancer57 • Blood Pressure Screening Secondary prevention measures focus on the sub-clinical stage and the early clinical stage, such as dysplasia in this case. These measures enable early detection and prompt effective intervention to correct departures from a state of health.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What mode of prevention is disability prevention by appropriate treatment an example of?
mcqs.explanation: Disability prevention by appropriate treatment is an example of secondary prevention. This is because disability has not occurred yet so correct treatment can stop it from developing. After the disability h as set in, prevention of progression of disability from transitioning into a handicap is tertiary prevention. It is also called disability limitation.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of disability limitation?

options.b: Starting a patient on anti-tuberculous therapy

mcqs.explanation: Prescribing spectacles for refractive error is an example of disability limitation which is a component of tertiary prevention. This mode of intervention is applicable when the patient presents late in the pathogenesis phase. The objective of this intervention is to prevent or halt the transition of the disease p rocess from impairment to handicap. Option B: Starting a patient on anti-tuberculous therapy is secondary prevention as it is a part of treatment. Option C: Abstinence from smoking is a modification of the risk factor. Hence it is an example of primary prevention. Option D: Early fixation of fractures will prevent disability. Hence, it is an example of secondary prevention.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which among the following diseases was eliminated in India in 2015?
mcqs.explanation: Maternal and neonatal tetanus was eliminated from India in 2015, as certified by the WHO. Important y ears for India (declared disease-free): • Infective trachoma - 2017 • Yaws - 2016 • Maternal & neonatal tetanus - 2015 • Polio - 2014 • Guinea worm disease (dracunculiasis) - 2000 Worldwide eradication:58 • Type-2 wild poliovirus - 2015 • Type-3 wild poliovirus- • Smallpox - 1980

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about ICD- 11?

options.a: It includes a new chapter on traditional medicine
options.b: Gender incongruence is now listed as part of mental health
options.c: The codes relating to antimicrobial resistance are more closely in line w ith the Global Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance System
options.d: It has come into full effect from January

mcqs.explanation: The new ICD-11 has a new chapter on sexual health that contains gender incongruence, which was previously listed under mental health conditions in the ICD-10. The ICD 11 was released by the WHO in June 2018 and was presented at the World Health Assembly in May 2019 for adoption by the Member States. It has come into effect from 1 January 2022. Its designations for antibiotic resistance align with the G lobal Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance System (GLASS). It is given by the WHO and is revised every 10 years. New chapters added in ICD-11 are: • Traditional medicine • Sexual health: Gender incongruence has been moved from mental health to sexual health. • Gaming disorder has been added under Addictive disorders. • Immune system disorders, which will enable the better study of allergies. It has more detail on cancer, specifically different types of skin cancer, as w ell as on heart health and weight disorders compared to ICD-10.59

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not included in the format of the death certificate recommended by the WHO?

options.c: Other significant conditions contributing to death
options.d: Age of person at the time of death

mcqs.explanation: Age at the time of death is not included in the WHO format for a death certificate.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are filling the death certificate of a patient who died from rupture of the myocardium following an acute myocardial infarction. This was because of thrombosis in the coronary artery due to longstanding atherosclerosis . What will you record in line I (
mcqs.explanation: Coronary artery thrombosis is to be filled in line I (c) of the death certificate as one of the antecedent causes in the order of the events that took place. The flow of events in this patient is as follows:69 As per the recommendations of Forty-Third World Health Assembly 1990, an additional line (d) was added below (c) in part I of the death certificate, as approved by the WHO. Part II will only be filled up with a significant condition contributing to the death but not related to the disease or condition causing it.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An HIV positive patient was suffering from multi-drug resistant tuberculosis. He died of respiratory failure due to lobar pneumonia. Which of the following options is the most appropriate for the line I (
mcqs.explanation: Lobar pneumonia is appropriate for line I (a) of the death certificate. Line I (a) consists of the immediate cause of death such as the disease/condition. Immediate cause i s the immediate /terminal event leading to death In this patient: • I(a) - Disease directly leading to death: Lobar pneumonia • I(b) - Antecedent cause: MDR tuberculosis. • II- HIV Respiratory failure is a mode of dying in this patient. It is not the cause of death. Terminal events like circulatory failure and respiratory failure, are modes of dying. They should not be written as the immediate cause of death in the death certificate because they are just signs of death. Simply p ut, respiratory failure is 'how he died' whereas lobar pneumonia is 'why he died'. Therefore, lobar pneumonia (why he died) is the cause of the death.70

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a morbidity indicator?
mcqs.explanation: Years of potential life lost is not a morbidity indicator. It is a mortality indicator. It is the years of potential life lost through premature death. Notification rates, spells of sickness and incidence are examples of morbidity indicators.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about rate is false?

options.a: It measures the occurrence of an event in a population.
options.b: It has no specification of time.
options.d: It's numerator is mostly part of the denominator.

mcqs.explanation: Rate is the measurement of the occurrence of a particular event in a given time. Hence, rates have a specification in time. Examples include crude death rate, incidence rate etc.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: To calculate the crude death rate of a country, at what time of the year is the population assessed?
mcqs.explanation: The crude death rate is a mortality indicator, which uses the mid-year population as its denominator . The mid-year population is always attributed as the population on 1st July of any year. Hence for calculating the crude death rate, the population is assessed on the 1st of July.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: For which of the following purposes is age-specific death rates not used?

options.a: Identifying specific age groups at risk
options.b: Comparison for different causes within the same population
options.c: Comparison between different sexes in relation to accidents
options.d: Comparison between different age groups in relation to accidents

mcqs.explanation: Sex-specific death rates are used for the comparison between sexes and not age-specific death rates.71 Age-specific death rates are used for: • Comparison for different causes within the same population. • Comparison between different age groups in relation to a particular event. • Identifying specific age groups at risk.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An epidemiologist is assessing an outbreak of acute diarrhoeal disease in a region. He wants to predict the virulence of the causative agent. Which of the following parameters will he use for this purpose?
mcqs.explanation: Case fatality rate is used in this scenario as it is the most useful parameter to predict the virulence of an acute illness. It represents the killing power of disease. Note: Case fatality rate is an incidence proportion and not a true rate as no time interval i s used for its calculation .

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Case fatality rate is ______.

options.b: Killing power of a disease in time
options.d: Killing power of a disease with no time interval

mcqs.explanation: Case fatality rate reflects the killing power of a disease with no specific time interval.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A village has a population o f 30,000 people. 500 of them contracted a disease X, out of which 75 died. What is the case fatality rate?
mcqs.explanation: Case fatality rate is given by the formula:The total number of cases of disease X= The total number of deaths= Hence the case fatality rate= 75/500 x 100 = 15%72

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a village of 5000 people, an outbreak of cholera led to 200 cases with 50 deaths. What is the case fatality rate?
mcqs.explanation: The case fatality rate is 25%. Case fatality rate: (Total number of deaths due to a particular disease)/(Total number of cases due to the same disease)x 100 : 50/200 * 100 = 25%

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the simplest measure of the burden of a disease in a community?
mcqs.explanation: The proportional mortality rate is the simplest measure to estimate the burden of a disease in a community. It is commonly used for broad disease groups and when population data is not available.It is of limited value in making comparisons between populations and in identifying risk groups.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Among the following, which measurement can be used as a yardstick for the assessment of standards of therapy?
mcqs.explanation: The survival rate can be used as a yardstick for the assessment of standards of therapy. It is used as a method of describing prognosis and is widely employed in cancer studies. The survival rate is given by the following formula.73

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Standardisation was done before comparing the mortality rates of two countries. What is the rationale behind this?

options.a: Due to difference in number of deaths.
options.b: Due to difference in age distribution.
options.c: Due to difference in the population density.
options.d: Due to difference in cause of death.

mcqs.explanation: While comparing the mortality rates of two countries, the standardization of rates is done due to differences in age distribution. The two types of standardisation include direct and indirect. In both methods, a standard population is chosen where the numbers in each age and sex group are known and its choice is arbitrary. The commonly used standard populations are the Segi world population and the European standard population.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about the standardized mortality ratio?

options.a: It is a form of direct standardization.
options.b: Observed deaths and expected deaths are part of its formula.
options.d: It can be used if the event of interest is occurrence of disease.

mcqs.explanation: Standardized mortality ratio is a form of indirect standardization.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A party was attended by 110 people out of which, 40 did not eat fruit salad. Among the rest of those who ate fruit salad, 55 developed food poisoning. What is the attack rate?
mcqs.explanation: The attack rate is calculated by the formula:74 In this scenario, the number of new cases is 55 and the total number of those at risk is 70 as they ate the fruit salad. Therefore attack rate = 55/70 X 100 = 78.6%. Attack rate is an incidence rate. It is used only when the population is exposed to risk for a limited period.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Out of a family of 4 members, one of them developed COVID-19 infection. Four days later, 2 other members developed the same. What is the secondary attack rate?
mcqs.explanation: Secondary attack rate is calculated by the following:In this scenario, there is one primary case. The total exposed contacts are the other 3 members of the family. The number of persons developing the disease is 2.75 So, secondary attack rate = 2/3 x 100 = 66%. Note: The primary case is excluded from both the numerator and denominator.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following study designs would you prefer for calculating the incidence of a disease?
mcqs.explanation: The study designs which can be used to calculate incidence are cohort studies and longitudinal studies.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about incidence are true?
mcqs.explanation: Incidence is not affected by the duration of the disease. Analysis of incidence rates may provide useful insights into the effectiveness of the health services provided. Incidence is the number of new cases occurring in a defined population during a period o f time. Prevalence is more than incidence as it is the product of incidence and duration. Incidence is a type of rate and not a proportion.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A medical officer noticed that there were 300 new cases of cholera in an area in a year. The total population in that area is 30,000. What is the incidence of cholera?
mcqs.explanation: The incidence of cholera is 10 per 1000. Incidence is given by the formula:In this scenario number of new cases = 300 Total population = 30,000 Hence the incidence rate = (300/30,000) \327 1000 = 1076 Therefore it is 10 per 1000 per year.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a good indicator of efficacy of health programs?
mcqs.explanation: Incidence is a good indicator of the efficacy of health services and programs.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false with regard to prevalence?

options.a: It is a product of incidence and duration.
options.b: It can be determined b y a cross-sectional study.
options.c: It is an example of rate.
options.d: It is point prevalence unless specified.

mcqs.explanation: Prevalence is a proportion, not a rate. Prevalence is the proportion of all cases, old and new, of a particular disease at a given point in time or over a period of time in a given population. It can be determined from cross-sectional studies. Types of prevalence: • Point prevalence is the prevalence at a point in time. Usually, prevalence is point prevalence unless o therwise specified. • Period prevalence is the prevalence over a period of time.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The incidence of a disease is 4 per 1000 of the population with an average duration of 2 years. What is the prevalence?
mcqs.explanation: The prevelance in the given situation is 8/1000 population. Prevalence is given by the formula : Prevalance = Incidence x Mean Duration Prevalence = 4/1000 x 2 = 8/1000 population

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A village has a total population of 100,000 with an under-16 population at 3%. The prevalence of goitre in the under-16 population is (0.3/100). What is the total number of under-16 population affected by goitre?
mcqs.explanation: The total number of persons in the under-16 with goitre is 9. Number of total under-16 population = 3% of 100,000 = 3000. Thus, total number of goitre patients who are under-16 with the prevalence at the given value = 000 *0.3/100= 9

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a population of 5000, new cases of TB are 500 and old cases are 50. What is the prevalence of TB in this case?
mcqs.explanation: Prevalence is given by the formula:77 In the given scenario total no.of cases :50(old)+ 500(new) =550. Hence prevalence = (550/5000) x 100 = 11%

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a village having a population of 5000, a diagnostic test for a particular disease showed the following result s. W hat is the prevalence of the disease?
mcqs.explanation: Prevalence is given by the formula:In this scenario, the number of cases: 1000+500 = 1500. Total population: Prevalence= 1500/5000 \327 100 = 30%.78

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A randomized control trial showed an effective treatment against an infectious disease. It was then incorporated by the health system. Which of the following is subsequently expected to happen?
mcqs.explanation: A new effective treatment for infectious disease would reduce the duration of the disease, thereby reducing prevalence. Note: Both prevalence and incidence decrease but prevalence is the first to show a change in pattern. Hence, 'prevalence decreases' is the better answer.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: There was an outbreak of hepatitis A infection in your town. Proper prevention strategies were enforced. What is expected to happen at first to the number of cases of hepatitis A?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, prevention of hepatitis A would lead to decrease in incidence at first. Prevention of an acute disease would prevent new cases, thus first decreasing incidence.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A new drug was approved for the treatment of prostate cancer. It has been shown to prevent e arly deaths but not cure the cancer. What is expected to happen to the cases of prostate cancer over a period of time?

options.a: Increase in incidence, no change in prevalence
options.b: Decrease in incidence, increase in prevalence
options.c: Increase in incidence, decrease in prevalence
options.d: Increase in prevalence, no change in incidence

mcqs.explanation: A new drug that prevents death yet does not cure the disease will cause an increase in prevalence but the incidence remains the same. In the given scenario, the drug reduces early deaths but does not cure prostate cancer. Hence, there is a paradoxical increase in the prevalence while the incidence remains the same. Prevalence depends on two factors, the incidence and duration of illness. If the population is stable and incidence and duration are unchanging, the relationship between incidence a nd prevalence can be expressed as: P = I X D (I - Incidence and D - Mean duration) This equation shows longer the duration of the disease, the greater the prevalence. Note: • In chronic diseases like TB, prevalence will be higher than incidence. • If a new treatment for a disease is effective, incidence does not change but prevalence decreases as the duration of disease decreases. • If the treatment only prevents death but doesn't cure the disease, it may cause a paradox ical i ncrease in prevalence.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Cross product ratio can be arrived from:
mcqs.explanation: Cross product ratio (Odds ratio) can be obtained from the case-control study.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A person wants to study about the relationship between smoking and lung cancer, so he collects data about people diseased with lung cancer from government hospitals and the number of cigarette packets sold at the same time period. Which type of study is this?
mcqs.explanation: 79 The type of study described is an ecological study as the unit of study is the population. The number of cigarette packets sold at the same time is data about the population. Option A: The unit of study in a cross-sectional study is an individual. Option C: There is no experiment done here. Hence, it is not experimental study. Option D: Quasi-experiments are nonrandomized, pre-post intervention studies done when it is not feasible or ethical to conduct a randomized controlled trial. The unit of study is therefore patients or individuals and not population.80

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A researcher is planning to study the etiology of certain painful idiopathic peripheral neuropathies. Which of the following study methods shall he choose?
mcqs.explanation: Diseases of unknown etiology or new diseases can be studied with descriptive epidemiology.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The preliminary observations made by Burkitt in Africa eventually found that the Epstein-Barr Virus is an etiological factor for Burkitt lymphoma. What is this study an example of?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is an example of a descriptive study.86 Descriptive studies are used to describe a disease of unknown etiology. These studies also led to the discovery of prions as the etiological agents of chronic degenerative neurological disorders (Kuru) in humans. This is also an example of a descriptive study. Types of epidemiological studies: • Observational studies - allow nature to take its own course, the investigator measures but does not intervene. • Descriptive studies - limited to the description of the occurrence o f a disease in a population. • Analytical studies - go further by analyzing the relationship between health status and other variables. • Ecological studies • Cross-sectional studies • Case-control studies • Cohort studies • Experimental studies or intervention studies involve an active attempt to change a disease determinant or the progress of a disease and are similar in design to experiments in other sciences. • Randomized controlled trials • Field trials • Com munity t rials

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following are included in descriptive epidemiology?
mcqs.explanation: Descriptive epidemiology involves describing the disease in terms of time, place, and person distribution.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes the term hypothesis?
mcqs.explanation: An epidemiological hypothesis is a supposition or variable. It is arrived at from observation and needs to be tested. Descriptive studies primarily focus on the formulation of a hypothesis. Analytical studies which include study designs like case-control and cohort are used to test the formulated hypothesis. The hypothesis can subsequently be r ejected or accepted. Experimental studies involve an intervention to provide scientific proof for etiological risk factors of diseases and to measure the efficiency of health services.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases is planning to study the natural history of COVID-19. Which of the following studies can be used?
mcqs.explanation: 87 Longitudinal studies are useful to study the natural history of a disease. It is also used to identify risk factors, and to find the incidence rate. In longitudinal studies, observations are repeated in the same population over a prolonged period of time by follow-up examinations. Their disadvantage is that they are difficult to organize and take a very long time.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What are prevalence studies also known as?
mcqs.explanation: Cross-sectional studies help in obtaining the prevalence of a disease. Hence, they are also known as prevalence s tudies. Cross -sectional study is a type of observational study where a cross-section of a population is examined once at one point in time. It is more useful in studying chronic diseases than acute ones. They do not provide information on the natural history of disease or incidence and also do not establish the time sequence.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following s tatements about point source epidemic is false?

options.b: Clustering of cases occur within a short period of time
options.c: It occurs only due to an infectious agent
options.d: All cases usually develop within one incubation period

mcqs.explanation: Point source epidemics are caused not only due to infectious agents but also by environmental pollution and contamination of food. Point source e pidemics belong to the common source type of epidemics. Exposure to disease agents is brief so they are also called single exposure epidemics. All cases develop within one incubation period. In the epidemic curve, there is a sharp rise and fall as all cases are clustered within one incubation period. There are no secondary waves and these epidemics tend to be explosive.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Identify the type of epidemic depicted from the following epidemic curve.
mcqs.explanation: Point-source epidemic is depicted in the given image. In the epidemic curve for a point-source epidemic, t here is a sharp rise and fall of the curve with no secondary waves. It tends to be explosive as all the cases are clustered in a narrow period of time. It occurs within one incubation period of the disease.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An outbreak of viral hepatitis A was reported from a town between June and September of a particular year. The peak of the outbreak occurred in July. What is this an example of?
mcqs.explanation: This outbreak of viral hepatitis A is an example of a common source, multiple exposure type of epidemic. The incubation period of hepatitis A is approximately 28 days (range 15 to 50 days). In this scenario, the cases of viral hepatitis A have occurred over a period from June to S eptember (120 days ) which is more than one incubation period of the disease. This is suggestive of multiple88 exposures from a common source. If the period of the outbreak falls within one incubation period, then the type of epidemic is common source ,single exposure or point source epidemic. Difference between single exposure and multiple exposure epidemics: Propagated epidemic results from person to person transmission of the infectious agent over a prolonged duration of time. For e.g. Polio epidemic, COVID-19. Note: Hepatitis A epidemic is generally an example of a propagated e pidemic. However , it does not always follow this pattern. In the given scenario, since the outbreak lasts for a short duration of 3 months (about 3 incubation periods for hepatitis A), it is considered to be a point source, multiple exposure outbreak.Common source , single expo sure epidemic Common source , multiple ex posure epidemic Nature of exposure Single , brief exposure Multiple , continuous or inter mittent exposures for a prolo nged time Nature of epidemic Explosivewith clustering of c ases within a short interval of time Less chance of clusteringof ca ses within short interval of ti me Duration of epidem ic Falls<1 incubation periodof a particular disease Extends >1 incubation period of a particular disease Example An epidemic offood poisonin g Outbreak ofcholera

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The sales team of a corporate company presents to the hospital w ith complaints of sudden onset nausea, vomiting and loose stools. They give a history of having food from a nearby bakery three hours ago. What is this an example of?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of food poisoning. It is a type of common-source (point-source), single exposure epidemic.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of disease following a seasonal trend?

options.a: Occurrence of rubella every 6-9 years in the pre-vaccination era
options.b: Occurrence of influenza pandemic every 7-10 years
options.c: Occurrence of bacterial gastroenteritis in summer
options.d: Increase in the occurrence of diabetes in developed countries

mcqs.explanation: Occurrence of bacterial gastroenteritis in summer is an example of a disease following seasonal trend. Seasonal trend is a type of periodic fluctuation. It refers to the occurrence of a disease in seasonal variation influenced by environmental conditions like climate, rainfall, life cycle of vectors, heat, etc. Examples are: • Measles and varicella i n early spring • Bacterial gastroenteritis in summer • Heatstroke in summer89 • Dengue in July-November • Respiratory infections in winter.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The influenza pandemic is anticipated to occur every 7-10 years due to the antigenic variation of the virus. What is thi s a n example of?
mcqs.explanation: The influenza pandemic occuring every 7–10 years due to antigenic variations of the virus is an example of a disease showing cyclical trend. Diseases occurring in cycles spread over a short period of time show cyclical trends of time distribution. Cyclical trend is a type of periodic fluctuation. Examples include: • Measles: every 2-3 years in the pre-vaccination era. • Rubella: 6-9 years in the pre-vaccination e ra. Non -infectious conditions can also show cyclical trends.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: How often did the cyclical trends of measles occured in the pre-vaccination era?
mcqs.explanation: In the pre-vaccination era, the cyclical trends of measles occurred every 2-3 years, while that of rubella occurred every 6-9 years.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is known as the change in the occurrence of a disease over very long periods of time?
mcqs.explanation: A secular trend refers to the changes in the occurrence of a disease over long periods of time (decade). Usually, disease distributions tend to move in one particular direction over a period of time. Examples: Decrease in diseases like polio, tuberculosis, and typhoid fever, b ut increase in diabetes and coronary artery disease in developed countries.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following cannot be depicted by the image given below?

options.b: Rural - urban distributions of a disease

mcqs.explanation: The given image is of a spot map. Spot maps are not used to depict rural-urban distributions of a disease. They help to understand the local distributions of a disease. They are also called shaded maps. This method was used by John Snow to investigate the epidemic of cholera in London in 1854. They depict areas of high or low frequency, the boundaries, and patterns of disease distribution.90

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What are migration studies used to evaluate?

options.a: Socio-demographic reasons for migration of a population
options.b: Prevalence of diseases in a population
options.c: Environmental and genetic factors of a disease in a population
options.d: Incidence of disease in the immigrant population

mcqs.explanation: Migration studies are used to evaluate the role of genetic and environmental factors of a disease in a population. The two methods used are: • Comparing disease and death rates of migrants with kin who stayed at home • Comparing disease and death rates of migrants with the local population of the host country Limitations of these studies: • Non-randomization of these groups • Environmental factors may act only up to a certain age • Not useful for diseases with long incubatio n periods

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What does bimodality in person distribution refer to?

options.a: Description of two etiological hypotheses of a disease in one person
options.b: Evaluation of two different environmental factors of a person in disease causation
options.c: Two separate peaks in the age incidence curve of a disease
options.d: Equal incidence of a disease in male and female population

mcqs.explanation: Bimodality refers to the occurence two separate peaks in the age incidence curve of a disease. Example: Hodgkin's lymphoma shows a bimodal curve with peaks at 15–20 years and 70–80 years. The image below shows bimodality in the age incidence curve:91

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are conducting a cohort study in a group of headload workers to identify the risk factors for developing low back pain in future. This type of study falls under which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: Cohort studies fall under non-experimental (observational) analytical studies. Classification of epidemiological studies: • Observational studies: allow nature to take its own course, the investigator measures but does not intervene. It is further classified into: • Descriptive studies: limited to describing the occurrence of a disease in a population. • Analytical studies: go further by analyzing the relationship between health status and other variables. It i ncludes: • Ecological studies • Cross-sectional studies • Case-control studies • Cohort studies • Experimental studies or interventional studies: it involves an active attempt to change a disease determinant or the progress of a disease, and is similar in design to experiments in other sciences. • Randomized controlled trials • Field trials • Community trials

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the unit of observation in ecological studies?
mcqs.explanation: In ecological studies, the unit of observation is the population or community.Type of study Unit Ecological / Correlational Population Cross-sectional / Prevalence Individual Case-control/ Case reference Individual Cohort/ Follow up Individual Randomised Controlled Tria ls Patients Field Trial Healthy peo ple102 Type of study Unit Community trial Community

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Identify the type of study f rom the following design:
mcqs.explanation: The design given is of a case-control study. It proceeds from effect to cause and is done after the exposure and outcome have occurred. It tries to determine the possible exposure factors after a known disease incidence. This is the first approach to test causal hypotheses and uses controls to support or refute an inference. Retrospective or historical cohort study, on the other hand, tries to compare the risk of developing a disease to some already known exposure factors. Ex: r isk of lung cancer in uranium miners, risk of angiosarcoma in persons exposed to polyvinyl chloride etc. Retrospective cohort studies are more economical and quicker than prospective cohort studies.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A study was conducted among a group of 500 patients with lung cancer and another group of 300 people chosen from the general population. Both the groups were questioned about their exposure to smoking. What kind of study is this?
mcqs.explanation: This is a case-control study. In this scenario, 500 patients constitute the cases and 300 people from the general population constitute the controls. The study is done from effect (lung cancer) to cause (smoking).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A case-control study was conducted to evaluate the association between l ifestyle risk factors and the prevalence of dyslipidemia. Which of the following is not an advantage of this type of study?
mcqs.explanation: Incidence cannot be calculated from case-control studies. Incidence can be calculated from cohort studies , also known as longitudinal studies.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A case-control study was conducted to see if symptoms of upper gastrointestinal dysfunction occurred more frequently in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Which of the following cannot be used as controls in this study?
mcqs.explanation: Siblings cannot be used as controls while studying genetic conditions because the outcome would be distorted due to their similarities. Controls in a case-control study: • Usually disease-free • Can be up to 4 times the number of cases in small studies • In large studies, a 1:1 ratio of cases and controls can be sought • Sources: general population, hospitals, relatives (spouses and s iblings), neighbors , or colleagues • Although, siblings cannot be used as controls for studies on genetic conditions103

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a cause of bias in a case-control study?
mcqs.explanation: Hawthorne bias is not seen in case-control studies. This bias occurs when the subjects change their attitude/ actions while under observation. This distorts the results of the cohort or experimental studies. The bias that are seen in the case-control study are: • Confounding • Recall bias • Selection bias • Berkesonian bias • Interviewer's bias

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about random errors?

options.d: Systematic errors are different from random errors

mcqs.explanation: Random errors are not causes of bias. Random error arises when a value of the sample measurement diverges, due to chance alone , f rom that of the true population value. They can never be completely eliminated. Sources of random errors are individual biological variations, sampling errors, and measurement errors. Systematic errors are also called biases. They are different from random errors.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following factors in a study will cause Berkesonian bias?

options.a: Interviewer asking leading questions to the subjects
options.b: Different rates o f hospital admission of different diseases
options.c: Researcher 's belief in the treatment changing the outcome of the study
options.d: Cases that are lost to follow-up

mcqs.explanation: Berkesonian bias occurs due to the different rates of hospital admission of people with different diseases. It is a type of selection bias termed after Joseph Berkeson who described it.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An epidemiologist plans to conduct a prospective study instead of a retrospective study. Which of the following disadvantages does he aim to eliminate by conducting this study?
mcqs.explanation: Recall bias can be eliminated in a prospective study. Recall bias is also called memory bias. It is widely seen in retrospective (case-control) studies as extensive history is taken from the participants.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A study conducted in a group revealed that consumption of alcohol increases the risk of esophageal cancer, but it may be actually due to cigarette smoking. This happens due to:
mcqs.explanation: 104 In this scenario, cigarette smoking is related to both the outcome of esophageal cancer and consumption of alcohol. Thus, this is an example of a confounding factor. A confounding factor is defined as one which is associated with both exposure and outcome and is distributed unequally in study and control groups. In this study to determine the role of alcohol in the etiology of esophageal cancer, smoking is considered as a confounding factor because: • It is associated with the c onsumption of alcohol (exposure). • It is an independent risk factor for oesophageal cancer (outcome). In these conditions, the effects of alcohol consumption can be determined only if the influence of smoking is neutralized by matching.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding confounding factor?

options.a: It can be reduced by matching
options.b: It is associated individually with both cause and effect
options.c: It is distributed equally in both study and control groups
options.d: I t is associated with the exposure of the study

mcqs.explanation: A confounding factor is a factor that is associated with both exposure and diseases and is distributed unequally in study and control groups. It can be reduced by matching. For example, if the study is that a sedentary lifestyle can lead t o coronary artery diseases, then age can act as a confounding factor as it is individually linked to both sedentary lifestyle and coronary artery diseases.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A researcher is planning to conduct a study to investigate the relationship between oral contraceptives and breast cancer. He wants to remove age as a confounding factor. Which of the following methods will not help him reduce this bias?
mcqs.explanation: Deletion is not a method to reduce confounding. Methods to reduce confounding are: • At the time of designing the study: • Randomization • Matching • Restriction • At the time of analysis: • Stratification • Statistical modelings like regression analysis, multivariate analysis, and the Cochran-Mantel-Haensz el m ethod.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Matching is done for which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: Matching helps only in removing the known confounding factors. Matching is the process by which controls are selected in a way that they are similar to cases in certain pertinent variables (e.g., age) that are known to influence the outcome of the disease. If not adequately matched for comparability, these variables could confound the results.105

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which among the following is not a type of matching?
mcqs.explanation: There is no type of matching called collective matching. Types of matching: • Group matching: It is also called frequency matching. It is done when a large stratum is used for study and a 1:1 ratio of cases and controls can be achieved. • Individual matching: It is also called matching by pairs. It can be done when the study is small and more controls can be selected for one case.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An epidemiologist determines to evaluate the strength of association between asbestos exposure and mesothelioma in a case-control study. Which of the following variables would he use for it?
mcqs.explanation: Odds ratio (OR), also known as cross-product ratio, is used to measure the strength of association between r isk factor (asbestos exposure) and outcome (mesothelioma) in case-control studies. A case-control study yields only odds ratio and not incidence or relative risk.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about the odds ratio?

options.b: It is obtained from case-control studies
options.d: It is a measure of strength of association

mcqs.explanation: An odds ratio (OR) of 1 indicates that there is no association or that the event is likely in both the groups.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A case-control study was done among 500 lung cancer patients and 400 controls. The study groups had 400 and 50 smokers respectively. Calculate the odds ratio.
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, the odds ratio (OR) is 28. The given data is represented as: Odds Ratio = ad/bc = (400 x 350) / (50 x 100) = (4 x 35)/5 = 4 x 7 = 28Diseas e + Disease - Exposur e + (a) 50 (b)106 Diseas e + Disease - Exposur e - (c) 350 (d)

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A research scholar is preparing to do a prospective cohort study in a hospital to evaluate the association of H. pylori with inflammatory bowel disease. Which of the following measures must she take, before starting the study?

options.a: Enrol all patients taking proton pump inhibitors
options.b: Enrol all patients on whom endoscopy was done
options.c: Exclude all patients diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease
options.d: Exclude all patients with positive urea breath test for H. pylori

mcqs.explanation: All patients diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) must be excluded from a prospective cohort study, as the study progresses from cause to effect. The study begins before the disease under study has occurred.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of t he following is not true about cohort study?

options.b: It is always a prospective study design
options.d: Outcome is not present at the start of study

mcqs.explanation: Although cohort studies are called prospective studies, there are subtypes of cohort studies that do not follow the prospective study design like historical (retrospective) cohort studies. Framingham Heart Study is one of the most famous long-term cardiovascular p rospective cohort studies.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Hawthorne effect is seen in which of the following studies?
mcqs.explanation: Hawthorne effect is seen in cohort studies. It refers to the phenomenon when study subjects change or alter their behaviour during the course of the study, which results in different outcomes and underestimation of risks.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the ratio of the incidence of the disease in the exposed to that of the non-exposed?
mcqs.explanation: The ratio of incidence of disease or death among exposed to that among the non-exposed is called relative risk (RR).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Calculate the risk ratio when the incidence of the disease in exposed is 30 and that in non-exposed is 5.
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, risk ratio or relative risk (RR) is 6. Here, the incidence of disease i n the exposed is 30 and that in the non-exposed is 5. Thus , RR = 30/5 = 6.107

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A cohort study was conducted among 10,000 smokers and 10,000 non-smokers. They were followed up over a period of 20 years. It was found that 100 of the smokers and 10 of the non-smokers developed oral squamous cell carcinoma. Calculate the relative risk.
mcqs.explanation: The relative risk in the given scenario is 10. Here, the incidence in exposed is 0.01 (100/10000). Incidence in non-exposed is 0.001 (10/10000). Relative Risk = Incidence in exposed/ Incidence in non-exposed = 0.01/0.001 = 10.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: While testing the deleterious h ealth hazards on a group of people after giving a new drug and a placebo, the following results were obtained as tabulated. Based on these results, which of the following is true?

options.a: Absolute risk reduction (ARR) is 1% and relative risk reduction (RRR) is 0.
options.b: Absolute risk reduction (ARR) is 10% and relative risk reduction (RRR) is 0.
options.c: Absolute risk reduction (ARR) is 1% and relative risk reduction (RRR) is
options.d: Absolute risk reduction (ARR) is 10% and relative risk redu ction (RRR) i s

mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, absolute risk reduction (ARR) is 1% and relative risk reduction (RRR) is 0.1. Let us reconstruct the design table in the following way: Relative risk (RR) is given as a/(a+b\ c/(c+d). RR = 1603/15225 \367 1804/15225 = 0.106/0.1 18 = 0.89 �o . 90. Relative risk reduction (RRR) = 1 – Relative risk. In this scenario, RRR = 1 – 0.9 = 0.1 or 10%. Incidence of a disease is the absolute risk of contracting it. Absolute risk rate of the group using new drug = a/(a+b) = 1603/15225 = 0.106 or 10.6% �o 11%. Absolute risk rate of the group using placebo = c/(c+d) = 1804/15225 = 0.118 or 11.8% �o 12%. Absolute risk reduction (ARR) is the difference in the absolute risk rates between the placebo and the drug. In this scenario, ARR = 12 % - 11% = 1%.Health hazard (+) Health hazard (-) Total New drug (a) (b) 15225 (a +b) Place bo 1804 (c) (d) 15225 (c+ d)

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The difference between the incidence of disease among exposed and incidence among non exposed is given by which of the following variables?
mcqs.explanation: The difference between the incidence of disease among exposed and incidence among non-exposed is given by attributable risk. Attributable risk is often expressed as a percentage.108

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A study conducted among smokers shows that 80% of the cases of lung cancer are due to cigarette smoking. Which of the following variables indicates this?
mcqs.explanation: Attributable risk indicates to what extent the disease under study can be attributed to the exposure. Here, cigarette smoking is attributed to be the cause of 80% of lung cancers in smokers.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A study found that the i ncidence of bladder carcinoma is 5 times higher in smokers than in non smokers. Calculate the attributable risk.
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, the attributable risk (AR) is 80%.Taking the incidence of disease in non-exposed as x, the incidence of disease in exposed would be 5x.109 Attributable risk (AR) would be given as [(5x - x)/5x] x 100 = 80%.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a population of 9000 people, 2100 are alcoholics. 70 alcoholics and 23 non-alcoholics developed cirrhosis. What is the attributable risk?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, the attributable risk (AR) is 90%. Number of people exposed (to alcohol) = 2100 Number of people not exposed (to alcohol) = 6900 Incidence of cirrhosis among exposed = 70/2100 (IExposed) Incidence of cirrhosis among non-exposed = 23/6900 (INon-exposed) Attributable risk (AR\ = [ ( IExposed - INon-exposed\ / IExposed ]*100 = [ (70/2100 - 23/6900) / (70/2100)] *100 = [ 9 / 10 ] *100 = Thus, the attri butable r isk (AR) is 90%.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the numerator in the formula for population-attributable risk?

options.a: Incidence among exposed minus incidence among non-exposed
options.b: Incidence among non-exposed minus incidence among exposed
options.c: Incidence in the total population minus incidence among non-exposed
options.d: Incidence in the total population minus incidence among exposed

mcqs.explanation: Incidence in the total population minus incidence among non-exposed is the numerator in population-attributable risk (PAR).Population attributable risk is obtained from cohort studies. It provides an estimate of the amount by which the disease could be reduced in that population if the suspected factor was eliminated or modified.110

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A study was done in the Indian population to correlate the deaths due to myocardial infarction and dietary practices. Wh at i s this type of study known as?
mcqs.explanation: This is an example of an ecological study. As the study was done in the Indian population, it can be inferred that population was taken as the unit of the study. The study was done to correlate the deaths and dietary practices, and hence ecological studies are also called correlational studies.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which among the following is the weakest study design to prove causation?
mcqs.explanation: Ecological studies take a population as a unit. They provide the weakest evidence for causality because of extrapolation to individuals from regional data. Randomized control trials (RCTs) p rovide the strongest design amongst the options given. Case-control and cohort studies have moderate ability to provide evidence for causality.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What kind of bias is implied by assigning group characteristics to people which they may not possess as individuals?
mcqs.explanation: An ecological fallacy results when characteristics of the group are assigned inappropriately to individuals.111

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following study designs is the best to prove causation?
mcqs.explanation: Randomized controlled trials (RCT) are the strongest and best study design to prove causation. They are the gold standard of clinical research. Case-control and cohort studies have a moderate ability to provide evidence for causality. Ecological studies or correlational studies are considered as the weakest study design in this aspect. The difference between analytical studies and randomised controlled trials is that in the former there is no randomisation becau se i t requires the participants to be divided into diseased and non -diseased. This can lead to a number of biases that are avoided in RCTs.117

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a clinical trial to evaluate a drug, randomisation was done before starting the trial. What is the purpose behind this?

options.a: The two groups will be similar in prognostic factors
options.b: The clinician has no control over the allocation of participants in each group
options.c: The clinician can predict in advance which treatment the s ubjects will receive
options.d: The sample may be referenced to a known population

mcqs.explanation: The main purpose behind randomisation is to eliminate selection bias. In an RCT, participants are randomly assigned to a study group or a control group. It is done only after obtaining consent. It removes both known and unknown confounding factors. The heart of a randomized controlled trial (RCT) is randomisation. This allows comparability between the study and the control population.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about randomised control trial?

options.a: Baseline characteristics are similar in both arms
options.b: Investigator's bias is minimized by double blinding
options.c: The sample size required depends upon the hypothesis
options.d: The dropouts from the trial are not included in the analysis

mcqs.explanation: The dropouts from an RCT are included in the final analysis. This type of analysis is called intention -to-treat (ITT) analysis. It ignores noncompliance, protocol change, withdrawal, cross-over, and anything that happens after randomization during analysis. The exclusion of dropouts may lead to the introduction of bias. Note: Per-protocol analysis is a comparison of treatment groups that include only those patients who completed the treatment originally allocated to them. Hence, comparability between the study and control group is limited an d randomisation is lost.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A researcher decided to use double-blinding in his trial evaluating two new therapies for cystic f ibrosis. W hat is the characteristic feature of this concept?

options.a: Study and control groups are blinded
options.c: Observer and group being observed are blinded
options.d: Group members and analyzer are blinded

mcqs.explanation: In double-blind trials, both the group members (study and control group) and the observers are not aware of the group allocation.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a clinical trial, what would be the best study design that ensures comparability between experimental and control groups?
mcqs.explanation: A cross-over study would be the best method to ensure comparability between the experimental and control group. In a cross over study design, patients are randomly assigned to the study and control group, and then after a period of time, their groups are switched. Here, each patient serves as his/her own control which a llows f or maximum comparability. In a concurrent parallel study design, comparisons are made between two randomly assigned groups and there is no switching of groups. This allows only for limited comparability between experimental and control groups. Quasi-experiments are studies that aim to evaluate interventions but that do not use randomization. The lack of randomisation is the major weakness of quasi trials. The comparability in a quasi trial is limited. A per-p rotocol a nalysis is a comparison of treatment groups that include only those patients who completed the treatment originally allocated. Hence, comparability is limited.118

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A new drug for multiple sclerosis is undergoing clinical trials where its therapeutic efficacy is being confirmed and adverse reactions are being monitored. Which o f the following phases is the drug most likely in?
mcqs.explanation: The confirmation of therapeutic efficacy and monitoring of adverse reactions of a new drug happens in phase III of the clinical trial. Purpose of phase III: • Confirmation of the effectiveness of the drug in patients with the target disease • Monitoring of adverse reactions Phase II involves therapeutic exploration which is the evaluation of the efficacy of the drug and dose-ranging (determination of the optimum tolerated dose).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In which of the following phases is the maximum drug failure rate seen?
mcqs.explanation: Maximum drug failure rates are seen in phase II followed by phase III of a clinical trial.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The maximum tolerable dose of a new drug for Alzheimer's disease is to be evaluated. In which of the following phases is this done?
mcqs.explanation: The maximum tolerated dose of a new drug is tested in phase I of a clinical trial. Phase I trials are usually performed on healthy volunteers to check the safety and pharmacokinetic properties of a drug. The participants in this phase do not gain any direct health benefits from taking part. They are generally paid a fee for their time, with the payments being regulated and not related to the risk involved.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A hypothesis stating that people who continue to smoke are at a higher risk of developing lung carcinoma than those who have quit is to be tested. Which of the following study designs would you choose for this purpose?
mcqs.explanation: To test the given hypothesis that smokers are at a higher risk of developing lung carcinoma than those who have quit, the study design chosen is a cessation experiment. The outcomes of termination of a habit or removal of an agent considered to be causally related to a disease can be evaluated in a cessation experiment. It is a type of RCT and preventive trial. If the outcome is a significant reduction in disease then the association of that habit or agent to the disease is strengthened. A trial of aetiological a gents is an experimental epidemiological study to confirm or refute an aetiological hypothesis. Clinical trials, for the most part, have been concerned with evaluating therapeutic agents, mainly drugs. An uncontrolled trial is an example of a non-randomised trial where there is no control group for comparison.119

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an example of a randomised controlled trial?

options.b: Before and after comparison s tudies

mcqs.explanation: Before and after comparison studies are a type of non-randomized trials.
