The overall objective of IDCF is to ensure high coverage of ORS and Zinc use rates in children with diarrhoea. It also complements awareness activities (including Swachh) for prevention and manag ement o f diarrhoea in under-five children.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: For a child with SAM, what s hould be the sodium content of his rehydration fluid?
mcqs.explanation: The sodium content of the rehydration solution to treat SAM is 45mmol/L.262 ReSoMal (rehydration solution for malnourished children) contains a lower amount of sodium (45mmol/L) and a higher amount of potassium (40 mmol/L ) than the standard WHO-ORS. ReSoMal is used in in-patient centers for the treatment of children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM). It is useful in correcting hypokalemia, and in lowering the risks of excess sodium and/or overhydration. Composition of ReSoMal and ORS:Component (mm ol/l) Standard OR S ReSo Mal Glucose (anhydro us) Sodium 45 Potassium 20 Chloride 70 Citrate 7 Magnesium - Zinc - 0.3 Copper - 0.04 Osmolality 245 300

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the average incubation period of typhoid fever?
mcqs.explanation: The average incubation period of typhoid is 10-14 days. However, it can vary from 3 days to 3 weeks depending on the dose of bacilli ingested.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a boys hostel, there has been an outbreak of typhoid. The hostel cook is identified as the carrier of the disease. Which is true among the following statements regarding her condition?

options.a: Gallbladder is usually not involved in carrier state
options.b: Chronic carriers are those who excrete the bacilli for more than a year
options.c: Tetracycline is the drug of choice for carriers
options.d: To treat th e c arrier state, treatment should be given for 4 weeks

mcqs.explanation: Chronic carriers of typhoid are those who excrete the bacilli for more than a year. Convalescent carriers excrete bacilli for 6-8 weeks and chronic carriers excrete for more than a year. The carrier rate in females is higher. Gallbladder and biliary tract are affected. To treat the carrier state, an intensive course of ampicillin or amoxicillin (4-6 g a d ay ) together with Probenecid (2 g/day) for 6 weeks is given. Cholecystectomy with concomitant ampicillin therapy is the most successful treatment for the carrier state.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In which of the following patients can the Ty21a vaccine be administered?

options.a: A 50-year-old HIV patient who is asymptomatic with CD4+ count 240/mm
options.b: A 42-year-old patient with fever and cough for 3 days
options.d: A 64-years-old alcoholic on colchicine therapy for acute gout

mcqs.explanation: 263 Ty21a vaccine can be administered in an HIV -positive asymptomatic patient as long as the CD4+ count is >200/ cubic mm. Ty21a is an oral vaccine for individuals \0345 years of age. It is given in 3 doses on the 1st, 3rd, and 5th day. Repeat every 3 years for endemic areas, and every year for traveling individuals. It is not recommended in: • Patients on antimitotic drugs and immunosuppressants • Acute febrile illness • Acute intestinal infestation Proguanil and antibacterial drugs s hould be stopped from 3 days before to 3 days after the vaccine .

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding dracunculiasis?

options.b: Niridazole p revents transmission of the disease.
options.c: The disease is limited to tropical and subtropical regions.
options.d: No animal reservoir has been proved.

mcqs.explanation: Niridazole does not prevent transmission of the disease. Dracunculiasis is treated by removing the worm by sequentially rolling them out over a small stick. Wet compresses may relieve discomfort. Occlusive dressings limit shedding of infectious larvae. Metronidazole and mebendazole are used to limit inflammation and facilitate worm removal. Dracunculiasis or Guinea-worm disease is amenable to eradication. The eradication strategy comprises the following elements : • Provision of safe drinking water. • Control of cyclops. • Health education regarding drinking boiled water. • Surveillance: Active search for new cases.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about hookworms?

options.a: Blood loss due to Necator americanus infection is more compared to Ancylostoma infection.
options.b: Malnutrition is a predisposing factor for this chronic disabling disease.
options.c: Chandler's index is used in epidemiological studies of hookworm.
options.d: Chronic blood loss in pregnant women may lead to abortions, stillbirth and low birth weight babies.

mcqs.explanation: The blood loss due to Ancylostoma (0.2 ml/day) is more compared to Necatur americanus (0.03ml/day) Malnutrition is a predisposing factor. The chronic disabling disease does not occur in individuals who are well-nourished and whose iron intake i s adequate. Chandler 's index is used to identify importance of hookworm infestation as a public health problem. It is calculated as average number of hookworm eggs/gram of stool. • <200: no significance • 200-250: the potential danger • 250-300: minor public health problem264 • >300: major public health problem Hookworm inection causes chronic blood loss and depletion of body's iron stores leading to iron deficiency anemia. This in pregnant women can lead to abortions, stillbirth and low birth weight babies.265

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which malarial parasite has the shortest incubation period?
mcqs.explanation: Plasmodium falciparum has the shortest incubation period of 12 days.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A patient from a hilly area was diagnosed with malaria. Which vector is most likely responsible for this?
mcqs.explanation: Anopheles fluviatilis is the vector for transmitting malaria in hilly areas, forests and forest fringes.Vector Area Anopheles stephensi Urban Anopheles culicifacies Rural Anopheles fluviatilis Hilly areas and forests

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Individuals with Duffy negative RBCs are resistant to:
mcqs.explanation: People with Duffy negative RBCs are resistant to P.vivax. Resistance to P.falciparum is seen in: • Individuals with sickle cell trait • Neonates, as fetal hemoglobin suppresses the development of P. falciparum

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which is the most sensitive index of recent transmission o f malaria?
mcqs.explanation: The infant parasite rate is regarded as the most sensitive index for recent transmission of malaria in a locality. It is defined as the % of infants showing malarial parasites in their blood films. The transmission of malaria is considered absent if the infant parasite r ate is zero for 3 consecutive years in a locality (even though the Anopheline vectors responsible for the previous transmission may remain).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a town with a population of 1,00,000, a total of 50,000 slides were examined for malaria. Among these, 100 cases of malaria were confirmed. What is the annual parasite incidence of this town?
mcqs.explanation: The annual parasite incidence of this town (API) is 1. API = Confirmed cases in a year ----------------------------------- x 1000273 Population under surveillance In this scenario, API = 100 x 1000/100000 = 1 API is based on the number of slide-confirmed cases that are found through active and passive surveillance. It is a measure of malaria incidence in a community and helps in determining the burden of the disease. Areas with API \034 2 / 1000 population are classified as high-risk areas and are eligible for vector control. Note: The number of slides examined is used to determine the annual blood examination r ate ( ABER).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which parameter is used to measure the operational efficiency of the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme?

options.d: Annual blood exam ination r ate

mcqs.explanation: The annual blood examination rate (ABER) is used to measure the operational efficiency of the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 44-year-old woman from Assam presented with fever and chills recurring every 48 hours. On examination, she was conscious, oriented, and febrile. CBC, LFT, and RFT were normal. Peripheral smear revealed the following. What is the drug of choice?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario and peripheral smear showing crescent-shaped gametocytes are suggestive of uncomplicated falciparum malaria. As this woman is from a North-Eastern state, the drug regimen of choice is ACT-AL (artemisinin combination therapy): • Artemether (20mg) • Lumefantrine (120mg) This regimen is followed in the North-Eastern states of India due to documented resistance to sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine in these areas. ACT-AL is contraindicated in: • 1st trimester of pregnancy • Children < 5 kg

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 23-year-old pregnant woman at 11 weeks of gestation was diagnosed with falciparum malaria. What is the drug of choice?
mcqs.explanation: Quinine is the drug of choice for falciparum malaria during 1st trimester of pregnancy. The treatment of falciparum malaria during pregnancy is as follows: • 1st trimester - quinine • 2nd and 3rd trimester - ACT-AL in North-Eastern states and ACT-SP in other st ates

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following patients with malaria can be treated with primaquine?

options.a: A 24-year-old pregnant woman at 30 weeks of gestation
options.b: A 10-year-old boy diagnosed w ith G6PD deficiency
options.c: A 40-year-old woman recently treated for a flare-up of SLE
options.d: A 60-year-old man who had a myocardial infarction 4 months ago

mcqs.explanation: Cardiac disease is not a contraindication for the use of primaquine. It is contraindicated in:274 • Infants • Pregnant and lactating women • Patients with G6PD deficiency • Patients at risk of developing granulocytopenia: • Systemic diseases including active RA and SLE • Drugs that cause hemolysis or bone marrow depression

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the dose of mefloquine given for chemoprophylaxis of malaria?
mcqs.explanation: Mefloquine 250 mg weekly is given for chemoprophylaxis against malaria in adults. It should be administered 2-3 weeks before travelling. Chemoprophylaxis is recommended for travellers from non-endemic areas and as a short term measure for soldiers, p olice and labour forces serving in highly endemic areas. It should be complemented by personal protection and vector control. The following drugs are used for malaria chemoprophylaxis: • Chloroquine - 300 mg/week • Proguanil - 200mg/day • Mefloquine - 250mg/week • Doxycycline - 100mg/day Mefloquine is contraindicated in cases with a history of convulsions, neuropsychiatric problems and cardiac conditions.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the most important strategy for the control of malaria in endemic areas?
mcqs.explanation: Vector control is the most important strategy to control malaria in endemic areas. Proper measures should be taken to kill both adult mosquitoes and larvae.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following was a component of the Roll back malaria programme?

options.c: Development of larvivorous fish for e radication of larvae

mcqs.explanation: Ensuring proper and expanded use of insecticide-treated mosquito nets was a component of the Roll Back Malaria (RBM) programme. The other components of the RBM initiative included: • Strengthening the health system to ensure better delivery of health care • Ensuring adequate access to basic health care and training of health workers • Encouraging the development of m ore effective and new anti-malaria drugs275

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which sequence of infection poses the highest risk of dengue hemorrhagic fever?
mcqs.explanation: The DENV-1 --> DENV-2 sequence of infection is associated with the highest risk of dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF). Multiple infections with different serotypes of the dengue virus lead to severe forms of dengue such as DHF/DSS. The first infection probably sensitizes the patient, while the second infection with a different serotype appears to produce immunological catastrophe. • DENV-1 --> DENV-2 - 500-fold risk (compared to primary infection alone) • DENV- 3 --> D ENV-2 - 150-fold risk • DENV -4 --> DENV-2 - 50-fold risk

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the extrinsic incubation period of the dengue virus?
mcqs.explanation: The extrinsic incubation period of the dengue virus is 8-10 days. This refers to the period necessary for the development of the disease agent in the arthropod host. Aedes mosquitoes become infective when they feed on infected patients from 1 day before onset of illness to the 5th day (viremia stage) of illness. After 8-10 days of extrinsic incubation of the virus in a mosquito, Aedes becomes infective and c an t ransmit the infection. Higher temperature results in shortening of the extrinsic incubation period, allowing mosquitoes to remain infectious for a longer duration.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the cornerstone of treatment for a patient of dengue with warning signs?
mcqs.explanation: The primary modality of treatment in patients with dengue with warning signs is IV fluids. The main pathology in dengue is plasma leakage resulting in intravascular volume depletion and thereby shock. Warning signs in dengue include: • Abdominal pain or tenderness • Persistent vomiting • Clinical fluid a ccumulation (ascites, pleural effusion) • Mucosal bleeding • Lethargy or restlessness • Hepatomegaly >2 cm • Increase in hematocrit concurrent with a rapid decrease in platelet count Inpatient management is advised to all patients of dengue with warning signs. The management of dengue includes: • IV crystalloids - mainstay of treatment276 • Platelet transfusion - severe thrombocytopenia (<10,000/mm3) and active bleeding FFP and cryoglobulins are not the preferred for treatment in dengue.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In patients with dengue fever, platelets should be transfused if the platelet count falls below which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: Prophylactic platelet transfusion in dengue is to be initiated when the platelet count is <10,000/cu.mm. Indications for platelet transfusion in dengue are as follows: • Platelet count <10,000/cu.mm • Prolonged shock with coagulopathy • Systemic massive bleeding

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: When can a patient with dengue hemorrhagic shock b e discharged?

options.a: No episode of fever for more than 24 hours with paracetamol

mcqs.explanation: A patient with dengue hemorrhagic shock can be discharged after the return of appetite. Criteria for the discharge of patients recovering from dengue: • Absence of fever for at least 24 hours without the use of antipyretic drugs • Platelet count >50,000/cu.mm • Return of appetite • Adequate urine output • Visible clinical improvement • Minimum of 2-3 days after recovery from shock • No respiratory distress from pleural effusion or ascites

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a WHO-approved dengue vaccine for individuals seropositive for dengue virus?
mcqs.explanation: Dengvaxia is a WHO-approved vaccine for individuals seropositive for dengue virus. It is currently licensed in 20 countries. A pre-vaccination screening strategy must be adopted so that only dengue-seropositive individuals are vaccinated. It is indicated for individuals between 9 to 16 years. It is given in 3 doses, months apart. Booster doses are not required. However, it carries an increased risk of severe dengue in those who experience their first natural dengue infection after vaccination (seronegative individuals). Note: T V0 03, a live, attenuated, tetravalent dengue vaccine is currently in Phase-3 trials. It has shown efficacy in promoting immunity in both seropositive and seronegative individuals between 2-59 years of age.277

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The prepatent period in lymphatic filariasis is the time interval between:

options.a: Invasion of infective larvae and blockage of lymphatics
options.b: Inoculation of infective larvae and detection of microfilaria
options.c: Ingestion of microfilaria and development of third stage larva
options.d: Inoculation of infective larvae and maturation into adu lt w orm

mcqs.explanation: The prepatent period in lymphatic filariasis is the time interval between inoculation of the infective larvae and the first appearance of detectable microfilaria. The clinical incubation period is the time interval from the invasion of infective larvae and the development of clinical manifestations. It is usually 8-16 months.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 44-year-old man presented with high-grade fever, chills, and pain in his groin area. Examination revealed reddish streaks over his lower limbs and bilateral non-pitting edema to the level of the knee. Swelling and tenderness in his scrotum was also noted. To diagnose the condition, when will you draw blood from the patient?
mcqs.explanation: This patient has features of lymphangitis, lymphedema, and epididymo-orchitis, which are suggestive of acute filariasis. Blood must be drawn b etween 10 pm to 2 am. This is because the maximum density of microfilaria are present in the peripheral blood at this time.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which is the most sensitive method to detect low-density microfilaremia in blood?
mcqs.explanation: The most sensitive method to detect low-density microfilaremia in the blood is by membrane filter concentration. The thick film is the most commonly used method for epidemiological assessment. The DEC provocative test is used to induce microfilaria to appear in the blood in the daytime.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the dose of diethylcarbamazine for the treatment of Bancroftian filariasis?
mcqs.explanation: The dose of diethylcarbamazine (DEC) for treatment of Bancroftian filariasis is 6 mg/kg/day orally for 12 days. Medicated common salt with 1-4g DEC/kg is a special form of mass treatment, particularly in endemic areas. By this method, very low doses of DEC are given over a long period of time.278

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A man is referred for fever and agitation for the past 4 days. Examination reveals a disoriented man who is unable to swallow water due to involuntary inspiratory muscle spasms of the pharynx. He had been bitten by a dog 3 months ago but was not treated. What genus does the causative organism of this condition belong to?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario with hydrophobia and a history of an untreated dog bite is highly suggestive of rabies. The causative virus belongs to the genus Lyssavirus. Rabies virus is an RNA virus that belongs to the family Rhabdoviridae. This family has 3 genera: • Lyssavirus • Vesiculovirus • Ephemerovirus

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about the fixed virus of rabies?

options.c: Does not multiply in extra neural tissues

mcqs.explanation: The fixed virus has a short incubation period. There are 2 types of rabies viruses:Fixed virus Street virus Isolated after several intracer ebral passages in rabbits Isolated from naturally occur ring cases of rabies Short, fixed , and reproducibl e incubation period of 6 to 7 days The incubation period is long and highly variable between 1 to 12 weeks Does not form Negri bodies o r multiply in extraneural tiss ues Forms Negri bodies and mult iplies in extraneural tissues Used in the preparation of liv e-attenuatedanti -rabies vacci ne It is the primary cause of rabi es disease

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not lead to the transmission of rabies to humans?

options.a: Nibbling by an infected animal on abraded skin
options.c: Direct contact of infected saliva with the mucosa
options.d: Ingestion of raw meat of infected animal

mcqs.explanation: Ingestion of the raw meat of the infected animal does not lead to the transmission of rabies.285 Mammals like dogs and bats are important animal sources. The important modes of transmission of rabies are as follows: • Scratches or deep bites • Exposure of infected saliva to intact mucosa or fresh skin wounds Human–to–human transmission through bites has never been confirmed.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You have witnessed your neighbor being bitten by a rabid dog. You should advise him to wash the wound with soap and water for a minimum of:
mcqs.explanation: Following dog bites, the bite wound should be washed with soap under running tap water for 15 minutes. Local treatment of the bite wound is essential for the prevention of rabies and can reduce the i nfection rate by up to 80%. The following steps must be followed: • Cleansing: Washing under running water with soap or irrigation with a catheter in case of deep wounds • Chemical agent: Alcohol or tincture /0.01% aqueous solution of iodine or povidone-iodine is effective for inactivation of residual virus • Suturing: Must be done only following 24-48 hours if necessary, under the cover of rabies immunoglobulin locally and minimal stitches • Antibiotics and anti-tetanus m easures when indicated

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A worker at a veterinary hospital has just received the 1st dose of rabies vaccine as a pre-exposure prophylactic measure. When should he return for the remaining doses?
mcqs.explanation: Pre-exposure prophylaxis for rabies consists of 3 doses to be given on days 0, 7, and 21 or 28. They are given intramuscularly or intradermally in the deltoid area of the arm. High-risk groups like laboratory staff, wildlife wardens, veterinarians, animal handlers, and travelers to endemic regions are candidates for pre-exposure prophylaxis.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 7-year-old boy was bitten by a suspected rabid dog . On examination, there are minor scratches and abrasions without bleeding. Which of the following is true about the category and management of t he wound?

options.a: Category II - Local treatment of wound with povidone and follow up
options.b: Category III - Local treatment of wound and give ARV and antibiotics
options.c: Category II - Local treatment of wound and give ARV
options.d: Category III - Give ARV and anti-rabies immunoglobulin

mcqs.explanation: Minor scratches and abrasions without bleeding are classified under category II wounds. Category II wounds are managed by immediate local treatment of wound and vaccination (ARV ). Antibiotics are not required in case of minor scratches and abrasions.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A public health worker was brought with multiple transdermal dog bites. He tells you that he had received pre-exposure prophylaxis 6 months ago. What is the next best step in management?

options.b: Only R IG should be given
options.c: Wound washing and ARV with half dose of RIG
options.d: Wound treatment and ARV ; RIG is not required

mcqs.explanation: This given clinical scenario of a patient with multiple transdermal dog bites would be categorised under category III. As the patient received pre-exposure prophylaxis 6 months ago, his line of286 management includes the following: • Wound treatment with soap and running water for 15 minutes and application of antiseptic • Anti-rabies vaccine 2 doses on day 0 and day 3, with either intradermal vaccine(0.1ml, 1 site) or intramuscular vaccine(1 vial, 1site). There is no requirement for Rabies Immunoglobulin (RIG), if previous pre-exposure prophylaxis or post exposure prophylaxis documentation is available. If documentation of PEP or PrEP is unavailable, patient s hould be treated as fresh case and given full PEP.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An\037 8-year-old child was brought with an unprovoked dog bite. Which of the following measures should be taken?

options.a: Withhold the vaccine and observe the dog for 10 days
options.b: Give half the dose of the vaccine

mcqs.explanation: This child should be given immediate post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) by administering a cell culture-derived vaccine to reduce the chances of getting rabies.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old boy had received a full course rabies vaccine taken in December 2018. His pet dog which has been fully vaccinated now (November 2019) bit him on the toe. Bleeding was present at the site of the bite. What woul d be the line of treatment?
mcqs.explanation: This boy should receive 2 doses of vaccine on days 0 & 3 as he has received a prior course of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) > 3 months ago. Management of a new dog bite in a previously immunized individual with either pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) or post-exposure p rophylaxis (PEP) is as follows: • Category I: Wound treatment only • Category II/ III: • Wound treatment with soap and running water for 15 min and apply antiseptic • Receive Anti-rabies vaccine (ARV ) 2 doses ID (0.1 ml, 1 site)/ 2 doses IM (1 VIAL, 1 site) on days 0 and 3. *Note: In developing countries like India, the vaccination status of animals alone, doesn't play a significant role in determining the initiation of prophylaxis in humans.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the incubation period of yellow fever?
mcqs.explanation: The incubation period of yellow fever is 3–6 days.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: According to the International Health Regulations, an Aedes aegypti index of which of the following must be maintained to achieve zero risk of spread of yellow fever?
mcqs.explanation: The Aedes aegypti index should be < 1% in endemic areas to achieve zero risk of spread of yellow fever. The Aedes aegypti index is a type of house index. It refers to the percentage of houses and premises in a limited well-defined area with actual breeding of Aedes aegypti larvae.287

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A woman is planning a trip to Morocco, which is endemic for yellow fever. As per travel regulations, she receives the yellow fever vaccine. After how many days following vaccination is she eligible to travel?
mcqs.explanation: This woman is eligible to travel to the endemic area 10 days after being vaccinated for yellow fever. This period is required for the majority of vaccine recipients to develop immunity. The 17D vaccine for yellow fever is given subcutaneously. Unvaccinated people are required to remain quarantined for 6 days (maximum period of incubation).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the yellow fever reference center in India?
mcqs.explanation: The reference centers for yellow fever in India are as follows: • Central Research Institute, Kasauli • National Institute of Virology, P une

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An outbreak of Kyasanur forest disease occurred among a g roup of forest officers in Karnataka . Which of the following vectors should be targeted to prevent the further spread of the disease?
mcqs.explanation: Kyasanur forest disease (KFD) is transmitted by the bite of infective hard ticks of Haemaphysalis species. Hence, control of ticks must be done to prevent spread of the disease. KFD is a hemorrhagic febrile disease caused by a flavivirus. Man is an incidental dead-end host in the life cycle of the vector (hard tick). Small mammals like rodents and squirrels are the reservoirs while monkeys serve as the amplifier hosts. KFD is endemic in 4 districts of Karnataka ( Shimoga, N orth Kannada, South Kannada, Chikmagalur). The incubation period is between 3 to 8 days. The disease presents with sudden onset of fever, headache, myalgia. In severe cases, gastrointestinal disturbances and hemorrhages from the nose, gums, stomach, and intestine may occur. The case fatality rate is 5 to 10%.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms follow a bird-arthropod-human transmission route?
mcqs.explanation: Japanese encephalitis follows bird-arthropod-human transmission. JE virus infects several extra-human hosts, e.g., pigs and birds (like pond herons). T he basic cycles of transmission are: (a)Pig \037 Mosquito \037 Pig (b) Bird \037 Mosquito \037 Bird Humans are incidental "dead-end" hosts and are infected by the bite of infected Culex mosquitoes.288

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which following is false about Japanese encephalitis?

options.a: Man is the incidental dead-end host
options.b: Culicines act as vectors for this condition
options.d: It is caused by a group B arbovirus

mcqs.explanation: The incubation period of Japanese encephalitis (JE) in man following a mosquito bite is 5-15 days. JE is mosquito-borne encephalitis caused by a group B arbovirus (Flavivirus). It is transmitted by Culex (culicine) mosquitoes mainly C.tritaeniorhynchus and C.vishnui. Ardeid birds (herons) are the reservoirs while pigs are the amplifier hosts. Man is an incidental dead-end host. Man-to-man transmission has not been recorded.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about Japanese encephalitis?

options.a: SA-14-14-2 strain vaccine is commonly used
options.b: Diagnosis is confirmed by CSF culture
options.c: Patients usually recover without any sequelae
options.d: Subclinical infec tion d oes not occur

mcqs.explanation: SA-14-14-2 strain vaccine is used for the prevention of Japanese encephalitis (JE). Japanese encephalitis (JE) is mosquito-borne encephalitis caused by a group B arbovirus (Flavivirus) and transmitted by Culex mosquitoes. Most individuals develop subclinical infection. The course of disease in man divided into 3 stages: • Prodromal stage - fever, headache, gastrointestinal disturbances, lethargy, and malaise • Acute encephalitic stage - high-grade fever, nuchal rigidity, convulsions, signs of raised i ntracranial pressure, paralysis, altered sensorium • Late-stage and sequelae - neurological or psychiatric sequelae seen in up to 50% of survivors Diagnosis is serological, using blood or CSF samples. The virus rarely grows in culture. The case fatality rate varies between 20-40%. There are 3 types of JE vaccines available: • Nakayama or Beijing strain - purified inactivated vaccine • Beijing P-3 strain - inactivated vaccine • SA-14-14-2 - live attenuated vaccine N ote : Killed JE vaccines (Inactivated SA 14-14-2 cell culture-derived and inactivated Vero cell culture-derived) are gradually replacing live attenuated vaccines. According to the national immunisation schedule, both live attenuated, killed-inactivated vaccines are now used for vaccination against the JE virus.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The life cycle of which of the following is depicted in the image below?
mcqs.explanation: The given image depicts the life cycle of the Nipah virus. Nipah virus is an RNA virus that belongs to the family Paramyxoviridae, genus Henipavirus . I t is a zoonotic virus that shows both animal-to-human (bats, pigs) and human-to-human transmission. The natural hosts are fruit bats of the Pteropodidae family. The clinical manifestations include asymptomatic subclinical infection, acute respiratory infection, and fatal encephalitis. There is no treatment or vaccine available for either people or animals. The primary treatment for humans is supportive care. Nipah virus is on the WHO list of Blueprint priority diseases.289

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following are transmitted biologically by invertebrate vectors?
mcqs.explanation: Metazoonoses are a type of zoonoses where the infective agents are transmitted by invertebrate vectors. They multiply and develop within the invertebrates (extrinsic incubation period) before transmission to a vertebrate host. A zoonosis is any disease or infection that is naturally transmissible from vertebrate animals to humans. They can be classified based on their reservoir hosts into: • Anthropozoonoses - transmitted from lower vertebrates to man • Zooanthroponoses - t ransmitted from man to lower vertebrates • Amphixenoses - may be transmitted in either direction They can also be classified based on the life cycle of the infecting agent:Category Mode Example Direct zoonos es Direct contact, fomites ,mech anical vectorNo development al or propagative changes dur ing transmission Rabies,brucellosis , trichinosi s Cyclo -zoonos es Require> 1 vertebrate hostto complete the developmental cycle Humantaeniasis,Echinococco sis, Pentastomid infections Meta -zoonose s Transmitted byinvertebrate v ectorsInfective agentdevelops and multiplieswithin the inv ertebrate (extrinsic incubatio n period ) after which it is tra nsmitted to another vertebrat e host Arboviral infections , plaguea ndschistosomiasis Sapro-zoonos es Has both avertebrate hostan d anon-animal(food, soil, pla nts) developmental site or res ervoir Various forms oflarva migran sandmycoses

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Multiple members of the same community presented with sudden-onset fever, chills, and painful inguinal swellings as shown below. Further questioning leads to the identification of a rat infestation in the locality. Which of the following is the likely source of transmission of this disease?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario and image showing buboes are suggestive of bubonic plague. It is transmitted by the bite of the infected rat flea, Xenopsylla cheopis. Rodents, including rats, are the reservoirs of infection. On the other hand, the pneumonic plague spreads from man to man by droplet infection.295

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following indices is the best determinant of a potential plague outbreak?
mcqs.explanation: Cheopis index is the best determinant of potential plague outbreaks. If this index is > 1, it indicates there is a high likelihood of an outbreak.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: All of the following are causes of different types of typhus except:
mcqs.explanation: R.rickettsii causes Rocky Mountain spotted fever. It is a type of spotted fever, not typhus. *Note:- Orientia tsutsugamushi was previously known as Rickettsia tsutsugamushi.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following rickettsial diseases is correctly matched with their respective vectors?
mcqs.explanation: Endemic typhus is caused by the bite of an infective flea. This condition, also called murine typhus or flea-borne typhus, is caused by Rickettsia t yphi. Rats serve as reservoirs. The incubation period is 1–2 weeks. The Weil Felix reaction is positive in 2nd week. The drug of choice is tetracycline. Rodent control is most important and is best done by BHC and malathion.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 38-year-old woman is being evaluated for fever and rash. All of the following can be included in the differential except:
mcqs.explanation: Rashes and local lesions are not a feature of Q-fever. It is caused by Coxiella burnetii. The mode of transmission is the inhalation of infected dust, entry through abrasions, or ingestion of contaminated milk. Rarely, ticks can be involved in transmission. T he incubation period is 2 to 3 weeks. The drug of choice is prolonged treatment with doxycycline. Pasteurization is advised to inactivate the causative agent.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about scrub typhus?

options.b: Adult mite feeds on vertebral host

mcqs.explanation: Both adult and nymphal stages of the mite are free-living in nature. They do not feed on the vertebral host. Scrub typhus is the most widespread rickettsial disease. It is caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi (previously known as Rickettsia tsutsugamushi) and transmitted by the bite of trombiculid mite. The i ncubation p eriod is 10-12 days. It presents with a typical eschar at the bite site. It is diagnosed by the Weil Felix reaction, which is strongly positive with proteus strain OXK. It is treated by tetracyclines.296

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following are the causative agent and vector of epidemic typhus respectively?
mcqs.explanation: The causative agent of epidemic typhus is Rickettsia prowazekii and the vector is a louse. The incubation period is 10 to 14 days. Brill-Zinsser disease refers to the recurrent form of epidemic typhus.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A patient presents with fever for 1 week, with abdominal distension, loss o f appetite, and lymphadenopathy . There is a poor response to antibiotics and antimalarials. The Widal test is negative but rk39 is positive. Which drug can be used in the treatment of this patient?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario is suggestive of visceral leishmaniasis. This patient should be managed with liposomal amphotericin B. This condition causes fever with rigor and chills associated with splenomegaly and hepatomegaly. Though lymphadenopathy is common in most endemic r egions, it is rare in India. It is diagnosed by ELISA, indirect immunofluorescent antibody test (IFAT), and rk39 which detects antibodies to Leishmania donovani. The treatment is as follows: • In most endemic regions: • Drug of choice - pentavalent antimonial (sodium stibogluconate or meglumine antimoniate) • If it fails or is unavailable - amphotericin B • In India and Mediterranian countries, the drug of choice is liposomal AmB. • Other drugs - paromomycin and miltefosine Option B: Fluconazole is an antifungal and is not useful in visceral leishmaniasis Option C: Linezolid is used in the treatment of MRSA and related infections. Option D: Bedaquiline is a newer anti-TB drug used in MDR-TB.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about Leishmania?

options.b: Extrinsic incubation period of kala-azar is 4 to 25 days
options.d: Post kala-azar dermal le ishmaniasis i s caused by L. donovani

mcqs.explanation: Leishmania is an intracellular parasite in the macrophages. The vector is Phlebotomus (sandfly). Man is the reservoir in the Indian kala-azar. The incubation period is 10 days to 2 years, whereas the extrinsic incubation period is 4 to 25 days. T he following conditions are caused by Leishmania: • Visceral leishmaniasis or kala-azar – L . donovani • Cutaneous leishmaniasis or oriental sore – L. tropica • Mucocutaneous leishmaniasis - L. braziliensis • Post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis - L. donovani297 The image below is a microscopic image of the LD body.According to the NVBDCP, the management is as follows: • First-line - single-dose liposomal amphotericin B (10 mg/kg IV infusion) • Alternate - paromomycin + miltefosine for 10 days Monotherapy with antimonials (sodium stibogluconate) is no longer recommended due to resistance and toxicity. Synthetic pyrethroid is used for indoor residual spraying in all the endemic areas.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Kala-Azar is endemic in all these areas except:
mcqs.explanation: Kala-Azar is not endemic in Assam. It is endemic in the following states in 54 districts: • Uttar P radesh • West Bengal • Bihar • Jharkhand

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In patients with vagabond disease, which of the following is implicated?
mcqs.explanation: Vagabond's disease or pediculosis corporis is caused by the body louse. The following image shows the body louse.298

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: When is World AIDS day observed?
mcqs.explanation: The World AIDS Day is observed on December 1st. The theme for 2021 is 'Ending the HIV epidemic: Equitable Access, Everyone's Voice'. Option A: The World Tuberculosis Day is on March 24. Option B: The World Cancer Day is on February 4. Option D: The World Malaria Day is on April 25.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What are the most common modes of transmission of HIV in India in descending order?
mcqs.explanation: The most common mode of transmission of HIV in India is heterosexual transmission, followed by transplacental and homosexual contact, respectively. The common modes of transmission of HIV are: • Heterosexual (83.7%) • I njecting drug users (5.6%) • Transplacental transmission (3.8 %) • Homosexual (2.5%) • Blood and blood products (0.8%) • Unknown (3.6%)309 The highest risk of transmission is seen in homosexuals due to the increased risk of abrasions during anal sex.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Health care workers will require post-exposure prophylaxis after exposure to which of the following body fluids of a n H IV patient?
mcqs.explanation: Health care workers exposed to the menstrual blood of an HIV -positive patient will require post-exposure prophylaxis. The risk of transmission of HIV during vaginal intercourse is higher when the woman is menstruating. Tears, non-blood-stained saliva, urine, and sweat do not pose a significant risk. Exposure to these fluids does not require post-exposure prophylaxis.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: As per WHO staging of HIV , which of the following HIV -positive patients cannot be classified as stage IV ?

options.a: A 29-year-old man diagnosed with cerebral toxoplasmosis
options.b: A 56-year-old woman with significant weight loss and muscle wasting
options.c: A 43-year-old lady being treated for Pneumocystis pneumonia

mcqs.explanation: Oral candidiasis is seen in stage 3, not stage 4 of HIV . The following conditions are included in the WHO stage IV of HIV : • HIV wasting syndrome (Slim disease) • HIV encephalopathy • HIV -associated nephropathy or cardiomyopathy • Infections: • Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia (previously known as Pneumocystis carinii) • Chronic herpes simplex infection, cytomegalovirus disease • Oesophageal/ tracheal candidiasis • Extrapulmonary TB or disseminated M. a vium infection • CNS toxoplasmosis • Extrapulmonary cryptococcosis • Chronic cryptosporidiosis or isosporiasis • Disseminated fungal infections (histoplasmosis, coccidioidomycosis) • Recurrent severe bacterial pneumonia or septicemia • Atypical disseminated leishmaniasis • Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy • Neoplasms: • Kaposi sarcoma • Lymphoma (cerebral or B cell non-Hodgkin) • Invasive cervical carcinoma310

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 45-year man with a high-risk sexual history now presents with prolonged fever for the past 1.5 months. On examination, the following finding is noted. Which one of the following additional features is required to diagnose this patient with AIDS?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario is suspicious for HIV infection. As per the WHO definition, the presence of chronic diarrhea > 1 month is needed to diagnose this patient with AIDS. The WHO clinical definition is used for AIDS surveillance in the clinical setting. Patients > years of age are said to have AIDS if they have at least 2 major and 1 minor signs, provided other clinically similar conditions are be ruled out. Major signs: • Weight loss \034 10% of body weight • Chronic diarrhea > 1 m onth • Prolonged fever for > 1 month (intermittent or constant) Minor signs: • A persistent cough > 1 month • Generalized pruritic dermatitis • History of herpes zoster • Oropharyngeal candidiasis • Chronic progressive or disseminated herpes simplex infection • Generalized lymphadenopathy For surveillance purposes, the presence of either of the following is also considered sufficient to diagnose AIDS: • Generalized Kaposi's sarcoma • Cryptococc al m eningitis

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect regarding the epidemiology of HIV ?

options.a: HIV infected infants and children do not progress rapidly to AIDS
options.b: Seminal secretions are more infectious than vaginal secretion
options.c: People are infectious during the window period
options.d: HIV prevalence has not exceeded 5% in any subpopulation

mcqs.explanation: Infants and children infected with HIV progress rapidly to AIDS. Semen is more infectious than vaginal or cervical fluids as it has a higher concentration of HIV . HIV -infected patients are highly infectious during: • Window period (very early stages before antibody production) • Advanced stages of infection (due to higher levels of viremia) HIV prevalence has consistently remained < 5% in all defined subpopulations.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In individuals exposed to HIV , within how many hours should prophylaxis be initiated?
mcqs.explanation: Post-exposure prophylaxis for HIV should ideally be initiated within 72 hours. It is recommended that it be started as even as early as < 2 hours.311

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A nurse sustained a needle stick injury while sampling the blood of a patient who is HIV -positive. Which of the following is incorrect?

options.a: Washing hands with soap and water
options.c: Measure baseline viral markers of health care worker immediately

mcqs.explanation: Triple therapy (tenofovir 300mg + lamivudine 300mg + dolutegravir 50mg) is recommended for HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), not monotherapy. Steps to be undertaken after a needlestick injury are: • Wash the wound and skin with water and soap. Do not scrub and avoid antiseptics. • Assess exposed individual: • Check baseline viral markers • Monitor for acute seroconversion illness within 3-6 weeks after exposure • If testing is positive, refer to ART center • Assess exposure source and determine the risk of transmission • Counseling and support • Initiate PEP at the earliest - preferably < 2 hours and ideally < 72 hours • 28-day prescription with drug information • HIV test at 3 months after exposure

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A resident doctor sustained a needlestick i njury while sampling blood of a patient who is HIV positive . A decision is taken to offer him post-exposure prophylaxis. Which one of the following would be the best recommendation?
mcqs.explanation: Triple therapy with tenofovir 300mg, lamivudine 300mg, and dolutegravir 50mg for 4 weeks is recommended for HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). Steps to be undertaken after a needlestick injury are: • Wash the wound and skin with water a nd soap. Do not scrub and avoid antiseptics. • Assess exposed individual: • Check baseline viral markers • Monitor for acute seroconversion illness within 3-6 weeks after exposure • If testing is positive, refer to ART center • Assess exposure source and determine the risk of transmission • Counseling and support • Initiate PEP at the earliest - preferably < 2 hours and ideally < 72 hours • 28-day prescription with drug information • HIV test at 3 months after expo sure312

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following HIV -infected patients would you start on cotrimoxazole prophylaxis?

options.a: A 24-year-old pregnant woman with WHO stage 2 disease.
options.b: A 47-year-old man in a malaria-endemic area with WHO stage 1 disease
options.c: A 2-week-old HIV -exposed infant who is being exclusively breastfed
options.d: A 7-year-old girl with a CD4 count of 400 cells/cubic mm

mcqs.explanation: All HIV infected adults and children in malaria-endemic areas should be given cotrimoxazole prophylaxis regardless of CD4 count or WHO clinical stage. Cotrimoxazole is also indicated in areas with a low prevalence of malaria as shown below:Age group Indication When to discontinue HIV -exposed infants > 4-6 w eeks of age All infants After HIV infection has been ruled out Children < 5 years All children At 5 years in areas with low p revalence of malaria (In high prevalence areas, continue til l adulthood ) Children > 5 years CD4 count <350 and/or WH O stage 3/4 When CD4 > 350 and they ha ve been on ART > 6 months Adults and pregnant women CD4 count <350 and/or WH O stage 3/4 When CD4 count is rising an d viral load is decreasing HIV and TB coinfection All patients —

mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man with HIV is being screened for symptoms of TB. He reports no cough, fever, night sweats, or weight loss. What is the next step in management?

options.a: Start 5 mg/kg/day Isoniazid daily for 9 months
options.b: Prophylaxis does not need to be started
options.d: Start weekly dose of rifapentine + isoniazid for 3 months

mcqs.explanation: The next step in management in this patient is to provide tuberculosis preventive therapy (TPT) with rifapentine+ isoniazid weekly for 3 months. According to the NTEP guidelines, TPT is indicated for the following groups: IGRA - interferon-gamma release assay; TST - tuberculin skin test; ATT - antituberculous therapy TPT is contraindicated under the following conditions: • Active TB • Active hepatitis • Peripheral neuropathy • Regular and heavy alcohol consumptionRisk group Criteria People living with HIV Negative 4 symptom test - sta rt TPT after ruling out TBPat ients with active TB - start T PT after completion of the A TT regimen Household contacts (HHC) of pulmonary TB patients < 5 years Start TPT after ruling out acti ve TB313 Risk group Criteria Household contacts of pulmo nary TB patients \034 5 yearsOt her risk groups :Children/adul ts on immunosuppressive the rapyPatients on anti-TNF tre atmentPatients on dialysis or post -transplantationPatients with silicosis First rule out active TBStart TPT ifIGRA or TSTispositive with a normal chest x-rayTarget Population Treatment option People living with HIV (adult s and children > 2 years)HH C of pulmonary TB patients 3-month weekly Isoniazid (3 00 mg) and Rifapentine (300 mg) in persons older than 2 years Infants <12 months of age an d Children < 2years of age wi th HIV 6-months daily isoniazid (6H) : 10 mg/kg/day

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the 2025 targets of the Global AIDS Strategy for 2021 to 2026?
mcqs.explanation: 95%, not 75% of HIV -exposed children are tested by 2 months of age and after stopping breastfeeding according to the 2025 targets. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 29-year-old man comes to you with complaints of painful swelling in his right groin, as shown below. He gives a history of 3-4 painless ulcers over his penis 4 weeks ago that had resolved on its own. What is the likely causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario and image showing the groove sign of Greenblatt are suggestive of lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV). The causative organism is Chlamydia trachomatis. LGV commonly presents with multiple small, painless ulcers on the genitalia that are often unrecognized and resolve spontaneously. This is followed by painful lymphadenopathy and bubo formation after 4-6 weeks. If left untreated, it can lead to extensive lymphatic damage, elephantiasis, and de formity o f the genitalia. The treatment of choice is doxycycline.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Match the following STDs with their respective incubation periods:
mcqs.explanation: The incubation periods of various STDs are as follows:315 STD Incubation peri od Syphilis 10 -90 days Chlamydia sis 7-21 days Donovano sis 3-40 days Chancroid 2-3 days

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a part of case detection i n STDs?
mcqs.explanation: Notification is not part of the case detection strategy for STDs. Case detection in STDs includes the following: • Screening • Contact tracing • Cluster testing

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old man is diagnosed with syphilis. On probing, he gives you the information of other people in the same sociosexual environment as him. You then refer all these people for testing. What is this method of case detection?
mcqs.explanation: This method of case detection is known as cluster testing. The methods employed in case detection of STDs are: • Screening - testing of apparently healthy volunteers from the general population for early detection of disease • Contact tracing - technique by which the sexual partners of diagnosed patients are identified, l ocated , investigated, and treated • Cluster testing - patients are asked to name other persons who move in the same socio-sexual environment, who are then tested

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 29-year-old man with urethral discharge is treated with the grey kit. This treatment is effective for the control of which of the following organisms?
mcqs.explanation: The grey kit is effective for the treatment of infections caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about the epidemiology o f leprosy?

options.a: Increased prevalence in childhood indicates that the disease is active and spreading.
options.b: Multibacillary cases are the most infectious in the community
options.c: Bacterial load is highest in patients with tuberculoid leprosy
options.d: Seldom may be transmitted by insect vectors

mcqs.explanation: The bacterial load is highest in patients with lepromatous leprosy. 1 gram of leproma contains as many as 2-7 billion bacilli.316 Multibacillary cases (lepromatous and borderline lepromatous) are the most important source of infection in the community. Infection can occur at any age. In general, cases rise to a peak between 10-20 years of age and then fall. In endemic areas, the disease is acquired commonly during childhood. A high prevalence in this age group indicates that the disease is active and spreading. The organism may also be transmitted by insect vectors or by tattooing needles. However , t his is not clinically significant.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Elimination of leprosy in India is defined as the prevalence of :
mcqs.explanation: Elimination of leprosy in India is defined as a prevalence of < 1 per 10,000.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the prevalence of leprosy in India per 10,000?
mcqs.explanation: The prevalence of leprosy in India is 0.41 per 10,000 as of March 2021.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The Ridley Jopling classification for leprosy uses which of the following parameters?
mcqs.explanation: The Ridley Jopling classification uses clinical, bacteriological, immunological, and histological parameters.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A pathologist is studying the split skin smears taken from 4 sites of a leprosy patient. The following find ings a re noted in the samples. What is the bacteriological index?
mcqs.explanation: The bacteriological index (BI) of the given samples is 3.5 According to Ridley's logarithmic scale, • 10 bacilli out of 100 oil immersion fields indicate an index of 1+ • & gt; 000 bacilli out of average fields imply an index of 6+ The bacteriological index is calculated by adding the index from each site examined and dividing the total by the number of sites examined. Hence, BI = (1+1+6+6) / 4 BI = 14/4 BI = 3.5

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The lepromin test was performed on a patient with suspected leprosy. When will you ask him to come back for interpretation of the test results?
mcqs.explanation: 317 The patient should be asked to come back after 48 hours and on the 21st day for interpretation of the test results. The lepromin test is a skin test for delayed hypersensitivity and is the only method to study immunity in leprosy patients. It is performed by injecting 0.1ml of lepromin reagent intradermally into the inner aspect of the forearm. The following 2 reactions are observed:Early reaction of Fernandez Late reaction of Mitsuda Develops in 24-48 hours Starts at 7-10 days, peaks at 3-4 weeks (read on day 21 ) Remains for 3-5 days Gradually subsides over the n ext few weeks Poorly defined erythema and induration. Carries less signif icance Considered positive if there i s a nodule > 5 mm in diamet er

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about the lepromin test?

options.a: It is negative in most children in the first 4 months of life
options.b: It can be used as a diagnostic test
options.c: It is used to classify leprosy cases
options.d: False positive may be seen in those who underwent BCG vacination

mcqs.explanation: The lepromin test is not a diagnostic test. It is only used to assess the immune status, classify the cases, and estimate the prognosis. The two main drawbacks of this test are: • False-positive results in those who received BCG vaccination • False-negative results in lepromatous and borderline lepromatous cases

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A group of public health workers is trying to identify trachoma cases at an ophthalmology camp. Which of the following is the best index to assess for trachoma inflammation?

options.a: Follicles on the upper tarsal conjuctiva
options.c: Presence of trichiasis a nd entropion
options.d: V ascular pannus at the superior limbus

mcqs.explanation: In epidemiological studies, the upper tarsal conjunctiva is the best index of trachomatous inflammation in the eye. For the purpose of diagnosis, any 2 of the following d iagnostic criteria must be present: • Follicles on the upper tarsal conjunctiva • Limbal follicles and Herbert's pits • Typical conjunctival scarring (trichiasis and entropion) • Vascular pannus, most marked at the superior limbus The following image shows follicles on the upper tarsal conjunctiva seen in trachomatous inflammation.318

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the organisms causing trachoma?

options.a: Morax- Axenfeld bacillus is the most widespread
options.b: Gonococcus is the most dangerous organism contributing to the disease process
options.c: Koch-Weeks bacillus is the most innocuous
options.d: C. trachomatis type D commonly causes permanent visual damage

mcqs.explanation: Gonococcus is the most dangerous organism contributing to the disease process in trachoma. Classic endemic trachoma is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis types A, B, C. Other pathogenic organisms that contribute to the disease process are: • Morax-Axenfeld diplobacillus - most innocuous • Kochs-Weeks bacillus - most widespread • Gonococcus - most dangerous The types D-K of C. trachomatis are sexually transmitted and cause inclusion conjunctivitis. It rarely causes permanent v ision loss.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The elimination of neonatal tetanus is defined as:
mcqs.explanation: The elimination of neonatal tetanus is defined as <1 case per 1000 live births in every district. Maternal and neonatal tetanus (MNT) was eliminated in India in 2015. Since July 2018, TT vaccines have been replaced by the Td vaccine for dual protection.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following diseases is called the 8th day disease?
mcqs.explanation: Neonatal tetanus is known as the 8th-day disease. This is because the clinical features are often seen after the 7th day after birth due to infection of the umbilical cord. Option A: Trench fever is also c alled the 5-day fever.319 Option B: Pertussis is called the 100-day cough. Option D: Scarlet fever is also known as the 2nd disease.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 13-year-old girl is brought to the casualty a few hours after being injured by a rusty knife. According to her parents, her course of tetanus vaccination was completed 7 years ago. What is the next best step in management?

options.d: Human tetanus immunoglobulin and single dose of toxoid

mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario is suggestive of a contaminated wound in a patient who received complete immunization against tetanus 7 years ago. She comes under category B of tetanus immunization and must be given a single dose of tetanus toxoid alone. The WHO recommends a 3-dose primary vaccination series with tetanus-diphtheria-containing vaccine followed by 3 booste r d oses. Ideally , there should be at least 4 years between booster doses.320

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The WHO has formulated a Global Action Plan for the prevention and control of non-communicable diseases. Which of the following is not a voluntary global target under this initiative?

options.a: 10% relative reduction in harmful use of alcohol
options.b: 30% relative reduction in mean population intake of sodium
options.c: 10% relative reduction in prevalence of insufficient physical activity
options.d: 10% relative reduction in use of trans-fat for cooking

mcqs.explanation: A 10 percent relative reduction in the use of trans-fat for cooking is not a voluntary global target under the WHO Global Action Plan for prevention and control of non-communicable diseases. There are 9 targets under this plan which are to be achieved by 2025. These are shown in the image below.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Project MONICA is related to:
mcqs.explanation: Project MONICA is related to cardiovascular diseases. It stands for multinational monitoring of trends and determinants in cardiovascular diseases. It was done to study the reasons for the changes in the trends of cardiovascular diseases in different countries.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the relationship between smoking and coronary heart disease (CHD)?

options.a: Smoking can cause sudden death from CHD.
options.b: Filters in cigarettes are protective against the development of CHD.
options.c: Risk of developing CHD 10-20 years after the cessation of smoking is equal in smokers and non smokers.
options.d: Degree of risk of developing CHD is directly related to the number o f cigarettes smoked per day .

mcqs.explanation: Filters are probably not protective against the development of coronary heart disease in smokers. Smoking is a modifiable risk factor for coronary heart disease (CHD). The degree of risk is directly related t o the number of cigarettes smoked per day. Several mechanisms have been suggested for this: • Carbon monoxide induced atherogenesis • Nicotine stimulation of adrenergic drive • Lipid metabolism with fall in levels of HDL Cigarettes also increase the risk of sudden death in patients with CHD who are below 50 years of age. The risk of death from CHD decreases with the cessation of smoking. The risk declines quite328 substantially within one year of stopping smoking and more gradually thereafter until, after 10- 20 years, it is the same as that of non-smokers. Risk factors for coronary heart disease are: • Modifiable: • Cigarette smoking • High blood pressure • Elevated serum cholesterol • Diabetes • Obesity • Sedentary habits • Stress • Non-modifiable: • Age • Sex • Family history • Genetic factors • Personality

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A chronic smoker was found to have a deranged lipid profile during his annual health checkup. Which of the following variables tested is most directly associated with the risk of developing coronary heart disease?
mcqs.explanation: The plasma LDL level is most directly associated with the risk of developing coronary heart disease (CHD). HDL is protective against the development of CHD. Its levels should ideally be more than 40 mg/dl. Recent evidence shows that levels of Apolipoprotein-A-1 and Apolipoprotein-B are better predictors of CHD than HDL or LDL. VLDL is more strongly associated with the risk of developing peripheral vascular disease.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old diabetic male is concerned about his risk of developing coronary heart disease. What cholesterol/HDL ratio would you aim to achieve in this patient?
mcqs.explanation: A cholesterol/HDL ratio <3.5 is recommended for the prevention of coronary heart disease (CHD).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: While conducting a screening camp for coronary heart disease, you encounter the following people. Who among them is at the highest risk for developing this disease?

options.a: A person who is competitive and ambitious
options.b: A person who is calm and relaxed
options.c: A person who tends to suppress their emotions
options.d: An introverted person with negative affectivity

mcqs.explanation: 329 A person who is competitive and ambitious is said to have a type A personality. Such people are more prone to develop coronary heart disease (CHD). Personality type is a non-modifiable risk factor for CHD. Risk factors for coronary heart disease are: • Modifiable: • Cigarette smoking • High blood pressure • Elevated serum cholesterol • Diabetes • Obesity • Sedentary habits • Stress • Non-modifiable: • Age • Sex • Family history • Genetic factors • Personality Option B: A calm and r elaxed person is said to have a type B personality. Option C: A person who tends to suppress their emotions, especially negative emotions, is said to have a type C personality. Option D: A person with negative affectivity and social inhibition is said to have a type D personality.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old obese woman enquires about ways she can reduce h er risk of coronary artery disease . Which of the following dietary modifications would you suggest?

options.a: Reduction of salt intake to less than 10g per day
options.b: Consumption of saturated fats limited to less than 10% of the total energy intake
options.c: Reduction of total fat intake to less than 5% of total energy intake
options.d: Dietary cholesterol increased to above 100 mg/1000 kcal energy intake

mcqs.explanation: Limiting the consumption of saturated fats to less than 10% of total energy intake is recommended for the prevention of coronary artery disease. The WHO'S Expert Committee suggested certain dietary m odifications for the prevention of coronary artery disease. These include: • Reduction of the total fat intake to 20–30% of total energy intake • Consumption of saturated fats must be limited to less than 10% of total energy intake • A reduction of dietary cholesterol to below 100mg per 1000 kcal per day • Increase in the complex carbohydrate consumption (i.e vegetables, fruits, whole grains and legumes) • Avoidance of alcohol consumption and reduction of salt intake t o 5g daily or less330

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man, under treatment for hypertension for the past two months, is found to have a blood pressure of 144/96 mmHg. How will you grade it according to the European society of cardiology guidelines-2018?
mcqs.explanation: According to the European society of cardiology guidelines-2018, a patient having a systolic BP\034140 and a diastolic BP\03490 mmHg is classified as having grade 1 hypertension.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A doctor records the BP of a patient as 142/90mmHg. One h our later, another doctor records the BP of the same patient as 160/98 mmHg. Both the readings are measured with the same apparatus under the same emotional and physical state of the patient. What type of error is seen here?
mcqs.explanation: Such errors can arise due to differences in hearing acuity and interpretation of Korotkoff sounds. The types of errors that can occur during the measurement of blood pressure include: • Observer errors - due to difference in hearing acuity and interpretation of Korotkoff sounds • Instrumental err ors - d ue to a leaking valve or cuffs that do not encircle the arm completely • Subject errors - due to anxiety, fear, etc. of the patient331

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What does number 2 in the given diagram related to hypertension denote?

options.c: Diagnosed hypertensive subjects not on treatment

mcqs.explanation: The above diagram depicts the "rule of halves", which shows the distribution of hypertension in the community. The number 2 in this diagram denotes normotensive subjects. The rule of halves is a way of depicting the iceberg phenomenon seen in hypertension. It depicts that only about half of the hypertensive subjects in the general population of most developed countries are aware of the condition and only half of those aware are being treated and only half of those being tr eated a re considered to be adequately treated. The circles marked by numbers in the given diagram correspond to the following parts of the population: • Whole community • Normotensive subjects • Hypertensive subjects • Undiagnosed hypertension • Diagnosed hypertension • Diagnosed but untreated • Diagnosed and treated • Inadequately treated • Adequately treated

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding tracking of blood pressure?

options.a: BP increases with age in all individuals
options.b: BP falls steadily in the elderly
options.c: Hypertensive children become hypotensive as they grow
options.d: BP of hypotensive children tends to remain low in adult life

mcqs.explanation: If the blood pressure of individuals is followed up over years from early childhood to adult life, low blood p ressures tend to remain low and high blood pressures become higher as the individuals grow older. This phenomenon of persistence of the rank order of blood pressure is described as tracking. This is helpful in identifying children and adolescents who are at risk of developing hypertension in the future. Although blood pressure is known to increase with age in both sexes, some communities have been identified whose mean blood pressure does not rise with age. This is becau se t heir salt intake and calorie consumption are at a subsistence level.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: While formulating a diet plan for a hypertensive patient, you advise s alt restriction. How much reduction in systolic blood pressure is expected by this intervention?
mcqs.explanation: Salt restriction or decreasing dietary sodium intake decreases the systolic blood pressure by 2-8 mmHg approximately. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a minor criterion for the diagnosis of rheumatic fever in a low risk population?
mcqs.explanation: Polyarthralgia is a minor criterion for the diagnosis of rheumatic fever in a low risk population.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A child having strep throat is being prescribed benzathine penicillin G. Which level of prevention of rheumatic fever does this intervention fall under?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is an example of primary mode of prevention of rheumatic fever. This is because the patient only has strep throat and rheumatic fever has not developed yet. In case benzathine penicillin G is given to a patient with rheumatic fever to prevent further complications, then it becomes secondary level of prevention.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old boy with rheumatic fever developed carditis which subsequently healed in a couple of weeks. How long will you administer benzathine penicillin G for secondary prophylaxis to him?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, benzathine penicillin G for secondary prophylaxis should be given for 10 years from the last attack i.e, till 26 years of age. The given case is of rheumatic fever with carditis but with no residual valvular disease, for which secondary prophylaxis is given for 10 years from the last attack or till 21 years of age, whichever is longer. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a protective factor for diabetes mellitus?
mcqs.explanation: A higher intake of saturated fats is associated with an increased risk of diabetes mellitus. Dietary factors that are protective for diabetes mellitus are: • Higher intake of unsaturated fatty acids • A minimum daily intake of 20g of dietary fibre334 • Exclusive breastfeeding

mcqs.question: A patient's fasting plasma glucose is 122 mg/dl and postprandial plasma glucose is 138 mg/dl. According to the WHO diagnostic criteria for diabetes, which category does this patient fall under?
mcqs.explanation: Fasting blood glucose of 122 mg/dl with a postprandial value of 138 mg/dl indicates the patient falls under the criteria for impaired fasting glucose. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements are incorrect regarding the benefits of various interventions in diabetes?
mcqs.explanation: The use of ACE inhibitors in diabetics reduces the risk of nephropathy by 42% and cardiovascular risk by 22%. Annual eye examination in diabetics reduces the incidence of serious visual loss by 60-70%. Interventions in diabetes: • Glycaemic control in diabetics with HbA1C > 9% reduces microvascular disease risk by 30% per 1% drop in HbA1c. • Blood pressure control in patients with BP > 130/80 mmHg reduces microvascular and macrovascular disease risk by 35% per 10 mm Hg d rop in blood pressure. • Lifestyle modification reduces the incidence of diabetes by 35-58%. • Metformin administered as a preventive therapy reduces the incidence of diabetes by 25-31%. • Proper foot care reduces the risk of serious foot disease by 50-60%.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms is least likely to be associated with malignancies?
mcqs.explanation: HPV 6 and 11 are considered low-risk subtypes and are associated mainly with genital warts (condyloma acuminata) and respiratory papillomatosis in both genders. HPV 16 and 18 are considered high-risk subtypes and are associated with cancer cervix and pre-cancerous cervical lesions. There is also evidence linking HPV 16 and 18 with cancers of the342 anus, vulva, vagina, penis, and oropharynx. Important agents associated with malignant conditions: • HHV -8 (mainly), cytomegalovirus - Kaposi's sarcoma • Epstein-Barr virus - Burkitt's lymphoma and nasopharyngeal carcinoma • HPV 16 and 18 - Cancer cervix • HBV and HCV - Hepatocellular carcinoma • Schistosoma - Bladder carcinoma

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which among the following is not a primary method of prevention of carcinoma in the population?
mcqs.explanation: Screening for cancer is a secondary level of prevention. This is because it detects the disease at a pre-invasive or pre-malignant stage when t he process of carcinogenesis has already started. It thereby aids in further treatment and improved survival. Immunization, restricting the use of tobacco and avoiding alcohol are primary levels of prevention because they prevent the start of carcinogenesis.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: According to Globocan 2020 India, which of the following are the most common malignancies among men and women respectively?

options.c: Ca oral cavity and Ca breast

mcqs.explanation: According to Globocan 2020 India data, the most common malignancy among men is cancer lip and oral cavity, and among women is cancer breast. The table below lists the top 5 common cancers according to the Globocan 2 020 India.Men Women Overall 1. Lip, oral cavity 1. Breast 1. Breast 2. Lung 2. Cervix uteri 2. Lip, oral cavity 3. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following women is not at an increased risk of developing breast cancer in future?

options.a: A woman who attained menarche at 9 years of age
options.b: A woman who has never breastfed in her lifetime
options.c: A woman who attained menopause at 56 years of age
options.d: A woman who had her first full term pregnancy at 26 years of age

mcqs.explanation: Women who have their first full-term pregnancy after 30 years of age are at increased risk for breast cancer. The risk of breast cancer increases with an increase in duration of exposure to estrogen. As progesterone levels are increased during pregnancy, it reduces the risks of conditions that occur due to hyperestrogenemia.343 Risk factors for breast cancer: • Modifiable risk factors: • Age at first live birth (First full-term pregnancy after 30 years) • Parity • Lack of breastfeeding • Obesity • Alcohol consumption • Tobacco smoking • Use of hormone replacement therapy • Decreased physical activity • Non-modifiable risk factors: • Increasing age • Early age at menarche (onset of menses before 12 years of age) • Menstrual factors • Female sex • Older age at menopause (onset beyond 55 years of age) • Nulliparity • R ace , ethnicity • Genetic predisposition • Family history • History of radiation exposure

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old woman is at increased risk of breast cancer as she is on hormone replacement therapy. Which of the following is the most sensitive method of screening for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Mammography is the most sensitive and specific investigation for detecting breast cancer. It can detect even small tumors that are missed during a self-breast examination, clinical examination by the physician and ultrasonographic examination.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the best level of prevention of breast cancer?
mcqs.explanation: Early diagnosis and treatment is the best level of prevention of breast cancer. It is a secondary level of prevention. T he earlier a disease is diagnosed and treated, the better is the prognosis. The occurrence of secondary cases or any long term disability can be prevented. This is of particular importance in chronic diseases.344 Early diagnosis and treatment is not as effective and economical as primary prevention. However, it may be critically important in reducing the high morbidity and mortality in diseases such as essential hypertension, cancer cervix and breast cancer.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A patient with Prader-Willi syndrome needs to be evaluated for obesity but the scale for measuring height in your clinic is broken. Which of the following indices can you still use in this situation?
mcqs.explanation: The corpulence index can be used in this scenario as it is independent of height. The formula for corpulence index is actual weight/ desired weight.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following indices of obesity is obtained by dividing weight in kg by square of height in metres?
mcqs.explanation: Quetelet's index (Body Mass Index) is obtained by dividing weight in kg by square of height in metres .

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The BMI of two Indian college students are 17 and 24.99 respectively. How will you classify them in terms of their BMI?
mcqs.explanation: An adult Indian with a BMI of 17 is classified as underweight and a BMI of 24.99 is classified as overweight.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The weight of a diabetic woman is 75 kg and her height is 150 cm. Calculate her BMI.
mcqs.explanation: The BMI of an individual with a weight of 75 kg and height of 150 cm is 33. It is calculated as follows, BMI = Weight (in kg) / Height2 (in metre2) = 75 / (1.5)2 = 33.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: For which of the following conditions, an obese individual is at the greatest risk of developing in the future?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options, an obese individual is at the greatest risk of developing type 2 diabetes. The relative risk of health problems associated with obesity:Greatly increased risk Moderately increased ris k Slightly increased risk Type 2 diabetes Coronary artery disease Cancer (breast cancer in post menopausal women, endome trial cancer, colon cancer) Gall bladder disease Hypertension Reproductive hormone abnor malities345 Greatly increased risk Moderately increased ris k Slightly increased risk Dyslipidaemia Osteoarthritis (knees) Polycystic ovary syndrome Insulin resistance Hyperuricaemia and gou t Impaired fertility Breathlessness Low back pain due to obesity Sleep apnea Increased risk of anaesthesia complications Fetal defects associated with maternal obesity

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding waist circumference?

options.a: The cut-off for normal waist circumference in Indian women is 90 cm
options.b: It is measured at the midpoint between the lower border of the rib cage and the iliac crest
options.c: It is an approximate index of intra-abdominal and total body fat
options.d: It is an indicator of the risk of chronic diseases

mcqs.explanation: The cut-off value for normal waist circumference in Indian women is 80cm, while in Indian men it is 90cm. Waist circumference is an approximate indicator of intra-abdominal and total body fat. It is measured at the midpoint between the lower border of the rib cage and the iliac crest. It is an indicator of the risk of chronic diseases.
