mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: According to the WHO, what is the cut-off for visual acuity for blindness?
mcqs.explanation: According to the WHO, blindness is defined as visual acuity of less than 3/60, or a corresponding visual field loss to less than 10\260, in the better eye with the best possible correction.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which o f the following is the most common cause of blindness in India?
mcqs.explanation: 346 According to the National Survey on Blindness (2015-2019), cataract is the most common cause of blindness in India accounting for 66.2% of the total cases.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You administer vitamin A prophylactically to a 15-month-old child during a routine checkup. What is the level of prevention being achieved here?
mcqs.explanation: Prophylactic administration of vitamin A to a normal child is an example of primary level of prevention. It is done to prevent xerophthalmia.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A boy is brought to the ophthalmologist with complaints of dryness in both the eyes and difficulty in reading. On examination, his eye appears as shown in the below image. What is the stage of xerophthalmia according to WHO?
mcqs.explanation: The finding in the given image is a Bitot's spot. It belongs to WHO class X1 B of vitamin A deficiency.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 2-year-old child on examination shows signs of vitamin A deficiency. What is the dose of vitamin A to be administered to this child?
mcqs.explanation: 2 lakh IU of vitamin A should be administered to a 2-year-old child with vitamin A deficiency. Dosage of vitamin A in children: • 50,000 IU for children less than 6 months of age • 1 lakh IU for children between 6 months to 12 months of age • 2 lakh IU for children above 12 months of age. These doses of vitamin A are to be administered on days 1, 2 and 14 for the treatment of vitamin A deficiency.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of injury-related death?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of injury-related deaths are road traffic accidents, followed by suicide.347

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are working as the PHC Medical Officer in your village. Which of the following diseases would you not target under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme?
mcqs.explanation: The National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) does not target the prevention and control of cutaneous leishmaniasis (also known as Chiclero's ulcer). NVBDCP is the nodal agency for the prevention and control of the following vector-borne diseases: • Kala-azar (also called visceral leishmaniasis) • Malaria • Dengue • Lymphatic filariasis • Japanese encephalitis • Chikungunya. The logo of the NVBDCP:355

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The insect shown below is a vector for a disease that is targetted under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme. Identify the disease.
mcqs.explanation: The image shown is of the Culex species of mosquitoes, which is a vector for Japanese encephalitis and Bancroftian filariasis. Mansonia species is the vector for Malayan filariasis.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is carried out by the Drug Distribution Centres under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme for Malaria?
mcqs.explanation: The Drug Distribution Centres are only for dispensing anti-malarial drugs, under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) for Malaria. The organizational structure for the Anti-Malaria Programme is as follows: • Central Government: supplies DDT and larvicides. • S tate government: procures the Indoor Residual Sprays (IRS) for the districts. • District Malaria Office: is the key unit for the implementation of the programme. • District Malaria Officer: has the direct responsibility of IRS spraying operations and is assisted by one Assistant Malaria Officer and Malaria Inspectors. • Medical officer of the PHC: has the overall responsibility for the surveillance and laboratory services. • Multi-Purpose Workers and ASHAs: carry out c ase-based surveillance and case detection in the community . • Drug Distribution Centres: only for dispensing the antimalarial drugs. • Fever Treatment Depots: collect blood slides in addition to the distribution of antimalarial drugs.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the surveillance system set up for malaria?

options.a: Active case detection is carried out when patients report with fever to the peripheral health workers
options.b: Blood smears are collected fortnightly during house visits by Accredited Social Health Activists
options.c: A ntibody detecting rapid diagnostic kits are used for passive case detection as part of surveillance
options.d: Passive case detection at the Primary Health Centre is done by examination of blood smears

mcqs.explanation: Passive case detection at Primary Health Centres (PHCs) is done by examination of blood smears. Malaria surveillance system: Active case detection: blood smears are collected by the Multipurpose Health Workers (MPHW)/ Auxiliary N urse Midwife (ANM) on house visits every fortnight. Passive case detection: detection of fever case by collecting of blood smears of those that report to ASHAs or peripheral health volunteers.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following measures for controlling malaria is the Urban Malaria Scheme mainly based on?
mcqs.explanation: 356 The Urban Malaria Scheme is mainly based on anti-larval measures for controlling malaria. In Urban Malaria Scheme, urban areas with a population of >50,000 and a slide positivity rate of \0345% are included. The vector in urban areas breeds in man-made containers. Therefore, anti-larval measures such as larvivorous fish and larvicides are used to control breeding as the primary method of vector control. In rural areas, anti-adult measures, such as Indoor Residual Spr ay (IRS) i s the primary method of vector control.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the most efficient anti-larval method to prevent urban malaria?
mcqs.explanation: The most efficient anti-larval method to prevent urban malaria is to cover overhead tanks and other man-made containers properly. This is because the vector of malaria in urban areas breeds largely in such man-made containers.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The blood smear slides (A) and (B) prepared from a patient suspected with malaria are shown below. Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding these tests?

options.a: Slide (A) is used for estimating the parasite concentration
options.b: Slide (A) has been air dried for 10 minutes
options.c: Slide (B) cannot be used for detecting the species of the parasite
options.d: Jaswant Singh Bhattacharya stain is used for both

mcqs.explanation: Slide (A) is a thin blood smear and slide (B) is a thick blood smear. Thin blood smears (slide A) are not used for estimating parasite concentration. They are used to detect the species of parasite. Microscopy i s the best method for the diagnosis of malaria due to its high sensitivity and specificity . Jaswant Singh Battacharya (JSB) stain is used for staining both thick and thin smears. Thick smear is used to detect infection and estimate parasite concentration. The correct thickness is the thickness through which a newsprint is barely visible. It is prepared by slow-drying for 30 minutes, which leads to hemolysis and distortion of the plasmodia morphology. Hence, sp ecies c annot be detected. Thin smear is used to identify the particular infecting species of Plasmodium. It is prepared by air drying for 10 minutes and fixed in methanol. Thus, the plasmodia morphology is not distorted.357

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The following two diagnostic techniques (A) and (B) were performed in a medical camp conducted for diagnosing malaria. Which is a true statement regarding these techniques?

options.a: Image (A) - It is used for identifying the species of the malarial parasite
options.b: Image (A) - It is not the established method of choice for diagnosing malaria in urban areas
options.c: Image (B) - Antibody detection by this test is the method of choice for diagnosing malaria in inaccessible and tribal areas
options.d: Image (B) - Bivalent type of this test was used for detecting Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax

mcqs.explanation: Image (A) is a thick blood smear and Image (B) is the Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT). Bivalent RDTs detect P. falciparum and P. vivax. Thin blood smear is used to identify the particular infecting species. Thick blood smear is used to detect infection and estimate parasite concentration. Antibody detecting Rapid Diagnostic Tests (RDTs) are not the method of choice anymore in diagnosing malaria in inaccessible and tribal areas. The Antigen detecting RDTs and blood smear ex amination a re the recommended methods for diagnosis of malaria. Note: According to the announcement by Union Health Ministry in April 2018, antibody detecting Rapid Diagnostic Tests (RDTs) for malaria is banned due to the high false-positive rates in endemic areas. Malaria Antigen detecting Rapid Diagnostic Test kit:

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following parameters would you use to check the efficiency of the surveillance s ystem for malaria under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme?
mcqs.explanation: The Annual Blood Examination Rate (ABER) is used to check the efficiency of the surveillance system for malaria. It takes into account the number of slides examined for the population under surveillance.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: According to the National Framework for Malaria Elimination in India, states are classified based on which of the following parameters?
mcqs.explanation: 358 The annual parasite incidence (API) is used in classifying states/UTs according to the National Framework for Malaria Elimination in India. The Annual Parasite Incidence is calculated as: (Cases in one year \3271000) / (Population under surveillance).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is correct about the classification of malaria endemic states under the National Strategic Plan for Malaria?

options.a: The states classified under Category 0 are in the elimination phase
options.b: The states with API <1 and all their districts reporting API <1 are in the elimination phase
options.c: The states with districts reporting API in between 1-2 per 1000 population are in the elimination phase
options.d: The states classified under category 2 a re in the phase of intensified control

mcqs.explanation: The National Strategic Plan for Malaria classifies the states under Category 1 of the NVBDCP to be in the elimination phase. Category 1 states are all states/UTs with API <1 and all their districts reporting API <1.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following months is observed as the anti-malaria month in India?
mcqs.explanation: The anti-malaria month is observed in the month of June every year in our country, just before the onset of monsoon (transmission season of malaria) to enhance the level of awareness. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A rural medical officer implements Integrated Vector Management in his village. Which of the following measures of vector control would you prefer in a rural area?
mcqs.explanation: The measure of vector control preferred for rural areas is indoor residual spray (IRS). Under integrated vector management (IVM), the preferred measures of vector control for359 • Rural areas include: Anti-adult measures, using indoor residual spray (IRS) • Urban areas include: Anti-larval measures, like environmental control by source reduction, chemical control (mineral oils, Paris green, synthetic insecticides, etc.), and biological control (fish species Gambusia affinis and Lebistes reticulatus which feed on mosquito larvae).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Select the correct option regarding I ntergrated Vector Management:

options.a: Malathion is the insecticide of choice used for vector management
options.b: Larvivorous fish and larvicides are the main methods of vector control in rural areas
options.c: Long Lasting Insecticide Nets are provided in areas with API \
options.d: Insecticide treated bed nets are supplied in areas with API \

mcqs.explanation: Under the Integrated Vector Management initiative, Long Lasting Insecticide Nets (LLIN) are provided i n areas with Annual Parasite Index (API) \034 5. Integrated Vector Management (IVM): • For adult mosquitoes: • Indoor Residual Sprays (IRS) are used as the main method of vector control in rural areas. The insecticide of choice will be the insecticide to which the local vector is susceptible as per the best available information. • Two rounds of spraying are done with DDT, and in DDT resistant areas, three rounds of spraying are done with malathion. • For larvae: • Larvivorous fish a nd larvicides are used. This is the main method of vector control in urban areas. • For personal protection: • Insecticide-treated bed nets are supplied in areas with Annual Parasite Index (API) \0342. • Long-Lasting Insecticide Nets (LLIN) are provided in areas with API \0345.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are working as a medical officer in Jharkhand, which is endemic to the disease transmitted by the vector shown below. Which of the following agents would you prefer to control this vector in view of resistance to commonly used agents?
mcqs.explanation: The image given is that of a sandfly, which is the vector for kala-azar. In endemic states with increasing resistance to commonly used agents like DDT, synthetic pyrethroids are preferred now. The four s tates endemic for kala-azar are Bihar, Jharkhand , West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: According to the revised strategy for the eradication of kala-azar, which of the following drugs would you use across all age groups in order to reduce the human reservoir of infection?
mcqs.explanation: A single dose of intravenous treatment with liposomal amphotericin B is used across all age groups in order to reduce the human reservoir of infection. WHO will supply this drug free of cost. Drugs for Kala Azar:360 • Single-dose intravenous liposomal amphotericin B for all age groups and for pregnant and HIV co-infected patients. • Miltefosine- an oral drug, once daily for 28 days. Contraindicated during pregnancy, lactation, and in women who refuse contraception. • Combination of miltefosine capsules with paromomycin i.m, for 10 days. Contraindications are the same as miltefosine. • The drug of choice for Post Kala-Azar Dermal Leishmaniasis (PKDL) is miltefosine 100mg orally p er day for 12 weeks. Ivermectin is used for lymphatic filariasis.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the elimination and eradication of lymphatic filariasis is true?

options.a: It will be considered as eliminated when the number of microfilaria carriers are less than 5 percent
options.b: It will be considered as eliminated when children born after initiation of the programme are free from antigenemia
options.c: India has set the target of eliminating lymphatic filariasis by
options.d: WHO recommends dual therapy with diethylcarbamazine and albendazole for elimination of transmission

mcqs.explanation: Lymphatic filariasis will be considered eliminated when the children born after the initiation of the programme are free from antigenemia. Antigenemia refers to the presence of adult filaria worms in the human body. According to the Elimination of Lymphatic Filariasis (ELF) Programme, there are two criteria to consider elimination of lymphatic filariasis: • Children born after the initiation of the e limination programme are free from circulating antigenemia . • The number of microfilaria carriers is <1%. Following the failure to achieve ELF by 2015, the target set to eliminate lymphatic filariasis by WHO was 2020. To achieve the same WHO recommended the use of triple therapy for lymphatic filariasis. It incorporated ivermectin along with diethylcarbamazine (DEC) and albendazole instead of the traditional DEC and albendazole therapy, for the elimination of transmission o f lymphatic filariasis. In 2021, WHO released the 'Road Map for Neglected Tropical Diseases (2021–2030)'. Under this, lymphatic filariasis is targeted for elimination as a public health problem by 2030. In February 2023, the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare in India launched a nationwide Sarva Dawa Sevan or Mass Drug Administration (MDA) campaign to eliminate LF by 2027, aiming to achieve this goal three years ahead of the global target.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: As the medical officer in a Japanese encephalitis endemic area, which of the following measures would you not advocate for controlling its transmission?

options.a: The use of Indoor Residual Sprays
options.c: Keeping pigs away from human dwellings
options.d: The use of malathion for outdoor fogging

mcqs.explanation: Indoor Residual Sprays (IRS) are not used in the vector control measures for Japanese Encephalitis (JE) as its vectors (Culex) are outdoor resters. Prevention and control of JE include: • Vaccination • Keeping pigs away from human dwellings from dusk to dawn (biting time of the vectors). Pigs act as important amplifiers of the virus.361 • Use of bed nets for personal protection. • Use of larvivorous fishes. • Using malathion for outdoor fogging to control an outbreak.362

mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: Identify the organization that has the given emblem:

options.a: National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme
options.d: National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Disease, and Stroke

mcqs.explanation: The given image is the emblem of National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP). Characteristics of NLEP emblem: • The lotus in the NLEP emblem symbolizes beauty and purity. • A partially affected thumb, a normal forefinger, and the shape of a house symbolize that leprosy can be cured and a patient with leprosy can be a useful member of the society. • The rising sun symbolizes hope and optimism. • The emblem captures the spirit of hope and positivity in the eradication of lepr osy. N LEP is a centrally sponsored health scheme of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Govt. of India. Option A: National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP)Option C: Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)372 Option D: National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Disease, and Stroke (NPCDCS).

mcqs.question: The Sparsh campaign was launched to spread awareness about which of the following diseases?
mcqs.explanation: Sparsh Leprosy Awareness Campaign (SLAC) was introduced in 2017 on the occasion of the anti-leprosy day (observed on the last Sunday of January) to promote awareness about various aspects of leprosy.373 Sapna refers to a local school-going girl who will help to spread awareness in the community. mcqs.question: A patient with leprosy comes to the PHC following a pinprick to his foot. He noticed it only after seeing bloodstains on the floor and complains of loss of sensation in his foot. After addressing the issue, the patient is referred to another centre. Where has he been referred to and why?

options.a: For secondary prevention to a district hospital.
options.b: For tertiary prevention to a district hospital.
options.c: For secondary prevention to a district nucleus.
options.d: For tertiary prevention to a district nucleus.

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of a patient with leprosy having neuropathy needs Micro Cellular Rubber (MCR) footwear, which is a form of tertiary prevention. He is to be referred to a district nucleus which supplies MCR footwear to patients.374

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: A patient with leprosy, who has completed a course of multi-drug therapy, presents with complaints of developing painful, tender, and raised lesions on his forehead recently as shown in the image below. What is the first-line treatment for him?

options.a: Restart multi drug therapy and start thalidomide
options.b: Restart multi drug therapy and start prednisolone

mcqs.explanation: The presence of new erythematous and tender subcutaneous nodules in a patient with leprosy indicates that he has developed type II lepra reaction. It is also known as Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL ) and the first line of treatment is prednisolone. Multi-drug therapy (MDT) should not be restarted in patients who develop lepra reactions after the completion of treatment. Prednisolone is started at a dose of 40 mg per day and gradually tapered by 5 mg every 2 weeks. 'Predniso lone c ard' is given when treatment is started. If the patient becomes steroid-dependent, then clofazimine is added. The key targets of the Global Leprosy Strategy 2021-2023 announced by WHO (Accelerating towards a leprosy-free world) are: • 120 countries reporting zero new autochthonous cases. • 70% reduction in the annual number of new cases detected. • 90% reduction in rate per million population of new cases with Grade 2 disability. • 90% reduction in rate per million children o f new child cases with leprosy. The current goal is the elimination of leprosy.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: ABSULS, which is an ASHA-based surveillance project, has been initiated for which of the following diseases?
mcqs.explanation: ABSULS which stands for Asha Based Surveillance for Leprosy Suspects has been initiated to prioritize leprosy case detection by ASHAs.375

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: The treatment of paucibacillary leprosy consists of MDT (which comprises rifampicin, dapsone, and clofazimine). The latest recommended regimen is:
mcqs.explanation: The latest recommendation is 3 drug therapy for 6 months to treat paucibacillary (PB) leprosy by WHO. The regimen consists of rifampicin, dapsone, and clofazimine. Meanwhile, multibacillary (MB) leprosy is treated using the same 3 drugs for a duration of 12 months. While the NLEP guidelines earlier mentioned a 2-drug MDT for PB leprosy, the National Strategic Plan and Roadmap for Leprosy (2023-2027) now recommends a uniform MDT of 3 drugs for both PB and MB leprosy. Note : T he central government has approved a new treatment regimen for paucibacillary (PB) leprosy . The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has introduced a 3-drug regimen for PB leprosy instead of a 2-drug regimen. This revised drug regimen will be applicable in India from April 1, 2025.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: A District Leprosy Officer is preparing the annual report as per NLEP 2020. Which of the following parameters would he not consider as an essential indicator?

options.c: R ate of new cases with Grade II disabilities per 10 lakh population per year
options.d: Proportion of new cases correctly diagnosed

mcqs.explanation: The proportion of new cases correctly diagnosed is not included under essential indicators. It is a part of the quality of service indicators as per NLEP 2020. The essential indicators include: • A nnual new case detection rate (ANCDR) per 1 lakh population. • Rate of new cases with grade II disabilities (G2D) per 10 lakh population per year. • Treatment completion rate (TCR) as a proxy to cure rate. • Prevalence rate (PR). Additional epidemiological indicators include: • Proportion of Grade II disabilities among new cases. • Proportion of females among new cases. • Proportion of multibacillary (MB) among new cases. • Proportion of child (0- 14 years) among new cases. • C hild rate per 100,000 population. • Scheduled Caste New Case Detection Rate.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: As per NLEP 2020, which of the following is not a quality of service indicator?

options.a: Patient month blister calendar pack stock
options.b: Proportion of grade II disabilities among new cases.
options.d: Proportion of cases who developed new or additional disability after starting MDT

mcqs.explanation: Proportion of grade II disabilities among new cases is not a quality of service indicator. It is an additional epidemiological indicator as per NLEP 2020. The quality of service indicators are: • Patient month blister calendar pack stock. • Absolute number of patients made released from treatment (RFT).376 • Number of relapse reported. • Proportion of cases who developed new or additional disability after starting MDT. • Proportion of treatment defaulters. • Proportion of new cases correctly diagnosed.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: You are part of a rural health camp organized under Project A xshya. Which of the following diseases does it aim to control?
mcqs.explanation: Project Axshya was launched in 2010 to control TB. Axshya means free from TB which is the ultimate goal of the project and the National TB Elimination Programme. Project Axshya is being implemented by the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (known simply a s The Union). The project works to improve access to quality TB care and control through a partnership between the government and civil society. The guiding principles of project Axshya are: • Universal access to quality TB services • Community participation in TB care and control • Sustainable interventions and equitable distribution of project benefits with social and gender sensitivity

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: You are working as a medical officer in a PHC where you diagnose a patient with TB. Within how many days do you have to report it to the District Health Officer?
mcqs.explanation: The guidelines for TB notification under the RNTCP is within 30 days (a month) of receiving a new case. The notification must be done to the District Health Officer or the Chief Medical Officer of a District Hospital by the practitioner who diagnosed it. Note: RNTCP has now been renamed to National Tuberculosis Elimination Program (NTEP).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme?

options.a: Follow-up sputum smear examination at the end of intensive phase only
options.b: Directly Observed Treatment Short course strategy is applied
options.c: Treatment is only given to smear positive cases
options.d: MDR TB is resistance t o either rifampicin or isoniazid

mcqs.explanation: DOTS stands for Directly Observed Treatment Short-course and is given by peripheral and voluntary health workers. Recent updates in RNTCP: • Active case finding for TB has been started. • Follow up: • On treatment: m onthly follow up. • After treatment: Follow up at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months. • A sputum smear examination must be done at the end of intensive phase (IP) and at the end of treatment.377

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: A patient presents with fever, productive cough, and weight loss. He gives a history of not having completed treatment for tuberculosis thrice in the past. Extensively drug-resistant TB is suspected. How is this entity defined?

options.a: Resistance to INH + Amikacin + Ofloxacin + Ethambutol
options.d: Resistance to INH + Rifampicin + Ofloxacin + Linez olid

mcqs.explanation: XDR-TB (extensively drug-resistant TB) is defined as multi-drug resistant TB (resistant to rifampicin and isoniazid) which is also resistant to one fluoroquinolone (eg. ofloxacin) AND resistant to atleast one additional group A drug (as of 2021, these are bedaquiline and linezolid) It is usually seen in patients who have previously received treatment for TB and have either failed to complete treatment or relapsed.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: A patient on HAART presents with complaints of fever and expectorant cough for two weeks. What is the investigation to be ordered first?
mcqs.explanation: An HIV patient suspected to have TB is directly investigated by CB-NAAT (Cartridge Based Nucleic Acid Amplification Test). TB is a very serious infection in the immunocompromised and can lead to its most severe form as miliary TB and cause death. Since TB in HIV does not have its typical presentation, early suspicion and advanced diagnosis is the key to preventing mortality. Diagnostic algorithm for TB:

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false under the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme?

options.a: Continuation phase for new sputum smear positive: HRE for 16 weeks
options.b: Intensive phase for sputum smear positive after loss to follow up: HRZE for 8 weeks
options.c: Continuation phase for sputum smear positive recurrent case: HRE for 16 weeks
options.d: Intensive phase for sputum smear positive after failure to treatment: HRZES for 12 weeks

mcqs.explanation: Under National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP) guidelines Initiation phase (IP) for both new and previously treated cases which are H and R sensitive is HRZE for 8 weeks.378

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: Which of the following i s the most peripheral centre under the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme organization structure?
mcqs.explanation: Among the options given, Designated Microscopy Centre is the most peripheral centre.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: Which is the new online software launched under the national tuberculosis elimination program (NTEP) by the government to monitor TB patients?
mcqs.explanation: Nikshay is the new online software launched under the national tuberculosis elimination program for monitoring TB patients. Nikusth is the new online software for monitoring leprosy patients. Nischay is a pregnancy test kit.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: Choose the false statement regarding the initiatives and s trategies for tuberculosis.

options.a: The Stop TB strategy was announced by the World Health Organisation
options.b: The STOP TB strategy has a target of ending TB by achieving an incidence rate of <10 people per 10,000 population per year
options.c: The "Practical approach to lung health" was launched by the WHO for syndromic managment of patients with respiratory symptoms
options.d: The End TB strategy is a 20 year programme

mcqs.explanation: The Stop TB strategy was announced by World Health Organisation to reduce the global burden of TB by 2015 (and not ending TB). The End TB strategy is a 20-year programme with tagline "A world free of TB - Zero TB deaths, Zero TB disease, and Zero TB suffering". I t aims to: • end TB by achieving an incidence rate of <10 people/1 lakh population per year by 2035. • reduce TB deaths by 95% and cut new cases by 90% by 2035. The "Practical approach to lung health initiative" was launched by the WHO as a syndromic approach to the management of patients who attend primary health care services for respiratory symptoms. Ending the TB epidemic is also one of the targets of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) specifically under Goal 3 ( to "ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages").379 WHO defines that "Tuberculosis control" would be achieved when the prevalence of the natural order of infection in the age group of 0-14 years is of the order of 1% (40% in India currently).Vision of End TB : A world fre e of TB - zero deaths , disease and suffering due to TB Goal: End the global TB epid emic Indicators Targets SDG 2030 End TB 2035 Reduction in no. of TB death s compared with 2015 90% 95% Reduction in TB incidence ra te compared with 2015 80%(<20 /1,00 ,0 00) 90%(<10 /1,00 ,0 00) TB -affected families facing ca tastrophic costs due to TB 0% 0%

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: Which of the following group of individuals would you not target under the programme represented by the logo shown below?
mcqs.explanation: The red ribbon shown is a part of the logo of the National AIDS Control Organization (NACO) programme. Industrial workers are not included in the target population under NACO. Target interventions for the control of AIDS transmission are done for: • High-risk groups like sex workers • Men who have sex with men • Transgender • Injecting drug users • Bridge population like migrants and long-distance truckers The services offered through targeted interventions include det ection and treatment for sexually transmitted diseases and condom distribution. The logo of NACO:380

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the target interventions under National AIDS Control Organisation?

options.a: Lubricants are given to homosexual men
options.b: Clean needles and syringes are given to injecting drug users
options.c: Condoms are not given to bridge population
options.d: Opioid substitution therapy is given to Injecting Drug Users

mcqs.explanation: Bridge populations are supplied with condoms under the NACO target interventions. Target interventions: General: • Detection and treatment for sexually transmitted diseases • Condom distribution For injecting drug users: • Distribution of clean needles and syringes. • Abscess prevention and management. • Opioid substitution therapy. • Linkage with detoxification and rehabilitation services. For homosexual men and transgenders: • Provision of lubricants. • P rovision o f project-based clinics for sexually transmitted infections.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: A physician follows the two test protocol for the diagnosis of HIV in a patient. It consists of:

options.a: Western blot as the first test
options.b: Line immunoassay as the second test
options.c: HIV ELISA as the second test
options.d: Western blot as the second test

mcqs.explanation: The two test protocol for the diagnosis of HIV consists of ELISA as the second test. If the initial ELISA is positive, a second ELISA is carried out. If the second ELISA is also positive, only then the case is reported to be positive. Investigations involved in HIV testing strategies:381 • ELISA/ rapid tests. • Confirmatory tests with high specificity like western blot and line immunoassays are used in problem cases eg: indeterminate/ discordant cases of rapid tests. In India, NACO provides western blot (WB) confirmatory testing only to resolve indeterminate results on previous serological testing. It is not used for routine confirmation after a positive result on screening tests. Drawbacks of WB include low rates of detection during acute HIV infec tion a nd misclassification of HIV - 2 infection. Note: The western blot is used as a confirmatory test after 2 indeterminate primary tests (ELISA). It is essentially the third test used and does not fit into the two test protocol.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: As a medical officer involved in the sentinel surveillance for HIV under the National AIDS Control Programme, your duties include all of the following except:

options.a: Estimation of total infection in the community
options.b: Estimation of total cases in hospitals
options.c: Estimation o f trend of disease

mcqs.explanation: As a medical officer involved in the sentinel surveillance, the estimation of total cases in hospitals is not included in the sentinel surveillance for HIV under National AIDS Control Programme (NACO). The aims of the HIV sentinel surveillance include: • D etermine the level of HIV infection in the community. • Understand the trends of HIV epidemic. • Understand the geographical spread of HIV infection and classify districts according to epidemiological and vulnerability criteria. These objectives are achieved by conducting annual cross-sectional surveys of the risk group in the same geographical place.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: Which of the following is targetted by the establishment bearing the logo shown below:
mcqs.explanation: The logo shown represents Suraksha Clinics which are established for the management of sexually transmitted d iseases ( STDs) where patients are given color-coded kits.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes II - NLEP, NTEP & NACO
mcqs.question: Choose the wrong combination of the colour-coded STI kits among the given options.
mcqs.explanation: Kit 4 is blue in colour and is used for genital ulcers. These kits are given at Suraksha clinics.382

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: A 9-month-old infant who has not been previously vaccinated is brought to the OPD. The mother is however adamant and is allowing you to inject the baby with only one vaccine. Which of the following vaccines would you choose to administer in this situation?
mcqs.explanation: In this situation, measles vaccine should be administered subcutaneously because, at 9 months of age, it is a priority to give the measles vaccine. OPV and vitamin A should be given orally.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: An intern posted in the labour room is administering birth dose vaccines to a newborn baby. According to the National Immunization Schedule, which of the following vaccines would he n ot administer?
mcqs.explanation: Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV ) and pentavalent vaccine are not given at birth. The vaccines given at birth are BCG, OPV (0 dose) and hepatitis B vaccines.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: A farmer residing in West Bengal brings his 16-month-old child to the OPD for routine immunization. The child has been adequately immunized till now and has already received a measles vaccine during a supplementary immunization activity drive a few months back. What will you administer to him now?

options.a: OPV booster, DPT booster and Vitamin A
options.b: OPV Booster, DPT booster, MR, JE and Vitamin A
options.c: OPV booster, DPT booster, JE vaccine a nd Vitamin A
options.d: OPV Booster, DPT booster, MR and Vitamin A

mcqs.explanation: Vaccines to be given at 16 months of age are OPV booster, DPT booster, MR, JE, and Vitamin A. The child should receive routine doses of t he measles vaccine according to the schedule irrespective of the measles supplementary immunisation activity (SIA) dose. So, the second dose of the measles vaccine is also given. Japanese Encephalitis (JE) is endemic in rural agricultural areas, often associated with rice cultivation and flood irrigation. Vaccination for JE is given in endemic states only. Two doses of a live attenuated JE vaccine are given under the Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP) schedu le. U nder the Indian Academy of Pediatrics (IAP) schedule , two doses of a new vero cell-derived inactivated JE vaccine are given.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: A three and a half-year-old child, who is completely unimmunized, is brought to a PHC. Which of the following vaccines can be given to the child now?

options.d: BCG, DPT-1, OPV-1, Measles, Vit A

mcqs.explanation: DPT-1, OPV-1, measles and vitamin A can be given to this child of 3.5 years of age in his first immunization visit. BCG can only be given up to 1 year of age, according to the National Immunisation Schedule (NIS). Note: BCG can be given up to 5 years of age, as part of the catch-up immunization schedule which is by the Indian Academy of Paediatrics (IAP) and i s not followed in government setups. OPV can be given till 5 years of age. Measles can be given till 5 years of age. DPT can be given till 7 years of age (with booster doses).395

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old girl is brought to your clinic for routine immunization. According to the National Immunisation Schedule, which of the following would you administer?
mcqs.explanation: At 5 years of age, the 2nd booster dose of DPT must be given along with the 9th (final) dose of vitamin A. 1st booster dose of DPT is given at 16 – 24 months of age. 1st dose of vitamin A is given at 9th month and the 2nd dose is given at 16 months followed by one dose every 6 months thereafter until the age of 5. Note: DPT booster + Vitamin A is a better answer than DPT booster + OPV because the 9th (final) dose of vitamin A must be given at 5 years but OPV at 5 years is an optional vaccine.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: A 9-year-old child is brought to the PHC for receiving the JE vaccine. The nurse cleans the injection site with a spirit swab and injects the live attenuated JE vaccine subcutaneously on the left upper arm. Which of the following statements is true regarding this scenario?

options.a: The procedure of administering the vaccine is wrong
options.b: The site of administering the JE vaccine is inappropriate
options.c: The JE vaccine cannot be administered under routine i mmunization in a PHC after 2 years of age
options.d: Only live attenuated JE vaccine is currently under use

mcqs.explanation: The procedure of administration is wrong as it is not advisable to clean the injection site with a spirit swab because some of the live components of the vaccine are killed if they come in contact with spirit. The child is eligible to receive the Japanese Encephalitis (JE) vaccine through routine immunization till 15 years of age. Live attenuated JE vaccine is administered in the left upper arm subcutaneously. JENVAC is a new inactivated vero cell culture derived JE vaccine produce d b y Bharath Biotech International limited in India. It is a Kolar strain-derived vaccine. The recommended dose is 0.5ml which is given intramuscularly at left anterolateral aspect of midthigh, 4 weeks apart starting from 1 year of age. Although a booster dose is recommended at a later period, the appropriate time for booster dose administration is not clear. JEEV is another inactivated vero cell culture derived vaccine from the SA-14-14-2 strain. The recommended dose i s: • - 3 years: 2 doses of 0.25 ml on 0 and 28 days • >3years, adolescents, and adults: 2 doses of 0.5ml on 0 and 28 days • A booster dose of this vaccine is suggested to be given after 12 months of primary vaccination in non-endemic areas. The inactivated vaccines are currently under the recommendation of IAP. Under the Universal Immunization Programme (UIP), a live attenuated vaccine is given.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Which of the following was launched to ensure complete immunization of children?
mcqs.explanation: Mission Indradhanush was launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in 2014 to fully immunize children (>90%) who are either partially immunized or completely unimmunized by 2020. It was later modified in 2017 to the Intensified Mission Indradhanush, to achieve the same goal by December 2018.396 Intensified Mission Indradhanush includes 12 vaccine-preventable diseases (updated from the 7 diseases that Mission Indradhanush focussed on). 4 rounds of immunization are proposed to be held for 7 days each month (from the 7th- 13th of each month). The diseases included in Mission Indradhanush are: • TB • Polio • Hep B • Diphtheria • Pertussis • Tetanus • Measles The diseases included recently in Intensified Mission Indradhanush are: • Rotavirus diarrhoea • Rubella (a s M R vaccine) • H . influenzae B diseases (as part of the pentavalent vaccine) • Pneumococcal meningitis • Japanese Encephalitis The Intensified Mission Indradhanush 2.0: The government of India introduced IMI 2.0 to accelerate the vaccine drive and extend the coverage to children and pregnant women in identified districts and blocks from December 2019- March 2020. Note: Currently, the government has completed Intensified Mission Indradhanush 5.0: Intensified Miss ion I ndradhanush (IMI 5.0), the flagship routine immunization campaign of the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare concluded all 3 rounds in October 2023. This is the first campaign to be conducted across all the districts in the country and includes children up to 5 years of age (Previous campaigns included children up to 2 years of age). It also had a special focus on improvement of Measles and Rubella vaccination coverage.397

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: You are visiting a rural area for a vaccination drive conducted under the Intensified Mission Indradhanush scheme. Which of the following vaccines would you not administer in this vaccination drive?
mcqs.explanation: Typhoid vaccine is not a part of the Intensified Mission Indradhanush scheme. The Intensified Mission Indradhanush scheme has been introduced to ensure full immunization (>90%) by December 2018. It now includes 12 vaccine-preventable diseases (VPDs) (updated from the 7 that Mission Indradhanush focussed on). 4 rounds of immunization are proposed to be held for 7 days each month (from the 7th-13th of each month). The diseases included in Mission Indradhanush are: • TB • P olio • Hep B • Diphtheria • Pertussis • Tetanus • Measles The diseases included recently in Intensified Mission Indradhanush are: • Rotavirus diarrhoea • Rubella (as MR vaccine) • H. influenzae B diseases (as part of the pentavalent vaccine) • Pneumococcal meningitis • Japanese Encephalitis The purpose of Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI) is to reach each and every child under 2 years of age and all those pregnant women who have been left uncovered under the routi ne398 immunization coverage.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the National Deworming Programme?

options.a: It is conducted in the months of March and September
options.b: Free tablets are given to children up to the age of 15 years
options.c: It is carried out in schools and anganwadis
options.d: Age appropriate dose of tablet metronidazole is recommended

mcqs.explanation: The National Deworming programme is carried out in schools and anganwadis. It is conducted twice a year, in the months of February and August, covering all the children from the age of 1 to 19 years. All the children are given age-appropriate dose of tablet albendazole. In the states of Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, it is carried out only once a year (as the prevalence is <20% in these states).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke?

options.a: No separate centres for stroke, DM and cancer
options.b: Implementation in over 10 districts in 5 states
options.d: Subcentre h as facility for diagnosis and treatment

mcqs.explanation: District hospital has specialized facilities for the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke (NPCDCS). The NPCDCS has separate components for cancer and other non-communicable diseases like diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and stroke. It has been implemented in over 100 districts in 21 states. At the subcentre level under NPCDCS, screening and referral are done. Note: The National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke( NPCDCS) h as been changed to the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases(NP-NCD) to include new diseases and new health initiatives. The new diseases included in the NP-NCD are: • Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease • Chronic Kidney disease399 • Asthma and Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease • ST elevation myocardial infarction

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a false statement about the Indian Hypertension Control Initiative (IHCI)?

options.a: The IHCI monitoring personnel includes cardiovascular health officers and senior treatment supervisors
options.b: Provision of real-time blood pressure monitoring for all patients via information systems
options.c: The IHCI provides 30-day medication for individuals registered for hypertension management
options.d: The target is a 90% reduction in the prevalence of hypertension by the year

mcqs.explanation: The false statement about the Indian Hypertension Control Initiative is a 90% reduction in the prevalence of hypertension by the year 2025. The IHCI is an initiative by the MoHFW, WHO, ICMR, and state governments to control hypertension in India. It has adopted the goal of "25 by 25" to reduce the prevalence of hypertension in India by 25% by 2025. The activities of IHCI are monitored by the cardiovascular health officers (CVHO's) at the state and district level and by the sen ior t reatment supervisors ( STS's) at the sub-district level. The IHCI has strengthened the prevention of hypertension by ensuring the provision of antihypertensive medications for 30 days to all patients registered under the IHCI. The 5 components of IHCI are: • Use of standardized hypertension treatment protocols approved by national and global policies. • Availability of recommended protocol drugs to provide a regular and uninterrupted supply of medications. • Task-sharing a nd team-based care involving nurses, health workers, and ASHAs to improve treatment compliance. • Patient-centered services provide easy access to BP monitoring at Health & wellness centers and PHCs. • Information systems that provide real-time BP monitoring to improve patient follow-ups: Use of the "Simple App" in all IHCI states. *Note: Amlodipine, telmisartan, and chlorthalidone are the drugs of choice in the standardized treatment protocols of t he IHCI.400

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Under the National Programme for Control of Blindness & Visual Impairment, NGO eye hospi tals a re considered as:
mcqs.explanation: NGO eye hospitals are considered secondary level centres under the National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment (NPCBVI). Levels of eye care centres according to NPCBVI: • Primary level: Sub-district level hospitals, community health centres, mobile ophthalmic units, upgraded PHCs, and link workers. • Secondary level: District hospitals and NGO eye hospitals. • Tertiary level: Regional institutes of ophthalmology and medical colleges. The g oal of NPCBVI is to reduce the prevalence of blindness to 0.25% by 2025.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is used to measure the output of the National Programme for Control of Blindness & Visual Impairment?

options.a: Number of cases of refractory errors corrected
options.b: Number of cataract surgeries leading to sight restoration
options.c: Number of cases of childhood blindness detected and cured
options.d: Prevalence of blindness reduced by 0.5% per yea r

mcqs.explanation: The measure of the output of the National Programme for Control of Blindness & Visual Impairment (NPCBVI) is indicated by the number of cataract surgeries leading to sight restoration. The most common cause of low vision in India is cataract (low vision is visual acuity <6/18- 6/60).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Which of the following diseases is not a part of the Vision 2020 programme in India?
mcqs.explanation: Onchocerciasis is not a part of the Vision 2020 programme in India. It is a part of the Global Vision 2020 programme.401 Global Vision 2020 India Vision 2020 CataractRefractive errors and low visionChildhood blindne ssTrachoma CataractRefractive errors and low visionChildhood blindne ss Onchocerciasis Glaucoma Diabetic Retinopathy Corneal blindness

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman from a rural area registers under Janani Suraksha Yojana. Which of the following services would not be provided to her under this scheme?

options.a: Safe motherhood services under Vandematharam scheme

mcqs.explanation: The Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) does not provide STD counseling. Janani Suraksha Yojana is a safe motherhood intervention launched under National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality by promoting institutional delivery among poor pregnant women. The services provided by the JSY are: • Cash is disbursed to the mother at the institution for having an institutional delivery. • Safe motherhood services (IFA tablets, TT vaccination) under the Vandemataram scheme. • V illage health and nutrition day • Maternal death review • Pregnancy tracking: ASHA worker/Anganwadi Worker (AWW) or any other link worker help in monitoring antenatal check-ups, and post-delivery care. • Safe abortion services: mifepristone followed by misoprostol and manual vacuum aspiration.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Where and how often is the Village Health Nutrition Day conducted?

options.c: Once every two weeks in PHC
options.d: Once every two weeks in Anganwadi

mcqs.explanation: Village Health Nutrition Day is conducted once a month in the Anganwadi centres in the village itself. The villagers interact with health workers a nd are provided with basic services and information about health care.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: A 20-day old baby is gasping for air and not feeding properly. The mother has no money to go to the nearby hospital. Which national programme has provisions to benefit this woman to take her baby to the health facility?
mcqs.explanation: The Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) has provisions for free transport of pregnant women and sick infants from: • home to the health facilities • between facilities in case of a referral • back home from the health facilities The provisions of JSSK include:402 • Free transport • Free treatment • Free drugs and consumables • Free diagnostics and diet • Free and cashless delivery • Free C-Section • Free provision of blood Note: Previously under JSSK, the free entitlements were provided only for sick newborns till 30 days after birth. Now it is expanded to cover infants also.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: The Navjat Shishu Suraksha Karyakram was designed for which of the following demographic groups?
mcqs.explanation: The Navjat Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (NSSK) was designed to train health personnel in basic newborn care and resuscitation. The training is aimed to improve the d elivery of excellent newborn care at every point and is usually done for 2 days.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: A 10-year-old girl has just started menstruating. Under which of the following national programmes, she will be provided with a pack of sanitary napkins by the ASHA worker in her village?
mcqs.explanation: The girl will be provided with a pack of 6 sanitary napkins for 6 Rupees (called Freedays) by the ASHA worker through the Menstrual Hygiene Scheme under the Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK). RKSK focuses on: • Development of adolescent population (10-19 years). • Weekly Iron and Folic Acid supplementation (100mg Fe + 500 mcg Folic Acid) • Menstrual hygiene: A pack of 6 sanitary napkins f or 6 Rupees (called Freedays) by the ASHA. • It also includes enhancement of mental health and prevention of substance abuse and violence. Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is a government-sponsored savings program for parents of girl children <10 years age. It helps parents to set aside money for their female child's potential college and marriage expenses by opening an account at any post office branch or any commercial bank approved by the central government. Kishori Shakti Y ojana (KSY) seeks to empower adolescent girls, so as to enable them to take charge of their lives. The objectives are to: • improve the nutritional, health and development status of adolescent girls • promote awareness of health, hygiene, nutrition and family care • opportunities for learning life skills403 • going back to school • help them gain a better understanding of their social environment • take initiatives to become productive members of society. Recent update: Department of Pharmaceuticals under Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers has recently launched 'Suvidha' (100% Oxo-biodegradable Sanitary Napkin), under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) on World menstrual hygiene day. 'Swachhta, Swasthya and Suvidha' will be available for R s. 1 per pad over 3200 Janaushadhi Kendras for the underprivileged women of India.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is not true about POSHAN Abhiyan?

options.a: It is a programme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development
options.b: The goals are to achieve improvement in neonatal m ortality
options.c: Launched on the date of International Women's Day
options.d: Targets to reduce low birth weight by 2% per annum

mcqs.explanation: The goal of POSHAN Abhiyaan /National Nutrition Mission (NNM) is to achieve an improvement in the nutritional status during the next three years beginning 2017-18. It is a flagship programme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD). Its target population include: • children from 0-6 years • adolescent girls • pregnant women • lactating mothers The logo is:404 The following image depicts the targets of this mission:Note: Nikshay Poshan Yojana is a government scheme in India to provide Rs.500 per month for TB patients to buy food.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the objective of the Ujjawala Scheme?

options.a: Provide LPG connections to families below poverty line
options.d: Provide LED bulbs in every household

mcqs.explanation: The Ujjawala Scheme is for the prevention of trafficking and for the rescue, rehabilitation, and reintegration of victims of trafficking for commercial sexual exploitation. The Ujjwala Yojana (note spelling without "a") is for providing 5 crores of free cooking LPG connections to all families below the poverty line till 2019. The Ujala Scheme (Unnat Jyoti by A ffordable LEDs and Appliances for All) is the largest domestic lighting project in the world, launched under the Ministry of Power. It aims at promoting the use405 of energy-efficient LED bulbs in every household in the country. INSPIRE strategy is a set of 7 evidence-based strategies introduced to select, implement, monitor, and evaluate effective policies, programs, and services to prevent and respond to violence against children.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: An ASHA worker is offering services under the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan in her village. All of the following services will be provided by h er e xcept:

options.d: Information, education, communication and public awareness

mcqs.explanation: Water pollution is not managed under the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan. The Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was launched in 2014 with an aim to eradicate open-air defecation by the year 2019 through the construction o f 12 million toilets. The two sub-missions of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan are Swachh Bharat Mission Gramin (SBM-G) and Swachh Bharat Mission Urban (SBM-U). • Components of this mission include: • Household toilets including improving unsanitary latrines • Community toilets • Public toilets • Solid waste management • Information, education, communication, and public awareness • Capacity building and administrative & office expenses

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about the Ayushman Bharat-National Health Protection Mission?

options.a: Government provides health insurance cover of up to Rs. 5,00,000 per family per year
options.b: The limit of the family size that is covered is up to 7 members
options.c: All pre-existing diseases of the individual are covered
options.d: It covers secondary and tertiary care hospitalization

mcqs.explanation: There is no cap on family size or the age of the members. All the families listed under the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) database are covered as per the defined criteria. The following are the benefits provided under this program: • Health insurance cover of up to Rs. 5,00,000 per family per year. • All families listed in the SECC database, as per the defined criteria, will be covered. There is no cap on family size and age of members. • Free treatment is available at all public and empanelled private hospitals • B oth secondary and tertiary care hospitalization is covered. • All pre-existing diseases are covered. Hospitals cannot deny treatment. • To control costs, the payments for treatment will be done on a package rate (to be defined by the Government in advance) basis. • Cashless and paperless access to quality health care services. Logo:406

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding Rajiv Gandhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana?

options.a: Unemployment allowance is not given in case of closure of factory
options.b: Unemployment allowance is given in case of employment injury
options.c: Allowance is given at 50% of the daily wage for a maximum of 2 years
options.d: To qualify for the scheme, worker must have worked for more than 2 years

mcqs.explanation: Unemployment allowance under Rajiv Gandhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana (RGSKY) is given at the rate of 50% of daily wage for a maximum of 2 years. RGSKY is a scheme of ESI that provides unemployment allowance to an insured person going out of employment involuntarily, on account of: • closure of a factory or establishment • retrenchment (laying off employees due to economic difficulty) • permanent disability due to nonemployment injury Allowance and eligibility criteria of Rajiv G andhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana (updated in 2019): • The allowance is given at the rate of 50% of the daily wage for a maximum of 2 years.407 • To qualify for the scheme the worker must have worked in that setup for >3 years. Note: Disability due to employment injury is covered under disablement benefits of ESI Act, 1948. • Temporary disability: 90% of wages until disablement lasts. • Permanent disability: 90% of wages as a life pension on the basis of loss of earning capacity. • Dependants benefit: 90% of wage as monthly payment to the dependants of the deceased person, in cases where death occurs due to employment i njury or occupational hazards.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Which of the following does the Laqshya initiative launched recently by the Government of India refer to?

options.a: Initiative for providing free sanitary pads
options.b: Initiative to provide vaccination to under-5 children
options.c: Initiative f or labour room quality improvement
options.d: Initiative to provide affordable healthcare to all

mcqs.explanation: The Laqshya initiative launched recently by the Government of India refers to the initiative for labour room quality improvement. There is enough evidence to support the fact that improving the quality of care in labour rooms, especially on the day of birth, is crucial to maternal and neonatal survival. Laqshya is expected to improve the quality of care being provided to the pregnant mother in the labour room and maternity operation theatres, t hereby preventing the undesirable adverse outcomes associated with childbirth. This initiative is implemented in government medical colleges besides district hospitals, and high delivery load sub-district hospitals, and community health centres. It plans to conduct quality certification of labour rooms and also incentivize facilities achieving the targets outlined. The goal is to reduce preventable maternal and new-born mortality, morbidity, and s tillbirths a ssociated with the care around delivery in labour room and maternity OT , and ensure respectful maternity care.

mcqs.explanation: The image shown is the new logo of the 360-degree holistic Family Planning Campaign. Logo of other options:408 "Beti bachao Beti padhao."India Newborn Action Plan (INAP)409 The logo of Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakaram (JSSK)

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: What is the main objective of the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Jan-aushadhi Pariyojana?

options.a: Improve maternal and child health services
options.b: Make quality, generic medicines affordable to all
options.c: Enhance quality of life and increase employment for the differently abled
options.d: Promote cleanliness and enhance quality of healthcare facilities in India

mcqs.explanation: The Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Jan-aushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) carries the objective of making quality, generic medicines affordable for everyone, especially the lower socio-economic groups. BPPI (Bureau of Pharma PSUs of India), under the Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers, is the implementation agency for PMBJP. The mission of this programme includes creating awareness and demand for generic medicines t hrough e ducation and supply of such medications. Kayakalp programme is a national initiative launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) under Swachh Bharat Abhiyan to promote cleanliness and enhance the quality of healthcare facilities in India.410

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: The Mid Day Meal P rogramme aims to supplement:
mcqs.explanation: Under the Mid-Day Meal (MDM) scheme, supplementary nutrition provided must cover at least 1/2 of total daily protein requirement and 1/3rd of total daily energy requirement of children in schools. The MDM scheme is also called School Lunch Programme and has been operational since 1961 in India. Currently, it functions under the broad coverage of the Minimum Needs Programme. Some other principles of the MDM are: • The meal provided under the MDM should only be a supplement a nd not a substitute for home diets . • The cost of meals should be reasonably low. • The meal should be easy to cook in schools. • Locally available foods must be used, for as far as possible. • The menu should be regularly changed to avoid monotony. Note: In September 2021, the Mid-Day Meal Scheme was renamed PM POSHAN or Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is not true regarding the Vandematharam scheme?

options.b: Its aim is to provide safe motherhood services
options.c: An MBBS graduate or an obstetrician can volunteer
options.d: IFA tablets and TT injections are provided by District Medical Officers

mcqs.explanation: The Vandematharam scheme does not include free treatment in private clinics. Vandematharam scheme is a voluntary scheme f or providing safe motherhood services. It can be volunteered by an obstetrician, maternity home, nursing home, lady doctor or an MBBS graduate. IFA tablets, OCPs, and TT injections are provided by the respective District Medical Officers (DMOs) to the Vandematharam doctors or clinics for free distribution to beneficiaries. Cases needing special care and treatment can be referred to government hospitals.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a component of the scheme depicted by the logo given below?
mcqs.explanation: National Health Protection Mission is a component of the Ayushman Bharat scheme. Ayushman Bharat-National Health Protection Mission (AB-NHPM) aims to build a comprehensive need-based health care service and targets to build a 'New India 2022'. Its components are: • Creation of 1,50,000 Health and Wellness Centres- these centres will provide Comprehensive Primary Health Care (CPHC), covering both maternal and child health services and non-communicable diseases, including free essential drugs and diagnostic services. • National H ealth Protection Mission (NHPM) provides health protection cover to poor and vulnerable families, screening for non-communicable diseases, and follow-up of hospitalization cases among others.411 Beneficiary Level: • The government provides health insurance cover of up to Rs. 5,00,000 per family per year. • All families listed in the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) database as per defined criteria will be covered. No cap on family size and age of members. • Priority to a girl child, women, and senior citizens. • Free treatment is available at all public and empanelled private hospitals in times of need. • Covers secondary and tertiary care hospitalization. • 1,35 0 m edical packages covering surgery, medical and daycare treatments, cost of medicines, and diagnostics. • All pre-existing diseases are covered. Hospitals cannot deny treatment. • Cashless and paperless access to quality health care services. • Hospitals will not be allowed to charge any additional money from beneficiaries for the treatment. • Can reach out for information, assistance, complaints, and grievances to a 24X7 helpline number.412

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Which of the following vaccines has not been introduced to the immunization programme in India?
mcqs.explanation: Influenza vaccine (Flu shot) has not been introduced to the National Immunization Programme in India. The Influenza vaccine provides protection against viral flu caused by the influenza virus. Note: Bacterial Hemophilus influenzae type-b (Hib) vaccine is different from the viral influenza (Flu) vaccine. HiB is a part of the pentavalent vaccine.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: The POCSO Act is related to which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: The POCSO (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences) Act is related to child sexual abuse. POCSO Act defines a child as any p erson below eighteen years of age. It defines different forms of sexual abuse, including penetrative and non-penetrative assault, as well as sexual harassment and pornography. The Act deems a sexual assault to be "aggravated" under certain circumstances, such as when the abused child is mentally ill or when the abuse is committed by a person in a position of trust or authority vis-\340-vis the child, like a family member, police officer, teacher, or doctor. People who tr affic c hildren for sexual purposes are also punishable under the provisions relating to abetment in the Act. The Act prescribes stringent punishment graded as per the gravity of the offence, with a maximum term of rigorous imprisonment for life and a fine.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Mass drug administration is not done for which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Mass drug administration is not done in case of vitamin A deficiency.413 Mass Drug Administration (MDA) is the administration of a drug to an entire concerned population irrespective of age and gender. For example, antimalarials are given as MDA in malaria-endemic island communities and in low-endemic non-island settings approaching elimination, where there is minimal risk of re-introduction of infection, good access to treatment, and implementation of vector control and surveillance. Vitamin A prophylaxis is given under National I mmunization S chedule (NIS) only to children up to 5 years. It is given as mass prophylaxis and not as a drug for treatment. Vitamin A as a treatment is given only to a child with features of vitamin A deficiency and such doses are not instituted to everyone in the community. Therefore, it is not considered under MDA. On the other hand, MDA is done in scabies (ivermectin), worm infestation (albendazole), and filariasis (DEC + albendazole).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: Monetary benefit is measured in which of the following analyses?
mcqs.explanation: The monetary benefit is measured in a cost-benefit analysis . In cost-benefit analysis, the economic benefits of any program are compared with the cost of the program. The benefits are expressed in monetary terms to determine whether a given programme is economically sound and to select the best out of several alternate programmes. The main drawback with this technique is that the benefits in the health field, as a result of a particular programme, cannot always be expressed in monetary terms. We generally express t he benefit in terms of births or deaths prevented, or illness avoided or overcome. In cost-effective analysis, the benefit is expressed in terms of results achieved. (Eg: number of lives saved or number of days free from disease). Input-output analysis: how much input is needed to produce a unit amount of output. In the health field, input refers to all health service activities which consume resources (manpower, money, materials, and time); and output refers to usef ul o utcomes such as cases treated, lives saved , or inoculations performed. Network analysis: a network is a graphic plan of all events and activities to be completed in order to reach an end objective. Management Methods in Health Programmes:Methods based on behavioral sciences Quantitative methods Organisational designPerson nel managementCommunicat ionInformation systemsMana gement by objectives (MBO) Cost–Benefit analysisCost -Eff ective analysisCost –Accounti ngInput–Output analysisMod elSystems analysisNetwork a nalysis- Includes Programme Evaluation and Review Tech nique (PERT ) and Critical Pa th Method (CPM)Planning–P rogramming –Budgeting Syst em (PPBS)Work samplingDe cision making414

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: As per NCEP- A TP III, which of the following is not a criterion for metabolic syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: As per NCEP- ATP III, high LDL is not included in the definition criteria of metabolic syndrome. Metabolic syndrome is present if three or more of the following five criteria are met, which is given by NCEP-ATP III (National Cholesterol Education Program and Adult Treatment Panel III). It includes: • Central obesity: waist circumference >102 cm (M), >88 cm (F) • Hypertriglyceridemia: triglyceride level \034 150 mg/dL • Low HDL cholesterol: <40 mg/dL and <50 mg/dL f or men and women, respectively . • Hypertension: blood pressure \034130 mmHg systolic or \034 85 mmHg diastolic. • Fasting plasma glucose level: \034100 mg/dL or previously diagnosed type 2 diabetes.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: In Sustainable Development Goal 3, the target 3.1 aims to reduce the Maternal Mortality Ratio by 2030 to ____ (per 1 lakh live births):
mcqs.explanation: In Sustainable Development Goal 3, the target 3.1 aims to reduce the Maternal Mortality Ratio by 2030 to <70 per 1 lakh live births. There are 17 global goals and 169 targets set for 2030 as part of the official Sustainable Development Goals of the Agenda 2030.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: As per the new National Policy for Rare Diseases, financial support of up to Rs. 20 lakhs can be given to which group of rare diseases?
mcqs.explanation: 415 As per the new National Policy for Rare Diseases, a provision for financial support of up to Rs. lakhs under the umbrella scheme of Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi is proposed for the treatment of rare diseases that require a one-time treatment (listed under Group 1 in the rare disease policy). National Policy for Rare Diseases is a comprehensive policy for the prevention and management of rare diseases. The policy lists rare diseases under 3 groups: • Group 1: Disorders amenable to o ne-time curative treatment: • Disorders amenable to hematopoietic stem cell transplantation eg: lysosomal storage disorders • Disorders amenable to organ transplantation eg: glycogen storage disorders, urea cycle disorders, ADPKD, etc. • Group 2: Diseases requiring long term/ lifelong treatment having a relatively lower cost of treatment: • This group includes disorders managed with special dietary formulae/ hormone/ specific drugs. eg: phenylketonuria, osteogenesis i mperfecta , etc. • Group 3: Diseases for which definitive treatment is available but treatment is lifelong or expensive: • This group includes diseases such as Pompe disease, Duchenne muscular dystrophy, etc. The objectives of the policy are: • Lowering the high cost of treatment for rare diseases with an increased focus on indigenous research. • Creating a national hospital-based registry of rare diseases. • Early screening and prevention through prima ry a nd secondary health care infrastructure, and through counselling for the high-risk parents. • Crowdfunding mechanism in which corporates and individuals will be encouraged to extend financial support.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: National Health Programmes III - NIS, JSY, RBSK...
mcqs.question: You are a medical officer at a PHC. Which of the following would you advise for mass prophylaxis/ treatment for anemia?

options.a: FeSO4 + Vit C + Folate + Vit B

mcqs.explanation: Among the given options, FeSO4 + vitamin C + Folate + vitamin B12 may be considered for mass prophylaxis against anemia. Vit C enhances the absorption of iron from the stomach by acting as a reducing substance. Subclinical folate deficiency is seen in up to 30% of North I ndian pregnant women. Moreover , it may be masked by widespread iron deficiency. It is, for this reason, iron and folate supplementation is carried out in national programmes. Clinical vitamin B12 deficiency is not commonly encountered, but subclinical cases might be seen in up to 30% of adults and children due to widespread restriction to consumption of vegetarian products only. Hence supplementing vitamin B12 is a good idea provided the cost factor is not an issue.
