Op tion B : Iron (III) hydroxide polymaltose was marketed as being superior to iron sulfate in terms of efficacy, but it lacked any data to back up the evidence.416 Option C: Ferrous fumarate may be considered for the treatment of iron deficiency anemia with similar efficacy as that of ferrous sulfate. Option D: Injection iron sucrose or any parenteral form is not used as a first-line option. It is only indicated if the oral form is not tolerated.417

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a demographic process?
mcqs.explanation: Morbidity is not a demographic process. Demography refers to the study of the population. Demographic processes include: • Fertility • Mortality • Marriage • Migration • Social mobility These processes continuously bring about changes in the population size, composition, and distribution.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: In which stage of the demographic cycle does the death rate start declining?
mcqs.explanation: The death rate starts declining in stage 2 or the early expanding phase of the demographic cycle.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: In which stage of the demographic cycle does the birth rate start declining?
mcqs.explanation: The birth rate starts declining in stage 3 or the late expanding phase of the demographic cycle. India is currently in this stage of the demographic cycle. The year 1921 is called the year of the great divide in India. This is because, since 1921, the absolute number of people getting added to the population during each decade has been on the rise. This is the year in which India moved from stage 1 to stage 2 of the demographic cycle.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: A group of demographers studied the changes in the birth and death rates of two countries, A and B from the year 2001 to 2011. The collected data is g ive n below. In which stages of the demographic cycle are countries A and B in respectively?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, country A is in stage 2 and country B is in stage 4 of the demographic cycle.423 According to the given data, in country A, the high birth rate has remained unchanged with a decline in the death rate. This will result in an exponential increase in the population. This means country A is in the early expanding stage of the demographic cycle. In country B, the low birth rate and death rates have remained unchanged. Thus, the population will attain a plateau phase and remain stationary. This means country B is in the low stationary stage of the demographic cyc le.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the fifth stage of the demographic cycle?

options.d: Birth rate falls below death rate

mcqs.explanation: In stage 5 of the demographic cycle, the birth rate falls below the death rate. In this stage, the death rate attains a low stable rate while the birth rate keeps declining. Thus, the curve of the birth rate will cross the curve of the death rate in a graph of the demographic cycle and falls further below. The demographic gap is negative and the population is declining. So, this stage is known as the declining stage.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: While studying the birth and death rates of a country, a demographer found it to be in the early expanding stage of the demographic cycle. Which of the following findings would lead him to such a conclusion?

options.a: Increased birth rate and decreased death rates
options.c: Decreased birth rate and increased death rates
options.d: Unchanged birth rate and decreased death rates

mcqs.explanation: Early expanding stage (stage 2) of the demographic cycle is characterized by an unchanged birth rate and decreasing death rate.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: A researcher is studying the demographic cycle of various countries. In which stages of the cycle will she notice an increase and a decrease in the demographic gap respectively?
mcqs.explanation: The demographic gap starts increasing in stage 2 and starts decreasing in stage 3. The demographic gap refers to the difference between birth rate and death rate which develops when a country undergoes a demographic transition. In stage 2 of the demographic cycle, the death rate declines but the birth rate remains unchanged. Hence, the demographic gap increases and reaches a maximum by the end of stage 2. In s tage 3, both the death rate and birth rate are declining so the demographic gap starts decreasing.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: At which stage of the demographic cycle will the demographic g ap be maximum?
mcqs.explanation: The demographic gap starts increasing and becomes maximum in the early expanding phase of the demographic cycle.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the stage of demographic cycle marked by the red arrow?
mcqs.explanation: 424 The marked stage is the late expanding phase (stage 3) of the demographic cycle. A demographic gift or demographic dividend is seen in this stage. This refers to the presence of a higher number of economically productive individuals (young and middle-aged adults) in the population due to a higher birth rate in the previous demographic phase (phase 2). India is currently experiencing the demographic gift. The birth rate starts declining alongside a death rate that continues t o fall in stage 3 causing a decline in the demographic gap. The death rate declines further and the birth rate falls in this stage.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: In which stage of the demographic cycle will the phenomenon of a demographic trap be maximally seen?
mcqs.explanation: The phenomenon of a demographic trap is seen maximally in the early expanding stage (stage 2). This phenomenon refers to a period in which there is high fertility and birth rate and a declining death rate. The population grows exponentially in this stage and this growing population exceeds the national or regional carrying capacity. Countries i n this stage are said to be caught in a demographic trap.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: While conducting a field study in a village, you found the birth and death rates of the population to be 42 and 31 respectively. What is the current annual growth rate of this population?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, the current annual growth rate is 1.1%. Here, the birth rate is 42 i.e 42 live births per 1000 population, and the death rate is 31 i.e 31 deaths per 1000 population. Current annual growth rate = crude birth rate – crude death rate. So, current annual growth rate = 42-31= 11 per 1000 population or 1.1%.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: The population of a country is 1 lakh in the year 2000 and its annual growth rate is 2%. By which year will the population of this country become 2 lakhs?
mcqs.explanation: For the given country, its population would become 2 lakhs i.e, double the population from the year 2 000, by the year 2035. As per the Malthusian growth model, when the annual growth rate is 1%, the population doubles in 70 years. Therefore, when the annual growth rate is 2%, the population will double in 35 years. The Malthusian growth model/ rule of 70: The growth rate of India is estimated at 1% as per 2020 UN data. Therefore, it falls in the rapidly growing phase of population growth.Rating Annual growth r ate Population doubles in Slow growth <0.5% >139 years425 Rating Annual growth r ate Population doubles in Moderate growt h from 0.5% ~139 years Rapid growth from 1% 70 years Very rapid grow th from 1.5% approximately 50 yea rs Explosive growt h from 2% 35 years Explosive growt h from 3% -25 years

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: What was the population of India, as of 2021?
mcqs.explanation: The population of India, as of 2021, was around 1.39 billion. This is as per UN 2021 data.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: According to the 2021 UN data, what is India's population growth rate?
mcqs.explanation: According to UN data, India's population growth rate in 2021 was 1%. As per the last published SRS data of the Indian government, it was 1.2% in 2018. India's population is currently increasing at a rate of 16 million each year. It currently falls in the rapidly growing phase of population growth.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: You have been tasked with studying the age and sex structure of a population with high rates of female infanticide. Which of the following methods will you prefer to use?
mcqs.explanation: The age and sex structure of a population may be best represented using a population pyramid. It is a histogram that shows the distribution of ages across a population. It is divided down the center between male and female members of the population.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Demography I: Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth ...
mcqs.question: What does the age pyramid of India look like?

options.a: Broad at base and narrow at apex
options.c: Broad at apex and narrow at base
options.d: Broad in the middle and narrow at base

mcqs.explanation: The age pyramid of India is broad at the base and narrow at the top. This is typical of most developing nations.426

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a vital statistic?
mcqs.explanation: 433 Sex ratio is not a vital statistic, it is a population statistic. Demographic indicators have been divided into 2 parts: • Population statistics include - • Population size • Sex ratio • Density • Dependency ratio • Vital statistics include - • Birth rate • Death rate • Natural growth rate • Life expectancy at birth • Mortality rate • Fertility rate

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: While conducting a demographic study, you need to calculate the total dependency ratio of the study population. Which of the following will you include in the numerator while calculating this?

options.a: Population under 10 years and above 60 years
options.b: Population under 15 years and above 60 years
options.c: Population under 10 years and above 65 years
options.d: Population under 15 y ears and above 65 years

mcqs.explanation: Population under 15 years and above 65 years are part of the numerator used to calculate the total dependency ratio. This is because t his population is considered the dependant population.The dependant population includes children below 15 years of age and adults above 65 years of age. The total dependency ratio is the ratio of the combined dependent population to those in the age group of 15 - 65 years. It is also called the societal dependency ratio. It can also be divided into the young-age and old-age dependency ratios.434 Note: As of mid-year 2020, the dependency ratio of India is 48.7%.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: While studying a community, the researcher found 30% of the population to be below 15 years of age, and 10% was over 65 years of age. What is the total dependency ratio of this population?
mcqs.explanation: The total dependency ratio in this population is 66.6%. This can be calculated as follows.Here, the total population below 15 years of age is = 30% Total population above 65 years of age = 10% So, total population between 15-65 years of age = 100 - (30 + 10) = 60% Hence, dependency ratio in this population = 100* (30% + 10%)/60% = 66.6%

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is potential support ratio?

options.a: Number of persons aged 15 to 64 per child below 15 years or less
options.b: Number of persons aged 15 to 64 per older person aged 65 or more
options.c: Number of persons aged 15 to 64 per each older person aged >65 and younger person aged <
options.d: Number of persons aged 15 to 64 per each older person aged > 60 and younger person aged <

mcqs.explanation: The potential support ratio is the number of persons aged 15 to 64 per one older person aged 65 or more. It is the inverse of the old-age dependency ratio.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the major contributor to demographic burden?
mcqs.explanation: Demographic burden refers to an increase in the total dependency ratio. It is mostly caused by an increased old-age dependency ratio. The term demographic bonus denotes the decline in dependency ratio due to declining fertility. A decline in dependency ratio especially the young-age dependency ratio has been identified to be a key factor in the underlying rapid economic development.435 The potential support ratio is the number of persons aged 15 to 64 per one older person aged 65 or more. This is the inverse of the old-age dependency ratio.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following determines the carrying capacity of a population?
mcqs.explanation: The carrying capacity is the number of individuals of a population that can be supported for a period of time given the resources of that area. Thus, the carrying capacity is determined by the limiting resources of an area.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about crude birth rate?
mcqs.explanation: The numerator of crude birth rate only includes live births and does not include stillbirths. Crude birth r ate = No. of live births during the year x 1000/ Estimated mid-year population

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: As part of the national maternity benefit scheme, you have been tasked with conducting a study in a community of 5000 people. What is the expected number of pregnant women in this community if the crude birth rate is 30 per 1000 people?
mcqs.explanation: The expected number of pregnant females in the given community would be 165. Step 1: In the given question, the crude birth rate is 30 per 1000 people i.e 30 children are born from pregnant mothers for every 1000 people. Therefore there are 30 pregnant females per 1000 population. Step 2: Since the total population is 5000, the total no of pregnant females = 5000 x 30/1000 = Step 3: Since some pregnancies m ay not result in live births (abortions and stillbirths), a correction factor of 10% should be added to avoid the underestimation of the number of pregnancies. Pregnancy wastage (i.e 10% of total live births) =10 x 150/100=15. Step 4: Total pregnant females = total live births + pregnancy wastage = 150+15=165.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: According to NFHS-5, what is the sex ratio in India?
mcqs.explanation: According to the NFHS-5 (2019-21), the sex ratio in India is 1020 females per 1000 males. It has increased from the 2011 Census which had found a sex ratio of 9 40 females per 1000 males. The sex ratio at birth is 929 females per 1000 males.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: For a population of 10,000, what does a sex ratio of more than 1000 m ean?
mcqs.explanation: For a population of 10000, if the sex ratio is more than 1000, it means males are less than 5000 i.e., less than half the population.436 The sex ratio refers to the number of females per 1000 males. An ideal sex ratio would be 1000, indicating the population comprises an equal number of males and females. Sex ratio >1000 indicates that there are more females than males in a population. Sex ratio <1000 indicates that there are fewer females compared to males in the population.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the definition of the net reproduction rate?

options.a: No. of children that would be born to married women assuming fixed age specific fertility and mortality rate
options.b: No. of girls that would be born to married women assuming fixed age specific fertility and mortality rate
options.c: No. of female children a new born girl will bear during her lifetime assuming fixed age specific f ertility and mortality rate
options.d: No. of children a new born girl will bear during her lifetime assuming fixed age specific fertility and mortality rate

mcqs.explanation: Net reproduction rate (NRR) is defined as the number of daughters a newborn girl will bear during her lifetime assuming fixed age-specific f ertility and mortality rate. India is aiming for an NRR of 1 as it is equivalent to the two-child norm.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An epidemiologist would consider the growth of his study population to be inadequate if he found the NRR to be:
mcqs.explanation: If the NRR is less than 1, then the population growth of a community is said to be inadequate. Net reproduction rate (NRR) is the number of daughters a newborn girl will bear during her lifetime assuming age-specific fertility and mortality rates.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What should the net reproductive rate of a population be to attain a 2 child norm?
mcqs.explanation: The net reproductive rate (NRR) should be 1 to attain the 2 child norm.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In order to reach the demographic goal of NRR=1, the couple protection rate should exceed?
mcqs.explanation: In order to reach the demographic goal of NRR=1, the couple protection rate (CPR) should exceed 60%. This coincides with every couple having 2 children.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the denominator used in the formula for calculating the general fertility rate?

options.a: Total number of women in the population
options.c: Mid-year population of women in the reproductive age group
options.d: Total number of married women in the age group 15 –

mcqs.explanation: The denominator used to calculate the general fertility rate is mid-year population of women in the reproductive age group.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: To assess the effects of the national population policy, data is being collected at the PHC level. You have been asked to submit data regarding the approximate magnitude of completed family size in the population under your PHC. Which of the following indicators will you calculate?
mcqs.explanation: The total fertility rate is an indicator of the approximate magnitude of completed family size.437

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the infant mortality rate in India as per the SRS Statistical Report (2020)?
mcqs.explanation: The infant mortality rate (IMR) in India as per the SRS statistical report (2020) is 28 per 1000 live births. IMR is defined as the number of infant deaths for every 1000 live births. As per the National Family Health Survey - 5 (2019-2021), the IMR is 35.2 per 1000 live births. IMR is considered the best indicator of the availability, utilization, and effectiveness of health care.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Maternal mortality ratio (MMR) for a country is best given as __________
mcqs.explanation: Maternal mortality ratio is the number of maternal deaths in a given period per 100,000 live births d uring the same period.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the maternal mortality ratio in India according to the Special Bulletin on Maternal Mortality (2018-2020) based on SRS data?
mcqs.explanation: The maternal mortality ratio (MMR) in India according to the Special Bulletin (2018-2020) based on SRS data is 97. MMR is defined as the number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births. The most common causes of maternal mortality in India are postpartum hemorrhage and infections.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: While collecting data for the census, which of the following people would you consider to be literate?

options.a: A person who is able to read, write and understand in any language
options.b: A person who is not able to read or write but can sign legal documents
options.c: A person who is able to speak fluently in his native language but is not able to read or write
options.d: A person who is able to read, but may not be able to write

mcqs.explanation: A person is considered literate if he or she can read, write and understand in any language.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the denominator of the formula used to calculate effective literacy rate?

options.c: Population less than 15 years of age

mcqs.explanation: The denominator used to calculate the effective literacy rate is the population aged 7 years or more. It is calculated as follows. Effective literacy rate = Number of literate persons aged 7 and above x 100/ Population aged 7 and above in a given year. This rate is generally used in Indian censuses including those in 1991, 2001, and 2011 for estimating literacy.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are studying the literacy rate of a community with a total population of 10000. Out of these, there are 2000 children from 0-6 years of age, and 4000 literate individuals above 7 years of age. What is the effective literacy rate of this population?
mcqs.explanation: 438 The effective literacy rate of this population is 50%. It is calculated as follows, Effective literacy rate = (Number of literate persons aged 7 and above x 100) / population aged 7 and above in a given year. In the given scenario, people aged 7 years and above = 10000 - 2000 = 8000. Out of these 8000 people, 4000 are literate. Thus, effective literacy rate = 4000 x 100/8000 = 50%.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding the criteria for an urban Indian city?

options.b: Having a density of 390 persons per square km
options.c: At least half of the adult male population employed in occupations other than agriculture

mcqs.explanation: In an urban area, at least three-fourths of the adult male population are employed in occupations other than a griculture. In the Indian context, the urban areas are places: • having 5,000 or more inhabitants • having a density of not less than 1,000 persons per square mile or 390 per square kilometer • having pronounced urban characteristics • having at least three-fourths of the adult male population employed in pursuits other than agriculture439

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the number of eligible couples per 1000 population in India?
mcqs.explanation: There are approximately 150 – 180 eligible couples per 1000 population in India. An eligible couple refers to a currently married couple wherein the wife belongs to the reproductive age group (15-49 years of age).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Scope of modern concept of family planning services include all of the following except:
mcqs.explanation: Screening for HIV infection does not come under the purview of family planning. The modern concepts of family planning services include: • Proper spacing and limitation of birth • Advice on sterility • Education for parenthood • Sex education • Screening for p athological c onditions related to the reproductive system (e.g. cervical cancer) • Genetic counseling • Premarital consultation and examination • Pregnancy tests • Marriage counseling • Preparation of couples for the first child • Providing services to unmarried mothers • Teaching home economics and nutrition • Providing adoption services

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A study was conducted in a village with 180 eligible couples, to gather data on the different contraceptive methods used. The data obtained a re g iven below. What is the couple protection rate in the village?
mcqs.explanation: 446 Couple protection rate (CPR) is defined as the percentage of eligible couples effectively protected against childbirth by one or the other approved methods of family planning. In the given scenario, 60 out of 180 eligible couples are using different contraceptive methods. Therefore, CPR = (60/180) x 100 = 33%.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a barrier method of contraception?
mcqs.explanation: Lippes loop is an intrauterine device and not a barrier method of contraception. Barrier methods of contraception include: • Physical methods – male and female condoms, d iaphragm, vaginal sponge (Today) • Chemical methods – foam tablets, aerosols, creams, jellies, suppositories, and soluble films (C-films)

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A sexually active woman has been using Today sponge as a contraceptive. What does this contain?
mcqs.explanation: Today is a type of vaginal sponge that contains 9 – nonoxynol. Today is a barrier contraceptive inserted vaginally. It has to be left in place for 6 hours after coitus. It can lead to toxic shock syndrome if left in place for more than 24 hours (rarely).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a second-generation intra-uterine device?
mcqs.explanation: Nova T and Cu-T-380 Ag are second-generation intrauterine devices (IUD). IUD is a contraceptive method inserted into the uterine cavity. The different generations of IUDs include:447 • First-generation IUDs – inert or non-medicated devices like Lippes loop • Second-generation IUDs - medicated with metallic elements like copper eg: Cu-T-220 C, Nova T, Multi-load Cu-250, Multi-load Cu-375 • Third-generation IUDs – hormone-containing IUDs like progestasert, Mirena (LNG-20)

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following women will not be considered ideal candidates for IUD insertion?

options.b: A woman in a monogamous relationship
options.c: A woman with no access t o follow up
options.d: A woman who has at least one living child

mcqs.explanation: A woman with no access to follow-up is not considered an ideal candidate for IUD insertion. An ideal candidate for an IUD must have the following attributes: • Has at least one child • No history of pelvic disease448 • Normal menstrual periods • Must be willing to check IUD tail • Has access to follow up and for treatment of potential problems • Is in a monogamous relationship

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A patient who underwent an IUD insertion is most likely to develop which of the following in the future?
mcqs.explanation: Patients who underwent IUD insertion are most likely to develop vaginal bleeding in the future. Side effects and complications of IUDs include: • Vaginal bleeding – most common • Abdominal pain – second most common • Pelvic infection • Uterine perforation • Pregnancy - due to failure of contraception • Ectopic preg nancy • E xpulsion of the IUD • Cancer and teratogenicity

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Insertion of an IUD is not contraindicated in patients with which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Cardiac problems are not a contraindication for IUD usage. Contraindications for IUD usage include:Absolute contraindications Relativecontraindications Suspected pregnancyPIDVagi nal bleeding of unknown etio logyCarcinoma cervix/uterus/ adnexa /other pelvic tumors AnemiaMenorrhagiaHistory of PID since the last pregnan cyPurulent cervical discharge Distortions of the uterine cav ity due tofibroidsUterine mal formationsAn unmotivated p erson

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following has the longest period of use?
mcqs.explanation: Cu-T-380 A has the longest period of use (10 years).449 IUD Years of u se Progestase rt Cu-T-200 4 Nova T 5 LNG IUD 7-10 Cu-T-380 A 10

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You have prescribed an IUCD to a multiparous woman. Which of the following is not a mechanism of action for this type of contraceptive?
mcqs.explanation: Prevention of ovulation is not a mechanism of action of IUCDs. Mechanisms of action of IUCDs include: • Causing cellular and biochemical changes in the uterus and endometrium. • Prevention of sperm penetration due to changes in cervical mucus consistency. • Prevention of implantation by making the uterus hostile to it.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: All of the following are non-contraceptive benefits of oral contraceptive pills except?
mcqs.explanation: Oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) do not confer protection against thyroid dysfunction. OCP usage can confer protection against: • Benign breast diseases l ike fibroadenoma and fibrocystic disease • Ovarian cysts • Iron-deficiency anemia • Pelvic inflammatory disease • Ectopic pregnancy • Ovarian cancer

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In patients with which of the following conditions can OCPs be safely prescribed?
mcqs.explanation: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) is not a contraindication for prescribing OCPs. Absolute contraindications of OCPs: (CULT) • Cancers - breast and genital • Cardiac abnormalities450 • Congenital hyperlipidemia • Undiagnosed AUB • Liver disease • Thromboembolism - past or present history. Medical surveillance is required while prescribing OCPs if the patient is/or has: • Age more than 40 years • Chronic smoker and age over 35 years • Amenorrhea • Chronic renal disease • Diabetes mellitus • Epilepsy • In the first 6 months of nursing • Gall bladder disease • History of infrequent bleeding • Mild hypertension • Migraine

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A sexually active woman who was using barrier contraceptives is planning on switching to DMPA injectables. Which of the following is the correct dosage of this contraceptive?
mcqs.explanation: The dosage for injectable depot-medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA) is 150 mg every 3 months. It acts by: • Bringing changes in the cervical mucus • Making the endometrium hostile • Preventing ovulation Disadvantages include spotting and intermediate per vaginal bleeding.451

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is also known as the Billings method of contraception?
mcqs.explanation: Billings method of contraception is also known as the cervical mucus method (or ovulation method). It is a natural method of contraception. It is based on the observation of changes in the cervical mucus. At ovulation, the mucus is watery clear, smooth, slippery and profuse. After ovulation, it becomes thicker and scarce. The pattern of cervical mucus secretion during a menstrual cycle is given below:452

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most effective natural method of contraception?
mcqs.explanation: The most effective natural method of contraception is the symptothermic method. It combines: • Calendar method • Cervical mucus method • Basal body method. In this method, if a woman is not able to identify one sign, she can double-check with her interpretation of the other signs.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a condition to be fulfilled by a male patient undergoing sterilization?

options.b: Has at least one living child
options.c: Age should be more than 60 years

mcqs.explanation: A man should be below 60 years of age to be eligible for sterilization. Eligibility for male sterilization: • Clients should be at least 22 years old • Clients should be below the age of 60 years • Cli ents s hould be married • The couple should have at least one child, whose age is above one year unless the sterilization is medically indicated • Clients or their spouses must not have undergone sterilization in the past (not applicable in the cases of failure of previous sterilization) • Clients must be in a sound state of mind, so as to understand the full implications of sterilization453 • Mentally ill clients must be certified by a psychiatrist, and a statement should be given by the legal guardian/spouse regarding the soundness of the client's state of mind

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common cause of failure of vasectomy?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of failure of vasectomy is the mistaken identification of the vas. This can be avoided by examining a stained smear prepared by squeezing the vas on a glass slide. If facilities are available a histological examination is preferred. Causes of failure of vasectomy include: • Mistaken i dentification of the vas - most common • Spontaneous recanalization of the vas • Presence of more than one vas on one side • Sexual intercourse before the disappearance of sperms from the reproductive tracts

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is important i n the calculation of the pearl index?

options.c: Total number of women in the population

mcqs.explanation: The numerator used for calculation of the pearl index is total accidental pregnancies. Pearl index = Total accidental pregnancies x 1200/Total months of exposure

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: As part of the National family planning program, you are conducting a study in a village to gather data on the efficacy of a new contraceptive. 20 out of 100 women became pregnant in the village despite using this contraceptive for a period of 2 years continuously. What is the pearl index of this contraceptive?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, the pearl index is 10 per HWY. Here, the total number of accidental pregnancies i s 20. The total months of exposure are 24 months for each woman. Hence, the total months of exposure for 100 women are 24 x 100 = 2400. Pearl index = Total accidental pregnancies x 1200/ Total months of exposure Hence, pearl index= 20 x 1200/2400 = 10 per HWY

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Out of 100 women who took oral contraceptive pills for contraception, 10 women got pregnant within 24 months. What is the Pearl index?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, the pearl index is 5 per HWY. Here, the total number of accidental pregnancies is 10. There are 100 couples who are exposed to the method. So, the total months of exposure are 24 months x 100 = 2400. Pearl index = Total a ccidental pregnancies x 1200/Total months of exposure454 Hence, pearl index = 10 x 1200/2400 = 5 per HWY.455

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman has come for her first antenatal visit at 10 weeks of gestation. How many more antenatal visits does she require to fulfill the minimum requirements as per the Maternal and Child Health program?
mcqs.explanation: This patient requires 3 more antenatal visits in order to fulfill the minimum requirements according to the Maternal and Child Health Program (MCH). The minimum number of antenatal visits according to MCH is 4. • 1st visit – within 12 weeks, preferably as soon as the pregnancy is suspected. • 2nd visit – between 14 and 26 weeks464 • 3rd visit – between 28 and 34 weeks • 4th visit – between 36 weeks and term The minimum number of antenatal visits according to the WHO is 8. Ideally, pregnant women should attend antenatal visits according to the following schedule: • Once a month during the first 7 months • Twice a month during the 8th month • Once a week, thereafter if everything is normal.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are a medical officer in a PHC. A pregnant woman comes to you for regular follow-up during her second trimester. Which of the following will you prescribe for her?

options.a: 100 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid
options.b: 100 mg elemental iron + 100 mcg folic acid
options.c: 50 mg e lemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid
options.d: 60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg of folic acid

mcqs.explanation: As per the Anemia Mukt Bharat program, pregnant women should be given 60 mg of elemental iron and 500 mcg of folic acid in the I I trimester. It should be started from the 4th month of pregnancy and continued for 180 days post-partum.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following vaccine is contraindicated in pregnancy?
mcqs.explanation: Varicella vaccine is contraindicated in pregnant women as it is a live vaccine. The live attenuated varicella virus vaccine is currently recommended for children between 12 to 18 months of age who have not had chickenpox.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the average weight gain during pregnancy in Indian women with inadequate calorie intake?
mcqs.explanation: Weight gain during pregnancy in women with inadequate calorie intake is around 5 - 6 kgs. Normally, a woman is expected to gain around 9-11 kgs of weight d uring pregnancy. An inadequate dietary intake can be suspected if the woman gains < 2 kg/ month.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about congenital syphilis?

options.a: It can be prevented by procaine penicillin administration
options.b: Infection of fetus most commonly occurs in the 1st trimester
options.c: Neurological damage with mental retardation is a serious complication
options.d: Chances of transmission are lower if mother has late syphilis

mcqs.explanation: The chances of transmission of syphilis during pregnancy is highest after 6th month of gestation. It does not occur before the 4th month. It is routine to test the mother for syphilis in antenatal clinics during her first visit. The chance of infection of the fetus is higher when the mother is suffering from early (primary or secondary) syphilis and are lower in case of lat e s yphilis. Neurological damage with mental retardation is a serious complication of congenital syphilis. It can be prevented by procaine penicillin administration.465

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The District Maternal Death Review Committee is reviewing the number of maternal deaths in the district during 2020. I n o rder to calculate the maternal mortality ratio, what other parameter is required?

options.d: Total women in child bearing age

mcqs.explanation: The maternal mortality ratio is calculated using the number of maternal deaths and total live births.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following maternal deaths is not included when calculating the maternal mortality ratio?

options.a: Death of a 30-year-old woman following spontaneous abortion at 11 weeks of gestation
options.b: Death of a 24-year-old woman due to ruptured ectopic pregnancy
options.c: Death of a 26-year-old woman following a road traffic a ccident at 36 weeks of gestation
options.d: Death of a 21-year-woman following secondary PPH on postpartum day

mcqs.explanation: The death of a pregnant woman following a road traffic accident is not included when calculating the maternal mortality ratio. It includes all deaths anytime during pregnancy or within 42 days of termination from any cause related to or aggravated by the pregnancy.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of maternal deaths in India?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of maternal deaths in India is hemorrhage.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a town, there were 2500 live births in a period of 6 months. During the same period, 15 women died due to the following causes. What is the maternal mortality ratio?
mcqs.explanation: The maternal mortality ratio (MMR) of this town is 400 per 100,000 live births. Maternal mortality refers to deaths during pregnancy or 42 days within termination, from causes related to pregnancy. Hence, in this town, there were 10 maternal deaths (peripartum infection, PPH, obstructed labor). MMR = Number of maternal deaths in a period x 100,000 / Number of live births in the same period Hence, MMR = 10 x 100000/2500 = 400 per 100,000 live births

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A baby was delivered at home in a village. Until which day of life should an ASHA worker visit this baby?
mcqs.explanation: Under the Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC) guidelines, ASHA workers should visit all newborns up to 42 days of life, according to the following schedule. During her visits, ASHA workers must record weight, ensure vaccination, and registration of births. On completion of all these visits, they receive an incentive of Rs. 250.Mode of delivery No. of visits Schedule of visits Home delivery Days 1, 3, 7, 14, , 28, Hospital -based normal vagin al delivery Days 3, 7, 14, , 28, 42(exce pt day 1) Hospital -based LSCS delivery 5 Days 7, 14, , 28, 42(except days 1, 3)466

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the best indicator of obstetric and neonatal care given before and around the time of birth?
mcqs.explanation: The perinatal mortality rate is the best indicator to evaluate obstetric and neonatal care given before and around the time of birth.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the 2030 target of the India Newborn Action Plan with regards to the stillbirth rate?
mcqs.explanation: The India Newborn Action Plan targets to achieve a stillbirth rate of < 10/ 1000 live births and neonatal mortality rate of < 10/ 1000 live births (single-digit SBR and NMR) by 2030. This program was launched to reduce preventable newborn deaths and stillbirths. It provides the following: • Pre-conception and antenatal care • Care during labor and childbirth • Immediate newborn care • Care of healthy newborn • Care of small and sick newborn • Care beyond newborn survival

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A group of health workers are conducting a perinatal mortality audit in a hospital. Which of the following must they take into account to calculate the perinatal mortality rate?
mcqs.explanation: The perinatal mortality rate (PMR) is calculated using the following parameters during a particular time period: • Late fetal deaths or stillbirths > 1000 g - correlates to 28 weeks of gestation • Early neonatal deaths - from birth to 7 days of life • Live births > 1000 g The neonatal mortality rate (NMR) refers to the deaths within the f irst 28 days of life. It is calculated using the following parameters: • Early neonatal deaths • Late neonatal deaths - after 7th day but before 28th completed day of life

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a given population, 4050 births were recorded over a period o f 1 year. Among these, 50 were stillbirths, 50 died in the 1st week of life and 150 died within 8-28 days of life. What is the neonatal mortality rate of this population?
mcqs.explanation: The neonatal mortality rate (NMR) of the given population is 50 per 1000 live births.467 Neonatal mortality rate = No. of deaths of neonates < 28 days within a year x 1000 / Total live births in the same year In this population, there were 4000 live births (no. of total births - no. of stillbirths). NMR = (50+150) x 1000/4000 = 100/2 = 50

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the leading cause of neonatal mortality?
mcqs.explanation: Prematurity is the leading cause of neonatal mortality.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In children aged 1 month to 1 year, all of the following are common causes of mortality except:
mcqs.explanation: Tetanus is not a common cause of mortality in children between the age of 1 month to 1 year (post-neonatal period). The main causes of post-neonatal deaths are diarrhea, respiratory i nfections , and malnutrition.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a given population, there were 5100 births during the year 2020. Of these, 100 babies were stillborn. Among the living children, the following deaths were recorded. Calculate the infant mortality rate for this population.
mcqs.explanation: The infant mortality rate (IMR) for this population is 100 / 1000 live births. IMR = No. of deaths within 1st year of life over a period of time x 1000 / No. of live births in the same period In this population, there were 5000 live births (5100 – 100) and 500 deaths within the 1st year of life. Hence, IMR = 500 x 1000/5000 = 100 per 1000 live births

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true for a newborn stabilization unit?

options.a: It is located in the delivery room.
options.b: It is for sick babies and LBW babies < 1800 g
options.c: It is present in all community health centres
options.d: All cases except major surgeries are managed here

mcqs.explanation: A newborn stabilization unit is present in all community health centers (CHC). India accounts for 30% o f neonatal deaths globally and 73.3% of these deaths occur in 1st week of life. To address this issue, the following facility-based newborn care services were introduced:Newborn care corner Newborn stabilization un it Special newborn care uni ts Present in Delivery room of all cent ers and hospitals Within or close to the ma ternity ward, in CHCs an d first referral units District hospitals and faci lities with >3000 deliveri es/ year Admits Immediate care to all ne wborns Sick and LBW >1800 gm s Sick and LBW < 1800 gm s468 Newborn care corner Newborn stabilization un it Special newborn care uni ts Service Immediate resuscitation , early initiation of breastf eeding , identification , an d referral of at-risk newb orns Hyperbilirubinemia, asp hyxia, pneumonia, diarrh ea, sepsis All care except assisted v entilation and major surg ery Training of health person nel appointed 2 days, under Navjat Shis hu Suraksha Karyakram 11 days in IMNCI 4 days of training and tw o weeks of observership Staff 1 doctor, 1 nurse, 1 auxili ary midwife 1 doctor, 4 nurses 3-4 doctors and 10 nurse s

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are a doctor at a child health clinic. You will consider all of the following children as at-risk infants except:

options.b: A 15-day-old baby with birth weight of 2.4 kgs
options.d: An 8-month-old baby being raised by a working mother

mcqs.explanation: The 2-month-old baby with 3 older siblings has a birth order of 4. Infants with birth order of 5 or more are considered at-risk infants. The following are considered at-risk infants: • Birth weight < 2.5 kgs • Twins • Birth order of 5 or more • Artificial feeding • Weight below 70% of the expected weight • Failure to gain weight during 3 successive months • Children with protein-energy malnutrition (PEM), diarrhea • Working mother or single parent

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A researcher is calculating the child survival indices for different populations. Which of the following should he use for calculating the same?
mcqs.explanation: The under-5 mortality rate is used in the calculation of the child survival index. It is calculated as (1000 – Under-5 mortality rate)/10.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Identify the false statement about the following tool:

options.a: Malnutrition can be detected even before signs and symptoms appear
options.b: It provides an objective basis for policy making on child healthcare
options.c: It can be used to teach the importance of adequate feeding
options.d: It can be used to indicate proof of government aid

mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a growth chart. It is not used as proof of government aid. The uses of growth charts are as follows: • Growth monitoring and diagnosis - can detect malnutrition before clinical features appear • Educational tool - to teach parents about the importance of adequate feeding.469 • Objective basis for planning and policy-making on child healthcares

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A juvenile delinquent was sentenced by the court to be placed in a center under the care of a doctor and psychiatrist. Which of the following fulfills this requirement?
mcqs.explanation: A remand home is an establishment where children are placed under the care of a doctor, psychiatrist and other trained personnel. An orphanage or shelter home is an institution where children who have no home or parents or for some reason can't be cared for are placed. Foster homes are arrangements where a family or a couple takes care of a child on a temporary basis. Borstal is a place that falls between a certified i nstitution and a prison. It is where boys > years who have misbehaved or are too difficult to handle are sent.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The police authorities rescued a girl from being trafficked for sexual exploitation. She is identified to be a refugee. As a part of the Ujjawala scheme, which of the following benefits will she not receive?
mcqs.explanation: The girl will not receive remuneration (monetary compensation) under the Ujjawala scheme. The Ujjawala scheme was launched to combat women and child trafficking in India. The components of the scheme include: • Prevention of trafficking by awareness, vigilance, education • Rescue of victims from the place of exploitation • Rehabilitation of victims • R e -integration of victims into their family and society • Repatriation of cross-border victims to their place of origin Some other legislations associated with children in India are: • The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, • Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, • Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 (amended in 2006 and 2016) • Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO), 2012 under the Nati onal C ommission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) • Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 4-year-old girl was brought by her parents who tell you that she fell down while playing. On examination, bruises and ecchymoses of varying ages are noted all over the body. An x-ray showed a spiral fracture of the right femur. Which of the following programs can provide support services to this child and prevent further such incidents?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario points towards child abuse. The INSPIRE strategy was introduced to eliminate such violence against children and also provide support services. It refers to a set of 7 evidence-based strategies to eliminate violence against children:470 Strategies Approach I Implementation and enforce ment of laws Banning violent punishment of children and criminalizing sexual abusePreventing alcoh ol misuse and limiting youth access to weapons N Norms and values Changing perceptions about harmful gender and social no rms S Safe environments Reducing the spread of viole nce P Parent and caregiver support Delivered through home visit s and in groups in communit y settings I Income and economic strengt hening Cash transfersProviding smal l loans R Response and support servic es Counseling and therapyTreat ment programs for juvenile o ffendersFoster care interventi ons E Education and life skills Increasing enrolment in scho olsEstablishing safe school e nvironmentsImproving sexua l education for children and t eaching self -defense strategie s

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: As a PHC medical officer, which of the following groups would y ou target as a part of Kishori Shakti Yojana?
mcqs.explanation: The Kishori Shakti Yojana (KSY) program is aimed at adolescent girls (11-18 years). This program is a component of the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme and is a redesign of the already existing Adolescent Girls (AG) scheme. The objectives of KSY are: • To improve the nutrition, health, and development status • To promote awareness on health, hygiene, nutrition, and family care • To teach life skills and encourage school attendance • To help understand their s ocial environment • Aspects aimed at empowerment and enhanced self-perception • To help them take initiatives to become productive members of society It also fosters convergence with other sectoral programs, addressing the interrelated needs of adolescent girls and women.471

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The school health programs are managed by which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: The school health programs are managed by the primary health center (PHC). The School Health Committee (1961) in India recommended that the school health services should be a part of the general health services administered through PHCs. Formation of school health committees at the village, block, district, state, and national levels was recommended. The National School Health Council was created as an advisory and coordinating body. PHCs provide the following school h ealth services: • Screening and general assessments for - • Anemia/nutritional status • Visual acuity and hearing problems • Dental check-up • Physical disabilities • Learning disorders and behavior problems • Basic medicines for common ailments • Immunization • Micronutrient management (vitamin A, iron, and folic acid) • Deworming • Mid-day meal

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 68-year-old man visits your outpatient clinic for a routine follow-up. Which of the following protocols would you use to assess his health literacy?
mcqs.explanation: The SPEAK protocol is used to assess health literacy in the geriatric population in a clinical setting. Health literacy i s defined as the degree to which individuals have the capacity to obtain, process , and understand basic health information needed to make appropriate health decisions. The SPEAK protocol provides a simple framework that healthcare providers can use to assess literacy. SPEAK stands for: • S - Speech • P - Perception • E - Education • A - Access • K - Knowledge Option A: The GATHER approach is mainly used for counseling (usually, family planning and reproductive counseling) to help people make decisions about health. It stands for:472 • G – Greet • A – Ask • T – Tell • H – Help • E – Explain • R – Return Option C: The SPIKES protocol is used to convey distressing information and break bad news in an organized manner to patients and families. It stands for: • S - Setting • P - Perception • I - Invitation or information • K - Knowledge • E - Empathy • S - Summarizing or strategizing. Option D: The S-BAR technique is used for prompt and appropriate communication among health care workers in hospital settings. It stands for: • S - Situation • B - Background • A - Assessment • R - Recommendation

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following comes under the Rashtriya Varishth Jan Swasthya Yojana?

options.a: Domiciliary visits to homes of elderly in the community by ANMs or male HCWs
options.b: Rehabilitation units with physiotherapy at CHCs
options.c: Super-specialty geriatric departments for training, guidelines and referral
options.d: Weekly geriatric clinics arranged at PHCs by medical officer

mcqs.explanation: The establishment of super-specialty geriatric departments for training, guidelines, and referral comes under the Rashtriya Varishth Jan Swasthya Yojna (RVJSY). It refers to the tertiary component of the National Programme for Healthcare of the Elderly (NPHCE). The NPHCE was established for geriatric care and includes provisions at primary, secondary, and tertiary levels. The tertiary component of the p rogram has been renamed as RVJSY and has the following provisions : • Geriatrics departments at 20 super specialty institutions- • 30-bedded inpatient facility and referral treatment • Research and manpower development, • Development of training, IEC material, and guidelines • Geriatric units at district hospitals (tertiary) - • 10 bedded geriatric ward473 • Dedicated geriatric OPDCenters Services according to NPHCE PHCs(primary) Weeklygeriatricclinicsat PHC Treatment of minor ailments Referralservices to higher cen ters Sub-centres (primar y) ANMs/ male health workers makedomiciliary visitsto the elderlyArrange supportive de vices for the disabledTreatme nt of minor ailments CHCs(secondary) Dedicatedgeriatricclinicstwic e weeklyRehabilitation unit w ith trainedphysiotherapists474

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following parameters is not indicative of reference Indian adult woman?
mcqs.explanation: According to the 2020 guidelines of the National Institute of Nutrition, the weight of the reference Indian adult woman is 55 kg.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The energy required by an adult for basal metabolism is:
mcqs.explanation: The energy required by an adult for basal metabolism is 1 kcal/ hour/ kg of body weight.479

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the likely energy requirement of a pregnant woman who leads a moderately active lifestyle?
mcqs.explanation: The energy requirement of a pregnant woman who leads a moderately active lifestyle is around 2500 kcal/day. An adult woman leading a moderately active lifestyle requires 2130 kcal daily and an additional 350 kcal is needed in pregnancy. Hence, the total requirement for a moderately working pregnant woman is 2480 kcal/ day (approximately 2500 kcal/ day).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A nutritionist i s preparing a meal plan for a healthy 32-year-old man. Which of the following principles must she follow?

options.a: Proteins must constitute 15-30% of the daily energy intake
options.b: Fats must constitute 10-15% of the daily energy intake
options.c: Carbohydrate requirement must be met first followed by protein and fat
options.d: The proportion of nutrients in the diet must be carbohydrates > fats > proteins

mcqs.explanation: The proportion of nutrients in the diet must be carbohydrates > fats > proteins. While constructing a balanced d iet, nutrient requirements must be calculated in the following sequence: • Protein requirements - 10-15% of daily energy intake • Fat requirement - 15-30% of daily energy intake • Carbohydrates - remaining food energy

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the daily requirement of high-quality protein for a 40-year-old man weighing 60 kgs?
mcqs.explanation: This man requires 50 g/day of high-quality protein. High-quality protein refers to proteins containing all the essential amino acids. According to the FAO/WHO 2007 guidelines, the recommended high-quality protein intake for adult men and women is 0 .83 g / kg/day. This man weighs 60 kgs. Hence he requires around 50 g (0.83*60 = 49.8) of high-quality protein per day. Recommended high-quality protein intake by FAO/WHO: However, the mixed Indian diet does not meet the requirement for high-quality protein. Hence, the protein requirement in Indian adults (men and women) is 1g/kg/day of mixed Indian diet protein according to the ICMR 2010 guidelines.Age Protein in g/kg/da y 1-5 years 0.94 6-10 years 0.91 Adolescent male 0.88 Adolescent fem ale 0.86480 Age Protein in g/kg/da y Adult man/wom an 0.83

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A dietary protein-energy percentage of which of the following is the threshold for inadequate protein intake?
mcqs.explanation: Dietary protein-energy percentage (PE %\ < 4% indicates inadequate protein intake. The PE % indicates the proportion of total energy in the diet that is derived from proteins. PE % = (Energy from protein / Total energy in the diet) * 100 Some of the food items and their protein-energy percentage are given below:Food PE% Fish 80 Cow milk Dal 24 Rice 8 Potat o Bana na Tapio ca 2

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the best indicator o f protein quality?

options.a: Protein digestibility corrected amino acid score

mcqs.explanation: Digestible indispensable amino acid score (DIAAS) is the best indicator for protein quality. DIAAS reflects the digestibility of individual amino acids in the protein. Total protein digestibility does not always reflect the digestibility of individual dietary indispensable amino acids. Hence, DIAAS has replaced the PDCAAS (protein digestibility corrected amino acid score) as the preferred index for the evaluation of protein quality.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following has the highest net protein utilization value?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options, meat has the highest net protein utilization (NPU). The NPU values of various food items in descending order are:481 • Egg - 100 • Meat - 80 • Milk - 75 • Rice - 65 • Soya - 61 Low NPU indicates a high protein requirement. The NPU of Indian diets is usually between 50 and 80.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A farmer has been consuming a maize-rich diet for many years. Which of the following would be lacking in his diet?
mcqs.explanation: His diet would be lacking lysine and tryptophan as maize is deficient in these amino acids.Principal Food Amino acid Deficient Cereals (in general ) Lysine Maize Lysine and Tryptopha n Wheat Lysine and Threonine Pulses (Poor man's mea t) Methionine and cystei ne

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following has the highest content of essential fatty acids?
mcqs.explanation: Safflower oil contains the highest content of essential fatty acids. Linoleic acid is the most important essential fatty acid. Milk is also rich in linoleic acid and oleic acid.Dietary sour ce % content of linoleic acid Safflower oil 75 Corn oil 50 Sunflower oi l Soybean oil 53

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are counseling a diabetic patient to consume foods with low glycemic index. Which of the following would you advise him to ea t?
mcqs.explanation: 482 The patient should be advised to eat whole grains since it has a low glycemic index (GI). GI is a number representing the relative ability of a carbohydrate food to increase the level of glucose in the blood. It is calculated by comparing the test carbohydrate to the standard (glucose or white bread). This measure has practical use in the management of diabetes and obesity. • Low GI foods – most fruits and vegetables, whole grains, pasta foods, beans, and lentils. • Moderate GI foods – sucrose, basmati rice, and brown rice. • High GI foods – corn flakes, baked potatoes, white bread, potatoes, watermelon, candies, and syrupy foods.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The renal feed of a patient suffering from end-stage renal disease (stage 5) should ideally be:
mcqs.explanation: The renal feed of a patient suffering from end-stage renal disease should ideally be low volume, high calories. Dietary factors may have an effect on the progression of kidney disease and its complications. A low-volume feed is preferred in order to avoid: • Sodium and volume overload • Hyperkalemia • Hyperphosphatemia • A ccumulation of toxic metabolites of protein degradation A high-calorie feed is preferred in order to combat the patient's risk of malnutrition and wasting seen in ESRD.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not used in the assessment of body fat?
mcqs.explanation: Breslow's staging is used for the staging of malignant melanoma, not for the assessment of body fat.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In the Indian population, individuals with BMI falling between which range are defined as overweight?
mcqs.explanation: In the Indian (Asian) population, a BMI of 23-24.99 is classified as overweight. However, in the global population, a BMI of 25-29.99 is considered overweight.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What value of BMI is considered as 'lethal' in men?
mcqs.explanation: A body mass index (BMI) of 13 or less is considered lethal in men. However, females can survive even at a lower BMI up to 11.483

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following indicators a re used in Waterlow's classification?
mcqs.explanation: Waterlow's classification makes use of height for age (HFA) and weight for height (WFH) to assess the nutritional status of children. HFA indicates stunting and denotes the chronicity of malnutrition. On the other hand, WFH indicates wasting and denotes the severity of malnutrition. The Gomez classification uses weight for age as an indicator of nutritional status. The disadvantage is that it is difficult to determine whether the low weight is due to an acute attack of malnutrition o r chronic undernutrition.484

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A patient presents with the following skin finding. You would advise supplementation with which of the following?

options.c: Vitamin B complex and vitamin K
options.d: Safflower oil and vitamin B complex

mcqs.explanation: The image shows rough, dry skin suggestive of phrynoderma. It is treated by supplementation of safflower oil (rich in essential fatty acids) and vitamin B complex. Phrynoderma or toad skin is a type of follicular hyperkeratosis. It is caused by a deficiency of vitamin E, B, A, C, and essential fatty acids.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following has the highest content of thiamine?
mcqs.explanation: Gingelly (sesame) seeds have the highest content of thiamine. The thiamine content in various foods in decreasing order are as follows: • Gingelly seeds • Groundnut • B engal g ram • Whole wheat • Raw rice Thiamine is lost from rice during the process of milling. As it is a water-soluble vitamin, washing, and cooking rice cause further losses. Hence, it is advisable to avoid highly polished rice and eat parboiled or under-milled rice.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A patient presented with loose stools and skin rashes over the sun-exposed areas. Diet history revealed that the patient had been consuming a jowar-rich diet since childhood. This condition results due to excess of which amino acid in the diet?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario is suggestive of pellagra. It is caused by the excess of leucine in jowar. Excess of leucine in jowar (sorghum) and maize interferes with the conversion of tryptophan to niacin causing pellagra. I t presents with the following features: • Diarrhea • Dermatitis (sun-exposed areas)490 • Dementia People consuming jowar also have a higher risk of developing genu valgum and osteoporosis due to greater retention of ingested fluoride.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the recommended daily allowance of vitamin A for a 9-month old baby?
mcqs.explanation: The RDA of vitamin A for infants is 350 mcg.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the dosage of vitamin A given for a 2-year-old baby with keratomalacia?

options.a: 2,00,000 IU immediately, followed by same dose after 24 hours
options.b: 1,00,000 IU immediately, followed by the same dose after 1 week
options.c: 1,00,000 IU immediately, followed by the same dose after 24 hours and after a week
options.d: 2,00,000 IU immediately, followed by the same dose 24 hours later and after 2 weeks

mcqs.explanation: The recommended vitamin A dosage for a 2-year-old child with keratomalacia is 2,00,000 IU given immediately, followed by the same age-specific dose 24 hours later and after 2 weeks.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Vitamin A deficiency is considered a public health problem if the prevalence of corneal xerosis among children aged 6 months - 6 years is more than:
mcqs.explanation: Vitamin A deficiency is considered a public health problem if the prevalence rate of corneal xerosis a mong children between 6 months to 6 years (high-risk category) is more than 0.01%. The presence of any 1 of the following criteria should be considered as evidence of a xerophthalmia problem in the community:Criteria Prevalence in population at ri sk (6 months - 6 years) Night blindness > 1% Bitot's spots > 0.5% Corneal xerosis / Corneal ulce r / Keratomalacia > 0.01 % Corneal scar > 0.05% Serum retinol < 10 mcg/dl >5 %

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The dose of iodine for lactating women in India according to the recommended dietary allowance is:
mcqs.explanation: According to the National Institute of Nutrition (NIN) 2020 guidelines, the recommended dietary allowance (RDA) for dietary iodine in lactating women in India is 280 �Mg/day. NIN guidelines on recommended dietary allowance for iodine per day: Note: According to the WHO guidelines, the RDA during both pregnancy and lactation is 250 mcg.491 Age Male Female Birth to 6 mont hs 100 mcg 100 mcg 7–12 months 130 mcg 130 mcg 1–9 years 90-120 mcg 90-120 mcg –12 years 150 mcg 150 mcg 14–18 years 150 mcg 150 mcg > 19 years 150 mcg 150 mcg Pregnancy — 250 mc g Lactation — 280 mc g

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect regarding the epidemiological assessment of iodine deficiency?

options.a: Median urinary iodine excretion <200 �Mg/ L indicates insufficient iodine intake
options.b: Neonatal hypothyroidism is a sensitive indicator of environmental iodine deficiency
options.c: Serum T4 level is a more sensitive indicator of thyroid i nsufficiency than T
options.d: Quality control of salt is performed by rapid testing with MBI kit

mcqs.explanation: Median urinary iodine excretion level < �Mg/L (in non-pregnant population) indicates insufficient iodine intake. Urinary excretion of iodine is used by the WHO for surveillance and epidemiological studies to classify countries according to the level of iodine deficiency. It is an effective indicator of national programmes against iodine deficiency. Neonatal hypothyroidism is a sensitive indicator of environmental iodine deficiency. It is also an effecti ve i ndicator to monitor the impact of a programme. Serum T4 level is a more sensitive indicator of thyroid insufficiency in the population than T3. Determination of iodine in salt is a part of the quality control of the product. The UNICEF uses MBI kits to rapidly assess the levels of iodine in salt.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the recommended dietary allowance of folic acid for a 5-year-old child?
mcqs.explanation: The recommended dietary allowance of folic acid in a 5-year-old child is 135�Mg.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Under the Anemia Mukt Bharat programme, what dose of iron and folic acid tablets will you prescribe for a 6-year-old child?

options.a: 20 mg iron and 100 mcg folic acid
options.b: 45 mg iron and 400 mcg folic acid
options.c: 50 mg iron and 350 mcg folic acid
options.d: 100 mg iron and 500 mcg folic acid

mcqs.explanation: Under the Anemia Mukt Bharat programme, a 6-year-old child should be given 45 mg elemental iron + 400 m cg folic acid (1 iron and folic acid tablet weekly). The tablet is sugar-coated and pink in color.492

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: How much calcium does a premenopausal woman require on a daily basis?
mcqs.explanation: A premenopausal woman requires 1000 mg calcium on a daily basis.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Individuals with fluoride intake above which of the following are at risk of developing crippling fluorosis?
mcqs.explanation: Individuals with fluoride intake > 10 mg/L are at risk of developing crippling fluorosis. Complications of fluorosis seen with corresponding levels of fluoride intake are: • Dental fluorosis - 1.5 mg/L • Skeletal fluorosis - 3-6 mg/L • Crippling fluorosis - > 10 mg/L Genu valgum may occur in people who consume jowar (sorghum), as it promotes greater retention of ingested fluoride. The Nalgonda tech nique i s used for the defluoridation of water bodies. It involves the addition of lime and alum followed by flocculation, sedimentation, and filtration.
