mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the normal daily requirement of magnesium in adults?
mcqs.explanation: The normal daily requirement of magnesium in adults is 400 mg/day The following are the approximate daily requirements of some electrolytes in adults: • Sodium: 1.2 to 1.5 grams (g)/day (up to 2g/day)494 • Potassium: 3500 mg/day • Calcium: 1000-1200 mg/day • Magnesium: 400 mg/day495

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following formulates food standards for the international food market?
mcqs.explanation: The Codex Alimentarius Commission formulates food standards for the international market. It is the principal organ of the FAO/WHO food standards program. The ISI standards (Indian Standards Institute) and AGMARK are the Indian food standards. They are based on the standards of Codex Alimentarius. The PFA (Prevention of Food Adulteration) Act was introduced to provide protection from adulteration or contamination of food.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the dose of vitamin A added during fortification of vanaspati?
mcqs.explanation: Vanaspati is fortified with 2500 IU of vitamin A and 175 IU of vitamin D. Note : 1g of double fortified salt contains 40 mcg iodine and 1 mg iron.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following contributes to a significant loss of beta carotene from food?
mcqs.explanation: Dehydration contributes to a significant loss in the beta carotene levels in food. Processes that do not affect beta carotene levels in the food are: • Boiling • Canning • Freezing

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In order to effectively prevent endemic goiter, what is the recommended iodine content i n salt at the consumer level?
mcqs.explanation: The recommended level of iodine content in salt is 15 ppm at the consumer level and 30 ppm at the production level. The iodization of salt is used as a prophylactic measure against endemic goiter. In India, t he level of iodization is fixed under the Prevention of Food Adulteration (PFA) Act.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a milk factory, the milk is heated at 63\260C for 30 minutes and then cooled quickly to less than 13\260C . Which bacteria can survive this method?
mcqs.explanation: The method described above is the holder method of pasteurization. Coxiella burnetti can survive this method since it is highly heat-resistant. It causes Q fever. The various methods of pasteurization are: • Holder/Vat method - 63-66 \260C for 30 minutes • HTST method (high-temperature short time) - 72\260C for 15 seconds499 • UHT method (ultra-high temperature) - 125 \260C for a few seconds

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following tests is not used to check the efficiency of pasteurization?
mcqs.explanation: Methylene blue reduction test is not used to check the efficiency of pasteurization. This test is used for grading raw milk quality prior to pasteurization. The following tests are used to check the efficiency of pasteurization: • Phosphatase test • Standard plate count • Coliform count

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a rice processing factory, paddy is soaked in hot water. After t his, the water is drained and the paddy is steamed and dried. Which of the following statements is false about the above process?

options.a: This method is used for partial cooking of rice
options.b: It makes the rice grains resistant to insects
options.c: Vitamins and minerals are driven into endosperm during this process

mcqs.explanation: The procedure mentioned above is parboiling. It hardens the rice grains. Parboiling is the process of partial cooking of rice i n steam. It is done by the hot soaking process that was initially developed by the Central Food Technological Research Institute (CFTRI), Mysore. The advantages of parboiling are: • Preserves nutritive quality by driving the vitamins and minerals into the endosperm. • Hardens the grains and makes them insect resistant.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man presented with gradually progressive muscle weakness and leg spasms for 2 months. He says that he had been consuming an inexpensiv e d al resembling red gram for the past 2 years. Pure motor paresis was seen on examination. Which of the following could have prevented this?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical features are suggestive of neurolathyrism. It can be prevented and treated by the administration of vitamin C at doses of 500-1000 m g. Lathyrism is a paralyzing disease of humans and animals. It is due to the consumption of khesari dal or Lathyrus sativus. When the husk is removed, it looks similar to red gram or Bengal gram. BOAA (beta oxalyl amino alanine) is the toxic compound causing this disease. It is water-soluble and can be removed by the following methods: • Soaking pulses in hot water and discarding the water • Overnight soaking in lime water followed by boiling • Parboiling - for large-scale detoxification

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman is being evaluated for sudden onset of hypersecretory glaucoma, diarrhea, and cardiac failure. Further probing reveals that she had been purchasing groceries from a dealer who was recently arrested for food adulteration. What toxin is likely responsible for her presentation?
mcqs.explanation: 500 This clinical scenario is suggestive of epidemic dropsy. It is caused by the toxic compound sanguinarine, which is present in argemone oil. It is commonly used as an adulterant in mustard oil. Epidemic dropsy results in sudden onset of swelling of lower limbs, diarrhea, and breathlessness. Some patients may develop hypersecretory glaucoma. It can lead to death due to cardiac failure. Adulteration with argemone oil can be detected by the following tests: • Paper chromatography - most s ensitive test • Nitric acid test501

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is meant by the term sociology?

options.a: Study of developments in the society
options.b: Study of formation of social organisations and government
options.c: Study of human relationships and behavior
options.d: Study of social and cultural history of man

mcqs.explanation: Sociology is considered to be both the study of human relationships and of human behavior.507

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following social sciences does not deal directly with human behavior?
mcqs.explanation: Political science refers to the study of the judicial systems and institutions that constitute the government. It does not deal directly with human behavior. Anthropology is the study of the physical, social, and cultural history of man. Social anthropology is extensively used in preventive and social medicine. Social psychology is aimed at understanding the basis of perception, thoughts, ideas, etc., among people in a society or group. Sociology is the study of human r elationships and human behavior.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Match the following:
mcqs.explanation: Social pathology refers to the study of social factors, which influence human disease and incite social disorganization. This includes crime, poverty, delinquency, abuse, etc. Social medicine is an organized investigation of the social, environmental, and genetic factors affecting disease patterns and disability. It also deals with the promotion of methods for the prevention of disease and health measures. Socialized medicine i s the provision of medical service and education by the State. It is operated and regulated by professional groups, and not the government. Social psychology is the effect of the social environment on people, their attitudes, and motivation. It deals with the study of human behavior, thoughts, and feelings and how they are influenced by the perception of others in society.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: 'Putting profit ahead of health' as a cause of disease belongs to which theory of sociology of health?
mcqs.explanation: Putting profit ahead of health is termed as the cause of disease in the Marxist theory of sociology of health. Elias' theory focused on the relationship between power, behavior, emotion, and knowledge over time.Theory Marxist Parsonian Foucauldian Description Emphasizedcausal role of economics in diseaseand the role of medical know ledge in sustaining class s tructure Emphasized role of medi cine in maintainingsocial harmony Emphasized the role of'h elping professions 'in indu cing individuals to compl y with social roles Model of Society Conflictual and exploitati ve Harmonious and stable s et of interlinked social rol es and structures Net of power relations wi th no one dominant sour ce508 Theory Marxist Parsonian Foucauldian Cause of Disease Putting profit ahead of he alth Social strain caused by m eeting the demands of so cial roles Diseases are labels used t o sort and segregate the p opulation to make it easie r to control Role of Medical Professi onal To discipline and control the working classTo provi de individualized explana tions of the disease Rehabilitate individuals t o carry out their social ro les To enforce compliance wi th the normal social roles and to ensure internaliza tion of these norms.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following refers to a system of social relationships between individuals?
mcqs.explanation: Society is the system of social relationships between people in an area. A community is a social group determined by geographical boundaries and/or common values and interests. A family is a group of biologically related individuals living together under the same roof and eating from a common kitchen. Social Institutions are organized complex patterns of behavior in which a number of people engage to further a common interest.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following options is correctly matched?

options.a: Social institution- the pattern of inter-relations between persons in a society
options.b: Socialism- organised complex patterns of behaviour in people with a common interest
options.c: Social structure- system of governance based on social ownership
options.d: Socialization - t he process by which a person imbibes the social beliefs and customes

mcqs.explanation: Socialization is the process by which a person in a society imbibes its beliefs, customs , etc. through daily interaction with its members. Social institutions are organized complex patterns of behaviour in which a number of people engage to further a common interest. Examples are families, schools, hospitals, etc. Socialism is a system of governance in which production and distribution is based on social ownership (and not private ownership). It is aimed at improving the living standard. Social structure is the p attern of inter-relations between persons in a society.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following terms is used to describe the preventive, therapeutic, and rehabilitative services for the protection of society from antisocial, criminal, or deviant conduct of man?
mcqs.explanation: Preventive, therapeutic and rehabilitative services for the protection of society from antisocial, criminal or deviant conduct of man is known as social defence. This is in the form of acts, laws and judicial instructions for elements like juvenile delinquency, begging, prison reforms, gambling, etc.509

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Match the following.
mcqs.explanation: Culture is the socially acquired learned behaviour. It is passed onto generations through formal and informal learning. It is the representation of customs, beliefs, laws, arts, and moral values of a society. Cultural factors have a large part to play in health. Customs are the traditionally accepted ways of behaving that is specific to a society. They can be folkways, which are referred to as the right ways of doing things in less vital areas of human conduct. Mores are st ringent c ustoms followed by a society. Standard of living refers to the scale of the expenditure of a society, the goods they consume and the services they enjoy. Role is the function or duties assumed by a person of a particular society.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not bring about acculturation?
mcqs.explanation: Acculturation is the process by which there is the diffusion of cultures between two culturally different groups of people. Acculturation does not take place by folklore. Folklore is the passage of customs and beliefs of a community throug h g enerations, merely by word of mouth. Acculturation can happen in the following ways: • Trade and commerce • Industrialization • Religious propagation • Education • Conquest This phenomenon is also known as culture contact.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct ascending order of the Maslow's hierarchy of needs?

options.c: Belonging, physiological, safety, self-actualization, e steem

mcqs.explanation: Maslow's hierarchy of needs was suggested by psychologist Abraham Maslow. It is a motivational theory in psychology where human needs are arranged according to hierarchy in a five-level pyramid. He suggested that the higher needs can be fulfilled o nly once the lower needs are fulfilled. The ascending order of the needs is shown in the image below.510

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following could be classified as an ego-integrative need of man?
mcqs.explanation: Ego-integrative needs of man include power, prestige and self-respect. The needs of man are as follows: • Biological needs- water, food, warmth, medicines, etc. • Social needs- love and affection, fellowship, education, etc. • Economic needs- money and security • Ego-integrative needs- power, prestige and self-respect.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the benefit that comes from solving one's own problems termed?
mcqs.explanation: Intrinsic incentives are the benefits that come from solving one's own problems. Incentives are entities that motivate or encourage a specific behaviour. T hey are generally positive motivators. The various types of incentives are: • Intrinsic incentives are the benefits that come from solving one's own problems. • Extrinsic incentives are rewards that do not relate directly to the goal of the desired behaviour like financial compensation for sterilization. • Psychological incentives include satisfaction, increased self-esteem, etc. • Material incentives include goods or services or financial compensation.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about attitudes in human behaviour?

options.a: It is acquired from social interactions
options.b: It includes an affective or feeling element
options.c: It pre-disposes one to respond in a preferential manner
options.d: It is a temporary and fleeting aspect of human behaviour

mcqs.explanation: 511 Attitude is usually a permanent aspect of a human's behaviour and is difficult to change. It is the enduring organization of beliefs around something that pre-disposes one to respond in a preferential manner. It is usually acquired through social interactions. Attitude includes three components: • A cognitive or knowledge element • An affective or feeling element • A tendency to act

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following terms represent the temporary and provisional views held by people at a point of dispute?
mcqs.explanation: Opinions are temporary and provisional views held by people at a point of dispute. Beliefs a re permanent and stable inner subjective thoughts of a person towards things that are without proof. These are usually acquired from family and other close contacts.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Match the f ollowing types of learning:
mcqs.explanation: Learning is any relative or permanent change in behaviour as a result of practice or experience. It includes acquiring knowledge and skills, formation of habits and development of perception. Types of learning: • Cognitive learning – knowledge • Affective learning – attitudes • Psychomotor learning – s kills The conditions that affect learning are as follows: • Intelligence • Age • Learning situation • Motivation • Physical and mental health Theories of learning: • Learning by conditioned reflex • Trial and error • Learning by observation and imitation • Learning by doing • Learning by remembering • Learning by insight512 • Demonstration • Field experience • Problem solving

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 6-yr-old boy is brought to the clinical psychologist for evaluation of intellectual disability. Which formula will she use to calculate the IQ of the child?
mcqs.explanation: The intelligence quotient is a score that is obtained from several standardized tests to assess human intelligence. Intelligence quotient (IQ) = Mental age x 100 / Chronological age

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Evaluation for mental retardation was done for a Down syndrome patient. His IQ was found to be 56. According to Levine and Mark's classification, you would classify him as?
mcqs.explanation: According to the Levine and Mark's classification, a moron would have an IQ of 50–74.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A clinical psychologist was asked to ascertain the IQ of a patient. She categorized the patient as having mild mental retardation. Which of the following rep resent's t he patient's IQ range?
mcqs.explanation: Mild mental retardation based on IQ score would fall in the range of 50–70.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: According to Wechsler's scale, which of the following persons would be categorized to have average intelligence?

options.c: A banker with an IQ of
options.d: An alcoholic man with an IQ of

mcqs.explanation: According to the Wechsler's Scale, average intelligence would fall in the range of 91–110.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an important epidemiological tool to assess disability in children?

options.b: Wing's Comprehensive Handicaps, Behaviour and Skills Schedule

mcqs.explanation: Wing's Comprehensive Handicaps, Behaviour and Skills Schedule (HBS) has been used in epidemiological studies to assess the total child population in terms of detailed scales of specific abilities and disabilities. HBS is not useful for children with mental retardation.513

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most powerful example of social cohesion in social organisation?
mcqs.explanation: The most powerful example of social cohesion in social organization is the family. It is the most basic and primary unit in all societies.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an unstable and emotional temporary social group with a leader?
mcqs.explanation: A mob is an unstable and emotional temporary social group with a leader. Temporary social groups can be classified into: • Crowd- It is a temporary group motivated by a common interest or curiosity. It lacks an internal organization and has no leader. • Mob- It is a crowd with a leader, and is more emotional than a crowd. It is unstable and has n o internal organization. • Herd- This social group has a leader and the members have to follow his/her orders without question. A band is a permanent spatial group that constitutes a few families living together. Other permanent spatial groups are villages, cities, towns and the state.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the correct order of a family cycle?

options.a: Formation, extension, complete extension, dissolution, contraction, complete contraction
options.b: Formation,contraction,extension, complete extension, dissolution, c omplete dissolution
options.c: Formation , contraction, complete contraction, extension, complete extension, dissolution
options.d: Formation, extension, complete extension, contraction, complete contraction, dissolution

mcqs.explanation: The order of the family cycle is formation, extension, complete extension, contraction, complete contraction and dissolution.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What are the constituents of a nuclear family?

options.a: Father, mother, son and his wife
options.b: Husband, wife and 4 year old daughter
options.c: Husband and wife only, without their children

mcqs.explanation: A nuclear family consists of a married couple and their children when they are dependant. They are also called elementary families.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Match the following:
mcqs.explanation: The correct match is A-4, B-1, C-5, D-3, E-2.Term Definition Problemfami ly A family whichlagsbehind the rest of the community521 Term Definition Communalfa mily A family in which all the me mbers play a part in its mana gement Brokenfamil y A family in which the parenta l system has beendisruptedby separation, divorce or death Newfamily A nuclear family which isless than 10 yearsconsisting of pa rents and children Jointfamily A number of married couples and their children who liveto getherin the same household with usually the men being re lated by blood

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In urbanized and industrialized countries, occupation is a major determinant of all of the following except:
mcqs.explanation: Occupation is not a determinant of community participation. Occupation in most urbanized and industrialized communities is a major determinant of: • Economic rewards • Extent of authority • Extent of obligations • Degree of status • Values and lifestyles

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a limitation of classifying social c lass according to occupation?

options.b: Inequality between men and women in same jobs

mcqs.explanation: Most classifications of social class based on occupational take skills into consideration. Occupation is a useful measure of social differentiation particularly in communities highly industrialised and urbanized. Li mitations of cccupational classification of social class: • Heterogenous grouping- occupations grouped together are not usually related to each other • Occupational mobility- occupations practiced by the members of a social class as well as the perception of a certain occupation in the hierarchy may change over a period of time • Gender biases- the same occupation may be considered as belonging to a superior class for men as compared to women522

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are tasked with conducting a health and wellness survey of the employees of your hospital. Which of the following scales will you not use to classify their socio-economic statuses?
mcqs.explanation: Likert scale is not a scale used for socio-economic status (SES). It is a psychometric scale used to understand the attitude of people from their responses. It is a scale widely used in questionnaire-based research. Scales that have been used for SES are: • Udai Pareek scale • Kuppuswamy scale • Radhukar scale • Jalota scale • Shirvastava scale • Bharadwaj scale • Kulshestra scale • Hollingshead scale.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: As a part of a community health survey team, you interview 50 families from a nearby village in your district. Which of the following scales would you use to classify the socio-economic statuses of these families?
mcqs.explanation: The Uday Pareek scale is used for the classification of socio-economic status in rural areas.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following components are included under the modified Kuppuswamy scale for socio-economic status ?
mcqs.explanation: The modified Kuppuswamy scale uses income of the family, education and occupation of head of family.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Match the following scores in accordance with Modified Kuppuswamy's scale.
mcqs.explanation: The correct match is 1-d, 2-b, 3-a, 4-c. Socioeconomic class according to Modified Kuppuswamy Scale:Socioeconomic cla ss Scor es Upper 25-2 Upper Middle 16-2 Lower Middle 11 -15523 Socioeconomic cla ss Scor es Upper Lower 05-1 Lower -0 4

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In the doctor-patient relationship, which of the following is not a level of communication?
mcqs.explanation: Communication on a psychological plane is not a level of communication in a doctor-patient relationship. For a successful doctor-patient relationship, a doctor must have in his/her regard communication on the following levels: • Communication on an emotional plane: To build rapport, ensure openness and incite trust from the patient. • Communication on a cultural plane: To understand the community to which the patient belongs, his/her cultural factors that may infl uence h ealth and disease and also for economic understanding of the patient. • Communication on an intellectual plane: To give adequate explanation for their conditions and help the patients develop insight into their ailments.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the best suited role for a medical social worker?

options.b: Designing coping strategies, interviewing and case work

mcqs.explanation: A medical social worker is a person who is trained mainly in social work and interviewing. He/she carries out duties that augment public and community healthcare by way of identifying, understanding and relaying important information about a patient's d eterminants of health. They are not involved in active treatment, prescribing or providing economic support.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following practices is covered under the COPRA act?
mcqs.explanation: Consumer Protection Act or COPRA was instituted in 1986 and deals with consumer rights. It recognizes six rights of the consumers, which are: • Right to safety • Right to be informed • Right to be heard • Right to choose • Right to seek redressal524 • Right to consumer education

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is used to describe an interview used to note the gradual influence of some social or psychological process?
mcqs.explanation: A repetitive interview is used to note the gradual influence of some social or psychological process. A record is maintained to understand the changes. Interviews are methods used widely in investigations and in research. A proper interview technique must be employed to achieve the objective. Aims of an interview: • To secure information usually through face to face association and to understand the individual/group being interviewed. • T o form a hypothesis. • To collect personal data for quantitative purposes. • To collect data from secondary sources of information. Types of interviews: • A direct or structured interview consists of predetermined questions and sequence. • A non-directive or unstructured interview doesn't have any sequence of questions set beforehand. The interviewer listens and allows the speaker to narrate his/her own experiences or opinions. • A focused interview is usually use d t o study effects of mass communication like radio broadcasts or film. In this, the interviewer/researcher focuses on a particular aspect on the problem and draws responses from people. • A repetitive interview is used to note the gradual influence of some social or psychological process. A record is maintained to understand the changes.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Arrange the following steps of an interview in the correct order in a sequence.

options.a: Starting an interview, making a report, establishing contact, securing rapport
options.b: Establishing contact, making a report, starting an interview, securing rapport
options.c: Establishing contact, starting an interview, securing rapport, making a report
options.d: Starting an interview, securing rapport, making a report, establishing contact

mcqs.explanation: The correct sequence of steps of interviewing are establishing contact, starting an interview, securing rapport, making a report. Techniqu e of interviewing involves: • Establishing contact • Starting an interview • Securing rapport • Recall • Probe questions • Encouragement525 • Guiding the interview • Recording • Closing the interview • Report

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the application of scientific methods to investigate the study of complex human organizations, services and management called?
mcqs.explanation: Operational research is the application of scientific methods of investigation to study complex human organizations, services and management. Pure research is also called fundamental research or basic research. It is aimed at improving scientific theories or understanding of them. Applied research is a methodology used for a specific, practical problem like diseases or business. It involves the practical a pplication of science.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What was the purpose of setting up the Nirbhaya Fund?

options.d: Providing free medical care for women

mcqs.explanation: The Nirbhaya Fund was set up by the government of India for promoting the safety of women.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Choose the correct match.

options.a: Gross Domestic Product- gross income generated only from within the country
options.b: Gross National Product- gross domestic product minus the depreciation on a country's capital g oods
options.c: Net National Product- income generated from within the country and income received from abroad
options.d: Net Domestic Product- market value of all final goods and services in a country during a year after allowing for depreciation

mcqs.explanation: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the income generated only from within the country and does not include income received from abroad.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What percentage of GDP was spent on public health in 2020?
mcqs.explanation: The total public health expenditure is around 1.25% percentage of India's GDP (National Health Profile 2020 report). The National Health Policy, 2017 states the aim to increase this to around 2.5% by 2025.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A mother brings her 4-year-old boy for a well-baby check-up. Upon examination the paediatrician diagnoses her son with hidden hunger. What is meant by the term hidden hunger?

options.a: Child's diet is deficient in carbohydrates
options.c: Child is taking a diet that is deficient in essential amino acids
options.d: Child suffers from deficiency of omega 3 fatty acids

mcqs.explanation: Hidden hunger refers to micronutrient deficiency. It occurs when there is deficiency in intake or absorption of micronutrients like vitamins, iron, zinc, etc. The health effects of these deficiencies are less obvious or invisible and thus referred to as hidden hunger. The consequences of hidden hunger are seen in all ages.526

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which o f the following statements is correct with regards to the estimation of poverty line?

options.a: Per capita expenditure of Rs. 32 per day in urban areas
options.b: Per capita expenditure of Rs. 47 per day in rural areas
options.c: Daily calorie intake of 2100 calories in urban areas
options.d: Daily calorie intake of 2700 calories in rural areas

mcqs.explanation: An estimate of the poverty line is the expenditure required for a daily calorie intake of 2100 in urban areas and 2400 in rural areas, per person. Income-based poverty line in India is per capita expenditure of Rs. 47 in urban areas and Rs. in rural areas per day.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following legislations does not offer social security for industrial workers?
mcqs.explanation: The Labour Charter Act does not offer social security for industrial workers. Social security is the security that society furnishes through appropriate organization, against certain risks to which its members a re exposed. These risks include sickness, maternity, old age and death. Social security for industrial workers is given by: • Workmen's Compensation Act • The Family Pension Scheme • Central Maternity Benefit Act • Employees' State Insurance Act Social security for civil servants is given by governments in the form of pension, gratuity, provident fund, etc. The Central Government Health Scheme provides security to employees of the Central Government. Insurance schemes f rom the likes of Life Insurance Corporation of India, etc . have security schemes for the general public.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a component of the global hunger index (GHI)?

options.d: Percentage of undernourished children under 5 years

mcqs.explanation: The infant mortality rate is not a component of the global hunger index. The Global Hunger Index (GHI) has three dimensions. These dimensions are measured by indicators. GHI score = (1/3 X standardized PUN) + (1/6 X standardised CWA) + (1/6 X standardised CST) + (1/3 X Standardised CM) Where, • PUN is the proportion of the population that is undernourished • CWA is the prevalence o f wasting in children under 5 years of age • CST is the prevalence of stunting in children under 5 years of age527 • CM is the proportion of children dying under the age of 5 years of age. The result lies on a scale from 0 to 100, with 0 meaning no hunger and 100 being the worst score. The GHI is given by the International Food Policy Research Institute. In 2021, India's GHI was 27.5. It ranks 101 among 116 countries. In the 2022,India's GHI stands at 29.1, and India ranks 107th out of the 121 countries.Dimensions Indicators Inadequate food supp ly Proportion of the population undernourished Child mortality Under 5 mortality rate Child undernutrition Wasting in children under 5 yearsStunting in children un der 5 years528

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a component of the definition of safe and wholesome water?
mcqs.explanation: Water intended for human consumption must be safe and wholesome. It must be colorless. Safe and wholesome water is defined as: • Free from pathogenic agents • Free from harmful chemicals • Pleasant to taste, free from colour and odour • Usable for domestic purposes Water is said to be polluted when it does not fulfill the above criteria.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: In an urban PHC, an increasing number of skin diseases are being reported due to inadequate water supply in the region. What would be the adequate supply of water for them to meet their needs for all domestic purposes?

options.b: 150–200 litres per capita per d ay

mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of skin diseases is suggestive of water-washed diseases caused by improper hygiene related to an inadequate water supply. I n urban areas, –200 litres per capita per day is the recommended allowance to meet the needs for all kinds of domestic purposes. In rural areas, the set target of water supply to be achieved in India is around 50-55 litres per capita per day.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: What are the norms for the required litres of water per capita per day in rural areas?
mcqs.explanation: According to the National Rural Drinking Water Programme, the requirement of water in rural areas (areas with public water posts) is 55 litres per capita per day. This is in accordance with the 12th Five Year Plan. For reasons of comparability, t he source of water provision in rural areas should be within a distance of 100 metres from the household or the time taken to fetch water should not be > minutes. Note: Park textbook mentions 40-50 litres per capita per day as the norm. However, in the 12th five year plan period, the Government of India enhanced the rural drinking water supply norms from 40 litres to 55 litres per capita per day.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: What is the purest form of water in nature?
mcqs.explanation: 537 Rain water is the purest form of water in nature. It contains a very low amount of total dissolved solids (TDS). Rain water is the origin of both surface and ground water. Sources of water: • Rain • Surface water: • Impounding reservoirs • Rivers and streams • Tanks, ponds and lakes • Ground water: • Shallow wells • Deep wells • Springs

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a source of surface water?
mcqs.explanation: Shallow wells are sources of ground water. Sources of water: • Rain • Surface water: • Impounding reservoirs • Rivers and streams • Tanks, ponds an d l akes • Ground water: • Shallow wells • Deep wells • Springs

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: What is the area from which water drains into impounding reservoirs known as?
mcqs.explanation: The area draining into the impounding reservoirs are known as catchment areas. Impounding reservoirs are also called embankment ponds. These reservoirs are artificial lake-like water bodies. They are made by building an embankment or earth fill in an area into which natural water flows and can be stored for usage. Dams are also built to create these reservoirs. Water from these reservoirs is second in purity to rainwater b ut is not completely free from impurities . Catchment areas are the main sources of impurities in the water in impounding538 reservoirs. The image given below shows catchment area:

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: What is the most common type of well in India?
mcqs.explanation: Dug wells are the most common type of wells in India.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about artesian wells?

options.a: It is not common in India
options.b: Water i s put under pressure between two impervious layers
options.c: No pump is required to bring water to surface
options.d: It is a type of shallow well

mcqs.explanation: Artesian wells are types of deep wells.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Step wells belong to which of the following types of wells?
mcqs.explanation: Step wells belong to the type of pucca dug wells.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: An outbreak of guinea worm disease was reported among villagers who used step wells for drinking water. In order to arrest the spread of disease, a decision was made to replace step wells with sanitary and safe wells. All of the following measures would be considered during its construction except:

options.a: Must be located at least 15 metres away from sources of contamination
options.b: A partition space for washing clothes and vessels
options.c: Lining must be made to a depth of 6 metres or more
options.d: Hand-pump must be made to handle rough use

mcqs.explanation: Washing clothes, vessels, and bathing must be prohibited around wells to avoid contamination of the water. Step wells are a type of pucca wells which enable people to descend into the well to fetch water. It is obsolete now, as there is considerable personal contact between the user and the water which can pose a health hazard to the com munity.539

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: What is the minimum length that the platform of a well should extend around it in all directions?
mcqs.explanation: The platform of a sanitary well should stretch for at least 1 metre around the well in all directions.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a water-washed disease?
mcqs.explanation: Cholera is a water-borne disease and not a water-washed disease. The diseases which are transmitted by improper hygiene and are widely related to circumstances where there is inadequate water supply are called water-washed diseases. Some examples of water-washed diseases are: • Conjunctivitis • Trachoma • Scabies • Typhus

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: A multipurpose worker is spraying herbicides on aquatic plants as part of vector control measures in your area. Which of the following water-related diseases can be controlled by this approach?
mcqs.explanation: Filariasis (caused by B.malayi) is transmitted by Mansonia species of mosquito that breeds in water bodies containing aquatic vegetation. It can be controlled by the use of herbicides to destroy aquatic vegetation. Water-related diseases are classified as:Category Examples Water-borne diseases Caused by ingestion of water contaminated by human or a nimal faeces , or urine contai ning pathogenic bacteria or v iruses.ex: Cholera, typhoid , a moebic and bacillary dysente ry, and other diarrhoeal disea ses . Water-washed diseases Caused by poor personal hygi ene .ex: Scabies , trachoma, fle a-, lice - and tick-borne diseas es, in addition to the majorit y of waterborne diseases (whi ch are also water-washed ). Water-based diseases Caused by parasites found in intermediate organisms livin g in water.ex: Dracunculiasis, schistosomiasis and some ot her helminths .540 Category Examples Water-related diseases trans mitted by insect vectors Caused by vectors that breed in waterex : Dengue , filariasis, malaria , onchocerciasis, tryp anosomiasis and yellow fever.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Which of the following methods of purification of water cannot be used on a large scale?
mcqs.explanation: Berkefeld filter is used for the purification of water on a small scale (ex: in households).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: During your posting as a rural m edical officer, you conduct an awareness drive prior to the monsoon season in order to highlight the necessity of water purification. Which of the following methods would you not recommend for a household setup?
mcqs.explanation: Slow sand filter is a method of filtration used for the purification of water on a large scale.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: When river water is stored properly, by how much percent does the bacterial count drop in the first 5-7 days?
mcqs.explanation: When river water is stored properly, the bacterial count drops by as much as 90% in the first 5 – days. Purification during the storage of water is a natural process that takes place by physical, chemical and biological phenomena. Components of water purification include storage, filtration a nd disinfection .

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: What is the other name for slow sand filters?
mcqs.explanation: Slow sand filters are also called biological filters.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a part of a slow sand filter?
mcqs.explanation: Components of a slow sand filter include: • Under-drainage system • Sand bed and a layer of organic matter • Filter control system • Supernatant water • Filter box541

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true about slow sand filters?

options.b: The thickness of sand bed i s 2 metres
options.c: It takes a longer duration for water purification
options.d: The sand grain size is 0.4 to 0.7 mm

mcqs.explanation: Slow sand filters take a longer duration than most other methods for purification of water.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes Schmutzdecke?

options.a: Layer of alum flocculate on supernatant water
options.b: Layer of algae and diatoms on supernatant water
options.c: Layer of alum flocculate on surface of sand bed filter
options.d: Layer of algae and diatoms on surface of sand bed filter

mcqs.explanation: Schmutzdecke refers to the vital layer which is formed by algae, plankton, diatoms and bacteria on the surface of the sand bed filter.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not the vital layer of a slow sand filter?
mcqs.explanation: The vital layer of a slow sand filter is also called the zoogleal layer, Schmutzdecke, or the biological layer.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Where is the vital layer of the slow sand filter seen?

options.a: On top of the raw water

mcqs.explanation: The vital layer of the slow sand filter is seen on the sand bed.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: What does the venturi meter measure in a slow sand filter?
mcqs.explanation: Venturi meters measure the bed resistance or loss of head in a slow sand filter. The following image shows a venturi meter:542

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an incorrect statement about rapid sand filters?

options.a: No preliminary storage of raw water is required
options.d: Can be gravity or pressure type

mcqs.explanation: Frequent washing of the filter bed is required in rapid sand filters. This is done by backwashing.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: What is the effective size of sand grains in a rapid sand filter?
mcqs.explanation: Effective size of sand grains in a rapid sand filter is 0.4 – 0.7 mm. Effective size of sand grains in a slow sand filter is 0.2 – 0.3 mm.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Rapid sand filter is different from the slow sand filter by which of the following features?

options.c: Sand particles are of smaller size
options.d: Skilled lab or i s needed

mcqs.explanation: Skilled labor is required for rapid sand filters. Unskilled labor is enough for slow sand filters. Comparison of rapid and slow sand filters:Rapid sand filter Slow sand filter Space Occupies very little space Occupies large area Rate of filtration (million gall ons per acre per day) 200 m.g.a.d 2-3 m.g.a.d. Effective size of sand 0.4-0.7 mm 0.2-0.3 mm Preliminary treatment Chemical coagulation and se dimentation Plain sedimentation Washing By back-washing By scraping the sand be d Operation Highly skilled Less skilled Loss of head allowed 6-8 feet (2- 2.5 m) 4 feet (1.5 m) Removal of bacteria 98-99% 99.9- 99.99%

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a ceramic filter that can be used for small scale purification of water?
mcqs.explanation: Filtration of water on a small scale is done by ceramic filters like Pasteur Chamberland, Berkefeld, and Katadyn filters. Ceramic filters are not widely used in India. The most important parts of these filters are the filter candles. Filter candles of the fine type help in removing bacteria but not viruses. These filter candles need to be cleaned periodically as they get clogged with impurities and bacteria. Types of ceramic filters include: • Pasteur Chamberland filter – I t has a candle made of porcelain. Image of a Pasteur Chamberland filter is shown below:543 • Berkefeld filter - it has a candle made of infusorial earth or kieselguhr. Image of a Berkefeld filter is shown below:• Katadyn filter - the surface of this filter is coated with a silver catalyst. The incoming bacteria are killed on contact with the surface by the oligodynamic action of silver ions which are liberated into the water. Image of a Katadyn filter is shown below:544

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - I: Sources and purification of water
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect about ceramic filters?

options.a: Surface of Berkefeld filter is lined with a silver catalyst
options.b: Chamberland filter has a porcelain filter candle
options.c: Oligodynamic action is seen with Katadyn filter
options.d: They are not widely used in India

mcqs.explanation: Berkefeld filter has a candle made of infusorial earth or kieselguhr. Ceramic filters are used for small scale purification of water. They are not widely used in India. The most important parts of these filters are the filter candles. Types of ceramic filters include: • Pasteur Chamberland filter – It has a candle made of porcelain. • Berkefeld filter - it has a candle made of infusorial earth or kieselguhr. • Katadyn filter - the surface of this filter is coated with a silver c atalyst. T he incoming bacteria are killed on contact with the surface by the oligodynamic action of silver ions which are liberated into the water.545

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the method of choice for the purification of highly polluted water on a large scale?
mcqs.explanation: Superchlorination followed by dechlorination is done for purification of highly polluted water on a large scale.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true regarding chlorination of water?

options.a: Orthotolidine test measures only combined chlorine
options.b: Chlorine acts best when the pH of water is around seven
options.c: It kills bacteria, viruses, spores a nd slime organisms
options.d: Hypochlorite ions are mainly responsible for its disinfectant activity

mcqs.explanation: Chlorine acts best when the pH of water is around seven because of the predominance of the hypochlorous acid. Most water sources have a pH around 6.5–7, making chlorination an effective form of disinfection. Option A: Orthotolidine test measures both free and combined chlorine in water. Option C: Chlorination kills pathogenic bacteria, but has no effect o n spores and certain viruses. Option D: The disinfecting action of chlorine is mainly due to hypochlorous acid.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You assign a male health worker at a sub-centre with the task of chlorinating public water resources. What is the minimum concentration of free residual chlorine that should be maintained for effective chlorination?

options.a: 0.5 mg/litre for a contact period of 1 hour
options.b: 0.5 mg/litre for a contact period of \275 hour
options.c: 0.8 mg/litre for a contact period of 1 hour
options.d: 0.8 mg/litre for a contact p eriod o f \275 hour

mcqs.explanation: The minimum recommended concentration of free residual chlorine for routine chlorination is 0.5 mg/litre for a contact period of 1 hour.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: As an epidemiologist, you are investigating an outbreak of cholera. What is the minimum free residual chlorine level that should be maintained in pipelines to prevent further spread of the outbreak?
mcqs.explanation: The minimum level of free residual chlorine to be maintained in pipelines following an outbreak of cholera is 0.5 mg/litre. After a disaster (such as a flood), the water bodies are contaminated with sewage and drainage. The m ixing of faeces in drinking bodies increases the risk of numerous microbial infections. The advisable level of free residual chlorine in water bodies after a disaster is, therefore, higher i.e. 0.7-0.9 mg/litre.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The municipal corporation in your area is performing routine chlorination of drinking water supplies. Which of the following statements about chlorination is incorrect?

options.a: Free chlorine is released in water after breakpoint chlorination
options.b: Chlorine demand is the amount needed to kill spores, protozoal cysts and helminthic ova
options.c: 0.5 ppm of free chlorine must be present in water after the breakpoint has been r eached
options.d: Contact period of 1 hour is necessary

mcqs.explanation: Chlorine demand is the amount of chlorine that is needed to kill bacteria, and to oxidize all the organic matter and ammoniacal substances in the water. It is the difference between the amount of chlorine added to the water and the amount of residual chlorine re maining a t the end of a specific period of contact (usually 1 hour) at a given temperature and pH of the water.551 0.5 ppm (0.5 mg) of free chlorine must be present in water after the breakpoint has been reached.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following tests identifies free and combined chlorine in water separately?
mcqs.explanation: Orthotolidine-arsenite test determines both free and combined chlorine in water separately. Orthotolidine test determines free and combined chlorine together. Chick Martin test and Garrod's test are used to test the efficacy of disinfectants.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following compounds is predominantly responsible for the disinfecting property of bleaching powder?
mcqs.explanation: The disinfectant property of bleaching powder is predominantly due to the action of hypochlorous acid. It is 70-80 times more effective t han hypochlorite ions. Bleaching powder, also known as chlorinated lime (CaOCl2), has 33 per cent of chlorine in it. When chlorine is added to water, there is the formation of hydrochloric and hypochlorous acids. The hydrochloric acid is neutralized by the alkalinity of the water. The hypochlorous acid ionizes to form hydrogen ions and hypochlorite ions, as follows: H2O + Cl2 \037 HCl + HOCl HOCl \037 H + OCl

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A village health and sanitation team is planning to disinfect 100 wells. Which of the following is the most cost-effective method in this scenario?
mcqs.explanation: Disinfection of wells using bleaching powder is the most widely used and cheapest method.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An outbreak of viral hepatitis A has been reported in a village. On investigating, you find a contaminated well in the locality to be the source of the outbreak. Which of the following method s would you advise for chlorinating the well in this scenario?
mcqs.explanation: The double pot method is used for disinfecting wells by chlorination in emergencies like hepatitis A outbreak in a village. Double pot method has an inner and outer pot, each with a hole in it and covered with a polyethylene foil. The inner pot is filled with bleaching powder and coarse sand. The double pot system is then lowered into a well. This device can work satisfactorily for 2 – 3 weeks in small wells containing about 4500 litres of water.552

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In your community medicine practicals, you are given an apparatus as shown in the image given below. Which of the following statements regarding the apparatus is true?

options.a: The indicator used is bromocresol purple
options.c: It is used to estimate free chlorine levels
options.d: It is used to estimate combined chlorine levels

mcqs.explanation: The image given is that of a Horrock's apparatus. The indicator used in Horrock's apparatus is starch iodide. Horrock's apparatus contains 6 white cups (200 ml each), 1 black cup with a circular mark, metal spoons with 2 grams of bleaching powder in each, 7 glass stirring rods, 1 special pipette and 2 droppers. It is not usful in measuring free and combined chlorine. It estimates the chlorine demand of water and is used to calculate the amount of bleaching powder used to disin fect t he well .

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the amount of bleaching powder required to disinfect 455 litres of water if the 4th, 5th, and 6th cups of a Horrock's apparatus show distinct blue color?
mcqs.explanation: The dose of bleaching powder required is 8 grams. It is given by (n x 2) gms for 455 litres of water, where n is the number of the first cup that shows distinct blue color. In this scenario, the dose of bleaching powder required to disinfect 455 litres of water is (4 x 2) = 8grams.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The water sample from a well is tested using Horrock's apparatus. It is observed that the 3rd cup shows a blue color after the addition of the starch-iod ine i ndicator. How much bleaching powder will be required to disinfect 2275 litres of the well water?
mcqs.explanation: The dose of bleaching powder required is 30 grams. It is given by (n x 2) gms for 455 liters of water, where n is the number of the first cup that shows a distinct blue color. In this scenario, the dose of b leaching powder required to disinfect 455 liters of water is (3 x 2) = 6 grams .553 Since 2275/455 = 5. The amount of bleaching powder required to disinfect 2275 litres of water = 6 x 5 = 30 grams.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following agents have residual germicidal effect when used for treatment of water?
mcqs.explanation: Chlorine has residual germicidal effect when used for treatment of water. UV radiation, ozone gas, iodine and potassium permanganate have good germicidal action but do not have residual germicidal effect.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following properties of ozone makes it less suitable for the disinfection of water on a large scale?

options.a: Ozone requires a long time period for action
options.d: It has no residual disinfectant action

mcqs.explanation: Ozone has no residual disinfectant action. Ozone gas can be used as a primary disinfectant of water in a large scale. Ozone disinfection is usually followed by b iological filtration or granular activated carbon to prevent further contamination during distribution. Chlorine residual treatment is also done as ozone does not provide for a residual disinfectant action.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a lower-pressure membrane process for treatment of water?
mcqs.explanation: Microfiltration is a lower-pressure membrane process used for the treatment of water. Membrane processes are employed in the large scale treatment of water. They are classified as high-pressure processes and lower-pressure processes. • High-pressure processes: • R everse osmosis - Rejects monovalent ions and organic molecules of molecular weight > daltons. It is most commonly used for desalination of brackish water and sea water. The membrane pore size is < 0.002 \265 m. • Nanofiltration - Allows monovalent ions such as sodium or potassium to pass but rejects a high proportion of divalent ions like calcium and magnesium and some higher molecular weight organics. The membrane pore size ranges from 0.001 – 0.01 \265m. • Lo wer-pressure p rocesses : • Ultrafiltration - Rejects organic molecules of molecular weight > 800 daltons. The membrane pore size ranges from 0.002 - 0.003 \265 m. • Microfiltration - Rejects colloidal and suspended material. It does not separate molecules and is usually used before reverse osmosis. The membrane pore size ranges from 0.01 – 12 \265m.554

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: Above what level does the turbidity of water become visible to the naked eye?
mcqs.explanation: Turbidity of water becomes visible to the naked eye above 4 nephelometric turbidity units (NTU). The ideal level of turbidity is <1.0 NTU for household drinking purposes. However, in situations where this is not achievable, the maximum permissible limit is <5 NTU.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: What is the maximum permissible level of chloride in drinking water?
mcqs.explanation: The maximum permissible level of chloride in drinking water is 600 mg/litre.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: A detectable taste begins to appear in drinking water if chloride levels in it exceed:
mcqs.explanation: A detectable taste begins to appear in drinking water if chloride levels in it exceed 250 mg/litre.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: A large number of cases of methemoglobinemia were reported among infants from a municipal area. On detailed investigation, the nitrate l evels i n drinking water were found to be elevated in that area. This complication can occur when nitrate level in drinking water exceeds:
mcqs.explanation: Nitrates in the excess of 45 mg/L may cause methaemoglobinemia in infants.561

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: Which is the most undesirable metal in drinking water?
mcqs.explanation: The most undesirable metal in drinking water is lead.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: What is the acceptable level of total dissolved solids in drinking water in India?
mcqs.explanation: According to the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), the acceptable level of total dissolved solids (TDS) in drinking water in India is 500 mg/L. Note: There is a variation in the value of the acceptable level of total dissolved solids in drinking water provided by WHO and the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). While the WHO sets the value at 600 mg/L, the BIS has set it at 500 mg/L for India.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: What is the proposed guideline for the permissible radioactivity values for drinking water?

options.a: Gross alpha activity up to 0.1 Bq/L and gross beta activity up to 1 Bq/L
options.b: Gross alpha activity up to 1 Bq/L and gross beta activity up to 0.5 Bq/L
options.c: Gross a lpha activity up to 0.5 Bq/L and gross beta activity up to 1 Bq/L
options.d: Gross alpha activity up to 0.1 Bq/L and gross beta activity up to 0.5 Bq/L

mcqs.explanation: The proposed guideline for the permissible radioactivity values for drinking water is: Gross alpha activity up to 0.5 Bq/litre. Gross beta activity up to 1.0 Bq/litre.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: In view of a hepatitis A outbreak in a hostel, samples of drinking water are collected to detect fecal contamination. Presence of which of the following organisms serves as the most reliable evidence of fecal contamination?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of Escherichia coli is the most suitable and reliable evidence of fecal contamination of water. Klebsiella aerogens is a typical example of the non-fecal group of coliform organisms.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: A microbiologist is testing a sample of drinking water to detect fecal contamination. The presence of all of the following organisms indicates a positive test result except:
mcqs.explanation: Presence of Staphylococcus and Klebsiella aerogens does not indicate fecal contamination of water. Biological indicators of fecal pollution o f water are: • Streptococcus faecalis • Escherichia coli • Clostridium perfringens

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect about water purification and pollution?

options.a: Presence of clostridial spores indicates recent contamination
options.b: Sodium thiosulphate c an be used to dechlorinate water
options.c: Coliforms must not be detectable in any 100 ml sample of drinking water
options.d: Coliforms can be detected by the multiple tube method

mcqs.explanation: The presence of clostridial spores indicates remote or intermittent contamination of water.562

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: Multiple tube method is done for which of the following?

options.a: Detecting the presence of coliform organisms in a sample of water
options.b: Detecting the presence of enteric viruses in a sample of water
options.c: Estimating the levels of mercury in a sample of water
options.d: Estimating turbidity of a sample of water

mcqs.explanation: The multiple tube method is done to detect the presence of coliform organisms in a sample of water. In order to estimate the presumptive coliform count, water to be tested is inoculated into tubes containing a suitable liquid medium. These tubes are then incubated and examined after an appropriate period of time. The test is called presumptive because the reaction observed in the tube may occasionally be due to other organisms. The proportion of false-positive reaction s o btained depends both on the bacterial flora of the water under examination and the medium used. Lactose broth, or MacConkey's broth, with bromocresol purple as an indicator and a standardized concentration of bile salts incubated between 35\260C–37\260C for 48 hours, seems to be the most suitable media for presumptive tests.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: What is the acceptable b acteriological quality of drinking water in small communities?

options.a: No coliform bacteria in 100 ml of water
options.b: Upto 10 coliform bacteria in 100 ml of water
options.c: Upto 10 coliform bacteria in 1000 ml of water
options.d: Upto 100 coliform bacteria in 1000 ml of water

mcqs.explanation: There must be no coliform bacteria in any 100 ml sample of drinking water as its presence indicates fecal contamination.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: Which of the following criteria is true for safe drinking water according to the WHO guidelines?
mcqs.explanation: The desirable pH of safe drinking water ranges from 6.5 to 8.5. The maximum permissible level of chloride in drinking water is 0.6 g/L (600 mg/L), and that of nitrates is 0.05 g/L (50mg/l). The concentration of lead must be kept at <0.01 mg/L. It is the most undesirable metal in drinking water.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a criterion included in the guidelines for drinking water quality recommended by WHO?
mcqs.explanation: According to WHO, the permissible level of color in drinking water is <15 true color units (TCU). The permissible level of turbidity in drinking water is <1 NTU. The permissible level of arsenic is up to 0.01 m g/l and nitrites is up to 3 mg/l.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: Temporary hardness of water is primarily due to the presence of which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: 563 The temporary hardness of water is primarily due to the presence of calcium and magnesium bicarbonates.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not cause hardness of water?
mcqs.explanation: Calcium carbonate does not cause hardness of water. Hardness of water is caused by bicarbonates and sulphates of calcium and magnesium. There are two types of hardness of water: • Temporary (carbonate) hardness is due to bicarbonates of calcium and magnesium. • Permanent (non-carbonate) hardness is due to sulphates, chlorides and nitrates.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: What is the level of hardness in soft water?
mcqs.explanation: The level of hardness in soft water is <1 mEq/litre.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: How would you classify a water sample that has a level of hardness of 200 mg/litre?
mcqs.explanation: When the level of hardness of water is in the range of 150 – 300 mg/litre, it is classified as hard water.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: A health worker is conducting periodic quality test for water sources in your area. What should be the hardness level of water used for drinking purpo ses?
mcqs.explanation: Water used for drinking purposes must have a hardness level of 1 – 3 mEq/L (moderately hard).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: Above what level of hardness is softening of water recommended?
mcqs.explanation: Softening of water is recommended when the hardness exceeds 3 mEq/l (150 mg/litre).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a method of removal of hardness of water?
mcqs.explanation: Filtration is not a method of removal of hardness of water. Methods for removal of hardness of water are: • Boiling • Addition of lime564 • Addition of sodium carbonate (soda ash) • Base exchange process

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Water - III: Water Quality and Standards
mcqs.question: What is the composition of permutit which is used for the base exchange process to remove hardness of water?
mcqs.explanation: Permutit is a complex chemical compound made of sodium, aluminium and silica. It is used to remove hardness of water by base exchange process. Permutit has the property of ion exchange and removes calcium and magnesium from water. It removes both permanent and temporary hardness.565

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The water vapor and pollutants tend to get trapped in the lowermost layers of the atmosphere in winters. What is the reason behind this occurrence?
mcqs.explanation: In winters, water vapor and pollutants get trapped in the lowermost layers of the atmosphere due to temperature inversion. This results in the formation of smog, especially in the winter months, and this is a possible threat to human health.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an indicator of air pollution?
mcqs.explanation: The heavy metal pollution index (HPI) is not an indicator of air pollution. It is a rating method and an effective tool to assess the water quality with respect to heavy metals. Indicators of air pollution: • Sulfur dioxide - best indicator • S moke or soiling index • Grit and dust measurement • The co-efficient of haze • Air pollution index • Suspended particle matter (SPM)

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which agency monitors air quality in India?
mcqs.explanation: Central Pollution Control Board is the main body that monitors air quality in India and sets standards.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Greenhouse gases include all of the following except:
mcqs.explanation: Carbon monoxide is not a greenhouse gas.574 Greenhouse gases include: • Water vapor • Carbon dioxide • Methane • Tropospheric ozone • Nitrous oxide • Chlorofluorocarbons (non-natural)

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following protocols set the standard to reduce the emission of greenhouse gases internationally?
mcqs.explanation: The Kyoto Protocol was an internal agreement to set internationally binding emission reduction targets. It is linked to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. The parties committed to reduce GHGs by 18% in the period between 2013-2020.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about global warming?

options.a: Carbon dioxide is the major greenhouse gas
options.c: CFC increases ozone levels in the stratosphere
options.d: Kyoto Protocol called for 10% reduction in greenhouse emissions

mcqs.explanation: Carbon dioxide is the major greenhouse gas. Tropospheric ozone and chlorofluorocarbons a re also important greenhouse gases. Water vapor is the most abundant greenhouse gas, but the water vapor produced directly by human activity contributes very little to the amount of water vapor in the atmosphere. Hence, its emissions have not been estimated. Greenhouse gases lead to global warming, which is the major cause of climate change. Climate change accelerates species extinction on earth.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following i s incorrect regarding indoor air pollutants?

options.a: Carbon monoxide is produced by fuel combustion
options.c: Radon is an indoor air pollutant
options.d: Mercury vapor is a source of indoor air pollution

mcqs.explanation: Mercury is not a source of indoor air pollution. Indoor a ir pollutants commonly arise from coal or fuel combustion. They include: • Carbon monoxide • Polyaromatic hydrocarbons • Nitrogen • Sulfur oxides • Pesticides • Asbestos575 • Lead • Radon

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is unlikely to be seen in individuals affected by indoor air pollution?
mcqs.explanation: Indoor air pollution has not been linked with neurodevelopmental disorders. It can result in a higher incidence of the following: • Pregnancy complications • Chronic lung disease • Childhood pneumonia

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The best indicators for routine monitoring of air pollution are:

options.a: Sulfur dioxide, smoke, and suspended particles
options.b: Sulfur dioxide, lead, and particulate matter

mcqs.explanation: The best indicators for routine monitoring of air pollution are sulfur dioxide, smoke, and suspended particles.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an index of thermal comfort?
mcqs.explanation: The heat transfer coefficient is a measure of the heat transfer by convection or phase transition. It is not an index of thermal comfort. Thermal c omfort is the subjective feeling of temperature in an environment. Optimum levels of thermal comfort help to increase productivity. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What are t he instruments used to measure atmospheric pressure called?
mcqs.explanation: Atmospheric pressure or barometric pressure is measured using barometers. The most commonly known barometers are Fortin's barometer, Kew pattern station barometer, and the barograph. The Indian Meteorological Department uses the Kew pattern station barometer. The pressure at Earth's surface, close to sea level averages around 760 mmHg, and man is adapted to live around this.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What sweat excretion rate in acclimatized, healthy young men is indicative of intolerable air temperature?
mcqs.explanation: A sweat excretion rate of > 4.5 L /4 hours in acclimatized, healthy young men is indicative of intolerable air temperature. This is known as McArdle's maximum allowable sweat rate. This is the maximum allowable sweat rate that is compatible with the normal physiological reaction of acclimatized, healthy young men who are exposed to heat. The predicted four-hour sweat rate (P4SR) is obtained from readings of air and mean radiant temperature and air velocity under different work intensities. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an index of heat stress?
mcqs.explanation: Air velocity index is not an index of heat stress. Heat stress is the load of heat that must be dissipated from the body if it is to remain in thermal equilibrium. Factors that affect heat stress are metabolic rate, air temperature, humidity, air movement, and radiant t emperature. Indices for heat stress are: • Predicted four-hour sweat rate • Equatorial comfort index • Heat stress index.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is unlikely to be seen in individuals suffering from heat stress?
mcqs.explanation: Numbness is an effect of cold stress, not heat stress. Effects of heat stress include: • Heatstroke • Heat hyperpyrexia • Heat exhaustion • Heat cramps • Heat syncope

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What level of heat stress index correlates with severe heat strain in individuals?
mcqs.explanation: A heat stress index of 40–60 indicates severe heat strain. It can pose a threat to health and greatly impair work if not fit or acclimatized. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about cold stress?

options.b: Dry-cold conditions occur at temperatures above freezing
options.c: Cold stress can cause desire to sleep
options.d: Frostbite is common at high altitudes

mcqs.explanation: Dry-cold conditions occur at temperatures below freezing and are common at high altitudes. It results in complications like frostbite. Wet-cold conditions occur at temperatures above freezing. It results in complications like trench foot. Cold stress also causes hypothermia which can induce numbness, loss of sensations, muscular weakness, desire to sleep, coma, and death.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about ventilation?

options.b: Involves quality control of outgoing air

mcqs.explanation: Ventilation involves the quality control of incoming air but not quality control of outgoing air. It also involves the replacement of vitiated air(air with decreased oxygen content) by a supply of fresh outdoor air. It aims to provide a comfortable thermal environment and reduce the risk of infections.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the ideal number of air changes in a drawing-room?
mcqs.explanation: The number of air changes in drawing rooms or living rooms must be 2 – 3 per hour. The number of air changes in work rooms and assemblies must be 4 – 6 per hour.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is ventilation provided by wind blowing through a space called?
mcqs.explanation: Ventilation provided by wind blowing through a space is called perflation. Ventilation can be broadly classified as natural and mechanical: Natural ventilation includes: • Perflation is the ventilation of a space achieved by allowing wind to blow through it and removing the obstacles for this to happen (e.g., opening windows and doors). • Aspiration occurs when there is an obstruction as wind bypasses it and creates a suction action • Diffusion is the passage of air through small spaces or o penings • Cross -ventilation is when air is allowed a natural path through the space by providing openings at appropriate places, opposite each other. The drawback of natural ventilation is that regulation of air quality is not possible. Mechanical ventilation includes: • Exhaust ventilation utilizes exhaust fans placed high up near the roof on the external walls. A vacuum is created by which fresh air enters the ventilated space. • Plenum ventilation uses centrifugal f ans to blow fresh air into the room and create a positive pressure , by which vitiated air is pushed out.586 • Balanced ventilation is the combination of both exhaust and plenum methods of ventilation. • Air conditioning can be done through mechanical ventilation. It is the simultaneous control of all or at least three factors that influence air quality in a confined room or space. These factors include temperature, humidity, air movement, distribution, dust, bacteria, odours and toxic gases.

mcqs.explanation: Perflation is not a type of mechanical ventilation. It is a type of natural ventilation. It is the simultaneous control of all or at least three factors that influence air quality in a confined room or space. These factors include temperature, humidity, air movement, distribution, dust, bacteria, odours and toxic gases.

mcqs.explanation: The mechanical system of ventilation that employs only centrifugal fans is plenum ventilation. mcqs.explanation: Prevention of non-infectious diseases is not a social goal of housing standards. The social goals of housing include: • Shelter • Family life • Access to community facilities • Family participation in community life • Economic stability

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an organization related to housing in India?
mcqs.explanation: National Rural Housing Services is not an organization related to housing in India. mcqs.question: Which of the following was launched to address rural housing in India?
mcqs.explanation: The Indira Awas Yojana was launched in 1985 to address rural housing in India. It is now called the Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awaas Yojana (2015), which is a social welfare flagship programme created to provide housing to the rural poor in India.
