mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about the requirements of good lighting?

options.a: Colour of light should approximate daylight
options.c: Ceilings and roofs must have a 50% reflection factor

mcqs.explanation: For good lighting in a room, ceilings and roofs must have an 80% reflection factor. The requirements of good lighting are: • Sufficient light to prevent eye strain. An illumination of 15 to 20-foot candles is accepted for satisfactory vision. • Distribution of light must be uniform with the same intensity over the whole field of work • Absence of glare • Absence of sharp shadows600 • The source of light should be constant and steady • The colour of light should approximate the colour of daylight • Ceilings and roofs must have an 80% reflection factor. mcqs.explanation: Daylight factor (D.F.) is the ratio of the illumination at a given point to illumination at a point exposed simultaneously to the whole hemisphere of the sky (taken as 500-foot candles) excluding direct sunlight. The D.F. is used for the measurement of daylight. It is determined by a modified photo-electric meter called daylight factor meter. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the upper limit of daily exposure to noise which people can tolerate without hearing damage?
mcqs.explanation: The upper limit of daily exposure to noise which people can tolerate without hearing damage is 85 dB. This is the maximum acceptable noise level. It has been observed that the human ear responds in a non-uniform way to different sound-pressure levels. A weighting curve, called curve A has been constructed which takes into account the subjective effects of sound. Sound-pressure levels are therefore expressed in dBA because this reflects the perception of that sound emiss ion b y the normal human ear. Acceptable noise levels in various surroundings are listed below.Locality Place Acceptable noise levels (dBA) Residenti al Bedroom 25 Living ro om Commerc ial Office 35 – 45 Conferen ce 40 – 45 Restaura nts 40 – 60 Industria l Worksho p 40 – 60 Laborato ry 40 – 50 Educatio nal Classroo m 30 – 40 Library 35 – 40 Hospitals Wards 20 – 35604

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the acceptable noise level in a hospital ward?
mcqs.explanation: The acceptable noise level in a hospital ward is 20 – 35 dBA. Acceptable noise levels in various surroundings are listed below.Locality Place Acceptable noise levels (dBA) Residenti al Bedroom 25 Living ro om Commerc ial Office 35 – 45 Conferen ce 40 – 45 Restaura nts 40 – 60 Industria l Worksho p 40 – 60 Laborato ry 40 – 50 Educatio nal Classroo m 30 – 40 Library 35 – 40 Hospitals Wards 20 – 35

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A steel plant worker presented with sudden onset of bilateral hearing loss after hearing a blast in the plant. On examination, both his tympanic membranes were ruptured. What would have been the minimum intensity of the blas t to cause this injury?
mcqs.explanation: A minimum intensity of 160 dB can lead to rupture of the tympanic membrane, resulting in hearing loss.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 32-year-old patient presents with complaints of whistling and buzzing in both his ears since yesterday. He gives a history of being exposed to continuous noise due to construction near his house. At what intensity of noise do such conditions begin to occur?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of auditory fatigue that begins to appear with exposure to noise at 90 dB.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An airline ground staff officer with difficulty hearing is found to have permanent hearing loss on follow up. Continuous exposure to sound above what intensity can cause this condition?
mcqs.explanation: 605 Continuous exposure to sound above 100 dB can cause permanent hearing loss.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The WHO defines disabling hearing loss in adults as a hearing loss of more than:
mcqs.explanation: According to WHO, disabling hearing loss refers to hearing loss greater than 35 dB in the better hearing ear in adults. WHO grades of hearing loss:Grade of hearing loss range Range of hearing los s 0: No impairment < 20 dB 1: Mild - 34 dB 2: Moderate 35 - 49 dB 3: Moderately Severe 50 - 64 dB 4: Severe 65 - 79 dB 5: Profound >80 dB

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a unit of absorbed dose of radiation?
mcqs.explanation: Rad is a unit of absorbed dose of radiation by tissue or material. It has been replaced by the SI unit which is gray (Gy).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the SI unit of radiation dose equivalent?
mcqs.explanation: The SI unit of radiation dose equivalent is sievert (Sv). Dose equivalent (H) = Absorbed dose (D) x Quality factor (Q) The quality factor depends upon the density of ionization produced in the tissue by radiation. The factor Q for X-rays, \033-rays and electrons is 1 and that for an alpha particle is 20.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the permissible dose of manmade radiation per year?
mcqs.explanation: The permissible dose of manmade radiation is 5 rads per year.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A young girl who is 1 month pregnant is concerned about a chest X-ray that she had taken 3 weeks back. What is the dose of radiation below which deterministic effects on the fetus are not seen?
mcqs.explanation: 606 Deterministic effects on the fetus are not seen below 5 rads or 50 mSv of radiation. Dose limits of radiation exposure are: • Occupational exposure - Effective dose should not exceed 20 mSv/year averaged over 5 consecutive years / 30 mSv in a year. • General public exposure - Effective dose should not exceed 1 mSv/year • Occupational exposure for pregnant staff - Effective dose to the fetus should not exceed 1mSv/year (same as the general public). For pregnant patients who require d iagnostics with exposure to ionising radiation, the radiation protection principles are followed: • The exposure should be justified • The dose should be as low as reasonably achievable (ALARA principle) • The dose limit is not particularly specified as it involves a single time exposure to diagnostic radiation. Usually, the effective dose to the fetus is <1msv and deterministic effects to the fetus are not seen below 50 mSv (5 Rad).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What was the 10 days rule in radiation related to?
mcqs.explanation: The 10 days rule in radiation was related to pregnancy. It is aimed at preventing unintentional exposure of the embryo or fetus to radiation. This rule states that if a radiograph is being done on the abdomen or pelvis of a woman in her childbearing age, then it should be done during the 10 days following the onset of menstruation. In most situations, there is growing evidence that strict adherence to the "ten-day rule" may be unnecessarily restrictive. Since organogenesis starts 3 to 5 weeks post-conception, i t was felt that radiation exposure in early pregnancy couldn't result in malformation. Based on this, it was suggested to do away with the 10-day rule and replace it with a 28-day rule. This means that radiological examination if justified, can be carried throughout the cycle until a period is missed.607

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Solid wastes generally should not contain:
mcqs.explanation: Solid wastes should not contain nightsoil, which is untreated human waste (feces). Solid wastes generally contain: • Garbage (food wastes) • Rubbish waste (papers, plastics, etc.) • Demolition products (bricks, masonry, etc.) • Sewage treatment residue614 • Dead animals and other waste materials

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a method of solid waste or refuse disposal?
mcqs.explanation: Oxidation ponds are not used for solid waste or refuse disposal. It is used for sewage treatment. Methods of solid waste disposal are: • Dumping • Controlled tipping • Incineration • Composting • Manure pits • Burial

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most insanitary method of waste disposal?
mcqs.explanation: The most insanitary method of waste disposal is dumping. Methods of waste disposal include: • Controlled tipping or sanitary landfill - Most satisfactory method of refuse disposal where suitable land is available • Incineration - Method o f choice where suitable land is not available • Composting • Manure pits • Burial • Dumping

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which method is most appropriate when suitable land for waste disposal is available?
mcqs.explanation: Controlled tipping is the most satisfactory method of refuse disposal when suitable land is available. In this method, waste materials are placed in a trench, compacted, and covered with earth at the end of the day. This method is also called a sanitary landfill. Chemical, bacteriological and physical changes occur in the buried refuse with temperatures risin g t o over 60 degrees Celsius within 7 days. Methods used for controlled tipping are: • Trench method615 • Ramp method • Area method Sewage farming is also a method of sewage disposal in places where sufficient and suitable land is available. It is also called land treatment or broad irrigation.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In controlled tipping, the amount of land required for the trench method to be practiced for a population of 10,000 is:
mcqs.explanation: In controlled tipping, one acre of land is required by the trench method to be practiced for a population of 10,000. It is also known as a sanitary landfill. It is the most satisfactory method of refuse disposal where suitable land is available. In this method, waste material is placed in a t rench or other prepared area . Then, it is adequately compacted and covered with earth at the end of the day. Methods used in controlled tipping are: • Trench method: Done in places where level ground is available • Ramp method: Well suited where the terrain is moderately sloping • Area method: Used for filling land depressions, disused quarries, and clay pits

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about composting?

options.a: Bangalore method is an aerobic process
options.b: Mechanical composting uses a controlled environment
options.c: Nightsoil can also be disposed with composting
options.d: Compost has few or no disease-causing pathogens

mcqs.explanation: The Bangalore method of composting is an anaerobic process. Composting is a method of combined disposal of refuse and n ightsoil. In this process, organic matter is broken down into compost. It has manure value and few or no disease-causing pathogens. Bangalore method is an anaerobic method and is also called hot fermentation process. Trenches with a depth of not more than 90cm are used for this. This is done by spreading a layer of refuse (15 cm thick) at the bottom of the trench and nightsoil (5cm thick) is added next. Layers of refuse and nightsoil are added alternatively till the heap ris es t o 30cm above ground level . The heap is then covered with excavated earth. At the end of 4 – 6 months, decomposition will be completed. Mechanical composting is an aerobic process. In this method, compost is manufactured on a large scale by processing raw materials and turning out a finished product. The refuse is first cleared of salvageable materials. It is then pulverised to reduce the size of particles to less than 2 inches. The pulverised refuse is then mixed with sewag e, s ludge or nightsoil in a rotating machine and incubated .

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: All of the following are methods of disposing only excreta except:
mcqs.explanation: 616 Bangalore method, also known as the hot fermentation process, is a form of composting that is used for disposing of both solid waste and nightsoil (excreta). Methods of excreta disposal: • Unsewered areas: • Service type latrines (conservancy system) - In this, nightsoil is collected manually from pail or bucket type latrines and then disposed of by burying or composting • Non-service type latrines (sanitary latrines) • Borehole latrine • Dug well or pit latrine • Water-s eal l atrines – Examples are P.R.A.I. type , R.C.A. type, and Sulabh shauchalaya • Septic tanks • Aqua privy • Latrines for camps and temporary use • Shallow and deep trench latrine • Pit latrine • Borehole latrine • Sewered areas: • Water carriage system and sewage treatment • Primary treatment – Screening, removal of grit and plain sedimentation • Secondary treatment – Trickling filters, activated sludge process • Other methods – sea and river outfalls, sewage farming, oxi dation ponds

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A military camp is being set up in an area for one month. Which of the following latrines will not be suitable here?
mcqs.explanation: Septic tanks cannot be used for camps and temporary purposes. Methods of excreta disposal: • Unsewered areas: • Service type latrines (conservancy system) - In this, nightsoil is collected manually from pail or bucket type latrines and then disposed of by burying or composting • Non-service type latrines (sanitary latrines) • Borehole latrine • Dug well or pit latrine • Water-seal latrines – Examples are P.R.A.I. type, R.C.A. type, and Sulabh shauchalaya • S eptic t anks • Aqua privy617 • Latrines for camps and temporary use • Shallow and deep trench latrine • Pit latrine • Borehole latrine • Sewered areas: • Water carriage system and sewage treatment • Primary treatment – Screening, removal of grit and plain sedimentation • Secondary treatment – Trickling filters, activated sludge process • Other methods – sea and river outfalls, sewage farming, oxidation ponds

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the oldest non-service type of latrines in India?
mcqs.explanation: The oldest non-service type of latrines in India is the borehole latrine. It was introduced in the 1930s to combat hookworm infections. Special equipment called auger is used to dig a borehole latrine. Advantages: • No special staff is needed for upkeep as after using the latrine is closed and another hole is dug elsewhere • Breeding of flies is less • No water pollution if located far from a water source Demerits: • Fills up rapidly • Augers are not readily available • Water pollution is still a risk618

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: There is an outbreak of hookworm infection in your locality. On investigation, it is found that the outbreak is a result of open-air defecation. The district council decides to construct an RCA type of latrine in every household. What is the optimum water seal required?
mcqs.explanation: The optimum water seal required for an RCA type of latrine is 2 – 2.5 cm. It was designed by the Research-cum-Action Projects (RCA) in Environmental Sanitation of the Ministry of Health. Water seals aids in preventing flies and other organisms from reaching the waste. It also prevents the escape of odors and foul gases, eliminating the nuisance from the smell.Features of RCA type of latri ne Location More than 15m away from th e water source Squatting plate Should be impervious and sh ould allow for drainage of wa ter Pan Receives the nightsoil , urine, and washes water. Trap Holds the water and provides thewater seal .A good trap ha s an effective seal of around 2 – 2.5 cms. Connecting pipe Present in indirect type and a bsent in direct type Dug well Has to be changed after it is f illed Superstructure Built for privacy and shelter619

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A h ealth committee formed under Swachh Bharat Mission is involved in constructing septic tanks in every household. Which of the following is true about a septic tank?
mcqs.explanation: The recommended retention period for a septic tank is 24 hours. If the retention period is too short, there is insufficient treatment of sewage and if it is too long, then undue septicity results. There are single and double-chambered septic tanks. The minimum capacity recommended for a septic tank is 500 gallons. The depth of a septic tank is usually 1.5 to 2m.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about the sewage treatment shown in the image below?

options.a: Desludging must be done at least once a year
options.c: Anaerobic digestion occurs inside the tank
options.d: Soap and disinfectants like phenol should not be used inside the tank

mcqs.explanation: The given image is of a septic tank. It is not useful for very large communities and is used for household sewage treatment.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is wastewater without human excreta called?
mcqs.explanation: Wastewater that doesn't contain human excreta is called sullage. It is also called greywater. E.g., waste water from the kitchen. Sewage is wastewater from a community that contains solid and liquid excreta along with street and yard washings. It is also called blackwater.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the average amount of sewage which flows though the sewerage system in 24 hours known as?
mcqs.explanation: The average amount of sewage which flows though the sewerage system in 24 hours is known as dry weather flow.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not used to express the strength of sewage?
mcqs.explanation: E. coli count is not used to express the strength of sewage. The strength of sewage is e xpressed only in terms of: • Biochemical oxygen demand • Chemical oxygen demand • Suspended solids

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What does the biochemical oxygen demand of sewage indicate?
mcqs.explanation: Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) indicates the organic content of sewage.620 It is defined as the amount of oxygen absorbed by a sample of sewage for aerobic destruction by living microorganisms. If wastewater contains toxic substances, the organic load is measured by the chemical oxygen demand.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following values of biochemical oxygen demand would indicate that the sewage is weak?
mcqs.explanation: Sewage with biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) of 100mg/L would indicate that it is weak. If the BOD is \034 300 mg/L, sewage is said to be strong.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a part of the p rimary treatment of sewage?
mcqs.explanation: Aeration tank is not a part of primary treatment of sewage. It is a part of secondary treatment of sewage.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the function of the grit chamber in modern sewage treatment plants?

options.d: Allow anaerobic auto-digestion of organic matter

mcqs.explanation: The function of the grit chamber in modern sewage treatment plants is to allow heavier particles in the sewage to settle.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Trickling filter method is used in which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: The trickling filter method is used in secondary sewage treatment.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the heart of the activated sludge process?
mcqs.explanation: The heart of the activated sludge process is the aeration tanks.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a requirement for an oxidation pond?
mcqs.explanation: Aeration is not a requirement for an oxidation pond. Oxidation ponds are also called waste stabilization ponds or redox ponds or sewage lagoons. They have become a popular method of purifying sewage for small communities. It is usually a n open, shallow pool of around 1 – 1.5m depth with an inlet and outlet. Requisites for an oxidation pond include:621 • Algae • Saprophytic bacteria • Sunlight All of the above factors help in the treatment of sewage waste through aerobic and anaerobic processes. The effluent formed can be used for land irrigation or can be forwarded for further treatment.622

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding mosquitoes?

options.a: It is the definitive host in malaria
options.b: Mansonia is a vector for Malayan filariasis
options.c: Life span of mosquitoes is around 8 to 34 days
options.d: All mosquitoes can travel only for 100 metres

mcqs.explanation: Most mosquitoes can travel or fly for distances up to 11 kms.631

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following species of mosquitoes breed in dirty water and water bodies containing aquatic vegetation respectively?
mcqs.explanation: Culex species of mosquitoes breed mostly in dirty and polluted water. Mansonia species of mosquitoes breed in water bodies containing aquatic vegetation.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements i s false about larva of mosquitoes?

options.b: Culex larva lies in water with head faced downwards
options.c: Anopheles larva lies parallel to the undersurface of water

mcqs.explanation: Anopheles larva has no siphon tube as shown in the image below.The image given below shows Culex larva having a siphon tube.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Identify the species of mosquito shown in the image below.
mcqs.explanation: 632 The given image is of an Aedes mosquito. They can be identified with the stripes on the legs and body. They are also called tiger mosquitoes because of their stripes.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old lady from a tribal area presented with fever, chills, vomiting, and abdominal pain for 4 days. The peripheral smear of the patient is given below. Which of the following is true about the mosquito which transmits this disease?

options.d: Keeps its body horizontal while feeding

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and peripheral smear showing ring form/ early trophozoites in erythrocytes are suggestive of Plasmodium falciparum malaria. It is transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes. They have spotted wings. They breed in clean water. Their larva has no siphon tube and lies parallel to the undersurface o f water . They tend to sit with their heads low and their rare ends raised high, especially when feeding.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A patient presented with fever, headache, and retro-orbital pain for 3 days. He tested positive for the NS1 antigen. Which of the following mosquitoes transmits the disease he's suffering from?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with the positive NS1 antigen test is suggestive of dengue fever. It is transmitted by the Aedes mosquito, which is also called as tiger mosquito.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following diseases is not transmitted by Aedes mosquito?
mcqs.explanation: Japanese encephalitis and West Nile fever are transmitted by Culex mosquitoes. Chikungunya, yellow fever, and rift valley fever are transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A banker who is scheduled to travel to Congo is advised to take the yellow fever vaccine. What is the flight range of the mosquito which transmits this disease?
mcqs.explanation: Yellow fever is transmitted by the Aedes mosquito. Its flight range is 100 metres.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A patient with fever and mucosal bleeding is diagnosed with dengue fever. Which of the following is false about the mosquito which transmits this disease?

options.b: Development of larva from egg does not require water
options.d: It has a striped body pattern

mcqs.explanation: Dengue fever is transmitted by the Aedes mosquito. The conversion from the egg stage to the larval stage of this mosquito requires water. Eggs of any mosquito species do not survive without water. But the eggs of Aedes mosquitoes lie dormant in dry conditions for up to about nine months. They can hatch if exposed to favourable conditions such as water and food.633

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 10-year-old boy is brought to the OPD with complaints of fever and headache for 5 days. Serological examination shows the presence of IgM antibodies to the JE virus. Which of the followin g mosquitoes transmits this disease?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Japanese encephalitis. It is transmitted by Culex mosquitoes like Culex tritaeniorhynchus

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Match the following diseases and the mosquitoes which transmit them.

options.a: l - c, ll - a, lll - d, iV - b
options.b: l - a, ll - b, lll - c, lV - d
options.c: l - b, ll - c, lll - d, lV - a
options.d: l - d, ll - a, lll - b, lV - c

mcqs.explanation: The correctly matched diseases with the mosquitoes which transmit them are:Disease Mosqu ito Yellow fever Aedes Bancroftian filariasis Culex Malaria Anoph eles Malayan filariasis Manso nia

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about pathogenic mosquitoes?
mcqs.explanation: Aedes and Anopheles lay eggs singly. Culex lays eggs in rafts and Mansonia lays eggs in star-shaped clusters. Anopheles has spotted wings while the other pathogenic species have unspotted wings. Aedes transmits yellow fever, dengue and chikungunya. Culex is the main vector for JE and filariasis.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are posted in a PHC in a coastal region as a part of your rural postings. Which of the following Anopheles species is most commonly found here?
mcqs.explanation: Anopheles stephensi and Anopheles sundaicus are found in coastal regions. Anopheles stephensi is also the main vector of malaria in urban regions. Anopheles culicifacies and A nopheles philippinensis are found in the plains. Anopheles fluviatilis and Anopheles minimus are found in foot-hill regions.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following species of Anopheles mosquitoes transmits urban malaria?
mcqs.explanation: Urban malaria is transmitted by Anopheles stephensi.634

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the distance around an airport or seaport t hat has to be kept free of all mosquitoes?
mcqs.explanation: The distance around an airport or seaport that has to be kept free of all mosquitoes is 400 metres. This helps in limiting the spread of vector-borne diseases to new geographic regions.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Identify the following vector.
mcqs.explanation: The given image is of a housefly, whose scientific name is Musca domestica.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a method of disease transmission by houseflies?
mcqs.explanation: Houseflies do not transmit diseases by biting. They transmit diseases by mechanical transmission by their legs or feet, vomit drop, and defecation. They transmit a variety of diseases like: • Typhoid • Polio • Dysentery • A moebiasis • Anthrax • Yaws

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which disease is transmitted by the following vector that is found in cracks and crevices of walls in the day time?
mcqs.explanation: The given image is of a sandfly. It transmits visceral leishmaniasis. Note: Sandfly acts as a vector for the following diseases: • Kala-azar • Oriental sore • Sandfly fever • Oroya fever Japanese encephalitis is transmitted by the Culex mosquito. Dengue is transmitted by the Aedes mosquito. Trypanosomiasis is transmitted by the tsetse fly.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Sandfly does not transmit:
mcqs.explanation: 635 Trench fever is not transmitted by sandflies. It is transmitted by lice and caused by Bartonella quintana.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following diseases is transmitted by the vector shown in the image given below?
mcqs.explanation: The vector shown in the image is a tsetse fly. It transmits African sleeping sickness (African human trypanosomiasis). Tsetse flies belong to the genus Glossina. They have not demonstrated insecticide resistance. Methods of tsetse fly control include spraying of DDT, clearing of vegetation, destruction of wild game and genetic control.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A patient presents with blurring of vision and a painless swelling over his left elbow which has gradually been increasing in size over the past 1 year. On examination, he is noted to have patchy depigmentation on his legs. Which of the following vectors transmits the disease he's suffering from?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of onchocerciasis, also known as river blindness. It is transmitted by blackfly. The usual presentation of onchocerciasis is the formation of a subcutaneous nodule or onchocercoma. It is a firm non-tender nodule arising from bony sites like the scalp, elbow, ribs, and iliac crest. It is associated with pruritus and rashes. Patients also present with patchy depigmentation on the legs called leopard skin. The presence of microfilaria in the eye causes photophobia a nd gradual loss of vision. The most severe manifestations are sclerosing keratitis and chorioretinitis which can lead to blindness. Blackfly is also called Simulium. It has a flight range of almost 100 miles, making control of adult flies difficult. Abate is widely used as a larvicidal insecticide. The image given below shows a blackfly.636

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Spot the wrongly matched arthropod and disease.
mcqs.explanation: Blackflies (Simulium) are the vector for onchocerciasis and not Chaga's disease. An arthropod or an invertebrate that transmits infection is called a vector. It transmits infection by: • Inoculation into or through the skin or mucous membrane • Biting • Deposit of infective materials on skin or food or other objects Note: Chagas disease is transmitted by the reduviid bugs or kissing bugs or triatomines.637

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: A veterinarian with fever, chills, and myalgia is diagnosed with Q fever. Which of the following is the most common reservoir of this disease?
mcqs.explanation: Ticks are the most common reservoir of Q fever. Coxiella burnetii is the causative pathogen. The most commonly identified sources of human infection are farm animals, such as cattle, goats, and sheep. Infected mammals shed C. burnetii in their urine, feces, milk, and placenta. Human exposure to C. burnetii may occur as a result of inhalation of contaminated aerosols arising from the placenta or parturient fluids of infected livestock or from contaminated secretions on t he surface of newborn animals. People working with farm animals and veterinarians are at a higher risk of infection.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not transmitted by hard ticks?
mcqs.explanation: Relapsing fever is not transmitted by hard ticks, but by soft ticks.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: Peripheral smear of a patient with high grade fever, arthralgia, and myalgia is given below. Which of the following transmits this disease?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with peripheral smear showing maltese cross appearance is suggestive of babesiosis. It is transmitted by ticks.647

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: A patient with fever and joint pain presented with the following lesion on his left leg. Which of the following transmits this disease?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with the image showing bulls eye rash is suggestive of Lyme disease. It is transmitted by Ixodes tick.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about the vector in the given image?
mcqs.explanation: The given image is of a soft tick. It can withstand starvation for over a year. The head of the soft tick lies ventrally and it does not have a scutum. It serves as a reservoir for Q fever and transmits relapsing fever.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about the vector in the given image?

options.c: Its nymphal stage has seven stages
options.d: It lays hundreds of eggs at once

mcqs.explanation: The given image is of a hard tick. The hard tick has only one nymphal stage. It has a hard chitinous shield called the scutum which c overs the entire back in males a small portion in the front in females. It feeds night and day and cannot withstand starvation. It lays several hundreds or thousands of eggs in one sitting.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: Which of the following are also known as chiggers?
mcqs.explanation: Larval forms of trombiculid mites are also known as chiggers. They are spider-like arthropods which are vectors for scrub typhus. The image given below shows trombiculid mite.648

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: Which of the following diseases is transmitted by the vector shown in the image given below?
mcqs.explanation: The given image is of a reduviid bug. It transmits American trypanosomiasis, also known as Chagas disease. Reduviid bug is also known as the kissing bug or triatomine bug. It lives in cracks, fissures and other spaces in the walls and ceilings of human dwellings. Residual spraying with HCH or dieldrin is used for the control of these bugs. Option B: African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness) is transmitted by the tsetse fly. Option C: Onchocerciasis is transmitted by the b lackfly (Simulium). Option D: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) is transmitted by the sandfly.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: A 10-year-old boy presents with complaints of nocturnal pruritus. Examination shows burrows over the skin of his hands. KOH mount prepared from these lesions is given below. Which of the following vectors transmits this disease?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and KOH mount showing the itch mite are suggestive of scabies. It is transmitted by itch mite or Sarcoptes scabiei. The female parasite burrows into the epidermis where it breeds. It is a small parasite, barely visible to the naked eye, with 4 pairs of legs. Its life cycle consists of four stages—egg, larva, nymph, and adult stages. Its spread can be t hrough close contact or contaminated clothes. Benzyl benzoate is very effective as a sarcopticide. HCH, tetmosol, and sulphur ointments are also used. The image given below shows itch mite.649

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: Which of the following diseases is not transmitted by mites?
mcqs.explanation: Kyasanur forest disease is not transmitted by mites. It is a viral hemorrhagic fever transmitted by hard ticks. Scabies, scrub typhus, and rickettsial pox are transmitted by mites.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: You are given the following slide during your community medicine practicals. Which of the following diseases is not transmitted by this vector?
mcqs.explanation: The above image is of a head louse. It does not transmit endemic typhus which is transmitted by fleas. Lice transmit epidemic typhus, relapsing fever, and trench fever.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: Which of the following diseases is transmitted by lice?
mcqs.explanation: Epidemic typhus is transmitted by lice and caused by Rickettsia prowazekii. Murine typhus is transmitted by the rat flea. T ick typhus is transmitted by a hard tick. Scrub typhus is transmitted by trombiculid mite.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not transmitted by lice?
mcqs.explanation: Q fever is not transmitted by lice. It is spread by the inhalation of contaminated aerosols containing Coxiella burnetti. Soft ticks are the most common reservoirs of Q fever. The aerosols arise from the placenta or parturient fluids of infected livestock or from contaminated secretions on the surface of newborn animals.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: Identify the following vector which transmits murine typhus.
mcqs.explanation: The given image is of a rat flea-Xenopsylla cheopis. It transmits murine typhus.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: Which of the following diseases is not transmitted by rat fleas?
mcqs.explanation: Pneumonic plague is not transmitted by rat fleas. It is transmitted by inhalation of aerosolized droplets. Rat fleas are vectors for murine or endemic typhus, bubonic plague, and hymenolepiasis caused by Hymenolepis nana and Hymenolepis diminuta.650

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: A flea survey is being conducted in an area prone to outbreaks of plague. Which of the following indices is not used for this purpose?
mcqs.explanation: Incidence of plague is not an index used in flea surveys. Flea indices that are used in flea surveys are: • General flea index • Specific flea index • Percentage incidence of flea species • Rodent infestation rate

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about sand fleas?
mcqs.explanation: Sand fleas cause ulcers in the feet. They are also called jigger or chigoe fleas. The species called Tunga penetrans is of particular importance as it causes tungiasis. The fertilized female burrows into the skin of the feet, often beneath the nail and causes ulcers. T etanus and gas gangrene frequently occur because of secondary infection. They flourish best in sandy soil and are found in the western parts of India. The below image shows a sand flea.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: Which of the following is transmitted by the vector shown in the image given below?
mcqs.explanation: 651 The given image is of a cyclops or water flea. It is the vector for guinea worm disease or dracunculiasis and fish tapeworm infection. Humans are infected with these diseases by drinking water that contains cyclops. Its average life span is 3 months. Physical methods like straining and boiling of water can ensure the killing of this organism. Chemicals that can be used to control cyclops are chlorine, lime, and abate. Biological methods include Gambusia fish and barbel fis h.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Medical Entomology - Ticks, Fleas and Mites
mcqs.question: Which of the following diseases is not associated with rodents?
mcqs.explanation: Ascariasis is not associated with rodents. Diseases related to rodents are: • Bacterial - • Plague • Tularemia • Salmonellosis • Leptospirosis • Rat-bite fever • Viral - • Lassa fever • Encephalitis • Hemorrhagic fever • Rickettsial - • Scrub typhus • Endemic typhus • Rickettsial pox • Parasitic - • Hymenolepis diminuta • Leishmaniasis • Amoebiasis • Trichinosis • Chagas disease • Fungal - • Histoplasmosis • Ringworm652

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following would you advise as the best approach to control arthropods?
mcqs.explanation: Environmental control is the best approach to control arthropods. The principles of arthropod control include: • Environmental control - Best approach • Chemical control - Use of insecticides, pesticides, etc. • Biological control - Use of larvivorous fish like Gambusia • Genetic control • Newer methods - • Chemosterilants • Insect growth regulators • Sex attractants • Integrated approach involves usage of more than one modality of arthropod control

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the best method to control houseflies?
mcqs.explanation: 659 The best method to control houseflies is environmental control by the elimination of breeding places. They have shown resistance to a number of insecticides, including DDT.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an organo-phosphate insecticide?
mcqs.explanation: Dieldrin is an organo-chlorine insecticide. It is a broad-spectrum insecticide that acts as a contact, stomach, and inhalation poison.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a n aryl organo-phosphate insecticide?
mcqs.explanation: Malathion is an alkyl organophosphate insecticide. It is used as an ultra-low volume spray in mosquito control.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following insecticides is least toxic to man?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options, malathion is the least toxic to man. It is the least toxic organo-phosphate insecticide.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about fenthion?

options.a: It is used as a residual spray
options.b: It is used as a repellent

mcqs.explanation: Fenthion is not used as a repellant. A commonly used repellant is N,N-diethyl-m-toluamide (DEET) that is used for protection from mosquitoes and ticks. Fenthion is a broad-spectrum insecticide that acts as both contact and stomach poison. It is used as a larvicide in mosquito control and also as a residual spray.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about pyrethrum?

options.a: Residual action as good as DDT
options.d: Can be used synergistically with DDT

mcqs.explanation: Pyrethrum does not have a residual action like DDT or other synthetic insecticides. So, most space sprays contain pyrethrum and DDT for synergistic action. Pyrethrum is a natural insecticide of vegetable origin. It is extracted from the flowers of Chrysanthemum cinerariafolium. It kills adult mosquitoes and other insects instantly on mere contact.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following cannot be used to describe p yrethrum?
mcqs.explanation: 660 Pyrethrum is not used as a residual spray. It is a contact and nerve poison that is also used as a space spray.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a synthetic pyrethroid insecticide?
mcqs.explanation: Permethrin is a synthetic pyrethroid. Pyrethroids are synthetic insecticides, which are derived from naturally occurring pyrethrins. Pyrethroids modify the sodium channels in neuronal membranes and thereby disrupt the electrical signalling in the nervous system.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following vectors has not shown resistance to synthetic pyrethroids, in a widespread manner in India yet?
mcqs.explanation: Sandflies (Phlebotomus) have not shown resistance to synthetic pyrethroids, in a widespread manner in India yet.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes DDT?
mcqs.explanation: DDT is a contact poison that belongs to the organochlorine family. It has been widely used but a number of organisms have become resistant to its effects now.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: During a dengue outbreak, the municipal corporation plans a DDT s praying initiative. Which of the following is false about this insecticide?

options.a: Para-para isomer is the most active fraction
options.c: It has residual action up to 18 months
options.d: It causes immediate death of insects

mcqs.explanation: DDT does not cause the immediate death of insects. It takes several hours for its action to be complete. It contains 70 – 80% of para-para isomer that is the most active fraction of DDT. It acts on the nervous system of insects. The residual action of DDT may last as long as 18 months depending upon the tr eated s urface.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the usage of Paris green for mosquito control?

options.c: Harmful in normal doses to man and animals

mcqs.explanation: Paris green is very effective against surface-feeding Anopheles. It is an anti-larval measure and is a stomach poison. It is not harmful in normal doses to man and animals.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following mosquitoes can be controlled by destroying aquatic plants with herbicides?
mcqs.explanation: Mansonia mosquitoes breed in water with aquatic vegetation, and destroying this vegetation with herbicides would control this mosquito.661

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a mosquito anti-larval measure?
mcqs.explanation: Pyrethrum is an anti-adult measure and not an anti-larval measure. Mineral oils, Gambusia, and Paris green are anti-larval measures used in mosquito control.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which among the following insecticides is most widely used as a space spray?
mcqs.explanation: The insecticide most widely used as a space spray is pyrethrum.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Match the following methods of mosquito control to the appropriate examples.

options.a: I – a, II – b, III – c, IV – d
options.b: I – b, II – d, III – c, IV – a
options.c: I – c, II – a, III – b, IV – d
options.d: I – d, II – b, III – a, IV – c

mcqs.explanation: The correctly matched methods of mosquito control are:Method of control Example Biological control Barbados millio ns Genetic control Sex distortion Chemical control Larvicidal oil Environmental contr ol Source reductio n

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: To curb an outbreak of plague in your locality, the municipal corporation decides to use rodenticides. Which of the following can be given as a single dose for this purpose?
mcqs.explanation: Zinc phosphide is a single-dose rodenticide that causes death in a one-time exposure. Acute or single-dose rodenticides are classified according to the precautions that need to be taken before their use: • Those requiring ordinary care - Red squill, norbormide, zinc phosphide • Those requiring maximal precaution - Sodium fluoroacetate, fluoroacetamide and strychnine • Too dangerous for use - Arsenic trioxide, phosphorus, thallium sulphate Multiple-dose or cumul ative r odenticides cause death after multiple times of exposure. Examples include : • Warfarin • Coumafuryl • Diphacinone662 • Pindone

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following color labels is used to indicate the most hazardous p esticides?
mcqs.explanation: The most hazardous pesticides must have labels in red color. Pesticide toxicity labels: These labels are depicted in the image below.Category of Pesticid e Color of Lab el Extremely toxic Bright red Highly toxic Bright yello w Moderately toxic Bright blue Slightly toxic Bright green663

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What proportion of healthcare waste is hazardous waste?
mcqs.explanation: 15% of health care waste is hazardous waste. It may be infectious, toxic, or radioactive in nature. The remaining 85% is general, non-hazardous waste. Bio-medical waste means any waste that is generated during: • Diagnosis, treatment, or immunization of human beings or animals • Research activities pertaining thereto • Production or testing of biologicals Bio-medical waste is handled as per the Bio-medical Waste Management Rules, 2016. However, these rules do not apply t o the following: • Radioactive wastes • Hazardous chemicals • Solid wastes • Lead-acid batteries • Hazardous wastes • e-Waste • Hazardous microorganisms

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Cytotoxic and expired drugs are disposed by:
mcqs.explanation: Cytotoxic and expired drugs are collected in a yellow bag and then disposed of by incineration. Expired cytotoxic drugs are to be returned to the manufacturer and subjected to incineration, encapsulation, or plasma pyrolysis. Other discarded medicines can be disposed by incineration.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following category of wastes are treated by autoclaving and microwaving?
mcqs.explanation: The final treatment of catheters, urine bags, and gloves is done by autoclaving and microwaving. They belong to recyclable contaminated waste and are disposed of in a red bag. Option A: Human anatomical waste is disposed of by incineration. Option C: Cytotoxic and expired/discarded medicine is disposed of by incineration/plasma pyrolysis/disposal in a secured landfill. Option D: Microbiological waste such as culture plates and slides are pre-treated with nonchlorinated chemicals and later d isposed of by incineration.671

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: While working as a 1st-year resident in the labor ward, where would y ou dispose of the placenta following a delivery?
mcqs.explanation: Human anatomical wastes, like the placenta, are discarded in a yellow bag and disposed of by incineration/ plasma pyrolysis/ deep burial.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements are true about yellow waste disposal bags?
mcqs.explanation: Yellow waste disposal bags are made from non-chlorinated plastic material and chemical liquid wastes are collected in them. Chlorinated items, glass, metal, and rubber are not sent for incineration as incinerating them would produce carcinogenic gases. The right disposal methods of the other options are: • Animal anatomical waste - Collected in yellow bags and later sent for incineration. • Metallic body implants - Collected in cardboard boxes with blue coloured marking and sent for recycling following autoclaving. • PVC gloves - Collected in red bags and sent for autoclaving followed by shredding.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following should not be incinerated?
mcqs.explanation: Specimens of microorganisms and live or attenuated vaccines can be incinerated. Wastes that should not be incinerated are: • Sharps • Pressurized gas containers • Reactive chemical waste • Waste w ith h eavy metals like mercury and cadmium • PV C • Photographic or radiographic waste

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An orthopedic resident has removed a K-wire from the fractured olecranon of a 13-year-old boy. Where should he discard this?

options.d: Le ak -proof and tamper-proof yellow bag

mcqs.explanation: Metallic body implants are disposed of in cardboard boxes with blue-colored markings. The contents of the blue box are sent to Common Biomedical Waste Treatment and Disposal Facility (CBWTF). In the facility, these items are sterilized by autoclaving or microwaving and then sent for recycling.672

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Blood bag is to be disposed in:
mcqs.explanation: Blood bag should be disposed off in the yellow bin.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An HIV -positive man is brought to you following an accident. How would you discard his blood-soaked dressing material?

options.a: Pour 1% hypochlorite on the dressing material and send for incineration
options.b: Pour 5% hypochlorite on the dressing material and send for incineration
options.c: Put the dressing material directly in an appropriate bag and send for incineration
options.d: Pour 10% non chlorinated chemicals on the dressing material and send for incineration

mcqs.explanation: The blood-soaked dressing material should be disposed of in a non-chlorinated yellow bag and sent for incineration. Pretreatment is not a requisite for incinerating soiled waste. Items that require pretreatment with non-chlorinated chemicals before incineration: • Used blood bags • Other infectious plastic and liquid wastes • Laboratory cultures, stocks, or specimens of microorganisms • Live or attenuated vacc ines • H uman and animal cell cultures used in research • Dishes, and devices used for cultures

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following d isposal methods is not as per biomedical waste management guidelines ?

options.a: Disposal of a dead fetus of 21 weeks in a yellow bag by deep burial in rural areas
options.b: Pre-treatment of laboratory cultures with non-chlorinated disinfectant
options.c: Disposal of a glass ampoule with its cytotoxic drug through incineration
options.d: Disposal of radiological waste by deep burial

mcqs.explanation: Radiological waste is not considered biomedical waste. Hence, deep burial is not done. Disposal of radiological is covered under the provisions of the Atomic Energy Act. The radiological effluents are incinerated in a dedicated incinerator having off-gas cleaning facility. Another method is to convert the organic base into an aqueous form by treating it with sodium hydroxide . O ption A: Dead fetuses under the age of viability are considered human anatomical waste. Anatomical waste can be disposed of by deep burial in rural areas, where a common biomedical treatment facility and incineration is not available. Option B: Laboratory cultures are classified under the category of microbiology, biotechnology, and other clinical laboratory waste. They are pretreated with a non-chlorinated disinfectant before they are sent for incineration. Op tion C : The cytotoxic drugs are disposed of along with their packaging, through incineration.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are asked to catheterize an HBsAg-positive man before hernia surgery. According to the BMW management rules , w here would you dispose of the plastic cover of the catheter?
mcqs.explanation: The outer plastic cover of the Foleys catheter is discarded in a black bag. Foleys catheters are packaged in plastic covers to keep them sterile. The plastic cover is not biomedical waste but is a part of general (municipal) waste. Hence, it is discarded in the black bag. The foleys catheter is disposed of in a red bag.673 As per Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, the general waste must be disposed of in green bins (for recyclable waste) and blue bins (for non-recyclable waste) containing black plastic bags.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following diseases should healthcare workers involved in handling biomedical waste be vaccinated against?
mcqs.explanation: Healthcare workers involved in handling biomedical waste should be vaccinated against hepatitis B and tetanus. These are most likely to be transmitted by the handling of biomedical waste. Yearly health check-ups should be done, and a booster dose should be given if needed.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An on-site waste treatment and disposal facility should be built in a hospital if the nearest common biomedical treatment facility is:
mcqs.explanation: According to biomedical waste management rules of 2016, healthcare establishments shall establish an on-site treatment and disposal facility only when a common biomedical treatment facility (CBMWTF) is more than 75 km away. According to these rules, biomedical waste (BMW) from healthcare facilities is to be transported to a CMBWTF. The establishment of CBMWTF reduces the need for transport and cost of treatment/ kg of BMW.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a high-heat system for the treatment of biomedical waste?
mcqs.explanation: Microwaving is a low-heat system for the treatment of biomedical waste. The heating systems used for the treatment and disposal of biomedical waste are:Low-heat system High-heat system Autoclaving:Uses steam. It is of two types -Gravity flow aut oclaveVacuum autoclaveMicr owaving:Uses moist heat and steam generated by microwa ve energy Incineration :Waste is destroy ed /denatured under high tem peraturesPlasma pyrolysis :W aste is treated at high temper atures under controlled condi tions to form gases that are s ubjected to combustion in th e secondary chamberHydrocl aving:The waste is subjected to indirect heating by applyin g steam to the outer jacketDr y heat sterilization:Waste sha rps are treated using dry heat at a temperature >185 C for 150 minutes674

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following disposal m ethods uses high temperature and dry oxidation?
mcqs.explanation: Incineration is a high-temperature dry oxidation process. Waste that is incinerated need not undergo any type of pre-treatment. It helps to reduce weight as well as volume. The temperature in the incinerator is 800\037C in the primary chamber and 1050\037C in the secondary chamber. Types of incinerators: • Rotary kilns • Single chamber pyrolytic • Double chamber pyrolytic The heating systems used for the treatment and disposal of biomedical waste are:Low-heat system High-heat system Autoclaving:Uses steam. It is of two types -Gravity flow aut oclaveVacuum autoclaveMicr owaving:Uses moist heat and steam generated by microwa ve energy Incineration :Waste is destroy ed /denatured under high tem peraturesPlasma pyrolysis :W aste is treated at high temper atures under controlled condi tions to form gases that are s ubjected to combustion in th e secondary chamberHydrocl aving:The waste is subjected to indirect heating by applyin g steam to the outer jacketDr y heat sterilization:Waste sha rps are treated using dry heat at a temperature >185 C for 150 minutes

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a treatment facility, which of the following cannot be used to verify the treatment of biomedical waste done by incineration?
mcqs.explanation: Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis is not used to verify thermal methods of biomedical waste disposal. It is a biological larvicide, used in nonpotable water for killing mosquito larvae. The following can be used to verify the adequacy of thermal methods of biomedical waste disposal: • Bacillus atropheus • Bacillus subtilis • Geobacillus stearothermophilus

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: At a waste treatment facility, pharmaceutical waste was mixed with cement, lime, and water before disposal. What is this method known as?
mcqs.explanation: 675 Inertization is the process of mixing biomedical waste with non-toxic substances to reduce the toxicity of the waste and to reduce the contamination of groundwater. It is most commonly done for incineration ash with high metal content. The typical composition of the inertization mixture is: • 65% pharmaceutical waste • 15% cement • 15% lime • 5% water

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the correct combination of temperature and duration used in a hot air oven?
mcqs.explanation: The correct combinations of temperature and duration of sterilisation in a hot air oven is: • 180\260C for 30 mins • 170\260C for 60 m ins • \037C for 2 hours It can be used to sterilize powders, glasswares, and oils. An autoclave is another apparatus that is used for sterilization. It uses steam at a temperature of 121\037C for 30 mins under 15 lbs of pressure.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: All the following a re the characteristics of waste that can be incinerated except:
mcqs.explanation: Only waste material containing <5% of noncombustible solids can be incinerated. Wastes that are incinerated go in the yellow bag. Waste products with the following characteristics can be incinerated: • Combustible matter >60% • Non-combustible s olid <5% • Non -combustible fine <20% • Low heating volume • Moisture content <30%.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Correctly match the following logos.
mcqs.explanation: The correctly matched logos are as shown below.676

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are working in a covid ward. After doffing, where will you dispose of the plastic coverall?
mcqs.explanation: The plastic coverall used by a healthcare worker during the COVID-19 pandemic should be disposed of in the red bin.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An intern asks for your advice regarding the disposal of needles from the needle tip cutter after a vaccine drive. Which of the following bins will you advise her to discard them in?
mcqs.explanation: Waste sharps including metals (both used, discarded, and contaminated metal sharps) are to be discarded in the white bin.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Chemical waste is disposed in _____ bags.
mcqs.explanation: Chemical waste is disposed of in yellow-colored containers or non-chlorinated plastic bags.677

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding a disaster?

options.a: Occurrence that causes damage to life and property
options.b: Occurrence that has the potential to cause disruption or damage to people
options.c: Occurrence that causes deterioration of health and health services
options.d: Occurrence that can cause substantial economic harm

mcqs.explanation: A disaster is defined as any occurrence that causes damage, ecological disruption, loss of human life, or deterioration of health and health services. It usually requires an extraordinary response from outside the affected community or area.683 A hazard is any phenomenon that has the potential to cause disruption or damage to people and their environment.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which type of natural disaster causes the most deaths?
mcqs.explanation: Hydrological natural disasters cause the most deaths. The Disaster Information Management System of Deslnventar classifies natural disasters into five major categories. They are: • Geophysical - earthquakes, tsunamis, and volcano eruptions • Hydrological - floods, debris flow, and landslides • Meteorological - cyclones, tornadoes, extreme temperatures, s andstorms, blizzards etc. • Climatological - drought, forest wildfire, glacial lake outburst etc. • Biological - epidemics and insect infestations

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following steps of disaster management is in c orrect order?
mcqs.explanation: The correct order is Disaster impact – Response – Rehabilitation – Mitigation. Disaster management includes three aspects: 1. Disaster impact and response: It involves immediate management of mass casualties as follows: • Search, rescue, and first-aid • Field care • Triage • Tagging • Identification of dead 2. Re habilitation o r recovery: It involves the restoration of the pre-disaster conditions by taking steps such as: • Water supply • Basic sanitation and personal hygiene • Food safety • Vector control 3. Mitigation: Measures designed either to prevent hazards from causing disaster or to reduce the effects of the disaster. This also includes preparedness for any impending disasters or in disaster-prone areas.684

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about disaster management?

options.a: Measures to prevent hazards are designed in mitigation phase
options.b: Rescue and evacuation occur in recovery phase
options.c: Measures on vector control are done in rehabilitation p hase
options.d: Field care and tagging are done in disaster impact and response phase

mcqs.explanation: Rescue and evacuation occur in the response phase, not in the recovery phase. Disaster management includes three aspects: 1. Disaster impact and response: It involves immediate management of mass casualties as follows: • Search, rescue, and first-aid • Field care • Triage • Tagging • Identification of dead 2. Rehabilitation or recovery: It involves the restoration of the pre-disaster conditions by taking steps such as: • Water supply • Basic sanitation and personal hy giene • F ood safety • Vector control 3. Mitigation: Measures designed either to prevent hazards from causing disaster or to reduce the effects of the disaster. This also includes preparedness for any impending disasters or disaster-prone areas.685

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common disease after a disaster?
mcqs.explanation: Gastroenteritis is the most commonly reported disease after a disaster. It occurs due to contamination of water supply, damage to the sewerage system, overcrowding and poor sanitation. Therefore, supply of safe drinking water and proper disposal of excreta are the most practical and effective strategies of disease prevention in the post–disaster period.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following diseases is not commonly seen in the post-disaster period?
mcqs.explanation: Leishmaniasis is not commonly seen in the post-disaster period. Diseases that are commonly seen in the post-disaster p hase are: • Gastroenteritis ( most common) • Acute respiratory infections • Leptospirosis • Rickettsiosis • Rabies • Equine encephalitis

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A district in Andhra Pradesh reported severe drought. Which of the following vitamin deficiencies woul d y ou expect to see in this population?
mcqs.explanation: Vitamin A deficiency is the most common deficiency in areas of famines and droughts. It leads to xerophthalmia and blindness.686

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Following a drought in Bihar, the government launched an immediate mass vaccination program. Which of the following vaccines is recommended in such cases?
mcqs.explanation: Measles vaccination is recommended for infants and children, immediately following a disaster. This should be given along with vitamin A supplementation as measles can exacerbate vitamin A deficiency. The vaccination of infants and children against measles is one of the most important public health response measures during a humanitarian crisis when less than 90% of the children or an unknown percentage have already been vaccinated against measles. Measles and po lio v accines are recommended immediately after an emergency. Option A: Cholera vaccine is not recommended. Option B: Hepatitis A vaccine is recommended at the outset of an outbreak. Option C: Tetanus vaccine is recommended in the early stages and post-emergency stage.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Immediately following a disaster, mass vaccination of which of the following vaccines does the WHO recommend?
mcqs.explanation: The WHO does not recommend typhoid, cholera, and rabies vaccines for mass vaccination after a disaster. However, high-risk populations are recommended to take the cholera vaccine. The rabies vaccine i s g iven only for post-exposure prophylaxis.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are a field doctor at the site of an earthquake. You assist in rapidly classifying the injured on the basis of the likelihood of their survival and need for intervention. What is this process called?
mcqs.explanation: The process of rapidly classifying the injured in a disaster on the basis of severity of injury and likelihood of survival with prompt medical intervention is called triage. It is carried out at the site of disaster. Tagging is the identification of patients in a disaster with tags stating their name, age, place of origin, triage category, diagnosis, and initial treatment.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about triage?
mcqs.explanation: In triage, green signifies low priority or ambulatory patients and those with minor illnesses. An internationally accepted four-color coded system, with red having the highest priority is used commonly here.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is correct about reverse triage?

options.a: Classifying the victims based on the severity of their injuries and their survival with treatment
options.b: Highest preference is given to severely injured patients
options.c: More injured victims are given the lowest preference
options.d: Color coding is done with red as the highest priority.

mcqs.explanation: 687 Reverse triage is a situation where the less injured are treated earlier than the ones that are injured more. This is used in wars and military settings, where soldiers may need to return to the field of battle soon after treatment. It is also done when there is a scarcity of medical resources after a disaster. The surge capacity of hospitals is increased to accommodate for the natural disaster, by discharging non-emergent existing patients. This enables hospitals to allow for a n acute increase in incoming patients.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Triage is done during disaster management to ensure treatment of casualties is done properly. What is true about triage done at the disaster site?

options.b: Green labels are for those who need to be transported on priority
options.c: Moribund patients receive the lowest priority
options.d: Most commo nly u sed system is three color code system

mcqs.explanation: Moribund patients receive the lowest priority. This is because despite paying quite a lot of attention, the benefit is still questionable.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the level of residual chlorine to be maintained in the water bodies after a disaster?
mcqs.explanation: The advisable level of residual chlorine in water bodies after a disaster is 0.7-0.9 mg/L. Chlorine is a disinfectant that is added to water bodies. In normal conditions, water should have free residual chlorine (FRC) of 0.2 - 0.5 mg/L. However, during a disaster, there is an increased risk of f ecal contamination of water sources from the sewage systems. Therefore , it is necessary to increase FRC to 0.7 - 0.9 mg/L.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following gas was responsible for the Bhopal Gas Tragedy?
mcqs.explanation: The gas responsible for the Bhopal Gas Tragedy, which occurred on 3rd December 1984 at the Union Carbide Pesticide Plant, was methyl isocyanate.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following emission occurred in Chernobyl explosion accident of 1986?
mcqs.explanation: Chernobyl nuclear explosion occurred on 26th April, 1986, in the Soviet Union. It caused the release of Iodine-I131, Cesium-Cs134, Cs137, and Strontium-Sr90, and other isotopes into the atmosphere.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the nodal ministry for disaster management in India?

options.b: Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate change

mcqs.explanation: The Ministry of Home Affairs is the nodal ministry for disaster management at the Centre except for dealing with droughts which are under the purview of the Ministry of Agriculture.688 Other parts of the Indian government involved in disaster management are the Emergency Medical Relief Wing under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. The Indian Meteorological Department plays a role in mitigation of disaster and its preparedness.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a nodal centre in case of disaster management?
mcqs.explanation: The district disaster management authority is the nodal center for disaster management. It is chaired by either, the District Collector, District Magistrate or the Deputy Commissioner. The Chief Medical Officer of t he district is a part of this authority.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The NIDM is involved in the mitigation a nd management of disasters in India. Who is the president of this institution?
mcqs.explanation: The National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) is under the Ministry of Home Affairs of India. Its president is the Union Home Minister. National Institute of Disaster Management is a premier institute for training and capacity development programs for managing natural disasters in India, on a national as well as regional basis.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Who is the chairman of the National Disaster Management Authority of India?

options.a: Minister of Health and Family Welfare

mcqs.explanation: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) is an apex body of the Government of India, with a m andate to lay down policies for disaster management. It is chaired by the Prime Minister of India. The image given below shows the logo of the NDMA.689

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are working as a medical officer in a ceramic factory. What particle size of the dust inhaled would you be most concerned about?
mcqs.explanation: Inhalation of dust particles in the size range of 0.5 to 3 microns is considered to be the most dangerous. It can lead to various occupational lung diseases called pneumoconioses.695

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Match the following causative agents with the disease caused by them:
mcqs.explanation: The correct match is: • Coal dust - Anthracosis • Hay dust - Farmer's lung • Cotton fibre - Byssinosis • Cane fibre - Baggasosis

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: While working as an MO, you noticed an increased number of bagassosis patients in the area. Which of the following fungal control measure s w ould you advise the sugarcane farmers to implement ?
mcqs.explanation: Fungal control on bagasse can be done by using 2% propionic acid and keeping the moisture content above 20%. Bagassosis is a hypersensitivity pneumonitis caused by inhaling bagasse dust contaminated by the fungus Thermoactinomyces sacchari. It is a reaction to the various antigens present in sugarcane molasses.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A shipyard worker is diagnosed with asbestosis. Which of the following is false about his condition?

options.a: The symptoms usually occur after 5-10 years of exposure
options.c: Peribronchial fibrosis is a characteristic finding
options.d: The most dangerous form of asbestos is chrysolite type

mcqs.explanation: Amphibole is the most dangerous form of asbestos. Chrysolite is a safer form of asbestos compared to amphibole. Asbestosis is a pneumoconiosis that occurs after 5-10 years of exposure to asbestos. It progresses even after the removal of contact with asbestos. Asbestosis affects the basal part of the lung causing diffuse peribronchial fibrosis. Sputum shows asbestos bodies, which are asbestos fibers coated with fibrin. The image given below shows asbestos bodies:696 The complications that can occur are: • Pulmonary fibrosis • Carcinoma of the lung • Mesothelioma of the pleura • Malignancy of the gastrointestinal tract

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A patient presents with abdominal colic and constipation. On examination, pallor and blue stippled lines on gums are observed. What is the most common mode of exposure to this particular toxicity?
mcqs.explanation: A patient presenting with constipation, pallor, and Burton's lines (blue stippled lines on gums), most likely has lead poisoning. The most common mode of exposure to lead toxicity is the inhalation of lead fumes. Lead poisoning occurs by lead exposure via the following modes: • Inhalation- lead fumes in gasoline and petroleum p roducts • Ingestion - lead paint • Absorption through the skin– seen only with organic leads The most toxic forms of lead are lead oxide, lead carbonate, and lead arsenate. The least toxic form is lead sulfide.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true about lead poisoning?

options.a: Signs and symptoms occur when blood lead levels >70mcg/dL
options.c: Wrist drop is the earliest sign

mcqs.explanation: The signs and symptoms of lead poisoning occur only when the blood lead levels exceed 70mcg/dL, which is known as the threshold phenomenon. Lead poisoning is also known as plumbism/ Saturnism/ painter's colic.697

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are screening the workers in a battery manufacturing factory for exposure to lead. Which of the following screening test will you use?
mcqs.explanation: The screening test used for estimating lead exposure is the measurement of coproporphyrin in urine. Diagnosis of lead poisoning Note: Cotinine is the primary metabolite of nicotine and is currently considered the best biomarker for tobacco smoke exposure (both active and passive).Laboratory parameter Value Remarks Coproporphyrin in urine >150 mc g/L Screening test - indicates exp osure Aminolevulinic acid (ALA ) in urine >5 mg/L Indicates lead absorption Lead in blood >70 mc g/dL Clinical symptoms appear Lead in urine 0.8 mg/ L Indicates lead absorption Basophilic stippling of RBCs Sensitive indicator

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Barosinusitis is likely to be seen in which of the following patients?

options.a: A person who is suffering from mountain sickness
options.b: A patient Infected by gas-forming bacteria
options.c: A patient diagnosed with Aspergillus sinusitis
options.d: A diver who developed decompression sickness

mcqs.explanation: Barosinusitis occurs in decompression sickness or Caisson's disease. It is due to the sudden expansion of air in the sinuses. It can be seen in: • Divers who ascend rapidly from deep-sea (high pressure) to the surface of the earth (low pressure) • Pilots of unpressurized aircraft or mountaineers who rapidly ascended from the surface of the earth (high-pressure zone) to a high altitude (low-pressure zone) Under high pressure, gases get compressed, and their solubility increases. W hen a person is in deep -sea (high-pressure zone) for a long time, an increased amount of nitrogen gets dissolved in his body. When he suddenly comes back to the surface (atmospheric pressure or a low-pressure zone), the solubility of gases decreases and they escape from the dissolved state forming nitrogen bubbles. These bubbles can cause sudden expansion of air in various parts of the body such as the middle ear (barotitis), sinuses (barosinusitis), beneath te eth (barodontalgia), i ntestinal loops (abdominal distension), and emphysema. Nitrogen bubbles can also cause chokes (dyspnoea), bends (joint pain), and prickles (nerve irritation).698 The definitive treatment for Caisson's disease is recompression.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Workers working at which of the following industries require periodical examination on a daily basis?
mcqs.explanation: Workers handling irritant chemicals like dichromates require periodical examination on a daily basis. Most occupational exposures require an annual periodical examination. Certain exposures like lead, radon, and dyes require monthly periodical examination.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Serial chest X-rays of an elderly man reveal progressive massive fibrosis. W hich of the following pneumoconiosis is associated with this?
mcqs.explanation: Progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) is associated with anthracosis. PMF classically develops in anthracosis and silicosis. Exposure to c oal dust causes progressive lung injury called anthracosis. Initially , it manifests as simple coal worker pneumoconiosis, which occurs after exposure for 10–12 years and is reversible. Later, it can progress to progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) which is irreversible.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Bronchoalveolar lavage from a patient with pneumoconiosis showed Micropolyspora faeni. What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Farmer's lung is a hypersensitivity pneumonitis caused by thermophilic actinomycetes like Saccharopolyspora rectivirgula (formerly known as Micropolyspora faeni). It occurs due to inhalat ion o f moldy hay and grains causing an immunological reaction. Woodworker 's lung is a hypersensitivity pneumonitis caused by Alternaria species, and Bacillus subtilis in persons exposed to oak, cedar, pine, and mahogany dust. Bird fancier's lung is caused by proteins derived from birds like pigeons and parakeets in persons exposed to their feathers and droppings. Malt worker's lung is caused by Aspergillus species in persons exposed to barley.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not belong to the 4 P's of occupational dermatitis?
mcqs.explanation: Post-selection check -up does not belong to the 4 P's of occupational dermatitis. The 4 P's help in the prevention of occupational dermatitis, which include: • Pre-selection check-up • Protection • Personal hygiene • Periodic inspection699

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true about occupational cancer?

options.a: Age of incidence is same as compared to general population for the same cancer
options.b: The localization of the tumor is variable within a particular industry
options.c: The most common occupational cancer is squamous cell carcinoma
options.d: Onset of cancer does not o ccur after the person has left the industry

mcqs.explanation: The most common occupational cancer is squamous cell carcinoma of the skin. It is associated with exposure to radiation, dyes, and coal tar. In occupational cancers, the age of incidence of cancer is earlier than that in the general population, affected by the same cancer type. The onset of cancer can occur even after leaving the industry. The localization of the cancer is remarkably constant for a particular industry.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Cystoscopy performed on a patient with painless hematuria showed a fungating mass in the bladder. Exposure to all of the following agents can cause this disease except:
