mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of bladder carcinoma. Benzol does not cause bladder cancer, it causes leukemia. Bladder carcinoma is associated with exposure to aniline dyes like benzidine, beta-naphthylamines, auramine, magenta, and drugs like cyclophosphamide.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A young woman is being evaluated for infertility. She gives a history of being employed in the printing industry. Exposure to which of the following is likely to cause this situation?
mcqs.explanation: A woman working in the printing industry is likely to suffer from infertility due to lead toxicity. More industrial workers are exposed to lead than to any other toxic metal. Occupational exposure to lead is seen in several industries including the m anufacturing of storage batteries, glass , shipbuilding, printing, potteries, and rubber industries. The effects of lead poisoning include abdominal colic, blue-line on the gums (Burton's line), stippling of red cells, anemia, wrist & foot drop, headache, and convulsions. In young or pregnant women, prolonged lead exposure can cause miscarriage, stillbirth, premature birth, and low birth weight.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a personal protective equipment?
mcqs.explanation: A lab coat is not a personal protective equipment. Personal P rotective Equipment (PPE) are : • Gloves – protect hands. • Gowns/ aprons – protect skin and clothing. • Masks protect the mouth/nose and respirators protect the respiratory tract from airborne infectious agents. • Goggles – protect eyes. • Face shields – protect face, mouth, nose, and eyes.700

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the definition of ergonomics?

options.a: Fitting the job to the worker
options.c: Process of improving industrial safety standards
options.d: Prevention of health problems of factory workers

mcqs.explanation: Ergonomics is defined as fitting the job to the worker. The aim of ergonomics is to achieve the best mutual adjustment of man and his work, for the improvement of human efficacy and well-being. Emporiatrics, also called travel medicine, deals with the prevention and management of health problems of international travelers.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Who is the Chairman of ESI corporation in India?

options.b: Union Minister of Health & Family Welfare
options.d: Union Minister of Human Resources Development

mcqs.explanation: The Union Minister of Labour is the Chairman of the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) in India. The Secretary to the Ministry of Labour i s the Vice-Chairman of ESIC.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are working as a medical officer in a factory. You are expected to notify all of the f ollowing occupational diseases, under the Factories Act, except:
mcqs.explanation: Bagassosis is not a notifiable disease, under the Factories Act.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: According to the Factories Act 1948, what is the maximum work hours per week including overtime work hours?
mcqs.explanation: 706 Maximum work hours per week including overtime work hours is 60 hours.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about Factories Act?

options.a: Children under 14 years of age must not be employed in factories
options.b: A child of 16 years can be employed only between 6 AM and 8 PM
options.c: The maximum working hours for an adult is 72 hours per week
options.d: A child of 16 years can work till 5 hours per day

mcqs.explanation: Factories act prohibits children of <14 years from being employed. Children between 15–18 years can be employed only in certain industries and work only between 6 AM–7 PM. They should not be made to work for more than four and a half hours. The maximum working hours for an adult industrial worker should be not more than 48 hours per week, not exceeding 9 hours a day; if overtime is paid, then it should be not m ore than 60 hrs per week.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the maximum daily working hours for an adolescent employee, according to the Factories Act of 1948?
mcqs.explanation: According to the Factories Act of 1948, adolescents should not be made to work for more than four and a half hours a day.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: According to Factories A ct of 1948, a welfare officer has to be employed if the number of employees is:
mcqs.explanation: A welfare officer has to be employed if the number of employees is > 500 according to the Factories Act of 1948. According to the Factories Act, safety and welfare measures include the provision of the following: • > 1000 employees – Safety Officer • > 500 employees – Welfare Officer • > 250 employees – Canteen • > 50 employe es - Cr\350che

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following establishments is covered by the Employees' State Insurance Act?
mcqs.explanation: Currently, private medical and educational institutes employing >20 people are covered under the ESI Act. The ESI Act is applicable to all industries except: • Defence • Railway • Mines707

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What percentage of the total wage bill is contributed by the employer under the ESI Act?
mcqs.explanation: The employer contributes 3.25% of the total wage bill under the ESI Act. The government has revised the rates of ESI contribution by employers (from 4.75% to 3.25%) and employees (from 1.75% to 0.75%) in 2019. The distribution of the financial contribution is given below: • Employee: 0.75% of the total wage bill • Employer: 3.25% of the total wage bill • Medical benefit: 1/8th by the state government and 7/8th by the central government

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Under the ESI Act, which of the following is not given as a cash benefit?
mcqs.explanation: Under the ESI Act, medical benefit is not given as a cash benefit. It is provided in the form of consultations, investigations and treatment by means of the ESI hospitals or ESI dispensaries.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is enhanced sickness benefit?

options.a: Benefit given at 70% of the wage for 91 days
options.b: Benefit given at 80% of the wage for 120 days
options.c: Benefit given for a d uration of 2 years for 34 specified diseases
options.d: Benefit given at full wages for undergoing sterilization procedure

mcqs.explanation: Enhanced sickness benefit under the ESI Act is the benefit given at full wages for undergoing sterilization procedures. Under the ESI Act, sickness benefit is given at 70% of the daily wage for a duration of 91 days in one year. There are two special types of sickness benefits given: • Enhanced sickness benefit: Benefit given at f ull wages for sterilization procedures; for a duration of 7 days post-vasectomy and 14 days post-tubectomy. • Extended sickness benefit: Benefit given for a duration of 2 years for 34 specified diseases.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a benefit given under the ESI Act?
mcqs.explanation: Welfare benefit is not given under the ESI act. The following benefits are given under the ESI act: • Medical benefit • Sickness benefit • Maternity benefit • Dependance benefit • Disablement benefit • Funeral benefit • Rehabilitation benefit708

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An employee diagnosed with TB gets extended sickness benefit for:
mcqs.explanation: Extended sickness benefit is given for a period of 2 years.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true about ESI Act?

options.b: State government covers 1/8th and ESI corporation covers 7/8th of the cost of medical care
options.c: Maternity benefit is payable at full wages for upto 24 weeks
options.d: It covers all employees getting income up to Rs.18,000/- per month

mcqs.explanation: The state government's share of expenditure on medical care is 1/8th, and the ESI corporation's share of expenditure on medical care is 7/8th of the total cost. Few important points about the ESI Act: • It covers all employees getting income up to Rs.21,000/- per month. • The employer contributes 3.25% of the total wage bill. • An employee contributes 0.75% of wages. • State and Central government share medical exp enditure i n the ratio 1:7. • Medical benefit: Full medical care • Sickness benefit: 70% of the average daily wages and is payable for 91 days. • Extended sickness benefit: Payable for 2 years for a set of 34 diseases. • Enhanced sickness benefit: Full average daily wage for a duration up to 7 days in case of vasectomy and up to 14 days in case of tubectomy. • Maternity benefit: Full average daily wage for a duration up to 26 weeks (confinement) or 6 weeks (miscarriage/MTP) or 4 weeks ( sickness a rising out of pregnancy). • Funeral expenses: Cash not exceeding Rs.15,000.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Who is the beneficiary u nder the Rajiv Gandhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana scheme of ESI?

options.b: An insured person rendered unemployed, involuntarily
options.c: An insured employee who is pregnant

mcqs.explanation: Rajiv Gandhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana (RGSKY) is a scheme of ESI that benefits an insured person rendered unemployed, involuntarily. Unemployment allowance under RGSKY is given when an insured person is going out of employment involuntarily, on account of: • Closure of a factory or establishment • Retrenchment (laying off employees due to economic difficulty) • Permanent disability due t o nonemployment injury Allowance and eligibility criteria of Rajiv Gandhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana (updated in 2019): • The allowance is given at the rate of 50% of the daily wage for a maximum of 2 years. • To qualify for the scheme the worker must have worked in that setup for more than 3 years.709 Note: Disability due to employment injury is covered under disablement benefits of ESI Act, 1948. • Temporary disability: 90% of wages until disablement lasts. • Permanent disability: 90% of wages as a life pension on the basis of loss of earning capacity. • Dependants benefit: 90% of wage as monthly payment to the dependants of the deceased person, in cases where death occurs due to employment injury or occupational hazards.710

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the correct order for the process of communication?
mcqs.explanation: The correct order for the process of communication is: Sender\037Message\037Channel\037Receiver\037Feedback The sender (communicator) is the originator of the message. A message is the information which the communicator transmits to his audience. Channel is the media of communication between the sender and the receiver (e.g., interpersonal communication, mass media, traditional or folk media). The audience who receives, understands, and acts upon the message is called the r eceiver . Feedback is the reaction to the message which flows from the receiver to the sender.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a didactic type of communication?
mcqs.explanation: Workshop is an example of Socratic type of communication. mcqs.explanation: 717 A panel discussion is an example of Socratic type of communication. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is not true about mass media?

options.a: It has increased influence only in below-average educated population
options.b: It gives greater support for concentrated programmes
options.c: Mass media alone is inadequate in changing human behavior
options.d: Mass media reaches the widest population

mcqs.explanation: The advantage of mass media includes that it has increased influence across all educational levels, especially in above-average educational level. Mass media includes TV , newspaper, radio, etc. • Advantages: • It reaches people even in the most remote areas. • It gets public attention. • It has increased influence across all educational levels, especially in above-average educational level. • It gives greater support for concentrated programmes. • Disadvantages: • O ne-way communication • Impersonal method and no face-to-face contact • Mass media alone is inadequate in changing human behavior.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a function of health communication?
mcqs.explanation: Community participation is not a function of health communication. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an approach to health education?
mcqs.explanation: Socio-environmental approach is not an approach to health education. There are four approaches to health education: Regulatory approach- external control or laws placed on people by the government. Ex: Child Marriage Act, No smoking in public places, Helmet law Service approach- government aims at providing health services to the people at their doorsteps. Its drawback is that people will not accept a service, even if it is offered free of cost unless it is based on their f elt needs. Ex : Government provided latrines free of cost yet people did not use them because its need was not felt Health education approach- creates awareness of health needs and problems. Awareness leads to motivation which includes the stages of interest, evaluation, and decision-making. It is followed by acceptance of the new idea which becomes part of his existing values, known as internalization. Ex: Adoption of ORS for diarrhea Primary health care approach- de livery o f health services with the active involvement of people. Principles of community participation and intersectoral coordination are stressed here. Its objective is to help individuals become self-reliant in health matters. Ex: People receive guidance from healthcare providers (Rogi Kalyana Samiti, Mahila Arogya Samiti).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In which model of health education does internalization occur?
mcqs.explanation: 719 Internalization belongs to the motivation model. There are three models of health education: • Medical model: transfer of proven medical information into education. It does not bridge the gap between knowledge and behavior. • Motivation model: creates awareness of health needs and problems. Awareness leads to motivation which includes stages of interest, evaluation, and decision-making. It is followed by acceptance of the new idea which becomes part of his existing v alues, known as internalization. • Social intervention model: focuses on changing the social environment which subsequently shapes the behavior of individual and the community.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a principle of health education?
mcqs.explanation: Drawing conclusions is not a principle of health education. Principles of Health Education: • Participation • Learning by doing • Setting an example • Good human relations • Feedback • Credibility • Leaders • Interest • Comprehension • Known to unknown • Motivation • Reinforcement Known to unknown m eans to start where the people are and with what they understand and then proceed to new knowledge.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about health education is false?

options.a: It aids in developing a reflective behavior

mcqs.explanation: Health education appeals to people's reason. Health propaganda appeals to people's emotions. mcqs.question: Which is the best method for counseling a patient who has tested positive for HIV ?
mcqs.explanation: Individual approach is the preferred counseling method for HIV pre- and post-testing. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A group discussion was conducted among villagers to assess their knowledge on personal hygiene. Which of the following statements is false regarding this format of health education?

options.a: Many different topics can be spoken about in one discussion
options.b: A group leader guides the conversation
options.c: It can bring about change in the attitude of participants
options.d: It usually consists of 6 to 12 people

mcqs.explanation: A group discussion discusses one topic on its agenda. Group discussion is an aggregation of people interacting in a face-to-face manner. Exchange of ideas, knowledge, and opinions is done by participants which influence a change in their attitudes. It usually involves 6–12 people with a group leader who guides the conversation, giving equal opportunity to everyone to voice themselves. In a group discussion, everyone must speak and be open to criticism without interrupting o thers. A limitation to this form of health education is that not everyone is open to speaking in public. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about panel discussion?

options.a: It usually consists of four to eight experts
options.d: Members of the audience are invited to take part at the end

mcqs.explanation: A moderator is required to regulate the panel discussion. In a panel discussion, 4 to 8 experts have a discussion on a topic in front of an audience. No speeches or order is set beforehand. The audience is invited to take part after the panelists speak and ask questions.

options.c: Series of four or more interactive meetings
options.d: Series of speeches on a given subject

mcqs.explanation: A workshop is a series of meetings with an emphasis on individual work within the group, using external consultants or experts. It helps increase individual efficiency as a professional worker.

mcqs.question: All of the following are types of combined audio-visual aids except:
mcqs.explanation: Flannelgraphs, podcasts, and tape recorders are not combined audio-visual (A-V) aids. Flannelgraph is a rough flannel fixed over a wooden board used for displaying pictures, cut-outs, etc. It is only a visual aid. Podcasts and tape recorders are auditory aids. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A Norovirus outbreak occurs in an urban slum where you are posted as the PHC medical officer. Which is the best method to teach the people about ORS?
mcqs.explanation: The best method to teach an urban slum about ORS is by demonstrations. Demonstration is a carefully prepared presentation on how to perform a certain task or skill or procedure. It shows the step-by-step process of a task. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is used to obtain consensus forecasts among a large number of people?
mcqs.explanation: Delphi method is a systematic interactive forecasting method, which is used to obtain a consensus forecast among a large number of people. It determines the degree of agreement on a topic. This can help in setting priorities or selecting alternatives in planning. This method uses questionnaires, which are answered by experts in two or more rounds.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is total communication used for?
mcqs.explanation: The philosophy of total communication is used in the education of hearing-impaired children. It requires the incorporation o f aural, oral , and manual modes of communication for effective communication with and among hearing-impaired people.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In which of the given scenarios would you use the GATHER approach?
mcqs.explanation: The GATHER approach is mainly used for counseling, like in contraceptive counseling, wherein a person is helped to make a decision about health. GATHER stands for: • G – Greet • A – Ask • T – Tell options or give answers • H – Help in making choices • E – Explain everything about the decision • R – Return for follow-up

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: SPIKES protocol is for:
mcqs.explanation: 724 SPIKES protocol is for breaking bad news. Each letter represents a phase in the six-step sequence. • S - setting • P - perception • I - invitation or information • K - knowledge • E - empathy • S - summarizing or strategizing Key components of the SPIKES strategy include: • Demonstrating empathy • Acknowledging and validating the patient's feelings • Exploring the patient's understanding and acceptance of the bad news • Providing information about possible interventions725

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the ultimate long-term desired state towards which all the resources are directed?
mcqs.explanation: The goal is the ultimate desired state towards which objectives and resources are directed. It is long-term and not constrained by time or resources. The plan is the blueprint for taking action in order to achieve the goal. Option A: Target refers to the quantifiable and achievable mid-term endpoints in the plan. Option B: Mission describes the cause of the existence of the programme. Option D: The objectives are short-term endpoints. They are precise points in the plan. They a re either achieved or unachieved.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a set of rules that helps ensure maximum use of the resources and efforts?
mcqs.explanation: Procedure is a set of rules for carrying out work. It helps to ensure the maximum use of resources and efforts. Option B: Programme is a sequence of activities designed to implement policies and accomplish objectives. Option C: Schedule is a time sequence for the work to be done. Option D: Target refers to the quantifiable and achievable mid-term endpoints in the plan.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A team of doctors is planning to conduct a survey on the prevalence of infective diarrhea in a village. What is the correct sequence of steps involved in the planning of this activity?
mcqs.explanation: The planning cycle includes the following steps: • Analysis of the h ealth situation • Establishment of objectives and goals • Assessment of resources • Fixing priorities732 • Writing-up of a formulated plan • Programming and implementation • Monitoring • Evaluation The planning cycle has been summarized in the following image:

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a component of the evaluation of health programs?
mcqs.explanation: Repeatability is not a component of the evaluation of health programs. Components of evaluation are: (Mnemonic: Ryan Always Ate An Egg Every Evening) • Relevance • Adequacy • Accessibility • Acceptability • Effectiveness • Efficiency • Effect or impact The steps of evaluation of a health programme are: • Determine what is to be evaluated: structure, process, or outcome • Establish standards and criteria • Plan the methodology to be applied733 • Gather information • Analyze the results • Take action • Re-evaluate

mcqs.question: Which of the following techniques is based on behavioral sciences?
mcqs.explanation: Management by objective is based on behavioral sciences. Management methods used in health programmes are either quantitative or based on behavioral sciences. Methods based on behavioral sciences include: • Organizational design • Personnel management • Communication • Information systems • Management by objectives (MBO) Quantitative methods include: • Cost-benefit analysis • Cost-effect ive a nalysis • Cost –accounting • Input-output analysis • Model • Systems analysis • Network analysis - includes programme evaluation and review technique (PERT) and critical path method (CPM) • Planning–programming–budgeting system (PPBS) • Work sampling • Decision making

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a quantitative method of management?
mcqs.explanation: Cost-benefit analysis is a quantitative method of management. In this method, the economic benefits of any programme are compared with the costs incurred. The benefit of the programme is expressed i n monetary units. The main drawback here is that the benefits of a health programme cannot always be expressed in monetary terms.734 Management methods used in health programmes are either quantitative or based on behavioral sciences. mcqs.question: What is the programme evaluation and review technique used for?
mcqs.explanation: The programme evaluation and review technique (PERT) is used for network analysis. It is a type of quantitative management technique which helps in detailed planning and comprehensive supervision.

options.b: It is a management method based on behavioral sciences

mcqs.question: A hospital administrator is systematically recording the activities of his team at regular intervals. What is this known as?
mcqs.explanation: Work sampling is a systematic observation and recording of activities of one or more individuals carried out at regular or random intervals. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which committee had recommended a bachelor degree in medical education for rural health services?

options.b: High-level expert group on universal health coverage
options.d: Committee on Integration of Health Services

mcqs.explanation: The high-level expert group (HLEG) on universal health coverage under the aegis of the Planning Commission of India suggested a 3.5 year bachelor degree course in medical education for rural health services. This was planned for the 12th five-year plan (2012-2017). The degree given was B.Sc Community Health, and these rur al h ealth care practitioners were to be called community health officers.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Who was appointed as the c hairman of the Health Survey and Development Committee in 1943 ?
mcqs.explanation: Sir Joseph William Bhore was appointed as the chairman of the Health Survey and Development Committee in 1943. This committee was hence named the Bhore committee.737

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which health planning committee proposed the 3 million plan?
mcqs.explanation: The 3 million plan was proposed by the Bhore Committee. It proposed to set up the following in the long-term: • Primary health units with 75-bedded hospitals for each 10,000 to 20,000 population • Secondary units with 650 beds • District hospitals with 2,500 beds As a short-term measure, it was proposed that each PHC must cater to 40,000 people and have: • 2 medical officers, 4 public health nurses, 1 nurse • 4 midwives, 4 dais, 2 sanitary inspectors, 2 health assistants • 1 phar macist • 5 other class IV employees

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the provision of preventive, curative, and promotional health services to every individual called?
mcqs.explanation: Comprehensive health care as stated by the Bhore committee means giving integrated preventive, curative, and promotional health care to every individual, irrespective of their ability to pay.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In the inventory management of drug stores, which of the following is a component of the VED method?
mcqs.explanation: The 'D' in the VED method stands for desirable. VED is a method of inventory management used mainly in drug stores and pharmacies.738 The drugs are classified in three categories as follows: • V - Vital drugs. Items whose absence cannot be tolerated (10% of total items). • E - Essential drugs. Items whose absence can be tolerated for some time (40% of total items). • D - Desirable drugs. Items whose absence can be tolerated for a long time (50% of total items).

mcqs.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution confers Right to Life to the citizens of India?
mcqs.explanation: The Right to Life is given in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution. Option A: Article 11 defines the right of the parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law. Option C: Article 23 defines the prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labor. Option D: Article 25 defines the freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.740

mcqs.question: Which of the following is part of the concurrent list of the Indian Constitution?

options.b: Fishing and fisheries beyond territorial waters

mcqs.explanation: Adulteration of food is included under the concurrent list. The legislative section of the seventh schedule is divided into three lists: • Union list - a list of 100 items on which the parliament has exclusive power to legislate • State list - a list of 61 items on which the state government has exclusive power to legislate • Concurrent list - a list of 52 items on which both central and state governments have the power to legislate741

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not included in the secondary level of the healthcare system?
mcqs.explanation: Medical colleges are included in the tertiary level of the health care system, which is also the second referral centre.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an element of primary healthcare?
mcqs.explanation: 748 Providing physical rehabilitation is not an element of primary health care. Primary health centers (PHCs) are only responsible for the popularization and mainstreaming of PMR in the community. Primary health care refers to essential health care made universally available to individuals and acceptable to them, through their full participation and at a cost the community and country can afford.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: All of the following are pillars of primary health care except:
mcqs.explanation: Health education is an element of primary health care, not a pillar.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statement is false regarding ASHA workers?

options.a: Few of their responsibilities are integrated with Anganwadi workers
options.b: They should have formal education at least up to class
options.c: A population of 1000 should have at least 1 ASHA
options.d: They have to procure ORS, OCPs, IFA tablets from CHC

mcqs.explanation: Accredited social health activist (ASHA) workers do not need to procure supplies from CHCs. They only act as depot holders for certain essential supplies so that they are readily available to their community. These essential supplies may include ORS, contraceptives, iron-folic acid tablets, chloroquine, disposable delivery kits, oral contraceptive pills, condoms, etc.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect regarding Anganwadi workers?

options.a: One AWW serves a population of
options.b: They are appointed under the ICDS scheme
options.c: They link the community with the health services
options.d: Their responsibilities include counsel for immunization, health education, and nutrition

mcqs.explanation: The norm is one Anganwadi worker (AWW) per 400-800 population. Anganwadi workers (AWW ) are allotted u nder the integrated child development services (ICDS). AWW are selected from the community they are to serve and act as links between the community and health services. They are mostly part-time workers. Responsibilities of an AWW include: • Health checkups and growth chart maintenance • Counsel women on birth preparedness, importance of safe delivery, immunization and contraception and prevention of common infections including STD and RTIs. • Nutrition • Health education • N on -formal school education • Referral services

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: One male health assistant is posted for a population of:
mcqs.explanation: One male and female health assistant are required for a population of 30,000 in plain areas and of 20,000 in hilly or remote areas.749

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: How many people does a Mahila Arogya Samiti member c ater to?
mcqs.explanation: 1 Mahila Arogya Samiti member is appointed for a population of 250-500 (covering about 50-100 households).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following duties would be performed by a male health worker?
mcqs.explanation: The duties of a male health worker include chlorination of water bodies, distribution of conventional contraceptives, and reproductive and child health services. Maintanence of eligible couple registers (part of family planning activities) and immunization are duties of female health workers. Health workers (male and female) are 1 per 5000 in plains and 1 per 3 000 in remote or hilly areas .

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a duty of a female health worker?
mcqs.explanation: Malaria surveillance activities, in accordance with the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme, are the duty of a male health worker. Health workers (male and female) are 1 per 5000 in plains and 1 per 3000 in remote or hilly areas.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following are not involved in providing antenatal support to pregnant women?
mcqs.explanation: Trained birth attendants or dais provide medical services during delivery and in the post-partum period. They cater to a population of 1000 in villages. Antenatal support is provided by the following: • H ealth workers (male and female) - 1 per 5000 in plains and 1 per 3000 in hilly or remote areas. • Health assistants (male and female) - 1 per 30,000 in plains and 1 per 20, 000 in remote or hilly areas. • Anganwadi workers - 1 per 400-800 in plains and 1 per 300-800 in hilly or remote areas.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: How many people does one sub-center in a hilly or remote area cater to?
mcqs.explanation: A sub-center caters to a population of 5000 in general areas and 3000 in hilly or remote areas. Services provided at sub-centers:750 • Maternal and child health, family planning • Counseling for abortion and adolescent health care • Water quality monitoring and sanitation promotion • Assistance to school health services • Field visits and treating minor ailments • Training of ASHA and birth attendants • Disease surveillance and National Health Programme functions

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What should be the maximum number of female h ealth workers at a sub-center?
mcqs.explanation: Two female health workers are to be at a sub-center as proposed by the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS). There are two types of sub- centers: • T ype A - It has all facilities except for conducting deliveries. It can be upgraded to Type B. • Type B - Also called MCH sub-centers. It has delivery facilities. mcqs.question: As a PHC medical officer, you would be responsible for all of the following activities except:

options.c: Formal education of children < 6 years of age
options.d: Collection and recording of vital events

mcqs.explanation: Formal education is not a function of primary health centers in India.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following category of workers are not part of the workforce at PHCs?
mcqs.explanation: 751 A radiographer is not a part of the manpower at a PHC. They are present in CHCs. Accountants cum data entry operators, health educators, and clerks are appointed at PHCs.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the minimum number of beds a HWC-PHC is required t o have?
mcqs.explanation: The minimum number of beds a HWC-PHC is required to have is 2. Per the IPHS 2022 guidelines, the desirable number of beds in a HWC-PHC is 4. Note: The desirable beds will be over and above the essential beds.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: One community health center (CHC) covers a population of:
mcqs.explanation: Each community (CHC) covers a population of 80,000-1,20,000. Services provided by CHC: • Care of routine a nd emergency cases in medicine and surgery • Maternal , newborn, and child health • Family planning • All the functions of national health programmes • Physical medicine and rehabilitation • Oral health • School and adolescent health services • Blood storage facility • Diagnostic services • Referral services • Maternal death review (MDR)

mcqs.question: What is the minimum number of beds required in a community health center?
mcqs.explanation: The minimum number of beds in a CHC is 30. mcqs.explanation: An urban CHC caters to a population of 5 lakh in a metropolitan city and 2.5 lakh in other cities. An urban PHC caters to a population of 50,000.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect regarding the staffing at urban primary health centers?
mcqs.explanation: An urban primary health center will cover 50,000-60,000 population and will be staffed with: • Two doctors (one regular and one on a part-time basis) • 3 staff nurses • 1 pharmacist • 1 lab technician • 1 lady health visitor • 4–5 ANMs (depending upon the population covered) • Other clerical and support staff and one program manager Basic functions p rovided are: • OPD • Basic lab diagnosis • Drug/contraceptive dispensing • Health education along with referral services *Note: The above data is according to IPHS 2017 guidelines. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the principal unit of administration in India?
mcqs.explanation: The principal unit of administration in India is the district under a collector. Under districts are the sub-divisions, tahsils or talukas, municipalities or corporations, villages, panchayats, etc. As of 2021, there are 748 districts in India.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrectly matched?
mcqs.explanation: The Panchayat Samiti or Janpada Panchayat operates at the block level. Panchayati Raj is a three-tier structure of rural self-government in India. It operates at the following levels: • Panchayat at the village level (includes G ram Sabha, Gram Panchayat, and Nyaya Panchayat) • Panchayat Samiti or Janpada Panchayat at the block level • Zilla Parishad at the district level

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Community or village health guides are selected by:
mcqs.explanation: Village health guides (VHGs) are selected by the medical officer-in-charge (MO). 2-3 candidates are put forward by the community for the position of a VHG. The MO selects one of them after consultation with the block development officer and field staff.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: As a PHC medical officer, you would keep all of the following i n mind while selecting a village health guide except:

options.a: They must be above 45 years of age
options.b: They must be a resident of the community that they will serve
options.c: They must be educated up to 6th grade
options.d: They should be able to spare 2-3 hours in a day for community work

mcqs.explanation: Village health guides (VHG) are chosen by the medical officer-in-charge (including PHC MO). Age is not a criterion for selection. The VHG scheme was introduced in 1977. Guidelines for choosing a VHG include: • They can be of either sex but must be residents of the village • They must know to read and write and have education up to 6th grade • They must be able to spare around 2-3 hours a day for community work • They must be acceptable to all parts of the community VHGs are trained for 2-3 months before beginning work. The norm is to have 1 VHG per 1000 popu lation.755

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following public health centers do First Referral Units (FRUs) and non-FRUs belong to?
mcqs.explanation: First Referral Units (FRUs) and non-FRUs belong to the Community Health Centers (CHCs). The Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) guidelines are a code of standards for uniformity in health facilities in the Indian public health system, under the National Health Mission (NHM), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), India. It aims to provide guidance on the infrastructure, human resources, drugs, diagnostics, equipment, quality, and governance requireme nts f or delivering health services at all levels of facilities in the system. The 2022 edition of IPHS mainly concentrates on comprehensive primary health care, increasing the human workforce, decentralized access to healthcare, and better implementation of universal health coverage.759

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A district has a population of 20 lakhs. According to the IPHS 2022 guidelines, approximately how many beds should the district public health system have for this population?
mcqs.explanation: In a district having a population of 20 lakhs, the number of beds the district public health system should have is given as follows: 2000 essential and 4000 desirable. According to IPHS 2022 norms for the number of beds in district hospitals, 1 bed per 1000 population is essential and 2 beds per thousand population would be desirable. Therefore, in a population of 20,00,000 the district public health system should have 2000 essential and 4000 desirable beds. The essential number o f beds should be achieved through the public health system of tertiary care ( medical colleges), secondary care (DH, SDH, CHCs), and primary care in the district (PHCs and CHCs).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are involved in the planning for a hospital in your district. If you decide that the minimum number of essential beds is 50, what should the population of your district be, according to the IPHS 2022 guidelines?
mcqs.explanation: According to the IPHS 2022 guidelines, a minimum number of 50 essential beds would be required for a district with a population of less than 2 lakhs. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about district and sub-district hospitals?

options.a: All districts need at least two district hospitals.
options.b: The minimum essential number of beds in a sub-district hospital is 100.
options.c: All districts do not need a sub-district hospital.
options.d: DNB training can be done in district hospitals.

mcqs.explanation: Every district should have at least one comprehensively functioning district hospital (DH). District hospitals and subdistrict hospitals provide secondary care health services. Every district should have at least one comprehensively functioning DH. Districts with a population of less than 5 lakhs and with a functional DH do not need a subdistrict hospital (SDH). Districts with a population of 5–10 lakhs can have one SDH. For a population of more than 10 lakhs, 1 SDH is needed f or every 10 lakh population. The three pillars of district hospital services are providing clinical care, providing a knowledge hub for capacity development, and public health programs. Important functions of DHs: • Providing curative services • Palliative and rehabilitative services • Implementation of health programs • Drugs and diagnostic services • Administrative and other support services • Health promotion and prevention, education • Providing edu cational s ervices, like Diplomate of National Board (DNB) training; training courses for healthcare professionals (HCPs) in auxiliary nursing and midwifery (ANM), telemedicine, and technology; and partnerships with universities

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct statement regarding Community Health Centers (CHCs)?

options.a: Non-FRU CHCs should have 50 essential beds.
options.b: Non-FRU CHCs can be located in urban areas.
options.c: FRU-CHCs can be located in rural areas.
options.d: Elective surgeries wi ll n ot be performed at FRU-CHCs.

mcqs.explanation: First Referral Unit - Community Health centers (FRU-CHCs) can be located in rural areas. Community health centers (CHC) can be classified into the following types: • Non-FRU-CHCs - They are located in rural areas. They provide preventive, p romotive, palliative , and rehabilitative services. They also have curative services for normal delivery, stabilization of761 common emergencies, etc. • FRU-CHCs are the first centers of referral from smaller centers such as sub-centers or primary health centers. They can be located in rural as well as urban areas. Apart from providing the abovementioned essential services, they also provide specialized services and elective surgeries. All the CHCs located in urban areas are FRU-CHCs. In addition to the above centers, CHCs called Block Health Public Units (BHPU) may be located in the block hea dquarters. A part from clinical and public health services, they have a health management information system (HMIS). They also help in decentralizing health services.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the essential number of beds in a non-First Referral Unit CHC (non-FRU-CHC)?
mcqs.explanation: The number of essential beds in a non-First Referral Unit CHC (non-FRU CHC) is 30. mcqs.question: A rural hilly area has a population of 40,000. How many Primary Health Centers (PHCs) should it have?
mcqs.explanation: A rural hilly area with a population of 40,000 should have 2 Primary Health Centers (PHCs). According to the latest IPHS 2022 guidelines, in hilly areas, there should be one PHC for every 20,000 population. Since this village has a population of 40,000, it should have 2 PHCs.

mcqs.question: All of the following surgical procedures can be conducted in a Primary Health Center (PHC) except _____.
mcqs.explanation: Cholecystectomy is not a surgical procedure that is conducted in a PHC. The surgical procedures done in PHC include suturing of wounds, incision and drainage of abscesses, vasectomy, tubectomy, and hydrocelectomy. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are a medical officer in an Urban Health and Wellness Center (UHWC). The population of the place is 10,000. How many ASHA workers are needed for your UHWC?
mcqs.explanation: In a place with a population of 10,000, 5 ASHA workers are needed. There are two forms of Health and Wellness Centers in Sub-Health Centers. • Health and Wellness Centre - Sub-Health Center (HWC-SHC) in rural areas: It requires 1 ASHA per 1000 population or 1 ASHA per habitation in hilly/tribal areas. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are posted as a medical officer in a rural H ealth and Wellness Center - Primary Health Center (HWC-PHC). According to the IPHS 2022 guidelines, which of the following is incorrect regarding the essential manpower required for this PHC?
mcqs.explanation: Specialists like ophthalmologists are not included as essential manpower for a PHC. Specialists for medicine, obstetrics & gynecology, pediatrics, ophthalmology, etc. are essential manpower included under polyclinics. According to the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) 2022 guidelines, a total of 12 staff is considered essential manpower for a PHC. They include 1 Medical Officer (MBBS), 2 staff nurses, 1 pharmacist, 1 health worker female/ANM, 1 health worker/health a ssistant (male), 1 health assistant (female)/lady health visitor, 1 laboratory technician, 1 data entry operator, dresser, 1 accountant, and 1 sanitation staff.765

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following was the world's first international health agency?

options.c: Health Organization of the League of Nations
options.d: United States Agency for International Development

mcqs.explanation: The first international health agency to be established was the Pan American Sanitary Bureau (PASB) in 1902. This was followed by the establishment of the Health Organization of the League of Nations in 1923. The World Health Organisation (WHO) was established on 7th April 1948.

mcqs.explanation: World No Tobacco Day is observed on 31st May. The theme of World No Tobacco Day 2021 is 'commit to quit'. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Where is the headquarters of the WHO located?
mcqs.explanation: The headquarters of the WHO is in Geneva, Switzerland. The WHO is a specialized, non-political health agency of t he United Nations. It came into force on 7th April 1948. Its objective is the attainment of the highest level of health by all people. The structure of the WHO includes: • The World Health Assembly • The Executive Board • The Secretariat Important headquarters of international organisations include: • The headquarters of UNICEF and UNDP is in New York, USA. • Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) headquarters is in Rome, Italy. • Headquarters of the International Labor Organization (ILO) a nd the International Red Cross are also in Geneva. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not one of the duties of the WHO?
mcqs.explanation: State health is not one of the duties of the WHO. It is the responsibility of the government. Work and duties of the WHO: • Prevention and control of specific diseases • Development of comprehensive health services • Family health • Environmental health • Health statistics • Biomedical research • Health literature and information • Cooperation with other organizations

mcqs.question: Where is the South East Asian Regional Office of the WHO located?
mcqs.explanation: The South-East Asian Regional Office (SEARO) of the WHO is located in New Delhi. Duties of the SEARO include p lanning for malaria eradication, tuberculosis control, and rural health services. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the surveillance reporting system used by the WHO?
mcqs.explanation: The surveillance reporting system used by the WHO is the Weekly Epidemiological Record (WER). The WHO collects and disseminates epidemiological information on diseases subject to International Health Regulations. It is done through an Automatic Telex Reply Service (ATRS) and the Weekly Epidemiological Record (WER).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: As a part of the 'Clean care is safer care' campaign, you have been asked to give a presentation to the nurses in the obstetrics and gynecology department. Which of the following areas is targeted in this campaign?
mcqs.explanation: 'Clean care is safer care' campaign was started by the WHO to improve hand hygiene practices. In 2005, WHO developed this campaign aimed at the reduction o f healthcare-associated infections ( HCAI) through the worldwide promotion of appropriate hand hygiene practices.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which agency of the United N ations has the given logo?
mcqs.explanation: 778 The given logo is that of the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF). It works closely with the WHO on health matters. UNICEF's content of services include: • Child health • Child nutrition • Family and child welfare • Formal and informal education UNICEF participates in urban basic services (UBS) with the aim to promote access to basic services like nutrition, water supply, and sanitation. UNICEF started the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative (BFHI) to promote breast feeding a nd improve maternal and child care. In 2016, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare launched the Mothers Absolute Affection (MAA) programme to revitalize efforts towards protection, promotion and support of breastfeeding practices.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following are components of UNICEF's GOBI FFF strategy?
mcqs.explanation: The components of the GOBI FFF strategy by the UNICEF are: • Growth monitoring with growth charts • Oral rehydration therapy for diarrhoea and dehydration • Breastfeeding • Immunization of children • Family planning and birt h s pacing • Food supplementation • Female literacy promotion The GOBI FFF strategy is aimed at revolutionising child health and survival. Initially, it was called GOBI strategy and later the FFF aspect was added to it.

mcqs.question: Which agency of the UN gives funds for technical assistance and has the following as part of its logo?
mcqs.explanation: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is an agency of the UN that gives funds for technical assistance. It has the following logo.779 Its main objective is to help poorer nations develop their human and natural resources to their potential. Some other agencies of the UN include: • UNESCO - United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization • UNEP - United Nations Environment Programme • UNHCR - United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees Their logos are given below.780

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which organisation gives the highest funding for reproductive health?
mcqs.explanation: United Nations Fund for Population Activities (UNFPA) gives the highest funding for reproductive health. It works in the area of health and family welfare. It mainly works by: • Developing the national capability in manufacturing contraceptives, • Promoting population education programmes • Introducing innovative approaches to family planning and MCH care. options.a: To better the condition of rural people
options.b: Improve nutrition of people of all countries

Aims of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO): • To help nations raise living standards • To improve the nutrition of people of all countries • To increase the efficiency of farming, forestry, and fisheries • To better the condition of rural people The FAO organized a Freedom from Hunger Campaign (FFHC) in 1960.
