mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which agency of the United Nations has the following logo?

options.c: United States Agency for International Development

mcqs.explanation: The given logo is of the World Bank. It helps less developed countries raise their living standards with economic support. The allocation of funds is decided by its Board of Governors.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What does the branch of medicine known as nosology deal with?
mcqs.explanation: Nosology is the branch of medicine that deals with the classification of diseases.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Study of which of the following is known as emporiatrics?
mcqs.explanation: Emporiatrics is the study of the health of travelers. It is also called travel medicine. It deals with the prevention and management of health problems of international travelers.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Quarantine measures were implemented for the first time to prevent the spread of:
mcqs.explanation: Quarantine was introduced for the first time to prevent the spread of the plague, also known as the black death. Quarantine is the restriction on the movement of people, animals, and goods that may have been exposed to a communicable disease. It is intended to prevent the spread of communicable diseases. Quarantine is distinct from medical isolation, in which those confirmed to be infected with a communicable disease are isolated from the healthy population.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the f ollowing is not included in the Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Disease (TDR) strategy of the WHO?
mcqs.explanation: Tick-borne encephalitis is not included in the Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Disease (TDR) strategy of the WHO. The diseases included under this programme are: • Chagas disease • Dengue • Ebola • Helminthiasis783 • Leishmaniasis • Leprosy • Lymphatic filariasis • Malaria • Onchocerciasis • Schistosomiasis • Trypanosomiasis • Tuberculosis The programme is sponsored by the WHO, UNICEF, UNDP, and World Bank.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: According to the International Health Regulations, on diagnosing a patient with which of the following diseases is notification not mandatory in all countries?
mcqs.explanation: According to the International Health Regulations(IHR), notification is not mandatory if a patient is diagnosed with tuberculosis in all countries. It needs to be notified only by the countries where the public health impact is serious and there is a risk of international spread. T he government of India made the reporting of new cases of TB mandatory for all medical practitioners from 2012. An online web-based application named Nikshay is available for this purpose. Treatment providers are given a nominal cash incentive of Rs.1000/- per TB patient reported.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following disease is not under international surveillance by the WHO?
mcqs.explanation: Chagas disease is not under international surveillance by the WHO. Surveillance is usually done for infectious diseases and diseases that have the potential to become epidemics or pandemics.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Patients with which of the following diseases do not require isolation or quarantine?
mcqs.explanation: Patients with West Nile fever do not require isolation or quarantine. Isolation and quarantine are used for highly infectious diseases that are at risk of becoming epidemics or pandemics.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are asked to investigate a possible act of terrorism using anthrax. Which of the following is false regarding this category of bioterrorism agent?
mcqs.explanation: 784 Anthrax falls under category A of bioterrorism agents. These organisms are usually easy to disseminate. Category A refers to high priority agents. They have high case-fatality rates and high transmissibility. Thus, a specialised public health response is required to combat such attacks.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: How many goals does the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) comprise of?
mcqs.explanation: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) are comprised of 17 goals. These were set as part of the official Sustainable Development Goals of the Agenda 2030. These goals consist of a total o f 169 targets. SDGs replaced the Millennium Development Goals on 1st January 2016. The 2030 agenda consists of five P's: • People • Planet • Prosperity • Peace • Partnership785

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: You are conducting a study to determine the mean height of children visiting the local PHC. Which type of statistical study is being done here?
mcqs.explanation: 794 A study to determine the mean height of children is an example of a descriptive statistical study. Descriptive statistics are the statistical methods that merely organize, describe or summarize the actual data available. For example, a study determining the mean blood pressure of patients visiting a PHC on a single day. Analytical statistics are the second major category of epidemiological studies, after descriptive statistics. The objective of an analytical study is t o test the hypothesis. An observational study is an empiric investigation in which the objective is to establish a relationship between cause and effect. It falls under the category of analytical statistics. It is performed when controlled experimentation cannot be feasibly used to determine a hypothesis. For example, in the case of cigarette smoking causing lung cancer, it would be unethical and not feasible to conduct a controlled experiment. So, an observational s tudy is preferred . Inferential statistics involve inductive reasoning i.e., generalizing observations to a population after having observed only a sample. An example of such a study would be a study determining the expected success rate of vasectomy Theoretical statistics is a mathematical approach to describe something, predict events, or analyze the relationship between things. Some of the concepts of theoretical statistics are mean, median, mode, standard d eviation and correlation.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about statistical terms is incorrect?

options.a: Population is the universe about which an investigator wishes to draw conclusions
options.b: A sample is a representative subset of the population that is being studied
options.c: An element is a group of observations i n the population
options.d: A population need not be only people but can be measurements too

mcqs.explanation: An element is a single observation in a study. For example, in a study of blood pressure values, the blood pressure value of one person is an element. In a statistical study, the population refers to the group about which information is to be gathered. The composition of the population in terms of its age, sex, occupation, cultural characters, etc need to be defined before a study is conducted. The population need not consist of just people but can al so b e made of measurements. For example, in a study of blood glucose measurements in Indians, the population consists of the blood glucose measurements. The part/subset of the population, which is being studied is known as a sample. For example, in a questionnaire-based study on cervical cancer in a population, the sample would include females attending the out-patient departments of a hospital. This is a subset of the entire population.795

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about probability is true? (Probability of event occurring is p)
mcqs.explanation: If the probability of an event occurring is 1, it means there is an absolute certainty that the event will occur. The addition rule and multiplication rule can be used to calculate the probability of an event. The addition rule is used to calculate the combined probability of the occurrence of two or more mutually exclusive events. The multiplication rule is used to calculate the combined probability of two or more statistically independent events occurring together. Pro bability v alues range from 0 (no probability) to 1 (absolute certainty). So negative value of p is not possible. Since p is the probability of an event occurring and q is the probability of the event not occurring, q = 1 - p

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: In which of the following processes is binomial distribution widely used?
mcqs.explanation: Binomial distribution is widely used in genetic counseling. Binomial distribution helps determine the probability of occurance of a specific combination of mutually exclusive independent events. In a binomial distribution, there are only two possible events l ike Yes/No or Male/Female or Alive/Dead. The results of the distribution gives the probabilities of obtaining an exact number of successes in a series of independent trials. For example, the inheritence of cystic fibrosis follows a binomial distribution. There are: a. Two possible events - inheriting the disease/ not inheriting it b. Events are mutually exclusive - one person cannot both have the disease and not have it796 c. Independent possibilities - if one child has inherited it, this will not affect if the other child will inherit it. The physician using this technique can explain to the patients the probabilities of their children suffering from the disease.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: If the events A and B are mutually exclusive events, what is the probability of either A or B occurring?
mcqs.explanation: If the events A and B are mutually exclusive, then the probability of either A or B occuring is given by, p (A or B) = p (A) + p (B) This is as per the addition rule of probability. The probability of both the mutually exclusive events happening a t the same time is given by, p (A and B) = p (A) x p (B) The probability of any of two mutually non-exclusive events occuring at a point of time is given by, p (A or B) = p (A) + p (B) - p (A and B) If p(A) and p(B) are the only two outcomes possible in a given event then, p (A) + p (B) = 1 For example, probability of patient suffering from lung cancer dying within 5 years and probability of patient suffering from lung cancer surviving these 5 years adds upto 1.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: You are conducting a study on birth weight. As per your data, the probability of a baby having birth weight <2500 grams is 0.50 and of having birth weight of 2500-2999 grams is 0.20. What is the probability that a baby will have a birth weight of < 3kg?
mcqs.explanation: The probability that a baby will have a birth weight of < 3kg is 0.70. In this scenario, the probability of having a baby with BW < 2500 grams, p (A) = 0.50 and that of having a baby with BW between 2500 – 2999 grams, p (B) = 0.20. Since both events are mutually exclusive, i.e., they cannot happen together, it satisfies the condition for the addition rule of probability. Thus, the probability of having a baby that weighs less than 3 kilos is, p (A or B) = p (A) + p (B) = 0.50 + 0.20 = 0.70. If p(A) and p(B) were non-mutually exclusive events, t hen the probability would have been calculated by p(A or B) = p(A) + p(B) - p(A and B).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: You select 3 people from a population where the prevalence of anemia is 20% .What is the probability that all the three randomly selected people from the population would have anemia?
mcqs.explanation: 797 In the given scenario, the probability of all 3 randomly selected individuals having anemia is 0.008. In this scenario, the prevalence of anemia is 20%. So, the probability of a person having anemia in the given population (p) = 20/100 = 0.2. If selecting 3 people from the population randomly, the chance of the first person having anemia is independent of the second or third person also having it and vice versa. This satisfies the condition for the multiplication rule of probability w hich states that the probability of two or more statistically independent events all occurring together is equal to the product of their individual probabilities. Thus, here the probability that all the 3 randomly selected people from the population would have anemia = 0.2 x 0.2 x 0.2 = 0.008.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: There are 50 patients admitted in a ward of your medical college. Here 20 are girls and 30 are boys. Out of this, 10 girls and 20 boys require surgery. What is the probability that a randomly selected boy and girl both require surgery?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, the probability that a randomly selected boy and girl both require surgery is 1/3. First, we have to calculate the probability of picking the boys requiring s urgery and the girls requiring surgery separately. These are mutually exclusive events. In this scenario, the probability of correctly picking a girl requiring surgery is p(A)=10/20= 1/2 The probability of correctly picking a boy requiring surgery is p(B)=20/30= 2/3 Next, we apply the multiplication rule of probability. The probability of picking boys and girls that require surgery, p(A and B)= p(A) x p(B)= \275 x \037 = 2/6= 1/3.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: The chance of passing a genetic disease X by affected parents to their first child is 0.16. If they plan to have two children, what is the probability that both the children will have the disease?
mcqs.explanation: The probability of both children having the disease is 0.0256. In this scenario, the chance of each child having the disease is 0.16. The second child having the disease is independent of the first child having it. So, the events are statistically independent. Applying the multiplication rule of probability, the probability of both children having the disease is, 0.16 x 0.16 = 0.0256. These are non-mutually exclusive events as the first child having the trait does not rule out the chance of the second child having it. O n the other hand, the probability of one of the two children having the disease is given by, p(A or B)= p(A) + p(B) - p(A and B)= 0.16 + 0.16 -(0.16 x 0.16)= 0.32- 0.0256= 0.2944798

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: Which o f the following is not a measurement scale for data?
mcqs.explanation: A proportion is not a measurement scale for data. It is a ratio, where the numerator is always a part of the denominator. It indicates a value as a part of the whole. It is usually expressed as a percentage. The four scales of measurement used for data can be remembered with the mnemonic NOIR. This stands for nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio data scales.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: Which of the following scales of data measurement do blood groups belong?
mcqs.explanation: Bloods groups are nominal scale data or categorical data. This is because they are just labels and have no numerical value o r meaningful order.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: Which of the following are examples of nominal scale data?
mcqs.explanation: Genders, types of anemia and types of hospitals come under nominal scale data. There is no meaningful order or quantifiable variable in this kind of data. It is arranged on the basis of labels, titles or categories. Kuppuswamy scale is an ordinal scale data. It is a scale representing socio-economic data. Height is a ratio scale data as it can be arranged in a meaningful order with a well-defined size interval.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: A physician classifies a group of patients based on disease severity as normal, mild, moderate and severe. Which of the following scales of data does this classification system belong to?
mcqs.explanation: The classification of this disease as normal, mild, moderate and severe belongs to the ordinal scale. This is because this arrangement is not only qualitative but also has a meaningful order with no interval in between.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: Which of the following are representative of ordinal scale data?
mcqs.explanation: TNM staging, Likert scale and severity of pain are measured on the ordinal scale. In such cases, the arrangement is qualitative, with a meaningful order but there is no way of quantifying the difference between the individual variables. For example, grading of pain as mild, moderate, and severe. The Li kert scale is used in collecting self-reported data in questionnaire-based research. It is a psychometric scale used to understand people's attitudes from responses. Usually, a 5-point scale of agreement is used which includes: • 1 – Strongly disagree799 • 2 – Disagree • 3 – Neither agree nor disagree • 4 – Agree • 5 – Strongly agree TNM staging is done for the staging of cancer. It is based on tumor size, lymph node status and metastasis. Lower stages indicate better prognosis than higher stages. Hemoglobin level is an example of ratio scale data. HIV positive or negative status falls under the category of nominal scale data.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a c ontinuous variable?

options.a: Blood glucose value of a diabetic patient
options.c: Number of visits to the hospital in a year

mcqs.explanation: The number of visits to the hospital in a year is a discrete variable. The only values it can take are whole numbers a nd none in between. For example, you can't visit the hospital 2.5 times. Blood glucose value, mid-arm circumference and birth weight are continuous variables. They can have any value within a limit or a range.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: Match the following.
mcqs.explanation: The number of cancer patients in a hospital is an example of discrete data. They can only take certain values and none in between. The temperature measured in the Celsius scale is an example of interval scale data. Such data are arranged in a meaningful order but they c an not have an absolute zero value. For example, degree celcius to not twice as hot as 40 degree celcius and 0 degree celcius does not indicate an absolute abscence of heat. Height and weight, blood pressure and temperature in the Kelvin scale are examples of ratio scale data. Such data are arranged in a meaningful order and the scales they are measured in have absolute zero value. For example, a temperature of 0 kelvin indicates an absolute abscense of heat. Height and w eight, blood pressure, and temperature are examples of continuous data as they can take any values between limits or a range.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: Identify the following representation of data.
mcqs.explanation: The image shown is of a boxplot. This is a method for graphically depicting groups of numerical data through their quartiles. Box plots may also have lines extending vertically from the boxes (i.e., whiskers) indicating variability outside the upper and lower quartiles. Hence, they are also known as box-and-whisker plots and box-and-whisker dia grams.800 The below image shows a boxplot depicting a series of experiments done to calculate the velocity of light.A stem and leaf plot is used to depict frequency distribution and individual values for numerical data. The stem is are usually arranged in ascending or descending order vertically, and a vertical line is drawn to separate it from the leaf. The number of leaf items total up to the number of observations. It is difficult to represent a large number of observations using this method. The below image shows a stem and leaf plot.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: The following diagram charts the population change over years from 1983 to 1989 in a given place. What is the statistical diagram used here?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a component bar graph. It is used to represent data in which the total magnitude is divided into different subsets or components.801 A bar chart or bar graph is used mainly for nominal or ordinal scale data. They can be simple, multiple or component bar graphs. The image given below shows a multiple bar graph showing the human losses of world war II by country. In a multiple bar chart, 2 or more sets of data are shown simultaneously.A bar chart can be distinguished from a histogram because the rectangles are separated by the spaces. This indicates that the data forms discrete categories. In a histogram, the rectangles are not separated by spaces as the data represented forms a continuous set instead of discrete groups.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: Identify the following graphical representation of data.
mcqs.explanation: The given image is of a frequency polygon. It is obtained by joining the midpoints of histogram blocks. It is used to diagrammatically represent frequency distribution. Scattergram is a g raph in which the values of two variables are plotted along two axes. The pattern of the resulting points reveals any correlation that may be present. The below image shows a scattergram.802 A line diagram is a type of chart that displays information as a series of data points called 'markers' connected by straight line segments. It is usually used to study time trends.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: During a cholera outbreak, you are asked to map the geographical distribution of the disease. What is the best method of doing this?
mcqs.explanation: Dot-density maps are the best way to plot the geographical distribution of diseases. The image given below shows a dot-density map of London that was plotted during the 1854 outbreak of cholera.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: What is the best way to plot the changes in incidence of a disease in a given area over time?
mcqs.explanation: 803 Line graphs or line diagrams are the best way to plot the changes in the incidence of a disease in a given area over time.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: A doctor is taking history from a diabetic patient and decides to make a chart to assess joint involvement. Which char t s hould he make to explain this?
mcqs.explanation: In this case, a tree diagram would help the doctor in explaining the possible outcomes to the patient's diabetes, with the perspective of joint involvement. A tree diagram is used mainly to chart the possible outcomes of a sample event. The following image shows the outline of a tree diagram.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: What type of data does the image given below represent?
mcqs.explanation: The given image is of a histogram. It is used to represent frequency distributions of continuous quantitative data. Nominal and ordinal data can be represented by a bar chart.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I - Probability and Data
mcqs.question: Which of the following can be used to represent quantitative data?
mcqs.explanation: An ogive, a line diagram and a histogram can be used to represent quantitative data. The images shown above are: A – Ogive B – Bar graph C – Line diagram804 D – Histogram Quantitative data cannot be represented by a bar graph. It is used mostly for nominal scale or qualitative data.805

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a measure of location?
mcqs.explanation: Percentile is a measure of position. It can be defined as a number that states the percentage of observations that fall below any particular score. Measures of location help in summarizing the data by locating its centre or middle. The three main measures of location include mean, median and mode. They are also called measures of central tendency.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: The mean can be calculated only if data is on:
mcqs.explanation: The mean can be worked out only for quantitative values. Thus, it can be calculated for interval or ratio scale data. A dichotomous s cale is a type of nominal scale data that can take only two values. Example : Male/ Female. For nominal scale data, the preferred measure of central tendency is mode. For ordinal scale data, both median and mode can be calculated. Median can be derived from ordinal, interval and ratio data scales. Mode can be derived from all scales of data- nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: During a school health survey on malnutrition, the children are arranged according to ascending order of their heights. Which of the following can be obtained by this arrangement?
mcqs.explanation: The 50th centile can be obtained when values are arranged in order and the central value is picked o ut. This is the same as the median. In a distribution that has an odd number of elements, the median is the middle value.812 In a distribution that has an even number of elements, the median is the average of the middle values, i.e., the arithmetic mean of the two middle values. An example of how to calculate the median of an odd and an even number of elements is given below.Option C: Geometric mean is obtained by taking the arithmetic mean of values on a logarithmic scale. Option D: Mean deviation is a measure of dispersion. The average of deviations from the arithmetic mean gives the mean deviation.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: Which of the following can have m ore than one value?
mcqs.explanation: The mode of a given sample can have more than one value. It is the most frequently occurring value in a distribution. For example, in the sample [1, 3, 6, 6, 6, 6, 7, 7, 12, 12, 17], the most repeated value i.e., the mode is 6. For the list of data [1, 1, 2, 4, 4], t he mode is 1 and 4. Therefore , the mode is not unique. This dataset may be said to be bimodal, while a set with more than two modes may be described as multimodal. Median can have only one value, obtained by arranging values in order and then picking out the central value. In a sample with an even number of elements, median is obtained by taking the average of the middle 2 elements. Mean can only have a single value. The harmonic mean is the reciprocal of the arithmetic mean of the r eciprocals of the data values. The geometric mean is obtained by taking the arithmetic mean of values on a logarithmic scale.813

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: While collecting data on which of the following variables would median not be the preferred measure of central tendency?
mcqs.explanation: Blood pressure usually forms a normal symmetrical distribution for which mean is the preferred measure of central tendency. Distributions of survival time, incubation period and health expenses have the probability of having extreme values, i.e., outliers. Thus, they form skewed distributions and in such cases, median is the preferred measure of central tendency.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true for the given distribution of ages of patients who are visiting a family planning clinic in a day?
mcqs.explanation: The arithmetic mean from the following data is given by the sum of all the values, 270 divided by the number o f values, = 30. The data can be arranged in ascending order as 20, 25, 28, 31, 31, 31, 31, 35, 38. After arranging in order, the median is obtained by picking out the central value which is 31. The mode is the most frequently occurring value, which is 31 here.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: You are conducting a study on birth weights in your hospital. Out of 11 births, 5 babies w eighed over 2.5 kg, one baby weighed 2.5 kg and 5 weighed less than 2.5 kg. What does the value 2.5 represent in this distribution?
mcqs.explanation: Out of the 11 birth weights, 2.5 kg would represent the middle value or the median. 5 babies weigh more than 2.5 kg and 5 less than that. This can be understood from the image below.Option A: Mean or arithmetic mean is the average value. In this case, the mean is the average of all the 11 values. It need not be 2.5. Option B: Geometric mean is obtained by taking the arithmetic mean of values on a logarithmic scale.814 Option D: Quartile is a measure of position, where the data is divided into four equal sets. 3/4 of the values are below the 3rd quartile reading. Hence, it cannot be the central reading.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: You are conducting an epidemiological study on malaria in a town X. The number of cases reported during the last 10 years is given below. What is the most appropriate measure of central tendency for this data?
mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, median is the preferred measure of central tendency as there are outliers. The value of 5000 is an outlier in the given set, i.e., an observed value which is very distant from other observations in the distribution. This indicates the usage of median as the measure of central tendency a s it is not sensitive to extreme values, unlike the mean. By arranging the data in order: 100, 160, 190, 250, 260, 300, 320, 320, 350, 5000, we get the median as (260 + 300) / 2 = 280. Options A and B: Mean is the most affected by the presence of outliers. Mode is the least affected by outliers but it is used mainly for measuring the central tendency of nominal data. Option D: Geometric mean can be used for datasets with extreme values but it is not used when the values can be zero or n egative. In the given scenario, the number of malaria cases reported in a town can also have a zero value.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: During a school health assessment, the mean value of weight for a group of 10 boys was found to be 18.2 kg. Later, it was found that the weight of one of the boys was wrongly recorded as 2.0 kg instead of 20 kg. What is the true mea n weight of the group?
mcqs.explanation: The true mean weight of the group is 20 kg. Mean is given as x\037 = \030x / n, where n is the number of elements and \030x denotes the sum of all the elements in the series. In this scenario, the incorrect mean is 18.2, i.e., \030x / 10 = 18.2, making \030x = 182 . But this is incorrect as one of the 10 weights was wrongly recorded as 2 instead of 20. The corrected \030x = (Incorrect \030x – incorrect value) + cor rect v alue. The incorrect sum of all elements = 182, incorrect value =2 and the correct value = 20. Thus, the correct sum of all the 10 weights would be, \030x = (182 – 2) + 20 = 200. From this, the correct mean value of the 10 weights can be given by: \030x / 10 = 200/ 10 = 20.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the given distribution of ages of patients attending a geriatric medicine clinic?
mcqs.explanation: For the given dataset, the modes are 70 and 76. The mode is the most frequently occurring value. It can have multiple values. In this scenario, the values 70 and 76 have been repeated twice.815 Median of this distribution is the central value, (76 + 80) / 2 = 78.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: The smoking history for the past 6 years of a patient with emphysema is given in the table below. If a pack has 20 cigarettes, what is the mean, median and mode of the given data?
mcqs.explanation: The distribution in this scenario in terms of the number of cigarettes smoked is 5, 10, 10, 10, 20, 40. The mean here is \030x/n = 95/6 = 15.833 rounded off to 16. The median here is the central value = average of 3rd and 4th values since the distribution has an even number of values. This comes to (10 + 10) / 2 = 10. The mode here is 10 which has a frequency of 3 in the given dataset.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: While reviewing a data distribution, you find that the highest value of 58 was wrongly recorded as 85 and so you correct it. How will this correction change the measures of central tendency?

options.a: No change in mean, decreased median
options.b: Decreased mean, no change in median

mcqs.explanation: The given change in a dataset would cause a decrease in the mean but the median would remain unchanged . The mean is sensitive to every value in the distribution. Since the correct value of 58 is much lesser than the wrongly recorded value of 85, the final mean will be decreased compared to the earlier recorded value. However, as only the highest value was wrongly recorded, the median i.e., the central value, will remain the same.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: While conducting a study on the age at death in males of a population Y, the distribution curve given below is obtained. Which of th e f ollowing is true?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a negatively skewed or a left-skewed distribution curve. Here, mean < median < m ode . Mode is the most frequently occurring value in the distribution and is given by the highest point of the graph. Since the given graph has only one peak, it is unimodal. A positively skewed distribution refers to a right-skewed distribution. In such cases, mean > median > mode.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: Which of the following sets of measures of central tendency is likely to match the distribution depicted in the given image?
mcqs.explanation: The given image is of a right-skewed or positively skewed distribution. So, among the given options, the most likely values of mean = 3, median = 2, and mode = 1. We can tell the direction o f skew of a distribution by observing the direction of the tail. Here , the tail of the distribution is towards the positive direction and thus it is positively skewed or right-skewed. In a positively skewed distribution, mean > median > mode.816 If the tail of the distribution is towards the negative direction, the distribution would be negatively skewed or left-skewed. In such distributions, mode > median > mean.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: You are conducting a study on blood pressure in a population. The systolic blood pressure values have a mean of 130 mmHg, a median of 140 mmHg and mode of 160 mmHg. What type of distribution is this?
mcqs.explanation: This is a unimodal negatively skewed distribution. In this scenario, the mean of 130 mmHg is less than the median of 140 mmHg which is less than mode of 160mmHg. Since mean<median<mode, this is an asymmetrical negatively skewed or left-skewed distribution. It is a unimodal distribution as t here is only a single value for mode. In a symmetrical distribution, the mean = median = mode. In a positively skewed distribution, mean > median > mode.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: The mean of a dataset is 2 and the m edian is 3. What is the mode?
mcqs.explanation: As the mean \027 median, this is an asymmetric distribution and so we can use the formula: Mode = 3 median - 2 mean. Using the given values, mode = (3x3) – (2x2) = 9 – 4 = 5. A distribution is termed symmetric when the mean, median and mode coincide i.e., mean= median= mode.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a measure of dispersion?
mcqs.explanation: 825 Z scores are not a measure of dispersion, they are measures of position. It indicates the position of any element in a distribution in terms of how many standard deviations it lies from the mean of the distribution. The most common measures of spread/dispersion are range, standard deviation and variance. They help in determining the extent to which data is stretched/scattered or squeezed/clustered. They are also called measures of spread or scatter or variability.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: What is standard deviation a measure of?
mcqs.explanation: Standard deviation is a measure of spread or dispersion or variability. Range and variability are other measures of spread.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct relationship between variance and standard deviation?

options.a: Variance = square root of standard deviation
options.b: Standard deviation = square root of variance

mcqs.explanation: Standard deviation is the square root of variance.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: You are conducting a study o n chronic kidney disease in a population. Your sample size is 28. What formula for standard deviation will you use here?
mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, the sample size is 28, which is <30. For a small sample, usually less than 30, the formula for standard deviation used is:It is better to use n-1 in the denominator in the case of a small sample. But in the case of a very large sample subtracting 1 from a huge number will not make much of a significant correction. In those cases, we may choose to ignore subtracting 1.826

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: Which among the following is true about standard deviation?

options.a: One standard deviation covers 95% of the values
options.c: It can be used only in normal distributions
options.d: It is a measure of central tendency

mcqs.explanation: The standard deviation (S.D) indicates the distribution of variables. It is a measure of dispersion. It can be used in normal and skewed distributions, but it is particularly useful in normal distributions. 1 S.D covers 68% of the values. 2 S.D covers 95% of the values. Measures of central tendency are mean, median and mode.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: You are using the Kuppuswamy scale to calculate the socio-economic status of 10 families in the railway staff quarters. You find that every family has a total monthly income of Rs. 73,355. What is the standard devia tion of this sample?
mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, the standard deviation will be zero. The monthly income of every family is Rs. 73,355. So, all the elements in this distribution are the s ame. Hence , there is no variability. Both the standard deviation and variance which is the square of standard deviation will be zero.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: Each value of a study sample is multiplied by 10. What would be the new standard deviation of the observations?
mcqs.explanation: When each element of a sample is multiplied by 10, the new standard deviation= 10 x original standard deviation. The formula for standard deviation, SD = \026\030(x - x\037)2/n-1. If each element of the distribution is multiplied by 10, the new mean will become 10 times the original mean. If all observations are multiplied by 10, then the new SD = \026\030( 10x-10x\037)2 /n -1 = \026\030(x - x\037)2/n-1 = 10 x Original SD Change in variance: variance = square of standard deviation, so when SD becomes 10 times, the variance will be 10\262 = 100 times the original variance.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: On plotting the blood pressure values of a population on a graph, you obtain the curve given below. Which of the following is true?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a normal distribution, also called bell curve or Gaussian distribution. It has no skew. It is defined by the mean and standard deviation. In a normal distribution, mean = median = mode. The total area under the curve of a normal distribution is 1.827

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the standard normal distribution?
mcqs.explanation: A standard normal distribution is a type of normal distribution. It is bell-shaped, has a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1. Thus the variance, the square of standard deviation is also 1 = the standard deviation.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: In a normal curve, what is the percentage of distribution of one standard deviation?
mcqs.explanation: Approximately 68% of a normal distribution falls within \261 1 standard deviations of the mean. This is as per the empirical rule of a normal distribution. Approximately 95% of the distribution falls within \261 2 standard deviations of the mean. Approximately 99. 7% o f the distribution falls within \261 standard deviations of the mean.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: During a study on anaemia in a population, a normal distribution curve with a mean of 13.5 g% is obtained. What proportion of the population constitutes people with haemoglobin values above 13.5 g%?
mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, 0.50, i.e., 50% of the population would have haemoglobin more than the mean, i.e., 13.5 gm%. In a normal distribution, 50% of the values lie above the mean.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: The IQ scores of your study population form a bell-shaped curve. How much of the population falls between the median (Mdn) and Mdn + 1 S.D?
mcqs.explanation: 34% or 0.34 of the population in a normal distribution falls between the median and median plus one standard deviation. The IQ values form a bell-shaped curve, which is seen in normal symmetric distributions. According to the empirical r ule of normal distributions, % of the distribution falls within 1 standard deviation of the mean, i.e., mean \261 1 SD covers 68% of the distribution. Now, in a normal distribution, mean = median. Therefore, this 68% includes values from median -1SD to median +1SD. The question asks about the percentage that falls under median +1SD, which would be half of 68%, that is 34% or 0.34. Below is the graphical representation of the question. The question is asking to calculate the s haded region in the graph.828

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: The fasting blood glucose levels of adults in a population forms a normal distribution. The st atistical m easures obtained are given below. Within what limits would 95% of the population have their blood glucose values?
mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, 95% of the population would have their blood sugar within the limits of 85 and 125 mg. Here, the mean blood sugar is 105 mg and the standard deviation is 10 mg. According to the empirical rule of normal distribution, 95% of the distribution falls within two standard deviations of the mean. In this question, 2 S.D = 10 x 2 = 20. We do, + and - 2 S.D from the mean to arrive at the limits within which 95% of the population would have their blood sugar, i.e., 85 and 125 mg. + and - 1 S . D = 10 from the mean, we get the limits within which 68% of the population would have their blood sugar value, i.e., 95 and 115 mg. + and - 3 S.D = 30, from the mean, we get limits within which 99% would have their values, i.e., 75 and 135 mg.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: While conducting a study on malnutrition, you record the following data. If it forms a normal distribution curve, which of the following is true for this sample?

options.a: Weight of 95 children is between 12 and 18 kg
options.b: Weight of 95 children is between 10.5 and 19.5 kg
options.c: Weight of 99 children is between 10 and 19 kg
options.d: Weight of 34 children is between 13.5 and 16.5 kg

mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, the weight of 95 children will be between 12 and 18 kg as the mean is 15 kg and the standard deviation is 1.5 kg. According to the empirical rule of normal distribution, 95% of the distribution falls within two standard deviations o f the mean. Two standard deviations = 2 x 1.5 = 3 kg The weight of 99.7% of children will be between 10.5-19.5 Kg, i.e., within three standard deviations. The weight of 68% of children will be between 13.5 to 16.5 Kg, i.e., within one standard deviation. Half will weigh between 13.5 and 15kg and the other half between 15 and 16.5kg829

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: The distribution of intraocular pressure (IOP) in 100 glaucoma patients form a normal distribution curve. It has a mean of 30 mm of Hg with a standard deviation (SD) of 1 mm of Hg. 97.5% of patients would have an IOP more than what value?
mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, 97.5% of patients would have an IOP of more than 28 mm of Hg. The mean IOP is 30mm of Hg and SD is 1.0 mm of Hg. According to the empirical rule of the normal distribution, 95% of the distribution falls within two standard deviations of the mean, i.e., mean \261 2 SD. So 95% of patients will have their IOP between 30 \261 2 = 28 to 32 mm of Hg. Out of the remaining 5%, half will have IOP < 28 and the other half will have > 32. So half of 5%= 2.5% has IOP <28mm Hg. Thus the remaining 9 7.5% has IOP > 28mm of Hg. This is shown in the image given below
