mcqs.question: A study is being conducted on anaemia in pregnancy. A normal distribution curve with a mean haemoglobin level of 10.6 gm/dL with a stand ard d eviation of 2 gm/dL is obtained. Below what level would 5% of the women in the group have their haemoglobin values?
mcqs.explanation: 5% of the pregnant women in this group will have their haemoglobin levels below 7.31 g/dL. Solution: Given Data : • Mean: 10.6 g/dL • Standard deviation : 2 g/dL Step 1:830 According to the empirical rule of a normal distribution, 95% of the population fall within 2 standard deviations of the mean, i.e., mean \261 2SD. This implies that the remaining 5% lie outside 2 SD, i.e. 2.5% below 2 SD and 2.5% above 2 SD. Therefore , Mean - 2SD = 10.6 � 2 (2) = 10.6 � = 6.6 g/dL Thus, 2.5% of pregnant women have Hb levels below 6.6 g/dL. However, the question asks about 5% and not 2.5%. So options C and D have been ruled out. Now Let's move to the next step. Step 2:831 According to the empirical rule of a normal distribution, 68% of the population fall within 1 standard deviation of the mean, i.e., mean\261 1SD. This implies that the remaining 32% lie outside 1 SD, i.e., 16% below 1 SD and 16% above 1 SD. The value of mean� 1 SD is 8.6 g/dL (i.e. 10.6 � 2) Thus, 16% of pregnant women have Hb levels below 8.6 g/dL. so now option A is ruled out Step 3: The value for 5% must lie between the values where 2.5% and 16% of the population lie, i.e., between 6.6g/dL a nd 8 g/dL. Only option B, 7.31 g/dL, satisfies this condition. Hence, 5% of pregnant women have their Hb levels below 7.31 g/dL.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: The peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) values of a group of 11-year-old girls have a mean of 300 l/min and a standard deviation of 20 l/min. What are the deviation scores for the PEFR values of two girls recorded as 280 l/min and 330 l/min respectively?
mcqs.explanation: The deviation scores for PEFR values 280 l/min and 330 l/min are -20 and 30 respectively. The Deviation score of an element in a distribution is the difference between the mean of the distribution and the element itself, i.e., it is obtained by subtracting the distribution's mean from the element. Applying this here, deviation score of the value 280 l/min = the e lement - the mean = 280 - 300 = -20. For the value 330 l/min, deviation score = 330 - 300 = 30.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: The shape of a normal distribution curve depends on?
mcqs.explanation: The shape of a normal distribution curve depends upon its mean and standard deviation. For example, for a particular mean value, a smaller standard deviation value gives a taller and narrower curve whereas, a larger value gives a flatter curve. The curve is centered at the mean �M which coincides with the median and the mode and is located at the point beneath the peak of the curve. T he mean, median and mode are equal.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a property of a normal distribution curve?
mcqs.explanation: In a normal distribution curve, mean = median. mean > median in positively/ rightward skewed distribution. mean < median in negatively/ leftward skewed distribution.832

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about the standard normal distribution?
mcqs.explanation: In a standard normal distribution, mean = 0.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: A population study showed a m ean glucose of 86 mg/dL. In a sample of 100 showing normal distribution, what percentage of people will have blood glucose above 86 mg/dL?
mcqs.explanation: In a normal distribution, 50% of the values lie above the mean. In this scenario, 50% of the people will have a blood glucose level of more than 86 mg/dL.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: The mean value of marks in a distribution of 100 students in a class is 105 and standard deviation is 10. How many students will have their marks between 85 and 125?
mcqs.explanation: According to the empirical rule of normal distribution, 95% of the distribution falls within two standard deviations of the mean, i.e., mean \261 2 SD. In this scenario, the marks between 85 and 125 fall within 2 standard deviation of the mean which is 105. Thus 95% of the students will have t he marks in this range.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: The systolic blood pressure of a group of normal people between the ages of 25–27 years was taken and a mean of 120 mmHg was found. What will be the expected number of individuals among a group of 100 people taken for the study whose BP will be below 120 mmHg?
mcqs.explanation: In a normal distribution, 50% of the values lie below the mean. In this scenario, 50%, i.e., 50 of the 100 people will have a systolic BP of less than 120 mmHg.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: In a normal distribution , w hat percentage of the distribution falls within 2 standard deviations of the mean?
mcqs.explanation: According to the empirical rule of normal distributions, 95% of the distribution falls within 2 standard deviations of the mean, i.e., mean \261 2 SD covers 95% of the distribution.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Disper...
mcqs.question: In a population study, the value of the mean is 200. If the standard deviation is 20, 68% of the population will lie between?
mcqs.explanation: 68% of the population will lie between 180- 220. In a normal distribution curve, 68% of the values lie within the mean +/- 1 s tandard deviation and the mean=median=mode. Since the mean = 200 and the standard deviation = 20: 68% of population will lie between Mean +/- 1SD, that is, 200 +/- 20 = 180-220 95% of population lies between Mean+/-2SD, 200+/- 2*20 = 160- 99% of population lies between Mean+/-3SD, 200+/- 3*20 = 140-

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics IV - Measures of Position
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a measure of position?
mcqs.explanation: Range is not a measure of position, it is a measure of dispersion or spread. The most common measures of position are quantiles, quartiles, centiles and z-scores (standard scores). Measures of position give the position of specific data in relation to other data in the set.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics IV - Measures of Position
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about quantiles are true?
mcqs.explanation: Quantiles are elements in a distribution that divide data into equal groups. They are also known as fractiles. Median divides a distribution into two equal parts, so it is considered as a quantile. Quantiles a re used for continuous, quantitative data. Quintiles are a type of quantile that divides data into 5 equal groups.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics IV - Measures of Position
mcqs.question: Centiles divide data into ____ equal parts?
mcqs.explanation: Centiles divide data into 100 equal parts.837

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics IV - Measures of Position
mcqs.question: During a school health camp, a group of 250 students are arranged in the ascending order of their height. Which student would have the 40th percentile value for height?
mcqs.explanation: Here, the 100th student will have the 40th percentile value for height. To arrive at this, we use the formula R = P/100 x (n + 1). where R is the rank of the desired observation, P is the quantile/percentile desired and n is the number of variables in the data. Thus, R = 40/100 x (250 + 1) = 0.4 x 251 = 100.4. This is rounded up to the closest number making R = 100.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics IV - Measures of Position
mcqs.question: By calculating which of the following can we obtain the central value of a sample with 180 elements?
mcqs.explanation: The 2nd quartile gives the central value of 180 elements. The central value of a distribution is given by the median. It divides the d istribution into the ratio of 1:1. In quartiles elements of the distribution are divided into 4 equal parts by 3 values. Each part contains a quarter, i.e., 25% of the values. So two quarters would give half of the values. So the element present at the position of the 2nd quartile would be the central value, i.e., the median, with half the values before and half the values after it. This is shown in the image given below.The 5th decile and 50th percentile represent the median values of a distribution in decile and percentile respectively.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics IV - Measures of Position
mcqs.question: Which measure of position divides the distribution in a ratio of 3:1?
mcqs.explanation: Third quartile Q3 divides the distribution into the ratio of 3:1.838 In quartiles: • the first quartile Q1 divides the distribution in the ratio of 1:3 • the second quartile Q2 divides it in the ratio of 1:1. The division of data by quartiles is shown in the below image.Centiles divide data into 100 equal parts. 33rd centile divides the distribution in the ratio of 33:67. Deciles divide data into 10 equal parts. 7th decile divides the distribution in the ratio of 7:3.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics IV - Measures of Position
mcqs.question: You are recording the blood pressure values of 200 adults in a population. The first quartile diastolic BP is 68 mmHg and the third quartile is 105 mmHg. How many patients are th ere i n the 3rd and 4th quarters?
mcqs.explanation: In a quartile, the data is divided into 4 equal parts, i.e., 4 quarters. Therefore, in this scenario, there are 50% of patients in the 3rd and 4th quarters, i.e 100 patients. The division of data by quartiles is shown in the image given below.839

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics IV - Measures of Position
mcqs.question: The forced expiratory volume (FEV) of 300 patients visiting the respiratory medicine outpatient department is recorded. The data has a median value of 2.5 litres with the first and third quartiles being 1.5 litres and 4.5 litres respectively. How many persons in the sample are expected to have an FEV between 1.5 and 4.5 litres?
mcqs.explanation: 150 persons are expected to have FEV between 1.5 and 4.5 litres. In a quartile, the data is divided by 3 values into 4 equal parts. Thus, each part will have 25% of the values in the distribution. In this scenario, each part will have 75 persons. Here, 1.5 is the first quartile Q1, 2.5 is the second quartile Q2 and 4.5 is the third quartile Q3. Between Q1 and Q3 there are two quarters, thus there will be 150 people with FEV between 1.5 and 4.5 litres. Data division by quartiles is shown in t he below image.840

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics IV - Measures of Position
mcqs.question: Which of the following distributions is preferred for the calculation of z scores?
mcqs.explanation: Z scores are usually calculated in normal distributions.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics IV - Measures of Position
mcqs.question: In a study on haemoglobin levels in healthy women, the data recorded has a mean of 13.5 gm/dL and a standard deviation of 1.5 g m/dL. W hat is the z score for an element with a haemoglobin value of 15.0 gm/dL?
mcqs.explanation: The Z score for the element with a haemoglobin value of 15 gm/dL is 1.0. The formula for z score, z = (X- \265\024. X is the value of the element, \265 is the mean and \024 is the standard deviation. In this scenario, z = (15 – 13.5) / 1.5 = 1.5/1.5 = 1.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics IV - Measures of Position
mcqs.question: The diastolic BP of 125 women aged between 18 and 60 years was recorded. The mean of the data is 70 mmHg with a standard deviation of 10 mmHg. What will be the 5th percentile value?
mcqs.explanation: The z value for the 5th percentile is -1.645. Using the formula for z scores, z = (X- \265\024, we get X = z\024 + \265. In this scenario, X = (-1.645 x 10) + 70 = -16.45 + 70 = 53.55 = 53.6.841

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The statistical methods that go further than merely summarizing data are a part of:
mcqs.explanation: Inferential statistics are those statistical methods that go further than just summarizing data. They involve inductive reasoning and using a statistic to estimate a parameter. E.g., the expected success rate of vasectomy or mean blood pressure of all Indians. One of the most common problems faced in research is using information gathered by researching a sample and then drawing conclusions about the population from which the sample is drawn. Here, sample statistics (sample m ean and SD) are known and population parameters (population mean and SD) are unknown. Inferential statistical methods are used to draw conclusions about the population parameters from sample statistics.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following measures relative variation between two different units?
mcqs.explanation: Co-efficient of variation (CV ) measures the relative variability between two different units, by using the mean and standard deviation.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The weight of the 100 children that presented in the pediatric OPD in the last week was analyzed. The median weight was 12 kg a nd t he standard deviation was 3. This data formed a normal distribution. What is the coefficient of variation?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, coefficient of variance (CV ) = 25%. Coefficient of variation, CV = standard deviation x 100/ mean = 3 x 1 00/12 = 25%. In a normal distribution, mean = median.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The means of all possible samples from a population are plotted on a linear graph. What is this called?
mcqs.explanation: The random sampling distribution of means is the distribution formed when all possible sample means from a population are plotted in a frequency distribution.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Central limit theorem is related to:
mcqs.explanation: The central limit theorem is related to the random sampling distribution of means. According to this theorem, as the sample size increases: • The sampling distribution tends towards a normal distribution curve (bell curve) • Regardless of the populati on's a ctual distribution shape • Assuming all samples are identical in size • The sample mean and standard deviations become closer to the population mean and standard deviations846

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A researcher wanted to calculate the mean age of onset of type II diabetes mellitus in a population. He got a sample mean of 45. To measure the extent of deviation from the population mean, which of the following sho uld he use?
mcqs.explanation: The standard error is a measure of the extent to which the sample means deviate from the true population means.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Standard deviation of mean measures variations caused by:
mcqs.explanation: The standard deviation of mean or standard error of means measures variations caused by sampling errors.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Consider a sample of 100 women with an average Hb of 10 g% and standard deviation of 1. What is the standard error of this sample?
mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, the standard error SE = 0.1. The formula for standard error: SE = Standard deviation/ \026sample size =1/\026100 = 1/10 = 0.1

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: All of the following are true about standard error except:

options.a: It increases as the sample size increases.
options.b: It is based on a normal distribution
options.c: It depends on the standard deviation of means
options.d: It is used to estimate confidence limits

mcqs.explanation: As the sample size increases, the standard error will decrease, not increase. The standard error is inversely related to t he square root of the sample size.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The incubation period for measles in a group of 25 children was calculated. Following findings were recorded. What is the standard error?
mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, the standard error = 0.4. The formula for standard error: SE = Standard deviation/\026sample size = 2/\02625 = 2/5 = 0.4

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The uppermost and lowermost values of standard errors within which a parameter v alue is expected to lie are called the:
mcqs.explanation: The uppermost and lowermost limits of standard errors within which a parameter value is expected to lie are called the confidence limits. The difference between upper and lower confidence limits is called the confidence interval.847

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following parameters are used to calculate the confidence limit?
mcqs.explanation: Confidence limits are calculated with the sample mean and standard error.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: During screening of a population, the mean cholesterol levels were found to be 230mg/dL . The standard error was 10. Calculate the 95% confidence limits.
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, 95% confidence limits are 210 – 250. In inferential statistics, 95% confidence limits = Sample mean (x\037\ 2 standard errors. In this case, mean is 230 and the standard error is 10. Hence, confidence limits are 210-250.848

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the hypothesis which states that an apparent effect is only due to chance, called as?
mcqs.explanation: The hypothesis that an apparent effect is only due to chance is a null hypothesis. If this is rejected as false, we have an alternative hypothesis.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the significance level in hypothesis testing called as?
mcqs.explanation: Significance level in hypothesis testing is called alpha level (\023) or criterion.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the p value?

options.a: Probability of declaring a significant difference when there is none in reality
options.b: Probability of declaring a significant difference w hen it is actually present
options.c: Probability of not declaring a significant difference when actually it is not present
options.d: Probability of not declaring a significant difference when actually it is present

mcqs.explanation: p-value can be defined as the probability of declaring a significant difference when there is none in reality.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about the p-value?

options.a: It is equal to the probability of committing a type I error
options.c: It is the chance that the presence of difference is concluded when actually there may be none
options.d: When the p value is less than \023, the result is statistically significant

mcqs.explanation: The power of a test is 1 – beta. The p value is the probability that a type I error is being made. It is the chance that the presence of difference i s concluded when actually there may be none. When the p value is less than \023, the result is statistically significant.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A randomized control trial comparing the efficacy of two chemotherapy regimens for Hodgkin's lymphoma showed that their difference is statistically significant with p < 0.001. However, in reality the two drugs do not differ in their efficacy. What type of error is this an example of?
mcqs.explanation: This is an example of a type I error. In this scenario, let us take the null hypothesis as the efficacy of two drugs being the same, which as the question states, is true in reality. The alternative hypothesis will then be that one drug is better than the other. The questions states that p-value was found to be < 0.001, which is statistically significant and s o the null hypothesis is rejected. But we already know that the null hypothesis is true and we are forced to accept the alternative hypothesis even though it is false. When an alternative hypothesis is accepted even when it is false and the null hypothesis is true, it is called as a type I error or an alpha error or a false positive error.853

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An investigator is conducting a study to assess the effect o f a mood stabiliser on patients with bipolar I disorder. What does it mean if the difference is significant in the results?

options.a: p > 0.05 and it is likely by chance
options.b: p > 0.05 and it is unlikely by chance
options.c: p < 0.05 and it is unlikely by chance
options.d: p < 0.05 and it is likely by chance

mcqs.explanation: When the difference is significant, it means that the difference is unlikely by chance and p will be \022 0.05.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: While assessing the effect of a new intervention for type II DM, you obtain the p-value of the study as 0.023. Based on this observation, what is your inference?

options.a: Null hypothesis is accepted and the study is rejected
options.b: Null hypothesis is rejected and the study is accepted
options.c: Null hypothesis is accepted and the study is accepted
options.d: Null hypothesis is rejected and the study is also rejected

mcqs.explanation: By convention, if the p value \022 0.05, the difference is said to be statistically significant. Thus, the null hypothesis is rejected and the study is accepted.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a false statement regarding hypothesis testing?

options.a: Alpha is the maximum tolerable probability of a type 1 error being made
options.b: Beta is the probability of a type II error
options.c: When the null hypothesis is true but rejected, it is a type II error
options.d: p value can be more or less than alpha

mcqs.explanation: When the null hypothesis is true but is still rejected, it is a type I error and not a type II error. Type II errors are when an alternative hypothesis is rejected even though it is true.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are conducting a randomised clinical trial to see if a new drug 'A' has better efficacy than the standard drug 'B', in patients with grade III hypertension. While analysing the results of this study, you conclude that no difference exists between the two. But in reality, a difference between them truly exists. What type of error are you making?
mcqs.explanation: Type II errors are when an alternative hypothesis is rejected when it is true. In this scenario, the null hypothesis is that there is no difference and the alternative hypothesis is that there is a difference. We failed to reject the null hypothesis that says there is no difference, and so we are making a type II error. In other words, we have rejected the alternative hypothesis that there is an difference when it is true.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Power of a study is the ability of a test to _____
mcqs.explanation: The power of a study is its ability to avoid or decrease beta errors or type II errors. The s tatistical power of a test is represented by 1 – \021.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A randomised control trial is being conducted in patients with direct inguinal hernia, to compare the outcomes of a new surgery 'A' and the gold standard surgery 'B'. The p value of thi s trial is found to be 0.04. What can we conclude from this?

options.a: Type II error is small and we can accept the findings of the study
options.b: The probability of false negative conclusion that operation A is better than B is 4%
options.c: The power of the study to detect the difference between operation A and B is 96%
options.d: The probability of a false positive conclusion that operation A is better than B is 4%

mcqs.explanation: Since the p-value of the study is found to be 0.04, we can infer that the probability of a false positive conclusion that the operation A is better than B is 4%. In this scenario, the p value is 0.04 which makes it, by convention, statistically significant. We can reject the null hypothesis and accept the alternative hypothesis that operation A is better than854 operation B.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: You are an investigator conducting a statistical test. You obtain the p value as 0.01 for your study. What does this mean?

options.a: The probability of finding a significant difference is 1%
options.b: There is a 1% probability that the difference is not by chance
options.c: The difference is not significant 1% of times and significant 99% of times
options.d: The power of the test used is 99%

mcqs.explanation: If the p-value = 0.01, then the difference is not significant 1% of the time and significant 99% of the time. In other words, there is a 99% probability that the difference is not by chance and there is a 1% probability that the difference is only by chance.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a well-designed cancer study, similar remission rates were obtained for a new treatment (33.2%) and the usual treatment (32.2%), w ith the p-value being 0.04. Which of the following statements is true regarding the study?

options.a: Both the treatments are equally effective
options.b: Neither of the treatments is effective
options.c: The new treatment is more effective than the usual treatment
options.d: The information given is not adequate to compare the efficacy of the treatments

mcqs.explanation: As the p-value is 0.04, we can conclude that the new treatment is more effective than the usual treatment. Even though both treatments have similar rates of remission, a valid statistical test is required to determine t he difference in their effectiveness. Statistically , p-value < 0.05 implies that the alternate hypothesis is true. In this scenario, we can consider: • Null hypothesis: Both the treatments are equally effective (in other terms, there is no difference between the effect of the two treatments). • Alternative hypothesis: New treatment is more effective than the usual treatment. As the p-value is 0.04, which is statistically significant (<0.05), the null hypothesis i s rejected and the alternative hypothesis is accepted. Hence the new treatment is more effective than the usual treatment.855

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of these tests is used in case of a nominal data?
mcqs.explanation: 862 Chi-square test deals with nominal/ non-parametric data (qualitative). Nominal data is one with a name and does not have a numerical value. Ex blood group, gender, religion Student's t test, ANOVA, and paired t test are used for parametric data (quantitative).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true for non-parametric tests?

options.a: ANOVA is an example of a non parametric test
options.b: It is used for skewed distributions
options.c: It involves the assumption that the data has a normal distribution
options.d: It cannot be used for small sample sizes

mcqs.explanation: Non-parametric tests are tests that do not assume that the data is normally distributed. Thus, they are used for skewed (asymmetric) distributions {skewed either to the lesser side (left-sided skewed) or towar ds t he greater side (right-sided skewed)}. The chi-square test is an example of a non-parametric test that is used to test hypotheses in relation to nominal scale data or categorical data. ANOVA is an example of a parametric test.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of these terms is used for paired t tests?
mcqs.explanation: Paired t tests are also called correlated pairs t test, paired samples t test, or dependent samples t test.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The test of significance done for two or more proportions:
mcqs.explanation: Chi-Square(\0202) test is a test used for proportions and associations. It is a non-parametric (non-numeric) test and it is used to test hypotheses i n relation to nominal scale data or categorical data.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A researcher can use the chi-square test in all of the following situations, except:

options.a: To test the hypothesis that drug A has the same potency as drug B
options.b: To calculate the degree of freedom of a 3 x 4 contingency table
options.c: To compare the mean corpuscular volume in normal subjects versus those suffering from hereditary spherocytosis
options.d: To compare the proportions of overweight boys and girls in a class

mcqs.explanation: The Chi-square test is not used for comparing means for different groups as means can only be calculated for quantitative data. The Chi-square test is used for qualitative data. It can be used: • To test the null hypothesis • To compare proportions • To calculate the degree of freedom

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about the Chi-square test?

options.a: Tests the significance of difference between two proportions
options.b: Tells about the presence or absence of an association between two variables
options.c: Directly measures the strength of association
options.d: It is usually used for skewed data

mcqs.explanation: 863 A Chi-square test does not directly measure the strength of association. It merely tells about the presence or lack of association.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A Chi-square test would be most appropriate for testing which of the following hypotheses?

options.a: The mean AIPGE score of Chennai students is greater than Mumbai students
options.b: A smaller proportion of people who were immunized against chicken pox subsequently develop z oster than those who were not immunized
options.c: The mean BP of indian, american and english hypertensive men taking ACE inhibitors is the same as that of indian, american and english hypertensive women on ACEIs
options.d: The mean cost of treating a patient with CAD by angioplasty is greater than the mean cost of providing medical treatment

mcqs.explanation: The Chi-square test is used to compare proportions or qualitative variables e.g., whether people developed zoster or not. Options A and D: Two independent groups are being compared with quantitative variables (exam scores and cost, respectively). Thus, an unpaired t test will be used. Option C: The blood pressure of 3 groups are being compared, t hus making analysis of variance ( ANOVA) the most appropriate method of testing significance.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The test of choice to measure the difference in means between two groups in a study, with one group being a control is:
mcqs.explanation: The test of choice to measure the difference in means between two groups in a study, with one group being a control is unpaired T test.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A cardiologist wants to study the effect of the atorvastatin drug. She measures the initial cholesterol levels of 50 patients. After a month's treatment, she measures the cholesterol level again. Which of the following tests will she use to test the statistical significance of the change in the cholesterol level?
mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, the variable (cholesterol level) is quantitative. Moreover, the comparison is being done before and after the treatment (dependent). Hence, a paired t test will be used.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a particular trial, the association of lung c ancer with smoking is found to be 40% in one sample and 60% in another. What is the best test to compare the results?
mcqs.explanation: Chi-square tests are best used in comparing proportions and associations.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A pediatrician carried out a study to assess the difference in growth velocities in boys and girls. The average height of a group of 20 boys aged 10 years was 140 \261 13 cm and for 20 girls of the same age was 135 \261 7 cm. To test the statistical significance of the difference in height, which test would she use?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, two independent groups are being compared with quantitative variables. Thus, a student t test or unpaired t-test is used.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A clinical trial was done between two groups to measure their blood pressure after treatment. Which of the following tests would be appropriate to use?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, two groups are being compared independent of each other. Hence, students t test/ unpaired t test should be used.864 T tests are used if 2 groups are being compared. If the same group is compared before and after, paired T test is used. Otherwise, unpaired T test is used.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Analysis of variance test is used in which scenario among the following?

options.a: Comparing proportions in more than 2 groups
options.b: Comparing means in more than 2 groups
options.c: Comparing means in same groups before and after intervention
options.d: Comparing means in less than or equal to 2 grou ps

mcqs.explanation: Analysis of variance or ANOVA is used when more than 2 groups are compared for a quantitative difference (means).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A study was done to assess nutritional status among young children in rural and urban areas. 30 children in rural and 20 children in urban areas were malnourished. Which of the following tests of significance is the most appropriate in this case?
mcqs.explanation: The most appropriate test of significance, in this case, is the chi-square test. It is used to compare qualitative data between 2 groups with independent measures. Option B: Paired t-test compares paired data or p re-intervention and post-intervention data of the same group. This doesn't apply here as the groups are not paired. Option C: The standard error of the mean is calculated for quantitative data, with a measure of central tendency as mean. Option D: ANOVA is used to compare more than 2 groups.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A study was conducted to compare the incidence of postpartum depression in mothers as compared to the sex of the child. For assessment, Edinburg Depression scale d s core (EDSS) was used. The study was divided into mothers with male babies as one group to be compared with mothers with female babies. Which of the following statistical test will be used to determine the association?
mcqs.explanation: The Chi-square test is used to compare qualitative data and compares 2 groups with independent measures. The variables used here are yes/no signifying the presence/absence of postpartum d epression . Hence it is the most appropriate test here. Option A: Student's t-test is for quantitative data. Here the data is qualitative, hence it can't be used. Option B: Paired t-test compares paired data or pre-intervention and post-intervention data of the same group. This doesn't apply here as the groups are not paired. Option C: ANOVA is used to compare more than 2 groups.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate test for testing the statistical significance of the difference in heights of school children?
mcqs.explanation: Analysis of variance or ANOVA is used when more than 2 variable groups are compared. In the s cenario of comparing heights of school children, we would divide the school children into classes or grades or sections or by schools themselves, etc. This would involve comparing more than 2 groups and thus ANOVA is used. Remember if the question limits its comparison within 2 groups, for example, comparison between boys and girls in a class then we have to choose unpaired t test.865

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An investigator wants to study the association between maternal intake of iron supplements and the incidence of low birth weight. He collects relevant data from 100 pregnant women regarding the status of usage of iron supplements and the status of birth weight in their newborns. Which of the following tests will he use for his study?
mcqs.explanation: Here, two qualitative variables are being evaluated. First, whether the child belongs to the low birth weight category or not (and not the actual weight of the child, which is a quantitative value). Second, whether or not the mother took iron supplements in the gestational period. Hence, the chi-square test is used as the test the significance of the association.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a study, two groups of newborns are checked for differences in their birth weights based on whether mothers received supplements or not. Which of the following would be most appropriate test of significance?
mcqs.explanation: The unpaired t-test is used to test the difference between two groups of parametric variables or means when the s amples are independent of each other. Here , birth weights (quantitative variable) of the two groups of newborns are being compared, which are independent of each other.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A study was planned to find out the effect of iron supplementation during pregnancy on the birth weight of newborn children. Two groups, one with iron supplementation and the other without, were compared. Birth weights of newborns were recorded as means + SD. Which statistical test is appropriate for the comparison of birth weights between the two groups?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, we aim to compare only the birth weights of the two groups, which is a quantitative data, and thus an unpaired t test is most appropriate.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: While applying the Chi-square test to a contingency table of 4 r ows and 4 columns, what would the degree of freedom be in this case?
mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, df = (4 – 1) (4 – 1) = 9. In a Chi-square test for a contingency table, the degrees of freedom (df) = (r-1) (c-1), where r is the number of rows a nd c is the number of columns.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a Chi-square test for the following data, the degrees of freedom will be:
mcqs.explanation: In this scenario,contingency table has 3 rows and 4 columns. Hence, the degree of freedom, df = (3 – 1) (4 – 1) = 6. In a Chi-square test for a contingency table, the degrees of freedom (df) = (r-1) (c-1), where r is the number of rows and c is the number of columns.866

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A study is conducted to find the relationship between the height and weight of school students. Which of the following would be useful in this study?
mcqs.explanation: The coefficient of correlation can be used to determine the relationship between both variables in this scenario. It is used to express the strength and direction of the relationship between two variables. It is represented by the letter 'r'. Its value ranges from -1 to +1.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which among the following is false about correlation?

options.a: It indicates the strength of relationship between 2 variables
options.b: Correlation coefficient of 1 indicates a linear relationship

mcqs.explanation: A correlation between 2 variables only indicates the strength of the relationship between two variables, not causation. A correlation coefficient of 1 indicates a linear relationship. It cannot measure t he risk.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: During a study conducted to assess the effect of smoking on life expectancy, the correlation coefficient was found to be 0.60. Calculate the coefficient of determination for this study.
mcqs.explanation: The coefficient of determination (CD) for this study is 0.36 (36%). It is calculated by r2, where r is the correlation coefficient. In this study, the correlation coefficient (r) is 0.6. Hence CD = (0.6)2 = 0.36 The coefficient of determination refers to the percentage variability in one variable due to a change in the other variable. In the above study, a coefficient of determination of 0.36 means that 36% of the variation in life expectancy is accounted for by s moking.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the best way to study relationship between two variables?
mcqs.explanation: A scattergram/ scatter plot is the best way to study the relationship between 2 variables. The following image shows a scatter plot.874 The following image shows a forest plot.The following image shows a funnel plot.875 The following image shows a frequency polygon.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A psychiatry resident is conducting a study to assess the relationship between prefrontal blood flow under cognitive load and the severity of psychotic symptoms in schizophrenic patients. He calculates the correlation coefficient as -1.24. You can therefore conclude that:

options.a: Prefrontal blood flow is a good predictor of the severity of psychotic symptoms
options.b: Prefrontal blood flow accounts for most of the variance in symptoms
options.c: Schizophrenia c auses low prefrontal blood flow
options.d: The correlation coefficient has been calculated incorrectly

mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, the correlation coefficient (r) of -1.24 is incorrect, as 'r' can only lie between -1 to +1.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a random sample of 5000 corporate workers, the correlation coefficient of work satisfaction and life expectancy was found to be +0.7 with a p-value of 0.01. What is your interpretation?

options.a: Work satisfaction does not improve life expectancy
options.b: Strong statistically significant positive association between the variables
options.c: 70% people who enjoy work will live longer
options.d: 30% p eople w ho do not enjoy work will have a shorter life expectancy

mcqs.explanation: The above study is statistically significant (p-value = 0.01) and indicates a strong positive correlation (correlation coefficient = +0.7) between work satisfaction and life expectancy.876 Correlation is a measure of the statistical association of the variables, not a causal relationship. Here, the coefficient of determination (r2\ = 0.7 x 0.7 = 0.49. This means that 49% of the variation in life expectancy can be explained by satisfaction at work.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A group of cardiologists found a correlation coefficient of 0.90 (p-value = 0.01) between the systolic BP and serum cholesterol levels of patients attending their clinics. Which of the following statements is an incorrect interpretation of this study?

options.a: The magnitude of systolic BP and serum cholesterol levels are closely related
options.b: A patient with a high systolic BP is likely to have high serum cholesterol
options.c: A patient w ith a low systolic BP is likely to have low serum cholesterol
options.d: 80 % of the variation in BP can be explained by serum cholesterol and vice versa

mcqs.explanation: Correlation is an indicator of the strength and direction of the relationship between 2 variables, not the magnitude. The given study is statistically significant (p-value = 0.01) with a strong positive correlation ( r = +0.90) between systolic BP and cholesterol levels. Thus, it is likely that patients with high systolic BP will have high cholesterol levels and those with low BP will have low cholesterol levels. The coefficient of determination (r2)here is 0.9 x 0.9 = 0.81. This indicates that around 80% of the variation in systolic BP among the patients can be explained by serum cholesterol levels.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Among the given options, what can be the likely value of the coefficient of correlation between infant mortality rate and economic status?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options, the coefficient of correlation between infant mortality rate and economic status (r) is likely to be -0.8. It is known that low economic status is associated with a high infant mortality rate. This indicates a negative correlation. However, the infant mortality rate is also influenced by other factors, indicating a moderate correlation (not equal to 1). This makes -0.8 the most likely value of correlation.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: High salt intake in individuals is associated with high blood pressure. What type of correlation is this?
mcqs.explanation: An increase in blood pressure with salt intake is an example of a positive correlation. The association of decreased life expectancy w ith increased smoking is an example of negative correlation.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A scattergram was plotted as shown below to study the relationship between two variables. What is the correct inte rpretation?

options.a: There is correlation between both variables and the Pearson's coefficient is
options.b: There is correlation between both variables and the Pearson's coefficient is –
options.c: There is non-linear correlation between both variables
options.d: There is no association between both variables

mcqs.explanation: The given scattergram depicts a non-linear correlation between the two variables. Correlation expresses the strength and direction of the relationship between two variables in terms of a correlation coefficient. There are two types of correlation coefficients:Pearson coefficient Spearman coefficient Used for data withcontinuous intervals Used for data withdiscrete or deredintervals877 Pearson coefficient Spearman coefficient Used to findlinearrelationshi ps(e.g. salt intake vs blood pr essure ) Used to findlinearornon-linea rrelationships(e.g. socioecono mic status vs parity)

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What conclusion can be drawn from the following scattergram?

options.a: There is a perfect negative correlation between the two variables
options.b: There is a high positive correlation between the two variables
options.c: There is a high negative correlation between the two variables
options.d: There is a perfect positive correlation between the two variables

mcqs.explanation: The given scattergram shows a high negative correlation between the two variables.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: The value of one parameter can be estimated from another related parameter by:
mcqs.explanation: The value of one parameter can be estimated from another related parameter by using regression techniques.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: If correlation is given by the equation y = a + bx, what would be the nature o f the graph?
mcqs.explanation: The equation, y = a + bx indicates a straight line.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Look at the image below and select the linear regression equation corresponding to the graph.
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options, the equation y=11+2x corresponds to the linear regression equation of the form y=\023 + \021x. When 2 variables are correlated, such that the dependent variable is represented on the y-axis and the independent variable o n the x-axis, then the value of y can be obtained by using the linear regression equation y = \023 + \021x, where: y - dependent variable \023 - intercept \021 - slope of the line x - independent variable In the equation y=11+2x, the intercept(\023\ = 11, while the slope of the line (\021) = 2. Option A: y=10-x, represents an intercept of 10, and a slope of -1 indicating a negative correlation. However, the given image shows a positive correlation. Options B and D: They do not fit the linear regres sion e quation of the form y = \023 + \021x.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a study, the total cholesterol was calculated as a + b\037x\037 + b\037x\037 + b\037 x\037, where x\037 indicates calorie intake, x\037 indicates physical activity, and x\037 indicates body mass index. What is this an example of?
mcqs.explanation: 878 The given equation of y = a + b1x1 +b2x2 \205..bnxn is an example of multiple linear regression. In this equation: b1, b2\205..bn represent different regression coefficients x1, x2\205\205.xn represent the known variables

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: An epidemiologist has determined five independent factors influencing the outcome of a particular disease. Which of the following statistical methods can he use to compare these factors?
mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, the outcome to be determined (dependent variable) is the occurrence of the disease, which is categorical (qualitative) in nature. Logistic regression can be used when a categorical dependent variable is being compared with either a categoric al o r numerical independent variable. Linear regression is used when the outcome is numerical.Dependent variable (outco me) Independent variable(risk factors, exposure ) Qualitative (categorical ) Quantitative (numeric al) Qualitative (categorical ) Logistic regressionChi -squ are Linear regressionT-testA NOVA Quantitative (numerical) Logistic regression Linear regression

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What test is used to compare Kaplan-Meier survival curves?
mcqs.explanation: The Cox proportional hazards test is used to compare Kaplan-Meier survival curves. Survival analysis is used for analyzing the expected duration of time until one event occurs, such as death. The following methods are used for this are: • Life table analysis • Kaplan-Meier analysis - it involves calculating the survival function (the probability that a person will survive past a certain time) Life tables and survival functions are graphically represented in a Kaplan-Meier p lot or curve.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not used to compare survival curves?
mcqs.explanation: Fisher's exact test is not used to compare survival curves. The following tests are used to compare the survival curves or Kaplan-Meier curves: • Mantel-Haenszel test • Log-rank test879 • Cox regression or Cox proportional hazards analysis

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What is the Spearman coefficient used to determine?
mcqs.explanation: Spearman coefficient is used to determine correlation. It is used to find linear or non-linear relationships for data with discrete ordered intervals. Pearson correlation coefficient is used to find linear relationships for data with continuous intervals.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A researcher wants to compare a newly developed test for COVID with the gold standard test. Which of the following methods can he use?
mcqs.explanation: The Bland-Altmann analysis is used for comparing a newly developed test with another test, which usually is the gold standard. This method involves the graphical c onstruction of a Bland -Altmann plot which is used to compare the measurements from both methods.880

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Facets of Clinical Research and Biostatistics
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about simple random sampling?

options.a: It is the sampling method of choice for heterogenous population
options.b: Members are selected without specifying any criteria for selection
options.c: Every 5th or 10th member is picked at regular interval
options.d: Population is first divided into strata then sampled randomly

mcqs.explanation: In simple random sampling, samples are drawn in such a way that every element in a population has equal chances of being included. In other words, the members are selected without specifying any criteria for selection.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Facets of Clinical Research and Biostatistics
mcqs.question: A study on the prevalence of diabetes was conducted and the sampling method shown below was used. Identify the sampling method used.
mcqs.explanation: In this study, the population is separated into homogenous sub-groups and from these, random samples are drawn. This sampling method is called stratified random sampling.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Facets of Clinical Research and Biostatistics
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about cluster sampling?

options.a: Clusters are created based on similarities
options.b: It is a two stage sampling
options.c: It is cheaper than most other methods
options.d: It is a method used for rapid assessment

mcqs.explanation: In cluster sampling, the clusters are created randomly. On the contrary, in stratified random sampling , the strata or groups are created based on similarities.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Facets of Clinical Research and Biostatistics
mcqs.question: Which sampling method is used for assessing the immunization status of children under the immunization program?
mcqs.explanation: Cluster sampling is the method of sampling done in immunization programs for assessing the immunization status of children.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Facets of Clinical Research and Biostatistics
mcqs.question: A research is being conducted to assess the nutritional status o f the children in a particular district . For this purpose, 2 children are randomly selected from every school in the district. What is this type of sampling known as?
mcqs.explanation: In the cluster sampling technique, the sub-groups of the population/ clusters are naturally occurring. These clusters are randomly made rather than based on any particular characteristic. The population of children here is naturally divided into various schoo ls w ithout being based on any characteristics.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Facets of Clinical Research and Biostatistics
mcqs.question: In which of the following sampling techniques is design effect used?
mcqs.explanation: 890 The design effect is used in cluster sampling to allow for design structure and correlation between clusters. The design effect (DEFF) is used to decide the sample size needed for cluster sampling. This is done by calculating the difference in sampling variability to the variability expected with simple random sampling (SRS). It can more simply be stated as the actual sample size divided by the effective sample size (what you would expect if you were using SRS). For exampl e, l et's say you were using cluster sampling. A DEFF of 2 means the variance is twice as large as you would expect with SRS. It also means that if you used cluster sampling, you'd have to use twice the sample size.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Facets of Clinical Research and Biostatistics
mcqs.question: Simple random sampling is ideal for which of the following study groups?

options.a: A study being conducted on all vaccinated people of an area
options.b: A study on occupational exposure in all workers of the same factory
options.c: A study being conducted on prevalence of acute gastroenteritis in all school children of an area
options.d: A study on prevalence of hypertension in men aged 50-75 years in an area

mcqs.explanation: Simple random sampling is ideal for a homogeneous population as the sample would be completely representative of the population and it would eliminate the need for systematization or stratification. Here, workers of the same factory form a homogeneous population. Option A : For a vaccinated population - cluster sampling Options C and D: For a heterogeneous population - stratified sampling

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Facets of Clinical Research and Biostatistics
mcqs.question: In a study, first schools were sampled, then sections and finally students. What is this type of samplin g k nown as?
mcqs.explanation: Multistage sampling is the taking of samples in stages using smaller and smaller sampling units at each stage. It involves dividing the population into groups (or clusters). Then, one or more clusters are chosen at random and everyone within the chosen cluster is sampled. Snowball sampling is a type of non-random sampling preferred in case of diseases w ith social stigma (eg., alcoholism, iv drug abuse etc).

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Facets of Clinical Research and Biostatistics
mcqs.question: For an epidemiological study, sampling was done as shown below. What is this type of sampling known as?
mcqs.explanation: Systematic sampling involves a systematic pattern to sampling, like choosing every 3rd person from an area or hospital, etc.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Facets of Clinical Research and Biostatistics
mcqs.question: In a study, subjects were assigned according to the potential factor that will influence the outcome of the study. What is this type of sampling known as?
mcqs.explanation: In stratified random sampling, the population is first divided into homogeneous groups or strata. From these strata, random samples are drawn. For example: If a researcher wants to conduct a research study to determine if alcohol consumption is a risk factor for lung cancer. He must first s tratify the population into smokers and non-smokers because smoking is a known risk factor and also smoking is associated with891 alcohol consumption.

mcqs.question: Results of various studies carried out to study the role of smoking in breast cancer are plotted below. Identify the plot.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Facets of Clinical Research and Biostatistics
mcqs.question: A study was done to assess the risk factors for breast cancer in 100 females from urban cities. A statistical group and analysis are shown below. The values indicate the odds ratio and the 95% confidence interval. How many risk factors may be ascertained from the statistical analysis of the research?
mcqs.explanation: Among the factors shown in the above statistical group, the odds ratio of early menarche, BRCA mutation, and obesity show positive association and are statistically significant. Hence these 3 factors can be ascertained as risk factors. High socioeconomic status is not a risk factor. Even though there is a positive association, it is not statistically significant. Any association that has a 95% confidence interval range that includes the value of 1.0 is considered to b e n on-significant. The value of 1.0 in the range means that the two factors may co-exist together but one is not causing the other to happen. Odds ratio (OR) is the key parameter in case-control studies to assess the strength of association between the exposure and outcome. The interpretation of the odds ratio can be done as below: • OR > 1 indicates a positive association. If both upper and lower limits of the 95% confidence limits are also >1, it suggests that the odds ratio i s significant and the factor can be ascertained as a risk factor. • OR = 1indicates no association. Irrespective of the odds ratio, if the lower limit of 95% CI is <1 and the upper limit of 95% CI >1, the OR is non-significant and cannot be ascertained either as a protective or a risk factor. • OR < 1 indicates a negative association. If both upper and lower limits of the 95% confidence limits are also <1, it suggests that the odds ratio is significant and the factor ca n b e ascertained as a protective factor. Interpretation of the individual factors given in the question:Factor Odds ratio(95%confidence li mits) Interpretation Early menarche 1.3(1.2-1.9) Positive association, significa nt,risk factor Age <50 years 0.04 (0.01 -0.32 ) Negative association, signific ant, protective factor Smoking 0.5 (0.02 -0.9) Negative association, signific ant, protective factor BRCA mutation 1.9 (1.1-2.8) Positive association, significa nt,risk factor Alcohol 1.0 (0.8-1.8) No association, non-significa nt High socioeconomic status 1.4 (0.5-3.5) Positive association, non-sign ificant Obesity 1.24 (1.1-1.7) Positive association, significa nt,risk factor No family history of Ca. brea st 0.3 (0.01 -0.9) Negative association, signific ant, protective factor893

mcqs.question: Identify the following statistical plot.
mcqs.explanation: The image shown is that of a box-and-whisker plot. McNemar's test is a statistical test used on paired nominal data. It is used as a transmission disequilibrium test for detecting linkage disequilibrium.

mcqs.chapter: Facets of Clinical Research and Biostatistics
mcqs.question: What is Dixon's Q test used for?
mcqs.explanation: The Dixon's Q test is used for identification and rejection of outliers. It is usually used in normal distributions.

mcqs.question: Regarding the given box-whisker plot, the true statement is:
