Mixed -cellularity Hodgkin lymphoma is seen in patients older than 50 years of age . There is a male predominance. The image given below shows the histology of nodular sclerosis showing a lacunar variant of Reed –Sternberg cells489

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A lymph node biopsy specimen of a patient shows giant cells with an owl-eyed appearance . Which of the following statements is incorrect with respect to the diagnosis in this case?

options.a: Single axial group of lymph nodes is affected
options.b: Spleen is the first extranodal tissue to be involved

mcqs.explanation: An owl-eyed appearance of giant cells in lymph nodes is characteristic of Hodgkin's lymphoma (HL ). Mesenteric lymph nodes are infrequently involved in HL . Hodgkin's lymphoma is a group of lymphoid neoplasms arising in a single group of lymph nodes . Extranodal involvement is uncommon. However, if it spreads from the nodes , the first organ to be involved is the spleen , then the liver, and finally the bone marrow . This pattern of spread is known as the contiguous spread . This predictable route of spread is important clinically as it aids in staging and prognosis as well as treatment of HL .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Activation of which of the following is a common event in classical Hodgkin's lymphoma?
mcqs.explanation: Activation of the transcription factor NF-\032B is a common event in classical Hodgkin's lymphoma (HL ). NF-\032B may be activated by Epstein –Barr virus (EBV) infection . EBV+ tumor cells express latent membrane protein-1 (LMP-1) which upregulates NF-\032B. Activation of NF-\032B may occur in EBV tumors as a result of the acquired loss-of-function mutations in TNF alpha-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3 ). Activation of NF-\032B by EBV rescues crippled germinal center B cells that cannot express Igs from apoptosis , eventually leading to the formation of Reed –Sternberg cells .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Copy -number gains of which proto-oncogene on chromosome 2p are common in Hodgkin lymphoma?
mcqs.explanation: 490 Copy -number gains in the REL proto-oncogene on chromosome 2p are particularly common in Hodgkin's lymphoma. It may also contribute to increased NF-\023\036 activity. Reed -Sternberg cells are aneuploid and possess diverse clonal chromosomal aberrations. Note : the MYC gene , commonly associated with Burkitt lymphoma is present on chromosome 8.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: In which of the following lesions can we see the Reed -Sternberg-like cells ?
mcqs.explanation: Reed –Sternberg-like cells (RSLC ) can be seen in the following : • Infectious mononucleosis • Large-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas (most common in immunoblastic NHL) • Solid tissue cancers While Reed -Sternberg cells (RS cells ) are seen in Hodgkin's lymphoma, there can be presence of Reed -Sternberg like cells which that may have morphologic features resembling RS cells . Diagnostic Reed –Sternberg cells are large cells with multiple nuclei or a single nucleus with multiple nuclear lobes , each with a large inclusion-like nucleolus , about the size of a small lymphocyte with abundant cytoplasm (owl-eye appearance ). The image given below shows the classic Reed Sternberg cells .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a variant of the Reed -Sternberg cell ?
mcqs.explanation: Monomorphic is not a variant of RS cell . Reed –Sternberg cell (RS cell ) is the characteristic tumor giant cell of Hodgkin Lymphoma. It is derived from the germinal center B cell . It has a classic owl-eyed appearance due to the presence of a symmetric or mirror -image bilobed nucleus , with prominent nucleoli surrounded by a clear491 space . It has the following variants : • Lacunar • Classic • L&H Popcorn cells • Pleomorphic • Mononuclear RS cells should be present in a background of non-neoplastic inflammatory cells like lymphocytes , plasma cells, and eosinophils , to make a diagnosis of Hodgkin's lymphoma. The image given below shows the diagnostic Reed -Sternberg cell , with two nuclear lobes , large inclusion-like nucleoli , and abundant cytoplasm , surrounded by lymphocytes , macrophages, and an eosinophil .The image below shows Reed -Sternberg cell , mononuclear variant .492 The image below shows Reed -Sternberg cell , lacunar variant . This variant has a folded or multilobated nucleus and lies within an open space , which is an artefact created by disruption of the cytoplasm during tissue sectioning .The image below shows the Reed -Sternberg cell , lymphohistiocytic variant . Several such variants with multiple infolded nuclear membranes, small nucleoli , fine chromatin, and abundant pale cytoplasm are present .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A patient with generalized lymphadenopathy and Pel-Ebstein fever is diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma. Which of the following is a characteristic finding seen in this condition?

options.a: Pain in nodes relieved by alcohol
options.b: Pain in nodes aggravated by alcohol

mcqs.explanation: In the case of Hodgkin's Lymphoma, the pain in the lymph nodes aggravates following the intake of alcohol.493 Clinical features of HL : • Painless enlargement of lymph nodes is the most common presenting symptom . • Cyclical fever (Pel–Ebstein fever) - cyclical increase, which then decreases over an average period of one or two weeks and night sweats in disseminated disease . This cyclical fever may be due to the release of cytokines. A unique paraneoplastic syndrome associated with Hodgkin's lymphoma is the occurrence of pain in the affected lymph nodes during alcohol consumption. This has been attributed to the enlargement of the affected lymph nodes following alcohol consumption, which stretches the capsule of the lymph node and produces pain.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A lymph node biopsy sample of a patient showed Reed -Sternberg cells that were CD15 & CD30 negative . Which of the variants of Hodgkin lymphoma is the patient most likely to have?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with biopsy findings of CD15 and CD30 negative Reed –Sternberg cell is suggestive of nodular lymphocyte -predominant Hodgkin lymphoma. The Reed –Sternberg cells are positive for CD15 and CD30 for most subtypes , except in lymphocyte -predominant HL , in which the neoplastic cells stains for CD20 and BCL -6.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which subtype of Hodgkin's lymphoma has an incidence as shown in the graph given below ?
mcqs.explanation: The given graph shows a disease with a biphasic incidence which is characteristically seen in mixed cellularity type of Hodgkin lymphoma. It has a male predominance, biphasic incidence , peaking in young adults and again in adults older than 55 years. It has more systemic symptoms like night sweats and weight loss. There is diffuse involvement of the entire lymph node. It consists of a mixture of cells composed of T cells , eosinophils , plasma cells , and benign macrophages mixed with Reed –Sternberg cells . The mononuclear variant and diagnostic Reed –Sternberg cells are seen in this type . Reed –Sternberg cell is infected with Epstein –Barr virus in 70% of cases . It has very good prognosis. Image given below shows mononuclear variant of RS cell .494

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which subtype of Hodgkin's lymphoma is associated with older age , systemic symptoms , and advanced tumor stage ?
mcqs.explanation: Mixed -cellularity Hodgkin's lymphoma is associated with older age , systemic symptoms like night sweats and weight loss, and advanced tumor stage . It has a biphasic incidence peaking in young adults and again in adults more than 55 years of age . It also has a strong association with HIV . It is more common in males than females . Nonetheless , the overall prognosis is very good .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: The given histological findings were noted on a lymph node biopsy of a patient with lymphadenopathy. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a lacunar variant of Reed –Sternberg cell . These are common in the nodular sclerosis subtype of Hodgkin lymphoma. Subtypes of Hodgkin's lymphoma along with their characteristic types of RS cells is given below :Hodgkin lymphoma (subty pes ) Diagnostic cells in histology Immunophenotype Nodular sclerosis Lacunar variant CD 15+, CD 30 + Mixed cellularity Mononuclear and Diagnostic RS cells (70% EBV +) CD 15+, CD 30 + Lymphocyte Rich Mononuclear and Diagnostic RS cells (40% EBV +) CD 15+, CD 30 + Lymphocyte Depletion Reticular variant ; (most EBV +) CD 15+, CD 30 + Lymphocyte predominance Lymphocytic and histiocytic variant , popcorn cells (EBV -) CD 20 +, BCL6 +CD 15 -, CD 3 0 -495 The image given below shows nodular sclerosis type of HL with lacunar cells .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the nodular sclerosis variant of Hodgkin lymphoma?

options.a: Reed -Sternberg cells are positive for PAX
options.b: It is uncommonly associated with Epstein Barr Virus
options.d: Reed -Sternberg cells are positive for CD

mcqs.explanation: Reed –Sternberg cells in nodular sclerosis variant of Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) are negative for CD45. It is the most common variant . These are characterized by the presence of lacunar variant Reed –Sternberg cells and the deposition of collagen bands. These bands divide involved lymph nodes into circumscribed nodules . The Reed -Sternberg cells are found in a polymorphous background of T cells , eosinophils , plasma cells , and macrophages . Diagnostic Reed -Sternberg cells are often uncommon. The Reed –Sternberg cells are positive for PAX5 (a B-cell transcription factor), CD15, and CD30, and negative for other B-cell markers , T-cell markers , and CD45 (leukocyte common antigen). This subtype is uncommonly associated with Epstein –Barr virus (EBV). Involvement of the spleen , liver, bone marrow and other organs and tissues can occur later in the disease . The prognosis is excellent .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Lymph node biopsy of which of the following variants of Hodgkin lymphoma will show the maximum area of necrosis?
mcqs.explanation: The lymphocyte -depleted subtype of Hodgkin lymphoma is associated with maximum necrosis of the lymph nodes . Lymphocyte -depleted is the least common type (<5%). It is seen in older and HIV -infected individuals and can present with systemic symptoms . There is a paucity of lymphocytes and a496 relative abundance of Reed –Sternberg (RS) cells or their pleomorphic variants . RS cells are CD15+ and CD30+ RS cells are infected with Epstein –Barr virus (EBV) in 90% of the cases . It has a poor prognosis.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which subtype of Hodgkin's lymphoma is most commonly associated with HIV ?
mcqs.explanation: The Mixed cellularity subtype of Hodgkin's lymphoma (HL) is most commonly associated with HIV . Note : Although both mixed cellularity and lymphocyte depletion are seen in patients with HIV , mixed cellularity is more commonly associated with HIV .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 15-year-old male patient came to the OPD with cervical lymph node enlargement . The biopsy was examined, which showed a variant of the Reed -Sternberg cell given in the image. Which of the following types of Hodgkin's lymphoma frequently has this cell in its histology ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows the lymphohistiocytic variant (L&H) of Reed –Sternberg (RS) cell . It is seen frequently in lymphocyte -predominant Hodgkin's lymphoma. The cell has the following features : • Polypoid nuclei • Inconspicuous nucleoli • Moderately abundant cytoplasm As it resembles popcorn in its morphology it is also termed popcorn cell . Note : A unique paraneoplastic syndrome associated with Hodgkin's lymphoma is the occurrence of pain in the affected lymph nodes during alcohol consumption. This has been attributed to the enlargement of the affected lymph nodes following alcohol consumption, which stretches the capsule of the lymph node and produces pain.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A young male presented with cervical lymphadenopathy . The biopsy of the lymph node showed RS cells with vague nodule formation and a background of reactive T-lymphocytes. The cells were positive for CD20 , LCA , EMA and negative for CD 15 and CD30. What is the diagnosis?

options.c: T cell rich B cell lymphoma

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of nodular lymphocyte -predominant Hodgkin's lymphoma (NLPHL ). Axial group (cervical) lymphadenopathy and along with the L&H variant of Reed -Sternberg cells is characteristic. RS cells are neoplastic giant cells . In NLPHL , the cells have vague nodular formation. Immunophenotyping is positive for CD20 (B cell -associated ), LCA (CD45), EMA (epithelial marker ), and negative for CD15 (monocyte or macrophage-associated ) and CD30 (activation marker ). The image given below shows the L&H variant of RS cells seen in NLPHL .497

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: In a patient with lymphocyte -predominant Hodgkin lymphoma, cells are found to be positive for which of the following marker ?
mcqs.explanation: Nodular-lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin Lymphomas have Reed Sternberg cells (aka L&H CELL ) that are BCL -6 positive & CD 20 positive and CD 15 & CD 30 negative . Note : • CD30 is the most sensitive marker of Reed –Sternberg cell . • PAX5 is the most specific marker of Reed –Sternberg cell .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about lymphocyte -predominant Hodgkin's lymphoma?

options.a: It can progress to a tumor resembling DLBCL
options.c: The bone marrow involvement is rare
options.d: A strong association with EBV is seen

mcqs.explanation: Lymphocyte -predominant Hodgkin's lymphoma (HL) is not associated with Epstein –Barr virus (EBV) infection. In 3% to 5% of cases , this type transforms into a tumor resembling diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. A majority of patients are males, usually younger than 35 years of age , who typically present with cervical or axillary lymphadenopathy . Mediastinal and bone marrow involvement is rare. This form of HL is more likely to recur than the classical subtypes , but the prognosis is excellent .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old man is diagnosed to have Stage II (A) Hodgkin's lymphoma. What staging system was most likely used to classify the tumor of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Clinical staging of both Hodgkin and Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is done by Ann-Arbor classification. Option B: Masaoka staging is used for thymoma.498 Option C: Modified Durie–Salmon staging is used for multiple myeloma.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Who among the following patients is likely to have the best prognosis?

options.a: A patient with mononuclear variant of Reed -Sternberg cells on lymph node biopsy
options.b: A patient whose lymph node biopsy showed lacunar Reed -Sternberg cells
options.c: A patient with predominant reticular variant of Reed - Sternberg cells
options.d: A patient with Reed -Sternberg cells amid mixed variety of background cells

mcqs.explanation: The prognosis of the nodular sclerosis ( a subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma) is excellent compared to the other subtypes mentioned in the options. Lacunar Reed -Sternberg cells are seen in this condition. The nodular sclerosis type occurs with equal frequency in males and females . It has a propensity to involve the lower cervical, supraclavicular, and mediastinal lymph nodes of adolescents or young adults . Subtypes of Hodgkin's lymphoma along with their characteristic types of RS cells is given below : Nodular lymphocyte -predominant non-classical Hodgkin lymphoma also has an excellent prognosis.Hodgkin lymphoma (subty pes ) Diagnostic cells in histology Immunophenotype Nodular sclerosis Lacunar variant CD 15+, CD 30 + Mixed cellularity Mononuclear and Diagnostic RS cells (70% EBV +) CD 15+, CD 30 + Lymphocyte Rich Mononuclear and Diagnostic RS cells (40% EBV -) CD 15+, CD 30 + Lymphocyte Depletion Reticular variant ; (most EBV +) CD 15+, CD 30 + Lymphocyte predominance Lymphocytic and histiocytic variant , popcorn cells (EBV -) CD 20 +, BCL6 +CD 15 -, CD 3 0 -

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which among the following is incorrect about Hodgkin's lymphoma?

options.a: Histologic type is the most important prognostic variable.
options.b: The cure rate of patients with stages I and IIA is close to 90%.
options.c: Long-term survivors treated with radiotherapy had a much higher incidence of secondary malignancies.
options.d: It most commonly presents as painless lymphadenopathy .

mcqs.explanation: With current treatment protocols , the tumor stage is the most important prognostic variable, not histologic type . Hodgkin's Lymphoma most commonly presents as painless lymphadenopathy . The cure rate of patients with stages I and IIA are close to 90%. Long-term survivors treated with radiotherapy had a much higher incidence of certain malignancies, such as lung cancer, melanoma, and breast cancer.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of these parameters would be considered a poor prognostic factor in patients with Hodgkin's lymphoma?
mcqs.explanation: 499 Absolute lymphocyte count <600 cells /cumm is a poor prognostic factor for Hodgkin lymphoma. Poor prognostic factors for Hodgkin's lymphoma: • Age >45 years • Male gender • Haemoglobin <10.5 g/dl • Total WBC count >15000 cells /mm3 • Lymphocytopenia : absolute count <600/mm3 or lymphocytes <8% of leukocytes • Serum albumin level : <4g/dl • Stage IV500

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the areas in the histology of lymph nodes show small-unchallenged B cells surrounding pale-staining germinal centres ?
mcqs.explanation: The mantle zone of the lymph nodes shows small, unchallenged B cells surrounding pale -staining germinal centres . Structures in a follicle : • Germinal centre - round/oval zone containing pale -staining cells surrounded by darker cells . • Mantle zone - small, unchallenged B cells surrounding pale -staining germinal centres . • Marginal zone - Light zone surrounding follicles ; contains post -follicular memory B cells derived after stimulation of recirculating cells from T-cell-dependent antigen.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a B lymphocyte marker ?
mcqs.explanation: CD13 is an antigen of monocyte /macrophage and not B-cell .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding Non-Hodgkin lymphoma?

options.a: It involves multiple peripheral lymph nodes
options.b: Mesenteric nodes and Waldeyer ring are rarely involved

mcqs.explanation: Mesenteric nodes and Waldeyer ring are commonly involved in non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL).503

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which is the most common non-Hodgkin lymphoma in adults ?
mcqs.explanation: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL ) is the most common form of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) in adults and children over the age of 15 years, worldwide and in India. Burkitt's lymphoma is the most common NHL in children under the age of 15 years.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a B-cell neoplasm ?
mcqs.explanation: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma is a T-cell lymphoma.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common site for primary extranodal lymphoma?
mcqs.explanation: The most common site for primary extranodal lymphoma is the stomach. The term primary extranodal non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (PE-NHL) refers to lymphomas that present with the disease at any organ or tissue other than lymph nodes or spleen . Gastrointestinal lymphoma is the most common form of primary extranodal lymphoma, accounting for 30%–40% of cases . The most common site involved is the stomach (60%–75 % of cases ), followed by the small bowel , ileum , cecum , colon, and rectum. Note : The most common site for extranodal non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) in AIDS is Primary CNS lymphoma.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which lymphoid neoplasm is associated with the human herpesvirus 8?
mcqs.explanation: Primary effusion lymphoma is associated with human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8). It is a rare type of diffuse large B cell lymphoma with lymphomatous effusions in pleural , pericardial, and abdominal cavities, but no tumor mass. Only one body cavity is typically involved. It is strongly associated with HHV8 and advanced HIV and usually EBV. It can also occurs in non-immunosuppressed patients , often the elderly .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is correctly matched with its associated etiological factor?
mcqs.explanation: The correctly matched neoplasms with their associated etiological factor: • Extranodal marginal cell lymphoma - H.pylori infection (c) • Intestinal T-cell lymphomas - Gluten -sensitive enteropathy (d) • Anaplastic large cell lymphoma - Breast implants (b)504 • Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma - Hepatitis C infection (e) • Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma - HIV infection (a)505

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: The peripheral smear finding of a patient with fever and lymphadenopathy is shown below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The peripheral smear finding shows Downey cells or ballerina skirt cells . These are typically seen in infectious mononucleosis caused by Epstein -Barr virus (EBV) and cytomegalovirus (CMV).517 They are atypical lymphocytes with abundant basophilic cytoplasm containing clear vacuolations and prominent nucleoli . They become large as a result of antigen stimulation.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Bruton tyrosine kinase is involved in which type of B-cell lymphoma?
mcqs.explanation: Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) is associated with B-cell chronic lymphocytic lymphoma/ small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL /SLL ). Tumour cells in CLL rely on signals generated by the B-cell receptor for growth and survival . These signals are transduced by a cascade of kinases that include BTK. Note : BTK is also defective in patients with congenital X-linked agammaglobulinemia.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old man presents with easy fatigability , weight loss, and anorexia. On examination, he is found to have generalized lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly . Investigations show a total WBC count of 1 lakh per microliter, with 80% lymphocytes . Peripheral smear is as shown below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical presentation and peripheral smear findings point toward a diagnosis of chronic lymphocytic leukemia. The peripheral smear shows smudge cells and increased lymphocytes with scant cytoplasm , round to slightly irregular nuclei containing clumped chromatin. This large number of monotonous, uniform-looking, mature lymphocytes is often described as a "convent-girl" appearance .518 Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL ) / Small lymphocytic lymphoma(SLL ) is the most common leukemia among adults in the western world. The differentiating point between CLL and SLL is that in CLL the absolute lymphocyte count is >5000 per mm\263 and in SLL :<5000 per mm\263. It is usually asymptomatic at diagnosis but can present with easy fatigability , weight loss, and anorexia. Generalized lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly are usually seen . • Total blood count: • Total leukocyte count is highly variable ; leukopenia is seen when the marrow is involved. • Hypogammaglobulinemia is common and contributes to increased susceptibility to infections . • % to 15% of patients develop hemolytic anemia or thrombocytopenia due to autoantibodies made by nonneoplastic B cells . • Peripheral smear: • Predominantly shows small lymphocytes with scant cytoplasm • Smudge cells or basket cells or parachute cells - artifacts of the lymphocytes which are disrupted during the process of making smears. • Contains a large number of monotonous, uniform-looking, mature lymphocytes , which is often described as a convent-girl appearance . • Spherocytes (due to coexisting autoimmune hemolytic anemia) and nucleated RBCs (due to premature release of progenitors in face of severe anemia, marrow infiltration by the tumor, or both) • Lymph node biopsy : • Diffuse effacement composed of small lymphocytes admixed with variable numbers of larger activated lymphocytes that often gather in loose aggregates • Referred to as proliferation centers , which contain mitotically active cells . Proliferation centers are pathognomonic for CLL / SLL .519 The chromosomal defects : • Deletion of 13q (commonest and has a good prognosis) • Deletion of 11q • Trisomy 12q • Deletion of 17p (poor prognosis).

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: The neoplastic cells in chronic lymphocytic leukemia/ small lymphocytic lymphoma originate from which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: The cell of origin for chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL /SLL ) is either a post -germinal center memory B cell or a naive B cell . The cells of CLL show both unmutated Ig segments (those of naive B-cell origin) and somatic hypermutated Ig segments (those of post -germinal center memory B cell ). Tumours with unmutated Ig segments (those of naive B-cell origin) pursue a more aggressive course.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a genetic anomaly seen in patients with chronic lymphocytic lymphoma/ small lymphocytic lymphoma?
mcqs.explanation: Deletion of 17p is a genetic anomaly seen in chronic lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL )/ small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL ), not trisomy 17p. The genetic anomalies seen in CLL /SLL are: • Trisomy 12q • Deletion of 13q • Deletion of 17p (bad prognosis) • Deletion of 11q (bad prognosis)

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man presents with weakness and generalized lymphadenopathy . Lymph node biopsy shows difuse effacement with small lymphocytes and proliferation centers . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL /SLL ). Lymph node biopsy in CLL /SLL shows effacement of normal nodal architecture by sheets of predominantly small lymphocytes . They have round to slightly irregular nuclei , condensed chromatin, and scant cytoplasm . Admixed are a variable number of larger activated lymphocytes that often gather in loose aggregates referred to as proliferation centers . These contain mitotically active cells . When present , proliferation centers are pathognomic for CLL /SLL (also known as a pseudofollicular pattern).520 The image given below shows a lymph node biopsy of CLL in a low-power view. It shows loss of normal architecture and a large, pale -staining area in the center of the node (a proliferation center )521

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 58-year-old man with cervical lymphadenopathy is suspected to have chronic lymphocytic leukemia. What should be the absolute lymphocyte count/mm3 to diagnose this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The diagnostic requirement for chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is absolute lymphocyte count >5000 per cubic millimetre . Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL ) differ only in the degree of peripheral blood lymphocytosis : • CLL - 5000/mm3 • SLL - <5000 cells /mm3 Note : CLL is the most common leukemia of adults in the western world.522

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Flow cytometric analysis of four patients is given below . Who among the following is most likely suffering from chronic lymphocytic leukemia?
mcqs.explanation: Small lymphocytes of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)/ small lymphocytic leukemia (SLL) are CD23 and CD5 positive . Hence , the flow cytometry of patient 1 (CD23 and CD5 positive ) correctly represents the phenotype of CLL . The tumour cells also express the pan B-cell markers CD19 and CD20 Low-level expression of surface Ig (usually IgM or IgM and IgD) is also typical . Given below is the explanation of how to interpret flow cytometry results :Interpretation of results : Quadrant 1- Cells marked in green : -VE for A antigen, +VE for B antigen Quadrant 2- Cells marked in purple : -VE for both the antigens. Quadrant 3- Cells marked in yellow : +VE for both the antigens Quadrant 4- Cells marked in red: +VE for A antigen, -VE for B antigen

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 73-year-old man came with complaints of malaise and low-grade fever. He had generalized lymphadenopathy. The histopathological examination of the lymph node is as shown below . These cells showed positivity for CD5, CD19, CD20 , and CD23 . Which of the following does not indicate a poor prognosis in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and histopathological findings are suggestive of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL ). The presence of NOTCH1 mutation is associated with a poor prognosis in chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL). The histopathological image shows small, darker staining lymphocytes with prominent nucleoli which are typically seen in chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL).523 Variables that correlate with a worse outcome include : • The presence of deletions of 11q and 17p • Lack of somatic hypermutation • Expression of ZAP -70 • Presence of NOTCH 1 mutations

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged woman presented with chronic fatigue and generalized lymphadenopathy . Investigations revealed overexpression of BCL2 . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of follicular lymphoma. This condition is associated with overexpression of BCL2 . It usually presents in middle age as painless generalized lymphadenopathy . The involvement of extranodal sites is relatively uncommon. It has an indolent waxing and waning course . In almost 50% of patients , this cancer gets transformed to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The median survival rate is for 7-9 years. The cell of origin for follicular lymphoma is germinal centre B cells . It shows (14;18) translocation. Lymph node biopsy shows closely packed follicles . Centrocytes (small cells with the cleaved nucleus and scant cytoplasm ) and centroblasts (large cells with open nuclear chromatin and multiple nucleoli ) are seen . Bone marrow is involved in 85% of the cases and shows para-trabecular lymphoid aggregates .524

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following chromosomal abnormality is likely to be seen in patients with follicular lymphoma?
mcqs.explanation: Follicular lymphoma shows t(14;18). Its hallmark is a translocation that juxtaposes the IgH locus on chromosome 14 and the BCL2 locus on chromosome 18. It is seen in up to 90% of follicular lymphomas and leads to overexpression of BCL2 . BCL2 inhibits apoptosis and promotes the survival of follicular lymphoma cells .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man presents with painless generalized lymphadenopathy and weakness . Lymph node biopsy shows the following picture . Which of the following is not true for this condition?

options.d: Possible transformation into diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

mcqs.explanation: 525 The lymph biopsy shows closely packed back-to-back follicles of variable areas and very less inter-follicular area. It is suggestive of follicular lymphoma.Follicular lymphoma usually follows an indolent waxing and waning course , not an aggressive course. Lymph node (LN) biopsy shows a nodular pattern with centrocytes and centroblasts as shown below .526 Immunophenotyping : • The cell of origin is germinal-center B cell , so it is positive for CD19, CD20 , CD10, BCL6 , and surface Ig. • BCL2 expression is positive in over 90% of cases . Histologic transformation to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL ) occurs in 30 to 50% of cases . Note : In contrast to follicular lymphoma, DLBCL has an aggressive course , shows a diffuse pattern of growth in lymph node biopsy and shows BCL -6 positivity .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A patient with longstanding cervical lymphadenopathy was diagnosed with mantle cell lymphoma. What is the cell of origin for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Mantle -cell lymphoma arises from the mantle-zone B cells which are naive B cells as they lack somatic hypermutation IgH gene . Mantle -cell lymphomas have an (11 ;14) translocation involving the IgH locus on chromosome 14 and overexpression of cyclin D1. It is CD5 positive and CD23 negative . Comparison between mantle-cell lymphoma and chronic lymphocytic leukemia/ small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL / SLL ):Mantle cell lympho ma CLL /S LL CD5 Positive Positi ve CD23 Negative Positi ve CyclinD Positive Negat ive527 Mantle cell lympho ma CLL /S LL FMC7 Positive Negat ive CD10, B CL6 Negative Negat ive

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about mantle cell lymphoma is false ?

options.b: Most common presentation is painless lymphadenopathy
options.c: Associated with overexpression of cyclin D
options.d: Tumor cells are CD5 + and CD23 +

mcqs.explanation: The neoplastic cells in mantle cell lymphoma are CD5 positive and CD23 negative . Mantle cell lymphoma usually presents as painless lymphadenopathy . Centroblasts and proliferation centers are absent, differentiating it from chronic lymphocytic lymphoma. Immunophenotyping reveals the cells expressing cyclin D1, CD5, CD19, CD20 , surface Ig. CD23 is negative in these cells .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 53-year-old man was evaluated for painless lymphadenopathy . Biopsy showed a homogenous population of small lymphocytes with cleaved nuclear contours. Which translocation is seen in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture and pathological findings point toward the diagnosis of mantle cell lymphoma. The lymph node biopsy typically shows proliferation consisting of a homogenous population of small lymphocytes . The nuclei of these cells have irregular or deeply cleaved contours. Mantle cell lymphoma has(11 ;14) translocation involving the IgH locus on chromosome 14 and the cyclin D1 locus on chromosome 11 that leads to overexpression of cyclin D1. Option A: Follicular lymphoma has t(14:18), not t(18:14). Hence , it is not the answer.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A patient with cervical lymphadenopathy has t(11;14) positive . Which of the following markers should be done to confirm the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Translocation (11 ;14) is characteristic of mantle cell lymphoma. The markers to be done to confirm the diagnosis, are Sox11 and Cyclin D1. Mantle cell lymphoma is seen in the fifth and sixth decades of life and has a male predominance. It is characterised by painless lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly . In some cases , there is multifocal mucosal involvement of the small bowel and colon known as lymphomatoid polyposis . It has (11 ;14) translocation. Lymph node biopsy shows nodal tumour cells may surround reactive germinal centres . A homogeneous population of small lymphocytes with irregular to occasionally deeply cleft (cleaved ) nuclear contours is typically seen .528 Large cells resembling centroblasts and proliferation centres are absent, distinguishing mantle cell lymphoma from follicular lymphoma and CLL /SLL , respectively . Immunophenotyping is positive for cyclin D and SOX -11 . SOX11 variant that often presents with circulating disease with splenomegaly but without significant lymphadenopathy and with a low Ki67 index (<10%). Other markers include : • CD 5, CD19 and CD20 +ve • CD 23 -ve • Moderately high levels of surface Ig (usually IgM and IgD with \032 or \022 light chain) The IgH genes lack somatic hypermutation, supporting an origin from a naive B cell .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the immunohistochemistry marker for cyclinD1 negative mantle cell lymphoma?
mcqs.explanation: SOX11 is the marker used for cyclinD1 negative mantle cell lymphoma. Note : MYD88 is a marker for Waldenstorm macroglobulinemia.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about marginal zone lymphoma is false ?

options.a: They arise within tissues involved by chronic inflammatory disorders
options.b: They spread rapidly to other sites
options.c: They may regress if the inciting agent is eradicated
options.d: Transformation to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma may occur

mcqs.explanation: Marginal zone lymphoma does not spread rapidly to other sites . It remains localised for prolonged periods and spread systematically in the later course of the disease . They are B-cell tumours that arise within lymph nodes , spleen , or extranodal tissues . It is the most common primary extranodal lymphoma. They arise within tissues involved by chronic inflammatory disorders of autoimmune or infectious aetiology : • Salivary gland in Sj\366gren disease • Thyroid gland in Hashimoto thyroiditis • Stomach in Helicobacter gastritis They may regress if the inciting agent is eradicated . Antibiotic therapy directed against Helicobacter pylori leads to tumour regression. Translocations are associated with MALToma are t(11;18),t(14;18) and t(1;14). These translocations then upregulate BCL -10 /MALT1 , a protein that activates NF-kB and promotes the growth and survival of B-cells . They may invade epithelial structures to form lymphoepithelial lesions . Transformation to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma may occur.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A patient with long-standing Hashimoto's thyroiditis was noted to have a swelling in the thyroid region. After evaluation, it was diagnosed as a marginal zone lymphoma. What is the cell of origin of this lymphoma?
mcqs.explanation: 529 Marginal zone lymphomas are considered to be of memory B cell origin. In most cases , they show evidence of somatic hypermutation . The category of marginal zone lymphoma encompasses a heterogeneous group of B cell tumours that arise within lymph nodes , spleen , or extranodal tissues . They are often referred to as MALTomas .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A patient presents to you with rapidly growing swelling on her right cheek . Past history is significant for Sj\366gren syndrome. You suspect a lymphoid neoplasm in her. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Lymphomas arising in the setting of Sj\366gren syndrome in the salivary gland is marginal-zone lymphomas. They often arise in tissues involved by chronic inflammatory disorders of autoimmune or infectious aetiology such as: • Salivary gland in Sj\366gren syndrome • Thyroid gland in Hashimoto thyroiditis • Stomach in Helicobacter gastritis.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following translocations is seen in extra-nodal marginal-zone lymphoma?
mcqs.explanation: The translocation seen in marginal-zone lymphoma is t(11;18). Other translocations include t(14;18), t(1;14). Marginal-zone lymphoma begins as a polyclonal immune reaction. Signals from the antigen-stimulated T helper cells , drive the growth and survival of the clonal B-cells . At this stage , it is reversible, as in gastric MALToma after antibiotics against Helicobacter pylori. With time tumour cells may acquire mutations that render their growth and survival antigen-independent . Translocations such as t(11;18), t(14;18), or t(1;14) up-regulate the expression and function of BCL10 or MALT1 and promote the growth and survival of B cells . These translocations are relatively specific for extranodal marginal-zone lymphomas.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old woman came with complaints of chronic lethargy and weakness . Complete blood counts revealed pancytopenia . The peripheral smear showed the following picture. Which of the following statements is false about this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of hairy cell leukemia. It is a B-cell neoplasm and not a T-cell lymphoma. The peripheral smear shows leukemic cells with fine circumferential cytoplasmic hairy projections as shown below .530 Patients present with massive splenomegaly and pancytopenia . There is an increased incidence of atypical mycobacterial infections , possibly related to frequent unexplained monocytopenia . Activating point mutations in the serine/threonine kinase BRAF is seen in 90% of cases . Peripheral smear shows fine circumferential cytoplasmic hairy projections which are best recognized under the phase -contrast microscope . The bone marrow aspirate produces a dry tap. A trephine biopsy reveals infiltration by the cancer cells often in the pattern of a honeycomb appearance . Leukemic cells have nuclei surrounded by a cytoplasmic halo (fried egg appearance ). The neoplastic cells stain positive for tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP ). Markers for hairy cell leukemia include : • pan-B-cell markers - CD 19, CD2O • CD11c • CD25 • CD103 • annexin A1

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old man with a dragging sensation in his abdomen is found to have massive splenomegaly . The peripheral blood smear findings are as follows . Which of the following markers would you test to confirm the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical features and peripheral smear showing fine circumferential cytoplasmic hairy projections point towards the diagnosis of hairy cell leukaemia. It's a rare but distinctive neoplasm of the B cells where splenomegaly is often the only abnormal finding. Pancytopenia from marrow involvement and sequestration of cells in the enlarged spleen is seen in half the cases and infections are seen in one-third of the affected patients . CD103 must be tested among the markers to confirm hairy cell leukaemia. Hairy-cell leukaemias typically express the following markers :531 • Pan B-cell markers CD19, CD20 , surface Ig (usually IgG) • CD11c • CD25 • CD103 • Annexin A1. Annexin A1 is the most specific and sensitive marker .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A histological specimen of the spleen is shown below . Which non-Hodgkin's lymphoma does not arise from the area marked as 1?
mcqs.explanation: The area marked '1' in the image is the white pulp of the spleen . Hairy-cell leukemia does not arise from the white pulp , it involves only the red pulp of the spleen . The other condition involving the red pulp is hepato -splenic lymphoma. All the other non-Hodgkin lymphomas (NHLs) involve white pulp . Splenomegaly is the most common and often the only abnormal physical finding in hairy-cell leukemia. The spleen in this condition is described as a beefy red spleen . The image given below shows the normal histology of the spleen .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old woman presented with generalized itching and mild hypoaesthesia of the skin. On examination, maculopapular patches were seen on her back. Biopsy revealed the presence of atypical lymphocytes with cerebriform nuclei infiltrating the dermis and epidermis . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given pathological feature is characteristic of a Pautrier's microabscess. These are seen in mycosis fungoides . It is a mature, cutaneous , CD4+ T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Skin lesions include truncal scaling, red-brown patches , plaques , and fungating nodules . Lesions may evolve into a systemic lymphoma, with visceral and nodal spread .532 Sezary syndrome is a variant of mycosis fungoides . It is the leukemic seeding of blood by malignant T cells from the skin (CD4+). It presents with diffuse erythroderma and scaling. Histological hallmark includes : • S\351zary-Lutzner cells - cells with cerebriform nuclei (infolded /hyper -convoluted nuclear membrane). • Pautrier's microabscesses - tumor cells invade the epidermis as single cells and small clusters . • Epidermotropism - invasion of the tumor cells into the epidermis . The image shows sezary cells with cerebriform nuclei in the peripheral smear.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A patient presents with generalized exfoliative erythroderma. The peripheral blood smear shows the following cell . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a classical Sezary cell with cerebriform nuclei which points towards a diagnosis of Sezary syndrome. These are neoplastic T cells . Sezary syndrome and mycosis fungoides are different manifestations of tumors of CD4+ helper T cells that are home to the skin. Sezary syndrome is a variant presenting as generalized exfoliative erythroderma. It rarely goes into tumefaction and there is associated leukemia of Sezary cells . In Mycosis fungoides , only the epidermis and upper dermis are infiltrated by neoplastic T cells with the characteristic cerebriform appearance . In the later stages of the disease , progression occurs to lymph nodes and bone marrow . Tumour cells are not seen in blood. The disease progresses through the premycotic phase , plaque phase , and tumour phase .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: You suspect a lymphoid neoplasm in a patient who is a known case of rheumatoid arthritis. On workup, she has splenomegaly and her blood count showed neutropenia and lymphocytosis . Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: 533 A triad of rheumatoid arthritis, splenomegaly , and neutropenia is known as Felty 's syndrome. Some patients with Felty 's syndrome have large granular lymphocytic leukemia as an underlying cause . Large granular lymphocytic leukemia is a T-cell (CD3+) and NK-cell (CD56+) variant leukemia. They are associated with mutations in the transcription factor, STAT3 . Patients usually presents with mild to moderate lymphocytosis and splenomegaly . Neutropenia and anemia are also present . Lymphadenopathy and hepatomegaly are usually absent. There is an increased incidence of rheumatological disorders associated with this condition. The peripheral smear picture shows large lymphocytes with abundant blue cytoplasm and few azurophilic granules.534

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old boy presents with weight loss, fever, and a painless swelling in the area of his jaw. CBC reveals anaemia and lymphocytosis . Biopsy findings from the swelling are shown in the image below . Which of the following is not true about this patient 's condition?

options.a: All forms of this tumour are associated with translocations of the MYC gene
options.b: Endemic forms are latently infected with EBV
options.c: Tumor exhibits a high mitotic index
options.d: Neoplastic cells are usually BCL2 positive

mcqs.explanation: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings point to a diagnosis of Burkitt's lymphoma. Neoplastic cells in Burkitt's lymphoma are usually BCL2 negative . The biopsy image shows the classical finding of Burkitt's lymphoma called the starry sky appearance . Tumour cells show multiple small nucleoli , minimal cytoplasm and a high mitotic index. They are closely apposed to each other forming a dark blue background (sky). The macrophages get stuffed in between along with cellular debris. They are called tingible body macrophages . Upon fixation, the cytoplasm of these phagocytes washes away leaving behind white spaces filled with debris (the stars).Burkitt lymphoma is the most common NHL in children <15 years. Three distinct clinical forms of Burkitt's lymphoma are: • Endemic - affects children in Africa, affects jaw, maxilla, and is EBV-associated . • Sporadic- in adults in western countries . • Immunodeficiency associated - is associated with HIV infection .542 It is the most rapidly proliferating human tumor, Ki-67 stains for 100 % of cells (DLBCL - 40% staining with Ki-67). Histology shows the characteristic starry sky pattern. Immunophenotypic markers include : • Surface IgM type and immunoglobulin light chains (kappa > lambda) • B cell -associated antigens -CD19, CD20 , CD22 , CD79a • Germinal centre -associated markers - CD10 & BCL -6 • HLA -DR and CD43 • Expression of CD21 -the Epstein -Barr virus (EBV)/C3d receptor , is dependent on the EBV status of the tumors • Endemic BL : EBV (+), express CD21 • Non-endemic BL : EBV (--) and lack CD21 expression Treatment must begin within 48h of diagnosis in both children and adults with an intensive combination of chemotherapy regimens with high doses of cyclophosphamide and CNS prophylaxis .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 7-year-old boy who presented with the following finding was diagnosed with Burkitt's lymphoma. Which of the following translocations is most likely to be seen in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The translocation seen in Burkitt's lymphoma is t(8;14) causing translocation of the MYC gene . It is the most common translocation and is seen in 70% of the cases . Other translocations that may be present include t(2;8) and t(8;22).

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Translocations of which of the following proto-oncogenes is most likely present in patients with Burkitt lymphoma?
mcqs.explanation: All forms of Burkitt lymphoma are highly associated with translocations of the MYC gene on chromosome 8 that lead to increased MYC protein levels . In addition to the MYC translocations in Burkitt lymphoma and a subset of other B and T cell tumours, MYC is amplified in some breast, colon, lung, and many other carcinomas. The functionally identical NMYC and LMYC genes are also amplified in neuroblastomas and small-cell cancers of the lung, respectively .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the most common site for sporadic Burkitt's lymphoma?
mcqs.explanation: Sporadic Burkitt's lymphoma most often presents as a mass involving the ileocecum and peritoneum . About 15 to 20 % of these are associated with Epstein –Barr virus (EBV). Endemic Burkitt's lymphoma, in contrast, presents as a mass involving the mandible. It shows an unusual predilection for the involvement of abdominal viscera, particularly kidneys, ovaries and adrenal glands. Involvement of the bone marrow and peripheral blood is uncommon.543 Immunodeficiency -associated Burkitt's lymphoma commonly involves the gastrointestinal tract (GIT ) and central nervous system (CNS).

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which lymphoma has ki67 index near 100 %?
mcqs.explanation: Burkitt's lymphoma is a very aggressive tumour, having a very high mitotic index and a ki67 of about 100 %. ki67 is a proliferation marker used to assess the mitotic index of the tumour. It is high in high-grade tumours and low in low-grade tumours. Both mantle-cell lymphoma and DLBCL also have a high ki67, but it is not as high as that seen in Burkitt's. Follicular lymphoma is a low-grade tumour, and hence , it has a low ki67 index. The following are the images of Burkitt's lymphoma. • Image a - sheets of medium-sized cells with numerous tingible body macrophages showing the classic starry-sky pattern. • Image b - BCL 6 stain positivity in lymphoma cells . • Image c - the Ki-67 proliferation rate of virtually 100 %. • Image d - EBER (Ebstein -Barr encoding region) in situ hybridization with numerous positive cells .544

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old presented with fever and ulcerated tonsils. His peripheral smear showed lymphocytosis . The Monospot test was negative . Tonsillectomy was done, and the biopsy showed the following picture . The larger cells were positive for CD20 , EBVLMP1 , MUM1, and CD79a and negative for CD15. Background cells were positive for CD3. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Epstein -Barr virus (EBV) positive diffuse large-cell lymphoma (DLBCL ). The histopathological findings show large cells with multilobed irregular nuclei . These cells are positive for CD20 , CD79a, IRF4 /MUM1, EBVLMP1 . The smaller cells in the background are CD3+ which is a T-cell marker . It is seen in the elderly (>50 years) and without immunodeficiency or prior lymphoma. 70% of the cases are extranodal and mainly affect skin, lung, tonsil, and stomach with or without LN involvement. 30% of the cases have LN disease alone. Option A: This is not infectious mononucleosis as the monospot test is negative . Option B: It is not Hodgkin lymphoma because it is positive for CD20 and CD79a and negative for CD15. Option D: It is not EBV positive mucocutaneous ulcer as the patient is immunocompetent and it is strongly positive for CD20 . Note : EBV positive mucocutaneous ulcer occurs in immunocompromised patients and reverts to treating the immunocompromised state . It shows polymorphous infiltrate and atypical large B cells with RS cell -like morphology admixed abundant T cells . There is a uniform expression of CD30, MUM1, PAX5, OCT2 . There is variable expression of CD20 ,CD45, CD15, CD79a, BCL6 .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A lymph node biopsy of a patient suffering from follicular lymphoma shows the presence of large cells with prominent multilobulated nuclei and abundant basophilic cytoplasm . Which of the following will test positive in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given history and histopathological examination point towards the diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL ). It is molecularly heterogeneous and can show the given abnormalities: • BCL6 (transcription factor) overexpression is most common • 10 to 20 % cases have t(14;18) leading to overexpression of BCL2 (a proto-oncogene ) • 5% are associated with MYC translocations (like Burkitt's lymphoma) • Mutations in gene encoding histone acetyltransferases DLBCL and follicular lymphoma, both are positive for CD19, CD20 , CD10, and BCL6 (germinal-center B-cell origin). While BCL2 is positive in >90% of the cases of follicular lymphoma, it can also be positive in DLBCL . To differentiate DLBCL from follicular lymphoma, the ki67 index is used . If ki67 >40% (high) it suggests DLBCL .546

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: You have been asked to use the International prognostic index for lymphomas to predict the prognosis of a patient suffering from DLBCL . Which of the following is not the component of this index?

options.b: Number of extra lymphatic sites involved

mcqs.explanation: Hemoglobin levels are not a part of the International prognostic index (IPI ) score. IPI is based on the presence or absence of five adverse prognostic factors: • Age >60 years • Raised serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH ) • Performance status >2 (ECOG ) or <70 (Karnfosky) • >1 site of extranodal (extra lymphatic) involvement • Ann Arbor stage III or IV

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old woman, on treatment for chronic lymphocytic leukemia, notices rapidly growing swellings in her neck and axilla. She also complains of fever and weight loss. The physician suspects a transformation to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. What is this condition called ?
mcqs.explanation: The transformation of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)/ small lymphocytic leukemia (SLL) to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is called Richter syndrome. It is seen in approximately 5% to 10 % of the cases . Option B: Ch\351diak–Higashi syndrome is an autosomal-recessive disorder that arises from a mutation of a lysosomal trafficking regulator protein. It leads to a decrease in phagocytosis , recurrent pyogenic infections , albinism, and peripheral neuropathy . S\351zary syndrome (SS) is a triad of erythroderma, generalized lymphadenopathy , and the presence of clonally related neoplastic T cells . These cells have cerebriform nuclei (S\351zary cells ) and are seen in the skin, lymph nodes , and peripheral blood. Kostmann's syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by severe neutropenia . It is associated with mutations in G-CSF.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 58-year-old woman came with complaints of swelling in her hard palate . Biopsy from the swelling showed the following picture . What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and histopathological image point towards a diagnosis of anaplastic large cell lymphoma. The biopsy shows characteristic large anaplastic cells , some containing horseshoe -shaped nuclei and voluminous cytoplasm called hallmark cells .547 It is a type of T-cell lymphoma that consists of large lymphoid cells . This occurs due to rearrangements in the ALK gene and usually affects children and young adults . It frequently involves soft tissue and carries a good prognosis. T-cell lymphomas with similar morphology without ALK positivity occur in older adults and have a bad prognosis. CD markers : T cell markers (CD3, CD4, CD8 etc ) +, CD30+.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which is an aggressive lymphoid neoplasm that classically occurs in the oral cavity of immunosuppressed patients ?
mcqs.explanation: Plasmablastic lymphoma is an aggressive lymphoid neoplasm that classically occurs in the oral cavity in immunosuppressed patients . Plasmablastic lymphoma usually occurs in HIV + patients (73%), immunosuppressed or elderly patients without known immunodeficiency , and EBV+ patients . Lymphomas more specific to HIV + patients : • Primary effusion lymphoma • Plasmablastic lymphoma • Primary CNS lymphoma

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 44-year-old man with nasal obstruction, nasal secretion , and facial erythema was diagnosed with facial cellulitis. When his condition did not improve on antibiotics, a CT scan was performed . It showed a destructive mass in the right nasal cavity extending into the nasopharynx. Which of the following is most likely to present this way?
mcqs.explanation: Extranodal NK/T-Cell Lymphoma is most likely to present as a destructive nasopharyngeal mass. Less common sites of presentation include the testis and the skin. It accounts for 3% of all non-Hodgkin lymphomas (NHLs) in Asia. Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma is highly associated with EBV.548 The tumor cells typically surround and invade the small vessels leading to extensive ischemic necrosis. In touch preparations, large azurophilic granules are seen in the cytoplasm of the tumor cells . They express NK-cell markers (CD16, CD56) supporting an NK-cell origin. Most extranodal NK/T-cell lymphomas are highly aggressive neoplasms that respond well to radiation therapy but are resistant to chemotherapy .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 63-year-old man presented with severe pallor and giddiness . Clinical examination revealed bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy . Peripheral blood examination showed lymphocytosis and the following findings. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and peripheral smear findings showing cloverleaf cells , point towards a diagnosis of adult T-cell leukemia/ lymphoma. Adult T-cell leukemia/ lymphoma occurs in adults infected by human T-cell leukemia retrovirus type 1 (HTLV -1). Common findings include skin lesions , generalized lymphadenopathy , hepatosplenomegaly and hypercalcemia . Peripheral smear blood shows characteristic cloverleaf cells or flower cells which are tumour cells with multilobulated nuclei . Lymphocytosis is also observed. It is a rapidly progressive disease that is fatal within months to 1 year. The image given below shows peripheral blood smear findings in adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma.Note : Apart from adult T-cell leukemia, HTLV -1 may also give rise to progressive demyelinating disease of the CNS and spinal cord.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man presents with weight loss and abdominal pain. He is a known case of celiac disease on a strict gluten -free diet . CT of the abdomen revealed a thickened loop of small bowel with stricture and associated lymphadenopathy . A lymphoid neoplasm is suspected . What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The most probable diagnosis in this patient is enteropathy -associated T-cell lymphoma.549 Individuals with celiac disease have a higher than normal rate of malignancy. The most common cancer associated with celiac disease is enteropathy -associated T-cell lymphoma. It is an aggressive lymphoma of intraepithelial T lymphocytes . When the symptoms in a celiac disease patient deteriorate , even being on a strict gluten -free diet , cancer must be considered . Note : Small intestinal adenocarcinoma is also more frequent in individuals with celiac disease .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 56-year-old woman came with complaints of pain and swelling in the left side of the abdomen. Investigations revealed multiple polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon. A preliminary biopsy report was suggestive of a lymphoid neoplasm . Which of the following is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario points towards the diagnosis of lymphomatoid polyposis . The most common among the non-Hodgkin's lymphoma to present like this is mantle cell lymphoma. Lymphomatoid polyposis is characterized by multifocal mucosal involvement of the proliferating lymphocytes . It has aggressive behavior and a relatively poor prognosis. It must be treated accordingly as a high-grade lymphoma with systemic chemotherapy .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: BRAF V600E mutation is not seen in which of the following condition?
mcqs.explanation: BRAF V600E (valine to glutamate substitution at residue 600 ) mutation is not seen in glioblastoma multiforme . BRAF is a serine/threonine kinase positioned immediately downstream of RAS in the MAPK signalling cascade . It is seen in the following conditions: • Hairy cell leukaemia • Malignant melanoma • Langerhans cell histiocytosis • Papillary carcinoma thyroid • Pilocytic astrocytoma • Erdheim–Chester disease550

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: What is the normal ratio between kappa and lambda light chains?
mcqs.explanation: The normal ratio of kappa to lambda light chains is 60:40. In multiple myeloma, usually this ratio is skewed , i.e., favorable secretion of one type of light chain occurs at the expense of the other. Serum-free light chain assay is a recommended part of the initial diagnostic workup for multiple myeloma.562

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: Patients with which of the following can be classified under smoldering multiple myeloma?

options.a: Lack of symptoms and a high plasma M component with bone marrow plasma cells >10%
options.b: Plasma cells >10% in the bone marrow , no paraprotein in blood and presence of lytic bone lesions
options.c: Plasma cells >10% in bone marrow, abnormal serum free light chain ratio and hypercalcemia
options.d: Presence of symptoms and a low plasma M component with plasma cells <10%

mcqs.explanation: Smoldering multiple myeloma refers to an uncommon variant defined by a lack of symptoms and a high plasma M component . The difference between MGUS , smouldering multiple myeloma, and multiple myeloma is given below :MGUS Smouldering multiple Myelo ma Multiple Myeloma Asymptomatic Asymptomatic Symptomatic M protein in serum <3g/dL M-protein in serum:IgG \0303 g/ dL,IgA >1 g/dL M protein in serum and urin e Bone Marrow (BM) plasma c ells <10 % BM plasma cells 10 -60% BM plasma cells \03060% No other organ or tissue imp airment No other organ or tissue imp airment Related impairment is seen .( CRAB )

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: A 76-year-old man presents for a routine health check-up and is found to be mildly anemic. Physical examination reveals no abnormalities. Serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation demonstrates an IgG-kappa monoclonal protein with markedly reduced IgM and IgA levels . Bone marrow biopsy shows 12 % plasma cells . A skeletal survey reveals osteopenia and several punched -out lytic lesions , but no fractures. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of multiple myeloma. Plasma cell dyscrasias are B-cell proliferations that contain neoplastic plasma cells that secrete a monoclonal Ig or Ig fragment. Multiple myeloma is a malignant neoplasm of plasma cells characterized by the presence of monoclonal immunoglobulin or light chains in the serum and urine. It is a disease of older adults , with a peak age of incidence of 65 to 70 years. Signs and symptoms include : • Hypercalcemia • Pathologic fractures/ lytic bone lesions • Renal failure • Anemia Investigations reveal: • Radiography - Punched -out lytic lesions on X-ray • Electrophoresis - Monoclonal elevation of one immunoglobulin • Urinalysis - Free kappa and lambda light chains (Bence Jones proteins ) • Bone marrow biopsy - 10 to 20 %plasma cells (normal is < 5%) • Peripheral smear - Rouleaux formation. A high level of M proteins in myeloma causes red cells in the peripheral blood smears to stick to one another in linear arrays , a finding referred to as rouleaux formation.563 Plasma cell tumors are positive for CD138.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: What is the most common cytogenetic abnormality in multiple myeloma?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cytogenetic abnormality in multiple myeloma is translocation 14q . Cytogenetic abnormalities in multiple myeloma include : • Translocations involving IGH on chromosome 14q - most frequent • Monosomy or partial deletion of chromosome 13 (13q14 ) - Found by FISH (nearly half the cases ) • Translocation of the IgH occurs frequently with cyclin D1 on chromosome 11q and cyclin D3 on chromosome 6p • Deletions of chromosome 17p involving TP53 tumor-suppressor locus Translocations with cyclin D1 are associated with a good outcome , whereas deletion of 17p and t(4;14) portend an aggressive course .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: Which cytokine is an important growth factor for plasma cells in multiple myeloma?
mcqs.explanation: The proliferation and survival of plasma cells are dependent on several cytokines, most notably IL-6. It is an important growth factor for plasma cells . It is produced by the tumor cells themselves and by resident marrow stromal cells . IL6 , along with other cytokines, promotes osteoclastic activity and lytic bone lesions . High serum levels of IL -6 are seen in patients with active disease and are associated with a poor prognosis.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common monoclonal immunoglobulin seen in patients with myeloma?
mcqs.explanation: The most common monoclonal Ig (M protein) in myeloma is IgG (approximately 55 % of patients ), followed by IgA (approximately 25% of cases ). The immunosecretory disorders are a diverse group of diseases associated with the proliferation of an abnormal clone of immunoglobulin-synthesizing, terminally differentiated B cells . These disorders include : • Multiple myeloma (MM) and its variants • Plasmacytoma • Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia • Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance • Monoclonal Ig deposition diseases - Includes primary amyloidosis and nonamyloidotic types . The immunoglobulin can be complete or can be composed of either heavy or light chains and is termed M-(monoclonal) protein. Most myelomas are associated with more than 3 gm/dL of serum564 immunoglobulin. Myelomas expressing IgM, IgD, or IgE occur, but they are rare.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: In patients with multiple myeloma, lytic lesions are most commonly seen in which bone?
mcqs.explanation: Lytic bony lesions in myeloma patients are most commonly seen in the vertebrae. Multiple myeloma usually presents as destructive plasma cell tumors involving the axial skeleton . The bones most commonly affected (in descending order of frequency) are: • Vertebral column • Ribs • Skull • Pelvis • Femur • Clavicle • Scapula Pathologic fractures are common in this condition. The bone lesions appear radiographically as punched -out defects , usually 1 to 4 cm in diameter . The image given below shows osteoblastic lesions of vertebra in multiple myeloma.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: Which substance is responsible for the marked increase in bone resorption and hypercalcemia in patients with multiple myeloma?
mcqs.explanation: MIP1 \037 secreted by myeloma cells is responsible for the marked increase in bone resorption and hypercalcemia. Factors produced by neoplastic plasma cells mediate bone destruction , the major pathologic feature of multiple myeloma. Of particular importance, myeloma-derived macrophage565 inflammatory protein 1\037 (MIP1 \037) upregulates the expression of the receptor activator of NF-\032B ligand (RANKL) by bone marrow stromal cells , which in turn activates osteoclasts . Other factors released from tumor cells, such as modulators of the Wnt pathway , are potent inhibitors of osteoblast function. The net effect is a marked increase in bone resorption, which leads to hypercalcemia and pathological fractures. Serum alkaline phosphate levels are normal in multiple myeloma.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: A pathologist observed the following finding in a peripheral blood smear. In patients with which of the following conditions is this seen ?
mcqs.explanation: The given peripheral smear shows rouleaux formation. It is seen in patients with early HIV , SLE, and multiple myeloma.566 Conditions that cause rouleaux formation are: • Multiple myeloma • Connective tissue disorders like SLE • Early HIV • Infections Rouleaux formation is retarded by albumin.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: Which of the following is least likely to be seen in patients with multiple myeloma?
mcqs.explanation: Mooser bodies are seen in Typhus fever, not in multiple myeloma. Histopathological findings seen in multiple myeloma: • Dutcher bodies - pale -staining intranuclear inclusions within plasma cells containing Ig, which are more common in IgA myeloma (Image below ).567 • Russell bodies - Hyaline intracytoplasmic inclusions containing Ig • Mott cells / morula cells - Plasma cells containing multiple grape-like cytoplasmic inclusions comprised of Ig • Flame cells - Vermillion-staining, glycogen -rich IgA in cytoplasmic projections • Thesaurocytes - Dilated endoplasmic reticulum cisternae

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: The peripheral smear of a patient diagnosed with multiple myeloma is shown below . What does the marked structure contain?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a Mott cell which is a plasma cell with globular cytoplasmic inclusions containing immunoglobulins called Russell bodies . Inclusions containing Ig are frequently seen in the cytoplasm (Russell bodies ) or the nucleus (Dutcher bodies ) of some of the plasma cells in myeloma.568

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: The marked finding in plasma cells is due to:
mcqs.explanation: The marked finding is perinuclear hof (perinuclear clearing) in plasma cells . It occurs due to a prominent Golgi apparatus. Plasma cell characteristics include : • Eccentric nuclei • Moderate to abundant basophilic cytoplasm • Pale perinuclear hof, representing the Golgi zone The image given below shows plasma cells with perinuclear hof.569

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old male presented with a history of intractable diarrhea. Based on the histological image shown below which of the following is the most appropriate diagnosis:
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario points to the diagnosis of multiple myeloma. The image shows Russell bodies which are eosinophilic , large, homogeneous immunoglobulin-containing inclusions usually found in a plasma cell undergoing excessive synthesis of immunoglobulins. Russell bodies are distended endoplasmic reticulum . Globular inclusions are Russell bodies (if cytoplasmic ) and Dutcher bodies (if nuclear). The below image shows Russell bodies:

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: A patient with pallor and pathological fracture is diagnosed with multiple myeloma. Which of the following is not a kidney finding of such patients ?
mcqs.explanation: Wire-loop lesions are seen in systemic lupus erythematosus and not in multiple myeloma. Renal insufficiency occurs in half the patients with multiple myeloma and several factors are responsible for it. They develop acute kidney injury with ologuria and chronic kidney disease . Tubular casts, amyloidosis , and renal tubular necrosis are all described in the myeloma kidneys. Features of myeloma kidney: • Bence–Jones proteinuria and cast nephropathy - The main cause of renal dysfunction is related to Bence–Jones (light -chain) proteinuria. Ig light chains are directly toxic to epithelial cells . Bence-Jones proteins form large, histologically distinct tubular casts that obstruct the tubular lumens and induce a characteristic inflammatory reaction (light -chain cast nephropathy ). • Amyloidosis of AL type , formed from free light chains (usually of \022 type ) • Light-chain deposition disease - light chains (usually of \032 type ) deposit in the glomerular basement membrane and mesangium causing a glomerulopathy and in tubular basement membranes, which may cause tubulointerstitial nephritis.570 • Hypercalcemia - Nephrocalcinosis

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: What do Bence Jones proteins in the urine of multiple myeloma patients represent ?
mcqs.explanation: Bence Jones proteins are immunoglobulin light chains (paraproteins) produced by neoplastic plasma cells. They can be kappa (most of the time) or lambda. The light chains can be immunoglobulin fragments or single homogeneous immunoglobulins . In patients with plasma cell tumors, the level of free light chains is usually elevated . One of the light chains is elevated with a reduction in the other. Free light chains are excreted in the urine because they are small in size, where they are referred to as Bence Jones proteins . Tests for Bence Jones protein are: • Heat test • Urine protein electrophoresis • Immunofixation

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: Hyperviscosity symptoms in patients with multiple myeloma occur due to which of the following types of M protein?
mcqs.explanation: Symptoms related to hyperviscosity in multiple myeloma occurs due to excessive production of M proteins, usually of IgG3 or IgA subtype. Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia (IgM myeloma) is the most common cause for hyperviscosity syndrome due to excess IgM paraprotein. Less commonly, it also occurs in multiple myeloma (with myeloma proteins IgA and IgG3 types ) and connective tissue diseases . Normal relative serum viscosity ranges from 1.4 to 1.8 units. Symptoms are not seen at <4, and hyperviscosity syndrome typically requires a viscosity of >5 units. Clinical features include : • Visual impairment • Neurologic problems • Bleeding • Cryoglobulinemia

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: Multiple myeloma patients associated with which type of M protein has the highest risk of renal insufficiency ?
mcqs.explanation: IgD type of multiple myeloma has the highest risk of renal insufficiency . IgG is most commonly involved in multiple myeloma. The higher the level of IgG, the more is the risk of renal failure in patients with multiple myeloma overall. But the rarer IgD predominant multiple myeloma has the highest risk of renal insufficiency when compared to other types .571 IgD type multiple myeloma is a rare type of multiple myeloma. In this condition, there is monoclonal IgD in serum. On serum electrophoresis , there is no or absent M spike. There is a higher incidence of extramedullary involvement, amyloidosis , proteinuria, and renal insufficiency in comparison to IgG or IgA type multiple myeloma. It has a poor prognosis.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: Which of the following tumor markers is least likely to be positive in a patient with multiple myeloma ?
mcqs.explanation: Plasma-cell tumors are least likely to show positivity for CD 21 . They are positive for CD138, an adhesion molecule also known as syndecan -1, CD 38, and often express CD56.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not considered as a myeloma-defining event, according to the revised criteria for the diagnosis of multiple myeloma?

options.a: More than one focal lesionon MRI of 5 mm or more
options.b: 60% or more clonal plasma cells on bone marrow examination
options.d: Serum involved/uninvolved free light -chain ratio of 100 or greater

mcqs.explanation: Biopsy-proven plasmacytoma is not considered as a myeloma-defining event (MDE ). Revised International Myeloma Working Group criteria for the diagnosis of multiple myeloma: Clonal bone marrow plasma cells \03010 % (or) Biopsy-proven bony or extramedullary plasmacytoma . AND Myeloma defining events (one or more): Evidence of end-organ damage attributable to the underlying plasma cell proliferative disorder, specifically - • HyperCalcemia: Serum calcium level >1 mg/dL higher than the upper limit of normal or >11 mg/dL • Renal insufficiency : Creatinine clearance <40 mL /min or serum creatinine >2 mg/dL • Anemia: Hemoglobin level of >20 g/L (2gm/dl) below the lowest limit of normal , or Hb <10 g/dL • Bone lesions : One or more osteolytic lesions on skeletal radiography, computed tomography (CT), or positron emission tomography (PET)/CT. • Any one or more biomarkers of malignancy: Clonal bone marrow plasma cells \03060%; Serum involved/uninvolved free light -chain ratio \030 ; >1 focal lesion on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) that is \030 5 mm in size.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old lady presents with complaints of pallor, recurrent UTI, and bone pain in lower limbs. Peripheral smear shows rouleaux formation. X-ray done is given below . Which is the best immunohistochemical marker for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and X-ray showing lytic lesions on the bone are suggestive of multiple myeloma . The best immunohistochemical (IHC) marker for this condition is cyclin D1. Multiple myeloma is associated with diverse translocations involving the IgH locus ; overexpression of D cyclins —cyclin D1 and D3 . Plasma cell tumors are positive for CD138 and often express CD56.572

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: A patient diagnosed with multiple myeloma develops features of restrictive cardiomyopathy and macroglossia. Which of the following amyloid is responsible for this?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of amyloidosis . The amyloid of the AL type is produced from free Ig light chains secreted by a monoclonal population of plasma cells and its deposition is associated with multiple myeloma.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of death in patients with myeloma?
