This condition is caused by translocations of the TFE3 gene located on Xp11.2, which results in overexpression of the TFE3 transcription factor. It often occurs in young patients and is associated with a poor prognosis. The histological section of Xp11 translocation carcinoma is given below :840

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding renal cell carcinoma ?

options.a: It can invade the renal vein
options.c: It may arise from the proximal convoluted tubule

mcqs.explanation: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is more common among males, with a male to female ratio of 2:1. Renal cell carcinoma may arise from the proximal convoluted tubules (PCT). The classical clinical features of renal cell carcinoma are costovertebral pain, palpable mass, and painless hematuria. It characteristically invades the renal vein and has a high tendency for distant metastasis . Paraneoplastic manifestations of renal cell carcinoma include : • Polycythemia • Hypercalcemia • Hypertension • Hepatic dysfunction841 • Feminization or masculinization • Cushing syndrome • Eosinophilia • Leukemoid reactions • Amyloidosis

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common site of metastasis of renal cell carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common site of metastasis in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the lung (more than 50%). Common sites of metastasis of renal cell carcinoma in descending order are: • Lungs • Bones - osteolytic lesions • Regional lymph nodes • Liver • Adrenals • Brain

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following types of renal cell carcinoma has the worst prognosis?
mcqs.explanation: Collecting duct renal cell carcinoma has the worst prognosis of all renal cell carcinoma subtypes . The renal cell carcinoma subtypes with poor prognosis in descending order are • Collecting duct renal cell carcinoma • Medullary renal cell carcinoma • Clear cell renal cell carcinoma Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma has the best prognosis.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following genes is not mutated in familial renal cell carcinoma syndromes?
mcqs.explanation: WT gene is mutated in Wilms' tumor, not renal cell carcinoma . The following gene mutations are associated with familial renal cell carcinoma syndromes: • C-met proto-oncogene • Fumarate hydratase gene • BHD gene • VHL gene842 • TSC1 gene • PTEN gene

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly describes the immunohistochemical property of renal cell carcinoma in a cancer of unknown origin?
mcqs.explanation: Renal cell carcinoma is CK7 negative and CK20 negative . The most common subtype of renal cell carcinoma is clear-cell renal cell carcinoma , which is CK7 negative . Therefore, in determining the origin of cancer of unknown primary, immunohistochemistry (IHC) expression of renal cell carcinoma will generally be CK7 negative and CK20 negative . Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma and papillary renal cell carcinoma are positive for CK7 .843

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 36-year-old woman presented with intermittent suprapubic pain, increased urinary frequency, and dysuria for 2 months. A cystoscopy revealed the presence of Hunner ulcers. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Hunner ulcers are chronic mucosal ulcers that are characteristic of interstitial cystitis or chronic pelvic pain syndrome.847 It is a rare idiopathic condition that occurs most frequently in women. It presents with intermittent severe suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, urgency , hematuria, and dysuria. The following cystoscopic findings are seen in the bladder mucosa: • Fissures • Punctate hemorrhages (glomerulations) The microscopic findings include : • Mucosal ulceration covered by fibrin and necrotic material • Increased numbers of mucosal mast cells • Submucosal edema In later stages , transmural fibrosis may occur, leading to a contracted bladder . Biopsy must be done to rule out carcinoma in situ, which may clinically mimic interstitial cystitis . The following image shows a Hunner's ulcer in a patient with interstitial cystitis .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 31 -year-old man presented with a history of recurrent UTIs and hematuria. Urine culture showed growth of E. coli. Flexible cystoscopy revealed yellow -brown soft plaques with a central umbilication. Microscopy of the plaque showed Michaelis -Gutmann bodies . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario with the presence of Michaelis -Gutmann bodies is suggestive of malakoplakia. Malakoplakia is a chronic inflammatory reaction resulting from acquired defects in phagocyte function, commonly affecting the urinary bladder . It can also be seen in other organ systems like the gastrointestinal tract, female genital tract, and central nervous system . It is seen in chronic bacterial infection , mostly by Escherichia coli or occasionally Proteus species . Grossly, it presents as soft , yellow -brown, slightly raised mucosal plaques . Microscopically , the following findings are seen :848 • Large, foamy macrophages containing - • Abundant granular cytoplasm due to undigested bacterial products • Michaelis -Gutmann bodies - PAS-positive basophilic concretions due to iron and calcium deposits in lysosomes • Occasional multinucleated giant cells and lymphocytesNote : Xanthogranulomatous cystitis is morphologically and probably pathogenetically similar to malakoplakia, but it lacks Michaelis –Gutmann bodies .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of polypoid cystitis ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of polypoid cystitis is indwelling catheters . Polypoid cystitis is an inflammatory lesion resulting from mucosal irritation . It may also be associated with radiation therapy and malignant tumors. It usually involves the posterior wall of the bladder . Grossly, it may show bulbous or papillary appearance and may be confused with papillary urothelial carcinoma . Microscopically , the papillary projections are broad-based , non-branching, and without atypia. Stroma is edematous with minimal inflammation. Options A and D: Adenovirus infection and the use of anti-cancer drugs like cyclophosphamide cause hemorrhagic cystitis . Option B: Systemic allergic disorders cause eosinophilic cystitis .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A pathologist observed a metaplastic lesion in a biopsy sample taken from the bladder mucosa of a patient. Which of the following is not a differential diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: 849 Malakoplakia is not a metaplastic lesion of the bladder . It is a type of chronic granulomatous cystitis due to defective phagocytic function that may mimic malignancy. Metaplastic lesions of the bladder include the following : • Nests of urothelium (Brunn nests ) may grow downward into the lamina propria resulting in the following lesions - • Cystitis glandularis - epithelial cells in the center of the nest undergo metaplasia and take on a cuboidal or columnar appearance • Cystitis cystica - epithelial cells retract to produce cystic spaces lined by flattened urothelium • Squamous metaplasia - in response to injury, urothelium is replaced by stratified squamous epithelium . • Nephrogenic adenoma - due to implantation of shed renal tubular cells at sites of injured urothelium, resulting in replacement of urothelium by cuboidal epithelium with a papillary growth pattern

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the most common tumor of the urinary bladder ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common tumor of the urinary bladder is transitional cell carcinoma or urothelial carcinoma . Other epithelial tumors like squamous cell carcinoma , adenocarcinoma, and small cell carcinoma may also occur. Sarcomas are distinctly uncommon in the bladder . However, the most common sarcoma in infancy or childhood is embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, and the most common sarcoma in the bladder in adults is leiomyosarcoma.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 57 -year-old man presented with chronic hematuria and dysuria. Microscopic examination of urine showed the following parasitic eggs . What type of bladder carcinoma is commonly associated with this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows oval-shaped eggs with the terminal spine which is characteristic of Schistosoma haematobium. It is most commonly associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder . The ova are deposited in the bladder wall and incite a brisk chronic inflammatory response . This induces progressive mucosal squamous metaplasia and dysplasia and, in some instances, neoplasia . Schistosomal infection can less frequently result in adenocarcinoma or transitional cell carcinoma .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a carcinogen for bladder cancer?
mcqs.explanation: Isopropyl alcohol is not implicated in the causation of bladder cancer. Benzidine, arylamines, and phenacetin are well -established risk factors for bladder cancer.850

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following genetic changes is not associated with bladder carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: Activating mutation in HRAS (not NRAS) is responsible for bladder carcinoma . Genetic changes associated with carcinoma bladder : • Noninvasive low-grade papillary urothelial carcinoma is associated with: • Gain-of-function mutations of FGFR3 and HRAS genes • Chromosome 9p and 9q deletions • High-grade invasive urothelial carcinoma (either papillary or flat) is associated with: • Loss-of-function mutations of TP53 and RB genes Note : Erdafitinib (kinase inhibitor) is the first targeted drug therapy approved by the FDA for the treatment of metastatic urothelial carcinoma especially in patients with mutations of FGFR3 or FGFR2.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: The most consistent and persistent feature of bladder carcinoma is:
mcqs.explanation: The most consistent and persistent feature of carcinoma bladder is painless hematuria. Bladder tumors produce a wide range of clinical features including: • Painless hematuria - classical feature and may be the only clinical manifestation • Irritative urinary symptoms (frequency, urgency , dysuria) - diffuse tumors or tumors at the bladder neck • Pyelonephritis or hydronephrosis - when the ureteral orifice is involved • Obstructive symptoms , palpable suprapubic mass, or lower extremity edema - late presentation with a large tumor mass • Weight loss and/or localized bone pain - metastatic disease

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not included in the latest International Society of Urological Pathology grading of urothelial tumors?

options.b: Urothelial neoplasm of low malignant potential

mcqs.explanation: International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) grading system classifies papillary urothelial carcinoma into 2 grades - low grade and high grade. The classification of papillary urothelial carcinoma into grades 1, 2, 3 was was part of the earlier WHO classification . Grading of urothelial (transitional cell) tumors: WHO/ISUP grades : • Urothelial papilloma • Urothelial neoplasm of low malignant potential851 • Papillary urothelial carcinoma , low grade • Papillary urothelial carcinoma , high grade WHO grades (old classification ): • Urothelial papilloma • Urothelial neoplasm of low malignant potential • Papillary urothelial carcinoma , grade 1 • Papillary urothelial carcinoma , grade 2 • Papillary urothelial carcinoma , grade 3

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 67-year-old chronic smoker with gross painless hematuria was diagnosed with infiltrating urothelial carcinoma. What is the most important prognostic factor for his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The staging (extent of spread ) at the time of initial diagnosis is the most important prognostic factor in infiltrating urothelial carcinoma. The prognosis of bladder carcinoma depends on the histologic grade and the stage at diagnosis. As most infiltrating urothelial carcinomas are high-grade, staging becomes the major factor to determine the prognosis.852

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman presented with purulent vaginal discharge associated with fever, malaise, and inguinal pain. A Pap smear revealed the following findings. What is the causative agent ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image of Pap smear shows cells with ground glass nuclei , viral inclusions, multinucleation, and margination of chromatin. These findings are characteristic of herpes simplex infection .Some infections of the female genital tract and their diagnostic features are given below :Infections Diagnostic features Herpes simplex Ground glass nuclei with3M's: MultinucleationMargination of chromatinMolding of nucl ei Molluscum contagio sum Pearly dome-shaped papule c ontaining cells withcytoplas mic viral inclusions Trichomonas vagina lis Strawberry cervix; pear-shap ed flagellated organism. Gardnerella vaginali s Clue cells -squamous cells co vered with a shaggy coating c occobacilli Candida Pseudospores and filamentou s fungal hyphae

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What are the cystic remnants of mesonephric ducts in the cervix and vagina called ?
mcqs.explanation: Cystic remnants of mesonephric ducts in the cervix and vagina are termed Gartner duct cysts . The mesonephric (Wolffian) ducts normally regress in females . Its remnants may persist into adult life as epithelial inclusions adjacent to the ovaries, tubes , and uterus . In the cervix and863 vagina , these ducts may be cystic and are termed Gartner duct cysts . The following images show the embryological development of the mesonephric duct and its persistence into adult life .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: The following histological image depicts a pathology in which of the following sites ?
mcqs.explanation: The given histopathological image shows benign papillary projections covered with columnar secretory epithelium and underlying myoepithelial cells . These are commonly seen in papillary hidradenoma of the vulva .It presents as a sharply circumscribed nodule , most commonly on the labia majora or interlabial folds. Like the breast, the vulva also contains modified apocrine sweat glands. Its histologic appearance is identical to that of intraductal papilloma of the breast.864

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 3-year-old girl presents with a mass protruding from the anterior vaginal wall that appears like grape clusters. Histopathological examination reveals tadpole cells . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma (sarcoma botryoides ). It is an uncommon vaginal tumor composed of malignant embryonal rhabdomyoblasts . It is most frequently found in infants and in children < 5 years of age . They are locally invasive tumors that cause death by penetration into the peritoneal cavity or by obstruction of the urinary tract. Grossly, polypoid , rounded , bulky masses that appear like grape clusters can be seen . On microscopy , small tumor cells with oval nuclei , and small protrusions of cytoplasm from one end resembling a tennis racket (tadpole cells ) can be seen . Beneath the vaginal epithelium , the tumor cells are crowded in a cambium layer, in the dermis.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding precursor squamous epithelial lesions of the cervix?

options.a: LSIL progress directly to invasive carcinoma
options.b: LSILs are 10 times more common than HSILs
options.c: HPV -16 is the most common HPV type in both LSIL and HSIL
options.d: They progress to invasive carcinoma over many years

mcqs.explanation: Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL ) does not progress directly to invasive carcinoma . They initially progress to a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL), then invasive carcinoma . The WHO currently recommends a 2-tier system of classification for cervical lesions - low and high-grade intraepithelial lesions (LSIL and HSIL ). HPV -16 is the most common HPV type associated with both LSIL and HSIL LSILs are 10 times more common than HSILs . Most of these lesions regress spontaneously . Progression to invasive carcinoma is unpredictable and can take place over years.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the most common type of human papilloma virus causing cervical carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: Human papillomavirus (HPV )-16 is the most common type of HPV causing cervical carcinoma . It accounts for almost 60% of cervical cancer cases . The ability of HPV to act as a carcinogen depends on the viral proteins E6 and E7 . These proteins interfere with the activity of tumor-suppressor proteins that regulate cell growth and survival . • E6 - binds with p53 gene and promote its degradation • E7 - binds with RB gene and promotes its degradation

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A young woman comes to the gynecology OPD for cervical cancer screening . What is the staining technique used for this?
mcqs.explanation: Cervical cancer screening test , commonly known as Pap smear, is stained using the Papanicolaou method . The time for initiating Pap smear screening is 21 years, regardless of the age of first sexual intercourse .865 The sample is collected using Ayre's spatula and endocervical brush. 2 samples are taken: • 1st slide - prepared from a sample taken from portio vaginalis of the cervix • 2nd slide - prepared from the sample taken from the endocervix (transformation zone) 95% ethanol is used as a fixative. It is a highly specific test . Colposcopic examination and biopsy are recommended in case of abnormal Pap smear results .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about type I endometrial carcinoma ?

options.a: It is associated with obesity and diabetes
options.c: Smoking is a high risk factor
options.d: It is caused by unopposed estrogen stimulation

mcqs.explanation: Smoking is strongly associated with mucinous cystadenocarcinoma of the ovary , but not endometrial carcinoma . Endometrial carcinoma is the most common invasive cancer of the female genital tract. Type 1 endometrial carcinoma shows endometrioid morphology and is associated with: • Unopposed estrogen exposure (endometrial hyperplasia ) • Obesity • Diabetes mellitus • Hypertension PTEN tumor-suppressor gene is mutated in approximately 20 % of endometrial hyperplasias . Genomic sequencing of endometrial carcinoma has revealed 4 major molecular subtypes of endometrioid and serous carcinomas: • Ultramutated / POLE tumors - mutations in DNA polymerase \031 (POLE) • Hypermutated / MSI (microsatellite instability ) tumors - mutations involving mismatch repair genes • Copy number low/ MSS (microsatellite stable ) tumors - mutations involving the PI3K/AKT pathway • Copy number high/ serous -like tumors - TP53 mutations and numerous genomic copy number variants

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a criterion to distinguish leiomyosarcoma from leiomyoma?
mcqs.explanation: The size of the tumor is not a criterion to distinguish between leiomyosarcoma and leiomyoma. The following features are seen in leiomyosarcomas: • Mitotic index - \03010 mitoses / 10 hpf • Nuclear atypia - in the presence of nuclear atypia, 5 mitoses / 10 hpf • Tumor cell necrosis - • Characterized by an abrupt transition from viable to non-viable areas866 • Within the necrotic zones, atypical cells can be seen

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Histopathological examination of an ovarian mass sent to the pathology department revealed the following . Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.a: It is more common in women with low parity
options.b: The pathogenesis is related to family history and heritable mutations
options.c: High-grade tumors are associated with TP53 mutations

mcqs.explanation: The given image denotes Psammoma bodies which are a histopathological finding seen in ovarian papillary serous cystadenoma and cystadenocarcinoma. These tumors are most commonly bilateral.The majority of serous tumors of the ovary are benign or borderline. But the serous carcinomas of the ovary include the most common malignant tumors of the ovary . Nulliparity , family history, and heritable mutations play a role in the development of these tumors. Mutations in the oncogenes KRAS, BRAF , or ERBB2 result in low-grade tumors, and mutation in TP53 is associated with high-grade tumors.867 There is a higher frequency of carcinoma in women with low parity. Women on oral contraceptive pills or those who have undergone tubal ligation are at a lower risk . The marker for ovarian tumors is CA-125.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding mucinous tumors of the ovary ?

options.c: It occurs principally in middle adult life
options.d: Mutation of the KRAS proto-oncogene is seen

mcqs.explanation: The vast majority of mucinous tumors of the ovary are benign or borderline tumors (not malignant). It occurs principally in middle adult life and is rare before puberty and after menopause . The surface of the ovary is rarely involved, they are rarely bilateral. It is associated with the mutation of KRAS proto-oncogene . Grossly it is multiloculated and filled with sticky, gelatinous fluid (rich in glycoproteins ).

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman underwent an evaluation for an abdominal mass. A laparotomy was decided upon for the removal of the mass. The gross appearance of the mass is as follows . Histopathological examination revealed no malignant change. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and image showing unilocular cystic space containing hair and sebaceous material are suggestive of mature teratoma.868 Dermoid cysts or mature teratomas are benign tumors, usually found in young women during the active reproductive years. It is bilateral in 10 % to 15% of cases . Microscopically , the cyst wall is composed of tissues from all 3 germ layers. This includes stratified squamous epithelium , with underlying sebaceous glands, hair shafts , and other skin adnexal structures . Sometimes cartilage , bone, thyroid, and neural tissue can be seen . About 1% of the dermoids undergo malignant transformation , most commonly to squamous cell carcinoma . It can also transform into other cancers (e.g., thyroid carcinoma , melanoma).869 The component tissue of immature malignant teratomas resembles embryonal and immature fetal tissue . It often consists of primitive neuroepithelial cells . The tumor is found chiefly in prepubertal adolescents and young women, the mean age being 18 years. Monodermal or specialized teratomas: • Struma ovarii - composed entirely of mature thyroid tissue , which may be functional and cause hyperthyroidism. • Ovarian carcinoid - arises from intestinal tissue , may be functional causing carcinoid syndrome in the absence of hepatic metastasis

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman presented to the gynecology OPD with a history of abdominal pain and distension of abdomen. Ultrasound imaging revealed tumor in the right ovary . Serum level of inhibin was raised. The histopathology of the tumor is given below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and histopathology showing Call-Exner bodies are suggestive of granulosa cell tumor. Call-Exner bodies are small, distinctive , glandlike structures filled with an acidophilic material resembling immature follicles . Additionally , small, cuboidal to polygonal cells are seen which may grow in anastomosing cords, sheets , or strands.870 Granulosa cell tumors are composed of cells that resemble granulosa cells of a developing ovarian follicle . It can be of adult and juvenile types . Elevated tissue and serum levels of inhibin, a product of granulosa cells , are associated with this tumor. Mutations of the FOXL2 gene are seen in most adult granulosa cell tumors.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 12 -year-old girl, who is yet to attain her menarche, presents with an ovarian mass. Her serum biomarkers are normal except for elevated AFP. Staging laparotomy was performed and the histopathological image is given below . What is your diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical features and the histopathological image showing Schiller Duval bodies are suggestive of endodermal sinus tumors. It is also known as yolk sac tumor. The Schiller-Duval body is a glomerulus -like structure composed of a central blood vessel enveloped by tumor cells within a space that is also lined by tumor cells .871 It is the second most common malignant tumor of germ cell origin. It is a unilateral tumor usually affecting children or young women.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following are sex cord-stromal tumors?
mcqs.explanation: Sex cord-stromal tumors include the following : • Granulosa cell tumor • Sertoli cell tumor • Fibroma Brenner tumor is an epithelial tumor and dysgerminoma is a germ cell tumor.872

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old woman presented with bilateral adnexal masses . Histopathological examination of the resected specimen showed sheets of mucin-producing signet -ring cells . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and histopathology findings are suggestive of metastatic carcinoma of the ovary or Krukenberg tumor. It can arise from primary carcinomas of the stomach (most common), colon, appendix , and breast (invasive lobular carcinoma ). It is often bilateral and on microscopy shows mucin-laden signet -ring cells with eccentric hyperchromatic nuclei .Metastatic tumors of the ovary include: • Tumors of M\374llerian origin (most common) - the uterus , fallopian tube , contralateral ovary , or pelvic peritoneum • Tumors of extra-M\374llerian tumors - breast and gastrointestinal tract carcinomas • Pseudomyxoma peritonei - derived from appendiceal tumors • Krukenberg tumor873

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old woman was diagnosed with molar pregnancy and underwent suction and evacuation. The resected specimen is shown below . Histopathological examination revealed thin-walled , cystic structures consisting of hydropic villi with extensive trophoblastic proliferation along its entire circumference . Immunohistochemistry was negative for p57 . Which of the following is false about this condition?

options.a: The genetic material is completely maternally derived
options.b: Embryo dies very early in development and therefore is usually not identified
options.c: It is associated with a 2.5% risk of subsequent choriocarcinoma

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and image showing grapelike vesicles are suggestive of a complete mole . It results from the fertilization of an egg that has lost its female chromosomes, and as a result , the genetic material is completely paternally derived.The pathogenesis of complete mole is as follows : • Androgenesis (most common) - 46XX karyotype stemming from the duplication of the genetic material of 1 sperm • Dispermy - 46XX or 46XY karyotype due to fertilization of an empty egg by 2 sperms Microscopically , thin-walled , cystic , grapelike structures consisting of hydropic villi are seen . Trophoblastic proliferation involving the entire circumference of the villi is seen .874 The embryo dies very early in development and, therefore , is usually not identified . Patients have a 2.5% risk of subsequent choriocarcinoma and a 15% risk of the persistent or invasive mole. The following image shows the pathogenesis of molar pregnancy.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old woman with a positive pregnancy test presented with vaginal bleeding in the first trimester. On examination, grape-like vesicles were noted in the vagina . A transvaginal ultrasound revealed the presence of fetal tissues . A suction evacuation was performed . What is the most likely karyotype of the evacuated material?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with grape-like vesicles in the vagina and the presence of fetal tissues on transvaginal ultrasound are suggestive of partial mole. The karyotype in a partial mole is triploid (e.g., 69XXY ) or occasionally tetraploid (92XXXY ). It results from the fertilization of an egg with 2 sperms. There is an increased risk of persistent molar disease but it is not associated with choriocarcinoma . Given below is an image showing the karyotype of molar pregnancy.875

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the most common site of metastasis in gestational choriocarcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: Lungs are the most common site of metastasis in gestational choriocarcinoma . It is followed by the vagina , brain , liver, bone, and kidney in descending order of frequency. Gestational choriocarcinomas are malignant neoplasm of trophoblastic cells derived from a previously normal or abnormal pregnancy, such as an extrauterine ectopic pregnancy. The hCG levels are elevated to levels above those encountered in hydatidiform moles . It shows hematogenous spread . It is rapidly invasive and metastasizes widely . Gestational choriocarcinomas are chemosensitive whereas non-gestational choriocarcinomas are chemoresistant .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: The genetic profile of malignant mixed M\374llerian tumors resembles that of:
mcqs.explanation: Malignant mixed M\374llerian tumors (MMMTs) are carcinosarcomas whose genetic profile closely resembles endometrial carcinomas. They involve mutations in the same genes - PTEN, TP53, and PIK3CA. The usual genetic alterations found in sarcomas are absent in MMMTs. MMMTs are endometrial adenocarcinomas with malignant mesenchymal components . The mesenchymal component may resemble uterine mesenchymal elements (stromal sarcoma, leiomyosarcoma) or contain heterologous malignant cell types (striated muscle , cartilage , adipose tissue , and bone). It occurs in postmenopausal women and presents with bleeding . It is associated with a poor outcome .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following are the components of Meig 's syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Meigs ' syndrome triad includes the following : • Solid benign ovarian tumor (fibroma) • Right-sided hydrothorax • Ascites - disappears after the removal of the tumor Pseudo -Meigs ' syndrome is characterized by the following : • Non-malignant ascites • Pleural effusion • Pelvic tumors - other than solid benign ovarian tumors Note : Ovarian fibroma is also associated with nevoid basal cell carcinoma . This association is known as Gorlin syndrome.876

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old woman was operated for an ovarian mass and the sample was sent for histopathological examination. The findings are given below . Which of the following is false about the given condition?

options.b: It expresses OCT-3, OCT4, and NANOG
options.d: It occurs in patients with gonadal dysgenesis

mcqs.explanation: The given histopathological image shows large cells with clear cytoplasm (fried egg appearance ), tumor cells arranged in sheets , and cords of fibrous stroma infiltrated by lymphocytes . These findings are suggestive of dysgerminoma. It is highly responsive to radiotherapy.Dysgerminomas are the ovarian counterparts of testicular seminoma. They may occur in childhood , but most commonly occur in the 2-3rd decades . It may occur in patients with gonadal dysgenesis , including pseudohermaphroditism. The majority of these tumors are unilateral. They express OCT-3, OCT4, and NANOG. All dysgerminomas are malignant, but the degree of histologic atypia is variable. Only about one-third of these lesions are aggressive. These neoplasms are responsive to chemoradiation, and overall survival exceeds 80%.877

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A young sexually active man presented with multiple polypoid growths over his penis . Histopathological image of an excised lesion is as shown below . What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given histopathological image showing papillary (villous) architecture with acanthosis, hyperkeratosis and koilocytosis of squamous epithelium , are characteristic findings of condyloma acuminatum. Koilocytes have a prominent cell membrane, hyperchromatic resinoid nucleus , and perinuclear halo.888 Grossly, they consist of single or multiple sessile or pedunculated , red papillary excrescences on the coronal sulcus , and the inner surface of the prepuce . Option A: Condyloma lata is a maculopapular/nodular lesion seen in secondary syphilis . Option B: Bowen's disease is carcinoma in situ of the penis characterized by the hyperproliferative epidermis and dysplastic epithelium . Option D: Verrucous carcinoma / very well -differentiated squamous cell carcinoma , shows hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and keratin pearls.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: All of the following are true regarding Bowen's disease except :

options.b: Marked dysplasia and hyperproliferative epidermis are seen
options.d: Virtually never develops into an invasive carcinoma

mcqs.explanation: Bowen's disease starts as a premalignant lesion and transforms into infiltrating squamous cell carcinoma in approximately 10 % of patients , usually over a span of many years. Bowen's disease occurs in the genital region of both men and women, usually in those older than age 35 years. These lesions have a strong association with infection by high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV ), most commonly type 16. Grossly, it appears as a solitary, thickened , gray-white , and opaque plaque. The below histological image of Bowen's disease shows dysplastic cells with large hyperchromatic nuclei , koilocytic atypia and an intact basement membrane.889 Premalignant lesions of invasive penile SCC: • Erythroplasia of Queyrat • Condyloma acuminatum • Bowen's disease Bowenoid papulosis occurs in young , sexually active adults . It presents as multiple reddish -brown papular lesions and it is histologically indistinguishable from Bowen's disease , but virtually never develops into invasive carcinoma .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: The biopsy of a resected inguinal mass from a patient shows marked fibrotic changes with prominent Leydig cells and hypoplastic Sertoli cells . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given histopathological features are strongly suggestive of cryptorchidism. Cryptorchidism is histopathologically characterized by the following : • Testicular atrophy: thickening of the basement membrane, arrested germ cell development , marked hyalinization • Tubules showing Sertoli cells but no spermatogenesis • Increase in the interstitial Leydig cells. Cryptorchidism is the failure of the descent of the intra-abdominal testes into the scrotal sac. It is the most common congenital abnormality of the genitourinary tract. The testes can arrest anywhere during descent , and the most common site is the inguinal region. Phases of testicular descent : • Transabdominal phase : Testes come to lie in the lower abdomen or pelvis. This phase of descent is regulated by Mullerian-inhibiting substances . • Inguinoscrotal phase : Testes descend along the inguinal canal and reach the scrotal sac. This phase of the descent is regulated by androgen-induced calcitonin gene -related peptide from the890 genitofemoral nerve. The exact pathogenesis remains unknown, however, deficiency in gonadotropins and Mullerian-inhibiting substance (MIS) and increased expression of estradiol in the placenta are thought to play a role. It is associated with testicular atrophy and dysfunction , which result in sterility . Cryptorchid testes carry a 3–5-fold higher risk for testicular cancer (usually seminoma).

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Testicular atrophy is not seen in which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Torsion testis does not cause testicular atrophy. It may cause intense congestion to widespread hemorrhage to testicular infarction. Causes of testicular atrophy: • Progressive atherosclerotic narrowing of the blood supply in old age • End-stage of an inflammatory orchitis • Cryptorchidism - associated with progressive tubular atrophy and sterility • Hypopituitarism • Generalized malnutrition or cachexia • Irradiation • Prolonged administration of antiandrogens (treatment for advanced carcinoma of the prostate ) • Liver cirrhosis - may cause testicular atrophy as a result of increased levels of circulating endogenous estrogens not metabolized by the diseased liver • Exhaustion atrophy, which may follow persistent stimulation by high levels of the follicle -stimulating pituitary hormone • Occasionally occurs as a primary failure of genetic origins, such as in Klinefelter (XXY ) syndrome The histological image below of testicular atrophy shows small tubules with few or no germ cells , thickening of the basement membrane of the spermatic tubules , and prominent Leydig cells . The near-normal seminiferous tubules are seen side -by-side with atrophic seminiferous tubules .891

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man undergoes testicular biopsy as part of infertility work-up. Sperm count shows oligospermia. Microscopy shows only Sertoli cells in the seminiferous tubules . What is the most likely finding seen in the condition?
mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario depicts that the patient is having Sertoli cell -only syndrome, and patients with this syndrome will have increased levels of follicle -stimulating hormone (FSH). The below image shows normal histology of testis :892 In normal males, as spermatogenesis and testosterone production increase, the Sertoli cells produce inhibin, which inhibits the release of FSH. The Sertoli cells are supporting cells that are under the action of FSH. Leydig cells , which are present in the interstitial spaces , are under the action of luteinizing hormone(LH ) and produce testosterone . Testosterone has a feedback inhibition on LH . In Sertoli cell -only syndrome, within the seminiferous tubules , only Sertoli cells are seen and no germ cells . Hence , there are no spermatozoa and there is no feedback inhibition, which results in increased FSH levels . So, testosterone levels , and LH levels remain unaffected since Leydig cells are not affected . Hence , the patient will have male secondary sexual characters. The most important indication of testicular biopsy is infertility workup.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: An 18-year-old boy presents with acute onset of testicular pain. On examination, the left testis is enlarged , tender and positioned higher than the right at an unusual angle. Pain is not relieved on elevation of the scrotum. What histopathological changes can be seen in this condition?

options.a: Marked fibrosis with prominent Leydig cells and hypoplastic Sertoli cells
options.b: Dysplastic cells with hyperchromatic nuclei , koilocytic atypia
options.d: Intense congestion , hemorrhage, and areas of infarction

mcqs.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is testicular torsion. The pathological changes range from intense congestion to widespread hemorrhage to testicular infarction. In advanced stages , the testis is markedly enlarged and consists entirely of soft , necrotic, hemorrhagic tissue .893 Adult torsion is typically seen in adolescence and presents with the sudden onset of testicular pain. Neonatal torsion can occur either in utero or shortly after birth and the cause is unknown. It results from a bilateral anatomic defect that leads to increased mobility of the testes (bell- clapper? abnormality). Twisting of the spermatic cord typically cuts off the venous drainage of the testis . But, thick-walled arteries remain patent , producing intense vascular engorgement , followed by hemorrhagic infarction. If the testis is manually untwisted within approximately 6 hours of the onset of torsion, there is a good chance that the testis will remain viable.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following infections primarily affects the testis ?
mcqs.explanation: Syphilis and mumps affect the testis primarily and later spread to surrounding structures .894 Syphilis can affect both the testis and epididymis , but invariably , the testis is involved first as gummas and diffuse interstitial inflammation. Mumps most commonly affects school-aged children, but testicular involvement is uncommon in this age . Mumps infection in postpubertal males can lead to acute interstitial orchitis in 20 to 30% of cases . Gonorrhea and tuberculosis affect the epididymis first, which can later spread to the testis .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following testicular tumors is derived from germ-cell neoplasia in situ?
mcqs.explanation: Germ-cell neoplasia in situ (GCNIS) is a common precursor lesion of seminoma. Most testicular germ-cell tumors originate from a precursor lesion called GCNIS. It is believed to arise in utero and stay dormant until puberty , after which it may progress to seminoma or non-seminomatous tumors. The exceptions to this rule are: • Prepubertal yolk-sac tumors • Teratomas • Adult spermatocyte tumors The lesion consists of atypical primordial germ cells , which have large nuclei and a clear cytoplasm and fail to develop into spermatogonia. This is because these cells retain the expression of the transcription factors OCT3/4 and NANOG, which maintain the pluripotency of germ cells and prevent their maturation.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: All of the following are true about tumors of the testis except :

options.b: Pure choriocarcinoma has an excellent prognosis
options.c: Seminomas only rarely occur in infants
options.d: Non-seminomatous germ-cell tumour metastasize using hematogenous route

mcqs.explanation: Pure choriocarcinoma is a rare, but aggressive , tumor and has a poor prognosis. It generally does not cause any testicular enlargement . It spreads rapidly via the bloodstream . This results in the frequent involvement of the lung and liver. However, pure germ-cell tumors (GCTs) are rare and about 60% of testicular GCTs are mixed tumors. Teratomas in children usually follow a benign course . But, in the postpubertal male, all teratomas are regarded as malignant because they are capable of metastatic behavior.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the most common testicular tumor in infants?
mcqs.explanation: Yolk sac tumor is the most common testicular tumor in infants and children up to 3 years of age . Prepubertal teratoma is the second most common testicular tumor in infants and children. In adults , pure yolk sac tumor is rare. The yolk sac elements frequently occur in combination with embryonal carcinoma (as a mixed tumor).895

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man presented with a painless testicular mass. Inguinal orchidectomy was done and the gross and histological image is given below . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The gross specimen showing a homogeneous , grey-white , lobulated cut surface that bulges around the surrounding parenchyma is characteristic of a seminomatous germ-cell tumor or seminoma. The histological image shows sheets of uniform cells with clear cytoplasm and central nucleus , with a prominent nucleolus (fried-egg appearance ), delicate fibrous septa containing a lymphocytic infiltrate.Seminoma is the most common type of GCT. The peak incidence is the 3rd decade and almost never occurs in infants. It is the testicular equivalent of an ovarian dysgerminoma. Immunohistochemistry is positive for KIT, (regardless of KIT mutational status ), OCT3/4, and placental alkaline phosphatase (PLAP ). Option B: Yolk sac tumor is non-encapsulated with mucinous appearance . Schiller–Duval bodies are characteristic. It is seen in children less than 3 years. Option C: Teratoma shows derivatives of more than one germ layer like cartilage , hair, sebaceous glands. Option D: Testicular lymphoma is a rare extranodal presentation of non-Hodgkin lymphoma Testicular biopsy is contraindicated in case of a suspicious testicular mass because it is associated with a risk of tumor cell spillage . High inguinal orchidectomy followed by histopathological evaluation is the preferred standard management. Fixative used for testicular biopsy is Bouin's fluid .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man presented with a testicular mass. Microscopic examination of the orchidectomy specimen was done. It showed highly anaplastic cells with hyperchromatic nuclei with prominent nucleoli growing in alveolar and tubular patterns . They stained positive for PLAP , cytokeratin, and CD30 and negative for KIT. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario of the germ-cell tumor is suggestive of embryonal carcinoma .896 It is a non-seminomatous germ cell tumor (NSGCTs) that occurs mostly in the 20 to 30 year age group. These tumors are more aggressive than seminomas. Embryonal carcinomas share some markers with seminomas such as OCT 3/4 and PLAP but differ by being positive for cytokeratin and CD30 and negative for KIT. Most patients present with a testicular mass, which can be painful due to rapid growth and may be mistaken for torsion. Grossly, the tumor is often variegated, poorly demarcated at the margins, and punctuated by foci of hemorrhage or necrosis. Histologically , the cells grow in alveolar or tubular patterns , sometimes with papillary convolutions; the neoplastic cells have an epithelial appearance , are large and anaplastic, and exhibit hyperchromatic nuclei with prominent nucleoli . The below image is the histology of embryonal carcinoma showing anaplastic cells with large hyperchromatic nuclei .897 Option A: Seminoma will have sheets of uniform cells with poor, demarcated lobules divided by delicate fibrous septa infiltrated by lymphocytes . Seminomas are positive PLAP and KIT, but negative for cytokeratin and CD30. Option C: Teratoma will show derivatives of more than one germ layer like cartilage , hairs, sebaceous glands in the histology . Option D: Yolk sac tumor affects children up to 3 yrs of age , will have elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), and exhibit Schiller–Duval bodies on histology .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A young man presented with a testicular mass and increased AFP levels . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Marked elevation of serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels is produced by the yolk sac tumor / endodermal sinus tumor. It is the most common testicular tumor in infants and children up to 3 years of age (prepubertal yolk sac tumor). Postpubertal yolk sac tumors are associated with germ-cell neoplasia in situ and almost always occur in mixed forms. Grossly, pure yolk sac tumors have a homogenous , mucinous appearance . The below image is of a yolk sac tumor showing lace-like architecture and Schiller–Duval bodies (Arrow) (a hallmark of YST), and hyaline-like globules . These structures consist of a mesodermal core with central capillary as well as a visceral and parietal layer of cells (glomeruloid pattern)898

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about teratomas?

options.a: In post -pubertal males, all teratomas are considered benign.
options.b: All teratomas are benign even if they show immature elements .
options.c: All teratomas are considered malignant in post -pubertal males.
options.d: Orchidectomy is curative for testicular teratomas.

mcqs.explanation: In post -pubertal males, teratomas are considered malignant, regardless of the presence of immature elements . Teratomas are non-seminomatous germ cell tumors (NSGCTs), which are characteristically composed of more than one germ layer derivative (ectoderm , mesoderm , endoderm ). Teratomas have complex histopathology and 2 variants may be seen : • Mature : Adult -type , well -differentiated cells or organoid structures • Immature: Embryonal-type , undifferentiated cells or primitive neural elements In ovarian teratomas, immature elememts are needed to consider it malignant. However, the degree of immaturity is clinically insignificant in testicular teratomas. In prepubertal children, testicular teratomas have a benign course. However, in postpubertal males, teratomas are considered malignant. The below image shows the histology of teratoma of the testis .899

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man presents with hemoptysis and loss of weight . Chest radiograph shows multiple canon-ball metastases . Physical examination revealed no palpable mass. The serum HCG level is raised, but no change in AFP and CEA levels . Biopsy from the lung lesion reveals the following finding. What is the most likely primary tumor?
mcqs.explanation: From the given clinical scenario and image showing cytotrophoblasts and multinucleated syncytiotrophoblasts in a hemorrhagic background, the most likely primary tumor appears to be choriocarcinoma . The syncytiotrophoblasts secrete �o -hCG, at levels that serve as important serological markers . Pure choriocarcinoma , although rare, is the most aggressive non-seminomatous germ cell tumor (NSGCT). It often does not cause any testicular enlargement ; instead , it spreads rapidly via the bloodstream . This results in the frequent involvement of the lung(cannon-ball metastases ) and liver and a poor prognosis.900

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: All of the following are true for spermatocytic tumors except :

options.a: It affects individuals generally younger than 35 years.
options.b: It does not have any extra-testicular sites of origin.
options.c: It is a slow -growing tumor that does not produce metastases .

mcqs.explanation: With a spermatocytic tumor, affected individuals are generally older than 65 years. A spermatocyte tumor (previously called spermatocytic seminoma) is a rare, slow -growing germ cell tumor that is distinct from classical seminoma, both clinically and histologically . GCNIS: Germ-cell neoplasia in situ PLAP : Placental alkaline phosphatase The below image is the histology of spermatocytic tumor showing a population of small, medium -sized, and large cells and mucoid lakesCharacteristics Seminoma Spermatocytic tumor Age –40 yrs >65 yrs Association with GCNIS, othe r GCT, cryptorchidism Present Absent Histology Uniform looking cellsLymph ocytes and granuloma Presen t Small, medium and large cell sLymphocytes and granulom a Absent Intracytoplasmic glycogen Present Absent PLAP reactivity Present Absent Extra testicular origin, metas tasis Present Absent901

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man presents with gynecomastia . Ultrasonography reveals a 1 cm solid mass within the body of the testis . His serum testosterone is 600 ng/dL and estradiol is 35 pg /mL . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of Leydig cell tumor of the testis . It is the most common sex-cord stromal type of testicular neoplasm . It is mostly benign and invariably unilateral. Most cases occur between 20 and 60 years of age . However, they can present at any age . The most common presenting feature is testicular swelling or gynecomastia (~15% of cases ). In children, hormonal effects manifested primarily as sexual precocity , are the dominant features . Tumors of Leydig cells may secrete androgens and estrogens , and even corticosteroids . Grossly it shows golden brown, homogeneous circumscribed nodules <5 cm in diameter . Histologically :902 • large, round, or polygonal cells • round central nucleus and prominent nucleoli • abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm containing lipid droplets , vacuoles, or lipofuscin pigment • crystalloids of Reinke, rod-shaped eosinophilic cytoplasmic bodies are seen in about 25% of the tumorsOption A: Spermatocytic tumor mainly occurs in older adults as a slow -growing testicular mass. They are usually hormonally silent Option B: Sertoli cell tumor mostly presents as a painless testicular mass. They are usually hormonally silent . Hence , gynecomastia and precocious puberty are very rare. Option C: Granulosa cell tumor usually presents as a slow -growing and non-functioning testicular mass. Gynecomastia is rare. They usualy secrete estrogen .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the most common testicular neoplasms in men older than 60 years?
mcqs.explanation: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is the most common testicular neoplasm in men older than 60 years. The most common types of testicular lymphomas in decreasing order of frequecy : • Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma • Burkitt lymphoma • Epstein –Barr virus - positive extranodal NK/T cell lymphoma. Testicular lymphomas are aggressive tumors with a poor prognosis. They have a higher propensity for CNS involvement.903

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: In patients with testicular tumors, what lymph nodes are primarily involved?
mcqs.explanation: Retroperitoneal para-aortic nodes are the first to be involved in the lymphatic spread of testicular tumors. Testicular tumors have a characteristic mode of spread : • Lymphatic spread is common to all forms of testicular tumors. Initially, it spreads to retroperitoneal para-aortic nodes , then spreads to the mediastinal and supraclavicular nodes . • Hematogenous spread is primarily to the lungs , but the liver, brain , and bones may also be involved.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Laboratory testing of a 30-year-old man diagnosed with a testicular mass showed increased levels of alpha-fetoprotein . All of the following can be included in the differential , except :
mcqs.explanation: Serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) level is raised in all the above conditions except pure choriocarcinoma and pure seminoma. Choriocarcinomas have elevated levels of HCG, which can be readily demonstrated in the cytoplasm of syncytiotrophoblastic cells . AFP is a marker of hepatocellular cancer and non-seminomatous germ cell tumors of testes , mainly yolk sac tumors.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which tumor responds best to radiation therapy ?
mcqs.explanation: Seminomas are extremely radiosensitive tumors. The counterpart of seminoma, which arises in the ovary , is dysgerminoma.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the most common malignant paratesticular tumor in children?
mcqs.explanation: The most common malignant paratesticular tumor in children is rhabdomyosarcoma. The paratesticular region is an extratesticular anatomical area, which includes the contents : • Spermatic cord, • Testicular tunics, • Epididymis • Vestigial remnants, such as the appendices epididymis and testis . The most common malignant paratesticular tumor in adults is liposarcoma. The most common benign paratesticular tumor is an adenomatoid tumor. The most common paratesticular mesenchymal tumor is a lipoma.904

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not used as a tumor marker for germ cell testicular tumors?
mcqs.explanation: Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) is not used as a tumor marker for germ-cell testicular tumors. It is an oncofetal antigen used as a tumor marker in adenocarcinoma of the colon, pancreas, lung, breast, and ovary . Markers of germ cell testicular tumors include alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), human chorionic gonadotropin, placental alkaline phosphatase , placental lactogen , and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH ).

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 61-year-old male patient with benign prostatic hyperplasia is planned for transurethral resection of the prostate . Which of the following is removed during the procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: Benign prostatic hyperplasia originates almost exclusively in the transitional zone, hence it is surgically removed. Nodular hyperplasia or benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is the most common benign prostatic disease in men above 50 years. It arises from the inner aspect of the prostate gland, i.e., the transitional zone. It is characterized by benign, hyperplastic proliferation of prostatic stroma and epithelial elements , which is driven by dihydrotestosterone . This growth progressively compresses the urethra resulting in urinary obstructive symptoms . The normal prostate contains several distinct regions, including a central zone (CZ), peripheral zone (PZ), transitional zone (TZ ), and periurethral zone, as shown in the image below .Note : Most carcinomas arise from the peripheral zone and maybe palpable during the digital examination of the rectum.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: An elderly man presenting with the features of urinary retention was thoroughly investigated and diagnosed with prostate carcinoma . All of the following statements about the Gleason system used for prognosis/survival of the patient are true except :

options.a: Grade group 1 represents the most well -differentiated tumors.
options.b: Tumors with Gleason scores 8 to 10 tend to be advanced cancers.
options.c: Gleason system correlates with pathologic stage and prognosis.
options.d: Gleason Score is reported from 1 to 10 .

mcqs.explanation: The Gleason score is currently reported from 6-10 .905 WHO/ISUP modified Gleason score is the histopathological grading system , which corresponds with the clinical behavior of prostate cancer. It is one of the key methods used in confirmation of the diagnosis, prognostication , and staging of prostate cancer (adenocarcinoma). The Gleason grading system is primarily based on analyzing the architecture of the tumor cells in the biopsy specimens obtained . The architecture , i.e., the Gleason Patterns are classified as: • Pattern 3: Well-formed glands • Pattern 4: Poorly formed/Fused /Cribriform glands/Glomeruloid glands • Pattern 5: Sheets of the tumor, individual cells , cords, and solid nests of cells , Comedo necrosis • Pattern 1 and 2 are no longer defined Most tumor specimens contain more than one pattern. Therefore, a numeric grade is assigned to both the primary pattern and the next most frequent secondary pattern. The sum of the numeric grades provides the Gleason score. • Scores 2–5 are no longer assigned . • Scores of 6 - 7 are potentially treatable cancers • Scores 8 - 10 are advanced cancers that are less likely to be cured . Based on the gleason score, they are classified into the following grade groups : • Grade group 1: score<=6 • Grade group 2: 3+4=7 • Grade group 3: 4+3=7 • Grade group 4: score 8 • Grade group 5: scores 9-10

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 68-year-old man presented with hesitancy , incomplete voiding, and pelvic pain. On a digital rectal examination, an irregularly enlarged prostate with a nodular surface was felt . Transrectal biopsy revealed poorly formed glands arranged in a cribriform pattern. According to the modified Gleason score, how would you classify the pattern seen in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of prostate cancer and all cribriform patterns are now defined as Gleason pattern 4 according to the 2014 WHO/ISUP grading consensus conference . The below image of prostate cancer with Gleason pattern 4 shows cribriform pattern906 Highlights of 2014 WHO/ISUP modified Gleason score: 1) Gleason Pattern: • Pattern 3- Well formed glands • Pattern 4- Poorly formed/Fused /Cribriform glands/Glomeruloid glands • Pattern 5- Sheets of the tumor, individual cells , cords and solid nests of cells , Comedo necrosis • Pattern 1 and 2 are no longer defined 2) Gleason Score: The current Gleason score ranges from 6–10 . Scores 2–5 are no longer assigned . 3) Grade group: • Grade group 1: score \0216 • Grade group 2: 3+4=7 • Grade group 3: 4+3=7 • Grade group 4: score 8 • Grade group 5: scores 9–10

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the normal upper limit of prostate -specific antigen value for a 75 -year-old man?
mcqs.explanation: The upper -age -specific reference value of serum prostate -specific antigen (PSA) in men of age 70–79 is 6.5 ng/mL . PSA is a product of prostatic epithelium secreted in the semen . Measurement of serum PSA levels is widely used to assist the diagnosis, prognosis, and management of prostate cancer. Older men have a higher serum PSA level than younger men, so the normal range varies with age .907 The serum PSA levels as a screening test for prostatic cancer has poor sensitivity and specificity . This is because various other factors such as trauma, infections , BPH, instrumentation/digital exam of the prostate , and ejaculation can increase serum PSA levels . A value of \0304 ng/mL usually warrants serial testing or further evaluation. In an effort to improve the sensitivity and specificity of serum PSA levels , many novel indices are used : • Age -specific PSA reference ranges • PSA velocity : Rate of change of PSA values with time. It is considered that PSA velocity of 0.75 ng/mL per year measured at least 3 times over a period of 1.5 to 2 yrs is significant to diagnose Prostate cancer. • PSA density : Serum PSA/volume of the prostate gland • The ratio of free to bound serum PSAAge Upper age -specific PSA(ng/m L) 40–49 yrs 2.5 50–59 yrs 3.5 60–69 yrs 4.5 70–79 yrs 6.5

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 68-year-old patient was diagnosed with prostate cancer. Hematogenous spread of this cancer would occur predominantly to which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Hematogenous spread of carcinoma prostrate occurs predominantly to the bones and are typically osteoblastic . The commonly involved bones in decreasing order of frequency: • Lumbar spine • Proximal femur • Pelvis • Thoracic spine • Ribs908

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man who developed myocardial infarction 3 days ago now presents with jaundice . Lab investigations done are given below . Which region of the liver lobule is most likely affected here?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of acute hepatocellular injury due to ischemia. Zone 3 (centrilobular zone) of the liver is most susceptible for ischemia because this zone is the farthest from the blood supply . On the basis of blood flow , liver parenchyma can be divided into three zones. Zone 1 is closest to the blood supply and zone 3 is the farthest . They are: • Zone 1 - Periportal (around portal triad) • Zone 2 - Midzonal parenchyma • Zone 3 - Centrilobular (around hepatic vein) A schematic diagram showing the hepatic lobule indicating the direction of blood flow and the zones of decreasing oxygenation is given below .Note : Zone most susceptible to toxin damage is zone 1.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Patients with which of the following conditions are least likely to develop centrilobular necrosis of liver?
mcqs.explanation: Centrilobular necrosis is not seen in yellow fever. In yellow fever, swelling and necrosis of hepatocytes are seen in the midzone of the liver lobule . Conditions causing tissue injury in the different zones of liver: • Centrilobular (Zone 3) • Chronic venous congestion (cardiac failure)919 • Acetaminophen toxicity • Budd Chiari syndrome • Ischemia • Alcoholic hepatitis • Midzonal (Zone 2) • Yellow fever • Periportal (Zone 1) • Viral hepatitis A schematic diagram showing the hepatic lobule indicating the direction of blood flow and the zones of decreasing oxygenation is given below .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A chronic alcoholic developed cirrhosis of the liver. Which is the principal cell type involved in scar deposition in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The principal cell type involved in scar deposition in cirrhosis of the liver is the hepatic stellate cell or Ito cell . Hepatic stellate cells deposit primarily type I and type III collagen in the lobule and cause fibrosis. In their quiescent form, these cells store lipids and vitamin A.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Histopathological examination of liver biopsy reveals steatosis . Which of the following conditions is least likely to cause this change?
mcqs.explanation: Steatosis or fatty change of liver is not seen in hepatitis B infections . Steatosis is the abnormal accumulation of triglycerides within a cell due to impaired lipid metabolism . In the liver, pathological steatosis is defined as fatty change involving >5% of hepatocytes . In the histologic sections, they appear as empty vacuoles within the hepatocyte920 cytoplasm . Hepatitis C genotype 3 is reported to cause periportal steatosis . It is due to its association with metabolic syndrome and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). In Wilson's disease , there is focal hepatocyte necrosis and steatosis due to toxic injury by the excess copper . In protein malnutrition, fatty liver results from the reduced synthesis of the carrier protein component of lipoproteins .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions causes macrovesicular steatosis of liver?
mcqs.explanation: Macrovesicular fatty liver (steatosis ) is seen in obesity . Macrovesicular steatosis is characterized by a single , large vacuole of fat that fills up the hepatocyte and displaces the nucleus to the periphery . Causes include : • Late alcoholic liver disease • Obesity • Protein-energy malnutrition • Non-alcohlic steatohepatitis (NASH) • Chronic hepatitis C Microvesicular steatosis is characterized by small intracytoplasmic fat vacuoles, which accumulate in the cell . Causes include : • Acute fatty liver of pregnancy • Reye syndrome • Early alcoholic liver disease • Drugs and toxins The image given below shows macrovesicular and microvesicular steatosis of liver:921

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 4-year-old girl, with a history of URTI , now presents with severe vomiting, lethargy , and altered mental status . You are suspecting Reye 's syndrome. Which of the following liver biopsy findings will confirm your diagnosis?

options.c: Portal tract edema and perisinusoidal fibrosis
options.d: Cirrhosis and periportal eosinophilic inclusion bodies

mcqs.explanation: The liver biopsy in Reye 's syndrome will show marked microvesicular steatosis . Reye 's syndrome is an acute illness , encountered exclusively in children <15 years. Its onset usually follows upper respiratory tract infections . The actual cause is unknown, although viral agents and salicylates (aspirin) have been implicated . Pathogenesis behind this condition is generalized mitochondrial dysfunction with structural and functional alterations of mitochondria in the liver, brain , and muscle . Liver is enlarged but jaundice is absent or minimum. It is characterized by clinical features such as: • Vomiting • Signs of progressive CNS damage • Signs of hepatic injury • Hypoglycemia Extensive accumulation of fat droplets within hepatocytes (microvesicular steatosis ) can be seen in histopathology . Extra-hepatic changes include fatty changes of renal tubular cells , cerebral edema , and neuronal degeneration of the brain . The image given below shows microvesicular steatosis of liver.922 Note : Aspirin is generally contraindicated in children, except in the treatment of Kawasaki disease and juvenile idiopathic arthritis.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Histopathological examination of liver biopsy in a patient with jaundice shows the following finding. Which of the following conditions is least likely in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The marked structure in the image is Mallory hyaline body which is not seen in primary sclerosing cholangitis. In this condition, onion skin fibrosis is seen . Mallory hyaline bodies (Mallory–Denk bodies ) are usually present as clumped , amorphous, eosinophilic material in ballooned hepatocytes . They are made up of cytokeratin 8 and cytokeratin 18. They have a twisted rope-like appearance . On trichrome stain, they appear green /dark brown. They are seen in: • Alcoholic liver disease • Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease • Wilson's disease • Hepatocellular carcinoma • Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency • Primary biliary cholangitis (formerly called primary biliary cirrhosis) • Indian childhood cirrhosis The image given below shows Mallory hyaline bodies .923

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following causes Laennec cirrhosis?
mcqs.explanation: Laennec cirrhosis is the classic micronodular cirrhosis seen in end-stage alcoholic liver disease . There are three distinctive , overlapping forms of alcoholic liver injury: • Hepatic steatosis (fatty liver) • Fatty change - completely reversible if there is abstention from further intake of alcohol • Starts in centrilobular area • Alcoholic (steato ) hepatitis • Ballooning degeneration and necrosis • Mallory–Denk bodies924 • Neutrophilic reaction • Alcoholic steatofibrosis • Perisinusoidal fibrosis and sclerosis of the central vein • Diffuse nodularity of liver surface • Micronodular/ Laennec cirrhosis • Irreversible

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following histopathological findings will be seen in patients with chronic alcoholism?
mcqs.explanation: Chicken-wire fence pattern of fibrosis is seen in the liver biopsy of patients with alcoholic steatohepatitis . This pattern is due to perisinusoidal fibrosis encircling small clusters of hepatocytes . Trichrome staining of liver biopsy specimen showing perisinusoidal fibrosis (stained blue ) in characteristic chicken-wire fence pattern is given below .925 Note : Other conditions with chicken-wire pattern in histopathology : • Chicken wire calcification - chondroblastoma • Chicken wire vasculature - oligodendroglioma and myxoid liposarcoma

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions does not result in micronodular cirrhosis?
mcqs.explanation: Viral hepatitis is associated with macronodular cirrhosis. Cirrhosis is comprised of regenerating parenchymal nodules surrounded by dense bands of the scar and variable degrees of vascular shunting. It is of two types : The images given below show gross and histopathological micronodular alcoholic cirrhosis.Macronodular cirrhosis Micronodular cirrhosis Irregularnodules with variati on insize>3 mm Uniformnodules of size<3 m m Causes :Chronicviral hepatitis Wilsons disease \0371-antitrypsi n deficiencyDrugs and toxins Hereditary hemorrhagic tela ngiectasiaCryptogenic cirrhos is Causes :Alcoholic cirrhosisPri mary biliary cirrhosisHepatic vein obstructionLarge bile d uct obstructionHemochromat osisIntestinal bypassCystic fi brosisIndian childhood cirrh osis926

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: In patients with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis , which of the following features is not seen on liver biopsy ?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of lymphoid follicles is not a feature on liver biopsy in patients with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). It is a feature of chronic hepatitis C infection . The histopathological features of NASH include : • Ballooning degeneration of hepatocytes • Steatosis • Perisinusoidal inflammation and fibrosis • Portal fibrosis • Mallory-Denk bodies927 • Mononuclear infiltrate NASH and alcoholic liver disease (ALD ) have almost similar histopathological features . They can be differentiated as follows :Features ALD NASH Mallory-Denk bod ies More prominent Less prominent Fibrosis Perivenular and perisinusoid al>portal Portal fibrosis is more promi nent Inflammation More pronounced Less pronounced Inflammatory cell s Neutrophils >macrophages Macrophages >neutrophils

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the most common hepatotoxin causing acute liver failure?
mcqs.explanation: The most common hepatotoxin causing acute liver failure is acetaminophen . Acetaminophen itself is not toxic. The toxic metabolite produced by the cytochrome P-450 system in zone 3 hepatocytes causes hepatocellular necrosis. The most common hepatotoxin causing chronic liver failure is alcohol.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not cause chronic infection ?
mcqs.explanation: Hepatitis A does not cause chronic infection . It is usually a benign, self -limited disease . Hepatitis B, C, and D can cause chronic infection . Hepatitis E causes chronic infection only in immunocompromised individuals, not in immunocompetent .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: There is an outbreak of hepatitis A infection in a college hostel . Which of the following is false about this infection ?

options.a: It does not cause hepatocellular carcinoma
options.c: Liver failure is not a complication

mcqs.explanation: Hepatitis A virus (HAV ) can cause acute hepatic failure in a few patients . However, it does not cause chronic hepatitis or a carrier state . HAV is a usually benign, self -limited disease , with an incubation period of 15- 50 days (2 - 6 weeks ). HAV is spread by feco -oral route and is shed in the stool for 2 to 3 weeks before and 1 week after the onset of jaundice . It can also spread by sexual route. Diagnosis is by the detection of serum IgM anti HAV . Since it does not progress to chronic infection , it does not cause hepatocellular carcinoma . The fatality rate associated with HAV is only about 0.1-0.3%.928

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which among the following is the most common cause of sporadic acute hepatitis in India?
mcqs.explanation: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection accounts for most of the cases of sporadic acute hepatitis in India. It exceeds the frequency of hepatitis A virus infection . A feature of HEV infection is the high mortality rate among pregnant women, approaching 20 %.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 53-year-old man who has a history of chronic hepatitis B is diagnosed to have hepatocellular carcinoma . Which of the following is involved in the pathogenesis of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: HBx protein has been implicated in the pathogenesis of hepatocellular carcinoma in hepatitis B virus (HBV ) infection . HBx protein is involved in the intracellular regulation of virus replication, transcription, and signal transduction. Option A: HBsAg (surface antigen) indicates current hepatitis B infection . Option B: HBeAg (precore antigen) is an indicator of active viral replication. It is a qualitative marker of infectivity . Option C: HBV DNA polymerase is an indicator of active viral replication. It is a quantitative marker of infectivity .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following serological markers can be used to diagnose hepatitis B infection during the window period ?
mcqs.explanation: During the window period of hepatitis B, the serologic diagnosis can be made by the detection of IgM anti-HBc antibody. The window period of hepatitis B refers to the time between the disappearance of the HBsAg antigen and appearance of Anti-HBs antibody. The window period for a test designed to detect a specific disease is the time between the first infection and when the test can reliably detect that infection .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: In a patient who is both HBsAg and HBeAg positive , what does declining IgM anti-HBc and rising total anti-HBc indicate ?
mcqs.explanation: In patients who are both HBsAg and HBeAg positive , declining IgM anti-HBc and rising total anti-HBc are indicative of chronic infective hepatitis . Anti-HBc IgM antibody signifies acute infection /window period , whereas , the presence of IgG anti-HBc indicates chronic infection . However, there is no test available to directly detect the IgG anti-HBC. Over a period of months, the IgM anti-HBc antibodies are replaced by the IgG anti-HBc antibodies . Thus a decline of IgM antibodies in the presence of rising total anti-HBC indicates that the IgM is being converted to IgG and thus the infection is chronic. HBeAg, HBV-DNA, and DNA polymerase appear in serum soon after HBsAg, and all signify active viral replication.929 Occasionally , mutated strains of HBV emerge that do not produce HBeAg but are replication -competent and express HBcAg.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A patient with a history of unprotected sexual intercourse turns out to be HBsAg positive . Which of the following is the best predictor for development of chronic disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The age at the time of infection is the best predictor of chronicity. Younger the age at the time of hepatitis B virus (HBV ) infection , higher the probability of chronicity. Other predictors in the development of chronic disease : • comorbid conditions (including exposure to other infectious agents ) • host immunity Presentations of hepatitis B infection : • Asymptomatic - 65% • Non-specific symptoms - 25% • Chronic disease - 5-10% • Acute fulminant liver disease - 0.1-0.5%

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: An IV drug abuser has been found to be seropositive for HBsAg, HBeAg, and anti-HBc IgM. Which of the following is least likely to be seen in the liver biopsy of such patients ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of acute hepatitis B infection . Ground-glass hepatocytes are not seen in the liver biopsy of such patients . Histopathological findings in acute hepatits are: • Ballooning degeneration - due to inflammation • Portal or lobular inflammatory infiltration - lymphocytes , plasma cells , and eosinophils • Necrosis • Confluent necrosis - group of hepatocytes • Panlobular or panacinar necrosis - entire lobule • Bridging necrosis (in severe cases ) - connecting vascular structures Ground-glass appearance of hepatocytes is due to the endoplasmic reticulum which is swollen with HBsAg accumulation. It is a diagnostic hallmark of chronic hepatitis B infection . The image given below shows ground glass hepatocytes in the liver biopsy .930

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A man with a history of intranasal cocaine abuse is at most risk for which of the following infections ?
mcqs.explanation: Intranasal cocaine abuse is a risk factor for hepatitis C. Contaminated implements (like straws used to inhale cocaine) inserted into the nasal cavity might come into contact with hepatitis C virus (HCV)-infected mucus or blood. This might then be transmitted to a susceptible individual while sharing the same implements . Transmission of hepatitis C infection : • Intravenous drug abuse (54%) - Most common • Multiple sex partners • Needle -stick injury • Multiple contacts with a person with hepatitis C virus infection931 • Employment in medical or dental fields • Blood transfusion • Perinatal - major route of infection in children

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common clinical course in patients diagnosed with hepatitis C infection ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common clinical course seen in hepatitis C infection is chronic carrier state . Acute clinical illness is often asymptomatic/mild with a high rate of conversion to chronic hepatitis (~85%).

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which genotype of hepatitis C virus is associated with metabolic syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 3 is associated with metabolic syndrome. HCV can give rise to insulin resistance and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD).

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old male patient with chronic hepatitis B infection comes for a follow -up visit. Which of the following is not a histopathological feature of the liver in such cases ?
mcqs.explanation: Ballooning degeneration is not associated with chronic hepatitis . It is seen in acute hepatitis .
