Red flag signs in developmental screening and surveillance are indicators that suggest a serious disorder in a child's development , requiring referral to a pediatrician. These are given below : Positive indicators: Presence of any of the following • Loss of developmental skills at any age • Concerns about vision or confirmed visual impairment80 • Hearing loss at any age • Persistently low muscle tone • Lack of speech by 18 months without other means of communication • Asymmetry of movements or features suggestive of cerebral palsy • Persistent toe walking • Complex disabilities • Unusual head circumference compared to norms • Clinician uncertainty about the developmental disorder. Negative Indicators: • Inability to sit unsupported by 12 months • Inability to walk by 18 months in boys or 2 years in girls. • Inability to walk normally • Inability to run by 2.5 years • Inability to hold objects in hand by 5 months or reach for them by 6 months. • Inability to point at objects to share interest by 2 years

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: After assessing a young child treated for unilateral retinoblastoma, you note significant delays in the cognitive and fine motor domains. The baby can stand without support and creep well . Normally, the highest fine motor skill a baby of this age is expected to have is ________
mcqs.explanation: A baby that stands without support is most likely to be 12 months. The highest fine motor skill she is expected to have is mature pincer grasp (12 months). Bidextrous reach is seen at 4 months and unidextrous reach at 6 months. Immature pincer grasp is seen at 9 months. Child begins to scribble after 15 months. Fine motor development is critically linked with hand-eye coordination. Children who have disease -related loss of vision in early infancy develop difficulties in visuomotor integration and lags behind in fine motor milestones .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: You are a pediatrics resident handling the well -child clinic for the week and you are teaching undergraduates how to do a simple developmental assessment . A preterm baby born at 32 weeks , is brought in for a follow -up visit at 6 months. What is the age you would ask the students to assume when undertaking developmental assessment in this child?
mcqs.explanation: The corrected age (in weeks ) to be assumed while undertaking developmental assessment is 16 weeks . Corrected age (in weeks ) = (Gestational age + postnatal age ) - 40 weeks In this case, since the baby is born 8 weeks preterm, the 8 weeks of intrauterine growth and development she missed , is accounted for post -natally. Thus, for assessing the correct developmental age , 8 weeks has to be subtracted from the chronological age . In babies born preterm, corrected age is used for their developmental assessment until 2 years of age .81

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: All of the following statements are true regarding principles of development except ?

options.a: It is dependent on the functional maturation of the nervous system
options.b: Specific responses replace mass activity as the child matures
options.d: In the extremities , development occurs distal to proximal

mcqs.explanation: In the extremities , development occurs proximal to distal . Rules of development : • It is a continuous process • It depends on the functional maturation of the nervous system • The sequence of attainment of milestones is the same in all children • It progresses in a cephalocaudal direction and proximal to distal . • Certain primitive reflexes have to be lost before relevant milestones are attained • The initial disorganized mass activity is gradually replaced by specific actions.Growth Development Denotes a net increase in size /mass of tissues Denotes maturation of functi ons CephalocaudalHead \035 Neck \035 Trunk & upper limbs \035 L ower limbs Distal\035ProximalHands incre ase in size before upper arms Proximal \035DistalHand use is learnt before the use of finger s

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A young infant is brought to you with a suspected developmental delay . The child is intently looking at his own hands. You would consider referring this child to a specialist if this milestone persists after ______.
mcqs.explanation: Between 12 and 20 weeks , the child observes his own hands very intently . This milestone is called hand regard and it should disappear by 20 weeks . Its persistence after 20 weeks is considered abnormal . In a blind child, however, it may persist beyond 20 weeks normally and is called apparent hand regard.82

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following fetal hormones does not play any role in fetal growth ?
mcqs.explanation: Growth hormone does not play any role in fetal growth , although it is present in high levels during the fetal period . However, it does have a role in the postnatal period . Insulin and thyroxine hormones are required for normal growth and development during late gestation . Glucocorticoid has a role in the prepartum maturation of organs such as liver, lungs, and gastrointestinal tract.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A child is brought to the pediatrician for vaccination . The child is able to speak in 2-3 word sentences and is able to make a tower of 6 cubes . What is the expected weight of the child, if his development is normal and birth weight was 3 Kgs ?
mcqs.explanation: The child is able to make a tower of 6 cubes and speaks in 2-3 word sentences which indicates the child is of 2 years of age . Birth weight quadruples by the age of 2 years. Hence the child's weight should be 3 kgs x 4= 12 Kgs . Infants may lose up to 10 % of their birth weight in the 1st week of life and regain it by their 2nd week.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false ?

options.a: Head circumference should be measured within 24 hours after birth
options.b: Head circumference equals chest circumference at 1 year of age
options.c: A boys height at 2 and half years is half of his adult height
options.d: A girls height at 2 years is half of her adult height

mcqs.explanation: Head circumference should not be measured within 24 hours because the head is subjected to molding during delivery , which makes the measurements unreliable .89 The maximum circumference of the head from the occipital protuberance to the supraorbital ridges on the forehead is recorded using the cross-tape method . • Head circumference increases by the following : • 2 cm/month in first 3 months • 1 cm/month in next 3 months • 0.5 cm/month in next 6 months Head circumference is more than chest circumference by 2.5 cm at birth. • At birth: Head circumference > Chest circumference • At 9-12 months: Head circumference = Chest circumference • After 1 year: Head circumference < Chest circumferenceAge Head circumfere nce At bir th 33 to 35cm 3 m 40 cm 6 m 43 cm 1 year 46 cm 2 year s 48 cm 3 year s 49 cm 4 year s 50 cm 12 yea rs 52 cm (adult size)

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the eruption of teeth is false ?
mcqs.explanation: Primary teeth in the upper jaw erupt earlier than their counterpart in the lower jaw, except for lower central incisors and second molar. No primary teeth till the age of 13 months is called delayed eruption . As seen in the image below , the first primary tooth to erupt is the lower (mandibular) central incisor, at 5-7 months. All primary teeth erupt by 1.5–2.5 years of age .90 The first secondary tooth to erupt is the first molar (maxillary or mandibular), at 6-7 years, followed by the lower central incisor. Causes of delayed eruption : • Idiopathic: Most common • Hypothyroidism • Hypoparathyroidism • Familial • Mechanical blockage of individual teeth

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 3-year-old boy presented to the clinic for a missed vaccination . His routine anthropometric measurements were noted . He was found to be 90 cm tall with a lower segment of 45 cm. Which among the following is the most likely diagnosis in this child?
mcqs.explanation: The upper segment to lower segment (U/L) ratio in this child is 1. The U/L ratio is low for his age which makes spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia most likely among the given options . The lower segment is defined as the length from the symphysis pubis to the floor. The upper segment is measured by subtracting the lower segment from the height . The U/L ratio is • 1.7 at birth • 1.3 at 3 years • 1 after 7 years • 0.9 in adults91 High U/L ratio: • Rickets • Achondroplasia • Untreated congenital hypothyroidism Low U/L ratio: • Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia • Vertebral anomalies Arm span: • Length between the tips of the middle finger of the outstretched hands is the arm span. • It is shorter than the length by 2.5 cm at birth; it equals height at 11 y and thereafter is slightly greater than height (usually <1 cm).

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A team participating in an Under-14 national athletics sports tournament suspects foul play by, a rival team member. He claims to fit the criteria for the age requirements for the tournament, but the opposing team does not agree . Which of the following X-ray would be most useful to verify the claims of the player ?

options.b: X-ray of the hands and wrist
options.d: X-ray of the elbow and hip

mcqs.explanation: The X-ray of choice to determine the skeletal age of a 14-year-old boy is X-ray of the elbow and hip. The bone age of a child indicates his/her level of biological and structural maturity. Methods used for bone age estimation are Gruelisch –Pyle atlas (more common) and Tanner –Whitehouse method . Note : There is overlap in the age ranges for X-ray of choice .Age X-ray of choice 3 to 9 month s X-ray shoulder92 Age X-ray of choice 1 to 13 years Single film of X-ray hands an d wrist 12 to 14 year s X-ray elbow and hip

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.a: Head reaches 90% of adult size at 1 year
options.b: Lymphoid growth follows a sigmoid-shaped pattern
options.c: Perinatal period is between 28 weeks of gestation to 7 days after birth
options.d: Growth of child is cephalocaudal and distal to proximal

mcqs.explanation: Growth of child is cephalocaudal and distal to proximal. During fetal life , the growth of the head occurs before that of the neck, and arms grow before legs . The distal parts of the body such as hands increase in size before the upper arms. Growth rate of different tissues :Growth Development Denotes a net increase in size /mass of tissues Denotes maturation of functi ons CephalocaudalHead \035 Neck \035 Trunk & upper limbs \035 L ower limbs Distal\035ProximalHands incre ase in size before upper arms Proximal \035DistalHand use is learnt before the use of finger s• Brain growth : At age of 1 month, the head size is about 36% of the expected head size in adults . It doubles in the first year of life to 72% and becomes 83% of adult size at 2 years. • Lymphoid growth : It is prominent in mid-childhood . It peaks at 4–8 years and regresses subsequently .93 • Gonadal growth : It stays dormant during childhood and shows a rise with the onset of puberty . • Somatic growth : General body growth shows an S-shaped curve. It is rapid during the fetal period and the first 3–4 years. It is steady in the following period , followed by a growth spurt during puberty . Later, it slows down considerably . Note : WHO defines the perinatal period from 22 weeks of gestation (or \034500 g) up to 7 days after birth.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A young boy is brought to the clinician by his parents with complaints of impulsive behavior and decreased levels of attention at school and everyday activities. The clinician is suspecting a case of ADHD. Which of the following is not included in the criteria for diagnosis of ADHD?

options.a: Symptoms begin before 7 years of age
options.b: Symptoms should be present for at least 6 months
options.c: Should be reported by independent observers
options.d: Behaviour must be developmentally inappropriate in two or more settings

mcqs.explanation: Attention -deficit hyperactive disorder (ADHD) must begin before 12 years of age , according to DSM-5 criteria. It was 7 years as per the previous DSM-4 criteria. Treatment: Presynaptic dopaminergic agonists, commonly called psychostimulant medications , including methylphenidate , dexmethylphenidate , amphetamine , and various amphetamine and dextroamphetamine preparations are used .DSM-5 Diagnostic Criteria fo r attention -deficit /Hyperactiv ity Disorder (ADHD)- 1. A persistent pattern ofinatt entionand/orhyperactivity/im pulsivitypresent forat least 6 months, that interferes with f unctioning or development . 2. Several inattentive or hype ractive/impulsive symptoms were presentbefore 12 years o f age. 3. Several inattentive or hype ractive/impulsivesymptoms a re present in 2 or more settin gs(e.g., at school [or work] or at home) and is documented independently . 4. There is clear evidence ofcl inically significant impairme nt in social, academic, or occ upational functioning. 5. Symptoms do not occur ex clusively during the course of schizophrenia, or another ps ychotic disorder, and arenot better accounted for by anoth er mental disorder(e.g., moo d disorder, anxiety disorder, dissociative disorder, person ality disorder, substance into xication or withdrawal ).94

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: In the image given below , the weight and height of a child are plotted against his age in years. Identify the correct statement .

options.a: WHO growth charts used now are developed by National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS).
options.b: Short stature is defined as a height below 5th percentile .
options.c: Puberty in this child will be normal .
options.d: Bone age of this child is less than chronological age .

mcqs.explanation: Bone age of this child is less than chronological age , as seen in cases of constitutional delay . As seen in the graph, the child was short initially, but the final height is within normal range. Hence , this child has constitutional delay . Other options : • The WHO growth charts are based on Multicentre Growth Reference Study (MGRS). National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) developed growth charts that were used in the past. • Short stature is defined as a height below the third percentile or more than 2 standard deviations below the median height for age and gender (<-2 SD) according to the population standard. • Puberty will be delayed in this child.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Identify the correct statement from the following .

options.a: Children with pica are at increased risk of megaloblastic anemia
options.b: Breath-holding spells are associated with hypertonia
options.c: Thumbsucking in a child is a way of discharging tension
options.d: Bedwetting after a period of 3 months of dryness at night is called secondary enuresis

mcqs.explanation: Thumbsucking in a child is a way of discharging tension. It is a self -limiting habit disorder, usually seen between 6 months to 2 years. Option A: Pica is persistent ingestion of non-nutritive substances for at least 1 month. It hampers the development of the child and requires clinical attention . Children with pica are at an increased risk of lead poisoning, iron-deficiency anemia, and parasitic infections . Option B: Breath-holding spells : It is preceded by a provocative event such as anger. Crying stops at full expiration. Child may have apnoea, cyanosis, pallor, hypotonia, or even loss of consciousness , and generalized tonic–clonic seizure (GTCS). Subtypes include cyanotic, pallid, and mixed episodes . Seizures and cardiac causes should be ruled out. Parents should be reassured that breath-holding spells are self -limiting. Option D: Enuresis : • When the child has never been dry, it is called primary enuresis . • When the bedwetting starts after a minimum period of six months of dryness at night, it is termed as secondary enuresis . • Nocturnal enuresis is caused due to maturational delay . In a normal individual, antidiuretic hormone (ADH) levels usually peak between 4 am and 8 am. This circadian rhythm is impaired in nocturnal enuresis , leading to bedwetting. • Treatment - Behavioural therapy with positive reinforcement , bladder alarms , and desmopressin reserved for cases resistant to behavioural therapy .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: As part of the annual school health check-up camp, the visual acuity of a 6-year-old girl is being tested by the optometrist . What is the expected visual acuity in this age ?
mcqs.explanation: 95 According to Parson 's diseases of the eye , visual acuity of 20 /20 is attained by the age of 6 years. Nelson 's Textbook of Paediatrics mentions that by the age of 5 or 6 years most children attain 20 /20 vision. Generally accepted visual acuity according to age : • Visual acuity of 20 /40 at 3 years of age • Visual acuity of 20 /30 at 4 years of age • Visual acuity of 20 /20 at 5 or 6 years of age

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 3-year-old boy was brought to the clinic by his mother who complains that for the past few months he has developed body-rocking movements and repeats words he hears on the television . He doesn 't respond immediately on calling his name and also makes limited eye contact during interactions. Based on clinical examination you suspect autism in the child. Which of the following screening tools can be used to detect the boy's condition?
mcqs.explanation: The symptoms are suggestive of Autism - which is a pervasive developmental disorder characterized by: • Impairment in quality of social interaction • Impairment in quality of communication • Restricted , repetitive , and stereotyped patterns of behaviors and interests Common symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder - • Repetition of set words and phrases (echolalia ) • Absent or delayed response to name being called , despite normal hearing • Reduced or absent responsive social smiling • Reduced or absent social use of eye contact • Reduced social interactions • Lacking the ability to initiate or sustain an interaction with peers or adults • Stereotypic movements and repetitive behaviors may include hand flapping , finger movements, body rocking, and lunging • Overly sensitive to noise, smells , or texture and may scream when they hear a siren or vacuum Modified Checklist for Autism in Toddlers (MCHAT) is a screening tool for the detection of autism.Test Disorder Modified Checklist for Autis m in Toddlers (MCHAT) Autism Conner Rating Scale Attention -deficit /hyperactivit y disorder (ADHD) CRAFFT(Car, Relax, Alone, F orget , Friends, Trouble) Substance abusein adolescent s Edinburgh Postnatal Depress ion Scale (EPDS) Postpartumdepression96

options.a: Macrocephaly is defined as an occipitofrontal circumference greater than 3 SD above the mean for age and sex
options.c: Microcephaly is defined as an occipitofrontal circumference more than 2 SD below the mean for age and sex
options.d: Infants with benign familial megalencephaly have normal head circumference at birth

mcqs.explanation: Microcephaly is defined as an occipitofrontal circumference more than 2 SD below the mean for age and sex. Macrocephaly is defined as an occipitofrontal circumference more than 2 SD above the mean for age and sex. Monosomy 1p36 is associated with microcephaly . Infants with benign familial megalencephaly have increased head circumference at birth. Important causes of macrocephaly : • Megalencephaly (enlargement of the brain parenchyma) • Benign familial • Neurocutaneous syndromes such as neurofibromatosis, tuberous sclerosis • Lysosomal storage diseases : Tay–Sachs, mucopolysaccharidosis , gangliosidosis • Increased cerebrospinal fluid • Hydrocephalus • Benign enlargement of subarachnoid space • Hydranencephaly (absence of cerebral hemispheres ; the cranial cavity is filled with cerebrospinal fluid [CSF]) • Enlarged vascular compartment • Arteriovenous malformation • Subdural, epidural , subarachnoid, or intraventricular hemorrhage • Increase in the bony compartment • Bone disease : Achondroplasia, osteogenesis imperfecta • Bone marrow expansion: Thalassemia major • Miscellaneous causes • Intracranial mass lesions : Cyst , abscess , or tumor98 • Raised intracranial pressure : Idiopathic pseudotumor cerebri

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A mother brings her baby of 14 months to the clinic after being concerned about the shape of the baby's head . You are suspecting a case of craniosynostosis. The premature fusion of which of the following suture is seen in this child?
mcqs.explanation: The picture is suggestive of a child with left posterior plagiocephaly (as the left side of the head is flattened ) which involves the premature fusion of the left lambdoid suture . In the case of a left anterior plagiocephaly, the premature fusion of the left coronal suture is seen . Other deformities of the skull: Craniosynostosis consists of premature fusion of one or more cranial sutures , resulting in an abnormal head shape . • Primary craniosynostosis: It results from a primary defect of ossification. • Secondary craniosynostosis: It results from the failure of brain growth .Deformity Suture involved Anterior Plagiocephaly Respective side coronal sutur e Posterior Plagiocephaly Respective side lambdoid sut ure Deformation Plagiocepha ly Positional skull flattening (wi thout suture fusion) Brachycephaly Bilateral Coronal suture Trigonocephaly Metopic suture Scaphocephaly Saggital suture99

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 7-year-old boy was found to have a height for age 2 standard deviations below the median. Furthermore, his bone age was found to be equal to chronological age . Which of the following is most likely?
mcqs.explanation: Familial short stature is most likely as bone age is equal to chronological age . Bone age is more than chronological age in precocious puberty . Bone age is less than chronological age in all other causes of short stature such as constitutional delay , undernutrition, genetic diseases, and endocrine causes .100

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: The most calorically dense macronutrient is _______
mcqs.explanation: Fat is the most calorically dense macronutrient providing approximately 9 kcal/g. The nutrients that provide energy intake in the child's diet are referred to as macronutrients. They include the following : • Fats (\0339 kcal/g) • Carbohydrates (4 kcal/g) • Proteins (\0334 kcal/g) The main dietary sources of fat are as follows : • For infants: human milk/formula • For older children: fat from animal products , vegetable oils, and margarine .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: The mother of a school-going child is worried that he eats a lot of junk food. She is anxious to learn about the healthy diet to be followed in the child. You would ideally advise the mother to restrict the dietary intake of saturated fat to less than ______ percentage of total energy intake.
mcqs.explanation: 107 According to current dietary guidelines for children, energy from saturated fats should be <10% of total energy intake. Current dietary guidelines for children and adolescents : • Total fat should account for <30% of total daily energy • Saturated fat less than 10 % of total daily energy • Dietary cholesterol <300 mg/day • No trans-fat

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Your school friend, the mother of a four-year-old child gives you a casual call. She had recently noticed an ad on margarine being a better alternative over butter /ghee and wishes to seek your opinion about adding it to her son's diet . What percentage of total daily energy requirement in children can come from margarine ?
mcqs.explanation: Margarine and other hydrogenated oils are trans fat. Trans fat is not recommended in children according to current dietary guidelines. Current dietary guidelines for children and adolescents : • Total fat should account for <30% of total daily energy • Saturated fat less than 10 % of total daily energy • Dietary cholesterol <300 mg/day • No trans-fat

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A newborn baby is ready to be discharged . As a part of your discharge advice, for how many months would you recommend exclusive breastfeeding ?
mcqs.explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for 6 months. Complementary foods rich in iron and other micronutrients should be introduced at about 6 months of age . Breastfeeding should continue for at least the first year.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: You are taking a neonatal case for presentation during your postings . The mother tells you that the child is exclusively breastfed . Which of the following is least likely to corroborate with this history of being exclusively breastfed ?
mcqs.explanation: Exclusively breastfed infants are least likely to have evening colic. The incidence of diarrhoea, allergy to bovine milk, and atopic eczema are least reported in exclusively breastfed infants. Option A: Vitamin K content of milk is low and may contribute to hemorrhagic disease of the newborn. Option B: Breast milk contains inhibitors of glucuronyl transferase and enhances absorption of bilirubin from the gut . This leads to the development of breast milk jaundice . Option C: During the first few days, the breastfed infant has a black-green coloured stool . It changes to golden yellow by the end of the first week .108

mcqs.question: Which of the following mothers can initiate breastfeeding ?
mcqs.explanation: The correct answer is 2 and 5 only. Breastfeeding is not contraindicated if the mother has hepatitis B infection or if she is a chronic smoker. Infants born to an HbsAg positive mother routinely receive hepatitis B immunoglobulin and hepatitis B vaccine. So, a delay in the initiation of breastfeeding is not required. Alcohol consumption and smoking are NOT contraindications of breastfeeding . However, smoking and alcohol consumption should be discouraged . mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: As a part of your neonatal rotation, you are asked to assess the adequacy of breastfeeding and breastfeeding techniques in a primi mother. Which of the following would be an indicator of inadequate breastfeeding in the neonate ?

options.a: Baby sleeping for 2-3 hours after feed

mcqs.explanation: Weight loss of >7-10 % of birth weight is an indicator of inadequate breastfeeding in a neonate . Indicators of inadequate breastfeeding in the newborn: • Weight loss >7-10 % of birth weight • Lethargy (sleeping longer than 2–3 hours) • Delayed passage of stools (Less than 4 times /day) • Decreased urine output (urinating less than 5–7 times /day) • Hypernatremic dehydration • Inconsolable crying and increased hunger109 Insufficient milk intake may be caused by insufficient milk production , failure of established breastfeeding , and health conditions in the infant that prevent proper breast stimulation. Breastfed neonates usually feed 8–12 times a day, with a minimum of 8 times per day. However, the neonate should be breastfed only on demand.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: For how long can freshly expressed breastmilk be stored at room temperature ?
mcqs.explanation: Expressed breast milk can be stored at room temperature for 6-8 hours. Note : This is a controversial question. A difference of opinion among authors is noted regarding the refrigeration of expressed breast milk. Nelson's (21st ed , page 324 ) mentions that breast milk can be refrigerated and used within 48 hours and frozen for around 6 months. However, AIIMS in collaboration with WHO recommends that breast milk can be refrigerated up to 24 hours and frozen at -20 degree C for about 3 months.Expressed breast milk Stored for / Used within(maxi mum time) Room Temperature 6 hours In refrigerator 24 hours Frozen breastmilk at -20 \260 C 3 months

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Shrija, a working mother planning to resume her work wishes to know more about expressed breast milk. Within how many hours would you advise her to use the refrigerated expressed breast milk?
mcqs.explanation: Breast milk stored in the refrigerator should be used within 24 hours. Refrigerated or frozen milk should be thawed rapidly by holding under running tepid water and used completely within 24 h after thawing. Milk should never be microwaved. Note : This is a controversial question. A difference of opinion among authors is noted regarding the refrigeration of expressed breast milk. Nelson's (21st ed , page 324 ) mentions that breast milk can be refrigerated and used within 48 hours and frozen for around 6 months. However, AIIMS in collaboration with WHO recommends that breast milk can be refrigerated up to 24 hours and frozen at -20 degree C for about 3 months.Expressed breast milk Stored for / Used within(maxi mum time) Room Temperature 6 hours In refrigerator 24 hours110 Expressed breast milk Stored for / Used within(maxi mum time) Frozen breastmilk at -20 \260 C 3 months

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: An anxious new mother feeding her child with expressed breastmilk (EBM) feels that the consistency and colour of her milk have changed recently . She adds that when she expresses breastmilk, the colour and consistency of the first portion and the ending portion is completely different and that she is worried about the same. Which statement is not true about different breast milk?

options.b: Mature milk is thicker with all the essential nutrients for growth
options.c: Foremilk is watery and is rich in proteins and sugar
options.d: Hindmilk is richer in fat and provides more energy

mcqs.explanation: Mature milk is thinner (not thicker) with all essential nutrients for growth . Various transitional forms of breastmilk: Colostrum • In the initial 3 to 4 days • Small quantity, thick, and yellow in colour • A large number of antibodies , immune component cells ; and vitamins A, D, E, and K. Transitional milk • Secreted after 3 to 4 days until 2 weeks • Immunoglobulin and protein content decreases , while the fat and sugar content increases. Mature milk • Follows transitional milk. • Thinner and more watery . • Contains all the nutrients essential for the optimal growth of the baby. Foremilk • Secreted at the start of the feed • Watery and rich in proteins , sugar, vitamins , minerals, and water that quenches the baby's thirst. Hindmilk • Comes towards the end of the feed • Provides more energy and a sense of satiety and it is richer in fat. Preterm milk • Milk of mother who delivers before 37 weeks . • Contains more proteins , sodium, iron, immunoglobins, and calories as per the requirement of the preterm infant. The given image shows watery foremilk and hindmilk which is rich in fat.111

mcqs.question: Following the delivery of a healthy baby boy, his COVID positive mother slipped into ARDS and passed away. The relatives have arranged a breast milk donor and wish to feed the baby using the device shown in the image. In newborns of which gestational age , would you recommend this as a method of primary feeding ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows paladai. It can be used as a primary feeding method during routine feeding in neonates born at gestational age 32 -34 weeks only. Sick mothers or mothers with contraindications to breastfeeding can feed their child using paladai. The milk can either be expressed breastmilk or they can resort to using undiluted cow milk or formula feeds . mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 2-month-old child is brought to your OPD with complaints of diarrhoea. The mother wants to know if she should continue breastfeeding . Which of these components in breast milk, beneficial in intestinal cell maturation and repair, prompt you to advise her to continue breastfeeding ?
mcqs.explanation: The epidermal growth factor present in breastmilk helps in intestinal cell maturation and repair. This is why mothers are advised to continue breastfeeding in an infant affected with diarrhoea. It is also beneficial in luminal surveillance. Lactoferrin (Option A) helps in immunomodulation, iron chelation , antimicrobial action. It is also an antiadhesive and trophic for intestinal growth . Para -aminobenzoic acid (Option C) is present in low levels and offers protection against plasmodium. Glutathione peroxidase (Option D) prevents lipid oxidation.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A young working mother wants to add formula feeds to the diet of her 5-month-old child as she would be unable to breastfeed her baby frequently and satiate her. Which of the following fatty acid should the mother look for in the formula to ensure optimal brain development in the child?
mcqs.explanation: Docosahexenoic acid (DHA) and arachidonic acid (ARA), both play an important role in the growth and CNS development in babies. DHA and ARA are essential poly unsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) present in breast milk. Both are essential for cognition functions, visual acuity , and immune responses . They have optimal effects on brain development when included together , in efficacious levels , in an infant's diet . Almost all infant formulae are now fortified with pre-formed DHA and ARA . It is advisable that all infants upto 6 months of age are to be exclusively breastfed and not formula fed . However, in unavoidable situations such as lactation failure or maternal infections where breastfeeding is contraindicated , the use of a formula feed that contains both DHA and ARA is recommended . Other options : • Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and Linolenic acid are other essential fatty acids that are present in breast milk.113 • These are required for the overall protection of the cardiovascular system as well as to reduce systemic inflammation.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Breast milk is superior to cow's milk because ________

options.c: Casein is 60% of the protein content
options.d: Whey is 70% of the protein content

mcqs.explanation: Whey constitutes 70-80% of breast milk's protein content . The Whey: Casein ratio in human milk fluctuates between 70:30 and 80:20 . This ratio is 20 :80 in cow's milk. The high fraction of soluble whey protein in breast milk makes it easily digestible . The predominant whey protein is \032-lactalbumin in human milk and \031-globulin in cow milk. Human milk contains amino acids like taurine and cysteine (lacking in cow's milk), which are necessary for neurotransmission and neuromodulation . Breast milk is rich in polyunsaturated fat (not saturated fat), which is necessary for myelination. Human breast milk is generally rich in oleic acid and linoleic acid. Sodium concentration is not high in breast milk. It has a low osmolality , and hence , the solute load on the kidneys is low. mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: An exclusively breastfed neonate in his 4th week of life was found to be jaundiced . His stools are yellow and urine appears pale straw, he is otherwise well . A provisional diagnosis of breastmilk jaundice is made. Which of the following is false about this condition?

options.b: Some babies need treatment with phototherapy
options.d: It is common in the second week of life

mcqs.explanation: Breastfeeding is not contraindicated in breast milk jaundice . Mothers are advised to continue breastfeeding at frequent intervals. Breastmilk jaundice is seen in about 2–4% of exclusively breastfed babies. There is significant unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia after the 7th day and may last for 2–3 weeks . This may be caused by the breast milk that might contain \031-glucuronidase , which deconjugates intestinal bilirubin and promotes its absorption and other inhibitors of glucuronyl transferase. Persistently high bilirubin levels may require changing from breast milk to infant formula for 24–48 h and/or treatment with phototherapy , without cessation of breastfeeding . Breastfeeding jaundice (BFJ) It is an early-onset , unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia of breastfed infants. Occurs in the 1st week after birth (usually appears after 24 - 72 hours of birth). It is due to decreased milk intake with dehydration and/or reduced caloric intake. The treatment would include continuing breastfeeding and supplementation with formula feeds if needed .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old nursing mother presents with fever and pain in her left breast. She has had difficulty with breastfeeding previously , and now examination reveals her left breast is warm, red, swollen , and painful to palpation . She was started on dicloxacillin. What advice should be given to the mother regarding breastfeeding ?

options.b: Continue feeding from both the breasts
options.c: Continue feeding from only right breast
options.d: Continue feeding from only left breast

mcqs.explanation: 115 Lactational mastitis is not a contraindication to breastfeeding and the mother should continue feeding on both breasts. It is most commonly caused due to Staphylococcus aureus present in the infant's nasopharynx. Dicloxacillin is safe to be given in nursing mothers.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements are true with respect to the WHO Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative for small, sick, and preterm newborns (2020 )?

options.a: Paladai feeding is indicated in very preterm infants with no suck-swallow -breath coordination
options.b: Finger-feeding is optimally indicated for short-term use and may improve breastfeeding rates at discharge
options.c: Feeding tubes are indicated only in neurologically compromised infants for long-term use
options.d: Bottle feeding can lead to overfeeding but has a reduced risk of aspiration in infants with immature suck-swallow -breathe reflex

mcqs.explanation: Finger-feeding is optimally indicated for short-term use and may improve breastfeeding rates at discharge. It is indicated in neurologically compromised and preterm infants for a short period of time. Paladai feeding is indicated in preterm, late preterm, and term infants for supplementation . It is economic, cheap , and is easy to use and clean. It has a risk of aspiration and is a slower method of feeding . Feeding tubes - orogastric or nasogastric tubes are an efficient way of measuring intake. It is optimally used in very preterm infants with no suck-swallow -breathe coordination for long-term use . It requires frequent replacement . Bottle and teat feeding , though not recommended is an efficient way to feed . Slow-flow teats mimic breastfeeding and are preferred to rapid-flow teats . They allow overfeeding and there is a risk of aspiration.116

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 9-month-old boy was brought to the well -baby clinic for routine immunization . He has a weight for height less than 2 standard deviations below the median. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: A low weight -for-height , or wasting , indicates acute malnutrition. Nutritional status is often assessed in terms of anthropometry • Low weight -for-height , or wasting , indicates acute malnutrition. • High weight -for-height indicates overweight . • Low height -for-age, or stunting , indicates chronic malnutrition. This is the best indicator of long-term nutritional status in the pediatric population . • Low weight for the age indicates acute or chronic malnutrition. It does not differentiate between wasting and stunting . Hence , it has limited clinical significance . Note : Mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC ) is an age -independent parameter used for screening wasting in children.122

mcqs.question: A child is brought to the OPD for regular follow -up. Which of the following anthropometric record would prompt you to suspect a diagnosis of moderate malnutrition?

options.b: Weight for height < -2 SD to > -3 SD
options.d: Weight for height +2 SD to +3 SD

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an age -independent index?
mcqs.explanation: All the indices listed , namely, Kanawati and Mclaren index, Jellife ratio, and Rao and Singh index, are age -independent indices . Age -independent indices :123 • Kanawati and Mclaren index: Mid-arm circumference /Head circumference • Jellife Ratio: Head circumference /Chest circumference • Rao and Singh Index: Weight (kg) \327 100/height2 (cm) • Dugdale Index: Weight (kg)/height1 .6 (cm)

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A child in your unit is diagnosed with severe acute malnutrition (SAM). According to the WHO criteria, SAM is defined best by:
mcqs.explanation: Severe acute malnutrition (SAM) is best defined as weight for height less than median minus -3SD Severe acute malnutrition (SAM) in children of ages 6 to 59 months is defined by the WHO as any of the following : • Weight-for-length (or height ) below � 3 SD of the median WHO child growth standards. • Presence of bipedal edema • Mid-upper arm circumference <11.5 cm Once the child is diagnosed with severe acute malnutrition, the doctor must assess for severe edema (+++); low appetite (failed appetite test ); medical complications (severe anemia, pneumonia, diarrhea, dehydration , cerebral palsy , tuberculosis , HIV , heart disease , etc .) and one or more danger signs as per IMNCI If any of the complications are present , the child is diagnosed with complicated SAM and is managed inpatient in the facility . If the above-mentioned signs are absent, the child is diagnosed with uncomplicated SAM and supervised management at home is given.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: You are an intern evaluating a 2-year-old girl child for malnutrition. The measurement with the WHO standard mid-upper -arm -circumference (MUAC ) tape shows yellow . This reading would correspond to?
mcqs.explanation: The yellow colour on the new WHO standard mid-upper arm circumference of (MUAC ) tape correlates to a MUAC of 11 .5 to 12 .5 cm. MUAC tape cut-offs :Colo ur Measurement s Indication Red < .5 cm Severe Acute Malnutrition (S AM) Yello w .5 to 12 .5 c m Under-nourished Gree n > .5 cm Normal124 Mid-upper arm circumference is used in children between 6 to 60 months. It is measured between the acromion and olecranon process and is an age -independent parameter. Alternative methods for evaluating malnutrition: Bangle Test - It has an internal diameter of 4 cms. Normally, it should not cross the elbow . QUAC stick test - It is given by the formula - Mid-upper arm circumference / Height of child Skinfold thickness: It is an age -independent parameter. Routinely , we measure the triceps skinfold thickness. It is measured with the help of Harpenden calliper . • Normal: 10 mm • Severe malnutrition: < 6 mm

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A young child is brought to you for a general check-up. The physician is examining as shown below in the image. What would be the cut-off to label the child as malnourished?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows the measurement of skinfold thickness using Harpenden calipers . The cut-off to label the child as malnourished would be the triceps skinfold thickness value of less than 6mm. This is an age -independent parameter. Alternative methods for evaluating malnutrition: Bangle Test - It has an internal diameter of 4 cms. Normally, it should not cross the elbow . QUAC stick test - It is given by the formula - mid-upper arm circumference / height of child.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A laborer's second child is brought to the OPD with a swollen belly and dull face . He has been fed rice water (rice milk) in his diet mostly . On investigations, the child is found to have low serum protein and low albumin. What is the probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of a child with a swollen belly , dull face with hypoproteinemia along with poor diet history suggests the diagnosis of kwashiorkor .125 Kwashiorkor is a form of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) characterized by edema and apathy. In edematous malnutrition, the initial appearance of edema is commonly observed in the feet and lower legs , progressing into generalized edema affecting the hands, arms, and face . The skin over the swollen areas may show dark , crackled, peeling patches (flaky paint dermatosis ) with pale skin underneath , making it susceptible to infections . There may be sparse and easily pluckable hair. Hepatomegaly with fatty infiltration is a common finding. Associated symptoms of misery, apathy, and loss of appetite are seen in children with edema . Other options : Option B: Marasmus is a severe form of wasting characterized by significant loss of fat and muscle tissue as the body utilizes these resources for energy . It is often triggered by acute starvation or illness in individuals with borderline nutritional status . Option C: Indian childhood cirrhosis (ICC) is a chronic liver disease that affects infants and young children. Common symptoms include jaundice , pruritus, lethargy , and hepatosplenomegaly . The disease progresses rapidly, leading to the development of cirrhosis. Option D: Kawasaki disease (KD) is a systemic inflammatory disorder with arteritis of medium to large-sized vessels . It presents with fever, rash, conjunctivitis, and cervical lymph node enlargement .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: You are sent for active field surveillance of malnourished children to a rural district in central India. Which of the following specific finding would prompt you to make a diagnosis of marasmus?
mcqs.explanation: Children with marasmus have a voracious appetite , whereas children with kwashiorkor often refuse to eat. Marasmus is a calorie deficit state and kwashiorkor is a protein deficit state . The signs of low protein manifesting as hypoalbuminemia and edema are characteristically seen in kwashiorkor .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Sheila, a widowed maid brings her youngest child to your OPD with complaints of cough and cold. She has not been able to feed her kids after the lockdown affected her work. The image of the child is shown below . Which of the following is least likely to be seen in this case?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a child with marasmus which is not associated with apathy. Apathy is a psychomotor change seen in kwashiorkor .

mcqs.question: A child from an urban slum area is admitted to your unit and is receiving treatment for Kwashiorkor . Which of the following is not true regarding the treatment ?

options.c: Suspect primary treatment failure if appetite is not regained by day
options.d: Suspect secondary treatment failure if oedema reappears after 4 weeks

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 20 -month-old child diagnosed with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) is receiving treatment in your clinic. Given below are five statements regarding the treatment . Pick out the incorrect statements .
mcqs.explanation: Vitamin A is not given daily in the treatment of SAM. It is given on day 1, day 2 and day 14. The general treatment involves 10 steps in 2 phases : Initial stabilization phase : It focuses on restoring homeostasis and treating medical conditions and requires 2-7 days of inpatient treatment . Mnemonic: SHIELDED • Sugar deficiency (hypoglycemia ) • Hypothermia • Infection • ELectrolyte imbalance • DEhydration • Deficiency of nutrients Rehabilitation phase : It focuses on rebuilding wasted tissue and generally takes several weeks . Steps : • Treat hypoglycemia (blood glucose level <54 mg/dl): if symptomatic , give 10 % Dextrose IV at 5ml/kg. Feeding should be initiated with starter F-75 (formula with 75 kcal/100 ml of feed ) • Treat hypothermia (axillary <35\260C or 95\260F): Skin -to-skin contact with care called "kangaroo technique" or dress in warmer clothes, cover head , wrap in a warmed blanket, and provide indirect heat . • Treat dehydration : Hydrate with ReSoMal (45 mmol Na/L). It is a low-sodium rehydration solution for malnutrition.128 • Correct electrolyte imbalance: There is a deficit of potassium and magnesium and excess sodium. Give extra potassium (3 to 4 mEq/kg/day) and magnesium (4 mEq/ kg/day) for at least 2 weeks . • Treat an infection : Starting on the first day, give broad-spectrum antibiotics to all children. • Correct micronutrient deficiencies : • Do not give iron in the stabilization phase , because excess iron leads to free radical injury. Give iron 3 mg/kg/day once the child starts gaining weight after the stabilization phase . • Give vitamin A on day 1. Repeat on day 2 and day 14. • Folic acid 1 mg (5 mg on day 1) • Zinc (2 mg/kg/day) • Copper (0.3 mg/kg/day) • Start cautious feeding : Give 8 to 12 small feeds of F75 feeds . It is low-lactose milk that contains 75 kcal and 0.9 g protein per 100 mL . After 3 days, transition to F100 feeds is made which is called a catch-up diet . This provides 100 kcal and 2.9 g protein per 100 mL . After 1 week , calories are further increased to 150–200 kcal/kg/day and protein to 4–6 g/kg/day. • Rehabilitation: The indications of entry to this phase are reduced /minimal oedema and the return of appetite . • Beginning of feeding . • After 3 days, the transition to energy-dense feeding • Stimulation of emotional and sensorial development • Transfer to home-based diet

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 3 year old child is brought to the hospital with complaints of multiple episodes of loose stools and progressive weight loss. She was found to have a mid-upper arm circumference of 10 .5 cm. Which of the following is true regarding the management of this child?

options.b: Administer 10 mL of 50% glucose IV , if unconscious
options.c: Continue aggressive hydration, even after dehydration resolves
options.d: Use ReSoMal for rehydration 5 mL /kg every 30 min for the first 2 hours

mcqs.explanation: 129 Progressive weight loss and mid-upper arm circumference of <11.5 cm denote severe acute protein-energy malnutrition (PEM). When accompanied by loose stools , management includes the use of low sodium ORS for rehydration of 5ml/kg every 30 min for the first 2 hours. Management of fluid /electrolyte status in SAM: • Do not give IV fluids unless the child is in shock. • Give ReSoMal (low-sodium rehydration solution for malnutrition) 5 mL /kg every 30 min for the first 2 hr orally or NG tube . • Then give 5-10 mL /kg in alternate hours for up to 10 hour. The amount depends on stool loss and eagerness to drink . Feed every other alternate hour. • Give ReSoMal after each watery stool as a prevention strategy . • Do not continue aggressive hydration even after dehydration resolves. Treatment of hypoglycemia in malnutrition: • If conscious : % glucose (50 mL ) orally or 1 teaspoon sugar under the tongue , whichever is the quickest . • If unconscious : Immediately give sterile 10 % glucose (5 mL /kg) by IV . Note : 50% glucose is never used in children as it is extremely viscous and concentrated . This could lead to injection site pain, severe thrombophlebitis , and irritation . Also, this can cause osmotic overload in a three -year-old.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A young girl who was grossly emaciated and undernourished was started on partial parenteral nutrition together with enteral nutrition via a nasogastric tube . In the first week , which among the following would be the hallmark for the development of refeeding syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: The hallmark of refeeding syndrome is the development of severe hypophosphatemia . Refeeding syndrome is a complication of the acute nutritional rehabilitation of children who are undernourished from any cause , and it may follow overly aggressive enteral or parenteral alimentation. When excessive carbohydrates are administered , the resultant increase in serum insulin levels may produce the following : • Hypophosphatemia (hallmark ) • Hypokalemia • Hypomagnesemia A controlled transition over 3 days from F-75 to F-100 is recommended by the WHO for treating malnutrition, to prevent refeeding syndrome.130

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an 'Anti-infective' vitamin ?
mcqs.explanation: Vitamin A is required for the maintenance of epithelial functions, creating an effective barrier against pathogens ; hence , it is called as an anti-infective vitamin . So, vitamin A deficiency can lead to changes in the epithelia of all mucosal surfaces , leading to increased chances of infections . Vitamin E (Tocopherol) helps is an anti-oxidant. Deficiency manifests as skin changes and hair loss. Vitamin D maintains calcium and phosphorus homeostasis . Deficiency can lead to rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults . Vitamin C helps in the formation of connective tissues and collagen in the skin, bone, and blood vessels . Deficiency leads to their fragility and causes scurvy.139

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: What would be the ideal dose of vitamin - A that you should prescribe to a 9-month-old infant along with the measles vaccine?
mcqs.explanation: For a child aged 9 months, the dose of vitamin A given is 100 ,000 IU.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 2-year-old unvaccinated girl is brought to the OPD with high-grade fever and maculopapular rashes for 2 days. On examination, she has blue -white spots on her buccal mucosa as shown in the image attached below . Which of the following vitamin deficiency is associated with this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The girl is suffering from measles . It is associated with vitamin A deficiency . Vitamin A deficiency is associated with an increased risk of infection and increased mortality with a variety of infectious diseases particularly measles . Hence , vitamin A therapy is indicated in all patients with measles . The main functions of vitamin A are as follows : • Maintenance of vision, especially night vision • Maintenance of epithelial tissues • Differentiation of various tissues , particularly during reproduction and gestation , by regulating gene expression . Features of vitamin A deficiency : • Eyes : Defective dark adaptation is a characteristic early clinical feature , resulting in night blindness (earliest manifestation). This can further progress to xerophthalmia, Bitot's spots , conjunctivitis, or keratomalacia, leading to blindness . • Poor overall growth , anaemia • Diarrhoea, susceptibility to infections • Increased intracranial pressure • Keratinization of mucous membranes and skin (hyperkeratosis)

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A young girl of class 4 complains of a burning sensation in the eye . Clinical examination of eyes reveals the finding shown below . What could be the mechanism for the development of such lesions ?

options.a: Deposition of calcium in the conjunctiva

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical image is showing Bitot spots , which occur due to keratinization of the conjunctival epithelium . Bitot spots are triangular, frequently bilateral, and present on the bulbar conjunctiva. Normally, bulbar conjunctiva is a stratified , columnar, non-keratinized epithelium . In vitamin A deficiency , there is squamous metaplasia of the conjunctival epithelium and tangles of keratin admixed with gas-forming bacteria producing a dry, scaly patch with a foamy appearance called Bitot spots . Option A: Deposition of calcium in the conjunctiva is termed conjunctival concretions, which usually occurs over the palpebral conjunctiva, in chronic inflammatory conditions of the eye . Option B: Scarring of the conjunctiva is seen in chlamydial infection of the eye . Option C: Excessive growth of conjunctival tissue is seen in the pterygium of the eye .140

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 6-year-old boy with complaints of dry, itchy eyes and night blindness had the following ophthalmic finding as given in the image. What is the stage of vitamin A deficiency as per WHO classification ?
mcqs.explanation: The image depicts a corneal ulcer occupying <1/3rd of the cornea under a slit lamp with a fluorescein stain. This corresponds to stage X3A of vitamin A deficiency .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 6-year-old boy is brought to the OPD with complaints of headache , desquamation of the skin , and bone pain. Pathological examination revealed lysosomal rupture within the cells , prompting a suspicion of hypervitaminosis A. Which of the following statement is false about the principle vitamin that is excess in the given condition?
mcqs.explanation: Both hypervitaminosis A and deficiency of vitamin A cause raised intracranial pressure (ICP) (not just hypervitaminosis A). -cis retinal(not trans) is required for vision. Hypervitaminosis A causes headache , vomiting, desquamation of the skin, and hyperostosis of long bones. Rupture of lysosomes in the cells is the pathological feature of hypervitaminosis A. All-trans retinoic acid is the most bioactive form of vitamin A, and it is required for cell differentiation and the regulation of transcription. On the other hand, -cis retinal is required for vision. Protein-energy malnutrition can cause vitamin A deficiency because of the impaired synthesis of retinol-binding protein (RBP).

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Your best friend is recently worried that she has a lot of hair fall. Which of the following vitamin capsules if added to her diet can help prevent free radical injury and thus be beneficial for her??
mcqs.explanation: Vitamin E/ Tocopherol is a potent antioxidant and is helpful in preventing hair fall. It promotes hair growth and prevents hair roots from getting damaged by free radical injury. Alpha-tocopherol is the active component of vitamin E and it is mainly located within cell membranes, preventing lipid peroxidation and the formation of free radicals. Deficiency of this can also lead to neurological defects , hemolysis , and posterior column defect . Treatment includes vitamin E supplementation (25–50 units/day for a week ). Note : The other vitamins having antioxidant properties are vitamins A, C, and E (vitamin E is the most important). The other vitamin beneficial in the treatment of hair fall is biotin.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: An anxious mother brings her 6-month-old child with concerns about not gaining weight and height . On examination, stunted growth , craniotabes, frontal bossing, and craniosynostosis are noted . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Craniotabes (soft skull), frontal bossing, stunted growth , and craniosynostosis are clinical features of rickets. General features include failure to thrive, listlessness , protruding abdomen, proximal muscle weakness, and fractures. Head to toe -examination would include the following features :141 Head examination would include craniotabes, frontal bossing, delayed fontanel closure , delayed dentition, and craniosynostosis. Chest examination would reveal rachitic rosary, Harrison 's sulcus , and repeated respiratory infections and atelectasis . Spinal deformities could include kyphosis, scoliosis , lordosis. Limb examination and extremities may show windswept deformity , anterior bowing of tibia, coxa vara , and enlargement of wrists and ankles. Bowings of legs (genu varum ) or knock knees (genu valgum) may be noted . These changes can be seen only in children of the weight -bearing age group/ toddlers . The image shows frontal bossing:The image below shows the rachitic rosary:The image below shows craniotabes:142

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: The X-ray image of a child with muscle weakness and failure to thrive is attached below . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical vignette with the above X-ray image shows fraying and cupping of the metaphysis , suggestive of rickets. Radiological features in rickets: • Fraying (Widening and irregularity of the growth plate ) • Cupping (Concavity of the metaphysis) • Splaying at metaphysis (widening of metaphyseal ends ) • Generalized rarefaction

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: An 8-year-old child from a rural slum area is brought to your OPD with deformity as shown in the image. Which of the following conditions is characteristically associated with this deformity ?
mcqs.explanation: Windswept deformity (combination of valgus deformity of one leg with varus deformity of the other leg ) is seen in rickets. It is also seen in rheumatoid arthritis but characteristically seen in rickets. Other deformities of extremities seen in rickets: • Enlargement of wrists and ankles • Valgus or varus deformities of limbs • Anterior bowing of the tibia and femur • Coxa vara143

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Your school friend brings his 5-year-old son to your OPD with small swellings on the chest that he had felt while giving the child a bath. On examination, you note swellings at the costochondral junctions. Which of the following conditions would be your differentials to this clinical presentation ?
mcqs.explanation: Swelling of the costochondral junctions is seen in all the 3 conditions mentioned above.Rachitic rosary Scorbutic rosary Beaded (rounded ) in appeara nce Angulated in appearance Non-tender Tenderness on palpation (sub periosteal haemorrhage) Due to metaphyseal widening Due to epiphyseal separationNote : Tietze syndrome is the benign inflammation of the costochondral junction. Image: Given below is a photo of the chest cage with pectus excavatum.144 Image: The above image shows a rachitic rosary type of appearance .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 22 -month-old girl presents with failure to thrive and delayed achievement of motor milestones . On examination, she seems irritable and is noted to have bowed legs , thick wrists, and dental caries. Which of the following is not a radiographic sign of this condition?

options.a: Increase in the width of the growth plate

mcqs.explanation: The child is suffering from rickets. Subperiosteal hemorrhage is not a radiographic sign of rickets. On the contrary, it is seen in scurvy. Radiographic features of rickets: • Widening of the growth plate : Decreased calcification leads to reduced bone density • Fraying: The edge of the metaphysis loses its sharp border. • Cupping : The edge of the metaphysis changes from a convex or flat surface to a more concave surface. • Splaying : Weight-bearing and stress on the uncalcified bone gives rise to the widening of the metaphyseal end. • Enlargement of the wrists and ankles due to the widening of the distal end of the metaphysis . • Coarse trabeculation of the diaphysis • Generalized rarefaction

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 2-year-old child from an urban slum is diagnosed with nutritional rickets. Which of the following biochemical markers can be seen in this child?
mcqs.explanation: In nutritional rickets serum, alkaline phosphatase levels are increased . Biochemical findings in nutritional rickets (nutritional vitamin D deficiency ): • Normal or low calcium (since due to low calcium and vitamin D deficiency , PTH increases which will try to normalize the low calcium)145 • Parathyroid hormone levels are elevated (in order to increase the serum calcium) • Hypophosphatemia (because of increased parathyroid hormone [PTH ]) • Metabolic acidosis (secondary to PTH induced renal bicarbonate wasting )

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A child in your unit is admitted with alopecia , oligodontia , and features of rickets with elevated serum levels of alkaline phosphatase activity and 1,25-dihydroxy vitamin D. What could be the pathology ?
mcqs.explanation: Alopecia and oligodontia (reduced number of teeth ) with features of rickets in a child is classically seen in vitamin D-dependant rickets type 2 where the pathology is end-organ resistance (receptor hyposensitivity ) to vitamin D. Rickets causes • Nutritional vitamin D deficiency • Secondary vitamin D deficiency • Vitamin D-dependant rickets, type 1 (defect in 1-alpha hydroxylase ) • Vitamin D-dependant rickets, type 2 (end organ resistance ) • Chronic kidney disease • Hypophosphatemic rickets • X-linked dominant hypophosphatemic rickets (PHEX gene mutation) • Autosomal dominant (fibroblast growth factor [FGF] resistance to endopeptidases ) • Oncogenous rickets (increased FGF 23 ) Note : Vitamin D antibodies are found in most patients of systemic sclerosis .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Stoss therapy is used in the treatment of which of the following micronutrient deficiencies ?
mcqs.explanation: Stoss therapy is used in the treatment of vitamin D deficiency . There are 2 strategies for the administration of vitamin D: • Stoss therapy : Here, ,000 -600 ,000 IU of vitamin D are administered orally or intramuscularly as 2 or 4 doses over 1 day. • The alternative strategy is daily vitamin D with a minimum dose of 2,000 IU/day for a minimum of 3 months. Both strategies should be followed by a daily vitamin D intake of 400 IU/day if the child is < 1-year-old or 600 IU/day if the child is >1-year-old. Children must also receive adequate dietary calcium and phosphorus .146

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A child with rickets not responding to treatment is being evaluated . Investigations show serum calcium level of 9 mg/dL, low phosphate level of 2 mg/dL, elevated alkaline phosphatase , and normal parathyroid hormone levels with normal arterial blood gas levels . What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario of a child with a history of treatment -resistant rickets, normal levels of calcium (9 to 11 mg/dL), parathyroid hormone, arterial blood gas (ABG), with decreased phosphate (normal , 2.5 to 4.3 mg/dL), and elevated levels of alkaline phosphatase (normal, 33 to 96 U/L) is suggestive of hypophosphatemic rickets. Hypophosphatemic rickets: X-linked dominant hypophosphatemic rickets is the most common genetic cause of rickets while the most common, overall is nutritional vitamin D deficiency . PHEX gene (phosphate -regulating endopeptidase on x chromosome) products are responsible for the inactivation of phosphatonin. Mutation of this PHEX leads to increased phosphatonin (FGF 23 ) levels , and hence , the excretion of phosphorous is increased . This is also associated with impaired renal tubular reabsorption of phosphate leading to its excess excretion. The chart attached below summarizes the evaluation of hypophosphatemic rickets.Treatment-resistant rickets : Patients respond well to a combination of oral phosphorus and 1,25-D (calcitriol). Frequent dosing helps prevent prolonged decrements in serum phosphorus levels because there is a rapid decline after each dose . In addition, frequent dosing decreases diarrhea, which is a complication of high-dose oral phosphorus .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A concerned mother of an infant, known case of cystic fibrosis, presents to your OPD with complaints of abdominal pain, loose stools not settling with antibiotics, and other medications . She recently stopped breastfeeding and switched to formula feeds . On examination, you find petechial rashes. Which of the following below mentioned causes would not prompt you to suspect a deficiency of Vitamin K in this child?
mcqs.explanation: Vitamin K deficiency occurs mostly in breastfed infants not in artificial milk-fed babies, as the formula milk is fortified . The use of broad-spectrum antibiotics that eliminate the intestinal vitamin K2- producing bacteria can cause vitamin K deficiency. Biliary atresia causes malabsorption of vitamin K, due to defective fat absorption.147 There are 3 forms of vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB) of the newborn: Early VKBD of the newborn is prevented by the administration of a single intramuscular (IM) injection of vitamin K (1 mg) at birth.Secondary to maternal intake of medications Early VKDB(classic hemorrh agic disease of the newborn) Late VKDB Onse t At birth 1 to 14 days 2 to 12 weeks Caus e Drugs that cross the placenta and interferes with Vit K fun ction eg . phenobarbital, phen ytoin, warfarin Low stores of Vitamin K at bi rth, poor transfer of Vitamin K across the placenta , Inadeq uate intake during the first fe w days of life . In breastfed babies and in th ose with malabsorption of vit amin K (cystic fibrosis, biliar y atresia)

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: What is the recommended dietary allowance (RDA) of vitamin D in a 4-year-old child?
mcqs.explanation: In a child of age 4 years, the recommended dietary allowance (RDA) of vitamin D is 600 IU. Note : • Vitamin A: 1 IU = 1 IU retinol = 0.3 mcg of Retinol Equivalents (RE) • Vitamin C: 1 IU = 50 mcg of ascorbic acid • Vitamin D: 1 IU = 0.025 mcg cholecalciferol

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Rickets in an infant presents as all except __________
mcqs.explanation: Bowing of legs is not a feature of rickets in infants, because it appears only after weight -bearing. Thus, bow legs are a feature of rickets in toddlers . Image: Rachitic rosary (widening of the costochondral junctions)148 Image: Wrist X-ray image

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding phosphatonins ?

options.b: It increases the renal reabsorption of phosphate

mcqs.explanation: Phosphatonin is a group of phosphate-regulating factors produced by osteocytes , and FGF 23 is the most important phosphatonin . Phosphatonin increases renal excretion (not reabsorption) of phosphate . Mechanism of phosphatonin action: Vitamin D receptor activation by 1,25 dihydroxy D (active vit D) \027 FGF 23 release by osteocytes149 \027 Reduces expression of sodium-phosphate transporter in proximal convoluted tubules of the kidney \027 Increased urinary phosphate excretion Meanwhile , phosphatonin decreases the activity of 1 alpha hydroxylase and, therefore , the production of 1,25-D as well . So, the absorption of phosphate from the intestine is also reduced .150

mcqs.chapter: Deficiency of Water-soluble Vitamins & Trace El...
mcqs.question: Li Jing, a young tourist boy from the Keshan district of China visits India for a novel scientific exchange program. He presents to the ER with severe breathlessness . His previous medical records give the diagnosis of congestive cardiomyopathy . Which micronutrient deficiency is most likely seen in this case?
mcqs.explanation: Keshan disease is due to the deficiency of selenium . It is a congestive cardiomyopathy that is caused due to dietary deficiency of selenium. Keshan is a county of China where the symptoms were noted first. The disease is also endemic to that province. The patients will mostly present with acute breathlessness , paroxysms of exacerbated attacks. Selenium is an enzyme cofactor for glutathione peroxidase , which prevents oxidative damage . Note : Kashin Beck disease is a chronic, endemic osteochondropathy due to selenium deficiency .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Deficiency of Water-soluble Vitamins & Trace El...
mcqs.question: Anika , a 6-year-old girl good at sprint events, has been avoiding her track practices over the recent few weeks . Her mother informs that she skips her classes owing to her knee pain. Her X-ray reveals subperiosteal haemorrhages. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical vignette is suggestive of pseudoparalysis which is a feature of scurvy - vitamin C deficiency The subperiosteal haemorrhages in the lower limb bones can cause acute swelling and pain; the condition might mimic acute osteomyelitis or arthritis. The child refuses to walk because of the pain; hence , it is called pseudoparalysis.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Deficiency of Water-soluble Vitamins & Trace El...
mcqs.question: A four-year-old boy presents with petechiae , perifollicular haemorrhages, and swollen , bleeding gums. On examination, you identify the child to be malnourished and suspect scurvy. Which of the following is/are part of biochemical functions of the vitamin deficient in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Scurvy is a deficiency of vitamin C. The correct answer is 1, 3, 5. Vitamin C is a water-soluble vitamin , which cannot be synthesized in the human body due to deficient L-gulonolactone oxidase enzyme. Breast milk contains adequate amounts of ascorbic acid, whereas the pasteurisation of animal milk at high temperature destroys vitamin C. Functions of Vitamin C / Ascorbic Acid : • Synthesis of collagen (Hydroxylation of proline, which is vital for collagen ; in the formation of the bone matrix). • Neurotransmitter metabolism (conversion of dopamine to norepinephrine and tryptophan to serotonin) • Cholesterol metabolism (conversion of cholesterol to steroid hormones and bile acids) • Biosynthesis of carnitine158 • Antioxidation (electron donor) • For the cellular and immunologic functions of the hematopoietic system The image below shows peri-follicular haemorrhages.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Deficiency of Water-soluble Vitamins & Trace El...
mcqs.question: A child in your unit is receiving treatment for chronic diarrhea. His diet history is remarkable for a high phytate -rich diet . His labs reveal low serum zinc. Which of the following findings is least likely to be seen in this child?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette is suggestive of chronic zinc deficiency . Zinc deficiency affects both cell -mediated and humoral immunity. The cell -mediated immunity is impaired predominantly , as zinc is essential for T-cell division, maturation, and differentiation . In a child with a phytate -rich diet , a chronic deficiency of zinc and iron usually co-exist . Isolated chronic zinc deficiency can be seen in the setting of a child suffering from chronic diarrhoea, repeated pneumonia or chest infections , and congenital malabsorption disorders. Chronic zinc deficiency manifests as: • Dwarfism • Hypogonadism • Dermatitis of extremities and around orifices • T-cell immunodeficiency • Diarrhoea The features of acute zinc deficiency include : • Decreased growth • Poor wound healing • Diarrhea159

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Deficiency of Water-soluble Vitamins & Trace El...
mcqs.question: The X-ray of a 7-year-old child diagnosed with scurvy showed the white line of Frankel. This would be best described as?

options.c: Opaque radiologic shadow surrounding epiphyseal centres of ossification

mcqs.explanation: Calcified cartilage at metaphysis is known as the white line of Frankel and it is seen in scurvy.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Deficiency of Water-soluble Vitamins & Trace El...
mcqs.question: The eldest child of a ragpicker from the urban slums of Bandra presents with severe lower limb pain. Examination reveals swelling of costochondral junctions. The X-ray image obtained is given below . What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical vignette involving a neglected child (eldest usually ) from a poor socio-economic background with bone pains due to subperiosteal haemorrhages and scorbutic rosary (swelling of costochondral junctions) is suggestive of scurvy. Radiological features of scurvy: Early changes • The white line of Frankel on the ends of the shafts of the tibia and fibula • Wimberger ring sign: Sclerotic rings around the epiphyses of the femur and tibia. Late changes • Trummerfeld zone: Zones of destruction in the femur and tibia • Pelkan spur at the cortical end The image sums up the X-ray features noted in scurvy.The image attached below shows a child with the scorbutic rosary.160

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Deficiency of Water-soluble Vitamins & Trace El...
mcqs.question: A farmer from Hoshiarpur, Punjab rushes his 10 -year-old boy to the paediatric ER. The father complained of intractable nausea and diarrhoea in the child. On examination, the child has a garlicky odour and is severely dehydrated . You notice neurologic manifestations along with nail and hair changes in the child. Which of the following mineral toxicities would you suspect ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical vignette is suggestive of acute selenium toxicity . Selenium toxicity is characterised by nausea, diarrhoea, neurologic manifestations , nail and hair changes , and garlicky odour. It is commonly seen in areas where drinking water and the collated soil is extremely rich in selenium . In India, selenium toxicity is endemic to agricultural sites located in the states of Punjab and Haryana . The presentations are usually acute in nature rather than chronic. Chromium toxicity (Option - B) is commonly seen only in adults with occupational exposure . Chromium is a pulmonary irritant and the symptoms are predominantly respiratory complaints similar to bronchitis. They also cause chronic allergic dermatitis and is carcinogenic too. Molybdenum toxicity (Option C) is very rarely seen in humans. It manifests usually as acute diarrhoea. Iodine toxicity (Option D) can range from mild GI illness to chronic thyroid dysfunction varying from hyperthyroidism to papillary thyroid carcinoma .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Deficiency of Water-soluble Vitamins & Trace El...
mcqs.question: A 2-month-old infant is brought to your OPD. The mother complains that the child refuses to feed and is not gaining adequate weight . She has recently noticed changes in her hair. On examination, the hair seems to resemble steel to wood . Labs reveal low serum copper levels . What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical vignette is suggestive of Menkes disease or Tricholipodystrophy or Steely hair disease caused by copper deficiency . It is an X\037linked recessive disorder caused by a mutation in ATP7A which encodes for a copper -transporting ATPase\037\032 polypeptide , leading to the disruption of copper transport in the intestine . The clinical features include : • Failure to thrive (First presenting complaint)161 • Neurological degeneration (myeloneuropathy) • Infections • Hair abnormalities (kinky hair with pili troti seen on a Trichogram ). • These infants have a characteristic cherubic appearance with a depressed nasal bridge , pudgy cheeks , 'cupids bow' upper lip, and doughy skin. A therapeutic trial with copper -histidinase may be helpful . Option A: De Vivo disease is a metabolic disorder due to GLUT1 deficiency . Options C and D: Keshan disease (cardiomyopathy ) and Kashin-beck disease (endemic osteochondropathy ) are caused by selenium deficiency . The image attached below shows the cherubic appearance of the child with kinky hair. The subsequent picture attached shows pili troti seen under the trichogram.162

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Deficiency of Water-soluble Vitamins & Trace El...
mcqs.question: The anxious mother of a 5-month-old baby informs you that the baby incessantly cries on touching or lifting . The baby is comfortable when it is made to lie down. Diet history is significant for the child being fed exclusively on cow's milk. What could be the probable cause ?
mcqs.explanation: The above scenario is suggestive of scurvy. A child who presents with a cry on touching or lifting is usually due to subperiosteal haemorrhages. Scurvy/Barlow's Disease is caused due to the deficiency of vitamin c, especially in children fed predominantly on heat -treated cow's milk. High temperature destroys vitamin C. JRA - Juvenile Rheumatoid arthritis (Option B) rarely presents in infancy. Rickets (Option C) presents with growth retardation or other features such as craniotabes, craniosynostosis in infancy. It is generally associated with individuals who have a milk deficient diet . Caffey 's disease (Option D) is infantile cortical hyperostosis . It usually presents at 6 months of age with painful soft tissue swelling and bone thickening. The mandible is the most common bone involved.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Deficiency of Water-soluble Vitamins & Trace El...
mcqs.question: A child is born with the following abnormality. What advice do you give to the mother, with regards to the next pregnancy?
