mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common cyanotic congenital heart disease ?
mcqs.explanation: 488 The most common cyanotic congenital heart disease is tetralogy of Fallot (ToF). Infants are often asymptomatic until later in life (beyond 1yr of life ). TOF has 4 components : • Obstruction to right ventricular outflow (pulmonary stenosis ) • Malalignment type of ventricular septal defect (VSD) • Dextroposition of the aorta so that it overrides the ventricular septum (overriding of the aorta), and • Right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH )

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Below is an X-ray of an infant with cyanotic heart diease . Which is not a finding seen here?
mcqs.explanation: Cyanosis and boot-shaped heart (c\234ur en sabot in French) points towards tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) and the atrial septal defect is not a finding seen in TOF. Clinical findings in TOF: • Right ventricular hypertrophy causing left anterior hemithorax bulge . • Single S2 or soft P2 because of the stenotic pulmonary valve • Systolic thrill in the left sternal border in 3rd and 4th parasternal spaces . • The large 'a' wave in the jugular pulse is a reflection of the forceful contraction of the right atrium at the end of diastole as there is reduced distensibility of the hypertrophic right ventricle. • There is a loud and harsh systolic murmur due to the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) obstruction. It becomes louder , longer, and harsher as obstruction increases in severity from mild to moderate . • However in severe obstruction, especially during tet spell , the murmur becomes less prominent as the blood is shunted towards the aortic valve and not through RVOT .489 X-Ray in TOF showing boot shaped heart:Acyanotic/pink tetralogy of Fallot : This occurs when obstruction to the right ventricular outflow is mild to moderate . The blood would flow more through the mildly obstructed RVOT and less through the VSD. Hence , there is less cyanosis.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A mother brings her 2-month-old blue baby to your pediatric clinic for the first time. Neonatal records were not available but the mother says that the X-ray of the baby looked like that of a shoe . Which of the following wouldn 't you expect in this baby?

options.d: Large "a" waves in jugular venous pulse

mcqs.explanation: The given history of the shoe (boot) shaped heart in cyanotic baby is suggestive of tetralogy of Fallot and cardiomegaly is not a part of TOF presentation . In the tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), we see concentric right ventricular hypertrophy without cardiac enlargement. It is because of pulmonary stenosis (PS) and the ventricular septal defect (VSD). Any build -up of pressure in the right ventricle due to PS is released through VSD to the left ventricle. Option A: P2 is of low intensity and soft because the right ventricular outflow obstruction results in reduced pulmonary artery pressure . Option B: The aortic root usually appears large because it overrides (straddling) the VSD, allowing deoxygenated blood shunted from the right ventricle mixed with blood from the left ventricle to exit the heart. Option D: The large 'a' wave in the jugular pulse is a reflection of the forceful contraction of the right atrium at the end of diastole as there is reduced distensibility of the hypertrophic right ventricle.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A primary school teacher notices a peculiar behavior in one of her pupils . Whenever he plays with his friends, she notices that her fingers and lips turn blue . The child then squats for sometime after which he feels better . Which of the following does not occur during squatting?

options.a: It increases the systemic vascular resistance
options.b: It increases the magnitude of right-to-left shunt
options.c: Leads to trapping of deoxygenated blood in lower limbs

mcqs.explanation: Squatting decreases the magnitude of the right-to-left shunt in a child with tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) .490 The child feels comfortable while squatting due to two compensatory mechanisms: • Increasing systemic vascular resistance and, thus , decreasing the magnitude of the right-to-left shunt across the ventricular septal defect (VSD). Therefore, more blood goes to the lungs for oxygenation . • Trapping deoxygenated venous blood in the lower limbs.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: While waiting for corrective open -heart surgery, you decide to manage a case of tet spells medically . Which of the following drugs would worsen the cyanosis?
mcqs.explanation: Isoprenaline/isoproterenol should be avoided in tet or hypercyanotic spells . It will cause a decrease in total peripheral resistance (TPR) or systemic vascular resistance (SVR ). So, more blood leaves the left ventricle leading to the increased right to left shunt. This results in the worsening of right ventricular outflow and causes worsening of cyanosis and the symptoms . Treatment of hypercyanotic spell involves placing child in knee–chest position (or squatting), and use of: • oxygen • morphine - sedates the patient • sodium bicarbonate - to counteract metabolic acidosis that develops when arterial Po2 <40 mmHg • alpha-agonists (phenylephrine )- vasopressor used in severe cases • beta -blockers (propranolol)- improves resting saturation and decreases the frequency of spells . Drugs that increase SVR , such as IV phenylephrine (alpha-1 agonist) or propranolol (non-selective beta-antagonist/beta -2 block), can improve right ventricular outflow , decrease the right-to-left shunt, and improve the symptoms . This is same principle as squatting.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Blalock-Taussig shunt is done between _________.
mcqs.explanation: Blalock–Taussig shunt is done between subclavian artery to pulmonary artery Blalock–Taussig shunt is currently the most common aortopulmonary shunt procedure and consists of a Gore-Tex conduit . Sometimes , the shunt is brought directly from the ascending aorta to the main pulmonary artery; in this case, it is called the central shunt. Corrective open -heart surgery performed in critically ill newborns and early infancy is the preferred surgical treatment now.Name of the surgery Connects Blalock–Taussig shunt (B S) Subclavian artery to pulmona ry artery Waterston's shunt (WA) Ascending aorta to right pul monary artery491 Name of the surgery Connects Pott's shunt (PD) Descending aorta to pulmon ary artery

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a component of the pentalogy of Fallot ?
mcqs.explanation: Pentalogy of Fallot consists of • Tetralogy of Fallot : Ventricular septal defect + Pulmonic stenosis + Overriding of the aorta + Right ventricular hypertrophy • Atrial septal defect

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: An adolescent who is a known case of VSD is brought by his parents with complaints of breathlessness on exertion which is gradually progressive , bluish discoloration, and swelling of toes and fingers. Investigations showed features suggestive of pulmonary hypertension . Which of the following is not a part of the condition?
mcqs.explanation: Given clinical scenario along with the development of pulmonary hypertension is seen in Eisenmenger 's syndrome and predominant right to left shunt (not left to right shunt) is seen here. Gradual onset of cyanosis, dyspnoea , fatigue , and in later stages , heart failure, chest pain, headaches , syncope , and hemoptysis in a setting of congenital acyanotic heart disease , are signs and symptoms of Eisenmenger 's syndrome. Reversal of the shunt at the level of atria/ventricles/patent ductus arteriosus due to irreversible pulmonary vascular obstructive changes is defined as Eisenmenger 's syndrome.Features of pulmonary hypertension in Eisenmenger physiology : Right ventricular heave, narrow split S 2 with a loud pulmonic component . Chest X-ray showing prominent pulmonary artery and right ventricle, peripheral pruning of pulmonary vessels .492 ECG shows features of right ventricular hypertrophy , with spiked P waves. Treatment: Calcium channel blockers, prostacyclin , and it's analog treprostinil and lung transplantation.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: The most common type of total anomalous pulmonary venous connection is _________.
mcqs.explanation: The most common type of total anomalous pulmonary venous connection (TAPVC ) is supracardiac. In TAPVC , pulmonary veins instead of draining into the left atrium drain into the right atrium directly or indirectly . • Supracardiac (most common): Common pulmonary vein drains into superior venacava or left innominate vein. • Cardiac: Pulmonary veins drain into right atrium or coronary sinus. • Infracardiac (always obstructive and most dangerous ): Pulmonary veins drain into the hepatic vein or portal vein or inferior vena cava .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A neonate was noted to have cyanosis of the oral mucosa. Chest x-ray revealed a snowman appearance of the cardiac silhouette . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Snowman's appearance on the chest X-ray image is classically seen in total anomalous pulmonary venous connection (TAPVC ). The supracardiac variant can classically depict a snowman appearance /figure of 8/cottage loaf heart on the frontal chest radiograph. The dilated vertical vein on the left , brachiocephalic vein on the top , and the superior vena cava on the right form the head of the snowman; the body of the snowman is formed by the enlarged right atrium. The image given above shows a snowman or figure -8 configuration. Cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascularity are evident .493

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: You are examining a week -old male infant who was severely cyanotic at birth in the post-operative ward. He has undergone balloon atrial septostomy following prostaglandin E1 administration. Post-surgery there was a marked improvement in cyanosis. The most likely diagnosis is______.
mcqs.explanation: Cyanosis at birth, prostagladin E1 administration, and septostomy to improve oxygenation are typical features of transposition of great vessels (TGA). TGA is characterized by the aorta arising from the right ventricle and pulmonary artery from the left ventricle. Since systemic and pulmonary circulations are separate , survival depends on the mixing of oxygenated pulmonary blood and deoxygenated systemic blood which can occur: • At atrial level : Through atrial septal defect (ASD) • At ventricle level : Through ventricular septal defect (VSD) • At great vessel level : Through patent ductus arteriosus Chest X-ray image shows cardiomegaly, a narrow mediastinum (the classic "egg -on-string appearance "), and normal to increased pulmonary blood flow . The narrow pedicle of the heart is because of the malposition of the great vessels . Treatment: Here, prostaglandin E1 administration and septostomy help initial stabilization by creating a communication between the right and left atria, thereby facilitating the mixing of systemic and pulmonary circulations.494

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old woman with bipolar disorder on lithium therapy expresses intent to conceive. She must be advised to stop the drug due to the risk of development of which of the following conditions in the fetus ?
mcqs.explanation: She must be asked to stop the intake of lithium as it can cause an Ebstein anomaly in the newborn. Ebstein anomaly is characterized by the downward displacement of the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, which results in a thin-walled , low-pressure , "atrialized" segment of the right ventricle due to the anomalous attachment of the tricuspid leaflets . Lithium can also cause macrocephaly as a teratogenic effect .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Akshay, a high schooler presents to you with swelling of fingers and toes . He said he gets palpitations while he is exercising and even when he hangs out with friends. An X-Ray of the patient is given below . ECG showed the presence of delta waves. What is your diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The diagnosis is Ebstein 's anomaly. The presence of clubbing and a box-shaped heart on chest X-Ray in the given case is suggestive of Ebstein 's anomaly. Clubbing develops secondary to cyanosis as ebstein 's anomaly is a right to left shunt. Delta wave is observed in Wolff-Parkinson -White (WPW ) syndrome. WPW and supraventricular tachycardia causing palpitations can be seen in association with Ebstein 's anomaly.495

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: In a 13 -year-old child with Ebstein 's anomaly, echocardiography would likely reveal:
mcqs.explanation: Tricuspid regurgitation would be seen in a child with an Ebstein anomaly. Mild cases develop cyanosis during adolescence or early adulthood . In severe cases , cyanosis manifests at birth. Ebstein anomaly is characterized by the downward displacement of the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, which results in a thin-walled , low-pressure , "atrialized" segment of the right ventricle due to the anomalous attachment of the tricuspid leaflets . In Ebstein 's, tricuspid valve tissue is dysplastic and results in tricuspid regurgitation . The right ventricle is hypoplastic , which leads to decreased pulmonary outflow and there will be functional pulmonary atresia. As a result , blood shunts through the foramen ovale/atrial septal defect (ASD) results in cyanosis at birth. Himalayan P wave (amplitude > 5 mm) is associated with tricuspid atresia, Ebstein anomaly, and combined tricuspid and pulmonary stenosis , where they indicate a dilated right atrium. Wolff–Parkinson –White syndrome (WPW ) and supraventricular tachycardia may be present in Ebstein anomaly. Note : In Ebstein anomaly, the malformed tricuspid valve is usually regurgitant , but may rarely be stenotic .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A cyanotic newborn is suspected of having congenital heart disease . He has an increased left ventricular impulse and a holosystolic murmur along the left sternal border. ECG shows left axis deviation and left ventricular hypertrophy . Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Clinical cyanosis in combination with left -axis deviation (LAD) and left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH ) noted on the electrocardiogram distinguishes tricuspid atresia from most other cyanotic heart lesions .496 Other points in favor : • Increased left ventricular impulse (in contrast to most other causes of cyanotic heart disease , in which an increased right ventricular impulse ). • Holosystolic murmurs audible along the left sternal border (due to associated ventricular septal defect ). Tricuspid atresia is the congenital absence of the tricuspid valve. So, blood cannot flow directly from the right atrium to the right ventricle, and the following associated defects are necessary for survival : • Patent foramen ovale or atrial septal defect : for the flow of blood from the right atrium to the left atrium • Ventricular septal defect : for the flow of blood from the left ventricle to the right ventricle • There is a hypoplastic right ventricle. Option B and D: Truncus arteriosus and tetralogy of Fallot and - The ECG demonstrates right axis deviation (RAD) and evidence of RVH . Option A: Transposition of great arteries- ECG is usually normal , showing the neonatal right-sided dominant pattern.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: You are examining a case of cyanosis in NICU as a resident . Which of the following cardiac features would make the diagnosis of tricuspid atresia unlikely?
mcqs.explanation: Left ventricular hypoplasia would make the diagnosis unlikely as right ventricular hypoplasia is seen in tricuspid atresia. Other features of tricuspid atresia: • An increased left ventricular impulse is noted in contrast to an increased right ventricular impulse seen in most other cyanotic diseases . • A VSD holosystolic murmur is audible along the left sternal border. • The second heart sound (S2) is usually single . • Left ventricular hypertrophy and left axis deviation on ECG. • Tall, peaked P waves on lead II known as Himalayan P waves which are suggestive of an enlarged right atrium.497

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following cases could develop recurrent infections due to pulmonary congestion ?
mcqs.explanation: Patients with atrial and ventricular septal defects have increased pulmonary blood flow . This results in recurrent pulmonary infection due to congestion in the lungs . Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) and tricuspid atresia (TA) are associated with reduced pulmonary blood flow (oligemic lung fields ). They do not cause pulmonary congestion and do not predispose to infections . Reduced pulmonary blood flow is due to • Right ventricular outflow obstruction in tetralogy of Fallot • Right ventricular inflow obstruction in tricuspid atresia Cyanotic congenital heart diseases (CCHD) with decreased and increased pulmonary blood flow :Decreased pulmonary blood f low Increased pulmonary blood fl ow Tetrology of FallotPulmonary atresiaEbstein 's anomalyTric uspid atresia with an intact v entricular septumTranspositi on of the great vessels with V SD and pulmonary stenosis Transposition of the great ve ssels with VSD or PDATotal a nomalous pulmonary venous return (TAPVC )Truncus arter iosusHypoplastic left heart sy ndrome (HLHS )

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A cyanotic baby at the 8th hour of life is being evaluated in NICU. Pulse oximetry shows 80 % not improving with 100 % O2. Records show that continuous machinery murmur was heard at birth but not anymore. Which of the following can be done?
mcqs.explanation: This baby has a cyanotic congenital heart disease that is dependent on a patent ductus arteriosus. Prostaglandin E1 infusion prevents the closure of PDA in term neonates with duct -dependent498 congenital heart disease (CHD). Cyanosis failing to improve with 100 % oxygen suggests an underlying cyanotic CHD.Functional closure of the PDA occurs soon after birth, usually within first week of life . The open PDA acted as a conduit between systemic and pulmonary circulations, thereby preventing the onset of cyanosis. Upon its closure , cyanosis manifested in the baby as the blood could not be pumped into the lungs for oxygenation . Deoxygenated blood is being shunted into the systemic circulation after the closure of PDA. Hence , you should maintain the patency of the duct with PGE1 infusion until surgery can be done. Duct-dependent lesions : Anomalies, in a newborn with CHD, which are dependent on the patency of ductus arteriosus for survival . • Right-sided lesions (Tetralogy of Fallot , PA/PS) cannot pump blood to the lungs . These patients are dependent on an open PDA for pulmonary circulation. • Left-sided lesions (Hypoplastic left heart syndrome, Aortic stenosis , Coarctation of aorta) cannot pump blood into the systemic circulation. These patients are dependent on open PDA for systemic circulation.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: The given chest X-ray is suggestive of:
mcqs.explanation: The given chest X-ray shows a boot-shaped cardiac silhouette which is suggestive of the Tetralogy of Fallot . The boot-shaped (coeur en sabot) cardiac silhouette is seen due to the right ventricular hypertrophy and upward shift of the cardiac apex. The hilar areas and lung fields appear relatively clear due to reduced pulmonary blood flow or the small size of the pulmonary arteries, or both. In Ebsteins 's anomaly (Option D) box-shaped heart is seen .499

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which among the following options describes the chest x-ray image?
mcqs.explanation: The given chest x-ray shows 'coeur-en-sabot' or boot-shaped heart, which is seen in tetralogy of Fallot (TOF). The characteristic silhouette is due to cardiac apex elevation as a result of right ventricular hypertrophy. The hilar areas and lung fields are relatively clear because of diminished pulmonary blood flow or the small size of the pulmonary arteries and the aorta is usually enlarged . The image below describes the likeness of the cardiac silhouette to a boot:TOF is cyanotic congenital heart disease with the following four components : • Obstruction to right ventricular outflow (pulmonary stenosis ) • Malalignment type of ventricular septal defect (VSD) • Dextroposition of the aorta so that it overrides the ventricular septum (overriding of the aorta) • Right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH ) The severity of symptoms depends on the degree of the right ventricular outflow obstruction. In mild degrees, the symptoms become pronounced as the baby grows due to RV infundibular hypertrophy and may present with heart failure. In severe degrees , pulmonary blood flow predominantly depends on the ductus arteriosus. As soon as the duct closes , the baby presents with cyanosis and circulatory collapse in the neonatal period . Clinical features include significant hypercyanotic spells in infants which are characterised by hyperpnea , cyanosis, and gasping followed by syncope . The spells occur most frequently in the morning on initially awakening or after episodes of vigorous crying. These spells are due to a prolonged reduction of pulmonary blood flow resulting in severe systemic hypoxia and metabolic acidosis. Older children present with exertional dyspnea and assume a squatting position to relieve the dyspneic episode after which the child is able to resume the activity.500

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Of the following , all are findings of the condition in the below chest x-ray except :
mcqs.explanation: The given chest x-ray shows an egg -on-string appearance seen in the transposition of great arteries (TGA). Enlargement of the left atrium is seen in TGA, not the right atrium. The reason for left atrial enlargement is due to increased pulmonary blood flow . TGA is characterized by the aorta arising from the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery from the left ventricle. This abnormal configuration leads to a narrow vascular pedicle . As pulmonary vascular resistance drops during the first few days of life , blood flow through the pulmonary vasculature is increased . There is also elevated pulmonary venous pressure seen in TGA, especially in infants with an intact interventricular septum . The globular (egg ) appearance of the heart due to abnormal convexity of the right atrial border and left atrial enlargement , and the narrow superior mediastinum (string) result in the classical egg -on-string appearance . TGA is the most specific heart disease in infants of diabetic mothers. Early management includes an immediate infusion of prostaglandin E1 which keeps the ductus arteriosus patent for improving oxygenation. Rashkind balloon atrial septostomy is a palliative catheter -based intervention that can be done to improve the hypoxic state before definitive surgery. The procedure creates an opening in the atrial septum which allows better inter-circulatory mixing of the blood. Jatene arterial switch procedure is the definitive surgery. Most infants with TGA do not survive till adulthood without corrective surgery.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Below is the chest X-ray image obtained for a neonate on day 7 of life who developed heart failure later\037. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The classic "egg on end" appearance on this chest X-ray image is seen in the transposition of great arteries (TGA). In the chest X-ray image, cardiomegaly with narrow mediastinum gives rise to the classic "egg -shaped heart." The superior mediastinum appears narrow due to the anteroposterior relationship of the transposed great vessels and the radiologic absence of the thymus .501

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Hematuria in children is defined as the presence of at least ______ RBCs per high power field in uncentrifuged urine.
mcqs.explanation: 511 Hematuria in children is defined as the presence of at least 5 RBCs/HPF (high power field ) in uncentrifuged urine. When using commercially available dipsticks (capable of detecting 3-5 RBCs / HPF of urine), the presence of 10 -50 RBCs/�ML suggests an underlying pathology . False -negative results can occur in the presence of • Formalin • High urinary concentrations of ascorbic acid False -positive results , on the other hand, may be seen • With alkaline urine (pH > 8) • Contamination with oxidizing agents such as hydrogen peroxide (used to clean the perineum before obtaining a specimen )

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: An 11 -year-old child was brought to the hospital by his mother with complaints of multiple episodes of passing blood in the urine. Which of the following condition is not associated with this symptom ?
mcqs.explanation: Hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) presents with acute -onset microscopic hematuria not recurrent gross hematuria. Causes of recurrent gross hematuria: • Alport's syndrome: hereditary nephritis • Thin glomerular basement membrane disease • IgA nephropathy : Berger's disease • Idiopathic hypercalciuria/hyperuricosuria • Sickle cell nephropathy (papillary necrosis)

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 6-year-old girl with urinary complaints was brought to the hospital by her parents. On further enquiry, they mention a history of skin lesions 5 weeks back. Low C3 levels are found during her investigations. Immunofluorescence microscopy reveals a "lumpy -bumpy " pattern of immunoglobulin and complement deposits on the glomerular basement membrane. Which of the following is not typically associated with this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Urinary complaints with a history of skin lesions (pyoderma ) point towards a likely diagnosis of glomerulonephritis . Results of complement study and immunofluorescence microscopy also correlate with this diagnosis. Frothy urine is due to proteinuria, which is a feature of nephrotic syndrome. Classic features of nephritic syndrome/glomerulonephritis : • Cola coloured urine (hematuria) • Oliguria • Hypertension • Facial or body edema512

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Akshay, accompanied by his father, presents to the OPD with complaints of cola-coloured urine and facial puffiness for 3 days. He has a history of fever with a sore throat that resolved 2 weeks back. Which of the following findings is consistent with the diagnosis of post -streptococcal glomerulonephritis ?

options.a: C3 level increases and ASO level increases
options.b: C3 level decreases and ASO level increases
options.c: C3 level decreases and ASO level decreases
options.d: C3 level increases and ASO level decreases

mcqs.explanation: C3 level decreases and ASO level increases in acute post -streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN). Acute PSGN is a classic example of an acute nephritic syndrome characterized by the sudden onset of gross hematuria, oedema , hypertension , and renal insufficiency . It follows infection of the throat or skin by certain nephritogenic strains of group A \031-hemolytic streptococci - • 1 to 2 weeks after an antecedent streptococcal pharyngitis or • 3 to 6 weeks after streptococcal pyoderma

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a characteristic feature of hematuria associated with glomerulonephritis ?
mcqs.explanation: Hematuria associated with glomerulonephritis is typically painless . Hematuria from within the glomerulus is often associated with brown-, cola-, or tea-colored urine. Urine analysis reveals RBC casts and deformed urinary RBCs (particularly acanthocytes ).

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 7-year-old boy presents with decreased urine output for 3 days. He has a history of sore throat 2 weeks back. On examination, he is hypertensive with pitting pedal oedema . The diagnosis is concluded as post -streptococcal glomerulonephritis . Which of the following is true about this condition?

options.d: Renal biopsy is indicated in severe impairment of renal function.

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette of oliguria, pedal edema and hypertension point towards glomerulonephritis . Severe impairment of renal functions in a background of post -streptococcal glomerulonephritis is an indication for renal biopsy . Indications for renal biopsy in glomerulonephritis: • Presence of acute renal failure or nephrotic syndrome • Absence of evidence of streptococcal infection • Presence of normal complement levels • Persistence of hematuria and proteinuria, diminished renal function, and/or a low C3 level for more than 2 months after the disease onset Serum triglycerides (Option A) are elevated in nephrotic syndrome, not in nephritic syndrome. The acute phase generally resolves within 6 to 8 weeks . Although urinary protein excretion and hypertension usually normalize by 4-6 wk after onset , microscopic hematuria (Option B) can persist for 1 to 2 years after the initial presentation . The serum C3 level (Option C) is significantly reduced in >90% of patients in the acute phase , and returns to normal 6-8 weeks after onset .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 6-year-old boy with a previously diagnosed renal disorder is brought to your OPD with the following reports for a second opinion. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The findings mentioned are characteristic of post -streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN). Findings in PSGN:513 • Light microscopy: Enlarged , pale glomeruli with diffuse mesangial proliferation and an increase in the mesangial matrix. Polymorphoneutrophil (PMN) infiltration in the early stages . • Immunofluorescence : "Lumpy-bumpy " deposits of immunoglobulin and complement on the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) and in the mesangium. • Electron microscopy: Electron -dense deposits , or "humps," are observed on the epithelial side of the GBM. The image given below depicts the microscopic picture of PSGN. It shows glomerular hypercellularity due to intracapillary leukocytes . Neutrophilic infiltration is present and is marked with purple hematoxylin stain (black arrows).Other options : Idiopathic rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis : • Light microscopy: Crescents develop in several forms of glomerulonephritis (are a characteristic response to the deposition of fibrin in Bowman's space ) • Electron microscopy: No deposits Focal segmental glomerulonephritis : • Light microscopy: Focal sclerotic lesions • Electron microscopy: Foot process fusion Minimal change disease : • Light microscopy: Normal • Electron microscopy Effacement of foot process

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: An 8-year-old boy presented with cola-coloured urine, decreased urine output , and facial puffiness for 3 days. He had a history of skin infection 4 weeks back. On examination, he is found to be hypertensive . His serum C3 levels are low and ASO levels are increased . What is the appropriate step in the management of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: 514 The features of hematuria, oliguria, facial oedema present with a history of skin infection points towards the diagnosis of post -streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN). Results of complement study and ASO levels also support this diagnosis. Supportive conservative therapy is the best step in the management of PSGN. Management of PSGN is directed at treating the acute effects of renal insufficiency (sodium restriction and prescribing diuretics - usually with intravenous furosemide ) and hypertension . Although a 10 -day course of systemic antibiotic therapy with penicillin is recommended to limit the spread of the nephritogenic organisms, antibiotic therapy does not a\037ect the natural history of acute PSGN. Note : Steroids and cyclosporine are not used in the management of PSGN.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Sarthak , a 7-year-old boy, was brought to the emergency department by his parents with complaints of blurred vision and severe headache since today morning . They mentioned an episode of fits 2 hours back following which they rushed him to the hospital . On further enquiry, it was elicited that the child had decreased urine output for 5 days with cola coloured urine. He was hypertensive with bilateral pitting pedal oedema . The doctor remembered that Sarthak has a glomerular disorder warranting him multiple prior ward admissions and his existing condition could be a possible complication of the same. All of the following are commonly seen as a complication of this disorder except -
mcqs.explanation: The given features of oliguria, hematuria, pedal edema and hypertension are likely of glomerulonephritis . The complication of hypertensive encephalopathy is seen in this case due to symptoms of seizure , blurred vision and severe headache . Hyperkalemia and left ventricular failure are also common complications of glomerulonephritis while bleeding diasthesis is not a complication of glomerulonephritis . Acute complications of glomerulonephritis result from hypertension and acute renal dysfunction - • Hypertension is seen in 60% of patients and is sometimes associated with hypertensive encephalopathy and intracranial bleeding . • Acute renal failure can occur, which may require treatment with dialysis . Other potential complications include the following : • Heart failure • Hyperkalemia • Hyperphosphatemia • Hypocalcemia • Hyponatremia • Acidosis • Seizures • Uremia

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 9-year-old boy presents with gross hematuria 2 days after an episode of diarrhoea. The serum C3 levels are normal . Light microscopy demonstrates focal and segmental mesangial proliferation and increased mesangial matrix in the glomerulus . What is the probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Gross hematuria following a gastrointestinal infection , associated with normal C3 levels , in a male patient is suggestive of immunoglobulin A nephropathy (Berger nephropathy ). • IgA nephropathy is the most common chronic glomerular disease in children.515 • Focal and segmental mesangial proliferation and increased mesangial matrix are seen in the glomerulus . • It is characterized by a predominance of IgA within mesangial glomerular deposits in the absence of systemic disease . • It is seen more often in males. • Gross hematuria occurs within 1-2 days of onset of an upper respiratory or gastrointestinal infection (in contrast to the long latency period observed in acute post -streptococcal glomerulonephritis ). • It can be associated with loin pain. • Normal serum levels of C3 in IgA nephropathy (help to distinguish this disorder from PSGN). • Serum IgA levels have no diagnostic value because they are elevated in only a few paediatric patients .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A child developed dark coloured urine and flank pain 2 days after an upper respiratory tract infection . The physician suspects IgA nephropathy . What is the location of cellular injury in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The location of cellular injury in IgA nephropathy (Berger nephropathy ) is the deposition of IgA antibodies in the mesangial cell . Mesangial cells are directly exposed to the circulation; therefore , they are affected in diseases characterized by the deposition of immune complexes . Mesangial cell diseases : • IgA nephropathy • IgM nephropathy • Mesangioproliferative glomerulonephritis • Class II lupus nephritis • Diabetic nephropathy Note : In IgA nephropathy gross hematuria often occurs within 1-2 days of onset of an upper respiratory or gastrointestinal infection. In contrast, a longer latency period of about 1-2 weeks is observed in acute postinfectious glomerulonephritis .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: ANCA-positive , pauci-immune glomerulonephritis include -
mcqs.explanation: Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA)-associated vasculitis is categorized into 3 distinct forms: • Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA; formerly Wegener granulomatosis) • Microscopic polyangiitis (MPA) • Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis , formerly called Churg–Strauss syndrome (CSS)516 Kidney biopsies typically demonstrate crescentic glomerulonephritis with little or no immune complex deposition . ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV) comprises a group of multi-systemic diseases affecting small-to-medium-sized vessels . It is characterized by the presence of ANCA with specificity for either proteinase -3 (PR3 ) or myeloperoxidase (MPO). Absence or paucity of immune complex deposits in vessel walls is very characteristic, hence the name "pauci-immune vasculitis."

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: An 8-year-old girl presented with complaints of cough , hemoptysis and swelling of both legs . Urinalysis was notable for hematuria and proteinuria. Serum anti-GBM antibodies were positive . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The diagnosis is Goodpasture disease (anti-GBM antibody disease ). Anti–glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) antibodies are diagnostic . "Goodpasture syndrome" is characterized by pulmonary haemorrhage and glomerulonephritis and "Goodpasture disease " is used for those patients with glomerulonephritis , pulmonary hemorrhage, and anti-GBM antibodies. It is caused due to autoantibodies directed against type IV collagen , which is present in the alveoli and glomerular basement membrane. Currently, the preferred term for both conditions is "anti-GBM antibody disease ". Other options along with the pathogenesis of glomerular diseases : • IgA nephropathy - mesangial cell disease due to immune complex deposition • Minimal change disease - epithelial cell disease due to flattening of podocytes

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 9-year-old boy has swelling of knee joints and non-blanching rashes as seen in the picture . Urine examination reveals hematuria +++ and proteinuria +. Microscopic analysis of his renal biopsy specimen is most likely to show which of the following finding?
mcqs.explanation: The boy in this clinical scenario has characteristic features of Henoch–Schonlein purpura (HSP). The renal biopsy in this patient will show mesangial proliferation with mesangial deposition of IgA • HSP is a common small-vessel vasculitis in childhood . • It is characterized by a purpuric rash and commonly accompanied by arthritis and abdominal pain. • About half the patients with HSP develop renal manifestations , which vary from asymptomatic microscopic hematuria to severe , progressive glomerulonephritis . • The nephritis associated with HSP usually follows the onset of the rash • The pathogenesis of HSP nephritis appears to be mediated by the deposition of polymeric immunoglobulin A (IgA) in glomeruli .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: All are features of Alport syndrome except -
mcqs.explanation: 517 Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss (not conductive hearing loss) is a feature of Alport syndrome (AS). AS or hereditary nephritis is a genetic disease (most have X-linked inheritance) caused by mutations in the genes coding for type IV collagen , a major component of the basement membranes. Clinical features of Alport syndrome: • Hematuria: All patients have asymptomatic microscopic hematuria. Recurrent episodes of gross hematuria may be seen 1-2 days after an upper respiratory infection . • Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss (not conductive ) • Ocular abnormalities: anterior lenticonus , macular flecks , corneal erosions • Proteinuria: Progressive proteinuria, often exceeding 1 g/ 24 hrs, is common by the 2nd decade of life .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old boy presented with dark coloured urine. Urinalysis was notable for macroscopic hematuria and heavy proteinuria. His father is a known case of Alport syndrome. What defect is responsible for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: A defect in type IV collagen , a major component of the basement membrane, is responsible for Alport syndrome. Alport syndrome is a genetically heterogeneous disease , 85% is X-linked and the rest may be autosomal recessive or autosomal dominant.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: All of the following syndromes are associated with renal disease except _______.
mcqs.explanation: Sinding–Larsen–Johansson syndrome is an insertional periostitis at the inferior pole of the patella (not associated with Renal disease ).Lowe syndrome Oculocerebrorenal syndrome: Hypotonia, renal disease Denys –Drash Syndrome Associated withWilm's tumor: Early-onset renal failure with renal mesangial sclerosis , m ale pseudohermaphroditism Alport syndrome Bilateral sensorineuralhearin g loss, renal disease Sinding–Larsen–Johansson s yndrome Periostitisat the inferior pole of the patella

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Microalbuminuria is defined as a urinary albumin excretion rate of _______.
mcqs.explanation: Microalbuminuria is defined as a urinary albumin excretion rate of 30–300 mg/24 hrs.518 Here, the presence of albumin in the urine is above the normal level but below the detectable range for the urine-dipstick methods . It is commonly associated with glomerular hyperfiltration and blood pressure elevation. In adults , persistent microalbuminuria indicates diabetic nephropathy and is also a predictor of cardiovascular and renal disease . In children, microalbuminuria is associated with obesity and predicts the development of diabetic nephropathy in type 1 diabetes mellitus.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old boy presents with facial puffiness and frothy urine. Upon investigating, his urine was positive for proteins with no hematuria and no RBC casts. To conclude the diagnosis of nephrotic syndrome, the range of proteinuria is defined as >_____ mg/m2/hr and urine protein:creatinine ratio of >________.
mcqs.explanation: The currently accepted definitions of "nephrotic range proteinuria" include : • Urine protein: creatinine ratio > • Urine protein > 40 mg/m2/hr • Urine protein 3+ or 4+ in dipstick test As a consequence of the large urinary loss of protein, the patient develops hypoalbuminemia (< 2.5 g/dL) and gross edema .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: It is expected to see all of the following clinical features in a 5-year-old boy with nephrotic syndrome except -
mcqs.explanation: Hematuria is not a usual feature of nephrotic syndrome. It is a feature of nephritic syndrome. However, occasionally it is seen in the FSGS variant of nephrotic syndrome as well . Classic features of nephrotic syndrome: • Nephrotic range proteinuria ( >40mg/m2/hr urine protein: creatinine ratio >2) • Hypoalbuminemia (<2.5 g/dL) • Edema • Hyperlipidemia (cholesterol > 200 mg/dL) • Hypercoagulability

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in children?
mcqs.explanation: The commonest cause of nephrotic syndrome in children is minimal change disease . (85% of cases ). The glomeruli appear almost normal on microscopy, hence the name. Immunofluorescence microscopy are negative , and electron microscopy shows effacement of the epithelial cell foot processes . Treatment: Steroids ; 95% of patients respond .519 Other options : • Membranous nephropathy is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in the elderly ; it is a rare cause of nephrotic syndrome in children. • Alport syndrome or hereditary nephritis: All patients have asymptomatic hematuria; progressive proteinuria is common only by the 2nd decade of life and can be severe enough to cause nephrotic syndrome. This nephrotic syndrome is not common in children. • IgA nephropathy presents more commonly as an acute nephritic syndrome or with asymptomatic hematuria. It presents with nephrotic syndrome quite rarely.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old child was brought to the hospital with complaints of progressive swelling around the eyes , abdomen and feet for 2 weeks. On investigating , his urine was positive for 4+ proteinuria with absent hematuria. A spot urine protein: creatinine ratio was reported to be 2.5. His serum albumin was 2.3 g/dL and serum creatinine was 0.5 mg/dL. Serum cholesterol and triglyceride levels were also elevated . A diagnosis of nephrotic syndrome was concluded . Which of the following correctly mentions the aetiology of its most common variant in children?
mcqs.explanation: Nephrotic syndrome is concluded as the diagnosis here because of the symptoms of anasarca and proteinuria. A spot urine protein:creatinine ratio >2, low serum albumin levels , and hyperlipidemia marked by high cholesterol and triglyceride levels , further add to this diagnosis. Minimal change disease is the commonest cause of nephrotic syndrome in children and constitutes 85% of all paediatric cases . The etiology is due to the flattening of foot processes (podocytes ) of epithelial cells (seen on electron microscopy). This finding is marked in the image given below .• Here, the glomeruli appear normal or show a minimal increase in mesangial cells and matrix. • It is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in children. • Epithelial cells , in conjunction with the basement membrane, allow the filtration of plasma solutes but block the passage of cells and plasma proteins . Hence , this epithelial cell disease , disrupts the filtration barrier , resulting in proteinuria. • More than 95% of children with minimal change disease respond to corticosteroid therapy . Causes of epithelial cell injury: • Minimal change disease520 • Membranous nephropathy • Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis • Class V lupus nephritis • Diabetic nephropathy

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a cause of hypercoagulability in nephrotic syndrome?

options.a: Vascular stasis due to hemoconcentration and intravascular volume depletion
options.b: Increase in hepatic production of fibrinogen
options.c: Urinary loss of antithrombin III and protein S

mcqs.explanation: Increased (and not decreased ) platelet number and aggregability cause hypercoagulability in nephrotic syndrome. Hypercoagulability in nephrotic syndrome is due to all of the following factors: • Vascular stasis due to hemoconcentration and intravascular volume depletion • Increase in hepatic production of fibrinogen • Urinary loss of antithrombin III and protein S • Increased platelet number and aggregability

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 4-year-old boy presents with facial oedema that has now progressed to total body swelling involving the face , abdomen, scrotum, and feet . Urinalysis revealed protein 4+ and serum cholesterol was also elevated . What is the initial treatment of choice ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical picture and investigations are highly suggestive of minimal change nephrotic syndrome and the initial treatment of choice is corticosteroids such as prednisolone . Minimal change nephrotic syndrome is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome. It is seen in ages 2-6 years with a clinical picture of nephrotic syndrome, that is, heavy proteinuria, oedema , hypoalbuminemia and hyperlipidemia . They may be asymptomatic or can present with peripheral oedema . Renal biopsy is not required for confirmation and treatment can be initiated if the child fits the standard clinical picture of nephrotic syndrome. They show excellent response to steroid therapy with prednisone or prednisolone . A daily dose of 2mg/kg (max 60mg) for 6 weeks followed by an alternate dose of 1.5mg/kg (max 40mg) for the next 6-8 weeks is recommended . Alternative drugs used in steroid -dependent patients , frequent relapsers , steroid -resistant patients , and those with severe corticosteroid toxicity are as follows : • Cyclophosphamide • Calcineurin inhibitors: Cyclosporine and Tacrolimus • Mycophenolate • Levamisole • Rituximab (chimeric monoclonal antibody against CD20 )

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Steroid -resistant nephrotic syndrome is defined as failure to achieve remission after _____ weeks of corticosteroid therapy .
mcqs.explanation: 521 Steroid -resistant nephrotic syndrome is defined as failure to achieve remission after 6 weeks of corticosteroid therapy . According to the latest Indian Society of Pediatric nephrology (ISPN) guidelines , it is defined as the absence of remission despite 6-weeks therapy with prednisolone at daily dose of 60mg/m2

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A child suffering from steroid -dependent nephrotic syndrome is brought to the OPD for vaccination. Which of the following is true about vaccination in this child?

options.a: All live vaccines under NIS can be given as per schedule
options.b: All killed vaccines under NIS can be given
options.c: Only pneumococcal vaccine should be given to the child in acute phase
options.d: Live vaccines are contraindicated in the child's sibling

mcqs.explanation: In a child with steroid -dependent nephrotic syndrome, all killed vaccines can be given. Option A: Live virus vaccines are administered with caution in children receiving corticosteroid therapy. They can be given to patients in whom the prednisone dose is below 1mg/kg daily or 2mg/kg on alternate days. If the patient is receiving corticosteroid -sparing agents (cyclophosphamide , cyclosporine ), live virus vaccines are contraindicated . Option C: Only live vaccines are contraindicated in this child. Full pneumococcal vaccination (with the 13 -valent conjugate vaccine and 23-valent polysaccharide vaccine) and influenza vaccination can be given annually to the child and their household contacts . Option D: Immunization of siblings/healthy household contacts with live vaccines is necessary to reduce the risk of infection transmission to the immunosuppressed child. Direct exposure to the gastrointestinal /respiratory secretions of the household contacts is avoided for about 3-6 weeks after vaccination . Minimal change nephrotic syndrome is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome. It is characterized by heavy proteinuria, edema , hypoalbuminemia , and hyperlipidemia . The diagnosis is confirmed by performing a urinalysis and urine protein: creatinine ratio. Nephrotic range proteinuria is proteinuria greater than 3.5 g per 24 hours (3+ or 4+) or a urine protein : creatinine ratio exceeding 2. The recommended initial treatment for nephrotic syndrome is a daily dose of 2mg/kg (max 60mg) of prednisolone for 6 weeks followed by an alternate dose of 1.5mg/kg (max 40mg) for the next 6-8 weeks . Definitions regarding the course of nephrotic syndrome: • Frequently relapsing nephrotic syndrome: \0342 relapses in 6 months or 3 or more relapses in 12 months. • Steroid -dependent nephrotic syndrome: Relapse during steroid tapering or within 2 weeks of d iscontinuation . • Steroid resistance : Failure to achieve remission despite therapy with daily prednisolone for 6 weeks Alternative drugs used in steroid -dependent patients , frequent relapsers , steroid -resistant patients , and those with severe corticosteroid toxicity are cyclophosphamide , calcineurin inhibitors: cyclosporine and Tacrolimus, mycophenolate , levamisole , and rituximab (a chimeric monoclonal antibody against CD20 ).

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Congenital nephrotic syndrome is defined as nephrotic syndrome manifesting ______.

options.b: At birth or within 3 months of life
options.c: At birth or within 6 months of life
options.d: At birth or within 1 year of life

mcqs.explanation: 522 Congenital nephrotic syndrome is defined as nephrotic syndrome manifesting at birth or within 3 months of life . It may be • Primary : Due to inherited disorders caused by mutations in NPHS 1, NPHS 2, WT1 , or LAMB2 . • Secondary: Due to in utero infections like cytomegalovirus infection , toxoplasmosis , syphilis , HIV infection , hepatitis B virus or hepatitis C virus HCV infection , infantile systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), or mercury exposure.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: An 11 -year-old boy with a chronic hepatitis B infection develops nephrotic syndrome. What would be the most likely pathology encountered in renal biopsy of this child?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario suggests that the pathology would be membranous nephropathy . Membranous nephropathy can be secondarily caused by Hepatitis B infection . Membranous nephropathy : Membranous nephropathy is a rare cause of nephrotic syndrome in children. • It is classified as the primary, idiopathic form, where there is an isolated renal disease , or secondary, where nephropathy is associated with other identifiable systemic diseases or medications • In children, secondary form is far more common. The most common etiologies of secondary form are systemic lupus erythematosus or chronic infections . Among the latter, chronic hepatitis B infection and congenital syphilis are the best characterized and recognized causes .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Finnish-type congenital nephrotic syndrome is caused by a mutation in the _____ gene .
mcqs.explanation: Finnish type congenital nephrotic syndrome is a steroid -resistant nephrotic syndrome caused by a mutation in the nephrin gene (NPHS 1). • Affected infants usually present at birth with edema caused by massive proteinuria. • They are delivered with a large placenta (>25% of the infant's weight ). • There is severe hypoalbuminemia , hyperlipidemia , and hypogammaglobulinemia . • Prenatal diagnosis can be made by elevated maternal and amniotic \032-fetoprotein levels .Gene Name Inheritan ce Renal disease NPH S1 Nephrin Recessive Finnish-type congenital neph rotic syndrome NPH S2 Podocin Recessive Focal segmental glomeruloscl erosis (FSGS) WT1 Wilms tumor-suppressor g ene Dominan t Denys –Drash syndrome with diffuse mesangial sclerosis Fr asier syndrome with FSGS523 Gene Name Inheritan ce Renal disease LMX 1B LIM -homeodomain protein Dominan t Nail–patella syndrome

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: FSGS is caused by mutations in the _____ gene .
mcqs.explanation: • focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) is caused by mutation in NPHS2 (podocin) gene . • Steroid resistant nephrotic syndrome is usually caused by FSGS (in 80% of cases ). • In FSGS, glomeruli show lesions of mesangial cell proliferation and segmental scarring that are both focal (present only in a proportion of glomeruli ) and segmental (localized to \0341 intraglomerular tufts ). • FSGS is associated with a 50% risk for end-stage kidney disease .Gene Name Inheritan ce Renal disease NPH S1 Nephrin Recessive Finnish-type congenital neph rotic syndrome NPH S2 Podocin Recessive Focal segmental glomeruloscl erosis (FSGS) WT1 Wilms tumor-suppressor g ene Dominan t Denys –Drash syndrome with diffuse mesangial sclerosis Fr asier syndrome with FSGS LMX 1B LIM -homeodomain protein Dominan t Nail–patella syndrome524

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: During her antenatal ward rounds, an intern noticed a USG report indicating the presence of just one kidney in the fetus . Which of the following association would be expected to be seen in the baby?
mcqs.explanation: 530 The presence of a single umbilical artery can be expected to be seen in the case of a baby with unilateral renal agenesis . Renal agenesis occurs secondary to a defect of the Wolffian duct , ureteric bud, or metanephric blastema . It is often discovered during the course of an evaluation for other congenital anomalies (VACTERL syndrome). Its incidence is increased in newborns with a single umbilical artery. The contralateral kidney undergoes compensatory hypertrophy . Some children also have contralateral vesicoureteral re\037ux. Most males have an ipsilateral absent vas deferens . NOTE: VACTERL syndrome - Vertebral defects, imperforate Anus, Congenital heart disease , Tracheo-Esophageal fistula , Renal and Limb defects

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 10 -month-old female is brought to the clinic with a 102 \260 F fever for 2 days. The mother says that she also cries during urination. The history is significant for similar episodes in the past which were treated with antibiotics. Urine analysis shows nitrite-positivity and gram-negative bacteria are seen on urine microscopy. Which of the following anomaly is most commonly associated with this child's condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of recurrent urinary tract infection . The most common anomaly associated with this condition in children is vesicoureteral reflux (VUR). VUR usually is congenital and often familial. It is more common in females . It occurs when the submucosal tunnel between the mucosa and detrusor muscle is short or absent. The image below shows VUR grading

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A pediatrician suspects vesicoureteric reflux in a girl with a history of recurrent urinary tract infections . What is the investigation of choice to confirm this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Voiding cystourethrogram (VCUG) is the investigation of choice for vesicoureteral reflux. Recurrent febrile urinary tract infections in a child should raise the suspicion of an anatomical defect like vesicoureteric reflux as the cause . Compared to other investigations, a VCUG provides more anatomic information. It can demonstrate :531 • Vesicoureteral reflux • Duplex collecting system • Ectopic ureter • Paraureteral (bladder ) diverticulum • Bladder outlet obstruction • Signs of voiding dysfunction , such as a spinning top urethra

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the first-line imaging investigation done in a child presenting with an episode of UTI?
mcqs.explanation: In a child presenting with an episode of urinary tract infection (UTI), initial imaging should be ultrasonography of the kidneys, ureters , and bladder . A voiding cystourethrogram is indicated only if the ultrasound study is abnormal , the patient has atypical features or after a recurrent febrile UTI. DMSA (dimercaptosuccinic acid) scan may be done after 4–6 months of acute infection as it may help to locate and delineate the scarring

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common cause of urinary tract infection in children?
mcqs.explanation: Urinary tract infections in children are most commonly caused by the following : • Escherichia coli (Most common) • Klebsiella species • Proteus species • Staphylococcus saprophyticus • Enterococcus • Adenovirus and other viral infections (cause cystitis and gross hematuria)

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A mother is concerned that her 1-year-old daughter has been having repeated episodes of UTI since birth. The pediatrician ordered a voiding cystourethrogram , which revealed reflux of urine into the upper collecting systems without any dilation. Under which grade of vesicoureteral reflux will this presentation be classified ?
mcqs.explanation: Vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) severity is graded according to the appearance of the urinary tract on a contrast voiding cystourethrogram . It is classified into 5 grades (Grade I to V ): Grading of vesicoureteral re\037ux: • Grade I- VUR into a non-dilated ureter • Grade II - VUR into the upper collecting system without dilation • Grade III - VUR into the dilated ureter and/or blunting of calyceal fornices.532 • Grade IV - VUR into a grossly dilated ureter • Grade V - Massive VUR, with significant ureteral dilation and tortuosity and loss of the papillary impression.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Ashi, a 12 -year-old girl presented with features of hematuria, headache , and blurring of vision. Her past history is significant for recurrent UTI. On examination, she was found to have a BP of 150/110 mmHg. Investigations revealed mild renal scarring and urine analysis showed broad casts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.c: Posterior urethral valve with chronic renal failure
options.d: Reflux uropathy with chronic renal failure

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of reflux uropathy with chronic renal failure. The pathogenesis of vesicoureteral reflux is as follows :Loss of renal parenchyma and renal scarring reduces renal function significantly . This renal insufficiency leads to renin-mediated hypertension and further progresses to end-stage renal disease . Re\037ux nephropathy remains a common cause of hypertension in children.533 Broad casts or renal failure casts are associated with end-stage renal disease .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common cause of abdominal mass in neonates ?
mcqs.explanation: Multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK ) is the most common cause of an abdominal mass in the newborn but is mostly non-palpable at birth. In most cases , it is discovered incidentally during prenatal sonography. In some patients , the cysts are identified prenatally , but the cysts regress in utero, and no kidney is identified on imaging at birth. MCDK is usually unilateral and generally not inherited , unlike polycystic kidney disease (PKD). Contralateral hydronephrosis is present in 5-10% of patients .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Komal, a high school student developed a fever after she came back from a trip with her friends. She also complained about pain while urinating. She says she has been having these episodes frequently for the past few years. Her father and her grandfather are a known case of cystic kidney disease . Her urine analysis is indicative of UTI with hematuria. Renal ultrasound was done and its findings are shown below . Which of the following chromosomes are associated with this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of multiple cysts seen on the ultrasound(image) along with a positive family history point towards the diagnosis of autosomal-dominant polycystic kidney disease . Chromosomes 16 and 4 are associated with this condition. Autosomal-dominant polycystic kidney disease inheritance:Chromosome invo lved Chr16 short arm Chr 4 long arm Gene PKD 1 PKD 2 Protein encoded Polycystin 1 Polycystin 2 Function Transmembrane glycoprot ein Non-selective cation channel Seen in 85 % –15 %

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions is not associated with the lesion seen in the image?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a horseshoe kidney. It is not associated with the posterior urethral valve. Horseshoe kidney is the most common congenital anomaly of the kidneys. Horseshoe kidney is caused due to the fusion of the lower poles of the kidney. The lower border of the kidneys usually lie in front of L3 vertebra due to arrest of ascent . The common associations of horseshoe kidney are: • Vesicoureteral reflux • Wilms tumor • Multicystic dysplastic kidney • Turner 's syndrome534

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A young girl presents with the complaints of continuous dribbling of urine. However, she also voids normally. Her parents tell you that she had never been totally dry since her birth. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical presentation of a young girl with continuous dribbling of urine, despite normal voiding, strongly suggests the diagnosis of an ectopic ureter. An ectopic ureter refers to a condition where the ureter drains outside the bladder . It is more common in females and opens either into the urethra below the sphincter or into the vagina . Hence , they present with constant urinary dripping all day, even though the child voids regularly (paradoxical incontinence). The terminal part of the ureter is frequently narrowed, leading to hydroureteronephrosis . Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are common due to urinary stasis. In males, ectopic ureters usually enter the posterior urethra above the external sphincter , hence they are usually continent and most patients present with UTI or epididymitis . Investigations include renal ultrasound (USG), voiding cystourethrogram (VCUG), and renal scan to assess function. USG shows a hydronephrotic kidney or dilated upper pole and ureter. If there is a satisfactory function, the recommended treatment options are ureteral reimplantation into the bladder or ureteroureterostomy . The poor function may require partial or total nephrectomy . Other options : Option B: A ureterocele is a cystic dilation of the terminal ureter , typically obstructive due to a small ureteral opening . In childhood , they commonly present with infections . Larger ureteroceles can cause obstruction at the bladder neck. Option C: Congenital megaureter (dilated ureter ) presents UTI, urinary stones , hematuria, and flank pain because of urinary stasis. Option D: Vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) is characterized by the retrograde flow of urine from the bladder to the ureter and kidney. They usually present with recurrent attacks of UTI.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 3 yr old male child with left flank pain is diagnosed to have an acute UTI. On USG, the left ureter was found to be duplicated . The most probable site of the opening of ectopic ureter will be?
mcqs.explanation: Opening of the ectopic ureter in male (most to least common) : • Posterior urethra (prostatic) above the external sphincter • Seminal vesicle • Prostatic utricle • Ejaculatory duct • Vas deferens

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A newborn is being evaluated for anuria . Imaging reveals renal agenesis and pulmonary hypoplasia . The delivery was complicated due to oligohydramnios. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: 535 A newborn infant with anuria , renal agenesis , and pulmonary hypoplasia , with a history of oligohydramnios, is suggestive of Potter's sequence Potter's sequence is characterized by the triad of: • Renal agenesis • Oligohydramnios • Pulmonary hypoplasiaOption B: Pierre–Robin syndrome: micrognathia, retrognathia, glossoptosis . Option C: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia: It can present with pulmonary hypoplasia but other features like renal agenesis , anuria will not be seen . Option D: CHARGE syndrome: Coloboma of the eye , Heart anomaly, choanal Atresia, Retardation, Genital and Ear anomalies.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Antenatal hydronephrosis due to PUJ obstruction is defined as the anteroposterior diameter of the renal pelvis of more than _____ in the third trimester.
mcqs.explanation: Anteroposterior diameter of the renal pelvis of >7 to 7.5 mm in the third trimester denotes antenatal hydronephrosis due to pelvic ureteric junction (PUJ) obstruction.
