mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of acute bronchial asthma which was most likely precipitated by timolol. Timolol is a non-selective beta -blocker that reduces intraocular pressure by decreasing aqueous formation. It precipitates bronchial asthma in susceptible individuals by beta -2 blockade. Betaxolol is a beta -1 selective blocker that is used in glaucoma and has a lower propensity to precipitate bronchial asthma. Latanoprost is a prostaglandin (PGF-2 alpha) analog and does not precipitate bronchial asthma. Acetazolamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor and does not precipitate bronchial asthma.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with diabetic macular edema developed glaucoma. Which of the following drugs would you consider giving last?
mcqs.explanation: Prostaglandin analogs are the last drugs to be considered in this patient since macular edema is one of their side effects . Adverse effects of PGF 2alpha analogs are: • Blurring of vision • Macular edema (especially in aphakic patients ) • Eyelash hypertrichosis • Iris pigmentation (Heterochromia iridis) • Peri-orbital fat depletion

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line medical therapy in a patient with open-angle glaucoma?
mcqs.explanation: The most appropriate first-line medical therapy for open -angle glaucoma is PGF-2 alpha analogs. They act by increasing the aqueous outflow . They have largely replaced beta -blockers and can be considered as first-line agents for open-angle glaucoma because of their following properties : • Once-daily dosing • Low incidence of systemic side effects • Potent IOP-lowering effect When the use of PGF-2 alpha analogs or beta -blockers is contraindicated , topical carbonic anhydrase inhibitors or alpha-2 agonists are used .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You diagnose a patient with primary open -angle glaucoma and decide to prescribe a PGF2 alpha analog. Which of the following drugs would you not choose ?
mcqs.explanation: 153 Dinoprost is a derivative of natural PGF-2 alpha. It is indicated in the termination of pregnancy and post -partum hemorrhage and not for use in glaucoma. PGF2 alpha analogs that are used topically for the treatment of glaucoma are: • Latanoprost • Bimatoprost • Travoprost • Tafluprost

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antiglaucoma medications is unsafe in infants?
mcqs.explanation: The use of brimonidine is unsafe in infants. It is an alpha-2 agonist that can cross the blood-brain barrier . This may result in CNS depression and apnoea in neonates . Therefore it is contraindicated in children less than 2 years. �o 2 agonists, through the activation of G-protein coupled receptor activation, inhibit the activity of adenylate cyclase . This reduces cAMP and hence reduces aqueous humor production by ciliary action.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following can be administered orally for the treatment of glaucoma?
mcqs.explanation: Acetazolamide and methazolamide are carbonic anhydrase inhibitors that can be used orally in the treatment of glaucoma. Acetazolamide can also be administered intravenously. Dorzolamide and brinzolamide are topical carbonic anhydrase inhibitors. Dichlorphenamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor approved for the treatment of familial periodic paralysis.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Intravenous mannitol is used in ____?
mcqs.explanation: Intravenous mannitol is used for the treatment of acute attacks of glaucoma. Uses of mannitol are: • To reduce cerebral edema and intracranial pressure • Enhancement of urinary excretion of salicylates , barbiturates, bromides, and lithium • Diagnosis of bronchial hyperreactivity (inhalation) • Antihemolytic urological irrigation during transurethral procedures • Treatment of acute attacks of glaucoma.154

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs should not be given in a patient prone to developing angle -closure glaucoma?
mcqs.explanation: Clozapine is an atypical antipsychotic having significant anticholinergic action. Drugs having significant anticholinergic action should be avoided or used with extreme caution in patients prone to developing acute angle-closure glaucoma. The anticholinergic action results in the relaxation of the sphincter pupillae muscle . This results in the iris coming in contact with the lens and thereby obstructing the movement of the aqueous from the posterior to the anterior chamber. This results in bulging of the iris and further leads to the obliteration of the narrow iridocorneal angle . This blocks the outflow of aqueous precipitating an acute attack of glaucoma.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: While examining a patient using a corneal esthesiometer , you find that corneal sensations are decreased . Which of the following drugs could have led to this adverse effect ?
mcqs.explanation: Corneal hypoesthesia is a side effect of ocular beta -blockers. For topical use in glaucoma, beta -blockers with no/minimal membrane-stabilizing action are used . This is the reason why propranolol is not formulated for ocular use . It has the highest membrane-stabilizing action and causes maximum corneal hypoesthesia if used .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presents with severe eye pain to the ophthalmology OPD. On examination, there is circumcorneal congestion and the IOP is 40 mm Hg. Which of the following drugs should not be administered immediately to this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of acute angle-closure glaucoma. Pilocarpine should not be administered immediately in this condition. During an acute attack, the elevated pressure in the anterior chamber causes pressure -induced ischemic paralysis of the iris. Pilocarpine would be ineffective in this phase . Once the IOP is reduced by other agents and reperfusion is achieved , pilocarpine can be used to overcome the pupillary block. Pilocarpine is avoided in conditions like pseudo -exfoliation syndrome, phacomorphic glaucoma, and aqueous misdirection syndrome as it may exacerbate pupillary block in such cases . Topical beta -blockers, alpha-2 agonists and prostaglandin analogs can be used to decrease the IOP initially at presentation . Oral or intravenous acetazolamide can also be used .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who is on treatment for glaucoma presented with the following finding during his routine follow -up. Which of the following drugs can cause this adverse effect ?
mcqs.explanation: The patient has presented with lid retraction which is most likely caused by the use of apraclonidine. It is a congener of clonidine that has primary �o 2 agonist action and a subsidiary �o 1 agonist action. Adverse effects like mydriasis and lid retraction are common with apraclonidine.155 Brimonidine is also a congener of clonidine with more �o 2 selectivity . Mydriasis and lid retraction are uncommon with this agent . Timolol and latanoprost do not cause lid retraction.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The ophthalmologic examination of a patient who is on anti-glaucoma drugs shows the following finding. Identify the drug that might have resulted in this adverse effect .
mcqs.explanation: The ophthalmological examination shows a pearly white opacity of the lens suggestive of cataract. Anticholinesterase agents like echothiophate and cholinergic agonists like pilocarpine are known to be associated with cataract formation.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who is on anti-glaucoma therapy presents with corneal findings as shown in the image below . This finding is most commonly observed with which of the following drugs?
mcqs.explanation: The bilateral whorl-like pattern of cream-colored lines on the cornea seen in the image is called cornea verticillata or vortex keratopathy. It is observed with the use of netarsudil . It is usually mild and reversible and not associated with any significant visual abnormalities. Netarsudil is approved for lowering intraocular pressure in patients with open -angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension . Other causes of corneal verticillata are: • Fabry's disease • Amiodarone • Chloroquine • Hydroxychloroquine • Indomethacin • Phenothiazines.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient on treatment for glaucoma presented with complaints of floaters and flashing lights . He complains of seeing a dark grey curtain move across his field of vision. Which of the following can lead to this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of retinal detachment . It is associated with the use of miotics i.e., both cholinergic agonists and anticholinesterase agents . Miotics produce ciliary body contraction which can lead to altered forces at the vitreous base resulting in retinal tears. Hence , they are to be used with extreme caution in patients who are at risk of developing retinal detachment .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Your friend who is on treatment for glaucoma tells you that she feels her eyes look prettier than before . On examination, you notice increased iris pigmentation and eyelash hypertrichosis . Which of the following drugs is associated with this effect ?
mcqs.explanation: Bimatoprost is a PGF-2 alpha analog. PGF-2 alpha analogs are associated with eyelash hypertrichosis and iris hyperpigmentation.156 Bimatoprost is approved for topical application in the treatment of eyelash hypotrichosis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the most probable diagnosis in a patient with a dilated pupil not responsive to 1% pilocarpine?
mcqs.explanation: The most appropriate answer would be a pharmacological block. Antimuscarinic will occupy the receptors and results in non-responsiveness to pilocarpine . In diabetic third nerve palsy , the dilated pupil is due to the loss of innervation to constrictor pupillae . Muscarinic receptors on constrictor pupillae will be intact resulting in miosis by pilocarpine . In Adie's tonic pupil , there is denervation hypersensitivity . Pupil responds to even lower concentrations of pilocarpine . Uncal herniation causes pressure on the third nerve leading to ipsilateral mydriasis. But muscarinic receptors are intact and thus the pupil responds to pilocarpine .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following cannot be used to decrease intraocular pressure in glaucoma?
mcqs.explanation: Dexamethasone is a long-acting glucocorticoid and is not used to decrease the intraocular pressure in glaucoma. Acetazolamide , apraclonidine, and mannitol are used in lowering intraocular pressure in glaucoma.157

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old male was rushed to the ER with complaints of chest pain for the past 45 minutes and was started on isosorbide mononitrate. How does this drug act?
mcqs.explanation: Nitrates like isosorbide mononitrate act by increasing the concentration of the second messenger cGMP. They are used to relieve angina and cause vasodilation.164

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is not used in angina?
mcqs.explanation: Sacubitril is not used in angina. Sacubitril is a neprilysin inhibitor, approved for use in the treatment of heart failure.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with Prinzmetal angina is administered isosorbide mononitrate and is noticed to have symptomatic relief . What is the mechanism of action of nitrate in this case?

options.c: Increased left ventricular end diastolic volume

mcqs.explanation: The mechanism of action of nitrates in prinzmetal angina is endothelium -independent coronary vasodilatation. Prinzmetal angina occurs due to vasospasm of the coronary arteries. Nitrates relax the smooth muscles of epicardial coronary arteries and relieve coronary artery spasm. In the case of stable angina, the primary mechanism of action of nitrates is preferential dilatation of veins (by increasing cGMP). Venous dilatation leads to a decrease in the venous return to the heart (preload ). This decreases the ventricular end-diastolic volume and thereby a decrease in myocardial oxygen consumption. The diastolic perfusion pressure (aortic blood pressure in diastole - left ventricular pressure in diastole ) is increased .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old patient who suffers from prinzmetal angina requires a formulation of nitroglycerine which has the most rapid onset of action. Which of the following formulations of nitroglycerin can be administered to the patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The sublingual route of administration has a very rapid onset of action (1-3 mins). The onset of action is more rapid when administered as a spray when compared to a tablet . The sublingual route is used for the termination of attacks. Oral extended -release capsule and transdermal patch are used for prophylaxis . The onset of action is approximately \03060 min.165 Topical nitroglycerine ointment can be used to provide symptomatic relief in patients with anal fissures .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In patients with angina, nitroglycerine should not be administered by which of the following routes ?
mcqs.explanation: Intramuscular nitroglycerin should be avoided due to severe pain in the injection area in patients with angina. Sublingual and intravenous nitroglycerin can be used for acute effects . Oral extended -release capsules are available for prophylactic use in angina.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man suspected to have cyanide poisoning is brought to the ER. The medical officer stabilizes the patient and asks the nurse to bring an ampoule of amyl nitrite. By which of the following routes is this drug administered ?
mcqs.explanation: Amyl nitrite is administered via the inhalational route for acute relief in angina and cyanide poisoning. Amyl nitrite is a highly volatile liquid available in glass ampoules . Its unpleasant odor and very short duration of action have made its use obsolete in angina.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An 18-year-old boy was brought to the ER in an unconscious state . His coworker states he works in a factory manufacturing pesticides . Based on this, the medical officer suspects cyanide poisoning and administers sodium nitrite. Which of the following is the mechanism of action of this drug in this case?
mcqs.explanation: The mechanism of action of sodium nitrite as an antidote for cyanide poisoning is by the development of methemoglobinemia . Cyanide binds to the cytochrome oxidase (complex IV ) of the electron transport chain (ETC), thereby blocking it. When sodium nitrite is administered , it releases the nitrite ion. This ion binds to hemoglobin to form methemoglobin . The methemoglobin so formed, has a high affinity for the cyanide ion and binds to it, thus , detaching it from the cytochrome oxidase . This regenerates active cytochrome normalizing the function of ETC. The cyanide ion with methemoglobin forms cyanmethemoglobin . Sodium thiosulphate is administered for the elimination of this compound . The thiosulfate forms thiocyanate ion with the cyanide and this is readily excreted .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man came to the casualty with complaints of abdominal pain. On examination, it is noted that the pain radiates from the loin to the groin of the patient . The resident wants to administer a drug to the patient for symptomatic relief . Which drug is not effective in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Abdominal pain radiating from loin to groin is suggestive of renal colic. Nitrates are not effective in renal colic. In renal colic, NSAIDs, and morphine are used for acute pain relief . Due to the short time of action of nitrates, their clinical efficacy as relaxants in genitourinary system is quite low. Therapeutic Uses of nitrates are: • Angina pectoris166 • Acute coronary syndrome • Myocardial infarction • CHF • Biliary colic • Esophageal spasm

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who is on treatment for angina, presents to you with erectile dysfunction . You decide against prescribing sildenafil because the patient is being treated with _____
mcqs.explanation: The patient would be on nitrates for angina and thus should not be prescribed sildenafil as sildenafil causes dangerous potentiation of nitrate action resulting in severe hypotension . The combination of the two drugs has a synergistic action on the intracellular cGMP levels that can result in uninhibited vasodilation and a precipitous fall in blood pressure . Hence , the use of sildenafil is a contraindication when on nitrates.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old male, who works in a factory that manufactures explosives , came to the OPD with a peculiar complaint. He says that he gets headaches and feels transient dizziness every Monday after his weekend off. Exposure to which compound is likely to produce his symptoms ?
mcqs.explanation: The patient is most likely suffering from Monday disease which is associated with exposure to nitroglycerin. Continuous exposure to high levels of nitrates can occur in the chemical industry, especially where explosives are manufactured . When contamination of the workplace with nitrate compounds is severe , workers find that upon starting their week , they suffer headaches and transient dizziness. After a day or so back at work, tolerance develops . Over the weekend , when exposure to the chemicals is reduced , tolerance disappears , so symptoms recur each Monday.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 60 year old male is on verapamil for angina. Which of the following is not an adverse effect of this medication?
mcqs.explanation: Tachycardia is not an adverse effect of verapamil. Verapamil has a direct negative chronotropic effect on the heart. It is more likely to cause bradycardia because of its significant cardio depressant action. Any reflex stimulation of heart due to peripheral vasodilation is effectively countered by the direct effect . Common side effects of verapamil include headache , gingival hyperplasia , and constipation .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Nifedipine acts by blocking ____calcium channels.
mcqs.explanation: Nifedipine acts by blocking L-type calcium channels.167 Verapamil, diltiazem, and dihydropyridines block L-type calcium channels by binding to alpha 1 subunit. Verapamil was the first clinically used calcium channel blocker.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which among the following is a newer dihydropyridine with additional N-type calcium channel blocking activity?
mcqs.explanation: Cilnidipine is a novel dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that blocks both L- and N-type calcium channels. Blockage of N-type calcium channels results in the reduction of sympathetic activity. It provides additional anti-hypertensive action without inducing reflex tachycardia.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is more likely to precipitate angina?
mcqs.explanation: Amongst the given calcium channel blockers, nifedipine is more likely to precipitate angina. Nifedipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker having a rapid onset and short duration of action. It results in an abrupt decrease in blood pressure resulting in reflex tachycardia. Increased contractility leads to an increase in O2 demand which may precipitate angina. Option A: Amlodipine and extended -release preparations of nifedipine do not cause a steep fall in blood pressure and subsequent activation of sympathetic tone. Therefore, they are less likely to precipitate angina. Options C and D: Verapamil and diltiazem have relatively less action on peripheral vascular smooth muscles . They have a direct inhibitory effect on cardiac tissue causing negative ionotropic effect (verapamil > diltiazem).

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with polycystic kidney disease came to the ER with complaints of severe headache . An NCCT brain was taken and it showed subarachnoid hemorrhage. Which of the following drugs is most appropriate for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Nimodipine is the most appropriate drug that can be given to this patient . Nimodipine is indicated in cerebral vasospasm following subarachnoid hemorrhage. It has a high affinity for cerebral blood vessels and appears to reduce mortality after subarachnoid hemorrhage.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Peripheral edema seen with the use of calcium channel blockers is primarily due to which of the following mechanisms?

options.a: Reduced glomerular filtration rate and renal blood flow
options.b: Increased hydrostatic pressure in the capillaries of lower extremeties
options.c: Decreased oncotic pressure due to loss of plasma proteins in urine
options.d: Precapillary constriction and post capillary dilation

mcqs.explanation: Calcium channel blockers induced peripheral edema is most likely due to increased hydrostatic pressure in the capillaries of the lower extremities . The increased hydrostatic pressure occurs due to precapillary dilation and reflex postcapillary constriction.168

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old athlete complained of chest pain during his practice sessions . He is diagnosed to be suffering from exertional angina and is prescribed atenolol . Which of the following changes are not caused by this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Atenolol is a beta -blocker which increases the coronary collateral circulation, thereby increasing the blood flow towards the ischaemic region. This provides relief in exertional angina. Beta-blockers decrease the heart rate, contractility , and arterial blood pressure . These effects are beneficial by decreasing the myocardial O2 demand. A decrease in heart rate increases the time available for myocardial perfusion .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs can be used to balance the undesirable effects of beta -blockers in angina?
mcqs.explanation: Beta-blockers cause an increase in end-diastolic volume and ejection time. These effects can be balanced using nitrates by preferential venous dilatation, thus reducing preload . Beta-blockers also block the baroreceptor mediated reflex tachycardia caused by nitrates due to vasodilation. Options A and D: Verapamil and diltiazem are not combined with beta -blockers as they can cause additive suppression of SA node and AV nodal conduction . Option C: Ivabradine is a pacemaker I(f) "funny" current inhibitor. Its addition does not reverse the undesirable effect but only adds to the bradycardia caused by beta blockers.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is associated with coronary steal phenomenon ?
mcqs.explanation: Coronary steal phenomenon is seen with dipyridamole . In patients with partial obstruction of coronary vasculature, a region of ischemia develops in the myocardium. In the absence of drugs, arterioles in the ischemic areas are usually maximally dilated as a result of local compensatory mechanisms. When dipyridamole is administered , it acts as a nonselective arteriolar dilator. It can only dilate the vessels of the normal myocardium as the vessels of the ischemic myocardium are already maximally dilated . This diverts (steals ) the blood away from the ischemic myocardium towards the normal myocardium. This is termed as coronary steal phenomenon .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about ranolazine is not true?

options.a: It is recommended as first-line treatment for acute angina.

mcqs.explanation: Ranolazine is not recommended as a first-line agent for acute angina. It is approved as a second -line agent for chronic angina. Ranolazine acts by reducing late sodium current (INa) that facilitates calcium entry via the sodium-calcium exchanger. The reduction in intracellular calcium concentration results in decreased cardiac contractility . Additionally , it also reduces cardiac fatty acid oxidation and stimulates glucose metabolism . It results in a small decrease in HBA1c , thus improving glycemic control.169 It is metabolized by CYP3A4 and hence should not be used with CYP3A4 inhibitors such as macrolides , imidazole antibiotics, and HIV protease inhibitors. The most frequent side effects are dizziness, headache , nausea, and constipation . Hypotension is uncommon.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a rho-kinase inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Fasudil is a selective RhoA /rho-kinase inhibitor. The Rho kinases (ROCK) are a family of enzymes that inhibit vascular relaxation. Their excessive activity has been noted in coronary spasm and pulmonary hypertension . Inhibiton of these enzymes results in vascular relaxation. Option B: Ranolazine acts by reducing late sodium current (INa). This reduces calcium entry via the sodium-calcium exchanger. Option C: Trimetazidine is a partial fatty acid oxidation (pFOX ) inhibitor. Option D: Nicorandil is an agonist of KATP channels

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs causes activation of K+-ATP channels?
mcqs.explanation: Nicorandil causes activation of K+-ATP channels. This leads to the hyperpolarization of the smooth muscle cells leading to vasodilatation. It also has nitrate like cGMP dependent action. Nicorandil dilates both arteries and veins leading to a decrease in afterload and preload of the heart. Molsidomine , isosorbide dinitrate, and nitroglycerin are nitrates. They do not act on K-ATP channels.170

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the half-life of digoxin?
mcqs.explanation: The plasma half-life of digoxin is around 40 hours (36-40 hours).Digitoxin Digoxin Oral absorption Very good (90-100 %) Good (60-80%) Plasma protein bindi ng 95%(t1/25-7 days) 25%(t1/240 hrs) Elimination Hepatic metabolis m Renal excretion (by glomerul ar filtration) Dose adjustment in Liver failure Kidney failureTherapeutic levels of digoxin in the range of 0.5-0.8 ng/ml are beneficial . An increase in levels >1.2 ng/mL is associated with increased mortality.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Digitalis inhibits Na+/ K+ ATPase pump in cardiac muscle cell membrane. How does this lead to its positive inotropic effect ?

options.a: By decreasing activity of Na+/Ca++ exchanger causing decreased influx of sodium and decreased efflux of Ca++
options.b: By decreasing efflux of Na+ leading to less negative resting membrane potential and opening of voltage gated Ca++ channels on the T tubules
options.c: By increasing intracellular Na+ causing increased efflux of Na+ and increased influx of Ca++ through Na+/Ca++ exchanger
options.d: By increasing intracellular Na+ decreasing the activity of Ca++ pump in the sarcoplasmic reticulum

mcqs.explanation: The positive ionotropic effect of digitalis is due to decreased activity of Na+/Ca2+ exchanger causing a decreased influx of sodium and decreased efflux of Ca2+. Digitalis selectively binds and inhibits the Na+/ K+ATPase pump of myocardial fibers which normally pushes Na+ outside and brings K+ inside. When this pump is inhibited , there is an intracellular accumulation of Na+ ions. This results in a relative decrease in the expulsion of Ca2+ ions via the Na+-Ca2+ exchanger (NCX) leading to the accumulation of calcium inside the cells resulting in increased contractility .178

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The action of digoxin will not be affected in which of the following patients ?
mcqs.explanation: The action of digoxin is not affected in chronic liver disease . Option B: Electrolyte disturbances like hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia , and hypercalcemia increase digitalis toxicity. Option C: Digoxin is excreted unchanged primarily by kidneys by glomerular filtration. Therefore, dose adjustment of digoxin has to be done in renal failure. Option D: Chances of arrhythmias increases manifold in post -MI duration. Hence , it is generally avoided post-MI as digitalis itself causes arrhythmias.Digitoxin Digoxin Oral absorption Very good (90-100 %) Good ( 60-80%) i/v also Plasma protein bindi ng 95% 25% Elimination Hepatic metabolis m Renal excretion (by glomerul ar filtration) Dose adjustment in Liver failure Kidney failure

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not increase the risk of digoxin toxicity ?
mcqs.explanation: Digoxin toxicity is not increased by hyperkalemia. In hyperkalemia, the ATPase alpha subunit is dephosphorylated , which is the binding site of digoxin. This reduces it's binding and effect . Therefore, hyperkalemia does not increase digoxin toxicity . Factors predisposing digoxin toxicity : • Hypokalemia (more digoxin binds to the Na+/K+ ATPase) • Hypercalcemia (increases the risk of arrhythmia ) • Hypomagnesemia (Mg++ is a co-factor for Na+/K+ ATPase) • Renal failure (for digoxin)

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient is to be started on digoxin therapy for heart failure. Despite already being on another drug, dose adjustment of digoxin is not necessary for this patient . Identify this drug.
mcqs.explanation: Levosimendan does not increase digitalis toxicity and hence would not require dose adjustment of digoxin. It is a combined Ca2+ channel sensitizer (troponin C binding) and PDE3 inhibitor.179 Digoxin is metabolized by P-glycoprotein and drugs that inhibit it increase the plasma levels of digoxin and may result in toxicity . The drugs that increase digoxin toxicity are: • Amiodarone • Quinidine • Propafenone • Verapamil • Captopril • Erythromycin • Gentamycin • Ranolazine

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the most appropriate treatment for a patient with severe digoxin toxicity ?
mcqs.explanation: The most appropriate treatment for severe digoxin toxicity is purified Fab fragments of digitalis antibodies (Digibind). It neutralizes the digoxin action and its dosage is based upon the total dose of digoxin ingested . Option A: KCl infusion is indicated in mild toxicity as hyperkalemia decreases the binding of digoxin by dephosphorylating Na/K ATPase pump . In acute severe poisoning, potassium is not indicated as it may already be high in plasma. Potassium is also not indicated when a higher degree of AV block is present . Options B and C: Quinidine and propafenone are not indicated in arrhythmias caused by digoxin.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An ECG is done for a patient suspected to have digoxin toxicity . Which of the following would you not expect to see on the ECG?

options.b: Paroxysmal atrial tachycardia with fast ventricular rate

mcqs.explanation: Digoxin can cause either paroxysmal or non-paroxysmal atrial tachycardia with variable A-V block but not a fast ventricular rate. Regularisation of atrial fibrillation with complete A-V block and junctional or ventricular escape rhythm can occur because of the blockade of A-V conduction . Due to the blockade of AV node by digoxin, it is contraindicated in WPW syndrome. Common arrhythmias associated with digoxin toxicity : • Ventricular bigeminy • Atrioventricular junctional rhythm • Bidirectional ventricular tachycardia • Premature ventricular depolarizations .180

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with heart disease presents to the emergency with severe vomiting and blurry vision and mentions that he sees a greenish -yellow tinge over all objects . He then develops ventricular arrhythmia . What would be the most appropriate drug for immediate management?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of digoxin toxicity . Xanthopsia i.e., yellowing of vision is characteristically seen in this condition. Lignocaine (and phenytoin ) has the least effect on AV nodal conduction and is the most appropriate drug for the treatment of digoxin-induced arrhythmias. Option A: Procainamide and other class IA anti-arrhythmic agents are not indicated in digoxin toxicity because of their inhibitory effects on AV nodal conduction . Option C: Atropine is used for atrial bradyarrhythmias associated with digoxin toxicity . Option D: Propranolol is used for atrial tachyarrhythmias associated with digoxin toxicity .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient is diagnosed with congestive heart failure. Which of the following is not prescribed to prevent progression and revert cardiac remodelling ?
mcqs.explanation: Digoxin has no role in preventing cardiac remodelling . It increases cardiac contractility and is indicated for symptomatic management of congestive heart failure. Drugs preventing ventricular remodelling: • ACE inhibitors/ ARBS • Beta-blockers • Aldosterone antagonists (spironolactone, eplerenone ) The activation of RAAS and the sympathetic nervous system leads to the remodelling and progressive LV dysfunction . The RAAS activation is prevented by the ACE inhibitors/ARBs and the aldosterone antagonists (spironolactone ), while the overactive sympathetic system is inhibited by the beta -blockers.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You are starting a treatment regimen containing an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor for a patient with congestive heart failure. Which of the following is true regarding its role in the regimen?

options.a: It is the drug of choice unless contraindicated
options.b: Used as an alternative to diuretics
options.c: It is a substitute for digitalis
options.d: Used as adjuncts only in resistant cases

mcqs.explanation: 181 ACE inhibitors and ARBs are the first choice drugs in congestive heart failure (CHF) unless contraindicated. Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS ) activation is pivotal in the development of the symptoms and disease progression in CHF. ACE inhibitors and ARBs afford symptomatic as well as disease -modifying benefits in CHF by causing vasodilation, retarding/preventing ventricular hypertrophy , myocardial cell apoptosis and fibrosis.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs can overcome an increase in heart rate and renin release seen in patients with CHF?
mcqs.explanation: Metoprolol is a selective \0351 blocker. Beta blockade reduces the sympathetic stimulation of the SA node and thus reduces the heart rate. In the same way, \0351 receptors in the JG apparatus are also inhibited by metoprolol , and thus , renin release is reduced . Option A: Minoxidil is a K+ channel opener that was earlier used in hypertensive emergencies for its vasodilatory action on blood vessels . This has no effect on renin release and heart rate can increase due to reflex sympathetic stimulation. Option C: Metolazone is a thiazide diuretic that can be used even in severe renal failure. Option D: Milrinone is an inodilator. It increases cardiac contractility and causes vasodilation by inhibiting the enzyme PDE3.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You see the cardiologist prescribe a non-selective beta -blocker for a patient with congestive heart failure. He mentions that the drug has several beneficial effects . Identify the drug.
mcqs.explanation: The drug most likely being discussed is carvedilol which is a non-selective beta -blocker approved for use in mild to severe CHF. Additional actions of carvedilol: • Blockade of alpha receptors • Blockade of L-type calcium channels • Antioxidant effect • Antiproliferative effect Options A and B: Propranolol and pindolol are non-selective beta -blockers but they are not approved for use in CHF. Option C: Metoprolol is approved for use in CHF but it is a cardioselective beta -blocker.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: \035 blocker therapy is to be started on a patient with congestive heart failure. Which of the following statements is false about the therapy ?

options.a: The drugs should be started at optimum doses
options.b: The dose should be gradually increased over weeks
options.c: Special precautions should be taken in cases of NYHA class III and IV
options.d: Carvedilol and metoprolol are the preferred drugs

mcqs.explanation: Beta-blockers are not started with optimum doses in patients with heart failure.182 Beta-blocker therapy in CHF requires caution, proper patient selection , and observance of several guidelines such as: • Generally , the starting dose is less than 1/8th (low dose ) of the target dose is and then titrated upwards slowly over weeks (doubling every 4 weeks ) • The greatest utility of beta -blocker therapy has been seen in mild to moderate CHF (NYHA I, II ) • There is no place for beta -blockers in decompensated heart disease • Carvedilol, bisoprolol , and metoprolol are commonly used beta -blockers in CHF.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You are going through the treatment chart of a patient with chronic congestive heart failure. Which of the following drugs will you not expect to see ?
mcqs.explanation: Adrenaline is used for the treatment of acute decompensated heart failure, not chronic congestive heart failure. Drugs used in chronic congestive heart failure include : • Diuretics • ACE inhibitors • Angiotensin receptor blockers • Angiotensin receptor -neprilysin inhibitor - sacubitril-valsartan • Hydralazine • Nitrates • Digoxin • Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists • Ivabradine - sinus node inhibitor

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man is brought with complaints of severe chest pain. The ECG shows anterolateral wall MI and echocardiography shows an ejection fraction of 38%. Which of the following is the drug of choice for his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of acute congestive heart failure with systolic dysfunction . Dobutamine is administered as it is the beta -adrenergic agonist of choice for managing this condition. Dobutamine has a well -balanced action with stimulation of cardiac output . It causes less tachycardia than epinephrine and also has an added advantage of a decrease in pulmonary artery wedge pressure . At doses that result in a positive inotropic effect , the beta -1 action on the myocardium predominates . In the vasculature, the alpha-1 effects are counterbalanced by beta -2 effects . The net result is an increase in stroke volume, augmented by a small decrease in systemic vascular resistance , thereby resulting in a decrease in afterload .183

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about nesiritide ?

options.b: It can be used in decompensated CHF
options.d: It causes loss of Na+ in the urine

mcqs.explanation: Nesiritide is available for intravenous administration only as it is a peptide and is digested by peptidases in the GIT . Nesiritide is a recombinant brain natriuretic peptide (BNP). It causes natriuresis and vasodilation. It has a half life of 18 minutes . It is approved to relieve dyspnoea and other symptoms in acute refractory decompensated CHF.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which enzyme degrades BNP?
mcqs.explanation: Brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) is degraded by neutral endopeptidase . Natriuretic peptides : • Atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) • Brain natriuretic peptide • C-type natriuretic peptide Nesiritide is a recombinant BNP approved to relieve dyspnoea and other symptoms in acute refractory decompensated CHF.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Isosorbide dinitrate is indicated for congestive heart failure in combination with which of the following vasodilators?
mcqs.explanation: Isosorbide dinitrate (ISDN) is indicated in combination with hydralazine for CHF. Hydralazine is a direct vasodilator and its mechanism of action is not known. It also reduces nitrate tolerance. The combination of ISDN and hydralazine showed mortality benefits in a specific group of population (African-Americans).

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with congestive heart failure develops hyponatremia. Which oral vasopressin receptor antagonist will you prescribe for him?
mcqs.explanation: Tolvaptan is an oral vasopressin receptor antagonist. It preferentially binds to V2 receptors over V1a receptors . It has been used in decompensated CHF patients to restore normal sodium levels . Conivaptan is also a vasopressin receptor antagonist that is administered intravenously and binds to both V2 and V1a receptors with similar affinity. It is more commonly used for hyponatremia rather than CHF. Oral conivaptan is not yet available.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the mechanism of action of milrinone?
mcqs.explanation: 184 Milrinone acts by inhibition of the enzyme phosphodiesterase -3 (PDE 3). The PDE-3 inhibitors decrease cellular cAMP degradation , resulting in increased levels of cAMP. This results in positive ionotropic and chronotropic action of the heart. It also dilates veins and arteries thereby decreasing the preload and afterload .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A trial is being conducted to determine the efficacy of a myofilament calcium sensitizer in patients with heart failure. Which among the following is the drug likely being studied ?
mcqs.explanation: Levosimendan is a myofilament calcium senstizer . Calcium sensitizers bind and induce a conformational change in thin-filament regulatory protein troponin C. Thus increasing the sensitivity of contractile myofilaments to calcium. The result is an increased force of contraction for a given cytosolic calcium concentration. Option B: Omapatrilat is a dual ACE and neprilysin inhibitor that failed clinical trials due to increased risk of angioedema . Option C: Sacubitril is a neprilysin inhibitor approved in combination with valsartan for CHF. Option D: Enoximone is a PDE-3 inhibitor.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Sacubitril is a new drug approved for chronic heart failure. The mechanism of action of sacubitril is:
mcqs.explanation: Sacubitril is a neutral endopeptidase (neprilysin) inhibitor. Sacubitril is a prodrug that is activated to sacubitrilat. It can inhibit the enzyme neprilysin (neutral endopeptidase ), which is responsible for the degradation of atrial and brain natriuretic peptides (reduction of blood volume). Therefore, it increases the levels of atrial and brain natriuretic peptides and lowers blood pressure . In 2015 , the FDA approved the use of sacubitril in combination with valsartan , at a ratio of 1:1, for the treatment of chronic heart failure.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not used in heart failure?
mcqs.explanation: Trimetazidine is not used in heart failure. Trimetazidine is a newer antianginal drug that is a pFOX inhibitor which partially inhibits the fatty acid oxidation pathway in the myocardium. This decreases the oxygen requirement of the heart. Nesiritide (natriuretic peptide ), sacubitril (neprilysin inhibitor) and metoprolol (beta -blocker) are used in the treatment of heart failure.185

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line medication for an elderly patient with hypertension?
mcqs.explanation: The most appropriate first-line antihypertensive among the given drugs is chlorthalidone . Thiazide diuretics are recommended as one of the first-line antihypertensive drugs for elderly patients without any comorbidities . Among them, guidelines recommend chlorthalidone over hydrochlorothiazide because of its longer duration of action. First-choice drugs used in the treatment of hypertension in patients without any comorbidities include : • ACE inhibitors or ARBs: No evidence of superiority of one class over the other. However, ACE inhibitors have a higher risk of side effects like dry cough and angioedema . • Calcium channel blockers: Extended -release , long-acting dihydropyridines are preferred . • Thiazide diuretics : Chlorthalidone is usually preferred to hydrochlorothiazide . Loop diuretics like furosemide and torsemide are less effective antihypertensives than thiazides . They are not indicated for the routine management of hypertension . In the presence of any associated conditions or comorbidities , the first choice drugs for the treatment of hypertension would be as follows :Comorbidities First choice drugs for hyperte nsion DiabetesChronic kidney disea se with proteinuria ACE inhibitors or ARBs Angina Beta-blockers or calcium cha nnel blockers Heart failure ACE inhibitors and alpha+be ta blockers (e.g., carvedilol) Benign prostatic hyperplasia �o 1 blockers Pregnancy Labetalol Atrial fibrillation Diltiazem or verapamil

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Chlorthalidone is being prescribed to an elderly patient for the management of hypertension . Which of the following side effects would not be expected in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Thiazide diuretics cause hypokalemia. Other side effects of thiazide diuretics include hyperuricemia , hypercalcemia , hyperglycemia and erectile dysfunction . All thiazide diuretics cross the placenta and therefore should be avoided in pregnancy.194

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient on lithium therapy developed hypertension . He was started on thiazides for hypertension . After few days, he developed coarse tremors and other symptoms suggestive of lithium toxicity . Explain the likely mechanism of this interaction.

options.a: Thiazide inhibits the metabolism of lithium
options.b: Thiazides act as an add on drug to lithium
options.c: Thiazides increase the tubular reabsorption of lithium
options.d: Thiazides cause water loss therby increase lithium levels

mcqs.explanation: Thiazides act by increasing the tubular rabesorption of lithium. Thiazide use is accompanied by sodium loss which is compensated in a few days by increased reabsorption of Na+ in the proximal tubule . The kidney handles both lithium and Na+ in the same way. Thus, along with Na+ reabsorption, there will be an increase in the reabsorption of lithium also, resulting in decreased excretion of lithium.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A hypertensive patient on losartan requires an add on drug to achieve his blood pressure goal. Which of the following drugs will not increase the risk of hyperkalemia when added to his current medication?
mcqs.explanation: Indapamide is a thiazide diuretic that increases K+ excretion decreases the risk of hyperkalemia associated with ACE inhibitors or ARBs such as losartan. Option A: Beta-blockers can contribute to K+ retention by decreasing renin release and further reducing aldosterone secretion . Non-selective beta -blockers may also interfere with the cellular uptake of K+ ions. Option B: K+ sparing diuretics like amiloride cause a decrease in K+ excretion and increase the risk of hyperkalemia. Option D: Aliskiren is a direct renin inhibitor and increases the risk of hyperkalemia when combined with losartan.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Long term reduction of blood pressure by thiazide diuretics is mainly by which of the following mechanisms?
mcqs.explanation: Long term reduction of blood pressure by thiazide diuretics is mainly due to a reduction in peripheral vascular resistance . Thiazide diuretics initially decrease extracellular volume by their action on NaCl transporter in distal convoluted tubules in the nephrons. However, the compensatory response from activation of RAAS raises the extracellular volume returns almost to pre-treatment levels after a few weeks .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A diabetic patient is diagnosed with hypertension during his annual health check-up. What is the treatment of choice for him?
mcqs.explanation: ACE inhibitors such as captopril or ARBs can be considered as a treatment of choice in hypertensive patients with diabetes because of the renoprotective action. It benefits diabetic patients by reducing the risk of occurrence and progression of diabetic nephropathy . They are also recommended in patients with CKD irrespective of diabetes status as they can delay the progression of nephropathy . Option A: Thiazide diuretics worsen glycemic control and are not preferred in diabetic patients . Option B: Beta-blockers, especially non-selective blockers, worsen glycemic control.195 Option D: Calcium channel blockers have a neutral effect on glycemic control and can be used in diabetes if ACE inhibitors or ARBs cannot be given.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient is diagnosed with hypertension during routine health evaluation. Which of the following is not recommended as first-line therapy for him?
mcqs.explanation: Alpha blockers like doxazosin are not recommended as first-line therapy for uncomplicated essential hypertension . As per the European Society of Cardiology 2018 guidelines for hypertension , the classes of drugs recommended as first line therapy are: • ACE inhibitors • Angiotensin receptor blockers • Calcium channel blockers • Thiazide diuretics

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which class of antihypertensive drugs has a favourable effect on lipid profile ?
mcqs.explanation: Alpha 1 selective blockers have a favourable effect on lipid profile . They decrease plasma concentrations of triglycerides , total LDL -cholesterol and increase HDL cholesterol . Option A: Thiazides increase plasma concentrations of triglycerides , LDL -cholesterol and total cholesterol . HDL may decrease or remain unchanged . Option B: Non-selective beta -blockers increase triglycerides and decrease HDL levels . However, total cholesterol remains unchanged . Option D: Calcium channel blockers have a neutral effect on the lipid profile .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Methyldopa is primarily used for which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Methyldopa is preferred for chronic hypertension in pregnancy based on its safety and efficacy data for both mother and fetus . Antihypertensives found safe in pregnancy: • Hydralazine • Methyldopa • Dihydropyridine CCBs like nifedipine, amlodipine - however, they should be stopped before labor as they weaken the uterine contractions • Cardioselective beta -blockers and those with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity Antihypertensives to be avoided in pregnancy: • ACE inhibitors, Angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARB)196 • Diuretics • Nonselective beta -blockers • Nitroprusside Labetalol is considered the first-line agent for hypertensive emergency in pregnancy.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman with hypertension , on treatment with methyldopa , comes for routine evaluation. She is found to have a positive Coombs test but is asymptomatic . What is the next course of action for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The best course of action for the patient is close monitoring for any signs or symptoms of hemolysis . Coombs test is done to test the presence of antibodies against Rh antigens on the red blood cells , which result in hemolysis . Positive Coombs test is seen in 20 % of patients who receive methyldopa . However, only 1-5% of such patients develop hemolytic anemia and hence , a positive Coombs test is not a necessary indication for stopping methyldopa treatment . They must be monitored closely and any signs that indicate hemolytic anemia needs prompt discontinuation of the drug.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about clonidine?

options.c: Sedation and xerostomia are common side effects
options.d: It can be combined with vasodilators

mcqs.explanation: Prazosin does not antagonize the effect of clonidine. Prazosin is a selective �o 1 receptor antagonist whereas clonidine is an alpha 2 receptor partial agonist. On oral administration, clonidine stimulates alpha 2A receptors in CNS and results in decreased central sympathetic flow . This causes a decrease in BP. However, on IV administration postsynaptic alpha 2B receptors are activated at higher doses which cause a transient rise in blood pressure . It also causes significant reductions in HDL lipids , apolipoproteins AI and AII . It can be combined with vasodilators but has to be used with caution as potentiation of each other's actions can occur.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presents with complaints of multiple episodes of intermittent palpitations , throbbing headache , and sweating . Blood pressure measured during one of these episodes is 210 /120 mm Hg. The results of 24-hour urinary metanephrines were inconclusive. Which of the following could be used for diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette is suggestive of pheochromocytoma . When first-line investigations like measurement of 24-hour urinary metanephrines are inconclusive, clonidine suppression test is used in the diagnosis of pheochromocytoma. An oral dose of 0.3 mg clonidine is given, followed by the measurement of norepinephrine (NE) concentration at 3 hours. A concentration of >500 pg /mL of NE indicates a positive test . Option A: Phentolamine test is not recommended due to its low sensitivity and specificity . Options B and D: Phenoxybenzamine and prazosin are used in the treatment of pheochromocytoma but have no role in its diagnosis.197

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a selective imidazoline receptor agonist?
mcqs.explanation: Moxonidine is a selective imidazoline (I1 ) receptor agonist. It is indicated as a second line agent in the long-term management of hypertension . It also has weak alpha 2 agonist action. Rilmenidine is another selective imidazoline receptor agonist. Option A: Clonidine is an alpha 2 receptor partial agonist and has additional imidazoline (I1 ) receptor agonist action. But the main mode of action is through alpha 2 agonism. Option B: Methyldopa does not have any action on imidazoline receptors Option D: Brimonidine is a congener of clonidine.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antihypertensives are not used in pregnancy?
mcqs.explanation: Propranolol is a non-selective beta -blocker and is not safe for use during pregnancy. Antihypertensives to be avoided in pregnancy: • ACE inhibitors, ARBS • Diuretics • Nonselective beta -blockers • Nitroprusside Antihypertensives found to be safe in pregnancy: • Hydralazine • Methyldopa • Dihydropyridine CCBs: should be stopped before labor as they weaken the uterine contractions • Cardioselective beta -blockers and those with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity: may be used as a last choice

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs reduces blood pressure primarily by directly decreasing the heart rate?
mcqs.explanation: Propranolol reduces blood pressure by directly decreasing the heart rate. It is a nonselective beta-blocker and blocks the beta 1 receptor of the heart (SA node) thus reducing the heart rate and blood pressure . It also reduces renin secretion by blocking beta 1 receptors in JG cells . Reduction in renin release also contributes to blood pressure reduction . Option B: Prazosin is a selective alpha 1 blocker and dilates both arteries and veins and may cause reflex tachycardia.198 Option C: Alpha methyldopa is a selective alpha 2 receptor agonist. Alpha 2 receptors are autoreceptors present on the presynaptic membrane. On stimulation, central sympathetic discharge is reduced . Alpha methyldopa can indirectly reduce heart rate. Option D: Nitroprusside is a vasodilator and may cause reflex tachycardia.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The blood pressure of a patient undergoing a coronary artery bypass surgery suddenly rises to 170/110mm Hg. Which of the following can you administer intravenously for immediate management?
mcqs.explanation: Clevidipine is a dihydropyridine available for intravenous administration and is indicated in the acute management of hypertension . It has a short half-life (1-2 minutes ) and a rapid onset of action. Option A: Nifedipine is a short-acting dihydropyridine that is no longer indicated in the management of hypertension . The rapid reduction in blood pressure and concurrent surges in sympathetic activity are not desirable . Options B and D: Amlodipine and felodipine are longer-acting dihydropyridines that are available in tablet forms. They are used for long-term treatment of hypertension .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An elderly hypertensive patient is diagnosed with bilateral renal artery stenosis . He is also on treatment for diabetes mellitus . Which among the following drugs would be the most appropriate for him?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, verapamil would be the most appropriate drug for the management of hypertension in the patient as it has no adverse effect on glycemic control. Option A: Efferent arteriolar constriction maintains the glomerular filtration pressure in bilateral renal artery stenosis . ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in bilateral renal stenosis as it can precipitate acute renal failure due to dilation of efferent arterioles and fall in glomerular filtration pressure . Options C and D: Beta-blockers and thiazides can worsen glycemic control and are not suitable in the given scenario.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a direct renin inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Aliskiren is a direct renin inhibitor. Though its efficacy as an antihypertensive is comparable to that of ACE inhibitors, it is not considered a first-line agent due to higher incidence of side effects . Option A: Captopril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor. Option B: Sacubitril is a neprilysin inhibitor indicated in combination with valsartan in chronic heart failure patients . Option D: Losartan is an angiotensin receptor blocker.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect about diazoxide?

options.a: It acts by causing prolonged opening of ATP dependent K+ channels in beta cells
options.c: It can be used to treat patients with insulinoma
options.d: It is used as an antihypertensive agent

mcqs.explanation: 199 Diazoxide causes hyperglycemia , not hypoglycemia . Diazoxide is a potent K+ channel opener and opens up the ATP -sensitive K+ channel and thus prevents depolarization of pancreatic beta cells and subsequent insulin release . It is used in some cases of insulinoma to reduce insulin secretion and prevent hypoglycemia . It was earlier used as an intravenous agent for hypertensive emergencies due to its strong vasodilatory action.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman with preeclampsia and is started on hydralazine. Which of the following statements is incorrect about the drug?

options.b: It causes equal dilatation of both arteries and veins
options.c: Postural hypotension is not a common problem

mcqs.explanation: Hydralazine causes preferential dilatation of arteries over veins. Hydralazine acts directly on vascular smooth muscles . The precise mechanism is unknown but involves a decrease in intracellular Ca2+ concentrations. Option A: It causes a selective decrease in vascular resistance in coronary , cerebral and renal circulation, with a smaller effect in skin and muscle . Option C: Because of preferential dilatation of arterioles over veins, postural hypotension is not a common problem. Option D: Hydralazine-induced vasodilation causes reflex activation of the sympathetic system through baroreceptor-mediated reflexes resulting in increased plasma renin activity.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The efficacy of an antihypertensive agent is being studied in a clinical trial. During the course of the trial, the researchers observed hair regrowth and generalized hypertrichosis in balding patients . What is the mechanism of action of the drug being studied ?

options.a: Closes K+ channels in vascular smooth muscle
options.b: Activates K+ channels in vascular smooth muscle
options.c: Activates Ca2+ channels in vascular smooth muscle
options.d: Closes Ca2+ channels in vascular smooth muscle

mcqs.explanation: The antihypertensive drug with the side effect of excess hair growth is minoxidil and it acts by activating ATP -sensitive K+ channels in smooth muscles . This causes hyperpolarization that results in the relaxation of smooth muscles of arterioles . Topical minoxidil is also used for the treatment of androgenetic alopecia .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presented to the ER with severe headache and vomiting. On examination, the blood pressure was found to be 220 /130 mm Hg and papilledema was also seen . What is the mechanism of the drug of choice for the condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of severe hypertension (blood pressure \030180/\030120 mmHg) with fundoscopic changes (flame haemorrhages and/or papilloedema ) is suggestive of malignant hypertension . The drug of choice is IV nicardipine which acts by calcium channel blockage . Nicardipine blocks the influx of extracellular calcium across the vascular and myocardial smooth muscle cell membranes by blocking the voltage -sensitive calcium channels during depolarization. The decrease in intracellular calcium causes dilation of the coronary and systemic arteries. Other preferred agents for malignant hypertension are clevidipine with labetalol or esmolol . Note : Sodium nitroprusside is no longer the treatment of choice for acute hypertensive problems200

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with malignant hypertension is being managed with sodium nitroprusside infusion. He is at risk of developing all of the following adverse effects except ?
mcqs.explanation: Drug-induced lupus is not an adverse effect of sodium nitroprusside infusion. When nitroprusside is administered at a high rate, it can result in the production of methemoglobin and cyanide . Cyanide is further metabolized to thiocyanate . On prolonged infusion, thiocyanate toxicity can also occur especially in patients with renal failure.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with gout develops hypertension . The uric acid level was found to be elevated . Which of the following is not administered ?
mcqs.explanation: Hydrochlorothiazides are not given to this patient . Gout is a metabolic disease associated with hyperuricemia .Thiazides increase direct urate reabsorption in the proximal renal tubules and are associated with elevated serum uric acid levels and may precipitate gout . Hence , hydrochlorothiazides are not used to treat hypertension in gout patients .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You will counsel patients regarding first-dose phenomenon while prescribing which of the following drugs?
mcqs.explanation: First-dose phenomenon is characteristic of prazosin and patients must be counselled regarding the effects . Within 30-90 minutes of the initial dose of prazosin or when the dosage is increased , there is marked orthostatic hypotension or syncope . This is known as the first-dose phenomenon . After a few initial doses , tolerance develops to this side effect . Initiating low doses at bedtime is recommended to minimize this phenomenon .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs can be given safely in a patient with chronic renal failure?
mcqs.explanation: Telmisartan can be given safely in a patient with chronic renal failure (CRF) because it is mainly cleared from circulation by biliary excretion. Options A and D: Sucralfate is a basic aluminum salt of sucrose sulfate . Sucralfate , aluminum hydroxide , and magnesium hydroxide in CRF patients can cause the accumulation of Al3+ and Mg2+ ions as they are preferentially excreted via the kidney after systemic absorption. Absorbed Al3+ can contribute to osteoporosis , encephalopathy and proximal myopathy in CRF patients . Option B: Candesartan is cleared from circulation by renal and biliary excretion. Hence , plasma clearance is affected by renal insufficiency .201

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Choose the correct pair matching with the diagram:

options.a: A: Loop diuretics , B: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors
options.d: A: Thiazides, B: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors

mcqs.explanation: A is the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle and loop diuretics act on this part of the nephron. B is the distal convoluted tubule and thiazides act on this part of the nephron. Site of action of other diuretics : • Proximal tubule - carbonic anhydrase inhibitors • Collecting ducts and late distal tubule - epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) inhibitors and aldosterone antagonists

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Diuretics acting on which part of the nephron have maximum efficacy ?

options.b: Thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle

mcqs.explanation: Loop diuretics have the maximum efficacy. They act on the thick ascending loop of Henle by blocking Na+-K+-2Cl- symporter. Option A: Although 65% of Na+ is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule , diuretics acting here do not have maximum efficacy . This is because the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle has a great reabsorptive capacity and it absorbs most of the filtrate from the proximal tubule . Options C and D: Diuretics acting distal to the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle have limited efficacy because most of the reabsorption of Na+ (>90%) would have already occurred by the time the tubular fluid reaches there .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about furosemide is true?

options.a: Acute pulmonary edema is an indication
options.b: Acts on the proximal convoluted tubules

mcqs.explanation: Furosemide is indicated in acute pulmonary edema . It is a loop diuretic that acts on the thick ascending loop of Henle and inhibits Na+-K+-2Cl- symporter.209 Loop diuretics have maximum efficacy amongst all the diuretics and are therefore called high ceiling diuretics . They can be given by both the oral and parenteral routes .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man with pulmonary edema is started on furosemide . Which of the following would you not expect after starting the drug?
mcqs.explanation: Furosemide causes metabolic alkalosis. The adverse effects of furosemide (loop diuretics ) are: • Hypovolemia • Hyponatremia • Hypokalemia • Hypocalcemia • Hypomagnesemia • Hyperuricemia • Increased LDL -C and decreased HDL -C • Glucose intolerance - hyperglycemia • Ototoxicity

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: High ceiling diuretics are used in the treatment of all of the following patients except :

options.b: 35-year-old woman with a head injury and cerebral edema

mcqs.explanation: High ceiling diuretics are not used in pulmonary hypertension . High ceiling or loop diuretics have diuretic properties as well as vasodilatory action. • Diuretic property - removing excess fluid in hepatic , renal, and cardiac diseases • Vasodilatory action - quick symptomatic relief of symptoms in LVF and acute pulmonary edema . They are also used for the treatment of chronic CHF. Pulmonary artery hypertension is a condition where there is increased pulmonary vascular resistance . Since nitric oxide is an important regulator of pulmonary vascular resistance , PDE5 inhibitors like sildenafil , vardenafil or tadalafil are primarily used in the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old woman with chronic kidney disease was given a diuretic intravenously. Following administration of the drug, she developed tinnitus and diminished hearing. Which of the following drugs was most likely given?
mcqs.explanation: Ethacrynic acid is the diuretic that was most likely given as it is commonly associated with ototoxicity . Ototoxicity occurs with rapid intravenous infusion and the hearing impairment and deafness are usually reversible. Ethacrynic acid should be used only in patients who are not able to tolerate other loop diuretics .210

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors do not cause :
mcqs.explanation: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors do not cause metabolic alkalosis. They cause metabolic acidosis due to increased bicarbonate excretion Option B: Increased bicarbonate excretion causes urinary alkalinization . Option D: Increased delivery of Na+ to distal tubules causes increased K+ excretion.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following can be administered intravenously?
mcqs.explanation: Acetazolamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor that can be administered intravenously. It is indicated in the acute management of angle-closure glaucoma for the rapid reduction of IOP before surgery. The oral formulation is given for open -angle glaucoma. Options A and B: Brinzolamide and dorzolamide are available only as ophthalmic drops and used in open -angle glaucoma. Option D: Methazolamide is available as an oral formulation and used for open -angle glaucoma.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man joins a pilgrimage to a shrine at a mountain peak. At the summit, he develops tightness in the chest , associated with breathlessness and altered sensorium. Which of the following can be given for symptomatic relief ?
mcqs.explanation: The symptoms are suggestive of acute mountain sickness and acetazolamide can be given for symptomatic relief . It can also be used for prophylaxis.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with a glioblastoma multiforme is started on mannitol as palliative therapy . Which of the following statements is false regarding its diuretic action?
mcqs.explanation: Mannitol is an osmotic diuretic . These drugs do not cause much change in the GFR. Osmotic diuretics cause extraction of fluid from the intracellular compartment resulting in the expansion of the extracellular compartment. The renal blood flow increases and renin release is inhibited . An increase in renal medullary blood flow removes NaCl and urea from the renal medulla thus reducing medullary tonicity. There is not much change in the total GFR.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman presents with complaints of swelling of both feet and of breathlessness on exertion. After evaluation, she was diagnosed with congestive cardiac failure. Which of the following drugs is contraindicated in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Mannitol is contraindicated in patients with cardiac failure. Mannitol is an osmotic diuretic . It acts by extracting water from the intracellular compartments, which results in the expansion of the extracellular fluid . This results in volume overload and frank pulmonary edema in patients with cardiac failure.211

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with hypertension is prescribed chlorthalidone . What would be the effect of this drug on the excretion of electrolytes ?
mcqs.explanation: Chlorthalidone is a thiazide diuretic which increases Na+ and K+ excretion and decreases Ca2+ excretion.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Thiazide diuretics are not used in the treatment of which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Thiazide diuretics are not used in the treatment of hyperlipidemia . They result in an increase in the levels of LDL , total cholesterol , and triglycerides . Option A: Thiazide reduces Ca2+ excretion and is used in the treatment of idiopathic hypercalciuria with nephrocalcinosis . Option C: They are also used in the treatment of edema associated with CHF, hepatic cirrhosis, and nephrotic syndrome. Option D: Thiazides are the mainstay for the treatment of nephrogenic diabetes insipidus . They reduce the kidney's ability to excrete free water. They increase proximal tubular water absorption and block the ability of DCT to form dilute urine.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man with hypertension is prescribed chlorthalidone . Which of the following is unlikely to occur in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Hypocalcemia is unlikely to occur in a patient on chlorthalidone , a thiazide diuretic . Thiazide diuretics do not cause hypocalcemia. They result in hypercalcemia . Thiazide and loop diuretics share similar side effects except that loop diuretics cause Ca2 +excretion (loop loses calcium) whereas thiazides retain Ca2+ and cause hypercalcemia . Other side effects of thiazide diuretics are: • Hypokalemia • Hyponatremia • Hypomagnesemia • Metabolic alkalosis • Hypercalcemia • Hyperuricemia

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 42-year-old man in the nephrology ward has a GFR of less than 30mL /min, suggestive of severe renal failure. What is the best drug that can be given to him?
mcqs.explanation: Metolazone is effective in severe renal failure (GFR<30ml/min).212 Metolazone works primarily in the distal convoluted tubule , rather than the proximal convoluted tubule , and has little effect on GFR and can hence be used in patients with a reduced GFR. Indapamide is another thiazide diuretic that may be effective in severe renal failure.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient has been on lisinopril since being diagnosed with hypertension last year. His blood pressure readings are quite high, and the doctor considers adding a diuretic . Which amongst the following would be the ideal add on drug?
mcqs.explanation: Hydrochlorothiazide would be the ideal add-on drug. It is a thiazide diuretic and causes hypokalemia, which can counteract the hyperkalemia caused by lisinopril, an ACE inhibitor. Aldosterone causes Na+ absorption in the collecting duct and the distal tubule in exchange for H+ and K+. ACE inhibitors decrease angiotensin II levels and thereby , decrease aldosterone levels . Decreased aldosterone level causes K+ retention by reducing the exchange . Therefore, ACE inhibitors cause retention of K+. Diuretics that cause elevation of plasma K+ levels are not suitable for combining with ACE inhibitors. Potassium-sparing diuretics like spironolactone , eplerenone , and amiloride are contraindicated with ACE inhibitors.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 10 -year-old boy is brought with complaints of vomiting and lethargy after swallowing several pills of his father's medication. Serum electrolytes indicate hyperkalemia. Which of the following drugs can you rule out?
mcqs.explanation: Indapamide can be ruled out as it is a thiazide diuretic that causes hypokalemia. The other drugs are potassium-sparing diuretics that cause hyperkalemia. K+ sparing diuretics work by 2 mechanisms: • Blocking the ENaC (epithelial sodium channel) • Triamterene • Amiloride • Aldosterone receptor antagonist • Spironolactone • Eplerenone • Canrenone

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following diuretics do not need to be present in the tubular lumen for pharmacological action?
mcqs.explanation: Aldosterone antagonist acts from the interstitial side of the tubular cells . They do not have to be present in the tubular lumen for their action. Aldosterone antagonists enter the tubular cells from the basolateral membrane. They competitively inhibit the binding of aldosterone to mineralocorticoid receptors .213 Thiazide diuretics , loop diuretics , ENaC inhibitors, and carbonic anhydrase inhibitors have to be present in the lumen for its action. They are all secreted from the proximal tubule into the tubular fluid through the organic anion/ cation transport process . Osmotic diuretics reach the lumen via glomerular filtration.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Canrenone is a metabolite of:
mcqs.explanation: Canrenone is a metabolite of spironolactone . Spironolactone is metabolized completely in the liver. It is also converted to an active metabolite , canrenone that is responsible for more than 50% of the spironolactone action. Spironolactone has a half-life of 1-2 hours while canrenone has a half-life of around 18 hours. Eplerenone is an aldosterone receptor antagonist similar to spironolactone and metabolized primarily by CYP3A4, but no active metabolites have been identified .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 52-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis develops ascites . What is the drug of choice for management ?
mcqs.explanation: The diuretic of choice in a patient with cirrhotic ascites is spironolactone . Spironolactone is a competitive inhibitor of the mineralocorticoid receptor in the late distal tubule and collecting duct of the kidneys. It causes a decrease in sodium reabsorption and potassium excretion in the distal tubule . As a result , spironolactone promotes sodium diuresis but maintains body potassium levels . Spironolactone is particularly helpful in edematous states caused or exacerbated by hyperaldosteronism such as in cirrhotic ascites .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a side effect seen in a patient receiving spironolactone ?
mcqs.explanation: Aldosterone antagonists cause hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis and not metabolic alkalosis. They inhibit H+ secretion in parallel with K+ secretion thus resulting in acidosis. Other side effects are: • Hyperkalemia • Gynecomastia • Renal insufficiency .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an indication for amiloride use ?
mcqs.explanation: Amiloride is not used in the treatment of calcium nephrolithiasis . The condition is sometimes treated with thiazide diuretics but not amiloride.214 Amiloride is a K+ sparing diuretic that acts by inhibiting the epithelial Na+ channels. The various uses of amiloride are: • Edema /hypertension - usually in combination with thiazides • Lithium-induced polyuria - blocks lithium transport into collecting tubules • Cystic fibrosis - aerosolized amiloride enhances mucociliary clearance; acts by inhibiting Na+ absorption from epithelial surfaces and increasing hydration of secretions • Liddle syndrome - hyperactive epithelial sodium channels (ENaC) activity is reduced

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man with asthma presents with complaints of increased urination. The doctor checks that he has been taking theophylline and counsels that it could be a side effect . What is the mechanism of action causing diuresis ?
mcqs.explanation: The diuretic effect of theophylline is due to the blockade of adenosine (A1) receptors . Theophylline is a methylxanthine drug that acts by - • Inhibition of phosphodiesterase enzyme (PDE) • PDE3 inhibition - relaxation of bronchial smooth muscle • PDE4 inhibition - inhibition cytokines and chemokine release , which leads to a decrease in immune cell migration and activation • Blockade of adenosine receptors inhibits bronchoconstriction, however, blockade of A1 receptors in the glomerular afferent arteriole and PCT causes diuresis . • Activating enzyme histone deacetylase-2, which is responsible for its anti-inflammatory action215

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient diagnosed with ventricular tachycardia was started on a class1B anti-arrhythmic drug. Identify the drug.
mcqs.explanation: Mexiletine is a class 1B antiarrhythmic drug. It is a lidocaine analog.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The additional mechanism by which class 1A drugs additionally prolong action potential duration is:
mcqs.explanation: Class IA antiarrhythmics block K+ channels leading to prolongation of action potential duration. The main action of class IA antiarrhythmics is blocking Na + channels causing: • Slowing the upstroke of the action potential • Slowing conduction • Prolonging the QRS duration

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antiarrhythmics has the fastest rate of recovery on Na+ channel blockade?
mcqs.explanation: Phenytoin and mexiletine which are class IB antiarrhythmic drugs have the fastest rate of recovery on Na+ channel blockade.
