They show the fastest dissociation kinetics to Na+ channel blockade (<1 sec ).224 Na+channel blockade Potassium channel Action potential duration Class IA Intermediate - 1-10 se c Significant K+channel blocke r Prolonged Class IB Rapid- <1 sec K+channel opener Shortened or no effect Class IC Slow- >10 sec Negligible K+channel blocker Variable or no effect

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Dofetilide belongs to which class of anti-arrhythmic drugs?
mcqs.explanation: Dofetilide belongs to class III of anti-arrhythmic drugs.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An athlete diagnosed with atrial fibrillation was administered an antiarrhythmic drug. Several hours later, he complains of lower abdominal pain and not having passed urine since admission. Examination reveals a palpable bladder . Which was the most probable drug administered ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of urinary retention . Disopyramide , a class 1A antiarrhythmic is the drug most likely to cause these symptoms in this patient . It causes prominent anticholinergic side effects like urinary retention , dry mouth, blurred vision, precipitation of glaucoma, and constipation. It is the drug of choice for vagally mediated atrial fibrillation such as sleep -induced or atrial fibrillation in athletes .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is associated with QT prolongation?
mcqs.explanation: QT prolongation is seen with quinidine.225 It causes torsades de pointes , a life -threatening form of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presents with sinus bradycardia and bronchospasm. She was previously diagnosed with AV nodal reentrant tachycardia and had been started on an antiarrhythmic drug. Which of the following drugs is most likely being used ?
mcqs.explanation: Propafenone is the most likely drug being used in this patient as sinus bradycardia and bronchospasm are adverse effects seen with the use of this drug. These side effects are due to its weak beta -blocking activity.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Blurred vision in a patient being treated for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia is most likely due to:
mcqs.explanation: Blurred vision is the most common dose -related non-cardiac adverse effect of flecainide therapy . Flecainide is a class 1C antiarrhythmic agent . It acts mainly by sodium channel blockade. It does not cause any change in the action potential duration. Flecainide is used in paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVTs ): • Atrioventricular nodal re-entrant tachycardia (AVNRT ) • AV re-entrant tachycardia (AVRT ) • Atrial fibrillation/atrial flutter (without structural heart disease )

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antiarrhythmics has both class II and class III action?
mcqs.explanation: Sotalol is a class III antiarrhythmic agent with additional beta -adrenergic blocking effects . (class II antiarrhythmic action)226 Propranolol is a class II antiarrhythmic agent that has an additional Na+ channel blocking effect . (class I antiarrhythmic action) Esmolol is a short-acting beta -blocker with minimal/no action on cardiac Na+ and K+ channels.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presented to the ER with dizziness and palpitations . ECG is shown below . Which of the following drugs cannot be used in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The scenario and ECG findings (absent P waves and RR intervals that are irregularly irregular) are suggestive of atrial fibrillation. Lignocaine is not used in atrial arrhythmias. Lignocaine is a class 1B anti-arrhythmic agent . It blocks Na+ channels mostly in the closed /inactivated state . It is not used in atrial arrhythmias because the atrial action potential is so short that the Na+ channels are in a closed / inactivated state for only a brief amount of time. Lignocaine is used in the acute treatment of ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation. Drugs mostly used for supraventricular arrhythmia are: • Adenosine • Verapamil • Diltiazem • Digoxin Drugs used for ventricular arrhythmia are: • Lidocaine • Mexiletine Drugs used in both conditions are: • Amiodarone • Beta-blockers • Class 1a / 1c antiarrhythmics

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect regarding lignocaine?

options.c: In heart failure patients , both loading and maintenance doses are decreased
options.d: Indicated for prophylaxis of arryhythmias in all cases of suspected MI

mcqs.explanation: Lignocaine decreases the incidence of arrhythmias in patients with suspected MI. However, it increases mortality probably by precipitating heart block or congestive heart failure. Hence it is not routinely used for prophylaxis in MI patients but it is used only when indicated . Gastrointestinal absorption of lignocaine is good but bioavailability is very less due to high first-pass hepatic metabolism . Therefore, it is not used through the oral route. Lignocaine has a high volume of distribution. The loading dose is required to achieve rapid action. In heart failure, both volumes of distribution and clearance are reduced . Both the loading dose and maintenance dose have to be reduced .227

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a correct statement regarding antiarrhythmics?

options.a: Sotalol has additional class II action
options.b: Esmolol has additional class IV action
options.c: Propranolol has additional class I action

mcqs.explanation: Sotalol has both class II (beta -blocker) and class III action (K+ channel blockade). Though it is a nonselective beta -blocker, as an antiarrhythmic, it is classified under class III . Propranolol is a non-selective beta -blocker with additional membrane-stabilizing action especially at higher doses : Na+ channel blockade/ class I action. Esmolol is a beta 1 selective blocker that does not have any additional class effect .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man presents to the OPD with complaints of bluish discoloration of the skin on the sun-exposed areas. He has been on medication for monomorphic ventricular tachycardia for the past 3 years. Which drug is most likely implicated in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The scenario is suggestive of blue man syndrome which is most likely caused by amiodarone. One of the side effects of amiodarone is photosensitivity . In some cases , bluish discoloration of the skin is seen , predominantly in the sun-exposed areas. This could be due to the immune response in dermal layers by amiodarone or the accumulation of amiodarone in superficial layers of skin. The symptoms are reversible on drug discontinuation. The syndrome is related to both dose and photosensitivity. The side effects of amiodarone include: • Pulmonary fibrosis • Hypotension , depressed ventricular function • Torsades de pointes • Corneal microdeposits • Hepatotoxicity • Neuropathies • Photosensitivity • Thyroid dysfunction Other such syndromes associated with drugs are: • Red man syndrome - Vancomycin • Gray baby syndrome - Chloramphenicol

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Chronic usage of an antiarrhythmic drug leads to optic neuritis and smurf skin or ceruloderma in a patient . Which of the following is not a mechanism of action of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Optic neuritis and smurf skin (blueman syndrome or ceruloderma ) are caused by amiodarone. It acts by blocking K+, Na+, and Ca2+ channels. It also blocks adrenergic effects . It does not block Cl- channels.228 Amiodarone is classified as a class III antiarrhythmic agent . It exerts its function through the following mechanisms: • Blockade of transient outward delayed rectifier and inward rectifier K+ currents • Blockade of inactivated Na+ channels with a rapid rate of recovery • Decreases Ca2+ current • Non-competitive adrenergic blockade It is the drug of choice for acute treatment of VT and VF. The side effects of amiodarone include: • Pulmonary fibrosis • Hypotension , depressed ventricular function • Torsades de pointes • Corneal microdeposits • Hepatotoxicity • Neuropathies • Photosensitivity • Thyroid dysfunction

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following adverse effects is least likely in a patient who is on chronic amiodarone therapy ?
mcqs.explanation: Nephrotoxicity is not an adverse effect of chronic amiodarone therapy . Pulmonary fibrosis associated with dry cough is the most serious side effect of chronic amiodarone therapy . It can rapidly progress and become fatal. The side effects of amiodarone include: • Pulmonary fibrosis • Hypotension , depressed ventricular function • Torsades de pointes • Corneal microdeposits • Hepatotoxicity • Neuropathies • Photosensitivity • Thyroid dysfunction

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antiarrhythmic drugs is contraindicated in a patient with interstitial lung disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Amiodarone is contraindicated in a patient with interstitial lung disease .229 The most serious adverse effect during chronic amiodarone therapy is pulmonary fibrosis, which can be rapidly progressive and fatal. Underlying lung disease , doses of 400 mg/day or more, and recent pulmonary insults such as pneumonia appear to be risk factors for this condition. Amiodarone is a class III antiarrhythmic drug. The side effects of amiodarone include: • Pulmonary fibrosis • Hypotension , depressed ventricular function • Torsades de pointes • Corneal microdeposits • Hepatotoxicity • Neuropathies • Photosensitivity • Thyroid dysfunction

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about dronedarone is incorrect?

options.a: It does not contain iodine moiety
options.b: Has stronger antiadrenergic effects than amiodarone
options.c: Less effective antiarrhythmic when compared to amiodarone
options.d: Dose adjustment has to be done in renal failure

mcqs.explanation: Dronedarone undergoes hepatic metabolism and hence dose adjustment is not required in renal failure as it is not excreted through the kidneys. Dronedarone is a non-iodinated congener of amiodarone. Like amiodarone, it is a blocker of multiple ion channels. It has stronger antiadrenergic effects than amiodarone. It is less effective in maintaining sinus rhythm and is considered less antiarrhythmic when compared to amiodarone. Unlike amiodarone, it does not cause thyroid dysfunction or pulmonary fibrosis. However, it causes hepatotoxicity and increases the risk of stroke and heart failure.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Given below is the ECG of a patient who presented to the emergency room with sudden onset palpitations and breathlessness . Which of the following drugs can be used in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario and the ECG findings are suggestive of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT ). Verapamil and diltiazem are used in both acute treatment and prophylaxis of PSVT . Their mechanism of action is by slowing SA node automaticity and AV nodal conduction velocity . Additionally , they also decrease cardiac contractility and reduce blood pressure . Dihydropyridines like nifedipine and amlodipine do not have any antiarrhythmic property . Drugs used for supraventricular arrhythmias are: • Adenosine • Verapamil • Diltiazem230 • Digoxin Drugs used for ventricular arrhythmias are: • Lidocaine • Mexiletine Drugs used in both conditions are: • Amiodarone • Beta-blockers • Class 1A / 1C antiarrhythmics

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Vernakalant is indicated in which of the following types of arrhythmias?
mcqs.explanation: Vernakalant is a newer antiarrhythmic agent indicated in atrial fibrillation. Its mechanisms of action include : • Frequency and voltage -dependent block of the early and late components of the sodium current • The muscarinic potassium current IKACh, which is constitutively activated in atrial fibrillation is also blocked It is indicated for rapid termination of atrial fibrillation in patients with no or minimal structural heart disease.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presented with palpitations and light -headedness . His ECG is shown below . Which of the following drugs is least likely to cause this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and the ECG findings (rapid asynchronous complexes and an undulating baseline ) point towards a diagnosis of torsades de pointes . Lidocaine use is unlikely to cause this condition.231 Lidocaine belongs to class IB antiarrhythmics. It is considered to have the least arrhythmogenic potential among antiarrhythmics. Among the antiarrhythmics, class Ia and class III drugs prolong action potential duration and thus prolong QT interval. They are also prone to cause torsades de pointes .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the drug of choice for the immediate management of a patient with paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia?
mcqs.explanation: The drug of choice for the termination of PSVT is adenosine . Drugs used for supraventricular arrhythmias are: • Adenosine • Verapamil • Diltiazem • Digoxin Drugs used for ventricular arrhythmias are: • Lidocaine • Mexiletine Drugs used in both conditions are: • Amiodarone • Beta-blockers • Class 1a / 1c antiarrhythmics

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who was recently diagnosed with a seizure disorder presents to the casualty with altered mental status . His ECG shows a prolonged QTc. There is history of sudden cardiac deaths in his family at an early age . On further evaluation, a diagnosis of congenital long QT syndrome is made. Which is the most suitable pharmacological agent to treat this condition?
mcqs.explanation: 232 Beta-blockers like metoprolol are the mainstay of pharmacological therapy in both asymptomatic and symptomatic patients with congenital LQTS . They reduce both syncope and sudden cardiac death (SCD). Long QT syndrome (LQTS) is a disorder of ventricular myocardial repolarization characterized by a prolonged QT interval on the electrocardiogram that can lead to symptomatic ventricular arrhythmias and an increased risk of sudden cardiac death .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An elderly patient with heart failure and atrial fibrillation is stabilized with digoxin. By what mechanism does it control the arrhythmia in this patient ?

options.d: Decreasing atrial repolarization by blocking Na+ channels

mcqs.explanation: Digoxin results in an increased vagal tone which helps in controlling the ventricular rate in atrial fibrillation. Increased vagal tone increases the AV nodal refractoriness due to blockade of Ca2+ channels. It also results in hyperpolarisation and shortening of atrial action potentials due to activation of ACh-mediated K+ channels in the atria.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A male patient who is suffering from a psychotic disorder is on antipsychotic , antidepressant and antihypertensive treatment . He suddenly developed tachycardia and chest tightness. On evaluation he had metabolic acidosis. ECG showed widened QRS complex and prolonged QT interval. Which of the following drugs is responsible for this?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of torsades de pointes . Only amitriptyline causes this condition, among the above drugs. Torsades de pointes (French: twisting of points) is a life -threatening form of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with rapid asynchronous complexes and an undulating baseline on ECG.233

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 58-year-old patient with coronary artery disease has a deranged lipid profile and is started on statins. Which enzyme does this drug act on?
mcqs.explanation: Statins act on the HMG-CoA reductase enzyme, thus inhibiting cholesterol synthesis .Note : Necrotizing myopathy is a newly defined form of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy . Patients who have anti-HMG Co-A reductase antibodies should not be given statins to control237 high cholesterol as they may develop this type of statin-induced necrotizing myopathy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Hepatic cholesterol synthesis is maximal between midnight and 2 am. So most of the statins are preferably administered in the evening for maximal effect . Which statin can be taken irrespective of the time of the day?
mcqs.explanation: Atorvastatin has a longer half-life (19 \261 9 hours) and may be taken at any time of the day. Other drugs that can be taken irrespective of the time of day: • Rosuvastatin - has a half-life of 20 \261 6 hours • Pitavastatin - has a half-life of 12 hours All other statins, which have a plasma half-life of around 4 hours or less , should preferably be administered in the evening.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with hypercholesterolemia on statin therapy presents to your OPD for follow -up. You notice his cholesterol is still high and decide to add on another drug that directly inhibits the absorption of cholesterol . Which of the following will you prescribe ?
mcqs.explanation: Ezetimibe is the drug that prevents hypercholesterolemia by directly inhibiting the absorption of cholesterol . Ezetimibe acts by interfering with a specific cholesterol transport protein NPC1L1 in the intestinal mucosa and reduces the absorption of both dietary and biliary cholesterol . It causes a compensatory increase in hepatic cholesterol synthesis but LDL cholesterol is decreased . Statins block this enhanced cholesterol synthesis (cholesterol synthesis inhibitors) and so their combination has a synergistic effect . Option B: Orlistat is an anti-obesity drug that acts by inhibiting pancreatic and gastric lipase and thus interferes with the digestion and absorption of dietary triglycerides . Option C: Cholestyramine is a bile acid sequestrant . The bile -acid sequestrants are highly positively charged and bind negatively charged bile acids. Because of their large size, the resins are not absorbed, and the bound bile acids are excreted in the stool . Cholestyramine primarily reduces LDL levels by increasing hepatic bile acid synthesis ; which results in increased LDL uptake and diversion of cholesterol to bile acid production . Option D: Niacin reduces lipolysis by hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL ) and reduces hepatic triglyceride synthesis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which drug decreases Lipoprotein(
mcqs.explanation: The drug that decreases Lipoprotein(a) is niacin. Niacin is the only lipid -lowering agent that lowers lipoprotein (a) levels significantly . It also results in a decrease in LDL , VLDL , and triglycerides along with an increase in HDL cholesterol . The main adverse effect of niacin is cutaneous flushing and pruritus which can be controlled by pretreatment with aspirin. Niacin can also cause hepatotoxicity , GI toxicity , and hyperuricemia .238

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs would you warn a patient taking statins against, due to the highest risk of myopathy ?
mcqs.explanation: Myopathy risk is highest when statins are used along with gemfibrozil. Gemfibrozil is a fibrate that inhibits the uptake of statins into the hepatocytes and prevents its metabolism , thereby increasing its bioavailability. Thus, the risk of toxicity of statins increases. Other drugs interacting similarly with statins include : • Cyclosporine • Digoxin • Warfarin • Macrolide antibiotics • Azole antifungals . Option A: Fenofibrate does not have much interaction with statins. Option C: Colestipol is a bile acid sequestrant and does not have much effect on statin metabolism . Option D: Niacin can also rarely increase the risk of statin-induced myopathy but the risk is much lower than that with gemfibrozil. So here gemfibrozil is the best answer.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who is on statin therapy asks about a new drug called evolocumab that his friend is taking for hyperlipidemia . What is the route of administration of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Evolocumab is a PCSK-9 inhibitor that is administered as a subcutaneous injection. PCSK-9 is a protease that binds to the LDL receptors on the surface of hepatocyte and enhances the lysosomal degradation of the LDL receptor . This results in higher plasma LDL levels . inhibition of PCSK-9 results in a reduction of plasma LDL levels . Two approved PCSK-9 inhibitors are alirocumab and evolocumab.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which among the following is a microsomal triglyceride transfer protein inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein (MTP) inhibitor is lomitapide . MTP adds triglycerides to nascent VLDL in the liver and to chylomicrons in the intestine . Its inhibition decreases VLDL secretion and thus decreases the accumulation of LDL in the plasma. It is approved for use in homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia . Options A: Ticlopidine is an antiplatelet agent . Option B: Gugulipid is a plant extract that is commonly used for hyperlipidemia but has very little /no evidence to support its use .239 Option D: Evinacumab is a recently approved angiopoietin -like 3 (ANGPTL3 ) inhibitor. It is indicated as an adjunct to other LDL -cholesterol lowering therapies for homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia in adults and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with hereditary hyperlipoproteinemia is prescribed a fibrate. What is the mechanism of action of this drug?

options.d: Binds bile acids and bile salts in the intestine

mcqs.explanation: Fibrates increase the lipoprotein lipase activity through PPAR -�o and cause increased lipolysis of triglycerides . Lipoprotein lipase (LPL ) is a key enzyme in the degradation of VLDL . Fibrates bind to PPAR alpha and cause stimulation of lipoprotein lipase enzyme. Increased LPL synthesis enhances the clearance of triglyceride -rich lipoproteins . Additionally , fibrates also stimulate fatty acid oxidation and reduce the expression of apo C-III (inhibitor of lipolysis ).Class HMG- CoA red uctase inhibitor s (statins) Fibrates Niacin Bile acid-bindin g resins Ezetimibe Important exa mples Lovastatin , ator vastatin, fluvast atin, pravastati n, simvastatin, rosuvastatin, pi tavastatin Gemfibrozil and fenofibrate Niacin Colestipol , chol estyramine , col esevelam Ezetimibe Mechanism of a ction Inhibits HMG- CoA reductase PPAR -�o mediat ed increased lip olysis Decreases the p roduction of VL DLs and decrea ses the cataboli sm of HDLs Binds to bile aci ds in the intesti nal lumen and i ncreases excreti on. This results in increased co nversion of hep atic cholesterol to bile acids, an d reduction in h epatic cholester ol content . mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old obese man presented to your OPD. His lipid profile showed elevated levels of cholesterol and triglycerides . On examination, you notice palmar xanthomas. What is the drug of choice for his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of elevated cholesterol and triglycerides along with the presence of palmar xanthomas (pathognomonic sign) is indicative of type III hyperlipoproteinemia . The drugs of choice for this condition are fibrates. Fibrates are also preferred in patients having severe hypertriglyceridemia (TG >1000 mg/dl) who are at risk for pancreatitis . The response to fibrate therapy in Type III hyperlipoproteinemia patients include : • Elevated cholesterol and triglyceride levels are dramatically lowered . • Tuberoeruptive and palmar xanthomas may regress completely . • Angina and intermittent claudication also improve. The image below shows palmar xanthoma.241

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the drug of choice for type IIa and IIb hyperlipoproteinemias ?
mcqs.explanation: The drugs of choice for type IIa and IIb hyperlipoproteinemias are statins. In type IIa or IIb hyperlipoproteinemias, there is increased LDL cholesterol with +/- increase in TG. Statins have the maximum LDL lowering property among the hypolipidemic drugs. Therefore, they are the drugs of choice in this case. In type III /IV hyperlipoproteinemias , there is mainly an increase in triglyceride (TG) level . Fibrates reduce the TGs contained in VLDL and increase the HDL . So they are the drugs of choice for these conditions.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia has mipomersen as part of his treatment regimen. By which of the following mechanisms does this drug act?
mcqs.explanation: Mipomersen is an antisense oligonucleotide that acts as an inhibitor of apo B-100 synthesis . Mipomersen binds to the mRNA of apo B-100 resulting in degradation of apo B-100 mRNA and eventually reduction of apo B-100 synthesis .242

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following ACE inhibitors is not a prodrug?
mcqs.explanation: Lisinopril is not a prodrug. All ACE inhibitors are prodrugs except lisinopril and captopril .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with BP 225/145 presents with acute pulmonary edema and is diagnosed with hypertensive emergency . The active metabolite of which ACE inhibitor is available for intravenous use in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Enalapril is available in its active form as enalaprilat for intravenous use . Enalapril is a prodrug of enalaprilat. It is indicated in conditions where oral drugs cannot be used or rapid onset of action is desired like in a case of hypertensive emergency .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding ACE inhibitors is true?

options.a: They inhibit the conversion of angiotensinogen to angiotensin I
options.b: Omission of prior diuretic dose decreases the risk of postural hypotension
options.c: Lisinopril is shorter acting than enalapril
options.d: They are contraindicated in diabetic patients

mcqs.explanation: The omission of prior diuretic dose decreases the risk of postural hypotension . ACE inhibitors cause arteriolar dilation and increase the compliance of larger arteries. ACE inhibitors induced hypotension is thereby due to a decrease in total peripheral resistance . In diuretic -treated patients , the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system is more active to compensate for volume loss. Hence , ACE inhibitors increase the risk of postural hypotension in these patients . Option A: ACE inhibitors inhibit the conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II . Option C: Lisinopril is longer acting than enalapril. Lisinopril is usually administered once daily in all patients . Enalapril requires twice -daily administration in some patients . Option D: ACE inhibitors and ARBs are first-line agents in diabetic patients because of their renoprotective effects .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: All of the following are indications for the use of ACE inhibitors except :
mcqs.explanation: ACE inhibitors are usually avoided in conditions like pheochromocytoma which is associated with high renin activity. Abrupt inhibition of the RAAS system can result in severe hypotension (usually postural ). The majority of pheochromocytomas are treated surgically . Phenoxybenzamine is often used in preparing the patient for surgery and also to manage hypertension in inoperable or malignant247 pheochromocytoma . Phentolamine can also be used in the short-term control of hypertension in these patients . ACE inhibitors are indicated in hypertensive emergency , myocardial infarction, and left ventricular dysfunction .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following patients are ACE inhibitors not contraindicated ?
mcqs.explanation: ACE inhibitors are not contraindicated in unilateral renal artery stenosis , left ventricular systolic dysfunction , and scleroderma renal crisis. Patient 1: ACE inhibitors are teratogenic and can cause hypoplasia of organs, renal failure, anuria , and growth retardation in the fetus . Therefore, they are contraindicated in pregnancy. Patient 2: ACE inhibitors can be used with caution in unilateral renal artery stenosis if the other kidney is functioning normally. Patient 3: Efferent arteriolar constriction maintains the glomerular filtration pressure in bilateral renal artery stenosis . ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in bilateral renal stenosis as they can precipitate acute renal failure due to dilation of efferent arterioles and fall in glomerular filtration pressure . Patient 4: ACE inhibition in patients with systolic dysfunction prevents or delays the progression of heart failure, decreases the incidence of sudden death and myocardial infarction, and improves the quality of life . ACE inhibition reduces afterload and systolic wall stress , and both cardiac output and cardiac index increase. Patient 5: The use of ACE inhibitors considerably improves the survival of patients with scleroderma renal crisis.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 53-year-old hypertensive patient has been on ACE inhibitors for the last 12 years. Which of the following effects would you expect to see in this patient ?

options.a: Rightward shift in renal pressure natriuresis curve
options.d: Decrease in compliance of large arteries

mcqs.explanation: ACE inhibitors, when used for a long time in patients with hypertension , cause a reduction in filtration fraction. Filtration fraction is the ratio of GFR to that of renal plasma flow . ACE inhibitors increase renal blood flow without altering GFR and thus result in reduction of filtration fraction. Option A: The graph plotted between urinary sodium excretion and mean blood pressure is known as the pressure natriuresis curve. For example , when dietary sodium intake is low, renin release is stimulated . Angiotensin II acts on the kidneys to shift the renal pressure – natriuresis curve to the right. This increases sodium and water retention . Conversely, when dietary Na+ is high or when ACE inhibitors are used , there is the withdrawal of angiotensin II . The renal pressure natriuresis curve shifts to the left . The following image depicts a pressure natriuresis curve :248 Options C and D: ACE inhibitors do not cause a significant increase in heart rate and can have a favorable change in the compliance of large arteries on long-term use .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who is started on lisinopril for hypertension is concerned about its adverse effects . Which among the following is not an adverse effect of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: ACE inhibitors are associated with the development of hyperkalemia. Hyperkalemia occurs due to the inhibition of angiotensin II -mediated aldosterone secretion . Decreased aldosterone levels result in decreased tubular excretion of potassium in the kidneys leading to hyperkalemia. The adverse effects of ACE inhibitors are: • Hypotension • Hyperkalemia • Cough • Angioedema • Skin rash • Teratogenicity • Dysgeusia (alteration in or loss of taste ) Extremely rare but reversible side effects include neutropenia , glycosuria in the absence of hyperglycemia, anemia, and hepatotoxicity.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presents to the casualty with cough , difficulty in breathing, and non-indurating edema of his face and lips. He had recently been started on ramipril for hypertension . Which among the following mediates these adverse effects ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of ACE inhibitor-induced angioedema which occurs due to bradykinin .249 Angioedema is most commonly mediated by histamine. However, bradykinin -mediated angioedema, though less common, can result due to hereditary or acquired defects in C1 esterase inhibitor and as a side effect of ACE inhibitors. ACE has structural similarity to another enzyme called kininase. Kininase normally metabolizes bradykinin , substance P, and prostaglandins. ACE inhibitors when administered also block kininase enzyme which results in an increase in the concentration of these substrates . An increase in the level of bradykinin / substance P levels results in persistent brassy cough and angioedema in the patients .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An 18-year-old boy is brought to the casualty with complaints of swelling of his face and lips as shown in the image below . On further enquiry, it is noted that he has suffered from similar episodes in the past whenever he becomes emotional. He is prescribed icatibant. What is the likely mechanism of action of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and image showing swelling of the face and lips is suggestive of hereditary angioedema . Icatibant is a selective bradykinin B2 receptor competitive antagonist indicated for the treatment of acute attacks of hereditary angioedema . The other drug which is approved for the treatment of acute attacks of hereditary angioedema is ecallantide which is a synthetic plasma kallikrein inhibitor. Both these drugs are administered subcutaneously .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old diabetic male is on ACE inhibitors for hypertension . Which among the following is the most serious adverse effect you would expect to see in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The most significant adverse effect seen with the use of ACE inhibitors is hypotension . ACE inhibitors are used in the management of hypertension and are one of the first-line drugs for this condition. Option B: ACE inhibitors may cause hyperkalemia in patients with renal insufficiency or diabetes . Options C and D: ACE inhibitors do not affect calcium levels significantly .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man is diagnosed with hypertension and is prescribed losartan. Which of the following statements about the drug is incorrect?

options.a: It is a competitive angiotensin receptor antagonist

mcqs.explanation: Losartan use is not associated with hyperuricemia . In fact, losartan is uricosuric and can also be used in patients with gout . Losartan is a competitive angiotensin II receptor antagonist. It binds to the AT1 receptor with high affinity. it is also a competitive antagonist of the thromboxane A2 receptor and attenuates platelet aggregation . Losartan has no effect on ACE and it does not inhibit bradykinin breakdown. This results in negligible incidences of cough .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Combined use of ACE inhibitors and ARBs are not routinely indicated primarily due to the increased risk of which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: 250 The combined use of ACE inhibitors and ARBs are not commonly indicated as they increase the risk of hyperkalemia. They also increase the risk of hypotension and renal injury. Any such use should be done under the supervision of specialists with frequent monitoring.251

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man was rushed to the ER with impaired consciousness following a hunger strike for a day. His wife reported , he had a head injury 1 month back and since then had complaints of polyuria. On examination, he was found to be severely dehydrated and MRI brain showed an absence of the characteristic bright spot in the pituitary . Which of the following is the drug of choice for his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of polyuria following a head injury and an absence of a pituitary bright spot on the MRI brain is suggestive of central diabetes insipidus . The drug of choice for this condition is desmopressin , a V2 receptor agonist. Mechanism of action of desmopressin is: It stimulates the V2 receptors on the basolateral membrane of the principal cells in the collecting tubules . This increases the insertion of water channels (aquaporin 2) into the apical membrane. This leads to increased water reabsorption in the collecting ducts . Activation of V2 receptors also increase the permeability of urea. Option B: Amiloride is a potassium -sparing diuretic . It is indicated for lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus . Option C: Thiazides paradoxically exert an antidiuretic effect in DI but are not the drugs of choice . They are generally used in nephrogenic DI. Option D: Triamterene is also a potassium-sparing diuretic that can be used to treat nephrogenic DI. Note : Patients with DI usually do not develop overt signs of dehydration due to increased intake of water to compensate for polyuria. But when water intake is impaired they can present with dehydration .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient having polyuria and polydipsia is diagnosed with central diabetes insipidus . He is started on intranasal desmopressin . Which of the following is not a reason for choosing this over intravenous vasopressin?
mcqs.explanation: Desmopressin is preferred in the treatment of central diabetes insipidus as it is a selective agonist of the V2 receptor . Desmopressin has minimal or no action on V1 receptors resulting in little vasoconstrictor activity. It is more potent than vasopressin. It is longer acting than vasopressin as enzymatic degradation of desmopressin is slow . Lypressin acts on both V1 and V2 receptors . Terlipressin is a synthetic vasopressin analog that has more selectivity for the V1 receptor and produces fewer adverse effects than lypressin .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman with pituitary adenoma is non-compliant with her treatment with cabergoline . She has now presented with bitemporal hemianopia and features suggestive of diabetes insipidus . Which of the following drugs cannot be used to manage her condition?
mcqs.explanation: Furosemide is not used for the treatment of diabetes insipidus . It is a loop diuretic that might further worsen diabetes insipidus . Option A: The drug of choice for central diabetes insipidus is desmopressin . Desmopressin is a V2 receptor agonist and synthetic analog vasopressin. Option C: Chlorpropamide enhances the action of circulating vasopressin and reduces urine formation in central DI.255 Option D: Carbamazepine also reduces urine formation in central DI. The exact mechanism is unknown .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Tachyphylaxis is a concern with the use of desmopressin in which of the following patients ?

options.a: A 50-year-old man with central DI post meningitis
options.b: A 25-year-old woman on lithium therapy with nephrogenic DI
options.c: A 17-year-old girl with von willebrand's disease
options.d: A 7-year-old child with primary nocturnal enuresis

mcqs.explanation: Tachyphylaxis refers to the rapid development of tolerance when doses of a drug are repeated in quick succession . It is a concern when desmopressin is used in bleeding disorders because long-term use of desmopressin can cause depletion of factor VIII and von Willebrand factor stores . The usefulness of desmopressin in bleeding disorders is limited to preoperative preparation, postoperative bleeding , excessive menstrual bleeding , and emergency situations . In patients with type I von Willebrand disease and in some with type IIn vWD , desmopressin elevates von Willebrand factor and shortens the bleeding time. Option A: It does not cause tachyphylaxis in central DI. Option B: Desmopressin is not indicated in nephrogenic DI. Option D: Bedtime administration of desmopressin for primary nocturnal enuresis provides a high response rate that is sustained with long-term use . However, intranasal desmopressin is no longer recommended for the treatment of primary nocturnal enuresis because of the increased risk of hyponatremia.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man who is on treatment for small cell carcinoma of the lung presents with acute onset confusion, nausea, and vomiting. He appears to be euvolemic . Laboratory investigations reveal serum sodium levels to be 120 mEq/l and urine osmolality is 300 mOsm/kg . Which of the following is not used as a treatment option in his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of syndrome of inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) which can occur as a paraneoplastic syndrome of small cancer of the lung. Desmopressin is not used in the treatment of SIADH. Since excess vasopressin is the cause for SIADH, giving a vasopressin analog like desmopressin would only worsen the condition. Management of SIADH: • Fluid restriction • Hypertonic saline( 3%) + loop diuretics is the treatment of choice in severe symptomatic hyponatremia. • Tolvaptan and conivaptan (vasopressin receptor antagonists) are preferred for long-term use . • Demeclocycline (a tetracycline drug) is used as an alternative.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The best approach in the treatment of chronic SIADH is ______

options.b: Reducing fluid intake to <500 ml per day

mcqs.explanation: The best approach in the treatment of chronic SIADH is the oral administration of a vaptan like tolvaptan, which is a selective V2 receptor antagonist. This increases urinary water256 excretion by blocking the antidiuretic effect of AVP . Other treatment options for chronic SIADH include : • Fluid intake < 500 ml/day • Demeclocycline • Fludrocortisone Increased thirst is a frequently observed characteristic of hyponatremia in SIADH. Fluid restriction is usually a burden to the patient . It is unreliable , impractical, and slow to work. As thirst is particularly difficult to suppress, water restriction in SIADH frequently leads to non-compliance in the long run. Vaptans would be especially suited for the treatment of these patients . Serum sodium concentrations are also corrected by vaptans and hence , vaptans substantially improve the quality of life in these patients .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with liver cirrhosis presenting with ascites and pedal edema is administered conivaptan. Which of the following statements regarding the drug is true?
mcqs.explanation: Conivaptan is a nonselective vasopressin receptor antagonist. Conivaptan antagonizes both V1a and V2 receptors . It is administered intravenously and is used in the treatment of euvolemic and hypervolemic hyponatremia. Vaptans have been proven to mobilize ascites and improve hyponatremia in patients with cirrhosis. Vasopressin receptor blockers are classified as:Classification of receptor bloc kers Drugs Nonselective (mixed V1 /V2 ) Conivaptan V1 selective (V1 RA) Relcovaptan V1b selective (V3 RA) Nelivaptan V2 selective (V2 RA) LixivaptanMozavaptanSatava ptanTolvaptan

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old alcoholic with deranged liver function tests is to be started on treatment for chronic SIADH. Which of the following drugs should not be used in his treatment regimen?
mcqs.explanation: Tolvaptan should not be used in patients with liver disease as it has been associated with liver damage. Administration of tolvaptan is generally limited to 30 days to limit the risk of hepatotoxicity .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who was diagnosed with ADPKD was prescribed tolvaptan. After a few weeks , he presented with dry mouth and increased thirst. What is the likely cause ?
mcqs.explanation: Tolvaptan causes increased free water clearance, which causes dehydration . Hence , the patient may present with dry mouth and increased thirst.257 Tolvaptan is a vasopressin V2 receptor antagonist. Decreased binding of vasopressin to the V2 receptor in the kidney lowers the adenyl cyclase activity leading to decreased intracellular cAMP. Decreased cAMP concentrations prevent the fusion of aquaporin 2 containing vesicles with the plasma membrane, leading to an increase in urinary water excretion (free water clearance), and a decrease in urine osmolality . The common side effects of tolvaptan include : • dehydration • hypernatremia • hypovolemia • liver injury Tolvaptan is used to delay disease progression in patients with ADPKD.258

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a benzodiazepine ?
mcqs.explanation: Flurazepam is a benzodiazepine .Class of drugs Mechanism of action Examples Benzodiazepines Facilitate the action of GABA byincreasingthefrequencyofo peningof GABA mediated chl oride channel AlprazolamClonazepamLoraz epamMidazolamOxazepamTe mazepamEstazolamFlurazep am Barbiturates Facilitate the action of GABA byincreasingtheopening dur ationof GABA mediated chlor ide channel AmobarbitalPhenobarbitalBu tabarbitalPentobarbital Z drugs Act like benzodiazepines ZaleplonZolpidemZopicloneE szopiclone Melatonin receptor agonist s Activates MT1and MT2recept ors RamelteonTasimelteon Orexin antagonist Blocks orexins, neuropeptide s that promote wakefulness SuvorexantDaridorexant 5HT receptor agonist Affinity for 5HT > D2recepto r Buspirone

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A physician prescribes clonazepam to a patient with generalized anxiety disorder. Choose the false statement regarding its mechanism of action.

options.a: Bind at the �o /\033 interface of GABA-A receptor
options.b: Increase the affinity of the GABA-A receptor for GABA
options.c: Activate GABA-A receptors directly opening the Cl channel
options.d: Increase the frequency of opening of GABA receptor Cl channel

mcqs.explanation: Clonazepam is a benzodiazepine . These are allosteric modulators of the GABAA receptor . They do not directly activate GABAA receptors to open the Cl- channel. GABAA receptor is a transmembrane inhibitory receptor in the CNS that functions as a chloride ion channel and has 5 subunits . Benzodiazepines are allosteric modulators of the GABAA receptor that bind at the �o /\033 interface of the receptor . This increases the affinity of the GABAA receptor for GABA thus increasing the263 frequency of the opening of the channel. Barbiturates, on the other hand, have a different binding site to the receptor and they increase the duration of the GABA gated chloride channel opening .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which is the shortest acting benzodiazepine ?
mcqs.explanation: Remimazolam is the shortest -acting benzodiazepine . Its half-life is just around 37-53 mins. Classification of benzodiazepines : • Long-acting: • Flurazepam • Diazepam • Quazepam • Chlordiazepoxide • Intermediate -acting: • Alprazolam • Temazepam • Lorazepam • Short-acting: • Triazolam • Midazolam • Ultra-short acting • Remimazolam Note : Remimazolam was approved by FDA in 2020 .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not act via GABA potentiation ?
mcqs.explanation: Promethazine does not act via GABA potentiation . It is a first-generation H1 receptor antagonist. Zopiclone, midazolam, and thiopentone act via GABA potentiation .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient diagnosed with insomnia is taking a drug belonging to the Z-compounds family. Which of the following does not belong to this family?
mcqs.explanation: Zonisamide is a sulfonamide anticonvulsant drug, that has no activity on GABA receptors . It does not belong to the Z-compound drugs. It is an adjunct drug for Parkinson 's disease , partial-onset seizures , infantile spasm, mixed seizure types of Lennox–Gastaut syndrome, myoclonic and generalized tonic-clonic seizure .264 Z compounds are benzodiazepine receptor agonists. They have less anticonvulsant and muscle relaxant properties when compared to benzodiazepines . They are used for the treatment of insomnia. They include : • Zolpidem • Zaleplon • Zopiclone • Eszopiclone

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following agents does not bind to GABA receptor chloride channel complex ?
mcqs.explanation: Buspirone does not bind to the GABA receptor chloride channel complex . It is a partial agonist at 5-HT1A receptor used in the treatment of anxiety. Option A: Ethanol releases GABA and also has a binding site on the GABA receptor chloride channel complex . Option B: Alphaxolone is a neurosteroid and it acts through activation of GABAA receptors . These receptors are BZD insensitive. Option C: Zolpidem belongs to novel benzodiazepine receptor agonists called Z compounds . It binds to the BZD receptor present on the GABA receptor chloride channel complex .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an inverse agonist at the benzodiazepine receptor ?
mcqs.explanation: The inverse agonist at the benzodiazepine receptor is beta -carboline. It impedes the action of GABA and can cause anxiogenic, convulsive, and memory-enhancing effects . Option A: Barbiturates (phenobarbitone) are agonists at an allosteric site on the GABAA receptor that facilitate the action of GABA. Option C: Flumazenil is a competitive antagonist at the benzodiazepine receptor . Option D: Picrotoxin blocks Cl- channel non-competitively .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 33-year-old woman with suspected diazepam overdose was administered the antidote for benzodiazepine poisoning. Which of the following statements is false about this antidote ?

options.a: It is a specific antagonist of benzodiazepines
options.b: It may be used to treat barbiturate poisoning
options.d: It acts at the same site on GABA channel where benzodiazepines bind

mcqs.explanation: Flumazenil is the antidote used in benzodiazepine poisoning. It is not used to treat barbiturate poisoning. Flumazenil is a benzodiazepine (BZD ) receptor -specific antagonist. It has no affinity for barbiturate binding sites on the GABA receptor Cl- channel complex . Flumazenil competes with BZD agonists and inverse agonists for the BZD receptors .265 Flumazenil is available only for intravenous use . It is used to treat benzodiazepine overdose and for the reversal of sedative effects produced by benzodiazepines administered during general anesthesia .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a competitive antagonist of GABA at the GABA-A receptor ?
mcqs.explanation: Bicuculline is a competitive antagonist of GABA at the GABA-A receptor . Option A: Flumazenil is a competitive antagonist at the alpha/gamma interface of the benzodiazepine site . This is different from the binding site of GABA which is the alpha/beta interface . Option B: Picrotoxin blocks Cl- channel non-competitively . Option D: Propofol is an agonist at the GABA-A receptor . Note : Muscimol is an agonist at the GABA-A receptor .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following patients is the administration of barbiturates contraindicated ?

options.a: 29-year-old lady with history of anxiety disorder
options.b: 33-year-old man with history of acute intermittent porphyria

mcqs.explanation: The administration of barbiturates is contraindicated in acute intermittent porphyria. The rate-limiting enzyme in porphyria synthesis is \027-aminolaevulinic acid (ALA )-synthetase . Barbiturates are enzyme inducers and they result in the increased synthesis of porphyrins and subsequent precipitation of acute intermittent porphyria. Options A and C: Barbiturates are used to treat anxiety and refractory status epilepticus . Option D: Phenobarbitone can be used to treat kernicterus in newborns as it increases hepatic glucuronosyltransferase (UGT) enzyme activity and the conjugation of bilirubin.266

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old man with insomnia is prescribed a melatonin analog by his physician. Which of the following drugs would have been prescribed ?
mcqs.explanation: Ramelteon is a melatonin analog approved for the treatment of insomnia, particularly with difficulties of sleep onset . It acts on both MT1 and MT2 receptors. • MT1 receptor - promotes the onset of sleep (hence used for induction of sleep ) • MT2 receptor - shifts the timing of the circadian system . The other melatonin agonists are: • Tasimelteon - used in insomnia in blind people • Agomelatine - used in major depressive disorder Option A: Doxepin is a tricyclic antidepressant and functions as a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor. It is used in depression , anxiety, and some forms of insomnia. Option B: Suvorexant is a dual orexin receptor antagonist used in the treatment of insomnia. Option D: Trazodone is a mixed agonist and antagonist at various serotonin receptors used as an antidepressant and in alcohol dependence .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A young woman, who is blind, presented with complaints of night-time insomnia. What is the drug of choice for her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The drug of choice for insomnia in blind people is tasimelteon . It is a selective agonist of the melatonin (MT1, MT2 ) receptors . Tasimelteon is approved for the treatment of non–24 -h sleep -wake syndrome (nighttime insomnia and daytime sleepiness , alternating with asymptomatic periods ) in totally blind patients experiencing circadian rhythm disorder.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Your senior resident asks you to prescribe an orexin receptor inhibitor to a patient with insomnia. Which of the following drugs would you prescribe ?
mcqs.explanation: Suvorexant is an inhibitor of both orexin1 and orexin2 receptors . It is approved for the treatment of insomnia. Orexins are produced in the lateral hypothalamus neurons and play a major role in maintaining the sleep cycle . Orexins promote wakefulness , while antagonists at orexin receptors enhance REM and non-REM sleep . Option B: Doxepin is a tricyclic antidepressant and has H1 receptor antagonism effect . It is used for insomnia at lower doses . Option C: Ritanserin is a 5HT2A /2C receptor antagonist indicated in insomnia. Option D: Agomelatine is a melatonin receptor agonist and a 5HT2C receptor antagonist indicated in insomnia.267

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 68-year-old man with alcoholic liver disease is scheduled to undergo surgery. Which of the following benzodiazepines should be avoided in him?
mcqs.explanation: Diazepam and its long-acting metabolites can accumulate significantly in elderly patients with liver disease and therefore should not be used in such cases . Diazepam is a long-acting benzodiazepine. It is metabolized in the liver to active metabolites like nordazepam which are long-acting. Nordazepam is further converted to oxazepam which is conjugated with glucuronic acid to form inactive metabolites . Lorazepam , oxazepam, and triazolam are also metabolized in the liver but do not form long-acting active metabolites . As such, they can be used in elderly patients with liver disease but with caution. Oxazepam and lorazepam are intermediate -acting and undergo glucuronide conjugation directly to form inactive metabolites . Triazolam is a short acting benzodiazepine . It forms alpha-hydroxy active metabolites but they are short-acting and undergo glucuronide conjugation to form inactive metabolites .268

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the most important mechanism of antiepileptic activity of phenytoin ?
mcqs.explanation: The most important mechanism of antiepileptic activity of phenytoin is the prolongation of Na+ ion channel inactivation. It slows down the rate of recovery of Na+ channels and thus limiting the propagation of the action potential . Phenytoin also inhibits voltage -gated Ca2+ channels. This reduces the influx of calcium inside the membrane and reduces the inflow of potassium ions during repolarization. At higher or toxic doses , phenytoin facilitates GABA response and inhibits the action of glutamate .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A known case of seizure disorder has been on long-term phenytoin therapy . Which of the following statements about this drug would be incorrect?

options.b: Metabolism follows only zero order kinetics
options.d: Metabolized extensively by the CYP enzymes in the liver

mcqs.explanation: Phenytoin follows first-order kinetics at lower concentrations and as the concentration increases, the elimination changes to zero-order kinetics. The rate of elimination of phenytoin varies with the serum concentration. As the blood levels rise, the maximal capacity of the liver to metabolize phenytoin is reached . Thus even a small increase in the dosage can result in disproportionally high plasma levels . Therefore, it requires therapeutic drug monitoring. About 90% of phenytoin is bound to plasma proteins , mainly albumin. Phenytoin is metabolized by the CYP enzymes in the liver.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an incorrect statement regarding fosphenytoin ?

options.b: Fosphenytoin displaces phenytoin from protein-binding sites
options.c: Causes hyperphosphatemia in renal failure patients
options.d: ECG monitoring is not required when administering IV

mcqs.explanation: Fosphenytoin like phenytoin requires continuous ECG monitoring during IV infusion due to the risk of arrhythmias. Fosphenytoin is a water-soluble prodrug of phenytoin . Fosphenytoin is also extensively protein bound, mainly albumin. This binding is saturable and fosphenytoin displaces phenytoin from protein-binding sites . Hydrolysis of fosphenytoin yields phosphate , which increases the risk of hyperphosphatemia in patients with renal failure. It is contraindicated in patients with sinus bradycardia, sino-atrial block, second and third-degree A-V block.278

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presenting to the ER with generalized tonic-clonic seizures is started on phenytoin therapy. All of the following adverse effects can be expected in this patient except ?
mcqs.explanation: Phenytoin causes hypocalcemia and hyperglycemia . It interferes with the metabolism of vitamin D and intestinal calcium absorption and results in hypocalcemia. Hyperglycemia and glycosuria can be seen due to the inhibition of insulin secretion . Long-term usage of phenytoin can also cause cutaneous pseudolymphoma which is mainly T-cell predominant.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following features would you not expect to find in a baby born to a woman on phenytoin therapy ?
mcqs.explanation: The newborn baby is unlikely to have gum hyperplasia . A baby born to a pregnant mother who was on phenytoin therapy will be suffering from fetal hydantoin syndrome. Features of fetal hydantoin syndrome are: • Microcephaly • Digital hypoplasia • Cleft lip/ cleft palate Gum hyperplasia is the most common adverse effect of phenytoin in children and young adolescents on chronic use .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with recent -onset primary generalized epilepsy develops a skin reaction due to phenytoin sodium. What is the most appropriate course of action?

options.b: Stop and restart phenytoin sodium after two weeks

mcqs.explanation: Hypersensitivity reaction to phenytoin warrants discontinuation of the drug. Switching to sodium valproate is the most appropriate course of action for this patient . Sodium valproate is one of the first-line agents indicated for GTCS. Clonazepam and ethosuximide are primarily used in absence seizures and are not indicated for GTCS. Clonazepam is indicated as adjunctive therapy in the absence seizures when first-line agents (ethosuximide, sodium valproate, lamotrigine) fail to control the seizures adequately .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 51-year-old male complains of severe , sharp, piercing intermittent electrical shock-like pain sensation on the left side of his face . The pain was triggered by talking, washing his face, eating , and brushing his teeth . Which of the following drugs is most effective to treat this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical features in this patient are suggestive of a diagnosis of trigeminal neuralgia and carbamazepine is the most effective agent for its treatment . If carbamazepine is ineffective , then second -line agents like lamotrigine and phenytoin are used . Sodium valproate although effective for trigeminal neuralgia lacks enough evidence for use .279

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true about carbamazepine?

options.a: It is indicated in focal seizures with impaired awareness
options.d: It is the drug of choice for status epilepticus

mcqs.explanation: Carbamazepine is indicated in focal seizures with impaired awareness . Carbamazepine is an antiepileptic drug that acts by prolonging the inactivated state of the Na+ channel similar to phenytoin . It is used in: • Focal seizures with impaired awareness • Focal seizures with intact awareness • Generalized tonic-clonic seizures • Trigeminal and related neuralgias • Manic depressive psychosis . Option B: Carbamazepine is an enzyme inducer. It is a substrate as well as an inducer of CYP3A4 and CYP2C9. Option C: Carbamazepine causes hyponatremia and not hypernatremia. Other side effects of carbamazepine include agranulocytosis or aplastic anemia, hepatotoxicity , water retention and hyponatremia (by potentiating ADH action ), and dose -related neurotoxicity . Option D: It is not used in status epilepticus . Lorazepam is the drug of choice for status epilepticus .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: If carbamazepine is added to ongoing valproate therapy , what adverse effect is risked?
mcqs.explanation: If carbamazepine is added to ongoing valproate therapy , it can result in hepatotoxicity . A combination of valproate and carbamazepine increases hepatotoxicity . Valproic acid may inhibit carbamazepine clearance and increase steady -state carbamazepine blood levels .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In patients recieving carbamazepine, which of the following idiosyncratic reactions are not expected to occur?
mcqs.explanation: Peripheral neuropathy is not an idiosyncratic reaction that can occur after carbamazepine use . It is a dose -dependent CNS adverse effect. It can be minimized by gradually increasing the dose from initiation or reducing the maintenance dose . Idiosyncratic reactions are hypersensitivity reactions like: • Rash • Steven-Johnson syndrome • Eosinophilia • Lymphadenopathy . • Diplopia280 Serious hematological toxicity includes aplastic anemia and agranulocytosis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man is on carbamazepine therapy . Which of the following is expected to occur in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Carbamazepine is expected to cause hyponatremia in this patient . Carbamazepine potentiates the action of antidiuretic hormone (ADH). It can result in water retention with decreased osmolarity and hyponatremia, especially in elderly patients with cardiac disease .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An 8-year-old child diagnosed to have focal seizures was initiated on oxcarbazepine. Which of the following would be incorrect regarding the agent being used ?

options.b: Enzyme induction potency is less when compared to carbamazepine
options.d: Hyponatremia risk is less when compared to carbamazepine

mcqs.explanation: The risk of hyponatremia with oxcarbazepine is higher when compared to carbamazepine. Option A: Oxcarbazepine is a keto analog of carbamazepine. It is a prodrug. The mechanism of action of oxcarbazepine is by blocking voltage -gated sodium channels (same as carbamazepine). Option C: Active form is metabolized by glucuronide conjugation. Option B: Oxcarbazepine does not cause auto-induction of metabolizing enzymes . It can induce CYP enzymes but less potent when compared to carbamazepine.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A neonate diagnosed with rhabdomyosarcoma was started on vincristine, cyclophosphamide , and cisplatin. A week after initiation of treatment , the baby had multiple episodes of seizures , refractory to diazepam and lidocaine . Workup revealed an elevated ADH level and euvolemic hyponatremia. Which of the following drugs can be used to treat this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of refractory seizures induced by hyponatremia caused by SIADH (due to anticancer drugs). Phenytoin is used to treat this patient . It is known to decrease ADH secretion and stop seizures by correcting severe hyponatremia. Options A and C: Carbamazepine and oxcarbazepine increase the antidiuretic hormone (ADH) levels . This leads to increased sensitivity of renal tubules to ADH levels and hyponatremia. Carbamazepine cannot be used in SIADH because of its antidiuretic effects . Option D: Phenobarbital does not affect ADH secretion or action and thus will be ineffective in stopping the seizures .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 5th -grade student , after receiving multiple complaints from teachers at school for repeated episodes of inattention was brought to the OPD. The mother gave a history that her child had brief spells of staring associated with lip-smacking movements. Which anti-epileptic drug is the most effective for this child?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical features are suggestive of absence seizures and ethosuximide is the most effective agent for this condition. First-line drugs in: • Typical absence seizures : Ethosuximide (drug of choice ), valproate, lamotrigine • Atypical absence seizures : Sodium valproate281

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A child with absence seizures improves after being treated with ethosuximide . Which of the following is the mechanism of action of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: The mechanism of action of ethosuximide is by inhibition of T-type Ca2+ channels in thalamic neurons at clinically relevant concentrations. It also affects other ion channels affected include voltage -gated sodium channels and potassium channels.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 10 -year-old child is brought to the OPD with a history of vacant stares lasting for about half a minute. The EEG shows a characteristic 3 Hz spike and wave pattern. Which of the following drugs can be used for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of absence seizures . Ethosuximide and valproate are the first-line drugs in this condition. Absence seizures are characterized by sudden , brief lapses of consciousness without loss of postural control. There is no postictal confusion. The following subtle motor signs may accompany the episodes • Rapid blinking of the eyelids • Chewing movements • Small-amplitude clonic movements of the hands Hyperventilation has a tendency to provoke absence seizures . First-line drugs include : • Typical absence seizures : Ethosuximide (drug of choice ), valproate, lamotrigine • Atypical absence seizures : Valproate

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an enzyme inducer?
mcqs.explanation: Sodium valproate is not an enzyme inducer. It is metabolized by CYP2C9/19 and is an inhibitor of CYP2C9. Phenytoin, phenobarbital, and carbamazepine are inducers of CYP and UGT enzymes .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not the mechanism of action of sodium valproate?

options.b: Inhibition of T type Ca2+ channels

mcqs.explanation: Sodium valproate has no action on the GABA transporter. Mechanism of action of sodium valproate: • Prolongation of sodium channel inactivation • Inhibition of T-type Ca2+ channels • Inhibition of GABA transaminase282 • Increases GABA synthesis from glutamic acid.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following are not adverse effects of sodium valproate?
mcqs.explanation: Osteomalacia is not an adverse effect of sodium valproate. The side effects of valproate (mnemonic: VALPROATE ) • Vomiting • Alopecia • Liver toxicity • Pancreatitis • Rash • Obesity • Anorexia • Teratogenicity (most common: spina bifida), thrombocytopenia , tremors • Edema

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antiepileptic drugs does not cause fulminant hepatitis as a serious complication?
mcqs.explanation: Vigabatrin is not associated with fulminant hepatitis . It is largely excreted unchanged in urine without undergoing any hepatic metabolism. Sodium valproate, felbamate and phenytoin are associated with fulminant hepatitis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old female patient is admitted to the neurology ward for evaluation of GTCS. She reports that she has been on oral contraceptive pills for the past 6 months. Which of the following drugs would you prescribe to this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Valproate is the drug used for this patient as it does not cause contraceptive failure. Valproate is an enzyme inhibitor and it inhibits the degradation of OCPs. OCPs thus have a longer duration of action and less incidence of contraceptive failure with valproate. However, other antiepileptic drugs like carbamazepine, phenytoin , phenobarbital, primidone, oxcarbazepine, topiramate are enzyme inducers. They cause increased degradation of OCPs and hence lead to contraceptive failure.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old patient was brought to the ER with bilateral jerking movements of arms. EEG revealed diffuse , symmetric, bilateral 4-6 Hz polyspike and wave discharges with a frontocentral predominance. What is the most appropriate drug for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical features and EEG findings are suggestive of juvenile myoclonic epilepsy . The most appropriate drug for management is sodium valproate.283 In patients with myoclonic seizures which are refractory to valproate, clonazepam or clobazam may be added .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old man visits the neurology OPD with complaints of tremors in both his hands which improve on alcohol intake. On examination, there is a significant worsening of tremors towards the end of finger-to-nose testing and head -nodding movements. Which antiepileptic is approved for use in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical features are suggestive of a diagnosis of essential tremors in this patient . Primidone is considered to be the first-line therapy for the same along with propranolol. Bilateral, symmetric tremors involving the hands associated with head nodding (titubation) and worsening of tremors towards the end of goal-directed movements such as drinking from a glass or finger-to-nose testing is suggestive of essential tremors. Primidone is a barbiturate and functions as a GABA enhancer. It is an enzyme inducer. It is used in the treatment of generalized tonic-clonic seizures and partial seizures . It has side effects like sedation , ataxia, and hyperactivity .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Pseudolymphoma may occur in patients on long-term therapy with:
mcqs.explanation: Phenytoin on long-term use can result in pseudolymphoma . This lymphadenopathy can be difficult to distinguish from malignant lymphoma. Although some studies suggest a causal relationship between phenytoin use and Hodgkin's disease , the data are far from conclusive. Almost all lesions are benign and termed as pseudolymphoma .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the most common adverse effect of phenytoin in children and young adolescents on chronic use ?
mcqs.explanation: Gingival hyperplasia occurs in patients on chronic phenytoin therapy . It is the most common manifestation in children and young adolescents . Gingival hyperplasia due to phenytoin therapy occurs due to tissue overgrowth secondary to altered collagen metabolism . The toothless portion of gums is not involved. It does not warrant discontinuation of the drug. It can be minimized by maintaining good oral hygiene .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a carbamazepine analogue that has an advantage of once daily dosing?
mcqs.explanation: Eslicarbazepine acetate is an analog of carbamazepine that has the advantage of once-daily dosing. It is a prodrug and is rapidly converted to active licarbazepine. Oxcarbazepine is an analog of carbamazepine that is also converted to licarbazepine. Oxcarbazepine does not have the advantage of once-daily dosing like eslicarbazepine acetate . Dacarbazine is not a carbamazepine analog like the other drugs and is a chemotherapy medication used in the treatment of melanoma and Hodgkin's lymphoma.284

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with a history of mitral stenosis presents with the given intractable finding that is refractory to conventional therapy . What is the drug of choice ?
mcqs.explanation: The drug used for refractory intractable rheumatic chorea is sodium valproate, as it doesn 't have extrapyramidal side effects . Sydenham's chorea is characterized by involuntary, purposeless , jerky movements which mainly affect the head and upper limbs. In the tongue , it is visible as the characteristic darting movements. Medications used to treat Sydenham chorea are: • Mild cases - Providing a calm environment. • Severe cases : • Dopamine antagonists - haloperidol , pimozide • Antiepileptic medications - sodium valproate, carbamazepine. • Severe, refractory cases - Steroids (thought to be immune-mediated ) • IV immunoglobulins, plasmapheresis - limited studies , decreased efficacy (not currently recommended)

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 10 -year-old child is brought to the OPD with a history of vacant stares lasting for about half a minute. The EEG shows <3 Hz spike and wave pattern. The first-line drug for the management of this condition is:
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and <3 Hz spike and wave pattern on EEG is suggestive of atypical absence seizures . The first-line drug in the treatment of atypical absence seizures is sodium valproate. Symmetric 3 Hz spike and wave pattern on EEG is seen in typical absence seizures . First-line drugs in its treatment include : • Ethosuximide (drug of choice ) • Valproate • Lamotrigine

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An 18-year-old girl was brought to the OPD with complaints of excessive growth of hair on her face and chest . She is a known case of epilepsy and is on treatment with phenytoin . Which of the following drugs would not cause this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette of excessive hair growth secondary to treatment with phenytoin is suggestive of hirsutism. Amantadine does not cause hirsutism or hypertrichosis but its characteristic side effect is livedo reticularis (bluish discoloration of the skin). Following are the drugs causing hirsutism: • Phenytoin • Anabolic steroids285 • Danazol • Metoclopramide • Methyldopa • Phenothiazines • Progestins • Reserpine • Testosterone Following are the drugs causing hypertrichosis: • Cyclosporine • Diazoxide • Hydrocortisone • Minoxidil • Penicillamine • Phenytoin • Psoralens • Streptomycin286

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following anti-epileptics is an AMPA glutamate receptor antagonist?
mcqs.explanation: Perampanel is a selective non-competitive antagonist of the AMPA-type glutamate receptor . It is approved for adjunctive therapy of focal-onset seizures . Options A and B: Levetiracetam and brivaracetam act on SV2A proteins and modulates GABA and glutamate release . Option D: Rufinamide acts on voltage -gated sodium channels.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following mechanisms of action is observed with levetiracetam ?

options.c: Binding to synaptic vesicular protein SV2A

mcqs.explanation: Levetiracetam has a binding affinity to synaptic vesicular protein SV2A . SV2A plays a role in vesicle recycling following exocytosis of neurotransmitter When levetiracetam bind to this synaptic vesicular protein, it decreases the release of excitatory neurotransmitter glutamate thus preventing seizures . Levetiracetam also inhibits N-type Ca2+ channels and Ca2+ release from intracellular stores .Thus, it is considered a broad-spectrum antiepileptic as it has an effect on multiple channels.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A known epileptic patient on levetiracetam has been seizure -free for 2 years. But he develops agitation and anger issues interfering with his day-to-day activities as a result of the drug intake. Which of the following measures is to be taken next?

options.a: Slowly taper the drug over next 6 months
options.b: Continue levetriacetam since a 5 year seizure free interval is needed
options.c: Stop levetiracetam and start on a different anti-epileptic
options.d: Discontinue the drug as he is seizure free

mcqs.explanation: The mood changes observed in the above patient must be due to an adverse effect of levetiracetam . Abrupt stoppage of the drug can result in rebound seizures . So the best management will be to slowly taper the drug over the next 6 months. Adverse effects of levetiracetam : • Somnolence • Asthenia • Ataxia • Dizziness. • Mood and behavioral changes • Psychotic reactions (rare)295

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Tiagabine has been initiated as an adjunctive treatment for focal seizures in a patient . What is the mechanism of action of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Tiagabine acts by inhibiting the GAT1 GABA transporter, thereby reducing its reuptake into neurons. It also increases the duration of inhibitory impulses in the synapse by prolonging the action of GABA. Tiagabine is approved as an add-on therapy for refractory partial seizures with or without generalization. Other antiepileptic drugs that have GABA enhancing activity are vigabatrin and stiripentol .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old patient diagnosed with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome was prescribed a drug with NMDA antagonist activity. Identify the drug.
mcqs.explanation: Felbamate is the NMDA receptor antagonist prescribed to this patient . It also potentiates GABA action. It is indicated in refractory primary or secondary generalized seizures and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. Felbamate is associated with aplastic anemia and liver failure. Option A: Memantine is used in Alzheimer's disease . Option B: Riluzole is used in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis . Option C: Ketamine causes dissociative anesthesia and used in general anesthesia .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An antiepileptic agent which acts by opening neuronal potassium channels was prescribed to a patient admitted to the neurology ward. On discharge , the patient was asked to have a regular ophthalmological examination every 6 months. Which drug is most likely prescribed ?
mcqs.explanation: Ezogabine (retigabine) acts by opening neuronal potassium channels. By opening the K+ channels, stabilizes the resting membrane potential and reduces the excitability of the nerve membrane. FDA recommends that patients on chronic ezogabine therapy need visual acuity and fundus examination every 6 months due to the possibility of retinal abnormalities. Option B: Rufinamide acts by prolonging an inactive state of the Na+ channel. Option C: Vigabatrin is a GABA transaminase inhibitor. Option D: Gabaculine is an irreversible GABA reuptake inhibitor, that has only experimental value , due to high toxicity .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: All of the following statements are true about zonisamide except :

options.b: Nephrolithiasis is not a side effect
options.d: Blocks low voltage gated Na+ channel

mcqs.explanation: Nephrolithiasis is a side effect of zonisamide. Zonisamide is a broad-spectrum antiepileptic , that acts by blocking low voltage Na+ channels and T type calcium channels. It also has carbonic anhydrase inhibiting activity that may result in metabolic acidosis and the formation of renal stones . It is used in the treatment of focal seizures .296

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Patients on which of the following antiepileptic drugs will experience weight loss?
mcqs.explanation: Topiramate causes weight loss as one of its common side effects .
