Topiramate has mixed mechanisms of action: • Reduces voltage gate Na+ currents • Activates hyperpolarizing K+ currents • Enhances postsynaptic GABAA current • Limits the activation of AMPA subtype of glutamate receptors . Topiramate is used in focal seizures , GTCS and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. The side effects : • Cognitive impairment • Weight loss • Fatigue • Renal calculi Sodium valproate, vigabatrin (highest incidence ), and carbamazepine cause weight gain.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old patient presented to the OPD with complaints of pain over a healed dermatomal rash on his lateral chest wall. Gabapentin was prescribed to this patient . The analgesic activity of this drug is mainly exerted by which of the following ?

options.a: Increasing the duration of GABA Cl- channel opening
options.c: Inhibiting the uptake of GABA at the presynaptic membrane

mcqs.explanation: Gabapentin exerts its analgesic activity by inhibiting the Ca2+ channel current in this patient who is most likely suffering from post -herpetic neuralgia. Gabapentin and pregabalin have close structural similarity to GABA. Still, they do not act through the effects of GABA receptors or any other mechanism related to GABA-mediated neurotransmission. They inhibit the calcium channel current which decreases the entry of calcium in the presynaptic neuron. When calcium entry in the neuron is reduced , there is a decrease in the release of glutamate . This lowers the excitability of the neuron, thus reducing seizure activity. Therapeutic use of these drugs: Gabapentin: Focal seizures , postherpetic neuralgia pain Pregabalin: Focal seizures , postherpetic neuralgia pain, diabetic neuropathy pain, spinal cord injury pain, fibromyalgia pain.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An infant presents with sudden jerky movements of the head , neck and arms. On EEG evaluation, a characteristic pattern of hypsarrhythmia is observed. Which is the GABA transaminase inhibitor approved for the treatment of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with hypsarrytmia on EEG is suggestive of West syndrome. Vigabatrin is an inhibitor of the GABA transaminase that can be used in this297 condition. Inhibition of the enzyme GABA transaminase leads to an increase in the concentration of GABA in the synaptic cleft which is an inhibitory neurotransmitter. This contributes to its anticonvulsant property of vigabatrin . West syndrome is a rare type of epilepsy syndrome that begins in infancy. It is characterized by a triad of: • Infantile seizures (also called salaam spells ) • Developmental regression • Hypsarrhythmia i.e Himalayan wave pattern on EEG Treatment of West syndrome includes : • ACTH • Vigabatrin if associated with tuberous sclerosis

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the drug of choice in the treatment of infantile spasms?
mcqs.explanation: The drug of choice in the treatment of infantile spasms or West syndrome is adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH.) The mechanism of action of ACTH or glucocorticoids is unknown but may involve a reduction in inflammatory processes . Vigabatrin is used if the spasms are associated with tuberous sclerosis . Other antiseizure medications that may be helpful are valproate, topiramate, zonisamide, or benzodiazepines .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which antiepileptic drug is associated with permanent visual loss?
mcqs.explanation: Vigabatrin is associated with progressive and permanent visual loss. It is a GABA transaminase inhibitor indicated in: • West syndrome associated with tuberous sclerosis • Refractory focal seizures with impaired awareness .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antiepileptic drugs are approved for prophylaxis in patients suffering from migraines?
mcqs.explanation: Sodium valproate, topiramate and gabapentin are approved anti-epileptics for use in prophylaxis of migraine. Carbamazepine, phenytoin and rufinamide are not used for prophylaxis of a migraine.298

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 22 -year-old female is brought to the casualty with seizures for the past 10 minutes . History from relatives suggests no seizure -free intervals in the past 10 minutes . After stabilizing the vitals of the patient , which is the first drug you administer to the patient ?
mcqs.explanation: This scenario described above is of status epilepticus . The first drug used in the management is lorazepam. Status epilepticus refers to continuous seizures or repetitive , discrete seizures with impaired consciousness in the inter-ictal period . For practical purposes , it is defined as any one of the following : • Continuing seizures >5 minutes or • No regaining of consciousness between 2 seizures . Management of status epilepticus :

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old newly married female comes to the OPD with a positive urine pregnancy test . Her history is suggestive of antiepileptic use since 8 years. Which of the following statements is incorrect about further management in this patient ?

options.a: Anti epileptic agents has to be continued at stabilised doses
options.b: Immediately stop antiepileptics once pregnancy is detected
options.d: No antiepiletic is deemed safe in pregnancy

mcqs.explanation: Stopping antiepileptics abruptly once pregnancy is detected in this patient is not recommended . If this is done, then there is a lot of risk to the fetus by uncontrolled seizures and can result in anoxia and intellectual disability . Antiepileptics have to be continued and then the dose can be tapered slowly if there are no episodes of seizures . Management of seizures in pregnancy: • If the patient is a known case of seizure and is on any antiepileptic drug: The same prescribed drug is continued • If the first episode occurs during pregnancy: The drug preferred is either lamotrigine or levetiracetam • Folic acid (1-4 mg/day) should be given to all No antiepileptic is deemed safe in pregnancy. So, it is important to have the patient on monotherapy at the lowest effective dose , especially during the first trimester.299

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An infant is born with a birth defect as shown in the image below . It is the most common teratogenic effect of:
mcqs.explanation: The above illustration is suggestive of an infant with spina bifida of the open type which is the most common teratogenic effect of sodium valproate. Option A: Phenytoin is usually associated with fetal hydantoin syndrome. Option B: Topiramate has shown growth defects in animal studies and hypospadias have been shown in the male fetus but the definite relationship is lacking. Option D: Phenobarbital has teratogenic effects similar to phenytoin .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which is the treatment of choice for juvenile myoclonic epilepsy in pregnancy?
mcqs.explanation: The drug of choice for juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (JME) in pregnancy is levetiracetam . Lamotrigine or levetiracetam are alternative first-line in pregnancy as they have fewer teratogenic effects . The drug of choice for JME is valproate. However, in pregnant women or women of childbearing age , valproate should be avoided because of the increased risks of fetal malformations and neurodevelopmental delay . Carbamazepine, vigabatrin , and phenytoin are not indicated in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy as they may worsen myoclonic jerks and absence seizures .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 29-year-old primigravida , at 4-months period of gestation and history of juvenile myoclonic epilepsy , visits your clinic. She has been regularly taking sodium valproate and is now concerned about the medication possibly affecting her child. What would you suggest to this patient ?

options.a: Immediately taper valproate and start lamotrigine
options.b: Continue valproate with serial drug monitoring

mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, the patient should be advised to continue valproate, and serial drug monitoring should be done. Valproate has a higher teratogenic potential . It is usually avoided before conception if other antiepileptics with less teratogenicity (lamotrigine. levetiracetam ) can be used . But for a woman who is pregnant and is already taking valproate, changing the drug is not recommended . Option A - The patient is presenting in the second trimester when organogenesis would have been complete . Therefore, tapering the drug and introducing lamotrigine is not an option as precipitating seizures has a greater risk of fetal harm at this stage . Option C: Carbamazepine is not indicated in JME as it may worsen the myoclonic jerks and absence seizures. Option D- Adding additional drugs to stabilized doses may increase teratogenicity . So adding lamotrigine to valproate is also not a viable option.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is recommended for prophylaxis in a pregnant woman who is on anti-epileptic drugs with an enzyme-inducing property ?
mcqs.explanation: 300 Vitamin K is recommended for prophylaxis in pregnant women who are on antiepileptic drugs having enzyme-inducing properties . Antiepileptic drugs with enzyme inducing properties : • Phenytoin • Carbamazepine • Oxcarbazepine • Topiramate • Phenobarbital • Primidone They induce CYP enzymes that interfere with the metabolism of vitamin K. Deficiency of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors can occur in the newborn leading to coagulopathy and intracerebral hemorrhage. Although hemorrhage is uncommon, the mother should be treated with oral vitamin K, 20 mg/day in the last two weeks of pregnancy. The infant should receive an intramuscular injection of vitamin K (1 mg) at birth.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antiepileptics is effective in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, but shows the highest propensity to cause rashes in young children warranting its withdrawal ?
mcqs.explanation: Lamotrigine is effective in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and has the highest propensity to cause rashes in young children. Lamotrigine is also associated with toxic epidermal necrosis and Stevens -Johnson Syndrome in some patients . The incidence of serious rash and other serious skin conditions is higher with lamotrigine than other anti-epileptics provided in the options . The occurrence of rash warrants the stoppage of the drug. Option A: Sodium valproate is the drug of choice in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. It can cause fulminant hepatitis especially in children < 2 years. Option B: Levetiracetam is also effective in most of the seizures present in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. It can increase blood pressure in children < 4 years. Option D: Vigabatrin is also effective in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, especially as an add-on therapy. It can cause permanent visual field defects .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Patients receiving which of the following anti-microbial drugs are least likely to develop seizures ?
mcqs.explanation: Macrolides are the least likely anti-microbial out of the given options to cause seizures . Antimicrobials associated with causing seizures : • Beta-lactam and related compounds • Quinolones301 • Acyclovir • Isoniazid • Ganciclovir Other groups of drugs that are implicated in causing epilepsy : • Alkylating agents - busulfan , chlorambucil • Antimalarials - chloroquine, mefloquine • Anesthetics / analgesics - meperidine , fentanyl , tramadol, local anesthetics • Immunomodulatory drugs - cyclosporine , tacrolimus, interferons • Psychotropics : • Antidepressants - bupropion • Antipsychotics - clozapine • Anti-manic drugs - lithium • Drugs of abuse - amphetamine , cocaine, phencyclidine , methylphenidate • Miscellaneous - Theophylline , memantine.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs of abuse is least likely to be associated with seizures ?
mcqs.explanation: Cannabinoids are being investigated for the treatment of various types of epilepsy and are least likely to cause seizures . Drugs of abuse that are implicated in causing seizures are: • Amphetamine • Cocaine • Phencyclidine • Methylphenidate

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presented to the OPD with a skin rash for 3 days. He gives a history of antiepileptic drug use for 2 months and is ataxic on examination. He is diagnosed to have Stevens -Johnson syndrome. Which of the following drugs are implicated in these adverse effects ?
mcqs.explanation: Lamotrigine is known to cause such adverse effects in patients . Adverse effects of lamotrigine: • Skin rash • Stevens -Johnson syndrome • Dizziness • Diplopia • Sedation302 • Ataxia • Headache

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs if used can lead to behavioral effects such as aggression ?
mcqs.explanation: Children who are on levetiracetam have a higher risk of developing several behavioral side -effects such as aggression , hostility , and nervousness compared to children who do not use levetiracetam . These side effects are seen in less frequency with brivaracetam .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drug is approved for use in fibromyalgia?
mcqs.explanation: Pregabalin is approved for use in fibromyalgia. It is also approved for use in diabetic peripheral neuropathy . Mechanism of analgesic action: • Interacts at the binding site of the alpha, delta subunit of voltage -dependent Ca2+ channels • Correlates with decreased Ca2+ channel function and release of neurotransmitters • Decreased neurotransmitter release is associated with reduced neuronal hyperexcitability . Options A and C: Gabapentin and tiagabine are also useful in fibromyalgia but are not approved for this indication and are used off-label . Option D: Topiramate's efficacy is not encouraging in fibromyalgia and neuropathic pain.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the first-line treatment for infantile spasms associated with tuberous sclerosis ?
mcqs.explanation: Vigabatrin is particularly effective in infantile spasms associated with tuberous sclerosis and is considered the first-line treatment in this condition. ACTH is considered to be the drug of choice for infantile spasms that are not associated with tuberous sclerosis .303

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the primary mechanism of action of typical antipsychotics ?
mcqs.explanation: Typical or first-generation antipsychotics primarily act by postsynaptic D2 receptor blockade. The second -generation or atypical antipsychotics mainly act by blocking 5HT2A receptors but they also have weak D2 blocking effect . Histaminic H1 and muscarinic M1 receptors are blocked by most of the first and second generation agents . This contributes to sedation and anticholinergic effects of antipsychotics . Option C: Ropinirole and pramipexole are D2 agonists used in restless leg syndrome and Parkinson 's disease . Option D: Lorcaserin is a 5HT2C agonist that was used to treat obesity . It was withdrawn in 2020 as it was linked to increased cancer risk .Antipsychotics Drugs First-generation D2 antagonistsChlorpromazi neHaloperidolFluphenazine , TrifluoperazineThiothixene Second -generati on 5HT2Aand D2antagonistsClo zapineIloperidoneOlanzapine QuetiapineRisperidoneZipras idoneD2partial agonistsAripi prazoleCariprazineD2and D3 antagonistAmisulpride5HT2 Ainverse agonist without D2b indingPimavanserin

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with psychosis was prescribed an antipsychotic medication. Which one of the following side effects cannot be explained by the antagonistic action of the drug on D2 receptors ?
mcqs.explanation: Constipation and dry mouth are side effects of antipsychotics that have potent antimuscarinic action. Hyperprolactinaemia , affective flattening, and rigidity in neuroleptic malignant syndrome occur due to D2 receptor blockade.311 Apart from their action on D2 and 5-HT receptors , antipsychotic drugs also exert the following effects :Action of dru g Example Side effect Anti-muscari nic ChlorpromazineThioridazine Olanzapine Dry mouth, constipation , dila ted pupil , urinary retention Alpha blocker ChlorpromazineClozapine Hypotension , sedation H1 blocker Risperidone Antiemetic , sedation

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A woman presented with sudden onset high-grade fever, muscle rigidity, and altered sensorium. She had been on antipsychotic therapy with chlorpromazine. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The features are suggestive of neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) that is associated with the use of typical antipsychotics like chlorpromazine. Malignant neuroleptic syndrome is characterized by extreme muscle rigidity, fever, unstable BP and myoglobinemia. It can even lead to death . It can occur weeks to months after initiation of antipsychotic therapy and can persist for up to a week after discontinuation of the drug. The probable mechanism of this condition is dopamine antagonism. It is treated by stopping the offending antipsychotic immediately , supportive care, dantrolene , and bromocriptine.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old patient presents to the OPD with complaints of a brownish hue to her vision since 2 weeks . She has a history of being on antipsychotic medication for the past 10 weeks . Complete workup reveals pigmentary retinopathy in this patient . Which of the following drugs is implicated in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The pigmentary retinopathy seen in this patient is an adverse effect seen with the use of thioridazine which is a typical antipsychotic . In advanced cases , the deposits may resemble retinitis pigmentosa and the deposits are associated with 'browning of vision'. The drug is rarely used as it causes prolongation of QTc interval.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient having both positive and negative symptoms of schizophrenia was prescribed an atypical antipsychotic with partial D2 agonism. Identify the drug.
mcqs.explanation: Aripiprazole is an atypical antipsychotic showing D2 partial agonism. It has a higher affinity for D2 receptors than for 5HT2A receptors . As a partial agonist, aripiprazole has a dual-action which makes it useful in patients with both positive and negative symptoms of schizophrenia. Options A & D: Clozapine and risperidone are atypical antipsychotics with predominant 5HT2A antagonistic activity over D2 antagonism. Option B: Fluphenazine is a typical antipsychotic . They have predominant D2 antagonism property and such action on the mesocortical pathway may increase the negative symptoms of312 schizophrenia.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following atypical antipsychotics is a preferential D3 receptor partial agonist?
mcqs.explanation: Cariprazine is an atypical antipsychotic which is also a preferential D3 receptor partial agonist. Like other atypical antipsychotics, it also blocks D2 and 5-HT2 receptors . Option A: Aripiprazole is a dual D2/D3 partial agonist but it has no preference for the D3 receptor . Option C: Clozapine is a D2 receptor antagonist. Option D: Amisulpride is a D2 and D3 receptor antagonist.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antipsychotics should be given sublingually ?
mcqs.explanation: Asenapine is only available as an orally disintegrating tablet preparation that has to be administered sublingually . It undergoes very high first-pass metabolism and so bioavailability is very low via the oral route. Hence , sublingual administration is preferred .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A schizophrenic patient was initiated on haloperidol therapy . 2 days later he presented to the OPD with deviation of his eyes , asymmetric neck posture and inability to open his mouth completely . What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of deviation of the eyes (oculogyric crisis), asymmetric position of the head or neck (torticollis) and inability to open the mouth (trismus) are pointing towards a diagnosis of haloperidol -induced acute dystonia. These extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS) occur due to the antagonism of dopamine D2 receptors . Acute dystonia is more commonly associated with high potency typical antipsychotics like haloperidol and occurs within 1 to 5 days of initiation of therapy . Benztropine or diphenhydramine may be used for treatment.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man complains of feeling restless and irritable with an irresistible urge to move. He had recently been started on antipsychotic therapy with haloperidol . He appears agitated and paces up and down the room. What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The features mentioned are suggestive of akathisia that is commonly associated with the use of high potency typical antipsychotics like haloperidol . Akathisia is described as subjective complaints of restlessness accompanied by observed movements such as movement of the legs , rocking from foot to foot, pacing, or inability to sit or stand still . It can occur at any time after 5-60 days from starting the drug. Treatment of akathisia: • Following a slower dose titration schedule , dose reduction , or switching to a less potent antipsychotic313 • First-line drugs - beta-blockers • Second line drugs - benzodiazepines like lorazepam • Third line drugs - anticholinergic agents like trihexyphenidyl , benztropine

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs does not cause neuroleptic malignant syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Amantadine does not cause neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome resembles very severe parkinsonism and is caused by D2 receptor antagonists. Amantadine increases the presynaptic release of dopamine and has agonist and modulatory action at postsynaptic D2 receptors . Option C: Quetiapine is an atypical antipsychotic . Although this class of antipsychotics has a lower chance of causing NMS compared to typical antipsychotics , but cases of fatal NMS following the administration of quetiapine have been recorded . Options B and D: Metoclopramide and domperidone are gastro kinetic agents with D2 antagonism. Although domperidone has restricted entry across blood-brain barrier when compared to metoclopramide , there are reports of NMS with this agent .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following effects of chlorpromazine is not due to its antidopaminergic activity?
mcqs.explanation: Orthostatic hypotension is due to the alpha-receptor blocking the action of chlorpromazine. Chlorpromazine is a typical or first-generation antipsychotic with D2 blocking and additional alpha-receptor-blocking and anticholinergic activity. Option A: Dopamine inhibits prolactin release causing hypoprolactinemia and hence antidopaminergic action of chlorpromazine causes hyperprolactinemia . Option B: Extrapyramidal side effects occur due to D2 antagonism in the nigrostriatal region. Option C: The antiemetic action is due to D2 antagonism in the chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ ).314

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following atypical antipsychotics has the highest risk of galactorrhea?
mcqs.explanation: Among atypical antipsychotics , risperidone and paliperidone have the highest risk of galactorrhea. The adverse effect occurs due to their higher D2 blocking potency .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old with schizophrenia has not responded to adequate treatment with two different antipsychotics . Which of the following would be the drug of choice for his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The drug of choice for treatment -resistant schizophrenia is clozapine. Treatment-resistant schizophrenia is the lack of response to two different antipsychotics given at adequate dosages for a minimum duration of 4-6 weeks . If patients demonstrate even a mild amount of improvement during this period, it may be reasonable to wait before changing the medication, since patients may improve at a steady rate for 3-6 months.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man is brought to the casualty following an episode of seizure . He says he was recently switched to a higher dose of his antipsychotic medication. Which drug is he most likely on?
mcqs.explanation: The drug most likely implicated here is clozapine as it has the highest risk of precipitating seizures . It causes dose -dependent lowering of the seizure threshold . Clozapine-associated seizures can be treated with sodium valproate. Clozapine side effects : (Mnemonic - "Some say Clozapine has too many nasty adverse effects ") • Seizures • Sedation • Constipation315 • Hypotension /hypersalivation • Tachycardia • Mass increase: weight gain and increased appetite • Nausea and vomiting • Agranulocytosis (neutropenia ) • Enuresis and polyuria

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true regarding clozapine?

options.a: More potently blocks D2 as compared to D1 receptors
options.b: Drug concentration is kept below 350ng/ml to avoid agranulocytosis
options.c: Should not be used along with carbamazepine
options.d: Should be discontinued if the neutrophil count is below 500/microL

mcqs.explanation: Agranulocytosis is an immune-mediated adverse effect and unlike seizures , it is not dependent on dose . Thus, agranulocytosis can happen at any plasma concentration of clozapine and concentration < 350 ng/mL does not lower the risk . Option A: Clozapine is an atypical antipsychotic , which acts by blocking the 5HT2, �o 2 and D4 receptors . The potency of block is D4 > D2 >D1. Option C: Concomitant administration of carbamazepine with clozapine is contraindicated because of the increased risk of leukopenia . In addition, carbamazepine is an enzyme inducer and reduces the half-life of clozapine. Option D: Administration of clozapine requires regular blood count monitoring due to the risk of agranulocytosis. Monitoring is performed weekly for the first 6 months and once in two weeks for the next 6 months. Patients must be asked to report for evaluation in case of symptoms such as fever or sore throat. Clozapine should be discontinued if the neutrophil count drops below 500 cells /�ML.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old woman presented to the ophthalmology OPD with complaints of diminution of vision. She has bipolar disorder and has been on antipsychotic therapy for the past 8 months. Ophthalmic examination revealed the finding seen in the below image . What drug was she most likely on?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a whitish opacity in the pupillary region and this in combination with the presenting features are suggestive of cataract. This is an adverse effect seen with the use of quetiapine which is an atypical antipsychotic .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antipsychotics cause QT prolongation at therapeutic doses ?
mcqs.explanation: Haloperidol , quetiapine and ziprasidone cause QT prolongation at therapeutic doses .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Patient X and patient Y are on different antipsychotics . X has gained a lot of weight and has been feeling dizzy when she stands. Y has not gained weight , but is very restless and keeps pacing around the room. The drugs they are most likely taking are:
mcqs.explanation: The most likely option amongst the given options is: Patient X is taking olanzapine which has side effects of weight gain and hypotension .316 Olanzapine and clozapine account for most cases of weight gain and drug-induced diabetes mellitus . Patient Y is taking haloperidol and has developed the side effect of akathisia. This is an extrapyramidal effect in which the patient is restless , irritable, and feels an urge to keep moving. Haloperidol has a high risk of developing extrapyramidal side effects such as akathisia, dystonia, and tardive dyskinesia.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a side effect of ziprasidone?
mcqs.explanation: Ziprasidone causes prolongation of QT interval. It should be avoided in patients with a history of cardiac arrhythmias and should not be given in combination with other drugs known to prolong the QT interval. The other options mentioned are side effects of clozapine.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman suffering from Huntington's chorea is on haloperidol . Which of the following adverse drug effects is best attributed to the supersensitivity of dopamine receptors ?

options.a: Muscle rigidity, labile blood pressure, hyperreflexia , hyperthermia , tachycardia, tremors
options.b: Lip smacking, facial dyskinesia, protrusion and rolling of the tongue , involuntary movements of the extremities
options.c: Facial grimacing, involuntary upward eye movement, laryngeal spasm and arching of the trunk forward
options.d: Stooped posture , rigidity, shuffling gait, bradykinesia, and pill rolling tremors

mcqs.explanation: Lip-smacking, facial dyskinesia, protrusion and rolling of the tongue , and involuntary movements of the extremities are characteristic of tardive dyskinesia. This is caused by supersensitivity of dopamine receptors . It occurs as a consequence of chronic postsynaptic D2 receptor blockade by antipsychotics , which results in upregulation and supersensitivity of postsynaptic dopamine receptors . Tardive dyskinesia is usually seen in patients treated with typical antipsychotics (first generation) for more than a year. This may be reversible with early recognition and drug discontinuation. Treatment is with valbenazine, deutetrabenazine (VMAT2 inhibitors).

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old man is brought by his family with complaints of mental instability . On questioning , he says that he sees his grandparents in the room and talks to them often but the family confirms that it's been 10 years since his grandparents passed away. He was then prescribed an antipsychotic drug following which he developed parkinsonism . Which of the following antiviral drugs\037 can be used for treating his condition?
mcqs.explanation: Amantadine is an antiviral agent that is the most commonly used medication for antipsychotic-induced parkinsonism . It increases the concentration of dopamine (DA) at the synapse and appears to act by certain mechanisms like: • presynaptic DA reuptake blockade • facilitation of DA release • postsynaptic DA agonism • receptor modulation317

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statement is false with respect to antipsychotics and pregnancy?

options.b: Olanzapine is unlikely to increase the risk of birth defects
options.c: There is a high risk of gestational diabetes and neonatal seizures with clozapine
options.d: Guidelines recommend switching from clozapine to another drug during pregnancy

mcqs.explanation: The guidelines recommend continuing the same antipsychotic , as switching the drug during pregnancy would cause a higher rate of relapse . Antipsychotic drugs and pregnancy: • Crossing the placenta : Olanzapine > Haloperidol > Risperidone > Quetiapine . • Olanzapine is unlikely to increase the risk of birth defects above the background population risk . However, it can cause low birth weight and increased NICU admissions. • Clozapine is associated with gestational diabetes and neonatal seizures . Note : Although antipsychotic drugs appear to be relatively safe in pregnancy, the available data does not provide adequate guidance on the choice of agent . Because of limited experience in humans, olanzapine should be used in pregnancy only when the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus .318

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which is a mood stabiliser with an anti-suicidal role?
mcqs.explanation: Lithium is a mood stabilizer with an antisuicidal role. Maintenance treatment with lithium has shown to decrease the rate of suicide in mood disorders. Lithium was found to be better than other mood stabilizers such as carbamazepine, lamotrigine, and valproate. Lithium is also used in recurrent depression with a cyclic pattern is controlled by either lithium or imipramine. It is also used to augment standard antidepressant response in acute major depression in those patients who have had an inadequate response to monotherapy.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old man is brought to the psychiatry OPD by his mother with complaints that he has been behaving aggressively for the last 10 days. He believes he owns the biggest automobile company in the world and talks about how his made-up company will put satellites into space someday . She also says that he sleeps for only 3 hours a day. Which of the following drugs cannot be used to treat this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical features given are suggestive of acute mania in this patient and lamotrigine is not indicated in this condition. It requires a slow , extended titration to minimize the risk of Stevens -Johnson syndrome and is used for maintenance therapy in bipolar disorder. Lithium, sodium valproate, carbamazepine , and atypical antipsychotics are indicated in acute mania. Lithium is indicated in both acute mania and maintenance therapy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient is being treated with lithium for manic-depressive psychosis . Which of the following is true about the use of this drug?

options.a: Can be given alone for acute episodes
options.b: Serum concentration monitoring is not used for dose adjustment
options.c: Cause benign and reversible flattening of T wave on ECG

mcqs.explanation: Prolonged use of lithium causes a benign and reversible flattening of T-wave. Option A: Lithium is usually not given alone in acute episodes as the onset of antimanic action is slow. Benzodiazepines , anticonvulsants, or atypical antipsychotics are administered along with lithium in the early phases of treatment . Option B: Lithium has a very narrow therapeutic index and monitoring of serum concentration is used for guiding dose adjustment . Option D: Lithium causes significant weight gain.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient on lithium therapy is diagnosed to be hypertensive . Which of the following antihypertensive drugs is contraindicated here?
mcqs.explanation: Thiazides are contraindicated in patients who are on lithium therapy . Thiazide diuretics cause significant reductions in Li + clearance that result in toxic levels .324 The K+ sparing diuretics have modest effects on lithium excretion, with a mild increase in serum levels . Loop diuretics have a limited impact on Li + serum levels .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with a history of mania , on lithium therapy , is brought with complaints of vomiting and multiple episodes of diarrhea. On examination, coarse tremors and an ataxic gait are noted . What is the expected level of serum lithium in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Clinical features are suggestive of lithium toxicity , where serum levels >1.5 mEq/L are considered toxic. Lithium has a narrow therapeutic index (0.8–1.2 mEq/L) and therefore requires monitoring to suspect toxicity . The toxic effects of lithium usually start manifesting when the serum level crosses 1.5 mEq/L . Acute intoxication is characterized by: • Vomiting • Profuse diarrhea • Coarse tremors • Ataxia • Coma • Convulsions. A fine action tremor is common in patients taking lithium at therapeutic doses and can develop at any time during treatment . Therapeutic lithium tremor is generally symmetric, limited to the arms, and nonprogressive.Tremor from lithium toxicity is coarser and more disabling, may also affect the legs , and occurs with other symptoms of toxicity . Serious effects of lithium toxicity will involve confusion, hyperreflexia , and seizures . Motor and cognitive side effects can become irreversible with persistent cerebellar tremor being the most common.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: At what serum lithium levels would you consider dialysis in acute lithium toxicity ?
mcqs.explanation: In acute overdoses , hemodialysis is indicated in: • Serum lithium level is > 4.0 mEq/L • Patients exhibiting symptoms of toxicity . Note : While hemodialysis is considered when serum lithium level is 4.0 mEq/L and above, signs of lithium toxicity usually start showing when the serum level is > 1.5 mEq/L . One should not get confused between the two .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Patients with which of the following conditions do not warrant lithium therapy ?
mcqs.explanation: 325 Lithium is not indicated in generalized anxiety disorder. Bipolar disorder is the primary indication for lithium. Option A: Effect of leukocytosis may hasten recovery from cancer chemotherapy -induced leukopenia and agranulocytosis . Option B: Unipolar depression can be treated with lithium as an adjuvant in resistant cases . Option C: Vasculogenic headaches like cluster headaches .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following must be administered initially in patients with acute mania with psychotic features ?
mcqs.explanation: In acute mania , even in patients without overt psychotic manifestations , atypical antipsychotics like olanzapine is used initially for rapid control of psychosis . Atypical antipsychotics are also effective as monotherapy. The therapeutic effects of lithium, carbamazepine, and valproic acid are seen only after a few days. Therefore they are effective only with daily dosing with adequate serum monitoring.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with mania has been initiated on lithium therapy . While counseling the patient about the medication, which of the following effects do you mention as the most common CNS adverse effect ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common CNS adverse effect of lithium in the therapeutic dose range is fine postural hand tremors. Therapeutic lithium tremor is generally symmetric, limited to the arms, and nonprogressive. Options A and B: Ataxia, slurred speech , and/or incoordination are adverse effects seen during peak CNS/serum concentrations. Single bedtime dosing can avoid these adverse effects . Option D: Coarse tremors are seen in case of lithium toxicity and is more disabling and may also affect the legs.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient on chronic lithium therapy is diagnosed to have hypothyroidism . What should be the next course of action?

options.a: Stop lithium immediately and start exogenous thyroid replacement
options.b: Stop lithium immediately and wait for normalisation of thyroid status
options.c: Continue lithium along with exogenous thyroid replacement
options.d: Decrease the dose of lithium and wait for normalisation of thyroid status

mcqs.explanation: Hypothyroidism developed in a patient on chronic lithium therapy is treated by exogenous replacement of thyroid hormones. It is not a reason for the discontinuation of lithium therapy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old woman presents with complaints of increased frequency of urination and fatigue . She gives a history of lithium intake for bipolar mood disorder for the past 6 years. On investigations, her serum osmolality was 300 mOsm/L and her urine osmolality was 250 mOsm/L. Which of the following drugs is used to treat this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with a history of lithium intake and investigations showing \032serum osmolality and \031urine osmolality is suggestive of nephrogenic diabetes insipidus secondary to lithium toxicity . Amiloride is the drug of choice for this condition.326 Amiloride is a potassium -sparing diuretic. It inhibits the renal epithelial Na+ channel (ENac channel) in collecting duct cells . It blocks the entry of Li + ions through the ENac channels and thus mitigates diabetes insipidus induced by lithium. Thiazide diuretics cause significant reductions in Li + clearance that result in toxic levels . Thiazides are contraindicated in patients who are on lithium therapy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A female patient is on first-line pharmacological therapy for bipolar disorder for 6 months. She is fasting for a few days due to religious reasons and presented with seizures , coarse tremors, confusion, and weakness of limbs. Which of the following investigations should be done to help diagnose her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical features given in the question are most likely suggestive of lithium toxicity , and hence serum lithium levels should be measured to confirm it. Lithium is a mood stabilizer with a very narrow therapeutic index and is the first line of management in bipolar disorder. The kidney handles both lithium and Na+ in the same way via ENac channel. Thus during fasting/dehydration , along with Na+ reabsorption in renal tubules , there will be an increase in the reabsorption of lithium leading to lithium toxicity . Lithium has a very narrow therapeutic index of 0.8-1.2 mEq/L . The severity of lithium toxicity is often divided into the following three grades : A fine tremor is common in patients taking lithium at therapeutic doses . Therapeutic lithium tremor is generally symmetric, limited to the arms, and nonprogressive. The tremor from lithium toxicity is coarser and more disabling, may also affect the legs , and occurs with other symptoms of toxicity . Other adverse effects include mental confusion, hypothyroidism , nephrogenic diabetes insipidus , and edema . As lithium is readily dialyzed , lithium overdose or toxicity is treated with hemodialysis . *Note - Serum Na+ levels are significant with respect to lithium toxicity , where as serum potassium levels becomes significant in digoxin toxicity . Hypokalemia increases the risk of digoxin toxicity .Grade Sr. lithium concentration(in mEq/L) Symptoms Mild symptoms 1.5-2.5 nausea, vomiting,tremor, and fatigue Moderate intoxicatio n 2.5-3.5 confusion, agitation, delirium, tachycardia, and hypertonia Severe intoxication >3.5 coma,seizures , hyperthermia , and hypotension

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old woman on lithium therapy now presents with a positive urine pregnancy test . Which of the following teratogenic effects can be expected in the fetus ?
mcqs.explanation: Lithium use in pregnancy can lead to cardiac defects . Ebstein 's anomaly is the specific cardiac defect with lithium use in pregnancy.327 In Ebstein 's anomaly, the radiological sign seen is a box-shaped heart.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which drug, when given to a mother in her third trimester of pregnancy, would result in the following finding in her newborn?
mcqs.explanation: Benzodiazepines , when given during the third trimester of pregnancy can lead to floppy baby syndrome. Benzodiazepines in pregnancy: • First trimester - cleft palate , GI anomalies • Third trimester - floppy baby syndrome with neonatal hypotonia, as a withdrawal effect . Note : Fetal lithium exposure is also associated with floppy baby syndrome.328

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs crosses the blood-brain barrier ?
mcqs.explanation: Levodopa crosses the blood-brain barrier. It is a naturally occurring aromatic amino acid and an immediate precursor of dopamine that can cross the blood-brain barrier . Dopamine does not cross the blood-brain barrier because of the polar nature of the molecule . Levodopa is also a polar compound but it can cross the blood-brain barrier through an aromatic amino acid transporter. Therefore, levodopa is used therapeutically when dopamine is required for central action. Levodopa is converted to dopamine by the decarboxylase enzyme. Carbidopa is a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor and does not penetrate the blood-brain barrier .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old is diagnosed with Parkinson 's disease and is started on levodopa therapy . Which of the following statements is incorrect about the drug?

options.a: In parkinsonism , phenothiazines reduce its efficacy
options.c: Pyridoxine reduces effect of levodopa in parkinsonism
options.d: Domperidone reduces levodopa induced emesis and its therapeutic potential

mcqs.explanation: Domperidone is an antidopaminergic antiemetic that can reverse levodopa -induced emesis without affecting the therapeutic potential as it cannot cross the blood-brain barrier . The antiemetic effect is through its action on CTZ which is outside the blood-brain barrier . Option A: Typical antipsychotics like phenothiazines can reduce the efficacy of levodopa because of its central D2 blocking property . Option B: Levodopa is a prodrug. It is converted into dopamine by the decarboxylase enzyme in CNS. Option C: Pyridoxine can reduce the effect of levodopa by increasing its peripheral conversion to dopamine by potentiating peripheral dopa decarboxylase enzyme.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: After initiation of levodopa therapy , a 55 -year-old patient starts experiencing adverse effects . Which of these side effects is not decreased by the addition of carbidopa?
mcqs.explanation: Behavioral adverse effects like confusion, hallucinations, nightmares, delusions , postural hypotension are not reduced after the addition of carbidopa. In fact, they are increased in patients who are taking levodopa with peripheral decarboxylase inhibitors. This is because higher levels of dopamine are formed in CNS. The combination of levodopa with peripheral decarboxylase inhibitors like carbidopa inhibits peripheral adverse effects of dopamine. This decreases the adverse effects like: • Anorexia, nausea, and vomiting • Cardiac arrhythmias • On and off effect of motor performance

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old male is brought to the casualty in a confused state . On examination, he has severe muscle rigidity. His son says that the patient is on treatment for Parkinson 's disease but has forgotten to take his medication as they went on a holiday trip. What is the likely diagnosis in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: 335 Abrupt withdrawal of levodopa or dopaminergic agonists can precipitate neuroleptic malignant syndrome. It is characterized by extreme rigidity, confusion, and hyperthermia . It is an emergency condition that can turn fatal if immediate intervention is not done. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is commonly associated with the use of typical antipsychotics . Option A: Wearing off phenomenon - Each dose of levodopa improves mobility for a period of 1-2 hours. After that, the effect of the drug wears off, and rigidity and akinesia return. This can be surpassed by increasing the dosing and frequency. Option B: On/off phenomenon - Rapid fluctuation between on and off periods . • On period : When the patient has a beneficial effect of the medications but with disabling dyskinesias • Off period : No beneficial effects from anti-Parkinsonism medications . 'Wearing off' and 'On / Off' phenomenon occur with long-term treatment of levodopa . Option D: Serotonin syndrome occurs with co-prescription of MAO-inhibitors and SSRIs.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient on long-term treatment with levodopa and carbidopa for Parkinson 's disease is diagnosed with on/off phenomenon . Which of the following drugs is used to treat this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Safinamide is used for the treatment of the on/off phenomenon . Management of On/Off phenomenon : • To prolong the 'On' phase : • COMT inhibitor - entacapone , tolcapone • Irreversible MAO-B inhibitor - selegiline , rasagiline • Reversible MAO-B inhibitor - safinamide. • Rescue from 'Off' phase : injection apomorphine Dopaminergic agonists like pramipexole, ropinirole, and rotigotine are also effective in the treatment of the on/off phenomenon .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who is on levodopa therapy presents with confusion, delusions of grandeur, and hallucinations. What is the most appropriate treatment for his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of levodopa -induced psychosis for which quetiapine is the most appropriate treatment . Quetiapine and clozapine are the two atypical antipsychotics that are most effective and best tolerated in levodopa -induced psychosis. Typical antipsychotics are effective against levodopa -induced psychosis but may cause marked worsening of parkinsonism . Hence , atypical antipsychotics are deemed safer.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: While discharging a patient with Parkinson 's disease , the treating physician writes a prescription of levodopa along with another drug that can increase the bioavailability of the former. Identify the drug.
mcqs.explanation: 336 Entacapone is a peripheral COMT inhibitor that increases the bioavailability of levodopa . It inhibits the peripheral metabolism of levodopa thereby increasing the bioavailability of levodopa. Options B and D: Ropinirole and apomorphine are dopamine receptor agonists and do not have any significant effect on levodopa bioavailability. Option C: Amantadine which is an antiviral drug is also anti-Parkinsonian due to its varied actions including increased release and decreased uptake of dopamine. It has no significant effect on the bioavailability of levodopa .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following anti-Parkinsonism drugs is correctly matched with its mechanism of action?
mcqs.explanation: Tolcapone and entacapone are selective , potent , and reversible COMT (catechol -O-methyl transferase) inhibitors. COMT metabolizes levodopa and blockade of this pathway prolongs the half-life of levodopa and allows a larger fraction of the administered dose to reach the brain . Option B: Rasagiline is a selective MAO-B inhibitor. Option C: Amantadine acts by antagonism of the NMDA type of glutamate receptors . Option D: Apomorphine is a dopaminergic agonist that is FDA-approved as a 'rescue therapy ' for the acute intermittent treatment of 'off' episodes .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the use of selegiline in Parkinsonism ?

options.a: It acts as a selective MAO A inhibitor
options.b: Incidence of cheese reaction is minimal
options.c: May be used for on / off phenomenon

mcqs.explanation: Selegiline acts as a selective MAO-B inhibitor. At higher doses , MAO-A can also be inhibited . Higher doses are used for depression and administered in the form of the transdermal patch. Option B: Selective MAO-B inhibitors do not interfere significantly with the peripheral metabolism of dietary amines and do not cause cheese reaction. Option C: It has lower efficacy than levodopa but when added with levodopa it prolongs its action and also decreases the wearing-off effect of levodopa . Option D: Selegiline forms metabolites like amphetamine and methamphetamine that can result in anxiety, insomnia, and other undesirable effects . Rasagiline, unlike selegiline , does not form amphetamines as metabolites .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following dopamine agonists is an ergot derivative?
mcqs.explanation: Bromocriptine and pergolide are ergot derivatives that act as potent agonists at the D2 receptor . Pramipexole and ropinirole are non-ergot derivatives having D2/D3 receptor agonistic action. They are better tolerated and have fewer GI symptoms than bromocriptine.337 Dopamine agonists can be classified as follows : • Ergot derivatives - Bromocriptine, pergolide , cabergoline • Non-ergot derivatives - Pramipexole, ropinirole, apomorphine, rotigotine Dopaminergic agonists exert subtype -selective activation of dopaminergic receptors involved in the Parkinsonism circuit of the striatum.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old female patient visits the OPD with complaints of burning sensation associated with an irresistible urge to move her legs since 2 weeks . It occurs especially at night and the discomfort gets relieved on moving her legs . Which is the first-line drug that can be prescribed for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The symptoms in this patient are suggestive of restless leg syndrome and gabapentin is the first-line choice of treatment for this condition. Restless leg syndrome is a typical sensory-motor disorder that generally affects the legs during rest periods, especially sleep . There is an irresistible urge to shake the legs associated with burning sensation, itching, and cramps of the legs . In idiopathic cases , dopaminergic hypofunction is postulated . In patients with restless legs syndrome, iron stores are initially repleted , and the aggravating factors are eliminated . If RLS still persists , initial therapy with a gabapentinoid (pregabalin, gabapentin , gabapentin enacarbil) are preferred , rather than a dopamine agonist (pramipexole , ropinirole, rotigotine ). This is due to the high frequency of intermediate and long-term augmentation with dopamine agonists, as well as their risk of impulse control disorders. FDA-approved drugs for the treatment of restless leg syndrome: • Gabapentin • Ropinirole • Pramipexole • Rotigotine A dopamine agonist is used as an alternative in patients with increased risk for side effects from gabapentinoids , such as those with obesity and its complications , a past or present history of moderate to severe depression , a disorder causing gait instability or respiratory failure, and a history of substance use disorder. Option A: Benztropine is an anticholinergic that can be used for drug-induced parkinsonism . Option C: Riluzole is a benzothiazole derivative that is used in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis . Option D: Benzodiazepines like clonazepam can be used as co-adjuvant drugs in the treatment of restless leg syndrome but should not be used as first-line therapy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following dopamine receptor agonists has antioxidant properties ?
mcqs.explanation: Pramipexole is a dopamine receptor agonist that has an additional antioxidant effect . Pramipexole has a possible neuroprotective effect by its ability to scavenge hydrogen peroxide and enhance neurotrophic activity.338

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs would you prescribe as a transdermal patch to patients with Parkinson 's disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Rotigotine is a dopamine agonist used in Parkinson 's disease as a transdermal patch. A transdermal patch can lead to various local reactions at the application site . Rotigotine was withdrawn from some markets due to crystal formation on the patch but later reintroduced with a newer formulation. Selegiline transdermal patch is approved for depression and not for Parkinson 's disease .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old female is on treatment with ropinirole for restless leg syndrome. Which of the following adverse effects are not expected to be seen in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Cardiac fibrosis is a side effect of pergolide , not ropinirole. The adverse effects of ropinirole include : • Nausea • Drowsiness • Postural hypotension • Hallucinations Cardiac and pleural fibrosis are seen with pergolide which is also a dopamine agonist. Pergolide was withdrawn from the market due to reports of serious valve damage .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which anti-Parkinsonism drug is an NMDA-glutamate receptor antagonist?
mcqs.explanation: Amantadine which is an antiviral agent, also used in parkinsonism has NMDA glutamate receptor antagonist action. This action is responsible for its antidyskinetic properties . It also promotes presynaptic synthesis and release of dopamine. Option B: Rotigotine is a dopamine agonist available as a transdermal patch. Options C and D: Benzhexol and trihexyphenidyl are central anticholinergics .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old patient presents to the dermatology OPD with findings as shown in the image below . Which of the following drugs can result in this adverse effect ?
mcqs.explanation: The above presentation is of livedo reticularis, which is an adverse effect of amantadine. The patient presents with a common skin finding consisting of a mottled vesicular pattern that appears as a lace-like purplish discoloration of the skin which is due to the local release of catecholamines resulting in post -capillary vasoconstriction. Adverse effects of amantadine are:339 • Insomnia , restlessness , confusion • Nightmares • Anticholinergic effects • Hallucinations • Livedo reticularis • Edema of ankles

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which is the 5HT2A inverse agonist approved for use in psychosis associated with Parkinsonism ?
mcqs.explanation: Pimavanserin is a selective 5-HT2A receptor inverse agonist that is approved for the management of delirium and hallucinations associated with Parkinson 's disease . Option A: Lorcaserin is a 5-HT2C agonist indicated as an anti-obesity agent . Option C: Pitolisant is an H3 receptor inverse agonist approved for the treatment of narcolepsy . Option D: Mianserin is an anti-depressant.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old male patient presented to the casualty department with bradykinesia, rigidity, and tremors. His attender reported that he had been diagnosed with schizophrenia and had recently started treatment . What is the drug of choice to treat the patient 's presenting symptoms ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of drug-induced parkinsonism , for which the drug of choice is benzhexol , also known as trihexiphenidyl . Drug-induced parkinsonism is caused by certain drugs that have D2 antagonistic action, such as typical antipsychotics . Due to the decrease in dopaminergic activity, they result in an unbalanced cholinergic activity. Benzhexol is a centrally acting antimuscarinic agent . It acts by restoring the cholinergic balance in the striatal interneurons. The following drugs are implicated in drug-induced parkinsonism :Drug class Examples Typical antipsychotics Phenothiazines, haloperidol Atypical antipsychotics Risperidone , olanzapine Dopamine depleters Reserpine , tetrabenazine Antiemetics Metoclopramide , levosulpirid e Calcium channel blocke rs Flunarizine, cinnarizine340

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes the mechanism of action of antidepressants ?
mcqs.explanation: 348 Antidepressants increase levels of neurotransmitters at the synapse by preventing their reuptake . Due to a prolonged increase in the levels of neurotransmitters, there is a change in neurotransmitter receptor sensitivity which is thought to be the major mechanism responsible for the treatment of depression . Chronic treatment with a number of antidepressants desensitizes presynaptic autoreceptors and heteroreceptors, producing long-lasting changes in monoaminergic neurotransmission. Postreceptor effects of antidepressant treatment , including modulation of GPCR signaling and activation of protein kinases and ion channels, are involved in the mediation of the long-term effects of antidepressant drugs.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Moclobemide belongs to which class of drugs?
mcqs.explanation: Moclobemide is a reversible and selective inhibitor of the MAO-A enzyme. Monoamine hypothesis states that in depression , there is a decrease in monoamines like serotonin (5HT) and norepinephrine . These monoamines are metabolized by the enzyme monoamine oxidase (MAO). MAO inhibitors, therefore , increase these monoamines by inhibiting the enzyme. The various classes of drugs used in depression and anxiety are listed below :Class of drugs Examples Selective serotonin reuptake i nhibitors (SSRI ) FluoxetineFluvoxamineParox etineSertralineCitalopram Serotonin-norepinephrine re uptake inhibitors VenlafaxineDesvenlafaxineD uloxetineMilnacipran Tricyclic antidepressants AmitriptylineImipramineNor triptylineDesipramineAmoxa pine Atypical antipsychotics AripiprazoleOlanzapineQueti apineRisperidone Monoamine oxidase inhibitor s (MAO) IsocarboxazidSelegilinePhene lzineMoclobemide Atypical antidepressants BupropionTrazodoneMirtaza pineMianserin

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a selective MAO-B inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Selegiline is a selective MAO-B inhibitor.Nonselective MAO inhibitors Selective MAO inhibitors PhenelzineIsocarboxazidTran ylcypromine MAO-A inhibitors - Moclobe mideMAO -B inhibitors - Sele giline , Rasagiline349

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following patients is transdermal selegiline approved for use ?
mcqs.explanation: Selegiline transdermal patch is approved for depression . The transdermal patch provides the high concentration required for antidepressant action. At higher doses , MAO-A is also inhibited and is highly effective in depression . Selegiline is a selective MAO-B inhibitor at low doses . It is used in Parkinson 's disease at low doses , administered orally.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A college student on MAO inhibitor therapy for depression consumed two bottles of beer during a party. The next day he started experiencing severe headache , nausea, and vomiting. He was taken to the casualty by his friends where his BP was recorded to be 180/110mmHg . Which of the following compounds would be responsible for this complication?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical presentation of a hypertensive crisis in a patient on MAO inhibitor therapy is suggestive of cheese reaction, which is seen after consumption of foods rich in tyramine (beer). Tyramine is an indirect sympathomimetic . It induces the release of catecholamines from the neurons. Tyramine can be produced in high concentrations in protein-rich foods by decarboxylation of tyrosine during fermentation. Normally tyramine is inactivated when taken orally because it is readily metabolized by MAO in the liver. In patients who are on MAO inhibitor therapy , the tyramine taken in the diet is not inactivated and results in its increased sympathomimetic effect resulting in elevated blood pressure , termed as hypertensive crisis or cheese reaction. Drug of choice for cheese reaction is IV phentolamine . When MAO inhibitors are taken along with SSRI or TCA, it results in serotonin syndrome due to the overstimulation of 5HT receptors . The clinical features are a triad of: • Cognitive effect - delirium, coma • Autonomic effects - hypertension , tachycardia • Somatic effects - myoclonus , hyperreflexia, tremors350

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presents to the medicine OPD with hypertension . He is already on imipramine for depression . Which of the following antihypertensive drugs will not be effective in him?
mcqs.explanation: Clonidine will not be effective in this patient . Imipramine , a tricyclic antidepressant would abolish the antihypertensive effect of clonidine, by inhibiting its transport into the adrenergic neurons. Side effects of tricyclic antidepressants :Receptor blocked Side effects Muscarinic receptor Anticholinergic - Dry mouth, dilated pupils , tachycardia, u rinary retention Alpha 1 adrenergic receptor Drowsiness , postural hypoten sion, sexual dysfunction H1 receptor Weight gain, drowsiness

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which tricyclic antidepressant has an additional dopaminergic receptor antagonist action?
mcqs.explanation: The tricyclic antidepressant having an additional dopaminergic receptor antagonist action is amoxapine. Tricyclic antidepressants block the transporter of norepinephrine (NET) and serotonin (SERT) thereby preventing their uptake . Some of the TCA additionally block other receptors like alpha 1, H1, and M1. • TCA blocking NET selectively - desipramine , nortriptyline, amoxapine. • TCA blocking both NET and SERT equally - imipramine, amitriptyline .351 Clomipramine, doxepin , and imipramine are tertiary amines and do not possess any dopaminergic antagonist effect .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antidepressants can be used for the treatment of a 6-year-old child diagnosed with nocturnal enuresis ?
mcqs.explanation: Imipramine is a tricyclic antidepressant that can be used for the treatment of nocturnal enuresis . In children above 5 years, imipramine 25 mg at bedtime is effective for nocturnal enuresis . Intranasal desmopressin is also effective in the treatment of nocturnal enuresis . Option B: Amitriptyline is used in postherpetic neuralgia. It is also used in neuropathic pain. Option C: Desipramine is used in the treatment of cocaine dependence . Option D: Clomipramine is the best TCA for OCD.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following side effects of tricyclic antidepressants are correctly matched to the receptor involved in their pathogenesis?
mcqs.explanation: The blockade of H1, alpha1, and muscarinic receptors causes sedation , postural hypotension , and constipation respectively . Tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) are drugs that act by inhibiting the reuptake of noradrenaline and serotonin from the synaptic clefts . The side effects of TCAs are due to blockade of other receptors : • Muscarinic (M) receptors : constipation , dry mouth (not sialorrhea), arrhythmia • Histamine (H1) receptors : sedation • 5HT receptors : weight gain due to increased appetite • Alpha1 receptors : postural hypotension

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman having depression took multiple tablets of amitriptyline in an attempt to commit suicide . Which of the following statements regarding the management is incorrect?

options.b: Sodium bicarbonate should be administered to treat acidosis
options.c: Atropine sulphate should be administered as an antidote
options.d: Diazepam should be injected to control seizures

mcqs.explanation: Tricyclic antidepressants like amitriptyline are competitive antagonists of muscarinic receptors . Atropine being an antimuscarinic drug should not be administered . Tricyclic antidepressant overdose presents with anticholinergic effects . Hypotension occurs because of alpha1 receptor blockade. TCAs act on Na+ channels and cause slowed conduction and depressed cardiac contractility resulting in serious arrhythmias. Seizures and agitation may occur followed by depression . Management of TCA overdose: • Initial resuscitation by securing airway, breathing, and circulation. • Hypotension - IV fluids and norepinephrine infusion.352 • Cardiac-depressant effects - bolus dose of sodium bicarbonate helps overcome Na+ blockade by increasing extracellular Na+. It also addresses metabolic acidosis which is often present . • Arrhythmias - lignocaine for ventricular arrhythmias. • Seizures - benzodiazepines like diazepam/lorazepam. Physostigmine can reverse anticholinergic effects but can aggravate cardiac depression and cause seizures . Therefore physostigmine is not recommended .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A psychiatrist plans to prescribe an SSRI to a patient diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder. Which of the following was not likely prescribed ?
mcqs.explanation: Duloxetine is not an SSRI but a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI ). It blocks the uptake of both serotonin and norepinephrine . The selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs ) are: • Fluoxetine • Fluvoxamine • Citalopram • Escitalopram • Sertraline • Dapoxetine • Paroxetine

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In a middle -aged man with a history of closed -angle glaucoma, which of the following SNRIs should be avoided?
mcqs.explanation: Duloxetine should be avoided as it is contraindicated in patients with closed -angle glaucoma. SNRIs like duloxetine and milnacipran have anticholinergic side effects like mydriasis which can precipitate closed -angle glaucoma attacks. Duloxetine is the longest -acting SNRI with no withdrawal symptoms . In addition to the treatment of depression and anxiety, it is also used in fibromyalgia, peripheral neuropathy , and stress incontinence. Option A: Venlafaxine is the shortest acting SNRI with the maximum risk of withdrawal symptoms . It is approved for use in PTSD, panic disorder, and depression associated with hypotension . It is contraindicated in pregnancy. Option C: Desvenlafaxine is a longer-acting SNRI and hence has lesser risk of withdrawal symptoms . Option D: Fluoxetine is an SSRI , not an SNRI . It is avoided as it can cause mydriasis and narrow the angle.353

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 27-year-old man on antidepressant therapy with TCAs for the past five years is being switched to SSRIs. Which of the following would not be an advantage of this change?
mcqs.explanation: SSRIs have a higher incidence of sexual dysfunction when compared to TCAs. SSRI -induced sexual dysfunction can result in loss of libido, delayed ejaculation , and interference with orgasm. Option A: The potential of SSRIs to lower the seizure threshold is less than that of TCAs. Options B and D: SSRIs have a selective action on serotonin reuptake with no effect on cholinergic or histaminergic receptors .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors are not the drug of choice in which of the following patients ?

options.a: A college student with an acute panic attack
options.b: An adolescent girl with social phobia
options.c: A young lady with post traumatic stress disorder
options.d: A middle -aged -man with generalized anxiety disorder

mcqs.explanation: In acute panic attacks, benzodiazepines or propranolol are the preferred anxiolytics. SSRIs are not the drug of choice as they have a long latent period before beneficial effects are seen . SSRIs are considered as the drug of choice for: • Social anxiety disorder • Post-traumatic stress disorder • Generalized anxiety disorder • Obsessive -compulsive disorder

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient diagnosed with depression has improved symptomatically after initiating SSRIs. On discontinuing the drug, he became irritable and complained of insomnia, nausea, and flu-like symptoms . Which of the following drugs has the least risk of causing these symptoms ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical presentation is suggestive of drug discontinuation or withdrawal symptoms which are seen after sudden discontinuation of SSRIs. Fluoxetine has the least risk of causing drug-discontinuation symptoms . Drug discontinuation symptoms of SSRIs are: • Nausea • Paresthesia • Flu-like symptoms • Insomnia • Irritability • Fatigue . Withdrawal is least with fluoxetine as its metabolite norfluoxetine has the longest half-life . Thus the plasma level of norfluoxetine is maintained for a long time even after stopping the drug, minimizing withdrawal symptoms . Withdrawal is seen maximum with paroxetine .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A young man with obsessive -compulsive disorder is taking SSRIs. Which of the following adverse effects would you not expect in him?
mcqs.explanation: 354 Weight loss is not an adverse effect of SSRIs. Side effects of SSRIs: • Nausea and diarrhea (early) • Loss of libido • Erectile dysfunction • Headache • Sleep disturbances - insomnia or hypersomnia.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is a serotonin receptor antagonist?
mcqs.explanation: Trazodone is a serotonin receptor antagonist. Trazodone blocks postsynaptic 5HT2A receptors and is considered an atypical antidepressant . It has weak serotonin reuptake inhibitory effect . Nefazodone is another serotonin receptor antagonist. Option A: Milnacipran is a serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor. Options C and D: Citalopram and fluoxetine are selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs inhibit dopamine and noradrenaline reuptake ?
mcqs.explanation: Bupropion is an atypical antidepressant that inhibits the reuptake of noradrenaline and dopamine. Indications of bupropion are: • Prevention of a seasonal depressive disorder • Smoking cessation • ADHD • Peripheral neuropathy Option A : Clozapine is an atypical antipsychotic that selectively blocks dopamine (D4) receptors in the brain . Option C : Zolpidem - It is a nonbenzodiazepine hypnotic . It acts as a selective agonist in benzodiazepine receptor . Option D : Mirtazapine - block histamine (H1) receptors .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A young woman diagnosed with major depressive disorder is refractory to first-line antidepressant therapy . The psychiatrist now decides to prescribe a recently approved NMDA antagonist. Which of the following was most likely prescribed ?
mcqs.explanation: 355 Esketamine is an NMDA antagonist recently approved for the treatment of treatment-resistant depression . Esketamine is a non-selective , non-competitive antagonist of the NMDA receptor , an ionotropic glutamate receptor . Though the exact mechanism by which it acts as an antidepressant is unknown, a single dose of intranasal Esketamine has shown to have short-term antidepressant efficacy suggesting a possible use in suicidality . Option A: Brexanolone has GABAA modulatory action. It is given via intravenous route for post-partum depression . Option C: Lurasidone is a second -generation antipsychotic that is an antagonist at dopamine (D2) and serotonin (5-HT2A) receptors . It is approved for use in depressive episodes in bipolar disorder. Option D: Lemborexant is an orexin receptor antagonist indicated for the treatment of adult patients with insomnia.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old married man complains of low energy and lack of motivation. He mentions that he feels useless and has no hope for the future . He is willing to take medication but is apprehensive about its side effects on his sexual life . Which of the following drugs would you prescribe to him?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical presentation is suggestive of depression . Mirtazapine can be prescribed to this patient as sexual dysfunction is not a side effect associated with its use . Mirtazapine and mianserin block histamine (H1) receptors , and also have high antagonistic activity against 5HT2A , 5HT2C, and 5HT3 receptors . Due to its sedative effect , mirtazapine is also used in depression with insomnia. Option A: Fluoxetine is an SSRI that can cause side effects like GI disturbances , risk of suicidal behavior, sexual dysfunction , and weight gain. Vilazodone is an SSRI that is not associated with sexual dysfunction or weight gain. Option B: SNRIs like venlafaxine have side effects that include nausea, dizziness, sexual dysfunction , and risk of suicidal thoughts or behavior. Option D: TCAs like imipramine have side effects like orthostatic hypotension , weight gain, GI disturbances, sexual dysfunction , seizures, and irregular heartbeats . The various classes of drugs used in depression and anxiety are listed belowClass of drugs Examples Selective serotonin reuptake i nhibitors (SSRI ) FluoxetineFluvoxamineParox etineSertralineCitalopram Serotonin-norepinephrine re uptake inhibitors VenlafaxineDesvenlafaxineD uloxetineMilnacipran Tricyclic antidepressants AmitriptylineImipramineNor triptylineDesipramineAmoxa pine Atypical antipsychotics AripiprazoleOlanzapineQueti apineRisperidone356 Class of drugs Examples Monoamine oxidase inhibitor s (MAO) IsocarboxazidSelegilinePhene lzine Atypical antidepressants BupropionTrazodoneMirtaza pineMianserin

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which group does the antianxiety drug buspirone belong to?
mcqs.explanation: The antianxiety drug buspirone is a partial agonist of 5-HT1A receptors . The most important locations of the 5-HT1A receptor are raphe nuclei of brainstem and hippocampus . It mimics the antianxiety properties of benzodiazepines but does not interact with GABAA receptors or display the sedative and anticonvulsant properties of benzodiazepines . Buspirone is primarily used in the treatment of generalized anxiety disorder. 5-HT1A partial agonists are: • Buspirone • Gepirone • Ipsapirone

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A psychiatry resident should not prescribe a tricyclic antidepressant to a patient having which of the following co-morbidities ?
mcqs.explanation: Tricyclic antidepressants produce anticholinergic effects of pupillary dilatation and are thus , contraindicated in narrow -angle glaucoma. Side effects of tricyclic antidepressants :Receptor blocked Side effect Muscarinic receptor Anticholinergic- dry mouth, dilated pupils , tachycardia, u rinary retention Alpha 1 adrenergic receptor Drowsiness , postural hypoten sion, sexual dysfunction H1 receptor Weight gain, drowsiness

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man was admitted to the emergency ward with priapism lasting for about 7 hours. A detailed history revealed the initiation of a drug for a mood disorder by a psychiatrist 3 weeks ago. Which of the following drugs is responsible for his condition?
mcqs.explanation: Trazadone causes priapism. Intracavernous injection of phenylephrine can be used to treat priapism.357

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A man feels frustrated because of his wife 's decreased sexual desire . She was recently diagnosed with depression and started on a drug for the same. Which of the following drugs was most likely prescribed ?
mcqs.explanation: Fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI ) that is associated with the side effect of sexual dysfunction . Fluoxetine is used in the treatment of major depression , obsessive -compulsive disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder, bulimia and anorexia nervosa, generalized anxiety disorders, and premenstrual dysphoric disorder. Other adverse effects include dry mouth, urinary retention , insomnia, GI disturbances , risk of suicidal behavior, and weight gain.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an adverse effect of escitalopram ?
mcqs.explanation: Sialorrhoea is not an adverse effect of escitalopram . Escitalopram is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI ) mainly used to treat major depressive disorder or generalized anxiety disorder. Nausea is the commonest side effect of SSRIs as they target the 5HT3 receptor . Vivid dreams may occur because the drug suppresses REM sleep (the stage of dream), hence when patients eventually fall into REM sleep it may be more intense . Anorgasmia is the persistent inability to achieve orgasm despite responding to sexual stimulation. A proposed mechanism of escitalopram causing sexual dysfunction involves stimulation of the 5HT2C receptors .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In children and adolescents treated with an SSRI , there appears to be an increased risk of particular ideations . Clinicians are therefore advised to remain vigilant of which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs ) should be used carefully in the young for the management of depression due to increased suicidal ideation . In children and adolescents , there appears to be a slightly increased risk of suicidal ideations and attempts , but not of completed suicide . Somatic symptoms of depression improve faster than psychological symptoms when a patient is started on SSRIs and hence patients have the energy to act on their thoughts of deliberate self -harm and suicide (paradoxical suicide ).358

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged woman with resistant intractable back pain is planned to receive neuraxial opioids for analgesia. Which of the following is the site of action of this drug in the spinal cord?
