options.d: No spinal component is seen with opioid analgesia

mcqs.explanation: The spinal component of opioid analgesia is seen due to the action in the dorsal horn of the spinal cord. Opioid analgesia: • Spinal component : opioids act in the substantia gelatinosa of the dorsal horn to inhibit the release of excitatory transmitters like substance P from primary afferents carrying pain impulses . This action is through interneurons that are involved in the gating of pain impulses . • Supraspinal component : action at the medulla , periaqueductal gray matter, limbic, and cortical areas alter the processing and interpretation of pain impulses . It also sends inhibitory impulses through descending pathways to the spinal cord. • Peripheral action: acts on small primary afferent terminals in the skin or deeper structures , decreasing their sensitization following tissue injury.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A primigravida in labor is administered opioids for epidural analgesia. Which of the following statements is false regarding the drug administered ?

options.a: Act on dorsal horn substantia gelatinosa
options.c: Function of the GIT is not affected

mcqs.explanation: Gastrointestinal motility is decreased by epidural opioids . Option A: The epidural opioids provide more direct access to the first pain-processing synapse i.e., substantia gelatinosa by acting on the dorsal horn of the spinal cord. Option B: Symptoms such as pruritus, nausea, and vomiting are also common with the epidural route . Option D: Respiratory depression is seen with epidural opioids but the incidence is lesser than the parenteral route.365

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient is receiving morphine for pain management. Which of the following findings would you not expect?
mcqs.explanation: Miosis (not mydriasis) would be expected in a patient receiving morphine. Opioids stimulate the Edinger -Westphal nucleus of the III cranial nerve resulting in miosis. Urinary retention , vomiting, and pruritus are actions of opiates .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An experimental drug that acts only as an agonist at the mu-opioid receptor is being developed . Which of the following effects would be seen with this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Mu opioid receptor activation results in miosis, nausea, and vomiting. Mu receptor actions (mnemonic- MUSCARINE): • Miosis • Urine retention • Sedation • Constipation • Analgesia • Respiratory depression • Increased muscular rigidity • Negative bile flow (contraction of the sphincter of Oddi ) • Euphoria

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Dysphoria is mediated by which opioid receptor ?
mcqs.explanation: Dysphoria is mediated by kappa opioid receptor . Kappa receptor actions: • Dysphoria, psychotomimetic • Analgesia (Spinal and supraspinal) • Miosis • Sedation • Physical dependence • Reduced GI motility

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient is administered intravenous opioids for postoperative pain management. This drug elicits its analgesic action through which of the following receptors ?
mcqs.explanation: 366 Analgesia produced by opioids is mediated by \265 ( mu), k (kappa), and \027 (delta ) receptors . Opioid receptors are part of the G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) family. Supraspinal analgesia is predominantly mediated by the \265 1 receptor and spinal analgesia by the k and \027 receptor.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Following surgery, a woman received multiple doses of intravenous opioids for pain management . Later, her respiratory rate became 8 per minute. Which receptor mediates this adverse effect ?
mcqs.explanation: The given features suggest opioid -induced respiratory depression , which is mediated by the action of opioids on \265 receptors (\265 2) in the brainstem respiratory centers . Drug of choice for opioid -induced respiratory depression is naloxone.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs does not aggravate opioid -induced respiratory depression ?
mcqs.explanation: Naloxone is an opioid antagonist, which can reverse the respiratory depression induced by opioids . Respiratory depression can be prolonged when opioids are taken with CNS depressant substances like alcohol, barbiturates, benzodiazepines , inhalational anesthetics , and other sedative hypnotics .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an opiate ?
mcqs.explanation: Morphine is an opiate . The term opiate specifically describes the naturally occurring alkaloids: morphine, codeine , thebaine , and papaverine. Options A and C: Pentazocine and fentanyl are synthetic opioids . Option B: Heroin is a semisynthetic opioid.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the other name for diacetylmorphine ?
mcqs.explanation: Heroin is structurally diacetylmorphine. It is more potent than morphine and causes more euphoric effects . It is banned in some countries . Diacetylmorphine is converted into monoacetylmorphine and morphine, to which the pharmacological actions of heroin are mainly attributed . Monoacetylmorphine is more lipid -soluble than morphine. Codeine is also known as methyl morphine. Meperidine is also known as pethidine.367

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who has a history of substance abuse with a semisynthetic opioid is now referred to a rehabilitation center . Which of the following drugs is he likely addicted to?
mcqs.explanation: He is likely addicted to heroin as it is the only semisynthetic opioid among the given options. Morphine, codeine , and thebaine are natural opioids derived from poppy Papaver somniferum.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old pregnant woman is in labor. Your senior administered her a synthetic opioid to provide labor analgesia. Which of the following would be the drug administered to her?
mcqs.explanation: Butorphanol would be the drug administered to her as it is the only synthetic opioid among the given options . Heroin, dihydromorphone, and buprenorphine are semisynthetic opioids .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 54-year-old woman is receiving acupuncture treatment for her back pain. Which of the following opioid peptides does not mediate analgesia in her?
mcqs.explanation: Morphine does not mediate analgesia in acupuncture as it is not an endogenous opioid . It is a naturally occurring opioid derived from poppy Papaver somniferum. One of the most accepted mechanisms of action of acupuncture is that it works by releasing endogenous opioid peptides resulting in analgesia. Endogenous opioid peptides are produced physiologically in the body and act through an opioid receptor . Endogenous opioid peptides : • Enkephalins (more potent at \027 receptor ) • \035-endorphins (more potent at �M receptor ) • Dynorphins (more potent at \026 receptor) • Orphanin FQ or Nociceptin • Neoendorphins • Endomorphins

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presented with biliary colic. The intern has administered an analgesic , following which the pain got aggravated. Which of the following could be responsible for the aggravation of the patient 's symptoms ?
mcqs.explanation: Morphine is the analgesic which could be responsible for the aggravation of the patient 's symptoms . It causes constriction of the sphincter of Oddi causing an increase in fluid pressure in the common bile duct and gall bladder . Note : Pethidine causes lesser spasm of the sphincter of Oddi and can be used in biliary colic.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You decide to administer morphine for analgesia in your patients . In which of the following patients would you avoid morphine?

options.a: A 50 year old man with hypotension
options.b: A 32 year old woman with head injury
options.c: A 44 year old woman with hypothyroidism
options.d: A 21 year old man with type 1 diabetes mellitus

mcqs.explanation: 368 Morphine should be avoided in a patient with head injury because : • Morphine retains CO2 that increases intracranial pressure (ICP) and adds to the already increased ICP. • Therapeutic doses can result in marked respiratory depression . • Interferes with the assessment of progress by causing miosis, vomiting, and altered mentation. Among the above options , head injury seems to be the most appropriate answer and some authorities consider head injury as a contraindication. Option A: Hypotension can increase the susceptibility to vasodilating effects of morphine. Caution needs to be exercised . Option C: Sensitivity to opioids is increased in hypothyroidism . Caution needs to be exercised . Option D: Diabetes is not a contraindication for morphine use .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements are true?
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2, 3 & 5 are true. Option 1: Morphine is used in pulmonary edema due to its vasodilatory and anxiolytic actions. Option 2: Morphine should be avoided as it causes constriction of the sphincter of Oddi causing an increase in fluid pressure in the common bile duct and gall bladder . Pethidine causes lesser spasm of the sphincter of Oddi and can be used in biliary colic. Option 3: Indomethacin is an NSAID used in headache . Option 4: The use of aspirin can worsen peptic ulcer disease . Option 5: Single dose of pethidine (meperidine ) can be effective in the treatment of postanesthetic shivering.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presented with pelvic fracture and head trauma after a road traffic accident . He was given IV morphine for pain relief following which he developed respiratory difficulty . What could be the most likely cause ?

options.b: CO2 retention due to opioid use

mcqs.explanation: The most likely cause of respiratory difficulty in the given clinical scenario is CO2 retention due to opioid use , as the patient was administered morphine after head trauma. Head injury is considered as a contraindication to morphine use because : • Morphine retains CO2 that increases intracranial pressure (ICP) and adds to the already increased ICP. • Therapeutic doses can result in marked respiratory depression . • Interferes with the assessment of progress by causing miosis, vomiting, and altered mentation.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a contraindication to the use of morphine?
mcqs.explanation: 369 Acute myocardial infarction is not a contraindication for morphine use . Morphine is the opioid of choice for myocardial infarction as it relieves anxiety, chest pain, and myocardial oxygen demand. Contraindications to the use of Morphine: • Bronchial asthma: Histamine release can cause bronchoconstriction and precipitate attacks of asthma. • Renal failure: Morphine-6-glucuronide (metabolite ) can accumulate and lead to prolonged respiratory depression . • Emphysema : Respiratory depression and decreased response to hypoxia can cause hypercapnia in patients with COPD • Head injury: Hypercapnia due to respiratory depression can increase ICP. Miosis, vomiting, and effect on wakefulness make interpreting the signs of head injury difficult . • Biliary colic: Constriction of sphincter of Oddi can worsen biliary spasm • Hypotension and shock

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the WHO analgesic ladder for chronic pain in adults ?

options.b: Adjuvants are indicated only for mild pain

mcqs.explanation: The true statement is the use of morphine falls under step 3 of WHO analgesic ladder for chronic pain in adults. WHO has developed 3 step ladder for chronic/cancer pain relief in adults . The 3 main principles are as follows : • By the clock: Drugs should be given "by the clock" or "around the clock" rather than "on-demand". • By the mouth: The oral route is preferred . If not feasible , the least invasive route should be considered . • By the ladder: Drugs are given in the following order, Non-opioids \037 Mild opioids \037 Strong opioids . Adjuvants are added at any stage of the WHO ladder to relieve anxiety. Note : This 3-step ladder approach is inexpensive and 80-90% effective when utilized optimally .370

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You prescribe a cough syrup to a patient that has an opioid cough suppressant as one of the constituents . Which would be the opioid present in the syrup?
mcqs.explanation: Codeine (methyl morphine) is an opioid used in the treatment of cough . It is a more selective cough suppressant than morphine and widely used as an antitussive agent . It has antitussive actions at subanalgesic doses . The analgesic action of codeine is mainly due to its conversion to morphine.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: How does dextromethorphan differ from codeine ?

options.a: Its antitussive action can be more easily blocked by naloxone
options.b: It depresses mucociliary function of the airway mucosa

mcqs.explanation: Dextromethorphan causes fewer gastrointestinal side effects like constipation when compared with codeine. It is a synthetic central NMDA (N-methyl D-aspartate ) receptor antagonist. It is used as an antitussive agent and has no analgesic property . Option A: The antitussive action of dextromethorphan is not blocked by naloxone. Option B: Dextromethorphan does not depress the mucociliary function of the airway mucosa. Option C: It has no addictive property.371

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following opioids has maximum plasma protein binding capacity ?
mcqs.explanation: Sufentanil has maximum plasma protein binding capacity . More than 90% of sufentanil is bound to alpha acid glycoprotein in plasma. Plasma protein binding capacity of opioids: • Sufentanil : 90% • Fentanyl : 80-85% • Pethidine (meperidine ): 65-75 % • Morphine: 36%

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which among the following is the most potent opioid analgesic ?
mcqs.explanation: Sufentanil is the most potent opioid . It is 1000 times more potent than morphine. On the other hand, fentanyl is around 100 times more potent than morphine.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following has the most rapid analgesic action?
mcqs.explanation: The most rapid analgesic action is achieved by remifentanil. Analgesic action (peak) is achieved within 1 to 1.5 min following intravenous administration. Analgesic action- duration for peak action: • Remifentanil: 1 to 1.5 min • Fentanyl : 5 min • Sufentanil : 5 min • Meperidine : 15 min380 The rapid onset of action and the rapid recovery (within 15 min) owing to metabolism by plasma esterases of remifentanil make it an ideal analgesic for short painful procedures .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man with liver metastasis and altered LFT is posted for a surgery. What would be the opioid of choice in him?
mcqs.explanation: Opioid of choice in patients with compromised hepatic function is remifentanil. Remifentanil is hydrolyzed by plasma and tissue esterases and hence its metabolism is independent of hepatic function. Other opioids like fentanyl , alfentanil, and sufentanil are metabolized by the liver.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 48-year-old woman with CKD is scheduled for a surgery. Her serum creatinine is 2.4mg/dL and eGFR is 13 . Which of the following opioids can be safely used in her?
mcqs.explanation: The given lab values in a CKD patient are suggestive of renal failure and remifentanil can be safely used in renal failure patients . Remifentanil is hydrolyzed by plasma and tissue esterases . The pharmacokinetics and the pharmacodynamics of remifentanil are not altered by renal dysfunction . Option A: Pethidine is metabolized to norpethidine , accumulation of which can lead to CNS excitatory effects (seizures ). Option C: High levels of alfentanil can lead to prolonged action. Option D: Morphine is metabolized to morphine-6-glucuronide which can accumulate leading to respiratory depression . Note : Fentanyl clearance is not altered by renal failure but its plasma protein binding is decreased which can alter the concentration of the free drug. Hence , fentanyl is the second drug of choice after remifentanil.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who underwent an intra-abdominal surgery is about to receive intraspinal opioid injection for analgesia. Which of the following drugs should not be used for this purpose ?
mcqs.explanation: Remifentanil should not be used for intraspinal injection. Remifentanil is formulated in combination with glycine . Glycine acts as an inhibitory neurotransmitter in the spinal dorsal horn that causes a reversible motor weakness when it is injected intrathecally . For this reason, remifentanil is not approved for spinal or epidural use .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the shortest acting opioid ?
mcqs.explanation: The shortest acting opioid is remifentanil with t1/2 of 8-20 minutes .381 The rapid metabolism by tissue esterases and rapid clearance results in its ultra short-acting nature. Remifentanil has the fastest onset of action and recovery, making it the opioid of choice in daycare surgery.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which among the following is not included in neuroleptic anesthesia ?
mcqs.explanation: Propofol is not included in neuroleptic anesthesia . Neuroleptic anesthesia includes fentanyl, droperidol , and nitrous oxide. Neuroleptic analgesia includes fentanyl and droperidol . Neuroleptic anesthesia is characterized by analgesia, the absence of clinically apparent motor activity, suppression of autonomic reflexes , maintenance of cardiovascular stability , and amnesia. QT interval prolongation and torsades de pointes due to droperidol have made this technique obsolete .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You are planning to use a transdermal patch for one of your patients who require around-the -clock opioids for his cancer pain. Which of the following drugs will you prescribe ?
mcqs.explanation: Fentanyl is available as a transdermal patch and can be prescribed to this patient . It is mainly used for chronic pain. Various routes of administration of fentanyl are: intravenous, epidural , spinal, transdermal therapeutic system (transdermal patch and transdermal iontophoresis ), oral (buccal tablets , films, lozenges ).

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the drug of choice for rescue analgesia?
mcqs.explanation: Fentanyl is the drug of choice for providing rescue analgesia. Rescue analgesia involves the use of medications to minimize post -operative pain. Mild pain can be controlled with oral analgesics but severe pain requires opioids like fentanyl . Fentanyl is preferred over morphine or oxycodone due to its rapid onset of action, lesser incidence of postoperative nausea, vomiting, and other adverse effects .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man was posted for bronchoscopy under procedural sedation . After the administration of anesthetic drugs, he developed chest wall rigidity and ineffective spontaneous ventilation. Attempts at manual ventilation were unsuccessful due to the non-compliant chest wall. The opioid that is most commonly associated with this condition is?
mcqs.explanation: Chest wall rigidity and ineffective ventilation is a classic presentation of 'wooden chest syndrome'. This opioid -induced muscle rigidity is most commonly associated with the use of lipophilic opioids such as fentanyl and its congeners (alfentanil, sufentanil , and remifentanil). Risk factors for wooden chest syndrome:382 • Rapid administration of a large dose of fentanyl • Concomitant use of nitrous oxide • Old age The clinical presentation can vary from mild hoarseness to chest wall rigidity severe enough to prevent adequate bag-and-mask ventilation. Management of wooden chest syndrome: • Discontinuation of the opioid • Replacement of the opioid with a non-lipophilic version (such as hydromorphone or morphine) for analgesia • Consider naloxone for reversal (you do not want to reverse analgesia on an intubated patient unless absolutely necessary ) • Addition of a non-depolarizing neuromuscular blocker for paralysis • Supportive ventilatory care

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Upon recovering from anesthesia , a patient started feeling cold accompanied by shivering. Which is the opioid indicated to treat this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Meperidine is commonly indicated for post -anesthetic shivering. It prevents post -anesthetic shivering by lowering the temperature threshold at which shivering is triggered by the hypothalamus . A single dose of 12 .5 to 35mg meperidine (pethidine ) is effective in the treatment of postanesthetic shivering. Infusion-related chills and rigors associated with amphotericin B, aldesleukin , trastuzumab, and alemtuzumab are also managed with meperidine in combination with other agents .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old housewife with diabetic nephropathy and receiving dialysis weekly comes to your clinic with an accidental burn on her left hand. On examination, 2nd-degree burns are seen . Which of the following opioids should not be prescribed to her for analgesia?
mcqs.explanation: Pethidine (meperidine ) should not be prescribed to her as it is contraindicated in patients with renal failure. In renal failure, there is an accumulation of its metabolite norpethidine which causes excitatory syndrome consisting of hallucinations, tremors, muscle twitches , and convulsions. Therefore, pethidine is avoided in renal failure patients . Methadone , alfentanil, and fentanyl primarily undergo hepatic metabolism .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A woman was administered an intravenous opioid for managing postoperative pain. Within 5 minutes , she started developing severe redness and pruritus along the distribution of the vein into which the drug was injected . Which of the following drugs would be responsible for this?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical findings are suggestive of histamine release , which is common with the use of meperidine (pethidine ) due to mast cell activation.383 Codeine , morphine, and hydromorphone are also associated with histamine release . Fentanyl , alfentanil, and remifentanil do not lead to histamine release .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old boy received an intravenous opioid for analgesia. A few minutes later, his heart rate decreased from 72/min to 58/min. Which among the following drugs is least likely to be associated with this finding?
mcqs.explanation: Meperidine (pethidine ) is least likely to be associated with bradycardia. Intravenous meperidine produces tachycardia as it has a structure similar to atropine. Unlike other opioids , meperidine causes mydriasis due to its anticholinergic effect . Pentazocine, which is an opioid agonist-antagonist, also produces tachycardia, hypertension, and mydriasis.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following opioids has local anesthetic property ?
mcqs.explanation: The opioid with local anesthetic property is pethidine (meperidine ), which is especially seen after intrathecal administration. Intrathecal pethidine can provide spinal anesthesia for endoscopic urological procedures and surgery of the lower limb, perineum , and lower abdomen including cesarean section . However, due to low potency and systemic opioid side effects , it is usually not used for this purpose .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Apart from mu-opioid receptors , on which other receptor does tramadol act?
mcqs.explanation: Tramadol inhibits the reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine , apart from its action on the mu-opioid receptor . It is a synthetic codeine analog that is a mu-opioid receptor agonist. Tramadol is a centrally acting analgesic used in the treatment of mild to moderate pain.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding tramadol?
mcqs.explanation: Tramadol is contraindicated in epileptics . Tramadol is epileptogenic and can cause seizures in predisposed individuals and in those taking medications like monoamine oxidase inhibitors and neuroleptic drugs. It is a synthetic analogue of codeine and a weak opioid agonist with 1/6000 affinity for \265 receptors as that of morphine. Apart from opioid action, it also inhibits the reuptake of 5HT and NE. Due to non-opioid receptor -mediated actions, it produces less respiratory depression and less constipation .384

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old woman requires an intranasal opioid spray for her migraine. Which of the following would you prescribe her?
mcqs.explanation: Butorphanol is a synthetic opioid available as a nasal spray for use in migraine headaches and painful conditions. It is used parenterally as an analgesic for moderate to severe pain or as an adjunct to general anesthesia . Opioids available for intranasal administration are butorphanol and fentanyl .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man, on treatment with fluoxetine for depression , was started on an opioid for severe neuropathic pain. A few days later he had an episode of syncope and was brought to the casualty . ECG taken is given below , with QTc = 477 ms. Which of the following drugs is most likely the cause ?
mcqs.explanation: The given ECG findings show QT prolongation which is associated primarily with the use of methadone . In the ECG QTc(corrected QT interval= QT/\025RR ) is 477ms . Normal QTc is about 440ms. Values of more than 440ms in males and 460ms in females are considered to be prolonged . QT prolongation can present as syncope or cardiac arrest. Methadone has additive action with agents known to cause QT prolongation. Serious cardiac arrhythmias including torsades de pointes have been noted with methadone use .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding methadone ?

options.c: Rapidly absorbed from GIT and appears in plasma within 30 min of oral administration
options.d: Onset of analgesia is 30-60 min after parenteral and 1-2 h after oral administration

mcqs.explanation: Methadone 's onset of analgesia is 10 -20 minutes after the parenteral route, and 30-60 minutes after the oral route of administration. Option A: Methadone is a long-acting mu receptor agonist with a plasma half-life of 15-40 hours. Option B: It is an analgesic and used for chronic pain relief . Option C: Absorption from GIT is rapid and appears in plasma within 30 minutes and reaches peak concentrations at around 4 hours.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A young man is scheduled for laparoscopic cholecystectomy . His medical history is significant for depression and he is on monoamine oxidase inhibitors for the same. Which of the following opioids can be safely administered to him?
mcqs.explanation: Morphine can be safely administered as it does not inhibit the neuronal reuptake of serotonin and hence does not trigger serotonin syndrome in patients on MAO inhibitors. Phenylpiperidine series of opioids such as meperidine , tramadol, dextromethorphan , and methadone inhibit the neuronal reuptake of serotonin leading to serotonergic overactivity. This can cause serotonin syndrome in patients receiving monoamine oxidase inhibitors.385

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A woman sustained multiple fractures in a motorcycle accident . Her physician prescribed an oral opioid for analgesia which is a partial agonist at mu and a full agonist at kappa receptors . Identify the drug given.
mcqs.explanation: Pentazocine is a partial agonist at mu and a full agonist at kappa receptors . Analgesia produced by pentazocine is predominantly mediated by the \026 receptor . Pentazocine is a mixed agonist-antagonist opioid agent . It is a full agonist at the \026 receptor and a partial agonist or weak antagonist at the \265 receptor . Buprenorphine is a partial agonist at mu receptors but an antagonist at kappa receptors .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A cancer patient is dependent on morphine for pain management. His physician decides to switch him to buprenorphine . Due to which property he chooses this new drug?
mcqs.explanation: Buprenorphine is a partial agonist at the mu receptor with a lower intrinsic activity compared to morphine and hence does not produce withdrawal symptoms in patients with morphine dependence . Buprenorphine is a synthetic thebaine congener and also acts as an antagonist at kappa receptor . It is more potent than morphine at mu receptor but with lower intrinsic activity and ceiling effect . Due to lower intrinsic activity, it has no withdrawal symptoms and can be used in the treatment of morphine dependence .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An elderly man with bone metastasis is receiving intravenous opioids for pain management. Which of the following drugs can be safely administered to him without a risk of developing respiratory depression ?
mcqs.explanation: Buprenorphine can be safely administered to this patient because of its ceiling effect on respiratory depression . Ceiling effect is defined as no further increase in the effect of the drug with a further increment in dose , once the ceiling level is reached . Opioid agonist-antagonist compounds produce respiratory depression (and analgesia) with a ceiling effect which means increasing the dose further does not produce any further respiratory depression and may actually result in increased ventilation (due to the predominance of antagonist actions). Other drugs that show the ceiling effect are: • Butorphanol • Nalbuphine • Pentazocine. Respiratory depression with morphine, fentanyl & alfentanyl does not have a ceiling effect because they are pure opioid agonists. As the dose increases, respiratory depression also increases progressing to respiratory arrest.386

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false ?

options.a: Naltrexone is an antagonist at \265 receptor
options.b: Meperidine is a pure agonist at \265 receptor
options.c: Nalbuphine is an agonist at k receptor
options.d: Butorphanol is an antagonist at k receptor

mcqs.explanation: Butorphanol is an agonist at \026 receptor. It may be a partial agonist or antagonist at \265 receptor . Pentazocine, butorphanol, buprenorphine , meptazinol, nalorphine, nalbuphine , and dezocine are mixed agonist-antagonist opioids . All opioid agonist-antagonists are \265 antagonists and k agonists, except buprenorphine , pentazocine, and dezocine . Buprenorphine, pentazocine , and dezocine are partial agonists at the �M receptor . Option A: Naltrexone is a pure antagonist at \265, k, and \027 receptors . Option B: Meperidine is a pure agonist of both �M and \026 receptors .387

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a pure opioid antagonist?
mcqs.explanation: Both naloxone and naltrexone are pure opioid antagonists. Nalorphine is an agonist-antagonist. It has antagonistic activity at the mu receptor and additional agonistic activity at the kappa receptor . Note : Nalmefene is sometimes classified as a pure antagonist but it has additional kappa receptor partial agonist activity.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect about opioid antagonists?

options.a: Naloxone is a short acting drug
options.c: Nalmefene can be used for treatment of opioid overdose
options.d: Nalmefene is shorter acting than naloxone

mcqs.explanation: Nalmefene is longer-acting (not shorter-acting) than naloxone.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about naltrexone?

options.b: Is used in the treatment of alcohol dependence

mcqs.explanation: Naltrexone is more potent than naloxone. Naltrexone is a pure opioid antagonist which is orally active. Alcohol craving is reduced by naltrexone. It is also approved for the prevention of relapse in opioid addiction treatment .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient is on chronic opioid therapy for pain management. He would not develop tolerance against which of the following actions of opioids ?
mcqs.explanation: Tolerance is developed to all the above actions of opioids except for miosis. Exceptions to opioid tolerance (3C's): • Constricted pupil (miosis) • Constipation • Convulsions

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An elderly man, who is on chronic morphine therapy for pain relief , visits your clinic with complaints of not passing stools for the last 4 days. Which of the following drugs is best suited to treat his condition?
mcqs.explanation: 392 The given clinical picture points towards opioid -induced constipation . Methylnaltrexone , an opioid antagonist with predominant peripheral action is best suited for treating opioid -induced constipation . Methylnaltrexone is a peripheral \265 receptor antagonist. It was introduced in the treatment of opioid-induced constipation refractory to other measures . It is a quaternary ammonium compound and hence cannot cross the blood-brain barrier . It can reverse the effects mediated by peripheral opioid receptors and spares CNS effects like analgesia. The peripherally acting opioid antagonists include : • Methylnaltrexone • Naloxegol • Naldemedine • Alvimopan

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an antagonist at \265 receptor ?
mcqs.explanation: Naltrindole is a new non-peptide drug which has a selective antagonistic activity on the \027 receptor . This drug is still in the trial phase and is not yet in use . Option B: Naloxone is considered a pure opioid receptor antagonist but at high doses , it is found to have partial agonistic activity on the �M- and \026-opioid receptors . Option C: Nalbuphine is an agonist-antagonist opioid which acts as an antagonist at the �M receptor and an agonist at the \026 receptor . Option D: Naltrexone is a �M-, \027- and \026-opioid receptor antagonist.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 27-year-old man presented to the casualty with slurred speech and shallow breathing. On examination , you find he has bradycardia, hypotension , and pin-point pupils . Which drug will you choose to treat him?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical features are suggestive of opioid overdose. Naloxone is the drug of choice for opioid overdose. Opioid overdose symptoms : • Triad of coma, respiratory depression, and pinpoint pupils (miosis) • Hypotension , bradycardia • Shallow breathing • Hypothermia Naloxone is also used for reversing neonatal asphyxia due to opioid usage in labor. Naloxone is a pure opioid antagonist which reverses all effects except sedation . Note : Naloxone is contraindicated in infants born to mothers with opiate addiction as it may precipitate acute neonatal withdrawal with seizures .393

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A college student who is addicted to intravenous heroin abruptly stopped abusing the drug during exams. Which of the following would you not expect as a part of withdrawal ?
mcqs.explanation: Diarrhea (not constipation ) is seen in opioid withdrawal . Opioid withdrawal symptoms (mnemonic- O MY WITHDRAWALS ): • Mydriasis • Yawning • Weakness • Insomnia , irritability • Tremors , tachycardia • Hypertension , hyperactive • Diarrhea • Rhinorrhoea • Apnoeic attacks • Weight loss • Anxiety • Lacrimation • Sweating

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An elderly woman who was dependent on morphine for her palliative care recently got switched to another opioid medication. A few days later she started developing withdrawal symptoms . Which of the following opioids would have been prescribed to her?
mcqs.explanation: Pentazocine can precipitate withdrawal symptoms in opioid -dependent patients . It acts as a weak antagonist or partial agonist at mu-opioid receptors which may precipitate withdrawal symptoms . Options A, C, and D: Pethidine , morphine, and methadone are pure agonists at mu-receptors and do not precipitate withdrawal symptoms .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 33-year-old man with a history of heroin addiction is referred to a rehabilitation center . Which of the following would you use as a substitute drug for maintenance therapy ?
mcqs.explanation: Methadone is used as a substitute drug for the maintenance therapy of opioid (heroin) dependence. This is because of its good oral bioavailability and long half-life . Methadone is substituted for opioids during detoxification to avoid withdrawal symptoms . Once stabilized , the dose is gradually reduced and the drug is stopped slowly over days. Due to its long half-life and accumulation in tissues , discontinuing the drug still results in low concentrations of the drug in plasma resulting in protracted withdrawal symptoms .394 Maintainance therapy for opioid dependence : • Long-acting opioid agonist - a safer substitute like methadone is given in a supervised manner to prevent withdrawal symptoms • Partial agonist - buprenorphine can also be used • Clonidine, lofexidine - alpha-2 agonists act as sympatholytic and reduce the withdrawal symptoms • LAAM(L -Alpha-Acetyl -Methadol ) - opioid agonist which reduces craving • Naltrexone - is an opioid antagonist used in maintenance therapy to prevent relapses

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A physician prescribes naltrexone to a patient undergoing treatment for opioid addiction. What is the function of this drug in opioid addiction?
mcqs.explanation: Naltrexone is used for the prevention of relapse in opioid addiction. It is given only after initial opioid detoxification. The patient should be opioid -free for 7-10 days and have a negative naloxone challenge (no withdrawal after naloxone administration). Naltrexone is a pure opioid antagonist which is more potent than naloxone. It is orally active and has a long duration of action which makes it suitable for opioid blockade therapy in post -addicts .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about the use of naltrexone in the treatment of opioid addiction?

options.a: Discontinuation of naltrexone does not cause withdrawal symptoms
options.b: It satisfies craving in opioid addicts
options.c: It blocks the effects of opioids if they are used
options.d: It is administered only when the patient has completed detoxification from opioids

mcqs.explanation: Naltrexone does not satisfy the craving of opioid addicts . It is an opioid antagonist with a high affinity for �M opioid receptors . Naltrexone does not suppress craving in opioid addiction but it suppresses craving in chronic alcoholics . Opioid agonists such as methadone and buprenorphine suppress craving and withdrawal symptoms and are therefore used in the first stage of detoxification in opioid addiction. Option A: Discontinuation of naltrexone ingestion has no negative physical consequences , as opposed to discontinuation of agonist maintenance therapies , which results in the emergence of opioid withdrawal symptoms . This is a major reason for noncompliance and treatment failure. Option C: It blocks the effects of opioids and prevents the user from experiencing subjective symptoms of opioid intoxication such as euphoria on subsequent use . As the user does not experience these symptoms , he does not develop a craving for the substance . Thus, naltrexone prevents relapse . Option D: It is only administered when the patient has completed a medically supervised detoxification from opioids because it can cause immediate withdrawal symptoms .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You are treating a 31 -year-old man with heroin dependence . Which of the following drugs would you not prescribe to him?
mcqs.explanation: Disulfiram cannot be used to treat heroin dependence .395 It is an aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibitor used in the maintenance therapy of alcohol abstinence . Maintainance therapy for opioid dependence : • Long-acting opioid agonist - a safer substitute like methadone is given in a supervised manner to prevent withdrawal symptoms • Partial agonist - buprenorphine can also be used • Clonidine, lofexidine - alpha-2 agonists act as sympatholytic and reduce the withdrawal symptoms • LAAM(L -Alpha-Acetyl -Methadol ) - opioid agonist which reduces craving • Naltrexone - is an opioid antagonist used in maintenance therapy to prevent relapses396

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Effect of acute ethanol consumption is inhibitory on which of the following ligand-gated ion channels?
mcqs.explanation: The effect of acute ethanol consumption is inhibitory on NMDA receptor -operated channels. Effects of acute ethanol on ion channels: Enhancement • GABA-A receptor -operated channels • Glycine receptor -operated channels • Nicotinic ACh receptor -operated channels • 5HT3 receptor -operated channels • G protein-coupled inwardly rectifying K+ channels • Large conductance , Ca2+/ voltage -activated K+ channels Inhibition • NMDA receptor -operated channels400 • Voltage-gated Ca2+ channels

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The black-outs associated with high levels of ethanol can be attributed to its action on which of the following receptors ?
mcqs.explanation: Blackouts are periods of memory loss that occur with high ethanol consumption and may result from the ability of ethanol to inhibit the action of glutamate on NMDA receptors . NMDA receptor is implicated in many aspects of cognitive function including learning and memory.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Ethanol ingestion results in enhanced diuresis . What is the most probable mechanism causing this?

options.a: Inhibition of ADH action in collecting tubules
options.b: Stimulation of ADH action in collecting tubules
options.c: Stimulation of ADH release from pituitary gland
options.d: Inhibition of ADH release from pituitary gland

mcqs.explanation: Ethanol inhibits the release of antidiuretic hormone (ADH)/ vasopressin from the posterior pituitary gland. This results in enhanced diuresis observed with ethanol ingestion . Inhibition of ADH action in collecting tubules is not the mechanism by which alcohol induces diuresis. Stimulation of ADH release or action will have an antidiuretic action.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What effect does acute consumption of ethanol have on cytochrome enzymes ?
mcqs.explanation: Acute consumption of ethanol inhibits the function of several cytochrome enzymes that are involved in the metabolism of drugs. CYP2E1 is one of the isoenzymes that is specifically inhibited . Chronic consumption of alcohol causes induction of cytochrome enzymes , particularly CYP2E1, increasing the rate of metabolism of drugs dependent on CYP2E1 for metabolism .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibitor that you would prescribe for the pharmacological management of a patient addicted to alcohol?
mcqs.explanation: Disulfiram is an irreversible inhibitor of both cytosolic and mitochondrial forms of aldehyde dehydrogenase. Ethanol consumption during disulfiram therapy can lead to increased concentrations of acetaldehyde. Increased acetaldehyde levels can cause flushing , pulsating headache , throbbing pain in the head and neck, and other aversive reactions. Disulfiram is indicated in alcohol deaddiction maintenance therapy . Option 1: Fomepizole is an inhibitor of alcohol dehydrogenase . Option 3: Acamprosate is an NMDA receptor antagonist with modest GABA-A receptor agonistic activity. Option 4: Naltrexone is an opioid antagonist that suppresses craving in chronic alcoholics .401 Option 5: Chlordiazepoxide is a benzodiazepine that can be used to treat acute alcohol withdrawal and anxiety.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 51-year-old diabetic patient presents to your OPD with severe restlessness , palpitations , flushing , and sweating . His medication history includes OHAs and an antibiotic that was started 3 days back. On enquiring, he admits that he consumed two shots of whiskey after taking his medications . Which of the following drugs is not likely to cause similar effects ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical presentation is suggestive of a disulfiram-like reaction. Metformin is not associated with a disulfiram-like reaction following alcohol ingestion . Disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol ingestion is seen with the following drugs: • Metronidazole • 1st generation sulfonylureas like chlorpropamide • Cephalosporins like cefoperazone , cefamandole • Griseofulvin • Procarbazine

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man with alcohol dependence is referred to a rehabilitation center for deaddiction . Which of the following drugs would you not prescribe for maintenance of deaddiction ?
mcqs.explanation: Morphine, an opioid receptor agonist, is not indicated for alcohol deaddiction maintenance. Opioid receptor antagonist is indicated for this condition. Drugs approved for the maintenance therapy and to prevent relapse : • Naltrexone : It is an orally active opioid receptor antagonist. • Acamprosate: An NMDA receptor antagonist with modest GABA-A receptor agonistic activity. • Disulfiram: A deterrent drug that works by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase enzyme.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following anti-epileptics is effective in maintaining abstinence in a patient undergoing treatment for alcohol deaddiction ?
mcqs.explanation: Topiramate has shown efficacy in maintaining abstinence and reducing craving in chronic alcoholism. Though effective , topiramate is not yet approved for use in alcohol deaddiction maintenance. It is used off-label for this indication. Ondansetron and baclofen are other drugs that are found to be effective but not yet approved for this use .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A young man presented to the ER with complaints of headache , vomiting, and blurring of vision after he consumed a bottle of illicit liquor. His ABG shows a high anion gap metabolic acidosis. Which of the following statements would be incorrect regarding his management?

options.b: Intravenous ethanol is an alternative to fomepizole
options.d: Folinic acid is also used in treatment

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture and labs are suggestive of accidental methanol toxicity . Hemodialysis is used in severe cases of methanol toxicity.402 A serum methanol concentration greater than 50 mg/dl is serious enough to consider hemodialysis. It can be used to remove both methanol and its toxic metabolite formic acid from the blood. Option A: Fomepizole , an alcohol dehydrogenase inhibitor, is administered intravenously in methanol toxicity. It acts by inhibiting the formation of formic acid. Option B: Intravenous ethanol is an alternative to fomepizole . It has a higher affinity to alcohol dehydrogenase than methanol. Thus, saturation of ADH enzymes results in less formation of toxic formic acid. Option D: Folate -dependent systems are responsible for the oxidation of formic acid to CO2. Both folinic and folic acid are often administered during methanol toxicity but the exact benefit is yet to be determined . Note : Ethanol is given intravenously in the management of methanol and ethylene glycol poisoning.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: How is the administration of ethanol going to help in the management of methanol poisoning?

options.b: Ethanol slows down metabolism of methanol
options.c: Ethanol reacts with methanol to form an inactive metabolite
options.d: Ethanol reverses the actions of methanol

mcqs.explanation: Administration of ethanol slows down the metabolism of methanol. Ethanol has a higher affinity for alcohol dehydrogenase than methanol. Formic acid is the metabolite of methanol which is highly toxic. Therefore, slowing down the metabolism of methanol reduces its toxic effects .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man undergoing treatment for alcohol deaddiction was started on disulfiram. Which of the following statements is true regarding this drug?

options.a: When used with alcohol it causes respiratory difficulties
options.c: It can be initiated even in minimally motivated persons
options.d: Its action persists up to 2-3 days after stopping the drug

mcqs.explanation: Alcohol consumption during disulfiram therapy can lead to increased concentrations of acetaldehyde. This can cause aversive reactions resulting in flushing , pulsating headache , throbbing pain in the head and neck, nausea, vomiting, rashes, respiratory difficulties , chest pain, and autonomic manifestations . Disulfiram is an irreversible inhibitor of both cytosolic and mitochondrial forms of aldehyde dehydrogenase. It is used in behavioral modification for alcohol de -addiction. Option B: The principle of action is aversive conditioning (not anti-craving ). Option C: Disulfiram can be given only to highly motivated individuals. It should not be administered until the person has abstained from alcohol for at least 12 hours. Option D: The disulfiram-alcohol reaction may persist as long as 14 days after the last dose of disulfiram.403

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Drugs for Alzheimer's Disease and Other Neurode...
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old male patient is brought to the OPD by his son, with complaints of increasing forgetfulness . Neuroimaging shows marked cortical atrophy of temporal and parietal lobes . What is the most striking neurochemical disturbance in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Alzheimer's disease (AD). The most striking neurochemical disturbance in AD is the deficiency of acetylcholine in the subcortical area (especially in the nucleus basalis of Meynert ). Neurotransmitters like glutamate and 5-HT and other areas of the brain like the hippocampus are also involved in the pathogenesis of this disease . The drugs used in Alzheimer's disease are: • Central acetylcholine esterase inhibitors targeting acetylcholine deficiency • NMDA antagonists targeting glutamate excitotoxicity407

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Drugs for Alzheimer's Disease and Other Neurode...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a reversible cholinesterase inhibitor indicated in a patient with Alzheimer's disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Memantine is an NMDA receptor antagonist used to treat moderate to severe dementia in Alzheimer's. Donepezil , rivastigmine, and galantamine are reversible cholinesterase inhibitors indicated in Alzheimer's disease . Irreversible antagonists are not indicated in Alzheimer's disease .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Drugs for Alzheimer's Disease and Other Neurode...
mcqs.question: A neurology resident changed the current oral medication of a patient with Alzheimer's disease to a transdermal patch of a cholinesterase inhibitor. What must be the new drug that was prescribed ?
mcqs.explanation: Rivastigmine is a cholinesterase inhibitor that is available as a transdermal patch for use in Alzheimer's disease . It can be applied for over 24 hours. Transdermal delivery reduces the fluctuation and avoids direct gastric irritation effects associated with oral formulations. Option A: Tacrine is an anticholinesterase that is obsolete because of its association with hepatotoxicity. Options B and D: Donepezil and galantamine transdermal formulations are under development and yet to be available in the market.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Drugs for Alzheimer's Disease and Other Neurode...
mcqs.question: Which of the following NMDA receptor antagonist would you prescribe to a patient with severe Alzheimer's disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Memantine is a noncompetitive N-methyl -D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist indicated in Alzheimer's disease . It slows the deterioration of patients with moderate and severe Alzheimer's disease . It is claimed to reduce the excitotoxicity of glutamate . Option B - Ketamine is an NMDA receptor antagonist indicated as an anesthetic agent . Option C - Piracetam is a nootropic agent (a drug that enhances cognitive function) that is used off-label to enhance memory. Option D - Amantadine is an antiviral agent with NMDA receptor antagonistic action which is also indicated in Parkinson 's disease due to its action on dopamine release and reuptake .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Drugs for Alzheimer's Disease and Other Neurode...
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the management of Alzheimer's disease ?

options.a: Monoclonal antibodies can be used in the treatment
options.c: Memantine is approved only in moderate to severe disease
options.d: Cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine have no effect on behavioral and psychiatric symptoms

mcqs.explanation: Cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine reduce some of the behavioral and psychiatric symptoms in Alzheimer's disease . SSRIs like citalopram or benzodiazepines for agitation and atypical antipsychotics for psychiatric symptoms may be considered in severe cases . But atypical antipsychotics in dementia -related psychosis have shown higher mortality. Option A - Amyloid beta -directed monoclonal antibodies approved for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease are - lecanemab, donanemab, aducanumab408 Option B - Cholinesterase inhibitors are commonly used and are considered as first-line in early or mild to moderate stages of Alzheimer's disease . Option C - Memantine is approved only in moderate -severe Alzheimer's disease . There is not enough data to support its use in mild to moderate stages . Note - Aducanumab has been discontinued in the treatment of Alzheimer's

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Drugs for Alzheimer's Disease and Other Neurode...
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old lady came to the OPD with complaints of occasional shock-like sensations down her spine and muscle spasms. T2 weighted MRI shows typical Dawson fingers and oligoclonal bands were detected in the CSF study . Which of the following is approved for the treatment of her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of multiple sclerosis . Interferon beta is approved for use in this condition. It reduces the frequency of attacks in relapsing -remitting multiple sclerosis . The probable mechanisms of action of interferon-beta are: • Immune modulation and a decrease in T cell proliferation. • Limiting the entry of T cells into CNS. • Reducing pro-inflammatory and increasing regulatory cytokines.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Drugs for Alzheimer's Disease and Other Neurode...
mcqs.question: You plan to start disease -modifying therapy in a 40-year-old patient with relapsing -remitting multiple sclerosis. Which of the following drugs would you not include in the treatment regimen?
mcqs.explanation: The disease -modifying therapy of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS) does not include methylprednisolone. It is used in acute attacks and exacerbations for MS symptom control. The long-term value or disease -modifying potential of glucocorticoid therapy is unknown. FDA approved disease -modifying therapy of relapsing -remitting multiple sclerosis are: • Interferon-beta 1a • Interferon-beta 1b • Glatiramer • Dimethyl fumarate • Teriflunomide • Alemtuzumab • Natalizumab • Fingolimod • Mitoxantrone • Cladribine

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Drugs for Alzheimer's Disease and Other Neurode...
mcqs.question: John Cunningham (JC) virus antibody titer is being measured in a patient with multiple sclerosis . During treatment with which of the following drugs are the titres mandatory?
mcqs.explanation: 409 John Cunningham (JC) virus antibody titre measurement is mandatory during treatment with monoclonal antibodies like natalizumab. Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) is a life -threatening disease caused by the JC virus in patients with multiple sclerosis . It is more common when the patient is immunocompromised during their treatment with natalizumab. The current recommendation is to start natalizumab only in a patient who tests negative for JC antibodies . Seroconversion can occur anytime during treatment . Regular monitoring for JC antibody every 6 months is recommended in JC antibody-negative patients on natalizumab.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Drugs for Alzheimer's Disease and Other Neurode...
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old lady presents with complaints of sudden , involuntary, and uncontrollable dance-like movements. Her mother had also developed similar symptoms at the age of 40. Which of the following drugs is indicated for the treatment of the involuntary movements associated with her condition?
mcqs.explanation: This patient is most likely suffering from chorea associated with Huntington's disease , for which tetrabenazine is indicated . It is a reversible inhibitor of vesicular monoamine transporter-2 (VMAT -2). Other drugs used in Huntington's disease are: • Reserpine , an irreversible inhibitor of VMAT -2 and a longer-acting agent as compared to tetrabenazine. • Deutetrabenazine refers to deuterium attached to carbon in place of hydrogen , in tetrabenazine (deuterated tetrabenazine ). It is a newer form of tetrabenazine approved for the treatment of chorea associated with Huntington's disease . It slows down its metabolism , hence it is longer acting than tetrabenazine . It is associated with better control of chorea. Option A - Benzhexol is a central anticholinergic indicated in parkinsonism . Option C - Tetrahydrozoline is a topical alpha-adrenergic agonist indicated for the relief of conjunctival congestion . Option D - Benztropine is a muscarinic receptor antagonist that can be used for the management of acute dystonia.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Drugs for Alzheimer's Disease and Other Neurode...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a mechanism of action of Riluzole?
mcqs.explanation: Riluzole does not act by causing inhibition of GABA reuptake . Riluzole is the only drug known to improve survival in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS ), also known as Lou Gehrig's disease . The mechanism of action involves the reduction of glutamate -induced excitotoxicity by: • Inhibition of glutamate release • Antagonism of NMDA and kainate-type glutamate receptor • Direct action on the voltage -dependent sodium channels.410

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Drugs for Alzheimer's Disease and Other Neurode...
mcqs.question: Which of the following new drugs has been approved for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis ?
mcqs.explanation: Edaravone was approved by the FDA for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS ). It has free radical scavenging properties that may reduce oxidative stress . The exact mechanism of action is unknown. It is to be administered as an IV infusion with an initial treatment cycle of daily dosing for 14 days, followed by a 14-day drug-free period . Subsequent treatment cycles consist of dosing on 10 of 14 days, followed by a 14 day drug-free period . The major adverse effect of edaravone is hypersensitivity because the infusion contains sodium bisulfite . Other adverse effects include bruising, gait disorder, and headache . Tafinlar (dabrafenib) and Mekinist (trametinib), are both indicated as monotherapy in BRAF V600E/K (BRAF V600E mutation-positive) melanoma. They are approved for combined administration, for the treatment of anaplastic thyroid cancer (ATC) that cannot be removed by surgery or that has spread to other parts of the body (metastatic ). Piracetam is a nootropic agent (a drug that enhances cognitive function) that is used off-label to enhance memory. It is also used to treat myoclonus .411

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A young man who collapsed at a concert was suspected to have bacterial meningitis. The other attendees of the concert were administered ciprofloxacin by the medical staff on duty . What is this kind of antimicrobial therapy called ?
mcqs.explanation: The antimicrobial treatment initiated in a patient who is not yet infected is called prophylactic therapy. The goal is to prevent infection in some patients and to prevent dangerous manifestations of infections in other patients . Option A: Preemptive therapy is therapy in an asymptomatic individual with evidence of infection (high-risk).415 Option C: Empirical therapy is broad-spectrum therapy in a patient with symptoms of infection but no microbiological confirmation of the causative agent . Option D: Suppressive therapy is given to patients when the infection is controlled but not completely eradicated by the initial round of antimicrobial treatment . This is usually indicated for immunosuppressed patients .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The total microbial population was found to be susceptible to antimicrobials on testing but a subset of the same population was resistant which was undetected . What is this phenomenon called ?
mcqs.explanation: Heteroresistance occurs when a subset of the total microbial population is resistant, despite the total microbial population being susceptible on testing . The resistant subpopulation is usually well below the assay-detection limits. Heteroresistant Staphylococci and M. tuberculosis have led to therapeutic failures and mortality. C. albicans and C. neoformans with heteroresistance to fluconazole have resulted in increased treatment failures . Note : For viruses, the resistant viral species occurring due to the above phenomenon is termed as 'quasi-species '. Quasi-species resistant to antiretroviral agents have resulted in the failure of antiretroviral therapy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs shows concentration-dependent killing?
mcqs.explanation: Aminoglycosides exhibit concentration-dependent killing and are preferably dosed once daily for maximum effect . Peak concentration above MIC (minimum inhibitory concentration) matters for certain classes of drugs for their antimicrobial action. It is referred to as concentration-dependent killing. The period during which the concentration remains above MIC is not relevant for such drugs. Aminoglycosides and quinolones have this property . Time-dependent killing: The antimicrobial action is dependent on the period for which the concentration of drug remains above the MIC. Penicillins, 5-fluorocytosine and vancomycin have this property .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient having pneumococcal pneumonia could not be treated using penicillin G as the microbe was found to be resistant to it. How is this resistance mainly acquired?
mcqs.explanation: Transformation is the molecular basis of penicillin G resistance in pneumococci and meningococci.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the extrachromosomal DNA present in bacteria that transmits drug resistance called ?
mcqs.explanation: Drug resistance transmitting extrachromosomal DNA present in bacteria is a plasmid.416 They are usually involved in the horizontal transfer of drug resistance gene in bacteria. Chromosomal DNA can also be involved in the transfer of resistance .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: How is multidrug resistance transferred among bacteria?
mcqs.explanation: Multidrug resistance is transferred through conjugation. Multiple genes , each encoding for resistance to a drug can be present in a single bacterial cell . Typically such genes are present on resistance (R) plasmids . The main mode of transfer of resistant gene -containing plasmids is through conjugation.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An example of a bacteriostatic drug is ______
mcqs.explanation: Linezolid is an example of a bacteriostatic drug.Primarily bacteriostatic drugs Primarily bactericidal drugs SulfonamidesErythromycinT etracyclinesClindamycinChlo ramphenicolLinezolidEtham butol Penicillins,CephalosporinsA minoglycosidesVancomycinP olypeptidesCiprofloxacinRifa mpinMetronidazoleIsoniazid CotrimoxazolePyrazinamide

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You want to prescribe a bactericidal drug to a patient having an infection . Which of the following drugs will you not choose ?
mcqs.explanation: Tigecycline is not a bactericidal drug. Tigecycline belongs to a new class of glycylcyclines which is a congener of teteracycline . It is a protein synthesis inhibitor and generally considered as a bacteriostatic . Isoniazid, daptomycin and ciprofloxacin are all bactericidal agents .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient developed a surgical site infection with Klebsiella , which is found to be sensitive to a cell wall synthesis inhibitor. Which of the following antibiotics is this likely to be?
mcqs.explanation: Cefepime is an antibiotic that acts by inhibiting cell wall synthesis . Cefepime is a fourth-generation cephalosporin. Cephalosporins act by inhibiting cell wall synthesis . Aminoglycosides , doxycycline , and erythromycin are protein synthesis inhibitors.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient has presented to your OPD complaining of vomiting and rice water stools . You decide to treat him with a protein synthesis inhibitor. Which antibiotic do you choose ?
mcqs.explanation: 417 Doxycycline is a tetracycline that acts by inhibiting protein synthesis . It is the drug of choice for cholera. Options A & D: Cefotetan and oxacillin are beta -lactam antibiotics that act by inhibiting cell wall synthesis. Option C: Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone that acts by inhibiting DNA gyrase .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antibacterial agents does not act by inhibiting cell wall synthesis ?
mcqs.explanation: Nitrofurantoin is an antibacterial drug that does not act by inhibiting cell wall synthesis . The antibacterial activity of nitrofurantoin appears to correlate with the rapid intracellular conversion of nitrofurantoin to highly reactive intermediates by bacterial reductases . These intermediates react nonspecifically with many ribosomal proteins and disrupt the synthesis of proteins , RNA, DNA, and metabolic processes . Carbapenems, monobactams, and cephalosporins are beta -lactam antibiotics that act by inhibiting cell wall synthesis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You are studying the susceptibility of Streptococci to bacitracin in the lab. What is the site of action of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Bacitracin acts on the cell wall by inhibiting the synthesis of the cell wall. It interferes with the dephosphorylation of bactoprenol (lipid carrier ) which carries peptidoglycan subunits outside the cell membrane to the growing cell wall. It can also alter the integrity of the cell membrane. Bacitracin is mainly active against gram-positive cocci and bacilli.418

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antimalarial drugs is a slow acting schizonticide ?
mcqs.explanation: 424 Pyrimethamine is a slow -acting schizonticide . Female Anopheles mosquito inoculates Plasmodium species in the form of sporozoites into the human host during blood meal. Sporozoites migrate to the liver and mature into hepatic schizonts. Hepatic schizonts are released into the blood in the form of merozoites . Merozoites in the erythrocyte transform into ring form and erythrocytic schizonts. Some merozoites in the blood transform into gametocytes . Antimalarial drugs are classified based on their onset of action of schizonticidal function as below : • Fast onset of action • Artemisinin derivatives like artemether , arteether and artesunate are fastest acting • Chloroquine • Intermediate onset of action • Mefloquine • Quinine • Proguanil • Lumefantrine • Slow onset of action • Pyrimethamine • Sulfonamides • Tetracyclines • Clindamycin

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is gametocidal to all the species causing malaria ?
mcqs.explanation: Primaquine is gametocidal to all species causing malaria . It inhibits transmission of malaria .425 The drugs with clinically important gametocidal activity (against all species ) are: • High activity: • Artemisinins • Primaquine • Low to moderate activity: • Chloroquine • Quinine • Atovaquone/proguanil • No activity: • Mefloquine • Pyrimethamine • Sulfadoxine • Tetracycline

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A researcher who was studying plasmodium species decided to visit a malaria -endemic place in Odisha to do his clinical study for 5 weeks . He is planning to leave after 2 days. Which of the following drugs can be taken as prophylaxis before visiting the malaria -endemic place ?
mcqs.explanation: Doxycycline can be taken as prophylaxis by the researcher before going to malaria -endemic places . Chemoprophylaxis against malaria for travelers: • If the duration of travel is less than 6 weeks then doxycycline 100mg once a day is to be started 2 days before travel and continued atleast 4 weeks after travel. • If the duration of travel is more than 6 weeks then mefloquine 250mg once a week is to be started 2 weeks before travel and continued atleast 4 weeks after travel.426

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old woman presented with fever and chills. Peripheral blood smear revealed findings suggestive of P. vivax malaria . Which among the following is the most appropriate drug for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Most approproate drug for the treatment of malaria due to P. vivax is chloroquine. P. vivax treatment recommendations are: • Chloroquine-susceptible infections : Chloroquine or artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT). • Chloroquine-resistant infections : ACT is the drug of choice but quinine is used during 1st trimester of pregnancy. In the absence of resistance data in the question, chloroquine appears to be the most appropriate answer.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Radical cure is required for malaria caused by which of the following species ?
mcqs.explanation: Radical cure is required for malaria caused by P. vivax and P. ovale. In case of Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium ovale, malarial parasites have an exoerythrocytic stage (hypnozoites ). In the exoerythrocytic phase malarial parasites are found in the liver that can cause relapse of malaria after clinical cure. Therefore, they require radical cure by drugs acting on the exoerythrocytic stage . Primaquine is effective against the exoerythrocytic stages of Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium ovale in the liver. Primaquine is administered for 14 days for radical cure.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Tafenoquine is used in which of the following conditions?

options.d: Treatment of malaria in children <2 years

mcqs.explanation: Tafenoquine is used in the radical cure of Plasmodium vivax . Total eradication of plasmodium species which includes clinical curative and hypnozoites phase are called radical cure. Primaquine and tafenoquine (derivative of primaquine) have very high activity against the latent tissue forms (hypnozoites ) of the species . It is primarily used for the chemoprophylaxis and radical cure of P. vivax and P. ovale infections .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Chloroquine is not useful in the treatment of which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Chloroquine is used in the treatment of systemic lupus erythematosus , porphyria cutanea tarda and giardiasis, due to its anti-inflammatory effect ; but it is not used in the treatment of Sjogren's Syndrome. Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine concentrate in lysosomes and have an anti-inflammatory effect . It also has antihistaminic and antiarrhythmic properties . Non-antimalarial uses of choloroquine are:427 • Hepatic amoebiasis • Giardiasis • Rheumatoid arthritis • Systemic lupus erythematosus • Discoid lupus erythematosus • Porphyria cutanea tarda • Severe polymorphous light eruption

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old woman who is 10 weeks pregnant, comes with history of fever and chills. She is diagnosed with falciparum malaria . Which of the following drugs will you choose for her treatment ?
mcqs.explanation: The woman is in the 1st trimester of pregnancy and falciparum malaria during 1st trimester of pregnancy is treated with quinine plus clindamycin. Worldwide , most species of Falciparum malaria are resistant to chloroquine. In all trimesters , pregnant women diagnosed with uncomplicated malaria caused by chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum infection can be treated with a combination of quinine and clindamycin. Quinine is considered the drug of choice in the first trimester. In the second and third trimesters artemether -lumefantrine can be used , but not in the first trimester. Vivax malaria during pregnancy is treated with chloroquine as chloroquine is safe in pregnancy and children. Clindamycin can be used in children for chloroquine-resistant cases . It is safe to use in children and pregnant women. Option B: Doxycycline is useful in the treatment of malaria but not used in pregnancy. Options C and D: Artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) is not recommended during the 1st trimester of pregnancy because of a lack of safety data.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old man presents with fever with chills and seizures . On examination, his blood pressure was 70/50 mm of Hg and labored breathing was present . Routine blood investigations revealed Hb of 4.8 g/dl. ABG was done and the pH was 7.21. Findings in peripheral blood smear are shown below . Which of the following is the drug of choice in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: This scenario depicts a case of severe complicated falciparum malaria , and the drug of choice in this condition is artesunate . The image shows ring forms/early trophozoites in erythrocyte , which are binucleate (double chromatin) and this is characteristic of P. falciparum malaria . Severe complicated malaria is caused by P. falciparum and is characterized by hyperparasitemia , hyperpyrexia, acidosis, respiratory distress , bleeding manifestation, cardiovascular collapse , renal failure and cerebral malaria . As per WHO guidelines , all patients with severe malaria should be treated with intravenous or intramuscular artesunate for at least 24 hours. Once the patient recovers and can tolerate oral medications , oral ACT for 3 days is recommended . Artemether is used only if parenteral artesunate is not available.428

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a WHO recommended artemisinin-based combination therapy ?
mcqs.explanation: WHO recommended artemisinin-based combination therapies are: • Artemether plus lumefantrine • Artesunate plus pyrimethamine -sulfadoxine • Artesunate plus mefloquine • Artesunate plus amodiaquine • Dihydroartemisinin plus piperaquine

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You are posted in a health centre in Nagaland as part of your rural service and a patient is diagnosed with uncomplicated falciparum malaria . Which of the following artemisinin-based combination therapy is recommended by NVBDCP for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) recommended by NVBDCP in the north-eastern states is a combination of artemether and lumefantrine . NVBDCP guidelines for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum cases : • North-eastern states : Artemether -lumefantrine based ACT • Rest of the country: Artesunate -sulfadoxine +pyrimethamine In the north-eastern states (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya , Mizoram, Nagaland, and Tripura), the presently recommended ACT for P. falciparum malaria is a fixed -dose combination of artemether -lumefantrine due to the recent reports of late treatment failures with the current combination of AS+SP.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Loading dose is essential for chloroquine because of which of the following properties ?
mcqs.explanation: Loading dose is essential for chloroquine because of its property of high volume of distribution. Chloroquine is distributed extensively in the liver, spleen , kidney, lungs , skin and, to a lesser extent, brain and spinal cord. Because of extensive tissue binding, a loading dose is required for achieving effective plasma concentrations earlier in the therapy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: While writing a prescription for a patient diagnosed with malaria , the medical officer instructed the patient to take a particular drug along with a high fatty meal. Identify the drug.
mcqs.explanation: The drug described here is lumefantrine and its absorption increases when it is administered along with fatty food or milk because it is highly lipophilic .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who was diagnosed with malaria was initiated on treatment about 3 days ago. Now she presents with seizures and confusion. Which of the following drugs is most likely to have caused this condition?
mcqs.explanation: 429 The case depicts neuropsychiatric adverse effects which are commonly associated with the use of mefloquine . The US FDA has put a "black box warning" for this drug due to permanent and serious neuropsychiatric side effects . The CNS toxicity caused by mefloquine includes : • Seizures • Acute psychosis • Severe vertigo • Confusion or decreased sensorium

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The finding shown in the image below is seen as a side effect of which of the following drugs?
mcqs.explanation: The finding shown in the image is bulls-eye maculopathy , and chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine use are associated with this side effect . Bull's-eye maculopathy refers to the ophthalmoscopic appearance of a central area of retinal pigment epithelial depigmentation surrounded by relatively normal retinal pigment epithelium , giving a bull's-eye appearance to the macula.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A pregnant patient with severe malaria is undergoing treatment with quinine. Which of the following adverse effects is not associated with this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Quinine is not associated with hypertension. It is associated with hypotension . Quinine is used in the treatment of drug-resistant and severe P. falciparum malaria . It acts against asexual erythrocytic forms but has no significant effect on hepatic forms of malarial parasites . Option A: Quinine use is associated with cinchonism which manifests as tinnitus, visual and auditory disturbances , headache , nausea, and vomiting. Option B: Quinine has a stimulatory effect on pancreatic beta cells and can cause hypoglycemia . Option D: Blackwater fever is a rare type of hypersensitivity reaction to quinine. It presents with massive hemolysis , hemoglobinemia, and hemoglobinuria that may lead to anuria , renal failure, and death .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who was initiated on treatment for malaria two days ago, now presents with complaints of passage of dark -colored urine. Hemolysis due to G6PD deficiency is suspected . With which of the following drugs is this condition more common?
mcqs.explanation: Hemolysis in a G6PD deficient patient is more common with primaquine. G6PD deficient patients are highly sensitive to oxidative stress . They are at increased risk of hemolysis due to the oxidant property of primaquine. Therefore, before initiating primaquine therapy , the G6PD status of the patient has to be determined . Passage of dark color urine is an indication of hemolysis and the drug has to be stopped if it occurs. Quinine, chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine can also cause hemolysis in G6PD deficient patients , but the incidence is less compared to primaquine.430

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
