mcqs.explanation: The first-generation cephalosporin indicated for surgical prophylaxis is Cefazolin. It is the preferred agent for surgical prophylaxis when skin flora is the likely pathogen . Cephalexin , cefadroxil, and cephradine are first-generation oral cephalosporins .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You want to prescribe an oral second -generation cephalosporin to a patient with pneumonia. Which of the following drugs will you choose ?
mcqs.explanation: Cefaclor is a second -generation oral cephalosporin . Option A: Cefepime is a fourth-generation cephalosporin . Options B and D: Cefadroxil and Cephradine are oral first-generation cephalosporins .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In comparison with first-generation cephalosporins , second -generation cephalosporins have which of the following properties ?

options.a: Greater activity against gram positive bacteria
options.b: Lesser activity against gram positive bacteria

mcqs.explanation: Second -generation cephalosporins have lesser activity against gram-positive bacteria when compared with first-generation cephalosporins. Properties of second -generation cephalosporins , when compared to first-generation cephalosporins , are: • Lesser activity against gram-positive bacteria • Broader gram-negative activity against Hemophilus species , indole -positive Proteus, and Klebsiella species • Anaerobes like B.fragilis are susceptible to second -generation cephalosporins like cefoxitin and cefotetan but not first-generation cephalosporins

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a third-generation cephalosporin that can be given orally?
mcqs.explanation: 508 Cefixime is a third-generation oral cephalosporin .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Cephalosporins are not useful in which of the following infections ?
mcqs.explanation: Ampicillin is the drug of choice for listeriosis , which is caused by Listeria monocytogenes , and cephalosporins are not useful in treating this condition. Ceftriaxone is a third-generation cephalosporin, which is considered as a treatment of choice for gonorrhea and severe forms of Lyme disease . Cefoperazone and ceftazidime are third-generation cephalosporins that have clinically significant activity against Pseudomonas .Cephalosporins Therapeutic uses First-generation Skin and soft tissue infection sSerious infections due to MS SAPerioperative surgical pro phylaxis Second generati on Upper respiratory tract infect ions (sinusitis, otitis media)C efoxitin/cefotetan - gynecolog ic infections , perioperative su rgical prophylaxis Third generatio n Community-acquired pneum onia, meningitis, urinary trac t infectionsStreptococcal end ocarditisGonorrheaSevere Ly me disease

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The pus culture and sensitivity report of a hospitalized patient with diabetic ulcer is positive for pseudomonas. Which of the following cephalosporins can be used in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The drug that can be used in this patient is Ceftazidime , which is a third-generation parenteral cephalosporin having significant anti-pseudomonal action. Cefpodoxime proxetil is a third-generation oral cephalosporin . It does not have significant antipseudomonal action. Cephradine and cefotetan are first and second -generation cephalosporins with no antipseudomonal action. Antipseudomonal cell wall synthesis inhibitors are: • Cephalosporins : • Third generation - Ceftazidime , Cefoperazone • Fourth generation - Cefepime and cefpirome . They are also used against enterobacter • Fifth generation - Ceftolozane509 • Extended -spectrum penicillins : • Carboxypenicillins - carbenicillin, ticarcillin • Ureidopenicillins - piperacillin , mezlocillin

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about cefepime is false ?

options.b: Dose should be reduced in renal failure

mcqs.explanation: Cefepime , which is a fourth-generation cephalosporin , has good activity against Pseudomonas, Enterobacter , and S. aureus, but not against MRSA. It is effective in serious infections like hospital -acquired pneumonia, septicemia and febrile neutropenia . Cefepime is excreted primarily through kidneys and dose reduction is necessary for renal failure. Encephalopathy and non-convulsive status epilepticus have been reported with the use of cefepime .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old man presents with a discharging wound post -operatively . Cultures reveal infection with MRSA. Which of the following cephalosporins can be used for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Ceftaroline is the cephalosporin that is indicated for MRSA infections and hence can be used in this patient . It is considered as anti-MRSA cephalosporin and along with ceftobiprole is grouped as fifth -generation cephalosporins . Ceftaroline has gram-negative and also enhanced gram-positive coverage. It is effective against MRSA and penicillin -resistant S. pneumoniae . Cefepime and cefpirome are fourth-generation cephalosporins with no significant action on MRSA. Ceftolozane is a fifth -generation antipseudomonal cephalosporin with no action on MRSA.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient is to be started on a cephalosporin antibiotic. His serum creatinine levels yesterday at the time of admission was 1.1 mg/dl and now it is 1.5 mg/dl. Which of the following cephalosporins can be started without dose reduction in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of acute kidney injury and the cephalosporin that does not require dose reduction in this patient is cefoperazone . All cephalosporins are usually excreted by glomerular filtration and tubular secretion . They need a dose reduction in renal failure, except cefpiramide and cefoperazone that have predominant biliary excretion. Dose reduction is necessary for cefoperazone and cefpiramide in patients with hepatic impairment.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the drug of choice for a patient who presents with an initial episode of Clostridium difficile infection ?
mcqs.explanation: The drug of choice for the treatment of initial episode of Clostridium difficile infection (CDI) is fidaxomicin. It is a macrocyclic antibiotic.510 Fidaxomicin is preferred because of its safety profile and higher beneficial effects . But in resource -limited settings where it is not available, vancomycin can be used for the treatment of this condition. Treatment of Clostridium difficile infection : • Fidaxomicin • Vancomycin • Metronidazole Vancomycin and fidaxomicin are more effective than metronidazole . All of the above drugs are given orally. Loracarbef is a second -generation cephalosporin and is not indicated in pseudomembranous colitis caused by Clostridium difficile . NOTE: As per the Infectious Disease Society of America (IDSA) management guidelines 2021 , Fidaxomicin is now preferred over Vancomycin for the treatment of initial episode of Clostridium difficile infection . Vancomycin can be used as an alternative drug.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the mechanism of action of vancomycin ?
mcqs.explanation: The mechanism of action of vancomycin is cell wall synthesis inhibition. The bacterial cell wall has long chains of peptidoglycan and is cross-linked to each other by the action of the enzyme transglycosylase . Vancomycin is a glycopeptide group of antibiotics that binds to the D-alanyl-D-alanine terminus of the synthesized peptidoglycan . This inhibits the transglycosylase enzyme and prevents elongation and cross-linking of peptidoglycan . This leads to the weakening of the cell wall causing lysis. It exhibits a time-dependant or concentration-independent killing of bacteria. It primarily acts on Gram +ve organisms which are resistant to other antibiotics such as methicillin -resistant staphylococcus and ampicillin resistant enterococci . Lipoglycopeptides are a new generation of glycopeptide congeners which include telavancin, dalbavancin, and oritavancin . Dalbavancin and Oritovancin are administered as a single intravenous dose for skin and soft -tissue infections .511

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Oral vancomycin is used in the treatment of :
mcqs.explanation: Oral vancomycin is used in the treatment of Clostridium difficile associated diarrhea and staphylococcal enterocolitis . Its oral formulation is not absorbed systemically and hence is used for local action in the gastrointestinal tract.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient on intravenous vancomycin develops flushing and erythematous lesions . On examination , tachycardia, and hypotension are noted . By what mechanism does vancomycin cause these effects ?

options.b: Direct toxic effect on mast cells

mcqs.explanation: The given scenario depicts red man syndrome associated with vancomycin . It occurs due to a direct toxic effect on mast cells resulting in the release of histamine. Red man or red neck syndrome is a non-allergic reaction due to rapid intravenous infusion of vancomycin characterized by: • Flushing • Erythematous , urticarial reactions • Tachycardia • Hypotension Slow infusion, prophylactic use of antihistamines can reduce the incidence .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Match the following bacteria with the drug of choice for each.
mcqs.explanation: Vancomycin is the drug of choice for methicillin -resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). It should be used only if the organism is resistant to other drugs.512 Metronidazole is the drug of choice for anaerobic infections caused by Bacteroides . Metronidazole is used in the treatment of the following conditions: • Giardiasis • Trichomoniasis • Amoebiasis • Bacterial vaginosis • Pseudomembranous colitis Meropenem is used in infections caused by ESBL producing bacteria like Klebsiella . Carbapenems are not hydrolyzed by ESBL (extended -spectrum beta -lactamases ). Therefore, carbapenems like imipenem , meropenem and ertapenem are resistant to hydrolysis by ESBLs. They are indicated in the treatment of infections caused by ESBL producing bacteria, like Klebsiella and E. coli. Penicillins like amoxicillin, ampicillin can be used in H. influenzae infections .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient allergic to penicillin requires antibiotic therapy . Which of the following can you safely prescribe?
mcqs.explanation: Aztreonam can be safely given to a patient with a history of allergy to penicillin . It is a monobactam group of \035-Lactam antibiotics resistant to narrow -spectrum beta -lactamase produced by bacteria. It lacks cross-sensitivity with the other beta -lactams, except for ceftazidime . It has activity only against gram-negative bacteria. It has no activity against gram-positive bacteria and anaerobes.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following carbapenems has increased risk of causing seizures ?
mcqs.explanation: Imipenem is the carbapenem that is associated with an increased risk of causing seizures , especially when high doses are given to patients with CNS lesions . Excretion of imipenem is mainly renal and dosage modification is required to avoid seizures in renal failure patients .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about extended -spectrum beta -lactamases ?

options.a: They can hydrolyse penicillins , cephalosporins as well as monobactam
options.c: Ambler classification of ESBL is based on amino acid sequence
options.d: Third and fourth generation cephalosporins are used for detection of ESBL

mcqs.explanation: Carbapenems like imipenem , meropenem , ertapenem are resistant to hydrolysis by extended -spectrum beta -lactamases (ESBL) and hence are indicated in the treatment of infections caused by ESBL producing bacteria. Beta-lactamases are enzymes produced by bacteria that are able to hydrolyze antibiotics and make them ineffective , thus making the bacteria resistant to these antibiotics. They confer resistance against:513 • Penicillins • Cephalosporins • Monobactams Beta lactamases hydrolyze first and second -generation cephalosporins but are ineffective against third and fourth-generation. Beta lactamases are classified into four categories based on their amino acid sequences , by the Ambler classification . ESBLs also hydrolyze third and fourth-generation cephalosporins - cefotaxime , ceftazidime, ceftriaxone and cefepime .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Cilastatin is administered to prolong the action of which of the following drugs?
mcqs.explanation: Cilastatin is administered to prolong the action of imipenem . Imipenem is rapidly hydrolyzed by the enzyme renal dehydropeptidase . It is administered with cilastatin, a reversible inhibitor of dehydropeptidase to inhibit the breakdown and prolong the action of imipenem . Meropenem is not hydrolyzed by renal dehydropeptidase . Cilastatin administration is not necessary with meropenem .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with a complicated urinary tract infection is put on a newly approved combination of meropenem and a non-suicidal beta -lactamase inhibitor. Identify this drug.
mcqs.explanation: Vaborbactam is a recently approved non-suicidal beta -lactamase inhibitor. It is indicated in combination with meropenem for complicated urinary tract infections . Sulbactam, tazobactam and clavulanic acid are suicidal inhibitors of beta -lactamase enzyme. Suicidal inhibitors are irreversible inhibitors that can permanently inactivate the \035-lactamase through secondary chemical reactions in the enzyme active site .514

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes pyronaridine?
mcqs.explanation: Pyronaridine is an antimalarial agent . It is an erythrocyte schizonticide with high efficacy and mechanism of action similar to chloroquine. It is used in combination with artesunate .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs gets deposited in the retina?
mcqs.explanation: Chloroquine has a large volume of distribution and is deposited in the retina. Long-term use of chloroquine results in retinopathy . The classical finding is 'bull's-eye retinopathy '

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman presented with itching and malodorous discharge in the vagina . Whiff's test was positive and microscopy of the discharge is shown below . What is the drug of choice for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: 519 The clinical scenario, a positive Whiff test and clue cells on microscopy point towards a diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis. Metronidazole (oral or intravaginal ) or intravaginal clindamycin are considered the drugs of choice . The male partner should be treated in case of recurrent infections of bacterial vaginosis.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is best associated with lumefantrine ?
mcqs.explanation: Lumefantrine is an antimalarial agent . Lumefantrine is an orally active, high efficacy ; long-acting erythrocytic schizonticide related structurally and acts similar to halofantrine. Lumefantrine is used only in combination with artemether .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Suramin is indicated in which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Suramin is primarily indicated in the treatment of African trypanosomiasis. It is indicated only in the early stages of African trypanosomiasis because of its limited entry across the blood-brain barrier . It has no clinical utility in American trypanosomiasis. Suramin has in vitro activity against retroviral reverse transcriptase but is ineffective in HIV infection .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presents with watery diarrhea, fever and abdominal pain. Investigations reveal a WBC count of 16,000 cells /microL . The patient has been on treatment with ampicillin for a few days. Which of the following antibiotics is approved for use in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The scenario is suggestive of pseudomembranous colitis caused by Clostridium difficile and fidaxomicin is a macrocyclic antibiotic that is indicated as an alternative to vancomycin in severe and recurring Clostridium difficile infections . It acts by inhibiting protein synthesis through the blockade of RNA polymerase .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes tolnaftate ?
mcqs.explanation: Tolnaftate is a topical synthetic antifungal agent . It distorts the mycelial growth of yeast -like fungi and molds. It is effective in the treatment of dermatomycosis and tinea.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A class of antibiotics that is clinically indicated in combination with penicillins is inactivated if combined with penicillins in the same solution before administration. Identify this class of drugs.
mcqs.explanation: Aminoglycosides can be inactivated by various penicillins in vitro and thus should not be admixed in solution before administration.520 Aminoglycosides and penicillin combination is indicated in several infections and they should not be admixed in the same solution before administration.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antibiotics is not excreted through bile ?
mcqs.explanation: Gentamicin is not excreted through bile. It is an aminoglycoside antibiotic and aminoglycosides undergo minimum metabolism and are excreted almost entirely by the renal route. Erythromycin, cefoperazone , and rifampicin are excreted predominantly in bile .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the mechanism of action of oseltamivir and zanamivir ?
mcqs.explanation: Oseltamivir and zanamivir are neuraminidase inhibitors. They competitively and reversibly interact with the enzyme sites to inhibit viral neuraminidase activity. This interferes with the release of the progeny from infected host cells , halting the spread of infection . Early administration hastens the resolution of symptoms if given within 48 h of infection . Oseltamivir is given at a dose of 75 mg, BD for 5 days for the treatment of Influenza A and B. For prophylaxis , it is given at a dose of 75mg , OD and continued for the duration of exposure .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Rifampicin can be used as first-line therapy in which of the following patients ?
mcqs.explanation: Rifampicin is the first-line therapy and is included in the regimens for both tuberculosis and leprosy . Doxycycline combined with rifampicin is considered a first-line agent for brucellosis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs gets deposited in cornea?
mcqs.explanation: Chloroquine, an anti-malarial drug may get deposited in the cornea leading to corneal opacity . Ocular toxicity of chloroquine: • Short-term therapy - blurring of vision and diplopia , reversible on stoppage of drug. • Long-term use (high-dose ): • Keratopathy • Pigmentary retinopathy • Optic atrophy Hydroxychloroquine has lower ocular toxicity compared to chloroquine.521 Drugs causing corneal opacity : • Amiodarone • Phenothiazine • Indomethacin • Chloroquine Long-term treatment with these drugs can cause a whorl-like opacity in the corneal epithelium called cornea verticillata. It is also seen in Fabry's disease .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an inhibitor of RNA synthesis ?
mcqs.explanation: Rifampicin is an inhibitor of RNA synthesis . It binds to the beta subunit of DNA dependent RNA-polymerase (rpoB) to form a stable drug-enzyme complex . The binding suppresses the chain formation in RNA synthesis . Option A: 5-Fluorouracil inhibits thymidylate synthesis . Option C: Nitrofurantoin produces highly reactive intermediates that cause DNA damage Option D: Novobiocin is a potent inhibitor of bacterial DNA gyrase .522

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old woman presents with malodorous vaginal discharge and dysuria. The examination finding is shown below . What is the drug of choice for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and image showing strawberry vagina and cervix are suggestive of trichomoniasis. The drug of choice is metronidazole . It is given as a single dose of 2g. Both metronidazole and tinidazole are effective in the management of trichomonas vaginitis. Tinidazole has been reported to have fewer GI-related side effects and less resistance compared to metronidazole . However, it is much more expensive and is preferred in cases refractory to metronidazole .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Metronidazole is selectively active against anaerobic and microaerophilic organisms because :

options.a: Aerobes have oxygen gradient inside the cell which deactivates metronidazole moiety
options.b: Only anaerobes and microaerophilic organisms reduce it to generate reactive nitro radicals
options.c: Aerobes have efflux drug pumping mechanism for metronidazole
options.d: Metronidazole inserts pore in the cell membrane of anaerobes and microaerophilic bacteria

mcqs.explanation: Metronidazole is selectively active against anaerobic and microaerophilic organisms because only these organisms reduce it to generate reactive nitro radicals. They contain electron transport components that donate an electron to metronidazole . This results in the formation of a highly reactive nitro radical anion that targets DNA and kills the organism.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A child presents with diarrhea, weight loss, and abdominal pain. His mother reports stools to be greasy and foul -smelling . A wet preparation of the stool sample is shown below . What is first-line therapy for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario and the presence of cysts of Giardia lamblia in stool point towards a diagnosis of giardiasis, and tinidazole is the treatment of choice for this condition. Both metronidazole and tinidazole are considered first-line drugs however, tinidazole is considered superior in its efficacy in comparison to metronidazole . Drug dosage : • Metronidazole : 250- 500mg TID orally for 7 days • Tinidazole: 2g single dose orally The cyst of Giardia is small and oval, and is surrounded by a hyaline cyst wall. Its internal structure includes two pairs of nuclei grouped at one end. A young cyst contains one pair of nuclei . The axostyle lies diagonally , forming a dividing line within the cyst wall.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Metronidazole is least likely to be effective in the treatment of:
mcqs.explanation: Metronidazole is not effective in the management of pneumocystosis caused by Pneumocystis jirovecii. Co-trimoxazole is used in the management of this condition. Metronidazole is used in the following conditions: • Giardiasis • Trichomoniasis • Amoebiasis535 • Bacterial vaginosis • Anaerobic infections - bacteroides and clostridium. • Pseudomembranous colitis (alternative to vancomycin & fidaxomicin)

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 6-year-old boy presents with lower abdominal pain and diarrhea. The stool examination finding is shown below . Which of the following drugs cannot be used for the eradication of intestinal cysts in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows hematophagous trophozoite of Entamoeba histolytica and metronidazole is not an effective agent against cysts of amoeba in the colon. Metronidazole is used in the treatment of amoebiasis (amoebic colitis , amoebic liver abscess ). It is well absorbed from the small intestine and only a small amount of the unabsorbed drug reaches the colon, which is insufficient to kill the cysts . Hence , luminal agents like diloxanide furoate , nitazoxanide or iodoquinol are required for the eradication of cysts and trophozoites in the intestine .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is used in the treatment of a patient with asymptomatic intestinal amoebiasis?
mcqs.explanation: The drug of choice for the treatment of asymptomatic intestinal luminal amoebiasis due to E. histolytica is paromomycin. Paromomycin (aminosidine) is an aminoglycoside that has poor oral absorption and hence it acts only in the intestinal lumen as a luminal amebicide . It has no effect against extraintestinal organisms.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 21 -year-old male presented to the OPD complaining of blood-streaked stools . Sigmoidoscopy was done and it showed ulcers in the sigmoid. Biopsy was taken from this area and the histopathological image is given below . Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture and the histopathological image showing flask-shaped ulcers are suggestive of intestinal amoebiasis. The most appropriate treatment is intravenous metronidazole . The amoebic ulcer which is flask-shaped is the typical lesion seen in intestinal amoebiasis. The ulcers are multiple and are confined to the colon. Sometimes , in secondary intestinal lesions , the ulcers are numerous in the cecum , followed by the sigmoido -rectal region. Three classes of drugs are used in the treatment of amebiasis: • Luminal amoebicides - diloxanide furoate , iodoquinol, paromomycin, and tetracycline . They act in the intestinal lumen but not in tissues . • Tissue amoebicides - emetine and chloroquine. They are effective in systemic infection but less effective in the intestine . • Both luminal and tissue amebicides - Metronidazole , tinidazole and imidazole. They act on both sites and are the drug of choice for treating amebic colitis and amebic liver abscess .536

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presents with sudden onset fever with chills and malaise. On examination splenomegaly was present . Bone marrow picture is shown in the image. Which of the following drugs is not used in the treatment of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and the bone marrow picture showing macrophages infected with intracellular Leishman-Donovan bodies point towards a diagnosis of visceral leishmaniasis. Hydroxychloroquine is not indicated in the treatment of this condition. The drugs effective in visceral leishmaniasis are: • Liposomal amphotericin B (preferred ) • Sodium stibogluconate (not in India) • Miltefosine • Paromomycin • Pentamidine (rarely used ) Hydroxychloroquine is an antimalarial agent and is also used in the treatment of dermatological conditions like: • Cutaneous lupus erythematosus • Cutaneous dermatomyositis • Polymorphous light eruption • Porphyria cutanea tarda • Sarcoidosis

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old woman presents with the finding as shown in the image. She gives history of travel to South America and was bitten by a reduvid bug. Which of the following is the drug of choice for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The scenario and the image showing Roma \361a sign point towards a diagnosis of Chagas disease (American trypanosomiasis) and the drug of choice in this condition is benznidazole. American trypanosomiasis is caused by Trypanosoma cruzi and can be managed by either benznidazole or nifurtimox. Due to its favorable safety profile , benznidazole is considered the drug of choice . Roma \361a sign is the unilateral painless periorbital swelling associated with the acute stage of Chagas disease . Albendazole and metronidazole are not indicated for American trypanosomiasis. Albendazole is used in infections with Ascaris lumbricoides , Trichuris trichiura and hookworms. Metronidazole is used in the treatment of trichomoniasis and amebiasis.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presents in the late stage of West African sleeping sickness. What is the drug of choice in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Nifurtimox in combination with eflornithine is the drug of choice for late -stage West African sleeping sickness. It is caused by Trypanosoma brucei gambiense . Nifurtimox alone is indicated in American trypanosomiasis.537 Melarsoprol is the drug of choice for late -stage East African (Rhodesian) trypanosomiasis. It is not indicated in combination with nifurtimox.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs can be used as first-line treatment in patients with early-stage of East African trypanosomiasis?
mcqs.explanation: Suramin is the first-line therapy for early-stage East African trypanosomiasis caused by Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense . It is also active against Trypanosoma brucei gambiense but only indicated as a second -line agent when pentamidine fails or is contraindicated . Melarsoprol is the only effective drug available for the treatment of the late encephalopathic stage of East African sleeping sickness. It is caused by Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense . Melarsoprol is effective in earlier stages also but is avoided because of its toxicity .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The microscopy of fecal sample of a patient showed presence of Ascaris lumbricoides eggs . This condition can most effectively be treated with which of the following drugs?
mcqs.explanation: Roundworm infestation is most effectively treated with albendazole . It is considered as the drug of choice for the treatment of roundworm (Ascaris lumbricoides ) infestation . Albendazole is considered as the drug of choice for treatment of infestation by: • Whipworm - Trichuris trichura causing trichuriasis • Hookworm - Ancylostoma duodenale • Roundworm - Ascaris lumbricoides • Dog tapeworm - Echinococcus granulosus causing hydatid disease Albendazole is administered as a single oral 400 -mg dose to adults and children more than 2 years of age . Safety is not established for children less than 2 years. However, according to WHO, if the benefit outweighs the risk , albendazole at 200 mg can be given to children between the ages of 1-2years.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the primary mechanism of action of benzimidazole?
mcqs.explanation: The primary mechanism of action of benzimidazoles is by inhibition of microtubule polymerization. Benzimidazoles bind to beta -tubulin and cause inhibition of microtubule polymerization. Drugs belonging to the benzimidazole group are: • Albendazole • Mebendazole • Triclabendazole • Thiabendazole.538 Mechanisms of action: • Inhibition of mitochondrial fumarate reductase • Reduced glucose transport • Uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A young man working at a dairy farm presents with fever and abdominal pain. Examination of his stool samples revealed the finding shown in the image. Which of the following benzimidazoles is indicated in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given image showing operculated egg (egg having a lid-like structure on its end) is suggestive of Fasciola hepatica and the benzimidazole indicated for infection with this organism is triclabendazole .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The MRI of a patient who presented with new-onset seizures is shown below . What is the drug of choice ?
mcqs.explanation: The MRI findings (multiple cysticerci within the brain ) are suggestive of neurocysticercosis and albendazole is the drug of choice in this condition. Glucocorticoid therapy is usually begun before initiating albendazole and continued for several days after the commencement of therapy. It reduces the inflammatory reaction to the dead and dying cysticerci of Taenia solium. Note : Even though Albendazole and Praziquantel are used as a combination, the single best answer choice to this question is Albendazole.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old man hospitalized with a hydatid cyst refused to undergo surgical removal of the cyst. He was treated with high dose albendazole for 3 months. This patient should be monitored for toxicity to the :
mcqs.explanation: The patient described above should be monitored for toxicity to the liver. Liver dysfunction is one of the common adverse effects of albendazole therapy and liver function tests should be routinely conducted when long-term therapy is initiated . Long-term albendazole therapy is also associated with bone marrow toxicity . Therefore, blood counts should also be regularly monitored.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the drug of choice in patients with onchocerciasis?
mcqs.explanation: Ivermectin is the drug of choice for onchocerciasis caused by Oncocerca volvulus in adults and children aged more than 5 years. Ivermectin is the drug of choice for: • Strongyloidiasis • Onchocerciasis539 It is associated with Mazzotti reaction (fever, pruritic rash, lymphadenopathy ) as a side effect when given for filariasis due to immune system activation by the dying parasite. This reaction is also seen with the use of diethylcarbamazine .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presents with itchy, serpiginous eruptions as shown in the image. He says that these lesions advance rapidly to different sites . What is the primary mechanism of action of the drug preferred for this disease ?

options.a: Activation of glutamate gated chloride channels
options.b: Inhibition of glutamate gated chloride channels

mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario and the image showing larva currens, points towards a diagnosis of strongyloidiasis , and the drug of choice in this condition is ivermectin. The mechanism of action of ivermectin primarily involves activation of glutamate -gated chloride channels found only in invertebrates. Ivermectin activates glutamate -activated chloride channels in the nerves and muscles of nematode and results in the influx of chloride into the cell . This causes hyperpolarization of cells and results in paralysis of nematodes .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the first-line treatment for a patient presenting with the finding shown below ?
mcqs.explanation: The above image shows cutaneous larva migrans. Ivermectin is the first-line drug for the treatment of cutaneous larva migrans. The first-line drugs used in cutaneous larva migrans include : • Ivermectin - 200 �Mg/kg orally single dose • Albendazole - 400mg orally for 3 days

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 17-year-old boy presents with painless hematuria. He has a history of travel to Kenya . Urine microscopy revealed the finding shown below . What is the drug of choice in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario and the image showing the egg of Schistosoma hematobium (egg with terminal spine ), point towards the diagnosis of schistosomiasis . Praziquantel is the drug of choice for schistosomiasis caused by all Schistosoma species that can infect humans. A single oral dose of 40 mg/kg or three doses of 20 mg/kg each, given 4–6 h apart, generally produce cure rates of 70%–95% and consistently high reductions (>85%) in egg counts.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs causes flaccid paralysis of Ascaris lumbricoides ?
mcqs.explanation: Piperazine causes flaccid paralysis of Ascaris lumbricoides . It acts as a GABA receptor agonist and increases chloride ion conductance across the Ascaris muscle membrane. This results in hyperpolarisation and reduced excitability , which leads to muscle relaxation and flaccid paralysis. Metrifonate , levamisole and tribendimidine are anthelminthic drugs that cause spastic paralysis.540

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Diethylcarbamazine is used for the treatment of:
mcqs.explanation: Diethylcarbamazine (DEC) is used for the control and treatment of lymphatic filariasis caused by W. bancrofti, B. malayi and B. timori. Other indications for the use of DEC are: • Loiasis • Tropical pulmonary eosinophilia

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presents with fever, fatigue , and malaise. Investigations reveal anemia and thrombocytopenia . Thin blood smear is shown below . What is the recommended therapy for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and the microscopic image showing tetrads or Maltese cross, point towards a diagnosis of babesiosis and the recommended therapy for this condition is azithromycin plus atovaquone. Babesiosis is a zoonotic infection that resembles malaria . It presents with febrile illness , hemolysis and hemoglobinuria. For mild or moderate disease : Azithromycin plus atovaquone. For severe disease : • Recommended regimen - azithromycin plus atovaquone. • Alternative regimen - clindamycin plus quinine. Severe babesiosis typically occurs in patients with one or more of the following characteristics: age >50 years, neonatal prematurity , asplenia /hyposplenism , HIV /AIDS, malignancy, and immunosuppressive therapy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presented with fever and cervical lymphadenopathy . Investigations revealed IgM toxoplasma antibodies . Which of the following agents is most effective in treating this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Pyrimethamine is the most effective agent against toxoplasmosis and is present in most of the regimens . It is combined with sulfadiazine or clindamycin for toxoplasmosis . Trimethoprim plus sulfamethoxazole (cotrimoxazole) is an alternative.541

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a polyene antifungal agent ?
mcqs.explanation: Amphotericin B is a polyene antifungal. Other polyene antifungals are: • Amphotericin B551 • Nystatin • Natamycin • Hamycin Amphotericin B is the least toxic among polyenes and is used systemically for fungal infections . Nystatin and hamycin have high systemic toxicity and are used only for local and topical actions.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the site of action of amphotericin B in fungi?
mcqs.explanation: The site of action of amphotericin B in fungi is the cell membrane. Amphotericin B binds to the ergosterol in the cell membrane of fungi and forms pores or channels. They increase the permeability of the membrane to ions and cause leakage of cytosolic molecules . This leads to a loss of integrity of the cell membrane and causes fungicidal effects . Recent evidence suggests that the amphotericin B sequesters ergosterol from lipid layers, much like a sponge , resulting in fungal cell death .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which formulation of amphotericin B has the highest risk of nephrotoxicity ?
mcqs.explanation: Nephrotoxicity risk is highest with conventional amphotericin B. Conventional amphotericin B (C-AMB) is not a lipid -based formulation of amphotericin B. Amphotericin B is insoluble in water, hence C-AMB is formulated by complexing with bile salt deoxycholate to make it suitable for intravenous infusion. Nephrotoxicity risk with amphotericin B formulations in decreasing order: • C-AMB > Amphotericin B lipid complex (ABLC) > Liposomal amphotericin B (L -AMB) • All lipid formulations of amphotericin B (ABLC , L-AMB, ABCD) are less nephrotoxic than conventional amphotericin B Note : Amphotericin B colloidal dispersion (ABCD) has not been compared with other lipid -based formulations

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A diabetic patient presents with periorbital swelling as shown below . She complains of significant visual impairment and a fungal etiology is suspected . What is the most appropriate drug for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of invasive mucormycosis in the form of orbital cellulitis . Intravenous administration of amphotericin B is the treatment of choice for invasive mucormycosis. Mucormycosis is an opportunistic infection seen in patients with diabetes mellitus , leukaemia, lymphoma and other immunocompromised states . The most prevalent species is Rhizopus Oryza.552

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient diagnosed with mucormycosis is being treated with intravenous amphotericin B. Following administration of the drug, he starts experiencing chills, fever and dyspnea . These symptoms occur most frequently with which formulation?
mcqs.explanation: Development of fever and chills following intravenous administration is suggestive of infusion-related reactions which occur most frequently with amphotericin B colloidal dispersions . Infusion-related adverse events are commonly seen with amphotericin B and it has been nicknamed 'shake and bake syndrome' due to the associated chills and fever. Decreasing order of frequency of infusion-related reactions with amphotericin B formulations: Amphotericin B colloidal dispersions (ABCD) > conventional amphotericin B (C-AMB) > amphotericin B lipid complex (ABLC ) > liposomal amphotericin B (L -AMB).

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An immunocompromised patient with invasive mucormycosis is administered intravenous amphotericin B. Which frequently associated electrolyte disturbance would you be concerned about?
mcqs.explanation: Amphotericin B causes hypokalemia and hence potassium levels should be monitored in this patient. Amphotericin B can cause renal tubular acidosis and renal wasting of K+ and Mg2+ leading to hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia during and several weeks after therapy . Potassium supplements are required in around one-third of patients on prolonged amphotericin B therapy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An HIV -positive patient presents with headache and nuchal stiffness . The CD4 count is 90 and CSF sample with India-ink staining shows the presence of encapsulated yeast cells. Which of the following is the treatment of choice for the patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the presence of encapsulated yeast cells in CSF with India ink staining are suggestive of cryptococcal meningitis. Amphotericin B plus flucytosine is the treatment of choice for this patient . Cryptococcal meningitis is an AIDS-defining opportunistic fungal CNS infection that generally occurs in untreated patients , with CD4+ T cell counts <100/�ML. In cryptococcal meningitis, amphotericin B combined with flucytosine is the current gold standard treatment in immunocompromised patients , especially in AIDS patients . In non-immunocompetent patients , the role of additional flucytosine along with amphotericin B is less clear. Oral fluconazole is used for consolidation and maintenance therapy after two weeks of induction therapy with amphotericin B.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Identify the wrongly matched pair of antifungals with its mechanism of action:

options.b: Flucytosine : Inhibits microtubule synthesis and thus hinders mitosis

mcqs.explanation: Flucytosine acts by inhibition of fungal DNA synthesis . It is a pyrimidine antimetabolite . After uptake into fungal cells , fungal cytosine deaminase activates it to 5-fluorouracil, which is an anticancer drug. This is further converted into metabolites that inhibit thymidylate synthase which is necessary for DNA synthesis . Thus fungal DNA synthesis is inhibited . Mammalian cells are spared as they lack cytosine deaminase enzyme.553 Flucytosine has clinically useful activity against (3C): • Cryptococcus • Candida species • Agents causing chromoblastomycosis

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A washerman presents with itchy, annular scaly plaques in the groin. He is prescribed with an antifungal that acts by interfering with mitosis. Identify the drug.
mcqs.explanation: Itchy annular plaques in the groin are suggestive of tinea cruris and the drug most likely given was griseofulvin which acts by interfering with fungal mitosis. Microtubule function is necessary for the formation of the mitotic spindle during cell division. Griseofulvin inhibits microtubule function and thereby disrupts mitotic spindle formation and inhibits cell division. Tinea cruris is a dermatophytosis involving the groin and is also known as jock itch or dhobi's itch.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: To which of the following patients will you not prescribe griseofulvin?

options.a: A middle aged man with tinea capitis

mcqs.explanation: Griseofulvin is not useful in the treatment of tinea versicolor. It is treated with topical azoles. Tinea capitis , tinea cruris and tinea pedis are dermatophytoses . Griseofulvin is indicated only for dermatophytoses caused by species of Microsporum, Epidermophyton , and Trichophyton. It is considered the drug of choice for tinea capitis in children. It is reserved only for large topical tinea infections when topical therapy is inadequate . Tinea versicolor is not a dermatophytosis. It is a superficial mycosis caused by lipophilic yeast Malassezia.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following can cause contraceptive failure in a lady on oral contraceptive pills ?
mcqs.explanation: Griseofulvin is a cytochrome enzyme inducer and can cause contraceptive failure when taken with oral contraceptive pills . It induces hepatic CYP enzymes and can increase the metabolism of drugs. Warfarin metabolism is increased and the dose has to be adjusted according to the change in response . Estrogen metabolism is also increased thereby reducing the efficacy of low-dose estrogen -based oral contraceptives . Note : Ketoconazole is a cytochrome enzyme inhibitor.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Fungal cell wall synthesis is altered by which of the following drugs?
mcqs.explanation: 554 Fungal cell wall synthesis is altered by caspofungin . 1,3-\035-D glucan is an essential component of the fungal cell wall which maintains cell integrity . Echinocandin group of antifungals like caspofungin , anidulafungin, and micafungin acts by inhibiting the synthesis of 1,3-\035-D-glucan and thereby weakens the fungal cell wall and increases the osmotic susceptibility . Echinocandins are fungicidal against Candida species . They show fungistatic activity against Aspergillus species .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the mechanism of triazoles?

options.a: Interferes with DNA and RNA synthesis
options.d: Inhibits epoxidation of squalene in fungi

mcqs.explanation: Triazoles act by inhibition of ergosterol synthesis . The azole group inhibits the fungal cytochrome P450 enzyme called 14-�o -sterol demethylase and results in an impairment of conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol . This results in the depletion of membrane ergosterol . Azole antifungals are of two types : • Imidazoles - clotrimazole, ketoconazole, luliconazole • Triazoles - itraconazole, fluconazole , voriconazole, posaconazole and isavuconazole

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient was diagnosed with coccidioidal meningitis. What is the drug of choice for the condition?
mcqs.explanation: Fluconazole is the drug of choice for coccidioidal meningitis caused by Coccidioides immitis because of better CSF penetration . Itraconazole is also effective in this condition but it is not the drug of choice . Amphotericin B is indicated in patients in whom triazoles have failed . Note : Amphotericin B is the drug of choice for initial treatment of cryptococcal meningitis caused by Cryptococcus neoformans and fluconazole is used for maintenance therapy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A middle aged man presents with the condition shown in the image. Which of the following drugs can cause this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The image above depicts gynecomastia and can be caused by ketoconazole due to its antiandrogenic action. Ketoconazole use results in various antiandrogenic effects . It decreases testosterone production and displaces testosterone from protein binding sites in plasma. It also decreases hydrocortisone production , especially at higher doses . Adverse effects that can occur are gynecomastia , loss of hair, libido, and oligozoospermia . Fluconazole , itraconazole and voriconazole do not have antiandrogenic action.555

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an indication for ketoconazole use ?
mcqs.explanation: Ketoconazole is not indicated for use in Addison's disease . It is a potent nonselective inhibitor of adrenal and gonadal steroidogenesis by inhibiting 17 �o -hydroxylase enzymes which are involved in steroid hormone synthesis and it can hence worsen Addison's disease . However, this property also makes it useful in the treatment of Cushing's syndrome. Azoles interfere with leishmanial cell membrane biosynthesis and are therefore used in dermal leishmaniasis and kala-azar .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: While administering which of the following drugs will you counsel patients regarding transient visual and auditory hallucinations?
mcqs.explanation: Transient visual or auditory hallucinations are commonly seen with the use of intravenous voriconazole. These usually occur at night. Other side effects of voriconazole are: • Hepatotoxicity • Prolonged QTc interval and increased risk of torsades de pointes • Anaphylactoid reaction when given intravenously

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Omeprazole dose is reduced when given along with voriconazole because of what action of the latter drug?
mcqs.explanation: Voriconazole is a strong inhibitor and substrate of CYP2C19 . Concomitant omeprazole administration can result in increased omeprazole levels because of inhibition of metabolism . In a patient on omeprazole 40 mg/day, the dose of omeprazole should be reduced to half when voriconazole is initiated . Additionally , higher levels of omeprazole can also interfere in voriconazole metabolism as omeprazole also inhibits CYP2C19 .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In a patient with athlete 's foot, which keratolytic ointment would you prescribe to enhance treatment outcome ?
mcqs.explanation: Salicylic acid is a keratolytic agent that can be prescribed to enhance the treatment outcome in patients with athlete 's foot (i.e. tinea pedis ). Salicylic acid accelerates the desquamation of the stratum corneum. It is used in combination with a fungistatic drug called benzoic acid because eradication of infection is possible only if the infected stratum corneum is shed . This combination is called Whitfield 's ointment and is used in the treatment of tinea pedis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presented with multiple annular itchy skin lesions with central clearing over his back. You may prescribe any of the following except ?
mcqs.explanation: 556 Pruritic annular skin lesions with central clearing are suggestive of dermatophytosis for which amphotericin B must not be prescribed. Azoles, terbinafine, and griseofulvin are indicated for the treatment of dermatophytosis . Dermatophytes are inhibited by amphotericin B but drug concentrations attained in the skin are very low and ineffective for the treatment of dermatophytosis . The uses of amphotericin B are: • Treatment of choice in invasive mucormycosis • Candida albicans infection • Cryptococcus neoformans infection • Endemic mycosis

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is not used to treat candida infections ?
mcqs.explanation: Griseofulvin is not used to treat candida infection . It is active against most dermatophytes but not against candida and other fungi causing deep mycosis. Ketoconazole , nystatin, and amphotericin B are used in the treatment of candida infections .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about antifungal drugs?

options.a: Amphotericin B is more effective parenterally
options.c: Ciclopirox olamine is effective in systemic mycoses
options.d: Fluconazole is effective orally as well as intravenously

mcqs.explanation: Ciclopirox olamine is a topical antifungal agent and is not effective in systemic mycoses . Ciclopirox olamine is a broad spectrum fungicidal agent that acts by chelating trivalent metal ions which leads to inhibition of the metal-dependent enzyme that degrades free radicals. It is available as a nail lacquer formulation in the treatment of onychomycosis . Option A: Amphotericin B is more effective parenterally for systemic mycoses . However, local or topical administration of amphotericin B drops is used in mycotic corneal ulcers . Option B: The absorption of griseofulvin is less when administered orally but microfining the drug particles increases the absorption. Option D: Fluconazole can be administered orally as well as intravenously.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Topical antifungal agents have no role in the treatment of patients with which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Topical antifungal agents have no role in the treatment of subcutaneous mycoses like chromoblastomycosis . Itraconazole is the first-line antifungal indicated in this condition. Topical antifungal agents are used in the treatment of: • Dermatophytosis • Candidiasis557 • Piedra • Tinea versicolor • Tinea nigra • Fungal keratitis

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antifungal drugs are used topically ?
mcqs.explanation: Tolnaftate, butenafine , naftifine, and clotrimazole are used topically . Allylamine antifungals available for topical application are: • Terbinafine • Naftifine • Butenafine Azoles that are used topically are: • Clotrimazole • Miconazole • Econazole Tolnaftate is a topical synthetic antifungal agent . It distorts the mycelial growth of yeast -like fungi and molds. It is effective in the treatment of dermatomycosis and tinea.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 48-year-old woman presented with yellowish discolouration of toenails . The discolouration spread proximally as a streak in the nail and later, the entire nail separated from the nailbed . What is the mechanism of action of the drug of choice for her?

options.b: Binding to ergosterol and altering membrane functions
options.c: Formation of pore in cell membrane

mcqs.explanation: The clinical features are suggestive of tinea unguium or onychomycosis . The drug of choice is oral terbinafine which acts by inhibition of ergosterol synthesis . Terbinafine acts as a non-competitive inhibitor of squalene epoxidase , an early step enzyme in the synthesis of fungal ergosterol . This results in the accumulation of sterol squalene which is toxic to the organism. The efficacy of terbinafine in onychomycosis is improved when combined with amorolfine 5% nail lacquer.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A farmer presented with complaints of redness and excessive watering from the right eye . Slit-lamp examination reveals the following finding. Microscopy of the corneal ulcer scraping shows branched septate hyphae . Which of the following drugs can be used in the treatment of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Slit-lamp examination showing a corneal ulcer with satellite lesions and a thick hypopyon are suggestive of mycotic keratitis (fungal corneal ulcer) while branched septate hyphae are seen with Aspergillus and Fusarium. Natamycin 5% suspension is the drug of choice in this condition. Treatment of fungal corneal ulcer:558 • Topical antifungals : Aspergillus and Fusarium infections are treated with natamycin, amphotericin B and voriconazole while Candida infections are treated with nystatin. • Systemic antifungals : Ketoconazole or voriconazole may be needed if there is a severe corneal ulcer, perforated ulcer, or suspicion of endophthalmitis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Voriconazole is not effective against which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Voriconazole is not effective against mucormycosis. Mucormycosis is treated by amphotericin B. Posaconazole can also be used . However, other azoles are not effective against this fungus . Voriconazole is the drug of choice for the treatment of aspergillosis . It can also be used for Candida species (including glabrata and krusei), Scedosporium and Fusarium.559

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old lady presents with pulmonary TB is started on anti-tubercular therapy . What is the rationale for administering multi-drug therapy to her?

options.d: To prevent toxin release from the organism

mcqs.explanation: The reason for administering multi-drug therapy in tuberculosis is to prevent the development of resistance . Resistance to individual drugs in Mycobacterium tuberculosis occurs by spontaneous point mutations that occur at a low but predictable rate (10-7 to 10 -10 ). Development of this drug resistance is almost invariably the result of monotherapy, i.e., the failure of the health care provider to prescribe at least 2 drugs to which the tubercle bacilli are susceptible . Hence , multi-drug therapy is recommended for the treatment of tuberculosis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which is the most effective drug against extracellular mycobacteria?
mcqs.explanation: The most effective drug against extracellular mycobacteria is Rifampicin.567 Option A: Isoniazid and Rifampicin act against both intracellular and extracellular mycobacterium . But, Rifampicin inhibits the extracellular mycobacteria at much lower drug concentrations than isoniazid. Option B: Pyrazinamide acts only against intracellular mycobacterium . Option C: Ethambutol acts against only extracellular mycobacteria but is not as effective as rifampicin. It is a bacteriostatic drug. Fast-multiplying bacteria are highly susceptible to its action. Note : Streptomycin is primarily active against only the extracellular tubercle bacilli as its penetration into the cells is very poor.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient was diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis and was started on first-line antitubercular drugs. Which of the following drug acts by inhibiting the synthesis of the marked layer shown in the image?
mcqs.explanation: Isoniazid is the first-line antitubercular drug that acts by inhibiting the synthesis of mycolic acid. Isoniazid is a first-line bactericidal drug that is used for the treatment of tuberculosis . This drug enters bacilli by passive diffusion . It then gets activated to its toxic form by the enzyme catalase -peroxidase (the enzyme encoded by the Kat gene ). Normally, InhA and KasA are involved in the synthesis of mycolic acid. Upon activation, the reactive metabolite of isoniazid forms complexes with NAD that inhibit InhA and KasA. Hence , isoniazid inhibits the production of mycolic acid. The reactive isoniazid metabolite also forms complexes with NADP. This complex inhibits mycobacterial dihydrofolate reductase which results in the interruption of DNA synthesis . Side effects of isoniazid include : • Peripheral neuritis due to interference with the production of active coenzyme pyridoxal phosphate from pyridoxine. Therefore, pyridoxine 10mg/day (vitamin B6) is given prophylactically along with isoniazid to prevent neurotoxicity . • Hepatitis - isoniazid must be stopped at the first sign of hepatotoxicity . • Rashes • Anaemia • Arthralgia Toxicity of isoniazid results in metabolic acidosis, seizures , and coma. Other options : Option B: Rifampin acts by binding to DNA-dependent RNA polymerase to form a stable drug-enzyme complex . This complex suppresses RNA synthesis . Side effects of rifampin are hepatitis , flu-like illness , orange-red colored urine, and body secretions . Option C: Pyrazinamide is a prodrug, it is converted into an active metabolite pyrazinoic acid which makes the intracellular environment acidic and collapses the transmembrane proton motive force, thereby killing the bacteria . Side effects include hyperuricemia and hepatotoxicity . Option D: Ethambutol inhibits arabinose transferase III , thereby decreasing arabinogalactan biosynthesis . This results in disruption in mycobacterial cell wall synthesis . Optic neuritis is an568 important side effect of ethambutol . It results in decreased visual acuity and loss of red-green discrimination.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A study was conducted to genotype NAT2 gene polymorphisms in patients receiving ATT . Among the 300 patients genotyped , 200 were slow acetylators (group A), 70 were intermediate (group B) and 30 were fast acetylators (group C). Patients in group A are prone to develop which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Isoniazid, a key agent in the ATT , is metabolized primarily through N-acetylation by the genetically polymorphic N-acetyltransferase -2 (NAT2 ) enzyme. Slow acetylators (group A) of isoniazid are prone to develop peripheral neuropathy . The rate of metabolism of isoniazid is determined by the genetic polymorphism of NAT2 enzyme and classified broadly into two groups - slow and fast acetylators . In slow acetylators , the drug accumulates due to slow metabolism resulting in an increased risk of side effects , and hence they should undergo periodic monitoring. Peripheral neuropathy is a more frequent side effect of INH when compared to hepatotoxicity . Fast acetylators metabolize the drug rapidly and show less response to standard doses and the therapy may be less effective .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Line probe assay done on sputum sample of a patient with TB revealed over-expression of InhA gene . This can lead to cross-resistance of isoniazid with which of the following drugs?
mcqs.explanation: Over-expression of the gene for InhA leads to cross-resistance of isoniazid (INH) with ethionamide.Mechanisms of INH resistan ce Mutation of KatG most common mechanismco nfers a high level of resistanc e Overexpression of InhA confers alow level of resistan cecross -resistance with ethio namide Overexpression of ahpC increases the bacterial surviv al under oxidative stress Induction of efflux pumps cross-resistance with ethamb utol

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 4-month-old boy was brought to the ER with recurrent seizures . His mother informs you that he is receiving isoniazid prophylaxis as she was diagnosed with TB during pregnancy. ABG revealed a high anion gap metabolic acidosis. What would be the mainstay of treatment ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of isoniazid overdose for which the mainstay of treatment is intravenous pyridoxine. Isoniazid overdose results in decreased pyridoxine availability to neurons. This decreases the levels of GABA, which in turn lowers the seizure threshold . Benzodiazepines can be used to569 control seizures . Prolonged treatment with isoniazid leads to the deficiency of pyridoxine which can lead to peripheral neuropathy and other neurological manifestations like ataxia, paresthesia , and numbness. Clinical triad of isoniazid overdose: • Seizures refractory to treatment with phenytoin and barbiturates • High anion gap metabolic acidosis (HAGMA) resistant to treatment with sodium bicarbonate • Coma

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man undergoing treatment for TB visits your OPD for follow -up. His wife states that recently he is forgetting the names of his colleagues and neighbors, but later recollects them correctly. Which drug is implicated to cause this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Isoniazid is the antitubercular drug that is implicated in the causation of transient memory loss. Neurological toxicities like peripheral neuropathy , optic neuritis, and seizures can occur with isoniazid therapy. It is also associated with abnormalities like: • Euphoria • Transient memory loss • Separation of ideas and reality • Loss of self -control • Florid psychosis Pyridoxine therapy can prevent and reverse most of the neurological toxicity and mental abnormalities.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 66-year-old woman, on anti-tubercular therapy , presented with pain in the right hand and shoulder for the past 1 month. On physical examination, her wrist was swollen and her shoulder was extremely painful with a limited range of motion. Which drug is most likely associated with this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical presentation is suggestive of shoulder -hand syndrome which is associated with the use of isoniazid. This syndrome is characterized by painful arthropathy in the upper extremity joints. It can also present as generalized arthropathy. Other drugs that can cause shoulder -hand syndrome are phenobarbitone and phenytoin .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Before initiating treatment for a sputum -positive TB patient , the physician orders for Cartridge Based Nucleic Acid Amplification Test in order to test for drug resistance . Which anti-tubercular drug resistance is he checking for?
mcqs.explanation: The Cartridge Based-Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (CBNAAT) is a molecular test for tuberculosis that detects the DNA of tubercle bacilli within 2 hours and mutations in the rpoB gene responsible for rifampicin resistance .570

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following rifamycin drugs would you advise a patient to take on an empty stomach?
mcqs.explanation: Rifampicin should be advised to be taken on an empty stomach because food decreases its absorption. Rifabutin absorption is not altered by food. Rifapentine absorption is enhanced by fatty food and hence it is recommended to be taken with food.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An HIV -positive patient on ART with zidovudine, lamivudine, and indinavir develops pulmonary tuberculosis . Which of the following anti-tubercular drugs should be avoided in him?
mcqs.explanation: Rifampicin should be avoided as it is a potent inducer of CYP enzymes including CYPs 1A2 , 3A4, 2C9, and 2C19 , which in turn can induce the metabolism of indinavir and results in therapeutic failure of ART . Rifabutin causes the least induction of cytochrome enzymes and is therefore preferred in HIV patients who are on protease inhibitors/NNRTIs . Cytochrome enzyme-inducing potency of rifamycins is: rifampicin > rifapentine > rifabutin. mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following rifamycins is not used for mycobacterial infections ?
mcqs.explanation: Rifaximin is not used for mycobacterial infections . It is a synthetic rifamycin that is poorly absorbed from the GIT and is indicated in the management of GI conditions like: • Traveler 's diarrhea • Irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea • Hepatic encephalopathy Rifamycins indicated in mycobacterial infections are rifampicin, rifapentine , and rifabutin.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A Gene Xpert test was conducted on the sputum sample of a patient with suspected TB . The results were positive and showed resistance to rifampicin. What is the primary mechanism of resistance against this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Rifampicin resistance is primarily due to alteration in the target enzyme.571 Rifampicin acts by binding to the \035 subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (rpoB) and inhibits chain formation in RNA synthesis . Rifampicin is a potent inducer of cytochrome enzymes CYP3A4, CYP1A2 , CYP2C9, and CYP2C19 . Alteration of the target enzyme (rpoB) by a mutation in the gene coding for rpoB is the primary mechanism of resistance to rifampicin. Gene Xpert identifies mutations in the rpoB gene to detect rifampicin resistance . Efflux pump induction has also been demonstrated as a mechanism of rifampicin resistance .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following conditions can rifampicin be used ?
mcqs.explanation: Besides its anti-tubercular action, rifampicin also has certain non-tubercular uses which include : • Prophylaxis of meningococcal and H. influenzae meningitis • Treatment of MRSA, diphtheroid , and legionella infections • Eradication of staphylococcal nasal carrier state in patients with chronic furunculosis • A combination of doxycycline and rifampicin is used as the first-line therapy for brucellosis • A part of the WHO regimen for standard therapy of both paucibacillary and multibacillary leprosy Rifampicin is not used in the treatment of Nocardia species . Cotrimoxazole is considered the drug of choice for pleuropulmonary nocardiosis.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You are prescribing first-line anti-tubercular therapy to a patient newly diagnosed with TB . Which of the following is incorrect about his therapy ?

options.a: Red green color impairment is an early sign of ethambutol induced optic neuritis
options.c: Flu-like syndrome is usually seen if rifampicin is taken on a daily basis
options.d: Hyperuricemia is a recognised side effect of pyrazinamide

mcqs.explanation: Flu-like syndrome is usually seen when rifampicin is administered less than twice weekly (high dose ) and it is uncommon when administered daily (lower dose ). Flu-like syndrome, characterized by fevers, chills, malaise, and arthralgia is a known dose -dependent adverse effect of rifampicin therapy and tends to occur late into the patient 's treatment course . It resolves with either discontinuation of rifampin or switching to a daily-dose regimen. It can often be confused with occult infections or treatment failure. Options A and B: Red-green colour impairment is one of the early signs of ethambutol -induced optic neuritis. Ethambutol is primarily excreted unchanged by kidneys and accumulation occurs in renal failure. Ethambutol does not undergo hepatic metabolism and can be safely prescribed for the treatment of TB in patients with hepatitis . Option D: Pyrazinamide interferes with urate excretion and can result in hyperuricemia .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A young woman undergoing treatment for tuberculosis visits your OPD for a routine checkup . She informs you that recently she has noticed an orange-colored discoloration of her contact lenses . Which of the following drugs is most likely to be responsible for this?
mcqs.explanation: Rifampicin is the drug most likely to cause orange-colored discoloration of contact lenses in this case.572 Drugs like rifampicin and rifabutin are known to cause reddish -orange discoloration of the skin, urine, feces , saliva, sweat , and tears (which can stain the patient 's contact lenses ).

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You are planning to start treatment in a middle -aged man diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis . He has a history of chronic kidney disease and his current creatinine clearance is 25 mL /min. Which of the following drugs is least likely to require dose modification?
mcqs.explanation: Rifampicin is the least likely drug to require dose modification in renal failure patients as it is metabolized in the liver and primarily excreted in bile . In patients with renal failure, the half-life of isoniazid will be prolonged , but its adverse effects are not significantly increased . Hence dose modification is not usually done for isoniazid in clinical practice as a reduction in dose may render the regimen ineffective and increase the chances of resistance . Ethambutol and streptomycin are primarily excreted unchanged through the renal system and need dose modification in renal failure.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Pseudojaundice is an adverse effect of which of the following drugs?
mcqs.explanation: Pseudojaundice is an adverse effect of rifabutin. It resolves on discontinuation of the drug. Unique adverse effects of rifabutin are: • Polymyalgia/arthralgia • Pseudojaundice • Anterior uveitis

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Mycobacterium tuberculosis nicotinamidase is involved in the activation of which of the following antitubercular drug?
mcqs.explanation: Mycobacterium tuberculosis nicotinamidase is involved in the activation of pyrazinamide. Nicotinamidase which is produced by M. tuberculosis is also called pyrazinamidase. It is encoded by the pncA gene and its mutations are associated with pyrazinamide resistance . It converts pyrazinamide to active pyrazinoic acid. Pyrazinoic acid has the following actions: • Inhibition of fatty acid synthetase type 1 leads to interference in mycolic acid synthesis • Reduction of intracellular pH • Disruption of membrane transport

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 47-year-old man on treatment for TB presents with complaints of severe pain and swelling in his left great toe since today morning, as shown in the image below . Which of the following drugs is most likely to cause this?
mcqs.explanation: 573 The given clinical history and findings of first metatarsophalangeal joint swelling are suggestive of an acute episode of gout . Antitubercular drugs that are most likely to cause hyperuricemia and precipitate gout are pyrazinamide and ethambutol . Both pyrazinamide and ethambutol inhibit uric acid excretion in the kidney causing hyperuricemia.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 33-year-old woman receiving treatment for TB presents to your OPD with complaints of blurry vision and pain on movement of the left eye for the past 2 days. Examination showed Marcus Gunn pupil . Which anti-tubercular drug is most likely associated with this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical features along with Marcus Gunn pupil are suggestive of optic neuritis, which is a dose -dependent adverse effect associated with ethambutol . Optic neuritis resulting in decreased visual acuity and loss of red-green discrimination is the most serious adverse effect of ethambutol . It can be unilateral or bilateral and usually recovers when the drug is stopped . Tests of visual acuity and red-green discrimination before the start of therapy and periodically thereafter are recommended .574

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is not hepatotoxic ?
mcqs.explanation: Cycloserine is not a hepatotoxic drug. The adverse effects of cycloserine are mainly neurological . Half of the patients on cycloserine (1g/day) experience neuropsychiatric symptoms . It ranges from headaches to psychosis , seizures , and suicidal ideas . Therefore, cycloserine is contraindicated in patients with epilepsy . Ethionamide , rifampicin, isoniazid and pyrazinamide are hepatotoxic agents . They are either contraindicated or used with extreme caution in hepatitis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old woman who was started on treatment for MDR-TB 6 months back, presented with complaints of fatigue , amenorrhea, and constipation since the past 1 month. On examination, a swelling was noticed on the anterior aspect of her neck. Her lab reports show raised TSH levels with low free T3 and T4 levels . Which anti-tubercular drug is likely to cause this adverse effect ?
mcqs.explanation: 578 The given clinical features and lab reports are suggestive of hypothyroidism with goiter , which is a known adverse effect of ethionamide . MDR-TB is treated with 2nd line agents that include ethionamide (ETH). ETH is not a first-line agent due to its gastrointestinal side effects . It is structurally related to thionamides (propylthiouracil and methimazole ) and therefore causes hypothyroidism by preventing organification of iodine in thyroid hormone synthesis . Another antitubercular drug that can cause hypothyroidism is Para -amino salicylic acid (PAS). ETH/PAS-induced hypothyroidism should be treated with thyroxine replacement therapy , instead of changing the regimen. Thyroid function usually optimizes within 2 months after completing MDR therapy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the mechanism of anti-mycobacterial action of bedaquiline ?
mcqs.explanation: The mechanism of anti-mycobacterial action of bedaquiline is by inhibition of ATP synthase . Bedaquiline is a diarylquinoline that targets the subunit c of the ATP synthase of M. tuberculosis . This leads to inhibition of the proton pump activity of the ATP synthase and causes a failure in the bacillary energy metabolism .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 68-year-old man with hypertension was diagnosed with drug-resistant pulmonary TB . One week after starting ATT he presented to the casualty following an episode of syncope . ECG showed a corrected QT interval of 477ms , which is shown below . Which drug used in his anti-tubercular therapy is responsible for this adverse effect ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with a corrected QT (QTc) interval of 477ms is suggestive of QTc prolongation which is an adverse effect associated with bedaquiline . In the ECG QTc (corrected QT interval= QT/\025RR ) is 477ms . Normal QTc is about 440ms. Values of more than 440ms in males and 460ms in females are considered to be prolonged . QTc prolongation usually presents as syncope or cardiac arrest. Although QT prolongation can cause Torsades de pointes , no cases have been reported with bedaquiline . A 5-fold higher rate of death has been reported in patients on bedaquiline versus those on placebo . Therefore, the World Health Organization (WHO) advises caution when administering this medication. Bedaquiline is contraindicated in the age group of <18 years.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the mechanism of action of delamanid?
mcqs.explanation: Delamanid acts by inhibiting mycolic acid synthesis . Pretomanid and delamanid are bicyclic nitroimidazoles that act by inhibiting mycolic acid (a component of the mycobacterial cell wall) and protein synthesis in the mycobacteria. Pretomanid in combination with bedaquiline and linezolid was approved by FDA in 2019 for the treatment of adult patients with extensively drug -resistant (XDR) TB and for patients who are treatment - intolerant or nonresponsive to multidrug -resistant pulmonary (MDR) TB treatment .579 In India, delamanid is only approved for the management of MDR-TB . Isoniazid also acts by inhibiting mycolic acid synthesis . Other options : Option A: Bedaquiline acts by inhibition of ATP synthase . It is a diarylquinoline that targets the subunit c of the ATP synthase of M. tuberculosis . This leads to inhibition of the proton pump activity of the ATP synthase and causes a failure in the bacillary energy metabolism . Option C: Fluoroquinolones act by inhibition of DNA gyrase . They are used as second -line agents in the treatment of tuberculosis . Option D: Cycloserine is a D-alanine analogue used as a second -line drug for MDR-TB that acts by inhibition of alanine racemase. Alanine racemase converts L-alanine to D-alanine which is needed for the mycobacterial cell wall.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old pregnant woman was diagnosed with tuberculosis . Which of the following antitubercular drugs should not be used in her?
mcqs.explanation: Streptomycin should not be used for the treatment of TB in a pregnant patient as it can cause hearing loss in the newborn. First-line treatment for tuberculosis in pregnancy is done with isoniazid(along with pyridoxine), rifampicin, ethambutol , and pyrazinamide.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An HIV -positive patient with a CD4 count of 40/mm3 requires prophylaxis against M. avium complex bacteremia. Which of the following drugs would you prefer ?
mcqs.explanation: Azithromycin 1200 mg given once a week , is preferred for prophylactic therapy against bacteremia caused by Mycobacterium -avium complex (MAC) in people living with AIDS. Clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily, may also be administered for prophylaxis . Rifabutin 300 mg once daily is used for patients who are intolerant to macrolides. Prophylaxis is indicated when CD4 counts are less than 50/mm3 and should be discontinued once the CD4 count is more than 100 /mm3 . Dapsone is used as an alternative agent for prophylaxis of pneumocystis jirovecii infection , whereas isoniazid is used for prophylaxis of mycobacterium tuberculosis infection .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An elderly woman on ART with a CD4 count of 35/�ML and a high viral load presents with a 2 week history of cough , fever, and night sweats . She was diagnosed with pulmonary M. avium complex infection . Which of the following is not included in the triple -drug therapy for the management of her condition?
