mcqs.explanation: Triple drug therapy for pulmonary Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) infections does not include isoniazid. Treatment for pulmonary MAC infection is triple -drug therapy with: • A rifamycin, like rifampicin or rifabutin (In HIV patients on ART , rifabutin is preferred ) • Ethambutol580 • A macrolide, like clarithromycin or azithromycin MAC infection is an AIDS-defining opportunistic infection , occurring predominantly at CD4+ T cell counts of <50/�ML and high viral load. The average CD4+ T cell count at the time of diagnosis is 10 /�ML. The most common presentation is disseminated disease with fever, weight loss, and night sweats .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient undergoing treatment for TB developed resistance to rifampicin and isoniazid after 3 months. He can be treated with all the following drugs except __________.
mcqs.explanation: Tobramycin cannot be used in the treatment of MDR-TB (rifampicin and isoniazid resistant) as it is not considered a second -line antitubercular drug. Injectable aminoglycosides like amikacin, kanamycin , capreomycin, and fluoroquinolones like moxifloxacin and ofloxacin are second -line drugs used for treating MDR-TB .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following beta lactam class has shown activity against MDR-TB ?
mcqs.explanation: Carbapenems have shown activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis . Note : Until recently beta -lactams were assumed to lack action against Mycobacterium tuberculosis . However, carbapenems in conjunction with clavulanate have demosntrated efficacy against Mycobacterium tuberculosis .581

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the mechanism of action of dapsone , considering that it is used in the treatment of leprosy , fungal infections and, also for immunomodulatory actions?
mcqs.explanation: The mechanism of action of dapsone is inhibition of folic acid synthesis . Dapsone [4,4\037diaminodiphenylsulphone (DDS)] is a structural analog of para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA ) and a competitive inhibitor of dihydropteroate synthase in the folate pathway . It is weakly bactericidal and can cause mild hemolysis, and rarely anemia or psychosis . DDS syndrome is a rare side effect of dapsone therapy in leprosy patients which starts after 5-6 weeks of starting dapsone and leads to exfoliative dermatitis , hepatosplenomegaly , lymphadenopathy , fever and hepatitis and may be fatal. It is also called 'five-week dermatitis '.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Dapsone would not be helpful in which of the following patients ?

options.a: HIV positive patient with CD4<100 and IgG positive for Toxoplasma
options.c: HIV positive patient with Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia

mcqs.explanation: Dapsone is not used in the treatment of schistosomiasis . Praziquantel is the drug recommended for this condition. Dapsone with pyrimethamine and leucovorin can be given for prophylaxis of Toxoplasma encephalitis in HIV patients with CD4<100. Along with trimethoprim, it can be given for prophylaxis and treatment of Pneumocystis pneumonia. However, cotrimoxazole remains the drug of choice in both conditions. The uses of dapsone are: Infections • Leprosy • Pneumocystis jerovecii infections (prophylaxis and treatment ) • Malaria • Toxoplasma gondi infections (prophylaxis) Inflammatory conditions • Dermatitis herpetiformis • Pemphigoid • Relapsing chondritis • Linear IgA bullous disease

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the treatment of choice for the patient 's condition depicted below ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image of a man with nodular lesions on his face depicts lepromatous leprosy and is treated by standard multidrug regimen (MDR-WHO recommended ) for 12 months. It consists of:586 • Rifampicin: 600 mg once a month • Dapsone : 100 mg daily • Clofazimine: 300 mg once a month + 50 mg once daily

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: All of the following are administered under supervision in India except ?
mcqs.explanation: Dapsone is administered daily in both multibacillary and paucibacillary leprosy without supervision. Clofazimine is indicated as a once-monthly supervised dose (300 mg) and daily unsupervised doses (50 mg) in multibacillary leprosy and paucibacillary leprosy . Pyrizanamide is an ATT drug which is administered under direct supervision. Rifampicin is indicated as a once-monthly supervised dose for both multibacillary and paucibacillary leprosy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presented with multiple hypopigmented skin lesions and loss of sensation over the lesions. What is the most bactericidal drug for the condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of leprosy and rifampicin is the most bactericidal anti-leprotic drug. Clofazimine and dapsone are bacteriostatic agents , while ethionamide is not indicated in leprosy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the most bactericidal anti leprotic drug amongst the given drugs?
mcqs.explanation: Ofloxacin is the most bactericidal anti leprotic drug amongst the given drugs. It exhibits high activity against M. leprae, and it is being used in alternative multidrug therapy (MDT) regimens in rifampicin-resistant cases . As a component of MDT, it has been found to hasten the bacteriological and clinical response . Among the macrolides, clarithromycin has activity against leprosy bacilli and is used for alternative MDT in cases resistant to both rifampicin and fluoroquinolones. Azithromycin shows activity against Mycobacterium avium complex but not lepra bacilli. Note : Rifampicin is the most potent bactericidal anti leprotic drug.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Thalidomide is useful in the treatment of which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Thalidomide is useful in the treatment of erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL) or type 2 lepra reaction. It is indicated in recurring and persistent ENL lesions despite the completion of at least two courses of glucocorticoid therapy .587 Thalidomide is not effective in type 1 lepra reaction. If type 1 reactions occur after initiation of antimycobacterial therapy , they are termed reversal reactions and it is histologically more tuberculoid . When they occur before the initiation, they are termed downgrading reactions and it is histologically more lepromatous .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with borderline leprosy develops severe type 1 lepra reaction during the course of his multidrug therapy . What would be the most appropriate treatment for him?
mcqs.explanation: The most appropriate therapy for severe type 1 lepra reactions is glucocorticoids . Clofazimine, though effective in type 1 lepra reaction, is less efficacious than glucocorticoids . Thalidomide and plasmapheresis are not indicated in the treatment of type 1 lepra reaction.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with leprosy , who is on multidrug therapy , presents with painful raised lesions on his forehead as shown in the image. Which of the following must be avoided in his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of tender , erythematous, subcutaneous nodules as seen in the image is suggestive of Type II lepra reaction in which rifampicin must be avoided. Rifampicin is highly bactericidal to M. leprae and results in high kill rates and massive release of bacterial antigens and may aggravate type 2 lepra reactions (also called erythema nodosum leprosum ). Options A and B: Clofazimine and corticosteroids are indicated in both type 1 and type 2 lepra reactions . Option C: Thalidomide is indicated in type 2 lepra reactions.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presents with complaints of reddish -black discolouration of skin and body secretions . Which anti-mycobacterial agent can cause this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Reddish -black discolouration of skin and body secretions is observed with the use of clofazimine. Clofazimine has good penetration into many tissues and results in reddish -black discolouration of skin and body secretions . This may take a long time to resolve.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Rifampin is not active against which of the following Mycobacterial species ?
mcqs.explanation: Rifampin is not active against Mycobacterium abscessus . It is innately resistant to rifampicin. First-line therapy for Mycobacterium abscessus includes cefoxitin (or imipenem ) + amikacin + clarithromycin. Rifampicin is effective against Mycobacterium avium complex , Mycobacterium leprae , and Mycobacterium kansasii . (Options A, B, D)588

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 54-year-old man was brought to the casualty with fever, headache , focal seizures , and right hemiparesis . MRI brain showed hyperintensity in the left frontotemporal region. PCR of his CSF sample was positive for HSV DNA. What would be the drug of choice for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and investigations are suggestive of HSV encephalitis for which the drug of choice is intravenous acyclovir. The treatment is effective only if it is started early. The clinical hallmark of HSV encephalitis is the acute onset of fever and focal neurologic signs with hemorrhagic necrosis of especially the temporal lobe . The most sensitive investigation is HSV DNA demonstration in CSF by PCR.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient diagnosed with shingles was prescribed acyclovir. Which of the following statements is false regarding this drug?

options.b: Nephrotoxicity is a dose limiting side effect of acyclovir
options.c: Valacyclovir has a higher bioavailability than acyclovir
options.d: Acyclovir does not enter the CSF

mcqs.explanation: Acyclovir can enter CSF as it is widely distributed into all body fluid compartments, including vesicular fluid and aqueous humor. It can be used for treating shingles caused by HZV . Option A: Acyclovir is a guanosine nucleoside congener . The other nucleoside congeners are cidofovir, ganciclovir, and famciclovir.594 Option B: Nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity, though rare and reversible, are dose -limiting side effects of acyclovir. Option C: Acyclovir has a low bioavailability which is overcome by administering valacyclovir , a prodrug with higher bioavailability. Mechanism of action of anti-viral drugs:

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of resistance to acyclovir in HSV -1?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of resistance to acyclovir in HSV -1 is deficient or absent viral thymidine kinase activity. Viral thymidine kinase is needed in the conversion of acyclovir to acyclovir triphosphate which competitively inhibits the viral DNA polymerase activity. Mutation of viral DNA polymerase is rare. Mechanism of action of anti-viral drugs:595

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following patients can valacyclovir be used as the drug of choice ?

options.a: An elderly woman with avian influenza
options.d: An immunocompromised patient with CMV retinitis

mcqs.explanation: Oral valacyclovir 1g three times daily for 5-7 days is considered the drug of choice for chickenpox (VZV ) in an immunocompetent patient . Treatment should be started ideally within 24 hours of rash onset . Oral acyclovir (800 mg five times daily) is an alternative drug, but valacyclovir is preferred due to its higher bioavailability and less frequent dosing. In immunocompromised patients , varicella infection is treated with IV acyclovir. Option A: Oseltamivir is used for the treatment of avian influenza. Option B: Ribavirin is used for treating RSV bronchiolitis. Option D: Ganciclovir , foscarnet, and cidofovir are approved for CMV retinitis.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient showed persistence of genital herpes lesions even after 7 days of high-dose oral acyclovir therapy . Which of the following antivirals can you use to manage this case?
mcqs.explanation: Intravenous foscarnet is used to treat acyclovir-resistant HSV (genital herpes ) and VZV infections . It inhibits viral nucleic acid synthesis by directly inhibiting HSV DNA polymerase (or HIV reverse transcriptase). It is active against herpes simplex , CMV, VZV , and HIV . Metabolic abnormalities are very common with foscarnet. Symptomatic hypocalcemia and nephrotoxicity are major dose -limiting toxicities of foscarnet.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a true statement about amantadine?

options.a: The most common side effect is CNS toxicity
options.b: It is effective only against Influenza B
options.c: It is routinely used for the treatment of influenza
options.d: It is largely metabolised by the liver

mcqs.explanation: 596 The most common side effect of amantadine is minor CNS toxicity which includes nervousness, difficulty concentrating, and insomnia. It is effective only against Influenza A. Most strains of influenza are now resistant to amantadine and hence , it is not routinely used for the treatment or prophylaxis of influenza infections . Amantadine is largely excreted unmetabolized in the urine.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A young woman with a recent travel history presented with fever and respiratory difficulty . She was diagnosed with Influenza A and was started on oseltamivir. What is the mechanism of action of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Oseltamivir is a neuraminidase inhibitor. Drugs like oseltamivir and zanamivir competitively and reversibly interact with the enzyme sites to inhibit viral neuraminidase activity. This interferes with the release of the progeny from infected host cells , halting the spread of infection . Early administration hastens the resolution of symptoms if given within 48 h of infection . Oseltamivir is given at a dose of 75 mg, twice a day for 5 days for the treatment of influenza A and B. For prophylaxis , it is given at a dose of 75mg , once per day, and continued for the duration of exposure .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Zanamivir is to be given for a patient with an influenza B infection . How will you administer this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Zanamivir is delivered by oral inhalation of dry powder in a lactose carrier . Its oral bioavailability is very low (<5%). Zanamivir is a neuraminidase inhibitor similar to oseltamivir and is active against both influenza A and B. The different routes of administration of neuraminidase inhibitors are as follows : • Zanamivir : Inhalational • Oseltamivir: Oral • Peramivir : Intravenous

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 22 -year-old man is admitted with acute H1N1 influenza pneumonia. He is having severe nausea and vomiting and is not able to take any oral medications . Which of the following drugs can be administered intravenously to him?
mcqs.explanation: Peramivir is a neuraminidase inhibitor available for intravenous administration for acute influenza (H1N1). It is indicated in acute influenza infections where the patient is not able to take drugs via the oral route or if inhalational (zanamivir ) formulation is unavailable.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man, who has history of contact with a known case of influenza, is having fever, cough , and runny nose since today morning . Rapid antigen test turns out to be positive . The endonuclease inhibitor that can be used for his treatment is ___________.
mcqs.explanation: 597 The endonuclease inhibitor which can be used for the treatment of acute uncomplicated influenza in adults is baloxavir marboxil. It is a novel drug that was approved by the FDA in 2018 . It is used to treat acute uncomplicated influenza in patients 12 years of age and older who have been symptomatic for less than 48 hours. It is a selective inhibitor of influenza cap-dependent endonuclease which blocks proliferation by inhibiting mRNA synthesis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is approved for prophylaxis against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV ) infection ?
mcqs.explanation: Palivizumab is a monoclonal antibody approved for prophylaxis against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV ) infection. It is a humanized monoclonal antibody against F-glycoprotein present on the surface of RSV . It is used in high-risk infants (prematurity and immunosuppressed conditions) and children (with cardiovascular and pulmonary diseases). The treatment of RSV infections is done with inhaled ribavirin . Option A: Omalizumab is a monoclonal antibody against IgE indicated in asthma. Option C: Denosumab is a monoclonal antibody against RANKL indicated in osteoporosis . Option D: Ribavirin is used for treatment of RSV infections but is not approved for prophylaxis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A hepatitis B infected patient awaiting liver transplantation is admitted with ascites and encephalopathy . Which of the following is the drug of choice for him?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of ascites and encephalopathy in a hepatitis B infected patient is suggestive of decompensated liver disease . Tenofovir is the drug of choice for decompensated cirrhosis due to hepatitis B infection . Tenofovir is one of the first-line drugs for chronic hepatitis B infections . It is available as two prodrug formulations tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF). Option A: Interferon-alpha is one of the first-line agents in individuals with ongoing HBV -DNA replication and liver inflammation. But it is contraindicated in decompensated cirrhosis with HBV infection as they can precipitate clinical deterioration and increase the risk of bacterial infections . Options B and D: Lamivudine and Telbivudine are not considered first-line agents for HBV infections because of the increased frequency of resistance associated with their use .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Sofosbuvir is indicated in the treatment of which of the following patients ?
mcqs.explanation: Sofosbuvir is indicated in the treatment of hepatitis C infection only. It is a directly acting antiviral , NS5B nucleotide polymerase inhibitor.598 The goal of treatment in hepatitis C is a sustained virologic response (SVR ). It is defined as the absence of a virus in the blood (undetectable HCV RNA), 12 weeks after completion of treatment . This can be achieved by the use of pan-genotypic directly acting antiviral drugs, irrespective of the disease stage .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a direct -acting agent (DAAs) used in the treatment of HCV infections ?
mcqs.explanation: NS4B inhibitors are not direct -acting agents (DAAs). Direct-acting agents (DAAs) are drugs that target specific viral proteins which are vital to the replication and lifecycle of HCV. The currently available DAAs inhibit 3 specific non-structural (NS) proteins : • NS3/4A protease inhibitors • NS5A inhibitors • NS5B polymerase inhibitors

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 52-year-old woman with history of hepatitis B infection presents with fatigue , vomiting, and weight loss. Her serological markers are given in the table below . What is the treatment of choice for her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and serology are suggestive of chronic hepatitis D infection in a hepatitis B carrier for which the treatment of choice is pegylated interferon-alpha (pegIFN -�o ). It is the only drug currently available to treat chronic hepatitis D infection .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A young woman presents with painless warty lesions on the vulva as shown in the image below . Which of the following is a topical agent that can be prescribed for her condition?
mcqs.explanation: Warty lesions on the vulva as seen in the given image is suggestive of condyloma acuminata caused by HPV (6, ). Imiquimod is a topical agent with antiviral and immunomodulatory properties indicated in the treatment of external genital and perianal warts. Other topical agents that can be used include podophyllotoxin and trichloroacetic acid.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is currently approved for the treatment of small pox?
mcqs.explanation: Tecovirimat has been recently approved as a treatment of smallpox. It was approved under the FDA's animal rule, which allows findings from animal studies to support an FDA approval when it is not feasible or ethical to conduct efficacy trials in599 humans. Cidofovir has also been approved by the FDA for smallpox under this rule. Both these drugs are currently stockpiled by CDC's strategic national stockpile , which has the medical supplies required to protect the public in case of a public health emergency . Tecovirimat could also be used under an investigational new drug (IND) protocol to treat adverse reactions from vaccinia vaccination . Option B: Lumacaftor is a drug approved for cystic fibrosis. Option C: Pegvaliase has been approved for the treatment of phenylketonuria in adults . Option D: Apalutamide is a nonsteroidal antiandrogen medication which is used in the treatment of prostate cancer. It is specifically indicated for use in conjunction with castration in the treatment of non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.600

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You decide to start recombinant growth hormone therapy in a child with idiopathic short stature . The treatment primarily works by the activation of which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Growth hormone primarily acts through activation of the JAK-STAT signaling pathway . Cytokines such as interferon-gamma and prolactin hormone also act by the JAK STAT pathway .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following conditions is growth hormone therapy not indicated ?
mcqs.explanation: 604 Growth hormone therapy is not indicated in Sotos syndrome. Indications for GH therapy are: • GH Deficiency in children & adults • AIDS-associated wasting • Malabsorption associated with the short-bowel syndrome (As GH stimulates the adaptation of GI epithelial cells ). • Children with other conditions associated with short stature despite adequate GH production : • Turner syndrome • Noonan syndrome • Prader-Willi syndrome • Chronic renal insufficiency • Small for gestational age babies • Idiopathic short stature Sotos syndrome (cerebral gigantism) is characterized by excessive physical growth during the first few years of life resulting in a disproportionately large and long head with a slightly protrusive forehead , large hands and feet , hypertelorism, and down-slanting eyes . It is accompanied by mild cognitive impairment, developmental abnormalities, hypotonia, and speech abnormalities. The image given below shows a large head , large hands, and characteristic eye features in a child with Sotos syndrome.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: All of the following are sound advice to the respective patients except :
mcqs.explanation: GH deferral is only recommended for the first year after treatment of leukemia.605 Because of the anti-insulin action of GH, there is an increased incidence of type 2 diabetes mellitus and therefore , fasting glucose levels should be monitored periodically during GH therapy . Due to the rare potential for developing intracranial hypertension , fundoscopic examination is recommended at the initiation of therapy and at periodic intervals thereafter . Rapid growth induced by GH can cause slipped epiphyses or scoliosis in children. Estrogens (OCPs and estrogen supplements) inhibit GH action so that a larger dose is needed to maintain the same IGF-1 level . The adverse effects of growth hormone are:Children Adults Intracranial hypertensionInc reased risk oftype 2 diabetes Slipped epiphysisScoliosis Peripheral edemaCarpal tunn el syndromeArthralgiasMyalg ia

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man with tall stature , frontal bossing, prognathism, large hands, and feet is started on a growth hormone receptor antagonist. Identify the drug.
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario depicts acromegaly. Pegvisomant is a growth hormone receptor antagonist that is indicated for the treatment of acromegaly. Octreotide and lanreotide are synthetic somatostatin analogs that can be used in the management of acromegaly. Cabergoline is a dopamine agonist used primarily to treat hyperprolactinemia also has an indication in the management of acromegaly.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old lady presented to the gynecology OPD with complaints of amenorrhea and milky discharge from her breasts. Her urine pregnancy test is negative and her serum prolactin level is 175 \265 g/L. The resident prescribes a long-acting D2 agonist. Which of the following drugs is she likely to have been prescribed ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario depicts hyperprolactinemia . Cabergoline is a long-acting D2 agonist. Its t1/2 is >60 hours. It is indicated for the treatment of hyperprolactinemia and acromegaly. Bromocriptine, lisuride , and apomorphine are short-acting when compared with cabergoline . Bromocriptine is an ergot alkaloid derivative used in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus , hyperprolactinemia, acromegaly, and Parkinson 's disease . Cabergoline is preferred over bromocriptine for hyperprolactinemia due to lower adverse effects such as nausea and also due to dosing advantage (twice a week instead of daily dosing). Lisuride is indicated in early Parkinson's disease but is also known to decrease prolactin levels and prevent migraine attacks. Apomorphine is a morphine derivative used to treat hypomobile "off" episodes of advanced Parkinson 's disease .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following conditions is octreotide not used ?
mcqs.explanation: 606 Octreotide is not used in glioma. Uses of octreotide are : • Secretory diarrhea in carcinoid syndrome and VIPoma • Short bowel syndrome, AIDS • Pituitary tumors causing acromegaly • Islet cell tumors like glucagonoma , insulinoma • Acute bleeding in esophageal varices • Thyrotrope adenoma Adverse effects include gall stones , sinus bradycardia, and conduction abnormalities. Vit B12 deficiency can occur on long term use .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Valvular heart disease is not associated with the use of which of the following drugs?
mcqs.explanation: Quinagolide is not associated with valvular heart disease . Quinagolide is a non-ergot D2 receptor agonist. Cabergoline , Bromocriptine, and Pergolide are ergot derivatives and are associated with valvular heart disease. The risk of valvular heart disease from ergot therapy is associated with higher doses of the drug (necessary for Parkinson 's disease treatment ) but not with the lower doses used in treating hyperprolactinemia . Note : Pergolide was withdrawn from the market due to reports of serious valve damage .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following patients is bromocriptine not indicated ?

options.c: A 23 -year old lady with endogenous depression
options.d: A 45-year old parkinson 's patient with type 2 diabetes mellitus

mcqs.explanation: Bromocriptine is not indicated in endogenous depression . It is a semisynthetic ergot D2 receptor agonist. Uses of bromocriptine: • Hyperprolactinemia (causing galactorrhoea, amenorrhea, or infertility in women and gynecomastia or infertility in men) • Parkinsonism • Acromegaly • Type 2 diabetes mellitus • Hepatic coma • Supression of lactation607

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old chronic alcoholic patient with a history of coronary bypass surgery presents with haematemesis to the casualty . An upper GI endoscopy shows the following finding. Which of the following drugs will you administer to this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history of the patient and the endoscopic image showing prominent cherry-red spots are suggestive of bleeding esophageal varices. Octreotide is indicated in the treatment of acute variceal bleeding . It is a somatostatin analog that reduces azygous blood flow significantly and decreases variceal bleeding . Other drugs that can be used for the management of bleeding esophageal varices: • Terlipressin • Vasopressin • Propranolol Option A: Desmopressin is a selective V2 receptor agonist used for central diabetes insipidus and nocturnal enuresis. Option B: Propranolol (non-selective beta -blocker) is used in the prophylaxis of variceal bleeding and not in its acute management. Option D: Terlipressin is a vasoconstrictor used for bleeding esophageal varices but may compromise cardiac function and induce ischemia and hence can't be used in this case. Note : Although terlipressin is a vasoconstrictor and is be used for bleeding oesophagal varices , the patient in this scenario has a history of MI (undergone coronary bypass surgery). Terlipressin can compromise cardiac function (reduces cardiac output and ejection fraction) and induce ischemia. Hence , it is not preferred in this case.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Pulsatile dosing of GnRH agonist is used for the treatment of __________.
mcqs.explanation: Pulsatile administration of GnRH agonists results in increased FSH and LH secretion and is therefore used to treat male and female infertility . Non-pulsatile or continuous dose of GnRH agonist results in suppression and decreased concentrations of gonadotropins LH and FSH. They are used in: • Endometriosis • Uterine fibroids • Central precocious puberty • Ca prostate • Ca ovary and breast • Controlled ovary stimulation

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old lady who is suffering from dysmenorrhea and infertility is diagnosed with endometriosis. She has been prescribed an intranasal spray containing a GnRH agonist. What is the likely drug?
mcqs.explanation: Nafarelin is a GnRH agonist administered via nasal spray.608 It is approved for use in endometriosis and central precocious puberty . Routes of administration of other GnRH agonists: • Intranasal and subcutaneous - Buserelin • Intramuscular and subcutaneous - Leuprolide • Subcutaneous implants - Histrelin and Goserelin Some GnRH antagonists are: • Degarelix • Ganirelix • Cetrorelix (Synthetic ) All GnRH antagonists are administered subcutaneously .609

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Levothyroxine/liothyronine acts by binding to thyroid receptors . Thyroid hormone receptors belong to which of the following class of receptors ?

options.a: Transmembrane receptor linked to tyrosine kinase

mcqs.explanation: Thyroid hormone receptors belong to the class of nuclear receptors . Nuclear receptors are a family of ligand-regulated transcription factors that are activated by various lipid-soluble signals, including retinoic acid, thyroid hormone, and steroid hormones. They primarily function as transcription factors and directly interact with the genomic DNA to regulate gene expression . Nuclear receptors can either remain anchored in the cytoplasm via chaperone proteins until freed by ligand-binding (e.g., steroid and vitamin D receptors ) or can reside in the nucleus bound to specific DNA response elements even in the absence of ligand (e.g., thyroid hormone, PPAR\033, and retinoic acid receptors ).

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In comparison to thyroxine, liothyronine has ___________.
mcqs.explanation: Liothyronine has better absorption compared to levothyroxine. It is almost completely absorbed (100 %) when compared to thyroxine (80%). Note : Liotrix is a 4:1 mixture of Levothyroxine sodium (LT4): Liothyronine sodium (LT3 )614 Liothyronine(T3 ) Levothyroxine(T4) Onset of action Rapid Slow Potency More potent Less potent Half-life T1 /2-18-24 hr T1 /2- 7-8 days Source 25% from gland; % from p eripheral conversion Solely produced by the glan d Plasma protein bindi ng 0.2% unbound 0.02 % unbound

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old hypothyroid patient taking levothyroxine regularly has now become pregnant. What would your advice be regarding levothyroxine?

options.a: Switch to liothyronine as levothyroxine is teratogenic
options.b: Increase the dose as pregnancy causes an increased demand for levothyroxine
options.c: Continue the same dose but monitor the serum levels on a fortnightly basis
options.d: Stop levothyroxine till the end of the first trimester as it has teratogenic potential

mcqs.explanation: The dose of levothyroxine in patients who become pregnant should usually be increased . This is because demand for levothyroxine increases in pregnancy and low thyroxine levels are associated with adverse fetal outcomes such as mental retardation. The dose of levothyroxine is increased by 30-50% by asking the patient to take 2 extra pills per week. Increased demand for levothyroxine in pregnancy is due to: • The increased serum concentration of thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) induced by estrogen • Increased expression of type 3 deiodinase in the placenta • A small amount of passage of levothyroxine to the fetus Thyroid hormones are not teratogenic . Liothyronine is not preferred in pregnancy because T3 has a short half-life and requires frequent dosing to limit large fluctuations in levels . In addition, excess T3 often acts to normalize TSH while lowering T4, thereby risking inadequate T4 availability to the fetus .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient on levothyroxine supplementation would need to increase her dose if she is taking _______.
mcqs.explanation: Patients who start estrogen therapy will need to increase their thyroid supplementation doses . Estrogens raise the circulating levels of thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG), thereby increasing the bound fraction and decreasing the free (bioactive) fraction of circulating thyroxine (T4). As a consequence , estrogen therapy increases the T4 supplementation requirements of women being treated for primary hypothyroidism . Drugs increasing TBG levels : • Estrogens • Tamoxifen • Methadone • 5-fluorouracil Drugs decreasing TBG levels :615 • Androgens • Corticosteroids • Niacin Drugs decreasing binding of T4 to TBG (by displacement ): • Salicylates (aspirin, mefenamic acid) • Heparin • Furosemide

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old patient suffering from Graves disease has been on treatment for the past three weeks . She has now developed fever and sore throat with an absolute neutrophil count of 80 neutrophils per microlitre of blood. The use of which of the following drugs can result in such a clinical picture ?
mcqs.explanation: This patient is suffering from agranulocytosis which is a serious adverse effect that can be seen with the use of either methimazole or propylthiouracil . Agranulocytosis usually occurs in the initial weeks or months of therapy . It occurs rapidly and periodic monitoring of granulocyte levels is generally ineffective . However, it is reversible on discontinuation of the drug. Therefore, patients who are on these drugs should be instructed to report immediately if they develop fever or sore throat.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient developed thyroid storm in the post -operative ward and was immediately started on IV propranolol and a loading dose of propylthiouracil . The antithyroid drug acts by inhibiting which of the following deiodinases ?
mcqs.explanation: Propylthiouracil inhibits only type I deiodinase (D1). Deiodinases are the enzymes that are involved in the peripheral conversion of T4 to either T3 or reverse T3 . Type I deiodinase (D1) and type II deiodinase (D2) convert T4 to T3 . Type III (D3) is involved in the conversion of T4 to reverse T3 . Note : Amiodarone inhibits both types I and type II deiodinases .616

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man presented with complaints of increased sweating and weight loss over the past two months. On examination, he is tachycardic, has exophthalmos , and a diffusely enlarged thyroid gland. Which of the following is the drug of choice for the management of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Graves disease and the drug of choice is methimazole . Option A: Methimazole is preferred over propylthiouracil due to fewer side effects and single -daily dosing (compared to PTU which is given TID ). Option C: Levothyroxine is used in hypothyroidism . Option D: Lugol's iodine is a thyroid hormone-release inhibitor but not used as a first-line drug.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old primiparous woman presented with features suggestive of thyrotoxicosis , at 7 weeks of gestation. Which of the following is the drug of choice for the treatment of her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The drug of choice for the treatment of thyrotoxicosis during the first trimester of pregnancy is propylthiouracil (PTU). It is because it has lower teratogenic effects than carbimazole or methimazole . Carbimazole and methimazole are associated with teratogenic effects such as: • Aplasia cutis congenita • Choanal atresia • Treacheosopageal fistula • Fetal goiter However, propylthiouracil use is limited to the first trimester due to the risk of hepatotoxicity . It is replaced with carbimazole or methimazole in the 2nd and 3rd trimesters of the pregnancy. The lowest effective antithyroid drug dose should be used throughout gestation . This is to maintain the maternal serum-free T4 level in the upper limit of the non-pregnant normal reference range. Radioiodine therapy is contraindicated during pregnancy and lactation.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best describes the Wolff-Chaikoff effect ?

options.a: Decrease in thyroid hormone release due to low doses of iodine
options.b: Increase in thyroid hormone release due to high doses of iodine
options.c: Decrease in thyroid hormone synthesis due to high doses of iodine
options.d: Increase in thyroid hormone synthesis due to low iodine intake

mcqs.explanation: The Wolff-Chaikoff effect is best described as iodine-induced hypothyroidism . It is a normal , protective downregulation of thyroid hormone synthesis and release via transient inhibition of iodide organification in the presence of an iodine load (exogenous supplementation , iodinated contrast dye , drugs like amiodarone). This occurs in the thyroid gland which is under pituitary control. With persistent high iodine load, an escape phenomenon occurs in normal individuals after around 10 days as the iodide levels fall inside the follicle . In autoimmune diseases (Hashimoto's or Grave's), however, the suppression may persist .617 The Jod-Basedow phenomenon is iodine-induced hyperthyroidism . It is also seen after an iodine load. However, it is seen in thyroid glands where autoregulation and pituitary control have failed . When exposed to an iodine load in excess , instead of blocking the organification process , the thyroid gland (areas of the autonomously functioning gland) continues to uptake the iodine, producing more thyroid hormone independent of normal regulatory mechanisms. It is seen in endemic goiter , toxic multinodular goiter, thyroid adenoma, and sometimes in Grave's disease .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient suffering from Graves disease is posted for thyroidectomy . He is administered iodides preoperatively. What is the primary benefit of administrating iodides in this patient ?

options.b: To make the gland firm and less vascular

mcqs.explanation: The primary benefit of the preoperative use of iodides in Grave's disease is to make the gland firm and less vascular. This makes manipulation and surgical resection easier. Antithyroid drugs like methimazole or carbimazole are indicated to render the patient euthyroid .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient suffering from hyperthyroidism is administered a drug that acts by inhibiting the release of thyroid hormone. Identify the drug.
mcqs.explanation: Potassium iodide inhibits the release of the thyroid hormone. Iodides of sodium and potassium and Lugol's iodine act by inhibiting thyroid hormone release . Hence , they are also called thyroid constipating agents . They are the fastest -acting agents . The beneficial effect of iodides peaks over 10 -15 days and gradually disappears . Tolerance is hence an issue with the use of iodides .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 43-year-old lady with papillary thyroid cancer is being treated with radioactive iodine 131 . What is the half-life of this isotope ?
mcqs.explanation: The half-life of radioactive I 131 is 8 days I131 emits both beta and gamma rays. It is used both for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes for thyroid disorders. I127 is the stable isotope of iodine. I123 is the radioactive isotope of iodine that emits only gamma rays. The action is short-lived with a half-life of around 13 hours. It is indicated for diagnostic indications only.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about Lugol's iodine is incorrect?

options.a: Used to make thyroid gland less vascular
options.b: Used to block thyroid hormone release rapidly
options.d: Augments radioactive iodine uptake into thyroid gland

mcqs.explanation: Lugol's iodine does not augment the uptake of radioactive iodine in the thyroid gland. Radioactive iodine uptake into the thyroid gland is reduced by Lugol's iodine as the uptake is inversely proportional to the serum concentration of stable iodine. Lugol's iodine makes the thyroid gland less vascular and firmer. It blocks the release of thyroid hormone. The beneficial effect peaks over 10 -15 days and gradually disappears . Therefore tolerance is an issue .618

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old lady who is a known case of Graves disease was posted for thyroidectomy . During the surgery, she developed hyperthermia , agitation and the monitors showed an arrhythmia . She was managed with aggressive IV fluid therapy , ice packs, and multiple drugs. Which of the following drugs that were used , do not inhibit the peripheral conversion of T4 to T3 ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture is suggestive of a thyrotoxic crisis/thyroid storm. Potassium iodide does not inhibit the peripheral conversion of T4 to T3 . The major action of potassium iodide is the inhibition of hormone release . It is usually given 1 hour after PTU administration to avoid iodine stimulating thyroid hormone synthesis . Drugs inhibiting the peripheral conversion of T4 to T3 are: • Propranolol • Glucocorticoids • Propylthiouracil • Amiodarone • Iopanoic acid619

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Glucocorticoids act on which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Glucocorticoids act on the intracellular cytoplasmic receptors . They diffuse into cytosol and bind to the cytoplasmic receptors and influence nuclear changes by activation of the receptor .626

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Glucocorticoids do not have permissive action on which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Glucocorticoids do not have permissive action on bradykinin . They inhibit inflammatory mediators such as histamine, bradykinin , and eicosanoids . Glucocorticoids possess permissive action on the vasoconstrictor effect of angiotensin and lipolytic action of adrenaline and noradrenaline. In the absence of glucocorticoids , these hormones have low activity but the presence enhances their activity several folds .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman diagnosed with Cushing's syndrome does not want surgery and requests medical treatment. Which of the following drugs can be recommended ?
mcqs.explanation: Metyrapone can be recommended as it is approved in the treatment of pregnant women with Cushing's syndrome. It inhibits the synthesis of cortisol by inhibiting steroid 11 \035-hydroxylase reversibly. Cushing's syndrome (CS) is a manifestation of symptoms that are precipitated by excessive cortisol production . Transsphenoidal surgery, radiation, and pharmacotherapy constitute the standard treatment for tumor-related causes of CS (e.g. pituitary adenoma). The three main pharmacological approaches are: • Cortisol synthesis inhibitors: Ketoconazole , metyrapone , mitotane, etomidate , aminoglutethimide • ACTH secretion inhibitors: Cyproheptadine , pasireotide , octreotide , cabergoline • Glucocorticoid receptor antagonist: Mifepristone Note : Metyrapone is also used to test the hypothalamic -pituitary feedback pathway in the diagnosis of Cushing syndrome.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The enzyme A in the following image corresponds to?
mcqs.explanation: "A" here corresponds to 11 -beta -HSD2 (11 \035-Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase2 ). It converts active cortisol to inactive cortisone. Cortisol is active and can bind to both glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoid receptors whereas cortisone is inactive and does not bind to either . The selective inactivation of cortisol is required in certain sites such as the distal nephron so that the specific autoregulatory responses to aldosterone can be achieved . Therefore, cortisol (active) is metabolized to cortisone (inactive) by 11 -beta -HSD2 in the kidney, so as to protect renal mineralocorticoid receptors from cortisol binding. Some tissues , like the liver, can convert inactive cortisone back to active cortisol through an enzyme called 11 -beta -HSD1 ("B" in the image). This completes the "cortisone–cortisol shuttle " because the kidney can inactivate cortisol where it is not needed and the liver can reactivate it afterward.627 However, when circulating cortisol levels are very high, as in severe Cushing syndrome, they can overwhelm this protective mechanism, allowing cortisol to bind to and activate the mineralocorticoid receptor . This leads to volume expansion, hypertension , and hypokalemia often observed in hypercortisolism . A mutation of 11 -beta -HSD2 also causes a similar clinical picture and is the reason for the syndrome of apparent mineralocorticoid excess . 17\035-Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase and 3\035-Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase are involved in the metabolism of sex steroids .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a prodrug?
mcqs.explanation: Prednisone is a prodrug. It is a synthetic glucocorticoid that is biologically inert until converted via hepatic metabolism (11 -beta HSD1) to the active component , prednisolone .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with moderate COVID -19 was started on a long-acting glucocorticoid . Which of the following drugs could it be?
mcqs.explanation: Dexamethasone is the longest acting glucocorticoid . Its t1/2 is >36 hours.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Highest mineralocorticoid activity is seen with which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: The highest mineralocorticoid activity is seen with aldosterone . However, it cannot be used clinically. The highest mineralocorticoid activity in a drug that is used clinically is fludrocortisone .628 Glucocorticoid activity Mineralocorticoid activity Short-acting glucocorticoids CortisoneHydrocortisone 0.81 0.81 Intermediate -acting glucocor ticoids Prednisone-prednisoloneMet hylprednisolone 0.80.5 Long-acting glucocorticoids DexamethasoneBetamethaso ne 00 Mineralocorticoids Deoxycorticosterone (DOCA) FludrocortisoneAldosterone 0.2150 -500

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist?
mcqs.explanation: Metyrapone is not a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist. It is a selective inhibitor of 11 \035-hydroxylase and thereby reduces cortisol and corticosterone synthesis . Options A and B - Spironolactone and eplerenone are aldosterone antagonist that is used in hypertension and chronic CHF for reversing the effects of aldosterone Option C - Drospirenone is a 4th generation progestin used as an oral contraceptive having mineralocorticoid antagonist action

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A woman diagnosed with Sheehan 's syndrome is planned for the initiation of hormone replacement . Glucocorticoids should be administered prior to thyroxine supplementation due to what concern?

options.c: Decrease in the metabolism of glucocorticoids

mcqs.explanation: Glucocorticoids are administered before initiating treatment with thyroid hormones as administration of thyroxine can precipitate acute adrenal insufficiency . In the case of combined adrenal insufficiency and hypothyroidism , as in panhypopituitarism (due to surgery or Sheehan 's syndrome), adrenal insufficiency is generally treated first. This is because giving thyroxine first can enhance cortisol clearance and precipitate an adrenal crisis. Also, levothyroxine increases the basal metabolic rate (BMR) leading to an increased requirement of cortisol, which if not met can also precipitate an adrenal crisis.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman came for routine antenatal screening . During prenatal testing , the fetus was suspected to have congenital adrenal hyperplasia . What is the drug of choice for treating the fetus in-utero?
mcqs.explanation: The drug of choice for treating the fetus in-utero when suspected of having congenital adrenal hyperplasia is dexamethasone .629 Dexamethasone readily crosses the placenta and suppresses the secretion of steroids and androgens by fetal adrenal glands. If started by 6 weeks of gestation , it reduces the virilization of external genitalia in affected females . Chorionic villus biopsy is then performed to determine the sex and the genotype of the fetus and therapy is only continued if the fetus is an affected female . This is not widely accepted currently due to insufficient data on long-term risks especially in unaffected females and males who derive no benefit from the treatment .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient is started on hormone replacement for chronic adrenal insufficiency . What is the replacement dose of hydrocortisone that has to be given (in mg/day)?
mcqs.explanation: The replacement dose of hydrocortisone for chronic adrenal insufficiency is 20 mg/day. The treatment of chronic adrenal insufficiency (not in crisis) requires glucocorticoid replacement at a dose that replaces the physiologic daily cortisol production . This is achieved by administering an oral replacement dose of 15-25mg Hydrocortisone. A midpoint dose of 20mg is given in 2-3 divided doses : 10mg + 5mg + 5mg. A higher morning dose is given at 8:30 am (usually 1/2 to 2/3 of the total dose ). The next dose is given at 1:30 pm and in the evening (4:30-5:00 pm). This is to follow the normal circadian rhythm.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman at 33 weeks of gestation presents to your antenatal clinic with preterm labour. Which corticosteroid will you administer for stimulation of fetal lung maturation?
mcqs.explanation: Betamethasone is indicated for the stimulation of fetal lung maturation in preterm labor. As compared to cortisol, betamethasone binds to maternal proteins less and has less placental metabolism . This allows increased transfer to the fetus . Additionally , infants exposed to betamethasone are less likely to require postnatal resuscitation . 2 doses of 12 mg each are administered 18-24 hours apart when the delivery is anticipated before 34 weeks of gestation . Dexamethasone is another long-acting glucocorticoid that can be given. It has benefits such as less risk of intraventricular hemorrhage and a shorter length of stay in the NICU.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with chronic adrenal insufficiency is on long term corticosteroid therapy . Which of the following side effects is he unlikely to experience ?
mcqs.explanation: Corticosteroid therapy does not cause muscular hypertrophy and the patient is unlikely to experience it as a side effect . Excess glucocorticoid activity results in muscle wasting and myopathy while excess mineralocorticoid activity results in hypokalemia and causes muscle weakness . Options B and C: Peptic ulceration and psychosis are known adverse effects of corticosteroids . Option D : Glucocorticoids with some mineralocorticoid activity will result in sodium and water retention and may cause hypertension.630

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You are planning to add oral steroids to manage a case of severe asthma. Presence of which of the following comorbidities is not a relative contraindication for starting the medication?
mcqs.explanation: Eczematous skin diseases are not a contraindication for the use of oral corticosteroids . In fact, they are highly effective and are indicated in this condition. All the contraindications to steroids are relative because of the life -saving nature of steroids . Risk -benefit should be assessed cautiously when initiating steroids in the following conditions: • Diabetes mellitus • Hypertension • Peptic ulcer • Viral and fungal infections • Tuberculosis and other infections • Osteoporosis • Herpes simplex keratitis • Epilepsy • CHF • Renal failure

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 54-year-old woman is being evaluated for chronic back pain. She mentions that she had been on corticosteroids for asthma since childhood . Which of the following actions of the drug would not cause her condition?
mcqs.explanation: Chronic back pain following long term corticosteroid therapy is suggestive of osteoporosis . Glucocorticoids do not inhibit of the action of osteoclasts . It causes stimulation of osteoclasts and increases bone resorption. Mechanism of glucocorticoids induced osteoporosis : • Inhibition of gonadal steroidal hormones • Reduced gastrointestinal absorption of calcium • Secondary effect of decreased calcium absorption: increased parathyroid hormone leading to further resorption • Suppressive action on osteoblasts • Stimulation of osteoclasts

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Osteonecrosis following glucocorticoid therapy is most commonly associated with which site ?
mcqs.explanation: The femoral head is the most frequently affected site by osteonecrosis due to glucocorticoid therapy.631 The earliest symptoms are joint pain and stiffness . When patients on steroid therapy develop hip, shoulder or knee pain, osteonecrosis must be considered and ruled out. Options B and D - It can also affect the distal femur and humeral head Option C - Osteonecrosis of the jaw is associated with the use of bisphosphonates

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with Cushing's syndrome has very high levels of ACTH. Which of the following is a CRH preparation that can be used to determine if it is a pituitary source or an ectopic source ?
mcqs.explanation: Corticorelin is a corticotrophin-releasing hormone (CRH) preparation used in CRH stimulation test which helps to differentiate between a pituitary source and an ectopic source for ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism . Pituitary tumors tend to be sensitive to CRH stimulation and responds with a rise in cortisol while ectopic tumors do not usually respond . Ectopic sources of ACTH include carcinoid, medullary thyroid carcinoma , and pheochromocytoma . It can also be used to test the HPA axis. Option A - Gonadorelin is a recombinant GnRH. Option C - Ganirelix is a GnRH antagonist. Option D - Cosyntropin is a synthetic preparation of ACTH.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a steroid receptor antagonist that can be given to a patient with Cushing's syndrome due to ectopic ACTH?
mcqs.explanation: Mifepristone is a steroid receptor antagonist that can be used in Cushing's syndrome. It is used in Cushing's syndrome especially in inoperable cases with ectopic ACTH secretion or adrenal carcinoma. Options A, B, and D - Ketoconazole , metyrapone , and aminoglutethimide reduce steroid synthesis by enzyme inhibition.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following intravenous anaesthetics can be used for acute control of hypercortisolism?
mcqs.explanation: The intravenous anesthetic that can be used for acute control of hypercortisolism is etomidate . Etomidate at sub-hypnotic doses inhibits cortisol secretion by selectively inhibiting 11-beta-hydroxylase activity. It is used off-label to treat hypercortisolism when rapid control is needed and the patient is not able to take oral medication.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient is diagnosed with inoperable adrenocortical carcinoma and needs medical adrenalectomy . Which of the following drugs could be used for him?
mcqs.explanation: 632 Mitotane is used for medical adrenalectomy in this patient . It has a non-selective toxic action on the adrenal cortex. It causes suppression of adrenal cortex hormone secretion comparable to that of adrenalectomy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antifungal drugs can be used in the treatment of a patient with Cushing syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Ketoconazole can be used in the treatment of Cushing syndrome for symptomatic control. It is a non-selective inhibitor of adrenal and gonadal steroid synthesis . These actions are more apparent at higher doses than those used for fungal infections .633

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following decreases both serum calcium and phosphate levels ?
mcqs.explanation: Calcitonin decreases both serum calcium and phosphate levels .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following interferes with the absorption of calcium?
mcqs.explanation: Glucocorticoids , phenytoin , tetracyclines , phytates , and oxalates all interfere with the absorption of calcium. Glucocorticoids and phenytoin depress intestinal calcium transport whereas , tetracyclines , phytates , phosphates , and oxalates form insoluble complexes with calcium and thereby interfere with calcium absorption.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Following a road traffic accident , a patient underwent transfusion with 5 units of packed red blood cells . Soon after, he developed tetany . His serum calcium level was 7.5 mg/dl on lab reports. Which of the following is preferred as the treatment of choice for the given condition?
mcqs.explanation: This is a case of hypocalcemia following a massive blood transfusion and IV calcium gluconate is the preferred treatment . The hypocalcemia results from Ca2+ chelation by citrate (added to the blood product as preservative and anticoagulant). Calcium gluconate is the preferred over calcium chloride for the emergency treatment of hypocalcemia because it is less irritating and better tolerated . However, calcium chloride may be preferable to calcium gluconate in the presence of abnormal liver function, because decreased citrate metabolism results in a slower release of ionized calcium. It is generally reserved for severe symptomatic hypocalcemia , (<4 mg/dL) and when given, should be administered via a central venous access device to avoid extravasation and tissue necrosis. Calcium carbonate and calcium lactate are oral preparations of calcium.639

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true regarding plasma calcium?

options.a: Ca2+ sensing receptor is a voltage gated ion channel
options.b: Albumin bound calcium is physiologically most important
options.c: Calcium is mainly absorbed from large intestine

mcqs.explanation: Acidosis favors the ionization of calcium. Hyperventilation by causing alkalosis favors the deionization of calcium. Alkalosis result in precipitation of tetany and laryngospasm in calcium-deficient patients Option A - Ca2+ sensing receptor is a type of G protein coupled receptor . Option B - 50% of the Ca2+ is in ionized form and is physiologically most important. Option C - Calcium is mainly absorbed from the small intestine .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 57 -year-old post menopausal lady has been on alendronate for the past two years. By which of the following mechanisms does this drug act?

options.c: Decreasing the osteoclast mediated resorption of bone

mcqs.explanation: Alendronate is a bisphosphonate which acts by decreasing osteoclast mediated bone resorption. Osteoclasts internalize bisphosphonates as they are released along with calcium from the bone surface and then reduce osteoclast activity by: • Promoting apoptosis of osteoclasts • Disrupting the cytoskeleton and ruffled border of osteoclasts • Inhibiting the differentiation of osteoclasts

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an indication to use bisphosphonates ?
mcqs.explanation: Bisphosphonates are not indicated in the treatment of vitamin D excess . Indications for the use of bisphosphonates: • Osteoporosis • Paget 's disease • Hypercalcemia of malignancy • Osteolytic bone metastasis

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old lady has been taking zoledronate for the treatment of osteoporosis . She is at a high risk of developing which of the following side effects ?
mcqs.explanation: Zoledronate use has been associated with acute renal failure. It is nephrotoxic. So baseline renal function and monitoring of renal function during therapy with zoledronate is recommended . Long term complications seen with bisphosphonate therapy are osteonecrosis of jaw and subtrochanteric fracture of femur.640

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is used in the first-line management of postmenopausal osteoporosis ?
mcqs.explanation: Bisphosphonates are used in the first-line management of postmenopausal osteoporosis . Bisphosphonates are analogs of pyrophosphates . They specifically inhibit bone resorption and thus are very effective for the treatment of postmenopausal osteoporosis . Bisphosphonates concentrate at sites of active remodeling . They remain in the matrix until the bone is remodeled . Then, they are released in the acid environment of the resorption lacunae and induce apoptosis in osteoclasts . Classification of bisphosphonates (mainly based on potency ): First-generation: • Etidronate (least potent ) • Clodronate • Tiludronate Second -generation: -100 times more potent than the first generation • Alendronate • Pamidronate • Ibadronate Third-generation: ,000 times more potent than the first generation • Risedronate • Zoledronate

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You start a patient on alendronate for osteoporosis . The patient enquires about the side effects and their management. Which of the following measures would you not recommend to decrease oesophageal irritation ?

options.b: Use of proton pump inhibitor at bedtime

mcqs.explanation: Bisphosphonates are not recommended to be administered with food to minimize esophageal irritation . Oral bisphosphonates have very limited bioavailability (<1-10 %). Bisphosphonates are recommended to be administered after an overnight fast with a full glass of water at least 30 minutes before breakfast. Options A and B- Remaining upright for 30 minutes after dosing and taking proton pump inhibitors at bedtime can decrease the symptoms . Option C- As esophageal irritation is due to the local direct effect of the oral formulation, shifting to intravenous formulations reduces the symptoms . Note - The prescribing information of all the oral bisphosphonates states that it has to be taken along with tap or filtered water, and not mineral water as it contains higher amounts of calcium which can interfere with the absorption of bisphosphonates . It is prudent to inform patients to not have the medications with water having higher calcium levels .641

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following conditions is teriparatide indicated ?
mcqs.explanation: Teriparatide is indicated in severe osteoporosis . Teriparatide is a recombinant human parathyroid preparation. It increases bone formation especially when given in low doses and intermittently . Although it may be more effective than bisphosphonates and estrogen , it has to be administered subcutaneously every day. Hence it indicated mostly in severe osteoporosis . Teriparatide increases the risk of osteosarcoma and it is contraindicated in conditions that causes high risk of osteosarcoma such as: • Paget disease • Prior h/o of radiotherapy • Young adults with open epiphysis • Unexplained elevated ALP • Hypercalcemia Abaloparatide is also a PTHrP preparation available.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs promotes bone formation?
mcqs.explanation: Teriparatide increases bone formation especially when given in low doses and intermittently . Teriparatide is a recombinant preparation of parathyroid hormone. The pharmacologic activity of teriparatide , which is similar to the physiologic activity of PTH , includes stimulating osteoblast function, increasing gastrointestinal calcium absorption, and increasing renal tubular reabsorption of calcium. Although it may be more effective than bisphosphonates and estrogen , it has to be administered subcutaneously every day. Hence it is indicated mostly in severe osteoporosis . Teriparatide increases the risk of osteosarcoma and it is contraindicated in conditions that cause high risk of osteosarcoma such as: • Paget disease • Prior h/o of radiotherapy • Young adults with open epiphysis • Unexplained elevated ALP • Hypercalcemia Option A: Calcitonin decreases bone resorption. Option B: Raloxifene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator, which decreases bone resorption. It is used to prevent and treat osteoporosis in postmenopausal women. Option C: Bisphosphonates like alendronate and etidronate decrease bone resorption.642

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following acts by causing both decreased bone resorption and increased bone formation?
mcqs.explanation: Strontium ranelate acts by both decreased bone resorption and increased bone formation. It is generally reserved for severe osteoporosis . Due to an increased incidence of myocardial infarction and other cardiovascular events, the use is restricted in all the approved regions. Option B- Ibandronate which is a bisphosphonate , decreases bone resorption only. Option C- The pharmacologic activity of teriparatide , which is similar to the physiologic activity of PTH, includes stimulating osteoblast function, increasing gastrointestinal calcium absorption, and increasing renal tubular reabsorption of calcium. Option D- Calcitonin also decreases bone resorption.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old patient with severe backache has a T-score of -3. He is started on a monoclonal antibody against RANKL. Identify the drug.
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history depicts a case of osteoporosis . Denosumab is a monoclonal antibody against RANKL that is indicated in the treatment of osteoporosis . It inhibits the binding of RANKL to RANK receptors on osteoclasts and thereby inhibiting the activation of osteoclast and also promotes their apoptosis . Options A and D: Romosozumab and blosozumab are monoclonal antibodies against sclerostin (sclerostin blocks osteoblast proliferation). Option C: Odanacatib is an inhibitor of cathepsin K which is an enzyme in osteoclast that facilitates bone resorption.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A post -menopausal lady who is taking estrogen as part of her hormone replacement therapy reads about raloxifene on the internet and wants to change her current treatment . Which of the following is not an advantage of using raloxifene over estrogen ?

options.d: No increase in incidence of breast carcinoma

mcqs.explanation: Raloxifene causes a 3-fold increase in deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. It is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) with the following actions: • Agonist actions: • Bone - increases bone mineral density and reduces the risk of vertebral fracture • Lipids - increases the risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. • Antagonist actions: • Breast - incidence of breast carcinoma is reduced • Uterus - endometrial hyperplasia is avoided

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old patient with chronic kidney disease developed secondary hyperparathyroidism for which he was treated appropriately , and was started on cinacalcet . Which of the following best describes the mechanism of action of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Cinacalcet is a calcimimetic agent .643 It activates the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) in the parathyroids and blocks PTH secretion . Cinacalcet is a type II calcimimetic agent , it means that it needs either Ca2+ or some other agonist to activate CaSR. It is indicated for secondary hyperparathyroidism due to chronic kidney disease and tumor of parathyroid gland. Type I calcimimetic agents are those which can activate CaSR directly such as aminoglycoside and polylysine .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old male patient who requires weekly hemodialysis is started on sevelamer. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of action of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Sevelamer is a phosphate binder indicated in chronic kidney disease . Sevelamer is a nonabsorbable polymer that acts as a nonselective anion exchanger that lowers serum phosphate concentration. It is indicated to lower phosphate levels in patients with chronic kidney disease who are on dialysis. Note : Patiromer is a potassium binder approved for use in hyperkalemia.644

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not cause insulin release ?
mcqs.explanation: Rosiglitazone does not increase insulin release from the beta cells of the pancreas. Rosiglitazone is a thiazolidinedione that acts by activating PPAR -gamma (nuclear receptor ) which induces several genes involved in lipid and glucose metabolism and thereby , decreases insulin resistance . Nateglinide (a meglitinide ) and glimepiride , tolbutamide (both sulfonylureas ) are insulin secretagogues that act by inhibiting the ATP -sensitive K+ channels of the beta cells of the pancreas to cause insulin release .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Insulin release due to the closure of K+ channels is seen with?
mcqs.explanation: 651 Repaglinide acts by increasing insulin secretion by blockage of ATP -sensitive K+ channels of the beta cells of the pancreas. When ATP -sensitive K+ channels are blocked , it will lead to depolarization of beta cells and the release of insulin. Sulfonylureas also act by this similar mechanism. Option B - Metformin is an insulin sensitizer and also inhibits gluconeogenesis and increases hepatic uptake of glucose . Option C - Exenatide is a GLP -1 analog. Option D - Sitagliptin is a DPP-4 inhibitor.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A diabetic patient being treated with an oral hypoglycemic agent develops dilutional hyponatremia. Which one of the following could be responsible for the effect ?
mcqs.explanation: Chlorpropamide use is associated with dilutional hyponatremia. It is a first generation sulfonylurea and can lead to SIADH. Along with alcohol use ,it can also lead to disulfiram-like reaction.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 62-year-old woman presents with complaints of fatigue . She is a known case of type 2 diabetes mellitus on treatment . On examination, there is pallor and knuckle pigmentation . Which of the following drugs could have caused her condition?
mcqs.explanation: Metformin can cause vitamin B12 deficiency which manifests as megaloblastic anemia (pallor, fatigue ) with knuckle pigmentation . The most common side effect of metformin is GI intolerance as nausea, bloating, abdominal cramps and diarrhoea. Note : The exact reason why metformin causes vitamin B12 deficiency is not known. The proposed mechanisms include :652 • Alterations in small bowel motility , which stimulates bacterial overgrowth and consequential vitamin B12 deficiency • Competitive inhibition or inactivation of vitamin B12 absorption • Alterations in intrinsic factor (IF) levels and interaction with the cubilin endocytic receptor . • Inhibition of the calcium-dependent absorption of the vitamin B12 -IF complex at the terminal ileum .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect regarding metformin?

options.a: Causes little or no hypoglycemia in non-diabetic patients
options.c: Increases peripheral utilization of glucose and decreases absorption of glucose from the intestine
options.d: Increase intake of calcium may prevent metformin induced B12 malabsorption

mcqs.explanation: Metformin does not act by increasing insulin secretion . It decreases insulin resistance and increases the peripheral utilization of glucose . Metformin is a biguanide that acts by activation of AMP-dependent protein kinase activation and thereby mediates a series of actions that helps in reducing hepatic glucose production . Option A - Metformin has minimal to nil effect on insulin secretion and as a result , has minimal or no hypoglycemic effect in non-diabetic patients . Option C - Metformin reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis , increases the insulin-mediated peripheral glucose uptake and also decreases the absorption of glucose from the gut . Option D - Increase intake of calcium will decrease the B12 malabsorption because metformin interferes with Ca2+ dependent B12 absorption.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the central pharmacological action of metformin in type 2 diabetes ?
mcqs.explanation: The central pharmacological action of metformin is to reduce hepatic glucose production by inhibiting gluconeogenesis . Metformin effect is mainly mediated through activation of AMPK and altering the energy dynamics at mitochondrial respiration. Option A - The reduction in glucose absorption can also occur but the contribution to the antihyperglycemic action is not significant Option B - Metformin increases peripheral glucose utilization by both insulin-dependent (reducing insulin resistance) and independent ways. But the current evidence does not support the reduction in insulin resistance as the primary mechanism of metformin's action. Option D - Recent evidence shows blunting of glucagon effects as one of the mechanisms of metformin's action Note : All are mechanisms of metformin, however, the key action is Option C and it is the most appropriate answer.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 58-year-old woman with chronic kidney disease with recently diagnosed Type 2 DM was started on metformin therapy . Her repeat eGFR was 40/min/1.73 m2 . Which of the following is not true regarding the further management of this lady?

options.a: Metformin dose has to be decreased.
options.b: Metformin should be discontinued and replaced with insulin.
options.c: eGFR should be measured at least annually in her.
options.d: eGFR is preferred over serum creatinine concentration to assess renal function for metformin therapy.

mcqs.explanation: 653 According to current guidelines (KDIGO 2020 ), metformin should be discontinued only in patients with eGFR less than 30 ml/min/1.73 m2 or kidney failure. Metformin dose should be reduced when the eGFR is less than 45 ml/min/1.73 m2 . Metformin is excreted by the kidneys, and accumulation with reduced kidney function may increase the risk of lactic acidosis (due to inhibition of hepatic gluconeogenesis ). It is contraindicated below eGFR<30. eGFR is obtained at baseline and at least annually in all patients taking metformin. It is recommended that the eligibility of CKD patients for metformin administration be changed from one based on a single laboratory parameter (blood creatinine concentration) to one that provides a better estimate of kidney function in patients with kidney disease i.e., glomerular filtration rate estimating equation (eGFR).

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 13 -year-old boy is diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus . Which of the following drugs can be prescribed ?
mcqs.explanation: Metformin can be prescribed as it is FDA approved for medical treatment of type 2 diabetes in pediatric population as young as 10 years of age . It is available as a liquid oral formulation (100mg /ml) for pediatric use .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect regarding pioglitazone ?

options.a: Metabolised in the liver by CYP3A
options.b: Selective agonist for the nuclear peroxisome proliferator activated receptor
options.c: It can modulate the transcription of genes for carbohydrate and fat metabolism in the absence of insulin
options.d: It should be avoided in any patient with cardiovascular disease

mcqs.explanation: Pioglitazone need not be avoided in all patients with cardiovascular disease . Pioglitazone is known to cause fluid retention and edema and is therefore avoided in patients who have heart failure. It is not avoided in all cardiovascular diseases . Option A - Pioglitazone is metabolized by CYP3A4 and CYP2C8. Option B - Pioglitazone is a selective agonist of nuclear peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR ). It modulates the expression of genes involved in lipid and glucose metabolism , insulin signal transduction and adipocyte differentiation . These effects increase the sensitivity of the tissues to insulin. Option C - Pioglitazone does not increase insulin levels in the body. It sensitizes the tissues to the action of insulin. Hence , insulin is needed for the action of pioglitazone . However, it does not need insulin to modulate the expression of genes .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old diabetic man on treatment presents with complaints of difficulty reading. Fundoscopy shows the following findings. Which antidiabetic drug class is likely to cause this?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows diabetic macular edema, with hard exudates surrounding the blood vessels . It is a rare adverse effect seen with thiazolidinediones , and it resolves when the drug is discontinued .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An elderly man was diagnosed with hypertension 2 years ago and has been on losartan. During a routine health checkup , his HbA1c was found to be 7.3%. Which of the following is a better alternative to losartan for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: 654 This patient has hypertension and diabetes mellitus (HbA1c >6.5% is diagnostic for diabetes ). Telmisartan would be a better alternative to losartan in patients with both hypertension and diabetes , due to its additional PPAR gamma agonist action. PPAR gamma agonists act by inducing several insulins sensitizing genes and thereby reducing the overall insulin resistance . While other angiotensin receptor blockers have been found to have PPAR gamma action, telmisartan has the highest and has been extensively studied in diabetes .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old woman with a known history of hypertension and dyslipidemia was admitted for evaluation of recurrent TIA . On workup, she was diagnosed with diabetes mellitus . Which of the following drugs should be avoided in the management of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Rosiglitazone should be avoided as it increases the risk of cardiovascular events like myocardial infarction and stroke. It remains banned in Europe , India, and other countries . It has not been withdrawn in the US and is marketed with a black box warning of increased risk of myocardial infarction and stroke. Option A: Several studies have shown relative cardiovascular safety of pioglitazone over rosiglitazone. Option C: Metformin use is associated with decreased risk of microvascular complications in diabetes . Option D: Troglitazone was withdrawn due to increased hepatotoxicity .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
