mcqs.question: A professional boxer is diagnosed with diabetes mellitus . He is concerned about weight changes as a side effect of anti-diabetic drugs and explains that he has to maintain his current weight category . Which of the following will you prescribe ?
mcqs.explanation: Saxagliptin, a DPP-4 inhibitor, can be prescribed for this patient as it has a weight -neutral effect . Note : *Metformin classification is a bit difficult . It can cause mild weight loss in some patients but few authorities do consider metformin as weight neutral.EFFECT DRUGS Weight gain Sulfonylureas , Insulin,Thiazo lidinediones Weight loss GLP -1 analogues , Pramlintid e, SGLT -2 inhibitors, Metfor min* Weight neut ral Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors, DPP-4 inhibitors

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In a middle -aged diabetic patient with chronic kidney disease stage 5, which of the following drugs can be given safely without altering the dose ?
mcqs.explanation: Linagliptin can be given safely without altering the dose for this patient .655 Linagliptin is a dipeptidyl -peptidase -4 (DPP-4) inhibitor and is eliminated by the hepatobiliary route . Hence no dosage adjustment is needed in renal failure. It is used in type 2 diabetes as monotherapy or as combination therapy with other drugs when metformin is not tolerated or contraindicated . Other DPP-4 inhibitors like sitagliptin , vildagliptin, saxagliptin, alogliptin show renal elimination.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about dapagliflozin ?

options.a: It is indicated in heart failure
options.d: It will increase the risk of fractures

mcqs.explanation: Dapagliflozin does not cause weight gain. It results in weight loss. It acts by inhibiting the SGLT2 (sodium glucose -2) transporter, which is present on the proximal segment of the renal tubule and responsible for the reabsorption of 80-90% of filtered glucose . It inhibits glucose reabsorption resulting in glycosuria and a decrease in blood glucose level . It is effective orally. The common adverse effects include urinary tract infections and genital mycotic infections due to the high glucose content of the urine and also the high risk of fractures. Other SGLT2 inhibitors include empagliflozin , canagliflozin, and ertugliflozin . Note : Empagliflozin has been found to decrease the risk of mortality from cardiovascular causes in diabetic patients . Dapagliflozin has been recently approved by the FDA for the treatment of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction(HFrEF) in both diabetic and non-diabetic patients .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with diabetes mellitus came to the OPD with a history suggestive of recurrent episodes of hypoglycemia . She was recently put on combination therapy . Her symptoms are least likely to be caused by which of the following drugs?
mcqs.explanation: Acarbose is least likely to cause hypoglycemia among the given options . It is an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor. It inhibits the intestinal degradation and absorption of starch and disaccharides and thereby lowers the postprandial rise in glucose levels . It has no role in stimulating insulin secretion and is therefore , least likely to cause hypoglycemia during monotherapy. Insulin and insulin secretagogues like sulfonylureas (gliclazide ) and meglitinides (repaglinide) can result in hypoglycemia .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: While at a bakery, a man complains of giddiness and palpitations . As the only doctor there , you're asked for help . The man says he had just taken his diabetic medications and shows a prescription listing insulin and acarbose. What would you give for immediate management?
mcqs.explanation: Giddiness and palpitations after taking insulin and acarbose are suggestive of hypoglycemia. Honey is the most suitable agent among the given options for the management of hypoglycemia in a patient who is on acarbose therapy . Acarbose is an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor. It inhibits the intestinal degradation of starch and disaccharides into glucose . Honey contains monosaccharides (fructose and glucose ) that do not need to be broken down and are directly absorbed and would be beneficial in hypoglycemia656 caused by alpha-glucosidase inhibitors. However, glucose or dextrose tablets is recommended when available. While alpha-glucosidase inhibitors themselves do not cause hypoglycemia , the risk of hypoglycemia is increased when they are taken along with insulin or insulin secretagogues . Disaccharides and complex carbohydrates will not be completely broken down and absorbed in a patient who is on alpha-glucosidase inhibitors. Option B - Bread predominantly contains complex carbohydrates like starch Option C - Sugar contains sucrose , a disaccharide Option D - Cake contains sugar (disaccharide ) and other complex carbohydrates

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 52-year-old diabetic patient presented to the ED with complaints of chest pain on exertion. Laboratory tests showed dyslipidemia and features of metabolic syndrome. Which of the following drugs was recently approved for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Saroglitazar is a dual PPAR alpha/gamma agonist and is approved for diabetic dyslipidemia only in India. Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs ) are a superfamily of nuclear receptors involved in the regulation of energy homeostasis and metabolic function. It has three subtypes : • PPAR �o - reduces triglyceride level • PPAR \033 - causes insulin sensitization • PPAR \027 - enhances fatty acids metabolism Of the three PPAR isoforms, synthetic pharmaceutical ligands that activate PPARalpha (the antidyslipidemic fibrates) and PPARgamma (the antidiabetic thiazolidinediones ) have been studied extensively . Recently developed dual PPARalpha/gamma agonists combine the therapeutic effects of these drugs to be used in type 2 diabetes with dyslipidemia . Options A and C - Aleglitazar and muraglitazar are also dual PPAR alpha/gamma agonists but their development was halted due to increased risk of cardiovascular mortality. Option D - Rosiglitazone is a PPAR gamma agonist indicated in type 2 diabetes mellitus . It has been withdrawn from many countries including India due to increased cardiovascular mortality.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is approved as an adjunctive treatment for type 2 diabetes mellitus ?
mcqs.explanation: Bromocriptine is a dopamine agonist that has been approved as an adjunctive treatment for diabetes mellitus . The exact mechanism is unknown but may involve alteration in circadian (hypothalamic) control of blood glucose levels . A fast-release , low-dose formulation of bromocriptine is approved for type 2 diabetes that has to be administered within 3 hours of awakening. Option B - Phenytoin is a Na+ channel blocker and is an antiepileptic drug Option C - Ropinirole is an antiparkinsonian drug that is a dopamine agonist and is also approved for treatment of restless leg syndrome657 Option D - Metoclopramide is a 5HT4 agonist and D2 blocker and used as an antiemetic agent

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 54-year-old woman comes to the diabetic clinic for follow up. Her lipid profile shows high LDL cholesterol . Which bile acid sequestrant would you prescribe for her?
mcqs.explanation: Colesevelam can be prescribed for her as it is the only bile acid sequestrant that is specifically approved for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus . It is used to reduce LDL cholesterol and improve glycemic control in diabetics .658

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the half-life of endogenously secreted insulin?
mcqs.explanation: Endogenously secreted insulin has a half-life of only 5-6 minutes due to its extensive hepatic clearance.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old nurse was brought to the casualty with seizures and altered mental status . Her plasma glucose was 35 mg/dl. Which test would help to rule out the possibility of exogenous insulin administration?
mcqs.explanation: C-peptide can be used to rule out the possibility of factitious hypoglycemia resulting from exogenously administered insulin. Endogenous insulin is initially synthesized as preproinsulin that is processed to proinsulin inside beta cells . Proinsulin is released by secretory granules after processing it to form insulin and C-peptide . Synthetic insulin usually lacks C-peptide , so in factitious hypoglycemia secondary to exogenous insulin administration, plasma insulin will be elevated , but there will be suppression of C-peptide and proinsulin, and insulin to C-peptide ratio will be greater than one. On the other hand, insulinomas and insulin secretagogues like sulfonylureas stimulate endogenous insulin production . As a result , plasma insulin, C-peptide , and proinsulin levels will be all elevated . The only way to differentiate between insulinoma and insulin secretagogues -induced hypoglycemia is by detecting the drug, e.g., sulfonylurea , in the blood or urine.665 C-peptide has no known physiological function or receptor . It has a half-life of about 30 min.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient requires the shortest acting formulation of insulin to prevent postprandial hyperglycemia . Which of the following formulations would you choose ?
mcqs.explanation: Inhaled insulin is the shortest acting formulation of insulin.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient on basal-bolus regimen for type 1 diabetes wants an alternative to multiple daily injections. She read about the new drug Afrezza and wants to know more about it. Which of the following is not true about this formulation?

options.b: Can be used as single or multiple pre meal doses
options.c: If multiple doses used then no need of basal insulin

mcqs.explanation: Afrezza should be used in combination with basal long-acting insulin to supplement it. Option A - Afrezza is an inhaled insulin that is available in dry powder form. It is the shortest acting insulin (2-3 hours) and it reduces the use of short-acting injectable insulin. Adverse events include cough and throat irritation . Option B - It is taken pre-meal to reduce postprandial hyperglycemia . Option D - Afrezza is contraindicated in active smokers, asthmatics and COPD patients .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following preparations of insulin is not rapid-acting?
mcqs.explanation: All of the following preparations of insulin are rapid-acting except glargine. Insulin preparations and duration of action Short-acting: • Insulin lispro, Insulin aspart, Insulin glulisine : 3-4 hours • Regular insulin: 4-6 hours Long-acting: • Insulin NPH: -16 hours • Insulin detemir : -24 hours • Insulin glargine: -24 hours • Insulin degludec : 24-42 hours

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Identify the correct insulin combination option.
mcqs.explanation: Detemir is a long-acting insulin and aspart is a rapid-acting insulin and matches with 1 and 2 respectively in the image showing basal-bolus regimen.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old patient with type 1 diabetes presented with complaints of vomiting and abdominal pain. On examination, she had fast, deep breathing with a fruity odor. Her capillary blood glucose was 450mg/dL. What is the clinical concern associated with administering insulin alone?
mcqs.explanation: 666 Deep breathing (Kussmaul respiration) and fruity breath (acetone odor) in a symptomatic patient with type 1 diabetes are suggestive of diabetic ketoacidosis . Insulin therapy alone in a patient with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) may result in hypokalemia. DKA is usually associated with a major K+ deficit . Potassium loss is caused by an extracellular shift of potassium (in exchange with hydrogen ions) due to acidosis. Much of the shifted extracellular potassium is lost due to emesis and osmotic diuresis . When insulin therapy is initiated for DKA, the serum K+ is shifted intracellularly . Dangerous hypokalemia might occur if K+ supplementation is not initiated subsequently . Insulin should be withheld if the serum level of potassium is below 3.3 mmol/L .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You see a nurse administering an insulin preparation that appears cloudy white . Which formulation of insulin could it be?
mcqs.explanation: The formulation is most likely NPH insulin as it produces a cloudy or whitish solution in contrast to the clear appearance of other insulin solutions . NPH or isophane insulin is a suspension of native insulin complexed with zinc and protamine in phosphate buffer .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient was recently diagnosed with diabetes . She was prescribed the longest -acting insulin as it has the least risk of hypoglycemia . Which insulin preparation is she on?
mcqs.explanation: Insulin degludec has the maximum duration of action (24-42 hours) among long-acting insulins. It is sometimes considered an ultra long-acting insulin.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A diabetic patient is in the postoperative area following cardiac surgery. He is to be given intravenous insulin for optimal glycemic control and to avoid sternal wound infection . Which of the following should not be administered ?
mcqs.explanation: Insulin detemir is a long-acting insulin and should not be given intravenously or intramuscularly. It is only given via subcutaneous route. Options A, C, and D: Regular insulin and short-acting insulins (glulisine and aspart) can be given intravenously. While short-acting insulins are approved for intravenous administration under supervision, regular insulin is preferred in perioperative glycemic control due to the lesser risk of hypoglycemia . Intravenous insulin is used in diabetic ketoacidosis and other conditions where insulin requirements change drastically like perioperative period , labor, and in intensive care situations .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following insulin precipitates into a cloudy white precipitate when mixed with short acting insulins?
mcqs.explanation: Insulin glargine forms a cloudy white precipitate when mixed with short-acting insulins. Due to the acidic pH (4.0) of insulin glargine, it cannot be mixed with short-acting insulin preparations that are formulated at a neutral pH as it aggregates at neutral pH into a cloudy white667 precipitate . This reduces the effectiveness of the insulin dose . Insulin degludec and detemir have a pH of 7.4 that is very near to neutral pH and they do not form such aggregates when mixed with short-acting insulins. But the manufacturers do not advise manual mixing with short-acting insulin as it may alter the activity profile of the combination that can turn unpredictable . Degludec is available as an approved fixed -dose combination with aspart that can be used with predictable effects .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Composition of Lente insulin is:
mcqs.explanation: Lente insulin is an intermediate -acting insulin and is a combination of Ultralente and Semilente in the ratio of 7:3 Two types of insulin zinc suspensions have been produced . The one with large particles is crystalline and practically insoluble in water (Ultralente ). It is long-acting. The other has smaller particles and is amorphous (Semilente), is short-acting. Their 7:3 ratio mixture is called 'Lente insulin' and is intermediate -acting.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You are counseling a diabetic patient and teaching her the technique to self -administer insulin at home every day. Which of the following sites would you not suggest as the preferred site for insulin administration?
mcqs.explanation: The medial part of the thigh is not a preferred site for insulin administration in patients . This is because of the relatively higher density of blood vessels and nerves in this area. Another consideration is that the inner thighs rub together while walking and may cause soreness at the injection sites . The preferred sites for insulin administration are: • Upper arm • Anterior and lateral aspects of the thigh • Buttocks • Abdomen (with the exception of a circle with a 2-inch radius around the navel) Rotation of the injection site is important to prevent lipodystrophy . However, rotating within one area is recommended (e.g., rotating injections systematically within the abdomen) rather than rotating to a different area with each injection. This helps decrease variability in absorption from day to day.668

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect regarding exenatide ?

options.b: It can be used for the treatment of type 1 diabetes mellitus

mcqs.explanation: Exenatide is not indicated in type 1 diabetes mellitus . Exenatide is a GLP -1 analog that acts as an insulin secretagogue . As the beta cells are already destroyed and do not secrete insulin in type 1 diabetes , there is no role of drugs that enhance insulin secretion . Option A - Exenatide is a GLP -1 analog and it is synthesized from exendin-4 Option C - It is a peptide and hence has to be administered subcutaneously Option D - It increases insulin secretion, decreases glucagon secretion , delays gastric emptying , and reduces food intake

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a GLP -1 receptor agonist?
mcqs.explanation: Pramlintide is an islet amyloid polypeptide (IAPP ) or amylin analogue . Amylin analogues reduce glucagon secretion , slows gastric emptying , and centrally decreases appetite . Options A, B and D - Liraglutide, semaglutide and exenatide are GLP -1 agonists.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is not true about pramlintide?

options.a: It can be used in both type 1 and type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.b: It has got weight reducing property by causing a central anorectic effect
options.c: It should not be administered with insulin in the same syringe

mcqs.explanation: Pramlintide is administered as a subcutaneous injection. Option A - It is a synthetic analogue of amylin and is approved for both type 1 and type 2 diabetes mellitus669 Option B - It has weight reducing property by causing a central anorectic effect . It acts by reducing glucagon secretion , delaying gastric emptying and decreasing appetite . Option C - It should not be administered with insulin in the same syringe because of a difference in pH

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old diabetic woman comes for follow up. Her BMI is 32 kg/m2 despite several months of diet and exercise . Which of the following is the drug preferred for her condition?
mcqs.explanation: Liraglutide is approved for the management of obesity . GLP -1 is a physiological regulator of appetite and calorie intake, and the GLP -1 receptor is present in several areas of the brain involved in appetite regulation . Liraglutide is a GLP -1 analog and lowers body weight by decreasing calorie intake. Note : FDA has recently approved semaglutide subcutaneous injection once weekly for chronic weight management. This is for use in patients with obesity and overweight individuals with at least one weight -related condition such as type 2 diabetes , hypertension or dyslipidemia .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man comes for a routine health check-up. He has a family history of medullary thyroid cancer. His thyroid examination is normal but his HbA1c is found to be 7.5%. In view of his history, which of the following should not be prescribed for him?
mcqs.explanation: GLP -1 analogues are contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer and in patients with MEN 2 syndrome. GLP -1 analogues cause thyroid C-cell tumours at clinically relevant exposures in rodents. However, studies have not yet shown if they cause thyroid C-cell tumours like medullary thyroid carcinoma in humans.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with superior mesenteric artery occlusion underwent extensive bowel resection . Following surgery, he developed short bowel syndrome and has been on parenteral nutrition. Which of the following drugs would be beneficial for his condition?
mcqs.explanation: Teduglutide is a GLP -2 analog and is approved for the treatment of short bowel syndrome. GLP -2 binds to enteric neurons and endocrine cells , stimulating the release of a number of hormones such as insulin-like growth factor. This stimulates mucosal epithelial growth and enhances fluid absorption. GLP -1 analogs: • Exenatide • Liraglutide • Albiglutide • Dulaglutide • Lixisenatide • Semaglutide Note : GLP -1 analogs are used for the treatment of Type II diabetes mellitus .670

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Identify the true statement regarding teduglutide .

options.a: It is not recommended for patients with colorectal cancer
options.d: It promotes gastric acid secretion and gastric emptying

mcqs.explanation: Teduglutide can potentially cause bowel cancer, therefore it is not recommended for patients with active malignancies. It is a GLP -2 analog that has been recently approved for the treatment of short bowel syndrome. It inhibits gastric acid secretion and gastric emptying , stimulates mucosal epithelial growth and intestinal blood flow , and enhances nutrient and fluid absorption The drug has a t1/2 of 1–2 hours and is administered subcutaneously once daily. Note : GLP -1 analogs are used for the treatment of Type II diabetes mellitus .671

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a natural estrogen ?
mcqs.explanation: Ethinylestradiol is a synthetic estrogen . Natural estrogens are: • Estradiol • Estriol • Estrone

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old postmenopausal lady is on estrogen as part of her hormone replacement therapy. Which of the following statements about estrogen is not true?
mcqs.explanation: Estrogen causes an increase in plasma HDL levels . Estrogen also causes an increase in triglycerides , apolipoprotein levels , and an increase in the turnover of LDL receptors .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A post -menopausal lady who is on estrogen therapy for hot flashes is concerned about its adverse effects . She is not at an increased risk of developing which of the following cancers?
mcqs.explanation: Women receiving estrogen therapy do not have an increased risk of developing gall bladder carcinoma . Long-term estrogen therapy can increase the risk of gall stones . Although gall stones can be associated with the development of gall bladder carcinoma , there is no direct correlation between long term estrogen therapy and gall bladder carcinoma . Estrogen therapy has been associated with breast, endometrial and hepatocellular carcinoma .680

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following conditions is hormone replacement therapy not helpful ?
mcqs.explanation: Hormone replacement therapy (HRT ) is not helpful in coronary heart disease . Progesterone used in the HRT is associated with an increased risk of coronary artery disease , thromboembolism, and related mortality. Estrogens promote coagulation and thromboembolic episodes . Options A and B: Estrogen is helpful in flushing and local preparations are preferred for vaginal atrophy. Option D: Estrogen is beneficial for osteoporosis if it is started before the onset of significant osteoporosis . Note : The use of HRT for cardiovascular benefits is quite controversial. The current consensus is that the HRT should be started only after assessing the benefit /risk profile individually and is not indicated for the prevention of cardiovascular events in all menopausal women as it was previously advocated .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Progestin dose remains constant throughout the cycle in which of the following type of combined contraceptive pills ?
mcqs.explanation: Monophasic pills contain constant amounts of progesterone and estrogen that is taken daily for 21 days, followed by a 7-day pill-free period. Biphasic and triphasic pills have variable amounts of active ingredients (especially progesterone ) that mimic the natural changes in the hormonal levels in the menstrual cycle . These pills reduce the total amount of steroids that needs to be administered .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A young lady who is on oral contraceptive pills refrains from taking any drug even for minor ailments due to the fear of contraceptive failure. Which of the following drugs can be taken safely ?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given drugs, aspirin use is least likely to cause contraceptive failure. Option B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics like tetracycline suppress the intestinal flora and interfere with the enterohepatic circulation of estrogen . This leads to lowering of plasma estrogen levels and can result in contraceptive failure. Options C and D: Enzyme inducers like phenytoin and rifampicin increase the metabolism of oral contraceptives and can cause contraceptive failure.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old lady has been on anti-epileptic therapy since childhood and now comes to the OPD seeking advice on a suitable method of contraception . Which contraceptive method should be avoided in her?
mcqs.explanation: Oral contraceptives must be avoided or used cautiously in epilepsy . The most important aspect to consider is the drug interactions between anti-epileptic drugs and contraceptives . There is no conclusive evidence on whether estrogen is beneficial or harmful for681 seizure control. Note : Convulsive disorder is not an absolute contraindication; it is safe to avoid but can be used with caution.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about oral contraceptive pills is true?

options.b: It is protective against ovarian cancer
options.c: OCP are used in treatment mastalgia
options.d: Rifamipicin decreases the metabolism of OCP

mcqs.explanation: Oral contraceptive pills (OCP) protect against ovarian cancer. This benefit is thought to be due to the prolonged suppression of gonadotropin stimulation of the ovary on long-term use of OCPs. Other benefits of oral contraceptive pills: • Lesser incidence of endometrial carcinoma due to progestin component in OCP • Regularisation of menstrual cycles results in relief of dysmenorrhea and menorrhagia • Reduced incidence of fibrocystic breast disease and ovarian cysts • Endometriosis and pelvic inflammatory disease are improved Option A: The estrogen component of combined oral contraceptive pills is mainly responsible for venous thromboembolism. Option C: OCP is not used in the treatment of mastalgia. Mastalgia , chloasma, and breakthrough bleeding are known side effects of oral contraceptive pills . Option D: OCPs are metabolized by CYP3A4 enzymes . Rifampicin is a strong inducer of CYP3A4. Hence , if administered together , rifampicin can cause enhanced metabolism of OCPs and may lead to contraceptive failure.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old lady on oral combined contraceptive pills misses a single dose and reports to you in the OPD the next morning . What will be the most appropriate advice to this patient ?

options.a: Continue taking the next dose as scheduled
options.b: Double the next dose to make up for the missed dose
options.c: Interrupt the course and start taking the medications again on 5th day of bleeding
options.d: Start a fresh course of OCP again

mcqs.explanation: The most appropriate advice for this patient who has missed a single dose of the oral contraceptive pill (OCP) is to double the next dose to make up for the missed dose . Missed dose considerations for oral combined contraceptive pills : • If a single dose is missed - a double dose can be taken on the next day to make up for the missed dose . • If two or more doses are missed on subsequent days - the last missed pill has to be taken along with the present pill and alternative methods of contraceptive must be used for the next 7 days. • If the pills were missed on the last week (days 15-21 ) - omit the hormone-free interval by finishing the hormonal pills in the current pack and starting the new pack from the next day.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following patients is combined oral contraceptive pills not absolutely contraindicated?

options.a: A perimenopausal woman with coronary heart disease
options.b: A 23 -year-old lady with a past history of hepatic adenoma
options.c: A multiparous lady with abnormal undiagnosed vaginal bleeding

mcqs.explanation: 682 A migraine headache is a relative contraindication for the use of combined oral contraceptives . Migraine with focal neurological symptoms is an absolute contraindication to combined oral contraceptive use . Absolute contraindications to combined oral contraceptive use : • Presence or history of thromboembolic disease , cerebrovascular disease , myocardial infarction, coronary artery disease • Congenital hyperlipidemia • Known or suspected carcinoma of the breast, female reproductive tract • Known or suspected pregnancy • Past or present liver tumors or impaired liver function • Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding . • Migraine with focal neurological symptoms Relative contraindications to combined oral contraceptive use : • Migraine headaches in >35 yrs female • Hypertension • Diabetes mellitus • Obstructive jaundice of pregnancy • Prior oral contraceptive use • Gallbladder disease

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Progestin-only pills do not act by which of the following mechanisms?

options.d: Eliciting an inflammatory action in the endometrium

mcqs.explanation: Copper intrauterine devices elicit an inflammatory reaction within the endometrium . This impairs sperm viability, motility , and fertilization. All the following actions contribute to the contraceptive action of progestin -only pills : • The effectiveness of this drug is largely due to the thickening of cervical mucus which in turn impair sperm penetration . • Inhibits ovulation via exerting negative feedback on the hypothalamus (GnRH). This leads to the absence of the FSH and LH surge , which is essential to mature the dominant follicle and trigger ovulation. • Interfere with the implantation of a zygote by altering the endometrial environment. The major reason women discontinue the use of progestin -only contraceptives is breakthrough bleeding .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old lady, P2L2 , has been taking depot medroxy progesterone acetate as a contraceptive . Which of the following best describes the formulation?
mcqs.explanation: 683 Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA) is a long-acting progestin -only injection formulation. DMPA is administered every 3 months intramuscularly as a contraceptive .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following progesterone is used in emergency contraception ?
mcqs.explanation: Levonorgestrel is the progesterone that is used in emergency contraception . Levonorgestrel -containing regimens are considered the standard regimen now. Option B: Micronised progesterone is indicated for amenorrhea and to counteract estrogen effects on the uterus . Option C: Norgesterone is usually used along with ethinyl estradiol for regular contraception . Option D: Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate is a long-acting depot preparation indicated for long-term contraception .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A newly married couple came to the OPD saying that they had unprotected intercourse two days back but are not desiring a baby at present . Which of the following drugs can be prescribed in this case?
mcqs.explanation: Ulipristal is a selective progesterone receptor modulator (SPRM) that can be given as an emergency contraceptive in this case. It should be administered within 5 days of unprotected intercourse . It inhibits ovulation by suppressing LH surge as well as by direct effect on follicular rupture . In addition, its action on the endometrium can interfere with implantation.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The standard emergency contraceptive pill regimen, levonorgestrel can be taken up to how many hours after unprotected intercourse ?
mcqs.explanation: Levonorgestrel regimen can be taken within 72 hours after unprotected intercourse but is most effective when taken as early as possible. Levonorgestrel for emergency contraception can be taken as either of the following : • 2 tablets of 0.75 mg 12 hours apart • 1.5 mg single -dose

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 20 -year old lady came to the OPD with complaints of missed period . You diagnose her to be 5 weeks pregnant but she is not willing to continue the pregnancy. You decide to prescribe her a drug that has anti-progestational activity. Which of the following drugs would you choose ?
mcqs.explanation: Mifepristone (RU-486) has potent anti-progestational (abortive activity) and significant anti-glucocorticoid and antiandrogenic activity. Options A and B: Levonorgestrel and desogestrel are progesterone preparations. Option C: Misoprostol is a synthetic prostaglandin (PGE1) preparation.684

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In the treatment of which of the following patients will you not consider clomiphene citrate?

options.b: A 48-year old perimenopausal woman with hot flashes

mcqs.explanation: Clomiphene citrate is not used in the treatment of hot flashes . Option A- Clomiphene increases gonadotropin secretion and stimulates ovulation. It mainly acts by blocking the inhibitory actions of estrogen on gonadotropin release from the pituitary gland. It is primarily indicated in the management of infertility . Option C - In men also, clomiphene increases gonadotropin secretion and promotes spermatogenesis . However, success rates are low. Option D - Studies have shown clomiphene citrate to be effective in treating and preventing short-lasting unilateral neuralgiform headache attacks (SUNCT). It has not yet been FDA-approved for the treatment of SUNCT.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old lady, diagnosed with breast cancer, is started on a selective estrogen receptor modulator. Identify the drug.
mcqs.explanation: Raloxifene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator. It has agonist action on bone and antagonist action on the breast and uterus . It is used in the treatment and prevention of osteoporosis and in breast cancer prevention in high-risk postmenopausal women.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old lady who is on tamoxifen, for the treatment of breast cancer is worried about its side effects . Which of the following side effects of tamoxifen is least likely to occur in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Tamoxifen acts as an estrogen receptor antagonist in breast tissues . The use of tamoxifen in carcinoma of breast patients decreases the incidence of carcinoma in opposite breasts. The estrogen agonistic action of tamoxifen and its consequences are: • Uterine endometrium - endometrial hypertrophy , vaginal bleeding , and endometrial cancer • Coagulation system - thromboembolism leading to pulmonary embolism (tamoxifen decreases the level of antithrombin III and protein C in the blood) • Bone metabolism - increase in bone mineral density • Liver - alterations of blood lipid profile • Cataract

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a selective estrogen receptor down regulator?
mcqs.explanation: Fulvestrant is a selective estrogen receptor down-regulator. It does not have estrogen agonistic activity for any tissue and is regarded as a pure estrogen antagonist.685 Tamoxifen, toremifene , and raloxifene are selective estrogen receptor modulators with the agonist or antagonist action at different tissues .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an aromatase inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Exemestane is an aromatase inhibitor. Estrogen is locally produced from androgen by the action of the aromatase enzyme. Locally synthesized estrogens play an important role in the development of breast cancer because they are estrogen -dependent for proliferation. Aromatase inhibitors decrease estrogen synthesis and are widely used now in the treatment of breast cancer in postmenopausal women. Aromatase inhibitors are: • Letrozole • Anastrozole • Exemestane (Irreversible inhibitor)

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You decide to change the chemotherapeutic regimen of a patient with breast cancer from tamoxifen to an aromatase inhibitor. Which of the following is not an advantage of the latter in the treatment of breast cancer?

options.a: No increase in risk of venous thromboembolism
options.b: No increase in risk of endometrial cancer
options.c: Can be used in advanced cases which are tamoxifen-resistant

mcqs.explanation: Aromatase inhibitors lack the property of maintaining bone mineral density when compared to tamoxifen. Aromatase inhibitors dramatically reduce estrogen levels that result in a decrease in the risk of venous thromboembolism and also decreases the risk of endometrial hyperplasia /cancer. It is also indicated in tamoxifen-resistant advanced breast cancer.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Yuzpe 's regimen of emergency contraception consists of which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Yuzpe 's regimen of emergency contraception consists of a combination of levonorgestrel and ethinylestradiol . The regimen includes two doses at 12 hours intervals within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse . It has a higher incidence of nausea and vomiting and is less efficacious than progesterone only standard regimen. Methods of Emergency contraception :Drug Dose Levonorgestrel 0.75mg stat and after 12 hour s Ethinyl estradiol 50 �Mg + Nor gestrel 0.25 mg 2 tab stat and 2 tab after 12 h ours686 Drug Dose Conjugated estrogen 15 mg BD x 5 days Ethinyl Estradiol 2.5 mg BD X 5 days Copper IUDs Insertion within 5-7 days afte r accidental unprotected exp osure.Not suitable for rape vi ctims Centchroman 2 tablets (60 mg) to be taken t wice at an interval of 12 hou rs within 24 hours of interco urse. Ulipristal 30 mg within 120 hours

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You are an intern posted in the medicine ward and you notice the given dermatological finding in a patient with abdominal distension . Which of the following hormones is implicated in this finding?
mcqs.explanation: The image shown is of spider nevus and the hormone implicated in its development is estrogen . It is commonly seen in hyperestrogenic states such as pregnancy and in those taking estrogen -containing contraceptives . It can also be seen in male patients with cirrhosis due to the decreased ability of the liver to metabolize circulating estrogens , specifically estrone , which derives from the androgen androstenedione . Estrogens cause blood vessels to enlarge and dilate .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old man presents to the OPD with the following condition. Which of the following drugs can cause this adverse effect ?
mcqs.explanation: This is a case of gynecomastia which can occur as an adverse effect of spironolactone or ketoconazole or chlorpromazine. Spironolactone - decreases testosterone production , increases peripheral conversion of testosterone to estradiol , and displaces estradiol from their plasma-protein-binding sites Ketoconazole - decreases testosterone production and displaces testosterone from their binding sites Chlorpromazine (neuroleptics ) - increase prolactin release by blocking the inhibitory action of dopamine on prolactin Clomiphene and tamoxifen are used mainly in reducing male gynecomastia .687

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most potent androgen?
mcqs.explanation: Dihydrotestosterone is the most potent androgen.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
mcqs.question: Aromatase converts testosterone into ____________
mcqs.explanation: Aromatase (CYP19) converts testosterone to estradiol . Certain effects of testosterone are mediated by estradiol . In men with deficient CYP19 or ER receptors , the epiphyses do not fuse , the long bones grow indefinitely and such patients are osteoporotic . Administration of estradiol can correct the bone abnormalities in CYP19 deficiency . However, this cannot be used in those with ER receptor defects . Testosterone is converted to dihydrotestosterone (DHT) by 5-alpha-reductase . Androstanedione and epiandrosterone are metabolites of DHT due to the action of 17-beta -HSD.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
mcqs.question: A 59-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer is started on flutamide therapy . What is the mechanism of action of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Flutamide acts by competitive inhibition of androgen receptors and is used to treat prostate cancer. Flutamide is a non-steroidal antiandrogen that competes with androgens such as testosterone and dihydrotestosterone for binding to the androgen receptors in the prostate gland. By doing so, it prevents them from stimulating the prostate cancer cells to grow. In addition to its use in prostate cancer, flutamide has been used to treat hyperandrogenism (excess androgen levels ) in women, such as in those with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and691 Hirsutism. Other anti-androgens are: • Bicalutamide , apalutamide , and nilutamide • Spironolactone (aldosterone antagonist with antiandrogen activity) • Cyproterone acetate (progestin with antiandrogen activity) • Cimetidine (H2 blocker with anti-androgen activity) Selective Androgen Receptor Modulators (SARMs) are a class of androgen receptor ligands that have similar anabolic properties to anabolic steroids , but with reduced androgenic side effects . There are no FDA-approved SARMs at present .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old medical student is worried about his receding hairline and is thinking about taking finasteride . The drug enhances hair growth by acting on which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Finasteride is a competitive inhibitor of 5 �o -reductase enzyme and thereby inhibits the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone . Finasteride selectively inhibits the Type 2 isoenzyme of 5�o -reductase . It is indicated for use in: • Benign prostatic hyperplasia • Male pattern baldness • Hirsutism.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
mcqs.question: Which of the following inhibits spermatogenesis ?
mcqs.explanation: Gossypol is a non-steroidal agent that inhibits spermatogenesis . Gossypol is obtained from cottonseed . It inhibits spermatogenesis by exerting toxic effects on seminiferous tubules but has low efficacy . Libido and potency are not significantly affected and fertility usually returns after a few months of discontinuation of the drug. But, around 10 % of the patients may remain infertile . Hypokalemia is a major adverse effect and may even lead to transient paralysis. Low efficacy and significant toxicity have caused gossypol to be abandoned as a candidate male contraceptive .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old male patient presented to the urology OPD with complaints of erectile dysfunction and was prescribed a PDE-5 inhibitor. Identify the drug.
mcqs.explanation: Tadalafil is a PDE-5 inhibitor used in the treatment of patients with erectile dysfunction . Penile erection is mediated by NO and cGMP. During arousal, the corpus cavernosum produces nitric oxide which in turn stimulates the formation of cGMP. This leads to relaxation of the smooth muscle of corpus cavernosum and penile arteries, causing engorgement of corpus cavernosum producing an erection . The biological actions of cGMP are terminated by692 phosphodiesterase enzymes and PDE-5 is the major cGMP metabolizing enzyme in the penile tissue . Phosphodiesterase -5-inhibitors include: • Sildenafil • Tadalafil - Longest acting (24-36 hrs), bioavailability is not affected by food • Vardenafil • Avanafil - Most Rapid-acting (within 15 -30 mins) Option A: Podofilox topical cream is used in the treatment of genital warts and molluscum contagiosum lesions . Option B: Finasteride is a 5 �o -reductase inhibitor. Option C: Apalutamide is a androgen receptor antagonist.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old diabetic patient was prescribed sildenafil for his erectile dysfunction . Following this, he develops a blurring of vision and complains that things seem to appear with a bluish-green hue . Inhibition of which of the following enzymes is likely to have caused his visual side effects ?
mcqs.explanation: Visual disturbance seen with sildenafil is due to PDE-6 inhibition. Sildenafil is used for the treatment of erectile dysfunction principally due to its inhibitory actions on PDE-5 (Phosphodiesterase 5) in the vascular tissues of the corpus cavernosa. However, it also exerts minor inhibitory action against PDE-6, which is present exclusively in rod and cone photoreceptors and results in blurring and blue -green tinting of vision. Tadalafil and avanafil have better PDE-5/PDE-6 selectivity , compared to sildenafil and vardenafil and hence have lesser visual side effects .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a prostaglandin that can be administered as an intracavernosal injection for erectile dysfunction ?
mcqs.explanation: Alprostadil can be given as a direct intracavernosal injection for erectile dysfunction . Alprostadil is a natural PGE1 preparation. It is usually used in patients who are not responding to PDE-5 inhibitors. It is also available as an intraurethral suppository .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old physician presented to the ED with a prolonged painful erection induced by intracorporeal injection of an alprostadil +phentolamine combination. He had been using this technique to overcome occasional performance anxiety. Corporeal aspiration reveals dark coloured blood and based on further workup, a diagnosis of low flow priapism is made. Which of the following is the drug of choice to treat his condition?
mcqs.explanation: Phenylephrine is the drug of choice for the treatment of low flow priapism. Characteristics of low-flow priapism include painful rigid erection and ischemic corpora, indicated by dark blood upon corporeal aspiration. Prazosin , and, phenoxybenzamine are alpha-blockers that cause vasodilation and can worsen priapism.693

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
mcqs.question: A 19-year-old male athlete seeks your opinion on the usage of anabolic steroids to improve his performance. What would be your advice?

options.a: Reassure the patient that all anabolic steroids are safe to use
options.b: Explain clearly that only newer anabolic steroids are safe to use as they have negligible androgenic action
options.c: Advice against use and sensitise the patient that all anabolic steroids have significant androgenic action
options.d: Explain that older testosterone preparations are more appropriate for use in male athletes

mcqs.explanation: All anabolic steroids have significant androgenic action and the use of anabolic steroids by athletes is not recommended . Testosterone and its derivatives are used for their anabolic effects but they have significant androgenic action. Some of them (17 methyl derivatives) are also hepatotoxic . The current consensus is to advise against the use of such anabolic steroids .694

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient is administered oxytocin as part of the active management of the third stage of labor (AMTSL ) protocol . Which of the following statements is correct regarding this drug?

options.b: It can be given by oral route
options.c: It is secreted by anterior pituitary
options.d: At higher doses , it exerts diuretic like action

mcqs.explanation: Oxytocin is responsible for galactokinesis (milk ejection reflex ). Option B: It is a peptide and inactive orally. Option C: It is secreted by posterior pituitary along with vasopressin. Option D: At higher doses , it can exert vasopressin like action and cause water retention .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an oxytocic ?
mcqs.explanation: Orciprenaline is a beta 2 receptor agonist that has uterine relaxing property . Oxytocics are uterine stimulants that increase uterine motility , especially at term. Uterine stimulants are: • Posterior pituitary hormones - oxytocin/pitocin • Ergot derivatives - ergometrine , methylergometrine • Prostaglandins - PGE2, PGF2 alpha, and others • Others - quinine, ethacridine Ethacridine is used as an abortifacient.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old multipara at 40 weeks gestation developed water intoxication and hyponatremia following prolonged IV infusion with oxytocin by an inexperienced junior resident . This adverse effect is due to oxytocin's action on which of the following sites ?

options.a: Vasopressin V2 receptors on serosal surface of renal tubular cells
options.b: Vasopressin V2 receptors on luminal surface of renal tubular cells
options.c: Vasopressin V1 receptors on serosal surface of renal tubular cells
options.d: Vasopressin V1 receptors on luminal surface of renal tubular cells

mcqs.explanation: Oxytocin can bind to V2 receptors on the serosal surface of renal tubular cells resulting in reduced free water clearance. This is because oxytocin and vasopressin have structural similarities. Oxytocin can have vasopressin (ADH) like activity at V2 receptors . The increase in water permeability occurs through the insertion of aquaporins (water channels) in collecting tubules . Prolonged i.v. administration at high doses in conjunction with large volumes of hypotonic fluid may cause water intoxication associated with hyponatremia.698 To avoid this complication, whenever high doses of oxytocin are administered over a long time: • An electrolyte -containing diluent must be used (not dextrose ) • The volume of infused fluid should be kept low (by infusing oxytocin at a higher concentration) • Fluid intake must be restricted , fluid balance chart should be kept and serum electrolytes should be monitored

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following patients is oxytocin not indicated ?

options.a: A primiparous woman with spontaneous premature labor
options.b: A multiparous woman with postpartum haemorrhage
options.c: A primiparous woman with uterine inertia
options.d: A patient with breast engorgement due to inefficient milk ejection reflex

mcqs.explanation: Spontaneous premature labor is not an indication for oxytocics . Infact, it is an indication for tocolytics . Uses of oxytocin are: • Induction of labor • Postpartum hemorrhage • Uterine inertia • Breast engorgement due to insufficient milk ejection reflex

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 33-year old lady with an obstetric score of G4P3L3 delivered a baby by cesarean section . She is at risk of developing uterine atony and the resident asks you to bring a long-acting analog of oxytocin. Which drug will you get ?
mcqs.explanation: Carbetocin is a long-acting analog of oxytocin. It is indicated for the prevention of uterine atony following caesarian section and for prevention of PPH. Option A: Desamino-oxytocin is a buccal formulation of oxytocin that is similar to oxytocin injection. Options C and D: Solifenacin and darifenacin are synthetic tertiary amine antimuscarinic agents that are indicated in overactive bladder .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a synthetic PGF2 alpha derivative used as an abortifacient?
mcqs.explanation: Carboprost is a 15-methyl synthetic derivative of PGF2 alpha. It is used as an abortifacient and in refractory PPH. Options A: Dinoprost is a natural PGF2 alpha preparation. Option B: Dinoprostone is natural PGE2 preparation. Option C: Misoprostol is a synthetic PGE1 analog. Gemeprost is also a synthetic PGE1 analog.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is/are the primary indication(s) of ergot alkaloids in obstetrics ?
mcqs.explanation: 699 Ergot derivatives are indicated for the prevention and/or treatment of postpartum hemorrhage. Ergot alkaloids markedly increase the motor activity of the uterus . The capacity to induce sustained uterine tetany and fetal distress exclude their use in the initiation or facilitation of labor. Due to the high incidence of postoperative vomiting and lack of evidence in reducing bleeding , routine or prophylactic use of uterotonic medications at the time of MTP is not recommended . Ergot alkaloids used in PPH include ergometrine and methylergometrine .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You administer methyl ergometrine to a patient with postpartum hemorrhage in the labor ward. Which of the following adverse effects will you not expect to occur in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Administration of Ergot alkaloids (such as methyl ergotamine ) result in hypertension . The use of ergot alkaloids is preferably avoided in hypertensive patients . Adverse effects of ergometrine /methylergometrine are: • Nausea and vomiting • Hypertension • Decrease in pain threshold but analgesia might be required • Decrease in milk secretion postpartum (due to dopaminergic action especially at higher doses )

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 23 -year old woman, G2P1L1 at 33 weeks of gestation is diagnosed with spontaneous preterm labor. The senior resident instructed you to give the patient antenatal steroids and a tocolytic . Which of the following drugs will you not choose ?
mcqs.explanation: Dopamine does not have any significant activity on the tone of the uterus , since uterine relaxation is mediated by beta -2 receptors . Specific tocolytic agents are: • Beta 2 agonists - ritodrine, isoxsuprine, terbutaline • Calcium channel blockers - nifedipine • Oxytocin receptor antagonist - atosiban • Magnesium sulfate • Indomethacin

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old pregnant woman has an obstetric history of preterm labor and 2 spontaneous abortions. She is very anxious about her current pregnancy and enquires if she can take any medication to prevent preterm labor. Which of the following drugs can be given to her?
mcqs.explanation: Progesterone can be given prophylactically to reduce the risk of preterm labor. It inhibits the secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines and delays cervical ripening. Therefore, progesterone and its derivatives have been advocated to diminish the onset of preterm labor in women at high risk due to previous preterm delivery .700 Intramuscular hydroxyprogesterone administered weekly as well as vaginal administration has both been shown to reduce the incidence of preterm delivery . Ritodrine, terbutaline , and nifedipine are tocolytics that are indicated for inhibition of uterine contractions of preterm labor and not for prophylaxis against preterm labor.701

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.b: NSAIDs act by inhibiting the phospholipases .

mcqs.explanation: Cyclooxygenase -1 (COX-1) is primarily a housekeeping enzyme. NSAIDs act by inhibiting both COX -1 and COX -2. • COX -1 is constitutively expressed in most cells . It performs housekeeping functions like gastrointestinal cytoprotection , fluid and electrolyte balance in the kidney. • COX -2 is normally present in insignificant amounts in most of the cells . It is induced by cytokines, growth factors and other stimuli during inflammation. Phospholipase -A2 is the initial enzyme that acts on the membrane phospholipids to generate arachidonic acid. Arachidonic acid produces prostaglandins by the action of the cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX ).

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with a history of myocardial infarction asks you why he is being prescribed aspirin. You tell him it prevents the formation of clots which reduces the risk of MI. Formation of which of the following eicosanoids is blocked by aspirin for this purpose ?
mcqs.explanation: 707 Thromboxane A2 is a pro-aggregatory eicosanoid whose formation requires the activity of COX enzyme. Aspirin blocks this step , thus reducing the chances of clot formation. Thromboxane A2 is an inducer of platelet aggregation and amplifies the signal of more potent platelet agonists, such as thrombin and ADP.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following helps in maintaining the patency of ductus arteriosus?
mcqs.explanation: Prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) maintains the patency of ductus arteriosus (PDA). This is used in term neonates with underlying cyanotic congenital heart disease awaiting surgical intervention as they have duct -dependant circulation. Indomethacin and Ibuprofen are the NSAID indicated for closing the ductus arteriosus in premature infants and neonates .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient of CREST syndrome has developed pulmonary hypertension . Which of the following drugs will you not prescribe to treat this?
mcqs.explanation: Rioprostil is a PGE1 analog and is not indicated in the treatment of pulmonary hypertension . Long term therapy with PGI2 analogs can delay or preclude the need for lung or heart-lung transplantation. PGI2 analogs used for the treatment of pulmonary hypertension are: • Epoprostenol (IV ) • Iloprost (IV ) • Treprostinil (IV or SC) PGI2 (Epoprostenol ) can also be used to prevent platelet aggregation and damage during haemodialysis or cardiopulmonary bypass. It also improves the harvest of platelets for transfusion.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old man has presented to the OPD with a complaint of erectile dysfunction not responding to oral medication. The issue is determined to be of vascular origin. Which prostaglandin preparation can be given as a local injection to treat this?
mcqs.explanation: Alprostadil (PGE1) is given as an intracavernosal injection or urethral suppository for erectile dysfunction . It is considered as a second -line therapy. Its use has been largely replaced by phosphodiesterase -5 inhibitors like sildenafil and tadalafil which are the drugs of choice .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about aspirin?

options.a: It is an irreversible inhibitor of the cyclooxygenase enzyme.
options.b: Its clearance is independent of plasma concentration at low dose .
options.c: Alkalinization of urine increases its rate of excretion.
options.d: Its antiplatelet effect at low dose is related to presystemic COX inhibition.

mcqs.explanation: Aspirin clearance is dependent on plasma concentration at a lower dose . Aspirin shows saturation kinetics. This means that at lower plasma concentrations it has first-order kinetics where the rate of elimination is proportional to the plasma708 concentration but at higher plasma concentrations it has zero-order kinetics where the rate of elimination is independent of its plasma concentration. Around 80-90% of aspirin (salicylates) are bound to plasma proteins , especially albumin. Low dose aspirin acetylates the COX enzyme of platelets in the portal circulation (pre-systemic ) and deactivates it which is responsible for antiplatelet action. Aspirin and salicylates are acidic in nature. Alkalinization of the urine increases the rate of excretion of aspirin, as ionised form of aspirin increases which is not reabsorbed from the tubular fluid in kidney.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 12 -year-old child developed fever during an epidemic of influenza. Which of the following drugs is contraindicated in this child?
mcqs.explanation: Aspirin is contraindicated in this child due to the risk of development of Reye syndrome. Children and young adults less than 20 years of age with viral fever have a risk of developing Reye 's syndrome on administration of aspirin or other salicylates . Features of Reye syndrome include : • Acute onset of encephalopathy • Liver dysfunction • Fatty infiltration of the liver Option A - Acetaminophen is considered the antipyretic of choice in children with viral infections . Options C and D - Oseltamivir and baloxavir are antiviral drugs used in influenza.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old pilot with low back pain requires a painkiller that is effective at once-daily dosing. You decide to prescribe the NSAID with the longest plasma half-life . Which drug will you choose ?
mcqs.explanation: Piroxicam is chosen as it has the longest plasma half-life among NSAIDs. Piroxicam is absorbed completely and undergoes enterohepatic circulation. Due to the long half-life , once-daily administration of the drug is sufficient for the therapeutic response .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with a history of gastritis complains of joint pain. You diagnose it to be a case of osteoarthritis and prescribe celecoxib . Which of the following statements is true regarding this drug?

options.b: It is more likely to cause gastric ulcers compared to ibuprofen
options.c: It is not associated with cardiotoxicity

mcqs.explanation: Celecoxib is a selective COX -2 inhibitor. As COX -2 enzyme is constitutively active within the kidney , recommended doses of selective COX -2 inhibitors cause renal toxicities similar to those associated with traditional NSAIDs. Option B - It is less likely to cause gastric ulcers . Celecoxib has analgesic , antipyretic , and anti-inflammatory effects similar to those of non-selective NSAIDs but with better gastrointestinal tolerability . Option C - It inhibits COX -2-mediated prostacyclin synthesis in the vascular endothelium . As a result , use of celecoxib is associated with increased cardiovascular risk .709 Option D - Celecoxib at usual doses does not inhibit platelet aggregation . This is because platelet aggregation is mediated by thromboxane produced by the COX -1. These points are also true for other selective COX -2 inhibitors.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs has the least COX -2 selectivity ?
mcqs.explanation: Celecoxib has the least COX -2 selectivity among the following . Some selective COX -2 inhibitors are withdrawn or have restricted use because of an increase in the risk of cardiovascular events like myocardial infarction, serious skin reactions (valdecoxib), fatal hepatic failure (lumiracoxib). Nowadays , dual inhibitors inhibiting 5-LOX and COX like licofelone and tepoxalin are also used for their anti-inflammatory property .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Your senior asks you to administer a selective COX -2 inhibitor intravenously to a patient for post-op analgesia. Which of the following will you choose ?
mcqs.explanation: Parecoxib is chosen as it is the only injectable COX -2 selective drug among the given options . It is a water-soluble prodrug of valdecoxib. It is effective in the perioperative period when oral medications are not indicated .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a true statement about acetaminophen ?

options.a: It has significant analgesic , antiinflammatory and antipyretic action.
options.c: It does not antagonize effects of uricosuric drugs.

mcqs.explanation: Acetaminophen does not antagonize effects of uricosuric agents . It may be used concomitantly with probenecid in the treatment of gout as it does not have any effect on uric acid levels . Option A - Acetaminophen has analgesic and antipyretic action equivalent to aspirin but lacks a significant anti-inflammatory effect . Option B - Acetaminophen toxicity causes centrilobular necrosis. Option D - It is a weak inhibitor of both COX -1 and COX -2 and has minimal or no effect on platelet activity.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old patient of major depression presented to the ER after having consumed 20 tablets of acetaminophen (500 mg each) 1 hour ago in a self -harm attempt . She does not have any symptoms at the moment. Which of the following should you administer to her?
mcqs.explanation: The patient in the given clinical scenario has ingested a potentially toxic dose of acetaminophen . N-acetylcysteine is considered as a definitive antidote for acetaminophen poisoning to prevent hepatic injury. N-acetyl -p-benzoquinone imine (NAPQI) is a toxic metabolite of acetaminophen which causes hepatotoxicity. In adults , hepatotoxicity may occur after ingestion of a single dose of 10 –15 g (150–250 mg/kg) of acetaminophen ; doses of 20 –25 g or more are potentially fatal.710 In acetaminophen poisoning, due to increased NAPQI, there is utilization of glutathione (GSH). This in turn leads to depletion of GSH leading to oxidative cellular damage of the hepatocytes . N-acetylcysteine replenishes GSH stores and also conjugates with NAPQI and prevents oxidative damage to the cell . It also protects against extrahepatic injury due to its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties . Option A: Flumazenil is an antidote for benzodiazepine toxicity . Option C: Methylene blue is used in methemoglobinemia . Option D: Symptoms may take upto 2 days to develop in a case of acetaminophen poisoning by which time the hepatic damage may become irreversible. Thus, early treatment is initiated in all suspected cases .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is not considered a hit and run drug?
mcqs.explanation: Piroxicam is a reversible inhibitor of cyclooxygenase enzyme and cannot be considered as a hit and run drug. Hit and run drugs are a group of drugs whose half-life is short, but cause irreversible inhibition of a particular enzyme. So, the effect of the drug is present even after the drug is cleared from the system . Examples include : • MAO inhibitors ( e.g.: Phenelzine ) • PPI (e.g.: omeprazole ) • Guanethidine • Reserpine • Aspirin

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following patients should be prescribed NSAIDs for pain relief ?

options.a: A hypertensive patient on chlorthalidone having osteoarthritis
options.c: Patient complaining of low back pain who is a known case of CKD

mcqs.explanation: NSAIDs can be used in the treatment of primary dysmenorrhea. Prostaglandin release from endometrium causes cramps and other symptoms . NSAIDs inhibit the synthesis of prostaglandin and cause symptomatic relief . Option A: NSAIDs interfere with the antihypertensive effect of diuretics . The exact mechanism is not yet known. So it should be avoided in such cases . Option C: NSAIDs are generally avoided in renal diseases as inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis worsens renal function. Option D: NSAIDs generally lack efficacy in cases of neuropathic pain like diabetic neuropathy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient of chronic low back pain has presented to your OPD with deranged LFT reports. He tells you he has been on long term treatment with a painkiller for his condition. Which NSAID has he most likely been taking?
mcqs.explanation: Diclofenac is the NSAID that has the highest risk of hepatotoxicity within the therapeutic dose .711 Liver injury occurs in acetaminophen overdose but it is extremely rare in therapeutic dose . NSAIDs are not recommended in advanced hepatic and renal failure.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old male on multiple drugs presents with a round macule on his right leg for the last 7 days. The patient gives a history of similar episodes in the past which resolved spontaneously . Which of the following drugs is the most likely cause ?
mcqs.explanation: This is a case of fixed drug eruption and the most likely cause is ibuprofen . Fixed drug eruptions are characterized by sharply demarcated dull red to brown lesions . They occur in lips, hands, legs , face , genitalia, and oral mucosa, and cause a burning sensation. The lesion recurs in the same locations upon re-exposure to the offending drug. Some of the drugs commonly known to cause fixed drug eruptions are Sulphonamides , NSAIDs, Analgesics , and Hypnotics . Diagnosis is based on history and lesion morphology . Discontinuation of the offending drug is the first step in management. Phenytoin and carbamazepine can lead to Stevens -Johnson syndrome (SJS)/toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) and drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome).712

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following receptors is a ligand-gated ion channel?
mcqs.explanation: 718 The 5-HT3 receptor is a ligand-gated ion channel receptor . It rapidly depolarizes nerve endings by opening the cation channels located within the receptor . The 5-HT3 receptors are located in the GI tract (vagal & splanchnic afferents ) and the brain (nucleus tractus solitarius & area postrema) and are involved in the emetic response . Hence 5-HT3 receptor antagonists like ondansetron, dolasetron etc are used as antiemetics . All other 5-HT receptors are G-protein-coupled receptors .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding triptans?

options.b: No action on adrenergic or cholinergic or dopaminergic receptors
options.d: They are used for prophylaxis of migraine

mcqs.explanation: Triptans are not used in prophylaxis of migraine. They are indicated in the management of acute attacks of migraine. Drugs used in prophylaxis of migraine are : • Beta-blocker - Propranolol, metoprolol • Antidepressant - Amitriptyline , nortriptyline • Anticonvulsant - Topiramate, valproate • Serotonergic drug - Pizotifen • Antihistamine - Flunarizine • Angiotensin receptor blocker - candesartan

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old patient presented to the ER with an acute attack of migraine. You decide to administer a long-acting triptan. Which among the following do you choose ?
mcqs.explanation: Frovatriptan is a long-acting triptan among other triptans. Headache recurrences in an attack are less with longer-acting triptans like frovatriptan and naratriptan but onset of action may be slow .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient of migraine has come to the OPD for follow up. She tells you that she gets very nauseous during the attacks and is not being able to take the oral drug. You decide to prescribe an intranasal formulation instead . Which of the following antimigraine agents will you not choose ?
mcqs.explanation: Naratriptan is not available for intranasal administration. It is available only for oral administration.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: After the administration of a drug for an acute attack of migraine, a patient developed nausea and vomiting. She also developed tingling and numbness at the tips of her fingers that eventually turned blue . Which of the following is the most likely drug implicated ?
mcqs.explanation: Nausea and vomiting, as well as tingling and numbness (paresthesia ), are common adverse effects of dihydroergotamine . The numbness progressing to bluish discolouration of the fingers are the initial signs of occlusion . It can eventually lead to gangrene if left untreated . This is a rare adverse effect of719 dihydroergotamine . Contraindications for ergotamine : • Peripheral vascular disease • Coronary artery disease • Uncontrolled hypertension • Fever and/or sepsis • Pregnancy • Within 24 hours of using triptans

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient has just been diagnosed with migraine. Which of the following drugs can you prescribe for prophylaxis?
mcqs.explanation: Topiramate is used in the prophylaxis of migraine. Long-term use of topiramate can cause weight loss. The drugs that have been approved by the FDA for the preventive treatment of migraine include : • Propranolol • Timolol • Sodium valproate • Topiramate Options A and B - Sumatriptan, a 5HT1B /1D agonist is a first-line agent for the termination of acute attacks. Ergotamines are also used in the termination of acute attacks. Option C - Domperidone is indicated as an adjuvant in acute attacks. Acute attacks are associated with gastric stasis and an increased incidence of nausea and vomiting. It is helpful in reducing gastrointestinal effects . It can also increase gastrointestinal absorption of other antimigraine agents that are not absorbed due to gastric stasis.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the mechanism of action of colchicine ?

options.d: Binds to tubulin and inhibits granulocyte migration

mcqs.explanation: Colchicine acts by binding to tubulin and inhibits granulocyte migration. Colchicine produces its anti-inflammatory effects by binding to the intracellular protein tubulin . This prevents the polymerization of tubulin into microtubules which is necessary for leukocyte migration and phagocytosis . Inhibition of microtubule formation prevents granulocyte migration and also arrests cell division at G1 phase.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which one of the following drugs inhibits neutrophil recruitment?
mcqs.explanation: Colchicine inhibits neutrophil (granulocyte ) recruitment.720 Colchicine acts by preventing the polymerisation of microtubules by binding to tubulin . This reduces neutrophil recruitment to inflamed tissue and also decreases the secretion of chemotactic factors by activated neutrophils , thus reducing the inflammatory response overall. Colchicine is used in gout and Mediterranean fever.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with chronic tophaceous gout was prescribed sulfinpyrazone . What is the mechanism of action of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Sulfinpyrazone is a uricosuric agent that promotes excretion of uric acid. It is used to decrease the body pool of urate in patients with gout. They act by inhibiting the organic anion transporter that is involved in uric acid reabsorption in renal tubules . Uricosuric agents used in gout are: • Probenecid • Sulfinpyrazone • Benzbromarone • Lesinurad Uricosuric therapy should be initiated in gouty patients with underexcretion of uric acid and when allopurinol or febuxostat is contraindicated or when tophi are present . Therapy should not be started until 2–3 weeks after an acute attack.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged obese man has presented to the OPD with acute pain around his left first metatarsophalangeal joint. He has a history of similar episodes in the past. X-ray is given below . Which drug is commonly used as initial treatment for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and the X-ray showing Martel 's sign point towards a diagnosis of acute on chronic presentation of gout . Indomethacin is commonly used in the initial treatment of gout . In addition to inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis , indomethacin and other NSAIDs also inhibit urate crystal phagocytosis . Option A - Aspirin is not used because it causes renal retention of uric acid at low doses . It is uricosuric only at higher doses that are poorly tolerated . Option C - Allopurinol is used for prophylaxis of gout . Option D - NSAIDs are selected over colchicine because of troublesome diarrhea associated with colchicine .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient undergoing chemotherapy was diagnosed with tumour lysis syndrome. She was administered rasburicase. Which group does this drug belong to?
mcqs.explanation: Rasburicase is a recombinant urate oxidase which converts uric acid into soluble and inactive allantoin. It is more effective in reducing the urate level than allopurinol. Recombinant uric acid oxidase is available as rasburicase and pegloticase . It is produced by genetically modified Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain. They are indicated in gout only for chronic refractory gout . It is primarily indicated for hyperuricemia associated with tumor lysis syndrome.721 Pegloticase is a recombinant pegylated uric acid oxidase that is indicated for treatment of severe , treatment-refractory, chronic gout and also prophylaxis of gout .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You have prescribed the first-line urate-lowering drug to a patient with chronic gout . Which of the following is true about this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Allopurinol is recommended as the first-line urate-lowering agent in all patients with gout . It is a purine antimetabolite and an inhibitor of xanthine oxidase enzyme. It prevents the conversion of hypoxanthine and xanthine to uric acid reducing plasma uric acid levels . Allopurinol is also a substrate for xanthine oxidase . The metabolite of allopurinol called oxypurinol is a non-competitive inhibitor of xanthine oxidase .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient was on treatment with indomethacin for gout . You decide to add a non-purine xanthine oxidase inhibitor to his treatment plan. Which of the following will you prescribe ?
mcqs.explanation: Febuxostat is a non-purine xanthine oxidase inhibitor that is indicated for reducing hyperuricemia in chronic gout . Both allopurinol and febuxostat can be used as first line agents but since the question mentions a non-purine inhibitor is chosen, febuxostat is the answer. Option A - Allopurinol is a purine xanthine oxidase inhibitor. Option D - Sulfinpyrazone is a uricosuric agent .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient , who is a known case of gout on treatment with allopurinol, comes to the OPD for follow up. His serum uric acid level is 11 mg/dl. You add lesinurad to his treatment regime for adequate disease control. Which group does this drug belong to?
mcqs.explanation: Lesinurad is a uricosuric agent . It is a URAT1 inhibitor indicated in combination with a xanthine oxidase inhibitor for the treatment of hyperuricemia associated with gout . By inhibiting URAT1 , it increases the urinary excretion of uric acid.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is pegloticase used for?
mcqs.explanation: Pegloticase is used in the treatment of chronic gout . Pegloticase is a pegylated uricase (urate oxidase ). It catalyzes the enzymatic oxidation of uric acid into allantoin, which is a more soluble and inactive metabolite . It is used in the treatment of severe , refractory chronic gout or in cases where other urate-lowering therapies are contraindicated .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An elderly woman on treatment for migraine presents with chest pain. She has a previous history of angina/MI. Which of the following mechanism of the prescribed drug for migraine might have caused this presentation ?
mcqs.explanation: 722 The patient may have been given sumatriptan, a 5-HT1b/1d receptor agonist which causes vasoconstriction and used in migraine. Thus, sumatriptan will worsen angina by causing coronary vasoconstriction. Angina will be worsened if the O2 demand of the heart is increased or there is reduced blood flow to the already ischemic areas.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is correct about the drugs used in gout ?
mcqs.explanation: Gout is a metabolic disease associated with hyperuricemia .
