options.b: Corticosteroids cause direct bronchodilatation when used with xanthines
options.c: Corticosteroids indirectly increase the effect of xanthines on adenosine receptor

mcqs.explanation: Corticosteroids improved the condition by increasing the airway responsiveness to salbutamol . Mechanism of action of corticosteroids in an acute asthma attack: • Increases responsiveness to \035-2 agonists • Decreases mucous secretion • Decreases inflammatory cell response. Steroids increase the transcription of \035-2 receptor genes and hence increases responsiveness to \035-2 agonists. \035-2 agonists increase the effect of steroids by enhancing the action of glucocorticoid receptors . Theophylline increases the effects of steroids by activating the enzyme histone deacetylase which is the target for steroids as well . Note : As per recent GINA 2021 guidelines, aminophyllines are no longer preferred in the management of acute severe asthma due to their low efficacy and poor safety profile .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient has had 2 acute exacerbations of asthma over the span of 1-month despite being on therapy. Which of the following is a systemic steroid that can be used to treat her?
mcqs.explanation: Prednisolone is a systemic steroid used for maintenance therapy after an acute exacerbation of asthma. Intravenous corticosteroids such as hydrocortisone are indicated if the lung function is predicted to be <30% or if there 's poor response to nebulized \0352 agonists. After the exacerbation, oral predisolone can be substituted with maximal beneficial effect at 30-40mg daily. Inhaled corticosteroids commonly used in asthma are: • Beclomethasone dipropionate799 • Budesonide • Ciclesonide • Fluticasone • Mometasone

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An asthmatic patient presented to the ER with dyspnea and wheezing . Intake of which of the following is unlikely to have precipitated this?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of an acute exacerbation of asthma. Caffeine does not precipitate this. Caffeine is a dietary xanthine similar in structure to methylxanthines (theophylline ) which are used as adjuvants in the treatment of asthma. NSAIDs (like phenylbutazone , naproxen, and aspirin) inhibit the cyclooxygenase pathway thereby diverting arachidonic acid towards the lipoxygenase pathway . This increases the level of pro-inflammatory leukotrienes and can precipitate an acute asthma attack.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with mild episodic asthma is prescribed daily low-dose inhaled budesonide therapy . Which of the following conditions is he not at increased risk of developing ?
mcqs.explanation: Inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) like budesonide do not increase the risk of developing carcinoma of the lung. Common problems with the use of ICS: • Hoarseness of voice • Weakness of voice (dysphonia ) • Increased risk of bacterial and mycobacterial lung infection • Oropharyngeal candidiasis

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An elderly man with a 30-year history of smoking complains of breathing difficulty . A diagnosis of COPD is made, and treatment with a long-acting muscarinic antagonist is initiated . Which of the following will you not prescribe ?
mcqs.explanation: Ipratropium is a short-acting muscarinic antagonist which is not used for the long-term management of COPD. It can be used to treat acute exacerbations. The long-acting muscarinic antagonists (LAMAs) are: • Tiotropium • Glycopyrronium • Umeclidinium • Aclidinium800

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Inhalational anticholinergics the mainstay of treatment in:
mcqs.explanation: Inhalational anticholinergics are the mainstay for the treatment of COPD. Ipratropium is as effective as albuterol in patients with COPD. Longer-acting antimuscarinic agents , including tiotropium, aclidinium, and umeclidinium , are approved for maintenance therapy of COPD. Anticholinergics are less effective than \035-2 agonists as bronchodilators in asthma and are not the mainstay in the treatment of asthma.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) patient requires a step -up in therapy due to symptom persistence . Which PDE-4 inhibitor can you prescribe as an add-on drug to his treatment regimen?
mcqs.explanation: Roflumilast is a PDE-4 selective inhibitor approved for use in COPD. PDE-4 is the major isoform present in inflammatory cells and its inhibition results in higher anti-inflammatory effects . Option A: Seratrodast is a thromboxane receptor antagonist used in the prophylaxis of asthma. It decreases the bronchial hypersensitivity caused by thromboxane. Option C: Zileuton is a lipoxygenase inhibitor that can be used in the treatment of asthma. Option D: Nedocromil is a mast cell stabilizer indicated in the prophylaxis of asthma.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs are antitussives ?
mcqs.explanation: Dextromethorphan, morphine, and gabapentin are all antitussives . Dextromethorphan is an NMDA receptor antagonist that suppresses the cough center . Opiates like morphine have a central mechanism of action on the medullary cough center and are indicated for intractable cough associated with bronchial carcinoma . Gabapentin and pregabalin are GABA analogs that have been shown to benefit chronic idiopathic cough involving neural hypersensitivity . Guaifenesin is an expectorant that is taken orally. Carbocysteine is a mucolytic that reduces the disulfide bridges that bind glycoproteins to other proteins, such as albumin and secretory IgA. It is also taken orally and helps reduce the viscosity of sputum .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A known case of CREST syndrome presents with dyspnea . On auscultation , a Graham -Steele murmur is heard. On further investigation, her pulmonary artery pressure is found to be mm Hg. Which drug will you use to manage her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario points to a diagnosis of pulmonary artery hypertension (pulmonary artery pressure > 20mmHg ) which can be managed using selective PDE-5 inhibitors. Inhibition of PDE-5 in the pulmonary bed leads to a reduction in the hydrolysis of cGMP which causes pulmonary vasodilation.801 Sildenafil and tadalafil are the PDE-5 inhibitors approved for use in PAH.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following groups does riociguat belong to?
mcqs.explanation: Riociguat is a soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator (sGC), indicated in the treatment of pulmonary artery hypertension. Riociguat increases the sensitivity of nitric oxide to sGC and also directly stimulates the sGC enzyme resulting in increased formation of cGMP. This leads to relaxation in the pulmonary vasculature.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is a prostacyclin analog that can be added to the treatment regimen of a patient with pulmonary artery hypertension ?
mcqs.explanation: Iloprost is a prostacyclin analog indicated in the management of pulmonary artery hypertension . It falls under the category of IP receptor (prostacyclin receptor ) agonists. Other drugs falling under the category of IP receptor agonists are: • Epoprostenol • Treprostinil • Iloprost • Selexipag Option A: Sildenafil is a PDE-5 inhibitor. Option B: Misoprostol is a synthetic PGE1 analog. Option C: Dinoprost is a natural PGF2-alpha preparation. It should not be confused with dinoprostone which is a synthetic analogue of PGE2.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which is a selective endothelin receptor A antagonist used in the management of pulmonary artery hypertension ?
mcqs.explanation: Ambrisentan is a selective endothelin receptor A (ET-A) antagonist which is used in the management of pulmonary artery hypertension (PAH). Bosentan, tezosentan , and macitantan are non-selective (ET-A and ET-B) endothelin receptor antagonists.802

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Dornase alfa is indicated in which of the following patients ?
mcqs.explanation: Dornase alfa is indicated in patients with cystic fibrosis and as a rescue treatment for refractory atelectasis in newborn and pediatric populations . Dornase alfa is a recombinant DNase 1 that digests neutrophil DNA deposited in the pulmonary mucus thereby reducing mucosal viscoelasticity .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following should not be prescribed with theophylline ?
mcqs.explanation: Erythromycin should not be prescribed with theophylline . Theophylline is mainly metabolized by CYP1A2 in the liver. Erythromycin inhibits CYP1A2 and thereby decreases the clearance of theophylline . Factors decreasing the clearance of theophylline are: • Drugs - erythromycin, cimetidine , ciprofloxacin, allopurinol, fluvoxamine, zileuton , zafirlukast • Congestive heart failure • Liver disease • Pneumonia • Viral infection and vaccination • High-carbohydrate diet • Old age

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: If codiene is coming to the market in combination with dextromethorphan as an anti-tussive , this combination _______

options.a: Should not be used due to risk of addiction
options.b: Can be used as both have different mechanism of action
options.c: Should not be used as it is irrational
options.d: Can be used to treat cough effectively

mcqs.explanation: It is an irrational drug combination and should not be given. Codeine is an opioid analgesic having specific antitussive action while dextromethorphan is a centrally active NMDA receptor antagonist that may be effective as an antitussive. Both are centrally acting antitussives , and do not provide any added advantage when combined. Hence it is an irrational drug combination. Rational fixed -dose combination drugs for the treatment of cough usually contain: • A centrally acting anti-tussive (either codeine or dextromethorphan ; not both), with • Antihistamines, decongestants and expectorants . Option A - Both of these drugs carry a risk of addiction, but it is not the reason to not give the drug. The main reason is that the combination is irrational . Options B & D - Both codeine and dextromethorphan have different mechanisms of action and can treat cough effectively . However, the combination of two centrally acting antitussives does not provide any added advantage compared to using one drug alone. Hence, the combination is irrational .803

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: The final step in gastric acid production is inhibited by:
mcqs.explanation: The final step in gastric acid production is inhibited by the proton pump inhibitors (PPIs ). The secretion of protons by the activated H+/K+- ATPase (proton pump ) in the parietal cells into the gastric lumen is the final step involved in the production of gastric acid. PPIs cause maximum suppression of gastric acid and also reduces basal acid secretion . Suppression of gastric acid occurs regardless of the stimulus present .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: Despite their short half-lives, how do proton-pump inhibitors cause prolonged suppression of acid secretion for up to 48 hours?

options.b: Exit from plasma and enter acid secretory canaliculi, blocking the secretion of acid for a long time
options.c: Irreversibly inhibit proton pump molecule , acid secretion requires synthesis of new proton pumps
options.d: Available as enteric coated capsules from which drug is gradually released

mcqs.explanation: 812 PPIs irreversibly inhibit the proton pump molecule and hence , acid secretion requires the synthesis of new proton pumps . PPIs are prodrugs, when ingested , get absorbed into the systemic circulation. It then diffuses into the parietal cells of the stomach and accumulates in the acidic secretory canaliculi. Acidic pH in the parietal cell canaliculi causes activation of the PPIs. These activated PPIs irreversibly inhibit H+/K+ ATPase (proton pump ) in the parietal cell . The maximum proton pump activation corresponds to the peak concentration of PPI resulting in maximum efficacy . The secretion resumes gradually over 3-4 days of stopping the drug when new proton pumps are synthesized .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: A patient with gastroesophageal reflux disease was prescribed an oral PPI preparation that causes the fastest acid suppression . Identify the drug.
mcqs.explanation: Rabeprazole is the oral PPI preparation that causes the fastest acid suppression . It has a higher pKa that causes more rapid conversion to active species in acidic canaliculi. The efficacy and potency are similar to that of omeprazole .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: A neighbor approaches you for advice on the best time to take pantoprazole for heartburn. What would you recommend?
mcqs.explanation: Proton-pump inhibitors (pantoprazole) should be ideally given shortly (20-30 minutes ) before food. PPIs are usually given before breakfast. Food hinders the absorption of PPIs and decreases their bioavailability. PPIs are prodrugs, when ingested , get absorbed into the systemic circulation. It then diffuses into the parietal cells of the stomach and accumulates in the acidic secretory canaliculi. Acidic pH in the parietal cell canaliculi causes activation of the PPIs. The maximum proton pump activation corresponds to the peak concentration of PPI resulting in maximum efficacy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: A patient undergoing evaluation for multiple gastroduodenal ulcers was diagnosed with Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. What would be the drug of choice for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Proton-pump inhibitors are the drug of choice in Zollinger–Ellison syndrome. Zollinger Ellison syndrome includes pancreatic or duodenal gastrinoma which leads to the secretion of large amounts of gastrin. This, in turn, increases gastric acid leading to severe gastroduodenal ulceration and other effects of hyperchlorhydria . Note : Netazepide is a gastrin/cholecystokinin -2 receptor antagonist used in the treatment of gastrinoma. It is also an antisecretory agent .813

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old woman with osteoarthritis developed gastric ulcers following long-term use of NSAIDs. Of the following , which drug is FDA-approved for her condition?
mcqs.explanation: PGE1 analog (misoprostol ) is approved by the FDA for NSAID-induced gastric ulcers . It reduces gastric acid secretion in a dose -dependent manner . Prostaglandins inhibit gastric acid secretion . Misoprostol also increases mucosal blood flow and stimulates bicarbonate and mucin secretion which contribute to its cytoprotective action. However, the reduction in acid secretion is less than that of H2 blockers.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: What is the most effective therapy for NSAID-induced ulcers ?
mcqs.explanation: The most effective therapy for NSAID-induced ulcers is proton pump inhibitors. They are proven to be more effective than misoprostol and H2 receptor antagonists.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: Which proton pump inhibitor should be avoided in a patient on warfarin anticoagulation ?
mcqs.explanation: Omeprazole should not be used in a patient on warfarin therapy as it decreases the metabolism of warfarin . All PPIs are metabolized by hepatic P450 cytochromes , including CYP2C19 and CYP3A4, and may interfere with the metabolism of the other drugs. It inhibits the metabolism of clopidogrel , diazepam, and phenytoin . Note : There is disagreement among different authors regarding the PPIs and their interactions with the metabolism of other drugs. • Goodman and Gilman mention that lansoprazole and rabeprazole along with omeprazole and esomeprazole interact with the metabolism of warfarin . • Katzung and various online sources agree that lansoprazole and rabeprazole do not or minimally interact with warfarin metabolism . • All of them agree that pantoprazole does not or minimally interacts with warfarin metabolism .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: You are counseling a patient with gastroesophageal reflux disease about the need for long-term therapy with proton-pump inhibitors. All of the following are complications of this therapy , except :
mcqs.explanation: Long-term PPI therapy is not associated with hypogastrinemia but is associated with hypergastrinemia. This hypergastrinemia contributes to rebound gastric acid hypersecretion if PPI therapy is discontinued . Chronic PPI therapy is associated with: • Decreased vitamin B12 absorption • Increased susceptibility to infections- hospital -acquired pneumonia, pseudomembranous enterocolitis • Reduced calcium absorption increases the risk of fractures814

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: Gynecomastia can occur as a side effect of:
mcqs.explanation: Gynecomastia can occur as a side effect of cimetidine . It inhibits the binding of dihydrotestosterone to androgen receptors, increases the serum prolactin level and inhibits the metabolism of estradiol by the liver. Cimetidine causes maximum hepatic inhibition. The specific side effect of high doses of cimetidine given for a long time is gynecomastia or impotence in males and galactorrhea in females . This property is not shared by other H2 blockers. Drugs causing gynecomastia : • Alcohol, marijuana , heroin • Antiretroviral therapy • Anabolic steroids • Digoxin • Risperidone • Ketoconazole • Spironolactone • �o -methyldopa • Bromocriptine • Cimetidine • Phenytoin therapy . • Androgens- testosterone and its esters (except dihydrotestosterone ).

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: A patient with peptic ulcer disease was prescribed ranitidine and sucralfate to be taken together . Why is this combination incorrect?

options.a: Ranitidine combines with sucralfate and forms a toxic metabolite
options.b: Sucralfate competes with ranitidine for H2 receptor
options.c: Ranitidine increases the gastric pH which reduces sucralfate efficacy
options.d: Sucralfate inhibits the absorption of ranitidine

mcqs.explanation: Ranitidine increases the gastric pH (i.e. less acidic) which reduces sucralfate efficacy ; hence the combination is incorrect. Polymerization of sucralfate occurs only at an acidic pH by crosslinking of the molecules which forms a sticky gel -like consistency . This adheres to the ulcer base predominantly and remains there for almost 6 hours, preventing the ulcer base from coming in contact with the acid. Concurrent use of H2 blockers like ranitidine increases the gastric pH and thus hinders the polymerization and reduces the efficacy of sucralfate . Sucralfate should be taken at least 2 hours after the administration of any other drug.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: Gastric bezoars are commonly associated with __________.
mcqs.explanation: Gastric bezoars are commonly associated with sucralfate .815 Sucralfate produces a viscous gel that has a 'sticky nature'. The sticky nature may be responsible for the formation of gastric bezoars, particularly in those with gastroparesis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a characteristic of milk-alkali syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Milk alkali syndrome is not characterized by hepatotoxicity . Characteristics of the milk-alkali syndrome include : • Alkalosis • Hypercalcemia • Renal insufficiency Milk alkali syndrome used to occur in patients who were administered high doses of NaHCO3 and CaCO3 along with milk or cream for the management of peptic ulcers . The syndrome is rare now and generally occurs with a large intake of calcium supplements along with milk.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: Which of the following can cause diarrhea?
mcqs.explanation: Magnesium salts have a laxative property and can cause diarrhoea. Aluminium salts can cause constipation by relaxing smooth muscles . The combination of aluminium and magnesium salts can neutralize each other's action, thus the combination is preferred .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: Which of the following antacids is more likely to induce rebound acid secretion ?
mcqs.explanation: Calcium carbonate is an antacid that is more likely to induce rebound acid secretion . Calcium containing antacids like calcium carbonate rapidly and effectively neutralizes gastric acid. Calcium in antacids causes rebound acid secretion , hence it is given at frequent intervals to reduce the incidence of rebound acid secretion. Magnesium , aluminium and sodium-containing antacids are less likely to cause this phenomenon .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: A patient presents with complaints of black stools and black coated tongue as shown in the image. Which of the following drugs is implicated ?
mcqs.explanation: Colloidal bismuth subsalicylate is known to cause blackening of the tongue , dentures and stools . It combines with trace amounts of sulfur in saliva and colon to form bismuth sulfide . Bismuth sulfide is a highly insoluble black salt. The adverse effect is claimed to be temporary and harmless.816

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an antifoaming agent ?
mcqs.explanation: Simethicone is a surfactant that decreases foaming. Due to this antifoaming action, it is included in many antacid preparations to reduce gastroesophageal reflux. Option A: Sucralfate acts as an ulcer protective agent by forming a viscous sticky polymer that binds to the ulcer base. Option D: Rebamipide is also a cytoprotective agent that acts by increasing the production of prostaglandin in gastric mucosa and by scavenging reactive oxygen species . Option C: Bismuth compounds bind to the base of the ulcer, promote mucin and bicarbonate production. They have significant antibacterial action and are part of many anti-H.pylori regimens.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: A patient with a history of peptic ulcer underwent endoscopic evaluation. The biopsy image is shown below . Which of the following drugs is not used in treating this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a Warthin silver starry stained biopsy specimen , diagnostic for Helicobacter pylori. Sucralfate does not have any anti-H. pylori action and is not used in the treatment of H. pylori gastritis. Option A: Metronidazole is used in the triple , quadruple therapy , and sequential therapy regimens . Option B: Proton pump inhibitors significantly enhance the effectiveness of regimens containing amoxicillin or clarithromycin. Option D: Bismuth compounds have significant anti-bacterial action and are given in quadruple therapy. Two or three antimicrobials are combined in regimens that range from 10 -14 days. Monotherapy is not recommended due to the development of resistance .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man presented with bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain for the past week . Pseudopolyps were noted on colonoscopy . Which of the following can be used in managing his condition?
mcqs.explanation: Bloody diarrhea and colonoscopy findings of pseudopolyps are suggestive of ulcerative colitis . The sulfa drug indicated is sulfasalazine . It is indicated mainly in mild-moderate ulcerative colitis and as an adjunctive in severe cases . Efficacy in Crohn's disease is less . Sulfasalazine consists of 5-ASA (mesalamine or 5-amino salicylic acid) linked to sulfapyridine with an azo bond. Individually, 5-ASA and sulfapyridine would be absorbed in the upper gastrointestinal tract, the azo bond prevents such absorption. Colonic bacteria break the azo bond to liberate sulfapyridine and 5-ASA. 5-ASA is considered to be the active moiety .817

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a prodrug?
mcqs.explanation: Mesalamine is not a prodrug. Mesalamine or 5-ASA is the active component that is responsible for the beneficial effects of inflammatory bowel disease . Cleavage of the bond of prodrugs that deliver mesalamine to the colon occurs by colonic bacteria. Option A: Sulfasalazine - 5-ASA + sulfapyridine Option C: Balsalazide - 5-ASA + an inert compound Option D: Olsalazine - 5-ASA + 5-ASA

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: A patient with Crohn's disease , refractory to steroid therapy is planned to be started on an anti-TNF alpha monoclonal antibody. Which of the following drugs does not belong in this class?
mcqs.explanation: Vedolizumab is a humanized anti-alpha-4-beta -7 integrin monoclonal antibody that prevents lymphocyte recruitment to the intestinal mucosa. It is approved for use in moderate -severe Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis . Anti-TNF alpha monoclonal antibodies indicated in IBD are: • Infliximab • Adalimumab • Certolizumab pegol

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Acid Peptic Disorders and Inflammatory Bowel Di...
mcqs.question: Which is not given in Wilson's disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Calcium citrate is not used in the treatment of Wilson's disease . The drugs used in the management of Wilson's disease are: Chelating agents : These drugs bind to copper to form complexes that get excreted in the urine. D-penicillamine and trientine are first-line drugs in symptomatic patients with hepatic diseases . • D-penicillamine : It is the recommended drug due to its availability and cost-effectiveness as compared to trientine. Since it is an antagonist to pyridoxine, supplementation of pyridoxine is required. It can precipitate various adverse effects including aplastic anemia, myasthenia gravis, and membranous nephropathy . It can also worsen neurological symptoms • Trientine: It is administered in those who cannot tolerate D-penicillamine • Tetrathiomolybdate : It has been identified to be effective in patients with neuropsychiatric manifestation Elemental zinc: • Zinc blocks the intestinal absorption of copper by inducing metallothionein (endogenous chelator in enterocytes ) • It is commonly used as a maintenance therapy along with chelating agents . It can also be used as first-line therapy in pregnancy818

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old man came to the OPD with complaints of vomiting for which he was prescribed metoclopramide. What is the primary mechanism of action of this drug?

options.b: Sensitization of muscarinic receptors on smooth muscles

mcqs.explanation: The mechanism of action of metoclopramide is primarily D2 antagonism in the chemoreceptor trigger zone. Metoclopramide has the following actions:828 • 5HT4 receptor agonism - prokinetic action • 5HT3 receptor antagonism - anti-emetic action at higher doses • Peripheral D2 antagonism - prokinetic action • Sensitization of muscarinic receptors on smooth muscles

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following actions is exhibited by metoclopramide ?

options.a: Inhibits cholinergic smooth muscle stimulation in the gastrointestinal tract
options.b: Decreases the lower esophageal sphincter pressure

mcqs.explanation: Metoclopramide enhances gastrointestinal motility . Acetylcholine increases gastrointestinal motility and lower esophageal sphincter (LES) tone. Dopamine which is an inhibitory neurotransmitter suppresses ACh release . This decreases gastrointestinal motility and LES tone. Therefore, D2 receptor inhibition augments ACh release and enhances GI motility and LES tone. The action of metoclopramide is generally confined to the upper digestive tract and an increase in colonic motility is clinically insignificant.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient presented to the casualty with signs of dehydration due to severe vomiting. The intern gave the patient a parenteral medication, following which the patient developed grimacing and abnormal posturing . What could have been the inciting drug for this reaction?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario describes the adverse effects characteristic of metoclopramide . The most common adverse effects of metoclopramide involve the central nervous system because it crosses the blood-brain barrier (BBB ) and blocks the central D2 receptors . The adverse effects include : • Restlessness • Drowsiness • Insomnia • Anxiety • Agitation • Extrapyramidal effects - acute reaction with high doses and long-term therapy . (due to central dopamine receptor blockade) • Dystonias • Akathisia • Parkinsonian features • Tardive dyskinesia Adverse events are more common among the elderly . Long-term use should be avoided unless absolutely necessary .829

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient developed abnormal posturing and grimacing following the administration of metoclopramide. Which drug will you administer to manage this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of dystonia associated with D2 blocker (metoclopramide ) use . Promethazine is the drug of choice . It is a first-generation antihistaminic having significant central anticholinergic activity.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is implicated in prolonging QT interval and causing serious arrhythmias?
mcqs.explanation: Cisapride is associated with prolongation of QT interval and causation of serious ventricular arrhythmias. Prolongation of QT interval is due to blockade of rapid delayed rectifier potassium channels. It is banned or has restricted use in most of the countries . Ondansetron is associated with asymptomatic electrocardiogram changes , including prolongation of PT and QTc intervals.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs do not act as a prokinetic agent by 5HT4 agonism?
mcqs.explanation: Domperidone does not have any 5HT4 agonist action. It mainly acts by D2 antagonist action. 5HT4 agonism and D2 antagonism can result in prokinetic action by increasing the cholinergic activity of the gut . The 5HT4 agonist action is shown by: • Metoclopramide • Cisapride • Mosapride • Itopride • Renzapride

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a prokinetic?
mcqs.explanation: Diphenylmethane is not a prokinetic agent . Its derivative (Bisacodyl) is used as a laxative. Prokinetic agents are the drugs that increase GI motility and transit of material in the GI tract. These agents include : • Dopamine receptor antagonists- metoclopramide and domperidone • Serotonin receptor agonists- cisapride and prucalopride • Motilin • Macrolide antibiotics mimicking motilin - erythromycin830 • Miscellaneous agents : • Sincalide (C-terminal octapeptide of CCK) • Camicinal (motilin receptor agonist) • Relamorelin (ghrelin receptor agonist) • Velusetrag and naronapride (5HT4 agonists)

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old male with unhealthy eating practices now complains of constipation . He took bisacodyl , following which he had symptomatic relief . Which group of drugs does this belong to?
mcqs.explanation: Bisacodyl is a stimulant laxative. Stimulant laxatives act by irritation of the intestinal mucosa and direct action on myenteric plexus neurons stimulating motility and secretion. Examples of stimulant/irritant laxatives are: • Bisacodyl • Sodium picosulfate • Anthraquinones like senna, cascara sagrada • Castor oil

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A colonoscopy of an elderly patient revealed brownish pigmented lesions as shown below . He admitted to chronic laxative abuse . Which of the following laxatives is most likely to cause this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The above colonoscopy image depicts a brownish moir\351 pattern that is indicative of melanosis coli. Chronic use of anthraquinone laxatives like senna and cascara sagrada can cause melanosis coli. Bisacodyl is also implicated in causing melanosis coli.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You want to prescribe a bulk-forming laxative to an elderly patient with constipation . Which among the following would you not prescribe ?
mcqs.explanation: Liquid paraffin is not a bulk-forming laxative. It is a mineral oil and acts as a stool softener . It is rarely used in clinical practice today because of its drawbacks, such as: • Bland and unpleasant taste • Risk of lipoid pneumonia • Anal leakage Bulk-forming laxatives are: • Bran • Psyllium • Methylcellulose831 • Polycarbophil

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 3-year-old child is brought to the pediatric OPD by his mother with complaints of acute watery diarrhea for 2 days. Oral rehydration solution , zinc supplement , and a peripheral enkephalinase inhibitor were prescribed . Which of the following drugs did he prescribe ?
mcqs.explanation: Racecadotril is a peripheral enkephalinase inhibitor. Enkephalins are endogenous delta -opioid receptor agonists that decrease intestinal secretions without affecting motility . Enkephalinase is the enzyme that degrades enkephalin. Racecadotril, by inhibiting the enkephalinase enzyme increases enkephalin level and acts as an antisecretory agent in diarrhea. It has minimal/no effect on motility . Racecadotril is indicated for symptomatic treatment of diarrhea in infants and children. Options B and C: Diphenoxylate and loperamide are �M-opioid receptor agonists. Option D: Linaclotide is a guanylate cyclase agonist.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old male who is on anti-retroviral therapy presents with complaints of diarrhea for three days. An infectious etiology is ruled out on work-up. Which of the following drugs is preferred to manage his diarrhea?
mcqs.explanation: This is a case of non-infectious diarrhea associated with antiretroviral therapy (ART ). Crofelemer is indicated for non-infectious diarrhea associated with ART in HIV /AIDS. Crofelemer has minimal systemic absorption. It acts by inhibiting the cyclic AMP-stimulated CFTR chloride channel and calcium-activated chloride channels on the luminal side of the intestine .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 38-year-old woman complains of recurrent episodes of constipation and crampy abdominal pain for the last 4 months. The pain is relieved on defecation . After investigations, a diagnosis of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation is considered . Which of the following drugs would you prescribe ?
mcqs.explanation: The drug used in irritable bowel syndrome with constipation is lubiprostone . It is approved for chronic idiopathic constipation and constipation -predominant irritable bowel syndrome (in female patients >18 years). It acts by stimulating Cl-channels in the intestine and increasing fluid secretion in the gut . This decreases the transit time. Eluxadoline is an FDA-approved opioid drug for the treatment of diarrhea-predominant IBS in adults .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The use of which of the following drugs is associated with ischemic colitis ?
mcqs.explanation: Ischemic colitis is associated with the use of alosetron. It is a 5HT3 antagonist that may suppress intestinal relaxation leading to ischemic colitis in susceptible individuals. It is approved for resistant diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome in female patients . It is either withdrawn/ has restricted use because of the serious side effect .832

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who is suffering from chronic constipation is prescribed a guanylcycline C agonist. Identify the drug.
mcqs.explanation: The guanylcycline -C (GC-C) agonist indicated in chronic constipation is linaclotide . Linaclotide is a peptide agonist that activates GC-C which leads to increased synthesis of cyclic-GMP. This results in enhanced chloride and bicarbonate secretion into the intestinal lumen leading to increased water secretion and enhanced motility . It is indicated in constipation -predominant IBS in females and in chronic idiopathic constipation in adults .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Prucalopride is a ______.
mcqs.explanation: Prucalopride is a specific 5HT4 receptor agonist which increases bowel movements. It is approved for use in women with chronic constipation where other laxatives have failed to provide relief .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old woman suffering from erratic bowel habits for the past few months is diagnosed with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome. Which antibiotic is specifically approved for the treatment of her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The antibiotic that is specifically approved for diarrhea-predominant IBS is rifaximin . It is an RNA synthesis inhibitor. It may provide benefit by altering the gastrointestinal flora favorably. Rifabutin, rifampicin and rifapentine are antitubercular agents .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 20 -year-old primiparous woman came to the OPD with complaints of nausea and vomiting at 8 weeks of gestation . Which of the following is specifically indicated to provide symptomatic relief in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Doxylamine is indicated with pyridoxine to reduce mild to moderate nausea and vomiting in the early stages of pregnancy. It is a histamine H1 antagonist and its efficacy is improved when combined with pyridoxine. Combinations of domperidone , dolasetron and metoclopramide with pyridoxine are not specifically indicated in pregnancy.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is the drug of choice in a patient complaining of nausea and vomiting, 2 days after commencement of a cisplatin-based chemotherapeutic regimen?
mcqs.explanation: This patient is most likely suffering from delayed emesis associated with cancer chemotherapy . Combined therapy with aprepitant (NK-1/ neurokinin -1 receptor antagonist), a 5-HT3-receptor antagonist, and dexamethasone is the best treatment in delayed emesis associated with cancer chemotherapy .833 Delayed chemotherapy -induced vomiting is any emesis occurring >24 hours after chemotherapy . If NK-1 receptor antagonists are not used in the combination, delayed emesis is prevented only in 30% of the patients . Usage of 5HT3 antagonists alone has no role in the treatment of delayed emesis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: An AIDS patient presents with anorexia and weight loss. Which of the following is a naturally extracted cannabinoid that is approved for his condition?
mcqs.explanation: Dronabinol or delta -9-tetrahydrocannabinol is a cannabinoid that can be extracted naturally. It is the only cannabinoid that is approved for anorexia and weight loss associated with AIDS. It is obtained from the marijuana plant or can be synthesized chemically . Option B: Nabilone is a synthetic cannabinoid. Dronabinol and nabilone are approved for the treatment of refractory cases of chemotherapy -induced nausea and vomiting. Option C: Tibolone is a 19-norsteroid derivative specifically to be used for hormone replacement therapy. Option D: Cannabidiol is a cannabinoid approved for the treatment of seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, Dravet syndrome, or tuberous sclerosis complex .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about aprepitant is false ?

options.c: Ameliorate nausea and vomiting induced by chemotherapy

mcqs.explanation: Aprepitant is a high-affinity NK1 receptor antagonist that blocks the emetic action of substance P. Aprepitant is well absorbed orally and crosses the blood-brain barrier . Co-administration of oral aprepitant with dexamethasone and ondansetron significantly enhances the antiemetic efficacy against the highly emetogenic side effects of chemotherapeutic drugs like cisplatin and cyclophosphamide . It is metabolized in the liver by the CYP450 enzyme.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antiemetic drugs also decreases acid secretion due to its action on H1 receptors ?
mcqs.explanation: An antiemetic drug that also decreases acid secretion due to its action on H1 histamine receptors is promethazine. The central anticholinergic activity of promethazine is responsible for antiemetic action.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The 5HT3 antagonist having maximum potency in chemotherapy -induced vomiting is:
mcqs.explanation: The 5HT3 antagonist having maximum potency in chemotherapy -induced vomiting is palonosetron.834 It has a high affinity for 5HT3 and is also the longest -acting 5HT3 antagonist. This makes it more effective in delayed emesis associated with chemotherapy . During chemotherapy , there is cell lysis and 5HT (serotonin) is released from the gut mucosa. The released serotonin acts on the 5HT3 receptors , activating the vagal afferents in the gut that carry the emetogenic impulses to the nucleus tractus solitarius and chemoreceptor trigger zone. The selective blockade of 5HT3 receptors reduces the emetogenic impulses . Granisetron, dolasetron , and ondansetron are also effective for chemotherapy -induced vomiting. Cilansetron is a new 5HT3 antagonist indicated for irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Most effective antiemetic for chemotherapy -induced vomiting is_________.
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , the most effective antiemetic for chemotherapy -induced vomiting is granisetron. Granisetron is a 5HT3 receptor antagonist. They are the most effective drugs for the treatment of chemotherapy -induced and post -operative nausea and vomiting. Palonosetron is a second -generation 5HT3 antagonist that has the highest affinity for 5HT3 receptors and has the maximum potency . It is also the longest acting that makes it effective in delayed emesis associated with chemotherapy . Palonosetron has minimal/no propensity to cause QT interval prolongation.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: QT interval prolongation is minimal with which of the following 5-HT3 antagonists?
mcqs.explanation: Palonosetron is a second -generation 5-HT3 antagonist and has minimal/no propensity to cause QT prolongation. First-generation 5-HT3 antagonists have an increased risk of QT interval prolongation. Intravenous dolasetron is contraindicated for prophylaxis of chemotherapy -induced nausea and vomiting for the same reason.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following NK1 receptor antagonists has the longest half-life ?
mcqs.explanation: Rolapitant has the longest plasma half-life of 180 hours. It is a highly selective NK1 receptor antagonist.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A young male developed 5 episodes of loose stools 2 hours after eating in a restaurant. He is afebrile and has mild dehydration . What should be the treatment ?
mcqs.explanation: It is a case of acute diarrhea in an afebrile, stable patient which can be managed with ORS alone. Management of diarrhea:835 • Mild -moderate dehydration - ORS. • Severe dehydration - IV fluids are given. • Afebrile patient - No antibiotics are given. • Febrile patient - empirical antibiotics. If only bacterial etiology is suspected , ciprofloxacin is given. If giardiasis is suspected , metronidazole or tinidazole are recommended .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: You and your friend plan for a mountain trip for the day after. What medication would you advise him to help with his motion sickness?

options.a: Ranitidine tablet before start of trip
options.c: Scopolamine patch the night before trip
options.d: Omeprazole the night before and before start of trip

mcqs.explanation: In the above case, a scopolamine patch the night before the trip should be advised. Treatment for motion sickness : • Scopolamine patch- preferred , most effective . • Do not give to children <10 years of age . • Place patch behind the ears at least 4 hours before travel and replace every 72 hours as needed . • Transdermal patch – Most effective • Oral dose - 0.4–0.6 mg one hour before travel and then TID may be recommended . • Cinnarizine – 30mg, 2 hours prior to travel, and 15mg TID as required. Not as effective as scopolamine . Moderately effective . • Promethazine • Other drugs (minimally effective ): • Cyclizine • Dimenhydrinate • Diphenhydramine • Meclizine PPI 's / ranitidine / traditional ginger – all are ineffective .836

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine , 2018 was awarded to James P. Allison and Tasuku Honjo for which of the following discoveries ?

options.b: Discoveries of molecular mechanisms controlling the circadian rhythm
options.c: Discovery of cancer therapy by inhibition of negative immune regulation
options.d: Discovery that mature cells can be reprogrammed to become pluripotent

mcqs.explanation: The Nobel prize in Physiology or Medicine , 2018 was awarded to James P. Allison and Tasuku Honjo for the discovery of cancer therapy by inhibition of negative immune regulation . Immune checkpoint inhibitors inhibit proteins that keep immune responses to cancer cells in check. When these proteins are blocked , the brake on the immune system is released and T cells are able to kill cancer cells more efficiently . The Nobel prize 2018 in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to James P. Allison and Tasuku Honjo for their breakthrough work on unleashing the body's immune system to attack cancer, that has led to an entirely new class of these drugs and brought lasting remissions to many patients who had run out of options .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a cell -cycle specific agent ?
mcqs.explanation: Vinblastine is a cell cycle -specific agent and a vinca alkaloid. It arrests mitosis and acts specifically on M-phase . Cyclophosphamide , melphalan, and ifosfamide are nitrogen mustards and are cell -cycle non-specific agents . Cell cycle specific agents : • Antimetabolites : S phase • Camptothecin analogs: S Phase • Taxanes, Vinca alkaloids: M phase846 • Epipodophyllotoxin : G1-S phase • Bleomycin: G2-M phase Cell cycle non-specific agents : • Alkylating agents • Platinum analogs • Anthracyclines • Mitomycin, dactinomycin

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an antimetabolite ?
mcqs.explanation: Methotrexate is an antimetabolite . It is a folic acid analog that inhibits the enzyme dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR). Methotrexate and its polyglutamate also inhibit the enzymes involved in denovo purine and thymidylate synthesis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following disease -modifying anti rheumatoid drug increases extracellular adenosine ?
mcqs.explanation: Methotrexate is the disease -modifying anti rheumatoid drug that increases extracellular adenosine . Methotrexate 's principal mechanism of action relates to inhibition of amino-imidazole carboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR ) transformylase and thymidylate synthetase . AICAR accumulates intracellularly , competitively inhibits AMP deaminase , leading to an accumulation of AMP. The AMP is released and converted extracellularly to adenosine , which is a potent inhibitor of inflammation. As a result , the inflammatory functions of neutrophils , macrophages , dendritic cells , and lymphocytes are suppressed .847

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following conditions is methotrexate not used ?
mcqs.explanation: Indications for methotrexate (inflammatory conditions) include : • Rheumatoid arthritis • Psoriasis • Psoriatic arthritis • Ankylosing spondylitis • Polymyositis • Dermatomyositis • Wegener 's granulomatosis • Giant cell arteritis • Systemic lupus erythematosus • Other systemic vasculitis • Graft versus host disease associated with organ transplantation. Sickle cell anemia appears to be the most appropriate answer among the options. Though small trials have shown positive results in sickle cell disease , it is neither extensively used nor approved for this indication.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following conditions is high dose methotrexate indicated in?
mcqs.explanation: High-dose methotrexate with leucovorin rescue (HDM-L) is a standard agent for adjuvant therapy of osteosarcoma. HDM is critical in the management of childhood acute lymphocytic leukemia (ALL ). HDM-L also produces a high response rate in CNS lymphomas.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old lady was diagnosed with gestational trophoblastic neoplasia and started on methotrexate . However the hCG levels of the patient kept rising. What could be the cause of this phenomenon ?
mcqs.explanation: The scenario depicts a case of Methotrexate resistance . This happens due to the overproduction of DHFR (dihydrofolate reductase ). Mechanism of resistance to methotrexate includes : • Impaired transport of methotrexate into cells • Production of altered forms of DHFR that have decreased affinity for methotrexate • The increased concentration of intracellular DHFR through gene amplification or gene regulation • Decreased ability to form methotrexate polyglutamates • Increased expression of drug efflux transporter848

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with impaired renal function, undergoing chemotherapy , develops methotrexate toxicity. Which of the following drugs is a methotrexate cleaving enzyme that can be used to manage this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Glucarpidase , which is a methotrexate cleaving enzyme, can be used in this condition. Glucarpidase is an FDA approved intravenous drug for the treatment of methotrexate toxicity in the treatment of cancer patients who have impaired kidney function. Glucarpidase is a recombinant bacterial enzyme that breaks down methotrexate into inactive metabolites rapidly after injection. These inactive metabolites are then eliminated by the liver. Note : Leucovorin is also a substrate of glucarpidase . Leucovorin is avoided 2 hours before and after the administration of glucarpidase to avoid its breakdown.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about methotrexate is false ?

options.c: Non-proliferative cells are resistant to it
options.d: It targets the S-phase of the cell cycle

mcqs.explanation: Folinic acid, also known as leucovorin, the active form of folic acid, is administered with methotrexate to reduce the toxicity associated with higher doses . It does not enhance the action of methotrexate . Methotrexate is an antimetabolite that inhibits dihydrofolate reductase . It is a cell cycle (S-phase ) specific antineoplastic agent and non-proliferative cells are relatively resistant to it. Bone marrow suppression and gastrointestinal mucosa inflammation (mucositis) are the common side effects seen due to inhibition of DNA synthesis . Methotrexate toxicity : • Prevention - administration of leucovorin /folinic acid. • Treatment - maintaining adequate hydration and forced alkaline diuresis in patients with normal renal function. • Glucarpidase is an intravenous drug administered in patients who have impaired renal function.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient is on methotrexate therapy as part of his chemotherapy regimen. Which of the following tests is not indicated for monitoring in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Fundoscopy is not monitored in a patient on methotrexate therapy . This is because no significant eye -related adverse effect is associated with either low, normal or high-dose methotrexate use , mandating frequent monitoring. Option A - Hepatic fibrosis or cirrhosis is a significant side effect of long-term therapy of methotrexate that requires regular hepatic function monitoring. Option B - Allergic interstitial pneumonitis and other pulmonary-related adverse effects are associated with methotrexate . Option D - Myelosuppression is a common and a serious adverse effect that mandates routine monitoring of hemogram.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: During rounds, one of your colleagues suggested alkalization of urine with sodium bicarbonate for a patient , to reduce the toxicity of a chemotherapeutic agent . Which is the chemotherapeutic drug being discussed here?
mcqs.explanation: 849 The drug being discussed here is methotrexate . Alkalization of urine ameliorates the toxicity of methotrexate. Methotrexate is an acidic drug and the excretion is increased by alkalization of urine. High-dose methotrexate with leucovorin (HDM-L) used in some conditions has a higher incidence of nephrotoxicity . It is attributed to the precipitation of methotrexate in the acidic tubular fluid . Vigorous hydration and alkalinization of urine prior to HDM-L administration is required to minimize the chance of nephrotoxicity .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an inhibitor of DNA synthesis ?
mcqs.explanation: 6-Mercaptopurine is an inhibitor of DNA synthesis . 6-Mercaptopurine is inactive in its parent form. It must be metabolized by hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase to form monophosphate nucleotide 6-thioinosinic acid. This inhibits several enzymes of de novo purine nucleotide synthesis . Option B- Mitomycin acts as an alkylating agent and crosslinks DNA. It also generates free radicals which damage DNA. Option C- Actinomycin causes single -strand breaks in DNA. It blocks RNA transcription as well . Option D- L-Asparaginase causes the breakdown of asparagine and thus interferes with protein synthesis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What should be done to the dose of intravenous 6-mercaptopurine when it is administered in a patient taking allopurinol?
mcqs.explanation: Intravenous dosing of 6-mercaptopurine (6MP) does not require any dosing adjustment when administered with allopurinol. 6MP undergoes the first-pass metabolism by xanthine oxidase in the liver and intestine . Since allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase , it causes elevated levels of 6-MP. Hence , the oral dose of 6MP needs to be reduced by 75 % if allopurinol is given. In the case of intravenous administration, the dosage need not be changed as it escapes the first-pass metabolism .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient developed the following lesions after 10 days of initiation of chemotherapy . The patient also complains of similar lesions over soles and they are sensitive to touch . Which is the most likely agent to cause this adverse effect ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image depicts classical findings of hand-foot syndrome and capecitabine is commonly associated with this prominent side effect . Hand foot syndrome or palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia consists of erythema , desquamation, pain and sensitivity to touch of the palms and soles . Drugs commonly implicated are: • Capecitabine850 • 5-Fluorouracil • Cytarabine • Pemetrexed • Doxorubicin

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following patients is pemetrexed the drug of choice ?

options.b: A patient with small cell carcinoma
options.c: A patient with stage II non-small cell lung carcinoma
options.d: A patient with inflammatory breast cancer

mcqs.explanation: Pemetrexed is the drug of choice for the treatment of malignant mesothelioma . It is an antifolate drug that belongs to the antimetabolite group. It acts by inhibiting thymidylate synthase and dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) and prevents the formation of DNA and RNA, which are required for the growth and survival of both normal cells and cancer cells . Pemetrexed is used for the treatment of stage IV non-small cell carcinoma along with cisplatin.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who is undergoing chemotherapy is to be started on allopurinol. Which of these drugs might require dose reduction ?
mcqs.explanation: A patient receiving allopurinol requires a dose reduction of 6-mercaptopurine . Allopurinol is a potent xanthine oxidase inhibitor that is often used in acute leukemias as supportive care to prevent the development of hyperuricemia due to tumor lysis syndrome. 6-mercaptopurine is converted to an inactive metabolite (6-thiouric acid) by xanthine oxidase in the liver and intestine . Therefore, the oral bioavailability of the 6-mercaptopurine is reduced significantly due to high first-pass metabolism . Concomitant allopurinol use increases 6-mercaptopurine availability which leads to toxicity , thereby mandating oral dose reduction. Note : Intravenous dosing of 6-mercaptopurine need not require any dosing adjustment when administered with allopurinol.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following enzymes is inhibited by pentostatin ?
mcqs.explanation: Pentostatin mimics adenosine and inhibits the enzyme adenosine deaminase . Adenosine deaminase inhibition leads to the accumulation of adenosine and deoxyadenosine nucleotides that blocks DNA synthesis by inhibiting RNR (ribonucleotide reductase ). Pentostatin also inhibits RNA synthesis , its triphosphate derivative is incorporated into DNA causing strand breakage. It is indicated in the treatment of hairy cell leukemia.851

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old patient presented with weakness , fatigue , and abdominal discomfort. On examination , splenomegaly was present. Investigations revealed pancytopenia , and his peripheral blood smear is shown below . Immunophenotype testing revealed CD11c, CD25, and CD103 positive . What is the drug of choice for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario, characteristic immunophenotype , and the presence of hairy cells on the Wright-stained peripheral blood smear point to a diagnosis of hairy cell leukaemia. Cladribine is considered the drug of choice for hairy cell leukemia. It is administered daily by continuous infusion for 7 days. A single course of therapy achieves a complete response in about 80% of the patients .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is a topoisomerase I inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Irinotecan is a topoisomerase I inhibitor. Doxorubicin and etoposide inhibit topoisomerase II . Vincristine is a vinca alkaloid derivative that inhibits microtubule polymerization.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a mitotic polymerization inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Vinca alkaloids like vinblastine and vincristine bind to beta -tubulin and inhibit its polymerization with alpha-tubulin into microtubules . Paclitaxel does not inhibit polymerization, rather it stabilizes polymerization and inhibits the breakdown of microtubules . Gemcitabine is an antimetabolite and a pyrimidine analog. Dactinomycin or actinomycin D is an actinomycin.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient who was diagnosed with myocardial infarction underwent PCI and stenting with paclitaxel coated drug-eluting stent . What is the mechanism of action of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Paclitaxel binds specifically to beta -tubulin and promotes the polymerization and inhibits the disassembly of this cytoskeletal protein, resulting in the arrest of the cell cycle in M-phase . The first generation drug eluting stents used in PCI were coated with paclitaxel or sirolimus as an anti-proliferative agent . Second -generation drug-eluting stents use newer agents such as everolimus, biolimus, and zotarolimus.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Bone marrow suppression is not seen with which of the following drugs?
mcqs.explanation: Bone marrow suppression is not seen with vincristine. Vinblastine and vinorelbine have prominent bone marrow depression . Bone marrow sparing cytotoxic drugs are: • Vincristine852 • Bleomycin • L-asparaginase

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man was diagnosed with AML and initiated on chemotherapy . During the course of his treatment , he develops ataxia and slurred speech . Which of the following drugs could have caused this?
mcqs.explanation: This scenario describes a case of cerebellar toxicity and cytarabine is associated with this condition. It is seen especially with intrathecal administration or high dose systemic use . Cerebellar toxicity manifests as ataxia and slurred speech . Cerebral toxicity (seizures , dementia , and coma) is also seen .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding vincristine?

options.b: Its use is associated with neurotoxicity
options.d: It is a useful drug for induction of remission in ALL

mcqs.explanation: Vincristine use is associated with alopecia. It is usually reversible frequently without discontinuation of the drug. Vincristine is a vinca alkaloid derivative. It is mainly indicated for induction of remission in acute leukemias including ALL . Neurotoxicity is one of the main side effects .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: In which of the following conditions can all-trans-retinoic acid be used for treatment ?
mcqs.explanation: All-trans-retinoic acid (tretinoin) is used in the treatment of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL ). RAR -alpha and retinoid X receptor dimer binds tretinoin tightly and causes differentiation of promyelocytes resulting in decreased proliferation. As monotherapy, tretinoin induces a high rate of complete remission and in combination with anthracyclines cures most of the patients.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following antineoplastic agents is extracted from the plant shown below ?
mcqs.explanation: The image shown is of the periwinkle plant (Catharanthus roseus ). Vinca alkaloids like vinblastine and vincristine are extracted from this plant. Sources of few other drugs are: • Epothilones - Myxobacterium Sorangium cellulosum • Camptothecin analogs - Camptotheca acuminata tree • Taxanes - bark of the western yew tree .853

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old woman is diagnosed with melanoma. On examination, a palpable lymph node was present in the posterior triangle. Biopsy revealed presence of tumour cells . Which of the following drugs used to treat this condition is a MEK inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: The scenario is suggestive of metastatic melanoma and trametinib is used in this condition. It is a reversible inhibitor of mitogen -activated extracellular signal regulated kinase (MEK ). It inhibits the serine-threonine kinase domain of BRAF V600E mutant of MEK . It is widely used in the treatment of metastatic or unresectable melanoma. It can be used as a single agent but it is more effective when used with BRAF inhibitors like dabrafenib. Adverse effects of this drug include rash, diarrhea, increased ALT , abdominal pain, stomatitis, increased AST, anemia, etc . Dabrafenib and vemurafenib are BRAF inhibitors used in metastatic melanoma. Ipilimumab is a human cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA -4) blocking antibody used in metastatic or unresectable melanoma. Recent update : The FDA has approved the combination of the BRAF inhibitor encorafenib and the MEK inhibitor binimetinib for the treatment of patients with BRAF -mutant unresectable or metastatic melanoma.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old woman had undergone modified radical mastectomy followed by chemotherapy with trastuzumab. She now presents with liver metastases . Which of the following drugs could be used in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario depicts a case of trastuzumab-refractory breast cancer and lapatinib is used in this condition.Drug Use Lapatinib Refractory and metastatic br east carcinoma Panitum umab Colorectal carcinoma Erlotinib Non small cell lung carcinom aPancreatic carcinoma Imatinib Chronic myeloid leukemiaGa strointestinal stromal tumour854

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: Which of the following is more likely to be susceptible to alkylation with a bifunctional alkylating agent ?
mcqs.explanation: The N7 atom of guanine is particularly susceptible to alkylation with bifunctional alkylating agents . It leads to the formation of a covalent bond with bifunctional alkylating agents and represents the key target in nucleic acids for alkylating agents . Alkylation results in cross-linking/abnormal base pairing of DNA which inhibits DNA replication.863 Other sites that can be involved are: • N1 and N3 of adenosine • N3 of cytosine • O6 of guanine

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: During a study on the cytotoxic effects of alkylating agents , you observe that cyclophosphamide has a higher cytotoxic effect compared to procarbazine. Which property of cyclophosphamide is the reason for this?
mcqs.explanation: Cyclophosphamide (nitrogen mustard) is a bifunctional alkylating agent and it results in cross-linking of DNA that causes a major disruption in nucleic acid function and increased cytotoxicity . Procarbazine is a monofunctional alkylating agent . Differences between bifunctional and monofunctional alkylating agents are:Bifunctional alkylating agent s Monofunctional alkylating a gents Usually transfers ethyl group to DNA resulting in cross-lin king Usually transfers a methyl gr oup resulting in simple meth ylation. No cross-linking of D NA Higher cytotoxicity because o f cross-linking results in a gre ater threat to cellular survival Higher carcinogenesis risk as simple methylation can be b ypassed by DNA polymerases resulting in permanent modi fication of DNA sequence

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: Which among the following is not an alkylating agent ?
mcqs.explanation: 5-Flourouracil is a pyrimidine analogue and is an antimetabolite .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a nitrogen mustard?
mcqs.explanation: Carmustine belongs to the nitrosourea class of alkylating agents .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: Temozolomide is used as a first-line agent for the management of which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Temozolomide is used as a first-line agent for the management of glioblastoma multiforme . It is used for newly diagnosed cases along with radiotherapy and also used for maintenance therapy .864 Temozolomide belongs to the triazene group of alkylating agents and is administered orally. The oral bioavailability of temozolomide is nearly 100 %. In anaplastic astrocytoma, refractory cases with disease progression are treated with a regimen containing nitrosourea and procarbazine.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A patient is diagnosed with astrocytoma. Which of the following drugs crosses the blood brain barrier and hence can be used for the treatment of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Lomustine can cross the blood-brain barrier and is used in the management of brain tumours like astrocytoma. Nitrosoureas like lomustine and carmustine are highly lipophilic drugs and can easily cross the blood-brain barrier . Hence , they are indicated in the management of brain tumors.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is not an anthracycline antibiotic?
mcqs.explanation: Dactinomycin or actinomycin D is an actinomycin and not an anthracycline antibiotic.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: Topical mitomycin C is used in which of the following patients ?

options.c: A patient undergoing endoscopic treatment of angiofibroma

mcqs.explanation: Topical mitomycin C is used in laryngotracheal stenosis . Mitomycin C is an antitumor antibiotic that inhibits cell division, protein synthesis and fibroblast proliferation. Topical mitomycin C has been shown to cause symptomatic improvement when applied to patients with laryngotracheal stenosis .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A patient with superficial bladder carcinoma is being treated with a drug by intravesical therapy. Identify this drug.
mcqs.explanation: Mitomycin C is used in the treatment of superficial transitional cell carcinoma by intravesical instillation. It is also used in upper gastrointestinal cancers (e.g. esophageal carcinoma ), anal cancers, and breast cancers. Topical mitomycin C is used in: • Superficial bladder cancer • Intraperitoneal tumors • Strabismus surgery to reduce scarring • To prevent tracheal and esophageal stenosis • Post nasal surgery synechae formation865

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A patient was diagnosed with acute promyelocytic leukemia and chemotherapy was initiated . The patient achieved complete remission. However, after a few months molecular relapse was detected . Which of the following drugs would be highly effective in this case?
mcqs.explanation: Arsenic trioxide (ATO) is highly effective in relapsed or refractory acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL ). It acts by enhancing reactive oxygen free radical generation in APL cells . Tretinoin and idarubicin (anthracycline) are usually first-line agents for acute promyelocytic leukemia.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A patient with osteosarcoma was initiated on chemotherapy . After a few days, he developed dysuria and hematuria. Which group of drugs among the following is most likely to have caused this complication?
mcqs.explanation: This scenario depicts haemorrhagic cystitis and the possible cause could be alkylating agents like ifosfamide . Chemotherapeutic agents used for the treatment of osteosarcoma include ifosfamide , which is one of the commonest drugs causing haemorrhagic cystitis . Ifosfamide is a nitrogen mustard and belongs to the alkylating agents .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: Hemorrhagic cystitis is a characteristic side effect of which of the following drugs?
mcqs.explanation: Hemorrhagic cystitis is a characteristic side effect of cyclophosphamide . The metabolite responsible for hemorrhagic cystitis is acrolein. This can be decreased by vigorous hydration and by the use of mercapto ethane sulfonic acid (mesna).

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A 62-year-old woman with breast carcinoma is started on cyclophosphamide . What is the rationale behind using sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate along with this drug?
mcqs.explanation: Sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate (MESNA ) is given along with cyclophosphamide to reduce the incidence of hemorrhagic cystitis . MESNA concentrates in the bladder where acrolein accumulates after administration of cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide . It forms a conjugate with acrolein and other urotoxic metabolites . This conjugation reaction inactivates the urotoxic compounds to harmless metabolites which are excreted in the urine.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about ifosfamide is false ?

options.c: Chloroacetaldehyde is the metabolite of ifosfamide

mcqs.explanation: Ifosfamide is more neurotoxic than cyclophosphamide . It causes greater platelet suppression , nephrotoxicity, and urothelial damage when compared to cyclophosphamide . Ifosfamide is a nitrogen mustard (alkylating agent ). It is metabolized by hydroxylation by cytochrome P450 enzymes . Chloroacetaldehyde is a metabolite of ifosfamide that is responsible for severe neurological adverse effects .866

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A 67 year old woman with a malignant lump in the breast who is undergoing chemotherapy , presents with shortness of breath, tachycardia and hypertension . ECG shows ST and T wave changes . Which among the following drugs could have led to this?
mcqs.explanation: This scenario depicts Doxorubicin induced cardiotoxicity. It is a unique adverse effect of doxorubicin. It is an anthracycline group of anticancer antibiotics. Doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy takes two forms: • Acute : pericarditis-myocarditis syndrome, arrhythmias, ST and T wave changes in ECG. • Chronic: dilated cardiomyopathy . Note : Dexrazoxane is a cardioprotective iron-chelating agent that is indicated for use along with high dose doxorubicin to avoid cardiotoxicity .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A 54-year-old man is diagnosed with Kaposi sarcoma. You are planning to start chemotherapy with doxorubicin, which can cause cardiotoxicity. Which of the following drugs would you prescribe to prevent this?
mcqs.explanation: Dexrazoxane is a cardioprotective iron-chelating agent that is indicated for use along with high dose doxorubicin to avoid cardiotoxicity. The exact cardioprotective mechanism of dexrazoxane is unknown and it appears not to compromise with anticancer activity of doxorubicin.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: Least cardiotoxicity is seen with which of the following anthracycline antibiotic?
mcqs.explanation: Idarubicin has least cardiotoxicity when compared to other anthracyclines. It is approved for use in acute myeloid leukemia along with cytarabine. Doxorubicin, daunorubicin and epirubicin share similar cardiotoxicity profile .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: While reviewing the drug chart of a patient undergoing radiotherapy, which of the following drugs would require a dose adjustment to prevent radiation toxicity ?
mcqs.explanation: Doxorubicin requires dose adjustment during or after radiotherapy in order to prevent radiation toxicity. Anthracyclines like doxorubicin can result in a radiation recall reaction, where erythema and desquamation of skin are observed at sites of previous radiation injury. The risk of cardiotoxicity also increases with previous irradiation . Therefore, careful monitoring and dosage adjustments are required for doxorubicin.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A patient is undergoing chemotherapy for glioblastoma multiforme . You notice that his serial blood investigations reveal sustained neutropenia . Which of the following drugs could have caused this?
mcqs.explanation: Sustained neutropenia is seen with nitrosoureas. Nitrosoureas like carmustine and lomustine cause profound and delayed myelosuppression with recovery 4-6 weeks after a single dose .867

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A patient with Hodgkin's disease on chemotherapy with an alkylating agent develops behavioral disturbances and experiences sedation . He presented to the emergency room with a disulfiram-like reaction. What is the drug being described here?
mcqs.explanation: The most likely alkylating agent being described here is procarbazine. It is associated with behavioural disturbances and sedation. Concomitant CNS depressants should be avoided. Procarbazine is a weak MAO inhibitor and can potentiate tyramine and catecholamines action. It also has disulfiram-like actions and alcohol should be avoided.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A 50 year old man who presented with dysphagia was diagnosed with esophageal carcinoma and underwent multiple cycles of chemotherapy . During the cycles , he had developed tingling and numbness in the lower limbs and the symptoms progressed even after cessation of the cycles . Which drug could have led to this?
mcqs.explanation: The scenario depicts coasting effect neuropathy , which is seen with cisplatin. The coasting effect means the progression of symptoms even after the cessation of the drug. Neurotoxicity is usually dependent on the cumulative dose of anticancer drugs. The severity of neuropathy increases with the duration of treatment and progression stops once drug treatment is completed . Platinum compounds are an exception , where sensory loss progresses for several months after cessation of treatment . The coasting effect is more common with cisplatin and oxaliplatin than with carboplatin.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A 65 year old man who was diagnosed with small cell carcinoma of the lung had undergone chemotherapy about 5 years ago. Now he presents with features suggestive of AML. Which of the following drugs could have caused this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The scenario is suggestive of secondary leukemia which is associated with cisplatin. Cisplatin is a platinum-containing anticancer agent that forms DNA adduct . It is associated with the development of AML usually more than 4 years after treatment . Procarbazine , a methylhydralazine (alkylating agent ), is most commonly associated with the development of leukemias with a 5-10% risk of acute leukemia in patients treated with the MOPP regimen. Cisplatin produces responses in cancers of the bladder , head and neck, cervix, and endometrium ; all forms of carcinoma of the lung; anal and rectal carcinomas; and neoplasms of childhood .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A patient who was diagnosed with gastric carcinoma is undergoing chemotherapy . His serum creatinine levels are rising and you suspect renal tubular damage caused by one of his chemotherapeutic drugs. Which drug could it be?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggesstive of nephrotoxicity and it is one of the dose -limiting toxicity of cisplatin therapy . Cisplatin achieves a high concentration in nephrons. Both direct toxicity and inflammation are responsible for nephrotoxicity . A high concentration of chloride stabilizes cisplatin and reduces nephrotoxicity . Therefore, chloride diuresis is used to reduce nephrotoxicity . Option B - Streptozotocin use can result in diabetes mellitus due to the destruction of beta cells of the pancreas. Option C - Methysergide use is associated with retroperitoneal fibrosis. Option D - Cyclophosphamide causes hemorrhagic cystitis as one of its characteristic side effect .868

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: Which among the following is a highly emetogenic anticancer drug?
