mcqs.explanation: Cisplatin is a highly emetogenic anticancer drug. Cisplatin causes marked nausea and vomiting in almost all cases and is usually administered along with anti-emetic regimens. This can usually be controlled with 5HT3 receptor antagonists, neurokinin (NK1) receptor antagonists (e.g., aprepitant ), and high-dose corticosteroids .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A patient who is undergoing chemotherapy for testicular cancer, now presents with dyspnea and dry cough . Investigations suggest pulmonary fibrosis. This condition is commonly associated with which of the following drugs?
mcqs.explanation: Pulmonary fibrosis is commonly seen with bleomycin . The main abnormality in bleomycin toxicity occurs in endothelial and epithelial cells . This leads to the destruction and desquamation of type I pneumocytes and the resultant hyperplasia of type II pneumocytes . Pulmonary toxicity begins with a dry cough , fine rales, and diffuse basal infiltrates on X-ray and may progress to life -threatening pulmonary fibrosis. No specific treatment is available to ameliorate the toxicity and managed by general symptomatic care. Note : Few case reports of methotrexate causing pulmonary fibrosis are reported . The association is still uncertain as the underlying disease process like RA can also contribute to fibrosis.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A patient who is undergoing chemotherapy , now presents with weight gain, ascites , hepatomegaly and hyperbilirubinemia. You suspect sinusoidal obstruction syndrome. Which drug is the most common cause of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome is most commonly associated with high-dose busulfan . Incidence increases when coadministered with CYP inhibitors. Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome, previously known as veno-occlusive hepatic disease (VOD), involves primary hepatic sinusoidal injury that progresses to diffuse hepatocyte involvement and panvasculitis. This leads to multi-organ failure, and can be life -threatening .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: A patient undergoing chemotherapy was brought to the ER with seizures . He is diagnosed with cerebrovascular accident which you suspect to be due to a drug-induced hypercoagulable state . Which of the following drugs is implicated ?
mcqs.explanation: L-asparaginase causes a hypercoagulable state . It is an enzyme and toxicity results due to the inhibition of protein synthesis in normal tissues . Side effects of L-asparaginase: • Thrombosis and increased coagulation - physiological anticlotting factors are impaired • Hemorrhage and bleeding - clotting factors are impaired • Hyperglycemia - insulin deficiency .869

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs causes flagellate pigmentation ?
mcqs.explanation: Flagellate hyperpigmentation /flagellate erythema is a characteristic cutaneous reaction to treatment with bleomycin . Clinical features include multiple linear streaks (erythematous or hyperpigmented ) at sites of trauma and generalized pruritus.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs cause carcinoma bladder ?
mcqs.explanation: The only chemotherapeutic agent that has been proven to cause bladder cancer is cyclophosphamide . The risk of the bladder cancer formation is linearly related to the duration and intensity of cyclophosphamide treatment , supporting a causative role. Phosphoramide mustard is the primary mutagenic metabolite that causes bladder cancer in patients exposed to cyclophosphamide .870

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Cetuximab is approved for use in which of the following conditions?

options.a: Palliation in head and neck cancer

mcqs.explanation: Cetuximab is used for palliation in head and neck cancer. Indications for use of cetuximab are: • Advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck in combination with radiotherapy for locally or regionally • Metastatic colorectal cancer Cetuximab is a recombinant chimeric monoclonal antibody against the external domain of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR).

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient diagnosed with metastatic colorectal carcinoma is being treated with panitumumab. This drug acts against which of the following receptors ?
mcqs.explanation: Panitumumab is a recombinant fully -humanized monoclonal antibody that binds specifically to the external domain of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). It is approved for use in patients with metastatic colorectal carcinoma .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 57 -year-old woman is diagnosed with HER 2/neu positive breast cancer. Which of the following monoclonal antibodies is indicated for the management of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Trastuzumab is indicated for adjuvant therapy in early and metastatic HER2 positive breast cancer. Trastuzumab is a humanized monoclonal antibody that binds to the extracellular domain of HER2/Neu. Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 tyrosine kinase receptor (HER-2-TK) inhibitors are:878 • Lapatinib • Neratinib Anti-Her-2 monoclonal antibodies are: • Trastuzumab • Pertuzumab

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 57 -year-old woman diagnosed with breast carcinoma was prescribed trastuzumab. Which of the following statements regarding this drug is true?

options.a: It is an antibody produced entirely from mouse containing no human component
options.b: It is a monoclonal antibody produced by injecting HER-2 antigen
options.d: It is a monoclonal antibody containing only human component

mcqs.explanation: Trastuzumab is a humanized monoclonal antibody against the external domain of HER2/neu. In humanized antibodies , all components are identical to human antibodies (95% human component ), except the complementary region of the variable chain that contains sequences from other species . It is indicated in the management of adjuvant therapy in early and metastatic HER-2 positive breast cancer. Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 tyrosine kinase receptor (HER-2-TK) inhibitors are: • Lapatinib • Neratinib Anti-Her-2 monoclonal antibodies are: • Trastuzumab • Pertuzumab

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient was diagnosed with HER2/neu positive breast cancer and was started on adjuvant therapy with trastuzumab. Which of the following is the most serious and dose -limiting toxicity of this drug?
mcqs.explanation: The most serious toxicity of trastuzumab is cardiac failure. Cardiac failure is a potentially disabling or fatal side effect unless recognized early and the drug is discontinued . Cardiotoxicity is caused by the interruption of HER2/4 heterodimer signaling in cardiomyocytes , which is a type of signaling that is essential for the maintenance of contractile function. Clinical correlation: • Baseline ECG and cardiac ejection fraction should be monitored to rule out underlying heart disease • Careful clinical follow -up for signs and symptoms of CHF Other side effects include fever, chills, nausea, dyspnea , and rashes. Dose -limiting toxicities are side effects of a drug or other treatment that are serious enough to prevent an increase in dose or level of that treatment .879

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient diagnosed with wet age -related macular degeneration is being administered ranibizumab intravitreally. All of the following are known side effects of the drug, except _______.
mcqs.explanation: Ranibizumab is associated with a raise in IOP, not a fall. Ranibizumab is a monoclonal antibody directed against VEGF-A (vascular endothelial growth factor-A). Ranibizumab is indicated in wet age -related macular degeneration and is used intravitreally where it inhibits VEGF-A induced ocular neovascularization.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which among the following is the monoclonal antibody that is targeted specifically against VEGFR?
mcqs.explanation: Ramucirumab is a monoclonal antibody that binds to VEGFR-2 and inhibits the binding of VEGFR ligands. It is indicated in NSCLC, gastric cancer and metastatic colorectal cancer. Bevacizumab, aflibercept and ranibizumab are monoclonal antibodies against VEGF ligands and not the receptor .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Rituximab is not used in which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Rituximab is used in all conditions, except paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria. Indications for rituximab include : (mnemonic- CANT MIS Ritu): • CLL • Autoimmune hemolytic anemia • Non-Hodgkin lymphoma • TTP • Marginal zone lymphomas, mantle cell lymphoma, myasthenia gravis • ITP880 • SLE • Rheumatoid arthritis It is a chimeric monoclonal antibody targeted against the CD20 receptor that is present on the surface of B lymphocytes . Ofatumumab and obinutuzumab are the other monoclonal antibodies directed against CD20 receptors . They are also approved for use in CLL .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man is found to have leukocytosis on his yearly health check-up. Further evaluation led to a diagnosis of chronic lymphocytic leukemia. Immunophenotyping was positive for CD52. Which is the monoclonal antibody indicated in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Alemtuzumab is a humanized monoclonal antibody against CD52 that is indicated in the management of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). Rituximab and obinutuzumab are monoclonal antibodies against CD20 that are also indicated in the treatment of chronic lymphocytic leukemia. Cetuximab is a chimeric human-mouse anti-epidermal growth factor receptor monoclonal antibody against the extracellular domain of EGFR.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following monoclonal antibodies is not a HER1 inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Pertuzumab is a monoclonal antibody against the HER2 receptor . Pertuzumab is indicated in HER2-positive breast cancer in combination with trastuzumab and docetaxel . Monoclonal antibodies against EGFR (HER1) are: • Panitumumab • Cetuximab • Necitumumab

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a monoclonal antibody directed against PDGFR-alpha?
mcqs.explanation: Olaratumab is a monoclonal antibody against PDGFR-alpha and blocks ligand-mediated receptor activation. It is indicated along with doxorubicin for adult patients with soft tissue sarcoma. Panitumumab and cetuximab are monoclonal antibodies against EGFR (HER1). Pertuzumab is a monoclonal antibody against HER2.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a bispecific monoclonal antibody?
mcqs.explanation: Blinatumomab is a bispecific monoclonal antibody.881 Bispecific monoclonal antibody simultaneously binds to two different types of antigen. It binds simultaneously to CD3 on T cells and to CD19 on B cells . This links the two cells and activates T cells to exert cytotoxic activity against CD19 B cells . Blinatumomab is approved for the treatment of Philadelphia chromosome-negative relapsed or refractory B-cell precursor ALL . Option A: Daratumumab is a monoclonal antibody against CD-38. Option B: Alemtuzumab is a monoclonal antibody against CD-52. Option D: Panitumumab is a monoclonal antibody against EGFR.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man who presented with fever, night sweats and weight loss was evaluated and diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Which of the following is a radioimmunoconjugate that can be used in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Ibritumomab tiuxetan is a radioimmunoconjugate that is approved for use in non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is a subtype of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. Ibritumomab is a monoclonal antibody against CD20 which is attached to the radioactive isotope yttrium-90 using the chelator tiuxetan . Beta emission from Y-90 destroys the surrounding tissues . Radioimmunoconjugates provide targeted delivery of radionuclides to tumor cells . It is made by attaching a radioactive molecule to a monoclonal antibody. Option A: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin is a monoclonal antibody against CD33 covalently linked to a semisynthetic derivative of calicheamicin which is a potent antitumor antibiotic. Option B: Brentuximab vedotin is a monoclonal antibody against CD30 linked with microtubule disrupting agent MMAE . Option C: Denileukin diftitox is an immunotoxin produced by genetic recombination of IL -2 and the catalytically active fragment of diphtheria toxin.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: What is basiliximab?
mcqs.explanation: Basiliximab exhibits a high affinity towards IL -2 receptor and inhibits it. It is an anti- CD-25 monoclonal antibody. It has a short plasma half-life of 1 week. It is used to prevent transplant rejection reactions. Its adverse effects are anaphylactic reactions & opportunistic infections .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A 2-year-old girl was brought to the hospital by her mother with complaints of abdominal pain and diarrhea. Examination revealed a palpable abdominal mass. Investigations showed elevated levels of urinary homovanillic acid and vanillyl mandelic acid. The lesion could not be completely resected during surgery and histopathology findings are shown in the image. Which of the following is a monoclonal antibody approved for use in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and the histopathology (image) showing small round blue tumor cells with Homer-Wright pseudorosettes , point towards a diagnosis of paediatric neuroblastoma. Dinutuximab is the monoclonal antibody against glycolipid GD2 which is indicated in this condition.882 GD2 glycolipid is expressed on neuroblastoma cells and on normal cells of neuroectodermal origin, including the central nervous system and peripheral nerves.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is recently approved for the treatment of colorectal cancer arising through Lynch Syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Pembrolizumab is the drug recently approved for the treatment of colorectal cancer arising through Lynch syndrome. The increased risk for colorectal cancer in Lynch Syndrome is due to inherited mutations that impair DNA mismatch repair. Immune checkpoint inhibitors inhibit proteins that help to keep immune responses to cancer cells in check. When these proteins are blocked , the brake on the immune system is released and T cells are able to kill cancer cells more efficiently . Pembrolizumab is an immune checkpoint inhibitor. It is a humanized monoclonal IgG4-\026 isotype antibody that blocks the interaction between programmed cell death protein (PD-1) and its ligands. The FDA has approved pembrolizumab for patients with recurrent, locally advanced or metastatic , squamous cell carcinoma of the esophagus and head and neck squamous cell cancer in combination with platin agents and 5-FU for the first-line treatment .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Pembrolizumab is not approved for use in which of the following malignancies?
mcqs.explanation: Pembrolizumab is not approved for use in non-metastatic small-cell lung cancer. It is approved for metastatic small cell lung cancer (SCLC). Pembrolizumab is a monoclonal antibody (IgG4) against PD-1 and blocks interaction between PD-1 and its ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2 . It is used in the following conditions: • Metastatic SCLC • Hodgkin's lymphoma883 • Metastatic urothelial cancer • Metastatic non SCLC • Merkel cell carcinoma • Chemotherapy -refractory head and neck cancers • Refractory melanoma • Triple-Negative Breast Cancer • Esophageal Cancer • Colorectal cancer due to Lynch syndrome

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which among the following is the Interleukin-5 antagonist indicated in the management of asthma?
mcqs.explanation: Reslizumab is a monoclonal antibody against interleukin-5 that is approved for use in severe asthma. Option A & B: Omalizumab is an anti-IgE antibody and lebrikizumab is an antibody against interleukin 13 , which are also indicated in the management of asthma. Option D: Atezolizumab is an immune checkpoint modulator that inhibits the interaction of PD-L1 with PD-1 and B7-H1. It is approved for use in metastatic urothelial cancer and for NSCLC.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the monoclonal antibody developed against Bacillus anthracis?
mcqs.explanation: Obiltoxaximab is a monoclonal antibody against the protective antigen of Bacillus anthracis. It is indicated in the treatment of inhalational anthrax due to B. anthracis in combination with appropriate antibacterial drugs. It is also indicated for prophylaxis of inhalational anthrax .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an immune checkpoint inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Durvalumab is an immune checkpoint inhibitor. It is an antagonist of PD-L1 which is a protein-ligand that is present on antigen-presenting cells , T cells , B cells , and some cancer cells . Immune checkpoint inhibitors inhibit proteins that help the cancer cells evade the immune response . When these proteins are blocked , the brake on the immune system is released and T cells are able to kill cancer cells more efficiently . Durvalumab is approved for use in metastatic urothelial and Merkel cell cancer. The FDA approved Durvalumab in combination with etoposide and either carboplatin or cisplatin as first-line treatment of patients with extensive -stage small-cell lung cancer. Other PD-L1 inhibitors include : • Atezolizumab884 • Avelumab • Durvalumab

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient with rheumatoid arthritis has inadequate disease control with methotrexate . Which Janus kinase inhibitor can you add to his treatment regimen?
mcqs.explanation: Baricitinib is a Janus kinase inhibitor approved for use in rheumatoid arthritis. Oral Janus kinase inhibitors for rheumatoid arthritis are: • Baricitinib • Tofacitinib Option A: Ruxolitinib is a Janus kinase inhibitor approved for use in various forms of myelofibrosis, polycythemia vera and acute graft vs host disease . Options C and D: Dasatinib and ponatinib are BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors indicated for CML.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: A patient has presented to the OPD with raised erythematous plaques on his arms and torso covered in silvery scales . You decide to prescribe a monoclonal antibody targeting interleukin-23 for treatment . Identify this drug.
mcqs.explanation: The scenario described in the question points towards a diagnosis of chronic plaque psoriasis. Tildrakizumab is a monoclonal antibody directed against IL -23 used in the treatment of this condition. IL -23 is a naturally occurring cytokine that is involved in inflammatory and immune responses . Tildrakizumab prevents the interaction of IL -23 with its receptors . It is indicated in moderate -to-severe plaque psoriasis. Secukinumab, ixekizumab, brodalumab are other monoclonal antibodies directed against IL -17A and indicated in moderate -to-severe plaque psoriasis. Note : Ustekinumab is a monoclonal antibody against both IL -12 and IL -23 . It is used for the treatment of Crohn's disease , ulcerative colitis , plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.question: Dupilumab is indicated in the management of _______.
mcqs.explanation: Dupilumab is indicated in the treatment of moderate -to-severe atopic dermatitis. Dupilumab inhibits interleukins IL -4 and IL -13 . When these interleukins are inhibited , they are unable to form complexes with their receptors . This results in a decrease in the immune response including the release of proinflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and IgE.885

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: What is the mechanism of action of imatinib mesylate ?

options.a: Increase in metabolism of P glycoprotein
options.b: Blocking the action of P glycoprotein
options.c: Blocks the action of chimeric fusion protein of BCR-ABL
options.d: Non-competitive inhibition of ATP binding site

mcqs.explanation: Imatinib mesylate blocks the action of the chimeric fusion protein of BCR-ABL . It targets the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase and inhibits the activity of the fusion protein. A single molecular event, 9:22 translocation, leads to the expression of the Abelson proto-oncogene kinase (ABL ) fused to BCR (breakpoint cluster region) yielding a constitutively activated protein kinase in chronic myelogenous leukemia. Imatinib causes remission in >90% of patients in the chronic phase of CML.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Erlotinib is an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) inhibitor. Classification of BCR-ABL kinase inhibitors: • First-generation: most likely to develop resistance . • Imatinib • Second generation: active against imatinib-resistant CML cases but not against T315I mutant cases . • Nilotinib • Dasatinib • Bosutinib • Third generation: active against T315I mutant CML cases and other known mutant cases . • Ponatinib

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: A patient presented with abdominal pain. Imaging revealed a mass in the small intestine and a lesion in the liver. A diagnosis of a c-KIT positive gastrointestinal stromal tumor with liver metastasis was made on further evaluation. What is the drug of choice ?
mcqs.explanation: 895 The drug of choice for the management of a patient with a metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumor is imatinib. It is an oral anticancer drug that acts by inhibiting tyrosine kinase activated due to BCR-ABL fusion. It also inhibits other related tyrosine kinases and hence is used in the treatment of conditions like gastrointestinal stromal tumor (driven by a c-KIT mutation). Imatinib is the agent of choice for GIST patients with metastatic disease and as adjuvant therapy for c-kit positive GIST .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: A patient with chronic myeloid leukemia was switched to nilotinib as he showed only partial response to imatinib therapy . What is the mechanism resulting in the loss of response ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of the development of resistance to imatinib, which is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor. This condition arises due to point mutations in three separate regions of the kinase domain. The contact points between imatinib and the enzyme become sites of mutations in drug-resistant leukemic cells and hence these mutations prevent tight binding of the drug and lock the enzyme in its open configuration (the configuration in which it has access to the substrate and is enzymatically active). Mechanisms other than BCR-ABL kinase mutations play a minor role in resistance to imatinib. They include: • Amplification of the wild -type kinase gene has been identified in some cases . • Overexpression of MDR-gene leading to increased drug efflux transporter has been shown experimentally but not implicated in clinical resistance . Nilotinib retains inhibitory activity in the presence of most point mutations that confer resistance to imatinib.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Imatinib is indicated in which of the following patients ?
mcqs.explanation: Imatinib is the agent of choice in patients with metastatic GIST and as adjuvant therapy for c-kit positive GIST. Imatinib also shows therapeutic benefits in patients with hypereosinophilia syndrome and dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (driven by activating mutations in the PDGFR). Imatinib is an oral anticancer drug that acts by inhibiting tyrosine kinase activated due to ABL -BCR fusion. Imatinib also inhibits other kinases and hence is used in the above-mentioned conditions. Indications for imatinib: • BCR-ABL kinase mutations: • Chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) • Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL ) • C-KIT mutations - gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) • PDGFR mutations:896 • Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans • Hypereosinophilia syndrome • Chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CML)

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a third generation BCR-ABL kinase inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Ponatinib is a third-generation BCR-ABL kinase inhibitor. Classification of BCR-ABL kinase inhibitors: • First-generation: most likely to develop resitance . • Imatinib • Second -generation: active against imatinib-resistant CML cases but not against T315I mutant cases . • Nilotinib • Dasatinib • Bosutinib • Third-generation: active against T315I mutant CML cases and other known mutant cases . • Ponatinib

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: A patient with trastuzumab-refractory breast cancer is started on lapatinib. Which of the following statements is true regarding this drug?

options.a: Dual inhibitor of VEGFR and HER 2 tyrosine kinase
options.b: Dual inhibitor of MET and HER 2 tyrosine kinase
options.c: Dual inhibitor of VEGFR and MET tyrosine kinase
options.d: Dual inhibitor of EGFR and HER 2 tyrosine kinase

mcqs.explanation: Lapatinib is a dual inhibitor of epidermal growth factor (EGFR) and human epidermal growth factor 2 (HER2 ) tyrosine kinase. Lapatinib in combination with capecitabine is approved for the treatment of patients with metastatic HER2-positive and trastuzumab-refractory breast cancer.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Which among the following is an irreversible inhibitor of EGFR tyrosine kinase?
mcqs.explanation: Afatinib binds covalently with epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase (EGFR-TK) also known as Her-1 receptor and inhibits it irreversibly. It is approved for the use of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. Gefitinib and erlotinib compete with ATP binding to EGFR and results in competitive inhibition, which is reversible.897

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: A patient undergoing treatment for colon cancer develops hypertension . Which of the following drugs is most commonly implicated ?
mcqs.explanation: Hypertension is one of the characteristic side effects of angiogenesis inhibitors like bevacizumab. The mechanism is not clear but may be related to decreased endothelial nitric oxide production. Patients receiving higher doses and prolonged treatment might require antihypertensive medications . Bevacizumab can be used in the treatment of metastatic colon cancer, in combination with FOLFOX or FOLFIRI regimen. It can also be used in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: A patient with uncontrolled diabetes is diagnosed to have diabetic macular edema . Which of the following anti-VEGF therapies is effective in the treatment of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Aflibercept is more effective in diabetic macular edema in patients with worse baseline values of visual impairment when compared to bevacizumab and ranibizumab . All of them are administered intravitreally . Clinical trials have shown the advantage of aflibercept over bevacizumab and ranibizumab in visual and anatomic terms at the end of one year. Ramucirumab which is a monoclonal antibody against VEGFR is not indicated for diabetic macular edema.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: A patient is referred to your center for the management of hepatocellular carcinoma . Imaging reveals a large lesion in the liver with multiple intrahepatic metastases . The tumor is found to be unresectable . Which of the following is considered as first-line treatment for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Sorafenib is indicated as a first-line treatment for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma . It is an angiogenesis inhibitor. Hepatocellular carcinoma management:898 • Resection , ablation, and other physical measures are the mainstay. • Only two drugs (angiogenesis inhibitors) are approved in this condition: • Sorafenib (first-line) • Regorafenib (second -line). Sunitinib and thalidomide are not indicated in hepatocellular carcinoma .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Thalidomide should not be used in which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Thalidomide use is associated with peripheral neuropathy and is usually avoided in HIV -associated peripheral neuropathy as it can worsen the condition. It is being investigated as an orphan drug for: • Recurrent aphthous ulcers • GVHD • Behcet syndrome • primary brain malignancies • Kaposi 's sarcoma • Crohn's disease . It is approved for use in multiple myeloma and erythema nodosum leprosum .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Use of lenalidomide over thalidomide would lead to the reduction of incidence of the following side effects , except ___________.
mcqs.explanation: Lenalidomide, which is a congener of thalidomide , suppresses bone marrow and is associated with significant leukopenia . Lenalidomide use is associated with a lesser incidence of sedation , constipation , and neuropathy when compared to thalidomide .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a proteasome inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Bortezomib is a proteasome inhibitor. It is a boron-containing anticancer drug that covalently binds to the proteasome and inhibits its proteolytic activity, thereby disrupting many intracellular signaling pathways . The most important of these is nuclear factor-\026B (NF-\026B) mediated signaling. It is indicated in the management of multiple myeloma. Option A: Paclitaxel is a taxane. Option C: Cetuximab is a monoclonal antibody against the extracellular domain of EGFR.899 Option D: Irinotecan is a topoisomerase I inhibitor.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs can be used for the treatment of a patient with hormone-responsive breast cancer?
mcqs.explanation: Tamoxifen is a selective estrogen receptor modulator that is indicated for hormone-responsive breast cancer. It is approved for endocrine treatment of women with ER+ metastatic breast cancer or following primary tumor excision as adjuvant therapy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: A patient undergoing adjuvant radiotherapy for an oral malignancy is prescribed a radioprotective drug. Identify this drug.
mcqs.explanation: Amifostine is the radioprotective drug that has been prescribed to this patient . It is an organic thiophosphate cytoprotective agent that is indicated for the following conditions: • Reduction of nephrotoxicity associated with cisplatin. • Reduction of xerostomia in patients with head and neck cancer undergoing postoperative irradiation .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Which among the following is a cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4/6 inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Palbociclib is a cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4/6 inhibitor. It is approved for use in advanced or metastatic ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer. Ruxolitinib is an inhibitor of Janus associated kinases: JAK1 and JAK2 . Tramitenib and cobimetinib are inhibitors of serine-threonine kinases.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Which of the following inhibits V600E mutated BRAF ?
mcqs.explanation: Vemurafenib and dabrafenib inhibit V600E mutated BRAF present in melanoma. Both are indicated in the management of melanoma. The name vemurafenib is derived from the target V600E mutated BRAF . Ibrutinib is a Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Which among the following is a hedgehog pathway inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Vismodegib acts as a competitive antagonist of the SMO (smoothens hedgehog ) receptor in the hedgehog signaling pathway .900 Hedgehog signaling plays a key role in stem cell regulation and tissue regeneration . Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is associated with dysregulation of this pathway . Vismodegib is indicated in patients with metastatic or relapsed BCC. Option A: Vemurafenib is a BRAF kinase inhibitor. Option C: Olaparib is an inhibitor of PARP [Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase ] enzyme. Option D: Neratinib is an irreversible inhibitor of HER-2 and EGFR.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Evaluation of a patient with CLL showed evidence of 17p deletion . Which of the following is a BCL-2 inhibitor approved for use in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Venetoclax is a small-molecule inhibitor of BCL -2 that is approved for use in CLL with a 17p deletion . Overexpression of BCL -2 has been demonstrated in CLL cells where it mediates tumor cell survival . Venetoclax helps restore the process of apoptosis by binding directly to the BCL -2 protein, displacing proapoptotic proteins like BIM, triggering mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and the activation of caspases . Olaparib and rucaparib are inhibitors of PARP [Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase ] enzymes .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Sipuleucel -T is the first vaccine approved for the treatment of cancer. This vaccine induces an immune response against which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Sipuleucel -T is a cell -based approach to induce an immune response against prostatic acid phosphatase (PAP) that is commonly expressed in prostatic cancer. It is approved for use in minimally symptomatic , hormone-refractory, metastatic prostate cancer. Sipuleucel -T preparation is done by isolating a patient 's peripheral blood cells by leukapheresis and then exposing them to PAP-GM-CSF (which is a human recombinant protein). When these treated cells are infused to a patient , the APCs present in the blood produces antibodies directed against PAP. Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a specific prostate epithelial cell membrane antigen, showing increased expression in prostate cancers, which is also a potential target for monoclonal antibody therapy .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a histone deacetylase inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: Febuxostat is a uric acid synthesis inhibitor that acts by inhibiting the enzyme xanthine oxidase and it is indicated in gout management. Examples of histone deacetylase inhibitors are: • Vorinostat - cutaneous T cell lymphoma • Belinostat - peripheral T cell lymphoma • Romidepsin - cutaneous /peripheral T cell lymphoma901 • Panobinostat - multiple myeloma

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old woman was diagnosed with melanoma. Sentinel lymph node biopsy showed malignant cells. Which of the following drugs used in this condition is a MEK inhibitor?
mcqs.explanation: The scenario is suggestive of metastatic melanoma and trametinib is used in this condition. It is a reversible inhibitor of the mitogen -activated extracellular signal-regulated kinase (MEK ). It inhibits the serine-threonine kinase domain of BRAF V600E mutant of MEK . It can be used as a single agent but it is more effective when used with BRAF inhibitors like dabrafenib. Adverse effects of this drug include : • Cutaneous rash • Acneiform dermatitis • Diarrhea • Fatigue • Nausea • Lymphedema . • Cardiomyopathy • Hypertension • Hemorrhage • Interstitial lung disease • Ocular toxic effects . Options A and B: Dabrafenib and vemurafenib are BRAF inhibitors used in metastatic melanoma. Option D: Ipilimumab is a human cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA -4) blocking antibody used in metastatic or unresectable melanoma.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: A 4-year-old child who was being evaluated for pancytopenia is diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Which of the following is the first gene therapy -based treatment approved for use in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Tisagenlecleucel is the first gene therapy-based treatment that is approved for use in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL ). The therapy involves reprogramming a patient 's own T-cells with a transgene encoding a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) to identify and eliminate CD19-expressing malignant and normal cells .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: A 67-year-old man presented with fatigue and weight loss. On examination, pallor and splenomegaly were noted . Peripheral blood smear examination findings are shown in the image. Which of the following BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors is not a first-line agent for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and the peripheral smear findings (increased WBCs with myelocytes , metamyelocytes , and band forms), is suggestive of chronic myelogenous leukemia902 (CML). Bosutinib is approved for use in this condition only for resistant and/or intolerant cases and not in newly diagnosed cases . Agents that can be used as first-line for CML are: • Imatinib • Dasatinib • Nilotinib Dasatinib and nilotinib can be used in newly diagnosed cases of CML, that are found to be imatinib-resistant.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: A 63-year-old postmenopausal woman came to the OPD with a 12 cm adnexal mass. Her CA-125 levels were raised and her risk of malignancy index was calculated to be 250. PET scan revealed hepatic metastases . Which PARP inhibitor can you use in her treatment ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario points towards a diagnosis of metastatic ovarian cancer. Rucaparib is a poly ADP-ribose polymerase / PARP inhibitor approved for the treatment of advanced ovarian cancer. PARP is a nuclear protein that transfers ADP-ribose from NAD+ to target proteins and this plays an important role in the DNA damage response . Rucaparib and olaparib are PARP inhibitors. Option A: Palbociclib is a selective inhibitor of the cyclin-dependent kinases CDK4 and CDK6. It is used in the treatment of metastatic breast cancer. Options C & D: Vorinostat and romidepsin are histone deacetylase inhibitors.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions has hydrogen peroxide been recently approved for?
mcqs.explanation: A topical solution of hydrogen peroxide has been approved for the treatment of raised seborrheic keratoses . Hydrogen peroxide is a keratolytic agent. Its exact mechanism of action in the treatment of seborrheic keratoses is not fully understood. Supraphysiologic concentrations may cause oxidative damage and death to seborrheic keratosis cells . Hydrogen peroxide is commonly used as a disinfectant to clean wounds . It can also be used as a mouthwash .

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions is apalutamide approved for?
mcqs.explanation: Apalutamide is an androgen receptor inhibitor indicated for the treatment of patients with non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old woman was diagnosed with melanoma. Sentinel lymph node biopsy showed malignant cells. Which among the following is a recombinant interleukin-2 preparation approved for use in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: 903 The clinical scenario is suggestive of metastatic melanoma. The recombinant interleukin-2 (IL -2) preparation that is approved for use in metastatic melanoma is aldesleukin . It acts as an IL -2 agonist and is also approved for use in metastatic renal cell cancer. Denileukin diftitox is an immunotoxin made from the recombinant combination of IL -2 and the catalytically active fragment of diphtheria toxin. It is approved for use in cutaneous T cell lymphoma. Imatinib and nilotinib are a BCR/ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor.

mcqs.subject: Pharmacology
mcqs.chapter: Interleukins, Growth Factors and Targeted Thera...
mcqs.question: Denileukin diftitox , a drug approved for the treatment of recurrent/refractory cutaneous T-cell lymphomas, is an immunotoxin made of:

options.a: Fusion protein of IL -2 and pertussis toxin
options.b: Fusion protein of IL -2 and diptheria toxin

mcqs.explanation: Denileukin diftitox is an immunotoxin made from the genetic recombination of IL -2 and the catalytically active fragment of diphtheria toxin. It is indicated for advanced cutaneous T-cell lymphoma in patients with >20% of T cells expressing the surface marker CD25. After binding to the IL -2 receptors , it is internalized by endocytosis . The active fragment of diphtheria toxin then is released into the cytosol , where it inhibits protein synthesis through ADP ribosylation, leading to cell death . Immunotoxins are proteins that contain a toxin along with an antibody that binds specifically to target cells . Antibody-drug conjugates are complex molecules composed of an antibody linked to a biologically active cytotoxic (anticancer) drug. These antibody-targeted drug therapies are cell -specific to kill efficiently the target cells that bind and internalize the drug conjugate . Examples are: • Gemtuzumab ozogamicin - Monoclonal antibody against CD33 linked to a semisynthetic derivative of calicheamicin, a potent antitumor antibiotic. It was approved for the treatment of acute myeloid leukemia. • Brentuximab vedotin - Anti-CD30 IgG1 monoclonal antibody linked with the microtubule-disrupting agent MMAE . It is used for the treatment of Hodgkin and anaplastic lymphoma. • Ado-trastuzumab emtansine - It combines the HER2-targeted properties of trastuzumab with the antimicrotubule agent DM1 (derived from maytansine), allowing preferential intracellular drug delivery to HER2+ cells . It is used in the treatment of HER+ breast cancer.904

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Homeostasis is called as dynamic equilibrium because ______

options.a: All variables are given equal importance
options.b: Can achieve a constancy in extreme environmental challenge
options.c: The set -point for all homeostatic variables is always fixed
options.d: Body maintains an internal balance within fluctuating limits

mcqs.explanation: Homeostasis is called dynamic equilibrium because the body maintains an internal balance within fluctuating limits. It describes the maintenance of nearly constant conditions in the internal environment despite changes in the outside world. A number of variables such as body temperature , blood sugar levels , blood pH, etc . are regulated within a range of values (homeostatic ranges) and not at fixed values. These variables are not given equal importance. There is a hierarchy of importance so that the constancy of certain variables may be altered markedly to maintain others within their normal range. For example , respiratory or metabolic compensation to maintain blood pH. The disruption of homeostasis either due to extreme environmental challenge or a breakdown of internal homeostatic mechanisms is termed as a disease .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which is a component of homeostatic control system ?
mcqs.explanation: Stimulus , receptor and effector are all components of a homeostatic control system . Components of homeostasis include : • Stimulus - It is a detectable change in the internal or external environment, such as change in temperature . • Receptor - It detects environmental changes . • Integrating centre • Effector - It is an organ or cell that acts in response to a stimulus .11

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Feedback regulation is seen in ______

options.a: The increased heart rate that occurs in an athlete just before a sprint begins
options.b: Smell of food triggers secretion of salivary and gastric juices
options.c: An increase in insulin before glucose absorption has raised blood glucose levels
options.d: The increased heart rate in response to a decrease in blood pressure

mcqs.explanation: Feedback regulation is seen in the increased heart rate in response to a decrease in blood pressure . This is because , in feedback regulation , the homeostatic response (increased heart rate) occurs after the change (decrease in blood pressure ) has occurred. On the other hand, in feedforward regulation , the homeostatic responses take place before the change has occurred. This is done in anticipation of the change to minimize fluctuations . Examples of feedforward regulation include : • The increased heart rate that occurs in an athlete just before a sprint begins . • The smell of food triggers the secretion of salivary and gastric juices . • An increase in insulin before glucose absorption has raised blood glucose levels .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Positive feedback is seen in all except _____
mcqs.explanation: Positive feedback is seen in all except gastric secretion . It is under negative feedback control. Negative feedback consists of certain changes that affect a deficient or excessive variable to pull it back to a certain mean value to maintain homeostasis . Most processes in the body are under negative feedback . For example , an increase in gastric acids leading to a decrease in gastric secretion . Positive feedback consists of changes that affect a variable to push it further away from a certain mean value. For example , an increase in LH leading to a further increase in LH . Instances, where positive feedback plays an important role are: • Clotting of blood • Calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum • LH Surge • Action potential • Shock • Parturition

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: On infusion of a large volume of blood, the MAP rises from 100 mmHg to 175 mmHg. Due to the baroreceptor feedback mechanism, the MAP falls down to 125 mmHg. Calculate the gain of the feedback system .
mcqs.explanation: The gain of the feedback system in the above case is -2. The gain of the system is then calculated by using the following formula: Gain = C/E Here, C is correction achieved from the deviated value and E is the remaining error post-correction. Calculation12 • The original value in the given case is 100 mmHg. • The deviated value in the given case is 175 mmHg. • The corrected value in the given case is 125 mmHg. • C is given by correction achieved from deviated value, Corrected value - Deviated value = 125 - = -50 mmHg. • E is given by the remaining error post-correction, Corrected value - Original value = 125 - 100 = 25 mmHg. • Gain = -50/25 = -2. The negative symbol indicates that the homeostatic mechanism acts in a direction opposite to the initial deviation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Plasma membrane in eukaryotes is made up of all except _______
mcqs.explanation: Plasma membrane in eukaryotes does not contain triglycerides . The plasma membrane is composed almost entirely of proteins and lipids . The major lipids include : • Phospholipids : Lecithin, cephalin , phosphatidylserine • Sphingolipids : Sphingomyelin • Cholesterol

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Membrane fluidity is increased by ____.
mcqs.explanation: Membrane fluidity is increased by linoleic acid, an unsaturated fatty acid. All other options are saturated fatty acids. Longer and saturated fatty acids decrease the fluidity because their side chains are straight and interact more strongly with each other. Conversely, unsaturated fatty acids increase the fluidity because their side chains are kinked and less compact. Cholesterol , also known as fluidity buffer helps to maintain the fluidity of the cell membrane.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of peripheral protein?
mcqs.explanation: Cell surface receptors are peripheral proteins . Proteins in the Plasma Membrane13 Integral Proteins Peripheral Proteins Transmembrane proteins i.e. , they span the thickness of t he membrane. Present either on the inner or outer surface of the membra ne Examples -Insulin receptor , p umps, transport proteins (car riers), G-protein coupled rece ptors Examples -Cell surface recept ors and enzymes

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following membranes has the highest protein content per gram tissue ?
mcqs.explanation: The inner mitochondrial membrane has the highest protein content per gram tissue . Myelin has the lowest protein content per gram tissue . Protein to Lipid Ratio in Different MembranesMembranes Protein: Lipid Rati o Myelin 0.23 Human RBC 1.1 Mitochondrial outer membr ane 1.1 Sarcoplasmic reticulum 2.0 Mitochondrial inner membr ane 3.214

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The sequence of vesicular transport in a cell is
mcqs.explanation: The sequence of vesicular transport in a cell is ER - Cis - Trans - Cell membrane. Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) - It is the site of protein synthesis . Proteins are taken to the Golgi apparatus through transport vesicles . Cis end of Golgi apparatus - Also called as receiving end, it is closest to RER Trans end of Golgi apparatus - Also called as releasing end, it is furthest away from RER. Cell membrane - Synthesised proteins within secretory vesicles are released into the extracellular space through the process of exocytosis .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: All of the following are enzyme markers of mitochondria except ____
mcqs.explanation: 5' Nucleotidase is an enzyme marker for plasma membrane. All the other options are mitochondrial enzyme markers .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following will test negative for all mitochondrial markers ?
mcqs.explanation: Mature red blood cells will test negative for all mitochondrial markers are as they do not have mitochondria. Lack of mitochondria is the reason why red blood cells exclusively use anaerobic glycolysis to generate ATP .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which is the characteristic enzyme present in peroxisome ?
mcqs.explanation: 15 Catalase is the characteristic enzyme of peroxisomes . All other are lysosomal enzymes .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Gap junctions are found in all except ______
mcqs.explanation: Gap junctions are absent in adult skeletal muscles . Gap junctions are intercellular connections with a channel in between . They are present in excitable tissues such as cardiac muscle , smooth muscle and neurons but not in skeletal muscles .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Tight junctions are not seen in ____.
mcqs.explanation: Tight junctions are not seen in cardiac muscle . Tight junctions form a water-tight seal between cells . They are characteristically seen in the following : • Intestinal mucosa • Renal tubules • Choroid plexus • Sertoli cells Functions of tight junctions are: • Prevents the diffusion of macromolecules between cells . • Maintains cell polarity. • Seals the paracellular pathway .16

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a cell adhesion molecule (CAM)?
mcqs.explanation: Spectrin is a cytoskeletal protein but not a cell adhesion molecule . Cells are attached to each other or to the basal lamina by cell adhesion molecules (CAMs). Some important classes of CAMs are: • Integrins: heterodimers that bind to various receptors • IgG superfamily of immunoglobulins • Cadherins: Ca2+-dependent molecules that mediate cell -to-cell adhesion by homophilic reactions • Selectins which have lectin -like domains that bind carbohydrates Clinical significance • Cancer cells have abnormal CAMs and hence cause decreased cell adhesion and allow individual cancer cells to detach from the parent cancer. • The decrease in the amount of E-cadherin maybe the reason for early metastasis of numerous tumors.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Identify the incorrectly matched pair of intercellular connections and their structural units
mcqs.explanation: Gap junctions are made of connexons. Connexons are in turn made of units called connexins.The different intercellular connections and their structural units are given below :Intercellular connections Structural units Tight junctions or zona occlu dens Occludins , claudins and junct ional adhesion molecules Gap junctions Connexons Zona adherens Cadherins17 Intercellular connections Structural units Desmosome Cadherins like desmoglein Hemidesmosome Integrins

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Integrin connects with:
mcqs.explanation: Integrin connects with fibronectin. Integrins are transmembrane glycoproteins (integral proteins ) that allow cells to attach to extracellular matrix constituents such as laminin , fibronectin and collagen . It helps in linking the intracellular cytoskeleton functionally and structurally with the outside world.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The force-generating proteins are _____.
mcqs.explanation: The force-generating proteins are dynein and kinesin. There are three superfamilies of proteins namely kinesin, dynein, myosin referred to as molecular motors. The molecular motors are the force generating proteins as they move proteins , organelles , and other cell parts (collectively referred to as "cargo") to all parts of the cell .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: An absent dynein arm in cilia can lead to all of the following except :
mcqs.explanation: An absent dynein arm in cilia leads to primary ciliary dyskinesia. Kartagener syndrome is a primary ciliary dyskinesia characterized by the classical triad of situs inversus, chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis . Ciliocytophthoria is the degradation of ciliated cells due to viral infections . It is not seen in primary ciliary dyskinesia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: In dividing cells , mitotic spindles are formed by ____.
mcqs.explanation: Tubulins constitute the microtubules that form the mitotic spindle in a dividing cell . Cytoskeletal elements of the cell . Ubiquitin helps in protein degradation .Cytoskeletal element Protein subunits Microfilament(smallest diam eter ) Actin18 Cytoskeletal element Protein subunits Intermediate filament Keratin, vimentin, desmin, la min etc . Microtubule (largest diameter ) Kinesin, dynein and tubulin19

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of a polypeptide hormone?
mcqs.explanation: Parathyroid hormone (PTH ) is an example of a polypeptide hormone. Cortisol is a steroid hormone. Adrenaline and thyroxine are derivatives of the amino acid tyrosine.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which hormone crosses the plasma membrane for its action?
mcqs.explanation: Thyroxine crosses the plasma membrane for its action. Thyroid hormones enter the nucleus and bind to thyroid hormone receptors . The hormone-receptor complex in the nucleus binds to DNA via zinc fingers. This increases the expression of a variety of different genes that code for proteins regulating cell function. Although thyroxine is an AA derivative, there are transporters to move it into the cell , hence they are intracellular receptors acting on the nucleus . Epinephrine , glucagon , and insulin bind to cell surface receptors .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following hormone is not stored before release ?
mcqs.explanation: 26 Cortisol is not stored before release . Usually , the polypeptide and protein hormones such as insulin, thyroxine or renin are stored in secretory vesicles before release . They are synthesized as much larger polypeptide chains (preprohormones) that are biologically inactive and then processed intracellularly by specific proteases to yield the final hormone molecule which is stored in the secretory vesicle until needed . On the other hand, steroid hormones such as cortisol are synthesised as needed and are not stored . They are lipid soluble and easily diffuse across cell membrane to enter the interstitial fluid and then blood.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Downregulation of receptors occurs due to all except _____
mcqs.explanation: Downregulation of receptors occurs due to internalisation, inactivation of receptors or desensitisation. A decrease in the level of stimulating hormones generally leads to an increase in the level of active receptors . This is called upregulation of receptors . On the other hand, an increase in the level of stimulating hormones generally leads to a decrease in the level of active receptors . This is called downregulation of receptors . Downregulation of receptors can occur by one of the following mechanisms: • Desensitisation - Receptors undergo chemical modifications that make them less responsive. • Internalisation - It is the temporary sequestration of the cell membrane receptors to the inside of the cell , away from the action of hormones. Following internalisation, the receptors are either destroyed or recycled . • Inactivation of receptors . • Decreased production of receptors .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Receptors on cell membrane that activate ion channel after binding with agonists are_____
mcqs.explanation: Nicotinic cholinergic receptors activate an ion channel after binding with its agonist. These receptors are called ligand-gated channels or ionotropic receptors . Receptors for neurotransmitters are classified into two broad families based on structure and function. They are: • Ligand-gated channels (Ionotropic receptors ) • When bound to these receptors , a membrane channel is opened leading to a brief increase in ionic conductance. • Important for fast synaptic transmission. • Examples - GABAA, GABAC, Nicotinic cholinergic, Glycine and Serotonin (5HT3 subtype ). • G-protein coupled receptors (Metabotropic receptors )27 • When bound to these receptors , secondary messengers are released that modulate voltage -gated channels on neuronal membranes. • Examples - GABAB , Muscarinic cholinergic, Catecholamines , Serotonin (all subtypes except 5HT3 ) and opioid receptors .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Adrenaline, noradrenaline and dopamine act through_____
mcqs.explanation: Adrenaline, noradrenaline and dopamine act through a 7 pass receptor called G-protein coupled receptor (GPCR). The catecholamines act through GPCRs which are cell membrane receptors that span across the membrane 7 times hence called seven helix or serpentine receptors .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true about the G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)?

options.a: G proteins bind to hormones on the surface of the nucleus .
options.b: All the three subunits �o , \035, and \037 should bind to each other for G proteins to act.
options.c: G proteins act as inhibitory or excitatory because of differences in �o subunit .
options.d: G protein is bound to GTP in resting state .

mcqs.explanation: G proteins act as inhibitory or excitatory because of differences in �o subunit . G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are cell membrane receptors that span across the membrane 7 times hence called seven helix or serpentine receptors . G proteins have 3 subunits (�o ,\035 and \037). In its resting state , �o subunit is bound to GDP. Upon ligand binding to GPCR, it undergoes a conformational change that activates G protein within the cell . The �o subunit dissociates and in turn alters the activity of second messengers such as cAMP, cGMP or Ca2+. Once the ligand is unbound, the intrinsic GTPase activity of the �o subunit converts GTP to GDP. This leads to reassociation of �o with the \035-\037 subunit and termination of effector activation.28

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Action of �o subunit of G protein is_____
mcqs.explanation: The action of �o subunit of G protein is the breakdown of GTP to GDP as it has an intrinsic GTPase activity. Guanine exchange factors (GEFs ) convert GDP to GTP by nucleotide exchange . G proteins can be either stimulatory (GS) or inhibitory (Gi) with respect to the production of the 2nd messenger cAMP by the enzyme adenylyl cyclase . Stimulatory or inhibitory activity resides in the �o subunit . • Cholera toxin acts on �o subunit of GS • Pertussis toxin acts on �o subunit of Gi

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: PDGF acts through which of the following signaling pathways ?
mcqs.explanation: PDGF (platelet -derived growth factor) acts through the activation of tyrosine kinases. All growth factors that foster the multiplication or development of various types of cells act through the activation of tyrosine kinases.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which hormone acts on JAK-STAT kinase receptor ?
mcqs.explanation: Growth hormone acts on JAK-STAT receptors . Janus tyrosine kinase receptors (JAK-STAT ) serves as receptors for: • Growth hormone • Prolactin • Erythropoietin29 • Leptin Thyroxine acts on nuclear receptors . TSH and FSH act on G protein-coupled receptors .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: All of the following act through cell surface receptors except ____
mcqs.explanation: Cortisol is a steroid hormone and acts on intracellular (cytoplasmic ) receptor .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Steroid hormone receptors have an attachment site for all except _____
mcqs.explanation: Steroid hormone receptors have an attachment site for steroid hormone, hormone-responsive element , and transcription activators, but not transcription repressors. Transcription repressors are proteins that bind to specific sites on DNA and prevent transcription of nearby genes .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: True statement about second messengers is _____

options.a: Are substances that interact with first messengers outside cells .
options.b: Mediate the intracellular responses to many different hormones and neurotransmitters
options.c: Are hormones secreted by cells in response to stimulation by another hormone
options.d: Are substances that bind to first messengers in the cell membrane.

mcqs.explanation: Second messengers mediate the intracellular responses to many different hormones and neurotransmitters. Cell surface receptors are substances that interact with the first messengers which are hormones and neurotransmitters. The second messengers are the intracellular signalling molecules . They bring about many short-term changes in cell function by altering enzyme function, triggering exocytosis , and other physiological effects . They can also lead to the alteration of transcription of various genes (long term effect ).30 Examples of second messengers are cAMP, cGMP, Ca2+ and IP3 -DAG (Inositol triphosphate and diacylglycerol).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which one of the following acts as a second messenger ?
mcqs.explanation: Among the following calcium (Ca2+) acts as a second messenger . Increased cytoplasmic Ca2+ binds to and activates calcium-binding proteins (calmodulin, troponin) or activate protein kinases (or phospholipase C) to bring about physiological effects . Cytoplasmic Ca2+ is increased by: • Direct entry of Ca2+ from the ECF through Ca2+ channels that could be ligand-gated , voltage -gated or stretch -activated (mechanically gated ). • Mobilisation of Ca2+ that are stored in high concentrations in the endoplasmic reticulum by other second messengers such as IP3 -DAG (Inositol triphosphate and diacylglycerol ).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A primigravida with 38 completed weeks of gestation has gone into labor. Oxytocin was started to augment labor. The second messenger system through which oxytocin acts is _____
mcqs.explanation: The second messenger system through which oxytocin acts is the phospholipase C system . It activates the enzyme phospholipase C which breaks down some phospholipids in the cell membrane into IP3 (phosphoinositol triphosphate ) and DAG (diacylglycerol ). DAG then activates protein kinase C and IP3 mobilises Ca2+ from mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum to bring about smooth muscle contraction and other cellular responses .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: cAMP is the exclusive second messenger for all the following except _________
mcqs.explanation: Vasopressin does not use cAMP exclusively. Vasopressin (ADH) acts on at least 3 kinds of receptors : V1A , V1B and V2 • All the 3 are G-protein coupled receptors • V1A and V1B receptors (Gq) act through IP3 as a second messenger , to increase the intracellular calcium concentration • V2 receptors (Gs) use cAMP as a second messenger cAMP is the exclusive second messenger for dopamine, corticotropin and glucagon . Dopamine has 5 receptors (D1, D2, D3, D4, D5) • all use cAMP as second messengers • D1, D5 act by increasing cAMP • D2, D3, D4 act by decreasing cAMP31

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: cGMP is the second messenger of
mcqs.explanation: Vasodilatory actions of NO are mediated by cGMP. NO is a hormone derived from the amino acid arginine. It activates guanylyl cyclases in vascular smooth muscle cells resulting in the conversion of cGTP to cGMP (2nd messenger ). cGMP activates cGMP dependent protein kinase, which causes blood vessels to relax. cGMP is the second messenger for nitric oxide and atrial natriuretic factor.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a second messenger ?
mcqs.explanation: Guanylyl cyclase is the enzyme that catalyzes the formation of cGMP. It is cGMP that acts as the second messenger . cAMP, IP3 and DAG are all second messengers .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Activation of protein kinase C causes _____
mcqs.explanation: Activation of protein kinase C causes phosphorylation of proteins Cellular Phosphorylation is under the control of two groups of proteins : • Kinases • enzymes that catalyse the phosphorylation of tyrosine or serine residues in protein • Example - Protein Kinase A, Protein Kinase C, Ca2+/Calmodulin Kinase • Phosphatases • that catalyses the dephosphorylation of tyrosine or serine residues in the protein Kinases play important roles in regulating cellular physiology , including cell growth and cell death . Philadelphia chromosome, t(9:22 ) or the bcr-abl fusion gene codes for an abnormal kinase that leads to chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML). The drug imatinib was developed to block the tyrosine kinase activity of bcr-abl protein and is an effective treatment option for CML.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 7-year-old girl presents with skin lesions as shown in the image. The parents also complain of early breast development , growth acceleration , and vaginal bleeding . On genetic studies , it was found that there is a gain of function mutation of G Protein. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , the most probable diagnosis is McCune -Albright syndrome as it is the only gain-of-function mutation of G Protein. G proteins or G protein-coupled receptor complexes can undergo a loss- or gain-of-function mutation. Some examples are given below : In McCune -Albright syndrome, a gain-of-function mutation in Gs�o is associated with the rough -bordered areas of skin pigmentation and hypercortisolism . This mutation occurs during fetal development , creating a mosaic of normal and abnormal cells .32 Receptor Type of mutati on Disease Cone opsin Loss Colour blindness Rhodopsin Loss Night blindness or retinitis pi gmentosa Endothelin recept or Loss Hirschsprung disease TSH receptor Loss Familialhypothyroidism TSH receptor Gain Familialhyperthyroidism LH receptor Gain Familial male precocious pub erty Gsprotein Gain Pituitary adenomas with acro megaly Gsprotein Gain (mosaic) McCune -Albright syndrome

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Nuclear signalling pathways are all except
mcqs.explanation: Rat proteins are not nuclear signalling pathways . Recombinant rat IFN- is a bioactive protein intended for use in cell culture applications. Importin: • Transporting protein molecules into nucleus by binding to specific recognition sequences , called Nuclear Localization Sequences (NLS). • 2 subunits , importin �o and importin \035. Caveolins: • Family of integral membrane proteins that are principal components of caveolae membranes • Involved in receptor -independent endocytosis . • Acts as scaffolding proteins within caveolar membranes by compartmentalizing and concentrating signaling molecules . NF-kB • Part of a prototypical proinflammatory signaling pathway • based on the role of NF-\034B in the expression of proinflammatory genes including cytokines, chemokines, and adhesion molecules33

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Transport of lipid-soluble substances across the cell membrane occurs via which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Lipid-soluble substances are transported across the cell membrane via diffusion . • The rate of diffusion depends directly on lipid solubility . • Characteristics of simple diffusion • The only form of transport that is not carrier -mediated • Occurs down an electrochemical gradient ("downhill ") • Does not require metabolic energy and therefore is passive • Permeability • Describes the ease with which a solute diffuses through a membrane • Depends on the characteristics of the solute and the membrane • Small hydrophobic solutes (e.g., O2) have the highest permeabilities in lipid membranes. • Hydrophilic solutes (e.g., Na+) must cross cell membranes through water-filled channels, or pores. If the solute is an ion, then its flux will depend on both the concentration difference and the potential difference across the membrane.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following will diffuse more rapidly through phospholipid membranes?
mcqs.explanation: Among the following substances , oxygen diffuses more rapidly through phospholipid membranes as it is a lipid-soluble substance . Phospholipid membranes are: • Permeable to lipid -soluble substances (e.g., O2, CO2, NH3, steroid hormones) • Impermeable to water-soluble substances (e.g., Na+, Cl-, glucose ) • Semipermeable to water

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is explained by the fick's law of diffusion ?
mcqs.explanation: Fick's law of diffusion explains passive diffusion along the concentration gradient. Fick's law of diffusion : The magnitude of the diffusing tendency is directly proportional to the cross-sectional area across which diffusion is taking place and the concentration gradient, or chemical gradient, which is the difference in concentration of the diffusing substance divided by the thickness of the membrane.41

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: For a membrane permeable substance , the intracellular concentration (IC) is 10 units and extracellular concentration (EC) is 5 units. If the intracellular concentration, surface area of the membrane and thickness of the membrane are doubled , and the EC remains the same, What will be the net effect on the diffusion ?
mcqs.explanation: The net effect on the diffusion is, it becomes 3x. The magnitude of the diffusion : where , • J = net rate of diffusion • D = diffusion coefficient • A = area of the membrane • \033x = thickness of the membrane or the distance the molecule must travel across for diffusion • \033c = concentration gradient In the condition mentioned above, the surface area, the thickness of the membrane and intracellular concentration becomes doubled . This means, • A is doubled = 2A • \033x is doubled = 2\033x • IC is doubled . 10x2 = 20 units; EC is 5 units. So, \033c = 20 - 5 = 15. \033c was 5 with the original concentrations. Hence \033c has been tripled . Now, J=-D x 2A x 3\033c/2\033x = 3 x [DA \033c/\033x] Therefore the diffusion of the substance increases by three -fold . 2nd method : J = - DA (\033c / \033x ) After applying changes ,\033c = intracellular conc. - extracellular conc. = 10 - 5 = 5 Therefore, J1 = - DA (5 / \033x ) After appropriate doublings , New intracellular conc. = 10 * 2 = 20 New extracellular conc. = 5 (since no change) \033c = 20 - 5 = 15 Therefore, J2 = - D 2*A (15 / 2*\033x ) = - D A (15 / \033x ) Now, J2 / J1 = [- DA (15 / \033x ) ] / [ = - DA (5 / \033x ) ] J2 / J1 = 15 / 5 = 3 Therefore the diffusion of the substance increases by three -fold .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not follow transport saturation kinetics?
mcqs.explanation: 42 Simple diffusion is not carrier -mediated transport hence do not follow saturation kinetics. • Facilitated diffusion , primary active transport, and secondary active transport all involve integral membrane proteins and are called carrier -mediated transport. • All carrier -mediated transport system follows saturation kinetics. • The figure shows that as the concentration of the diffusing substance increases, the rate of simple diffusion continues to increase proportionately , but in the case of facilitated diffusion , the rate of diffusion cannot rise greater than the transport maximum (Tm). Tm is analogous to the maximum velocity (Vmax ) level in enzyme kinetics.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which statement about the facilitated diffusion is true?
mcqs.explanation: When carrier proteins help in the movement of substances in the direction of their chemical or electrical gradients (downhill movement), no energy input is required and the process is called facilitated diffusion . Examples • GLUT • Urea Transporters : • UTA 1, 2, 3, 4 in Kidney • UTB in RBC • Amino Acid Transporters Other options are wrong because : • Facilitated diffusion is a type of passive transport. • It follows saturation kinetics. • No energy input is required in facilitated diffusion .43

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The movement of which of the following substance across the membrane is most affected by osmotic pressure ?
mcqs.explanation: The movement of water across the membrane is most affected by osmotic pressure . Osmotic pressure is the pressure that would have to be applied to prevent the movement of water molecules to the more concentrated solution i.e. to a region in which there is higher concentration of a solute to which the membrane is impermeable .• Osmotic pressure is calculated by Vant Hoff's law.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Osmolarity is defined as _______
mcqs.explanation: 44 Difference between osmolarity & osmolality : • Osmolarity is the number of osmoles per litre of solution , • Osmolality is the number of osmoles per kilogram of solvent. • Therefore, osmolarity is affected by the volume of the various solutes in the solution and the temperature , while the osmolality is not.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Passive transfer of only solvent occurs in ______
mcqs.explanation: Passive transfer of the only solvent occurs in Osmosis. The diffusion of solvent molecules into a region in which there is a higher concentration of a solute to which the membrane is impermeable is called osmosis. Note : Membrane is impermeable to the solute .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 47-year-old diabetic man takes a low-dose aspirin daily due to cardiovascular risk . The absorption of aspirin in the stomach is an example of which type of transport?
mcqs.explanation: The absorption of salicylates like aspirin in the stomach is an example of nonionic diffusion . • Some weak acids and bases are quite soluble in cell membranes in the undissociated form, but they cannot cross membranes in the charged (i.e. dissociated ) form. Consequently , molecules of the undissociated substance diffuse from one side of the membrane to the other and then dissociate . This phenomenon is called nonionic diffusion . Examples • Ammonia excretion in collecting ducts • Excretion of weak acids and bases in the kidney • Absorption of salicylates in the stomach • Absorption of bile acids in the distal ileum

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Energy is required in which of the following mode of transport.
mcqs.explanation: When a carrier protein transports substances against their electrical and chemical gradients (uphill movement) it requires energy and this type of transport is called active transport.45

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Movement of calcium from the cytosol to the extracellular space takes place by
mcqs.explanation: The movement of calcium from the cytosol to the extracellular space takes place by primary active transport. Two primary active transport calcium pumps maintain low intracellular calcium levels . One pumps calcium ions to the extracellular space and another to the sarcoplasmic reticulum . Calcium transport also takes place via secondary active transport. A sodium-calcium exchanger/antiporter moves sodium ions to the interior and calcium ions to the exterior.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Na+-K+ ATP pump uses ________
mcqs.explanation: Na+- K+ ATPase or Na+-K+ ATP pump catalyzes the hydrolysis of ATP to ADP and uses the energy to extrude three Na+ from the cell and take two K+ into the cell for each molecule of ATP hydrolyzed . Sodium-Potassium Pump/ Na+– K+ Pump: • Carrier protein located on the plasma membrane of all cells • Pumps 3 Na+ out of the cell & 2 K+ into the cell (coupling ratio 3:2 ) • 2 separate globular proteins : • Larger - �o subunit & smaller- \035 subunit , �o subunit concerned with Na+- K+ transport • Binding sites on �o subunit : • 3 intracellular sites - for Na+, ATP , and one phosphorylation site • 2 extracellular sites - for K+ and oubain46 Mechanism Of ActionFunctions: • Controlling Cell Volume. • Electrogenic Nature- maintains Resting membrane potential • The energy from the Na+–K+ pump also indirectly serves as the energy source for secondary active transport. Regulation : • Pump activity is altered by second messenger molecules eg . cAMP, DAG • Stimulated by thyroid hormones, insulin and aldosterone • Inhibition by dopamine ,digitalis glycosides , ouabain47

mcqs.question: Primary active transport is mediated by which one of the following enzymes ?
mcqs.explanation: In active transport the energy is provided almost exclusively by the hydrolysis of ATP . Hence many carrier molecules are ATPases (eg .
