Criteria for the substance to be neurotransmitter • the substance must be demonstrated to be present in the presynaptic terminal • the cell must be able to synthesize the substance . • should be released on depolarization of the terminal . • there should be specific receptors for it on the postsynaptic membrane. • if the substance is applied exogenously to the postsynaptic membrane at physiologic concentration, the response of the postsynaptic cell must mimic the in vivo response194

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Neurotransmitter can be degraded by all except _____

options.a: Can diffuse out of synaptic cleft

mcqs.explanation: The final steps in the process lead to termination of the actions of the neurotransmitter and include • Reuptake into the nerve terminal or glial cell • Enzymatic degradation . • Diffusion away from the synaptic cleft

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following endogenous opioids is correctly matched with the receptor at which it has maximum potency ?
mcqs.explanation: Enkephalins have maximum potency at \024 receptors . Dynorphins have maximum potency at \034 receptors . Endorphins have maximum potency at �M receptors . Note : There is a difference of opinion among Goodman & Gillman's textbook and Ganong's review of medical physiology (26th edition pg 151). According to Goodman & Gillman's textbook above answer is correct.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following physiologic processes is not correctly paired with a structure ?

options.c: Synaptic vesicle docking and fusion : presynaptic nerve terminal

mcqs.explanation: Endplate potential is generated via nicotinic cholinergic receptor . The acetylcholine released from the motor neuron diffuses to nicotinic cholinergic (NM) receptors that are concentrated at the tops of the junctional folds of the membrane of the motor endplate .195

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following electrophysiologic events is correctly paired with the change in ionic currents causing the event?

options.a: Fast inhibitory postsynaptic potentials (IPSPs) and closing of Cl– channels
options.b: Fast excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs) and an decrease in Ca2+ conductance
options.c: Endplate potential and an increase in Na+ conductance
options.d: Presynaptic inhibition and closure of voltage -gated K+ channels

mcqs.explanation: Binding of acetylcholine to neuromuscular junction receptors increases the Na+ and K+ conductance , and the resultant influx of Na+ produces a depolarizing potential , the endplate potential . IPSP may be due to • Opening of chloride ion channels through the postsynaptic neuronal membrane • Increase in conductance of potassium ions out of the neuron. • Activation of receptor enzymes that increase the number of inhibitory synaptic receptors or decrease the number of excitatory receptors . EPSP may be due to • The opening of sodium channels to allow large numbers of positive electrical charges to flow to the interior of the postsynaptic cell . • Depressed conduction through chloride or potassium channels, or both. • Various changes in the internal metabolism of the postsynaptic neuron to increase the number of excitatory membrane receptors or decrease the number of inhibitory membrane receptors .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: How is an electrical synapse different from a chemical synapse ?

options.a: No cytoplasmic continuity between presynaptic and postsynaptic membrane
options.c: Connexons are involved in electrical synapse
options.d: Electrical synapse has more latent period than chemical synapse

mcqs.explanation: In electrical synapses , the cytoplasm of adjacent cells is directly connected by gap junctions (connexons) that allow free movement of ions from the interior of one cell to the interior of the next cell . The transmission in electrical synapses is bidirectional and there is no synaptic delay . Unlike chemical synapses , electrical synapse has cytoplasmic continuity .196 Note : Most of the synapses used for signal transmission in the central nervous system are chemical synapses .197

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following neurotransmitter is not a biogenic amine?
mcqs.explanation: Glycine is not a biogenic amine. It is an amino acid. Biogenic amines are made from amino acid precursors. They have a nitrogen containing amine (NH2) group. Unlike the amino acids, the biogenic amines lack a carboxyl (COOH) group. Norepinephrine , epinephrine , dopamine, serotonin and histamine are biogenic amines.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The main excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmitters in the CNS are ______
mcqs.explanation: Glutamate is the main excitatory neurotransmitter in the CNS. It is responsible for 75 % of the excitatory transmission in the brain . Glycine and GABA are the main inhibitory neurotransmitters in the CNS. Glycine is the main inhibitory neurotransmitter in the spinal cord. GABA is the major inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: 'A' delta fibers and 'C' fibers carry pain sensation. The neurotransmitter released by 'A' delta fibers is ______
mcqs.explanation: The neurotransmitter released by A delta fibers, which carry sharp pricking pain, is glutamate . The substance released by C fibers, which carry diffuse , chronic, burning pain is substance P.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The most important neurotransmitter of reward pathway is ______
mcqs.explanation: The most important neurotransmitter of reward pathway is dopamine.203 Reward pathway (mesolimbic pathway) connects the ventral tegmental area in the midbrain to the nucleus accumbens and limbic subcortical areas. This pathway is involved in reward behaviour, addiction and in psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Dopamine beta hydroxylase converts dopamine to ______
mcqs.explanation: Dopamine beta hydroxylase converts dopamine to norepinephrine . Vitamin C is required as a cofactor for the enzyme.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of these is not a dopaminergic pathway ?
mcqs.explanation: Corticostrial pathway is not a dopaminergic pathway . The corticostrial pathway is the primary input pathway for the basal ganglia which uses glutamate as the neurotransmitter. Important dopaminergic pathways are: • Mesolimbic pathway - Increased activity responsible for positive symptoms of schizophrenia. • Mesocortical pathway - Decreased activity responsible for negative symptoms of schizophrenia. • Nigrostriatal pathway - Decreased activity causes extrapyramidal symptoms . • Tuberoinfundibular pathway - Decreased activity causes increase in prolactin.204

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Find the incorrect match.
mcqs.explanation: Basal forebrain complex (nucleus basalis of Meynert ) is rich in acetylcholine . A loss of cholinergic neurons in the nucleus basalis of Meynert is seen in alzheimer's disease .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with involuntary jerking and writhing movements is diagnosed with Huntington's disease . Loss of which of the following is responsible for hyperkinetic symptoms in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The hyperkinetic feature of Huntington's disease is due to the loss of intrastriatal GABAergic and cholinergic neurons. The loss of the GABAergic pathway (which is an inhibitory pathway ) to the globus pallidus external segment and loss of cholinergic neurons in many parts of the brain decreases inhibition, causing the hyperkinetic feature of the disease to develop . Huntington's disease is an autosomal dominant trinucleotide repeat disorder with multiple CAG repeats . The abnormal gene responsible for the disease is located on chromosome 4.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: An infant develops features of botulism following honey intake. This toxin blocks neuromuscular transmission by which of the following mechanisms?

options.a: Prevents release of Ach at presynaptic membrane
options.b: Opening of calcium channels at the presynaptic membrane
options.c: Prevents the binding of Ach at the postsynatic membrane
options.d: Prevents the action of Ach at the postsynaptic membrane

mcqs.explanation: Botulinum toxin prevents the release of Ach at the presynaptic membrane. Botulinum toxins A, B, and E are toxic to humans. They cleave components of SNARE - a complex of proteins necessary for the exocytosis of acetylcholine . Toxins A and E cleave SNAP-25 whereas toxin B cleaves vesicle -associated membrane protein (VAMP) also known as synaptobrevin. Cleavage of SNARE proteins prevents the release of acetylcholine as the vesicles containing Ach are unable to bind to the presynaptic membrane.205

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A farmer presents with difficulty swallowing and jaw tightening . He gives a history of getting his finger jammed in the rustic gate a few days ago. He gives no history of previous tetanus immunization . After evaluation, he was diagnosed with tetanus . The release of which of the following neurotransmitters is affected by the toxin responsible for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Tetanus toxin affects the release of GABA. Tetanus toxin escapes normal lysosomal degradation and crosses the synapse to the GABA-ergic presynaptic inhibitory interneuron terminals . The toxin blocks the release of inhibitory neurotransmitters (glycine and gamma-aminobutyric acid) across the synaptic cleft . This blockage of the inhibitory neurotransmitters causes spastic paralysis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The neurotransmitter released by Renshaw cell interneuron is ______.
mcqs.explanation: The neurotransmitter released by Renshaw cell interneuron is glycine . Renshaw cell is an inhibitory interneuron which is activated by collaterals from spinal motor neurons. Renshaw cell terminates on the cell body of the same and other spinal motor neurons. It reduces or stops the discharge of the motor neuron by releasing glycine .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following neurotransmitters is increased during REM sleep ?
mcqs.explanation: Acetylcholine increases during REM sleep . In REM sleep , there is increase in acetylcholine and decrease in norepinephrine and serotonin. The reverse of this pattern leads to wakefulness .Neurotransmitters in REM sl eep Levels of neurotransmitte r Acetylcholine Increased Serotonin Decreased Norepinephrine Decreased206

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the wrong match?

options.c: Sympathetic post ganglionic fibres - release noradrenaline
options.d: Sweat glands - innervated by sympathetic adrenergic fibres

mcqs.explanation: Sweat glands are innervated by sympathetic cholinergic fibres (not adrenergic fibres). Pre-ganglionic fibres of the sympathetic nervous system , pre-ganglionic fibers of the parasympathetic nervous system and post -ganglionic parasympathetic fibres release acetylcholine . Post-ganglionic sympathetic fibres release noradrenaline in most of the sites , except in certain places such as sweat glands, piloerector muscles and blood vessels in some skeletal muscles where acetylcholine is released .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which part of the basal ganglia is the neurotransmitter glutamate secreted from?
mcqs.explanation: Projections from subthalamic nucleus to globus pallidus are glutaminergic . Neurotransmitters secreted by various regions of basal ganglia: • Substantia nigra pars compacta = dopamine • Substantia nigra pars reticulata = GABA • Subthalmic nuclei = glutamate • Corpus striatum to globus pallidus = GABA • Intrastriate neurons = acetylcholine • Globus pallidus = GABADiagrammatic representation of the principal connections of the basal ganglia. Acetylcholine is the transmitter produced by interneurons in the striatum.207 (SNr : substantia nigra pars reticulata ; SNc: substantia nigra pars compacta; STN: Subthalamic nucleus ; GPe: globus pallidus externa ; GPi: Globus pallidus interna).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: All of the following are excitatory neurotransmitters except :
mcqs.explanation: Serotonin is an inhibitory neurotransmitter. Acetylcholine , glutamate and norepinephrine are excitatory neurotransmitters.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about serotonin receptor ?
mcqs.explanation: 5-HT2C receptor agonists increase satiety (state of being fed beyond capacity ). Important serotonin receptors : • 5-HT2A receptors mediate platelet aggregation and smooth muscle contraction. • 5-HT3 receptors are present in the GIT and the area postrema and are related to vomiting. • 5-HT4 receptors are present in the GIT and brain . They facilitate secretion and peristalsis in GIT . • 5-HT6 and 5-HT7 are distributed throughout the limbic system . Note : All are G protein coupled receptors except 5-HT3 which is a ligand gated ion channel receptor .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Serotonin is present in highest concentration in ________
mcqs.explanation: Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine ; 5-HT) is present in highest concentration in platelets and in the gastrointestinal tract, where it is found in the enterochromaffin cells and the myenteric plexus . It is also found within the brain stem in the midline Raphe nuclei . Note : The precursor of serotonin is tryptophan .208

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which statement regarding the NMDA receptor is incorrect?

options.b: Glycine is essential for this receptor's response to its endogenous agonist
options.c: It is a chloride ion channel
options.d: It is present in hippocampal neurons

mcqs.explanation: NMDA receptor permits passage of Ca2+ and other cations (Na+), not of chloride . Glutamate is the agonist for NMDA receptor . Glycine binding to the NMDA receptor is essential for the receptor to respond to glutamate. NMDA receptors are present on hippocampal neurons. Note : GABA and glycine receptors act by increasing Cl- conductance .209

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Spatial distribution from which a stimulus produces a response is called _____
mcqs.explanation: Spatial distribution from which a stimulus produces a response is called receptive field . Sensory Unit: A single afferent neuron with all its receptor endings . Motor unit: Each single motor neuron and the muscle fibers it innervates. Dermatome: Each spinal nerve innervates a "segmental field " of the skin.216

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Fast vibration sense is mediated by ______.
mcqs.explanation: Fast vibration sense is mediated by Pacinian corpuscles . Pacinian corpuscle is the most sensitive mechanoreceptor in the somatosensory system . It is responsive to high-frequency (30–500 Hz) vibratory stimuli and pressure . They are rapidly adapting receptors . Option A: Merkel's disc sense touch and sustained pressure . They are slow adapting receptors . Present in epidermis . Option B: Meissner 's corpuscle sense tap and flutter . They are present in dermal papillae . They are rapidly adapting receptors . Option D: Ruffini endings sense skin stretch and fluttering vibration . The following image shows Merkel's disc and Meissner 's corpuscle being more superficial (reponsive to touch ) than Ruffini endings and Pacinian corpuscle (which are deeper in the dermis and responsive to pressure ).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The phasic receptor is______
mcqs.explanation: Meissner 's corpuscles are phasic (rapidly adapting ) receptors . Merkel's disc, Ruffini's end organs, and muscle spindle are tonic (slowly adapting ) receptors.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: You are doing a CNS examination of a patient with a spinal injury. At which of the following sites would the distance of two -point discrimination be greatest ?
mcqs.explanation: The distance of two -point discrimination is greatest at the back of the scapula .217 The relative tactile acuity of a given region can be determined by the two -point discrimination test . Here, calipers are used to determine the minimum distance between the two points which can be perceived as two points. Greater the density of receptors \032 Smaller the receptive field \032 More precise the localization. For e.g., Stimulus points on the back, for instance, must be separated by at least 65 mm before they can be distinguished as separate , whereas on the fingertips two stimuli are recognized if they are separated by as little as 2 mm. The lips have the greatest acuity (two -point discrimination threshold ~ 1 mm). Clinical significance : Blind individuals benefit from the tactile acuity of fingertips to facilitate the ability to read Braille. The dots forming Braille symbols are separated by 2.5 mm. Two-point discrimination is used to test the integrity of the dorsal column (medial lemniscus ) system .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the nature of the sensory receptor given below :
mcqs.explanation: The sensory receptor shown in the above image is Pacinian corpuscle . The Pacinian corpuscle is a rapidly adapting receptor and is an encapsulated receptor . When a stimulus of the same strength is continuously given to a sensory receptor , the frequency of the action potentials generated by the receptor gradually decreases . This phenomenon is known as receptor adaptation. Depending on whether the receptor stops responding to a stimulus rapidly or slowly , they are classified as rapidly adapting (phasic) or slow adapting receptors (tonic).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following classification of receptors is the same?
mcqs.explanation: Mechanoreceptors and exteroceptors have the same classification of receptors . Exteroceptors are concerned with the external environment or receptors which receives external stimuli. Mechanoreceptors are cutaneous receptors for touch and pressure . Thus mechanoreceptors can be considered to be exteroceptors . Nociceptors are pain receptors which detect physical and chemical damage occuring in the tissue . Interoceptors are concerned with the internal environment. Chemoreceptors are receptors stimulated by a change in the chemical composition of the environment in which they are located . These include receptors for taste and smell as well as visceral receptors such as those sensitive to changes in the plasma level of O2, pH, and osmolality . Teleceptors (distance receivers) are concerned with events at a distance , example - p hotorecep tors. Proprioceptors provide information about the position of the body in space at any given instant.218

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true regarding sensory receptor properties ?

options.a: Magnitude of sensation felt is directly proportional to the intensity of the stimulus
options.b: A touch receptor will generate a constant rate of discharge of its axon for as long as the receptor is stimulated
options.c: Meissner 's and Pacinian corpuscles adapt slowly , the others adapt rapidly
options.d: The frequency of a train of action potentials in an afferent fibre reflects the intensity of the stimulus given to its receptor

mcqs.explanation: The frequency of a train of action potentials in an afferent fibre reflects the intensity of the stimulus given to its receptor . Intensity of stimulus applied to a sensory receptor can be determined by the following : • Variation in frequency of action potentials generated • Variations in the number of receptors activated Option A : Weber-Fechner Law states that magnitude of sensation felt is directly proportional to the log of the intensity of the stimulus . Option B: A touch receptor will not generate a constant rate of discharge , even if the receptor is continuously stimulated . This is called desensitization or adaptation. If the opposite were true (if option B was correct), when we have our clothes on, we would have constant firing of neurons unnecessarily , in response to touch stimulus . Option C:Slowadapting (Tonic receptor s) Rapidlyadapting (Phasic rece ptors) Merkel's disc, Ruffini's end o rgans, Joint capsule Muscle s pindle , Golgi tendon organs Pacinian corpuscle , Meissner ' s corpuscles , Hair end organs

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A\024 fibers do not transmit _____.
mcqs.explanation: A\024 fibers do not transmit slow pain. They transmit fast pain. Activation of A\024 fibers, which release glutamate , is responsible for first pain (also called fast pain or epicritic pain), which is a rapid response and mediates the ability to localize the site and intensity of the noxious stimulus . Neuropathic pain can also be burning, dull and poorly localized (protopathic pain, transmitted by C nociceptor fibers (which release substance P). Dual Pain Pathway Pain can be carried by either A\024 fiber (fast pain/ epicritic pain) or by C fiber (slow pain/protopathic pain)Feature A\024fiber C fiber Stimuli MechanicalThermal Polymodal Myelination and trac t Myelinatedand carried viaNe ospinothalamic tract Unmyelinatedand carried via paleospinothalamic tract Conduction velocity 12 –30 m/s 0.5–2 m/s Impulse conduction Fast componentof pain Slow componentof pain219 Feature A\024fiber C fiber Neurotransmitter Glutamate Substance P

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The most potent algogenic substance is ______.
mcqs.explanation: Bradykinin is the most potent algogenic substance . An algogenic substance is a chemical released at the site of injury which mediates pain. These include bradykinin, serotonin, histamine, potassium ions, acids, acetylcholine , and proteolytic enzymes . Prostaglandins and substance P enhance the sensitivity of pain endings but do not directly excite them. Note : This is a controversial question According to Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology , 13th Edition , Page 622 - "One chemical that seems to be more painful than others is bradykinin . Researchers have suggested that bradykinin might be the agent most responsible for causing pain after tissue damage ." Hence , bradykinin is the better answer (not serotonin)

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Vanilloid receptors are activated by all except ______.
mcqs.explanation: Vanilloid receptors are not activated by vibration . Vanilloid receptors or TRPV1 (transient receptor potential vanilloid1 ) receptors are a part of family of nonselective cation channels called transient receptor potential (TRP ) channels. These channels respond to intense heat , acids, and chemicals such as capsaicin.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Heat-pain fibers are stimulated at temperatures around _____.
mcqs.explanation: Heat-pain fibers begin to be stimulated at around 45 \260C. Thermal Receptors and their ExcitationCold receptor Warm receptor Peak:24 \260C Peak:45 \260C. Cold nociceptor stimulated w hen temperature is around5 \260 C. Heat nociceptor is stimulated at temperatures around45 \260 C. Cold receptor fibers areA\024 an d C Warm receptor fibers areun myelinated C fibers220

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Weber-Fechner law relates magnitude of sensation to ____.
mcqs.explanation: Weber-Fechner Law states that the magnitude of sensation felt is proportionate to the log of the intensity of the stimulus . Other Laws in Physiology : • Doctrine of specific nerve energies - When the nerve pathways from a particular sense organ are stimulated , the sensation evoked is that for which the receptor is specialized no matter how or where along the pathway the activity is initiated . • Law of projection - No matter where a particular sensory pathway is stimulated along its course to the cortex, the conscious sensation produced is referred to the location of the receptor . This principle is called the law of projection .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient 's right leg was amputated because it was unsalvageable after the motor vehicle accident . After 2 weeks of her surgery, she started feeling episodes of severe pain in the amputated area. This pain is most likely based on which of the following mechanisms?
mcqs.explanation: This patient is having phantom limb pain. This pain is based on cortical plasticity . Cortical structures are capable of reorganization after the loss of a body part. The cortical representation of the neighboring parts spreads into the cortical area that was formerly occupied by the representation of the amputated part. This is called cortical plasticity leads to the phenomenon of phantom limb pain

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Perception of normal sensory stimuli as painful is ________
mcqs.explanation: Perception of normal sensory stimuli as painful is allodynia. Hyperalgesia is an exaggerated response to a noxious stimulus . An example of primary hyperalgesia is the extreme sensitivity of sunburned skin, which results from sensitization of the skin pain endings by local tissue products released due to burns — histamine, prostaglandins, and others. Causalgia is a type of neuropathic pain.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about anandamide?

options.c: There are anandamide-containing neurons in the periaqueductal gray

mcqs.explanation: There are anandamide-containing neurons in the periaqueductal gray and other areas concerned with pain. There are 2 types of endogenous cannabinoids: 2-arachidonyl glycerol and Anandamide. They bind to CB1 and CB2 receptors . They have an anti-nociceptive effect .221 Descending pathways from the mesencephalic periaqueductal gray inhibit transmission in nociceptive pathways . This descending pathway includes a synapse in the ventromedial medulla (Raphe nucleus ) and the release of endogenous opiates . So periaqueductal gray matter releases endogenous opiates .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about visceral pain?

options.c: It is mediated by B fibers

mcqs.explanation: Visceral pain is poorly localized , unpleasant and associated with nausea and autonomic symptoms . It often originates from thoracic and abdominal cavities, transmitted through small type C pain fibers. It often radiates (or is referred ) to other somatic structures perhaps due to convergence of somatic and visceral nociceptive afferent fibers on the same second -order neurons in the spinal dorsal horn that project to the thalamus and then to the primary somatosensory cortex. When pain is referred , it is usually to a structure that developed from the same embryonic segment or dermatome as the structure in which the pain originates. This principle is called the dermatomal rule. Example : the heart and the arm have the same segmental origin.Feature A\024fiber C fiber Stimuli MechanicalThermal Polymodal Myelination and trac t Myelinatedand carried viaNe ospinothalamic tract Unmyelinatedand carried via paleospinothalamic tract Conduction velocity 12 –30 m/s 0.5–2 m/s Impulse conduction Fast componentof pain Slow componentof pain Neurotransmitter Glutamate Substance P

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Pain insensitive structure is _____.
mcqs.explanation: Alveoli are pain insensitive structures . Alveoli of lungs and parenchyma of liver are almost completely insensitive to the pain of any type . However, the liver capsule is extremely sensitive to both direct trauma and stretch . The bile ducts , arterial walls, bronchi and the parietal pleura are very sensitive to pain.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with chronic pain is undergoing transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation for pain relief . What is the basis of this procedure?
mcqs.explanation: Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) of pain relief is based on the gate theory of pain. This method uses electrodes to activate A�o and A\035 fibers near the injury to relieve pain. Gate control theory operates at the substantia gelatinosa of the dorsal horn of the spinal cord.222 The relief may result from inhibition of pain pathways (Inhibition of C fibers and A-delta fibers) in the dorsal horn gate , by stimulation of large-diameter touch -pressure afferents (A-beta fibers). This is called the gate -control hypothesis . Interesting clinical application : Touching or shaking an injured area decreases the pain due to the injury. Stimulation with an electric vibrator at the site of pain also gives some relief . The same mechanism is probably responsible for the efficacy of counterirritants. Stimulation of the skin over an area of visceral inflammation produces some relief of the pain due to the visceral disease . The old-fashioned mustard plaster works on this principle .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Primary cutaneous hyperalgesia _____

options.a: Develops in the normal skin region around the area of flare
options.b: Is an abnormal condition in the skin in which painful stimuli become less severe
options.c: Is due to changes in threshold of pain receptors
options.d: Is associated with throbbing type of pain

mcqs.explanation: Hyperalgesia is an exaggerated response to a noxious stimulus . • Hyperalgesia and allodynia signify increased sensitivity of nociceptive afferent fibers. • Causes of hyperalgesia • The excessive sensitivity of the pain receptors , which is called primary hyperalgesia • Facilitation of sensory transmission, which is called secondary hyperalgesia . An example of primary hyperalgesia is the extreme sensitivity of sunburned skin, which results from sensitization of the skin pain endings, by local tissue products from the burn — histamine, prostaglandins, and others. Secondary hyperalgesia frequently results from lesions in the spinal cord or the thalamus.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The transient receptor potential (TRP ) channel that is most active at normal skin temperature is _______.
mcqs.explanation: At normal skin temperatures , TRPV3 is the most active receptor .223

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A soldier posted in Siachen is brought to you in the ER. In order to rule out hypothermia , how do you best measure his temperature ?
mcqs.explanation: In the given clinical scenario rectal temperature would be the preferred site to measure the core body temperature . During low or high temperatures like in Siachen, the axillary and the oral temperatures are highly misleading and should not be used to measure the core body temperatures Infrared tympanic thermometer measures the temperature of the eardrum which is representative of core body temperature . However, more often the thermometer is not inserted adequately or for safety reasons, they are manufactured in such a way that they do not reach deep into the ear canal, or the ear canal contains cerumen which can disturb the measurement . Hence the infrared thermometer more commonly delivers the temperature of ear canal cerumen and hence not a reliable method of measuring the core body temperature .224

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The principle that " In spinal cords, dorsal roots are sensory and ventral roots are motor" is known as ______
mcqs.explanation: The principle that in the spinal cord the dorsal roots are sensory and the ventral roots are motor is known as the Bell–Magendie law. Laws in Sensory Physiology • Muller 's doctrine of specific nerve energies : When the nerve pathways from a particular sense organ are stimulated , the sensation evoked is that for which the receptor is specialized , no matter how or where along the pathway the activity is initiated .231 • Law of projection : No matter where a particular sensory pathway is stimulated along its course to the cortex, the conscious sensation produced is referred to the location of the receptor . • Weber-Fechner Law: Magnitude of sensation felt is directly proportional to the log of the intensity of the stimulus . • Labelled line theory : All the sensations from the different parts of the body travel along specified paths. For example , in the posterior column, fibers from the lower parts of the body are placed medially .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient admitted to the ward does not feel a sensation of the heat on touching a hot object . Considering the signal reaches the thalamus, which of the following is not transmitting the signal to an intact postcentral gyrus?
mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, the tertiary neuron does not transmit the signal to the postcentral gyrus. In the thalamus, secondary sensory neurons synapse onto tertiary sensory neurons, which in turn project to the somatosensory region of the cerebral cortex. The question tests your knowledge of this pathway . It is said that the signal reaches the thalamus and the postcentral gyrus is intact. Still, the person cannot perceive the sensation, so the pathway is broken between the thalamus and the gyrus, which has to be at the tertiary neuron.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Decussation of ascending spinal pathways occurs mainly within the ______
mcqs.explanation: Decussation of ascending spinal pathways occurs mainly within the spinal cord and medulla oblongata. Most of the ascending pathways and tracts do decussate or cross; however, some remain uncrossed . Dorsal column pathway crosses in the medulla oblongata. The anterior and lateral spinothalamic tract crosses obliquely in the spinal segments .232

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Conscious proprioception is carried by_____.
mcqs.explanation: Conscious proprioception is carried by dorsal column. Unconscious proprioception is carried by spinocerebellar tract. Option B and C: Anterolateral system carries pain, temperature , crude touch .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a property of fibers in the dorsal column pathway ?
mcqs.explanation: The dorsal column–medial lemniscal system is composed of large, myelinated nerve fibers and thus transmit signals to the brain , at high velocities of 30 to 110 m/sec. Option B: Dorsal column carries fine touch and anterolateral column carries crude touch233

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient comes to you for his annual health checkup . He lost his vision due to an accident a few years ago. He now experiences the world through touch . Which of the following Brodmann 's areas processes this tactile stimulation?
mcqs.explanation: Processing of tactile stimulation occurs in Brodmann 's area in 3, 1, 2. The human cerebral cortex is divided into about 50 distinct areas called Brodmann 's areas based on histological structural differences . Areas 3, 1, 2 which constitute primary somatosensory area I, and areas 5 and 7, which constitute the somatosensory association area process sensory information like tactile stimulation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Cortical representation of body in the cerebrum is_______
mcqs.explanation: Cortical representation of body in the cerebrum is vertical. Parts of the body are represented in order along the postcentral gyrus, with the legs on top and head at the bottom of the gyrus. A cortical homunculus is a distorted representation of the human body, based on a neurological map of the areas and proportions of the human brain dedicated to processing motor functions, or sensory functions, for different parts of the body. The size of the cortical receiving area for impulses from a particular part of the body is proportionate to the use of the part. Sensory Homunculus is a topographical representation of distribution of sensory input to the somatosensory cortex from different parts of the body. Motor homunculus is a topographical representation of distribution of motor output from primary motor cortex to different parts of the body. Sensory homunculus is depicted below :234

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Somatosensory area has the largest representation for_____
mcqs.explanation: Somatosensory area has the largest representation for lips. The relative sizes of the cortical receiving areas of the sensory homunculus are proportionate to the use of the part. The sizes of these areas are directly proportional to the number of specialized sensory receptors in each respective peripheral area of the body. Some body parts are represented by large areas in the somatic cortex—the lips the greatest of all, followed by the face and thumb, whereas the trunk and lower part of the body are represented by relatively small areas.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient sustains an injury to the lateral portion of the postcentral gyrus in the right hemisphere . Loss of sensation is likely to be seen at which of the following sites in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: In this case, injury to the lateral portion of the postcentral gyrus in the right hemisphere would result in loss of sensation in the left facial area. Each hemisphere receives somatic sensory information from the opposite side of the body in the postcentral gyrus (somatosensory area). The lateral portion of the postcentral gyrus receives somatic sensory information from the facial and neck region while the medial portion of the postcentral gyrus received somatic sensory information from the trunk and appendages .235

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Lesion of somatosensory area I affects _______
mcqs.explanation: Lesion of the somatosensory area I affects the localization of sensations . Bilateral lesion of the somatosensory area I leads to the following impairment of sensory judgment : • Inability to localize different sensations in different parts of the body • Inability to judge degrees of pressure against the body • Inability to judge the weight of the objects • Inability to judge shapes of forms of objects - astereognosis • Inability to judge the texture of the materials Pain and temperature are not affected both in quality and intensity in the lesion of the somatosensory area I. However, they are poorly localised . Pain and temperature localization depends greatly on the topographical map of the body in somatosensory area I to localize the source .`

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man was rushed to the casualty after getting stabbed in the back with a knife. On MRI, a complete transection of one side of the spinal cord is suspected . Which of the following is likely to be seen in this patient ?

options.a: Pain and temperature loss on the opposite side
options.b: Fine touch lost on the opposite side
options.c: Pain and temperature lost on the same side
options.d: Only pain lost on the same side

mcqs.explanation: This patient most likely has Brown-Sequard syndrome. It is characterized by loss of pain and temperature on the opposite side . Hemisection of the spinal cord causes damage to ascending sensory (dorsal column pathway , ventrolateral spinothalamic tract) and descending motor (corticospinal tract) pathways , which is called the Brown-S\351quard syndrome. The lesion to fasciculus gracilus or fasciculus cuneatus leads to ipsilateral loss of discriminative touch, vibration , and proprioception below the level of the lesion.236 The loss of the spinothalamic tract leads to contralateral loss of pain and temperature sensation beginning one or two segments below the lesion. Damage to the corticospinal tract produces weakness and spasticity in certain muscle groups on the same side of the body.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following findings are seen in a patient with Brown-Sequard syndrome?

options.a: Upper Motor Neuron type of paralysis below the lesion on the opposite side
options.b: Impaired fine touch below the lesion on the opposite side
options.c: Loss of crude touch below the lesion on the same side
options.d: Loss of vibration sense below the lesion on the same side

mcqs.explanation: A patient with Brown Sequard syndrome will have a loss of vibration sense below the lesion on the same side . Brown-sequard syndrome is caused due to hemisection of the Spinal cord. It can be caused by fracture-dislocation of the vertebral column, by a bullet or stab wound , or by an expanding tumor. Clinical features : • Pyramidal tract: Pyramidal weakness (ipsilateral upper motor neuron type of paralysis) below the level of the lesion on the same side as the lesion (pyramidal tract crosses in the medulla ). • Dorsal columns: Impaired fine touch, 2 point discrimination, proprioception , vibration below the level of lesion on the same side of lesion (dorsal column fibres cross in the medulla ). • Spinothalamic tract: Loss of pain, temperature, crude touch , pressure sensation below the level of the lesion on the contralateral side of the lesion (spinothalamic tract crosses midline after entering the cord).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Itch is carried by______
mcqs.explanation: Itch-specific fibers have been demonstrated in the anterolateral spinothalamic tract. They are carried by unmyelinated nerve fiber C. Itching can be produced by repeated local mechanical stimulation of skin, variety of chemical agents including histamine and kinins released in the skin in response to tissue damage Simple scratching relieves itching because it activates large fast conducting afferents (A\035) that gate the transmission in the dorsal horn in a manner analogous to inhibition of pain by stimulation of similar afferents (Gate control theory ).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Following are the endogenous opioids except _____
mcqs.explanation: Endogenous opioids , a group of neuropeptides that includes beta-endorphin, dynorphins, and enkephalins. Opioids cause both presynaptic and post synaptic inhibition reducing excitatory post -synaptic potential (EPSP). Opioids are released from the descending analgesic pathway and bind with opiate receptors on the afferent pain-fiber terminal. This binding suppresses the release of substance P, blocking further transmission of the pain signal.237

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: You are examining a patient for a follow-up of severe pain in his right leg . He tells you that he feels much better now that he is taking acupuncture therapy too. Which of the following is responsible for pain relief in acupuncture ?
mcqs.explanation: Pain relief in acupuncture is by the release of endorphin. The acupuncture endorphin hypothesis is the primary mechanism of acupuncture analgesia. According to this hypothesis , Acupuncture is thought to activate afferent neurons leading to spinal cord and midbrain centers that release endogenous opioids implicated in pain relief .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Fast pain is carried by_______
mcqs.explanation: Fast pain is carried by neospinothalamic tract. Pain signals take two pathways to the brain : • Neospinothalmic tract for fast pain/epicritic pain (A\024 fibres) • Paleospinothalamic tract for slow pain/Protopathic pain (C fibres)

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Soldiers wounded in the heat of battle often feel no pain until the battle is over which is an example of stress -induced analgesia. This is due to______
mcqs.explanation: Stress induced analgesia is due to cannabinoids. The stress -induced analgesia, i.e., reduced pain sensitivity during stressful events might be due to: • Release of endogenous cannabinoids such as 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG) and anandamide • Release of Norepinephrine from brainstem catecholaminergic neurons in the amygdala.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not carry proprioceptive impulses ?
mcqs.explanation: Tectocerebellar tract does not carry proprioceptive impluses . Tectocerebellar tract carry visual and auditory impulses . Spinocerebellar , olivo cerebellar , cuneo cerebellar tracts carry Proprioceptive impulses . Vestibulocerebellar tract carry vestibular impulses .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Pain and temperature in the thalamus are controlled by which of the following nuclei ?
mcqs.explanation: Pain and temperature in thalamus are controlled by the ventral posterior lateral nucleus . Pain and temperature is carried by anterolateral spinothalamic tract. Fibres from anterolateral spinothalamic tract and dorsal column synapse in the ventral posteriorlateral (VPL ) nucleus of thalamus.238 Option B: The pathway from taste receptors includes synapses in the nucleus of the tractus solitarius in the brainstem and ventral posterior medial nucleus in the thalamus. Option C: Anterior nucleus functions as a relay station for the hippocampal impulses . It receives afferents from mammillothalamic tract. It sends efferents to cingulate gyrus. Option D: Intralaminar nucleus participates in arousal reaction, it recieves afferents from reticular formation of brain stem .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Ventrolateral cordotomy for relief of pain in the right lower limb is being performed on a patient . Which of the following is cut in this procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: In ventrolateral cordotomy, selected pain-conducting tracts in the spinal cord, i.e. fibers in the lateral spinothalamic pathway , are cut leading to contralateral loss of pain and temperature sensation below the level of the lesion. In the more recent percutaneous approach, destruction of the lateral spinothalamic at the level of C1-C2 results in a contralateral disruption of painful sensations beyond C4. Note : The fibers carrying pain sensation ascend in the lateral spinothalamic tract while the fibers carrying crude touch and pressure sensations ascend in the anterior spinothalamic tract.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Pick the correct statement :

options.a: Spinal lemniscus carries fibres of dorsal spinothalamic tract
options.b: Trigeminal lemniscus carries pain and temperature sensations from the ipsilateral orofacial region
options.c: Lateral lemniscus carries fibres from cochlear nuclei
options.d: Medial lemniscus carries fibres from of vestibular nuclei

mcqs.explanation: Lateral lemniscus carries fibres from cochlear nuclei Medial lemniscus carries fibres from of dorsal column nuclei Spinal lemniscus carries fibres of anterolateral spinothalamic tract Trigeminal lemniscus carries pain and temperature sensations from the contralateral orofacial region239

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Lesion in the medial lemniscus at the level of pons causes which of the following ?

options.a: Pain and temperature loss in the same side
options.b: Pain and temperature loss in the opposite side
options.c: Loss of tactile and proprioception on the same side
options.d: Loss of tactile and proprioception on the opposite side

mcqs.explanation: Lesion in the medial lemniscus at the level of pons causes loss of tactile and proprioception on the opposite side . Fibers of medial lemniscus ascend ipsilaterally in the dorsal columns of the spinal cord to the medulla , where they synapse in the gracilus and cuneate nuclei . The second -order neurons from these nuclei cross the midline and ascend in the medial lemniscus to end in the contralateral ventral posterior lateral (VPL ) nucleus and related specific sensory relay nuclei of the thalamus.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Ablation of somatosensory area 1 leads to______

options.c: Loss of tactile but not 2 point discrimination
options.d: Loss of tactile and 2 point discrimination

mcqs.explanation: Ablation of somatosensory area 1 leads to Loss of tactile and 2 point discrimination. Widespread bilateral excision of the somatosensory area I causes loss of the following types of sensory judgment : • The person is unable to localize discretely the different sensations in the different parts of the body. However, he or she can localize these sensations crudely , such as to a particular hand. The brain stem , thalamus, or parts of the cerebral cortex can perform some degree of localization. • The person is unable to judge critical degrees of pressure /weight /texture .240

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Light entering the eye first passes through ______ retinal layer.
mcqs.explanation: Light passes first through the retinal ganglion layer, the most anterior/inner layer of the retina. Light then passes through other layers of the retina until it reaches the photoreceptors in the posterior/outer region of the retina. Retina is organized into 10 layers or zones where distinctive components are clustered together to form continuous strata. • Light passes in the direction: Vitreous humor(anterior)\032 choroid(most posterior) encountering the cell layers in that direction (ganglion cell layer\032photoreceptors ) • Visual processing /Phototransduction occurs in the opposite direction (Photoreceptors \032 ganglion cell layer)

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Initiation of visual impulse is associated with_____

options.a: Condensation of opsin with Vitamin A
options.b: Photoisomerisation and hydrolysis of visual purple

mcqs.explanation: Initiation of visual impulse is associated with photoisomerisation and hydrolysis of visual purple Rhodopsin or visual purple , the photosensitive pigment , is composed of opsin (a protein belonging to the superfamily of G protein–coupled receptors ) and retinal (an aldehyde of vitamin A). When light strikes the photoreceptors, retinal is chemically transformed in a process called photoisomerization, which begins the transduction process .247

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which form of vitamin A combines with opsin to make rhodopsin?
mcqs.explanation: 11 -cis –retinaldehyde combines with opsin to make rhodopsin. All-trans retinol is one form of Vitamin A which is converted to 11 -cis retinol under the influence of Isomerase. Finally, -cis retinol is converted into 11 -cis retinal which combines with Scotopsin to form rhodopsin.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding distribution of rods and cones in retina?

options.a: Macula lutea is the blind spot
options.b: low density of photoreceptors are present in macula
options.d: Peripheral retina has greater cones to rods ratio

mcqs.explanation: Central fovea (foveola) contains only cones (rod-free area) and is a region of highest resolution . Regional Variations in the Retina248 Macula lutea • Located at posterior pole , temporal to the optic disc • Area of central vision • High density of photoreceptors and interneurons Optic disc • Lacks photoreceptors • Is called "Blind spot " • Normally a person is unaware of blind spot because • Corresponding part of the visual field can be seen by the contralateral eye • Neurological processes complete the incomplete image perceptually Peripheral retina • Higher ratio of rods to cones =Rod to cone\03220:1 • Greater degree of convergence of photoreceptors to the target interneuron (bipolar cells ) • More sensitivity to light • Lower visual acuity

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The rod receptor potential differs from other surface receptors in that it shows ______.
mcqs.explanation: The rod receptor potential differs from other surface receptors in that it shows hyperpolarization. In most sensory receptors : Arrival of stimulus \032 Ion channels are opened up allowing current to flow => depolarisation of the receptor . In photoreceptors : When the light strikes the outer segment , a cascade of reactions (refer figure ) are initiated, that close some of the Na+ channels in the outer segment and results in hyperpolarization.249

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which is the first-order neuron in the optic pathway ?
mcqs.explanation: Photoreceptors - rods and cones are the first-order neurons in the visual pathway .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Purely depolarizing cells in optic pathway are ______
mcqs.explanation: The responses of the rods, cones, and horizontal cells are hyperpolarizing, and the responses of the bipolar cells are either hyperpolarizing or depolarizing , whereas amacrine cells produce purely depolarizing potential .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Amacrine cells secrete _____
mcqs.explanation: Amacrine cells release acetylcholine . Amacrine cells are one of the neuronal cell types of the retina. They transmit signals in two directions, either directly from bipolar cells to ganglion cells or horizontally within the inner plexiform layer from axons of the bipolar cells to dendrites of the ganglion cells or to other amacrine cells . Amacrine cells release GABA, glycine , dopamine, acetylcholine & indolamine. Other neuronal cell types of the retina are: • The photoreceptors : rods & cones • Horizontal cells • Bipolar cells • Ganglion cells Of these cell types , only neurotransmitters secreted by photoreceptors & amacrine cells have been discovered . Rods and cones release glutamate at their synapses with the bipolar cells .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The only neurons in retina showing action potential are _____
mcqs.explanation: All neural elements in the retina exhibit local graded potentials except ganglion cells which shows action potential.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The fibers from contralateral nasal retina project to the following layers of lateral geniculate nucleus ______
mcqs.explanation: 250 On each side , layers 1, 4, and 6 of the lateral geniculate nucleus receive input from the contralateral eye , whereas layers 2, 3, and 5 receive input from the ipsilateral eye . (Refer figure ).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Parvocellular pathway carries signal for detection of_____
mcqs.explanation: From the Lateral Geniculate Nucleus (LGN), a magnocellular pathway (from layers 1 and 2) and a parvocellular pathway (from the rest of the layers) project to the visual cortex.Parvocellular pathway Magnocellular pathway Receive input entirely from t ype X retinal ganglion cells , a nd transmit color. Formed by Y ganglion cells p roject to magnocellular layers of the lateral geniculate nucl eus . Convey accurate point-to-poi nt spatial information. Colorblind, transmitting only black-and-white information. Terminate in layer 4C of the primary visual cortex. Terminate in layer 4C of the primary visual cortex. Carries signals for color visio n, texture , shape , and fine de tails. Carries signals for detection of movement, depth , and flic ker.251

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The axons from lateral geniculate nucleus terminate in _____ layer of primary visual cortex.
mcqs.explanation: The axons from the lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN) mostly end in layer 4. The primary visual receiving area (primary visual cortex) is located principally on the sides of the calcarine fissure and has 6 layers similar to the neocortex . Layer 4 recieves most of the input from the LGN, which is divided further into 4A, 4B, 4C�o , and 4C\035. The magnocellular pathways from layers 1 and 2 of the LGN end in layer 4C�o while the parvocellular pathways from layers 3-6 of the LGN end in layer 4C\035.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: An ophthalmologist explains to a patient that he is a protanope . These patients have difficulty in identifying which of the following color?
mcqs.explanation: Protanopes are dichromats with difficulty in identifying red color. • Anomalous Trichromatic Vision • Deficiency of red is Protanomaly. • Deficiency of green is Deuteranomaly . • Deficiency of blue is Tritanomaly . • Dichromatic Vision (Individuals with only two cone systems ) • Blindness to red color Protanopia (Protanope). • Blindness to green color Deuteranopia (Deuteranope ). • Blindness to blue color Tritanopia (Tritanope). • Monochromatic Vision Have only one cone system . • Color blindness is X-linked recessive.252 • Achromatopsia/ Achromasia- Color blindness is due to lesions of area V8 of the visual cortex.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Auditory information is relayed through ______ thalamic nucleus .
mcqs.explanation: The medial geniculate nucleus is the thalamic nucleus that conveys auditory information from the brainstem to the primary auditory cortex. Lateral geniculate nucleus is the thalamic nucleus that conveys visual information.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: In the auditory pathway , which is the first structure that can determine the direction of the perceived sound?
mcqs.explanation: The superior olivary nuclei receive information from both ears and begin the process of detecting the direction from which a sound comes . The eighth nerves reach their respective cohlear nuclei in the medulla from where the nerves travel to both the ipsilateral and contralteral superior olivary nuclei in the pons and hence giving it the ability to detect the direction of the sound. The lateral part of superior olivary nucleus does so by comparing the difference in intensities of sound reaching the two ears, whereas the medial part of the superior olivary nucleus detects the time lag between the signals entering the two ears.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following events prompts the auditory system to interpret a sound as loud ?

options.a: Decreased number of inner hair cells become stimulated
options.b: Decreased number of outer hair cells become stimulated
options.c: Hair cells excite nerve endings at a diminished rate
options.d: Amplitude of vibration of the basilar membrane increases

mcqs.explanation: There are at least three ways that the auditory system determines loudness : • As the sound becomes louder - the amplitude of vibration of the basilar membrane increases so that hair cells excite the nerve endings at more rapid rates. • As the amplitude increases- more and more hair cells on the fringes of the resonating portion of the basilar membrane become stimulated . • As the amplitude of vibration reaches high intensity , the outer hair cells become recruited at a significant rate.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Umami taste is evoked by____
mcqs.explanation: Umami taste is triggered particularly by the monosodium glutamate (MSG) used so extensively in Asian cooking. Taste Receptors • Humans have five established basic tastes : sweet , salt, sour, bitter and umami. • The taste receptors for these five basic tastes are of two major types : • Ligand-gated channels (ionotropic receptors ): for salt and sour taste253 • G-Protein Coupled Receptors (metabotropic receptors ): for sweet , bitter and umami • Salt and sour taste are mediated through epithelial sodium channels (ENaC) • Na+ movement through ENaC \032salt taste • H+ movement through ENaC \032 sour taste • Sweet , bitter, and umami are sensed via GPCRs • T1R2 and T1R3 families \032 sweet taste • T2R family \032 bitter taste • Metabotropic glutamate receptor (mGluR4) \032 Umami

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Mitral cells are seen in ______
mcqs.explanation: Mitral cells are seen in Olfactory bulb. Axons of Olfactory nerves (First cranial nerve) synapse with the mitral cells and tufted cells in the olfactory bulb to form anatomically discrete units called olfactory glomeruli . The olfactory bulb also contains periglomerular cells that are inhibitory interneurons and granule cells that make reciprocal synapses with mitral and tufted cells . These mitral and tufted cells (second -order neurons) terminate in Olfactory cortex.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following sensory systems has the smallest range of intensity discrimination?
mcqs.explanation: The olfactory system has the smallest range of intensity discrimination. Smell is concerned more with detecting the presence or absence of odors , than with the quantitative detection of their intensities . Concentrations that are only 10 to 50 times above threshold values will evoke maximum intensity of smell , which is in contrast to most other254 sensory system of the body.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Number of cones in the retina (millions) is_______
mcqs.explanation: There are approximately 6 million cones and 120 million rods in each human eye . Features of Photoreceptors • Each rod and cone are divided into outer segment , inner segment , nuclear region and a synaptic zone. • Saccules and discs in the outer segment contain photosensitive pigments . • If a person spends a considerable length of time in brightly lighted surroundings and then moves to a dimly lighted environment, the retinas slowly become "accustomed to the dark ." This decline in visual threshold is known as dark adaptation . It is nearly maximal in about 20 min, much longer than the time taken for light adaptation which is 5 min. • When one passes suddenly from a dim to a brightly lighted environment, the light seems intensely and even uncomfortably bright until the eyes adapt to the increased illumination and the visual threshold rises. This adaptation occurs over a period of about 5 min and is called light adaptation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: What is the site of lesion in Wernicke's hemianopic pupil ?
mcqs.explanation: The site of lesion in Wernicke's hemianopic pupil is optic tract. Wernicke hemianopic pupil is the light reflex , where , illumination of the blind half of the retina shows no pupillary reaction while stimulating the normal side of the retina shows a pupillary reaction. It is seen in lesions involving the optic tract. It is also seen in cases such as TB , syphilis and tumours of the optic thalamus.255 Homonymous hemianopia (HH) involves loss of vision on the same side of the visual field in both eyes . HH is characteristically seen in lesions involving the visual pathway posterior to the optic chiasma.256

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Each muscle spindle consists of ______ intrafusal fibers.
mcqs.explanation: • Each muscle spindle is 3 to 10 millimeters long. It is built around 3 to 12 tiny intrafusal muscle fibers that are attached to the glycocalyx of the surrounding large extrafusal skeletal muscle fibers. • Each intrafusal muscle fiber is a tiny skeletal muscle fiber. However, the central region of each of these fibers has few or no actin and myosin filaments . Therefore, this central portion does not contract when the ends do. Instead, it functions as a sensory receptor . The end portions that do contract are excited by small gamma motor nerve fibers.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Motor supply to muscle spindle is _______
mcqs.explanation: Motor supply to muscle spindle is \025 Muscle spindles have a motor nerve supply of their own.These nerves belong to Erlanger and Gasser's A\037 group. They are just 3–6 �M in diameter (hence called small motor nerve system /\037 efferents of Leksell) and go exclusively to muscle spindles . Note : • Motor innervation of muscle spindle is by gamma efferents • Motor innervation of extrafusal fibers is by alpha motor neurons Nuclear bag muscle fibers: 1–3 per muscle spindle . Nuclear chain muscle fibers: 3–9 per muscle spindle .268

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Identify the type of nerve fibre in the diagram below .
mcqs.explanation: In the given figure , the fiber in yellow innervates the ends of the muscle spindle . Therefore, it is a gamma motor neuron. Many much smaller gamma motor neurons are located in the spinal cord anterior horns (shown as the yellow efferent fiber). These gamma motor neurons average 5 micrometers in diameter , which go to small, special skeletal muscle fibers called intrafusal fibers or the muscle spindle . These fibers constitute the ends of the muscle spindle , which help control basic muscle "tone." Option (b): The alpha motor neurons (shown as the blue efferent fibre) are on an average 14 micrometers in diameter. These fibers branch many times after they enter the muscle and innervate the large skeletal muscle fibers at the motor endplate . Stimulation of a single alpha nerve fiber excites269 anywhere from three to several hundred skeletal muscle fibers, which are collectively called the motor unit. Option (c): A-beta fibers are fibers for touch and pressure . Option (d): A-delta fibers are fibers for pain and temperature .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false with respect to muscle spindles ?

options.a: The intrafusal and extrafusal fibers are positioned paralled to each other
options.b: The primary endings of intrafusal fibers are most sensitive to a dynamic response
options.c: Type II nerve fibers do not innervate static nuclear bag fibers
options.d: Two types of \025 motor neurons supply the muscle spindle

mcqs.explanation: Type II nerve fibers do innervate the static nuclear bag fibers. They do not innervate dynamic nuclear bag fibers. A muscle spindle has: • Intrafusal fibers - these are tiny skeletal muscles which have few or no actin and myosin filaments in the central portion. This portion acts as a sensory receptor . • Extrafusal fibers These fibers are positioned parallel to each other (Option A). There are two types of intrafusal fibers: • Nuclear bag fibers - subdivided as dynamic and static nuclear bag fibers • Nuclear chain fibers Sensory nerve supply : There are two types of sensory endings : • Primary endings - (annulospiral ending) from Type Ia nerve fibers. This innervates both the nuclear bag and nuclear chain fibers. They are most sensitive to the velocity of the change in muscle length . This is called a dynamic response . (Option B)270 • Secondary endings - from Type II nerve fibers. This innervates static nuclear bag and nuclear chain fibers. They do not innervate dynamic nuclear bag fibers. (Option C) Both primary and secondary endings show a static response . Motor nerve supply : The muscle spindles are supplied by \025 motor neurons. There are two types of \025 motor neurons- dynamic that supply dynamic nuclear bag fibers and static that supply static nuclear bag fibers and nuclear chain fibers. (Option D)

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is sensed by the nuclear bag fibers?
mcqs.explanation: The nuclear bag fibers sense the dynamic length of the muscle . Nuclear bag fibers are intrafusal fibers, which are a part of the muscle spindle . Intrafusal fibers serve a purely sensory function in the muscle spindle . Types of intrafusal fibers in muscle spindles : Note - Golgi tendon organ senses changes in muscle tension. Muscle spindle also provides sense of joint position.Feature Nuclear bag fibers Nuclear chain fibers Structure Nuclei in central dilated area Nuclei in rows Types StaticDynamic ---- Primary sensory afferent Ia (for both the types ) Ia Secondary sensory ending II (only for static bag fiber) II Efferent static & dynamic \025-motor neu rons static \025-motor neuron s Way of detection of the chan ge in muscle length Static & dynamic changes Static change271

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The afferents for deep tendon reflexes innervate _____
mcqs.explanation: The afferents for deep tendon reflexes innervate both - nuclear bag and chain fibers. The afferents for the DTRs are the type Ia and type II nerve fibers. There are three types of intrafusal muscle fibers: dynamic nuclear bag, static nuclear bag, and nuclear chain fibers. A single Ia afferent fiber innervates all three types of fibers to form a primary sensory ending. A group II sensory fiber innervates nuclear chain and static bag fibers to form a secondary sensory ending. Deep tendon reflexes are an example of stretch reflex or myotatic reflex .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Stimulus for stretch reflex is_____
mcqs.explanation: Stretch reflex occurs when the muscle is stretched passively . Stretch (myotatic) reflex is monosynaptic. (As illustrated in the figure given below , steps 1\0325).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Withdrawal reflexes are not____

options.b: Prolonged if the stimulus is strong
options.c: An example of a flexor reflex
options.d: Accompanied by the same response on both sides of the body

mcqs.explanation: Withdrawal reflexes are not accompanied by the same response on both sides of the body. On the ipsilateral side of the pain stimulus , flexors are stimulated (they contract) and extensors are inhibited (they relax), and the arm is jerked away from the stove. On the contralateral side , flexors are inhibited and extensors are stimulated (crossed extension reflex ) to maintain balance. It results in flexion on the ipsilateral side and extension on the contralateral side . Somatosensory and pain afferent fibers elicit withdrawal of the stimulated body part from the noxious stimulus.272 Pain (e.g., touching a hot stove) stimulates the flexor reflex afferents of groups II , III , and IV . The afferent fibers synapse polysynaptically (via interneurons) onto motoneurons in the spinal cord. As a result of persistent neural activity in the polysynaptic circuits, an afterdischarge occurs. The afterdischarge prevents the muscle from relaxing for some time.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The maintenance of normal posture depends on_____
mcqs.explanation: The maintenance of normal posture depends on the Integrity of reflex arc. The muscles that maintain upright posture —that is, support the body's weight against gravity—are controlled by the brain and by reflex mechanisms. Three levels of the nervous system control movement: • The spinal cord, which integrates spinal reflexes and contains central pattern generators. • The brain stem and cerebellum , which control postural reflexes and hand and eye movements. • The cerebral cortex and basal ganglia, which are responsible for voluntary movements.273

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Receptor for inverse stretch reflex _____
mcqs.explanation: Golgi tendon organ is the receptor for inverse stretch reflex (refer figure ). The Golgi tendon organs, unlike the spindles , are in series with the muscle fibers; therefore, they are stimulated by both passive stretch and active contraction of the muscle . The degree of stimulation by contraction of muscles is much greater than that caused by the stretching of muscles . Muscle contraction \032 Ib fibers from the Golgi tendon organ excite an inhibitory interneuron that releases inhibitory mediator glycine \032 hyperpolarization (inhibition) of �o motor neurons \032 muscle relaxation.274

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The number of muscle fibers per Golgi tendon organ is ___.
mcqs.explanation: There are 3-20 muscle fibers per Golgi tendon organ. • Golgi tendon organ consists of a netlike collection of knobby nerve endings among the fascicles of a tendon. • There are 3–25 muscle fibers per Golgi tendon organ. • The fibers from the Golgi tendon organs make up the Ib group of myelinated , rapidly conducting sensory nerve fibers. • Golgi tendon organs help in regulating the velocity of the muscle contraction, muscle length, and muscle force. • They are the receptor for inverse stretch reflex .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The inverse stretch reflex _____

options.a: Occurs when Ia spindle afferents are inhibited
options.b: Is a monosynaptic reflex initiated by activation of the Golgi tendon organ
options.c: Is a disynaptic reflex with a single interneuron inserted between the afferent and efferent limbs
options.d: Is a polysynaptic reflex with many interneurons inserted between the afferent and efferent limbs

mcqs.explanation: Golgi tendon reflex (Inverse myotatic/Inverse stretch reflex ) is disynaptic , is the opposite , or inverse, of the stretch reflex . When tension on the muscle —and therefore on the tendon—becomes extreme , the inhibitory effect from the golgi tendon organ can be so great that it leads instantaneous relaxation of the entire muscle . This effect is called the lengthening reaction; it is probably a protective mechanism to prevent tearing of the muscle or avulsion of the tendon from its attachments to the bone.275

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: All of the following are true about withdrawal reflex except ______

options.a: Diverging circuits to spread the reflex to the necessary muscles for withdrawal are present
options.b: Circuits to inhibit the antagonist muscles , called reciprocal inhibition circuits are present
options.c: Circuits to cause afterdischarge that lasts many fractions of a second after the stimulus is over are present
options.d: The pathways for eliciting the flexor withdrawal reflex pass directly to the anterior motor neurons making it a monosynaptic reflex

mcqs.explanation: The pathways for eliciting the flexor withdrawal reflex do not pass directly to the anterior motor neurons; instead , they first pass into the spinal cord interneuron pool of neurons and only secondarily to the motor neurons. The shortest possible circuit is a three - or four-neuron pathway. The following basic types of circuits are present : • Diverging circuits to spread the reflex to the necessary muscles for withdrawal ; • Circuits to inhibit the antagonist muscles , called reciprocal inhibition circuits; and • Circuits to cause after-discharge are present . They prolong the reflex contraction of the muscles that last many fractions of a second after the stimulus is over.276 The flexor reflex is organized to withdraw a pained or otherwise irritated part of the body from a stimulus . Further, because of after-discharge , the reflex can hold the irritated part away from the stimulus for 0.1 to 3 seconds after the irritation is over. During this time, other reflexes and actions of the central nervous system can move the entire body away from the painful stimulus .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Muscle tone is maintained by_____
mcqs.explanation: The resistance of a muscle to stretch is often referred to as its tone or tonus and muscle spindle helps to control basic muscle tone. The tonic (static) stretch reflex circuit includes both group Ia and group II afferent fibers from muscle spindles . Normally, there is ongoing activity in the Ia and II afferents that helps maintain a baseline firing of �o motor neurons; therefore , the tonic stretch reflex contributes to muscle tone.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true during initiation of voluntary movements?

options.a: \022 �o motor neurons are activated followed by \025 motor neuron
options.b: \022 \025 motor neurons are activated followed by �o motor neuron
options.c: Both �o and \037 motor neurons are activated together

mcqs.explanation: The cell bodies of �o and \025 motor neurons to a given muscle lie close together . Both types are activated by interneurons in their immediate vicinity and sometimes directly by neurons of the descending pathways . During many voluntary and involuntary movements, they are coactivated , i.e., they are excited at almost the same time. (�o -\037 coactivation) The purpose of �o -\037 coactivation: • First, it keeps the length of the receptor portion of the muscle spindle from changing during the course of the whole muscle contraction. Hence , the muscle contraction is not opposed by the stretch reflex . • Second , if the muscle spindle did not contract and relax along with the large muscle fibers, the receptor portion of the spindle would sometimes be flail and sometimes be overstretched . Coactivation thus ensures that information about muscle length will be continuously available to provide for adjustment during ongoing actions and to plan and program future movements.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Righting reflex is____
mcqs.explanation: Righting reflexes operate to maintain the normal standing position and keep an animal's head upright. These reflexes are a series of responses integrated for the most part in the nuclei of the midbrain .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: In a patient with decerebrate rigidity, on applying pressure on the footpad , extension of that limb occurs. Which of the following statements is false regarding this phenomenon ?

options.b: It is integrated at the Spinal Level
options.c: It helps to prevent falling on that side
options.d: It is a righting reflex integrated at midbrain level

mcqs.explanation: Pressure on the footpad of a decerebrate patient causes the limb to extend against the pressure applied to the foot . This reflex is called the positive supportive reaction and is a righting reflex integrated at the spinal level .277 Pressure on one side causes extension in that direction (e.g., on applying pressure on the right footpad , extension of the right lower limb occurs), an effect called the magnet reaction. It is seen in infants and following spinal transection. From an evolutionary perspective , this reflex helps to prevent falling on the side where the stimulus is given.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Pyramids are formed by____
mcqs.explanation: The corticospinal pathways are also called the pyramidal tracts or pyramidal system because of their triangular shape as they pass along the ventral surface of the medulla oblongata.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about corticospinal tract?
mcqs.explanation: The corticospinal tract contains crossed fibers (majority). Fibers of the corticospinal tract originate from the primary motor cortex (about 30%), the premotor and supplementary motor areas (30%), and the somatosensory areas posterior to the central sulcus (40%). Most fibers (80% fibers) decussate (cross) in the medullary pyramids and descend in the lateral white matter of the spinal cord to form the lateral corticospinal tract. They control the movements of the contralateral limbs. The remaining 20 % make up the ventral corticospinal tract. These fibers remain uncrossed until reaching the spinal cord where axons terminate bilaterally on spinal interneurons antecedent to motor neurons. These fibers control the movements of the axial musculature .278

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding the origin of corticospinal tract?

options.a: Corticospinal tract fibers originate from Betz Cells
options.b: 30% from premotor and supplementary motor areas

mcqs.explanation: 30% of corticospinal tract originates about from the primary motor cortex, not 90%. 30 % from the premotor and supplementary motor areas. 40 % from the somatosensory areas posterior to the central sulcus . Betz cells • Some large myelinated fibres in the corticospinal tract originate from giant pyramidal cells , also known as Betz cells . • Found in the layer 5 of primary motor cortex. • These large fibers represent only 3 percent of the total fibers of the corticospinal tract. (The other 97 percent less than 4 micrometers in diameter that conduct background tonic signals to the motor areas of the cord.)279

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an extrapyramidal tract?
mcqs.explanation: Corticospinal tract is a pyramidal tract . Pyramidal tracts (corticospinal and corticobulbar) pass through the medullary pyramids. All others are extrapyramidal tracts and originate primarily in the the brain stem .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which pathway is not involved in maintainence of posture ?
mcqs.explanation: Rubrospinal tract is not involved in posture maintenance. Medial motor system • Controls the axial muscles (muscles of the trunk) • Axial muscles are concerned with postural adjustments and gross movements Lateral motor system • Controls the distal muscles • Distal muscles mediate fine, skilled movements280

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Gamma motor neurons are mainly influenced by _____
