mcqs.question: The duration of atrial diastole is _____
mcqs.explanation: The duration of atrial diastole is 0.7 sec .Cardiac Cycle Even ts Systole ( s) Diastole ( s) Total ( s) Ventricles 0.3 0.5 0.8 Atria 0.1 0.7 0.8

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The indication of the end of the isovolumetric relaxation phase is when ____

options.a: Ventricular pressure raise above atrial pressure
options.b: Ventricular pressure falls below atrial pressure
options.c: Ventricular pressure falls below aortic pressure
options.d: ventricular pressure rises above aortic pressure

mcqs.explanation: The indication of the end of the isovolumetric relaxation phase is when ventricular pressure falls below atrial pressure . Events of the Cardiac Cycle Diastole • Protodiastole Before the semilunar valve closes , even though ventricular muscle is relaxed , blood flow into great vessels is due to momentum of blood. • Iso-volumetric Relaxation The ventricular muscle continues to relax, even though the ventricular volume does not change, with all valves closed . • Ventricular Filling Isovolumetric relaxation ends when the ventricular pressure falls below the atrial pressure and the AV valves open , permitting the ventricles to fill. • Atrial Systole During the last third of diastole , the atria contract and give additional thrust to the inflow of blood into the ventricles. It correlates with 'a' wave in JVP . Systole • Isovolumetric Contraction509 The ventricular muscle continues to contract, even though the ventricular volume does not change, with all valves closed . It correlates with the 'c' wave of JVP . • Ventricular Ejection When the ventricular pressures rise above aortic and pulmonary pressures the valves open , and ventricular ejection begins . Peak pressures in the left and right ventricles are about 120 and 25 mmHg, respectively .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: During the cardiac cycle , the opening of the aortic valve takes place at the ______
mcqs.explanation: Opening of the aortic valve takes place at the end of the isovolumetric contraction. When the ventricular pressures rise above aortic and pulmonary pressures the semilunar valves (aortic and pulmonary valves) open , and ventricular ejection begins .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The effect of increased heart rate on cardiac cycle is that it____.

options.a: Decrease the duration of systole and diastole .
options.b: Increase the duration of systole and diastole .
options.c: Decrease the duration of systole more than diastole .
options.d: Decrease the duration of diastole more than systole .

mcqs.explanation: The effect of increased heart rate on cardiac cycle is that it decreases the duration of diastole more than systole . The duration of systole is much more fixed than that of diastole , so when the heart rate is increased , diastole is shortened to a much greater degree . Coronary blood flow and ventricular filling occur in diastole .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Electromechanical systole is the time interval between _______

options.c: R wave and first heart sound
options.d: Q wave and second heart sound

mcqs.explanation: 510 Electromechanical systole is the time interval between Q wave and second heart sound. To record this both ECG and phonocardiography are required.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The pressure -volume curve is shifted to the left in:
mcqs.explanation: The pressure -volume curve is shifted to the left in Mitral stenosis . The PV loop is shifted to the right when there is volume overload (increased EDV). The PV loop is shifted to the left in case of increased contractility or decreased compliance (decreased EDV). Effect of Valvular Diseases on PV loop : • Mitral stenosis : Left and down. • Mitral regurgitation : Width increased and height decreased . • Aortic stenosis : Tall with steep slope . • Aortic regurgitation : Right and tall.511

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Dicrotic notch is caused by _________
mcqs.explanation: Dicrotic notch is caused by closing of aortic valve. The dicrotic notch, a small oscillation in the falling phase of the pulse wave caused by vibrations set up when the aortic valve shuts .512

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: First heart sound and second heart sound are respectively due to ________

options.a: Opening of semilunar and atrioventricular valves
options.b: Closure of semilunar and atrioventricular valves
options.c: Closure of atrioventricular and semilunar valves
options.d: Opening of atrioventricular and semilunar valves

mcqs.explanation: First heart sound and second heart sound are respectively due to closure of atrioventricular (AV ) and semilunar valves.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The fourth heart sound is caused by:

options.a: Closure of aortic and pulmonary valves
options.b: Vibrations in the ventricular wall during systole
options.d: Closure of mitral and tricuspid valves

mcqs.explanation: The fourth heart sound is caused by ventricular filling. A fourth sound is heard immediately before the first sound when atrial pressure is high or the ventricle is stiff in conditions such as ventricular hypertrophy . It is due to ventricular filling and is rarely heard in normal adults .513

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: "a" wave on JVP is for
mcqs.explanation: "a" wave in JVP represents atrial contraction. Waves of JVP : • a- atrial systole pushing the blood to the ventricles. • c- isovolumetric contraction of ventricles causing the tricuspid valve to bulge . • x'- fall in atrial pressure during ventricular systole due to pull of valve leaflets . • v- venous filling which creates an increase in atrial pressure . • y- passive filling of ventricles by a passive flow of the blood from the right atrium.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: 'c' wave in JVP is seen in

options.b: Slow filling at end of diastole

mcqs.explanation: 'c' waves are produced by bulging of the tricuspid valve into the right atrium during the Iso-volumetric contraction of the right ventricle.514

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The x descent in jugular venous pressure corresponds to _______ phase of the cardiac cycle .
mcqs.explanation: The x descent in jugular venous pressure corresponds to the ventricular systole of the cardiac cycle . The jugular venous pulse • The waves in JVP reflect the pressure changes in the right atrium. • The internal jugular vein is preferred because the external jugular vein is valved and not directly in line with the superior vena cava and right atrium.• a wave: Corresponds to right atrial contraction. • c wave: Corresponds to the bulging of the tricuspid valve into the right atrium during isovolumetric ventricular contraction.515 • x descent : Corresponds to the atrial relaxation as the ventricular systole pulls the tricuspid valve during ejection. • v wave: Corresponds to the venous filling of the right atrium against a closed tricuspid valve. • y descent : Corresponds to fall in right atrial pressure during passive emptying of the right atrium into the right ventricle.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: C wave of JVP represents :

options.a: Tricuspid bulge into right atrium during isovolumetric ventricular contraction

mcqs.explanation: 'C' wave in JVP represents tricuspid bulge into right atrium during isovolumetric ventricular contraction. Characteristics of JVP : • a wave corresponds to atrial systole which causes regurgitation of some blood into the great veins. • c wave occurs due to the increase in atrial pressure caused by bulging of the tricuspid valve into the right atrium during isovolumetric ventricular contraction. • x descent occurs due to the fall in atrial pressure during ventricular systole due to pulling of valve leaflets. • v wave is seen at the end of ventricular contraction and occurs due to the slow venous filling which causes an increase in atrial pressure. • y descent occurs due to the passive emptying of the right atrium into the right ventricle.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Reflex responsible for tachycardia during right atrial distension is:
mcqs.explanation: Reflex responsible for tachycardia during right atrial distension is Bainbridge reflex .516 Atrial Reflex Control of Heart Rate: The Bainbridge Reflex • The stretch receptors of the atria that elicit the Bainbridge reflex transmit their afferent signals through the vagus nerves to the medulla of the brain . • Then efferent signals are transmitted back through vagal and sympathetic nerves to increase heart rate and strength of heart contraction. Bezold-Jarisch Reflex : • Activation of chemosensitive vagal C fibres in the cardiopulmonary region (e.g. Juxta capillary region of alveoli, ventricles, atria, great veins, and pulmonary artery) causes profound brady- cardia, hypotension and a brief period of apnea followed by rapid shallow breathing. Cushing Reflex : • When ICP is increased , the blood supply to RVLM neurons is compromised . • The local hypoxia and hypercapnia causes an increase in discharge from the neurons, producing hypertension, bradycardia and irregular respiration. • The resultant rise in systemic arterial pressure tends to restore the blood flow to the medulla .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Arrange the following events in the sequence in which they occur, after 'p wave' in ECG:
mcqs.explanation: The correct sequence of events that occur after the p-wave is 1-2-4-3, ie:- a wave in JVP \032 First heart sound \032 T wave in ECG \032 Rapid filling of ventricles. The sequence of the events in this question can be better understood with the following diagram:• The p wave in the ECG represents atrial depolarization, which causes contraction of the atria, represented by the 'a' wave in the JVP . Atrial contraction causes final filling of the ventricles (fourth phase of ventricular diastole )517 • Atrial contraction is followed by the closure of the mitral valve, which causes the first-heart sound. • This is followed by the isovolumetric contraction of the ventricle, which causes c wave in JVP , due to bulging of the tricuspid valve. This is followed by the rapid ejection phase of the ventricle. • The T wave of ECG occurs during ventricular repolarization, which is followed by the opening of the mitral valve, followed by rapid filling phase of the ventricle (second phase of ventricular diastole ). Note : Passive rapid filling occurs as the mitral valve opens just before atrial contraction occurs.

mcqs.explanation: Cardiac output is increased in pregnancy. mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The SA Node acts as the pacemaker of the heart because , it ____.
mcqs.explanation: The SA node acts as the pacemaker of the heart as it generates impulses at the highest rate (60-100 /min), compared to AV node (40-60/min) and Purkinje fibres (15-40). The impulses generated by SA node are conducted through AV node and purkinje fibres repetedly that it will prevent AV node or Purkinje fibres reach their own thresholds for self -excitation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: In which of the following the conduction velocity is least ?
mcqs.explanation: The conduction velocity is least in AV node.525 The slow conduction in the AV node is caused mainly by diminished numbers of gap junctions between successive cells in the conducting pathways .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The velocity of conduction of impulse is maximum in____.
mcqs.explanation: The velocity of conduction of impulse is maximum in Purkinje fibers. Purkinje fibers have the maximum number of gap junctions hence the maximum conduction velocity (4m/s).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The AV nodal delay is ___(seconds ).
mcqs.explanation: The AV nodal delay is 0.1 second . The slow conduction is caused mainly by diminished numbers of gap junctions between successive cells in the conducting pathways .It ensures that the atria have ejected their blood into the ventricles first before the ventricles contract.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: If the SA node discharges at 0.00 sec , when will the action potential normally arrive at the epicardial surface at the base of the left ventricle?
mcqs.explanation: The duration of action potential to arrive at the epicardial surface at the base of the left ventricle is 0.22sec. Impulse initiated from SA node at 0.00s \023 Impulse reaches AV node at 0.03s \023 Delay of impulse at AV node by 0.13s resulting in a total time of 0.16s (0.03 +0.13 ) to reach the beginning of Purkinje fibres \023 Impulse reaches base of Purkinje fibres by 0.03s resulting in a total of time of 0.19s (0.16+0.0.3) to reach the endocardial surface of the base of the ventricle \023 Impulse travels from endocardial to epicardial surface in 0.03s (due to arrangement of myocardial fibres) \023 Hence , a total time of 0.22s (0.19+0.03) is taken for the impulse to travel from SA node to epicardial surface of the base of ventricles526

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The order of depolarization after stimulation of Purkinje fibers is:
mcqs.explanation: The order of depolarization is from septum \032 endocardium\032 epicardium . The spread of Cardiac Excitation: Atrial depolarization is initiated from SA node spreads radially through atria, then converges on the AV node. A delay of about 0.1s (AV nodal delay ) occurs before excitation spreads to the ventricles. Ventricular depolarization starts at the left side of the interventricular septum and moves first to the right across the midportion of the septum . It moves along the ventricular walls to the AV groove, proceeding from the endocardial to the epicardial surface .527

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Phases of the ventricular muscle action potential are shown below . At which phase of the below image, the action potential is most dependant on sodium permeability ?
mcqs.explanation: The action potential is most dependant on sodium permeability in phase 0. Action potential of myocardium: • Phase 0: Depolarisation : Influx of Na+ into myocyte . • Phase 1: Early repolarization: Efflux of K+ from myocyte . • Phase 2: Plateau : Ca2+ enters myocardial cells via voltage regulated L-type Ca2+ channels. • Phase 3: Repolarisation: Efflux of K+. • Phase 4: Restoration of RMP: Restoration of Na+ and K+ by Na-K ATPase.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Plateau phase of ventricular muscle is due to opening of :
mcqs.explanation: Plateau phase of ventricular muscle is due to opening of Ca channel. Action potential of myocardium: • Phase 0: Depolarisation : Influx of Na+ into myocyte . • Phase 1: Early repolarization: Efflux of K+ from myocyte . • Phase 2: Plateau : Ca2+ enters myocardial cells via voltage regulated L-type Ca2+ channels. • Phase 3: Repolarisation: Efflux of K+. • Phase 4: Restoration of RMP: Restoration of Na+ and K+ by Na-K ATPase.528

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Repolarization of cardiac muscle proceeds from:
mcqs.explanation: Repolarization of cardiac muscle proceeds from epicardium to endocardium. Depolarisation proceeds from endocardium to epicardium in an intact cardiac muscle .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Phase 0 of pacemaker potential is initiated by:

options.b: Opening of voltage gated Ca2+ channel
options.c: Inactivation of voltage gated Ca2+ channel
options.d: Inactivation of voltage gated Na+ channel

mcqs.explanation: Phase 0 of pacemaker potential is initiated by opening of voltage -gated Ca2+ channels. The pacemaker potential consists of: • Phase 0 - this is upstroke seen due to the opening of voltage -gated Ca2+ channels. This causes an influx of calcium leading to the upstroke . • Phase 3 - This is followed by inactivation of the calcium channels and simultaneous activation of K+ channels. This leads to efflux of K+ bringing about repolarization. • Phase 4- As the K+ efflux declines , a channel permeable to both Na+ and K+ opens leading to an influx of both Na+ and K+. This is the If channel. This is responsible for slow spontaneous diastolic depolarization. This accounts for the automaticity of SA and AV node. The slope of Phase 4 in the SA node determines the heart rate. Note : Fast voltage -gated Na+ channels seen in myocyte potential are permanently inactivated because of the less negative resting potential of the pacemaker cells .529

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: You are researching the benefits of vagus nerve stimulation as a potential treatment for epilepsy . Which of the following parameters can be increased due to vagal stimulation?
mcqs.explanation: Vagal stimulation can cause an increase in the R-R interval in the ECG as it decreases heart rate.

mcqs.explanation: Einthoven's law states Lead I + Lead III = Lead II . Einthoven's triangle is an imaginary formation of three limb leads in a triangle used in electrocardiography .

mcqs.question: In Einthoven's triangle, what is the value of lead III when lead I = 1mV and lead II = 2mV ?
mcqs.explanation: According to Einthoven's law, Lead I + Lead III =Lead II . Lead III = Lead II – Lead I = (2-1) =1 mV .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: In a standard ECG, an augmented limb lead measures the electrical potential difference between :
mcqs.explanation: 531 In a standard ECG, an augmented lead measures the electrical potential difference between one limb and the other two limbs. aVR , aVL , aVF are the augmented limb leads .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which part of the ECG corresponds to ventricular repolarization?
mcqs.explanation: The part of the ECG that corresponds to ventricular repolarization is T wave.ECG wav es Events in the heart P wave Atrial depolarization QRS com plex Ventricular depolarization T wave Ventricular repolarization U wave Repolarization of ventricular myocytes with long action po tential532

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The PR interval indicates ____.
mcqs.explanation: The PR interval indicates atrial depolarisation(P wave) and AV node conduction time(PR segment ). PR interval is the time between the beginning of the P wave and the beginning of the QRS complex . It is the interval between the beginning of electrical excitation of the atria and the beginning of excitation of the ventricles. Normal duration is 0.12 -0.20s .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The P wave is absent in ___.
mcqs.explanation: The P wave is absent in atrial fibrillation.533 In atrial fibrillation, numerous small depolarization waves spread in all directions through the atria. The waves are weak and many of them are of opposite polarity at any given time, they almost electrically neutralize one another. Therefore, P waves are absent from ECG in atrial fibrillation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The normal mean QRS axis lies between ______
mcqs.explanation: The normal mean QRS axis lies between –30\260 and +110 \260. The QRS axis represents the major vector of ventricular activation, which is the overall direction of electrical activity.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The sympathetic innervation to AV node is by___.
mcqs.explanation: The sympathetic innervation to AV node is by Left stellate ganglion. Innervation of SA Node and AV Node : The SA node develops from structures on the right side of the embryo and the AV node from structures on the left .Therefore -ANS SA node AV node Parasympath etic Right vagus Left vagus Sympathetic Right stellate ganglion Left stellate ganglion534

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: You are following up with a patient on a sympathomimetic drug. Which of the following effects is unlikely to be due to sympathetic stimulation?
mcqs.explanation: Sympathetic stimulation causes faster conduction , therefore decreased refractory period . Effects of sympathetic stimulation: • Chronotropic- It increases the rate of sinus nodal discharge . • Dromotropic- It increases the rate of conduction . • Bathmotropic- It increases the level of excitability in all portions of the heart. • Inotropic- It increases the force of contraction of all the cardiac musculature .

mcqs.question: The AH interval on His Bundle Electrocardiogram (HBE) corresponds to the conduction of _____ on ECG.
