mcqs.question: Which of the following does not form filtration barrier ?
mcqs.explanation: Mesangium does not form a filtration barrier . It is made up of mesangial cells , supporting glomerular capillaries . The filtration barrier consists of: • Endothelium of the capillary • Basement membrane: • Lamina densa - electron -dense layer. It contains type IV collagen • Lamina rara interna - contains glycosaminoglycan heparan sulfate which has a negative charge • Lamina rara externa - contains glycosaminoglycan heparan sulfate which has a negative charge • Layer of epithelial cells (podocytes ) surrounding the outer surface of the capillary basement membrane636 A. mcqs.question: Two particles share the same diameter . The one which will pass through the glomerular membrane has ______

options.d: Filtration across GBM does not depend on charge

mcqs.explanation: For any given molecular radius, positively charged molecules are filtered much more readily than are negatively charged molecules . This is because the sialoproteins in the glomerular capillary wall are negatively charged , and this negative charge repels the negatively charged substances in the blood. Studies have showed that for tracer molecules presumed to be of similar size, charges which are filtered are positive charge > neutral charge > negative charge.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: What size of neutral substances are permitted by the filtration barriers ?
mcqs.explanation: Filtration barriers permit neutral substances that have the size of 4-8 nm. Neutral substances with diameters : • <4 nm - freely filtered • >8 nm - not filtered • Between 4-8 nm - the permeability is inversely proportional to the diameter Clinical correlation: • Genetically abnormal basement membranes: Alport's syndrome (�o 3 and �o 4 chains on the long arm of chromosome 2 involved in autosomal dominant and recessive pattern; �o 5 chain on X637 chromosome involved in X-linked inheritance) • Autoimmune response to basement membrane collagen IV (�o 3 NC1 domain): Goodpasture 's syndrome

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a part of the juxtaglomerular apparatus?
mcqs.explanation: Glomerular mesangial cells are not a part of the juxtaglomerular apparatus. Juxtaglomerular apparatus contains: • Macula densa: Specialized cells at the end of the thick ascending limb of Henle forms the macula densa. They detect sodium concentration of the fluid in the tubule (Chemoreceptor ). In response to elevated sodium, the macula densa cells trigger contraction of the afferent arteriole, reducing flow of blood to the glomerulus and the glomerular filtration rate. • Lacis cells : Extraglomerular mesangial cells situated between afferent and efferent arteriole. • Granular cells /JG cells : Modified smooth muscle cells of the afferent arteriole, that secrete renin. Fall in pressure in afferent arteriole stimulates renin release (mechanoreceptor ), which, in turn, increases blood pressure . Note : The distal convoluted tubule starts at the macula densa.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: In patients with renal diseases , albumin is the first to appear in the urine. What is the reason behind this?
mcqs.explanation: In renal diseases , albumin is the first to appear because of its effective molecular diameter . In minimal change nephropathy , the negative charges on the basement membrane are lost even before there are noticeable changes in kidney histology . As a result of this loss of negative charges on the basement membranes, some of the lower molecular weight proteins , especially albumin (effective molecular diameter of 7 nm), are filtered and appear in the urine, a condition known as638 proteinuria or albuminuria.

mcqs.question: What is the effect of sympathetic stimulation on GFR?
mcqs.explanation: GFR decreases with sympathetic stimulation as there is afferent arteriolar constriction. Strong activation of the renal sympathetic nerves constrict the afferent and efferent renal arterioles through the �o 1 receptors . As the afferent areterioles have far more �o 1 receptors than the efferent , it results in decreased renal blood flow and GFR.642

mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: If a patient is on a high protein diet , what will be the effect on the GFR?
mcqs.explanation: High protein intake increases GFR.Note : Increase in the plasma protein concentration is not the same as high protein intake. An increase in the plasma protein concentration decreases GFR due to a raised oncotic pressure . A high protein intake raises the amino acid concentration in the blood, not the plasma protein concentration.

mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: Which of the following would cause an increase in both GFR and RPF?
mcqs.explanation: Dilation of the afferent arteriole will increase both GFR and RPF. • Increase renal plasma flow (RPF) - because renal vascular resistance is decreased • Increase glomerular filtration rate (GFR) - because glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure is increased . • Filtration fraction (FF) remains normal Dilation of the efferent arteriole will increase RPF but decrease GFR.

mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: Which of the following causes relaxation of the mesangial cells ?
mcqs.explanation: cAMP causes relaxation of the mesangial cells . The other agents mentioned in the options cause contraction of the mesangial cells . Agents causing relaxation of mesangial cells (mnemonic - DAnCE)643 • Dopamine • ANP • cAMP • PGE2 Angiotensin II is an important regulator of mesangial contraction, and there are angiotensin II receptors in the glomeruli .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: What is the effect of prostaglandins on renal blood flow ?

options.a: Increase blood flow to cortex and medulla
options.b: Increase blood flow to cortex and decrease blood flow to medulla
options.c: Decrease blood flow to cortex and increase blood flow to medulla
options.d: Decrease blood flow to cortex as well as medulla

mcqs.explanation: Prostaglandins increase blood flow in the renal cortex and decrease blood flow in the renal medulla . PGE2 is partially responsible for the vasodilatation of the afferent arteriole, which increases blood flow to the glomerulus . This phenomenon describes why NSAIDs (which inhibit prostaglandin synthesis ) result in afferent arteriole vasoconstriction. It can cause a reduced GFR in patients who rely heavily on prostaglandin synthesis to maintain renal blood flow .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: Which part of the proximal tubule is most susceptible to ischemic injury?
mcqs.explanation: Regions of the kidney most prone to ischemic injury are the S3 segment of the proximal tubule and the medullary thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle (mTAL ). These tubular areas exist physiologically in relatively lower oxygen conditions. The S3 segment , in particular, has a much lower capability of producing energy through glycolysis under anaerobic conditions than the mTAL . Based on the ultrastructure proximal tubule is divided into three segments : • S1 segment : 1st half of PCT • S2 segment : 2nd half of PCT and 1st half of proximal straight tubule • S3 segment : 2nd half of proximal straight tubule644

mcqs.question: What is the effective renal plasma flow ?
mcqs.explanation: In humans, the effective renal plasma flow (eRPF) averages about 625 mL /min. Measurement of renal plasma flow (RPF) is done by measuring the clearance of para -aminohippuric acid (PAH). PAH is filtered and secreted by the renal tubules , hence it it can be used for RPF measurement .where : • RPF = renal plasma flow (mL /min or mL /24 hour) • CPAH = clearance of PAH (mL /min or mL /24 hourr) • UPAH = urine concentration of PAH (mg/mL )645 • V = urine flow rate (mL/min or mL /24 hour) • PPAH = plasma concentration of PAH (mg/mL ) Note : Renal blood flow = Renal plasma flow / 1- Hematocrit

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: Which of the following formulae is correct?
mcqs.explanation: True renal plasma flow (RPF) is obtained by dividing effective renal plasma flow (ERPF) by extraction ratio.When we inject para-aminohippuric acid, 90% of it is filtered through the glomerulus at the rate of 625mL per minute - which is the effective renal plasma flow (ERPF). Using that, to we calculate the true RPF, we divide it by the extraction ratio to account for the 10 % that is not filtered by dividing the ERPF by 0.9, hence getting the final value of ~ 700mL per minute When peripheral venous plasma concentration of PAH is used for calculation of RPF, RPF obtained is called effective renal plasma flow (ERPF). This is because PAH concentration is essentially identical to that in the arterial plasma reaching the kidney.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: In a patient with renal disease , you want to measure the filtration fraction. Which of the following substances will you use ?
mcqs.explanation: Inulin and PAHA are used to determine the filtration fraction. The filtration fraction is the ratio of GFR and RPF Inulin, a polymer of fructose can be used to measure GFR. Para -aminohippuric acid (PAHA) is used to measure RPF.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: According to myogenic hypothesis of renal autoregulation the afferent arterioles contract in response to stretch -induced by______
mcqs.explanation: 646 The afferent arterioles contract in response to stretch induced by the opening of calcium channels. The mechanism is called myogenic autoregulation of renal blood flow and GFR. The stretch of the vascular wall allows increased movement of calcium ions from the extracellular fluid into the cells , causing them to contract. This contraction prevents excessive stretch of the vessel . This prevents excessive increase of renal blood flow and GFR by raising vascular resistance . This mechanism may be more important in protecting the kidney from hypertension -induced injury. Autoregulation has two main mechanisms: • Metabolic mechanism: Tissues produce vasodilatory metabolites that regulate flow e.g. prostaglandins, NO, CO2, H+ and K+ • Myogenic mechanism

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: Tubuloglomerular feedback is mediated by the sensing of_____

options.a: Increased Na + concentration in thick ascending loop of Henle
options.b: Increased Cl - concentration in thick ascending loop of Henle
options.c: Increased Na + concentration in macula densa
options.d: Increased Cl- concentration in macula densa

mcqs.explanation: Tubuloglomerular feedback is mediated by the sensing of increased Na+ concentration in macula densa. Macula densa are the specialized cells present at the distal end of the thick ascending loop of Henle where it reaches the glomerulus. Distal convoluted tubule starts from macula densa. Macula forms part of the juxtaglomerular apparatus. While both Na+ and Cl- are delivered to the macula densa cells , it is the increased concentration of Na+ in the cells that increases the Na+-K ATPase activity leading to the feedback .647

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: Renal autoregulation is absent in which of the following cases ?
mcqs.explanation: Renal autoregulation is absent in case of paralysis of vascular smooth muscle . Paralysis of vascular smooth muscles abolishes its action i.e., autoregulation of renal blood flow and GFR. Vascular smooth muscles act through myogenic mechanism of renal autoregulation . Paralysis of vascular smooth muscles can be brought about by administration of drugs. Renal autoregulation is present in denervated and in isolated , perfused kidneys. Feedback mechanisms intrinsic to the kidneys keep the renal blood flow and GFR relatively constant, despite marked changes in arterial blood pressure . This relative constancy of GFR and renal blood flow is referred to as autoregulation .648

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: Kidney responds to shock by _______.
mcqs.explanation: Kidney responds to shock by increasing afferent arteriolar resistance . During shock, both afferent and efferent arterioles in kidney are constricted , however, the efferent vessels are constricted much more. The glomerular filtration rate and the plasma renal flow is decreased during shock. As plasma renal flow is decreased to a greater extent , the filtration fraction increases. (Option 1 & 3)

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: What is the function of tubuloglomerular feedback ?
mcqs.explanation: Tubuloglomerular feedback regulates glomerular filtration rate (GFR). As the rate of \037ow through the ascending limb of the loop of Henle and first part of the distal tubule increases, glomerular filtration in the same nephron decreases , and, conversely, a decrease in \037ow increases the GFR.

Reabsorption and secretion happen between the tubular lumen of the nephron and the peritubular capillaries and not the efferent arteriole.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: The protein in the glomerular basement membrane responsible for charge-dependent filtration is?
mcqs.explanation: The protein in the glomerular basement membrane responsible for charge-dependent filtration is heparan sulfate . It prevents filtration by repelling negatively charged proteins . Collagen type IV , fibronectin, entactin are structural components of basement membrane.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: Efferent arteriolar constriction causes all except :

options.c: Decreases oncotic pressure in glomerular capillaries
options.d: Increases hydrostatic pressure in glomerular capillaries

mcqs.explanation: Efferent arteriolar constriction increases oncotic pressure in glomerular capillaries . Efferent arteriolar constriction has a biphasic response on GFR depending on the severity of resistance .649 Moderate efferent arteriolar constriction causes increased glomerular hydrostatic pressure and slightly increased GFR. However, in cases of severe efferent arteriolar constriction (more than threefold increase in efferent arteriolar resistance ), the renal blood flow is significantly reduced . This results in increased plasma protein concentration, thereby increasing the glomerular colloid oncotic pressure . As the increase in colloid oncotic pressure exceeds the increase in hydrostatic pressure , the net force for filtration decreases , resulting in decreased GFR.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: GFR is increased by all except
mcqs.explanation: Ureteric stone causes a reduction in glomerular filtration rate (GFR). Following ureteral obstruction, there is a progressive fall in glomerular filtration rate (GFR) due to a reduction in a single -nephron glomerular filtration rate (SNGFR) and a reduced number of filtering nephrons. All the other factors/options increase GFR.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Glomerular Filtration Rate, Renal Blood Flow, a...
mcqs.question: This is the graph depicting the filterability of dextran through the kidney, 1 representing complete filtration and 0 representing no filtration. Choose the substance A, B, C respectively .
mcqs.explanation: In the given graph, the order of filterability is A>B>C, which likely indicates that the substances are Polycationic, Neutral , Polyanionic. The glomerular filtration barrier is negatively charged , which will repel most of the negative charged (anionic substances ). Whereas, the cationic substances are easily filtered . Hence , the order of filterability would be: Polycationic > Neutral > Polyanionic, represented by A, B, and C in the graph shown. The glomerular filtration barrier consists of:650 • Endothelium of the capillary • Basement membrane: • Lamina densa - electron -dense layer. It contains type IV collagen • Lamina rara interna - contains glycosaminoglycan heparan sulfate which has a negative charge • Lamina rara externa - contains glycosaminoglycan heparan sulfate which has a negative charge • Layer of epithelial cells (podocytes ) surrounding the outer surface of the capillary basement membrane The capillary endothelium is perforated by thousands of small holes called fenestrae , which measure from 4 nm up to 8nm. Therefore, neutral substances with molecular diameters of less than 4 nm are freely filtered , and filtration of those with diameters of more than 8 nm approaches zero. However, in addition to the size of the particles , the filtration also depends mainly on the charge of the particle being filtered . The glomerular capillary wall consists of highly negatively charged proteins called sialoproteins , which repel the negatively charged substances (anions). The property can be studied by using charged dextran. When the filtration of the negatively and positively charged dextrans was studied , the results indicated that the negatively charged dextrans in the blood are repelled , with the result that filtration of anionic substances 4 nm in diameter is less than half that of neutral substances of the same size. This explains, why albumin despite having an effective molecular diameter of approximately 7 nm, has a very low filtration rate.651

mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: What is implied if a drug has more renal clearance than GFR?

options.a: Drug is reabsorbed by the renal tubules
options.b: Drug is secreted in the renal tubules
options.c: Drug is excreted in renal tubules
options.d: Drug is neither excreted nor reabsorbed in renal tubules

mcqs.explanation: If drug has more renal clearance than GFR, then drug is secreted in renal tubules . Excretion rate= (filtration rate- reabsorption rate)+ secretion rate. The clearance of the substance : • Equals the GFR if there is no net tubular secretion or reabsorption. • Exceeds the GFR if there is net tubular secretion . • Less than the GFR if there is net tubular reabsorption.

mcqs.question: Choose the correct formula regarding renal physiology .
mcqs.explanation: The correct formula is Excretion rate = UV. • Filtration fraction = ( GFR / RPF ) * 100 = 20 % (or ) 0.2 (approx) • Filtration rate = GFR * Plasma concentration • Clearance = U*V/P Where,662 GFR = Glomerular filtration rate RPF = Renal plasma flow U = Concentration of the substance in urine V = Urine flow rate P = Concentration of the substance in plasma

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Choose the correct option.

options.a: Inulin is completely secreted and never reabsorbed .
options.b: Glucose is completely reabsorbed in DCT.
options.d: PAH at any plasma concentration is completely filtered and secreted .

mcqs.explanation: Creatinine is partially secreted and never reabsorbed . Clearance of creatinine (CCr) can also be used to determine GFR. Since creatinine is secreted by the tubules , the clearance of creatinine will be slightly higher than inulin. Hence , it overestimates GFR. Inulin is completely filtered and never reabsorbed . Hence , it can be used for GFR estimation. Glucose is completely reabsorbed below the renal threshold (i.e ~180mg/dl) in PCT. PAH(para amino hippuric acid) at low plasma concentrations is completely filtered and secreted . Hence , it can be used for estimation of renal blood flow .

mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Renal plasma flow is being calculated using PAH in a patient . The technician inadvertently uses PAH thrice the recommended dose . What will be the estimated effective renal plasma flow ?
mcqs.explanation: Effective renal plasma flow in this patient will be falsely low. It is equal to the clearance of para-aminohippurate (PAH) as shown by the following equation.Where, • ERPF = Effective Renal Plasma Flow • UPAH = [PAH] in urine663 • V = Urine flow rate • PPAH = [PAH] in plasma • CPAH = Clearance of PAH At high concentrations of PAH, as given in this question, tubular secretion attains saturation after which the clearance of PAH falls. Hence, a low ERPF will be seen .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Which of the following transporter is present in the ascending loop of Henle ?
mcqs.explanation: Thick ascending limb of loop of Henle has Na+ - 2Cl- - K+ co transporter that cotransports one Na+, one K+, and 2Cl– from the tubular lumen into the tubular cells . This is an example of secondary active transport. Na+ is transported out of the cell into the interstitium by Na, K ATPase in the basolateral membrane of the cell . Cl– exits in basolateral ClC–Kb Cl– channels. Barttin, a protein in the cell membrane, is essential for normal ClC–Kb function. K+ moves from the cell to the interstitium and the tubular lumen by ROMK(renal outer medullary potassium channel) and other K+ channels.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: The principal site of absorption of Na + is_____

options.c: Thick ascending limb of Loop of Henle

mcqs.explanation: The principal site of absorption of Na + is PCT. About 60-65% of filtered sodium is reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT), coupled with the movement of H+, glucose , amino acids, organic acids, phosphate , and other electrolytes and substances . All segments of nephron are involved in sodium reabsorption except thin descending loop of Henle .664 % of filtered Na reabsorbed Part of nephron Main transporter involved PCT Na+–H+exchanger Thick ascending limb of the l oop of Henle Na+–2Cl-–K cotransporter DCT Na–Cl cotransporter Collecting ducts ENaC channels (regulated by aldosterone to permit homeo static adjustments )

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Potassium is maximally absorbed in____
mcqs.explanation: Potassium is maximally absorbed in PCT. Potassium is freely filtered by the glomerulus . The bulk of filtered K+ is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule . In the proximal tubule, K+ absorption is primarily passive and proportional to Na+ and water through paracellular transport. K+ reabsorption in the thick ascending limb of Henle occurs through both transcellular (Na+- K+- 2Cl- cotransport) and paracellular pathways . K+ secretion begins in the early distal convoluted tubule and progressively increases along the distal nephron into the cortical collecting duct . Most urinary K+ can be accounted for by K+ secretion mediated by principal cells . Under conditions of K+ depletion , reabsorption of K+ occurs in the collecting duct . It is the only electrolyte to be reabsorbed as well as secreted .665

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Bicarbonate is reabsorbed across the luminal membrane with the help of ______
mcqs.explanation: Bicarbonate is reabsorbed at the luminal membrane in the form of CO2 and H2O with the help of Na+ - H+ exchanger. In the tubular cell of the PCT, CO2 and H2O recombine with the help of carbonic anhydrase II , and then dissociate into H+ and HCO3-. From here, the H+ moves back into the tubular lumen via the Na+ - H+ exchanger while the HCO3- is reabsorbed at the basolateral membrane via the Na+ - HCO3- co-transporter.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: True about renal tubular transport_____

options.c: H+ is absorbed in proximal tubule
options.d: Amino acid is reabsorbed in proximal tubule

mcqs.explanation: 666 Glucose and amino acids are completely reabsorbed in the proximal tubule . Option A: Maximum reabsorption occurs in proximal tubule Option B: Urea is reabsorbed and secreted . It is reabsorbed in PCT and in collecting duct . It is secreted in thin ascending loop of henle. Option C: H+ is secreted in PCT as well as in collecting ducts .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Which of the following occurs along with glucose transport into the cell ?
mcqs.explanation: Sodium symport occurs along with glucose transport into the cell . Sodium and glucose are co-transported across the luminal membrane of proximal tubular cells . This occurs via sodium glucose co-transporters (SGLT2 and SGLT1 ). The energy derived from the movement of Na+ is used to move glucose against its concentration gradient into the tubular cell . This is referred to as secondary active transport. The Na+ is then pumped out of the cell into the interstitium , and the glucose exits by facilitated diffusion via glucose transporter (GLUT)-2 along the basolateral membrane into the interstitial fluid . Clinical correlation: Fanconi-Bickel syndrome: Defective GLUT2 Isolated renal glycosuria : Defective SGLT2667

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Normal renal threshold (g/L) and transport maxima (mg/min) for glucose respectively are _______, _________
mcqs.explanation: The actual renal threshold is about 200 mg/dL (i.e., 2 g/L ) (1g/L=100mg /dl) and the transport maximum for glucose is 375 mg/min. For substances that are actively reabsorbed or secreted , there is a limit to the rate at which the solute can be transported , which is referred to as the transport maximum. This limit is due to saturation of the specific transport systems involved. Normally, measurable glucose does not appear in the urine because essentially all the filtered glucose is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule . The transport maximum for glucose is about 375 mg/min, whereas the filtered load of glucose is only about 125 mg/min. With large increases in GFR and/or plasma glucose concentration that increase the filtered load of glucose above 375 mg/min, the excess glucose filtered is not reabsorbed and passes into the urine. When the plasma glucose concentration is 100 mg/100 ml and the filtered load is at its normal level (125 mg/min) there is no loss of glucose in the urine. However, when the plasma concentration of glucose rises above about 200 mg/100 ml, increasing the filtered load to about 250 mg/min, a small amount of glucose begins to appear in the urine. This point is termed as the threshold for glucose . Splay is due to separation between filtered load and exceretion . It occurs due to different transport maximums of different nephrons.668

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: The image of PAH excretion is depicted below . Match the labellings .

options.a: a. Filtered , b. Excreted , c. Tm, d. Secreted
options.b: a. Filtered , b. Secreted , c. Tm, d. Excreted
options.c: a. Secreted , b. Filtered , c. Tm, d. Excreted
options.d: a. Excreted , b. Filtered , c. Tm, d. Secreted

mcqs.explanation: The labellings depticed are a. Filtered , b. Secreted , c. Tm, d. Excreted Filtered Load: The filtered load of PAH increases linearly as the unbound concentration of PAH increases (filtered load = GFR. [P]PAH). Secretion : At low concentrations of PAH, many carriers are available and secretion increases linearly as the plasma concentration increases. When the PAH concentration increases to a level where the carriers are saturated , Tm is reached . After this point, no matter how much the PAH concentration increases, there can be no further increase in the secretion rate. Excretion. For a secreted substance such as PAH, excretion is the sum of filtration and secretion . At low PAH concentrations (below Tm), excretion increases steeply with increases in plasma PAH concentration because both filtration and secretion are increasing. At PAH concentrations above Tm, excretion increases less steeply (and parallels the curve for filtration) because only the filtration component increases as concentration increases; secretion is already saturated .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: In a patient with uncontrolled diabetes , what is the value of plasma clearance of glucose ?
mcqs.explanation: In uncontrolled diabetes , the plasma clearance of glucose is greater than zero. Normally, all the glucose that is filtered is reabsorbed and no glucose is excreted in the urine. Hence , the clearance is zero. In uncontrolled diabetes , since the plasma glucose concentration is greater than the renal threshold for reabsorption, excess glucose is excreted in the urine and the clearance is greater than zero. Clearance of different substances can be shown in a graph as follows :669 The above graph depicts renal handling of glucose , inulin, and para-aminohippurate (PAH) and can be explained as follows : Glucose clearance: Normally, all the glucose that is filtered is reabsorbed and no glucose is excreted in the urine. Hence , the clearance is zero. In uncontrolled diabetes , since the plasma glucose concentration is greater than the renal threshold for reabsorption, excess glucose is excreted in the urine and the clearance is greater than zero. Inulin clearance: Inulin is freely filtered and is neither reabsorbed nor secreted . Hence , it is constant and equal to the glomerular filtration rate. PAH clearance: PAH is both filtered and secreted . When plasma PAH is low, clearance is high. However, as plasma PAH rises above the threshold level for PAH secretion , clearance falls progressively .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: A patient has a \037blood glucose level of 200 mg/dL and GFR of 90 ml/min. What is the amount of glucose excreted if the transport maximum of the patient is as shown below ?
mcqs.explanation: The amount of glucose excreted in the above scenario is 30 mg/min. Calculation: Step 1: Calculate total filtered glucose : In this question, • GFR = 90 ml/min • Plasma glucose concentration = 200 mg/dL= 2 mg/ml (1 dL=100 ml). • Total filtered glucose = GFR X Plasma glucose concentration. = 90 ml/min X 2 mg/ml = 180 mg/min. Step 2: Check transport maximum:670 In the above question transport maximum is 150 mg/min. Step 3: Calculate the excretion: Excretion = Total filtered glucose - Total reabsorbed glucose (Transport Maximum) = 180-150 mg/min = 30 mg/min

options.a: Concentration of glucose in tubular fluid is more than that of plasma
options.b: Concentration of urea in tubular fluid is more than that of plasma
options.c: Concentration of bicarbonate in tubular fluid is more than that of plasma
options.d: Concentration of sodium in tubular fluid is less than that of plasma

mcqs.explanation: The concentration of urea in tubular fluid is more than that of plasma.[TF/P]>1, when solute is reabsorbed less quickly than water or when solute is secreted . Ex- PAH, Creatinine, Inulin, Urea. [TF/P]=1, when solute and water are reabsorbed at the same rate Ex - Na. [TF/P]<1, when solute is reabsorbed more quickly than water. mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: The mechanism by which majority of water is reabsorbed in PCT is
mcqs.explanation: Water reabsorption in PCT mainly occurs by osmosis. The proximal tubule reabsorbs 67% of the filtered water. The driving force for water reabsorption is a transtubular osmotic gradient established by reabsorption of solutes .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: A dehydrated patient is excreting hypertonic urine. Absorption of water in which part of the nephron causes this?
mcqs.explanation: 671 Hypertonic urine is excreted due to absorption of water in collecting duct . The final concentration of urine is determined by the amount of water reabsorption that occurs in the collecting ducts . The changes in osmolarity of the urine (hypo/hypertonic ) depends on the amount of ADH (vasopressin) acting on the collecting ducts . The basic requirements for forming a concentrated urine (hypertonic urine) are • A high level of ADH, which increases the permeability of the distal tubules and collecting ducts to water, thereby allowing these tubular segments to avidly reabsorb water. • A high osmolarity of the renal medullary interstitial fluid , which provides the osmotic gradient necessary for water reabsorption to occur in the presence of high levels of ADH.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: A patient with diabetes insipidus is prescribed vasopressin. This drug has its maximum effect on which part of the renal tubule ?
mcqs.explanation: Vasopressin has the maximum effect on the collecting ducts . Vasopressin acts by inserting aquaporin 2 present in cytoplasmic vesicles of principal cells on to the apical membrane. The effect is mediated via the vasopressin V2 receptor , cyclic adenosine 5-monophosphate (cAMP), and protein kinase A. When vasopressin is absent, the collecting duct epithelium is relatively impermeable to water.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about free water clearance?
mcqs.explanation: Free water clearance is regulated by ADH. Free water clearance is defined as the amount of solute -free water generated by the kidneys, either when dilute urine or when concentrated urine is formed. Free -water clearance is positive , when excess water is being excreted (dilute urine).672 Free -water clearance is negative , when excess solutes are being removed and water is being conserved (concentrated urine).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: The following picture shows the composition of solute in the urine and plasma sample of 3 patients . Identify the true statement .

options.a: A shows negative free water clearance, B is isotonic, C is positive free water clearance
options.b: A shows positive free water clearance B is isotonic C is positive free water clearance
options.c: A shows positive free water clearance B is isotonic C is negative free water clearance
options.d: A shows negative free water clearance B is isotonic C is negative free water clearance

mcqs.explanation: Patient A shows positive free water clearance B is isotonic C shows negative free water clearance. Free water clearance is defined as the amount of solute -free water generated by the kidneys, either when dilute urine or when concentrated urine is formed. Patient A has positive free -water clearance, since excess water is being excreted (dilute urine). Patient C has negative free -water clearance, since excess solutes are being removed and water is being conserved (concentrated urine).

mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: All are true except that ____.

options.b: Descending limb of loop of henle is permeable to water
options.c: Thick ascending limb is permeable to water
options.d: Distal tubule is permeable to water

mcqs.explanation: The ascending limb is always impermeable to H2O.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: The average urine osmolality in mosm/kg is _____.
mcqs.explanation: The average urine osmolality is 100 -800 mosm/kg.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: What are the requirements for a patient to excrete concentrated urine?

options.a: High ADH levels and hypoosmolar renal medulla
options.b: Low ADH levels and hypoosmolar renal medulla
options.c: High ADH levels and hyperosmolar renal medulla
options.d: Low ADH levels and hyperosmolar renal medulla

mcqs.explanation: The requirements for excreting concentrated urine are high ADH levels and hyperosmolar renal medulla . A high level of ADH, which increases the permeability of the distal tubules and collecting ducts to water, thereby allowing these tubular segments to avidly reabsorb water, and a high osmolarity of the renal medullary interstitial fluid , which provides the osmotic gradient necessary for water reabsorption to occur in the presence of high levels of ADH.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Maximum osmotic gradient is found in____
mcqs.explanation: Maximum osmotic gradient is found in the inner medulla . The gradient of osmolarity from the cortex (300 mosm/L ) to the inner medulla (1200 mosm/L ) is produced by the loops of Henle as countercurrent multipliers and maintained by operation of the vasa recta as countercurrent exchangers .673

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Hyperosmolarity of renal medulla is due to____
mcqs.explanation: Hyperosmolarity of the medullary interstitium is mainly due to NaCl and urea. The major factors that contribute to the buildup of solute concentration into the renal medulla are • Active transport of Na+ and co-transport of K+, Cl-, and other ions out of the thick portion of the ascending limb of the loop of Henle into the medullary interstitium . • Active transport of ions from the collecting ducts into the medullary interstitium . • Facilitated diffusion of urea from the inner medullary collecting ducts into the medullary interstitium . • Diffusion of only small amounts of water from the medullary tubules into the medullary interstitium

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a component of the countercurrent mechanism?

options.d: Descending limb of loop of Henle

mcqs.explanation: Proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) does not play a role in countercurrent mechanism. The countercurrent mechanism consists of 2 components : • Countercurrent multiplier : a. Absorption of water via Aquaporin 1 in thin descending limb b. Active transport of Na+- K+- 2Cl- in thick ascending limb c. Flow of fluid from PCT to DCT • Countercurrent exchanger: Vasa recta are involved in this process . They help in maintaining the osmotic gradient in the renal medulla . This is a passive process .674

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Maximum osmolality that can be reached at the tip of medulla is proportional to

options.a: Distribution of Na-K-2Cl channel in the thick ascending loop of Henle
options.b: Permeability of descending loop to water

mcqs.explanation: The maximum osmolality that can be reached at the tip of the medulla is proportional to the length of the loop of Henle , because the Loop of Henle acts as Countercurrent multiplier to maitain the gradient in medulla . Greater is the length of loop of Henle , greater will be the osmolality that can be reached at the tip of the medulla . In case of juxtamedullary nephrons with longer loops and thin ascending limbs, the osmotic gradient is spread over a greater distance and the osmolality at the tip of the loop is greater.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Counter current blood flow is seen in all except _____
mcqs.explanation: The eye does not have a countercurrent blood flow system . Heat and substances , including gases , steroids and peptide hormones, can pass from venous blood, interstitial fluid and lymph to the arterial blood; the process is called local counter-current transfer. Examples of countercurrent blood flow • Heat exchange between the arteries and venae comitantes of the limbs. • Vasa recta in the kidneys • Testes • Small intestine

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: All of the following are components responsible for the countercurrent mechanism in the kidney except _____.

options.a: Sodium outflow in thick ascending limb
options.b: Water outflow in thin descending limb
options.c: Sodium outflow in thin ascending limb
options.d: Flow of tubular fluid from PCT to DCT

mcqs.explanation: 675 Thin ascending limb is not a component of the countercurrent mechanism. The loop of Henle function as countercurrent multipliers and vasa recta as countercurrent exchangers. The functioning of the loop of Henle depends upon: • High permeability of the thin descending limb to water ( via aquaporin -1) • Active transport of Na+ and Cl- from the thick ascending limb • Inflow of tubular fluid from proximal tubule and outflow to the distal tubule . Note : The thin ascending limbs of juxtamedullary nephrons are permeable to Na+ and Cl- and hence do contribute passively to countercurrent multiplication . However, among the options provided, Option C is the best answer as the other options are directly responsible for the countercurrent mechanism.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the diluting segment of the kidney?
mcqs.explanation: The ascending thick limb of the loop of Henle is called the diluting segment . In the ascending limb, there is the movement of Na+ and Cl– out of the tubular lumen, and the tubular fluid becomes more dilute . When the fluid reaches the top of the ascending limb, it becomes hypotonic to plasma.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: As filtrate flows through PCT, the concentration of all of the following decreases except :
mcqs.explanation: As the filtrate flows through the proximal convoluted tubule , the concentration of the chloride increases . • The concentration of chloride in the early part of the pCT is \013105 mEq/L . • As the sodium is reabsorbed , it preferentially carries glucose , amino acids, and bicarbonate. • This leaves behind the solute , that has a higher concentration of the chloride , which as it reaches the second half of the PCT is \013140 mEq/L .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Renal Tubular Functions, Urine Concentration an...
mcqs.question: Macula densa is formed by which part of the nephron?
mcqs.explanation: Macula densa is formed by specialized tubular epithelial cells of the distal convoluted tubule .676 The juxtaglomerular apparatus consists of the following parts: • Macula densa: At the end of the thick ascending limb of Henle , and at the beginning of the distal tubule , the tubular epithelial cells are specialized to form the macula densa. They detect sodium concentration of the fluid in the tubule (chemoreceptor ). In response to elevated sodium, the macula densa cells trigger the contraction of the afferent arteriole, reducing the flow of blood to the glomerulus and the glomerular filtration rate. This happens as follows : When there is increased sodium, there is increased sodium-potassium ATPase activity which leads to increased ATP hydrolysis causing more adenosine formation. The adenosine receptors on the macula densa cells stimulate it to release more calcium, so that there is vasoconstriction of the afferent arteriole, thereby decreasing the GFR. • Lacis cells : Extraglomerular mesangial cells situated between afferent and efferent arteriole. • Granular cells /JG cells : Modified smooth muscle cells of the afferent arteriole, they secrete renin. Fall in pressure in afferent arteriole stimulates renin release (mechanoreceptor ), which, in turn, increases blood pressure .677

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: Principal site of acidification of urine______
mcqs.explanation: Principal site of acidification of urine is collecting duct . Acidification occurs in both distal tubule and collecting duct , but collecting duct is more important. The urinary pH of 4.5 (limiting pH) is normally reached in the collecting ducts . In the late distal tubules and collecting ducts , the tubular epithelium secretes H+ by primary active transport. Primary active secretion of H+ occurs in type A intercalated cells of the late distal tubule and in the collecting tubules . H+ concentration can be increased as much as 900 -fold in the collecting tubules .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: Most important extracellular buffer _____
mcqs.explanation: The most important extracellular buffer is bicarbonate. The source of bicarbonate is plasma by filteration. It is a non inducible buffer . Proteins: Are the most abundant intracellular buffer . Phosphate : minor buffer in kidney. The source is plasma by filteration . It is a noninducible buffer . Ammonia is a minor buffer , locally produced by tubular cells . Its production increases in metabolic acidosis. It is the only inducible buffer .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: Normal anion gap is mostly due to_____
mcqs.explanation: Normal anion gap is mostly due to unmeasured proteins . Normally in the plasma, the concentrations of anions and cations are equal to maintain electrical neutrality . Thus no real "anion gap" exists in the plasma and this is purely a diagnostic concept . Diagnostically , when the electrolytes are measured in the blood, routinely only certain cations and anions are measured . These are Na+, Cl- and HCO3-. The anion gap is the difference between the unmeasured anions and unmeasured cations. This is estimated as : Plasma anion gap= [Na+] - [Cl-] - [HCO3-]685 The unmeasured cations include calcium, magnesium and potassium . The unmeasured anions include albumin, phosphate , sulphate and organic anions. This is primarily used in measurement of different causes of metabolic acidosis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: Normal anion gap is _________mEq / L .
mcqs.explanation: The normal anion gap ranges between 8 and 16 mEq/L . The concentrations of anions and cations in plasma must be equal to maintain electrical neutrality . Therefore, there is no real "anion gap" in the plasma. However, only certain cations and anions are routinely measured in the clinical laboratory. The cation normally measured is Na+, and the anions are usually Cl� and HCO3� . The "anion gap" (which is only a diagnostic concept ) is the difference between unmeasured anions and unmeasured cations and is estimated as Plasma anion gap = [Na+ ] � [HCO3� ] � [Cl� ]=144� 24� 108 =12 mEq/L The anion gap will increase if unmeasured anions rise or if unmeasured cations fall. The most important unmeasured cations include calcium, magnesium and potassium and the major unmeasured anions are albumin, phosphate , sulfate and other organic anions. Usually the unmeasured anions exceed the unmeasured cations and the anion gap ranges between 8 and 16 mEq/L .

mcqs.question: Endocrine functions associated with kidney include all of the following except ______
mcqs.explanation: ANP is secreted by the heart. Endocrine/Paracrine Functions of the Kidney :Substance Site of secretion Renin Granular cells or juxtaglomer ular cells (JG cells ) of the jux taglomerular apparatus (JGA) Erythropoietin Interstitial cells in the peritu bular capillary bed Prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) Renal medullary interstitial c ells (RMICs), macula densa, and by cells of collecting duct PGI2and other prostaglandin s Arterioles and glomeruli 1,25-Dihydroxycholecalciferol (calcitriol or vitamin D3) Cells of proximal tubules of t he kidneys.686

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: The major prostanoid synthesized in kidney is ________
mcqs.explanation: PGE2 is the major prostanoid synthesized in the kidney. It is secreted by: • RMICs (Renal Medullary Interstitial Cells ) • Macula densa • Cells in the collecting ducts . Prostacyclin (PGI2 ) and other prostaglandins are secreted by the arterioles and glomeruli . Renal medullary interstitial cells (RMICs) are specialized fibroblast-like cells which are major site of cyclooxygenase 2 (COX-2) and prostaglandin synthase (PGES) expression .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: All of the following results in increased renin secretion except _____.

options.b: Increased amount of Na+ in DCT
options.c: Decreased amount of Na+ in PCT

mcqs.explanation: The increased amount of Na+ and Cl- reabsorption across macula densa (DCT) is inhibitory to renin secretion. All other factors increase renin secretion . Renin leads to a series of events through the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone pathway that finally, in simple terms, leads to salt and water retention and increases blood pressure . Therefore, it is easy to remember that all factors that cause decreased effective volume, pressure , or sodium delivery will increase the renin levels and vice versa. Note : Renin is secreted by the juxtaglomerular cells (granular cells ) which are epitheloid cells located in the media of afferent arterioles of the glomerulus .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: Angiotensin II causes all of the following except _____
mcqs.explanation: Angiotensin II is one of the most potent vasoconstrictors in the body. It constricts efferent arteriole, thereby increasing filteration fraction and glomerular filteration rate, when there is decreased renal bloodflow

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: Vasopressin secretion is increased by_____
mcqs.explanation: Vasopressin (ADH) secretion increases in response to decreased ECF volume to bring about water retention to restore the ECF volume. ADH exerts its antidiuretic effect by acting on the V2 receptors and involves the insertion of aquaporin 2 (AQP2 ) into the apical (luminal) membranes of the principal cells of the collecting ducts .687

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: A patient who got into an accident is brought to the casualty and is bleeding from his right leg . His blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg. Which of the following plays the most important role for sodium and water retention in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The renin-angiotensin system plays the most important role for sodium and water retention in this patient as the patient has hypovolemia due to blood loss. (refer to figure ) The plasma concentration of renin is the rate-limiting step in the renin-angiotensin system ; it is the major determinant of plasma angiotensin II concentration. Angiotensin II stimulates the aldosterone and ADH secretion ; it also constricts the blood vessels and causes thirst, which helps in maintaining blood pressure .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: Atriopeptin (ANP) acts at _____
mcqs.explanation: ANP acts on the collecting duct . ANP is secreted by the atria in response to an increase in ECF volume. It decreases Na+ reabsorption in the late distal tubule and collecting ducts . It causes natriuresis. ANP causes dilation of afferent arterioles and constriction of efferent arterioles resulting in an increased RBF(Because the dilatory effect of ANP on afferent arterioles is more than the constrictor effect on efferent arterioles, there is an overall decrease in renal vascular resistance and resulting increase in RBF) and increased GFR.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: ANP secretion is raised by all except ____
mcqs.explanation: It is \031 in ECF volume and not hypovolemia that causes increased secretion of ANP.688 Stimuli that increase the secretion of ANP • \031atrial stretch or ventricular stretch • \031isotonic saline administration • \031ECF volume Stimuli that decrease ANP secretion • Rising from supine to standing position (as this decreases the central venous pressure ).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: Several hormones regulate the tubular reabsorption of water and electrolytes at different sites in the nephron physiologically in a patient . Which of the following combination is correct?
mcqs.explanation: The combination which is correct is Aldosterone in collecting ducts . Aldosterone acts on principal cells and intercalated cells , which are present in collecting ducts . It regulates ECF volume and Na+ content. Major stimulus for aldosterone secretion is Hyperkalemia. The functions of aldosterone are Na+ and H2O reabsorption, K+ and H+excretion. Option A: Angiotensin II acts on efferent arteriole. It causes vasoconstriction increasing BP. It causes constriction of efferent arteriole, increases filteration fraction, preserving GFR when RBF \023. Option B: ADH acts on principal cells in collecting ducts . It primarily regulates serum osmolarity. Stimulates reabsorption of water in collecting ducts via Aquaporin -2. Option D: ANP is released from atria and BNP is released from ventricles in response to \031 volume, it inhibits RAAS, relaxes mesangial cells and promotes natriuresis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: The areas associated with micturition reflex is/are ______________
mcqs.explanation: The micturition center is located in the pons. The paracentral lobule is also associated with micturition. The micturition reflex is an autonomic spinal cord reflex , but it can be inhibited or facilitated by centers in the brain . These centers include - • A strong facilitative and inhibitory centers in the brain stem , located mainly in the pons. • Centers located in the cerebral cortex that are mainly inhibitory but can become excitatory .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: Hypoxia-induced factors stimulate ___________ cells of the kidney to initiate erythropoiesis .
mcqs.explanation: Hypoxia induced factors stimulate interstitial cells to initiate erythropoiesis Erythropoietin is produced by interstitial cells in the peritubular capillary bed of the kidney.689 Erythropoietin inturn initiates erythropoiesis

mcqs.subject: Physiology

mcqs.question: Choose the correct option mentioning the correct site of product conversion
mcqs.explanation: Angiotensin 1 \032 angiotensin 2 @ lungs Cholecalciferol \032 25 hydroxy vitamin D3 @ liver 25 hydroxy vitamin D3 \032 1,25 dihydroxy vitamin D3 @ Kidney Angiotensin I is converted to Angiotensin II by Angiotensin Converting Enzyme (ACE) which is expressed in the lungs .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: ADH acts through which aquaporin channel?
mcqs.explanation: The antidiuretic hormone acts through aquaporin channel 2. ADH binds to V2 receptors in the late distal tubules , collecting tubules , and collecting ducts , and stimulates the movement of an intracellular protein, called aquaporin -2 (AQP-2), to the luminal side of the cell membranes.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: Ureteric peristalsis is mainly due to_____

options.d: Pacemaker activity of smooth muscles of renal pelvis

mcqs.explanation: Urine flowing from the collecting ducts into the renal calyces stretches the calyces and increases their inherent pacemaker activity, which in turn initiates peristaltic contractions occurring 1 to 5 times per minute that spread to the renal pelvis and then downward along the length of the ureter, thereby forcing urine from the renal pelvis toward the bladder .690 • The walls of the ureters contain smooth muscle and are innervated by both sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves, as well as by an intramural plexus of neurons and nerve fibers that extends along the entire length of the ureters . • As with other visceral smooth muscle, peristaltic contractions in the ureter are • Enhanced by parasympathetic stimulation • Inhibited by sympathetic stimulation

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: In micturition reflex , the first change to occur is_____
mcqs.explanation: • One of the initial events is the relaxation of the muscles of the pelvic floor, and this may cause a sufficient downward tug on the detrusor muscle to initiate its contraction. • Micturition Reflex • Micturition is fundamentally a spinal reflex facilitated and inhibited by higher brain centers and is subject to voluntary facilitation and inhibition. • These centers include • strong facilitative and inhibitory centers in the brain stem , located mainly in the pons • several centers located in the cerebral cortex that is mainly inhibitory but can become excitatory. • The micturition reflex is the basic cause of micturition, but the higher centers normally exert final control of micturition. • Micturition Reflex is the result of a stretch reflex initiated by sensory stretch receptors in the bladder wall, especially by the receptors in the posterior urethra when this area begins to fill with urine at the higher bladder pressures . • Sensory signals from the bladder stretch receptors are conducted to the sacral segments of the cord through the pelvic nerves and then reflexively back again to the bladder through the parasympathetic nerve fibers by way of these same nerves. (refer figure ) • As the bladder continues to fill, the micturition reflexes become more frequent and cause greater contractions of the detrusor muscle . • Once a micturition reflex begins , it is "self -regenerative ." • It is a single complete cycle of • The progressive and rapid increase of pressure , • A period of sustained pressure , and • Return of the pressure to the basal tone of the bladder . • As the bladder becomes more and more filled , micturition reflexes occur more and more often and more and more powerfully . • Once the micturition reflex becomes powerful enough , it causes another reflex , which passes through the pudendal nerves to the external sphincter to inhibit it . If this inhibition is more potent in the brain than the voluntary constrictor signals to the external sphincter , urination will occur. If not, urination will not occur until the bladder fills still further and the micturition reflex691 becomes more powerful .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: How much urine in the bladder will cause the first urge to void in a patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The first urge to void is felt at a bladder volume of about 150 mL , and a marked sense of fullness at about 400 mL . Cystometrogram (refer figure ) A plot of intravesical pressure against the volume of fluid in the bladder is called a cystometrogram. The curve shows • An initial slight rise in pressure when the first increments in the volume are produced (Ia); • A long, nearly flat segment as further increments are produced (Ib);692 • A sudden , sharp rise in pressure as the micturition reflex is triggered (II ). • The flatness of segment Ib is a manifestation of the law of Laplace. • This law states that the pressure in a spherical viscus is equal to twice the wall tension divided by the radius. • P= 2T /R • In the case of the bladder , the tension increases as the organ fill but so does the radius. Therefore , the pressure increase is slight until the organ is relatively full .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: In a patient , pO2 is 85mmHg, pCO2 is 50mmHg, pH is 7.2, and HCO3- is 36mmol/L . Identify the condition.

options.a: Respiratory acidosis with compensatory metabolic alkalosis
options.c: Respiratory alkalosis with compensatory metabolic acidosis
options.d: Respiratory acidosis with compensatory metabolic acidosis

mcqs.explanation: This patient has respiratory acidosis with compensatory metabolic alkalosis. pH is decreased (<7.35) so it is acidosis. The CO2 levels are increased (>45mmHg), which is in line with the change in pH (in respiratory acidosis CO2 is expected to raise), thus the primary problem is respiratory. The HCO3- levels are increased (>30mmol/L), which is opposite to change in pH (i.e there is acidosis and HCO3- levels are high), thus , there is compensatory metabolic alkalosis. Thus, this is a case of respiratory acidosis with compensatory metabolic alkalosis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: A patient with salicylic acid poisoning has the following arterial blood gas analysis report: pH = 7.1, pCO2 =18mmHg, HCO3-=12mmol /L. Identify the acid-base disorder here.

options.b: Respiratory acidosis with compensatory metabolic alkalosis
options.c: Metabolic acidosis with uncompensated respiratory alkalosis

mcqs.explanation: The acid-base disorder here is a mixed disorder of metabolic acidosis and respiratory alkalosis. It should not be confused with metabolic acidosis with uncompensated respiratory alkalosis. This can be understood by the following calculation: Step 1: The pH in this patient is 7.1 (pH <7.35) which indicates acidosis693 Step 2: HCO3- is 12 mmol/L (Normal HCO3- - 22 –30 mmol/L ). In metabolic acidosis, HCO3- levels decrease . Hence , this is a case of metabolic acidosis. Step 3: As per Winter's formula, the expected respiratory compensation in metabolic acidosis can be calculated using, pCO2 =( 1.5 x [HCO3-] ) +8 \261 2 In this case, Expected pCO2 = ( 1.5 x [12 ] ) +8 \261 2 = 26 \261 2 = 24 - 28 mmHg The pCO2 in this patient is 18 mmHg, which implies there is an overcompensation of pCO2. This overcompensation can happen only if there is an additional component of respiratory alkalosis contributing to reduced pCO2. Hence , this patient has a mixed disorder - metabolic acidosis and respiratory alkalosis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: Which of the following patients will have metabolic alkalosis?

options.b: A patient with chronic renal failure who is recommended dialysis
options.c: A patient who was diagnosed with hyperaldosteronism
options.d: A patient who took a whole bottle of aspirin to get rid of the headache

mcqs.explanation: Metabolic alkalosis is seen in patients with hyperaldosteronism . In hyperaldosteronism : increased aldosterone levels cause increased H+ secretion by the distal tubule and increased reabsorption of HCO3- \032 Metabolic alkalosis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: In a patient with metabolic acidosis, which of the following changes are seen ?
mcqs.explanation: K+ secretion into the renal tubules is decreased when the H+ secretion is increased (Intracellular Buffering of H+). Thus in metabolic acidosis, there is decreased K+ excretion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturiti...
mcqs.question: A normal anion gap metabolic acidosis occurs in patients with_____
mcqs.explanation: Diarrhoea is a cause of normal anion gap metabolic acidosis produced as a result of increased HCO3- loss in feces . This is because a decrease in HCO3- is replaced by an increase in the concentration of Cl-. This is a measurable anion and hence the anion gap is normal . Extra - edge : Siggard-Anderson curve normogram is used to plot the acid-base composition of the blood694

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is secreted from acidophilic cells of pituitary ?
mcqs.explanation: Growth hormone is secreted from acidophilic cells of anterior pituitary . Acidophilic cells secrete growth hormone and prolactin. Basophilic cells secrete TSH, ACTH, FSH and LH .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man is suffering from hypertension , buffalo hump and hyperpigmentation of the skin, including oral mucosa. He is diagnosed with Cushing syndrome due to pituitary cause . Which of the following is responsible for the hyperpigmentation seen in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: ACTH is more responsible than MSH for the hyperpigmentation seen in a patient with Cushing syndrome due to pituitary cause (ACTH hypersecretion ). ACTH is a derivative of POMC (Pro-opiomelanocortin). POMC is the precursor of ACTH, melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH), \035 lipotropin and \035 endorphin. Since the melanocyte -stimulating hormone is the byproduct of ACTH synthesis from POMC, any disease process which leads to ACTH overproduction will also lead to an increased level of MSH. ACTH has mild MSH activity, hence elevated levels of ACTH acts on melanotropin-1 receptors causing generalized hyperpigmentation . A similar manifestation will also be seen in Addison's disease where the ACTH level is high.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Inhibitory control by the hypothalamus is exerted on:
mcqs.explanation: Inhibitory control by the hypothalamus is exerted mainly on prolactin and growth hormone. The major hypothalamic releasing hormones are: • Thyrotropin releasing hormone (TRH ) • Corticotropin releasing hormone (CRH)702 • Growth hormone releasing hormone (GHRH) • Gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH ) The major hypothalamic inhibitory hormones are: • Prolactin inhibitory hormone or dopamine • Growth hormone inhibitory hormone (GHIH), also called Somatostatin.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with a known brain tumour learns that his pituitary stalk has been affected . Secretion of which of the following hormones is increased after the sectioning of the pituitary stalk?
mcqs.explanation: The secretion of prolactin is increased after the sectioning of the pituitary stalk. Prolactin is unique among the pituitary hormones because the predominant central control mechanism is inhibitory, i.e., dopamine inhibits prolactin secretion . Hence , sectioning of the pituitary stalk (Ex: In head trauma or compressive skull lesions ) prevents this inhibition and leads to increased secretion of prolactin. Note : If the pituitary stalk is cut above the pituitary gland but the entire hypothalamus is left intact, the posterior pituitary hormones (ADH & Oxytocin) show a transient decrease because they are initially synthesized in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus and are then transported down to the nerve endings to the posterior pituitary gland, requiring several days to reach the gland.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a cause of elevated prolactin level ?
mcqs.explanation: L- Dopa is not a cause of increased prolactin level , it decreases prolactin secretion by increasing the formation of dopamine (prolactin inhibitory hormone).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the effect of continuous GnRH administration?
mcqs.explanation: Continuous GnRH administration suppresses the hypothalamic -pituitary axis. Pulsatile GnRH stimulates the pulsatile release of LH and FSH. Note : Long-acting GnRH agonists are used to suppress gonadotropin levels in children with precocious puberty and in men with prostate cancer.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following actions of GH is mediated by IGF–1?
mcqs.explanation: Antilipolysis is mediated by IGF-1. The actions of growth hormone-mediated via IGF-1 (somatomedin-C) are the indirect effects of growth hormone and include :703 • Antilipolytic activity • Insulin-like activity • Protein synthesis • Epiphyseal growth The direct effects of GH include : • Sodium retention • Decreased insulin sensitivity • Lipolysis • Protein synthesis • Epiphyseal growth

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: GH has its effect on bone growth through______
mcqs.explanation: Growth hormone (GH) has both direct and indirect effects on bone growth . GH stimulates prechondrocytes to differentiate into chondrocytes . GH strongly stimulates osteoblasts and chondrocytes causing increased deposition of proteins \032 bone growth . GH also increases insulin-like growth factor (IGF) levels , which stimulate bone growth . Note : The pygmies of Africa have a congenital inability to synthesize significant amounts of somatomedin C (IGF-I). Therefore, even though their plasma concentration of growth hormone is either normal or high, they have diminished amounts of IGF-I in the plasma, which accounts for the short stature . Some other dwarfs (e.g., the Levi -Lorain dwarf) also have this problem.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following hormones demonstrates the fluctuations depicted below ?
mcqs.explanation: Growth hormone demonstrates the depicted fluctuations . Growth hormone is secreted in a pulsatile fashion, with increase during strenuous exercise and during the early period of sleep , (Non-REM Sleep ) as shown in the graph. It is reduced during the later stages of sleep . (REM sleep ) Other options : Option A: ACTH levels are high in the early morning and low in the late evening. Option C: TSH is secreted in pulses , but the fluctuations are less in comparison to other pituitary hormones because of the low amplitude of the pulses and the relatively long half-life of TSH. Option D: Prolactin is secreted in a pulsatile fashion, with the highest secretory peak between 4:00 and 6:00 a.m. (REM Sleep )

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Growth hormone level is decreased in which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: 704 Growth hormone(GH) level is decreased during deep sleep . Specifically , it is reduced during REM sleep as the levels of GHRH reduces and levels of cortisol are higher compared to slow wave sleep . Hypoglycemia , fasting, and exercise cause an increase in GH secretion . GH levels are increased during non-REM sleep . GH levels also decline with age and obesity .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 35 yr old man presents with hypertension , coarse facial features , frontal bossing, large hands and feet, mandibular enlargement and a large fleshy nose. His age -matched serum IGF-I levels are elevated . What is the most likely cause of his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of acromegaly and is due to excess growth hormone (GH). Acromegaly occurs when excessive GH is secreted after puberty (after fusion of long bone epiphysis ). Features include • Prognathism (protrusion of jaw), hypertrophy of frontal bones • Acral enlargement in hands and feet (due to thickening of soft tissues ) • Visceromegaly : Enlargement of most organs especially the tongue , thyroid, salivary gland, liver, spleen , kidney, and prostate Serious complications include cardiomyopathy with arrhythmias, diabetes mellitus , obstructive sleep apnoea, and increased risk of colonic polyps and cancer. Age -matched IGF-I levels are elevated .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: What does the neurohypophysis release ?
mcqs.explanation: The posterior pituitary or neurohypophysis releases oxytocin and anti-diuretic hormone (ADH or vasopressin) Note : ADH and oxytocin are synthesised by the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus. Thereafter, they are stored and released from the posterior pituitary .705

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which pair of vasopressin receptors is incorrect?
mcqs.explanation: The pair V4 -CNS is incorrect. Vasopressin mediates its effect via 3 kinds of receptors - V1a , V1b and V2 . There is no V4 .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: "Vasopressin escape " in SIADH results due to:
mcqs.explanation: Vasopressin escape in SIADH (Syndrome of inappropriate ADH secretion ) results due to downregulation of aquaporin 2 production . Prolonged exposure to elevated levels of vasopressin (ADH) leads eventually to downregulation of aquaporin -2 receptors . This prevents excessive reabsorption of water, despite high serum ADH levels and hence maintains euvolemia. This is known as vasopressin escape . This helps prevent excessive dilutional hyponatremia in SIADH.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Sodium-iodide symport is absent in which of the following sites ?
mcqs.explanation: Sodium-iodide symport is absent in the pituitary . Na+/I– symporter is present in • Basolateral membranes of thyrocytes facing the capillaries . • Salivary glands • Gastric mucosa • Placenta • Ciliary body of the eye • Choroid plexus • Mammary glands

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old lady is diagnosed with Hashimoto thyroiditis and a positive antibody titer against thyroid peroxidase enzyme. Which of the following is not a function of the affected enzyme?
mcqs.explanation: Iodide trapping (iodide uptake ) is not catalyzed by thyroid peroxidase . Oxidation, organification, and coupling are catalyzed by it. Steps in synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormone: • Iodide uptake : The basolateral sodium-iodide symporter (NIS) actively takes up I-(iodide) from the circulation into the follicular cells . It is then transported into the colloid through a pendrin (chloride -iodide ) transporter706 • Thyroglobulin synthesis : Thyroglobulin (Tg), is a large glycoprotein rich in tyrosine residues . It is synthesized by follicular cells . • Iodination of thyroglobulin : This is regulated by the thyroid peroxidase (TPO) enzyme. TPO has three functions: • Oxidation: TPO oxidizes I- to I2 (iodine) in the presence of H2O2 • Organification: TPO links tyrosine residues of thyroglobulin with iodine (I2) to form monoiodotyrosine (MIT), diiodotyrosine (DIT ) • Coupling reactions: TPO combines iodinated tyrosine residues to make MIT + DIT = T3 (triiodothyronine), DIT + DIT = T4 (tetraiodothyronine) • Storage : Thyroid hormones are bound to thyroglobulin and stored in the follicular lumen as colloids . The colloid has hormone reserves for 2-3 months • Release : Iodinated thyroglobulin is taken up by the thyroid follicles via endocytosis and fuses with lysosomes. It is cleaved by lysosomal proteolytic enzymes into MIT, DIT , T3 , and T4. T4 (80%) and T3 (20 %) are released into the blood • Peripheral T3 conversion: T4 undergoes deiodination in extrathyroidal tissue to form T3 , which is the active form of the hormone

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with hyperthyroidism is planned for thyroidectomy . In order to achieve a euthyroid status preoperatively, he is started on Lugol's iodine solution . Which of the following best describes its mechanism of action?

options.d: Inhibition of organification and synthesis of thyroid hormones

mcqs.explanation: Introduction of exogenous iodine in the form of lugol 's iodine solution leads to transient inhibition of organification and synthesis of thyroid hormones. This is known as the wolff -chaikoff effect . In individuals with a normal thyroid, the gland escapes from this inhibitory effect and iodide organification resumes ; but the suppressive action of high iodide may persist in patients with hyperthyroidism due to underlying autoimmune thyroid disease .707 Note : Jod-Basedow effect is iodine-induced hyperthyroidism , usually occurring after the use of an I-based contrast agent . It is often seen in the presence of pre-existing thyroid conditions like multinodular goitre .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: How long is thyroxine stored in thyroid follicles ?
mcqs.explanation: Thyroxine is stored in the thyroid follicles for 2-3 months, bound to thyroglobulin . Serves as a reserve of T3 and T4, thus delaying the occurrence of hypothyroidism , if thyroid secretion ceases .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The major thyroxine-binding protein is _____.
mcqs.explanation: Thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) is the major thyroxine-binding protein. Other thyroxine-binding proteins are: • Albumin • Transthyretin (TTR )/ thyroxine-binding pre-albumin (TBPA) • Lipoproteins

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding thyroid hormone?

options.a: T3 is more avidly bound to nuclear receptor than T
options.c: T3 is more active than T
options.d: T4 has shorter half- life than T

mcqs.explanation: T4 doesn 't have a shorter half-life than T3 , rather T3 has a shorter half-life and more rapid action than T4. The table compares T4 and T3 :T3 T4 More potent (4x) Less potent More active Less active Rapid onset of action Slow onset of action Shorter half-life (1 day) Longer half-life (7 days) Less plasma concentration More plasma concentrati on Less in colloid More in colloid Responsible for physiological actions Used for pharmacothera py708

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Half-life of T4_____
mcqs.explanation: The half-life of T4 is 6 - 7 days. T3 has the shorter half-life of 1 day.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 35 yr old woman presents with heat intolerance and menstrual abnormalities. On examination , a diffusely enlarged thyroid gland is present . Which of the following features will not be present in her?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of hyperthyroidism , which does not cause decreased protein breakdown. Rather it causes increased protein breakdown.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Prolactin level is highest during :
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , the prolactin level is highest 24 hours after delivery . The maximum level of prolactin is seen during pregnancy and in the immediate postpartum period. During pregnancy, the secretion is increased reaching a peak at the time of delivery . After delivery , the plasma concentration falls to nonpregnant levels in a few weeks . Suckling produces surges of prolactin release .

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions would have the highest levels of ACTH and cortisol?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given conditions, the levels of ACTH and cortisol will be highest in Cushing's disease . Cushing's disease is caused by an ACTH secreting pituitary adenoma. The increased ACTH causes increased cortisol production . Note : In normal physiologic state , ACTH levels are higher in the early morning but not as high as in Cushing's disease .709

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Which scientists were awarded the Nobel Prize for the discovery of insulin?
mcqs.explanation: Banting and McLeod were awarded the Nobel Prize for the discovery of insulin. In 1921 , Banting took his idea to Professor John Macleod at the University of Toronto, who was a leading figure in the study of diabetes in Canada. Macleod gave Banting a laboratory with a minimum equipments and ten dogs . Banting also got an assistant, a medical student by the name of Charles Best .
