Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis, and treatment should never be delayed awaiting radiological confirmation. Management includes : • Immediate management: Needle decompression or needle thoracostomy with a wide bore needle in the 5th intercostal space anterior to the mid-axillary line. In the pediatric age group, the needle thoracostomy location is at the 2nd intercostal space in the mid-clavicular line. • Definitive management: Tube thoracostomy or chest tube insertion in the 5th intercostal space in the triangle of safety . The triangle of safety is bounded anteriorly by the lateral border of the pectoralis major , posteriorly by latissmus dorsi and inferiorly by a horizontal line at the level of the nipple . The X-ray below shows a left -sided tension pneumothorax. There is a large, well -demarcated area devoid of lung markings on the left side . The yellow arrows are pointing to the tracheal deviation and the mediastinal shift to the right side .163 Other options : Options A: Pericardial tamponade can mimic tension pneumothorax, but the absence of a tympanic note on percussion rules out its possibility . A patient with pericardial tamponade can present with hypotension , raised JVP , and muffled heart sounds (Beck's triad), with normal breath sounds and no tracheal shift. Option C: Dullness in percussion at the base of the left inferior angle of scapula in conjunction with tubular breath sounds (Ewart's sign), chest pain that improves while sitting upright and worsens when lying down and pulsus paradoxus are indicative of pericardial effusion . Pericardial effusion develops into tamponade when the effusion leads to increased pressure , impairing ventricular filling and reducing cardiac output . Option D: Massive hemothorax is the accumulation of >1500 ml of blood or one-third or more of the patient 's blood volume in the chest cavity. The patient will have collapsed neck veins, decreased breath sounds and a dull note on percussion .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: A 20 -year-old patient presented to the ER with tension pneumothorax following a road traffic accident . What is the first line of management?

options.a: Insert wide bore needle in 5th ICS anterior to the mid-axillary line
options.b: Insert wide bore needle in 5th ICS in the mid-clavicular line
options.c: Insert wide bore needle in 2nd ICS in the mid-axillary line
options.d: Insert wide bore needle in 2nd ICS in the mid-clavicular line

mcqs.explanation: Insertion of a wide -bore needle in the 5th intercostal space anterior to the mid-axillary line is the first-line management in adults with tension pneumothorax. Management of tension pneumothorax: • Immediate management: Needle decompression or needle thoracostomy i.e. insertion of a wide -bore needle in the 5th ICS anterior to the midaxillary line • Definitive management: Tube thoracostomy or chest tube insertion in the 5th ICS in the triangle of safety If a sucking wound is present , the immediate step is to cover the wound with gauze pieces and tape on 3 sides . Following this, chest tube is inserted away from the site of the wound . Note : According to ATLS 10th edition164 • In adults , needle thoracostomy or needle decompression location is changed to 5th ICS anterior to the midaxillary line from 2nd ICS midclavicular line. • In the pediatric age group, the needle thoracostomy location remains at the 2nd ICS midclavicular line. This update was recommended since chest wall thickness influences the likelihood of success with needle decompression. Inserting needle in 5th ICS anterior to the midaxillary line had better outcomes .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: An intern placed an intercostal drainage tube in a patient . Which of the following steps is incorrect?

options.a: Identified 5th intercostal space anterior to mid axillary line to place the tube
options.b: Inserted tube along the lower border of upper rib
options.c: Directed tube posteriorly to prevent injury

mcqs.explanation: An intercostal tube (ICD) is placed along the upper border of the lower rib at the 5th intercostal space (ICS) to prevent damage to the neurovascular bundle . Hence , option B is incorrect. Chest tube insertion (thoracostomy) is indicated in pneumothorax, hemothorax, chylothorax, and pleural effusion in order to drain air/fluid from the pleural space . The triangle of safety , usually in the 5th intercostal space , is the safest site for chest tube insertion, it is bound by: • anterior to the midaxillary line • above the horizontal line marked by the level of the nipple • below and lateral to the pectoralis major muscle165 Contraindications include pulmonary adhesions , pulmonary trauma, coagulopathy , and diaphragmatic hernia. Complications of this procedure : • Infection at the site of insertion • Unintentional injury to the lung - hemothorax • Intercostal nerve/ vessel injury • Subcutaneous hematoma/ emphysema

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: Proper functioning of ICD tube is indicated by _____.

options.a: Continuous air bubbles coming out of the underwater drain
options.b: Oscillation of water column in the tube

mcqs.explanation: Oscillation of the water column level (moving up and down during respiration) within the tube in the water seal chamber is indicative of a functioning (patent ) ICD tube . During spontaneous respiration, the water level rises with inspiration and falls with expiration. Whereas during positive pressure ventilation, the opposite occurs. This oscillation is also known as tidaling. Other options : Option A: Continous bubbling indicates an air leak in the drainage system , which should be corrected Option B: Chest X-ray is useful for assessing the position of the ICD tube inside the chest , not its functioning. Option C: Auscultation is not useful for assessing the functioning of an ICD tube .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: A 40-year old man is brought to the emergency room with a stab injury to his chest . On examination , the patient is found to be hemodynamically unstable . His neck veins are engorged and heart sounds are muffled . Which of the following statements about the patient is false ?

options.a: Cardiac tamponade is likely to be present
options.b: The entry wound is sealed on all 4 sides with an occlusive dressing if pneumothorax is suspected
options.c: eFAST is done to confirm blood in pericardial sac

mcqs.explanation: 166 The given clinical scenario of hemodynamic instability and muffled heart sounds are suggestive of cardiac tamponade . The entry wound is sealed on only 3 sides with an occlusive dressing if a pneumothorax is suspected . When there is a pneumothorax with a sucking wound , the immediate step is to cover the wound with gauze pieces and tape on 3 sides . As the patient breathes in, the dressing occludes the wound , preventing air from entering into the thoracic cavity. During exhalation, the open end of the dressing allows air to escape from the pleural space . This is known as a flutter -valve effect . Following this, a chest tube is inserted away from the site of the wound .Cardiac tamponade must be di\037erentiated from tension pneumothorax in a patient with hemodynamic instability and distended neck veins. Cardiac tamponade is characterized by Beck's triad: • Muffled heart sounds • Distended neck veins • Hypotension Tension pneumothorax is characterized by absent breath sounds and hyper resonance on percussion on the affected side . These are not present in a patient with cardiac tamponade . Diagnosis of cardiac tamponade can be done by eFAST which shows fluid in the pericardial sac. • Definitive management - emergency thoracotomy or sternotomy

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: In a blast injury, which of the following organs is least vulnerable to the blast wave?
mcqs.explanation: In a blast injury, the liver is the least vulnerable to blast wave (primary blast) injury.167 Blast injury is a complex type of physical trauma resulting from direct or indirect exposure to an explosion. Primary blast injuries result from the rapid overpressure or shock waves produced by an explosion . These injuries result from the dramatic changes in barometric pressure projecting outwards from the point of detonation. They predominantly cause damage to air-filled hollow organs of the body from rapid pressure change (barotrauma). This includes the middle ear, lungs , and GIT . The most sensitive and most frequently injured hollow organs are the tympanic membranes > lungs. Blast damage to the lungs is the most common cause of life -threatening injury following an explosion . Solid organs are the most resistant to blast injuries as the parenchymal disruption requires very high levels of overpressure . Classification of blast injuries:Classification Explanation Injury type Examples Primary blast Due to air pressure from the blast Shockwave (overpressure) Tympanic membraneinjury, blast lung, intestinal blast inj ury Secondary blas t Fragments from the blast, fo llowing a detonation Penetrating /fragmentation Allpenetratinginjuries Tertiary blast Gross movements of persons, objects , or infrastructure by the blast wind Blunt trauma Blunt and crushinjuries. Tra umatic amputation. Quaternary bl ast Miscellaneous causes Exposure to explosive produ cts or toxic substances Burns, inhalation injury Quinary blast Theintentional additionof bi ological or radioactive mater ial to the explosive device Environmental contaminant s Radiationsickness,infection .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: Following a motor vehicle collision, a 30-year-old male sustained blunt trauma to his abdomen. What is the organ most likely to be injured?
mcqs.explanation: The spleen is the most common organ involved in blunt trauma injury of the abdomen. In blunt trauma, organs that cannot yield to impact by elastic deformation are most likely to be injured, namely, the solid organs (liver, spleen , and kidneys). For penetrating trauma, organs with the largest surface area when viewed from the front are most prone to injury (small bowel , liver, and colon). Additionally , since bullets and knives usually follow straight lines, adjacent structures are commonly injured (e.g., the pancreas and duodenum ). Deceleration injures the pedicled organs by shearing the organs from their points of attachment to the retroperitoneum (intestines and kidney). The most commonly injured bowel in cases of blunt trauma of the abdomen is jejunum.168

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man stabbed his elder brother using a knife over a property dispute . Which is the most common organ that is likely to be injured in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The liver is the most common organ to be injured in penetrating stab injury of the abdomen. It is due to its anterior location, size and fragile parenchyma. The most common organ injured in blunt trauma to the abdomen is spleen > liver. The most common organ injured in gunshot injury is the small intestine > colon.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: A landlord who was stabbed in his abdomen by one of his tenants for demanding rent was brought to the casualty . He was taken up for laparotomy which revealed a severely injured cecum . What is the best management option for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The best management option for this patient is right hemicolectomy with ileocolostomy . Injuries proximal to the middle colic artery are best managed by this procedure .Injuries distal to the middle colic artery require segmental resection with colocolostomy anastomosis. Immediate anastomosis should be avoided in patients with shock due to the high incidence of leaks following the procedure. In such patients , colostomy and delayed primary anastomosis should be done. Option A: Catheter tube cecostomy is of therapeutic value in refractory colonic pseudo -obstruction, cecal volvulus, or distal colonic obstruction. Option C: Transverse colostomy is generally done in patients with distal obstruction for temporary fecal diversion. Option D: An end-loop sigmoid colostomy is an ideal stoma for distal fecal diversion for incontinence or in association with complex anorectal procedures .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: A patient is shifted for emergency laparotomy for the management of an intra-abdominal haemorrhage, following a road traffic accident . Intraoperatively, you find an active bleed from the liver. Which of the following techniques will you use to control the bleed ?
mcqs.explanation: 169 The hepatoduodenal ligament can be clamped to decrease active hemorrhage from the liver. This is called Pringle's maneuver. This maneuver applies pressure on the portal triad which contains bile duct , portal vein and hepatic artery. This helps distinguish hepatic arterial and portal venous bleeding from hepatic vein bleeding . Hepatic venous bleed will persist with the hepatoduodenal ligament clamped . The liver laceration can then be explored and any actively bleeding vessels controlled with suture ligation. 4 P's in the management of liver injuries are: • Push - compression of the edges of the laceration • Pringle - applying pressure on the portal triad • Plug the defects with silicon tubes • Pack - apply packs in and around the liver to arrest bleeding .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: A patient develops abdominal compartment syndrome following an emergency laparotomy. Which of the following is false about this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Central venous pressure (CVP ) increases due to inferior vena cava (IVC ) and portal vein compression in abdominal compartment syndrome. Abdominal Compartment Syndrome (ACS) is defined as increased intra-abdominal pressure (IAP ) >20 mm Hg resulting in compression of abdominal structures (Normal IAP = 5-7 mmHg and intraabdominal hypertension IAP �o 12 mmHg). This produces fatal complications due to pulmonary failure and mesenteric vascular compromise. Elevated intra-abdominal pressure leads to a decrease in venous return resulting in decreased cardiac output . An increase in heart rate partly compensates this. Systemic vascular resistance (afterload ) is increased by the compression of both the aorta and systemic vasculature. This also leads to an increase in renal vascular resistance leading to a reduced glomerular filtration rate.170 Causes of primary ACS include : • Abdominal trauma • Hemorrhage • Intestinal obstruction • Retroperitoneal hematoma Causes of secondary ACS include : • Pregnancy • Ascites • Ileus • Intra -abdominal sepsis • Large-volume fluid replacement (greater than 3L )

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about abdominal compartment syndrome is false ?

options.b: Hypoxia due to increased peak inspiratory pressure
options.c: Hypotension due to decrease in venous return

mcqs.explanation: Oliguria is due to reduced renal blood flow . An increase in renal vascular resistance leads to a reduction in glomerular filtration rate and impaired urine output . Abdominal compartment syndrome is characterized by : • A sudden increase in intraabdominal pressure • Increased peak inspiratory pressure • Hypercarbia and respiratory acidosis • Decreased urinary output – due to reduced renal blood flow • Hypotension - secondary to decreased venous return to the heart.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: You are evaluating a patient in the burns unit, who had sustained third-degree burns to her abdomen and lower limbs (BSA of 30%). She had received 9 liters of Ringer's lactate at a primary center . On examination, extensive abdominal eschars are seen . BP - 84/50 mmHg, HR - 118 bpm and urine output has been less than 15 ml for the past 2 hours. The ventilator shows a peak airway pressure of 42 cm H2O. What is the most appropriate next step ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS). Measurement of bladder pressure using a urinary bladder catheter is the next best step in the management of this patient . The oliguria and hypotension in isolation could be suggestive of under-resuscitation . However, the history of large volume fluid administration, presence of abdominal eschars along with very high peak airway pressures should raise the suspicion for ACS. Abdominal compartment syndrome refers to an elevation of intra-abdominal pressure > 20mmHg with associated organ compression and dysfunction : • Compression of the IVC leads to decreased cardiac output , and consequent increase in systemic vascular resistance , leading to hypotension .171 • Cephalad displacement of the diaphragm results in decreased thoracic volumes and results in elevated peak and plateau pressures . • Renal compression can lead to increased renal vascular resistance , decreased GFR and low urine output . Measurement of bladder (intravesical) pressure is the standard method to screen for intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH ) and abdominal compartment syndrome. Note : Direct methods such as pressure transducers and intraperitoneal catheters are more accurate but are limited by their invasiveness.Grade of Intra -abdominal hy pertension (IAH ) Intra -abdominal pressure (IA P) Grade I –15 mmHg Grade II 16–20 mmHg Grade III –25 mmHg Grade IV >25 mmHg

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: A patient is admitted to the intensive care unit following a trauma to the abdomen. His intraabdominal pressure is found to be 24 mmHg. What is the grade of abdominal hypertension ?
mcqs.explanation: Intraabdominal pressure (IAP ) of 24 mm Hg falls under grade III of intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH ). Normal intraabdominal pressure is 5 to 7 mmHg. Any acute process in the abdomen such as trauma, intestinal perforation, peritonitis , or acute pancreatitis can increase the intra-abdominal pressure . Increased abdominal pressure can diminish the blood flow to the abdominal organs and decrease the venous return to the heart. Measurement of bladder (intravesical) pressure is the standard method to screen for intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH ) and abdominal compartment syndrome. Grade III intra-abdominal hypertension is associated with hypoxia, ARDS and serious complications. It is associated with abdominal compartment syndrome which is defined as a sustained IAP >20 mmHg associated with organ dysfunction /failure.Grade of Intra -abdominal hy pertension (IAH ) Intra -abdominal pressure (IA P) Grade I –15 mmHg Grade II 16–20 mmHg Grade III –25 mmHg Grade IV >25 mmHg

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: Following a road traffic accident , a child presents with abdominal pain. On examination, vitals are stable and tenderness is present in the left lumbar region. Which is the best investigation of choice for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: 172 The given clinical vignette with abdominal pain and tenderness in the left lumbar region following a road traffic accident is suggestive of blunt renal trauma. The investigation of choice is CECT in a hemodynamically stable patient . Blunt trauma is the main cause of renal injuries and is self -limiting. Radiological investigations are indicated when there is gross haematuria, shock in combination with microscopic haematuria, pediatric renal trauma, and penetrating injuries. CECT is the investigation of choice . It assesses the extent of the injury, showing laceration, extravasation , surrounding hemorrhage, and vessel injury. It also shows non-renal injuries and effectively stages renal pedicle injuries. Arterial occlusion will manifest as rim enhancement of the normal renal contour. Blunt trauma is mostly treated conservatively. Most of the penetrating injuries require surgical renal exploration. Absolute indications for surgical intervention in renal trauma are: • Massive hemorrhage • Renal pedicle avulsion (grade 5 injury) • Expanding, pulsatile , or uncontained retroperitoneal hematoma Relative indications are: • Large laceration of the renal pelvis or avulsion of the ureteropelvic junction • Bowel or pancreatic injuries • Persistent urinary leakage , postinjury urinoma , or perinephric abscess • Complete renal artery thrombosis of both kidneys • Renal hypertension Exploratory laparotomy is recommended in stable patients with penetrating renal injuries.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: A trauma patient suffers a renal laceration with urine extravasation. He is managed conservatively. However, after a few days, he presents with a urinoma . The next best management for this patient would be?
mcqs.explanation: The patient with a history of grade IV renal injury (renal laceration with urine extravasation) who develops a persistent urinoma (a mass formed by encapsulated extravasated urine) should be managed with the placement of an internal ureteral stent . In patients not cured by ureteral stenting , percutaneous nephrostomy or transcutaneous drain may be required. Management of renal injuries Blunt trauma is the main cause of renal injuries and is self -limiting. Blunt trauma is mostly treated conservatively. Most penetrating injuries require surgical renal exploration. • Grading of injury through CECT • If hemodynamically stable • Conservative management - Bedrest & hemodynamic monitoring173 • In grade IV , a repeat CT scan to ensure the extravasation of urine has resolved . • If hemodynamically unstable • Surgical exploration and repair • In grade V , nephrectomy .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: While performing emergency laparotomy for an unstable RTA case with blunt abdominal trauma, the surgeon notices a hematoma around the left kidney. What will be the next step in the management of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The next step in the surgical management of the patient found to have a hematoma around the kidney , intraoperatively, will be a single -shot intravenous pyelography (IVP ). If immediate operative exploration for other injuries is required, renal injury staging can be performed while the patient is still in the operating room, using single -shot IVP . It is useful in assessing the function of the kidneys and the extent of the injury. If the IVP is abnormal or the hematoma is pulsatile , then renal exploration should be performed . Note : CECT is the method of choice for staging a patient with hemodynamically stable renal trauma presenting at the emergency room.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: An 8-year-old child presents with grade 2 splenic injury following blunt trauma to the abdomen. On examination, there are no signs of bleeding . Which of the following is the most appropriate management for this child?
mcqs.explanation: Conservative management is the most appropriate management in this child. Selective Non-Operative Management (SNOM) is usually followed in: • Stable patients with no active bleeding • Patients younger than 55 years of age • Patients with grade I, II , III injuries. Any patient who is hemodynamically unstable , has active bleeding , and has grade IV and V splenic injury should be managed by surgery.174

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a correct statement regarding retroperitoneal trauma?

options.a: All zone 1 injury to be treated conservatively
options.b: Zone 3 injury whether blunt or penetrative should always be explored
options.c: Zone 2 injury with expanding hematoma should be treated surgically
options.d: Mattox maneuver is when the ascending colon is mobilized to the right to visualise the aorta

mcqs.explanation: A zone 2 retroperitoneal injury with expanding hematoma should be treated surgically .Zone of retroperitoneal injur y Type of viscer a Differential management Zone 1 Central Always explored , after proxi mo-distal vascular control Zone 2 Lateral Only explored if the hemato ma is pulsatile or expanding , else conservative/ angioembo lization Zone 3 Pelvic Only explored if the hemato ma is pulsatile or expanding , else conservative/ angioembo lization175 Surgical exploration is done in cases of penetrating injuries to any zone. Other options : Option A: Zone 1 injuries are always explored . Option B: Depending on the situation, zone 3 injuries can be managed with surgical exploration or conservatively. Option D: Mattox manoeuvre is left medial visceral rotation to expose the aorta, while the Cattell -Braasch manoeuvre is done by right medial visceral rotation to expose IVC .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: A young male patient is taken up for laparotomy following a stab injury. Pringle's maneuver is done. Which of the following statements is false about this maneuver?

options.a: It is used to differentiate between hepatic arterial and hepatic venous bleed
options.b: Arterial bleed persists on performing the maneuver
options.c: Hepatic pedicle is compressed at the epiploic foramen
options.d: Prolonged application of pressure can lead to hepatic necrosis

mcqs.explanation: Pringle maneuver may be required for the treatment of liver laceration. Hepatic venous bleed persists on performing this maneuver. When there is severe bleeding from the liver, this maneuver is a viable adjunct to slow blood flow enough to visualize liver injury. The hepatoduodenal ligament is clamped at the epiploic foramen or the foramen of Winslow. This applies pressure on the portal triad that contains bile duct, portal vein and hepatic artery. This helps to distinguish hepatic arterial and portal venous bleeding from hepatic vein bleeding . Hepatic venous bleed will persist when the hepatoduodenal ligament clamped . The liver laceration can then be explored and any actively bleeding vessels controlled with suture ligation.176 4 P's in the management of liver injuries are: • Push - compression of the edges of the laceration • Pringle - applying pressure on the portal triad • Plug the defects with silicon tubes • Pack - apply packs in and around the liver to arrest bleeding . Prolonged intraoperative use of Pringle maneuver can lead to hepatic ischemia and necrosis.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: An elderly lady presents to the trauma care centre following a motor vehicle collision. She complains of chest pain and abdominal pain. On examination, breath sounds are decreased on the right side . X ray chest revealed the following finding. Which of the following statements is false regarding the management of this patient ?

options.a: Most accurate evaluation of this condition is by VATS
options.b: Operative repair is indicated in all cases
options.c: In case of penetrating injury, repair can be done via thoracic incision
options.d: The defect must be closed with polypropylene sutures

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history and X-ray image showing obliteration of the diaphragmatic outline are suggestive of traumatic diaphragmatic injury in this patient . Penetrating diaphragmatic injury must be repaired via the abdomen and not the thorax, to rule out penetrating hollow viscus injury. Patients with diaphragmatic injury are generally asymptomatic . Chest X ray after the insertion of a nasogastric tube may help in identifying the herniation of the stomach in the thoracic cavity. However, the most accurate evaluation is by video assisted thoracoscopy (VATS ) or laparoscopy . Abdominal contents may get herniated into the chest and get strangulated later. This is associated with high mortality. Hence , operative repair is indicated in all patients . The defect is closed with running 1-0 polypropylene suture .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: A 17-year-old boy is brought to the ED after being involved in a high-speed motorcycle collision. He is hypotensive with a systolic pressure of 60 mm Hg. A FAST scan is positive . At laparotomy, he is found to have a large amount of bleeding from behind the liver with hollow -viscous perforation. Temporary application of a Pringle manoeuvre does not control the bleeding . However, laparotomy packs are placed , and the bleeding appears to slow down. The systolic blood pressure fails to increase even after aggressive resuscitation . The patient 's pH is 7.06 and his temperature is 34\260C. What would be the next best step in the management of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: This patient has a blunt trauma abdomen. He is hypothermic and he is battling acidosis. Thus, he should be subjected to damage control surgery and must be shifted to ICU for further resuscitation .177 Damage control surgery is minimal intervention done to stabilize the patient and do the definite surgery later. It centers on coordinating staged operative interventions with periods of aggressive resuscitation to salvage trauma patients sustaining major injuries. 3 Phases : Phase I (Initial Exploration) - This phase consists of an initial operative exploration to attain rapid control of active hemorrhage and contamination. Phase II (Secondary Resuscitation ) - This phase focuses on secondary resuscitation to correct hypothermia , coagulopathy , and acidosis. Phase III (Definitive Operation) - It consists of planned re-exploration and definitive repair of injuries. This phase typically occurs 48 to 72 hours following initial and after successful secondary resuscitation . Pringle's manoeuvre can be performed to decrease the active haemorrhage from the liver in a liver laceration. It is done by applying pressure on the portal triad at the Foramen of Winslow. The pressure can be applied either digitally or with the use of a soft clamp. Rapid control of the vessels entering the porta hepatis can be obtained by compressing them in the free edge of the lesser omentum. Porta hepatis is a deep , transverse fissure that is situated on the inferior surface of the right lobe of the liver. Structures entering at porta hepatis : • Portal vein • Hepatic artery • Hepatic nervous plexus Structures exiting the porta hepatis : • Right and left hepatic bile ducts • Lymphatics The images attached below shows the porta hepatis and the gif demonstrates the pringles manoeuvre.178 4 P's in the management of liver injuries are: • Push- Compression of the edges of the laceration • Pringle- Applying pressure on the portal triad • Plug the defects with silicon tubes • Pack- Apply packs in and around the liver to arrest bleeding General guidelines for the management of blunt trauma to the liver: • Patients who are haemodynamically unstable will require an immediate laparotomy for damage control resuscitation . • For the patient who is haemodynamically stable , imaging by CT should be performed to further evaluate the nature of the injury. • Most patients with a blunt liver injury who are haemodynamically stable can be managed conservatively. • The indication for discontinuing conservative treatment is the development of haemodynamic instability , evidence of ongoing blood loss despite correction of any underlying coagulopathy and the development of signs of generalised peritonitis . • Interventional radiology has an important role in the management of liver trauma and embolisation to control hepatic artery bleeding is safe and effective in a stable patient with no evidence of hollow viscus perforation.180

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: Which of the following hormones will stimulate lobular development of the breast?
mcqs.explanation: Progesterone stimulates lobular development of the breast and differentiation of the epithelium .Hormone Action Estrogen Ductal development Progestero ne Lobular development and dif ferentiation of the epithelium Prolactin Lactogenesis Oxytocin Milk ejection190

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true regarding lymphatic drainage of the breast?

options.a: The axillary nodes receive approximately 85% of the drainage.
options.b: The lateral group is located along the axillary vein.
options.c: The anterior group drains most of the breast.
options.d: Lymph nodes are divided on the basis of their relation to the pectoralis major .

mcqs.explanation: Lymph nodes are divided on the basis of their relation to the pectoralis minor , not the pectoralis major.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old woman presented to the OPD with a 4 x 2 cm painless lump in the left breast. She is planned for a mastectomy . Sentinel lymph node biopsy done showed involvement of level 1 lymph nodes . Which of the following lymph nodes will not be affected in her case?
mcqs.explanation: Interpectoral lymph nodes are level 2 axillary lymph nodes . Level 1 axillary lymph nodes include anterior, lateral, and posterior/subscapular nodes .191

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: During a routine antenatal checkup , a pregnant woman in her third trimester is noticed to have accessory nipples . Which of the following does this condition refer to?
mcqs.explanation: Polythelia or supernumerary nipples refer to the presence of accessory nipples . Polymastia or polymazia is a congenital anomaly with the presence of accessory breast tissue . Symmastia is a condition characterized by webbing between the breasts, at the midline. Supernumerary mazia is the presence of accessory breasts with a complete ductal system , areola, and nipple in addition to two normal breasts. Note : Athelia refers to the absence of nipples , and amastia refers to the congenital absence of the breast and nipple . The image below shows a third nipple below the left breast:192

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true regarding accessory breast tissue ?

options.a: It is associated with Poland's syndrome
options.c: It develops along the line of Schultz
options.d: It is also known as polymazia

mcqs.explanation: Poland's syndrome is not associated with accessory breast tissue . It is associated with amastia with the absence of the sternal portion of the pectoralis major muscle . Polymastia or polymazia is a congenital anomaly in which there is presence of accessory breast tissue . Axilla is the most frequent site for accessory breast tissue along the line of Schultz . Accessory breast tissue develops along the milk line/ line of Schultz , which appears by the 6th week of embryonic development . The milk line extends from the axilla to the inguinal region. It is ectodermal in origin. The image below shows the milk line/ line of Schultz :The image below shows accessory breast tissue in the right axilla:193

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: All of the following statements about amazia are true except _____.

options.a: Amazia may be associated with Poland's syndrome
options.b: Amazia is the absence of the nipple .
options.c: Amazia is often the result of surgical intervention.
options.d: Amazia may be caused by radiation therapy .

mcqs.explanation: Amazia is a condition wherein the breast tissue is absent, but the nipple -areolar complex is present . It results from iatrogenic causes such as radiation, excision of a misdiagnosed infantile or childhood mass that actually represented breast buds or incision and drainage of a suspected abscess . Note : Amastia is the congenital absence of the breast and nipple . Athelia is the absence of the nipple .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: Which of the following will you not see in a patient with Poland's syndrome?

options.a: Athelia with the absence of the pectoralis major
options.b: Amastia with the absence of pectoralis major

mcqs.explanation: Athelia with absence of pectoralis major is not associated with Poland's syndrome. Poland's syndrome is associated with unilateral: • Amastia with the absence of the sternal portion of the pectoralis major muscle • Abnormalities of the chest wall muscles • Loss of costal cartilage • Digital abnormalities such as brachysyndactyly , which is the abnormal shortness of the fingers or toes combined with webbing between the adjacent digits In some cases , associated skeletal abnormalities, such as underdeveloped or absent upper ribs, underdeveloped forearm bones, and elevation of the shoulder blade (Sprengel deformity ) may also be present . Note : Poland's syndrome is a constellation of anomalies with varying clinical presentations . Patients with this syndrome can present with amazia (absence of one or both of the mammary glands) or amastia (complete absence of breast tissue , nipple , and areola) in addition to any or all194 of the above-mentioned abnormalities.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman presents to the clinic with pain over the lateral aspect of her right breast for the past 5 days. Examination finding is as shown in the image. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Mondor's disease . The image shows the presence of a subcutaneous cord and a narrow shallow groove along the side of the cord. Mondor's disease is the thrombophlebitis of the superficial veins of the breast and anterior chest wall. The most commonly involved vein is the lateral thoracic vein. Patients usually present with pain along the lateral chest wall and a tender , firm cord below the breast. It is a benign condition and gets resolved on its own within 4-6 weeks . Warm compresses and anti-inflammatory medicines can be used to reduce pain. If the symptoms persist despite medications , the affected segment of the vein can be excised . Option A: Tietze's syndrome is a benign inflammation of one or more costal cartilages . Option B: Zuska disease is the subcutaneous abscess of the breast tissue beneath the areola of the nipple . It is also called a subareolar abscess . Option D: Stewart –Treves Syndrome is characterized by lymphangiosarcoma in chronic long-standing lymphedema following mastectomy .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the commonest cause of pathological nipple discharge in a non-lactating woman?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of nipple discharge in a non-lactating woman is duct ectasia . The discharge is usually black or greenish in color. Option B: Intraductal papilloma is the most common cause of bloody nipple discharge . It is a true polyp of the epithelium -lined ducts of the breast. Contrary to what one might expect , they are not associated with an increased risk of breast cancer. Option C: Paget 's disease of the breast can present with discharge from the surface of the nipple .195 Option D: Galactorrhea is the milk production from breasts unrelated to pregnancy or lactation.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: A chronic smoker presented with complaints of intermittent discharge from bilateral nipples for the past few months. On compression of her breast during the examination, a discharge was observed as shown below . Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The most likely diagnosis of a patient with greenish discharge from multiple ducts is duct ectasia . Duct ectasia is the dilatation of breast ducts . It is the most common cause of nipple discharge in non-lactating women. This condition is associated with smoking and diabetes . The initial stage of this disease consists of dilatation of one or more lactiferous ducts . These ducts get filled with stagnant brown or green -colored secretions . In the later stages , the accumulation of fluid in the lactiferous ducts leads to infection and inflammation, causing periductal mastitis. Patients may present with nipple discharge , abscess, fistula , or nipple retraction. Treatment includes : • Initial stages - oral antibiotics, needle aspiration, or incision and drainage of the abscess • Recurrent episodes - Hadfield operation (cone excision of multiple ducts ) • A single duct involvement - microdochectomy .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: What is the best method of management in a patient with recurrent episodes of multiple duct ectasia?

options.c: Wide excision involving the affected ducts

mcqs.explanation: The best method of management in a patient with multiple duct ectasia is to perform Hadfield 's operation. This operation consists of the excision of all the major lactiferous ducts . The initial stages of duct ectasia can be managed by oral antibiotics, needle aspiration, or incision and drainage of the abscess . Recurrent episodes of infection are best managed by Hadfield operation. If a single duct is involved, then microdochectomy is performed .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: Amongst the following , the most common cause of blood-stained nipple discharge from a single duct is:
mcqs.explanation: Ductal papilloma is the most common cause of blood-stained nipple discharge from a single duct . Solitary intraductal papillomas are true polyps of the ducts which are usually small (<1 cm) but may grow to 4-5 cm. They are often associated with bloody nipple discharge . They do not have malignant potential . Treatment is by excision. Note : The most common cause of blood-stained discharge from multiple ducts is carcinoma .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: A probe is inserted into the duct from which the nipple discharge is emerging . A tennis racquet incision is made and the flap is dissected to reach the duct . The duct is then excised . This procedure is known as?

options.d: Wide excision of the lactiferous duct.

mcqs.explanation: Microdochectomy is the excision of the entire lactiferous duct (single duct disease ). It is done for duct papilloma. Microdochectomy :196 • In a duct papilloma where no palpable mass is present , the duct is expressed to observe the discharge. • A fine probe or stiff nylon suture is gently inserted into the duct , and the probe is secured to the nipple skin using silk sutures to prevent displacement during the procedure . • A tennis racquet shaped incision is made to elevate the skin flaps , and the duct with the probe is excised along with the skin flap for 5 cm until the papilloma is identified (The papilloma will always be located within 5 cm from the duct orifice). • The wound is closed without a drain, and a compression bandage is applied . It is ideal to rule out DCIS by frozen section biopsy . Cone excision and wide excision are done under major duct excision (Adair-Haldfield operation). It is done for duct ectasias with multiple duct involvement and multiple papillomas .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: Which of the following aberration of normal development and involution of breast tissue is present in patients with fibroadenoma?
mcqs.explanation: In fibroadenoma, aberration of normal lobular development is present . It arises from hyperplasia of a single lobule and presents as a well -circumscribed, smooth, firm, non-tender , solitary, freely mobile mass (mouse in the breast). It is a biphasic tumor consisting of fibroblastic stroma and epithelium -lined gland. ANDI Classification of benign breast disorders:Normal Disorders Early reproductive years (15- 25 yrs) Lobular development Fibroadenoma Stromal development Adolescent hypertrophy (Gig antomastia) Nipple eversion Nipple inversion (subareolar abscess , Mammary duct fistu la) Later reproductive years (25- 40 yrs) Cyclical changes in menstrua tion Cyclical mastalgia Involution (35-55 yrs) Lobular involution Macrocysts , sclerosing lesion s Duct involution Dilation (duct ectasia )Scleros is (nipple retraction) Epithelial turnover Epithelial hyperplasia (with a typia )197

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: A 19-year-old girl presents with a lump in her right breast for the past 6 months. On examination , the lump is around 1 x1 cm in size, firm, and freely movable on the breast tissue . Ultrasound shows the presence of a circumscribed oval lobulated mass. Which of the following is not true regarding the given condition?

options.a: Peak incidence is in second decade
options.d: It is a form of ANDI

mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario is suggestive of fibroadenoma. Mammography may show the presence of popcorn calcification. Eggshell calcification can be seen in traumatic fat necrosis. Fibroadenoma is a form of aberrations of normal development and involution of the breast (ANDI). The most common age group affected is 15-25 years (early reproductive period ) with a peak incidence in the second decade . It arises from hyperplasia of a single lobule and presents as a well -circumscribed, smooth, firm, non-tender, solitary, freely mobile mass (mouse in the breast). It is a biphasic tumor consisting of fibroblastic stroma and epithelium -lined gland. Excision is not advised unless there is suspicious histology on FNAC. Giant fibroadenoma is more than 5cm in size and is common in adolescent girls. It requires excision by submammary incision. The image below shows popcorn calcification on mammography:

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: A giant fibroadenoma has a diameter greater than _____
mcqs.explanation: Giant fibroadenomas are over 5 cm in diameter and occasionally occur during puberty . They are often rapidly growing but are similar to smaller fibroadenomas and are enucleated through a submammary incision.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman presented with a lump in the left breast as shown in the image below . Biopsy done revealed increased stromal cellularity with typical leaflike architecture . Which of the following is false about this condition?

options.c: Treatment is wide excision with margin
options.d: Originates from hormonally responsive stromal cells of the breast

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and histopathology report point to malignant cystosarcoma phyllodes , which metastasize via the bloodstream . Metastasis to lymph nodes is rare.198 Phyllodes tumor also known as a sero-cystic disease of Brodie or cystosarcoma phyllodes , originates from hormonally responsive stromal cells of the breast. It is usually a benign condition and affects women >40 years of age, but can be seen in younger women. Sometimes , may develop malignant transformation . Clinical features : • Large, sometimes massive, with an unevenly bosselated surface • Ulceration of overlying skin occurs because of pressure necrosis • Remains mobile on the chest wall There is no role of FNAC in phyllodes tumor. Histopathology of the lump biopsy shows increased stromal cellularity , overgrowth, and typical leaflike architecture .Tumors are treated by excision with margins of at least 2 cm to prevent local recurrence. Large or malignant phyllodes tumors may require a mastectomy . The axillary dissection is not recommended because axillary lymph nodes rarely get involved. Note : Malignant phyllodes tumors contain liposarcomatous or rhabdomyosarcomatous elements rather than fibrosarcomatous elements .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: A breastfeeding mother presented to the clinic with fever and breast pain for the past 2 days. The affected breast appears as shown in the image below . There is extreme tenderness on palpation . Which of the following is the most common source for the organism causing this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of lactational mastitis. The most common source of infection is from the infant's nasopharynx. Lactational mastitis is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus present in the infant's nasopharynx. The organism enters the breast tissue through cracked nipples and multiplies in the stagnant breast milk. Patients present with fever with a firm, red, tender , and swollen quadrant of the unilateral breast.199 Painful breasts must be managed by the use of analgesics . Breastfeeding should be continued if the pain is less severe . Antibiotics like flucloxacillin , co-amoxiclav are used to treat the infection . If the patient develops an abscess , then the abscess has to be drained by aspiration or incision.Bacterial mastitis Breast abscess Condition Localized inflammation due t o ascending infection or infec tion due to milk stasis Occurs as a complication of mastitis, with pus formation Symptoms Dull pain Throbbing pain Signs (if any) Tenderness , erythema Point tenderness , erythema , i nduration of skin (if chronic) lymphadenopathy ,fluctuation test +ve Managemen t Analgesics , antibiotics Analgesics , aspiration of pus , antibiotics

mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: A female patient presents with a breast abscess . An aspiration was attempted under antibiotic cover which failed to reveal any aspirate. What is the next step in management?

options.d: Stop antibiotics as no aspirate was collected

mcqs.explanation: In a patient with a breast abscess , the next step after a failed aspiration is to attempt aspiration once again under antibiotic cover. Incision and drainage is not preferred , as it can potentially interfere with breastfeeding , and delicate structures such as ducts , lobules , and tubules may be injured, possibly leading to a non-healing milk fistula . A breast abscess is a complication of acute mastitis, which is more common in new mothers at the beginning of lactation (lactational mastitis). Non-lactational mastitis is more common in diabetic , immunosuppressed people and people predisposed by duct ectasia and periareolar infections . Clinical features of a breast abscess include : • Fever and malaise • Localized pain and tenderness • Redness and swelling of the affected breast • Positive fluctuation test .200 An ultrasonogram of the affected breast is performed to confirm the abscess , and treatment proceeds as follows : • Analgesics , antipyretics , and breast support for pain and fever relief . • Aspiration is performed under antibiotic cover, and the pus is cultured . If aspiration proves unsuccessful , it should be reattempted after a few days. • Incision and drainage should be considered in cases of: • Mastitis unresponsive to antibiotics for 48 hours. • Brawny induration. • Progressive mastitis with persistent fever Note :Bacterial mastitis Breast abscess Condition Localized inflammation due t o ascending infection or infec tion due to milk stasis Occurs as a complication of mastitisPus formation Symptoms Dullpain Throbbingpain Signs (if any) TendernessErythema Point tendernessErythemaIn duration of skin(if chronic)Ly mphadenopathyFluctuation t est +vePus pointmay be prese nt Managemen t AnalgesicsAntibiotics (Diclox acillin500 mg every 6 hours orally; Erythromycin if allergi c to penicillin )Adequate brea st support AnalgesicsAdequate breast su pportAspiration of Pus under antibiotic cover; repeated as pirations if requiredIncision & drainage201

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: A 37- year-old woman presented to the clinic with a breast lump. Clinical examination and ultrasound revealed the presence of a single large cyst in her right breast. On aspirating the cyst , you find blood-stained fluid . What will be the next best step in the management of this patient ?

options.a: Wait for refilling and reattempt aspiration
options.d: Perform mammogram to rule out carcinoma

mcqs.explanation: The next step in management is the excision of the cyst . Treatment of breast cyst : • If the aspirate is clear (non-blood stained ) or if the cyst resolves completely then no further treatment is required. • If the aspirate is blood-stained or if the cyst recurs, then a core biopsy or local excision should be performed. The resulting tissue should be sent for histopathology for the exclusion of cystadenocarcinoma, especially in elderly women.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: Physiological gynecomastia is not seen in which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Physiological gynecomastia is not seen in obese males. In obese men, increased fat deposition over the breasts is referred to as pseudo -gynecomastia . Gynecomastia is defined as �o 2 cm subareolar breast tissue . It can be physiological or pathological. Physiologic gynecomastia occurs during three phases of life : • Neonatal period • Adolescence • Senescence Common to each of these phases is an excess of circulating estrogens in relation to circulating testosterone . Neonatal gynecomastia is caused by the action of placental estrogens on neonatal breast tissues . In adolescence , there is an excess of estradiol relative to testosterone . In senescence , the circulating testosterone level falls, resulting in relative hyperestrogenism .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old woman has been experiencing breast pain for the past 6 months. The pain is present just before her menstrual period. Breast examination and mammography are normal . All of the following medications /supplements can help in reducing the pain except :
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario is suggestive of cyclical mastalgia. Caffeine is not useful in reducing pain. On the contrary, caffeine has to be avoided to reduce pain. Medications that can be used to treat mastalgia are evening primrose oil, danazol, and tamoxifen.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: A breastfeeding mother presented to the clinic with a gradually progressive painless breast lump. On examination, a well -circumscribed and freely mobile mass was palpable . USG showed a solitary, well -defined , anechoic lesion with thin, echogenic walls . Aspiration revealed a white fluid . What is the best treatment option for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of galactocele . The best treatment option for this condition is USG guided fine-needle aspiration. A galactocele is a milk-filled cavity in the breast of a woman who is usually lactating. It can be caused due to lactation problems , prolactin stimulation by drugs, or duct obstruction.202 It presents as a palpable , round, well -circumscribed, and freely mobile mass with no fever, pain, or inflammation. It is usually subareolar and unilateral. USG guided fine-needle aspiration is both diagnostic and therapeutic . It will show thick milky white secretion confirming the diagnosis. Aspiration resolves galactocele in most cases . Surgery is done for infected cysts or recurrent cases . Antibiotic therapy is not needed if the galactocele is not infected .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old female footballer presented with complaints of a lump in the breast. On examination , a hard, irregular lump was palpated . Mammography revealed calcifications as shown below . Which of the following conditions is she most likely to have?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, palpable mass and egg -shell calcifications on mammography in a young woman are suggestive of fat necrosis. It mimics breast carcinoma clinically and mammographically but has no malignant potential .203

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: Which one of the following pathological features has a higher risk of developing into invasive breast carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: Atypical hyperplasia has a higher risk of developing into invasive breast carcinoma .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: A woman with a family history of breast and ovarian cancers underwent genetic testing . She is found to have a BRCA1 gene mutation. Which of the following is she at risk of developing ?
mcqs.explanation: Individuals with BRCA1 mutations are likely to develop triple receptor -negative and high-grade breast carcinomas.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: Which of the following does not increase the risk of breast carcinoma in women?
mcqs.explanation: Early age of first pregnancy, breastfeeding , and multiparity are protective factors for carcinoma of the breast. This is due to a reduction in the overall number of ovulatory cycles thereby reducing the duration of estrogen 's action on the breast tissues .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: The most common location of breast carcinoma is the _______.
mcqs.explanation: The upper outer quadrant of the breast has a greater volume of tissue and is the most common site of breast carcinoma .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: A woman presented to the clinic with redness and itching over the left breast as shown in the image below . Histopathology showed large pale vacuolated cells with round nuclei in the epithelium . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical picture and histology are suggestive of Paget 's disease of the breast. Paget 's disease is a rare type of cancer involving the nipple -areolar complex , often with an underlying in-situ or invasive ductal carcinoma . It presents as a chronic, eczematous eruption of the nipple which may progress to ulceration. Paget disease of the breast is often mistaken for eczema. A nipple biopsy specimen of Paget 's disease will show a population of cells that are identical to the underlying malignant cells . The presence of large, pale , vacuolated cells (Paget cells ) with round or oval nuclei are pathognomonic for this condition.210 Depending on the type and extent of underlying malignancy, it can be treated with lumpectomy or mastectomy.Paget 's disease Eczema Lateralit y Unilateral Bilateral Age gro up Menopausal wo men Lactating women Edges Distinct Indistinct Vesicles Absent Present Nipple Usually destroy ed Usually intact Lump Usually present No underlying lu mpNote : Histologically , Paget 's disease can be confused with superficial spreading melanoma, particularly if they have incorporated melanin from adjacent epidermis . Paget 's disease shows positive immunostaining with carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), while superficial spreading melanoma is positive for S-100 antigen.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: Which is the most common variant of breast carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: Invasive ductal carcinoma (not otherwise specified ) is the most common variant of breast carcinoma . It is also known as infiltrating ductal carcinoma .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true regarding breast carcinoma ?

options.a: Cutaneous oedema in inflammatory carcinoma is the result of blockage of the sub-dermal lymphatics with carcinoma cells
options.b: Mucinous carcinomas are usually hormone negative
options.c: Calcifications are frequently associated with ductal carcinoma in situ
options.d: Lobular carcinoma in situ is multi centric and bilateral

mcqs.explanation: 211 Mucinous carcinoma is usually hormone-positive (90%). It is also called colloid carcinoma . It is a low-grade tumor with a good prognosis. It typically presents as a bulky mass in the elderly . Option A: Pathologic hallmark of inflammatory carcinoma is a painful, swollen breast, which is warm with cutaneous edema due to blockage of subdermal lymphatics with carcinoma cells . Option C: Calcification is usually associated with ductal carcinoma in-situ (DCIS). It is the most common malignancy detected in screening mammograms . Option D: Lobular carcinoma in situ (LCIS) is mainly multicentric (sometimes multifocal ) and bilateral.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: Arrange the following subtypes of breast carcinomas according to the best to worst prognosis?
mcqs.explanation: Tubular carcinoma has the best prognosis. Inflammatory carcinoma has the worst prognosis. Order of breast carcinomas from best to worst prognosis: • Tubular carcinoma (Best prognosis) • Adenocystic • Cribriform carcinoma • Papillary carcinoma • Medullary carcinoma • Invasive lobular carcinoma • Invasive ductal carcinoma (NOS)* • Inflammatory carcinoma breast (Worst prognosis) NOS- Not otherwise specified

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old woman presents with complaints of swelling of the right breast over the past 15 days. On examination, there was local rise of temperature , and the swelling was mobile over the chest wall. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, the rapid onset of the disease and the examination findings are suggestive of inflammatory carcinoma of the breast. Inflammatory breast cancer is the most aggressive subtype of breast cancer. It mimics acute mastitis. The hallmark of inflammatory breast carcinoma is the diffuse tumor involvement of the dermal lymphatics within the breast and the overlying skin, often without a discrete underlying tumor mass (peau d' orange appearance). The patient presents with rapidly progressive swelling of the breast, warmth, erythema and edema. A breast lump may or may not be present . A diagnosis of inflammatory breast carcinoma should be suspected when a patient with rapidly progressive swelling with inflammatory skin changes does not respond to antibiotics. The imaging features with ultrasound and a mammograph is non-specific due to the underlying erythema and edema . A biopsy should be done to confirm the diagnosis. Treatment includes combined-modality treatment :212 • Neoadjuvant chemotherapy • Mastectomy • Radiation therapy • Hormonal therapy - for ER-positive tumors • Trastuzumab for HER-2-positive tumors Option B: Giant fibroadenomas occasionally occur during puberty . These are benign solid encapsulated slow -growing tumors over 5 cm in diameter . It presents as a painless lump in the breast. They are managed by excision via a submammary incision. Option C: Phyllodes tumors usually occur in women over the age of 40 years but can appear in younger women. Phyllodes tumor is mostly benign even though it is also called cystosarcoma phyllodes . It presents as a large tumor with an unevenly bosselated surface . They are usually mobile over the chest wall despite their large size. This tumor does not infiltrate the skin. Nipple retraction is not seen in this condition. Benign lesions can be treated with enucleation or wide local excision. Massive tumours, recurrent tumours and malignant lesions are treated with a mastectomy . Option D: Galactocele are the most common benign breast lesions in lactating women. It is a cystic enlargement of the mammary gland containing milk. They are mostly detected during lactation or in the third trimester of pregnancy but rarely, may also present after stopping breastfeeding . Clinically, the mass is usually firm and non-tender and presents as a solid tumour-like lesion on physical examination. The patient usually notes the lesion during lactation or some period after lactation. Needle aspiration, followed by excision should it recur, is the standard method of treating galactocele .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: A postmenopausal lady came to the clinic with complaints of breast pain and a lump in her right breast for the past 2 months. On examination, the breast appears as shown in the image. What is the most likely cause for this finding?
mcqs.explanation: In the given image, the orange peel -like appearance , also called as peau d'orange is caused by cutaneous lymphatic edema , due to the obstruction of subcutaneous lymphatics . It is the hallmark of inflammatory carcinoma . Option A: Infiltration of Cooper 's ligaments leads to dimpling of the skin. Option C: Infiltration of the lactiferous ducts leads to nipple retraction. Cancer-en-cuirasse is an aggressive form of cancer, where there is cutaneous and subcutaneous infiltration of the cancer cells . Note : While Peau d'orange indicates skin involvement, dimpling of the skin and nipple retraction d o not indicate skin involvement.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: A middle -aged woman presented with a painless lump in the breast. Mammography done showed suspicious microcalcifications. USG-guided core biopsy revealed large cells with cytoplasmic mucoid globules and neighborhood calcifications . There is no invasion into the basement membrane and fibrovascular stroma. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of large cells with cytoplasmic mucoid globules with an intact basement membrane, and neighborhood calcifications are characteristic of lobular carcinoma in situ (LCIS).213 Lobular carcinoma in-situ is usually detected as an incidental finding on evaluation of either a mass lesion or abnormalities on mammography. The slide below shows cytoplasmic mucoid globules seen in lobular carcinoma in situ.Option A: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) can have various histological appearances like solid, comedo , papillary cribriform , etcOption B: Histology of Paget 's disease of the breast shows the presence of large pale vacuolated cells (Paget cells ) in the rete pegs of the epithelium .214 Option D: Histology of phyllodes tumor consists of nodules of proliferating stromal cells , that are covered by epithelium . This resembles a leaf and is hence termed as phyllodes .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: Which of the following is most likely in a woman with bilateral and multicentric breast lumps?
mcqs.explanation: Bilaterality and multicentricity are most commonly associated with lobular carcinoma in situ (LCIS ). LCIS occurs bilaterally in 50 - 70% of cases . Multicentricity is seen in 60 - 90% of patients with LCIS. Multicentricity refers to the occurrence of second breast cancer outside the breast quadrant of the primary cancer (or at least 4 cm away). Multifocality refers to the occurrence of a second cancer within the same breast quadrant as the primary cancer (or within 4 cm of it).215

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: An annual screening mammogram done for a middle -aged woman showed clusters of microcalcifications. Stereotactic trucut biopsy revealed a comedo growth pattern. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of microcalcifications on mammography and comedo pattern on histology is suggestive of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). Treatment: • Breast conservation surgery with radiotherapy or, • Simple mastectomy - least loco-regional recurrence • No role of chemotherapy • If ER, PR +ve- hormonal therapy216 Comedo subtype refers to the presence of necrosis. It implies that the tumor cells are growing rapidly and the blood vessel is not able to supply all the malignant cells . On the contrary, non-comedo subtype implies that the tumor is growing slowly and the blood vessel is able to supply all the cells . Therefore, the comedo subtypes are of high-grade DCIS.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: A woman with BRCA1 gene mutation presented with lumps in both breasts and enlarged axillary lymphadenopathy . She gives a history of breast cancer in her sister. MRI and trucut biopsy done confirmed the diagnosis of medullary carcinoma of the breast. Which of the following statements is true regarding the given condition?

options.a: Lymph node enlargement can be due to reactive hyperplasia
options.b: It is a slow growing tumor
options.c: Tamoxifen can be used in the treatment
options.d: Has poorer prognosis than invasive lobular carcinoma

mcqs.explanation: Medullary carcinoma of the breast is associated with intense lymphocyte proliferation. Therefore, the lymph node enlargement can be due to reactive hyperplasia rather than the spread of the cancer cells to the lymph nodes . Medullary carcinoma is a common type of breast cancer associated with BRCA1 gene mutation. Bilateral tumors are common when family history is present . The tumor can enlarge rapidly due to necrosis and hemorrhage. The majority of the tumors are triple -negative (ER/PR/Her-2 negative ). Histopathology consists of: • A dense lymphoreticular infiltration composed predominantly of lymphocytes and plasma cells • A sheet -like growth pattern of anaplastic cells with absent ductal or lobular differentiation It has a better prognosis than invasive ductal or invasive lobular carcinoma .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: A male patient who presented with a lump in his right breast is diagnosed to have breast carcinoma . Which of the following is true regarding the given condition?

options.a: The prognosis is worse than in females
options.b: Infiltrating ductal carcinoma is the most common type
options.d: Tamoxifen is not effective in treatment

mcqs.explanation: Infiltrating ductal carcinoma is the most common type of breast cancer seen in men. Breast cancer in men accounts for less than 1% of all breast cancers. The peak incidence is between 60-70 years of age . Majority of the patients present with a hard mass in the breast. Important risk factors are:217 • BRCA2 mutation • Radiation exposure • Estrogen therapy • Testicular feminizing syndrome • Klinefelter syndrome Diagnosis of male breast carcinoma is similar to females which involves a clinical examination, imaging, and tissue biopsy . Grading, treatment , and prognosis are the same as female breast cancer. The majority of male breast cancers are hormone receptor -positive and hence tamoxifen is used in the treatment .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Carcinoma Breast - Risk Factors and Types
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old woman is worried about developing breast cancer. Her mother and sister had developed breast cancer at the age of 30 years and 32 years respectively . She has 2 daughters . After evaluation, she is found to have a BRCA -1 gene mutation. Which of the following methods will you suggest for the maximum risk reduction of developing carcinoma breast in this patient ?

options.a: Close surveillance with MRI every 6 months

mcqs.explanation: Prophylactic mastectomy with bilateral salpingo -oophorectomy will provide maximum risk reduction in this patient with a complete family, a positive gene mutation, and positive family history. Breast cancer risk reduction techniques : • Lifestyle modification: Low-calorie diet , daily exercise , no smoking, no drinking , etc . • More frequent screening every 6-12 months with mammogram +- MRI • Chemoprevention : Preferred in women >35 years of age in patients who are ER/PR positive . Given for 5-10 years. • SERMS (selective estrogen receptor modulators) - Tamoxifen and raloxifene - have adverse effects . If a patient on tamoxifen develops abnormal uterine bleeding , the drug needs to be stopped . • Aromatase Inhibitors (AIs): Better tolerated than SERMs have a low risk of cardiovascular and endometrial complications . They are used only in post -menopausal women. • Risk -reduction surgeries : done in patients with gene mutations or patients with first-degree relatives with breast cancers. Provides >90% risk -reduction . Preferred in patients who have completed their family. Best results when done < 40 years of age . • Bilateral mastectomy • Salpingo-oophorectomy : preferred in patients with BRCA1 /2 mutations to prevent the risk of ovarian cancer too.218

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the recommended age for starting screening mammography?
mcqs.explanation: The recommended age for women to start annual screening mammography is 40 years of age . • Until 44 years of age , it is her individual choice to decide on whether she wants screening mammography or not. • For ages between 45 and 49 years, it is mandatory to get annual breast screening done. • After the age of 50 years, it is advised that women get a second yearly screening done.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding screening mammography?

options.a: Sensitivity of the test will increase with her age .
options.b: It is best performed in the 2nd half of her menstrual cycle .
options.c: Mediolateral oblique view will show the greatest volume of her breast tissue .
options.d: Craniocaudal view will provide better visualization of the medial aspect of her breast.

mcqs.explanation: Mammography is best performed in the 1st half of the menstrual cycle , as breast tissue is less dense in the follicular phase . Also, in the 2nd half of the menstrual cycle , since ovulation occurs and there is a chance for pregnancy, the radiation can potentially affect the embryo. The sensitivity of mammography increases with age , as the breast tissue becomes less dense . It involves 2 standard views: • Mediolateral oblique (MLO) view- covers a greater volume of breast tissue , including the upper outer quadrant and the axillary tail of Spence . • Craniocaudal (CC) view- provides better visualization of the medial aspect of the breast. Mammography uses low-voltage , high-amperage X-rays. The radiation dose from mammography is around 0.1 cGy per study .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old woman underwent screening mammography. Which of the following findings in her mammogram is least suggestive of a malignancy?
mcqs.explanation: Macrocalcification in a lesion is least suggestive of a malignancy. It is commonly seen in benign breast disorders. Microcalcification (<0.5 mm in diameter ) is suggestive of malignancy.
