A few weeks later, she complains of vague abdominal pain and progressive abdominal distension . Ultrasound reveals the presence of ascites . CT reveals a thickened peritoneum , multiple loculated fluid collections , and scalloping of the liver and spleen margin. Which of the following statements is false regarding her condition?

options.a: The patient is most likely suffering from disseminated peritoneal carcinomatosis
options.b: The histology of the appendiceal tumor is an important predictor of survival
options.c: Cytoreductive surgery with IPHC maybe required for management
options.d: This condition can also occur in patients with ovarian neoplasms

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of a patient with mucinous cystadenoma appendix and imaging findings are suggestive of pseudomyxoma peritonei . Pseudomyxoma peritonei refers to a condition of mucinous ascites arising due to the rupture of a mucinous tumor of appendix or ovary . It most commonly occurs in patients between 40-50 years of age . They are often asymptomatic or present with non-specific complaints like abdominal pain and distension . Physical examination may reveal ascites with non shifting dullness and rarely, a palpable abdominal mass. CT scan may reveal accumulation of mucinous material and scalloped indentation of the visceral surfaces of the liver and spleen . The peritoneal surfaces may be thickened due to the solid components of the tumor. The histology of the primary appendiceal tumor is an important predictor of survival . Management consists of extensive resection of the tumor (cytoreduction ) and intraperitoneal heated chemotherapy (IPHC). Surgical management may include omentectomy , resection of the peritoneum and involved organs, appendectomy or a right hemicolectomy .562

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old woman underwent a screening colonoscopy . A single polyp is found, resected , and sent for histopathological examination. Which of the following biopsy findings will have the highest risk of malignancy?
mcqs.explanation: Villous adenoma has the highest risk of malignancy. Adenomatous polyps can be tubular, tubulovillous , and villous adenomas. Among these , tubular adenoma has the least risk and villous adenoma has the highest risk of malignancy.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: During a colonoscopy on a 58-year-old female patient , a smooth nodular polyp is found and excised . The microscopic image is given. Choose the incorrect statement regarding the polyp .

options.c: Usually seen in the 6th and 7th decade of life
options.d: Malignant transformation takes place within 5 years

mcqs.explanation: Hyperplastic polyps , as seen in the histological picture , do not have malignant potential . Elongated crypts , i.e., serrated (saw-toothed ) or star-shaped appearance , is a characteristic feature of a hyperplastic polyp . They are the most common type of colorectal polyps and are usually seen in the 6th and 7th decade of life . More than 90% occur in rectosigmoid region.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: The biopsy of a polyp reported dysplasia up to the colonic submucosa . Classify this lesion using Haggitt 's classification :
mcqs.explanation: According to Haggitt 's classification , a polyp invading the submucosa comes under level 4.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old patient undergoes a screening colonoscopy after his brother was diagnosed with colorectal cancer. Which of the following , if detected , does not indicate a risk of developing colon cancer?

options.a: Villous adenomas in the ascending colon
options.b: More than 100 polyps in the transverse and descending colon
options.c: Inflammatory polyps in the sigmoid colon and rectum
options.d: Sessile serrated adenomatous polyps in the sigmoid colon

mcqs.explanation: Inflammatory polyps are not premalignant.576 Inflammatory polyps (pseudopolyps ) are found in cases of: • Inflammatory bowel disease (most common) • Amebic colitis • Ischemic colitis • Schistosomal colitis Microscopic examination shows islands of normal , regenerating mucosa (the polyp ) surrounded by areas of mucosal loss.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 12 -year-old is brought to the emergency with features of intestinal obstruction. An ultrasound reveals a target sign, suggesting intussusception . On closer examination, her palm and oral mucosa are spotted with multiple 1-2 mm blue -gray macules . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The patient most likely has Peutz–Jeghers syndrome. It is characterized by hamartomatous polyps of the intestinal tract (more commonly small intestine ) and hyperpigmentation of the buccal mucosa, lips, and digits . In the given clinical scenario, the patient has had an intestinal intussusception . The numerous polyps in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome often serve as a lead point. Option A: Turcot syndrome constitutes colorectal polyps and brain tumors (including cerebellar medulloblastoma and glioblastomas ) Option B: Lynch syndrome is also called hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer (HNPCC). It is due to defective mismatch repair (MMR) of DNA. Option D: Cowden syndrome is characterized by polyps of the stomach or colon, macrocephaly and benign tumors of thyroid, breast, and uterus .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Ophthalmoscopy performed on a 14-year-old boy had the given incidental finding. Family history revealed that his grandfather had colon cancer and an aunt was diagnosed with endometrial carcinoma . Genetic testing confirmed APC gene mutation. Which of the following is false about his condition?

options.a: Condition can be passed on to his daughter in the future
options.b: Mutation of APC gene is on chromosome

mcqs.explanation: 577 The given image showing a pigmented retina, the patient 's family history and APC gene mutation is suggestive of familial adenomatous polyposis . Familial adenomatous polyposis is due to the mutation of APC gene located on the long arm of chromosome 5 (5q21 ), not 15. Familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) is autosomal dominant. It is characterized by the presence of >100 adenomatous polyps in colon and rectum. It usually manifests by the late 2nd or early 3rd decade . Although it accounts for 1% of all colorectal carcinoma , the risk of development of cancer is 100 %. CHRPE (Congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epthelium ) is the earliest extra-colonic manifestation of FAP, present in up to 75 % of patients .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: All of the following are gastrointestinal manifestations seen in patients with FAP except :

options.b: Fundal gland hyperplasia in gastric polyp

mcqs.explanation: Esophageal carcinoma is not associated with FAP Familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) is associated with gastric and duodenal polyps in approximately 50% of the affected individuals. Most of the gastric polyps represent fundic gland hyperplasia and have limited malignant potential . Duodenal polyps are adenomatous in nature and premalignant. Patients with FAP have an increased risk for duodenal ampullary cancer.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a component of Gardner's syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Gardner's syndrome does not include brain tumors. Components of Gardner's syndrome: • Osteomas : most common manifestation, most commonly in the mandible • Polyposis colon • Dental anomalies (supernumerary tooth , absent tooth , impacted tooth ) • Epidermal inclusion cysts • Desmoid tumors Note : Turcot's syndrome includes brain tumor and colorectal polyps .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common presentation of abdominal desmoid tumor?
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The most common presentation of an abdominal desmoid tumor is an abdominal mass.578 Desmoid tumors, also known as fibromatosis, aggressive fibromatosis or desmoid -type fibromatosis are locally aggressive tumors that lack metastatic potential . Desmoid tumors can be sporadic in origin or associated with familial adenomatous polyposis . These tumors arise from fibro-aponeurotic tissue and typically are manifested as a slowly growing mass. They present as firm, non-painful, non-tender masses in the abdominal wall, shoulder, hip and limbs, mesentery , and pelvis. They are also associated with trauma, pregnancy, and oral contraceptive usage . The investigation of choice for a desmoid tumor is MRI. It is superior to CT in defining the pattern and the extent of involvement and can determine recurrence after surgery. Diagnosis is established by a biopsy with immunohistochemistry , which stains positive for beta -catenin, actin and vimentin, and negative for desmin, cytokeratin and S-100 . Treatment: • An initial observation is preferred for stable , asymptomatic , primary or recurrent desmoids , especially if surgery can cause high mortality. • Surgical resection with negative margin clearance is reserved for patients with small abdominal wall tumors associated with pain or an increase in size. • Tamoxifen and NSAIDs are used as first-line medical therapy . Other systemic treatment options are low-dose chemotherapy , tyrosinase kinase inhibitors, and full -dose chemotherapy • Radiotherapy is preferred for candidates unfit for surgery, patients refusing surgery and when surgical resection is associated with high morbidity.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 29-year-old man was brought to the hospital with a history of headache and vomiting for the past 7 days and an episode of a tonic-clonic seizure . The image of the MRI scan is shown below . Colonoscopy revealed numerous polyps in the colon and the rectum which were found to be adenomatous on biopsy . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: In the given clinical scenario, the patient has numerous adenomatous polyps and a tumor in the brain . Therefore the most likely diagnosis is Turcot's syndrome. It is a variant of familial adenomatous polyposis . Familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) is an autosomal dominant condition and is caused due to the mutation in the APC gene located on chromosome 5. Clinically, patients develop hundreds to thousands of adenomatous polyps in the colon and rectum . Some patients may also develop duodenal adenomas. The lifetime risk of developing colorectal carcinoma in these patients is 100 %. The treatment of the FAP includes total proctocolectomy with ileal pouch -anal anastomosis (IPAA ). Variants of FAP are : • Gardner 's syndrome- It is an autosomal dominant variant of FAP. In addition to colonic polyps the patients will have • Osteomas of the mandible or skull • Epidermal cysts • Soft tissue tumors like desmoid tumor579 • Turcot's syndrome- In addition to the colonic polyps the patients will have central nervous system tumors (primary brain tumors). Option D: Peutz-Jegher's syndrome is not related to familial adenomatous polyposis . It is an autosomal dominant disease characterized by • Pigmentation of the mouth and lips • Multiple hamartomatous polyps in the small and large intestine .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Colonoscopy and biopsy on a 35-year-old man revealed hundreds of adenomatous polyps in the entire descending and sigmoid colon. Options for prophylactic surgery are discussed . Which of the following procedures will reduce the occurrence of malignancy the most?

options.b: Total colectomy with ileal pouch -anal anastomosis
options.c: Total proctocolectomy with ileal pouch -anal anastomosis

mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario is diagnostic of familial adenomatous polyposis syndrome. To prevent an occurrence of cancer, total proctocolectomy with ileal pouch -anal anastomosis is the management of choice . This procedure is usually accompanied by resection of the rectal mucosa. Following surgery, the patient has to be routinely followed up for ileoanal-pouch surveillance. Upper GI endoscopy should also be performed to evaluate for the presence of duodenal adenomas.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man was recently diagnosed and treated for an autosomal dominant disorder. The gross specimen of his resected colon is given in the image. What is the initial step in screening his 9-year-old child?

options.a: Genetic testing for APC gene mutation
options.b: Genetic testing for MSH-6 gene mutation
options.c: Routine flexible sigmoidoscopy starting from 10 years of age
options.d: Routine colonoscopy starting from 10 years of age

mcqs.explanation: More than 100 colonic polyps are diagnostic of familial adenomatous polyposis syndrome and the initial step in screening the child syndrome is to perform genetic testing for APC gene mutation. If screening is positive , flexible sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy is done annually starting from 10 years of age . If the APC testing is negative , then the risk of developing colorectal carcinoma in the relative is similar to the general population . The screening can be started from 50 years of age .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which among the following is true about Amsterdam criteria?

options.b: At least 2 or more first-degree relatives affected
options.c: At least one case diagnosed before 50 years of age

mcqs.explanation: According to the Amsterdam criteria for hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC), at least one case should be diagnosed before 50 years of age . Option A: According to the Amsterdam criteria for a presumptive diagnosis of HNPCC, at least 2 (not 3) successive generations should be affected . Option B: According to the Amsterdam criteria for a presumptive diagnosis of HNPCC, at least 3 relatives (not 2) with at least one being first-degree relatives should be affected .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the most common extra-colonic cancer in patients with a mutation in MMR genes ?
mcqs.explanation: 580 Endometrial carcinoma is the most common extracolonic carcinoma in patients with mutated MMR genes. Autosomal dominant mutation in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes , such as hMLH1 , hMSH2, hMSH6, PMS1, and PMS2 lead to various cancers. This condition is known as Lynch Syndrome/HNPCC. Gastric and ovarian carcinoma are also commonly found.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which among the following is false about colorectal carcinoma in HNPCC?

options.a: The onset of cancer occurs early
options.b: The progression of the carcinoma is slow
options.c: Mucinous adenocarcinoma is the most common type
options.d: Tumors predominantly develop in right sided colon

mcqs.explanation: In hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC), there is accelerated tumor progression and normal tumor initiation. Accelerated tumor initiation is seen in familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP). In Hereditary Non-polyposis Colorectal Cancer (HNPCC), the onset of cancer is at a relatively young age (mean, 44 years). Proximal distribution is more common and nearly 70% of cancers are located in the right colon. Mucinous or poorly differentiated (signet cell ) adenocarcinoma predominate . There is an increased number of synchronous and metachronous cancers. The outcome after surgery is relatively good .581

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old man presented to the dermatologist 's office with multiple small bumps on his forehead . Excisional biopsy findings are suggestive of multiple small sebaceous adenomas. Detailed family history reveals that his grandfather and brother have colon cancer while his aunt was diagnosed with rectal cancer. Which syndrome should be suspected ?
mcqs.explanation: Multiple cutaneous sebaceous adenomas and a family history of various cancers are seen in Muir–Torre syndrome. Muir–Torre variant of hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC) may have: • Sebaceous adenomas • Keratoacanthomas • Sebaceous epitheliomas • Basal cell epitheliomas

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which criteria is used to select patients for microsatellite instability (MSI) testing ?
mcqs.explanation: Bethesda criteria is used to select patients for microsatellite instability testing . Microsatellites are regions of repeated DNA that change in length (show instability ) when mismatch repair is not functioning. Defects in mismatch repair genes (as in Lynch syndrome/HNPCC) leads to microsatellite instability . Amsterdam criteria is used for a presumptive diagnosis of HNPCC in a family. Because the Amsterdam criteria do not include some patients with known germline MMR gene mutations, another set of guidelines , known as the Bethesda guidelines , was established to help decide whether or not a patient should undergo further molecular testing to rule out HNPCC.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In which part of the colon does colorectal carcinoma most commonly develop ?
mcqs.explanation: 582 In the colon, colorectal carcinoma most commonly develops in the sigmoid colon. Overall, the most common site of colorectal carcinoma is the rectum. The sites of development of colorectal carcinoma in order of frequency are: • Rectum • Sigmoid colon • Caecum • Transverse colon • Ascending colon • Descending colon • Splenic flexure • Hepatic flexure

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following are risk factors for colon carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: Ulcerative colitis , familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), cholecystectomy , ureterosigmoidostomy, and smoking are risk factors for colon cancer.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following dietary recommendation puts patients at risk of developing colon cancer?
mcqs.explanation: High-calorie, low-fiber, and high-animal-fat diet as well as alcohol consumption increase the risk of colon cancer. Calcium, selenium , vitamins A, C, and E, carotenoids , and plant phenols are protective .583

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following colonoscopic findings has the highest risk of developing colorectal cancer?
mcqs.explanation: Sessile /flat polyps are at a higher risk of malignancy compared to pedunculated polyps . Multiple polyps increase the risk of malignancy. The probability of development of malignancy of a polyp depends on the following : • Gross appearance of lesion: Sessile polyps are at higher risk for malignancy than pedunculated tumors. • Histology : Villous > Tubulovillous > tubular • Size: Polyps of size >2 cm are at higher risk .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Mutations in which gene is responsible for malignant changes in late colonic adenomas?
mcqs.explanation: p53 mutation is responsible for the transformation of late adenoma to carcinoma . The earliest mutations in the adenoma-carcinoma sequence occur in the APC gene and the earliest phenotypic change is known as aberrant crypt formation. The most consistent genetic aberrations within these cells abnormally result in the formation of short proteins known as APC truncations. They occur in the mutational cluster region of the gene , an area responsible for \031-catenin binding.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correctly matched set regarding risk category and colon cancer screening recommendation?

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 61-year-old man presents with complaints of fatigue and shortness of breath. He has conjunctival pallor and has lost significant weight over 3 months. A CBC reveals low haemoglobin and MCV. A stool occult blood test is positive . What is the next best step in evaluation?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario of an elderly patient with sudden onset anemia always warrants screening for colorectal cancer, as cancers in the right colon often manifest as melena and fatigue associated with anemia. Thus, the next best investigation is a colonoscopy . Colonoscopy is the investigation of choice & gold standard for establishing the diagnosis of colon cancer. It permits biopsy of the tumor to verify the diagnosis while allowing inspection of the entire colon to exclude metachronous polyps or cancers. Colonoscopy is generally performed even after cancer is detected by barium enema, in order to obtain a biopsy specimen and to detect (and remove) small polyps that may have been missed in the contrast study .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old woman presents with abdominal pain and constipation . A barium enema reveals an apple core sign. In which part of the colon is such a growth commonly seen ?
mcqs.explanation: Apple core sign on barium enema is suggestive of a constricting type of colon cancer that is more common on the left side . Ulcerative type is more common on the right side . Most patients with left -sided colon cancers often present with increasing constipation while patients with right-sided colon cancer often present with melena and fatigue associated with anemia. The apple core sign describes a short segment irregular circumferential stricture of the large bowel that has abrupt shouldered margins resembling an apple core.585

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the most common presenting feature in patients with right sided colon cancer ?
mcqs.explanation: Anemia is the most common presenting feature in patients with right-sided colon cancer. Cancers in the right colon are more often manifested as melena, fatigue associated with anemia, or abdominal pain (if the tumor is advanced). Cancer of the left colon mainly presents with altered bowel habits, usually constipation and intestinal obstruction.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which among the following statements is false about virtual colonoscopy as compared to conventional colonoscopy ?

options.a: Virtual colonoscopy is less sensitive for small polyps
options.b: Provids a better image than conventional colonoscopy
options.c: Easier to take tissue biopsy during virtual colonoscopy
options.d: Less time consuming than conventional colonoscopy

mcqs.explanation: Virtual colonoscopy is a non-invasive technique and is not useful in taking biopsy .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old female presented with low-grade fever, easy fatiguability , and pain in the right hypochondrium. On examination, pallor and moderate hepatomegaly were present . A CT scan revealed non-enhancing masses . The biopsy showed adenocarcinoma, not of hepatic origin. A combination of IHC tests was done and was reported as CK 7 (-\ CK20 (+\Which of the following is the most likely primary site of origin?
mcqs.explanation: Colorectal carcinoma is the most likely primary tumor for the given metastases . Among the given options, cytokeratin 7 is negative only in colon carcinoma . The most common site of distant metastasis from colorectal cancer is the liver. These metastases arise from hematogenous spread via the portal venous system .The lung is the next most common site for metastasis . mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the most important prognostic factor in patients with colorectal carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: The most important determinant of prognosis for colorectal carcinoma is the tumour stage and, in particular, lymph node status . The T-stage (depth of invasion ) is the single most significant predictor of lymph node spread .586

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Choose the parameters used to stage colorectal carcinoma according to Duke's classification ?
mcqs.explanation: Duke's classification is based on the depth of tumor and lymph node status .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Match the following patients with colon cancer to the procedure that is best suited .
mcqs.explanation: All of the given procedures may be performed in a patient with colonic cancer presenting with features of left colonic obstruction. The most appropriate answer is 1-B,2-C,3-A. In Hartmann 's procedure , the segment of the colon containing the obstructing cancer is resected and closure of the distal sigmoid or rectum is performed . A colostomy is made. Later, intestinal continuity is re-established by the closure of the colostomy and fashioning a colorectal anastomosis.588 This procedure is preferred in patients when a resection and primary anastomosis cannot be performed immediately due to complications such as inflammation of the bowel , perforation, or peritonitis . Resection and primary anastomosis is done in patients who are hemodynamically stable and have pliable , nonedematous , well -vascularized bowel . In this procedure , the segment of the left colon containing the cancer is resected . The remaining colon is cleaned with saline lavage by inserting a catheter through the appendix or ileum into the cecum and irrigating the contents from the colon. Primary anastomosis between the prepared colon and rectum is fashioned subsequently , without the need for a temporary colostomy Stent placement via colonoscope is a temporary measure to obtain time for bowel preparation for primary anastomosis. A stent that traverses the tumor is placed to relieve the obstruction. It is done in partial obstruction and is preferred in old and frail patients .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man was rushed to the ER with abdominal pain, obstipation , and altered mental status for the last 2 days. Physical examination and imaging findings are suggestive of perforated intestinal obstruction with peritonitis . After stabilization, he is immediately taken to the operating room, where a suspicious ascending colon mass is seen . Which of the following is the most appropriate management for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The elderly man with ascending colon mass leading to perforated intestinal obstruction with peritonitis should ideally be treated with right hemicolectomy and ileocolostomy . In case of suspected colorectal cancer presenting with intestinal obstruction the following surgeries are done: • Right-sided lesion: • A resection (right hemicolectomy ) and anastomosis if the patient is stable • Perforation with substantial contamination or if the patient is unstable : right hemicolectomy + ileocolostomy • Left-sided lesion: • Resection and anastomosis if the patient is stable • Perforation with substantial contamination or if the patient is unstable : Hartmann procedure is done. Later, intestinal continuity is re-established by the closure of the colostomy and fashioning a colorectal anastomosis. • Where endoscopic and radiological facilities are present an obstructing left -sided lesion can be treated with an expanding metal stent provided bowel perforation is absent.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man is diagnosed with stage II colorectal carcinoma located in the transverse colon. Which of the following is the surgical procedure of choice for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Extended right hemicolectomy is the most appropriate surgical procedure for a neoplastic tumor in the transverse colon. This procedure involves resection of the • Terminal ileum with Ileocecal junction • Cecum • Ascending colon589 • Hepatic flexure , and • Distal transverse colon Very small and localized lesions in the transverse colon may be resected by transverse colectomy . mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A male patient presented with dull abdominal pain and rectal bleeding . On investigations, he was diagnosed with colon carcinoma . Which of the following statements is false regarding the management of colorectal carcinoma ?

options.a: Stage III cancer is treated with surgical resection and chemotherapy
options.b: Stage II cancer with young age is an indication for chemotherapy
options.c: FOLFOX regimen is used for colorectal carcinoma
options.d: Immunotherapy is ineffective in metastatic colorectal carcinoma

mcqs.explanation: Immunotherapy is not ineffective in metastatic colorectal cancer. Metastatic or recurrent colorectal cancers are the indications for immunotherapy. Monoclonal antibodies such as • Bevacizumab (Anti-VEGF), • Cetuximab (anti-EGFR), • Panitumumab (anti-EGFR), • Pembrolizumab (anti-PDL1 ), • Nivolumab (anti-PDL ), etc . are the commonly used immunotherapeutic drugs in colorectal carcinoma . Option A: Surgical resection is indicated in all the stages of colon carcinoma . Management of Stage III colorectal carcinoma should also include chemotherapy , in addition to surgical resection . The stage -specific therapies are as follows : Option B: Stage II cancer in young patients should be considered for chemotherapy . Treatment of stage II colon carcinoma is surgical resection of the cancerous mass. Adjuvant chemotherapy is indicated in patients with at least one poor prognostic indicator like: • Young patients • Inadequate lymph node excision(<12 lymph nodes ) • Poorly differentiated histology • Positive margin of resection • T4 lesions • Bowel obstruction or perforation591 • Presence of perineural or lymphovascular invasion Option C: FOLFOX is a chemotherapy regimen used for the treatment of colorectal cancer, made up of the drugs folinic acid, 5-fluorouracil, and oxaliplatin.Stage Management Stage I: Surgical resection Stage II : Surgical resectionAdjuvant c hemotherapyinhigh -riskpatie nts (presence ofpoor prognos tic factors) Stage II I: Surgical resectionAdjuvant c hemotherapy (folinic acid, 5-fl uorouracil, oxaliplatin) Stage IV : Surgical resection with adjuv ant chemotherapyRadiothera pyImmunotherapy (monoclo nal antibodies )Palliative treat ment in extensive metastasis .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a false statement regarding different types of artificial stoma?

options.a: Output from an ileostomy is liquid in nature
options.b: In Hartmann procedure , a loop colostomy is formed
options.c: Skin excoriation is the most common complication of ileostomy
options.d: Parastomal herniation is more common in Loop colostomy

mcqs.explanation: Colostomy formed during the Hartmann procedure is not a loop colostomy . It is an example of end-colostomy . Artificial stomas are surgically created openings on the abdominal wall following certain types of surgeries , to serve as an alternate path for internal organs to drain externally . Ileostomy and colostomy are the two most common types of artificial stomas for the GI system . Based on the structural pattern, stomas can be classified into different types : • End stoma • Loop stoma • Double barrel stoma End stoma is preferred as a permanent stoma. Loop and double barrel stomas are used as temporary stomas. Complications of stoma include • Skin excoriation (most common) • Stoma infection • Diarrhea • Stoma leakage • Parastomal herniation592 Ileostomy Colostomy Any portion of the entire ileu m can be chosen for stoma cr eation Only mobile parts of the colo n (transverse colonandsigmoi d colon) can be used Gross appearance -marginof t he stoma iselevated (pouting ) from the skin Gross appearance - at the sa me level as that of skin The output isliquidin nature and therefore higher in volu me The output issemi-solid or so lidin nature Higher chance of skin excoria tion and electrolyte imbalanc e Easier to handle593

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: The anorectal angle is formed by which muscle ?
mcqs.explanation: The puborectalis muscle encircles the posterior and lateral aspects of the anorectal junction, creating the anorectal angle. At rest, the anorectal angle is held at 90 - 100 \260. This becomes more acute (70 - 90\260) during squeezing due to the contraction and shortening of the puborectalis muscle . This brings the600 anorectal junction higher and nearer to the pubic symphysis . During straining and defecation , the anorectal angle becomes more obtuse (110 - 180\260) due to relaxation of the puborectalis muscle . The anorectal ring is formed by the fusion of: • Puborectalis • Deep external anal sphincter • Internal anal sphincter Note : Anismus, is caused by a failure of the puborectalis and external anal sphincter to relax during defecation straining. This results in a failure of the anorectal angle to straighten during defecation .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the length of the adult rectum?
mcqs.explanation: The adult rectum is approximately 12 –18 cm in length and is conventionally divided into three equal parts - the upper , middle and lower 1/3rd.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which fascial layer should be dissected to separate the rectum from the coccyx while operating on a patient with rectal adenocarcinoma?
mcqs.explanation: Waldeyer's fascia separates the rectum from the coccyx. The lower third of the rectum is separated by the following : • from the prostate or vagina anteriorly - by Denonvilliers' fascia • from the coccyx and lower two sacral vertebrae- by Waldeyer's fascia Waldeyer's fascia originates at the S2 to S4 level from the presacral parietal fascia and fuses with the rectal visceral fascia at the posterior aspect of the rectum. It divides the retrorectal space into601 superior and inferior compartments. Identification and preservation of the presacral fascia play an important role in preventing complications and reducing local recurrences of rectal cancer.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Up to what length of the patient 's rectum will you be able to visualize while using a proctoscope ?
mcqs.explanation: Proctoscopes can be used to inspect the anus, anorectal junction, and 10 -15cm of the lower rectum .Scope Lengt h Anoscope 8 cm Proctoscope –15 cm Rigid Sigmoidoscope and Rec toscope 25 cm Flexible sigmoidoscope 60 cm Colonoscope 160 c m

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: The instrument shown below will be least useful for examining patients with which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a proctoscope . It is not used for examining patients with anal fissures . Due to pain, digital rectal examination and anoscopy are not performed immediately in an acute anal fissure . It is reserved for later when the symptoms resolve or the patient is in the operating room.602 Proctoscopy is indicated in patients with the following : • Rectal bleeding • Change in bowel habit, especially recurring attacks of diarrhea • Pain or difficulty in defecation • Lesions around the anal opening - abscesses , fistulae , discharge , ulcers , external hemorrhoids • Rectal prolapse .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An anxious mother rushed her 2-year-old child to the casualty when she noticed a red -coloured mass protruding from his anus. The mother gave a history of the child straining while passing stools for the past 2 weeks . There was no abdominal tenderness , and on local examination, a 6 cm mass with circumferential folds and slight edema was noted . How will you manage this child?
mcqs.explanation: The given history and examination finding is suggestive of rectal prolapse . In children, the prolapse is usually mucosal and should be treated conservatively. Rectal prolapse occurs when a mucosal or full -thickness layer of rectal tissue protrudes through the anal orifice. Conservative treatment for rectal prolapse in children is to control: • Diarrhea • Worm infestation • Malnutrition Sclerotherapy can also be used .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is not true regarding the management of patients with rectal prolapse ?

options.a: Surgery is necessary for full -thickness rectal prolapse
options.b: Delorme 's operation is done via the perineal approach
options.c: Ripstein's procedure is done via abdominal approach
options.d: Abdominal rectopexy is often preferred in high risk individuals

mcqs.explanation: The perineal approach is often preferred in patients with high operative risk and limited life expectancy , i.e. in the elderly . It is associated with less morbidity but has a higher recurrence rate. Abdominal approaches (laparoscopic , robotic, or open ) are preferred for younger patients , particularly those with constipation or associated pelvic floor disorders. Perineal procedures : • Delorme's mucosectomy - involves mucosal stripping and muscle plication of the rectal prolapse using interrupted sutures . It is performed externally under regional or general anaesthesia . • Thiersch's encirclement - a steel wire, or Silastic or nylon tape , is placed around the anal canal. Largely obsolete now due to problems with chronic perineal sepsis , anal stenosis , and obstructed defaecation • Altemeier rectosigmoidectomy - involves removal of the prolapsed rectum and associated sigmoid colon, followed by which a coloanal anastomosis is created . It is often complicated by poor bowel control with faecal soiling secondary to the loss of rectal reservoir. Abdominal procedures : • Suture rectopexy603 • Mesh rectopexy • Posterior (Well's and lvalon's) • Anterior (Ripstein's) • Lateral (Orr -Loygue ) • Ventral • Resection Rectopexy (Frykman –Goldberg ) The principle of all abdominal operations for rectal prolapse is to fix the rectum in its normal anatomical position.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true regarding solitary rectal ulcers ?

options.a: Commonly seen on the posterior wall
options.b: Rectal bleeding Is a common presentation
options.d: Colonoscopy with biopsy is the investigation of choice

mcqs.explanation: A solitary rectal ulcer is usually located on the anterior rectal wall, 6-8 cm from the anal verge. It commonly presents with rectal bleeding in the setting of chronic straining or constipation. Histology reveals a thick layer of fibrosis obliterating the lamina propria and a central fibrinous exudate . Colonoscopy with biopsy is the investigation of choice for diagnostic evaluation, while defecography (proctography ) is the radiologic procedure of choice . Stapled trans-anal rectal resection (STARR procedure ) is the management of choice .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the radiological procedure of choice in patients suspected to have a solitary rectal ulcer?
mcqs.explanation: Defecography (proctography ) is the radiologic procedure of choice for diagnostic evaluation in solitary rectal ulcer syndrome (SRUS). Some common findings include : • Full -thickness rectal prolapse604 • Internal prolapse • Paradoxical puborectalis syndrome • Thickened rectal folds Defecography evaluates in real-time the morphology of the rectum and anal canal in a physiologic setting by injection of a thick barium paste into the rectum and its subsequent evacuation. It is primarily performed for workup of patients with: • Longstanding constipation • Unexplained anal or rectal pain • Residual sensation after defecation • Suspected prolapse .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the earliest manifestation in patients with rectal carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: Per-rectal bleeding is the earliest and most common symptom of rectal carcinoma . Other symptoms of rectal carcinoma include : • Mucus drainage • Tenesmus • Early morning diarrhoea • Pain • Weight loss.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following staging systems is used for rectal carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: Duke's staging is used in rectal carcinoma . mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An elderly man with per-rectal bleeding is suspected to have rectal carcinoma . Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.a: Majority of the cancers are sporadic
options.b: Dose of radiation used for this tumor is 45 Gy
options.c: Dissection lateral to the endopelvic fascia investing the mesorectum causes local recurrence
options.d: Precise location of the tumor is determined with rigid proctosigmoidoscopy

mcqs.explanation: Dissection medial (not lateral) to the endopelvic fascia investing the mesorectum causes local recurrence . Dissection lateral to the avascular anatomic space , risks injury to the mixed autonomic nerves, causing impotence in men and bladder dysfunction in men and women. Transmesorectal resection involves complete removal of the lymph node bearing mesorectum along with its intact enveloping fascia. It is a curative resection of rectal tumours of the middle and lower thirds of the rectum, either as part of Low Anterior Resection (LAR ) or Abdominoperineal Resection (APR ).606 Option A: The majority of colorectal cancers are sporadic. Approximately 5% of all colorectal cancers are attributed to familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) and Lynch syndrome (hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer). Option B: The large bowel can tolerate delivered radiation doses of up to 6000 cGy. However, a lower dose of 45 Gy is recommended for colorectal tumours. High levels of radiation targeted at colon tumours would include the small bowel in the treatment field . This results in complications such as radiation enteritis . Option D: The precise location of the rectal tumour is determined using rigid proctosigmoidoscope or flexible sigmoidoscopy and biopsy . The other investigations used in rectal cancer include : • Digital rectal examination - for assessing the depth of penetration • Endorectal ultrasound or MRI - provides an accurate assessment of the extent of invasion of the bowel wall • MRI with an endorectal coil - is the investigation of choice to assess the 'T' and 'N' stages • CECT - for evaluation of metastasis .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding rectal carcinoma ?

options.a: Hartmann 's operation is done in elderly debilitated patients
options.b: Adenocarcinoma is a rare variant of rectal carcinoma
options.c: Early morning spurious diarrhoea and tenesmus can occur
options.d: Growth confined to the rectal mucosa is stage A of modified Duke's staging

mcqs.explanation: Adenocarcinoma is the most common variant of rectal carcinoma . Colorectal cancer is: • The second most common malignancy globally • The second most common cancer in women • The third most common cancer in men • The fourth most common cause of death due to cancer. Symptoms of rectal carcinoma include : • Painless bleeding - earliest and most common • Alteration of bowel habits - change in frequency and consistency of the stool • Tenesmus - unable to pass a motion even when there is the sensation of needing to evacuate the bowel . It is suggestive of a tumor of the lower half of the rectum • Early morning bloody diarrhea (option C) - passage of blood and mucus in addition to feces . Pain and weight loss are usually late symptoms Abdominal examination and digital rectal examination are used for the primary evaluation. Rigid sigmoidoscopy is performed to obtain a biopsy . A synchronous tumor (primary tumor with a different origin than the one currently investigated ) is excluded by performing a colonoscopy . Modified Duke's classification :607 A Growth limited up to the rect al mucosa (option D) B B1 : Tumor invading muscular is propria, no lymph node in vasion .B2 : Tumors invading i nto or through serosa, no ly mph node invasion . C C1: The tumour did not excee d the bowel wall, lymph node metastasis .C2: Tumour exce eded the intestinal wall and l ymph node metastasis . D Distant metastasisSurgery is the mainstay of management for rectal carcinoma . Non-operative management is offered to only those patients who have a complete clinical response to neoadjuvant. The type of surgery depends on multiple factors (size, location, age of the patient , etc ). However, the general consensus is: • Early cancer (T1 and a few T2 ) is locally excised via the transanal approach. • Most rectal cancer is treated by anterior resection and colorectal /coloanal anastomosis. • Low extensive tumors are treated by laparoscopic abdominoperineal resection (APR ) and permanent colostomy . • Hartmann 's operation (option A) is preferred in old and frail patients due to poor anal sphincter and postoperative incontinence.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In patients with rectal carcinoma , what is the investigation of choice for assessment of perirectal nodes and the depth of penetration?
mcqs.explanation: 608 Endorectal -coil magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the best modality for predicting lymph node invasion and overall local staging . It can identify involved perirectal nodes on the basis of characteristics other than size. It can also identify foci at sites not only within the mesorectum but also outside the mesorectal fascia, such as pelvic sidewalls , and can identify the depth of penetration .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common site of blood-borne metastasis in patients with rectal carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: The principal sites for blood-borne metastases in rectal carcinoma are the liver > lungs > adrenals.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In a patient with rectal carcinoma , the tumour was found to invade through the muscularis propria into the perirectal tissues . Two lymph nodes near the tumour site were enlarged . Which of the following will be the appropriate modality of treatment in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: In the above clinical scenario, the TNM staging is T3 N1b M0 (Stage IIIB ), since: • Tumor invasion through the muscularis propria into the perirectal tissues - T3 • Involvement of two lymph nodes - N1b • No evidence of metastasis - M0 The treatment of choice for Stage III tumors is preoperative chemoradiation followed by radical resection . Treatment of Rectal Carcinoma : TNM staging for rectal carcinoma :Stage Treatment Stage 0 (Tis, N0, M0) Local excision Stage I: Localized Rectal Carc inoma (T1 –2, N0, M0) Polypectomy with clear marg insRadical resection in high-r isk patients with unfavourabl e histologic characteristics lo cated in the distal third of th e rectum Stage II : Localized Rectal Car cinoma (T3 –4, N0, M0) Preoperative chemoradiation + radical resection Stage III : Lymph Node Metas tasis(Tany, N1, M0) Preoperative chemoradiation + radical resection Stage IV : Distant Metastasis ( Tany, Nany, M1) Palliative proceduresResectio n to control pain, bleeding , o r tenesmus609 Stage Def inition Primary tumor (T)Tx Primary tumor cannot be ass essed T0 No evidence of primary tumo r Tis Carcinoma in situ, intraepith elial or invasion of lamina pr opria T1 Tumor invades submucosa T2 Tumor invades muscularis pr opria T3 Tumor invades through musc ularis propria into the subser osa or into non-peritonealize d pericolic or perirectal tissu es T4a Tumor perforates visceral per itoneum T4b Tumor directly invades other organs or structuresRegional lymph nodes ( N)Nx Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed N0 No regional lymph node met astasis N1 Metastasis to 1-3 regional LN s N1a Metastasis in 1 regional LN N1b Metastasis in 2-3 regional LN s N1c Tumor deposits in the subser osa, mesentery , or non-perito nealized pericolic or perirecta l tissues without regional LN metastasis N2 Metastasis in 4 or more regio nal LNs610 Nx Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed N2a Metastasis in 4-6 regional LN s N2b Metastasis in 7 or more regio nal LNsDistant metastasis (M)M0 No distant metastasis M1 Distant metastasis M1a Metastasis confined to one or gan or site M1b Metastasis in more than one organ/site or the peritoneumStaging based on TNM:TNM Stag e T1 -2 N0 I T3 N IIA T4 N IIB T1 -2 N1 IIIA T1 -2 N2 IIIB T3 N IIIB T3 N IIIC T4 N 1-2 IIIC

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient with rectal carcinoma is posted under your unit for surgery. Which of the following correctly describes the margins of clearance that will be required in this surgery?
mcqs.explanation: The margins of clearance required for the surgery of rectal carcinoma is: • Proximal - 5 cm611 • Distal - 2 cm • Radial- 5 cm (for the removal of mesorectal nodes ) Historically, a 5 cm clearance margin was the common practice . However, the 5 cm rule has been replaced by the 2 cm rule to help preserve the anal sphincters . When a negative distal margin can be achieved by sparing the sphincter , a sphincter sparing surgery such as low anterior resection (LAR ) is performed . If it is not possible to achieve a negative distal margin and spare the sphincter (when the tumour is within 5cm of anal verge), abdominal perineal resection (APR ) is done. APR /LAR must include total mesorectal excision (TME) to ensure margin clearance and lymph node retrieval.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old man presents to the clinic with a history of intermittent blood in stools for the past 3 months. After a detailed workup, he is diagnosed with rectal adenocarcinoma which is located 8 cm from the anal verge. There is no nodal or distant metastasis . Which of the following surgeries would you prefer in managing this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Low anterior resection (LAR ) is the preferred surgery in rectal carcinoma which is located at least 5 - 5.5 cm away from the anal verge. It is not performed : • If adequate margin could not be achieved even after preoperative chemoradiotherapy • If the sphincters have to be sacrificed to achieve an adequate margin • In patients who cannot tolerate low anastomosis. In such cases , where anterior resection cannot be performed in distal rectal cancers, abdominoperineal resection (APR ) is done. APR /LAR must include total mesorectal excision (TME) to ensure margin clearance and lymph node retrieval.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Transanal local excision can be done in rectal carcinoma patients with all of the following tumour features except ____.

options.a: Tumor within 8 cm of the anal verge
options.d: T2 tumor without lymph node involvement

mcqs.explanation: T2 rectal cancers are managed by transabdominal resection . Transanal local excision is recommended for selected T1 , N0 early-stage cancers which fulfill the following criteria: • Small (<3 cm), well - to moderately -differentiated tumors • Tumors within 8 cm of the anal verge • Tumors limited to <30% of the rectal circumference • Tumors with no evidence of nodal involvement • Full -thickness excision must be feasible.612

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following chemotherapy regimens is used for treating patients with rectal carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: 5-Fluorouracil-based regimens with leucovorin and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) reduce recurrence and improve survival in patients with colorectal carcinoma . Irinotecan (FOLFIRI regimen) is also used as a second -line chemotherapy agent . Adjuvant chemotherapy is routinely recommended in patients with lymph node involvement. Option B: ABVD regimen is used for Hodgkin's lymphoma. Option C: RCHOP regimen is used for B-cell Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. Option D: MVAC regimen is used for advanced bladder carcinoma .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An 80-year-old man with rectal carcinoma presented with features of intestinal obstruction. How will you manage this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Hartmann 's operation is an excellent procedure in an elderly , frail patient in whom there is concern about anal sphincter function or the viability of an anastomosis. Through an abdominal incision, the rectum is excised , the rectal stump is stapled closed and the proximal colon exteriorized as a permanent end colostomy . Note : Endoluminal stenting is being increasingly used in patients with obstructing carcinomas. It can be either used as a palliative procedure or to relieve the obstruction. Only rectosigmoid and upper rectal tumours are suitable for stenting because stent impingement on the anorectum in low cancers can result in tenesmus .613

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the anatomy of the anal canal below the pectinate line?

options.a: Lymphatic drainage is to inguinal nodes
options.b: Innervation is by the inferior rectal nerves
options.c: Venous drainage is into the systemic circulation
options.d: Tumors are more likely to be adenocarcinoma

mcqs.explanation: Adenocarcinoma is more likely to be seen above the pectinate line. Tumors below the pectinate line are more likely to be squamous cell carcinoma . The pectinate line is at the junction of the upper two -thirds and the lower one-third of the anal canal. Developmentally , it represents the hindgut –proctodeum junction. The part of the anal canal above this line developed from the hindgut and the part below developed from the proctodeum .622

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following are not true regarding external hemorrhoids?
mcqs.explanation: External hemorrhoids are painful, self-curing and covered by squamous epithelium . The branches of the superior rectal vein, located at 3, 7, and 11 o'clock positions in the anal canal are common sites for internal hemorrhoids. Banding is preferred for internal hemorrhoids. Hemorrhoids are cushions of submucosal tissue containing venules , arterioles , smooth muscle fibres, and elastic connective tissue . They can be classified according to their location into 2 types : • Internal Hemorrhoids • External Hemorrhoids Note : Repeated thrombosis leads to a semi-ripe black currant appearance of external hemorrhoids.623

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following will you not consider as a differential in a patient presenting with anorectal pain?
mcqs.explanation: Internal hemorrhoids are painless . Causes of anorectal pain: • External hemorrhoids • Anal fissure • Proctalgia fugax • Levator ani syndrome • Fistula in ano/anal abscess • Inflammatory bowel disease • Coccydynia • Prostatitis • Carcinoma anus/lower rectum

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old male patient presented to the OPD with complaints of painless bleeding during defecation . On examination, a pinkish mass appears at the anal orifice when the patient is asked to strain. It reduces spontaneously when the patient relaxes. What will be the grade of this hemorrhoid?
mcqs.explanation: Prolapse with spontaneous reduction is suggestive of second -degree hemorrhoids.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A man presented with bleeding per rectum which he noticed after passing stools for the past 2 weeks . On straining, a reddish mass as shown in the image was seen protruding out of the anal canal. It did not reduce spontaneously and had to be manually reduced . What is the grade of hemorrhoids in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, as the prolapsed haemorrhoids required manual reduction , it is suggestive of third-degree haemorrhoids.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In patients with which of the following conditions can injection sclerotherapy be ideally used ?
mcqs.explanation: Injection sclerotherapy is ideal for the treatment of first and second -degree hemorrhoids (bleeding or spontaneously reducing hemorrhoids). 1 to 3 mL of a sclerosing solution (phenol in olive oil, sodium morrhuate, or quinine urea) is injected into the submucosa of each hemorrhoid. Complications of sclerotherapy include infection and fibrosis.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 48-year-old man presents to the clinic with severe anorectal pain during and after defecation . The pain was present for 6 months but has increased in severity over the past 1 day. Examination finding is shown below . A per-rectal examination could not be performed due to pain. How will you manage this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: 624 The clinical features and the image are suggestive of thrombosed external hemorrhoids. Patients who present within 48 hours of thrombosis should undergo thrombus evacuation under local anesthesia . This procedure involves the removal of the clot with an elliptical incision on the skin. After the initial 48-72 hours, pain typically plateaus and hence the patient is treated conservatively with analgesics and a sitz bath. Grade1, grade 2, and some grade 3 hemorrhoids with only an internal component can be treated with simple procedures like rubber band ligation, sclerotherapy , infrared and laser coagulation , and cryotherapy . Surgery is indicated in: • Internal grade 3 or grade 4 hemorrhoids • Hemorrhoids with a significant external component • Early grade hemorrhoids not responding to simple procedures Surgical procedures used in the removal of hemorrhoids are: • Open (Milligan–Morgan) hemorrhoidectomy • Closed (Ferguson ) hemorrhoidectomy • Stapled hemorrhoidopexy - is circumferential rectal mucosectomy . It is associated with reduced postoperative pain, faster recovery and shorter hospital stay • Doppler -guided hemorrhoidal artery ligation Open hemorrhoidectomy - Artery forceps are applied to the skin-covered external components of the hemorrhoid and traction is given to reveal the internal components . Dissection of the lateral pedicle is performed and finally, the pedicles are transfixed. Mucocutaneous bridges are left intact in this technique . The image below shows the procedure .Closed hemorrhoidectomy - The hemorrhoid is excised with the overlying mucosa. The hemorrhoid is dissected from the underlying sphincter and the mucus defect is then closed . This technique is associated with higher chances of recurrence. This procedure is however quick to perform and less painful. The image below describes the procedure .625

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the most common complication following hemorrhoidectomy ?
mcqs.explanation: Urinary retention is the most common complication following hemorrhoidectomy . Conventional hemorrhoidectomy (open or closed technique ), is considered to be an extremely painful procedure . Dysfunction of the detrusor muscle or the trigone in response to pain or distention of the anal canal or perineum has been postulated as the cause of urinary retention post hemorrhoidectomy . Other complications include : • Fecal incontinence • Infection • Delayed hemorrhage • Stricture

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man came with complaints of chronic constipation , blood-streaked stools , and pain during defecation for 2 months. On examination, a sentinel tag was noted at the anal orifice. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, the presence of a sentinel tag is suggestive of chronic anal fissure . An anal fissure is a linear or oval-shaped tear in the anal canal starting just below the dentate line extending to the anal verge. It can be acute or chronic. Chronic anal fissures last for more than 6-8 weeks , and are frequently associated with a triad of findings: • Sentinel tag • Hypertrophied anal papillae at the upper end of the fissure in the anal canal • Deep canoe-shaped ulcer626 Acute fissures are shallow tears in the anoderm. They are associated with: • Anal pain • Spasm • Bleeding with defecation The below image shows features of a chronic anal fissure

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common location of anal fissures ?
mcqs.explanation: Over 90% of fissures are located in the posterior midline, with the rest being located in the anterior midline of the anal canal. The main hypothesis is that the posterior midline area may have decreased blood flow due to the configuration of the blood vessels of the anus. Also, the spasm of the internal anal sphincter may cause further reduction of the blood flow to the posterior anal canal.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the procedure of choice in a patient with chronic anal fissure ?
mcqs.explanation: Lateral internal sphincterotomy is the procedure of choice for chronic anal fissures . Surgical therapy has traditionally been recommended for chronic anal fissures that have failed medical therapy. The aim of this procedure is to decrease the spasms of the internal sphincter by dividing a portion of the muscle . Approximately 30% of the muscle sphincter fibers are divided laterally using an open or closed technique . The initial treatment of anal fissures includes : • Frequent sitz baths • Analgesics627 • Stool softeners • High-fiber diet If conservative management with dietary changes and laxatives fail, other options including topical analgesics such as 2% lidocaine jelly , topical nifedipine , topical nitroglycerin, or a combination of topical nifedipine and lidocaine can be attempted . Option A: Miligan-Morgan procedure is an open hemorrhoidectomy Option C: Transanal resection is used to remove early-stage rectal cancers in the lower rectum Option D: Altermeier 's procedure is used for rectal prolapse

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which type of anal fistula is seen in this image?
mcqs.explanation: In the given image, the fistula traverses the internal sphincter and tracks down the space between the internal and external anal sphincters . Hence , it is an inter-sphincteric type of anal fistula . It is the most common anal fistula . A fistula -in-ano is an epithelial -lined tract connecting the anal canal to the perianal skin. Patients usually complain of intermittent purulent discharge and pain. Anal fistulas can be simplex or complex fistulas . • Simple fistulas - include a single tract, subcutaneous tract, and those that involve less than 30% of the external sphincter . They are easier to treat, and have lower chances of recurrence. • Complex fistulas - include fistulas involving more than 30% of the external sphincter , with multiple tracts, recurrent fistulas , and those associated with other predisposing factors, such as Crohn disease and radiation treatment . Fistulas can also be classified into high or low-lying fistulas , based on their location with respect to the puborectalis muscle .628

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old male patient presents to the clinic with a history of discharge from the perianal region for the past 1 week . On examination, an external opening was seen at 2 o'clock position around the anal orifice. On per rectal examination, an opening was palpable at 3 o'clock position at the dentate line. What is the gold standard investigation for assessing this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of an anal fistula . Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the gold standard investigation for fistula imaging. It helps to identify the secondary extensions of the track, which when missed may cause persistence of the fistula . Investigations available for fistula -in-ano are: • Fistulogram • Endoanal ultrasound • MRI • Computed tomography (CT) scan • Endocoil MRI • Hydrogen peroxide –enhanced 3-D endoanal ultrasonography

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient presented with serous discharge from an opening located in the perianal region. On examination , the location of the external opening was at 8'O clock position. According to Goodsall 's rule at what position from the dentate line will the internal opening be palpated in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of fistula -in-ano with external opening at 8'O clock position which implies that the external opening of the fistula is lying posterior to the midline. According to the Goodsall rule, fistulas with an external opening posteriorly track in a curvilinear fashion to the posterior midline. Hence , the fistulous tract opens internally at a 6'O clock position. A fistula -in-ano is an abnormal hollow tract or cavity that is lined with granulation tissue and that connects a primary opening inside the anal canal to a secondary opening in the perianal skin. Goodsall 's rule: • Fistulas with an external opening anteriorly connect to the internal opening by a short, radial tract. • Fistulas with an external opening posteriorly track in a curvilinear fashion to the posterior midline. However, exceptions to this rule often occur. Fistulas with an anterior external opening greater than 3 cm from the anal margin usually track to the posterior midline629

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A known case of Crohn's disease presented to the clinic with a history of discharge from the anal region for the past 2 weeks . The patient underwent drainage of an ischiorectal abscess 2 months back. Clinical examination and imaging reveal the presence of a supra-sphincteric perianal fistula . How will you manage this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, a history of Crohn's disease , recurrent anorectal abscess , and the imaging findings point towards a complex anal fistula . It will be managed using Seton's placement , which is done in two stages . A seton is a drain placed through a fistula to maintain drainage and/or induce fibrosis. Setons can be classified as draining or cutting .Cutting seton A cutting seton has been used as a staged fistulectomy , especially in high trans-sphincteric fistulas . After the seton is passed during the primary surgery, it has to be tightened at regular intervals, till it cuts through completely .630 Loose/draining seton In this method , the seton is placed to maintain drainage and create scar tissue around the sphincter so that its edges do not retract after cutting .Option B: Fistulotomy involves opening the fistula tract and possibly dividing the sphincter muscle . It is very effective for simple fistulas with minimal sphincter involvement. Option C: Lateral internal sphincterotomy is a technique used for chronic anal fissures . Option D: In fistulectomy , the fistulous tract is cut out completely . Other surgeries for fistula in-ano include : • Endorectal advancement flap- involves closure of the internal opening of the tract, debridement of the tract, and mobilization of anorectal mucosa to cover the defect . It is usually done for complex fistulas . • LIFT - Ligation of the intersphincteric fistula tract involves identification of the internal opening with suture ligation of the intersphincteric portion of the fistula . The tract and infected gland are then excised and the wound is debrided with curettage . It can be done for both simple and complex fistulas .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common cause of anorectal suppuration ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of anorectal suppuration is nonspecific cryptoglandular infection . Anorectal abscess originates from an infection arising in the cryptoglandular epithelium lining the anal canal. The increased incidence of ischio-rectal fossa infection is due to poor blood supply . It may also be caused by other reasons such as: • Crohn's disease • Trauma631 • Immunodeficiency resulting from human immunodeficiency virus (HIV ) infection or malignancy (both hematologic and anorectal cancer) • Tuberculosis • Hidradenitis suppurativa

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common type of anorectal abscess ?
mcqs.explanation: A perianal abscess is the most common type of anorectal abscess . Anorectal abscess refers to a collection of pus in the anal or rectal region. More commonly seen in men. There are four types of anorectal abscesses : • Peri-anal (most common) • Ischio-rectal • Inter-sphincteric • Supra-levator Treatment: Drainage of pus + Antibiotics

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A jeep driver presented with a swelling in the natal cleft , with pain, difficulty in sitting , and occasional purulent discharge from the area. Examination finding is shown below . Which of the following is not true regarding this condition?

options.b: Hair follicles are seen in the wall of sinus
options.c: Hirsute habitus is a risk factor
options.d: Commonly seen between the ages of 15 and 40 years

mcqs.explanation: The given condition is a pilonidal sinus. Hair follicles have almost never been demonstrated in the walls of the sinus. The hair projecting from the sinus is dead hair, with its pointed ends directed towards the blind end of the sinus. Pilonidal sinus disease is a disease of the inter-gluteal region, characterized by the formation of a sinus in the cleft of the buttocks . It is more common in males between 15-40 years of age . Risk factors include :632 • Male sex • Family history • Being overweight or obese • Trauma or irritation to the perianal region • Occupations involving sitting for long periods - jeep /lorry drivers • Hirsute habitus - thick body hair • Poor hygiene Sites involved: • Natal cleft (most commonly) • Interdigital cleft • Face • Axilla Buttock friction and shearing forces in these areas allow broken hairs to enter the skin and create a subcutaneous, chronically infected midline track. An infected hair follicle can also form such a track. Secondary tracks can arise as openings , lined with granulation tissue and discharge . Clinical features : • Intermittent pain, swelling , and discharge at the base of the spine • Abscess - due to a foreign-body-type reaction Treatment • Conservative treatment : Strict hygiene and regular shaving of hair in the area. • Abscess : • Rest, baths, local antiseptic dressings , and broad-spectrum antibiotics. • If refractory to the above treatment - drainage with thorough curettage of granulation tissue and hair. • Surgical techniques : Bascom's, Karydaki's procedures are for chronic pilonidal disease . Recurrence is common even after adequate excision of the tract.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not used in the treatment of pilonidal sinus diseases ?
mcqs.explanation: Surgical approaches parallel to the natal cleft , and not along the natal cleft are preferred , to reduce chances of recurrence. Pilonidal sinus disease treatment includes non-surgical and surgical approaches . The non-surgical approach includes conservative treatment with proper hygiene and regular shaving of hair in the area. In case of an abscess - adequate rest, baths, local antiseptic dressings , and broad-spectrum antibiotics are advised.633 Surgical approaches for the management of pilonidal sinus disease include : • Incision and drainage- for pilonidal abscess refractory to medical treatment • Bascom's procedure - is a cleft lift procedure in which hair follicles parallel to the natal cleft are removed under local anesthesia • Karydakis procedure - an ovoid area of pathologic tissue is excised parallel to the natal cleft and a fasciocutaneous flap is mobilized to cover the defect • Limberg/ rhomboid flap- excises the pilonidal disease in a rhomboid shape and rotates a fasciocutaneous flap for wound closure • Others - VY advancement flaps , and Z-plasty The given image shows a Limberg/rhomboid flap done in pilonidal sinus surgery:

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An elderly female presented with severe persisting per rectal itching for the past 1 year, despite standard topical therapy . On examination, irregular eczematous lesions were seen at the anal orifice. Biopsy of the lesion revealed large vacuolated cells containing mucin. Which of the following is it likely to be?
mcqs.explanation: The given history and presence of large vacuolated cells (Paget cells ) on biopsy is suggestive of Paget 's disease of the anal canal. It is a rare intraepithelial adenocarcinoma. Paget 's disease is most commonly seen in areas with a high density of apocrine sweat glands, in elderly females . These can develop into an invasive cancer of the underlying apocrine glands. Clinical features include intractable itching, burning, bleeding per rectally . % of the patients are asymptomatic. On examination, eczematous, well -demarcated plaque, with occasional ulceration and scaling can be seen . On histology presence of Paget cells (large, vacuolated cells with mucin) confirms the diagnosis. Treatment: • Treatment of choice - complete excision • Limited, noninvasive disease -wide local excision and closure of the defect with primary sutures or with V -Y advancement flaps634 • Invasive component - radical resection with abdominoperineal resection (APR ) • Medically unfit for surgery - topical 5-FU, imiquimod, cryotherapy , or argon beam laser therapy • Recurrence- re-excision (as long as the disease remains noninvasive ) Note : Most common site of extra-mammary Paget 's disease – anogenital region > axilla > eyelid . Perianal Paget 's disease is usually associated with underlying visceral malignancy, most commonly colorectal adenocarcinoma.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true regarding squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal?

options.a: Proctoscopy is the investigation of choice
options.c: Most common presentation is ano-rectal pain
options.d: Most common type of anal canal carcinoma

mcqs.explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is the most common anal canal carcinoma . SCC > Basal cell carcinoma >Melanoma The median age at diagnosis for SCC is 60 years. Patients most commonly present with bleeding per rectum. Commonly metastasizes to the liver and lungs . The most common site of lymph node metastasis is to inguinal lymph nodes . Risk Factors: • Human papillomavirus (HPV ) (types 16, 18, , 33) infection • Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV ) or immunosuppression • Smoking • Anal receptive intercourse • Sexual promiscuity • Anal intraepithelial neoplasia • History of vulvar or cervical cancer Diagnosis: • Proctoscopy with biopsy - investigation of choice • MRI- for local staging • CT scan- to evaluate for distant metastasis Treatment : • Nigro regimen- chemoradiation is the treatment of choice • If any residual tumor is left behind after chemoradiation, abdominoperineal resection (APR ) is performed8th AJCC: TNM Classificatio n of Carcinoma of the Anal C anal and Anal Margin Primary Tumor :635 8th AJCC: TNM Classificatio n of Carcinoma of the Anal C anal and Anal Margin Tis - high-grade squamous in traepithelial lesionT1 - 2 cm or lessT2 - >2 - 5 cmT3 - >5 c mT4 - invades adjacent organ, e.g. vagina , urethra, bladder . (invasion of the rectal wall, p erirectal skin, subcutaneous t issue, or sphincter muscle is not included as T4). Regional Nodes : Regional lymph nodes includ e mesorectal , inguinal (superf icial, deep ), superior rectal (h emorrhoidal), external iliac, a nd internal iliac (hypogastric ) groups .N0 - no regional lym ph node metastasesN1a - ing uinal, mesorectal , or internal iliac lymph nodesN1b - exter nal iliac nodesN1c - external i liac nodes + N1a Distant Metastases : M0 - noM1 - yes Stage grouping : 0 - TisI - T1 N0IIA - T2 N0II B - T3 N0IIIA - T1 -2 N1IIIB - T4 N0IIIC - T3 -4 N1IV - M1

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man with bleeding per rectum is suspected to have squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal. What is the treatment of choice for this condition?

options.d: Surgical excision with CO2 laser treatment

mcqs.explanation: Treatment of choice for squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal is Nigro regimen/ chemoradiation. A combination of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) with mitomycin C/ cisplatin is followed by external beam radiation to the pelvis with a minimum dose of 45 Gy.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about melanoma of the anal canal?

options.a: Wide local excision is done for tumors with sphincter involvement
options.b: Staged by depth or thickness of melanoma lesion

mcqs.explanation: Anorectal melanoma is staged by the depth or thickness of the lesion. Anal canal melanoma is more common in females . The tumor appears as small and polypoidal or large and ulcerating . Clinical features include : • Anorectal bleeding , itching, pain, mass636 • Tenesmus , and changes in bowel habits • Mesorectal lymph node metastases • Inguinal lymphadenopathy • Distant spread - to bones, lungs , and liver Diagnosis is frequently made following hemorrhoidectomy or local excision of the perianal mass. Treatment: • Tumors without anal sphincter involvement- wide local excision with negative margins • Large tumors invading sphincters - palliative APR Regardless of stage , 5-year survival rates for anorectal melanoma are very poor, averaging at about 6%. The median survival time following diagnosis is 12 –18 months. Note : Most common sites of melanoma are skin >eye > anorectal region637

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a false statement regarding the inguinal canal?

options.a: Conjoint tendon forms a part of the posterior wall
options.b: Superficial ring is an opening in the external oblique aponeurosis
options.c: Deep ring is an opening in the transverse abdominis
options.d: Internal oblique forms both the anterior and superior walls

mcqs.explanation: The deep inguinal ring is an opening in the fascia transversalis, not in the transversus abdominis.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: All of the following are contents of inguinal canal except _______.
mcqs.explanation: The femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve is not a content of the inguinal canal. The contents of the inguinal canal include : • Spermatic cord in males • Round ligament in females • Ilioinguinal nerve in both the sexes . The contents of the spermatic cord include : • Cremaster muscle fibers • Testicular artery and accompanying veins • Genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve • Vas deferens • Cremasteric vessels • Lymphatics • Processus vaginalis

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following structures does not form the boundary of Hesselbach 's triangle?
mcqs.explanation: Vas deferens does not form the boundary of Hesselbach 's triangle. Hesselbach 's triangle (also called the inguinal triangle) is a region of the deep part of the anterior abdominal wall.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A resident while assisting a case of laparoscopic hernia repair observes the surgeon dissect certain anatomical landmarks to expose the triangle of doom. Which of the following does not form a boundary of this triangle?
mcqs.explanation: Cooper 's ligament does not form the boundary of the triangle of doom.649

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true regarding inguinal hernia?
mcqs.explanation: The medial border of the triangle of doom is bounded by vas deferens and the medial border of the myopectineal orifice is bounded by the lateral border of rectus abdominis. The triangle of doom is bounded : • Medially by the vas deferens • Laterally by the vessels of the spermatic cord (gonadal vessels ) • Inferiorly by peritoneal reflection The myopectineal orifice is an osseo -myo-aponeurotic tunnel . It is through this tunnel that all groin hernias occur. It is bounded : • Medially by the lateral border of the rectus sheath . • Above by the arched fibers of the internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscle . • Laterally by the iliopsoas muscle . • Below by the pectin pubis and fascia covering it.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the most common type of hernia in females ?
mcqs.explanation: Indirect inguinal hernias are by far the most common type of hernia in women. It is the most common hernia regardless of gender . In men, indirect hernias predominate over direct hernias at a ratio of 2:1. Femoral hernia and umbilical hernias are more common in females compared to males at ratios of 10 :1 and 2:1, respectively . Although femoral hernias occur more frequently in women than in men, inguinal hernia remains the most common hernia in women.650

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman presents with a history of swelling in the right groin for the past 6 months. On examination, an irreducible hernia is present in the right groin. Which of the following structures would be helpful in identifying if the hernia is inguinal or femoral in origin?
mcqs.explanation: Pubic tubercle is used to differentiate between inguinal and femoral hernias. Inguinal hernia is above and medial to the pubic tubercle . Femoral hernia is below and lateral to the pubic tubercle . Another structure that is useful in differentiating between inguinal and femoral hernia is inguinal ligament. An inguinal hernia leaves the abdominal cavity just above the inguinal ligament and a femoral hernia leaves just below the inguinal ligament .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An elderly male patient is diagnosed with direct inguinal hernia. Which of the following statements is true?

options.a: The sac lies medial to the inferior epigastric artery
options.b: Cough impulse is felt on the index finger
