options.c: Can descend till the bottom of scrotum
options.d: The neck is narrow and is prone for strangulation

mcqs.explanation: The sac and contents of a direct hernia protrude through Hesselbach 's triangle, i.e., medial to the inferior epigastric artery.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Bubonocele is a type of _________.
mcqs.explanation: Bubonocele is a type of indirect inguinal hernia where the hernia is limited to the inguinal canal. Indirect inguinal hernia is more common on the right side because of the delay in atrophy of the processus vaginalis after the normal slower descent of the right testis to the scrotum during fetal development .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the most common serious complication expected to occur in patients with hernia?
mcqs.explanation: Strangulation is the most common serious complication of a hernia. An incarcerated hernia is a part of the intestine or abdominal tissue that becomes trapped in the sac of a hernia.An incarcerated hernia can lead to a bowel obstruction or strangulation. Obstruction is characterized by colicky abdominal pain, vomiting, abdominal distension and obstipation . Features of obstruction along with vascular compromise is seen in strangluation. Strangulation occurs in 1% to 3% of groin hernias. It is more common at the extremes of life . Most strangulated hernias are indirect inguinal hernias. However, femoral hernias have the highest rate of strangulation (15% to 20 %) of all hernias, and it is, therefore , recommended that all femoral hernias be repaired at the time of discovery. Tenderness is the first sign of strangulation. The first step is the correction of hypovolemia. The treatment of choice is immediate surgery. The fundus is opened first during surgery.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient presents with a hernia medial to the inferior epigastric artery. What is the most likely diagnosis and appropriate management for the same?

options.b: Direct hernia and Lichtenstein mesh repair
options.d: Indirect hernia and Lichtenstein mesh repair

mcqs.explanation: 651 The given clinical scenario of a hernia medial to the inferior epigastric artery is suggestive of a direct hernia, for which Lichtenstein mesh repair is the appropriate surgical method for its management. The contents of a direct hernia protrude outward , forward, and medial to the inferior epigastric artery and the deep inguinal ring. Whereas, the contents of an indirect hernia protrude lateral to the inferior epigastric artery. The sac of an indirect inguinal hernia passes from the deep inguinal ring obliquely towards the superficial inguinal ring and then to the scrotum. A direct hernia protrudes through the Hesselbach triangle, which is a zone of weakness for direct hernias. A Lichtenstein mesh repair is currently one of the most frequently used methods for treating an inguinal hernia. It is done for the reconstruction of the inguinal floor in adults . It is an anterior tension-free mesh repair that reduces the chances of recurrence of a hernia. A piece of prosthetic nonabsorbable mesh is used to bridge the defect in this repair.Other surgical methods used for the repair of an inguinal hernia are: • Bassini repair - It is done for the reconstruction of the inguinal floor in adults . In this method , a mesh is not used . It is associated with a high recurrence and is not used frequently now. It is used only in cases of hernial strangulation and peritonitis where the use of a mesh is not preferred. It is performed by suturing the transversus abdominis and internal oblique musculoaponeurotic arches/conjoined tendon to the inguinal ligament . • Shouldice repair - It is a multilayered repair, where the posterior wall of the inguinal canal is strengthened by continuous sutures . It involves double -breasting of the transversalis fascia. It is associated with a very low recurrence rate. • Gilbert repair (plug and patch repair) - It is an extension of Lichtenstein 's original mesh repair and has now become the most commonly performed primary anterior inguinal hernia repair. In this technique , a cone-shaped plug of polypropylene mesh is used . It is deployed like an upside -down umbrella when inserted into the internal inguinal ring to occlude the hernia • McVay repair (Cooper's ligament repair) is used for the correction of direct inguinal hernia, large indirect hernia, recurrent hernia, femoral hernias (particularly suited for strangulated femoral652 hernias). In this method , the transversus abdominis aponeurosis is approximated to Cooper 's ligament. • Stoppa -Rives repair - It is used for the repair of large, recurrent, or bilateral hernias. In this method , a sub-umbilical midline incision is given to place a large mesh into the preperitoneal space . • Herniotomy - It is used to treat inguinal hernia in a child which occurs due to the presence of a patent processus vaginalis. Therefore in herniotomy, the repair of the inguinal ring is not done.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old obese male patient presented with bilateral, large inguinal hernias. He had been operated on for hernia twice in the past and is now posted for Stoppa 's repair. Which of the following statements regarding this procedure is false ?

options.a: This procedure refers to open preperitoneal hernia repair
options.b: The mesh is placed in the retromuscular space
options.c: The mesh needs to be sutured to the posterior rectus sheath in case of small defects
options.d: This procedure is based on the principle of Pascal's law

mcqs.explanation: With smaller defects , the mesh does not need to be sutured in Stoppa 's repair. This is based on Pascal's law. Pascal's law states that any additional pressure exerted on an enclosed fluid mass is transmitted equally in all directions .The abdomen is an enclosed space and intra-abdominal pressure is distributed equally over the mesh, thereby keeping the mesh in place . Stoppa 's repair is an open preperitoneal mesh repair primarily indicated for large, recurrent, bilateral hernias. In Stoppa 's mesh repair, a large piece of mesh is placed in the retro muscular space , over the posterior rectus sheath or peritoneum . This mesh is not sutured in patients with small defects because it is held in place by intra-abdominal pressure (Pascal's law). This allows the eventual incorporation of the mesh with the surrounding tissues . Alternatively, in larger defects , the mesh can be secured laterally with several sutures .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 2-year-old boy was brought to the clinic with a history of a reducible and painless swelling in the right groin for the past 2 months. After the clinical and radiological investigations, the diagnosis of a right-sided inguinal hernia was made. The patient is posted for hernia repair surgery. Which of the following steps will not be done in this patient during the repair?
mcqs.explanation: Inguinal hernia in a child is treated by herniotomy. In this procedure , repair of the inguinal ring is not done.653 This is because the inguinal hernia in the pediatric population is due to the presence of patent processus vaginalis and not due to the weakening of the abdominal muscles or the ligaments . Herniotomy involves either reduction of the hernial sac alone, or opening of the hernial sac, reduction of the contents , transfixation of the neck, and excision of the patent processus vaginalis/ hernial sac.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate mesh for use in hernioplasty ?
mcqs.explanation: The most appropriate mesh used in hernioplasty is a lightweight mesh with large pores . Lightweight meshes generally contain less material and induce a less -pronounced foreign body reaction and decreased inflammatory response , which results in better tissue incorporation, increased prosthesis compliance , and decreased patient discomfort and pain. Meshes with large pores exhibit less inflammatory infiltrate, connective tissue , and scar bridging, which allows increased soft tissue ingrowth. They have greater elasticity and flexibility and also shrink less resulting in lesser adhesions, better tissue incorporation, and decreased patient discomfort and pain. So the best mesh type among the given options is lightweight mesh with large pores . Meshes used in hernioplasty can be synthetic or biological depending on their composition. Synthetic meshes are made from polypropylene , polyester , or PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene). PTFE meshes are hydrophobic with a lower risk of adhesion. Biological meshes are acellular matrix materials derived from humans or animals and have lesser complications. But due to poor collagen deposition and absorption, they rapidly lose mechanical strength and hence their use is restricted to infected environments. Note : To promote better tissue integration, a composite mesh was developed which combines the attributes of polypropylene and PTFE by layering the two substances on top of one another.POLYPROP YLENE POLYESTE R PTFE monofilam ent multifilame nt solid hydrophobi c hydrophilic hydropho bic rigid elastic rigid

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient operated for direct inguinal hernia developed sensory loss at the root of the penis and adjacent part of the scrotum. Which of the following nerves is most likely injured?
mcqs.explanation: Loss of sensation in the root of the penis and adjacent part of the scrotum is suggestive of an injury to the ilioinguinal nerve. It is most commonly injured within the inguinal canal in open hernia repair due to traction or thermal injury.654 The iliohypogastric nerve carries the sensory supply from the suprapubic area. Injury to this nerve in the right iliac fossa rarely causes sensory disturbances , as the suprapubic area has a rich nerve supply from other sources too. If the nerve is severed above the anterior superior iliac spine , it can lead to the weakened posterior wall of the inguinal canal resulting in direct inguinal hernia. Iliohypogastric nerve can also get injured following appendicectomy . Injury to the genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve results in loss of sensation in the skin of the scrotum of males, and loss of sensation of the mons pubis and labia majora in females . Injury to the femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve causes hypoesthesia over the anterior thigh below the inguinal ligament .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old male patient with chronic constipation is diagnosed with Type 7 Gilbert hernia. This refers to ______
mcqs.explanation: Femoral hernia is classified under type 7 Gilbert hernia. As per Nyhus classification system , femoral hernia is classified under type 3C.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about femoral hernia is true?

options.b: All femoral hernias should be repaired
options.d: Femoral vein lies medial to the sac

mcqs.explanation: All femoral hernias should be repaired and incarcerated femoral hernias should have the hernia sac contents examined for viability. Option A: Femoral hernia occurs in both males and females , but it is more common in multiparous females . Femoral hernia is more common on the right side because of the tamponading effect of the sigmoid colon on the left femoral canal. This effect is absent on the right side . Option C: The incidence of strangulation in femoral hernias is high because of the narrowness of the neck of the sac and rigidity of the femoral ring. Option D: Femoral vein is situated lateral to a femoral hernia (femoral canal).655

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Match the following surgeries for femoral hernia with their indications:
mcqs.explanation: The correct option is 1-B, 2-A, 3-D, 4-C.Surgery Indication 1.Lockwood'ssurgery B.Electiverepair 2.McEvedy 'ssurgery A. Presence of bowelinfarctio n 3.Lotheissen'ssurger y D.Trans -inguinalapproach 4.McVay'ssurgery C. For bothfemoralandinguin alhernia

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In Laugier's hernia, the opening is in the _____
mcqs.explanation: Laugier's hernia is an atypical femoral hernia where the sac herniates through a gap in the lacunar (Gimbernat's) ligament .656

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about Spigelian hernia is false ?

options.a: It occurs above the level of the arcuate line
options.b: The hernia sac is posterior to the external oblique aponeurosis
options.c: Most commonly presents as a painless mass

mcqs.explanation: Usually , Spigelian hernias do not present as a mass because it is beneath the intact external oblique aponeurosis . The most common presentation in Spigelian hernia is pain. There is a common misconception that they protrude below the arcuate line owing to the deficiency of the posterior rectus sheath at that level ; but in fact, the defect is almost always above the arcuate line.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: While performing an elective hernia repair, the surgeon notices that the posterior wall of the hernia sac is formed by the sigmoid colon. What is this type of hernia known as?
mcqs.explanation: 657 The given clinical scenario is that of a sliding hernia. Sliding hernia occurs when an internal organ composes a portion of the wall of the hernia sac. The most common viscus involved are as follows : • Left side : sigmoid colon and its mesentery • Right side : cecum It is more common on the left side . Most sliding hernias are variants of indirect inguinal hernias. The primary danger associated with a sliding hernia is the failure to recognize the visceral component of the hernia sac resulting in injury to the bowel or bladder . Option A: A lumbar hernia is a posterolateral body wall hernia where the bowel , omentum, or pre-peritoneal fat herniates through the lumbar triangles. Option C: A Spigelian hernia occurs through slit-like defects in the anterior abdominal wall adjacent to the semilunar line. Most spigelian hernias occur in the lower abdomen where the posterior sheath is deficient . It is also called "spontaneous lateral ventral hernia" or "hernia of the semilunar line". Option D: A pantaloon hernia occurs when both a direct and an indirect hernia develop on the same side of the groin. The hernia is named pantaloon because the two hernia sacs are divided by epigastric vessels , and so they look like a pair of pants.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A middle -aged male patient underwent adrenalectomy for Cushing's syndrome one year back. He now presents with a history of chronic lower back pain. On examination, a partially reducible mass that increased in size during Valsalva maneuver was noticed on his lower back. Which of the following statements regarding the patient 's condition is false ?

options.a: Herniation may have occured through the Grynfelt 's triangle
options.b: The inferior lumbar triangle is bound by the external oblique and latismus dorsi muscle
options.c: Herniation is relatively more common on the right side
options.d: Dowd Ponka technique is used for surgical repair

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of an iatrogenic lumbar hernia which developed due to weakening of the posterior abdominal wall due to surgery. It occurs more commonly on the left side . A lumbar hernia is a posterolateral body wall hernia where the bowel , omentum, or pre-peritoneal fat herniates through the lumbar triangles. Causes can be congenital , acquired, traumatic, or iatrogenic. It is frequently confused for lipomas, muscle strains, fibromas, abscesses , and kidney tumors.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which type of hernia is depicted in the following diagram?
mcqs.explanation: The diagram shows Maydl 's hernia/Hernia-en-W/retrograde hernia, where 2 loops of the bowel remain in the hernia sac with the connecting loop inside the abdomen. Option A: In Richter's hernia, a small portion of the antimesenteric wall of the intestine is trapped within the hernia. Strangulation can occur without the presence of intestinal obstruction . Clinically , it mimics gastroenteritis . Option B: In Littre's hernia, Meckel 's diverticulum is the content . Amyand's hernia is an inguinal hernia in which the hernia sac contains a normal or acutely inflamed appendix . Option C: Petersen hernia is caused by the herniation of intestinal loops through the defect between the small bowel limbs, the transverse mesocolon , and the retroperitoneum , after any type658 of gastrojejunostomy .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old fit athlete presents to the OPD with complaints of nausea and heartburn. On examination , a soft , pea -sized swelling could be palpated on his abdomen. What is the likely diagnosis in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The likely diagnosis in this patient is epigastric hernia, also known as fatty hernia of linea alba. Epigastric hernia is located between the xiphoid process and umbilicus , usually in the midline. It occurs more commonly in males. A soft midline swelling can be felt more easily than seen . Pain occurs due to the incarceration of the preperitoneal fat and may simulate peptic ulcer. There is no overlying sac.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An 83-year-old lady was brought to the OPD with a two -day history of nausea, thigh pain and obstipation. Her family reported a significant weight loss over the last year attributed to grieving over her son's death . On examination, there is no lump in her groin. But, she experiences pain along the anteromedial aspect of her thigh which is relieved by thigh flexion. Which of the following statements regarding her condition is true?

options.a: Femoral hernia is the most likely diagnosis
options.b: Howship Romberg sign can be elicited
options.c: Transinguinal approach is preferred for surgery
options.d: These hernias are almost always interparietal

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and examination findings are suggestive of obturator hernia. Howship -Romberg sign can be seen in patients with obturator hernia. Howship -Romberg sign refers to pain in the anteromedial aspect of the thigh due to compression of the obturator nerve that is relieved by thigh flexion. Obturator hernia is also known as skinny old lady hernia and French hernia. It occurs more commonly in thin, elderly , debilitated females . Predisposing factors are: • Women with wider pelvis and more triangular obturator canal • Malnutrition • Chronic constipation • Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) • Multiparity • Ascites • Kyphoscoliosis Intestinal obstruction can occur. Option A: Femoral hernias commonly present as a small lump in the groin. They may be asymptomatic or present with strangulation in about 30% of patients . Option C: A posterior approach, open or laparoscopic surgery is the treatment of choice . This approach provides direct access to the hernia. Option D: Interparietal hernias are rare and occur when the sac lies between layers of the abdominal wall. These hernias most frequently occur in previous incisions. Spigelian hernias are almost always interparietal .659

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Hernia with hydrocele is known as ________.
mcqs.explanation: Gibbon's hernia is a hernia with hydrocele . Option B: Berger's hernia is hernia into the pouch of Douglas . Option C: Beclard's hernia is femoral hernia through the opening of the saphenous vein. Option D: Ogilvie's hernia is hernia through a defect in conjoint tendon just lateral to where it inserts with the rectus sheath . Edward Gibbon, the author of "The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire," was greatly embarrassed by a large hydrocele . The second time that it was tapped , it became infected , and Gibbon died a few days later. The hydrocele was associated with a large scrotal hernia which had probably been punctured .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: According to the European Hernia Society classification , M3 incisional hernia refers to:
mcqs.explanation: According to the European Hernia Society classification , M3 incisional hernia refers to umbilical hernia. According to the European Hernia Society classification of incisional hernias: Midline incisional hernias are classified as- Lateral incisional hernias are classified as-M1 Subxiphoida l M2 Epigastric M3 Umbilical660 M1 Subxiphoida l M4 Infraumbilic al M5 SuprapubicL1 Subcos tal L2 Flank L3 Iliac L4 Lumba r

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A young female patient who had been suffering from chronic abdominal pain is rushed to the casualty due to acute exacerbation. On further investigations, she is diagnosed with intestinal obstruction secondary to a paraduodenal hernia. Which of the following statements regarding the hernia is false ?

options.a: Left-sided hernia is found in the fossa of Landzert
options.b: Right sided hernia is found in the fossa of Kolb
options.d: It is more common on the right side

mcqs.explanation: Paraduodenal hernia is more common on the left side (75 %). Option A: In Left-sided paraduodenal hernia, bowel herniates through the fossa of Landzert.Option B: In right-sided paraduodenal hernia, bowel herniates through the fossa of Waldeyer /Kolb.661 Both the fossa of Landzert and the fossa of Waldeyer/Kolb are formed due to congenital mesenteric fusion defects . Option C: Paraduodenal hernia is the most common internal hernia and they are usually congenital .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An infant who is diagnosed with congenital hypothyroidism presents with the following hernia. Which of the following statements is false regarding the management of this child?

options.a: The hernia may spontaneously resolve by 2 years of age
options.b: Surgical repair is indicated if the hernia persists for more than 5 years of age
options.c: Strangulation is a common complication associated with this hernia in this child
options.d: Mayo's procedure or mesh repair can be done for this hernia

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical history of congenital hypothyroidism and the image showing a mass protruding out of the umbilicus are indicative of an umbilical hernia. Obstruction and strangulation are uncommon below the age of 3 years. Mayo's operation is done for umbilical hernia. A small curved incision is made below the umbilicus and the neck of the sac is opened . The contents are returned to the peritoneal cavity and the redundant sac is excised after closing it. Defect in the linea alba is closed with interrupted sutures . Indications for surgery in umbilical hernia are: • Defect size >2cm • Persisting beyond 5 years • Progressively enlarging after 2 years of age (usually regresses spontaneously by 2 years of age ) • Symptomatic • Strangulated In adults , defects up to 2cm in diameter may be sutured primarily with minimal tension. However, with larger defects , mesh reinforcement will be beneficial .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A baby was born with a congenital defect as shown below . Which of the following statements is false regarding this condition?

options.b: It is due to failure of physiological hernia to reduce before 7 weeks
options.d: Topical application of silver nitrate is done

mcqs.explanation: 662 The congenital defect showing herniation of the intestinal contents enclosed in a sac from the umbilicus is suggestive of omphalocele. It is due to the failure of the physiological hernia to reduce into the abdominal cavity before 10 weeks resulting in non-closure of the umbilical ring. Physiological herniation of the midgut through the umbilicus occurs during the 5th week so as to accommodate the rapidly growing intestine and persists until the 10th week . Omphalocele is seen in term babies and is usually associated with other congenital anomalies (e.g., trisomy 13 , trisomy 18, or Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome) and with increased levels of \033-fetoprotein . An omphalocele may contain the stomach, liver, and intestines . These contents are enclosed in a sac. The treatment is as follows : • Preservation of the intact sac with a sterile , moistened , saline gauze or transparent bowel bag. • IV fluids should be started , along with gastric tube decompression and IV antibiotics. • Topical application of povidone-iodine ointment, merbromin (mercurochrome), or silver nitrate allows the sac to thicken and epithelialize gradually . • Primary surgical closure is preferred for small to medium-sized defects .663

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 3-month-old child presented with umbilical discharge . Abdomen examination was normal except for the below finding. The next step of management is?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical image is that of a congenital umbilical anomaly such as patent urachus, urachal cyst, and vitelline cyst (resulting from the persistence of omphalomesenteric duct ). The next best step is the USG abdomen to diagnose if the anomaly is cystic , fibrous or fistula and it's connections. Omphalomesenteric duct abnormalities: Vitello intestinal duct or omphalomesenteric duct is the connection between the yolk sac and the midgut during embryonic life , which eventually gets obliterated . The persistence of the vitellointestinal duct leads to various abnormalities depending on which part of the duct remains patent . • Persistence of the proximal intestinal end of the duct leads to Meckel 's diverticula. • Persistence of the distal end near the umbilicus leads to the umbilical polyp or sinus. • Persistence of the distal end with mucus retention leads to the cyst , which may be associated with the intestine or the umbilicus by a fibrous band. • A fully patent vitellointestinal duct can lead to an enterocutaneous fistula .664 Patent urachus occurs due to the failure of urachus to obliterate , resulting in a connection between the bladder and the umbilicus. Urachal cyst occurs when the urachus fails to obliterate but there is no connection between the bladder and the umbilicus . The given image below shows a urachal cyst (UC) attached to Meckel 's diverticulum (MD) on one side and urinary bladder (UB) on the other side with a patent tract- urachus (U).

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most commonly seen tumor in the retroperitoneal space ?
mcqs.explanation: Liposarcoma is the most commonly seen tumor in retroperitoneal space . Retroperitoneal tumors can be benign or malignant. Malignant retroperitoneal tumors may be mesodermal (75 %), neuroectodermal (24%), or embryonic remnant (1%) in origin. Rarely it can665 be urologic or metastatic also. The order of frequency of primary retroperitoneal malignancy is as follows : • Liposarcoma • Leiomyosarcoma • Rhabdomyosarcoma • Fibrosarcoma • Malignant nerve sheath tumors Liposarcoma is composed of three histologic varieties (listed in order of decreasing frequency): • Well-differentiated and undifferentiated liposarcoma • Pleomorphic liposarcoma • Myxoid /round cell liposarcoma Among the three subtypes , pleomorphic liposarcoma is the most malignant and often metastasizes, while the well -differentiated is the least malignant. Myxoid liposarcoma has intermediate malignant behavior. Diagnosis is confirmed by contrast-enhanced CT with CT of the chest to look for metastases . Surgery is the main modality of treatment . Wide excision with complete en bloc dissection is done. Post-operative radiotherapy and chemotherapy are used as adjuvant methods . Radiotherapy is given at a dose of 5000 cGY, it can be external beam or intra-operative radiotherapy. Chemotherapeutic agents used are mesna, adriamycin, ifosfamide and dacarbazine (MAID regimen).666

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a false statement regarding the anatomy of the liver?

options.a: Cantlie's line divides the liver functionally into two hemi-livers
options.b: The liver has 2 major and 2 minor fissures .
options.c: Three main hepatic veins divide the liver into four portal sectors
options.d: Each Couinaud's segment has its own vascular supply , biliary drainage and lymphatic drainage

mcqs.explanation: The liver has 3 major and 3 minor fissures .678 The major portal fissures (are not visible on the liver surface and run through the parenchyma) • Middle /main portal fissure (Cantlie's line) • extends from the midpoint of the gallbladder fossa at the inferior margin of the liver back to the midpoint of the inferior vena cava . • Contains the middle hepatic vein • Separates the liver into the right and left hemi-livers. • Right portal fissure • Contains the right hepatic vein • Divides the liver into the right anterior/medial sector (segments V and VIII ) and right posterior/lateral sector (segments VI and VII ). • Left portal fissure • Contains the left hepatic vein • Separates the left anterior/medial (segments IV ) and left posterior/lateral sectors (Segment II and III ) The three minor fissures (are visible as physical clefts of the liver surface ) • Umbilical fissure or fissure for the ligamentum teres • Venous fissure or fissure for the ligamentum venosum • Fissure of gans or Rouvi \350re's sulcus

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A young patient presents with distension of the abdomen and yellowish discoloration of the eyes for the past 6 months. After a detailed workup, he is diagnosed with early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma in the left lobe of the liver. The surgeon decides to perform a left hemi-hepatectomy . Which of the following segments has to be removed in the patient ?
mcqs.explanation: In the left hemi-hepatectomy (also called left hepatectomy ) the segments marked as II , III , and IV should be removed. Couinaud classification is the commonly used classification of the liver. It divides the liver is divided into eight segments . Each segment has its own vascular supply , biliary drainage, and lymphatic drainage. Segment I corresponds to the caudate lobe of the liver and segment IV corresponds to the quadrate lobe of the liver. The Couinaud's Liver Segments are as follows :679

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the most common anomaly of the hepatic artery?

options.a: Independent origin of the right and left hepatic arteries from the cealic axis
options.b: Replaced right hepatic artery arising from the superior mesentric artery

mcqs.explanation: The most common anomaly of the hepatic artery is replaced right hepatic artery arising from the superior mesenteric artery. Normally, the common hepatic artery gives off the right and left hepatic arteries. A middle hepatic artery branches off from the proximal left hepatic artery. The replaced right hepatic artery directly supplies the right lobe of the liver. Surgical significance : In individuals with replaced right hepatic artery, the diameter of the common hepatic artery is smaller. In liver transplant recipients , this can be a cause for the increased incidence of complications such as thrombosis. Whereas, replaced right hepatic artery is a beneficial variant for donors undergoing donation of the right lobe of the liver. The replaced right hepatic artery provides a longer and larger graft thus reducing chances of thrombosis.680

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: The free hepatic venous pressure (FHVP ) and wedged hepatic venous pressure (WHVP ) of a patient , with suspected portal hypertension, are measured . How will the hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) be determined from these values?
mcqs.explanation: Hepatic Venous Pressure Gradient is measured by subtracting Free Hepatic Venous Pressure from Wedged Hepatic Venous Pressure. HVPG = WHVP – FHVP Hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) is the pressure gradient between the portal vein and the inferior vena cava (IVC ). It is a measure of portal venous pressure . It can quantify the degree of portal hypertension due to sinusoidal resistance to blood flow . The most accurate method of determining portal hypertension is by measuring HVPG . The most commonly used procedure involves placing a balloon catheter in the hepatic vein after a jugular vein puncture . The free hepatic venous pressure (FHVP ) is measured with the balloon deflated , and the wedged hepatic venous pressure (WHVP ) with the balloon inflated to occlude the hepatic681 vein.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following values indicate a normal portal venous pressure ?
mcqs.explanation: The normal portal venous pressure is 5 to 10 mmHg. Normal portal blood flow is 1 to 1.5 L/minute. Hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) is the difference between the wedge and free hepatic venous pressure, which is 1 to 5 mmHg. HVPG interpretation : • Normal HVPG is between 1 and 5 mmHg. • Portal hypertension is present if the HVPG is �o 6 mmHg. • Portal hypertension typically becomes clinically significant when the HVPG is �o 10 mmHg, at which point varices may develop . • HVPG �o 12 mmHg, patients are at risk for variceal bleeding and the development of ascites .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: All of the following are post -hepatic causes for portal hypertension , except _____
mcqs.explanation: Splenomegaly is a pre-hepatic cause of portal hypertension . Sarcoidosis and primary biliary cholangitis are presinusoidal intrahepatic causes of portal hypertension . Portal hypertension occurs when the pressure in the portal vein increases due to either increased resistance to blood flow secondary to fibrosis, active vasoconstriction, or hyperdynamic systemic circulation.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient who is a known case of chronic pancreatitis is diagnosed with splenic vein thrombosis. Which of the following is not true about this condition?

options.b: USG abdomen showed normal liver and an enlarged spleen .
options.d: TIPSS is done as part of treatment

mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario points to a case of splenic vein thrombosis which can cause left -sided portal hypertension. It is a pre-hepatic cause of portal hypertension . It is managed by splenectomy . Splenic vein thrombosis can be due to pancreatic inflammation or neoplasms (acute or chronic pancreatitis, pseudocysts , and carcinomas) that extend outside the pancreas and invades the splenic vein. This causes increased pressure in the splenic vein leading to the formation of collaterals and ultimately gastric variceal hemorrhage (not esophageal varices). Normal liver function tests , normal portal venous pressures , and splenomegaly are the distinguishing features from other forms of portal hypertension . The portal vein pressures remain normal as there is no obstruction of the hepatic venous vasculature. Diagnosis is done by gastroscopy , liver function tests , ultrasound examination (with doppler ), and contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen. Treatment includes splenectomy and management of the primary pancreatic pathology .682

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An elderly patient with chronic black tarry stools underwent an upper GI endoscopy . Gastric mucosa appeared as shown below . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows the snake-skin appearance of the gastric mucosa, which is seen in cases of portal hypertensive gastropathy . Portal hypertensive gastropathy is characterized by the diffuse dilation of the mucosal and submucosal venous plexus of the stomach associated with overlying gastritis. Option A: Gastric antral vascular ectasia (GAVE) also known as watermelon stomach is a significant cause of acute or chronic gastrointestinal blood loss in the elderly , characterized endoscopically by watermelon stripes . It is associated with heterogeneous medical conditions, including hepatic , cardiac, and renal diseases .683 Option C: Hypoproteinemic hypertrophic gastropathy also known as Menetrier 's disease is a rare, acquired premalignant disease of the stomach characterized by massive gastric folds , little or no acid production , and excessive mucous production with resultant protein loss. The disorder is associated with excessive secretion of transforming growth factor-alpha.Option D: Dieulafoy 's lesion is a medical condition characterized by a large tortuous arteriole that erodes and bleeds and occurs most commonly in the stomach wall.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding Budd-Chiari syndrome?

options.a: Caudate lobe hypertrophy is seen in approximately 50% of the patients
options.b: Doppler ultrasonography is the initial investigation of choice
options.c: It becomes clinically significant when one or more major hepatic veins are obstructed
options.d: Oral contraceptive use is a risk factor

mcqs.explanation: Budd–Chiari syndrome (BCS) is an uncommon congestive hepatopathy characterized by the obstruction of hepatic venous outflow and it becomes clinically significant when two or more major hepatic veins are obstructed .684 Types : • Primary Budd–Chiari syndrome: when the obstructive process involves an endoluminal venous thrombosis. • Secondary Budd–Chiari syndrome: when the veins are compressed or invaded by a neighboring lesion originating outside the vein. Most common presentation : ascites and abdominal discomfort. Risk factors include -Primary myeloproliferative disorders, anticardiolipin antibodies , hyperhomocysteinemia , and oral contraceptive use . Caudate lobe hypertrophy is seen in approximately 50% of the cases and it is because the caudate lobe drains directly into the IVC . Abdominal ultrasonography with color Doppler is the initial investigation of choice and can demonstrate the absence of hepatic vein flow , spider web hepatic veins, and collateral hepatic veins. The definitive radiographic study is hepatic venography to determine the presence and extent of hepatic vein thrombus as well as measure inferior vena cava (IVC ) pressures .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 43-year-old woman presented to the hospital with complaints of abdominal pain and distension for the past 3 months. Her past medical records show that she has a JAK2 mutation and investigations revealed serum protein to be 3 g/dL and ascitic fluid protein to be 1.5 g/dL. Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.a: Anticoagulation is the mainstay of treatment
options.b: Colour flow doppler is the initial investigation of choice
options.c: Surgical intervention is done in all cases
options.d: Ascites is a bad prognostic factor

mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario describes a case of late budd -chiari syndrome and surgical interventions are not done in all cases of budd chiari syndrome. SAAG = (serum albumin) � (ascitic fluid albumin) = (3) - (1.5) = 1.5g/dL As SAAG is >1.1g/dL( 1.5g/dL) and ascitic fluid protein is < 2.5 g/dL, the most likely cause is late Budd-Chiari syndrome.Surgical interventions are done in those patients of Budd Chiari syndrome who are not responding to medical therapy . Colour flow doppler is the initial investigation of choice . Treatment: • Initial treatment consists of medically managing the underlying disease process and preventing the extension of the hepatic vein thrombosis through systemic anticoagulation . • The associated portal hypertension and ascites are managed in a manner similar to that in most cirrhotic patients . • Radiologic and surgical intervention should be reserved for patients whose condition is nonresponsive to medical therapy . Percutaneous angioplasty and transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS), in combination with thrombolytic therapy , are the preferred strategies to restore the outflow of blood from the liver. • Surgical shunting, particularly with the side -to-side portacaval shunt, turns the portal vein into a hepatic outflow tract . Factors contributing to a bad prognosis in Budd-Chiari syndrome: • 685 Involvement of all three hepatic veins and/or portal vein • Presence of ascites • Older age at the time of presentation • High Child-Pugh score • Chronic disease at presentation Note : JAK2 mutation points to a possibility of polycythemia vera predisposing the patient to hypercoagulable states and the formation of thrombus anywhere in the body. From the serum and ascitic protein values, we can calculate the SAAG (serum protein-ascitic protein).

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient comes with active variceal bleeding . Which of the following is not done?
mcqs.explanation: Platelet transfusion is not done in the case of active variceal bleeding unless coagulopathy is confirmed as the cause . Platelet transfusions are indicated only in patients with a platelet count of <50,000/microL or in patients with evidence of microvascular bleeding . Variceal hemorrhage is a medical emergency . Varices usually present with the acute onset large-volume haematemesis , the lower esophagus being the most common site for variceal bleeding . The sites for portosystemic anastomosis are: • Left gastric vein to distal oesophageal veins: oesophageal and gastric variceal bleeding • Superior rectal veins to Middle and inferior rectal veins: hemorrhoids and rectal bleeding • Left branch of the portal vein to Periumbilical veins: caput -medusae • The right branch of the portal vein to retroperitoneal veins draining into azygos, hemiazygos , lumbar, intercostal , and phrenic veins • Omental and colonic veins near hepatic and splenic \037exures to Retroperitoneal veins near hepatic and splenic \037exures Medical management of variceal bleeding includes blood transfusion (option B) and drug therapy with somatostatin analogs like octreotide (option C). Short-term antibiotics like ceftriaxone are known to decrease bacterial infection and increase survival . Surgical measures are preferred if medical management fails. They include balloon tamponade , endoscopic banding (option D), transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS), portosystemic shunts, splenectomy , and gastric revascularization Note : Sugiura procedure is the non-shunt surgical management of refractory oesophageal variceal bleeding . It is a procedure of de -vascularizing the distal esophagus and stomach.686

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 56-year-old patient with intractable ascites underwent a procedure as shown below . Identify the procedure .
mcqs.explanation: The image shows the transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt(TIPS) procedure with the viatorr device. The main indication of TIPS is for variceal bleeds not responding to medical or endoscopic treatment, and intractable ascites . The shunts are inserted under local anaesthetic , analgesia and sedation , using fluoroscopic guidance and ultrasonography . Via the internal jugular vein and superior venacava , a guidewire is inserted into a hepatic vein and through the hepatic parenchyma into a branch of the portal vein. The main early complication of this technique is the perforation of the liver capsule and the main contraindication to TIPSS is portal vein occlusion . Shunts for Portal Hypertension : • Non- Selective Shunt- bowel and splenic blood is shunted • Linton shunt (proximal lienorenal shunt with splenectomy ) • ECK fistula (portocaval shunt) • Mitra shunt (splenorenal shunt) • Selective Shunt- only splenic blood is shunted • Warren shunt (distal lienorenal shunt) • Inokuchi shunt687

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient with liver cirrhosis is scheduled to undergo a laparotomy for a perforated appendix . According to the Child-Turcotte-Pugh score, which of the following parameters will you not use for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Creatinine is not included in the Child–Turcotte–Pugh score or Child-Pugh scoring system . It is used to assess the surgical mortality of cirrhotic patients undergoing intra-abdominal operations.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a component of MELD score?
mcqs.explanation: In MELD (model for end-stage liver disease ) score, urea is not one of the components .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old male patient who was diagnosed with gangrenous appendix underwent an appendicectomy . On the second postoperative day, he developed fever, chills, jaundice , and right upper quadrant pain. Blood cultures revealed bacteremia and ultrasound abdomen revealed multiple hepatic abscesses . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: In the setting of existing appendicitis , the above clinical scenario points to a diagnosis of pylephlebitis (portal pyemia ). Pylephlebitis is thrombophlebitis of the portal venous system . It is a rare but very serious complication of intra-abdominal infections, such as gangrenous appendicitis , diverticulitis , etc . It spreads to the portal circulation via the mesenteric vein. Clinical features are high fever, rigors, and jaundice and intrahepatic abscesses (often multiple ) due to septicemia in the portal venous system . Treatment is with systemic antibiotics and percutaneous drainage of hepatic abscesses . Option A: Peliosis hepatis is an uncommon vascular condition characterized by hemorrhagic dilatation of the hepatic sinusoids . Option C: Hepatic necrotic nodules are usually small, solitary lesions , mainly located under the liver capsule of the right lobe . It is characterized by a necrotic central core surrounded by a dense688 hyalinized fibrotic capsule . Option D: Melioidosis is an infectious disease caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei characterised by fever and multiple abscess formation in the lungs , liver, prostate , and spleen .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old male patient presented to the hospital with right upper quadrant pain and jaundice for the past 5 days. CT abdomen revealed the following finding and cultures of aspirate showed extensive bacterial growth . Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.a: Anchovy sauce pus is seen on aspiration of abscess
options.b: Fever with chills is the most common presenting complaint
options.c: Eschericia coli and Klebsiella species are the most common organisms implicated
options.d: Ascending infection from the biliary tract is the most common route of spread

mcqs.explanation: The given CT image shows cluster sign and the above clinical scenario is suggestive of pyogenic liver abscess . Anchovy sauce pus on aspiration is seen in amoebic liver abscess . Pyogenic liver abscess is a polymicrobial infection seen more commonly in the elderly and immunocompromised. Ascending infection from the biliary tree (ascending suppurative cholangitis ) is the most common route of spread . The portal vein is the second most common source of infection leading to pylephlebitis (thrombophlebitis of the portal venous system causing portal pyemia ) secondary to diverticulitis , appendicitis , pancreatitis , etc . Organism: • Most common in western countries : Escherichia coli • Most common in Asian countries : Klebsiella pneumoniae • Most common in children suffering from the chronic granulomatous disease : Staphylococcus • Most common in gas-forming abscess: Klebsiella Order of affected lobe : Right lobe (75 %) > left lobe (20 %) > caudate lobe (5%). Right lobe predilection might be due to preferential laminar blood flow .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding investigations in a pyogenic liver abscess is true?

options.b: USG shows hypoechoic lesion with poorly defined borders
options.c: Elevated ALP is the most common abnormal LFT .

mcqs.explanation: Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP ) level is the most common abnormal liver function test (LFT ) in pyogenic liver abscess . Laboratory features in pyogenic liver abscess : • Non-specific findings such as leukocytosis , anemia • Elevated ALP (most common), elevated bilirubin levels , increased prothrombin time (PT) and INR (chronic infection ). • Positive blood culture in 50% cases Ultrasonography (USG) and computed tomography (CT) are investigations of choice . In ultrasound, pyogenic liver abscess appears as round or oval hypoechoic lesions with well defined borders and variable number of internal echoes . On CT, cluster sign is a feature of pyogenic hepatic abscesses . Cluster sign in CT:689

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A healthy 55 -year-old man presented with a 1-week history of fevers, chills, right upper quadrant tenderness , and hepatomegaly . CT was suggestive of a pyogenic liver abscess . Which of the following statements regarding management is true?

options.a: Empiric IV antibiotic therapy is first line
options.b: Percutaneous drainage is not routinely done
options.c: Open drainage is done with T-tube placement
options.d: Resection of the affected lobe is the treatment of choice

mcqs.explanation: Empiric IV antibiotic therapy is the first-line treatment for pyogenic liver abscess . Percutaneous drainage using a pigtail catheter is done routinely . It helps in the slow decompression of a cyst with viscous contents . It also has a lesser chance of dislodgement . Drainage tube catheter is placed under US/CT guidance into the liver abscess . Surgical drainage using a laparoscopic or open approach is tried only when antibiotic therapy and percutaneous drainage fails. Open drainage is becoming less common at present . Liver resection is only occasionally required in severe hepatic destruction . Pigtail catheter :690

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old daily wage laborer presented with fever and abdominal pain for the past 1 week . Laboratory investigations showed anti-amoebic antibodies and CT abdomen showed the following . Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.b: Anchovy sauce pus is seen on aspiration

mcqs.explanation: The patient most likely has an amoebic liver abscess . It is more common in males than females (10 :1). Risk factors include : • Males , -40 years of age • Heavy alcohol consumption - liver becomes more susceptible • Travel to an endemic area • Poverty and cramped living conditions • Impaired host immunity • Colonic infection The most common sites for amoebic liver abscesses are liver and paracaecal areas. The aspirate shows a characteristic anchovy sauce pus . Even though this disease process is secondary to a colonic infection , the presence of diarrhoea is unusual.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding amoebic liver abscess is false ?

options.a: Culture of the aspirate is positive .
options.b: The diagnosis is based on the detection of antiamebic antibodies .
options.c: Management mainly consists of conservative treatment with metronidazole .

mcqs.explanation: The culture of the amoebic abscess is usually sterile or negative . The most useful laboratory evaluation is the measurement of circulating anti-amoebic antibodies , by enzyme immunoassay. The antibody can be present because of prior infection , and hence , detection of Entamoeba histolytica lectin antigen in the serum and liver abscess pus is more useful for acute infections than chronic infection. Nuclear medicine studies , such as gallium scanning or technetium (99mTc ) liver scans, can be helpful in differentiating pyogenic from amebic abscesses because amebic abscesses typically do not contain leukocytes and therefore do not light up on these scans. The mainstay of treatment for amebic abscesses is metronidazole (750 mg orally, three times daily for 10 days), which is curative. Luminal agents such as iodoquinol, paromomycin, and diloxanide furoate can be administered into the cysts .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following are not indications for percutaneous aspiration in a patient with a suspected amoebic liver abscess ?

options.c: Failure to respond to medical therapy

mcqs.explanation: Percutaneous aspiration should be performed in amoebic liver abscess more than 5 cm. Indications for percutaneous aspiration in amoebic liver abscess are: • Large abscesses (>5 cm) • Lack of response to medical therapy (in 5 days) • Suspicion of superinfection691 • Abscesses of the left lobe of the liver at risk for rupture into the pericardium • Uncertain diagnosis Laboratory investigations may reveal similar complete blood cell count and liver function test abnormalities in patients with amoebic liver abscesses and pyogenic liver abscesses . An elevated serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP ) level is seen in both and is not specific .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In the given image, which of the following structures are matched correctly?
mcqs.explanation: F -Endocyst and H-Hydatid sand are matched correctly.Hydatid disease or echinococcosis is a zoonotic infection caused by the Echinococcus species of flatworms. Its life cycle consists of sheep and dogs as hosts . Humans are accidental hosts . A hydatid cyst usually develops three weeks after the infection . The cyst is surrounded by a fibrous capsule called pericyst that is derived from the host tissue . The cyst wall is composed of two layers, ectocyst (outer gelatinous membrane), and endocyst (inner germinal membrane). Ectocyst is a laminated membrane, which is acellular . It helps in the passage of nutrients. The endocyst helps in producing the laminated membrane and scoleces . The brood capsules are cellular masses in the hydatid fluid which consists of scoleces . In a definitive host, these scoleces develop into adult tapeworm while in the intermediate hosts these develop into new hydatid cysts . The brood capsules are attached to the endocyst by a pedicle or stalk. The brood capsules may mature and detach from the mother cyst and become the daughter cysts , which are an exact replica of the mother cysts . The freed brood capsules and scoleces present in the hydatid fluid are called hydatid sand.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient was incidentally found to have a fluid filled cyst in his liver when he underwent a USG abdomen to check for renal calculi. It was later diagnosed as echinococcosis . Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.b: Rupture can lead to severe anaphylactic reaction
options.d: Echinococcus multilocularis is the most common causative agent

mcqs.explanation: 692 Echinococcus granulosus is the most common causative agent in hydatid cysts , while Echinococcus multilocularis and Echinococcus ligartus account for a small number of cases . Dogs are the definitive hosts of E. granulosus. Sheep are the usual intermediate hosts , and humans are accidental intermediate hosts . Humans are end-stage hosts of the parasite since there is no human to human transmission. The clinical presentation of a hydatid cyst is largely asymptomatic , until complications occur. The most common presenting symptoms are abdominal pain, dyspepsia , and vomiting. The most frequent sign is hepatomegaly . Approximately 75 % of hydatid cysts are located in the right lobe of the liver and are solitary. The life cycle of Echinococcus :Multiple hydatid cysts :693

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A young villager presents to the clinic with abdominal pain for the past 1 month. He mentions that he keeps sheep inside the house . On examination, you feel a firm mass in the right hypochondrium and a hepatic hydatid cyst is suspected . Which of the following investigations have the highest sensitivity in confirming the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Computed tomography (CT) scan is the best imaging modality for hydatid cyst . It shows the presence of a space -occupying lesion with a smooth outline with septa . CT scan has an accuracy of 98% in the detection of hydatid cysts and higher sensitivity to demonstrate the daughter cysts and extra-hepatic cysts . The indirect hemagglutination test and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) have a sensitivity of 80% overall and are the initial screening tests of choice . The Casoni test is a skin test used in the diagnosis of hydatid disease and involves the intradermal injection of 0.25 ml of sterilised fluid from hydatid cysts /human cysts . A wheal response occurring at the injection site within 20 minutes is considered positive (immediate hypersensitivity ). The test is positive in less than 50% of patients with hydatid disease elsewhere in the body and false -positive results are also common so it's not preferred . Note : First/Initial imaging test is USG, best imaging test is CT scan CT scan showing multiple hydatid cysts with detached wavy membranes:

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient is suspected to have a hydatid cyst of the liver. If imaging studies are performed , all of the following signs will denote detached or collapsed cyst except ____
mcqs.explanation: The double line sign is seen in an unruptured unilocular cyst with a double -layered wall representing the pericyst and endocyst . Serpent sign is seen as wavy membranes within the cyst , on CT imaging.694 Ball of wool sign is seen on ultrasound when the contents settle in the dependent portion of the cyst, as seen below .The water-lily sign is seen in hydatid infections when there is detachment of the endocyst membrane which results in floating membranes within the pericyst that mimic the appearance of a water lily, on USG.695

mcqs.question: A young sheep farmer presents to the OPD with pain in the right upper part of the abdomen. On examination, there is tenderness and enlargement of the liver. Abdominal ultrasound shows the following finding. As per the WHO classification of cystic echinococcosis , which class does this belong to?
mcqs.explanation: The ultrasound image is of active hydatid cyst with multiple septations and rosette or honeycomb appearance . As per the WHO classification of cystic echinococcosis (CE), it belongs to type 2 (CE2). mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man presents with right upper quadrant pain for the last 6 weeks . On examination , a firm mass is palpable in the right hypochondrium region. CECT abdomen shows a 6 cm cystic structure in the right lobe of the liver along with water lily sign. Which of the following is the ideal management for him?

options.d: Careful observation with imaging every 6 months

mcqs.explanation: The given imaging finding on CECT is suggestive of class CE3A hydatid cyst disease of the liver. The ideal management for type CE3A hydatid cyst of dimension >5cm is Albendazole therapy 400 mg twice daily and PAIR (puncture, aspiration, injection, and reaspiration) therapy . Classification of CE based on ultrasound imagingType Ultrasound features Active cyst CE1 Univesicular fluid collection CE2 Honeycomb appearance :Mult ivesicular fluid collection wit h daughter cysts separated by septae Transitional cyst CE3A Water lily sign:Fluid collectio n with detached membrane CE3B Daughter cysts present in a s olid matrix Inactive/dead cys t CE4 Cysts in a heterogeneous mat rix with no daughter cysts CE5 Solid cystic wall697 CE: cystic echinococcosis ; PAIR : puncture, aspiration, injection, and reaspiration When PAIR is contraindicated ( CE2, CE3B), surgical resection involving laparoscopic or open complete cystectomy with instillation of a scolicidal agent is preferred and is usually curative. mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a contraindication for performing PAIR technique in hydatid cyst disease ?

options.b: Pregnant woman with CE1 hydatid cyst
options.d: Cyst > 5 cm in different liver segments

mcqs.explanation: A hydatid cyst with honeycomb appearance (CE2) is a contraindication for PAIR (Puncture-Aspiration-Injection-Reaspiration). PAIR is unlikely to be successful in CE2 due to the presence of multiple internal septa . The PAIR technique is performed using either ultrasound or computed tomography (CT) guidance . It involves aspiration of the cyst contents via a special cannula, followed by injection of a scolicidal agent for at least 15 minutes, and then reaspiration of the cystic contents . This is repeated until the return is clear. An initial course of albendazole is administered before the procedure . When PAIR is contraindicated , surgical resection involving laparoscopic or open complete cystectomy with instillation of a scolicidal agent is preferred and is usually curative. If complete cystectomy is not possible , then anatomic liver resection can be undertaken.698

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A dog trainer presented to the hospital with a history of pain in the upper part of the abdomen. The surgeon decides to perform a percutaneous aspiration, injection, and reaspiration (PAIR ) of the cyst after a 6 cm single hydatid cyst was detected . All of the following can be used as scolicidal agents in this procedure except ?
mcqs.explanation: Formalin is not used as a scolicidal agent since it causes sclerosing cholangitis . Scolicidal agents (used to avoid dissemination of parasite during surgery): • Hypertonic saline • Cetrimide • Alcohol • Sodium hypochlorite • Povidone-iodine

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Capitonnage is used in the treatment of which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Capitonnage is used in the treatment of hydatid cyst disease . It is the spiral suturing of the cavity upward from the base of the cavity to the edge of the cyst wall. Pyogenic liver abscess is treated with antibiotics and percutaneous drainage. Hepatic tuberculosis is treated with quadruple therapy (isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol )699

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following do not cause peliosis hepatis ?
mcqs.explanation: Analgesics will not cause peliosis hepatis. Peliosis hepatis is an uncommon vascular condition characterized by hemorrhagic dilatation of the hepatic sinusoids . Conditions causing peliosis hepatis are: • Bartonella henselae infection , tuberculosis , and human immunodeficiency virus • Use of anabolic steroids • Immunosuppressants such as 6-mercaptopurine , azathioprine, methotrexate , and tamoxifen • X-linked myotubular myopathy Biopsy showing hemorrhagic dilatation:700 Often an incidental finding, many patients present without symptoms . Less frequently , patients may present with signs more consistent with hepatobiliary pathology such as right upper quadrant pain, jaundice , and signs of portal hypertension . Laboratory studies , such as LFT may or may not demonstrate changes . CT or MRI angiography often demonstrates contrast accumulating within the parenchyma itself or the sinusoids . A biopsy is the best modality to confirm the diagnosis.701

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the most common benign lesion of liver?
mcqs.explanation: Hemangiomas are the most common benign tumor of the liver. Focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) is the second most common benign tumor of the liver.707

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is not true about epithelioid hemangioma?

options.a: Exposure to vinyl chloride is a risk factor
options.b: Treatment of choice is liver transplantation
options.c: Factor VIII staining is used for diagnosis

mcqs.explanation: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma is more common in females . Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma is a rare vascular tumour. The infantile variety is benign, while the adult variety is malignant. It may undergo malignant degeneration into angiosarcoma. It is related to exposure to vinyl chloride and oral contraceptive pills (OCPs). It can affect the lungs , liver, and bones. In the liver, it manifests as multiple bilateral hepatic masses . Extrahepatic metastases occur in approximately 25% of patients . Liver failure is a fatal complication. Hypervascular enhancement is observed on CECT. A percutaneous biopsy can help differentiate from other tumours. Factor VIII staining differentiates it from other nonvascular tumours. Treatment is total hepatectomy with liver transplantation.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman was incidentally found to have a lesion in the right lobe of the liver during an abdominal ultrasound. CECT showed the following finding. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given CECT abdomen shows a well -defined hypodense lesion in the liver with asymmetrical nodular peripheral enhancement which is characteristic of hemangioma. Hemangioma is a benign tumor composed of increased proliferation of blood vessels . It is the most common benign tumour of the liver and is mainly seen in women at a mean age of 45 years. Small capillary hemangiomas are of no clinical significance . They are usually solitary, <5 cm in diameter, with equal occurrence in the right and left halves of the liver. However, giant hemangiomas of diameter >5 cm require attention . They are most commonly asymptomatic and incidentally found during imaging studies . Large compressive masses may cause vague upper abdominal symptoms . The appearance of hepatic hemangioma in a contrast-enhanced CT scan is as follows : • Non-contrast phase : Well-defined hypodense lesion • Arterial phase : Peripheral nodular enhancement • Washout phase : Homogenous enhancement The image given below shows early phase with peripheral high attenuation (a) and late phase with homogenous high attenuation (b).708

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following hepatic lesions can be accurately diagnosed with 99mTc -labelled red blood cells when CT and MRI are unavailable?
mcqs.explanation: Hemangiomas can be accurately diagnosed with 99mTc -labelled red cells when CT and MRI are unavailable. In hemangioma, an increase in uptake is observed in blood pool studies such as 99mTc -labelled red cells and appear as photopenic regions. The nuclear imaging techniques for the diagnosis of hemangiomas are used only when high-quality CT and MRI are unavailable. CECT is the investigation of choice wherein a typical peripheral nodular enhancement pattern is seen . On magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), hemangiomas are hypointense on T1 -weighted images and hyperintense on T2 -weighted images. The below MRI image shows the light bulb sign seen in hemangioma of the liver.709 Percutaneous biopsy is potentially dangerous and inaccurate and, therefore , not recommended . Isotope scans used for the investigation of hepatobiliary disease are: • Technetium -99m colloid scan - parenchymal diseases of the liver, such as cirrhosis and alcoholic hepatitis • Technetium -99m hepatobiliary iminodiacetic acid (HIDA) scan - acute cholecystitis and congenital biliary atresia • Technetium -99m sulphur colloid scan - focal nodular hyperplasia

mcqs.question: A 2-year-old boy is brought to the ER with complaints of petechiae , bruising, and abdominal distension as shown in the image. Investigations reveal thrombocytopenia and elevated D-dimer. CECT shows solitary growth in the liver with peripheral nodular enhancement . Which of the following statements is false regarding this condition?

options.a: Kasai procedure is done for symptomatic cases
options.c: LFT and tumour markers are normal

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Kasabach-Merritt syndrome because of hemangioma of the liver. Kasai procedure or hepatoportoenterostomy is done for biliary atresia, and not in Kasabach-Merritt syndrome. Rarely a rapidly enlarging hemangioma can cause thrombocytopenia and disseminated intravascular coagulation (indicated by the elevated D-dimer) because platelets and other clotting factors are being used up within the tumour. This is called Kasabach-Merritt syndrome. LFT and tumour markers are normal in a hemangioma. Large hemangiomas in children can result in congestive heart failure secondary to arteriovenous shunting and they require medical management. Management : Observation is the mode of management in asymptomatic liver hemangiomas that are <5cm because they may show spontaneous regression. Therapeutic embolisation and enucleation with arterial inflow control is the treatment of choice for patients with symptomatic liver hemangiomas.

mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old woman presented with abdominal pain and discomfort for the past 2 months. She has been using oral contraceptive pills for more than 5 years. Imaging studies revealed a mass as shown in the image. Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.a: Rupture and intraperitoneal hemorrhage is unlikely
options.b: Malignant transformation is seen in 10 % of cases
options.c: Histology shows cords of hepatocytes with absence of bile ductules

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and MRI showing homogeneous mass with well -defined margins is suggestive of hepatic adenoma. Rupture leading to life -threatening intraperitoneal hemorrhage is a major complication associated with hepatic adenomas. Hepatic adenomas are benign solid neoplasms of the liver. They are usually seen in young women between 20 -40 years of age and are typically solitary. Prolonged oral contraceptive use is a clear risk factor. Clinical presentation may be abdominal pain. Histological studies show cords of benign hepatocytes containing excessive glycogen and fat, giving a congested or vacuolated appearance. There is an absence of bile duct glands and Kupffer cells . In some patients , hepatic adenomas present with spontaneous intraperitoneal hemorrhage. There is a risk of malignant transformation in 10 % of cases .710 The histopathological image given below shows hepatic adenoma.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following types of hepatic adenomas is associated with an increased risk of malignant transformation?
mcqs.explanation: \031-catenin mutated subtype of hepatic adenoma is associated with an increased risk of malignant transformation . The 2017 Bordeaux molecular-pathologic classification of hepatocellular adenomas (HCA) includes six subtypes : • HNF1A-inactivated HCA • Inflammatory HCA • \031-catenin exon 3 mutated HCA • \031-catenin exon 7/8 mutated HCA • Sonic hedgehog activated HCA • Unclassified HCA

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: During USG in a 30-year-old bodybuilder on anabolic steroids , a liver mass was noted . The surgeon suspects hepatic adenoma. Which of the following is false regarding investigations performed for this condition?

options.b: Imaging shows a well circumscribed vascular tumor
options.c: Resection and biopsy are done when other investigations are equivocal
options.d: MRI with gadobenate dimeglumine as contrast helps to distinguish from other tumors

mcqs.explanation: AFP levels are usually within the normal range in hepatic adenoma. In this patient , the use of anabolic steroids is a risk factor for developing hepatic adenoma. Computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrates a well -circumscribed and vascular solid tumor. Arterial phase CT demonstrates a well -developed peripheral arterialization of a tumor. Dynamic magnetic resonance imaging with liver-specific MRI contrast agents such as gadobenate dimeglumine helps to better distinguish hepatic adenomas from follicular nodular hyperplasia by711 their enhancement characteristics during the hepatobiliary phase of imaging. A biopsy may be necessary for the confirmation and characterization of the nature of these lesions when imaging studies are equivocal.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Spontaneous rupture of the liver occurs in ______.
mcqs.explanation: Hepatic adenoma can manifest as a case of spontaneous rupture , with the sudden onset of abdominal pain followed by hypovolemic shock secondary to intraperitoneal bleeding . The clinical presentation may be abdominal pain. In some cases , it can hepatic adenomas present with spontaneous intraperitoneal hemorrhage.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which statement regarding the management of hepatic adenoma is false ?

options.a: MRI surveillance is done for 5 years
options.b: Hepatic artery embolization is done in cases of hemorrhage
options.c: In women, the risk of malignant transformation is low if tumour <10 cm
options.d: In men, resection is done independent of the tumour size

mcqs.explanation: In women, the risk of malignant transformation is low if tumour <5 cm. Due to the high risk of malignancy in males, hepatic adenomas should be resected independent of the tumour size or subtype of the lesion. In female patients , conservative management with discontinuation of oral contraceptive pills and MRI surveillance is recommended if the tumour is <5 cm in diameter . Either annual (non-inflammatory adenoma) or biannual (inflammatory hepatocellular adenoma) MRI surveillance is done for at least 5 years, depending on the tumour subtype . If the tumour is >5 cm, resection is done. In patients presenting with acute hemorrhage, hepatic artery embolization is done to prevent further hemorrhage till the patient can be taken up for resection of the tumour.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements are false regarding focal nodular hyperplasia ?

options.a: Resection is done for persistent symptomatic cases
options.c: Appears as hotspots in Tc 99m sulphur colloid scan

mcqs.explanation: Malignant transformation is unlikely in focal nodular hyperplasia . Contrast-enhanced CT is diagnostic for FNH. It is seen as a well -circumscribed lesion with a typical central scar. They show intense homogeneous enhancement on the arterial phase and isodense as compared to the background liver on the venous phase . Due to the presence of Kupffer cells , FNH appears as hotspots on Tc 99m sulphur colloid scans. Asymptomatic patients with typical radiologic features do not require treatment . Careful observation of symptomatic FNH with serial imaging is reasonable, as symptoms may resolve in a significant number of cases . Patients with persistent symptomatic FNH or an enlarging mass should be considered for resection . If diagnostic uncertainty exists , resection may be necessary for histologic confirmation.712

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 27-year-old woman was incidentally found to have a liver mass while undergoing ultrasound for renal calculi. CECT showed the following image. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario with contrast-enhanced CT showing hypervascular lesion with a central non-enhancing scar points towards focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH).Focal nodular hyperplasia is the second most common benign tumour in the liver and is mostly seen in women. This condition is characterised by focal overgrowth of functional liver tissue and the supporting fibrous stroma. Patients are mostly asymptomatic and FNH is often an incidental finding. If patients are symptomatic , they usually complain of abdominal pain. On histological examination, cords of hepatocytes are seen with atypical biliary epithelium scattered throughout . A central stellate scar containing a large artery branching out in a spoke-wheel pattern is also seen .
