mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Patients with hepatocellular carcinoma are least likely to present with ______.
mcqs.explanation: Jaundice is an uncommon sign of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Hepatocellular carcinoma is the most common primary malignancy of the liver. It is commonly seen in men aged 50-60 years who present with right upper quadrant abdominal pain, weight loss, and a palpable mass. Non-specific symptoms of the advanced malignant disease are anorexia, nausea, lethargy . The gross appearance shows unifocal or multifocal or diffusely infiltrative lesions that are paler than the surrounding tissue .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: Oral contraceptive use is not an independent risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma . It is a risk factor for developing hepatic adenoma.721 Although hepatocellular adenoma can undergo malignant transformation , the true risk is low (10 %). Major risk factors for hepatocellular carcinoma : • Infection: • Hepatitis B • Hepatitis C • Toxins/drugs: • Alcoholic cirrhosis • Aflatoxins • Anabolic steroids • Genetic : • Hemochromatosis • \0331-Antitrypsin deficiency • Immunological: • Autoimmune chronic active hepatitis • Primary biliary cirrhosis • Others : • Obesity • Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis • Cirrhosis (other causes and idiopathic).

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following can be seen with HCC?
mcqs.explanation: Paraneoplastic syndrome due to hepatocellular carcinoma can manifest as: • Hypercalcemia • Hypoglycemia • Erythrocytosis Hypercalcemia in patients with HCC is associated with increased renal reabsorption of calcium and increased bone resorption by parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP ) generated by HCC. Less than 1% of cases of HCC manifest with a paraneoplastic syndrome.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 57 -year-old man presented with persistent upper abdominal pain and weight loss. Ultrasound revealed a lesion in the right lobe of the liver and contrast-enhanced CT was suggestive of hepatocellular carcinoma . Which of the following tumor markers can be elevated in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Alpha-2-macroglobulin is not a tumor marker of HCC.722 Tumor markers of HCC are: • Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) • Normal (<20 ng/mL ), • Elevated (21 –400 ng/mL ), and • Diagnostic for HCC (>400 ng/mL ). • Protein Induced by Vitamin K Absence or Antagonist - II (PIVKA -II ) also called des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin (DCP) • Glypican 3. • Neurotensin (in fibrolamellar type )

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 43-year-old man presented to the hospital with complaints of abdominal pain, ascites , and weight loss for 6 months. Investigations revealed a thrombus in the portal vein along with invasion from nearby tumor growth . Which of the following conditions can cause this?
mcqs.explanation: In the above clinical scenario, the patient has a secondary Budd-Chiari syndrome due to portal vein obstruction by a neighboring invasive lesion. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has the highest tendency to invade the portal vein. Budd–Chiari syndrome (BCS) is an uncommon congestive hepatopathy characterized by the obstruction of hepatic venous outflow .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true regarding the fibrolamellar variant of HCC?

options.b: Recurrences are seen despite better prognosis
options.c: Occur under the age of 35 years
options.d: Not commonly associated with chronic hepatitis B infection

mcqs.explanation: Fibrolamellar variant of HCC is not commonly associated with liver cirrhosis. Fibrolamellar carcinoma is a distinctive variant (<5%) of HCC. They occur under the age of 35 years, without any gender predilection or identifiable predisposing conditions. It usually presents as a single large, hard 'scirrhous' tumor. The tumor is well -demarcated , encapsulated , and may have a central fibrotic area. Histology shows large polygonal cells embedded in a fibrous stroma forming lamellar structures .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old male patient is found to have a well -circumscribed mass in his liver and is suspected to have fibrolamellar HCC. Which of the following tumor markers will be elevated in his condition?
mcqs.explanation: Neurotensin is the tumor marker of fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Neurotensin is a mitogen which induces cell proliferation in fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma . There is increased serum unsaturated vitamin B12 binding capacity seen in fibrolamellar HCC which can also aid in diagnosis.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is not true about alpha-fetoprotein ?

options.a: AFP level does not return back to normal after hepatic resection
options.b: Levels of >400 ng/mL with typical radiological findings is suggestive of HCC
options.c: AFP level can be raised in benign conditions

mcqs.explanation: 723 Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) level returns to normal after resection . Alpha-fetoprotein is a glycoprotein that is produced in early fetal life by the liver. It is also produced by a variety of tumors, such as: • Hepatocellular carcinoma • Hepatoblastoma • Non-seminomatous germ cell tumors of the ovary and testis (e.g., yolk sac and embryonal carcinoma ). AFP is also elevated during the following conditions: • Pregnancy and in benign liver disease (e.g., viral hepatitis , cirrhosis) • Gastrointestinal tract tumors • Along with carcinoembryonic antigen in ataxia-telangiectasia Limitations of AFP include low sensitivity and specificity . It is not specific to HCC and can occur with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and colorectal metastases . Levels >400 ng/mL with typical radiological findings are suggestive of HCC. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is not elevated in fibrolamellar HCC.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: AFP is used as a tumor marker in which of the following cancers?
mcqs.explanation: Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is not a tumor marker used to detect cholangiocarcinoma or fibrolamellar HCC. It is produced by a variety of tumors such as: • Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) • Hepatoblastoma • Non-seminomatous germ cell tumors of the ovary and testis (e.g., yolk sac and embryonal carcinoma ).

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following are modalities of treatment in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: All of the given modalities can be used for the treatment of HCC. Treatment options for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC): • Surgical • Resection (the mainstay of treatment) • Orthotopic liver transplantation • Ablative • Percutaneous ethanol injection (PEI) (less frequently used nowadays) • Thermal ablation (cryotherapy , radiofrequency ablation, microwave, Nd-YAG laser)724 • Transarterial • Embolization • Chemoembolization • Radiotherapy • Combination of transarterial and ablative: external beam radiation • Systemic • Chemotherapy • Hormonal • Immunotherapy

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man has been diagnosed with localized hepatocellular carcinoma . He falls into child-pugh class A and his future liver remnant is 22 % of the total liver volume. Which of the following will decrease the tumor burden and improve his hepatic functional reserve?

options.b: Preoperative portal vein embolization followed by resection

mcqs.explanation: The patient should ideally be treated by preoperative portal vein embolization to improve hepatic functional reserve, followed by resection which will decrease the tumor burden. Portal venous embolization on the side of the tumor will lead to compensatory hypertrophy of the unaffected liver lobe . This improves the volume and function of the future liver remnant (FLR ). Localized hepatocellular carcinoma • Child-Pugh class A: Patients with child-pugh class A should undergo resection of the tumor. • Those with low FLR (<30%) should ideally be treated by preoperative portal vein embolization followed by resection . Preoperative embolization helps in improving the FLR volume function prior to resection . • Those with adequate FLR (>30-40%) can usually tolerate resection alone. • Child-Pugh class B/C or portal hypertension: Patients with early-stage HCC and child-Pugh class B/C or portal hypertension should be considered for transplantation. Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma Patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma are treated with palliative intent. Following are the management options : • Drug therapy - Sorafenib/ Sunitinib/ Regorafenib • Transarterial chemoembolisation (TACE) and transarterial radioembolisation (TARE) offer the best results in multifocal disease • Radiofrequency ablation, microwave ablation, high-frequency ultrasound therapy are alternative options • Patients with extreme deterioration of performance status and liver function should be offered supportive treatment only.

mcqs.question: Which of the following parameters is not considered in OKUDA staging ?
mcqs.explanation: 725 OKUDA staging includes assessment of all the above factors except alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). The OKUDA staging system distinguishes patients with poor prognosis from those with more potential for long-term survival . The OKUDA staging system is an older system . mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following scoring systems will you not use to assess oncological outcomes of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma?
mcqs.explanation: MELD (model for end-stage liver disease) score is not used to assess the oncological outcome of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma . MELD is used to predict the severity of end-stage chronic liver disease . Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer staging system (BCLC) is the most commonly used scoring system for staging and management of HCC. The staging or management of HCC is done by the following : 1. Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer staging system (BCLC) • Tumor score (TNM) • Child-Pugh score • Performance score(Barcelona clinic score) 2. Cancer of the Liver Italian Program (CLIP ) • Tumor size • Child-Pugh score • AFP • Portal vein thrombosis 3. OKUDA staging • Bilirubin • Ascites726 • Tumor size • Albumin 4. Chinese University Prognostic Index (CUPI) Note : MELD can be used in prioritizing HCC patients in need of liver transplants.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true regarding LI -RADS scoring?

options.a: LI -RADS 2 has an intermediate probability of malignancy
options.b: Treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma can be initiated in LI -RADS 5 without biopsy
options.c: LI -RADS 3 is an indication for immediate liver biopsy
options.d: LI -RADS 4 is definitive of hepatocellular carcinoma

mcqs.explanation: LI -RADS 5 indicates a definitive probability(~100%) of hepatocellular carcinoma . Therefore treatment can be initiated as early as possible without waiting for a biopsy . • Routine surveillance should be continued for LI -RADS 1, 2. Additional imaging may be required for LI -RADS 2 based on individual risk . • LI -RADS 3 should be evaluated by serial imaging every 3-6 months. • Evaluation with a biopsy should be done in LI -RADS 4. • Since LI -RADS 5 indicates a definitive probability of hepatocellular carcinoma , treatment can be initiated as early as possible without waiting for a biopsy .Liver Imaging Reporting and Data Systems (LI -RADS) cate gories Category Assessment LI -RADS 1 Definitely benign LI -RADS 2 Probably benign LI -RADS 3 Intermediate probability of malignancy LI -RADS 4 Probably HCC LI -RADS 5 Definitely HCC

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old retiree was employed for two decades in a plastic industry, where he was exposed to vinyl chloride . He is at an increased risk of developing which of the following tumors?
mcqs.explanation: Angiosarcoma of the liver is seen in workers who have been exposed to vinyl chloride for prolonged periods . Angiosarcoma is the most common malignant mesenchymal tumor of the liver. It is a rare and fatal tumor. They are associated with the following conditions: • Hemochromatosis • Neurofibromatosis type I • Exposure to vinyl chloride , thorium dioxide , and arsenic.727 Patients usually present with vague symptoms of abdominal pain, weakness , fatigue , and weight loss. A hepatic bruit is occasionally heard, reflecting the vascular nature of the tumor. Central hypovascularity , vascular lakes, and peripheral contrast staining on arteriography are suggestive of an angiosarcoma. Biopsy shows the presence of dilated sinusoids lined by atypical endothelial cells .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An infant is brought to the hospital by his parents with complaints of poor feeding and abdominal distension . On evaluation, a mass is detected in the liver which is later diagnosed to be a hepatoblastoma . Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.a: It is associated with familial adenomatous polyposis
options.b: Most cases occur before the age of 3 years
options.c: Treatment is surgical resection followed by chemotherapy
options.d: Prognosis is extremely poor for pulmonary metastasis

mcqs.explanation: In hepatoblastoma , 85% of patients with pulmonary metastases can be successfully treated with resection of the hepatic tumor and chemotherapy or resection of the pulmonary metastases . Hepatoblastoma is the most common primary hepatic tumor of childhood . The median age at presentation is 18 months, and almost all cases occur before 3 years of age . It has been associated with familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) syndrome. This tumor generally manifests as an asymptomatic mass. Mild anemia and thrombocytosis are commonly found at presentation . Serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels are elevated in the majority of patients and can serve as a useful marker for therapeutic response. Treatment includes chemotherapy that can help downstage tumors such that they are amenable to resection . In patients without metastatic disease or the anaplastic variant , long-term survival rates of 60% to 70% can be expected with complete resection . mcqs.question: A woman was diagnosed to have metastatic liver adenocarcinoma with CK 7 (-\CK20 (+\ and CDX-1 (+) IHC markers . Which of the following is the most likely primary site of origin for this metastasis ?
mcqs.explanation: Colorectal carcinoma is the most likely primary tumor for the given metastases . Among the given options, cytokeratin 7 is negative only in colon carcinoma .728 The most common site of distant metastasis of colorectal cancer is the liver. These metastases arise from hematogenous spread via the portal venous system . The lung is the next most common site for metastasis . mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In patients with colorectal carcinoma , which of the following is not a bad prognostic factor?
mcqs.explanation: Metachronous lesions are not associated with a bad prognosis in case of liver metastasis from colon carcinoma . A metachronous cancer is defined as secondary cancer occurring more than 6 months after the index cancer. Synchronous cancer is defined as two or more neoplasms identified simultaneously in the same patient, or a second tumor identified within six months after the initial diagnosis. Predictors of poor outcome in colorectal carcinoma with liver metastasis : • Lymph-node-positive primary • Disease -free interval <12 months • More than one tumor • Tumor size >5 cm • Serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) level >200 ng/mL

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Patients with which of the following conditions are not suitable for liver transplantation?
mcqs.explanation: Cholangiocarcinoma is not an indication for a liver transplant. Orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT ) for patients with cholangiocarcinoma had very poor results and this treatment strategy has largely been abandoned.729

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the most common indication for liver transplant in children?
mcqs.explanation: The most common indication for liver transplant in children is biliary atresia. In biliary atresia, the extrahepatic bile ducts are occluded , causing obstructive jaundice (conjugated hyper -bilirubinemia) and progressive liver fibrosis in early infancy. Liver transplantation is required if not diagnosed and managed early. (option B) Indian childhood cirrhosis (ICC) is a progressive liver failure in young children, associated with marked hepatic copper overload (in excess of 800 �Mg/g dry weight ). Unlike Wilson disease , ICC is associated with normal or elevated ceruloplasmin levels , indicating a defect late in the copper excretory pathway .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old child with Wilson's disease is being considered for liver transplantation. Which of the following is not a parameter in the selection criteria for transplantation?

options.d: Jaundice less than 7 days before development of encephalopathy

mcqs.explanation: A 5-year-old child with Wilson's disease is a case of non-paracetamol-induced acute liver failure and jaundice for more than 7 days before the development of encephalopathy is one of the parameters in the King's College criteria for liver transplantation. It includes the following parameters: Non-paracetamol-induced acute liver failure: • PT >100 s (INR >6.5) or/and • Any three of the following : • Age <10 years or >40 years • Etiology non-A, non-B hepatitis , or idiosyncratic drug reaction • Jaundice more than 7 days before the development of encephalopathy i.e., not hyperacute • PT >50 s (INR > 3.5) • Bilirubin > 18 mg/dl (300 �Mmol/L) Paracetamol-induced acute liver failure: • pH <7.30 (irrespective of the grade of encephalopathy ) or/and • All three of the following : • Prothrombin time >100 s (INR >6.5) • Serum creatinine >3.4 mg/dl (300 �Mmol/L) • Grade 3 or 4 hepatic encephalopathy

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Auxiliary orthotopic liver transplantation is indicated in which of the following conditions?

options.b: As standby procedure till a suitable donor is found
options.c: Acute fulminant liver failure that is irreversible

mcqs.explanation: 730 Auxiliary orthotopic liver transplantation (A-OLTX) is indicated in non-cirrhotic metabolic liver disease . Auxiliary partial orthotopic liver transplantation is a technique where part of the diseased native liver is removed and replaced with a part of the healthy donor liver. This is done so the retained native liver can regenerate . In selective cases of acute liver failure, auxiliary partial orthotopic liver transplantation could provide a chance for native liver regeneration and immunosuppression -free life . Auxillary orthotopic liver transplant is indicated for the following : • Patients aged <40 years • Reversible fulminant hepatic failure (auxiliary liver transplantation cannot be done in cases of irreversible liver failure) • Non-cirrhotic metabolic liver disease • No hemodynamic instability • Hyperacute (not in other cases ) Liver failure with Acetaminophen overdose.Total orthotopic liver transpl antation (OLTX) Auxiliary orthotopic liver tra nsplantation (A-OLTX) The entire liver is transplante d Only a portion of the liver is t ransplanted Indications:Fulminant hepati c failure (FHF)Liver cirrhosis Primary biliary cirrhosis Indications:Crigler–Najjar sy ndrome type IHomozygous fa milial hypercholesterolemiaG alactosemiaHereditary tyrosi nemiaNeimann-Pick's disease Life-long immunosuppressio n is required. Immunosuppression is requir ed until the native liver regen erates731

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the anatomy of the gallbladder is false ?

options.a: Valves of Heister are present around the neck of the gallbladder
options.b: Gall bladder has a very thick submucosal layer
options.c: Hartmann 's pouch may hinder safe dissection of the cystic pedicle
options.d: Phrygian cap anomaly is not an indication for cholecystectomy

mcqs.explanation: The gallbladder does not have muscularis mucosa and submucosa . Those layers are absent in the gallbladder . The mucosa of the cystic duct is arranged in spiral folds known as the valves of the Heister . The valves act to keep gallstones from entering the common bile duct in spite of distention and intraluminal pressure . Hartmann 's pouch is a diverticulum that can occur at the neck of the gallbladder . It may obscure the cystic duct and Calot's triangle during laparascopic surgical dissection . The Phrygian cap is present in 2–6 percent of cholecystograms and may be mistaken for a pathological deformity of the organ. It is not an indication for cholecystectomy .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: While assisting a laparoscopic cholecystectomy for gallstones , the surgeon asks you to identify the Calot's triangle. Which of the following structures does not form the boundaries of this triangle?

options.d: The inferior surface of the liver

mcqs.explanation: 744 The inferior surface of the liver forms the boundary of the hepatobiliary triangle, not Calot's triangle. Calot's triangle is an important surgical landmark as the cystic artery usually can be found within its boundaries. The cystic artery should be identified while performing a cholecystectomy to avoid damage to the extrahepatic biliary system . Occasionally , there can be a tortuous course of the right hepatic artery in some patients . This is called Moynihan's hump or caterpillar hump. It is an important anomaly that should be recognized in order to prevent intraoperative vascular and biliary injuries.Note : The cystic artery is one of the contents as well as forms the superior boundary of the Calot's triangle (originally described in 1891 by Jean-Fran \347ois Calot)

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which type of gallstones is most likely to be seen in the Asian population ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common type of gallstone to be seen in the asian population is pigment stone (80%). The most common type of gallstone worldwide is mixed stone . Three main types of gallstones include: • Cholesterol stones - They consist of cholesterol monohydrate crystals. Pure cholesterol stones are uncommon and account for <10% of all cases . • Pigment stones (brown or black) contain <30% cholesterol : • Black stones - Made up of insoluble bilirubin pigment polymer mixed with calcium phosphate and calcium bicarbonate. They are associated with hemolysis , usually seen in hereditary spherocytosis or sickle cell disease . • Brown stones - Contain calcium bilirubinate, calcium palmitate , and calcium stearate , as well as cholesterol . They are also associated with the presence of foreign bodies within the bile ducts , such as endoprostheses (stents ), or parasites , such as Clonorchis sinensis and Ascaris lumbricoides .745 • Mixed stones . The image below shows a resected specimen of the gallbladder with pigment stones .Struvite stone (triple phosphate stone ) is a type of renal calculi. It is made of magnesium, ammonium, and phosphate .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old obese woman underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy and the specimen of gallstones removed is given below . Which of the following is least likely to be a risk factor for the formation of this type of gallstone in her?
mcqs.explanation: The above image shows cholesterol gallstones . Hereditary spherocytosis is not a risk factor for the formation of cholesterol gallstones . Hereditary spherocytosis leads to the production of black pigment stones . Obesity , high-caloric diets , prolonged fasting, certain medications (e.g., oral contraceptives ), and resection of the terminal ileum result in increased secretion of cholesterol and supersaturation of bile . This enhances the lithogenicity of bile.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman was brought to the casualty with complaints of abdominal pain and vomiting. CT scan of the abdomen revealed the following finding. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The CT image shows the Mercedes -Benz sign. It is a characteristic sign seen in gallstones . In gallstone , rarely, the center of the stone may contain radiolucent gas in a triradiate or biradiate fissure. This gives rise to characteristic dark shapes on a radiograph called the Mercedes –Benz sign (triradiate sign) or seagull sign (biradiate sign).746

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What percentage of gallstones are radio-opaque?
mcqs.explanation: Only 10 % of gallstones are radiopaque. Approximately 90% of renal stones , 10% of gall stones , and 5% of appendicoliths contain enough calcium to appear radiopaque on plain films. Gallbladder diseases are regularly diagnosed by ultrasound because of the superficial location of the gallbladder and the absence of overlying bowel gas. Ultrasound has a high specificity and sensitivity for cholelithiasis . It is considered as the first test of choice for delineation of any biliary pathology . Stones appear acoustically dense and also produce an acoustic shadow . They also move with a change in posture . However, CT provides superior anatomic information and therefore is indicated when more anatomic delineation is required.747

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: While performing the HIDA scan in a patient with gallstones , the gallbladder was not visualized . What could be the possible diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Non-visualization of the gallbladder in HIDA (hepatobiliary iminodiacetic acid) scan is suggestive of acute cholecystitis . Acute cholecystitis is the inflammation of the gallbladder that develops over hours, usually because a gallstone obstructs the cystic duct . In the majority of cases , the process is limited by the stone slipping back into the body of the gallbladder . Clinical features include : • Pain in the right hypochondrium with referred pain to the back • Fever • Nausea , vomiting, dyspepsia • Jaundice • Positive Murphy 's sign • Positive Boas' sign Murphy 's sign: After asking the patient to exhale , the examiner places his hand below the costal margin on the right side at the mid-clavicular line of the patient . The patient is then instructed to take a deep inspiration. If the patient stops breathing and winces with a 'catch' of breath, Murphy 's sign is said to be positive . Boas' sign: It is the presence of an area of hyperaesthesia at the site of radiation of the pain to the back, typically , below the scapula . USG and CT scans are helpful in establishing a diagnosis. The gold standard investigation of acute cholecystitis is the HIDA scan. The radioisotope used is Technetium -99m ( 99mTc )-labeled derivative of iminodiacetic acid. The following image depicts the radioisotope scan in which the gallbladder is not visualized even after 4 hours.748 Unlike bilirubin, iminodiacetic acid (IDA) compounds do not undergo conjugation in the hepatocytes. They are rapidly excreted into the bile . This enables excellent visualization of the bile ducts and gallbladder within 30–60 minutes of injection. Since cystic duct obstruction initiates acute cholecystitis , there is non-visualization of the gallbladder 3 - 4 hours after the intravenous injection of 99m Tc-IDA. This is characteristic of acute cholecystitis . Thus visualization of the GB establishes cystic duct patency and rules out acute cholecystitis .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old patient was admitted with right hypochondriac pain and vomiting. USG demonstrates a stone within the bile duct . All of the following clinical features can be seen in this patient except :
mcqs.explanation: The presence of a stone within the bile duct is called choledocholithiasis . Murphy 's sign is not seen in choledocholithiasis . It is seen in acute cholecystitis . Clinical features of choledocholithiasis: • Right upper quadrant or epigastric pain, which may radiate to the back • Biliary colic • Vomiting • Dyspepsia • Flatulence • Food intolerance particularly to fatty foods • Altered bowel habits • Jaundice. Other Murphy 's in surgery: Murphy 's punch sign: This test is performed by the examiner using the fist to make jabbing thrusts over the costovertebral angle. The test is positive in infection , inflammation, or obstruction of the kidney. The angle shown in the image is the costovertebral angle formed between the lower border of the 12th rib and the vertebral column.749 Murphy 's triad is associated with acute appendicitis . • Pain in the right illiac fossa • Vomiting • Fever

mcqs.question: According to the Tokyo Consensus Guidelines for grading the severity of acute cholecystitis , which of the following conditions is classified under moderate (Grade II ) acute cholecystitis ?
mcqs.explanation: If the duration of complaints is >72 hours, the patient is classified as having moderate (Grade II) acute cholecystitis . Acute cholecystitis is treated by keeping the patient nil per oral (NPO), administering intravenous fluids , analgesics , and IV antibiotics. The timing of surgery in acute cholecystitis remains controversial: • If the patient presents within 3 days, emergency cholecystectomy is done. • If the patient presents after 3 days, conservative management is done initially. Once the inflammation subsides , cholecystectomy is performed after 6 weeks (interval cholecystectomy ).Tokyo Consensus Guidelines forgrading the severity of acu te cholecystitis Grade III (severe ) acute chole cystitis Associated with organ dysfun ction750 Tokyo Consensus Guidelines forgrading the severity of acu te cholecystitis 1. mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man with a past medical history of diabetes mellitus , hypertension and ischemic heart disease presented with fever, nausea and right upper abdominal pain for the past 2 days. On evaluation, he is hypotensive and has a right upper quadrant palpable mass. Laboratory findings are mentioned below . Which of the following is the most appropriate management for this patient ?

options.a: Percutaneous cholecystostomy , followed by interval cholecystectomy
options.c: Conservative management, followed by delayed cholecystectomy after 6 weeks

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette is suggestive of severe acute cholecystitis (grade III ) based on Tokyo Consensus Guideline . Patients who have multiple comorbidities and present with severely acute cholecystitis should ideally undergo USG guided percutaneous cholecystostomy , followed by751 interval cholecystectomy once the condition has been stabilized .. Management of cholecystitis • Nil per oral (NPO) • IV fluids • Analgesics • IV antibiotics • Surgery • Grade III • with comorbidities - a percutaneous cholecystostomy can be performed by a radiologist under ultrasound guidance . An interval cholecystectomy once the condition has been stabilized . • without comorbidities - unless the patient is extremely hemodynamically unstable , operative intervention (cholecystectomy ) should be performed . • Grade I-II • presenting within 3 days - emergency cholecystectomy is done. • presenting after 3 days - conservative management is done initially. Once the inflammation subsides , cholecystectomy is performed after 6 weeks (interval cholecystectomy ).Tokyo Consensus Guidelines forgrading the severity of acu te cholecystitis Grade III (severe ) acute chole cystitis Associated with organ dysfun ction 1. Respiratory dysfunction PaO2/FiO2ratio <300 4. Renal dysfunction Oliguria; serum creatinine >2 mg/dL 5. Hepatic dysfunction Prothrombin time (PT-INR )> 1.5 6. Hematological dysfunction Platelet count, <100,000 /mm Grade II (moderate ) acute ch olecystitis752 Tokyo Consensus Guidelines forgrading the severity of acu te cholecystitis Associated with dysfunction of any one of the following:El evated white blood cell count (>18,000 /mm3 )Palpable ten der mass in the right upper a bdominal quadrantDuration of complaints >72 hoursMark ed local inflammation (gangr enous cholecystitis , perichole cystic abscess , hepatic absces s, biliary peritonitis , emphyse matous cholecystitis ) Grade I (mild) acute cholecys titis Does not meet the criteria of grade II or III acute cholecyst itis.Acute cholecystitis in a he althy person with no organ d ysfunction and mild inflamm atory changes in the gall blad der, making cholecystectomy a safe and low-risk operative procedure .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A diabetic patient presents with complaints of right upper quadrant pain, fever and nausea. On examination, there is tenderness over the right upper quadrant . CT scan revealed the following finding. What is the most common organism implicated in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the CT scan showing gas within the wall of the gallbladder are diagnostic of acute emphysematous cholecystitis . Clostridia species are the most commonly implicated organisms in acute emphysematous cholecystitis . Other causative organisms include E. coli and anaerobic streptococci . Emphysematous cholecystitis is a rare form of acute cholecystitis where gallbladder wall necrosis causes gas formation in the lumen or wall. Clinical features include : • Right upper quadrant pain • Nausea • Vomiting • Fever • Presence of crepitus during physical examination On imaging, the condition is diagnosed when there is a radiographic demonstration of air in the gallbladder wall +/- biliary ducts .753 Emphysematous cholecystitis has a high mortality rate due to the development of gangrene , perforation, and other complications . Hence , emergency cholecystectomy is indicated for the management of these patients . Tube cholecystostomy is done for patients who are not suitable for surgery. The given image shows a postoperative specimen of an emphysematous gallbladder along with an X-ray showing air in the gallbladder wall.Note : E. coli is the most commonly implicated organism in acute emphysematous pyelonephritis .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient in the burns ward complains of right hypochondriac pain and fever. USG reveals a thickened , hyperemic gallbladder with sludge formation surrounded by pericholecystic fluid but no gallstones . Which of the following statements is false regarding this condition?

options.a: CT-guided cholecystostomy is the treatment of choice
options.b: It has a high mortality rate
options.d: E. coli is the causative agent

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with the USG findings point to a diagnosis of acalculous cholecystitis . E. coli is not a causative agent of acalculous cholecystitis . Acute and chronic inflammation of the gallbladder can occur in the absence of stones and are referred to as acalculous cholecystitis . It is mainly seen in critically ill patients and those recovering from major surgery, trauma, and burns. It has a high mortality rate. The bacterial infections of the gallbladder causing acalculous cholecystitis include : • Leptospira • Streptococcus • Salmonella • Vibrio cholerae Clinical features are similar to that of acute calculous cholecystitis , such as: • Right upper quadrant pain • Fever754 • Positive Murphy 's sign • Leukocytosis • Sepsis A USG demonstrates a distended gallbladder with thickened wall, biliary sludge , pericholecystic fluid, and the presence or absence of abscess formation. HIDA scan shows a non-visualization of the gallbladder . Acalculous cholecystitis requires urgent intervention. Percutaneous ultrasound or CT-guided cholecystostomy is the treatment of choice for these patients , as they are usually unfit for surgery. Cholecystectomy is performed after the patient has recovered from the underlying illness .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old lady was incidentally found to have gallstones during the abdominal ultrasound. She is otherwise healthy and does not complain of any symptoms . In which of the following clinical scenarios you will not advise her for prophylactic cholecystectomy ?
mcqs.explanation: Prophylactic cholecystectomy in asymptomatic cholelithiasis is indicated only when gallstones >3 cm. Indications for consideration of prophylactic cholecystectomy in asymptomatic patients : • Risk factors for carcinoma • Choledochal cysts • Gallbladder adenomas • Porcelain (calcified ) gallbladder • Solitary gallbladder polyp larger than 1 cm • Choledocholithiasis • Gallstones >3 cm • The patient lives in a remote location from a healthcare facility • Sickle cell disease /spherocytosis • Transplant or immunosuppressant therapy . Note : Some books also mention "Prophylactic cholecystectomy is indicated in asymptomatic cholelithiasis when gallstones >2 cm."

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Medical therapy for gallstones using ursodeoxycholic acid will be considered in all of the following conditions, except :

options.a: If the size of the cholesterol stone is < 10mm
options.b: If the patient has biliary pain without any complications
options.d: In the presence of radio-opaque cholesterol gallstones

mcqs.explanation: Medical therapy using ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) for gall stones is indicated for radiolucent cholesterol stones . Selection criteria for oral bile acid dissolution therapy : • Symptomatic patients without complications • Patients with normal gallbladder functioning and a patent cystic duct • Patients with radiolucent stones and diameter < 10 mm755 Stones >10 mm in size rarely dissolve. Patients with cholesterol gallstone disease who develop recurrent choledocholithiasis after cholecystectomy should be on long-term treatment with UDCA. The dose of UDCA should be 10 –15 mg/kg per day. Pigment stones are non-responsive to UDCA therapy .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient with symptomatic gallstones but refusing surgery is at risk of developing all of the following complications except :
mcqs.explanation: Diverticulosis is not a complication due to gallstones . Clinical complications due to gallstones include the following : • Biliary colic • Acute cholecystitis • Chronic cholecystitis • Empyema of the gallbladder • Mucocele • Perforation • Biliary obstruction • Acute cholangitis • Acute pancreatitis • Intestinal obstruction (gallstone ileus ).

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statement is false regarding the mucocele of the gallbladder ?

options.a: Caused due to prolonged obstruction of cystic duct
options.b: Early cholecystectomy needs to be done
options.c: Obstruction can be seen in the neck of the gallbladder
options.d: A tender , non palpable gallbladder is characteristic of this condition

mcqs.explanation: The gallbladder is palpable but non-tender in the mucocele of the gallbladder . Mucocele of the gallbladder results from prolonged obstruction of the cystic duct , usually by a large solitary calculus . The obstructed gall bladder lumen is progressively distended by mucus (mucocele ) or by a clear transudate (hydrops ) produced by mucosal epithelial cells . It is usually asymptomatic , although chronic right upper quadrant pain may also occur. On examination , a visible, easily palpable , non-tender gallbladder , sometimes extending from the right upper quadrant into the right iliac fossa may be seen . Ultrasonography is helpful for the diagnosis. Early cholecystectomy needs to be done, because empyema , perforation, or gangrene may complicate the condition. The image below shows mucocele of the gallbladder .756 The image below shows empyema of the gallbladder .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A middle -aged woman with a history of cholelithiasis was rushed to the casualty with complaints of vomiting, abdominal distension , and obstipation . On examination, high-pitched bowel sounds were heard. Her X-ray erect abdomen is given below . Which statement is false regarding this condition?

options.a: It is associated with Rigler's triad
options.b: Jejunum is the most common site of obstruction
options.c: CT scan is the investigation of choice
options.d: Enterotomy is done in the absence of strangulation

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with an X-ray showing gas in the biliary tract (pneumobilia ) and multiple air-fluid levels indicating small bowel obstruction is suggestive of gallstone ileus . The distal ileum is the most common site to be obstructed in gallstone ileus because it tapers before entering the cecum . Gallstone ileus is caused by the obstruction of the intestinal lumen by a gallstone , leading to a mechanical blockage . Big gallstones will not be able to pass through the normal cystic duct . This causes inflammation of the gallbladder and results in pressure necrosis. This in turn leads to biliary-enteric fistula formation.757 Plain radiographs demonstrate air-fluid levels consistent with a small bowel obstruction. Rigler's triad is seen in gallstone ileus . It includes : • Intestinal obstruction • Gas in the biliary tract (pneumobilia ) • Ectopic gallstone (Radio-opaque shadow in the right iliac fossa) The investigation of choice is the CT scan. Pneumobilia is a ubiquitous finding because the fistula that permitted a stone to pass into the duodenum allows air into the gallbladder and the biliary tree . Initial management involves keeping the patient nil per-oral, IV fluids , IV antibiotics, and analgesics . If there is no strangulation or peritonitis , it can be managed by: • Milking the stone beyond ileocaecal junction • Crushing the stone • Enterotomy to remove the stone If there is perforation or strangulation, resection and anastomosis are done. Cholecystectomy should be performed to avoid future complications . Fistula closure can be performed along with cholecystectomy or it can be performed later (two -stage procedure ). Given below is a plain X-ray of the erect abdomen showing air in the biliary tract (pneumobilia).A large gallstone causing gallstone ileus is shown below .758

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In what condition would you see the gallbladder as shown below ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a strawberry gallbladder . Strawberry gallbladder is seen in cholesterolosis and is associated with cholesterol stones. Cholesterolosis is characterized by mucosal villous hyperplasia . The interior of the gallbladder resembles a strawberry. The yellow specks are aggregations of cholesterol crystals and cholesterol esters in the lamina propria. This corresponds to the seeds of a strawberry. Option A: Cholesterol polyposis - Cholecystography or ultrasonography shows negative shadows in a functioning gallbladder , indicating the presence of a well -defined polyp . Options B and C: Cholecystitis glandularis proliferans/adenomyomatosis - All layers of the gallbladder wall may be thickened , but sometimes , an incomplete septum forms that separate the hyperplastic from the normal layer. Intraparietal "mixed" calculi may be present .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old lady presented with colicky abdominal pain, jaundice and generalized pruritus. She has a palpable gallbladder . Which of the following is the least likely cause ?

options.a: Stone impacted in the cystic duct
options.b: Stone impacted in the fundus of gallbladder
options.c: Stone impacted within the gallbladder and common bile duct
options.d: Carcinoma of the head of the pancreas

mcqs.explanation: A stone impacted within the fundus of the gallbladder is least likely to cause jaundice with a palpable gallbladder . According to Courvoisier's law, the presence of a painless , palpable , enlarged gallbladder and mild jaundice , is unlikely due to gallstones . It usually indicates a possibility of carcinoma in the head of the pancreas. However, apart from a cancer in the pancreatic head , certain other conditions may also cause a palpable gallbladder in presence of jaundice . For example , • Double impacted stones (stones in both the cystic duct and the distal common bile duct ) • Primary CBD stone • Oriental cholangiohepatitis759 • Mirizzi's syndrome (an impacted gallstone in the cystic duct or neck of the gallbladder due to inflammation, causing common bile duct (CBD) obstruction, jaundice and a palpable gallbladder ) These are considered exceptions to Courvoisier's law.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old lady presented with abdominal pain, vomiting and jaundice . Her ALP and direct bilirubin levels were raised. She had undergone laparoscopic cholecystectomy 1 year back. On USG there is dilatation of biliary radicles. Which of the following is the ideal management for this patient ?

options.a: Laparoscopic exploration of common bile duct
options.b: Open surgical exploration of common bile duct
options.d: Addition of ursodeoxycholic acid, followed by repeat USG after 10 days

mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of choledocholithiasis . When diagnosed postoperatively (after cholecystectomy ), it should be managed with ERCP + sphincterotomy . Stone detected within 2 years after cholecystectomy is called retained stone . Stone detected more than 2 years after cholecystectomy is considered recurrent stone . CBD stone and GB stone detected before cholecystectomy : • ERCP+Sphincterotomy , followed by laparoscopic cholecystectomy after a few days should be done. CBD stone detected during surgery (intraoperatively): • Laparoscopic cholecystectomy + laparoscopic CBD exploration should ideally be done in the same sitting to avoid the need for additional operative sitting and anaesthesia . • A transcystic approach is preferred usually . • If there is a small, friable cystic duct ; numerous (more than eight ) stones in the common bile duct; and large stones (>1 cm), laparoscopic choledocholithotomy is performed . • If laparoscopic choledocholithotomy exploration is not feasible , it would necessitate the need for an open CBD exploration. • A T-tube is placed in the CBD after laparoscopic choledocholithotomy or open CBD exploration. It is followed by a cholangiography to exclude retained stone . CBD stone detected after surgery: • Endoscopic removal (ERCP) with sphincterotomy is usually the management of choice .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An 80-year-old woman presented with complaints of fatigue . On imaging, she was found to have a scleroatrophic gall bladder with impacted stones in it. A large stone was also present in the common bile duct and the biliary tree is dilated . What is the next step in management?

options.a: Immediately take up patient for cholecystectomy

mcqs.explanation: An 80-year-old woman with imaging showing a scleroatrophic gall bladder with impacted stones and a stone in the bile duct is suggestive of chronic cholelithiasis with choledocholithiasis . ERCP is the next line of management for this patient . Choledocholithiasis is the presence of stone in the common bile duct (CBD) or biliary tree . It can be primary or secondary: • Primary stones are formed in the CBD or biliary tree itself and are rare. • Secondary stones are passed from the gallbladder to the CBD. They are easier to manage than primary stones. It can be an asymptomatic and incidental finding or present with features such as jaundice ( most common ), abdominal pain, and fatigue . When there is inflammation of the biliary tree760 (cholangitis ), the patient will have intermittent pain, fever, and jaundice (Charcot's triad). Investigations: • Liver function tests will show elevated direct bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase levels . • Abdominal ultrasound is the first imaging modality done and may show gallstones and dilated bile duct (>8 mm). • CT is sensitive for CBD stones . It shows stones , location, ductal stricture or block, ductal dilatation, and intrahepatic biliary changes . • MRCP is highly sensitive and specific for CBD stones , but it is only diagnostic and intervention cannot be performed . Management : • ERCP with sphincterotomy is the procedure of choice , followed by the removal of stones using a dormia basket or placement of a stent. • Despite ERCP being an invasive procedure , it has the advantage of being both a diagnostic and therapeutic procedure and is more suited for elderly patients who cannot tolerate anesthesia and surgery. Other options : Option A: Cholecystectomy is not recommended for elderly patients , owing to the risk of old age and associated anesthetic and surgical complications . Option C: Wait and watch approach can be done for asymptomatic patients , and patients with smaller stones . Option D: CT is sensitive for CBD stones , but it is only diagnostic and intervention cannot be performed.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the best investigation in a patient suspected to have an impacted gallstone at the ampulla of Vater?
mcqs.explanation: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) will be the best investigation in the management of impacted stone at the ampulla of Vater. It allows the surgeon to visualize the presence of gallstone at the ampulla of Vater along with the therapeutic extraction of the stone . The following image shows an ERCP procedure (endoscope visible).761

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following features are part of Reynold's pentad ?
mcqs.explanation: Vomiting and diaphoresis are not part of Reynold's pentad . Reynold's pentad is seen in acute suppurative cholangitis .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A jaundiced patient presented with complaints of colicky abdominal pain and itching all over the body. USG abdomen showed thickening of the gallbladder wall and pericholecystic fluid . MRCP showed extrinsic compression of the common bile duct , suggestive of Mirizzi syndrome. Identify the incorrect statement about this condition.

options.a: Surgery consists of removing the cystic duct , gallbladder , and the stone
options.b: Cystic duct obstruction will be present
options.c: Fistula forms between the gallbladder and common bile duct

mcqs.explanation: A palpable gallbladder will not rule out gallstones in Mirizzi syndrome. It is an exception to Courvoisier's law. Courvoisier's law states that in the presence of a painless , palpable , enlarged gallbladder and mild jaundice , the cause is unlikely to be gallstones . Its exceptions include : • Double impacted stones (stones in both the cystic duct and the distal common bile duct ) • Primary CBD stone • Oriental cholangiohepatitis • Mirizzi's syndrome In Mirizzi's syndrome, gallstones become impacted in the cystic duct or neck of the gallbladder due to inflammation. This causes common bile duct (CBD) obstruction and jaundice . The gallbladder is distended and may be palpable . ERCP, PTC (Percutaneous transhepatic cholangiography ), or MRCP will usually demonstrate the characteristic extrinsic compression of the CBD. Surgery consists of removing the cystic duct , diseased gallbladder , and the impacted stone . In patients whose gallbladder is densely adherent to the common bile duct , partial cholecystectomy should be done.762 If left untreated , a fistula forms between the gallbladder and common bile duct (cholecysto -choledochal fistula ).

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Identify the condition.
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a resected specimen of a gallbladder with a polyp on the inner surface . Specimen of gallbladder carcinoma would include an en-bloc dissection of the gall bladder , surrounding liver tissue and regional lymph nodes (option D). In specimens of cholesterolosis , also known as strawberry gallbladder , the gall bladder would appear yellow and coarsely granular due to the presence lipid nodules (options A and B). Gall bladder polyps are usually incidental findings during abdominal imaging. Most of them are benign and comprise cholesterol polyps , adenomyomas or inflammatory polyps . Adenomatous polyps are the most common neoplastic polyps . The majority of patients with polyps are stable and smaller polyps are kept under observation. Cholecystectomy is done for symptomatic patients (biliary colic, pancreatitis ), patients >50 years, sessile polyps with thickening >4 mm and polyps >10 mm. The risk factors for malignancy in an adenomatous polyp include age >50 years, size >10 mm, sessile polyp , documented increase in size, and coexistence with gallstones . Other options : Option D: The gallbladder in a patient with carcinoma is removed via an en-bloc dissection with surrounding liver tissue along with regional lymph nodes . The given image below shows a cut surface of the resected gallbladder with a tumor at the neck along with liver bed involvement (marked by the red arrow).Options A and B: Cholesterolosis (strawberry gallbladder ) is characterized by the accumulation of lipids (triglycerides , cholesterol precursors and cholesterol esters ) in the lamina propria of the gallbladder wall. The nodules are less than 1 mm in diameter and there is mucous villous hyperplasia , which gives it a coarse, yellow and granular appearance , giving it a strawberry-like763 appearance . The given images below show cholesterolosis .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 45-year old lady is found to have a gall bladder polyp of size 1.2cm on abdominal USG. She appears to be healthy and is asymptomatic . How will you manage this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Gallbladder polyps larger than 1 cm have an increased risk of malignancy and should be treated by performing a cholecystectomy .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the treatment of choice for the condition shown below ?
mcqs.explanation: The X-ray image shows calcification of the gallbladder , also known as porcelain gallbladder . This condition is associated with the risk of gall bladder carcinoma . Cholecystectomy is the treatment of choice .764 Extended cholecystectomy includes removal of the gall bladder with a 2 cm non-anatomical wedge of the liver and lymphadenectomy . It is performed for stage Ib with perineural, lymphatic , vascular invasion , and stage II of gallbladder carcinoma .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: All of the following are risk factors for gallbladder carcinoma , except :
mcqs.explanation: Adenomyomatosis is not a risk factor for carcinoma gallbladder . Adenomyomatosis is a benign condition of the gallbladder characterized by hypertrophy of the mucosal epithelium. It invaginates into the thickened muscularis forming Rokitansky -Aschoff sinuses . Risk factors for carcinoma gallbladder : • Gallstones of size >3 cm (most important risk factor) • Porcelain gallbladder • Anomalous pancreato-biliary junction • Choledochal cyst • Adenomatous polyps • Primary sclerosing cholangitis • Obesity • Salmonella typhii infection .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding gallbladder carcinoma ?

options.a: Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common type
options.c: Depth of invasion is the most important prognostic factor

mcqs.explanation: The most common type of gallbladder carcinoma is adenocarcinoma (80–90%). Squamous carcinomas also occur and are believed to arise from areas of mucosal squamous metaplasia . Gallbladder carcinoma is a rare malignancy that is seen in the elderly . It is associated with a poor prognosis and is indistinguishable from cholecystitis or cholelithiasis . It is usually diagnosed when patients undergo cholecystectomy for gallstones . Its clinical features include right upper quadrant pain, nausea, vomiting, and anorexia. Jaundice is a late feature. CA 19-9 is elevated in the carcinoma gallbladder and is used for monitoring. The preoperative diagnosis is often made on ultrasonography and followed up by a CT scan or MRI /Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography . A percutaneous biopsy under radiological guidance is done for pathological examination. PET scanning helps in detecting metastatic disease . In select cases , a laparoscopic examination is useful in staging the disease . Laparoscopy can also detect peritoneal or liver metastases . The most important prognostic factor is the depth of invasion (T-stage ).765

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy for cholelithiasis . Histopathology of the resected gall bladder is reported as Stage T1a of gallbladder cancer. What is the next step in management?
mcqs.explanation: Cholecystectomy is sufficient for gallbladder carcinoma with T1a lesions , wherein the tumor penetrates the lamina propria but does not invade the muscle layer. Treatment of gallbladder carcinoma (in general ): If the carcinoma gall bladder was found incidentally after cholecystectomy : • Up to stage Ia and stage Ib with negative margins, standard cholecystectomy would suffice • Stage Ib with perineural, lymphatic , vascular invasion and stage II , extended cholecystectomy should be performed If the initial procedure was performed laparoscopically , the surgeon should examine the laparoscopic port sites . The finding of disease at the port sites is a sign of generalized peritoneal disease and carries a very poor prognosis. However, resection of port sites is no longer recommended . Chemotherapy is not required in early gall bladder cancer. Radiation has no role.TNM sta ging Treatment T1a Simple cholecystectomy T1b , T2 , T3 Radical cholecystectomy T4 Unresectable , chemotherapy and palliative nonsurgical the rapy are provided N1 Regional lymphadenectomy N2 Radical cholecystectomy plus hepatopancreatic duodenect omy766

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man presented with recurrent episodes of fever with chills. MRCP image is shown below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of fever and chills, along with the MRCP showing multiple areas of intrahepatic beading is typical of primary sclerosing cholangitis . Option B: Caroli's disease is a rare congenital condition characterized by irregular dilatation of the intrahepatic bile ducts with a normal extrahepatic duct system . It is common in both sexes and mostly presents before the age of 30 years with abdominal pain, cholangitis , or end-stage liver disease . MRCP shows irregular, cystic dilation of the large proximal intrahepatic bile ducts with a normal common bile duct . Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is an autoimmune condition characterized by inflammatory strictures involving the intra and extra-hepatic biliary tree . It is a progressive condition that leads to secondary biliary cirrhosis.771 MRCP or ERCP will show demonstrate multifocal , diffuse dilatation and strictures of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary trees , this pattern is a beading or chain of lakes appearance . Pseudodiverticula of extrahepatic bile ducts are pathognomic of PSC. MRCP is useful in diagnosis and surveillance, while ERCP is reserved for the treatment of dominant strictures and to exclude malignancy. The below image shows a cholangiogram of primary sclerosing cholangitis :The common age group of primary sclerosing cholangitis is 30-45 years. Men are affected twice as commonly as women. Two-thirds of these cases are associated with ulcerative colitis . It is also associated with Riedel 's thyroiditis and retroperitoneal fibrosis. –20 % of patients develop cholangiocarcinoma. Clinical features of a patient with PSC include pruritis, fever, chills, right upper quadrant discomfort, jaundice , and weight loss. Liver function tests show a cholestatic pattern with an elevation of ALP and GGT and smaller rises in the aminotransferases. Bilirubin values may be variable. Liver biopsy excludes other causes of cholestatic liver disease and defines the stage of PSC. It shows onion skin concentric periductal fibrosis. With disease progression, periportal fibrosis occurs, progressing to bridging necrosis, and eventually biliary cirrhosis. Currently, there is no known effective medical therapy . Surgical management involving resection of extrahepatic biliary tree and hepaticojejunostomy has shown reasonable effects . For patients with advanced liver disease , liver transplantation is the only available option. Other options : Option C: Oriental cholangitis , also known as recurrent pyogenic cholangitis is characterized by recurrent attacks of cholangitis due to bile stasis and stone formation. Patients between 30-40 years and both sexes are equally affected . It is caused due to infections (liver flukes , E.coli, Klebsiella , Pseudomonas , and Proteus). Patients present with Charcot's triad (intermittent fever, pain, and jaundice ). MRCP shows intra or extrahepatic calculi, dilatation of ducts , and strictures . Option D: Biliary carcinoma (cholangiocarcinoma) most commonly affects patients >60 years and presents with fever, abdominal pain, weight loss, and features of obstructive jaundice . MRCP772 shows irregular narrowing of the bile duct involved by the tumor, with asymmetric upstream dilatation of the intrahepatic ducts .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: According to Strasberg's classification of bile duct injuries, injury to the right aberrant posterior sectoral duct with bile leak is:
mcqs.explanation: Injury to the right aberrant posterior sectoral duct associated with bile leak is classified as Strasberg's type C injury. Biliary injury may occur post -laparoscopic cholecystectomy . The most common site of bile leak following cholecystectomy is the cystic duct . MRCP is the gold standard for complete morphological evaluation of the biliary tree . MRCP with magnetic resonance angiography is more useful in cases of associated vascular injury. A HIDA scan can confirm the presence of a bile leak or biliary obstruction. The Strasberg classification of bile duct injury is widely used to anatomically define bile duct injuries. Classification • Type A: Bile leak from cystic duct stump or a minor biliary radical in the gallbladder fossa • Type B: Occluded right posterior sectoral duct . • Type C: Bile leak from the divided right posterior sectoral duct . • Type D: Bile leak from the main bile duct without major tissue loss. • Type E: Injury to the main hepatic duct ; classified according to the level of injury • E1: Transected main bile duct with a stricture more than 2cm from the hilus. • E2: Transected main bile duct with a stricture less than 2cm from the hilus • E3: Stricture of the hilus with right and left ducts in communication. • E4: Stricture of the hilus with separation of right and left hepatic ducts . • E5 : Stricture of the right aberrant sectoral and main bile ducts .773 Management of bile duct injuries is shown below :

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient presents with pain in the right upper quadrant on the second postoperative day following a cholecystectomy . Evaluation reveals a collection in the subhepatic space . A bile leak was suspected . Which of the following is the best investigation for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is the best investigation in a patient suspected of post -cholecystectomy biliary leaks. Patients with post -cholecystectomy biliary leak usually present with fever, jaundice and abdominal pain. USG is used for an initial evaluation in such cases and can show a collection in the sub-hepatic space . The most common bile leak following cholecystectomy is from the cystic duct . This can be treated by placing a biliary endoprosthesis (stent ) in the common bile duct across the origin of the cystic duct .774 MRCP shows fluid collections arising from bile leaks but cannot differentiate these from other causes of fluid collections . ERCP is the best investigation as it has the advantage of being both diagnostic and therapeutic . ERCP is useful post -cholecystectomy as there is a high likelihood of a retained stone and stone extraction and/or temporary stenting may be required. HIDA scan is the most sensitive investigation for biliary leakage . CT scan can show focal fluid collections , ascites , biliary obstruction, hepatic atrophy, signs of secondary biliary cirrhosis and any vascular injury.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy and was discharged after removing the drain tube on the first postoperative day. On day three , the patient came back to the hospital and was febrile . On ultrasound examination, there was a 5 x 5 cm collection in the subhepatic space . What is the next best step ?

options.a: To give oral antibiotics since the given accumulation is normal
options.b: To re-explore the wound and insert a T-tube

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical situation suggests a bile duct injury following laparoscopic cholecystectomy . The next best step after imaging would be to control inflammation by drainage of fluid collections by pigtail insertion and administration of broad-spectrum IV antibiotics.775

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Five days following a common bile duct injury resulting in a leak, a patient presents with fever and abdominal pain. What would be the next step in management?
mcqs.explanation: In the case of a common bile duct injury with a leak and a patient presenting with signs of localized peritonitis , the next step of management is an ultrasound-guided aspiration. This will be followed by ERCP and stenting . Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is the most common cause of bile duct injury. Major biliary leakage is usually seen 2 to 10 days after cholecystectomy . Affected patients typically present with: • Fever • Abdominal pain • Bilious ascites • Mild jaundice • Leukocytosis • Elevations in the serum levels of ALP and GGT. Management of bile duct injury: If the injury is identified during surgery: • Partial injury to the bile duct (<3mm) - repair the injury • Complete transection without loss of segment - anastomose over T-tube • Complete transection with loss of segment - close distal end and carry out Roux-en-Y hepaticoduodenostomy /jejunostomy If the leak is suspected postoperatively: Transabdominal ultrasonography is initially performed to assess the leak. • If the patient presents within 48 hours - Re-explore and repair • If the patient presents after 48 hours - USG-guided aspiration or pigtail catheter insertion.776 This is followed by ERCP and stenting .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Where does biliary stricture most commonly occur after laparoscopic cholecystectomy ?
mcqs.explanation: Biliary stricture after laparoscopic cholecystectomy usually occurs in the common hepatic duct, distal to the confluence of the right and left hepatic ducts . After open cholecystectomy , biliary strictures are more common in the common bile duct .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about hemobilia?

options.a: It is associated with Quincke's triad
options.b: Tumors are the most common cause of bleeding
options.d: Arterial angiography is the diagnostic procedure of choice

mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of hemobilia is iatrogenic trauma. Hemobilia is defined as bleeding into the biliary tree from abnormal communication between a blood vessel and bile duct . Causes of hemobilia include : • Traumatic or operative injury to the liver or bile ducts • Intraductal rupture of a hepatic abscess or aneur\026sm of the hepatic artery • Biliary or hepatic tumor hemorrhage • Mechanical complications of choledocholithiasis or hepatobiliary parasitism • Diagnostic procedures , such as liver biopsy , percutaneous transhepatic cholangiography (PTC), and transhepatic biliary drainage catheter placement • Vascular disorders Patients often present with a classic triad (Quincke's triad/Sandblom triad) of: • Biliary pain777 • Obstructive jaundice • Melena or occult blood in the stools Investigation of choice : Arterial angiography (CT angiography) is the diagnostic procedure of choice . Management : Minor hemobilia can be managed conservatively. Major hemobilia: Transarterial embolization is indicated for major hemobilia requiring blood transfusion. Ligation of the bleeding vessel may also be required.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: How will you confirm the diagnosis in a patient suspected to have bilhemia?
mcqs.explanation: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is the best investigation for the diagnosis of bilhemia. Bilhemia is a condition in which bile flows into the bloodstream through the hepatic veins or portal vein branches. This flow occurs due to a high intrabiliary pressure , exceeding that of the venous system . The cause can be the erosion of gallstones into the portal vein, or accidental /iatrogenic trauma. This condition can be fatal secondary to the embolization of large amounts of bile into the lungs . Usually , bile flow is low, and the fistulas close spontaneously . Its clinical features include : • Rapidly progressive jaundice • Marked direct hyperbilirubinemia, without elevation of the hepatocellular enzyme levels . • Septicemia . Diagnosis of bilhemia is best made by ERCP. Treatment is directed at reducing the intrabiliary pressure through stent placement or sphincterotomy . Endovascular embolization can also be done.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Cholangiohepatitis is associated with which of the following parasites ?
mcqs.explanation: Cholangiohepatitis or recurrent pyogenic cholangitis is associated with biliary parasites such as: • Clonorchis sinensis • Opisthorchis viverrini • Ascaris lumbricoides . It is caused by bacterial contamination of the biliary tree . Some commonly implicated organisms are Escherichia coli, Klebsiella species , Bacteroides species , or Enterococcus faecalis . Cholangiohepatitis is a pre-malignant condition and can result in cholangiocarcinoma.778 Schistosoma haematobium primarily causes genito -urinary schistosomiasis . Paragonimus westermani (oriental lung fluke ) causes a pulmonary syndrome characterized by cough , chest pain, and hemoptysis .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man presented with complaints of weight loss, clay coloured stools , and abdominal pain. CT scan and MRCP was suggestive of cholangiocarcinoma. What is the most common site at which this occurs?

options.a: Distal third of the common bile duct
options.b: Middle third of the common bile duct
options.c: Confluence of the right and left hepatic ducts

mcqs.explanation: Cholangiocarcinomas are most common at the location where the right and left hepatic ducts meet i.e., the confluence of the hepatic ducts . Cholangiocellular carcinomas (CCCs) or cholangiocarcinomas are mucin-producing adenocarcinomas of the biliary duct system that may originate in the liver and extrahepatic bile ducts . Cholangiocarcinomas are encountered in three anatomic regions: • Intrahepatic • Hilar (65%) - also known as Klatskin tumours • Peripheral (30%) The sclerosing variant of cholangiocarcinoma is the most common and most difficult to treat. The nodular variant is usually intrahepatic and presents as a mass lesion. The papillary variant is rare and is associated with favourable outcomes. Portoenterostomy is done for hilar cholangiocarcioma and for peripheral cholangiocarcionoma, Whipple 's surgery is done. In Bismuth-Corlette classification they are classified according to their location:The FDA approved Pemigatinib, FGFR2 inhibitor for patients with cholangiocarcinoma that is locally advanced or metastatic , and tumors with fusion or rearrangement of fibroblast growth factor receptor 2 (FGFR2) gene .779

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Match the following triads:
mcqs.explanation: The correct option is 1-c, 2-a, 3-d, 4-b.Triad Condition Components Saint's triad Hiatus herniaGallstonesColo nic diverticulosis Sandblom tr iad Hemobilia MalenaBiliary colicObstructiv e jaundice Charcot tria d Acute cholangiti s JaundiceFeverRight upper qu adrant pain Rigler's triad Gallstone ileus Small bowel obstructionPneu mobiliaEctopic gallstone

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 19-year-old patient presented with right upper quadrant pain. USG and CT scans showed no evidence of gallstones . MRCP shows fusiform dilatation of the common bile duct . Identify the false statement regarding this condition.

options.d: Jaundice will be the most consistent finding

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and MRCP showing fusiform dilation of extrahepatic biliary tree point towards the diagnosis of a choledochal cyst (Type I). Choledochal cysts are more commonly seen in females . A choledochal cyst is a premalignant condition leading to the development of cholangiocarcinoma. The classic clinical triad of symptoms includes abdominal pain, jaundice (most consistent finding), and a mass in the abdomen. Diagnosis of choledochal cyst can be made by: • USG (Initial investigation) • MRCP (Investigation of choice ) • ERCP (Gold standard investigation) • Endoscopic ultrasound (Most sensitive ) Management includes effective drainage and removal of abnormal mucosa to reduce the risk of malignancy.Type of choledochal cys t Surgical management Type I Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunosto my Type II Diverticulectomy + common bile duct repair Type III ERCP + sphincterotomy (Onl y cyst in which reconstructio n is not required)780 Type of choledochal cys t Surgical management Type IVa and Type V Liver transplant Type IVb Kasai procedure (portoentero stomy)

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the most common type of choledochal cyst ?
mcqs.explanation: Type I is the most common type of choledochal cyst (75 %). Choledochal cysts are congenital dilations of the intra- and/or extra-hepatic biliary system .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In which of the following conditions will you perform the Kasai procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: Kasai procedure (Roux-en-Y hepatoportoenterostomy ) is done for extrahepatic biliary atresia. In the Kasai procedure , the occluded extrahepatic bile ducts are excised and a jejunal Roux loop is anastomosed to the hepatic hilum. Extrahepatic biliary atresia (EHBA) is defined as a partial or total absence of permeable bile duct between porta hepatis and the duodenum. It is due to inflammatory fibrosis of the biliary tree . It leads to obstruction to bile flow thereby causing leaking of conjugated bilirubin into the circulation. Associated anomalies include cardiac lesions , polysplenia , situs inversus, absent vena cava , and a preduodenal portal vein. HIDA scan is the investigation of choice for EHBA. Intraoperative cholangiogram is the gold standard for diagnosis. Infants with biliary atresia, who do not achieve successful drainage after Kasai's procedure , require liver transplantation within the first year of life . It is the most common reason for liver transplantation in children. Kasai procedure :Management of extrahepatic biliary atresia Type I Atresia restricted to the com mon bile duct Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunosto my Type II Atresia of the common hepati c duct Kasai procedure (Roux-en-Y h epatoportoenterostomy ) Type III Atresia of the right and left h epatic duct781

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which among the following statements is true regarding the anatomy of the spleen ?

options.a: The spleen develops from the ventral mesogastrium
options.b: The axis of the spleen lies along the 9th rib
options.d: The spleen is partly covered by the peritoneum

mcqs.explanation: The superior border of the spleen is notched . The superior border of the spleen separates the diaphragmatic surface from the gastric impression of the visceral surface . It often contains one or two notches . Additionally , there can be a notch on the inferolateral border, and this may be palpated only when the spleen is enlarged . Option A: The spleen arises from the primitive mesoderm as an outgrowth of the left side of the dorsal mesogastrium. Option B: The spleen is related to the 9th, 10th, and 11th ribs, with its long axis along the 10th rib. Option D: The spleen is completely intraperitoneal.788

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: The downward displacement of the spleen is prevented by which of the following ligaments ?
mcqs.explanation: The phrenocolic ligament prevents the downward displacement of the spleen . The phrenicocolic ligament is not attached to the spleen . It attaches the splenic flexure of the colon to the diaphragm. When the spleen gets enlarged , the phrenicocolic ligament along with the splenic flexure of the colon restricts its downward displacement .The enlargement of the spleen occurs towards the right iliac fossa and is directed obliquely . Splenic ligaments and their attachments :Splenic ligament Attachments Contents Phrenicocolic ligament Diaphragmto the splenic flex ure of thecolon - Phrenicosplenic ligament Posterior abdominal wall to t he upper pole of the spleen - Splenorenal (lienorenal) liga ment Hilum of the spleen to the an terior surface of the left kidn ey Tail of pancreasSplenic arter y and vein Gastrosplenicligament Greater curvature of the stom ach to the upper pole of the s pleen Short gastric vesselsLeft gast roepiploic artery789 The below image shows the cross-sectional view of the spleen and its ligaments :

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common site for an accessory spleen ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common site for accessory spleen or splenunculi is the splenic hilum. It is the most common anomaly of splenic embryology. Other locations for accessory spleen in descending order of frequency are: • Gastrocolic ligament • Pancreatic tail • Greater omentum • Greater curvature of the stomach790 • Splenocolic ligament • Small and large bowel mesentery • Left broad ligament in women • Left spermatic cord in men

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old lady presents with complaints of epigastric and lower back pain. Past history is significant for post -traumatic splenectomy at the age of 12 years. CT scan showed multiple nodules scattered across the intestinal loops and under the diaphragm. The tumours were excised following laparotomy and histology was typical for splenic tissue . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of splenosis . Splenosis refers to the rupture of the spleen and distribution of splenic tissue on the peritoneum . This should be considered as a differential diagnosis when a patient with a splenic injury in the past presents with tumour-like lesions on abdominal imaging.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Two weeks following an upper respiratory tract infection , a 5-year-old child presents with a skin rash as shown in the image. She also complains of bleeding gums and her platelet count is 18,000 /\265 L. Which among the following is false about her condition?

options.a: Chronic form of this condition is more common in females
options.c: Bone marrow examination shows increased megathrombocytes
options.d: Splenectomy is the best alternative treatment for this condition

mcqs.explanation: The image showing petechiae and the given history of a child presenting with mucocutaneous bleed following an upper respiratory tract infection are highly suggestive of immune thrombocytopenic purpura. In idiopathic /immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP ), the spleen is palpable in fewer than 10 % of the patients , and the presence of gross splenic enlargement should raise the suspicion of an alternative diagnosis. Management of ITP : • In patients with platelet counts <30,000 /�ML, treatment may be instituted if there are symptoms of life -threatening bleeding. • Prednisone at 1 mg/kg is the initial treatment of choice . • Rh(D) immune globulin is used only in Rh-positive patients . • Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG ). • Splenectomy is indicated in patients who have relapsed on glucocorticoid therapy . Relapse patients with intermittent or high platelet count can be managed with anti-Rh0 (D) immunoglobulin, IVIG , or with a thrombopoietin receptor agonist. • Subcutaneous romiplostim and oral eltrombopag are thrombopoietin receptor agonists used in adults who are at risk of bleeding even after splenectomy .
