mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: The image shows a surgical technique used to release Dupuytren 's contracture. Which of the following statements is true regarding this?

options.a: It can also be used in the surgical management of keloid scars and contractures
options.b: It reorients the direction of the central wound by 90 degrees
options.c: Triangular flaps created using 60 degrees can lengthen the scar by 50%
options.d: It is a type of local advancement flap

mcqs.explanation: The image shows a typical example of a Z Plasty. It is a type of transposition flap that incorporates qualities of both advancement and rotation flaps. Z plasty is used for the lengthening of linear scars. It is best used in releasing simple contractures. Usually , all the limbs are of equal length and ideally , the angle between them is 60\260. Two triangular flaps are raised. Theoretically , a 60-degree angle flap will result in a 75 % increase in the length of the scar and a 90-degree reorientation of central wound . Angles smaller than 60 degrees are easier to transpose but result in less lengthening and realignment of the scar to less than 90 degrees . Angles larger than 60 degrees should be avoided because the force required to transpose the flaps increases markedly, making the closure of the wound difficult . Relative contraindications to Z-plasty include patients with keloids and hypertrophic scarring tendencies .1122

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A truck driver undergoes a Limberg flap operation using a random flap for recurrent pilonidal sinus infections. What is the generally accepted safe and reliable length : width ratio for this type of flap?
mcqs.explanation: The Limberg flap is a type of random flap and the safe and reliable length :width ratio for the random flap 3:1. Random pattern flaps have a blood supply based on small, unnamed blood vessels in the dermal-subdermal plexus , as opposed to the discrete , well described , directional vessels of axial pattern flaps . As random flaps have a variable blood supply , they need an adequate base (width) to survive. The rhomboid (Limberg) flap involves creating a skin flap with two opposing angles of 60\260 and \260 at the corners, forming a rhomboid shape positioned directly next to the defect . The design allows the flap to be rotated into the defect , with the donor site closed primarily, ensuring minimal distortion to the surrounding tissues . This method is especially useful in areas like the gluteal region, where complex closure techniques help achieve optimal results .

mcqs.question: A free flap is used to resurface a tendoachilles defect in a 58-year-old chronic smoker. As a first-year surgical resident , you are asked to monitor the flap for venous occlusion . Which of the following should you be looking out for?
mcqs.explanation: The first sign of venous occlusion in a free flap is increasing warmth. mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the flap given in the image.

options.a: Pedicled TRAM based on superior epigastric artery
options.b: Free TRAM based on superior and inferior epigastric artery
options.c: DIEP based on deep inferior epigastric artery
options.d: Lower Abdominal Fat based inferior epigastric vessels

mcqs.explanation: The given image showing only skin and fat moved to the chest is suggestive of a deep inferior epigastric artery perforator flap (DIEP), based on the deep inferior epigastric artery. DIEP is a variant of TRAM flap and free flap where only the skin and fat are moved to the chest . A microvascular technique is used in which no muscle is taken and the perforating vessels are dissected out.1123 As the muscle is spared in DIEP, there is a reduced risk of abdominal wall weakness and its associated complications . Other options : Options A and B: The pedicled TRAM flap is based on the superior epigastric artery and the free TRAM flap is based on superior and inferior epigastric arteries (supercharged TRAM flap); however, the given image depicts a deep inferior epigastric artery flap. In TRAM flaps : • The skin, fat, and muscle are moved to the chest . • It provides good cosmesis and bulk since it has a soft tissue consistency similar to the breast. • Disadvantages include epigastric bulge , partial flap loss, fat necrosis, abdominal wall weakness , and hernias. mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman who underwent a skin-sparing mastectomy a year ago has returned to your clinic to discuss her options for breast reconstruction. All of the following are options to consider except :

options.a: A TRAM flap provides the best cosmetic result than LD flap
options.b: An LD flap provides adequate bulk of breast tissue
options.c: Reconstruction may be delayed or immediate
options.d: Capsular contraction is a dreaded complication of silicone implants

mcqs.explanation: An LD flap does not provide the bulk required and is usually used along with an implant. It is based on the thoracodorsal pedicle . It is an axial flap.1124 Transverse rectus abdominus myocutaneous (TRAM) flap is either based on superior epigastric or inferior epigastric or both (supercharged TRAM ). Skin , fat, and muscle are moved to the chest . It provides good cosmesis and bulk. An implant is usually not required.Since the rectus abdominis muscle is excised in the procedure , it can lead to abdominal wall weakness and hernias.The timing of reconstruction may be immediate or delayed . Impediments to immediate reconstruction include insufficient theatre time and a lack of experienced reconstructive surgeons . In addition, the patient is likely to need post -op radiotherapy, then a delayed reconstruction using a flap often gives better results . The easiest type of reconstruction is using a silicone gel implant under the pectoralis major muscle . Capsular contraction is a dreaded complication of silicone implants.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man with osteosarcoma of the mandibular ramus is planned for resection and reconstruction with a flap. The flap used most commonly in mandibular reconstruction is based on which of the following vascular structures ?
mcqs.explanation: 1125 The most commonly used osseous flap for mandibular reconstruction is the fibular free flap. The fibular free flap is based on the peroneal artery and vein, and the blood supply to the foot should be investigated before harvesting this flap. Common flaps and their uses The free fibular flap may also be used to correct the Andy Gump deformity . mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 56-year-old patient suffering from alcoholic cirrhosis receives a healthy liver from his biological son. What is this type of transplant known as?
mcqs.explanation: Transplant of an organ/tissue from a son to a parent is an example of an allograft. An allograft is transplant of cells /tissues/organs from a genetically non-identical donor of the same species . Isografts are allografts in which cells /tissues /organs are transplanted from a donor to a genetically identical recipient . (monozygotic twins)

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What incision would you make to excise a lesion on the bridge of the nose, in order to cause minimal scarring?
mcqs.explanation: A horizontal incision should be taken as the relaxed skin tension lines (Borge's lines) at the bridge of the nose are horizontal. Aligning a surgical incision or excision with skin tension lines results in minimal tension across the closure of the defect . This leads to optimal scar formation and minimizes wound contraction. Skin tension lines reflect internal tension within the skin and are produced by the parallel alignment of connective tissue of the dermis. Several different skin tension lines have been described . Borge's lines which are also called relaxed skin tension lines are most useful to guide surgical incision. These are often confused with Langer's lines. Langer's lines, also called cleavage lines are topological lines drawn based on the shape of wounds on cadavers. These were not intended as a guide for surgical incisions and they do not always correspond to the best orientation of skin tension and often run perpendicular to skin folds . On the face , these two sets of lines often run at right angles to one another.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A plastic surgeon performs an upper eyelid reconstruction using a tarsoconjunctival flap for a patient who underwent a sebaceous gland carcinoma excision. What is the maximum tissue loss for which a primary repair would have sufficed ?
mcqs.explanation: 1127 Defects comprising <25% of the upper eyelid can generally be closed primarily in pentagonal approximating fashion. For defects involving 25–50% of the upper eyelid , lateral canthotomy and cantholysis can be performed. Defects more than 50% need proper flap cover.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A mother brings her 3-week -old baby to the pediatrics OPD, with a lesion on his abdomen which has been growing in size since birth. On examination, the lesion is red, nodular, and blanches on pressure . What is the next step in management?

options.a: Local resection with carbon dioxide laser
options.b: En bloc excision with skin grafting

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture is suggestive of infantile hemangioma. Only monitoring of the lesion is required as in 50% of cases , complete involution is seen by 5 years of age . Hemangioma growth frequently peaks before the first year, and then the lesions enter the involuting phase . The involution phase begins in 50% of children by 5 years of age and in 70% by 7 years of age . It continues until 10 years of age . Indications for immediate treatment are complications such as ulceration or those pertaining to the location of the mass (e.g. visual issues due to large hemangioma over eyelid ). Treatment options include : • Beta blockers - oral propranolol • Steroids - intralesional triamcinolone, topical clobetasol , systemic steroids • Interferon alfa-2a and vincristine - for steroid -resistant lesions • Local resection with cutting cautery or carbon dioxide laser1128

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about the surgical anatomy of the lungs ?

options.a: There are 10 bronchopulmonary segments on the right lung.
options.b: Each bronchopulmonary segment has a separate lymphatic drainage.
options.c: The tracheobronchial tree is normally lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar cells .
options.d: Segmentectomy is done after locating the segmental branch of bronchial artery.

mcqs.explanation: In segmentectomy , the segment is removed from the lobe after locating the intersegmental vein. Bronchopulmonary segments are well-defined , anatomic, functional, and surgical areas of the lung. There are 10 bronchopulmonary segments each on the right and the left lung. The segments help in segmental resection and bronchoscopy as each segment has a separate : • Tertiary bronchus • Segmental artery • Autonomic nerve supply • Lymphatic drainageThe tracheobronchial tree is normally lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar cells and mucous cells.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An infant has a congenital bronchopulmonary malformation as shown in the CT scan given below . Which of the following is most likely to supply the marked structure ?
mcqs.explanation: The given CT shows an intralobar pulmonary sequestration of the left lung. The thoracic aorta commonly supplies the sequestered lobe of the lung. Pulmonary sequestration is an area of embryonic lung tissue , separate from the lung. It receives blood supply from an anomalous systemic artery from the aorta. It is of two types : • Extralobar sequestration occurs primarily on the left side and blood supply is usually from the thoracic or upper abdominal aorta • Intralobar sequestration occurs in the lower lobes predominantly (>95%). It is equally distributed between the right and left lower lobe and blood supply is from the descending thoracic1140 aorta, venous drainage via pulmonary veins Treatment involves resection of the pulmonary sequestration .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old patient on DOTS therapy was rushed to the casualty after having massive hemoptysis . Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.a: Intubation is done into the non-bleeding lung.
options.b: Massive hemoptysis is defined as expectoration of over 750 mL of blood within 24-hours.
options.c: Presence of significant cavitary disease is an indication for urgent surgery.
options.d: Bleeding is most likely due to pulmonary artery erosion.

mcqs.explanation: Massive hemoptysis is defined as the expectoration of over 600 mL of blood within a 24-hour period. Common causes include tuberculosis, bronchiectasis , and cancer. It is a medical emergency . Any hemoptysis that can cause airway compromise or lead to hemodynamic collapse is called massive hemoptysis . This includes blood loss of >600mL/24h or >150ml/h which can flood the anatomical dead space of the lung. Bleeding can either be from the bronchial artery circulation (most common) or from the pulmonary artery circulation. Bleeding from cavitary lesions is due to pulmonary artery erosion. The chest X-ray is the first investigation followed by rigid or flexible bronchoscopy . The cause of death in massive hemoptysis is usually due to asphyxiation (rather than blood loss itself ). This is why airway stabilization by intubating into the non-bleeding lung is the priority. After ventilation is achieved , the bleeding site should be identified using bronchoscopy . Bleeding is controlled by laser, bronchial occlusion , or arterial embolization. Surgical resection of the involved area is also done in some cases . Indications for urgent surgical intervention for massive hemoptysis : • Presence of a fungus ball • Presence of a lung abscess • Presence of significant cavitary disease • Failure to control the bleeding .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Where is Rasmussen's aneurysm seen ?
mcqs.explanation: The aneurysm of the pulmonary artery within the tuberculous cavity is called Rasmussen's aneurysm. Rasmussen's aneurysm is an inflammatory pseudo -aneurysmal dilatation. This occurs during the healing of the tuberculous cavity. There is a progressive weakening of the arterial wall, in which both the tunica adventitia and media are replaced by granulation tissue . This is gradually replaced by fibrin resulting in thinning of the arterial wall leading to pseudoaneurysm formation. Rupture of Rasmussen's aneurysm can cause massive hemoptysis . CT angiography plays an important role in locating the aneurysm. Most cases of massive hemoptysis arise from the bronchial arterial tree because of high pressure within bronchial arteries. Even when a pulmonary aneurysm is present , the actual bleeding may be from the bronchial artery , rather than from the pulmonary artery itself .1141

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old chronic smoker with left -sided lung cancer is rushed to the emergency department with massive hemoptysis . On examination, pulse - 102 bpm, BP - 80/50 mmHg, RR - 30/min. Which of the following will be part of your management plan for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The left side is most likely to be the bleeding side in this patient . Hence , the patient should be placed in the left lateral decubitus position to prevent aspiration into the unaffected lung. Also, a CT scan is not indicated as he is hemodynamically unstable . Treatment priorities in the management of massive hemoptysis : • First priorities are to maintain the airway, optimize oxygenation and stabilize the hemodynamic status by administering IV fluids . • Chest X-ray is the first investigation of choice . CT scan is done only in hemodynamically stable patients . • If the bleeding side is known, the patient should be placed in a lateral decubitus position, with the bleeding side down to prevent aspiration into the unaffected lung and given supplemental oxygen . • If large-volume bleeding continues or the airway is compromised , the patient should be intubated and undergo emergency bronchoscopy . • The bleeding site is localized using flexible /rigid bronchoscopy . • Control the hemorrhage: • Endobronchially with Nd: YAG laser or bronchial occlusion • Endovascularly with bronchial and/or pulmonary artery embolization • Electrocauterization • Surgically with resection of the involved lobe The cause of the hemoptysis must be determined to definitively prevent a recurrence.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 54-year-old comes to the casualty with a history of massive hemoptysis . His routine investigation and chest X-ray were normal . Which of the following you will not do to prevent hemoptysis ?
mcqs.explanation: Procoagulant drugs are not used to prevent hemoptysis . Procoagulant drugs like vasopressin are indicated only if there is an abnormal coagulation profile . Massive hemoptysis is generally defined as the expectoration of over 600 mL of blood within a 24-h period . Treatment priorities in the management of massive hemoptysis : • First priorities are to secure the airway, optimize oxygenation and stabilize the hemodynamic status by administering IV fluids . • Chest X-ray is the first investigation of choice . CT scan is done only in hemodynamically stable patients . • If the bleeding site is known, the patient should be placed in a lateral decubitus position with the bleeding side down to prevent aspiration into the unaffected lung. Supplemental oxygen should be given.1142 • If large-volume bleeding continues or the airway is compromised , the patient should be intubated and undergo an emergency bronchoscopy . • The bleeding site is localized using flexible /rigid bronchoscopy . • Control the hemorrhage: • Endobronchially with Nd: YAG laser or bronchial occlusion • Endovascularly with bronchial and/or pulmonary artery embolization • Electrocauterization • Surgically with resection of the involved lobe The cause of the hemoptysis must be determined to definitively prevent a recurrence.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 20 -year-old man presents with h/o sudden breathlessness while watching television . Upon examination , he is noticed to be 6 ft tall and very lean. He is not breathless at the moment. Chest X-ray reveals a right-sided pneumothorax of 1.5 cm. He does not smoke or drink . Which of the following is the next step in the management of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of primary pneumothorax. The next step would be to discharge and follow up in 2-4 weeks as the size is <2cm. Pneumothorax is the abnormal accumulation of air in the pleural space . It can be primary or secondary. Primary pneumothorax can occur spontaneously due to rupture of the apical blebs . Risk factors include : • Males > Females • Young , tall, and thin individuals • Family history • Smoking It resolves spontaneously hence just follow -up is usually needed in most cases . Secondary pneumothorax occurs due to some underlying pathology . Risk factors include : • Age > 50 years • Smoking • COPD • Asthma • Cystic fibrosis • Infection (pneumonia, abscess , and tuberculosis ) • Interstitial lung disease • Connective tissue disease • Procedures (subclavian lines, thoracentesis , bronchoscopy , and mechanical ventilation) • Blunt trauma1143 Patients with pneumothorax present with acute dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain. A physical examination will reveal: • An enlarged hemithorax • Decreased chest movements • Hyper-resonance on percussion • Absent vocal fremitus • Diminished breath sounds Diagnosis is made by chest X-ray (best initial test ), CT scan, or USG. Management of pneumothorax: • Primary pneumothorax • <2 cm size: Discharge and follow -up in 2-4 weeks • >2 cm size and/or breathless : Aspirate with 16 G cannula \037 If fails, place a chest drain of size 8-14 Fr • Secondary pneumothorax • <1 cm size: High-flow oxygen with observation for 24 hours • 1-2 cm size: Aspirate with 16 G cannula \037 If fails, place a chest drain of size 8-14 Fr • >2 cm size: Place chest drain of size 8-14 Fr

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: The ultrasound diagnosis of pneumothorax depends on :
mcqs.explanation: The ultrasound diagnosis of pneumothorax depends on the presence of barcode sign, absence of the sliding lung and absence of comet-tail artifacts that are seen in relation to a normal lung–pleural interface . Normally, lung sliding corresponds to the to-and-fro movement of the visceral pleura on the parietal pleura that occurs with respiration. It is a dynamic sign and can be identified on ultrasound as horizontal movement along the pleural line. In pneumothorax, the air separates visceral and parietal pleura and prevents visualization of visceral pleura. Hence lung sliding is absent and typical to and fro movement and shimmering of the pleural lines will not be present . Comet tail artifacts are seen in the normal lungs due to the acoustic impedance differences between water and air, whereas it is absent in pneumothorax. The image given below shows a sliding sign seen in a normal lung.1144 Option A: The quad sign is seen in pleural effusion . It consists of four lines representing the pleura, rib, fluid , and lung. Option C: The motionless portion of the chest above the pleural line creates horizontal 'waves,' and the sliding below the pleural line creates a granular pattern, the 'sand'. The resultant picture is one that resembles waves crashing onto the sand and is therefore called the 'seashore sign' and is present in normal lungs .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient presents with breathlessness to the casualty after a motorcycle accident . On examination , the left chest is hyper -resonant on percussion and shows reduced air entry over the same side . His pulse is 110 bpm, RR - 25/min, BP - 80/45mmHg, and JVP was elevated . What will be your immediate management?

options.a: Insert a wide bore needle in 5th intercostal space anterior to the mid axillary line
options.c: Insert a chest tube in the 5th intercostal space in the anterior axillary line

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of tension pneumothorax. The first line of management in tension pneumothorax is to insert a wide -bore needle in the 5th intercostal space just anterior to the midaxillary line. Pneumothorax is the abnormal accumulation of air in the pleural space . Tension pneumothorax develops when air enters the pleural space through a point that acts as a one-way valve. More and more air enters with every breath without any way for the air to escape . This is a medical emergency where the patient can quickly deteriorate . A patient with pneumothorax presents with acute dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain. A physical examination will reveal: • An enlarged hemithorax • Decreased chest movements • Hyper-resonance on percussion • Absent vocal fremitus • Diminished breath sounds In addition to the above findings, a tension pneumothorax would also have the following : • Deviation of trachea to the opposite side1145 • Distended neck vein • Cyanosis • Sudden onset hemodynamic compromise: • Hypotension • Tachycardia • Low O2 saturation • Loss of consciousness A diagnosis of tension pneumothorax is usually made based on the clinical findings. If the tension in the pleural cavity is not relieved , the patient can die due to hemodynamic collapse . Hence, treatment should never be delayed waiting for radiological confirmation. The management of tension pneumothorax is to convert a tension pneumothorax into a simple pneumothorax . This can be done by rapid decompression using a wide -bore cannula on the affected side , followed by the insertion of a chest tube for definitive management. The safest site for insertion of a drain is in the triangle (Triangle of safety ) that lies : • Anterior to the mid-axillary line • Above the level of the nipple • Below and lateral to the pectoralis major muscleNote : If immediate management is asked, the answer will be to insert a wide -bore needle in the 5th intercostal space in the midaxillary line. If definitive management is asked, the answer will be to insert an intercostal tube in the triangle of safety .1146

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old man is brought to the emergency department with a stab wound to his right chest following a fight at the local bar. His vitals are normal . On examination, the trachea is central and a penetrating wound is noted on the right chest . A sucking sound is heard during inspiration. Which of the following is the initial management in this case?

options.a: Occlusive dressing tapped on the 3 sides
options.b: Placing chest drain at the site of the wound

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of open pneumothorax. Initial management, in this case, is to apply occlusive dressing taped on the 3 sides . Open pneumothorax is due to a large open defect in the chest , making intrathoracic pressure equal to atmospheric pressure . In this defect , the air is preferentially drawn through the defect , rather than through the trachea. Air gets accumulated causing pneumothorax leading to hypoventilation and hypoxia. It acts as a sucking chest wound . Sucking sound during inspiration is characteristic. It is managed initially with the application of a sterile occlusive dressing tapped on the 3 sides . Then a chest tube is inserted at a different site , away from the wound .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient presents with a productive cough , fever, and breathlessness . On examination, decreased breath sounds and dull note on percussion is noted on the left side . A chest X-ray is given below . USG-guided aspiration revealed frank pus . Chest tube was inserted but there was no improvement in symptoms . How will you manage this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of empyema thoracis. Symptoms failed to resolve on treatment with chest tube insertion, hence it is managed by VATS debridement . Empyema thoracis is an infection of the pleural space . It commonly progresses from an acute phase with thin fluid that can be drained completely with a chest tube or small-bore catheter to a more turbid and thick fluid that might loculate . It is an exudative effusion . It can be caused due to: • Underlying infection of the lung (pneumonia or abscess ) • Complication after chest surgery • Infected hemothorax • Complication of Pleural effusion1147 • Trauma (esophageal perforation) • Osteomyelitis of ribs An empyema thoracis on chest x-ray can mimic a pleural effusion or a lung abscess . The procedure VATS (Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery) is used in the debridement of empyema. At the end of the procedure , chest drains are placed for dependent drainage. If VATS fails to re-expand the lung after drainage, a more radical procedure (decortication ) may be done.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an indication for performing thoracotomy in patients with blunt chest injury?

options.a: >1500 ml drainage after placing an intercostal tube
options.b: Continuous bleeding through intercostal tube of more than 200 ml/hour for three or more hours

mcqs.explanation: A rib fracture is not an indication for thoracotomy. Indications for thoracotomy: • Initial tube thoracostomy drainage of >1000 ml (penetrating injury) or >1500 ml (blunt injury) of frank blood • Ongoing tube thoracostomy drainage of >200 ml/ hr for 3 consecutive hours in non-coagulopathic patients with hemothorax • Caked hemothorax despite the placement of two chest tubes • Massive air leak from chest tube with inadequate ventilation • Open pneumothorax • Great vessel injury • Pericardial tamponade • Cardiac herniation • Tracheobronchial injury • Esophageal perforation

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: All of the following will be your differential diagnosis in a patient with anterior mediastinal mass except :
mcqs.explanation: Neurogenic tumors are found in the posterior mediastinum and not in the anterior mediastinum. They are the most common primary tumors of the posterior mediastinum. Schwannomas and Neurilemomas are the most common neurogenic tumors.1148

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old patient complains of double vision that gets worse after he watches television . He also has drooping of the eyelids that gets better after a nap. Serology is positive for anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies . A CT scan of his chest is given below . Which of the following is false regarding his condition?

options.a: It is the most common tumor of the anterior mediastinum.
options.b: Masoaka classification system is used for staging .
options.c: Tumor size is a reliable indicator of malignancy.
options.d: Surgery can be performed through a median sternotomy approach.

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical features of myasthenia gravis along with the CT scan image showing an anterior mediastinal mass are suggestive of thymoma. The only reliable indicator of malignancy in thymoma is the capsular invasion , not tumor size. Thymoma is the most common mediastinal tumor and is derived from the thymus gland. Thymomas vary in behavior from benign to aggressively invasive . Masoaka classification system is used to stage thymomas. Myasthenia gravis is often related to thymomas. Symptoms of myasthenia gravis improve after excision of the thymus gland even in the absence of a thymoma. Complete thymectomy is the treatment for thymoma. It can be performed by two approaches : • A median sternotomy approach • A transcervical approach with or without an additional VATS procedure (Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery) for smaller thymomas

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which stage of Masaoka staging does a patient with thymoma invading the great vessels come under?
mcqs.explanation: Thymoma invading great vessels come under stage III of the Masaoka staging system . Masaoka staging system is the most commonly accepted staging system for thymoma. It is based on the presence or absence of gross or microscopic invasion of the capsule and of surrounding structures , and metastasis .1149 Stage Features Stage I Encapsulated tumor with no gross or microscopic evidenc e of capsular invasion Stage I I Grosscapsular invasionor inv asion into the mediastinal fat or pleura or microscopic cap sular invasion Stage I II Gross invasion into the peric ardium, great vessels , or lung Stage I VA Pleural or pericardialdissemi nation Stage I VB Lymphogenous or hematoge nousmetastasis

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A toddler with cough and progressive breathing difficulty was found to have a poorly defined solid mass in the mediastinum. What is the most common mediastinal mass in this age group?
mcqs.explanation: The most common mediastinal mass in young children is neurogenic tumors (50%-60%). In most cases (< 4 years of age ), they are invariably malignant. The most common mediastinal masses in adults are thymomas and thymic cysts .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Lymphomas most commonly a\037ect which compartment of the mediastinum?
mcqs.explanation: Lymphoma most commonly occurs in the anterior mediastinum. Occasional involvement of the middle compartment and rare involvement of posterior mediastinum is seen . Chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy results in a cure rate of up to 90% for early-stage Hodgkin's disease and up to 60% for more advanced stages . Note : • Most common tumor of the middle mediastinum: Lymphoma. • Most common mass of the middle mediastinum: Pericardial Cyst .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the most common benign tumor of the lung?
mcqs.explanation: The most common benign tumor of the lung is hamartoma . Hamartoma is a developmental abnormality containing mesothelial and endothelial elements . They are manifested by the overgrowth of cartilage . It is typically seen in 40-60 years of age , more common in males. It is usually seen in the periphery of the lung and grows slowly . Popcorn calcification in chest X-ray is suggestive of a hamartoma .1150 Chest X-ray showing a popcorn calcification in the apex of the right lung.Diagnosis and definitive treatment are achieved by excision of the lesion. Gross specimen showing hamartoma of the lung.Note : Popcorn calcification is also seen in: • Chondroid lesions like chondrosarcoma • Fibrous dysplasia • Fibroadenoma breast • Calcified uterine fibroid • Metaphyses and epiphyses of long bones of children with osteogenesis imperfecta1151

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about bronchial carcinoid?
mcqs.explanation: Bronchial carcinoid is usually asymptomatic . Bronchial carcinoids are the most indolent of the spectrum of pulmonary neuroendocrine tumors. They arise from the Kulchitsky cells in the bronchial epithelium . Most tumors are confined to the main stem bronchus and commonly project into the lumen. It is associated with MEN 1. Most patients affected are <40 years and it is not related to smoking. It is usually asymptomatic and only 10 % of bronchial carcinoids give rise to carcinoid syndrome which is characterized by intermittent attacks of: • Diarrhea • Flushing • Bronchospasm • Cyanosis Bronchial carcinoids follow a relatively benign course and do not metastasize to distant sites . They have a good prognosis and can be easily resected .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In patients with lung cancer, presence of which of the following indicates an immune-mediated paraneoplastic syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Peripheral neuropathy is an immune-mediated paraneoplastic syndrome. It is due to the secretion of antigens normally expressed only by the nervous system which leads to antibodies production against CNS. Lung cancers are capable of producing a variety of paraneoplastic syndromes. They may produce symptoms even before any local symptoms are produced by the primary tumor, thereby aiding in early diagnosis. mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Identify the incorrectly matched pair based on the type of lung cancer and their paraneoplastic effects .
mcqs.explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) causes hypercalcemia . Cushing's syndrome is caused by small cell lung cancer. Paraneoplastic syndrome is usually associated with small cell carcinoma , even though all varieties of lung cancer are capable of causing it.Lung cancer Paraneoplastic syndromes Squamous cell carcinoma (SC C) Hypercalcemia Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) Syndrome of inappropriate s ecretion of antidiuretic horm one (SIADH)Cushing's syndr omeEaton - Lambert syndrom eRetinal blindness Adenocarcinoma Hypertrophic primary osteoa rthropathy Non-small cell lung cancer (N SCLC) Clubbing

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 52-year-old smoker presents with cough and pain along the right arm for the past few weeks . He appears cachexic. On examination, clubbing and right-sided ptosis were noted . Chest X-ray of the patient is given below. Which of the following statements is false about this condition?

options.a: CT scan is preferred over MRI.
options.d: N2 nodal stage requires definitive chemoradiotherapy .

mcqs.explanation: 1155 The given clinical scenario along with the X-ray showing opacity of the apex of the right lung is suggestive of Pancoast syndrome. MRI is preferred over CT because of the associated soft tissue infiltration, the extent of which can be best visualized using an MRI. Pancoast syndrome/superior sulcus tumor results from a local extension of a tumor growing in the apex of the lung, with the involvement of C8, T1 , and T2 nerve roots. Regional spread can cause : • Pain that radiates to the ulnar distribution of the arm , often with the destruction of the 1st and 2nd ribs • Recurrent laryngeal nerve paralysis with hoarseness of voice • Endobronchial growth of the primary tumor may present with a cough , hemoptysis , wheeze , stridor, dyspnea , or post -obstructive pneumonitis • Phrenic nerve palsy with the elevation of the hemidiaphragm. • Sympathetic nerve paralysis with Horner's syndrome (enophthalmos , ptosis , miosis, and anhydrosis). It occurs due to invasion of the sympathetic chain and of the inferior cervical (stellate ) ganglion • Tracheal obstruction • Esophageal compression with dysphagia Bronchoscopy can be done to obtain a tissue diagnosis. Surgery with curative intent is offered to patients with early-stage cancer (T1 –3, N0–1). Management is summarized in the flowchart as shown below :

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: During a health checkup in a factory, a 52-year-old worker complained of progressive cough and weight loss for the past 6 months. Chest X-ray showed a mass in the right apical region of the lung with pleural effusion . The biopsy sample obtained stained positive for calretinin. Which of the following is false about this condition?

options.a: Immunohistochemical analysis will be positive for TTF -1.
options.c: Asbestos exposure is the major risk factor.

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with biopsy showing positive calretinin is suggestive of mesothelioma . The immunohistochemical analysis will be negative for TTF -1 in mesothelioma . TTF -1 is positive1156 in adenocarcinoma of the lung. Malignant mesothelioma is the most common tumor of the pleura . Exposure to asbestos is the major known risk factor. The latency period between asbestos exposure and the development of mesothelioma is at least 20 years. It is more common in males, usually seen after 40 years of age . It has a very poor prognosis. Histological subtypes include : • Epithelial • Sarcomatous • Biphasic The physical characteristics of specific fibers are important for causation. They are: • Serpentine fibers: Large and curly, not able to travel beyond larger airways. • Amphibole fibers: The narrow , straight amphibole fibers, in particular, the crocidolite fibers navigate distally into the pulmonary parenchyma and are most clearly associated with mesotheliomas . It is not bilaterally symmetrical. Its clinical features include : • Dyspnoea • Chest pain • Pleural effusion – in 90% cases Diagnostic imaging includes chest X-ray, CT scan, and FDG-PET scan to determine the extent of tumor invasion and to evaluate occult metastases . Thoracoscopy or open pleural biopsy with special staining of tumor samples is required to differentiate mesotheliomas from adenocarcinomas. Treatment includes a combination of surgery, chemotherapy , and radiation therapy . Extrapleural pneumonectomy and total pleurectomy are two commonly used surgical procedures .1157

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 48-year-old man with a chronic history of smoking is diagnosed with small cell lung carcinoma . Which of the following statement is false regarding the management of the patient ?

options.b: In wedge resection , anatomical bronchopulmonary segment is removed.
options.c: Posterolateral thoracotomy approach is used for surgical resection .
options.d: Lobectomy is the treatment of choice for early-stage lung cancer.

mcqs.explanation: Wedge resection involves the non-anatomical excision of the tumor. Excision of the anatomical bronchopulmonary segment is called segmentectomy . Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a type of tumor that originates from neuroendocrine progenitor cells (Kulchitsky cells ) in the lining bronchial epithelium . They tend to metastasize early to lymph nodes and by the blood-borne spread . SCLC is very responsive to chemotherapy such that median survival may be doubled . Surgery for lung cancers: Surgery with curative intent is offered to patients with early-stage lung cancer (T1 –3, N0–1). Lung cancer resection can be approached through: • Posterolateral thoracotomy • Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS)Complications of surgery include : • Bleeding • Respiratory infection • Persistent air-leak • Bronchopleural fistula

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a component of Thoracoscore?
mcqs.explanation: The complication of surgery is not a component of thoracoscore. Thoracoscore is used to assess the risk of operative mortality in a patient undergoing thoracic surgery. It includes 9 variables:1158 • Age • Sex • American Society of Anesthesiologists score (ASA) • Performance status • Dyspnoea score • Priority of surgery • Extent of surgery • Malignant diagnosis • Composite comorbidity score

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient with a mediastinal mass undergoes the following procedure . Which of the following statements is false ?

options.a: The patient is positioned in a lateral decubitus with the diseased side up.
options.b: It is contraindicated if the patient is having empyema .
options.c: Lobectomy can be done via this procedure .
options.d: It allows direct visualization of the pleural cavity.

mcqs.explanation: The procedure that is shown is Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery (VATS ) and empyema is not a contraindication for the procedure . VATS is a minimally invasive surgical technique used to diagnose and treat disorders of the thoracic cavity. It also allows direct visualization of the pleural cavity. Lung biopsy and recurrent pneumothorax are the most frequent indications for VATS . Other conditions where VATS is used include : • Malignancies • Empyema • Oesophageal surgeries • Patent ductus areteriosus • Undiagnosed pleural effusion • Pneumonectomy • Lobectomy • Pleural biopsy • Pleurodesis The patient is usually positioned with the diseased side up in a lateral decubitus position. A double lumen endotracheal -bronchial tube is placed by the anesthetist for single -lung ventilation. At the end of the procedure, chest drains are placed to allow dependent drainage. The following precautions must be noted before placing the drains: • The drain should exit the skin anterior to the midaxillary line. If this is not done then the patient will have to lie on the tube which will cause pain and obstruction of the tube . • The course of the drain should be oblique to the skin, chest wall, and pleura , or else it will lead to kinking of the tube .1159 The main advantage of VATS is that a large incision is avoided. This causes less postoperative pain and a rapid recovery. However, VATS procedure limits the ability of the surgeon to palpate the lung to identify occult metastases .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the conduit of choice for the left anterior descending artery while performing CABG?
mcqs.explanation: The left internal mammary artery (LIMA ) or internal thoracic artery is the conduit of choice for the left anterior descending (LAD ) coronary artery. The most important criterion in conduit selection is graft patency . The conduit with the highest patency rate is the left internal mammary artery or internal thoracic artery. Left internal mammary artery > Radial artery > long saphenous vein represents the correct order of graft patency in a patient undergoing CABG procedure . Venous grafts: • The long saphenous vein is the most common vein used as a conduit as it is straightforward to harvest, provides good length , and is easy to handle. • The ten-year patency rate for long saphenous vein grafts is reported to be 50–60 percent . Arterial grafts: • The left internal mammary artery (LIMA ) or internal thoracic artery has become the conduit of choice for the left anterior descending (LAD ) coronary artery. The radial artery can be used as a second or alternative arterial bypass graft. Other arterial bypass grafts include the gastroepiploic artery and the inferior epigastric artery. • Long patency rates of >98 percent have been reported .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old man has been in the ICU for the past 1 month due to end-stage liver failure. He is not eligible for a transplant and his doctors have said there is nothing they can do at this stage . His family has consented to organ donation once his heart stops . Which of the categories of non-beating heart donors would this patient fall into as per the modified Maastricht classification ?
mcqs.explanation: The patient would fall under category III . Modified Maastricht classification - Categories of non-heart-beating donors: • Uncontrolled - transplant team not present or prepared • Category I - includes victims of accident and suicide who are found dead at the scene and resuscitation is deemed pointless (e.g. fatal cervical spine fracture). • Category II - donors are mostly victims of sudden cardiac or cerebral catastrophes who are brought to emergency departments while being resuscitated by ambulance personnel or who die in the department . Other sources include patients suffering an isolated brain injury, anoxia, and stroke, and victims of major trauma who died soon after hospital admission. • Category V - Unexpected cardiac arrest during intensive care. • Controlled - transplant team present and prepared • Category III - encompasses patients who are dying, often in an intensive care unit. These are the patients awaiting cardiac arrest where the treating clinicians have decided to withdraw treatment and not commence resuscitation for various reasons.1160 • Category IV - comprises patients who suffer unexpected cardiac arrest during or after the determination of brain death .1161

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: The most common cause of peripheral vascular disease is?
mcqs.explanation: Atherosclerosis is the most common cause of peripheral occlusive vascular disease (POVD). Other causes are trauma and emboli. Peripheral arterial insufficiency is predominantly a disease of the lower extremities with the superficial femoral and iliac arteries commonly affected .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the most common symptom of peripheral occlusive vascular disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common symptom of peripheral obstructive vascular disease is intermittent claudication. Intermittent claudication is the debilitating cramp-like pain felt in the leg muscles due to reduced blood flow brought on by peripheral arterial disease . It usually signifies mild to moderate chronic vascular occlusive disease . Rest pain is when the disease progresses to a degree that perfusion is severely reduced and cramp-like pain in the calf is felt even at rest. A swollen and erythematous limb is seen in critical limb ischemia. When the limb is in the dependent position, there is pooling of blood which causes the limb to appear red and swollen (sunset foot sign). Buerger's test is done to assess the severity of peripheral vascular disease . In normal individuals, the elevation of the lower limb to a 90-degree angle does not produce any pallor but in affected individuals, even at an elevation of 20 -degrees , pallor and venous guttering of the limb can be seen .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man presented to the OPD with complaints of pain in the lower limbs, on walking a certain distance . He noticed that the pain subsides on resting. Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.a: Pain is usually felt in the calf muscles
options.b: Muscle group affected is below the level of arterial disease
options.c: Distance at which pain occurs varies greatly from day to day
options.d: Worsened by anemia or heart failure

mcqs.explanation: The patient is likely experiencing intermittent claudication due to peripheral occlusive vascular disease .1171 Intermittent claudication is the debilitating cramp-like pain felt in the leg muscles due to reduced blood flow brought on by peripheral arterial disease . It usually signifies mild to moderate chronic vascular occlusive disease . The pain classically occurs during activity and is relieved with rest. The distance that a patient can walk without stopping till the pain is experienced in the muscles is known as claudication distance . This distance varies only slightly from day-to-day. The muscle group affected is one anatomical level below the arterial disease . Boyd's classification Class l - Pain on walking but pain decreases on continuation of walking. Class ll - Pain on walking, but continues to walk despite the pain. Class lll - Pain forces the patient to stop walking. Class lV - Pain at rest. It is worsened by health conditions such as anemia and heart failure.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old male who is a chronic smoker presented to the hospital with intermittent claudication pain of both thigh and buttock region on walking about 500 m. Which of the following is a likely diagnosis?

options.a: Arterial disease involving the superficial femoral artery
options.d: Arterial disease involving the profunda femoris artery

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of arterial disease with aortoiliac involvement. Classically , the muscle group affected by claudication is one anatomical level below the level of arterial disease . Intermittent claudication is a feature of chronic arterial disease or occlusion of the artery. Aortoiliac disease affects the infrarenal aorta and iliac arteries. Management involves smoking cessation, lifestyle modifications, and treatment of underlying diabetes or hyperlipidemia if present . For claudication , cilostazol or pentoxyfilline is used . Cilostazol is superior to pentoxyfilline . mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Critical limb ischemia is characterized by all except _____
mcqs.explanation: Critical limb ischemia is characterized by rest pain and/or ulceration and gangrene . Intermittent claudication progresses to rest pain in critical limb ischemia. Rest pain occurs with the limb at rest and is felt in the foot; it is exacerbated by lying down or elevation of the foot. Characteristically , the pain is worse at night and it may be lessened by hanging the foot out of bed or by sleeping in a chair. The pressure of clothes on the foot usually makes the pain worse . Ulceration occurs with severe arterial insufficiency and may present as painful erosion between toes or as shallow , non-healing ulcers on the dorsum of the feet , on the shins, and especially around the malleoli . The blackened mummified tissues of frank gangrene are unmistakable and superadded infection often makes the gangrene wet .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In a patient with critical limb ischemia, what is the ankle-brachial pressure index (ABPI ) likely to be?
mcqs.explanation: In a patient with critical limb ischemia, the ABPI is < 0.4.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old chronic smoker presents with bluish discoloration of the toe along with intermittent claudication. Which of the following will be the next appropriate investigation in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Chronic smoker presenting with bluish discoloration of the toe along with intermittent claudication is suggestive of peripheral arterial disease and duplex scanning will be the next appropriate investigation. Duplex Scanning is a major non-invasive technique that uses B-mode ultrasound to provide an image of the vessel . Most scanners now have color coding, which allows detailed visualization of blood flow in a vessel . Different colors indicate changes in the direction and velocity of flow , with areas of high flow usually indicating stenotic lesions . Other options : Option A: CT Angiography (CTA) is more useful in the evaluation of visceral arterial disease (eg . mesenteric ischemia). It can be beneficial in peripheral artery diseases where a duplex scan shows poor images (aortoiliac segment involvement). CTA is not routinely recommended in peripheral artery disease because of concomitant renal dysfunction in these patients which can lead to contrast-induced nephropathy . Option B: MR Angiography is time-consuming and expensive , hence not done as the next investigation. It is contraindicated in patients with claustrophobia and metallic implants.1173 Option C: Digital subtraction angiography (DSA) is an invasive and expensive procedure compared to other investigations. The benefits of DSA are that it provides dynamic arterial flow information and can be combined with a definitive endovascular intervention when indicated . DSA is indicated only when there is a discrepancy in diagnosis or intervention is planned . Complications associated with DSA include bleeding , hematoma, false aneurysm formation, thrombosis, arterial dissection, distal embolisation , renal dysfunction , and allergic reaction.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding the investigation of peripheral arterial disease ?

options.a: Duplex scanning is a non invasive technique
options.b: On doppler ultrasound a normal artery has a biphasic signal
options.c: DSA is now the standard technique used
options.d: Computed tomographic angiography is not used routinely to diagnose PAD

mcqs.explanation: A normal artery has a triphasic signal. The waveform becomes biphasic in mild-moderate stenosis and monophasic in severe stenosis . Option A: Duplex scanning is a major non-invasive technique that uses B-mode ultrasound to provide an image of the vessel . Option C: Digital subtraction angiography (DSA) is now the standard technique whereby the images obtained are digitized by computer and the extraneous background (bone, soft tissues , etc .) is removed to provide clearer images. Option D: Computed tomographic angiography (CTA), and conventional catheter -based angiography should not be used for routine diagnostic testing but are performed before potential revascularization . These tests define the anatomy that assists in planning for revascularization procedures .1174

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient with right leg arterial stenosis is being taken up for angioplasty . Which one of the following is incorrect about this procedure ?

options.a: It is done for patients with rest pain or tissue necrosis
options.b: It gives best results for management of stenosis below the knee
options.c: Satisfactory dilatation is confirmed by performing angiogram

mcqs.explanation: Angioplasty gives the best results for medium-sized vessels hence it is preferred for treating the vessels above the knee in peripheral arterial disease . Angioplasty is indicated in patients with rest pain or tissue necrosis. Steps of angioplasty : • Patients posted for angioplasty are given aspirin (325 mg) and clopidogrel (loading dose of 300–600 mg). • During the procedure , anticoagulation is achieved by administration of unfractionated heparin, enoxaparin , or bivalirudin (a direct thrombin inhibitor). • The femoral artery is punctured under local anesthetic , followed by insertion of a guidewire . The guidewire is negotiated through the stenosis or occlusion under fluoroscopic control. • A balloon catheter is then inserted over the guidewire and positioned within the lesion. The balloon is then inflated at high pressure for approximately 1 minute and deflated . • Once the angioplasty is done, dilatation is confirmed by performing angiogram.1175

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which is the best graft for a femoropopliteal bypass ?
mcqs.explanation: The great saphenous vein (GSV) is the best as it lasts longer than polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), dacron, and human umbilical vein as a graft in a femoropopliteal bypass . The GSV is the conduit of choice for arterial bypass grafts below the inguinal ligament . For bypass above the inguinal ligament, while both GSV and PTFE grafts have similar patency rates in the first 2 years, the GSV is superior thereafter and hence preferred over PTFE or any other grafts. The ipsilateral GSV is the conduit of choice for femoropopliteal bypass . When it is not available, contralateral GSV should be used . Other veins are preferred when both ipsilateral and contralateral GSV is not available and they include a small saphenous vein, cephalic vein, and basilic vein. Non-autogenous grafts are used for patients who lack a suitable venous conduit . The most commonly used prosthetic conduit is PTFE. Recent studies have shown that heparin-bonded PTFE is superior to compared to PTFE without heparin.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 52-year-old man presented with complaints of pain in the right leg right for a day. He has a history of recurrent episodes of atrial fibrillation. Which of the following statements are false regarding his condition?

options.a: Ischemia beyond 6 hrs is usually irreversible
options.b: Pain, pallor, pulselessness , and parasthesia/anesthesia are characteristic
options.c: Movement of the digits is not affected
options.d: Embolectomy and thrombolysis are treatment options

mcqs.explanation: The patient most likely has acute arterial occlusion and atrial fibrillation can predispose to emboli formation. In acute arterial occlusion , the movement of the digits will be affected and the limb will be cold. Whereas, in venous occlusion , muscle function is not affected . The leg is often affected with: • Pain • Pallor1176 • Paralysis • Loss of pulsation • Paraesthesia (or anesthesia ). Embolic arterial occlusion is an emergency that requires immediate treatment . Ischaemia beyond 6 hours is usually irreversible and results in limb loss. The diagnosis can be made clinically in a patient who has no history of claudication and has a source of emboli, who suddenly develops severe pain or numbness of the limb, which becomes cold and mottled .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An elderly man is brought to the emergency department with sudden onset severe pain and numbness of the left lower limb. He has no previous history of any limb claudication . The limb appears to be cold and peripheral pulses are not palpable . What is the most appropriate next step ?

options.c: CT Angiogram to check for embolus
options.d: Thrombolysis with intra-arterial tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) infusion

mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario is suggestive of sudden arterial occlusion . The immediate next step is to administer 5000 IU of heparin to prevent extension of clot. Management of sudden arterial occlusion : • Embolectomy with Fogarty's balloon catheter is the definitive treatment of choice . • Thrombolysis with tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) can be done in cases where there are no acute signs of limb ischemia as complete lysis of thrombus in tPA infusion is achieved within 24 hours, however, it is cautiously used in the elderly due to risk of bleeding diathesis . • A CT angiogram is performed after the procedure to ensure that the flow to the distal leg has been restored . Ischaemia beyond 6 hours is usually irreversible and may result in limb loss. Complications of arterial revascularization • Compartment syndrome • Reperfusion syndrome • Ischaemic neuropathy • Myoglobinuria • Renal failure Usually , a prophylactic fasciotomy is done in patients undergoing revascularization surgery to prevent compartment syndrome.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 71-year-old man had an acute STEMI for which coronary stenting was performed . On the follow -up visit, he reported pain over his toes and discoloration of both feet as shown in the image. His creatinine was also elevated . What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of atheroembolism . It is also called cholesterol embolism or blue toe syndrome. Atheroembolism is a condition in which multiple small deposits of fibrin, platelets , and cholesterol debris embolize from proximal atherosclerotic lesions or aneurysmal sites .1177 The typical presentation is a patient with ST-elevation myocardial infarction presenting with features of limb ischemia (cyanotic discoloration of the toes with pain and tenderness ) following an intraarterial procedure (angioplasty ). Digital vascular occlusion may result in ischemia and the "blue toe " syndrome; digital necrosis and gangrene may develop . Localized areas of tenderness , pallor, and livedo reticularis occur at sites of emboli. Since the atheroemboli tend to lodge in the small vessels of the limbs and may not occlude the large vessels , distal pulses are usually palpable . Large protruding aortic atheromas are a source of emboli that may lead to limb ischemia, as well as stroke and renal insufficiency . Skin or muscle biopsy may demonstrate cholesterol crystals. Sharp syndrome, also known as mixed connective tissue disease , is an autoimmune condition with features of SLE, systemic sclerosis , and polymyositis . Clinical features include Raynaud's syndrome, polyarthritis, myositis, swollen hands, and fingers.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient with untreated severe peripheral arterial disease comes to the surgery OPD with a right leg as shown in the image. Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.a: Usually affects most distal part of a limb
options.b: It is a surgical emergency if crepitus is felt on palpation
options.c: Occurs when tissues are desiccated by gradual slowing of blood stream
options.d: Amputation is not done if severe sepsis is present

mcqs.explanation: The patient is suffering from gangrene of the foot. If there is severe sepsis and if re-establishing blood supply is difficult (revascularization ) then amputation is the preferred choice of treatment . Gangrene refers to death of macroscopic portions of tissue which turn black because of the breakdown of haemoglobin and the formation of iron sulphide . It usually affects the most distal part of a limb because of arterial obstruction (from thrombosis, embolus or arteritis). Dry gangrene occurs when the tissues are desiccated by gradual slowing of the bloodstream . Wet Gangrene occurs when superadded infection and putrefaction are present . Crepitus may be palpated as a result of infection by gas-forming organisms commonly in diabetic foot problems .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 51-year-old, diabetic patient presents with the following features during a village health camp. Which of the following statements is false regarding this condition?

options.a: Due to immunosuppression caused by elevated glucose levels
options.b: Repeated injury leads to Charcot's foot
options.c: Glycemic control and antibiotic therapy is first line managment
options.d: Sensory nerves are affected in the late stage of disease

mcqs.explanation: The image and clinical scenario are suggestive of diabetic gangrene of the foot. It is accompanied by sensory loss in the early stage of the disease and motor involvement in the late stage . Diabetic gangrene is caused by a combination of three factors: • Ischemia secondary to macrovascular disease and microvascular dysfunction , • Peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy , which leads to trophic skin changes • Immunosuppression is caused by excess sugar in the tissues , which predisposes to infection Diabetic gangrene is accompanied by loss of sensation and reflexes which lead to repeated injury . There occurs an imbalance between the flexors and extensors of the foot which causes deformities known as Charcot's foot (neuropathic joints). Initial treatment comprises strict glycemic control and antibiotic therapy . The gangrene is treated by drainage of pus , debridement of dead tissue with local amputation of necrotic digits .1178

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man presents to the casualty with complaints of recurrent episodes of syncope and cramping of his left arm . Symptoms mostly occur during his evening badminton practice sessions . Which of the following is incorrect about this condition?

options.a: Due to occlusion in the 3rd part of subclavian artery
options.b: Distal pulse of the affected side is feeble
options.c: CT angiography is used to visualize retrograde blood flow

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario points to a diagnosis of subclavian steal syndrome. In subclavian steal syndrome, the first part of the subclavian artery is occluded . Subclavian steal syndrome is characterized by the presence of stenosis in the first part of the subclavian artery either due to atherosclerotic changes or emboli. It leads to reversed flow in the vertebral artery causing cerebral ischemia. Symptoms include dizziness, syncope on arm exercise . Occasionally , distal pulses in the arm of the affected side are found to be feeble . Investigations include duplex ultrasonography, CT, and MR angiography. It can be treated by angioplasty , stenting or by extra-thoracic subclavian bypass .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In Paget -Schroetter syndrome which of the following structure is affected ?
mcqs.explanation: In Paget -Schroetter syndrome, the subclavian vein is affected . Compression of subclavian vein between anterior scalene , clavicle, and the first rib can produce axillary-subclavian vein thrombosis. It results in severe upper extremity pain and swelling , that is exaggerated by exercise . Activities such as throwing, swimming, and weightlifting can cause microtrauma of the venous intima that initiates thrombus formation.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old male patient who came to the OPD with complaints of pain and numbness of the arm is diagnosed with thoracic outlet syndrome. Which nerve is involved in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: In thoracic outlet syndrome (TOS) the lower two nerve roots of the brachial plexus , C8 and T1 are most commonly involved and produce pain and paresthesia along the ulnar nerve distribution.1179

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A resident is trying to elicit symptoms of thoracic outlet syndrome in a patient . He asks the patient to keep both arms in the 90\260 abduction -external rotation position and to open and close the hands slowly over a 3-minute period . What is this test called ?
mcqs.explanation: The test described in the question is a provocative test for thoracic outlet syndrome called Roos test (extended arm stress test ).

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A young woman presents to the hospital with sudden discoloration of the hands. Which of the following would suggest a diagnosis of acrocyanosis over Raynaud's phenomenon ?
mcqs.explanation: In acrocyanosis, there is no pain or numbness. In Raynaud's phenomenon , there is pain and tingling sensation. Acrocyanosis is a chronic, benign vasoconstrictive disorder. It is due to arterial vasoconstriction and secondary dilation of the capillaries and venules that results in persistent cyanosis of the hands and feet . It can be primary or secondary. Primary acrocyanosis is more common in females with an onset <30 years. Trophic skin changes and ulcerations do not occur and examination reveals normal pulses . The disorder can be distinguished from Raynaud's phenomenon : • Because it is persistent and not episodic • There is no pain in acrocyanosis whereas in Raynaud's phenomenon there is pain and numbness • The discoloration extends proximally from the digits • Blanching does not occur

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old female nurse was on her way to the hospital for her early morning shift. Suddenly she started to notice pain in her fingers which were turning pale and numb after which they turned blue . Which of the following statements are false regarding this condition?

options.a: Triggered by cold as well as stress
options.b: Calcium channel blockers are used for treatment
options.c: Mainstay of treatment includes avoidance of triggers
options.d: Is not associated with autoimmune diseases

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Raynaud's phenomenon . Secondary causes of Raynaud's phenomenon are seen in association with autoimmune diseases such as scleroderma, systemic lupus erythematosus etc . Raynaud's phenomenon is characterized by triphasic color response of the fingers or toes : • Digital blanching or pallor • Cyanosis • Rubor1180 Primary Raynaud's phenome non (Raynaud's disease ) Secondary Raynaud's pheno menon Idiopathic and more commo n Secondary to other condition s (autoimmune diseases , vibr ation injury) Women are more commonly affected No gender predisposition Age of presentation is betwee n 20 to 40 years Present later in life Episodic - Affects both hands and feet Affects either both hands or both feet

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an incorrect statement about Buerger's disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are false . In thromboangitis obliterans, there is normal brachial and popliteal pulses but reduced or absent radial, ulnar, and/or tibial pulses . It is most common in male smokers, usually under the age of 30 years. Thromboangiitis obliterans (Buerger's disease ) is an inflammatory occlusive vascular disorder involving small and medium-sized arteries and veins in the distal upper and lower extremities . The clinical features include a triad of: • Claudication of the affected extremity • Raynaud's phenomenon • Migratory superficial vein thrombophlebitis Patients frequently have rest pain, ulceration, and digital gangrene .1181

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old male construction worker presents with exertional pain and darkening of the skin in both forearms and hands as shown in the image. He smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day and has no comorbidities On examination, brachial pulses are palpable but radial and ulnar pulses are feeble . Angiography of his upper extremity shows smooth tapering segmental lesions in the distal arterial vessels . Which of the following treatments has the greatest chance of success ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario points to a diagnosis of thromboangiitis obliterans. There is no specific treatment except abstinence from tobacco. Key findings in this patient is age < 40 years, smoker, and involvement of upper extremity . Although the cause of thromboangiitis obliterans is not known, there is a definite relationship to cigarette smoking in patients with this disorder. There is no specific treatment except abstention from tobacco. MRA, CTA, and conventional arteriography show smooth, tapering segmental lesions in the distal vessels with collateral vessels at sites of vascular occlusion . The prognosis is poor in individuals who continue to smoke. Surgical revascularization is not possible due to extensive vascular inflammation and damage . Anticoagulants and glucocorticoids are not helpful . If the condition worsens, amputation may be required.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old chronic smoker presented with cramping pain in the buttocks and erectile dysfunction for the past 6 months. He has no history of bladder dysfunction or fecal incontinence. Examination revealed absent femoral pulses and normal sensory and motor system . How will you surgically manage this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario is suggestive of Leriche syndrome. The treatment of choice here is aortobifemoral grafting. Leriche syndrome is due to occlusion at the aortic bifurcation and is characterized by • Buttock claudication • Impotence • Absence of femoral pulse . • No sensory or motor deficit • Normal reflexes Atherosclerosis is the most common cause of Leriche syndrome. Differential diagnosis includes • Abdominal dissection • Spinal canal stenosis • Spinal disc herniation Aortofemoral grafting is done in unilateral iliac vessel occlusion . Iliofemoral grafting is done for unilateral occlusion of distal common iliac or external iliac artery. Illiopopliteal grafting is done for femoral artery occlusion .1182 Intermittent claudication Neurogenic claudication osteoarthritis Pain after walking a certain d istance Pain after walking or standin g for some time Maximum pain on the first st ep . Pain quickly relieved on resti ng. Pain relieved on flexion Pain relieved on resting.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an indication for a carotid endarterectomy ?
mcqs.explanation: Dysphonia is not an indication for carotid endarterectomy . Carotid endarterectomy is done in carotid artery stenosis . Indications of carotid endarterectomy in symptomatic patients . CT angiography showing 70% or more stenosis and • Ipsilateral amaurosis fugax or monocular blindness • Contralateral facial paralysis or paresthesia • Arm /leg paralysis or paresthesia • Hemianopia • Dysphasia1183

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the most common location of aortic aneurysm?
mcqs.explanation: The most common location of aortic aneurysms is the infrarenal aorta.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient is found to have an abdominal aortic aneurysm when an ultrasound abdomen was done to look for gallstones . He is otherwise healthy . What is the diameter of the aneurysm above which elective repair is indicated ?
mcqs.explanation: Asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm �o 5.5 cm should undergo operative repair. Indications for operative repair in abdominal aortic aneurysm: • Symptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm of any size or one that is expanding rapidly • Asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm >5.5 cm Indications for operative repair in aortic aneurysm:Clinical scenario Indication for operative repai r Symptomatic aneurysm Any size Asymptomaticabdominal aor ticaneursym �o 5.5cm1191 Clinical scenario Indication for operative repai r Asymptomaticascending thor acicaortic diameter > 5.5 cm When the diameter of an asc ending aortic aneurysm has i ncreased > 0.5 cm per year Asymptomaticdescendingtho racicaortic diameter or > 6 cm When the diameter ofdescen dingaorticaneurysm has incre ased > 1 cm per year Asymptomatic ascending tho racic aortic diameter in patie nts with Marfan's syndrome or bicuspid aortic valve 4-5cm

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding abdominal aortic aneurysm is false ?

options.a: Abdominal aneurysms are more suitable for endovascular repair than open repair
options.b: Most abdominal aortic aneurysms rupture into the retroperitoneal space
options.c: Systolic pressure is maintained at <100 mm of Hg in aortic aneurysm rupture
options.d: USG is used to diagnose abdominal aortic aneurysm rupture

mcqs.explanation: CT scan is used to diagnose an abdominal aortic aneurysm rupture and to determine suitability for endovascular repair. If there is a doubt about the presence of an abdominal aortic aneurysm, USG may help in visualizing aneurysm but it cannot be used to diagnose rupture . 80% of abdominal aortic aneurysms rupture into the retroperitoneal space and 20 % rupture into the peritoneal cavity. During the initial resuscitation of a patient with abdominal aortic aneurysm rupture , the systolic pressure is maintained at less than 100mm of Hg (permissive hypotension ) to avoid provoking further uncontrolled hemorrhage. It is maintained at adequate levels to preserve cerebral perfusion till the patient can be taken up for surgery.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Most common site of traumatic aneurysm of aorta?
mcqs.explanation: Most common site of a traumatic aneurysm is descending thoracic aorta just beyond the site of insertion of the ligamentum arteriosum. Traumatic aneurysms may occur after penetrating or nonpenetrating chest trauma.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 41-year-old female patient presented with a tortuous swelling over the left side of the scalp and face as shown in the image given below . On local examination, the swelling was pulsatile . On auscultation , a bruit was heard. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of a tortuous , pulsatile swelling over the scalp and face is suggestive of a cirsoid aneurysm.1192 Cirsoid aneurysm is a slow -growing, tortuous swelling that develops due to abnormal arteriovenous connections among the subcutaneous blood vessels . They are usually congenital . However, in some cases , they may be traumatic. The superficial temporal artery is most commonly involved.Patients present with a tortuous , pulsatile swelling over the scalp or face . They are usually asymptomatic and present to the clinic due to cosmetic deformity . However, some patients may have headache , tinnitus, and/or bleeding. A loud bruit is heard on auscultation . Angiography is the investigation of choice . Treatment includes surgical resection , endovascular occlusion or injection of percutaneous sclerosing agents .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old male patient , during his routine annual checkup , is found to have an abdominal aortic aneurysm measuring 40 mm in diameter on USG. Which of the following is true about the management of this patient ?

options.b: Surgery is indicated if aneurysmal diameter is >55mm
options.c: Urgently wheel the patient to OT for surgery
options.d: Surgery is indicated only if aneurysm is >77mm

mcqs.explanation: Surgery is indicated in an asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) only if its diameter is more than 55 mm in a male patient . If the diameter is less than 55 mm, regular ultrasound monitoring is required. This is because elective open surgery has a higher rate of mortality when compared to conservative management for aneurysms of size < 55 mm. Indications for surgery in abdominal aortic aneurysm: • Size >5.5 cm in males • Size >5 cm in females • Expansion of >1 cm in one year • Painful tender aneurysm • Thrombosed aneurysm; aneurysm with distal emboli1193 Management of aortic aneurysm: AAA is surgically managed by dacron graft repair. It can be either open or EVAR (endovascular aneurysm repair) • Open surgical repair is done by exposing the aorta through a mid-sternal incision and graft replacement. To expose the aorta the descending colon should be mobilized medially and this is known as left visceral rotation or Mattox procedure . • EVAR is a minimally invasive procedure in which an aortic stent graft is placed on the nonaneurysmal aortoiliac segment . Complications following an AAA repair are: • Cardiovascular (ischemia and infarction) • Respiratory (atelectasis or consolidation). • Colonic ischemia. • Renal failure. • Aortoduodenal fistula • spinal cord ischemia The given image below shows the technique of EVAR :

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which is the most common site for peripheral aneurysms?
mcqs.explanation: Femoral and popliteal artery aneurysms account for more than 90% of peripheral aneurysms, with popliteal artery aneurysms being the most common (70%). Two-thirds of popliteal artery aneurysms are bilateral.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man presented to the emergency department with complaints of fever and severe back pain. He is an IV drug abuser. CT scan of the abdomen revealed a saccular, lobulated dilatation of the aorta as shown in the image. What organism is his blood culture most likely to grow?
mcqs.explanation: 1194 The above clinical scenario points to a diagnosis of mycotic aneurysm and it is secondary to microbial aortitis. The most common organism causing mycotic aneurysm is staphylococcus and is mostly due to IV drug abuse . Symptoms may include hypotension , abdominal pain, pulsatile abdominal mass with concomitant fever. Laboratory findings reveal elevated inflammatory parameters such as CRP, ESR, and increased white cell count. A contrast-enhanced CT scan is the initial imaging modality of choice . Patients require prolonged antibiotic therapy tailored to the culture and sensitivity findings. Surgical management includes debridement , revascularization , or bypass techniques . The term 'mycotic aneurysm' is a misnomer as the aneurysm commonly occurs secondary to bacterial infection , and is rarely caused by a fungal infection . Any major artery may be infected , however, the aorta is most commonly affected . The organisms infect the aorta and destroy the wall of the aorta, which may lead to an aneurysm.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
