mcqs.question: A patient presents with complaints of swelling behind the knee for the last 3 years. On evaluation, he is diagnosed to have a popliteal artery aneurysm. Beyond what diameter is repair indicated ?
mcqs.explanation: Popliteal artery aneurysm repair is indicated when the diameter exceeds 2–3 cm, owing to the risk of thrombosis, embolism, or rupture and when they are symptomatic .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an indication for operative repair of thoracic aortic aneurysm?

options.a: Asymptomatic ascending thoracic aortic diameter of 3 cm with bicuspid aortic valve
options.b: Asymptomatic ascending thoracic aortic diameter > 5 cm
options.c: Asymptomatic descending thoracic aortic diameter > 5 cm
options.d: When diameter of an ascending aortic aneurysm has increased more than 0.5 cm per year

mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , the patient in whom the diameter of ascending aortic aneurysm has increased more than 0.5 cm per year, is considered for operative repair. Option A: Asymptomatic ascending thoracic aortic diameter of 4-5 cm with Marfan's syndrome or bicuspid aortic valve is an indication. Option B: Asymptomatic ascending thoracic aortic diameter > 5.5 cm, not 5 cm. Option C: Asymptomatic descending thoracic aortic diameter > 6cm, not 5cm. The indications for operative repair of the thoracic aortic aneurysm are given in the table below .Clinical scenario Indication for operative repai r Symptomatic aneurysm Any size Asymptomaticabdominal aor ticaneursym �o 5.5cm Asymptomaticascending thor acicaortic diameter > 5.5 cm When the diameter of an asc ending aortic aneurysm hasin creased > 0.5 cm per year Asymptomaticdescendingtho racicaortic diameter or > 6 cm1195 Clinical scenario Indication for operative repai r When the diameter ofdescen dingaorticaneurysm has incre ased > 1 cm per year Asymptomatic ascending tho racic aortic diameter in patie nts withMarfan's syndromeor bicuspid aortic valve 4-5cm

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An elderly man presented with a new-onset pulsatile swelling over his wrist as shown in the image. He was recently discharged after a one-month-long ICU admission for urosepsis . On examination, systolic bruit was audible and a doppler revealed bidirectional flow of blood. Which of the following is false regarding the given condition?

options.a: Due to focal dilation in a vessel in which only the intimal layer is disrupted
options.b: Treatment includes endovascular stent insertion and thrombin therapy
options.d: Yin-yang sign is seen on doppler ultrasound of the swelling

mcqs.explanation: The patient most likely has a pseudoaneurysm of the radial artery due to repeated arterial blood gas sampling done in the ICU. Dilatation of vessel due to tear involving only the intima is a dissection , not a pseudoaneurysm . In pseudoaneurysm , the intimal and medial layers are disrupted and the dilated segment of the aorta is lined by adventitia only and at times by perivascular clot. Pseudoaneurysm is most commonly seen due to repeated arterial puncture for blood sampling or catheterization procedures where there is an increased chance of arterial wall injury. It is usually pulsatile and systolic bruit can be heard on auscultation . Doppler ultrasound reveals bidirectional, 'to-and-fro' flow of blood which is known as the yin-yang sign. Treatment options include endovascular stent insertion, ultrasound-guided thrombin injection, and surgical repair. Note : A true aneurysm involves all three layers of the vessel wall.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man presents with acute pain in the chest which radiates to the interscapular region of the back. He is a known hypertensive for the past 7 years. His CT is shown below . Which of the following statements regarding the condition is false ?

options.a: Men are affected more than women
options.b: In Stanford type B ascending aorta is affected
options.c: Pleural effusion associated with aortic dissection is usually left sided
options.d: Sensitivity of transthoracic echocardiography in diagnosing proximal ascending aortic dissections is higher

mcqs.explanation: 1196 The given clinical scenario and the CT image showing the double -lumen of the aorta are suggestive of aortic dissection . Stanford type A is when ascending aorta and arch are affected while Stanford Type B involves descending aorta only, commencing after the origin of the left subclavian artery. Aortic dissection occurs when a defect or flap occurs in the intima of the aorta. Predisposing factors include increasing age , hypertension , Marfan syndrome. The most typical presentation of aortic dissection is a tearing interscapular pain. Aortic dissection affects men more than women by a ratio of 2:1. Pleural effusion associated with aortic dissection is usually left -sided . Transthoracic echocardiography has an overall sensitivity of 60–85% for aortic dissection . For diagnosing proximal ascending aortic dissections , its sensitivity exceeds 80%. It is less useful for detecting dissection of the arch and descending thoracic aorta.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 57 -year-old male patient presented with a sudden tearing type of chest pain. He has had hypertension for the past 15 years and has not been on regular treatment . The patient was hemodynamically stable . A CECT chest was done and is given below . What is the preferred treatment option for this patient ?

options.b: Medical management with blood pressure control
options.d: Further diagnostic workup with transesophageal echocardiography

mcqs.explanation: The patient seems to be having an aortic dissection and CT chest indicates a Stanford Type A aortic dissection from the aortic root. He requires urgent surgical management.1197 The Stanford classification is used to separate aortic dissections into those that need surgical repair, and those that usually require only medical management. The Stanford classification divides dissections by the most proximal involvement. Type A is when ascending aorta and arch are affected . It requires urgent surgical management and may result in: • Coronary artery occlusion • Aortic incompetence • Rupture into the pericardial sac with resulting cardiac tamponade Type B begins beyond brachiocephalic vessels and dissection commences distal to the left subclavian artery affecting only the descending aorta. Medical management with blood pressure control is the preferred choice of treatment . The DeBakey classification divides dissections into: • Type I: involves ascending and descending aorta (= Stanford A) • Type II : involves ascending aorta only (= Stanford A) • Type III : involves descending aorta only, commencing after the origin of the left subclavian artery (= Stanford B) Further diagnostic workup with TEE(transesophageal echocardiography ) or MRA (magnetic resonance angiography) is not required as CT is showing ascending aorta dissection clearly.1198

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In which of the following conditions is a double -barrelled aorta seen ?
mcqs.explanation: A double -barrelled aorta is seen in an aortic dissection . An aortic dissection usually initiates with an intimal tear. In some instances, the dissecting hematoma reenters the lumen of the aorta through a second distal intimal tear, creating a new vascular channel and forming a double -barreled aorta with a false channel. Acute aortic dissection can be classified by the original DeBakey system , based on location of proximal tear and distal extent of the dissection flap, or the Stanford system that uses location of proximal tear alone. DeBakey system : • Type I: involves the ascending aorta and extends through the aortic arch and into the descending aorta/abdominal aorta • Type II : confined to the ascending aorta • Type IIIa : limited to the descending aorta • Type IIIb : descending aorta and abdominal aorta1199

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An AV fistula in the forearm is created in a patient with end-stage renal disease so that he can undergo dialysis. Which of the following responses will you not see when you apply pressure proximal to the AV fistula ?
mcqs.explanation: Pulse pressure returns to normal when pressure is applied to an artery proximal to an AV fistula . In an AV fistula , peripheral resistance is decreased because of which diastolic pressure is less leading to higher pulse pressure . Compression of the artery proximal to the AV fistula increases peripheral resistance leading to increased diastolic pressure and the pulse pressure returns to normal . Compression of the artery proximal to an arteriovenous fistula results in: • Reflex bradycardia • Pulse pressure returns to normal • Decrease in size of swelling • Bruit will decrease or disappear The reflex bradycardia and increase in blood pressure that immediately follows the sudden occlusion of an arteriovenous (A-V ) fistula is known as the Nicoladoni-Branham sign.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the investigation of choice for evaluation of peripheral AV malformation?
mcqs.explanation: MRI has become the imaging study of choice for the evaluation and follow -up of peripheral arteriovenous malformations. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers numerous advantages over both CT and radiographs and has become the most important modality to diagnose AVM's. MRI techniques including time-of-flight and phase contrast can be used to isolate inflow blood supply to better predict the risk of ischemia following embolization.1200 MRI also provides well -defined images defining boundaries between the AVM, surrounding fat, and neurovascular bundles , which is necessary for the planning of surgical or embolic interventions.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease (CAD) presents with complaints of recurrent postprandial abdominal pain associated with vomiting and diarrhea. Abdominal examination shows no tenderness or rigidity. What could be the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Postprandial abdominal pain in the background of CAD is suggestive of chronic mesenteric ischemia(CMI). The most common cause of chronic mesenteric ischemia is atherosclerotic disease . The three classic symptoms pathognomonic of CMI are: • Postprandial pain (crampy periumbilical abdominal pain within 30 minutes of meals) • Food fear (foods that precipitate symptoms are avoided by the patient and unintentional weight loss can result ) • Significant weight loss CT angiogram demonstrates both the arterial lesion and the patterns of collateral blood flow . Percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA ) and stenting have gained acceptance as the first line of therapy for mesenteric ischemia. Nutcracker syndrome refers to compression of the left renal vein, most commonly between the aorta and the superior mesenteric artery, with impaired blood outflow often accompanied by distention of the distal portion of the vein. Most commonly presents with hematuria, flank pain, and varicoceles. CT image of nutcracker syndrome showing compression of the LRV between the aorta and the SMA:

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: All of the following are true about superior mesenteric artery syndrome except ?

options.a: Third part of duodenum is compressed
options.b: Angle between SMA and aorta is more than 70 degrees

mcqs.explanation: 1201 Option B is the false statement . In superior mesenteric artery (SMA) syndrome, the aortomesenteric angle is reduced to less than 25 degrees . The normal aortomesenteric angle is approximately between 38-65 degrees . SMA syndrome, also called Wilkie's syndrome (option D), is characterized by an obstruction of the third part of the duodenum by the SMA (option A) due to compression against fixed retroperitoneal structures . Symptoms include episodic epigastric pain associated with vomiting. Risk factors include rapid childhood growth without compensatory weight gain, profound weight loss, abdominal surgery, inflammatory diseases of the abdomen, and immobilization in a cast that increases lordosis and accentuates the angle of the SMA with the aorta. Abdominal CT angiography is the investigation of choice . The CT image below shows narrowed aortomesenteric angle in SMA syndrome:Lifestyle therapy includes frequent small feedings and patients may benefit from lying prone or on their left side postprandially . In some cases , weight gain or removal of a body cast improves symptoms . Laparoscopic lysis of the ligament of Treitz is beneficial in few cases . The preferred surgical treatment is Strong's procedure involving duodenojejunostomy (option C).1202

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not part of Virchow's triad?
mcqs.explanation: Thrombus formation is not included in Virchow's triad. Virchow's triad refers to three primary influences that predispose to thrombus formation: • Endothelial injury • Stasis or low turbulence of blood flow1213 • Blood hypercoagulability

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following patients are not at an increased risk for developing deep vein thrombosis?

options.a: Woman on high dose oestrogen therapy for menopausal symptoms
options.c: Middle aged man with polycythemia vera
options.d: Teenager who has sustained major trauma in an accident

mcqs.explanation: Nephritic syndrome is not associated with an increased risk of DVT . Nephrotic syndrome is associated with an increased risk of developing deep vein thrombosis. Deep vein thrombosis is the presence or formation of a thrombus is present in the deep venous system , usually in the deep veins lower limbs.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding deep vein thrombosis (DVT )?

options.c: Most common clinical presentation is pain and tenderness in calf
options.d: Some cases may directly present as pulmonary thromboembolism

mcqs.explanation: Most cases of deep vein thrombosis (DVT ) are unilateral. It is bilateral in only 30% of the individuals. DVT refers to thrombosis of the deep venous system . Caused by: • Postoperative thrombosis (most common cause ) • Oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) • After childbirth • Immobility Sites : • Pelvic veins—common • Leg veins—common in femoral and popliteal veins (common on the left side ). Fever is the earliest symptom , which is also most commonly accompanied by pain and tenderness in the calf and thigh (option C). The following signs could be elicited : • Positive Homan's sign: Resistance of calf muscles on passive foreceful dorsiflexion of the foot. • Mose 's sign: Gentle squeezing of the lower part of the calf from side to side is painful. • Neuhof 's sign: Thickening and deep tenderness seen on deep palpation of the calf muscles . Sometimes , the thrombus may get dislodged and present as pulmonary thromboembolism (option D) with features of dyspnoea , tachypnoea , and chest pain. Clinical features are unreliable for making a definitive diagnosis (option A), and a venous Doppler is the best modality for confirming DVT . It reveals a non-compressible dilated vein. The likelihood of pulmonary embolism can be predicted using modified Wells criteria. Patients with DVT should be immediately started with subcutaneous low molecular weight heparin (LMWH ). If contraindicated due to renal insufficiency or thrombocytopenia -related conditions, they should be started on fondaparinux (indirect factor Xa inhibitor) or bivalirudin (direct thrombin inhibitor). Anticoagulants should be administered for a minimum period of 31214 months. Vena cava filters are used in patients with bleeding risks (like hemophilia ).

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: When performing the test on a patient as shown in the image, you noticed that there was tenderness and resistance on flexion. What is this finding known as?
mcqs.explanation: The given findings can be seen in a patient with DVT and this is known as Homan's sign i.e. calf tenderness and resistance on forced ankle dorsiflexion. Moses Sign - calf tenderness on squeezing the calf from sides . Lowenberg's sign- pain when blood pressure cuff placed on the calf is inflated to 80 mm of Hg

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman who is in the third trimester of pregnancy started to experience pain in her left leg . She also noticed that her left leg was turning pale and edematous as given in the image below . What is the cause of this condition?

options.a: Femoral vein thrombosis and lymphatic obstruction
options.d: Due to pressure exerted by uterus on the iliac veins

mcqs.explanation: The patient is having phlegmasia alba dolens also known milk leg or white leg . It is due to ileofemoral deep vein thrombosis. It is usually seen in pregnant women and in individuals at risk of developing deep vein thrombosis. They typically present with painful, oedematous , and pale lower limb that blanches to touch . The lack of cyanosis differentiates this entity from phlegmasia cerulea dolens . In phlegmasia alba dolens , the thrombosis involves only major deep venous channels of the extremity, thus sparing collateral veins. The venous drainage is decreased but still present .In phlegmasia cerulea dolens , the thrombosis extends to collateral veins, resulting in severe venous congestion with massive fluid sequestration and more significant edema . Both phlegmasia cerulea dolens and phlegmasia alba dolens results from acute massive deep vein thrombosis and can be complicated by venous gangrene . Edema of pregnancy does not present with pain in the lower limbs but edema due to pressure exerted by the gravid uterus on the iliac veins.1215

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: You are tasked with giving post -operative care to a patient who just underwent open abdominal surgery. Which of the following is the most effective treatment to prevent the patient from developing deep vein thrombosis?
mcqs.explanation: Heparin, especially low molecular weight heparin (LMWH ) is more effective for prophylaxis of DVT in patients who have undergone major surgeries where early ambulation is not possible . The choice of prophylaxis depends on the type of surgery, trauma, and duration of postoperative immobilisation. Major trauma, abdominal and orthopaedic surgeries warrant a longer duration of postoperative immobilisation. So, the pharmacological method is preferred in these situations . Mechanical methods are advised in patients who are expected to be up and walking within 24 to 48 hours such as after minor trauma. The simplest method is for the patient to ambulate . The activation of the calf pump mechanism is an effective means of prophylaxis . Additionally , compression stockings are advised. It can reduce the risk of DVT by exerting graduated pressure on the leg , with the pressure being greatest at the ankle. Advantages of LMWH over unfractionated heparin: • LMWH has a longer plasma half-life and significantly higher bioavailability. • The consistent bioavailability and clearance of LMWH do not require monitoring of aPTT or anti-factor Xa activity. • Dosing is merely based on the patient 's weight . • There is a more predictable anticoagulant response than with unfractionated heparin. LMWH inhibits factor Xa and not IIa activity, with the ratio of anti-factor Xa to anti-factor IIa activity ranging from 1:1 to 4:1.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: All of the following are risk factors for developing varicose veins, except ?
mcqs.explanation: Superficial venous thrombosis is not a risk factor for developing varicose veins because the deep venous system is not affected and there is no increased stasis of blood. Varicose veins are defined as dilated , usually tortuous , subcutaneous veins >3 mm in diameter measured in the upright position with demonstrable reflux. Important risk factors for varicose veins are: • Sex – Females > Males • Age – increases with age • Pregnancy (especially multiparity ) • Family history • Body mass and height : Increasing BMI (obesity) and height are associated with a high prevalence of varicose veins. There is inconclusive evidence regarding the increased prevalence of varicose veins in smokers, patients who suffer constipation , and occupations that involve prolonged standing .1216 Primary varicose veins are due to genetic or developmental defects in the vein wall that causes diminished elasticity and valvular incompetence . Secondary varicose veins arise from destruction or dysfunction of valves caused by trauma, DVT , AV fistula , non-traumatic proximal venous obstruction (pregnancy, pelvic tumor).

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A truck driver presents with dilated , tortuous veins of 4 mm in the foot. What is the stage of clinical classification according to CEAP(Clinical-etiology -anatomy-pathophysiology for chronic venous disorders)?
mcqs.explanation: Dilated tortuous veins of 4 mm indicate varicose veins, so the stage is C2.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 42-year-old daily wage laborer comes to you with discoloration of her legs . She was diagnosed with varicose veins 5 years ago which was left untreated . Identify the feature given in the picture .
mcqs.explanation: Atrophia blanche is localised white atrophic skin frequently surrounded by dilated capillaries and hyperpigmentation, usually seen around the ankles. This is a sign of chronic venous disease . Lipodermatosclerosis is changes in the skin of the lower legs due to chronic venous insufficiency . It is a form of panniculitis (inflammation of the layer of fat under the skin). There is swelling and a tapering of the legs above the ankles, leading to 'inverted champagne bottle ' appearance .Corona phlebectatica are fan-shaped patterns of small intradermal veins on the medial or lateral aspects of the ankle or foot. It is also called ankle flare or malleolar flare. It is an early sign of advanced venous disease .1217

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A bus conductor was diagnosed with varicose veins. On examination, skin eczema and lipodermatosclerosis were noted . According to the CEAP classification system , He would be classified as
mcqs.explanation: According to CEAP classification , varicose veins with skin eczema and lipodermatosclerosis come under the clinical class of C4. The clinical class of C4 under CEAP includes changes in skin and subcutaneous tissue secondary to chronic venous disease . It is further classified as, • C4a- pigmentation or eczema • C4b- lipodermatosclerosis or atrophie blanche • C4c- corona phlebectatica Recent 2020 update on the CEAP system : • C2r for recurrent varicose veins • C4c for Corona phlebectatica • C6r for recurrent active venous ulcer.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding Klippel -Trenaunay syndrome?

options.c: Surgery is indicated in all cases
options.d: Increased risk of deep vein thrombosis

mcqs.explanation: All patients with Klippel –Trenaunay syndrome should be treated conservatively with elastic compression. A surgical intervention is only indicated for affected large superficial veins provided the underlying deep system is normal and demonstrates only mild-to-moderate reflux. Klippel -Trenaunay syndrome is a sporadic nonhereditary mesodermal abnormality that usually affects a single lower limb with deep veins which have hypoplastic or aplastic segments . It is characterized by a triad of: • Haemangioma presenting as nevus flammeus (port-wine stain)1218 • Varicose veins • Soft tissue and bone hypertrophy Venous stripping , ligation, excision, or sclerotherapy are done in suitable cases . Low molecular weight heparin should be given to all patients undergoing surgical procedures as this syndrome is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient presents to you with dilated , tortuous veins of the legs . Which is the best investigation to perform that will confirm the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Duplex ultrasound is the best investigation to confirm varicose veins. Duplex ultrasound gives information about the presence of blood flow in the studied vessels such as its speed , direction and turbulence alongwith image of surrounding tissues . The aim of the duplex scan in patients with varicose veins is to establish : • If saphenous junctions are incompetent and the extent of reflux in the saphenous veins and their diameters. • Number, location, and diameter of incompetent perforating veins • Source of all superficial varices • Competence and evidence of previous venous thrombosis in the deep venous system . Doppler study only gives information about the presence of blood flow in the studied vessels such as its speed , direction, and turbulence, not the surrounding tissue . Very rarely if pelvic and iliac veins are involved then CT or MR venography might be opted for, when duplex ultrasound fails to visualise properly .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which vessel is not involved in the formation of mickey mouse sign that is seen while performing a duplex ultrasound?
mcqs.explanation: Mickey mouse sign is seen in transverse B mode image of duplex ultrasound formed by: • Common Femoral Vein (CFV) • Common Femoral Artery (CFA) • Greater Saphenous Vein (GSV) at the Saphenofemoral junction (SFJ). It represents the normal anatomy of the femoral vessels as seen in a duplex ultrasound.1219

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A duplex ultrasound was done on a patient with varicose veins. It revealed incompetence of the perforator connecting the great saphenous vein to the superficial femoral vein. What is this perforator known as?
mcqs.explanation: Dodd's perforator connects the great saphenous vein to the superficial femoral veins. It is also known as 'above knee' perforator and is seen at the inferior \037 of the thigh. Perforating veins connect the superficial venous system to the deep venous system by penetrating the fascial layers of the lower extremity. Although the total number of perforator veins is variable, up to 100 have been documented . Named perforators: • Adductor Canal (thigh) – Hunter's perforator • Above Knee – Dodd's perforator • Below Knee – Boyd's perforator • Medial Calf – Cockett I, II , and III perforator • Ankle - May or Kustner perforator1220

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Presence of which of the following would make a patient with varicose veins unsuitable for sclerotherapy ?

options.d: Recurrence of varicose veins after ligation and stripping surgery

mcqs.explanation: Deep vein thrombosis is a contraindication for sclerotherapy in varicose veins. This is because , in patients with DVT , the superficial veins are the only valved venous pathway carrying blood back to the heart, and excising them in the presence of deep venous thrombosis will only aggravate the condition.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which sclerosant is most commonly used when performing sclerotherapy for varicose veins?
mcqs.explanation: The most commonly used sclerosant is sodium tetradecyl sulfate . In injection sclerotherapy a detergent is injected directly into the superficial veins. The detergent destroys the lipid membranes of endothelial cells causing them to shed , leading to thrombosis, fibrosis and obliteration (sclerosis ). Injection sclerotherapy alone can be successful in varicose veins <3 mm in diameter and in telangiectatic vessels . Complications of sclerotherapy : • Allergic reaction, • Local hyperpigmentation • Thrombophlebitis • DVT • Skin necrosis Patients with symptomatic GSV or SSV reflux may be treated with endovenous ablation techniques or surgical removal of the affected vein.1221 Saphenous vein ligation and stripping is preferred therapy for patients with GSVs of very large diameter (>2 cm). Types of sclerosants : Detergents • Sodium tetradecyl sulfate • Polidocanol • Sodium morrhuate • Ethanolamine oleate Osmotic agents • Hypertonic saline Chemical irritants • Chromated glycerin • Polyiodinated iodine • Alcoholic solution of zein • Bleomycin Tessari method • Widely used method to prepare foam for sclerotherapy • Sclerosant : Air ratio taken is 1:3 or 1:4.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is done in Trendelenburg operation?

options.a: Stripping of the superficial varicose vein
options.d: Ligation of small tributaries at the distal end of superficial varicose vein

mcqs.explanation: Saphenofemoral flush ligation is done in Trendelenburg 's procedure . The great saphenous vein is stripped and tied close to the common femoral vein at the saphenofemoral junction so that there aren't any branches left that lead to recurrences. Procedure : An oblique groin incision is made at the level of and lateral to the pubic tubercle . The great saphenous vein is identified and dissected to the saphenofemoral junction. Six great saphenous vein tributaries are normally encountered close to the saphenofemoral junction: • The superficial inferior epigastric vein and superficial circumflex iliac vein laterally • The deep and superficial external pudendal veins medially • More distally the anterolateral and posteromedial thigh veins A flush saphenofemoral junction ligation is then performed and the great saphenous vein retrogradely stripped to the knee. Flush ligation is when the great saphenous vein is stripped and tied close to the common femoral vein at the saphenofemoral junction so that there aren't any tributaries that lead to recurrences .1222

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding complications of varicose vein surgery is false ?

options.a: Injury to the lymphatic system can cause secondary lymphoedema
options.b: Saphenous nerve injury causes loss of sensation in the medial aspect of the leg
options.c: The sural nerve is in danger during stripping of the great saphenous vein

mcqs.explanation: The sural nerve accompanies the short saphenous vein laterally along its course and supplies cutaneous sensation to the lateral malleolar region. Thus it is more prone to injury during stripping of the short saphenous vein, not the great saphenous vein. The saphenous nerve accompanies the great saphenous vein medially from the ankle to the level of the knee and supplies cutaneous sensation to the medial leg and ankle. Thus it is more prone to injury during stripping of the great saphenous vein. Surgery for the varicose veins extraction may trigger injury of the lymph vessels and may lead to secondary lymphedema . Injury and inflammation to the venous system during varicose vein surgery can cause slowing and stasis of blood flow in the lower limb, making them prone to develop deep vein thrombosis postoperatively .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In patients with chronic venous insufficiency , where are venous ulcers most likely to develop ?
mcqs.explanation: Venous ulcers due to chronic venous insufficiency are most commonly seen in the lower \037 of the leg and foot. They usually lie just proximal to the medial or lateral malleolus . Venous ulcers are accompanied by lipodermatosclerosis and hemosiderosis .Feature Venous ulcer Arterial ulcer Predisposing factors Varicose veinsPrevious DVT Recurrent superficial thromb ophlebitis Peripheral arterial diseaseDia betesSmokingHypertension Location Lower 1/3 of leg 'gaiters area' Lateral malleolus and tibial a spect of legToes and feet Ulcer characteristics Shallowandflat marginsExud ate with slough and granulati on tissue at base of wound Punched out,deep ,and irregul ar in shapeNecrotic and unhe althy tissue at base of wound Appearance of the lower lim b LipodermatosclerosisAtrophi e blancheLimb oedemaNorm alcapillary refill time Pale, shiny skinAbsent or we ak peripheral pulsesDelayedc apillary refill time1223

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 61-year-old man presented with a recurrent, tender , erythematous rash on the medial aspect of the right forearm and lower limb as shown in the image. He was diagnosed with pancreatic adenocarcinoma 1 year ago. Blood investigations showed normal eosinophil counts and no signs of infections . What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.c: Secondary to repeated cannulation of vein

mcqs.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is migratory thrombophlebitis . It is a paraneoplastic syndrome that is also known as Trousseau's syndrome or Trousseau's sign of malignancy. It is characterised by recurrent episodes of localised thrombosis of the superficial veins of limbs. It can lead to tender and erythematous rashes. Migratory thrombophlebitis is seen in: • Pancreatic cancer (most common) • Lung cancer • Gastrointestinal cancer • Ovarian cancer • Prostate cancer • Lymphoma Note : Trousseau's sign is seen in hypocalcemia where there is an involuntary contraction of the muscles of the hand and wrist when a blood pressure cuff is placed on the arm and inflated to 20mm of Hg above systolic blood pressure .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old male patient with sudden onset pain, cyanosis, and edema of the left upper limb. Doppler ultrasound revealed thrombosis of the left subclavian vein. Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.a: Can be caused by indwelling venous catheters
options.c: Primary axillary vein thrombosis is seen in hypercoagulable states
options.d: May occur following excessive arm exercise

mcqs.explanation: The patient has axillary-subclavian vein thrombosis. Hypercoagulable states lead to secondary axillary vein thrombosis. Axillary-subclavian vein thrombosis (ASVT ) is of 2 types .1224 Primary ASVT occurs as a result of compression of the subclavian vein in the costoclavicular space by repeated contraction of muscles that surround the thoracic outlet . There is repeated compression and traumatization to the vein. This leads to the formation of clots . It is also known as: • Paget -Schrotter Syndrome • Venous thoracic outlet syndrome • Effort thrombosis Secondary ASVT occurs due to venous injury by indwelling central venous catheters , external trauma or pacemaker wires. It is also seen in hypercoagulable states . Symptoms and signs include pain, edema , and cyanosis of the upper extremity . Significant superficial venous distension can be seen in arm , forearm, shoulder and anterior chest wall. Doppler study is the investigation of choice . Anticoagulation is initiated once ASVT is diagnosed to prevent pulmonary embolism.In severe cases , thrombolytic therapy is done using tissue plasminogen activator (rtPA) or streptokinase . Adjuvant procedures following thrombolytic therapy may include balloon angioplasty for residual venous narrowing and cervical or first rib resection for thoracic outlet abnormalities.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Identify the device given below .
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a chemoport . Chemoports are implantable venous access devices used to facilitate chemotherapy administration. Internal jugular veins and subclavian veins are the commonly used access veins for port placement . These devices are usually retained for a period of 1 to 2 years or more after which the device is explanted .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following vessel is affected in May-Thurner syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: May-Thurner syndrome refers to iliofemoral venous thrombosis. At the site where the right iliac artery crosses over the left iliac vein, the left iliac vein may become chronically narrowed predisposing to iliofemoral venous thrombosis.1225

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old woman with a history of varicose vein, presented with a painless lesion on her left leg for the past 1 month. On examination, an ulcer of size 5 \036 5 cm with an irregular margin and sloping edge was found on the medial malleolus of the left leg . All the following can be used to manage this patient except ?[Image unavailable]

options.b: Surgical excision and pinch mesh grafting

mcqs.explanation: The likely diagnosis, in this case, is a venous ulcer secondary to the varicose vein. Revascularization is not a part of the management of venous ulcers . Venous ulcers are due to chronic venous insufficiency and are particularly seen in the area between the muscles of the calf and ankle. It has a sloping edge and the floor contains granulation tissue covered by slough and exudate . Marjolin's ulcer is a type of squamous cell carcinoma seen in chronic long-standing venous ulcers. Management of venous ulcers : • Bisgaard's regimen • Education • Elevation of the affected limb to reduce the edema • Elastic compression stockings - The ideal interface pressure in venous ulceration is 35-40 mmHg. • Evaluation • 4 layer bandaging system comprising of: • Orthopedic wool • Cotton crepe • Elastic bandage - first compressive layer • Cohesive bandage - second compressive layer • Antibiotics are given only if the wound is infected . • Regular dressing .1226 • Medical management by oral pentoxifylline is considered which helps in reducing the viscosity and improving circulation. • Surgery - Ulcer excision with pinch mesh grafting has a good outcome and helps in preventing recurrence .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old hairdresser presented with complaints of swelling , throbbing pain, and heaviness in her left leg for the past 1 year. A duplex scan done showed great saphenous vein incompetence . Which of the following is the treatment of choice ?
mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario is suggestive of varicose veins and the treatment of choice in this patient is endothermal ablation. Management of varicose veins 1. Great saphenous vein (GSV) and saphenofemoral incompetence (SFJ) • Endothermal ablation - It is the gold standard method . It includes : • Endovenous laser ablation (EVLA ) • Radiofrequency ablation (RFA. • Trendelenburg procedure \261 stripping - Flush ligation of SFJ and ligation of 6 tributaries. 2. Short saphenous vein (SSJ) and saphenopopliteal incompetence (SPJ ). • Flush ligation of SPJ . No stripping is done to prevent nerve injury • EVLA or RFA. 3. Perforator incompetence • Dodd and Crockett surgery - Multiple subfacial ligations. • Subfascial endoscopic perforator surgery (SEPS) • EVLA or RFA New treatment modalities • Foam sclerotherapy • Endovenous glue therapy • TriVex - Transilluminated powered phlebectomy

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old locomotive operator presents with complaints of worm-like swelling over his right leg . During clinical examination, a Brodie Trendelenburg test is performed . Which of the following statements is false regarding the test ?

options.a: A tourniquet can be used for occluding the saphenofemoral junction
options.b: Rapid filling from above indicates saphenofemoral incompetence
options.c: Gradual filling from below upwards indicates saphenopopliteal incompetence
options.d: Positive Brodie Trendelenburg test indicates a need for surgery

mcqs.explanation: The gradual filling of veins from below upwards indicates the perforator incompetence . Brodie Trendelenberg test is performed to test for the incompetence of the saphenofemoral valve and the communicating system . 1. Trendelenburg 's test - Lay the patient down and elevate the leg . Empty the vessels and tie a tourniquet below the SFJ. Ask the patient to stand up: • Trendelenburg 's test part ll - Here the tourniquet is not released . A gradual filling from below to upwards indicates perforator incompetence .1227 • Trendelenburg 's test part l - Here the tourniquet is released . A rapid filling from above shows the saphenofemoral incompetence . 2. Morrisey's cough impulse : the patient is asked to cough . A cough impulse at the saphenofemoral junction indicates SFJ incompetence . 3. Schwartz test : If a thrill is felt at SFJ on tapping over the incompetent vein, indicates SFJ incompetence. 4. Modified Perthes test : A tourniquet is tied below SFJ and the patient is asked to walk. An increase in pain and prominence of dilated veins indicate DVT . 5. Fegan's method - Mark the places of excessive bulges within the varicosities. Ask the patient to lie down and empty the varicose vessels . Palpate along the marked area to look for gaps and pits in the deep fascia, which indicates perforator incompetence .1228

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient comes with long-standing non-pitting edema in the legs . What is the most probable cause ?
mcqs.explanation: Lymphedema is the most probable cause of long-standing non-pitting edema in the limbs. Lymphedema is the abnormal accumulation of protein-rich fluid in the interstitial spaces of the tissues . Lymphedema can be primary or secondary. Primary lymphedema includes : • Lymphedema congenita (0-2 years): more common in males, involves multiple limbs, face, and genitalia. It can be familial or sporadic. The familial type is called Nonne Milroy syndrome. • Lymphedema praecox (2-35 years): more common in females , the most common type of primary lymphedema with a peak incidence in puberty . It can be familial or sporadic. The familial type is called Meig 's disease . • Lymphedema tarda (>35 years): Rare and uncommon. Secondary lymphedema is more common than primary and is the most common cause of lymphedema overall. Causes include lymph node dissection (axillary or inguinal), post -mastectomy , postoperative radiotherapy, obesity , varicose vein surgery, and trauma. Complications of lymphedema include infections , skin changes , recurent cellulitis , non-healing ulcers, and lymphangiosarcoma. Treatment mostly includes patient education and nonsurgical interventions, which include limb elevation, and external compressive garments. When the above methods fail, surgery can be1234 considered .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient comes to you with complaints of long-standing swelling of the left leg , as shown in the image. The swelling disappears in the morning and on examination, pitting is seen . What grade of lymphedema is this?
mcqs.explanation: In the given clinical scenario, pitting edema which disappears completely on elevation and bed rest indicates grade I lymphedema , according to Brunner 's classification . Skin changes seen in lymphedema include peau d'orange, erythema , hyperkeratosis , ulceration, stemmer sign, and buffalo hump. Stemmer sign is the inability to pinch a fold of skin on the dorsum of the toes due to lymphedema . Clinical classification of lymphedema :Grade (Brunn er) Clinical features Subclinical There is excessive interstitial fluid and histological abnorm alities in lymphatics and lym ph nodes , but no clinically ap parent lymphedema . Grade I Edema pits on pressure and t he swelling completely disap pears on elevation and bed re st. Grade II Edema does not pit and does not significantly reduce on el evation Grade III Edema is associated with irre versible skin changes , i.e. fibr osis and papillae .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: While examining a patient with lymphoedema , you are unable to pinch the skin of the patient on the base of the toes . What is this sign called ?
mcqs.explanation: In lymphedema , skin on the base of the toes cannot be pinched due to subcutaneous fibrosis. This sign is called Stemmer's sign.Sign Description Stemmer's sign Seen in lymphoedemaSkin o n the dorsum of the toes can not be pinched due to Subcut aneous Fibrosis.1235 Sign Description Frank 's sign A diagonal crease in the earlo be that runs backward from t he tragus at a 45-degree angl e across the lobule to the rear edge of the auricle.May be a predictor of coronary artery disease . Levine's sign Clenched fist held over the ch est to describe ischemic chest pain. Winterbottom's si gn Posterior cervical lymphaden opathy in african trypanosom iasis.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An 8-month-old girl child was brought to the hospital with complaints of swelling of both feet as shown in the image. On examination pitting is seen . Her ECG, RFT , and urine analysis were normal . What is the true statement regarding this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The patient most likely has Milroy disease which is the familial version of congenital lymphedema . It is inherited as a dominant trait. Primary lymphedema is classified on the basis of age of onset and the presence of familial clustering . • Congenital lymphoedema - onset before 2 years of age • Lymphedema precox - most common type . onset between 2 to 35 years of age • Lymphedema tarda - rare. onset after 35 years of age Treatment includes conservative management such as massage , compression stockings, or bandaging. Surgical management includes vascularized lymph node transfer (VLNT ). It involves the transfer of functional lymph nodes from a healthy donor site to an area of the body with damaged or diseased lymphatic drainage.Features Congenital lymphoedma Lymphedema precox Onset Before2nd yearof life Between2 -35 yearsof life Extent Extends to multiple limbs, ge nitalia, and/or the face Mostly unilateraland extends only to the knees Eponyms Known asMilroy disease Known asMeige 's disease Sexual predilectio n None More common in females

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following will you perform when asked to do a lymphangiography of the leg ?

options.a: Inject sodium diatrizoate subcutaneously on the dorsum of the foot
options.b: Inject sodium diatrizoate retrogradely under pressure into a small vein on the dorsum of foot
options.c: Dissect the lymphatics through an incision on the dorsum of foot and injecting contrast
options.d: Insertion of guidewire into the lymphatic system of the leg and inject contrast

mcqs.explanation: 1236 Direct contrast lymphangiography is done by dissecting the lymphatic vasculature through an incision on the dorsum of the foot and injecting contrast. Direct contrast lymphangiography is an invasive study done to visualise the lymphatic system . It involves exposure and cannulation of lymphatics and slow injection of contrast medium such as ethiodized oil. Complications : • Damage to the visualized lymphatics • Allergic reactions • Pulmonary embolism if the oil-based contrast agent enters the venous system through lymphovenous anastomosis. Contrast magnetic resonance lymphangiography is a newer testing method . It is performed after intracutaneous injection of gadobenate dimeglumine into the interdigital webs of the dorsal foot. It is capable of visualizing the anatomy and functional status of lymph flow transport of lymphatic vessels and lymph nodes of lymphedematous limbs.Image A shows a lymphangiography with normal uptake . Image B shows a lymphangiography scan with no uptake in Milroy's disease . Image C depicts a lymphangiography scan in a patient with lymphoedema and reflux.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following complications are least likely to develop , in patients with chronic lymphoedema ?
mcqs.explanation: Marjolin's ulcers are unlikely to develop in patients with chronic lymphedema . Marjolin's ulcers are malignant ulcers that develop over chronic scars, most commonly from burns. Marjolin's ulcer may also develop in chronic long standing venous ulcers but are not seen in chronic lymphedema .1237 Initially, the lymphedema is soft and pits on the pressure but with time the skin becomes thickened and non-pitting due to fibrosis, dermal thickening, and hyperkeratosis . Frequent episodes of lymphangitis and cellulitis may occur. This is due to loss of local immune defense mechanisms. Chronic eczema, the fungal infection of skin and nails, fissuring, verrucae, and papillae (warts) are frequently seen in advanced disease . Rarely malignancy (lymphangiosarcoma or angiosarcoma) may occur in chronic lymphedema . This neoplastic transformation of blood vessels and lymphatics is called Stewart -Treves syndrome.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding mediastinal lymphoma is false ?

options.a: Middle mediastinum is the most common site of mediastinal lymphoma
options.c: Chemotherapy is the treatment of choice
options.d: Video assisted thoracoscopy is used to diagnose the condition

mcqs.explanation: Anterior compartment is the most common site of lymphoma in the mediastinum. Other sites include the middle compartment and hilar nodes . Primary mediastinal lymphoma is an uncommon type of lymphoma. Hodgkin's lymphoma (HL), primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma (PMBCL), and T-lymphoblastic lymphoma are the most common primary mediastinal lymphomas. In about 50% of patients who have both Hodgkin's and Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma, the mediastinum may be the primary site . Superior vena cava (SVC) syndrome refers to symptoms produced by the obstruction of blood flow through the SVC by the enlarging mediastinal mass, resulting in symptoms of dyspnea , facial and upper -extremity edema , cough , chest pain, and dysphagia . Video-assisted thoracoscopy (VATS ) is used to obtain a biopsy of the mediastinal mass for confirmation and diagnosis. Chemotherapy with six cycles of R-CHOP regimen is preferred . Rituximab is a chimeric monoclonal anti-CD20 antibody and has become a standard component of treating all B-cell lymphoma histologies that express CD20 . Note : Thymoma is the most common mediastinal tumor in adults (overall).

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 5-month-old boy is brought to the hospital with complaints of swelling in the neck as given in the image. Which of the following is true regarding this condition?

options.b: It is a congenital sequestration of lymphatic channel
options.d: Sclerotherapy is not used in treatment

mcqs.explanation: The given image depicts a lymphangioma, also known as cystic hygroma. They are brilliantly transilluminant. Lymphangiomas are congenital benign tumors of the lymphatic system . They are the isolated cystic mass of lymphatic tissue that has the ability to produce lymph. Over time the tumor enlarges due to the accumulation of lymph within the cyst . Types of lymphangiomas: • Simple or capillary lymphangioma: They occur subcutaneously in the head , neck , and axilla. They may also occur within the internal organs and connective tissues in the thoracic and abdominal cavities. • Cavernous lymphangioma or cystic hygroma: They also occur in the neck or axilla. Rarely they may occur in retroperitoneum .1238 Treatment includes surgical excision of the tumor and image-guided sclerotherapy . If there is any residual lymphatic malformation after the treatment , then a conservative excision or unroofing of the cyst is done. It may be combined with sclerosing therapy or repeated partial excisions. Note : The terms lymphangioma and cystic hygromas are older terms. They are now called lymphatic malformations.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Where is lymphangiosarcoma most commonly seen ?
mcqs.explanation: Lymphangiosarcoma is most commonly seen in post -mastectomy edema of the arm . Lymphangiosarcoma is a rare tumor that develops as a complication of long-standing lymph- edema.Clinically, the patients present with acute worsening of the edema and appearance of subcutaneous nodules that have a propensity toward hemorrhage and ulceration. The tumor can be treated , like other sarcomas, with preoperative chemotherapy and radiation followed by surgical excision, which usually may take the form of radical amputation. Overall, the prognosis is very poor.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient underwent surgery for breast carcinoma . She now presents with painless swelling involving the arm as shown in the image below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette and the image are suggestive of post -mastectomy lymphedema involving the upper limb. Lymphoedema occurs when interstitial fluid accumulates due to defective lymphatic drainage. It is a common complication of breast cancer treatment involving axillary lymph node dissection and radiotherapy. Sentinel lymph node dissection (SLND) reduces the risk of1239 lymphedema significantly . Clinical signs and symptoms are observed in the ipsilateral arm . A significant increase in the limb size due to swelling is seen . Other symptoms are heaviness, tightness , numbness, tingling, limb fatigue , and reduced limb mobility. Diagnosis is predominantly based on the clinical swelling of the arm . The girth of the affected arm >2 centimeters than the normal limb, a 200 -mL or more increase in limb volume, or a 5% or greater limb volume change are other diagnostic criteria. Management : Limb elevation, elastic arm stockings, and pneumatic compression devices can help reduce swelling . Dry skin can be seen due to fluid accumulation, which can lead to cellulitis /skin infections . Using a low pH water-based moisturizer is helpful . Manual lymphatic drainage (MLD) by a therapist followed by simple lymphatic drainage (SLD) by the patient daily aids interstitial fluid evacuation. Benzpyrones and flavonoids are some naturally occurring substances that may be of use to treat lymphedema . Surgical options are lymphaticovenular anastomosis, liposuction , and debulking . Other options : Option B: Stewart -Treves syndrome refers to lymphangiosarcoma seen in chronic long-standing lymphedema following mastectomy (more than 10 years). They present as single /multiple bluish-red skin and subcutaneous nodules . They can ulcerate and hemorrhage. Option C: Axillary venous thrombosis or Paget -Schrotter disease is seen in patients doing rigorous exercise and in weightlifters . The subclavian vein is compressed at the thoracic outlet . Painful swelling of the arm is observed. Option D: Cellulitis usually presents with an ulcer and the skin is erythematous , swollen , and painful. Fever, chills, and rigor follow .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a part of decongestive lymphoedema therapy (DLT )?
mcqs.explanation: Diuretics and Homan's procedure are not a part of DLT , and are a part of drug therapy and surgical management. Decongestive lymphoedema therapy (DLT ) is the currently used method for controlling swelling in lymphoedema . It consists of 2 phases : intensive and maintenance. Intensive phase includes : • Skin care: Prevent drying of skin and exposure to the sun, avoid venipuncture from the affected limb . • Limb elevation • Manual lymphatic drainage (MLD) - Proximal massage along lymphatic channels.1240 • Compression therapy : Multilayer lymphoedema bandaging (MLLB ), Pneumatic lymphoedema stockings, Graded compression stockings (100% in the ankle/foot, 70% in the knee, 50% in mid-thigh , and 40% in the groin). • Exercise : Slow rhythmic isotonic movements are beneficial , while vigorous, anaerobic isometric exercises are to be avoided. Standard MLLB is only done if ABPI is �o 0.8. It is contraindicated if ABPI is < 0.5. Maintenance phase includes : • Simple lymphatic drainage (SLD) - It is a simple massage technique done by the patient . • Pain relief

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which among the following is not a limb reduction surgery for lymphoedema ?
mcqs.explanation: Kinmonth procedure is a bypass surgery done for lymphoedema not a limb reduction surgery. Surgical management of lymphoedema is divided into bypass procedures , liposuction , and limb reduction procedures . • Bypass procedures include : • Neilubowicz procedure - anastomosing lymph nodes to the veins. • Kinmonth procedure - using ileal mucosal patch . • Limb reduction procedures include : • Sistrunk procedure - A wedge of skin and subcutaneous tissue is excised and the wound closed primarily . This is the most commonly carried out procedure to reduce the girth of the thigh. • Homan's procedure - Skin flaps are raised, and then subcutaneous tissue is excised from beneath the flaps . • Thompson's procedure - Modification of Homan's procedure . • Charles procedure - Excision of all of the skin and subcutaneous tissues down to the deep fascia, with coverage using split -skin grafts.1241

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A biopsy done for a chronic verrucous lesion over the right cheek in an elderly man revealed the given histopathological finding. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows keratin pearls which are characteristic of squamous cell carcinoma . Squamous cell carcinoma is characterized by the proliferation of atypical squamous cells with horn pearls/keratin pearls.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: During rounds, you have been asked to examine a patient with an ulcer over the face . Which of the following features will raise the suspicion of it being squamous cell carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: On examination of an ulcer, everted margins will be suggestive of squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). SCC is the second most common skin cancer, while BCC is the most common skin cancer. Variants of SCC in-situ include : • Bowen's disease • Erythroplasia of Queyrat SCC initially presents as smooth nodular, verrucous, papillomatous lesions . These lesions then ulcerate and form a characteristic, everted edge , surrounded by inflamed, indurated skin. Surgical excision is the treatment of choice . Other modalities of treatment include : • Cautery ablation • Cryotherapy • Drug therapy including imiquimod • Moh's microsurgery • Radiation therapy The below image shows SCC with everted margins:1253

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following can increase the risk of developing squamous cell carcinoma ?
mcqs.explanation: HPV 6 & 11 are not risk factors for squamous cell carcinoma , HPV 16 & 18 are risk factors for squamous cell carcinoma . Note : Skin cancer is the most frequent malignant neoplasm in organ transplant recipients , with SCC and BCC representing 95% of cancer.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true regarding squamous cell carcinoma ?

options.a: Skin biopsy is mandatory in all cases
options.b: Mohs micrographic surgery is indicated for recurrent tumors
options.c: Broder's staging is based on the depth of the lesion
options.d: Lesion on the ear is a high-risk feature

mcqs.explanation: Broder's staging for SCC is based on histological grading. Depth or size of the tumor and lymph node involvement are not included in Broder's staging .1254 A skin biopsy is mandatory in all patients with suspected squamous cell carcinoma . Mohs micrographic surgery is indicated in patients with aggressive and high-risk SCC. High-risk features of SCC include : • Perineural invasion • Depth of lesion greater than 2 mm • Lesions on the ear • Poorly differentiated lesions Note : Mohs micrographic surgery is the treatment of choice in BCC.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old farmer presented with a slow -growing lesion over his left hand for the past 5 months. The lesion was initially nodular, which then ulcerated . On examination, a 2 x 1 cm ulcer with everted margins was noted . Biopsy revealed keratin pearls. Which of the following stains will be positive for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: SCC is a malignant tumor of keratinizing cells of the epidermis arising from the stratum germinatum (basalis) and expresses cytokeratins 1 and 10 . CK-20 is specific for Merkel cell carcinoma. BCL2 is used to distinguish between basal cell carcinomas and trichoepitheliomas . HMB-45 is used to detect melanocytes .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 75 -year old man came with complaints of a painless nodule on the left palm for the past 4 weeks . He gave a history of sustaining a thorn prick injury to the palm 5 weeks ago. On examination, the lesion appears as shown below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and image showing an exophytic nodule with central keratinous debris is suggestive of keratoacanthoma. Keratoacanthoma is a low-grade squamous cell carcinoma . It presents clinically as a proliferating dome-shaped keratin-filled crater. Patients usually give a prior history of minor trauma. Treatment of choice is an excisional procedure with 4 mm margins. Option A: Actinic keratoses consist of hyperkeratotic erythematous papules and patches on the sun-exposed skin. They arise in middle -aged to older adults and have some potential for malignant transformation .1255 Option B: Bowen's disease appears histologically as SCC in situ. It initially presents with a red- dened? area that progresses to thickened plaques and may vary from small lesions (<1 cm) to large areas. When it is confined to the glans penis or vulva , Bowen disease is sometimes referred to as Erythroplasia of Queyrat .Option D: Mycosis fungoides is a cutaneous T cell lymphoma, and plaque-stage lesions are seen .1256

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A firefighter presented with a chronic non-healing painless ulcer over his left leg . He gave a history of sustaining 2nd-degree burns injury to the leg 10 years back during a rescue mission. The examination finding is as shown below . All of the following are true about this condition, except ______.
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and image showing an irregular ulcer with cauliflower shaped granulation tissue points to a diagnosis of Marjolin's ulcer. It is avascular.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old man has the following lesion over the face . He complains of bleeding while itching. The most likely diagnosis is
mcqs.explanation: The given history with the image showing an ulcer over the face with pearly , rolled -out borders points to a diagnosis of basal cell carcinoma . Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is an epithelial tumor arising from basal cells . It is the most common type of skin cancer most commonly seen over the face , above the line joining corner of the mouth, and lobule of the ear. Risk factors for BCC include ultraviolet radiation (strongest risk factor), age 40-80 years with excessive sun exposure , light -skinned people , and exposure to arsenic compounds , coal tar, aromatic hydrocarbons, and infrared light . It is more common in males than females . It is also associated with syndromes such as xeroderma pigmentosum and Gorlin's syndrome. Features of BCC include : • Pearly nodule with rolled border • Tortuous telangiectatic vessels • Surface which can get ulcerated with raised and beaded edge , often with a central depression or umbilication • Bleeding on minor trauma BCC has various subtypes such as nodular (most common type ), pigmented , nodulocystic , morphoeic , infiltrative, and fibroepithelioma of Pinkus.1257 It is locally aggressive and can erode the bone or facial sinuses . It rarely metastasizes via lymph nodes . The occasional presence of melanin in the nodular variant of BCC (pigmented BCC) may lead to confusion with melanoma. Depending upon the type of the lesion, a shave, punch or excisional biopsy may be employed for diagnosis. X-ray or CT may be needed if there is a local invasion . Histology shows peripheral palisading of cells . Treatment: • Surgical: Wide excision (4-6 mm clearance) with a skin graft or flap or primary suturing • Mohs' surgery for BCC close to the eyes , nose, or ear to preserve more tissue . • Non-surgical: Radiotherapy, vismodegib and sonedegib . Other options : Option A: Dermatofibrosarcoma, also known as dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) is a rare, slow -growing, well -differentiated primary fibrosarcoma of the skin, associated with increased production of platelet -derived growth factor-beta . It presents as a protuberant nodule within a firm, indurated plaque that can ulcerate . They are locally aggressive tumors with high recurrence rates. Treatment is wide excision and Mohs microscopic surgery. Imatinib is used for unresectable , metastatic , and recurrent tumors. The given image below shows a DFSP near the umbilicus .Option B: Marjolin's ulcer is a painless , slow -growing, locally malignant, well -differentiated squamous cell carcinoma that occurs in a chronic scar (burns scar, scar of venous ulcer). It presents as an indurated , non-tender ulcer with raised and everted edges with scarring in the surrounding area with marked fibrosis. The ulcer can spread to the lymph nodes when it reaches the normal skin. A wedge biopsy and MRI of the region involved confirm the diagnosis. Management is by wide excision, for larger ulcers , amputation is done. The given image below shows a marjolin 's ulcer of the leg .1258 Option D: Naevus is a common benign neoplasm caused due to mutations in the components of the RAS signaling pathway . It has various types , such as congenital naevus, blue naevus, Spitz naevus, halo naevus, and dysplastic naevus. The given image below shows a patient with multiple dysplastic nevi.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true regarding basal cell carcinoma ?

options.a: Nodular is the most common type
options.c: Most commonly seen over the neck
options.d: Only punch biopsy is used for diagnosis

mcqs.explanation: The most common form of BCC (60%) is the nodular variant . Other types of BCC are: • Superficial BCC- typically appears on the trunk as a pink or erythematous plaque with a thin pearly border • Infiltrative BCC1259 • Pigmented variant of nodular BCC • Morpheaform variant - is an uncommon variant and is the most aggressive form • Fibroepithelioma of Pinkus Option B: Patients with BCC show excellent prognosis with 100 % survival rates for cases that have not spread to other sites . Option C: Most of the basal cell carcinoma occurs on the face above the line joining the corner of the mouth and lobule of the ear. Option D: Depending upon the type of lesion, a shave, punch, or exicision biopsy can be used to confirm the diagnosis. The below image shows a nodular BCC

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Lymph node involvement may be seen in patients with all of the following cutaneous malignancies except ?
mcqs.explanation: Basal cell carcinoma does not show lymphatic or hematogenous metastasis . It is locally invasive .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A construction worker presented to the clinic with a slowly enlarging lesion near the left inner canthus for the past 2 years. He noticed bleeding from the lesion for the past 2 months. On examination, a 3 x 1 cm ulcer with pearly rolled -out margins was noted . A biopsy was done. Which of the following is the characteristic finding that will be seen in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The characteristic finding of basal cell carcinoma is of ovoid cells in nests with a single 'palisading' layer. The cells of a BCC resemble those of the basal layer of the epidermis . They are basophilic , have a large nucleus , and appear to form a basal layer by forming an orderly line around the periphery of tumor nests in the dermis, a feature referred to as palisading .1260

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In patients with BCC, Mohs microscopic surgery will be indicated for which of the following features of the tumor?
mcqs.explanation: Moh's microscopic surgery is indicated in patients with the following features of BCC: • Primary lesions of the ear or lip • Recurrent lesions • With perineural invasion • Poorly differentiated lesions • Tumors more than 2 cm in size Moh's microscopic surgery involves initial surgical excision of the tumor, followed by repeated tissue sampling along lateral and deep margins. These tissue samples are examined immediately under a frozen section for evidence of tumor. This process is repeated until the clearance is finally obtained .1261

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is unlikely to be seen in a patient with Gorlin syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Osteoma is not a part of Gorlin syndrome. Gorlin syndrome/basal cell naevus syndrome is an autosomal dominant condition caused by a mutation in the PTCH gene . Components of Gorlin syndrome include : • Basal cell carcinomas • Medulloblastoma • Bifid ribs • Odontogenic keratocysts

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: ABCDE rule applies for:
mcqs.explanation: ABCDE algorithm is used to diagnose melanoma. It comprises of: • Asymmetry • Border irregularity • Color variegation • Diameter of more than 6 mm • Evolution or change Melanoma is a malignant tumor arising from melanocytes at the epidermal -dermal junction. Though it represents only 4% of skin cancers, it accounts for 80% of deaths (high mortality rate).1262 It presents as a pigmented lesion that has enlarged , ulcerated , or bled . Histopathological confirmation is the gold standard in the diagnosis of melanoma. It is divided into four main types : nodular melanoma (NM), superficial spreading melanoma (SSM), lentigo maligna melanoma (LMM), and acral lentiginous melanoma (ALM). The treatment consists of wide local excision of the tumor and follow -up to detect any local recurrence around the scar and excluding nodal spread .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: An anxious patient with a black mole over his back presents to the clinic for evaluation. All of the following features according to the ABCDE rule will point towards a diagnosis of melanoma in this patient except ?
mcqs.explanation: D stands for diameter >6 mm and not depth > 6mm.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true regarding malignant melanoma?

options.a: Lentigo maligna type has the worst prognosis
options.d: Acral melanoma is the most common type in dark -skinned individuals

mcqs.explanation: Lentigo maligna melanoma has the best prognosis. Nodular melanoma has the worst prognosis. Option B: Malignant melanoma arises from melanocytes at the dermo-epidermal junction (junctional melanocytes ). They may also arise from mucosal surfaces of the eyes , pharynx, esophagus , anorectal and genital areas. Option C: Malignant melanoma most commonly metastasizes to the lungs . Option D: Acral melanoma is the most common type in dark -skinned individuals.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common type of malignant melanoma?
mcqs.explanation: Superficial spreading melanoma is the most common type of malignant melanoma. It usually arises in a pre-existent naevus. Other types of malignant melanoma include : • Nodular melanoma - presents as a nodule , and has the worst prognosis. • Acral lentiginous melanoma - commonly seen over palms and soles . Most common melanoma in dark -skinned individuals. • Lentigo maligna melanoma - also known as Hutchinson's melanotic freckle. More commonly seen on sun-exposed areas like the face , neck, or hands of the elderly . It is the least common and has the best prognosis.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What does the finding depicted in the image signify ?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows Hutchinsons's nail sign in subungual melanoma. It arises from the nail matrix, most commonly in the great toe or thumb.1263 Hutchinson's nail sign is an important clinical clue to subungual melanoma. It is characterized by the extension of brown or black pigment from the nail bed , matrix, and nail plate to the adjacent cuticle and proximal or lateral nail folds . It is also associated with nail dystrophy . Note : Pseudo -Hutchison's sign is a reflection of the pigmentation of the nail bed and nail matrix through the transparent nail folds . Option A: Subungal hematoma is a close differential of subungual melanoma. It is seen secondary to trauma which causes bleeding and resultant hematoma formation and pigmentation . It is important to note that the features of Hutchinson's nail sign are not seen with subungual hematoma.Option B: Nodular melanoma is a condition where malignant melanoma cells proliferate downwards through the skin – this is known as vertical growth . The lesion presents as a nodule that has been rapidly enlarging.1264 Option D: Lentigo maligna is an early form of melanoma, in which the malignant cells are confined to the tissue of origin, the epidermis, hence it is often reported as in-situ melanoma.Note : Subungual melanoma can be either superficial spreading melanoma or acral lentiginous melanoma. A difference of opinion has been noted in Bailey and Love, 27th ed . where it has been mentioned that melanoma under the fingernail is usually superficial spreading melanoma. However, most dermatology textbooks including the Rooks 9th ed . and Fitzpatrick's 9th ed and several research articles mentioned subungual melanoma as a variant of acral lentiginous melanoma.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Most common site of lentigo maligna melanoma is ______
mcqs.explanation: Lentigo maligna melanoma also known as Hutchison's melanotic freckle is more commonly seen on sun-exposed areas like face , neck or hands of the elderly . It is the least common and least malignant type .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following can be used for staging patients with melanoma?
mcqs.explanation: Both Breslow and Clark 's system is used for melanoma staging . Breslow thickness is the depth of invasion measured from the granular layer of the epidermis to the base of the lesion. As the thickness of the melanoma increases, the prognosis worsens. Clark 's is based on the layer of skin to which melanoma has invaded. Breslow thickness has largely supplanted Clark 's as it is a more accurate method of predicting prognosis. Van -nyus prognostic index is used for DCIS. Atlanta's is used for acute pancreatitis .1265 Onodera's prognostic index is used for hepatocellular carcinoma after initial hepatectomy

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A farmer presented with a brownish lesion over the plantar aspect of the left foot for 2 years. Over the last few months, he noticed that the lesion was increasing in size. On examination, a 2 x 1.5cm asymmetric lesion with notched edges was noted . Excision biopsy revealed cells containing large, pleomorphic nuclei and numerous mitotic figures . Which of the following will be used as a marker for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given history and biopsy finding is suggestive of melanoma. S-100 is a marker for melanoma. Other markers for melanoma are: • MELAN-A • HMB (Human Melanoma Black)-45 • LDH

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following will be the most important prognostic indicator in patients with stage 1 melanoma?
mcqs.explanation: The best prognostic factor in primary stage 1 melanoma (T1N0 ) is the tumor thickness or depth of the melanoma. The presence of lymph node metastases is the single most important prognostic index for melanoma in general . But in Stage 1 melanoma, as there is no lymph node involvement, the depth of the melanoma is the best prognostic factor. Other major prognostic factors, in order of impact on survival , include : • Presence of lymph node metastases • Ulceration • Age • Anatomic location of the primary tumor • Gender

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Arrange the types of melanoma from best to worst according to their prognosis?
mcqs.explanation: The order of prognosis for types of melanoma from better to worse is: Lentigo maligna melanoma (LMM) and acral lentiginous melanoma (ALM) > superficial spreading melanoma (SSM) > nodular melanoma (NM) The LMM and ALM both have long horizontal phases . As a result of this, there will be more time to detect them before they enter the vertical phase of growth . Thus LMM and ALM have a better prognosis than other subtypes . The SSM has an intermediate prognosis, as the horizontal phase is rapidly followed by the vertical phase. The NM has the worst prognosis, as there is no horizontal phase and it starts with a vertical growth phase . This leads to a greater average tumor thickness.1266

mcqs.question: A patient presented from the dermatology out-patient with a biopsy -proven melanoma on her right arm with a Breslow depth of 2.1 mm. Nodes were clinically negative . What is the surgical management for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Wide local excision with a resection margin of 2 cm along with sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB ) will be recommended for melanomas invading to a depth > 2mm . Recommended margins of wide local excision: Wide local excision with SLNB is preferred for early-stage tumours. SLNB should be performed for lesions >1mm in depth . If SLNB is positive or if nodes are clinically positive , lymph node dissection should be performed . SLN biopsy is more challenging in the head and neck than in other regions because of the rich lymphatic drainage network, and the false -negative rate for SLN biopsy is generally higher for melanomas in these locations. mcqs.question: Which of the following FDA-approved adjuvant therapy will be recommended for patients with malignant melanoma?
mcqs.explanation: The only systemic adjuvant therapy approved by the US FDA for malignant melanoma is high-dose interferon alpha 2b. It is administered at nearly the maximum tolerated dose , with 1 month of intravenous injections followed by 11 months of subcutaneous injections three times weekly . Note : Dabrafenib is a BRAF inhibitor used in advanced stages of melanoma.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is false regarding Merkel cell carcinoma ?

options.a: Regional lymph nodes will be involved in 30% of the cases
options.b: It is characterized by a rapidly growing, flesh -colored papule
options.d: Wide local excision is usually done

mcqs.explanation: Recurrence is common in Merkel cell carcinoma .1267 Merkel cell carcinoma is a rare and aggressive neuroendocrine tumor of the skin, most commonly found in white men and diagnosed at a mean age of 70 years. A rapidly growing, flesh -colored papule or plaque characterizes the disease . Regional lymph nodes are involved in 30% of the patients and 50% will develop systemic disease . CK-20 is a specific marker for Merkel cell carcinoma . Wide local excision is usually necessary .

mcqs.question: A lady comes with a reddish firm nodule on her chest which hasn't grown in size. Its histolopathological image is shown below . What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of a woman with reddish firm nodule on her chest and histology showing multiple dilated vascular structures with a single layer of epithelial cells is suggestive of a hemangioma. Hemangioma is a benign tumor caused by the abnormal growth of blood vessels . Types of hemangioma are capillary hemangioma (most common), juvenile/ strawberry hemangioma, cavernous hemangioma and pyogenic hemangioma. Indications for immediate treatment are complications such as ulceration or those pertaining to the location of the mass (e.g. visual issues due to a large hemangioma over the eyelid ). Treatment options include : • Beta-blockers - oral propranolol • Steroids - intralesional triamcinolone, topical clobetasol , systemic steroids • Interferon alfa-2a and vincristine - for steroid -resistant lesions • Local resection with cutting cautery or carbon dioxide laser The given image shows a flat to elevated , irregular, pinkish-red mass over the skin of the abdomen suggestive of a strawberry hemangioma.The given image shows a capillary hemangioma in a child1268

mcqs.question: Extra mammary Paget 's disease is commonly seen in the :
mcqs.explanation: Extramammary Paget 's disease arises most frequently on the vulva . Other sites include the perineum, scrotum, perianal skin, and penis . Extramammary Paget 's disease (EMPD) can be primary or secondary. • Primary EMPD is more common and occurs in the absence of an underlying malignancy, thought to arise from intraepidermal parts of apocrine glands or from pluripotent cells from the epidermis . • Secondary EMPD arises from an underlying adnexal carcinoma or internal malignancy due to the epidermotropic spread of malignant cells from the underlying tumor. Visceral malignancies associated with EMPD are carcinomas of the colon, rectum, bladder , urethra, cervix, and prostate . The patient presents with well -defined , moist, erythematous scaly plaques and severe pruritis. Lichenification and excoriations may also be seen . Diagnosis is confirmed by punch, wedge , or excisional skin biopsy . A systemic workup should also be done to identify any underlying malignancy and they include colonoscopy , cystoscopy , colposcopy , and pelvic examination with pap smear in females . Treatment: • Mohs microscopic surgery with 5 cm margin clearance • Radiotherapy • Topical 5-fluorouracil and imiquimod • Chemotherapy • Photodynamic therapy The given image below shows extramammary Paget 's disease of the vulva .1269

mcqs.question: A postmenopausal lady presented with an itchy plaque over the vulva for the past 2 years, which persisted despite multiple topical treatments . Biopsy of the lesion revealed large vacuolated cells with mucin. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and presence of large vacuolated cells with mucin (Paget 's cells ) points to a diagnosis of extramammary Paget 's disease . It is a form of intraepidermal adenocarcinoma. Extramammary Paget 's disease usually presents in the sixth to eighth decades of life . It may occur in the genital or perianal regions, or in cutaneous sites rich in apocrine glands such as the axilla. Approximately 25% of the cases are associated with an underlying in situ or invasive neoplasm . It most commonly presents with pruritus. The clinical appearance is similar to mammary Paget 's Disease . Scattered areas of erosion and white scale can give rise to a "strawberries and cream" appearance . The invasion of the lymphatic system by the tumor gives rise to underpants -pattern erythema . Surgical excision forms the basis of treatment . The given image shows large vacuolated cells with mucin (Paget 's cells )1270

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In which of the following subtypes of soft tissue sarcoma is lymph node dissection mandatory?
mcqs.explanation: Most of the soft tissue sarcomas undergo hematogenous dissemination to metastasize to lungs , liver, bones, and subcutaneous tissue . Regional lymph node involvement is relatively uncommon. However, the most common subtypes with nodal metastasis are: • Clear cell sarcoma • Liposarcoma • Rhabdomyosarcoma • Angiosarcoma • Epitheloid sarcoma • Malignant fibrous histiocytoma Lymph node involvement is an important prognostic indicator for survival . Hence , lymph node dissection is mandatory in these cases .1271
